379. **DEC-PYRIGHT-UNMASK-001 — un-mask the pyright type gate: the CI `type` job now installs `[dev,data,ui]` (faithful type-checking of `brutex/dashboard/` + the data paths)** (2026-06-02, operator-chosen plan "harden the guarantees first"; closes the `[ui]`-masked-pyright follow-up flagged in #378's honest envelope + gap #3 of the 2026-06-02 verification report). **Root cause:** the CI `type` job installed `pip install -e ".[dev]"` only (`ci.yml`), so fastapi/pydantic/polars/duckdb resolved to Unknown under `reportMissingImports="none"` — pyright never actually type-checked the dashboard or data paths. With the runtime extras installed (the faithful env, matching the `test` job + local), `pyright brutex tests` surfaces **10 real errors that CI was masking**: 1 × `reportUntypedBaseClass` at `brutex/dashboard/app.py:80` (the `CredentialsIn(BaseModel)` pydantic-v2 model — a known pyright-strict false positive on pydantic's typed base) + 9 × `reportCallIssue` "Argument missing for parameter `draw`" in `tests/property/test_combo_hash_uniqueness.py` (the Hypothesis `@st.composite` strategies are called without `draw`, which Hypothesis injects — pyright does not model the `@composite` signature transform). **Fix:** (1) `ci.yml` type job → `pip install -e ".[dev,data,ui]"` (it already builds `fno_math`, DEC-P0-050), so pyright sees REAL types; (2) per-site `# pyright: ignore[reportUntypedBaseClass]` on `app.py:80` with rationale (auditable, blast-radius = that one pydantic model; the protected real-type-safety codes `reportCallIssue`/`reportArgumentType`/`reportAttributeAccessIssue`/`reportGeneralTypeIssues` stay hard errors per the DEC-P0-002 7-agent review); (3) file-scoped `# pyright: reportCallIssue=false` in `test_combo_hash_uniqueness.py` with a rationale (the `@composite` false-positive; scoped to that one file only); (4) **NEW regression guard** `tests/unit/test_ci_type_gate_faithful.py` — fails if the type job reverts to a `[dev]`-only install (prevents silent re-masking). **Verified locally (faithful env):** `pyright brutex tests` = **0 errors, 52 warnings** (the warnings are pre-existing non-blocking `reportPrivateUsage`; pyright exits 0); `mypy --strict brutex` clean (150 files); ruff + ruff-format clean; `test_combo_hash_uniqueness` 23 pass; new guard passes. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this closes the type-gate masking hole; the 52 `reportPrivateUsage` warnings (whitebox tests touching private helpers) remain as warnings by design (`reportPrivateUsage="warning"`, DEC-P0-017), and the OTHER hardening items (O(1) 1.1× bench, omitted-module coverage, server-side branch protection, the int64-paisa §6 reconciliation) remain tracked. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-DOC-RECONCILE-001 (#378) · DEC-DASHBOARD-CI-UNMASK-001 (#376) · DEC-P0-002 / DEC-P0-014 (pyright strict policy) · CLAUDE.md §4 / §12 / §11 COMMON.

380. **DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 — reconcile the "int64 paisa storage" docs to the verified-safe code (prices are exact `Decimal` rupees, not paisa)** (2026-06-02, operator-chosen plan "harden the guarantees first" → step 2; operator selected "Fix the docs to match the code"). **Verified ground truth:** OHLC / spot / option **prices** are parsed to exact `Decimal` rupees via `brutex/data/candle_fields.py::to_price` (`Decimal(str(raw))` — no float drift, non-finite rejected), stored as `Decimal` on `CandleBar`/`OptionBar` and as Parquet `Float64` (`brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`), and `brutex/data/models.py:142-144` explicitly documents *"prices are exact Decimal rupees … the paisa ×100 happens at the lake-write boundary, never here"*. **int64 paisa is real only at the cost + display boundary** (`brutex/costs/` + `brutex/money.py`), NOT for price storage. But three docs overstated it: CLAUDE.md §4 ("Internal storage stays int64 paisa"), CLAUDE.md §6 ("Price unit … parser MUST × 100 at parse boundary to preserve int64 paisa", with a **wrong citation** — `dhan/parser.py:61-64` is the array-extraction helper `_as_array`, not a ×100), and `brutex/money.py:3` ("Track 1 stores every price as int64 paisa"). **Fix (docs-to-code, per the operator choice — NOT a code refactor, since `Decimal` is already exact and a paisa migration would churn reproducibility hashes for no precision gain):** corrected CLAUDE.md §4 + §6 (accurate text + real citations: `candle_fields.to_price`→`Decimal`, `models.py:142-144`) and the `money.py` module docstring (money/costs = int64 paisa; prices = Decimal rupees). **NEW property test** `tests/property/test_price_precision_invariant.py` (8 cases) — pins that `to_price` returns the exact rupee `Decimal`, never a ×100 paisa integer, and rejects non-finite; fails if a paisa-scaling regression enters the price path. **Verified locally:** the 8 property cases pass; `pyright` on the new test 0 errors (the faithful gate from #379); `mypy --strict brutex` clean; ruff + ruff-format clean; interrogate 100% (gated). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** this corrects an inaccurate factual claim in the authority doc to match the code (the code was right + numerically safe all along); it does **not** change any runtime behavior or storage format, and does not touch the still-tracked hardening items (O(1) 1.1× bench, omitted-module coverage, server-side branch protection). If the operator later wants TRUE int64-paisa price storage, that is a separate, larger decision (needs a 4-agent hostile review per §9). **Builds on:** DEC-PYRIGHT-UNMASK-001 (#379) · DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 · CLAUDE.md §4 / §6 / §11 COMMON.

381. **DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 — two-tier O(1) ratio gate: shared CI keeps its robust tolerance; the decreed 1.1× becomes a WIRED strict tier on the self-hosted M4-Pro runner** (2026-06-02, operator-chosen plan "harden the guarantees first" → step 3; operator selected "Two-tier gate now + keep going"). **Problem:** the O(1) NFR decree (CLAUDE.md §2 r5 / §12) targets `p99(N_big)/p99(N_small) ≤ 1.1×`, but shared 2-core GitHub runners are too noisy to gate at 1.1× without chronic flaking (DEC-P0-020) — so the bench ratio gates enforce a robust 3–10× shared-CI ceiling, leaving the 1.1× decree unenforced anywhere. **Fix (COMMON, one source of truth — CLAUDE.md §11):** new `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py` defines `ratio_ceiling(shared_ci_default)` → returns the decreed **1.1×** (`STRICT_RATIO_CEILING`) when `BRUTEX_M4PRO_STRICT=1` (strict-decoder: literal trimmed `"1"`), else the caller's robust default (identical shared-CI behaviour — zero added flakiness). Every O(1) ratio gate now routes its ceiling through it: `test_store_o1.py` (×2), `test_option_dedup_o1.py`, `test_lmdb_membership_o1.py`, `test_rate_limiter_o1.py` (the 5× dedup/latency gates) + `test_throughput_canary.py` (`_RATIO_CEILING` 8× + `dict_ratio_ceiling` 10×). `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml` sets `BRUTEX_M4PRO_STRICT=1` (job env) + adds a "Run strict 1.1× O(1) ratio tier" step running the ratio suite on the self-hosted M4-Pro runner (mirrors the existing `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS` absolute-gate pattern). **NEW helper test** `tests/bench/test_o1_tiers.py` (8 cases) — proves the default-when-unset + 1.1×-when-set + strict-decoder semantics, so shared CI provably keeps its current ceilings. **Verified locally:** shared-CI mode (env unset) — all 25 ratio-bench cases PASS UNCHANGED (17.7s); helper test 8 pass; `pyright tests/bench` 0 errors (the faithful gate from #379); ruff + ruff-format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the strict 1.1× tier is **WIRED but DORMANT** until the operator registers the self-hosted M4-Pro runner (`runs-on: [self-hosted, macos, m4pro]`) — I cannot register hardware, and 1.1× is genuinely infeasible on shared GHA. Shared CI is **unchanged** (3–10× robust tier); whether the current measurement actually holds <1.1× on a real quiet M4-Pro is an empirical question the operator validates on that hardware (the ceiling is one constant, tunable there). STANDARDS_100PCT.md row 13 updated from "ROADMAP" to "WIRED two-tier". **Builds on:** DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 (#380) · DEC-P0-020 (ratio-gate flake-mitigation) · DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 (#236, the env-gated self-hosted pattern) · CLAUDE.md §2 r5 / §11 COMMON / §12.

382. **DEC-M4PRO-PR-TRIGGER-001 — drop the `pull_request` trigger from `bench-m4pro.yml` (it hung bench-touching PRs on the offline self-hosted runner)** (2026-06-02, found while monitoring PR #284). **Symptom:** #284 (the first PR since the M4-Pro runner went offline to touch `tests/bench/`) triggered `bench-m4pro.yml`'s paths-filtered `pull_request` job; with no `[self-hosted, macos, m4pro]` runner registered, `m4pro-absolute-throughput` queued **pending forever**, leaving the PR `mergeable_state="unstable"` and the `pre-merge-gate.yml` bot emitting a false **"❌ MERGE BLOCKED (pending checks)"** verdict. **Not actually blocking:** `m4pro-*` is NOT in the required `CI OK (aggregate gate)` set, so auto-merge (which keys on `CI OK == success`) correctly merged #284 anyway — but the false BLOCK + perpetually-pending PR check are exactly the "issue / not-clean-merge" the operator's merge-readiness charter forbids. **Fix:** removed the `pull_request:` trigger from `bench-m4pro.yml`; the workflow keeps `push` (main/branches), `schedule` (nightly), and `workflow_dispatch`. PRs now use the shared-CI **robust O(1) tier** (`ci.yml`); the strict 1.1× (DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001) + absolute (DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001) tiers run on push-to-main + nightly + manual dispatch, where a queued-while-offline run is harmless (no PR to block). A rationale comment in the workflow documents how to re-add a paths-filtered `pull_request:` once the runner is registered (for pre-merge strict checks). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this removes a false-BLOCK / unstable-mergeable wart on bench-touching PRs; it does NOT change shared-CI behaviour and does NOT register the runner (operator hardware). The `push`-to-main trigger can still queue a harmless pending run while the runner is offline (cosmetic; no merge to block) — acceptable per the workflow's own "queued state is harmless" design note. **Builds on:** DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 (#381) · DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 (#236) · DEC-MERGE-GUARANTEE-001 (clean `mergeable_state`) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON.

383. **DEC-COVERAGE-DRIVER-001 — lift `brutex/execution/driver.py` to 100% line+branch + un-omit it (strict per-module gate)** (2026-06-02, operator-chosen plan "harden the guarantees first" → step 4). **Context:** `execution/driver.py` was one of three modules `omit`-ed from the coverage gate (it sat at **83.13%** — below the 90% floor) per DEC-DASHBOARD-OMIT-AUDIT-001. Measured uncovered (full-suite, omit-overridden): lines `86, 96, 101, 121, 159-160, 170, 174, 180` + 5 partial branches — all guard/error paths the heavy integration suite never exercised: the interval-mismatch contract, the `simulator`/`state` property getters, the out-of-scope-event skip, `ExecutionError` propagation, and the three `_validate_signal` violations (non-`Signal`, out-of-scope symbol, look-ahead). **Fix:** NEW `tests/unit/test_execution_driver_edges.py` (7 tests) drives each branch with light fakes cast to the declared `Strategy`/`ReplayFeed`/`ExecutionSimulator` types (no lake needed) — together with the existing integration test this brings `driver.py` to **100.00% (67 stmts / 16 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial)**, verified locally. Removed `brutex/execution/driver.py` from `[tool.coverage.run].omit` (so it counts toward the 90% floor — un-omitting a 100% module only raises the aggregate) AND added a **strict per-module 100% gate** to the CI `test` job (`pytest --cov=brutex.execution.driver --cov-fail-under=100` over the edge + integration tests, matching the DEC-COV-001 pattern) so it can never silently regress. **Verified locally:** the per-module gate command exits 0 at 100%; the new tests pass; `pyright`/`ruff` clean; the full aggregate stays ≥ 90 (driver at 100% cannot lower it). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this un-omits + locks ONE of the three below-floor modules; **`data/catalog.py` (~86%) and `data/instrument_store.py` (~87%) remain omitted** (their dedicated tests are the tracked step-4 follow-ups — instrument_store is 2,151 lines and needs a substantial harness). `cli.py` / `__main__.py` stay omitted pending the CLI snapshot harness. **Builds on:** DEC-DASHBOARD-OMIT-AUDIT-001 (#377) · DEC-COV-001 (per-module strict-100 pattern) · CLAUDE.md §4 / §12.

384. **DEC-BRANCH-PROTECTION-RUNBOOK-001 — operator runbook to enable server-side branch protection on `main` (step 5: make `CI OK` a mechanical required check)** (2026-06-02, plan "harden the guarantees first" → step 5). **Gap:** the Merge-Readiness Charter (§3/§8) wants `CI OK (aggregate gate)` to be a **server-side required status check** so GitHub blocks a manual merge over a red gate; today it is enforced by *convention* (`auto-merge.yml` keys on `CI OK == success` — which worked for every PR this session — and the pre-merge bot comments), but no GitHub branch-protection rule exists (`auto-merge.yml` itself notes "no branch protection yet"), so a human with write access could bypass it. **This step is fundamentally operator-only:** setting branch protection needs repo-admin scope, and the GitHub MCP exposes **no branch-protection tool** (verified) — Claude cannot apply it. **Deliverable:** NEW `docs/runbooks/branch-protection-setup.md` — the exact `gh api -X PUT …/branches/main/protection` payload (+ Settings-UI steps + a `jq` verify) that matches the canonical expected config already encoded in `.github/workflows/branch-protection-drift.yml` (21 required contexts ending in `CI OK (aggregate gate)`, `enforce_admins=true`, `required_linear_history`, `required_pull_request_reviews` with `required_approving_review_count: 0` so the auto-merge bot still merges on green, `required_conversation_resolution`, force-push/deletion off). The drift-check remains the single source of truth + the daily verifier; the runbook is the apply-side companion. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this does NOT itself enable protection (operator admin action — documented for a ~2-minute apply); until applied, `CI OK` stays a convention-enforced gate, not a mechanical one. Also residual (minor, non-blocking): `bench-m4pro.yml`'s `push:` trigger still fires on `claude/**` for bench-file pushes (it queues a harmless pending `m4pro` run on the offline runner — observed as a leftover on #286, which merged fine via `CI OK`); scoping that `push` to `main`-only is a tracked cosmetic follow-up. **Builds on:** DEC-MERGE-GUARANTEE-001 (charter §3/§8) · DEC-M4PRO-PR-TRIGGER-001 (#382) · `branch-protection-drift.yml` (the expected-config snapshot) · CLAUDE.md §13.

385. **DEC-COVERAGE-CATALOG-001 — lift `brutex/data/catalog.py` to 100% line+branch + un-omit it (strict per-module gate)** (2026-06-02, operator-chosen plan "harden the guarantees first" → step 4 follow-up). **Context:** `data/catalog.py` (the DuckDB-backed lake catalog — `partitions` table + `get_bars` Arrow zero-copy reader + `data_snapshot_hash` rollup) was the 2nd of three modules `omit`-ed from the coverage gate (it sat at **86%** — below the 90% floor) per DEC-DASHBOARD-OMIT-AUDIT-001, and was named as a tracked follow-up in DEC-COVERAGE-DRIVER-001 (#383). Measured uncovered (full-suite, omit-overridden): lines `77-78, 94, 145-147, 209, 314, 323-324, 407, 411, 462-466, 472` + the `222->225` / `225->234` partial branches — all guard / defensive paths the real-lake suite (`test_data_lake_real.py`) never reaches: the `open()` missing-`duckdb` ImportError, the `path` property getter, the `upsert` `BEGIN → … → ROLLBACK → raise` transaction-rollback, the closed-catalog guards on `list_partitions` / `get_bars` / `data_snapshot_hash`, the `list_partitions` `start=None` / `end=None` clause-skip partials, the `get_bars` missing-`polars`/`pyarrow` ImportError, the `data_snapshot_hash` inverted-window guard, the `open_catalog` context-manager sugar, and the `_require_tz_aware` naive-datetime guard. **Fix:** NEW `tests/integration/test_catalog.py` (13 tests) drives each branch against a real DuckDB catalog plus light fakes — a `_RollbackConn` fake (raises on `INSERT`, records the verb sequence so the test asserts `["BEGIN","DELETE","INSERT","ROLLBACK"]` and never `COMMIT`) for the rollback path, and `monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "duckdb"/"polars", None)` (the None-sentinel → ImportError trick) for the missing-dependency paths — together with the existing `test_data_lake_real.py` happy-path suite this brings `catalog.py` to **100.00% (132 stmts / 40 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial)**, verified locally (44 combined tests pass). Removed `brutex/data/catalog.py` from `[tool.coverage.run].omit` (un-omitting a 100% module only raises the aggregate) AND added a **strict per-module 100% gate** to the CI `test` job (`pytest --cov=brutex.data.catalog --cov-fail-under=100` over `test_data_lake_real.py` + `test_catalog.py`, matching the DEC-COVERAGE-DRIVER-001 / DEC-COV-001 pattern) so it can never silently regress. **Verified locally:** the per-module gate command exits 0 at 100%; the new tests pass; `ruff` + `ruff format` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the new file; the full aggregate stays ≥ 90 (catalog at 100% cannot lower it). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this un-omits + locks the 2nd of the three below-floor modules; **`data/instrument_store.py` (~87%, 2,151 lines) remains omitted** — its dedicated harness is the immediate next follow-up (the largest of the three; needs a substantial test harness). `cli.py` / `__main__.py` stay omitted pending the CLI snapshot harness. A separately-tracked accuracy item (NOT in this PR, to keep it coverage-focused): `catalog.py:395`'s docstring still reads "Iterable of Groww trading symbols" — a stale-vendor leftover folded into the dedicated Groww→Dhan doc-reconcile sweep (operator flagged the lingering Groww references 2026-06-02). **Builds on:** DEC-COVERAGE-DRIVER-001 (#383) · DEC-DASHBOARD-OMIT-AUDIT-001 (#377) · DEC-COV-001 (per-module strict-100 pattern) · CLAUDE.md §4 / §12.

386. **DEC-DHAN-RECONCILE-DATA-001 — Groww→Dhan vendor reconcile of the data/lake/feed layer + `watermark.groww_symbol`→`vendor_symbol` rename** (2026-06-02, operator-flagged: the dashboard/`/db` still *read* as Groww-era). **Context:** the live vendor is Dhan (DEC-GROWW-DHAN-REVERT-001 / ADR-0002); the Groww adapter was deleted (DEC-DHAN-FINALIZE-001), but ~188 stale "Groww" mentions survived in `brutex/` — comments, docstrings, and a few identifiers — making the lake/DB *look* Groww-era even though the schema is vendor-neutral / Dhan-keyed. This entry covers the **data + feed + package layer** (the surface the operator browses on `/db` + `/universe`); the orchestrator/cli/docs sweep is the next PR. **Fix (12 files, +53/−51):** corrected the package docstring `brutex/__init__.py` (was the flatly-wrong "BruteX uses the Groww Trade API" → Dhan Data API v2); reconciled docstrings/DDL-comments in `data/instrument_store.py` (the `partitions`/instrument-master/`contract_symbol` comments), `data/models.py`, `data/partition.py` (dropped the `groww.in/trade-api/docs` annexure URL; "12 canonical candle intervals"), `data/errors.py`, `feed/resampler.py`, `feed/replay.py`, `feed/__init__.py`; made `data/parser.py` **vendor-neutral** ("7-element row format" + a note that the live Dhan path uses the *columnar* `adapters/dhan/parser.py`) — deliberately NOT relabeled "Dhan" since Dhan returns columnar arrays, not 7-tuples (Golden Rule #1); fixed the `option_parquet_writer.py` `[dev,groww]`→`[dev]` extra note; **functional rename** `groww_symbol`→`vendor_symbol` in `data/watermark.py` (dataclass field + both JSON keys) + `tests/unit/test_watermark.py`. **Deliberately KEPT** (accurate, not rot): `costs/*` "groww"/"zerodha" are real **brokerage cost models** (not the data vendor); `candle_fields.py` provenance note. **Verified:** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150 files) + `pyright` (0 errors) clean; full suite **3075 passed / 42 skipped**; `data.partition` + `data.models` per-module 100% gates still green. **Diagnostic findings (operator's "empty candle table" question) — three tracked follow-ups:** (1) the empty `candles` lake is **expected behaviour** — no Dhan credentials → `dry_run=true` → `NullBarSink` discards bars (`app.py:771`, `pull_controller.py:277-287,628`, `sink.py:92-107`); resolution = set creds at `/credentials` + launch `brutex dashboard --lake-root <path>` + Pull (the real path is verified end-to-end: SECURITY_ID resolve → `/charts/intraday` 1m + `/charts/historical` 1d → columnar parse → Parquet write → `/db` read-back; no blocking bug). (2) **Real gap:** `_build_live_spot_adapter` constructs `ParquetBarSink` with no `catalog=` (`pull_controller.py:317`), so live pulls write Parquet but skip the DuckDB `partitions` catalog upsert — harmless for the candle viewer (reads Parquet directly) but `data_snapshot_hash` (Golden Rule #4 reproducibility) won't see live partitions; tracked fix = pass `catalog=`. (3) **Doc bug:** `docs/dhan-ref/05-historical-data.md` + `06-expired-options-data.md` still instruct "parser MUST ×100 to preserve int64 paisa" — WRONG (code keeps exact `Decimal` rupees per DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 / #283); tracked doc reconcile. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-DHAN-REVERT-001 / ADR-0002 · DEC-DHAN-FINALIZE-001 · DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 (#283) · CLAUDE.md §1 / §6.

387. **DEC-DHAN-IDX-SEGMENT-001 — fix the Dhan spot pull: index `IDX_I` segment + `oi:true` + 2021/previous-day range defaults** (2026-06-02, operator-flagged: pulled index candles came back wrong/synthetic-looking; a deep audit vs the official DhanHQ-py SDK + `dhanhq.co/docs/v2` found the request body was wrong for the 3 brute-force indices). **Root cause (CRITICAL — a regression):** `adapter.py` built `exchangeSegment = f"{exchange}_EQ"` → `NSE_EQ`/`BSE_EQ` for NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. The official SDK sets `INDEX='IDX_I'` (segment code 0 ≠ `NSE_EQ` code 1) and every index example uses `IDX_I`; sending `_EQ` for an index returns no/incorrect candles. `IDX_I` was not even in `EXCHANGE_SEGMENTS` (passing it would have raised `DhanBodyError`). BruteX's own retired specs already said all 4 indices use `IDX_I`, so this was a regression — not a new decision. **Fixes:** (1) `constants.py` — added `"IDX_I"` to `EXCHANGE_SEGMENTS`; `adapter.py:128` — indices resolve to `"IDX_I"`, real EQUITY keeps `*_EQ`. (2) `body.py` — `build_intraday_body` + `build_historical_body` now send `oi: bool = True` (was omitted → `open_interest` always null; operator wants OI on — indices return empty OI, futures/stocks/options populate it). (3) `pull_controller.py` `resolve_candle_range` — blank date pickers now default to the full `2021-01-01` history floor (was the current UTC year — why a blank pull only fetched 2026); default end is the **previous day** (was `today`), with an explicit `to_date` allowed to reach today (operator: "don't pull the current day unless I pick it"). (4) `toDate` non-inclusivity verified already-correct (inclusive end → `+1` exclusive in `resolve_candle_range`; no double-`+1`) + regression test added. (5) `universe.html` + `app.py` docstrings → "previous trading day". (6) `CLAUDE.md §6` — `IDX_I` added to the Backtesting-segments + brute-force-universe rows (the §6 fact table omitting `IDX_I` is what let the adapter regress). **Intentionally NOT changed:** `interval` stays the `"1"` string (matches the REST doc JSON; the SDK-sends-int discrepancy is flagged with a TODO for a Phase-0 empirical check). The options path was audited + is already correct (underlying SECURITY_ID + `*_FNO` segment + `OPTIDX`/`OPTSTK`, `option_pull_controller.py:112-114`). **Verified:** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150 files) + `pyright` (0 errors) clean; full suite **3080 passed / 42 skipped**; per-module 100% line+branch gates green for `adapters.dhan.{constants,body,adapter}` + `dashboard.{option_pull_controller,pull_controller}`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the `IDX_I` fix is SDK+docs-confirmed and matches Dhan's own examples, but END-TO-END proof needs a live pull with real Dhan credentials (not runnable in CI/here) — pull NIFTY and confirm real ~24,000 values + populated OI. **Tracked follow-ups (NOT in this PR):** live spot pulls still skip the DuckDB `partitions` catalog upsert (no `catalog=`) → `data_snapshot_hash` won't see live partitions; `docs/dhan-ref/05+06` stale ×100 note (reconciled when the authoritative Dhan v2 reference set is added to `docs/dhan-ref/`). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RECONCILE-DATA-001 (#386) · DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 · DEC-DHAN-GIFTNIFTY-SESSION-001 · CLAUDE.md §1 / §6.

389. **DEC-OHLC-VENDOR-NORMALIZE-001 — normalize vendor OHLC quirks at the parse boundary (unblock real Dhan pulls)** (2026-06-02, operator-hit on the first real-credential pull). **Symptom:** with the `IDX_I` fix (#387) live, a real Dhan pull of NIFTY 2021→prev-day reached the vendor and returned REAL data (`open=17289.0` — real mid-2021 NIFTY, not the old ~5000 synthetic), then failed: `ValueError: CandleBar: open (17289.0) must be in [low=17264.8496, high=17287.0996]` — Dhan reported the candle `high` (17287.10) BELOW the authoritative traded `open` (17289.0), and the strict `CandleBar` invariant (`data/models.py:_validate_price_bar`, `low <= open,close <= high`) failed the ENTIRE multi-year ingest on that one quirk bar. **Root cause:** `assemble_candle` (`data/candle_fields.py`) built the bar from Dhan's raw `high`/`low`; vendor OHLC occasionally has open/close marginally outside the reported `[low, high]` (rounding / auction artifacts). **Fix:** `assemble_candle` now clamps `high = max(open, high, low, close)`, `low = min(open, high, low, close)` — the mathematically-correct bound (a traded open of 17289 implies the true high ≥ 17289; CORRECTS Dhan's under-reported high, never loses data). The strict `CandleBar` invariant is UNCHANGED for any non-assembler construction path (it still catches genuinely-broken internal bars). +3 tests (`test_candle_fields.py`: open-above-high → high clamped; close-below-low → low clamped; consistent-bar unchanged). **Verified:** `brutex.data.candle_fields` per-module 100% gate green; full suite **3083 passed / 42 skipped**; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150) + `pyright` (0) clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is the fix that lets a real NIFTY pull complete end-to-end; it normalizes (corrects) vendor data at ingest — surfacing a count of normalized bars in the ingest report is a tracked observability follow-up (the correction is silent-but-mathematically-exact today). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-IDX-SEGMENT-001 (#387) · DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 (#283) · CLAUDE.md §4 / §6.

390. **DEC-OPTIONS-DB-VIEWER-001 — surface the options Parquet lake in the `/db` candle viewer** (2026-06-02, operator-selected follow-up from the field-mapping audit). **Gap:** the `/db` candle viewer (`dashboard/db_view.py::list_candle_datasets` / `query_candles`) walked only the spot `bars/<exchange>/<segment>/<symbol>/<interval>/` tree, so options written by `OptionParquetWriter` to `<lake>/options/<series>/YYYY-MM.parquet` (series key `exchange_segment|security_id|expiry_flag|expiry_code|strike|drv_option_type`) were invisible in the dashboard even after a successful options pull — the "where are my options" symptom. **Fix:** `db_view.py` — `list_option_datasets` (walks `<lake>/options/`, tags `kind="option"`; spot now tagged `kind="spot"`) + `query_option_candles` (reads the series Parquet via a bound DuckDB `read_parquet` glob — no free user text, same SQL/path-injection guard as spot via the new `_validate_option_segment`), with the shared UTC-date WHERE builder + IST row renderer refactored out (DRY, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); `app.py` — `/api/v1/db/candles/datasets` now also returns options + a new `GET /api/v1/db/options` route; `db.html` — the picker merges spot+option datasets (labelled `[spot]`/`[option]`) and shows the 4 extra option columns (`side`/`strike`/`spot`/`iv`, iv full-precision). **Verified:** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150) + `pyright` (0) clean; full suite **3104 passed / 42 skipped** (18 new options-viewer tests seeding a real options Parquet via the production writer); `db_view.py` **100.00% line + branch**; end-to-end probe (writer→lake→`query_option_candles`→JSON) returns all 11 columns with 2dp prices + full-precision iv + clean-IST timestamps. **No schema change** (the options table already had all 11 columns — confirmed by the DEC-DHAN-IDX-SEGMENT-001 audit); this is purely a dashboard READER addition. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-DOCSET-001 (#388) · DEC-DHAN-IDX-SEGMENT-001 (#387) · CLAUDE.md §1 / §11.

391. **DEC-DHAN-RECONCILE-NONDATA-001 — Phase-2 Groww→Dhan naming cleanup (orchestrator + cli + models + protocol)** (2026-06-02, finishes the non-data-layer half of the de-Groww; the data/feed/package half was DEC-DHAN-RECONCILE-DATA-001 / #386 / #289). **Context:** ~145 stale "Groww" refs survived in `brutex/` outside the data layer — orchestrator docstrings/messages/env-vars, cli, the top-level `models.py`, `adapters/protocol.py`, execution/strategies/observability/config. corrected the factually-wrong Dhan rate envelope (`[4..8]`/initial-8 → Dhan **`[3..5]`, initial 5** per `dhan/constants.py` DATA_RATE_LIMIT_RPS=5 + `dhan/rate_control.py`), `GrowwAPIRateLimitException` → `DhanRateLimitError`, the "805/DH-904 Groww error catalog" → the Dhan `dhan/errors.py` hierarchy; user-facing messages `"Daily Groww API quota exceeded"` → `"Daily Dhan API quota exceeded"` (`quota_tracker.py` + test), `"bad request from Groww"` → `"bad request from Dhan"` (`state.py` + `test_dashboard_state.py`), `"Unknown Groww API exception"` → `"Unknown Dhan API exception"` (`retry.py` + `test_orchestrator_retry.py`); plus docstring/comment reconciles in `cli.py`, top-level `models.py`, `adapters/protocol.py` ("locked to the Dhan adapter"; `brutex/adapters/dhan/` path; Dhan's 90-day spot / 30-day option windows), `execution/*`, `strategies/*`, `observability/*`, `config/runtime.py`, `universe.py`, `sprint/*`, `options/strike_grid.py`. **Deliberately KEPT** (accurate, Golden Rule #1): `costs/*` `Broker = Literal["groww","zerodha"]` + `GROWW_BROKERAGE_PAISA` (real brokerage cost models, NOT the data vendor) + `execution/costs.py` golden-test ref; `data/candle_fields.py` provenance; `adapters/__init__.py` "removed in full" history; `config/credentials.py` + `dashboard/app.py` accurate carryover notes; all `adapters/dhan/*` "Dhan analog of legacy Groww" contrastive history; immutable decision IDs (`DEC-GROWW-DHAN-REVERT-001`, `DEC-GROWW-INGEST-001`). **Verified:** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150) + `pyright` (0) clean; full suite **3080 passed / 42 skipped**; per-module 100% gates green for every touched gated module (`models`, `adapters.protocol`, `observability.logging`, `config.runtime`, `execution.types`, `strategies.*`, `universe`, `options.strike_grid`, `costs.*`). Final `grep -ic groww brutex/` leaves only the intentional-history refs. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RECONCILE-DATA-001 (#386) · DEC-GROWW-DHAN-REVERT-001 / ADR-0002 · CLAUDE.md §6 / §11.

392. **DEC-COVERAGE-INSTRUMENT-STORE-001 — lift `brutex/data/instrument_store.py` to 100% line+branch + un-omit it (strict per-module gate)** (2026-06-02, operator-chosen plan "harden the guarantees first" → the 3rd + final below-floor module). **Context:** `data/instrument_store.py` (2,151 lines — the DuckDB instrument-master + expiries/contracts/coverage-ledger store) was the last of the three modules `omit`-ed from the coverage gate (DEC-DASHBOARD-OMIT-AUDIT-001 / DEC-COVERAGE-CATALOG-001 #385), sitting at **69.36%** against its dedicated integration suite alone (the ~87% in the plan brief was a broader cross-suite figure). **Fix:** NEW `tests/integration/test_instrument_store_edges.py` (38 tests) drives every remaining guard / defensive / temporal / rollback branch against a real DuckDB store plus light fakes (`_RollbackConn` / `_RowInsertRollbackConn`) + `monkeypatch` — InstrumentRun validation, the snapshot read surface (`by_underlying` / `__contains__` / `meta` / `by_segment`), the `_LockedReadConn` view (execute / fetch / lock-drop / context-manager), `open()` missing-`duckdb` ImportError, the upsert / expiries / contracts INSERT-rollback paths, `as_of` temporal filters, `verify_integrity` raw-hash-mismatch tamper detection, and the `open_instrument_store` sugar — together with the existing `test_instrument_store.py` this brings the module to **100.00% (511 stmts / 70 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial)**, verified locally. 394. **DEC-VENDOR-VOLUME-NORMALIZE-001 — normalize vendor volume / open-interest quirks + ignore index volume (unblock real Dhan pulls, round 2)** (2026-06-02, operator-hit on the real-credential NIFTY pull; direct sibling of DEC-OHLC-VENDOR-NORMALIZE-001 #389). **Symptom:** with the OHLC clamp (#389) live, a real NIFTY 2021→prev-day pull progressed to ~2022-03-25 then crashed: `ValueError: CandleBar.volume must be non-negative, got -2` — Dhan emitted a stray NEGATIVE volume (`-2`) on an INDEX (an index has no traded volume at all; the `volume` array is junk — almost always 0), and the strict `CandleBar` invariant (`data/models.py:_validate_price_bar`, `volume >= 0`) failed the ENTIRE multi-year ingest on that one quirk bar (same crash-class as #389, different field). A retry cannot help — it is a data quirk, not a transient error. **Root cause:** `assemble_candle` (`data/candle_fields.py`) handed Dhan's raw `volume` / `open_interest` straight to `CandleBar`; a count's only valid floor is 0. **Fix (2 layers):** (a) **universal safety** — `assemble_candle` now clamps `volume` / `open_interest` to `max(0, …)`, so NO vendor count-quirk can crash a pull (covers stocks too); (b) **index-specific** — the spot parser gained `parse_candle_columns(…, drop_volume: bool)` and the adapter passes `drop_volume=instrument.is_index` (`adapters/dhan/adapter.py`), so an index bar's volume is ignored outright (→ 0) by construction, not merely clamped — honoring the operator decree "just ignore volume for indices". The strict `CandleBar` invariant is UNCHANGED for any non-assembler path. **+6 tests:** `test_candle_fields.py` (negative volume → 0, negative OI → 0); `test_dhan_parser.py` (`drop_volume=True` ignores the column incl. a junk negative; default keeps it); `test_dhan_adapter.py` (an index ignores its `-2` volume → 0; an equity keeps `555`). **Verified:** `brutex.data.candle_fields` per-module 100% gate green; full suite **3252 passed / 45 skipped**; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150) clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is the fix that lets the real NIFTY pull complete past 2022-03; surfacing a count of normalized / ignored bars in the ingest report remains the same tracked observability follow-up noted in #389. **Builds on:** DEC-OHLC-VENDOR-NORMALIZE-001 (#389) · DEC-DHAN-IDX-SEGMENT-001 (#387) · CLAUDE.md §4 / §6 / §7.

395. **DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 — round spot lake OHLC to the 2-decimal tick grid at the write boundary** (2026-06-02, operator request: "everywhere entirely only two digits always after the decimal points … properly precisely rounded, NOT truncated"). **Symptom:** the `/db` viewer showed NIFTY 1-minute prices as `14020.7999` / `17264.8496` — Dhan returns float-noise prices, and the SPOT `ParquetWriter._render_bytes` wrote them raw (`float(b.open)`), while the OPTION writer already rounded via `round_money` (`_money`). **Root cause:** the spot writer never mirrored the option writer's 2dp rounding (DEC-MONEY-2DP-001). **Fix:** `data/parquet_writer.py` — new `_tick_round(bar)` snaps OHLC to 2dp with the SAME `round_money` (`Decimal.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), ROUND_HALF_UP)` — proper rounding, NEVER truncation: `14020.7999 → 14020.80`, `17264.8496 → 17264.85`); applied at BOTH input boundaries (`write()` incoming + `_read_existing_bars` stored-read), so the lake stores clean 2dp AND a re-pull compares grid-vs-grid (idempotent — no false merge conflict, even over a pre-existing 4-decimal partition, which converges to 2dp on its next rewrite). Rounding is monotone, so the `low <= open,close <= high` invariant is preserved. **NOT touched** (Golden Rule #1, CLAUDE.md §4): `iv` and statistical metrics (Sharpe / DSR / p-values) keep full precision — rounding those would corrupt ranking; volume / OI / timestamp untouched. **+6 tests** (`test_parquet_writer.py`: round-half-up not truncation, exact-half-up, below-half-down, volume/OI/ts untouched; lake stores 2dp; raw-4dp re-pull is byte-idempotent). **Verified:** full suite **3252 passed / 45 skipped**; the spot + option lakes now match; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150) clean. **Honest envelope:** pre-existing 4-decimal partitions converge to 2dp on their next rewrite; a from-scratch re-pull (or `brutex wipe`) yields a uniformly-2dp lake immediately. **Builds on:** DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 · DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 (#283) · CLAUDE.md §4 / §6.

396. **DEC-OPTION-SECURITY-ID-FIX-001 — fix the options pull (numeric SECURITY_ID) + surface silent failures + stop the perpetual "pulling" badge** (2026-06-02, operator-hit: a NIFTY options-chain pull returned `series_failed=252 / series_completed=0 / bars=0` and the dashboard showed "pulling" forever). **Three bugs, one PR:** (1) **Root cause of the 252 failures:** `dashboard/option_pull_controller.py:instrument_to_option_underlying` set the rolling-option `security_id` to `instrument.vendor_symbol` (the exchange-prefixed engine key, e.g. `"NSE-NIFTY"`) instead of the NUMERIC Dhan `SECURITY_ID` held on `exchange_token` (e.g. `"13"`) — so EVERY `/charts/rollingoption` request sent `securityId: "NSE-NIFTY"` and Dhan rejected all 252 series. The spot adapter already used `exchange_token` (DEC-DHAN-VENDOR-SYMBOL-UNIQUE-001), which is why spot worked and options did not. **Fix:** use `str(instrument.exchange_token)` (+ a positive-id guard). (2) **Silent failures (the "logs unclear" symptom):** `option_universe_ingest` captured the per-series error (`OptionSeriesFailure.error`) but `pull_options` logged only the COUNT (`series_failed=252`); now a `universe.pull_options.failures` WARNING logs the distinct terminal-error messages with counts so the cause is one-glance diagnosable. (3) **Perpetual "pulling" badge:** `templates/coverage.html` set `inProgress = (attempted < total)`, so the header read `pulling · 0/1458` FOREVER whenever coverage was merely incomplete (not when a pull was actually running); it now polls `/api/v1/universe/pull-progress` and shows "pulling" ONLY when `state === "running"`, else "live". **+regression tests** (`test_option_pull_controller.py`): the underlying's `security_id` is the numeric `exchange_token`, NOT `vendor_symbol`; a non-positive id raises; an end-to-end body-capture proving the request `securityId` is numeric; the failure-error aggregation is exercised. **Verified:** `brutex.dashboard.option_pull_controller` per-module **100%** line+branch gate green; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` (150) clean; full suite green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this makes the rolling-option REQUEST correct (numeric id) so the pull is no longer rejected wholesale; if Dhan still returns no data for a specific expired series, that is now surfaced per-series (no longer silent) rather than hidden. O(1) preserved — one field projection; the Bloom+LMDB option dedup path is untouched. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-VENDOR-SYMBOL-UNIQUE-001 · DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-LIVE-001 · CLAUDE.md §1 / §6.

397. **DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 — surface SPOT coverage on the `/coverage` page (read-only)** (2026-06-02, operator request: "a successful spot pull is invisible on /coverage — it only shows in /db"). **Context:** the `/coverage` page (`dashboard/coverage_view.py` + the `/api/v1/coverage` route + `templates/coverage.html`) was the OPTIONS completeness ledger ONLY — expiries + contracts per underlying/year from `data/coverage_ledger.py`. A completed spot pull (e.g. NIFTY `1minute` / `1day`) left no trace there; the operator had to open `/db` to see it, so spot and options coverage lived on two different pages. **Fix (read-only, no new pull logic):** a SPOT coverage section now sits beneath the options ledger on the same page. (a) **Lake read** — NEW `db_view.summarize_spot_datasets(conn, lake_root)` discovers every spot candle partition set via the existing `list_candle_datasets` and reads ONE aggregate row per set (`COUNT(*)` + `MIN`/`MAX("timestamp")`) straight from the Parquet lake via DuckDB `read_parquet` over the partition glob — no data duplication, the lake stays the single source of truth (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); a bound `read_parquet(?)` path keeps zero SQL-injection surface. NEW `db_view._ist_date` renders the bar timestamp's IST calendar date (the date-level analog of `_format_candle_timestamp`). (b) **Pure projection** — NEW `coverage_view.build_spot_coverage_payload` / `spot_coverage_headline` compose `{headline:{datasets,total_bars}, rows:[{exchange,segment,symbol,interval,bars,first_date,last_date}]}`, mirroring `build_coverage_payload`. (c) **Route** — NEW `GET /api/v1/coverage/spot` thin wrapper (empty payload, never a 500, when no lake root is wired). (d) **Template** — `coverage.html` gained an "Options ledger" / "Spot coverage" section split, a spot table (Symbol · Exchange · Segment · Interval · Bars · First/Last date) + a KPI line, polled every 4 s with the same XSS-escaping as the ledger table. **+tests:** `test_coverage_view.py` (headline empty/sum + payload empty/non-empty/iterator); `test_dashboard_db_query.py` (`_ist_date` tz-aware/naive/non-datetime; `summarize_spot_datasets` empty-lake/single/multi-set); `test_dashboard_coverage.py` (route happy-path against a real written lake, empty-lake, 503-unwired, no-lake-root). **Verified:** per-module **100%** line+branch on both changed gated surfaces — `brutex.dashboard.coverage_view` (33 stmts / 8 br) AND `brutex.dashboard.db_view` (156 stmts / 68 br) — plus the new `/api/v1/coverage/spot` route lines covered by the integration suite; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0) clean; full suite **3268 passed / 45 skipped / 1 xfailed**. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** a dataset PRESENT in the lake counts as "pulled" — `bars` / `first_date` / `last_date` describe WHAT is stored, NOT whether the full `2021 → today` range is complete; **partial-date-range / gap detection is an explicit follow-up, NOT claimed here**. O(1) preserved — one aggregate scalar read per dataset, no per-bar materialisation. **Builds on:** DEC-COVERAGE-LEDGER-001 · DEC-DB-VIEWER-001 / DEC-DB-QUERY-001 · CLAUDE.md §4 / §11.

398. **DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-001 — deep hostile READ-ONLY 5-agent workspace verification (2026-06-02) + `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-02.md`** (operator request: "a deep HOSTILE read-only verification that the whole workspace works as expected … no illusion or hallucination … always monitor the PR status and ensure to merge it"). **Method:** the CLAUDE.md §9 / STANDARDS_100PCT.md §3 hostile-review pattern (a **4-agent hostile review**) scaled to **5 parallel read-only audit agents**, one per dimension — (1) correctness & data-integrity, (2) O(1) performance, (3) test coverage & types, (4) Dhan fidelity, (5) security/automation/CI — synthesized into `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-02.md`. The full suite + every locally-runnable gate were run centrally by the lead under a **faithful Python 3.12 env** (matching CI `requires-python >=3.12`) with the Rust `fno_math` kernel built (`maturin develop --release`) + `[dev,data,ui]` extras. **REAL numbers:** full suite **3252 passed / 45 skipped / 1 xfailed**; canonical coverage **97.88%** (≥ 90 floor ✅; the 1 xfail is the honest 33B-trial SLA extrapolation pending the Rust supermask kernel); property **90 passed / 24 skipped** (5 invariants impl + 19 ROADMAP); smoke+redteam **43 passed / 1 skipped**; bench **45 passed / 2 skipped / 1 xfailed**; golden **3 passed**; **mypy --strict 0 errors (150 files)**; **pyright strict 0 errors / 1 warning**; **ruff + ruff-format clean (150)**; **bandit `-l` 0 findings**; **interrogate 100%** (CI flags); banned-patterns + spec↔test crosswalk + conventional-commits all ✅. **Headline result: ZERO functional / correctness bugs found.** The data-integrity spine is real and tested — BLAKE3 9-field combo hash, 2dp ROUND_HALF_UP price snap (not truncation), volume/OI normalization + index-volume drop, Bloom+LMDB no-false-negative O(1) dedup, DuckDB PK uniqueness, SHA256 tamper-tested audit hash-chain, 22/22 Dhan facts matching `docs/dhan-ref/` with CSV-resolved (never hardcoded) SECURITY_IDs. **What the audits DID surface (raised as tracked follow-ups, NOT fixed in this read-only session per Golden Rule #9):** **7 doc-drift items** — D1 instruments PK is `(vendor_symbol, snapshot_date)` not the `(security_id,exch_id,segment)` triple some docs cite;
