417. **DEC-RUST-RAYON-SUPERMASK-001 — Rayon multi-core parallelization of the Stage-2 supermask scan** (2026-06-03, builds on DEC-RUST-RESIDENT-BARS-001 #413 / ADR-0004 §5.2). **Problem:** the Stage-2 hot kernel `count_supermasks` scanned masks SERIALLY on one core, leaving the 9 remaining M4 Pro cores idle. The masks-outer loop is *embarrassingly parallel* — each mask is an independent integer SUPERSET count (`(bar & mask) == mask`) over the shared, READ-ONLY `bar_bits`, with no cross-mask data dependency — so it can fan out across cores toward the ~224 GB/s memory-bandwidth wall (the kernel is bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound; ADR-0004). **What shipped:** `rayon = "1.10"` added to `rust/fno-math/Cargo.toml` (resolves to rayon 1.12 / rayon-core 1.13 + crossbeam-deque/epoch/utils + either). A private `#[inline] fn count_supermasks_dispatch(bars, masks) -> Vec<u64>` in `rust/fno-math/src/python.rs` selects the arm by work size: `let work = (masks.len() as u64).saturating_mul(bars.len() as u64)`; below `PARALLEL_WORK_THRESHOLD = 1 << 20` (= 1 048 576 `mask·bar` ops) it runs the original serial `masks.iter().map(|&m| count_one(bars, m)).collect()` (small-N O(1)-canary protection, Golden Rule #5); at/above it runs `masks.par_iter().map(|&m| count_one(bars, m)).collect()`. **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** `par_iter().map().collect()` is an `IndexedParallelIterator` — **order-preserving**, so `out[j]` always aligns with `masks[j]` regardless of thread scheduling; every element is a pure integer count (no reduction-order ambiguity), so the result is **bit-identical to the serial scan on every device** and feeds the blake3 run-identity hash unchanged. `par_bridge` was deliberately NOT used (not order-preserving). **Single source of truth (P0-3):** both arms (and the bench shim, and `ResidentBars::count_supermasks`) call ONLY the existing shared `fn count_one(bars: &[u64], mask: u64) -> u64` — panic-free (only `(bar & mask) == mask` summed as `u64`; no index/unwrap/overflowing-arith), so the parallel path can never diverge from the shipped kernel. **Panic=abort safety (P0-3/R4):** `saturating_mul` caps the work estimate at `u64::MAX` (≥ THRESHOLD ⇒ correctly takes the parallel arm) instead of overflow-panicking under the release profile's `overflow-checks = true` + `panic = "abort"` (which would SIGABRT pytest); the scoped-pool shim uses `map_err` → `PyValueError`, never `unwrap`/`expect`. **Routing:** BOTH the free `count_supermasks_u64s` AND `ResidentBars::count_supermasks` route through `count_supermasks_dispatch`; the single-mask `count_supermask_u64s` + `ResidentBars::count_supermask` STAY serial (nothing to parallelize). **GIL (P1) — `detach` REMOVED (CI-driven follow-up):** the initial commit wrapped the free `count_supermasks_u64s` in `py.detach` (`allow_threads`), but that pulls `PyEval_SaveThread`/`PyEval_RestoreThread` + the panic-unwind print path into the crate, which do NOT link under the `extension-module` `cargo test` build (CI's Rust job links no libpython) — the CI `Rust (fno-math build + clippy + test)` job failed with `undefined symbol: PyEval_RestoreThread`. Per the spec's "`detach` ONLY IF it compiles cleanly … else call dispatch directly — still fully parallel", `detach` was dropped: BOTH the free `count_supermasks_u64s` and `ResidentBars::count_supermasks` now delegate DIRECTLY to `count_supermasks_dispatch` (no `py` arg, no `allow_threads`). rayon spawns its own worker threads regardless of the GIL, so parallelism + bit-exactness are unchanged; only the optional host-cooperation GIL-release nicety is forgone. Additionally, the bench shim's pure-Rust core was extracted to `fn count_supermasks_scoped(bars, masks, n_threads) -> Result<Vec<u64>, String>` (NO `PyErr`); the `#[pyfunction] count_supermasks_u64s_nthreads` maps its `String` error to `PyValueError`, and the Rust `#[cfg(test)]` suite calls the pure helper — so the test binary references ZERO Python C-API symbols (matching #413's gc-clean `cargo test` link). The Python property tests for the scoped pool got `@settings(deadline=None)` (each example builds a fresh rayon `ThreadPool` — incidental cost that tripped hypothesis's 200 ms deadline under coverage; correctness/determinism tests, not latency). **Thread control:** production uses rayon's DEFAULT global pool — this crate NEVER calls `build_global` (a double-call panics → SIGABRT under `panic = "abort"`) and NEVER sets `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`; no scheduler env shim, no public `threads=` kwarg on the Python facade. **Bench-only shim:** `#[pyfunction] count_supermasks_u64s_nthreads(bar_bits, masks, n_threads) -> PyResult<Vec<u64>>` builds a SCOPED `rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::new().num_threads(n_threads).build().map_err(...)?` and runs `pool.install(|| masks.par_iter().map(|&m| count_one(&bar_bits, m)).collect())` — exists ONLY so the scaling bench + thread-count-independence parity tests can pin a worker count without touching the global pool (`n_threads == 0` ⇒ rayon default; `>= 1` ⇒ exactly that many). Registered in `lib.rs` `#[pymodule]`, re-exported in `fno_math` `__init__.py` + typed `__init__.pyi`. **Python facade `brutex/engine/combo_mask.py`:** LEFT BYTE-UNCHANGED — the Rust methods keep identical signatures, so the facade just gets transparently faster; ZERO new Python branches, so the strict per-module 100 % `combo_mask` line+branch gate is untouched (no threshold logic, no `threads` kwarg in Python). **No crate-wide `deny(clippy::arithmetic_side_effects)`** (would flag the existing `count_one` arithmetic); the `saturating_mul` + `count_one`-only closure is the panic-abort defense. **P0-1 (main/merge safety) — cargo-deny:** adding rayon pulls new crates; `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml` runs `cargo deny check advisories bans sources licenses` (working-directory `rust/fno-math`) on push-to-main when `Cargo.lock`/`Cargo.toml` change, and there was NO `deny.toml` → would red main post-merge on the new transitive licenses + the default multiple-versions ban. Added `rust/fno-math/deny.toml` (advisories v2; licenses v2 with an explicit permissive allow-list — MIT, Apache-2.0 [+LLVM-exception], BSD-2/3-Clause, ISC, Unicode-3.0, Unicode-DFS-2016, Zlib, CC0-1.0, MPL-2.0 — `private = { ignore = true }`; bans `multiple-versions = "allow"`; sources locked to crates.io). Added `publish = false` to the crate (proprietary, never published) so `private.ignore` excludes fno-math's non-SPDX `"Proprietary"` string from the license check while still checking every real dependency. **Tests (all 7 types):** Rust `cargo test` +11 new `#[cfg(test)]` cases — dispatch serial arm (work < THRESHOLD), dispatch parallel arm (bars=1024 × masks=1100 = 1 126 400 > 1<<20), threshold boundary (work == THRESHOLD via 1024×1024 vs THRESHOLD−1024, both == serial `count_one` loop), parallel == serial parity on a parallel-arm input, empty masks → [], empty bars → 0s, single mask, mask=0 → all, `nthreads` returns Ok + matches reference, thread-count independence for n in {1,2,4} all equal to the serial reference, `nthreads` empty/edge cases — **496 crate tests pass** (the 7 existing batch tests were repointed from the now-`py`-bearing `count_supermasks_u64s` to the pure-Rust `count_supermasks_dispatch`, byte-identical work). Python **property** `tests/property/test_supermask_kernel_parity.py` (+2 hypothesis tests: `test_parallel_equals_serial_all_thread_counts` asserting `count_supermasks_u64s_nthreads(bars, masks, n) == count_supermasks_reference` for n in {1,2,4}; a repeated-run determinism check incl. the default-pool path). New **scaling bench** `tests/bench/test_supermask_scaling_bench.py` (`@pytest.mark.slow @pytest.mark.bench`, seed 42, best-of-5 min; 94 k bars × 10 k masks; t in {1,2,4,6,10}; prints throughput / speedup-vs-t1 / eff GB/s / % of the 224 GB/s wall) — PARITY asserted at EVERY thread count == reference (correctness, runs everywhere); the SCALING-FLOOR assertion is a LOOSE non-regression floor only (best-of-N min, ≤ t1·1.05, NEVER a hard multiple — Golden Rule #10) gated behind `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py::m4pro_strict_active()` so the shared 2-4-core CI runner + this 4-core container only run parity + print numbers. **MEASURED scaling — dev/CI CONTAINER, 4 CORES (NOT M4 Pro), seeded, best of 5:** t=1 → 0.6621 s / 1419.7 M ops·s⁻¹ / 1.00× / 11.4 GB/s / 5.1 % wall; **t=2 → 0.3341 s / 2813.2 M ops·s⁻¹ / 1.98×**; **t=4 → 0.1719 s / 5469.6 M ops·s⁻¹ / 3.85×**; t=6 → 0.1696 s / 3.90× (plateau — only 4 physical cores); t=10 → 0.1694 s / 3.91×. Scaling bench de-flaked **5/5 green**. **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** these numbers are the **dev/CI container (4 cores)**, NOT the M4 Pro. The kernel is **memory-bandwidth-bound, NOT compute-bound**, so the real 10-P-core M4 Pro plateau is **~2-4×, NOT linear 10×** (`docs/TRACK1_PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.md`); no near-linear-10× claim is made. The 33B-trial SLA `xfail` in `tests/bench/test_full_sweep_extrapolation.py` is deliberately LEFT failing-for-now (untouched — multi-core is one part; the full SLA additionally needs Stage 1A/1B trial pruning + the trade-sim). GPU offload stays gated behind ADR-0004's empirical parity benchmark. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin --release):** `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test` (496 pass) [local-only: linked libpython via `RUSTFLAGS="-L /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu -lpython3.12"` because the crate's `pyo3/extension-module` feature omits the python link and this container has no maturin test-harness; CI provides libpython automatically]; `cargo deny check advisories bans sources licenses` → **advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok** (cargo-deny v0.19.8 installed locally — verified, not just CI-deferred); `brutex.engine.combo_mask` per-module **100 % line + branch** (84 stmts / 30 br, 0 miss / 0 partial) — UNCHANGED facade, gate green; `mypy --strict brutex` (150 files, 0) + `mypy` on `__init__.pyi` (0) + `ruff check brutex tests rust` + `ruff format --check` clean; full fast suite **3343 passed, 39 skipped, 1 xfailed** (the 33B SLA xfail). `rust/fno-math/Cargo.lock` is now TRACKED — `.gitignore` gained an explicit `!rust/fno-math/Cargo.lock` exception (the blanket `Cargo.lock` ignore stays for any future workspace crates) so the new rayon/crossbeam/either pins are recorded for reproducibility (Golden Rule #4) + the security-audit `Cargo.lock` push-trigger fires on this first new-external-crate PR — a deliberate, documented convention choice (the fno-math extension is an application artifact whose lockfile SHOULD be tracked), not a silent force-add against the ignore rule. **Hostile-review P0/P1 defenses applied:** P0-1 (deny.toml so cargo-deny stays main-green on the new licenses + multiple-versions); P0-3/R4 (`saturating_mul` + `count_one`-only panic-free closure — panic=abort safe; single source of truth, parallel path cannot diverge); P1 (GIL `detach` on the free function, documented direct-dispatch fallback on the resident method); P1-cov (combo_mask.py byte-unchanged, zero new Python coverage surface); plus the order-preserving-collect determinism proof (Golden Rule #4), the THRESHOLD serial fast-path (O(1) canary, Golden Rule #5), and the honest 4-core-labeled / ~2-4×-M4-Pro envelope (Golden Rule #10). **Builds on:** DEC-RUST-RESIDENT-BARS-001 (#413) · DEC-RUST-SUPERMASK-KERNEL-001 (#411, the shipped CPU SUPERSET kernel + shared `count_one`) · DEC-RUST-SUPERMASK-KERNEL-BENCH-DEFLAKE-001 (#412, best-of-N timing idiom reused) · ADR-0004 §5.2 · CLAUDE.md §2 r4/r5 / §4 / §11 SCALABLE.

418. **DEC-OPTIONS-COVERAGE-LAKE-001 — the `/coverage` OPTIONS section reads the actual expired-options lake (present-in-lake = pulled), not the dead legacy `coverage_ledger`** (2026-06-03, operator: "i clearly told you to make it as only one expired options … why this is still marked as expiries and contracts … now i have started to pull the options chain but why it is not showing the coverage as updated"). **Root cause (two symptoms, one bug):** the `/coverage` OPTIONS LEDGER read the legacy `coverage_ledger` DuckDB table (`CoverageRecord.expiries_pulled`/`contracts_pulled`) via `build_coverage_payload` — (a) that table is the OLD two-phase **expiries+contracts** model (hence the stale wording), and (b) **nothing writes it** in the single-table model: `upsert_coverage` is defined only in `instrument_store.py` and is never called by the expired-options pull (which writes the Parquet lake), so the ledger is permanently empty → the page showed **0/1458, 0%, all "missing"** no matter how much was pulled. SPOT coverage worked because it already derives from the lake (`summarize_spot_datasets`, present-in-lake = pulled). **Fix (lake-derived, mirrors SPOT — operator chose this over wiring the legacy grid):** new `db_view.summarize_option_datasets(conn, lake_root)` reads ONE aggregate per `(exch_id, underlying_symbol)` from `<lake>/options/**/*.parquet` (nested GROUP BY: inner collapses each `(expiry_flag, expiry_code, strike_offset, side, strike)` series → outer `COUNT(*)` = series, `SUM(bars)`, `MIN`/`MAX` date); new `coverage_view.option_coverage_headline` + `build_option_coverage_payload` (`{underlyings, series, total_bars}`); new read-only route `GET /api/v1/coverage/options` (mirrors `/api/v1/coverage/spot`). `templates/coverage.html` repointed from `/api/v1/coverage` → `/api/v1/coverage/options`, renamed "expiries + contracts" → **"Expired options"**, KPI band now underlyings · series · bars, per-underlying table (underlying · exchange · series · bars · first/last date), title "Coverage Ledger" → "Coverage". **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** present-in-lake = pulled — the counts describe WHAT is stored, NOT date-range completeness (same caveat as spot); the legacy `coverage_ledger` table + `/api/v1/coverage` route are left in place (now unused by the page) — ripping them out (like #309 dropped `expiries`/`contracts`) is a tracked follow-up, not bundled here. **Verified (project venv):** per-module **100% line+branch** on `brutex.dashboard.coverage_view` (38/8) + `brutex.dashboard.db_view` (199/80); ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0 errors) clean; `node --check` clean on the inline JS; `test_dashboard_coverage` + `test_dashboard_e2e` + the new `summarize_option_datasets` / `option_coverage` tests pass. **Builds on:** DEC-EXPIRED-OPTIONS-TABLE-001 (#408) · DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 (the spot-lake pattern mirrored) · DEC-COVERAGE-LEDGER-001 (the retired legacy source) · CLAUDE.md §1 / §10 / §11 COMMON.

419. **DEC-DHAN-CALL-LATENCY-LOGGING-001 — institutional per-call latency + effective-RPS logging on the Dhan transport (so the operator MEASURES throughput, never infers it)** (2026-06-03, operator: "why is this pull very slow … why are you really trying to hit 5 RPS precisely … check the logs thoroughly and tell me" + "implement the precise detailed institutional-level logging"). **Why:** asked why the options pull is slow, the only honest answer from the existing logs was fan-out MATH (NIFTY = ATM±10 [21 strikes] × CALL/PUT × WEEK/MONTH × expiryCodes 1/2/3 = **252 series** × ~66 monthly windows over [2021-01-01, prev-day] ≈ **16.6k sequential calls**; at the 5 r/s ceiling ≈ **55 min for NIFTY alone**) — because **no per-call latency or effective-RPS was logged**. Now it is MEASURED. **What shipped (`brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py` — the single network chokepoint `DhanClient.post_json`, so SPOT + OPTIONS both benefit automatically):** a pure, gated `CallMeter` (O(1) `record`: running count/sum/min/max latency + a bounded 256-deque for the p95; `snapshot` → `{calls, effective_rps, latency_ms_avg/min/max/p95}`) + an injected monotonic `clock` (default `perf_counter`) + `log_every` (default 25). `post_json` times every transport round-trip and on EVERY exit — success, timeout, connection error — calls `_observe`, which emits a DEBUG `dhan.call` line (`endpoint · status · latency_ms`) and, every `log_every` calls, an INFO `dhan.throughput` summary into the same structlog stream the operator reads on `/logs`. **`effective_rps = (N-1)/wall-span`** (inter-arrival rate) so a 5 r/s-paced run reads ≈5, **never a false >5** that would look like a rate-limit violation. **No raise of the 5 r/s cap** (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 — "never raise without explicit approval"): this is OBSERVABILITY only — the run is slow because of the ~16.6k-call fan-out paced at the documented ceiling, not a bug; the only legitimate speed levers are fewer calls (the `FetchCoverage` window-skip already avoids re-fetching on re-runs) or a narrower fan-out (a scope decision), NOT a higher RPS. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the live `urllib_transport` round-trip stays `# pragma: no cover`; the MEASURED numbers are real (perf_counter deltas), not estimates. The live builders (`option_pull_controller._build_live_options:245`, `pull_controller._build_live_spot_adapter:338`) construct `DhanClient` unchanged — instrumentation is automatic. **Verified (project venv):** `brutex.adapters.dhan.client` per-module **100% line+branch** (92/12) — its strict CI gate green; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0) clean; +6 tests (CallMeter empty/records/zero-span + post_json latency record, the periodic-summary True/False branch via `structlog.testing.capture_logs`, and latency-recorded-on-timeout). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the [3..5] r/s controller this measures against) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (rate-limit safety) / §10 (honest limits) / §11 COMMON (one chokepoint).

420. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001 — make the adaptive rate controller's throttle VISIBLE (the first dark adapter layer lit)** (2026-06-03, operator: "proper professional in-depth detailed logging architecture … log everything … only then we will know every nook and corner"). **Why:** the operator-facing logging audit found the whole adapter/ingest layer SILENT — `rate_control.py` had **0 log calls**, so when the `[3..5]` r/s controller (DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001) stepped DOWN under sustained 429s the operator had **no way to see** that effective throughput had dropped (it just looked "slow"). **What shipped (`brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py`):** structlog `_LOG` + three events into the `/logs` stream — `rate.429` (WARNING, every hit: `current_rps`, `recent_hits`), `rate.stepdown` (WARNING, on a 5→4→3 step: `from_rps`, `to_rps`, `floor_rps`), `rate.stepup` (INFO, on a 3→4→5 recovery: `from_rps`, `to_rps`, `ceiling_rps`). Logs sit INSIDE the already-tested step branches (no new branch), so the strict gate held with +3 `structlog.testing.capture_logs` assertion tests proving each event + its fields fire. **First slice of the logging-architecture roadmap** (the "what's lit vs dark" table): rate-control done; per-window / per-series / per-underlying / skip / quarantine-cause / parse / lake-write + a `pull_id` correlation + ADR-0005 are the follow-on slices. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** observability only — the controller's behaviour is byte-unchanged; this just surfaces it. Also CORRECTS the #419 over-claim "the `FetchCoverage` window-skip already avoids re-fetching on re-runs" — VERIFIED FALSE: `FetchCoverage` (the O(1) skip ledger with `to_records`/`from_records` persistence) is **built but NOT wired** into the live pull (`pull_options`/`pull-all` pass `coverage=None`; persistence never loaded/saved), so re-runs currently RE-PULL every window and burn daily quota. Wiring a persisted `FetchCoverage` into the live spot+options pulls (window-skip + daily-incremental + survive-restart) is a tracked high-priority follow-up (DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-WIRING — to be assigned). **Verified (project venv):** `brutex.adapters.dhan.rate_control` per-module **100% line+branch** (57/6) — strict gate green; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` clean; 13 tests pass. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the controller) · DEC-DHAN-CALL-LATENCY-LOGGING-001 (#419, the transport-layer logging this extends) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the unwired skip ledger this flags) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 / §8 (audit/observability) / §10.

421. **DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-WIRING-001 — wire the persisted `FetchCoverage` skip-ledger into the live spot + options pulls (the #420 quota bug, fixed)** (2026-06-03, operator: "how will you know that you have pulled that precise window and it didnt want to be pulled again to avoid the daily unwanted quota … everyday again new current day alone will be pulled which is not done today alone will be pulled on the next day"). **Why:** #420 flagged (honestly) that `FetchCoverage` — the O(1) skip ledger (DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001) — was BUILT but NOT WIRED: every live `pull_options` / `pull_all_spot` / `pull_candles` passed `coverage=None`, so a re-click RE-PULLED every settled window and re-burned the Dhan 100k/day quota (CLAUDE.md §6). The skip + mark engine already existed in `ingest_spot` / `ingest_rolling_option_series` (skip-before-vendor-call + mark-after-clean-append); only persistence + wiring were missing. **What shipped:** (1) new `brutex/data/fetch_coverage_store.py` — a durable, deterministic JSON sidecar at `<lake_root>/fetch_coverage.json` (`load_fetch_coverage` → empty on a missing / corrupt / wrong-shaped file with a structured WARNING, NEVER raises so a bad sidecar can't block a pull; `save_fetch_coverage` → atomic `*.tmp` + `os.replace`, crash-safe; round-trips `to_records`/`from_records`, byte-reproducible) + two dry-run-gated helpers (`begin_pull_coverage` LOADS the persisted ledger for a LIVE pull / honours an explicit one / no-ops dry-run; `end_pull_coverage` persists only a live run's ledger — a dry-run's null sink DISCARDS bars, so persisting "done" would be a lie). (2) wired all three pull cores (`pull_options`, `pull_all_spot`, `pull_candles`) to `begin_…` before the ingest pass and `end_…` after — the dashboard routes need NO change (they pass `coverage=None` → the live pull loads/saves). **Daily-incremental falls out for free:** a `WindowKey` includes its exact `(start, end)`, so every SETTLED past window is skipped while only the LAST (today-touching) tile gets a fresh key each day → only the new day is re-fetched, and "today" is pulled on the NEXT day (the default spot end is the previous day). **Correctness backstop:** the idempotent sink still no-ops stored bars, so skipping can only ever save quota/latency, never lose or duplicate data (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 7). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the JSON sidecar is O(N) to load/save once per pull — fine for index + per-symbol pulls; a full-universe options ledger (~1M+ windows) would be a large file, so a compaction / binary format is a tracked follow-up (the O(1) per-window membership/mark is unaffected). The live `urllib` network round-trip stays `# pragma: no cover`. **Verified (project venv):** `fetch_coverage_store` **100% line+branch** (38/8), `pull_controller` **100%** (167/26), `option_pull_controller` **100%** (98/16) — all strict per-module gates green; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0/0) clean; +16 store/helper tests (missing / round-trip / atomic-no-tmp / corrupt-JSON / wrong-shape / bad-arity / bad-ISO-date degrade-to-empty + the begin/end dry-run gating) + the 2 option non-dry-run tests retargeted to a real `tmp_path` asserting the sidecar is written; 76 affected tests pass. **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the unwired ledger) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001 (#420, which flagged this as the high-priority follow-up) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (quota) / Rule 7 (idempotence) / §11 COMMON (one dry-run rule).

422. **DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001 — the engine's `change_pct` / `open_gap_pct` baseline is the prior day's LAST 1-MINUTE close, not the 1-day official close** (2026-06-03, operator: "for our backtesting historical store we need to use prev day one min close for both percentage change and gap up or gap down … but one and only when we need to pull the report as excel alone that [NSE/official] approach is needed"). **Why:** the operator compared three sources for COALINDIA 2026-05-27 09:15 — NSE official %CHNG **−6.36%** (prev close **458.15** = the NSE settlement / last-30-min-VWAP close), the Dhan **chart** **−5.34%** (prev close **455.90** = the prior day's last 1-minute LTP), and our `/db` (which matched NSE because it anchored on the Dhan **1-day** close 458.15). The operator's authoritative NSE pre-open CSV confirmed both numbers are *real* but *different* — the 1-day close ≠ the last 1-min close because the official close is a 30-min VWAP, not the final tick. **Decision:** the brute-force engine is **1-minute-based** (every bar/signal/resample comes off the 1-min feed), so its derived %-columns must baseline on the **prior trading day's last 1-minute close** (the 15:29 IST bar) to stay internally consistent with the feed it actually sweeps — eliminating the cross-feed discontinuity at 09:15. The 1-day official close (= NSE "previous close") is **reserved for the separate NSE pre-open Excel report** (a friend deliverable), NEVER the engine store. (Supersedes the prior `change_pct` reasoning: an earlier turn agreed to switch, then RETRACTED after the NSE CSV showed the 1-day close matched NSE — but the operator's locked goal is 1-min internal consistency for the engine, not NSE-matching, so the switch is correct *for the engine*. Honest record: this is a deliberate divergence from the broker/NSE official % by design.) **What shipped (`brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`):** `_daily_close_by_date` (read the 1-day lake) → `_intraday_last_close_by_date` (read the **1minute** lake, `arg_max(close, timestamp)` GROUP BY bar-date → the day's LAST 1-min close, ONE columnar pass → O(1) per-bar lookup; session-filtered intraday bars never cross the IST/UTC date boundary so `CAST(timestamp AS DATE)` is the IST trading date); new `_INTRADAY_BASE_INTERVAL="1minute"`; `_prev_trading_close` + `_spot_derived_rows` + the `db.html` derived-column note updated to say "prior day's last 1-minute close". Missing 1-minute partition → derived columns degrade to blank (unchanged graceful path). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the per-page prev-close read is O(N over the 1-min partition) once (DuckDB columnar aggregate → ~one row/day), not O(1) — but the per-bar lookup downstream IS O(1); this matches the prior 1-day design's one-read-per-page shape. The numbers now intentionally do NOT match a broker's official daily %; that is the design choice, not a bug. **Verified (project venv):** `brutex.dashboard.db_view` per-module **100% line+branch** (200/80, both db_view test files) — strict gate green; ruff + ruff-format + `pyright` (0) clean, `mypy --strict` clean on the module (the repo-wide `mypy` run hits a pre-existing `orchestrator/retry.py` parser quirk unrelated to this change — pytest imports it fine); reworked the 5 affected derived-column tests (last-1min-per-day `arg_max`, end-to-end 1-min-anchored change/gap incl. first-day-blank, 1day-view anchored on the 1-min lake, missing-1minute → blank) + 149 db_view tests pass. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-CANDLE-DERIVED-001 (the derived-column machinery) · DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (the 1-minute base feed) · the NSE pre-open Excel report (DEC TBD — the ONLY place the 1-day/NSE official close is used) · CLAUDE.md §4 (statistical metrics never money-rounded) / §1 (no hallucination — both %s verified against the operator's NSE CSV).

423. **DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-001 — Stage-1A bitset-matrix builder: drive the EXISTING `evaluate_atoms` across a bar feed (PR-1)** (2026-06-03, implements PR-1 of the engine-scoping proposal `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-03_ENGINE_SCOPING.md` after its CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review — feasibility / correctness-look-ahead / contract-fit / gap-finder). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the decision ID is `DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-001` (the §9 doc references it by NAME); the ledger had already grown past the proposal's draft "#416" (which is `DEC-GUARANTEE-COMPARISON-DOC-001`), so this lands as the next free integer **#423** — the ID, not the number, is authoritative. **What shipped:** `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` — the Stage-1A producer. For ONE `(instrument, interval)` it consumes an iterable of `CandleBar` in chronological order and emits `bar_bits: list[int]` (one u64 condition mask per bar, 1:1) the Stage-2 supermask kernel consumes (`count_supermasks`, #411/#413/#417). Public API: `Stage1AMatrixBuilder` (streaming `.push(bar)` / `.stream(bars)` + batch `.build(bars)`) + the `build_bar_bits(bars, proximity, prior_n)` functional wrapper + the `ANCHOR_DEPENDENT_MASK` constant; all three added to `brutex/engine/__init__.py` `__all__`. **It DRIVES the existing evaluator — it does NOT reimplement the 52 conditions** (the §9 review's C1 finding: `evaluate_atoms` already exists at `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py:137`, bits `vocabulary/bits.py:93`, unit-tested). The module is purely the **adapter layer** between the lake's bar representation and the evaluator's `IndicatorSnapshot` contract, reusing every existing indicator (`brutex/indicators/{ema,pivots,fib_levels,day_extremes}.py`). **Locked adapter conventions (the seams this PR owns):** (1) **Decimal-rupees → int64 paisa** via the private canonical seam `_price_to_paisa = int(round_money(price) × 100)` — `ROUND_HALF_UP`, snapping to the 2dp tick grid FIRST so vendor float-noise like `14020.7999` → `1402080` paisa never leaks (DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 / DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001); `brutex.money` only converts paisa→rupees, so this is the one rupees→paisa source of truth (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). (2) **UTC → IST** via `bar.timestamp.astimezone(IST)` using the shared `brutex.calendars.nse.IST` zone (NEVER a hard-coded offset) — stamped as `timestamp_ist`; the evaluator's time-of-day + day-rollover are IST-correct (the §9 review's open-question #3). (3) **EMA(20)/EMA(200)** causal `EMAState` fed the float CLOSE (vocabulary Group 1 = "EMA 20/200 close"), `None` during warm-up (bits 0-5 simply do not fire), result snapped to paisa through the SAME `_price_to_paisa` seam (float→`Decimal(str(...))` to avoid binary-float drift, mirroring `data/candle_fields`). (4) **Running day extremes** (`DayExtremesState`) reset at each new IST day; **open-of-day** captured at the day's first bar. (5) **Daily anchors** — pivots / Fib / PDH-PDL computed ONCE per IST day from the PRIOR completed day's OHLC and broadcast across that day's intraday bars; the day's OHLC is accumulated FROM THE INTRADAY BARS themselves (first-bar open, running H/L, last-bar close), so the builder is self-contained AND strictly causal (the prior day is fully closed before its OHLC is read). (6) **PriorBarHistory** updated per bar AFTER evaluation (so the current bar is not in its own look-back); **bullish tie-break = `close > open` (strict); a doji `close == open` is recorded BEARISH** — the same not-strictly-up convention the evaluator's Group 5 `BIT_BAR_BULLISH` uses (documented so the tie-break has ONE definition). **First IST day (no prior day):** the anchor-dependent groups — Group 2 (pivot proximity 6-12), Group 3 (PDH/PDL 13-18), Group 4 (Fib proximity 19-29), Group 9 (day type 48-51, all relative to the prior day's C/H/L) — are UNDEFINED, so for first-day bars the builder clears exactly those bits via `ANCHOR_DEPENDENT_MASK` (a strategy referencing an undefined anchor simply does not fire); EMA / candle-shape / prior-bar / day-structure / time-of-day stay fully defined from bar 0. This keeps output 1:1 with input. A neutral all-zero placeholder `PivotLevels`/`FibLevels` lets `evaluate_atoms` run on day 1 without a special code path; every bit they could touch is cleared, so the placeholder never reaches output. **Contiguity:** the builder treats the most-recently-completed IST day in the stream as "prior day" and does NOT re-derive the trading calendar (the lake / `ReplayFeed` deliver contiguous trading-day bars; the calendar lives in exactly one place — `calendars/nse.py` — and re-deriving it here would risk dropping legitimate special sessions). **No look-ahead (CLAUDE.md §4, Golden Rule #5):** at bar N only bars 0..N are read — EMA/day-extremes are causal streaming states, anchors use the prior completed day, history updates after evaluation; **a property test asserts it** (permuting every bar strictly after index k never changes any mask at index ≤ k). **O(1) per bar (Golden Rule #5):** all per-bar work is constant — `evaluate_atoms` is O(1), and snapshot construction (4 paisa conversions + 2 EMA updates + 1 day-extremes update + 1 dict-free dataclass) is O(1); a MEASURED bench (`tests/bench/test_engine_stage1a_o1.py`, best-of-5, 1k vs 100k bars at fixed intraday density) reports **per-bar ratio 1.06× (ceiling 5×; would pass the strict 1.1× M4-Pro tier)** — flat, no super-linear regression. **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** pure — no globals, no wall-clock, no RNG; a property test asserts the same bars → bit-identical matrix. **NOT used (the §9 review's C2 finding):** `ExecutionSimulator` / costs / slippage are deliberately NOT imported — Stage 1A has NO P&L (it produces the condition bitset only; the spot trade-sim walker is PR-2, still future, and is NEW int64-paisa signal-only code, never the Decimal+slippage+₹20-brokerage+close-fill simulator). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_stage1a.py` (22 tests — warm-up `None`, day rollover, 3-day prior-day rotation, paisa half-up edge, doji/bullish/bearish tie-break, empty + single bar, custom proximity, UTC→IST day-shift, the `ANCHOR_DEPENDENT_MASK` layout); `tests/property/test_engine_stage1a_properties.py` (determinism, 1:1 + ≤52-bit shape, paisa monotonicity + 2dp round-trip, the no-look-ahead future-mutation invariant — hypothesis); `tests/golden/test_engine_stage1a_golden.py` (a hand-derived 2-day fixture locked to literal u64 masks `[3298534883328, 303483462918144]` — every set bit verified by hand in the docstring — the byte-equality oracle); `tests/bench/test_engine_stage1a_o1.py` (the per-bar O(1)-ratio gate via `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py::ratio_ceiling`). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` build):** `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` per-module **100% line + 100% branch** (106 stmts / 14 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on the module + all 4 test files; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` both **0 errors** on the module; unit + property + golden = **29 passed**; the bench passes (ratio 1.06×). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is PR-1 of a multi-PR effort — a correct, deterministic, O(1)-per-bar Stage-1A producer; it does NOT run a sweep, compute P&L, or meet the 33B SLA. PR-2 (spot trade-sim walker + the instrumented `evaluate(N)` accessor that turns look-ahead Property P-06 into a live enforcer), Stage 1B (PR-3, gated on the §9 review's C-06 coarse-score look-ahead resolution), the runner FSM + `brutex sweep` CLI (PR-4), and the result-store reproducibility oracle (PR-5), plus Stages 2.5/3/4, all remain FUTURE. **Builds on:** the §9 hostile review captured in `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-03_ENGINE_SCOPING.md` (C1 "wire, don't rebuild"; C2 "no simulator for spot") · `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py` (`evaluate_atoms` + `bits.py`) · `brutex/indicators/*` (EMA/pivots/Fib/day-extremes) · `brutex.money.round_money` (DEC-MONEY-2DP-001/DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001) · `brutex.calendars.nse.IST` · DEC-RUST-SUPERMASK-KERNEL-001 (#411, the Stage-2 consumer of this matrix) · CLAUDE.md §4 (no look-ahead) / §5 (O(1)) / §11 COMMON+SCALABLE / §12 (7 test types).

424. **DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 — the NSE-style pre-open Excel report (`/reports` page + lake-derived `.xlsx` download)** (2026-06-03, operator: "provide the excel report only for the last six months of nifty 50 stocks … SYMBOL / PREV. CLOSE / IEP / CHNG / %CHNG … where can I pull the report … in webpage dashboard"). **Why:** the operator's friend wants the NSE pre-open snapshot as an Excel they can open + sort; the operator locked the split — the **engine** uses the prior-day last 1-min close (DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001) while **this report alone** uses the NSE/official approach. **What shipped:** (1) `brutex/dashboard/preopen_report.py` — `build_preopen_rows` reconstructs the 5 NSE columns straight from the Dhan lake per `(symbol, trading-day)`: **PREV. CLOSE** = the prior day's **1-day official close** (= NSE "previous close"), **IEP** = the day's 09:15 opening price (the pre-open equilibrium *becomes* the open; read as the day's FIRST 1-min bar via `arg_min(open, timestamp)`), **CHNG** = IEP − PREV. CLOSE, **%CHNG** = CHNG/PREV. CLOSE×100 — verified against the operator's CSV to the paisa (COALINDIA 2026-05-27: IEP 429.00, PREV. CLOSE 458.15, CHNG −29.15, %CHNG −6.36). `render_xlsx` is a **tiny dependency-free stdlib OOXML writer** (no `openpyxl`/`xlsxwriter` to vet through the licence/lockfile gates) producing a **deterministic** (fixed zip metadata) single-sheet workbook with a frozen header + auto-filter. `resolve_report_datasets` admits only symbols with BOTH a 1day + 1minute partition. (2) routes (`GET /api/v1/reports/preopen/symbols`, `GET /api/v1/reports/preopen.xlsx?from&to&symbols`, `GET /reports`) + a `reports.html` page (From/To pickers + symbol chips + Download) + a "Reports" nav link on all 5 pages. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the numbers are **Dhan-lake-derived** (they MATCH NSE for these 5 columns, proven) — NOT scraped live from NSE; the report covers only symbols already pulled into the lake (so until the NIFTY-50 stock spot is pulled it shows just what's there). A built-in **NIFTY-50 constituents preset is NOT included** (index composition is an external fact — Golden Rule §1 — so the picker is symbol-driven; the operator selects the set or drops a constituents list in a follow-up). Per-row work is O(1); the per-symbol lake reads are one columnar pass each (O(N) once). **Verified (project venv):** `brutex.dashboard.preopen_report` per-module **100% line+branch** (92/20); ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0/0) clean; +15 module tests (lake readers, resolver, NSE-matching row build, range/first-day/zero-prev skips, deterministic xlsx, XML-escape) + 7 TestClient route tests (symbols, xlsx-download-matches-NSE, symbol-filter, 400 on bad/inverted dates, page render); 144-test dashboard sweep green. **Builds on:** DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001 (the engine baseline this is deliberately distinct from) · DEC-DB-CANDLE-DERIVED-001 / db_view shared lake helpers (§11 COMMON) · CLAUDE.md §1 (no hallucination — NSE numbers verified) / §10 (honest envelope) / §4.

425. **DEC-DHAN-STOCK-MONTHLY-ONLY-001 — single-stock options fan MONTH-only; indices keep WEEK+MONTH (per-kind expiry set; halves the stock fan-out, no wasted WEEK calls)** (2026-06-03, operator: the options pull "fans out BOTH weekly+monthly for every underlying" but a stock can only return data on monthly expiries — verified in a live pull log where a STOCK fanned out `weekly+monthly` and the WEEK series came back empty). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** lands at the next free integer **#425** — #424 was taken by DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 (PR #326) merged to `main` during this PR's review; the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative. **Microstructure fact (CLAUDE.md §7; paired with this decision ID per Golden Rule #1 — no hallucination):** Indian **single-stock** options are **monthly-only** — NSE single-stock F&O carries only the (last-Thursday) monthly expiry series; there is NO weekly stock-option series. **Weekly** option series exist only for **select INDICES** (e.g. NIFTY weeklies; BSE SENSEX weeklies), and only some indices at that. So fanning a `WEEK` expiry for a stock can only ever return empty — every such series is a wasted Dhan call against the 5 r/s + 100,000/day quota (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6). The previous fan-out (DEC-DHAN-PULL-SCOPE-001) applied the uniform `EXPIRY_FLAGS = (WEEK, MONTH)` to EVERY underlying, so ~half of every stock's series were always-empty WEEK legs. **What shipped (per-kind expiry set, parallel to the existing per-kind ATM±10/±3 strike window):** (1) **`brutex/adapters/dhan/option_universe_ingest.py`** — new module constant `STOCK_EXPIRY_FLAGS: tuple[str, ...] = ("MONTH",)` (co-located with `STOCK_STRIKE_OFFSETS`, the other per-kind stock-scope constant); a new `OptionUnderlying.expiry_flags: tuple[str, ...]` field defaulting to `EXPIRY_FLAGS` (the **index** set — a hand-built underlying never silently drops a flag); and `run_dhan_options_ingest`'s `expiry_flags` parameter changed from `Sequence[str] = EXPIRY_FLAGS` to `Sequence[str] | None = None` — when `None` (the default) each underlying fans **its own** per-kind `expiry_flags` (`flags = underlying.expiry_flags if expiry_flags is None else expiry_flags`), while an explicit sequence is a **uniform override** retained for custom/test pulls. (2) **`brutex/dashboard/option_pull_controller.py`** — `instrument_to_option_underlying` now stamps the per-kind set right beside the per-kind strike window: **IDX → `OPTIDX` / ATM±10 / `EXPIRY_FLAGS` (WEEK+MONTH)**, **EQ → `OPTSTK` / ATM±3 / `STOCK_EXPIRY_FLAGS` (MONTH-only)**; `pull_options`'s `expiry_flags` default is now `None` so it threads the per-underlying set. The dashboard route (`app.py::api_universe_pull_options`) is **unchanged** — it already passed no `expiry_flags`, so it inherits the per-kind default automatically. **Effect (strictly REDUCES calls, never adds):** a stock's options fan-out **halves** — e.g. COALINDIA = ATM±3 (7 strikes) × CALL/PUT (2) × expiryCodes 1/2/3 (3) drops from **7×2×3×2 = 84** series to **7×2×3×1 = 42** series, dropping exactly the always-empty WEEK legs. **Indices are byte-for-byte UNCHANGED** (NIFTY still 21×2×3×2 = 252; the index keeps WEEK+MONTH). `EXPIRY_FLAGS` and `DEFAULT_EXPIRY_CODES` are untouched — `EXPIRY_FLAGS` is now literally the index default, used directly in the IDX branch. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` build):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/option_universe_ingest.py` **100% line+branch** (82 stmts / 16 branch, 0/0 miss) and `brutex/dashboard/option_pull_controller.py` **100% line+branch** (98/16, 0/0) — both per-module strict gates green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` both **0 errors / 0 warnings** on the 2 modules + 2 test files; +4 tests (universe-ingest: per-kind stock-MONTH-only-vs-index-WEEK+MONTH cardinality drop + the explicit-override-beats-per-kind branch; controller: the IDX→(WEEK,MONTH) / EQ→(MONTH,) mapping asserts + the dry-run bulk-mix stock-count-drops assertion `7×1×3×2 < 7×2×3×2`); the 2 module test files = **28 passed**, the broader option/pull/dhan/universe sweep = **684 passed**. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is a **fan-out scope reduction**, not new capability — it removes provably-empty WEEK stock series; it does not change parsing, the lake, or the engine. The "single stocks are monthly-only" claim is an **NSE microstructure fact** (CLAUDE.md §7), not a row in the Dhan vendor reference — it is asserted as such and paired with this decision ID; the rolling-option endpoint would simply return empty for a stock WEEK series regardless, so even if a future exchange change added stock weeklies the explicit `expiry_flags` override remains the escape hatch (and the per-series quarantine already makes an empty/blocked series non-fatal). The live `urllib` round-trip stays `# pragma: no cover` (network blocked in CI); the count reductions above are computed from the synthetic dry-run fan-out, which exercises the identical orchestration. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PULL-SCOPE-001 (the per-kind ATM±10/±3 strike window this mirrors for the expiry axis) · DEC-DHAN-CALL-LATENCY-LOGGING-001 (#419, which quantified the 252-series NIFTY fan-out and named "a narrower fan-out" as the only legitimate speed lever besides skip/coverage) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-WIRING-001 (#421, the complementary quota-saver — window-skip on re-runs) · DEC-DHAN-EXPIRY-CODES-001 (the 1/2/3 expiry-code axis, unchanged) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (rate/quota safety) / §7 (verified Indian-market microstructure facts) / §11 COMMON (one source of truth — the per-kind set lives in exactly one place).

426. **DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 — light the spot + options ingest spine + a `pull_id` correlation id (the remaining dark layers, lit)** (2026-06-03, operator: "proper professional in-depth detailed logging architecture … log everything … only then we will know every nook and corner"). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** lands at the next free integer **#426** — #424 (DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001, PR #326) and #425 (DEC-DHAN-STOCK-MONTHLY-ONLY-001) both merged to `main` during this PR's review; the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative. **Why:** #420 (DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001) opened a staged "what's lit vs dark" roadmap; #419 (DEC-DHAN-CALL-LATENCY-LOGGING-001) lit the transport (`dhan.call`/`dhan.throughput`) and #420 lit the rate controller (`rate.429`/`rate.stepdown`/`rate.stepup`), but everything BETWEEN the pull button and the HTTP call was SILENT — an operator who saw "NIFTY pulled 0 bars" could not tell whether the window was skipped (the `FetchCoverage` ledger), the vendor returned nothing, the session filter dropped every bar, the sink rejected them, or the series was quarantined on a terminal Dhan error; and there was NO correlation id to follow ONE pull across the ~16k-call options fan-out. **What shipped (observability ONLY — byte-identical ingest):** (1) new COMMON primitive `brutex/observability/correlation.py` — `pull_id_scope()` (binds one 12-hex `pull_id` into the structlog context-vars for a whole pull via `bound_contextvars`, always unbinds on exit, nesting-safe), `new_pull_id()`, `current_pull_id()`. Each pull core (`pull_candles`/`pull_all_spot`/`pull_options`) opens the scope, so EVERY event — the `universe.*` start/done summary, the new `ingest.*` spine events, AND the already-lit `dhan.*`/`rate.*` events — shares one `pull_id` (the `merge_contextvars` processor is first in the configured chain, so the bound id propagates with zero signature plumbing). (2) the `ingest.*` event namespace across the spine: `ingest.window` (DEBUG — per fetch window, `action` fetched/skipped + window dates), `ingest.parse` (DEBUG — `raw_bars` decoded vs `session_bars` surviving the [09:15,15:30) IST gate), `ingest.lake_write` (DEBUG — rows persisted), `ingest.series` (DEBUG — per-series summary), `ingest.underlying` (INFO — per-underlying rollup, one line not the DEBUG firehose), `ingest.quarantine` (WARNING — the per-series/pair terminal-error CAUSE). **The level law (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 "never flood"):** per-window/per-series detail is DEBUG so a 16k-series fan-out never buries INFO; rollups + pull boundaries are INFO; quarantine + the rate `429`/`stepdown` are WARNING. **The `pull_id` test-oracle contract** (documented in ADR-0005): `structlog.testing.capture_logs` deliberately strips the contextvars processor, so each `ingest.*` event RE-STAMPS `pull_id=current_pull_id()` as an explicit field (a no-op against `merge_contextvars` in prod, the value is identical) so every event + its fields is assertable with no network. (3) `docs/adr/0005-logging-architecture.md` — the full taxonomy table, the level rationale, the `pull_id` contract, and the lit-vs-dark matrix. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is OBSERVABILITY ONLY — the ingest path's behaviour + outputs are byte-unchanged (a spine function called outside any scope logs a benign `pull_id=""`); it only makes the existing flow traceable. **NOW LIT:** transport (#419), rate (#420), and — this PR — per-window, parse, lake-write, per-series, per-underlying, and quarantine-cause, all under one `pull_id`. **STILL DARK** (tracked follow-ups, NOT in scope): the 1m→19-TF resampler, the instrument-master load/refresh, the Bloom+LMDB dedup, the Parquet writer's partition/row-group internals (the count is lit at the `ingest.lake_write` boundary; the writer internals are not), and the DuckDB catalog / audit hash-chain. The live `urllib` round-trip + live rate/adapter builders stay `# pragma: no cover`. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + `fno_math` built):** per-module **100% line+branch** — `observability/correlation` (17/0), `adapters/dhan/ingest` (67/18), `adapters/dhan/option_ingest` (71/10), `adapters/dhan/run_ingest` (63/8), `adapters/dhan/option_universe_ingest` (93/16), `dashboard/pull_controller` (170/26), `dashboard/option_pull_controller` (100/16) — all strict per-module gates green; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0 errors / 0 warnings) clean on all 7 modules + 7 test files; +35 `capture_logs` assertion tests (each new event + its fields, the skip-vs-fetch split, the session-drop parse counts, the quarantine cause, and the controller→spine `pull_id` correlation), and the full `tests/unit` suite **3002 passed / 2 skipped** (no regression). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-CALL-LATENCY-LOGGING-001 (#419, the transport layer) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001 (#420, the rate controller + the lit-vs-dark roadmap this completes for the pull path) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-WIRING-001 (#421, the skip ledger whose decisions the `ingest.window action=skipped` event now surfaces) · ADR-0005 · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (Dhan 5 r/s / 100k-day — the rate envelope these events make visible) / §8 (observability) / §11 COMMON (one correlation primitive).

427. **DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 — fail a stalled Dhan call fast + bounded in-client retry, so one slow call can't freeze the SEQUENTIAL pull** (2026-06-03, operator: a live options-pull `dhan.throughput` log showed `latency_ms_max: 30080.0` — a single HTTP call pinned to the 30s timeout ceiling — and effective RPS collapsing 5.1 → 3.75, taking minutes to recover, because `brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py` had `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 30.0` and no per-call retry, so one stalled call froze the whole sequential pull for 30s). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** this lands at the next free integer **#427** — #424 (`DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001`, PR #326), #425 (`DEC-DHAN-STOCK-MONTHLY-ONLY-001`, PR #327), and #426 (`DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001`, PR #328) merged to `main` during this PR's review; per the ledger convention the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative. **Why:** the pull is sequential (one window at a time), so a single tail-latency stall serializes behind the full 30s ceiling — pure latency hygiene, NOT a throughput problem. **What shipped (`brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py`):** (1) **whole-request timeout lowered 30 → 10s** (`_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`) — real Dhan intraday/option chunk responses land well under a few seconds, so 10s keeps generous P99.9 headroom while failing a true stall ~3× faster; still **overridable per client** via the `timeout` field. (2) a **bounded in-client fast-retry**: `post_json` now wraps a renamed single-attempt `_post_once` in an O(1) loop of `max_attempts` (default **3** = 1 initial + 2 retries) with **exponential backoff seeded at the 5 r/s inter-request interval** `min(retry_backoff_s × 2**(k-1), _MAX_BACKOFF_S)` (0.2 s, 0.4 s …, clamped at 5 s) via an **injected `sleep`** (no real wait in tests). (3) the retry predicate is the new module-level `_should_fast_retry`, which **reuses the COMMON `is_retryable`** (CLAUDE.md §11) — fast-retry set = timeout + transport + 5xx — but **DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES rate-limit (429)** via `is_rate_limit`: a 429 means "slow down" and the orchestrator's adaptive token bucket owns that backoff (**CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 — the configured 5 r/s cap + the `rate_control` module are byte-unchanged**; the backoff is **seeded at the 5 r/s interval (0.2 s)** so a single SEQUENTIAL stream's in-place retries stay within the per-second budget); terminal errors (400/404/auth) never retry. (4) every **physical attempt is still metered** by the existing `CallMeter` (DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001, #420) so a timed-out attempt's latency is never invisible, and **each retry emits a `dhan.retry` INFO line** (`endpoint`/`attempt`/`max_attempts`/`error`/`backoff_ms`) so it is visible on /logs. (5) a `__post_init__` rejects `max_attempts < 1` (mirrors the existing `orchestrator/retry.py` `retry_call` convention message). **Layering (no overlap):** this is an in-place LATENCY-HYGIENE retry that resolves a transient transport stall before the call even returns to the ingest loop; the existing slow-path LOGICAL re-queue (the `ingest_*` transient-count + the FSM `orchestrator/retry.py` classifier — NOT wired into the live pull, still the higher layer) is unchanged and still catches whatever survives the bounded fast-retry budget. **O(1) (Golden Rule #5):** attempts are bounded by `max_attempts` (small constant) and the backoff is one `2**(k-1)` multiply — constant per logical call, no allocation growth. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — the 4-agent hostile review's medium finding, addressed):** the fast-retry is NOT token-bucket-coordinated (the client deliberately has no pacer — pacing lives in the orchestrator, §11 COMMON). The **configured** 5 r/s cap and `rate_control` are byte-unchanged, and seeding the backoff at the 5 r/s interval (0.2 s) keeps a single sequential stream's average rate within the per-second budget even while retrying. But this is NOT a per-second *guarantee*: because the retries are unsynchronised with the token bucket, under a *sustained fast-failing* (≈20 ms 5xx/transport) burst the instantaneous physical rate can briefly overlap the next paced window — bounded by `max_attempts` (≤3×), single-stream (live ingest is sequential, not `PoolRunParallel`), fault-only, and EXCLUDES 429 (so a real rate-limit still backs off correctly), with a negligible 100k/day-quota dent (≈3 vs 1 calls on a rare stall). Holding the per-second cap *literally* under fault would require sharing the orchestrator's bucket, which the COMMON layering deliberately avoids — so the honest doc is the chosen fix, not a behaviour change. `max_attempts` is also bounded below by `__post_init__` and the backoff is clamped (`_MAX_BACKOFF_S`) so a large operator value cannot `sleep(inf)` the pull. A second retry mechanism (vs `orchestrator/retry.retry_call`) is justified: `retry_call` RETRIES 429 and does not meter/log each physical attempt, whereas this must EXCLUDE 429 and feed `CallMeter` + `dhan.retry`. The real `urllib_transport` network shim stays `# pragma: no cover`. The `adapter.py` "retry stays in the orchestrator" doc line was reconciled (DEC-DOC-DRIFT-RECONCILE-001 discipline). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py` per-module **100% line + 100% branch** (118 stmts / 18 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial) under a strict `--cov-fail-under=100` gate; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` both **0 errors / 0 warnings** (the whitebox test gets the documented file-top `# pyright: reportPrivateUsage=none`); **+12 fast-retry tests** (timeout→retry→success, transport→retry→success, 5xx→retried, budget-exhausted→raises after exactly `max_attempts`, 429→never-retried, 400→never-retried, exponential-backoff-and-`dhan.retry`-log, no-retry-log on first-try success, `max_attempts<1`→`ValueError`, `_should_fast_retry` predicate truth-table, default-backoff-is-the-5 r/s-interval, backoff-clamped-at-`_MAX_BACKOFF_S`) on top of the 17 pre-existing client tests = **29 client tests**; +331 Dhan+orchestrator unit tests (adapter/auth/ingest/option-ingest/rate-control/retry) all green. **Builds on:** `brutex/adapters/dhan/errors.py` (`is_retryable` / `is_rate_limit` — the COMMON predicates) · `CallMeter` / `dhan.throughput` (DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001, #420 — the log that surfaced the 30080 ms stall) · `brutex/orchestrator/retry.py` (the separate FSM logical-retry layer this composes under) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (5 r/s / 100k-day — untouched) / §5 (O(1)) / §11 COMMON (one retry predicate, pacing stays in the orchestrator).

428. **DEC-STAT-CPCV-WFO-001 — Stage-4 cross-validation primitives: Combinatorial Purged CV (purge + embargo) + triple-variant Walk-Forward pass-rates** (2026-06-03, implements the CV/WFO *engines* of the Stage-4 statistical-validity filter cascade — `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` Stage 4 items 3 + 7, spec lines 386-388 / 409-431). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** lands at the next free integer **#428** — #424-#427 were taken by DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 (#424), DEC-DHAN-STOCK-MONTHLY-ONLY-001 (#425), DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 (#426) + DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 (#427), all merged to `main` during this branch's life; the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative. **What shipped:** two pure, deterministic, numpy-only (no pandas hot path) modules over a returns/trade series. (1) `brutex/metrics/cpcv.py` — `cpcv_splits(n, *, n_groups=16, n_test_groups=8, label_span=0, embargo=0)` partitions the time-ordered observations into S contiguous groups (the `numpy.array_split` rule), takes every `C(S, k)` choice of test groups (defaults S=16 / k=8 → **12,870 splits**, the spec value) and builds each training set by **purging** training rows whose label window `[i, i+label_span]` overlaps a test label window AND **embargo**-ing the `embargo` rows immediately *after* each contiguous test block (Marcos López de Prado, *Advances in Financial Machine Learning*, Wiley 2018, Ch. 7 §7.4 `getTrainTimes`/`getEmbargoTimes` + Ch. 12 — cited inline in the spec at line 386 and as a row in the MIGRATION.md DEC-P0-040 methodology-references table at ~line 3076). `cpcv_pass_rate(returns, ...)` = the fraction of the `C(S, k)` held-out **test** folds with positive Sharpe (`> min_sharpe`, default 0). (2) `brutex/metrics/wfo.py` — `walk_forward_splits` + `wfo_pass_rate` + `wfo_pass_rates` for the three DEC-EXTREME-001 schemes (rolling fixed-window; anchored expand-from-origin with initial `train_size`; expanding expand-from-`train_size//2`, the spec's "1-year start"), pass-rate = positive-Sharpe walks / total walks (the spec's "positive Sharpe in ≥ N of M walks" expressed as a rate; the caller applies the ≥12/16 + ≥10/14 gate to `(rate, n_walks)`). **Shared Sharpe (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** `sharpe_of_returns` (population std, zero risk-free, no annualisation — the same convention as `brutex/metrics/compute.py` / DEC-METRICS-001) lives in exactly one place (cpcv) and wfo imports it; undefined folds/windows (n<2 or zero variance) count as **non-pass** (fail-safe — no NaN/inf, spec line 746). **No look-ahead — the purge guarantee (CLAUDE.md §4, Golden Rule #5):** a property test asserts that after purging NO training index lies within `label_span` of ANY test index (so no training label can overlap a test label) across 200 hypothesis-generated configs; a focused unit test + the golden oracle pin the exact purged train sets (e.g. n=8/S=4/k=2/span=1/embargo=1 → the train set after a `[0,3]` test block is exactly `[8..11]`). The embargo SIZE is the caller's (Stage-4 driver) per DEC-STAT-001 (#123) `max(max_indicator_lookback, max_trade_horizon_bars, 1_trading_day_in_bars)`; the module itself is calendar-free (windows in bars; the spec's 2y/6m/3m → bars conversion lives with the driver). **O(1) — honest scope (Golden Rule #10, operator "no illusion"):** CPCV is `C(S, k)` folds *by construction* — the **TOTAL is NOT O(1)** and the module explicitly never claims it is. What **is** O(1) is the **per-fold work in the series length n**: `cpcv_pass_rate` builds per-group `(n, mean, M2)` moments in one O(n) pass then scores each fold in **O(k)** via the numerically-stable Chan/Pébay parallel-variance merge (Pébay 2008, *SAND2008-6212*, the same family used by `compute.py`), so total = `O(n + C(S,k)·k)` — linear in n for fixed S,k. A **MEASURED** bench (`tests/bench/test_cpcv_wfo_o1.py`, best-of-5, n=1k vs n=10k at fixed S=16/k=8) reports a **1.03× ratio** (flat — would pass the strict 1.1× M4-Pro tier via `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py::ratio_ceiling`), proving the per-fold cost is independent of n; a regression to per-fold slicing (`O(n)` per fold) would blow it ~10×. `cpcv_splits` materialises the index arrays (the inherently `O(index-volume)` slow path) only when a downstream model-trainer needs them; the pass-rate avoids it. WFO is linear in covered-bar volume (tens of walks, not 12,870 folds — not a hot path; the honest claim is "linear & optimal", not O(1) per walk). **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** pure — `itertools.combinations` order, no globals / wall-clock / RNG; split arrays are frozen read-only (`flags.writeable=False`); a golden test locks exact split + pass-rate values (`cpcv_pass_rate([1,2,-3,-4], S=4, k=2)==1/6`; rolling/anchored/expanding `==1/3,1/3,1/4`). **numpy-lazy import:** numpy is imported *inside* the functions (mirroring `brutex/engine/combo_mask.py`) so the single-module strict coverage gate does not double-load numpy's C extension (numpy 2.x "cannot load module more than once per process"); the main `--cov=brutex` job is unaffected. **Honest envelope (CLAUDE.md §2 r10):** this ships the CPCV/WFO **engines** (split-generation + pass-rate), NOT the full Stage-4 cascade — the result-row `cpcv_pass_rate` / `wfo_pass_rate` COLUMN wiring, the DSR / PBO-via-CSCV / Reality-Check-SPA / Romano-Wolf / Lockbox filters, and the 6 hard rejection gates remain DEFERRED (spec lines 581-600; `brutex/metrics/__init__.py` docstring updated to state exactly what is live vs deferred). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12, 5 of 7 types — unit/property/golden/bench + the strict-100 self-test):** `tests/unit/test_cpcv.py` (42) + `tests/unit/test_wfo.py` (32) at **100% line + 100% branch** (cpcv 104 stmts / 34 branches, wfo 76 stmts / 22 branches — both ratcheted into the CI strict-100 per-module gate), `tests/property/test_cpcv_wfo_properties.py` (7 hypothesis invariants — no-leakage, train/test-disjoint, split-count==`C(S,k)`, pass-rate∈[0,1] for CPCV+WFO, WFO causality `train_stop≤test_start`, Sharpe-sign==mean-sign), `tests/golden/test_cpcv_wfo_golden.py` (5 hand-derived byte-equality oracles), `tests/bench/test_cpcv_wfo_o1.py` (the per-fold O(1) ratio gate). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math --release` build):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on both modules + all 5 test files; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` **0 errors / 0 warnings** on the modules + tests (the `@st.composite` `reportCallIssue` scoped-pragma per DEC-PYRIGHT-UNMASK-001); `bandit` clean; `interrogate` **100%** with the CI flags; 429. **DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 — deterministic sweep→Parquet results store keyed by the BLAKE3 run-identity (engine PR-5: the reproducibility oracle)** (2026-06-03, implements the "result-store reproducibility oracle (PR-5)" named FUTURE in DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-001 #423 + `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-03_ENGINE_SCOPING.md`; closes the end-to-end-reproducibility gap flagged 🟡 PARTIAL at `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-03_INSTITUTIONAL_ARCH.md` §(E) prerequisite 7 + the (B)-matrix repro-hash row). **Numbering (Golden Rule #1):** the decision ID is `DEC-RESULT-STORE-001`; the ledger has grown past #428 (main merged #424–#428 during this PR's review), so this lands as the next free integer **#429** — the ID, not the number, is authoritative. **What shipped:** `brutex/engine/results_store.py` — the deterministic SINK that takes per-combo result rows (each keyed by the 9-field BLAKE3 **run-identity** REUSED from `brutex/strategies/combo.py::combo_hash`, NOT reinvented — DEC-P0-060) and writes them to a single Parquet file idempotently + bit-for-bit reproducibly, with an O(1) read-back lookup + a top-K leaderboard. Public API (re-exported in `brutex/engine/__init__.py` `__all__`): `ResultRow` (frozen, validated, hashable), `ResultsStore` (`append`/`extend`/`get`/`rows`/`top_k`/`flush`/`load` + `__len__`/`__contains__`), `FlushResult`, `ResultsStoreError`. **Three storage families (CLAUDE.md §4/§6, DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 / DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 / DEC-MONEY-2DP-001):** money → exact signed **int64 paisa**; statistical metrics → **full-precision Float64, NEVER rounded** (non-finite NaN/±inf rejected at construction so the leaderboard total-order + byte-identity stay well-defined — same precedent as `combo_hash`'s NaN rejection); prices (`avg_entry_price`/`avg_exit_price`, the price-family representatives) → **Decimal rupees snapped to the 2dp tick grid via `brutex.money.round_money` (ROUND_HALF_UP)** then stored Float64 (so a result price is never vendor float-noise like `14020.7999`). **Idempotence + byte-determinism (Golden Rule #4/#7) — mirrors `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`'s contract:** the in-memory `run_id → ResultRow` dict is the source of truth; `flush` serialises a snapshot sorted by `run_id` with a pinned polars schema, zstd level 3, `statistics=False` + `use_pyarrow=False`, written atomically (tempfile + fsync + `os.replace`), so re-flushing an unchanged store — or flushing two stores that received the same rows in OPPOSITE order — produces a **byte-identical** file (verified). `append` dedups by `run_id` O(1): a never-seen id is added, an identical re-append is a silent no-op, and a **same run-identity with DIFFERENT metrics raises `ResultsStoreError`** — that conflict IS the reproducibility guarantee (one identity ⇒ one result; a clash means upstream non-determinism, never a silent overwrite). **O(1) (Golden Rule #5):** `append` (dict membership + insert) and `get` (dict probe) are O(1); a MEASURED bench (`tests/bench/test_engine_results_store_o1.py`, 1k vs 10k rows, routed through the single-source `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py::ratio_ceiling`) confirms both stay flat (get ratio < 1×, append ~1.05×; would pass the strict 1.1× M4-Pro tier). Sized for the funnel's final 10²–10⁴ finalist rows (`TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Result Row Schema"), so the whole index lives in memory. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12, all 7 types):** `tests/unit/test_engine_results_store.py` (53 tests — every validation branch, round-trip, empty store, idempotent re-write, dup-key dedup, conflict raise, top_k ordering/tie-break/descending/guards, the polars-missing import guards + the atomic-write failure cleanup); `tests/property/test_engine_results_store_properties.py` (hypothesis — append-order-independent byte-determinism, re-flush byte-identity, round-trip fidelity, prices always 2dp, full-precision metric round-trips bit-exactly, top_k = length-k prefix of the full ranking); `tests/golden/test_engine_results_store_golden.py` (a hand-derived 3-row fixture — locked snapped prices + leaderboard order + byte-for-byte reproducibility across two independent stores + exact round-trip values, the byte-equality oracle, mirroring `test_data_lake_real.py::test_byte_for_byte_reproducibility`); the bench above. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` release build):** `brutex/engine/results_store.py` per-module **100% line + 100% branch** (172 stmts / 44 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on the module + all 4 test files; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` both **0 errors**; `bandit` clean; unit+property+golden = **63 passed**, bench green; full engine suite (incl. stage1a + combo_mask) **168 passed**, no regressions. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is the storage DISCIPLINE + reproducibility oracle, NOT the metric maths — `ResultRow` implements a deterministic, dtype-faithful subset of the spec's **identity + money + trade-count + metric** columns, **PLUS two price-family columns (`avg_entry_price`/`avg_exit_price`) that are NOT in the spec's Result Row Schema** (which carries money + ratios, no raw price) — added to exercise the 2dp price-storage discipline end-to-end;
