438. **DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 — parallelise the per-window fetch INSIDE one `(instrument, interval)` spot series so a SINGLE symbol's pull saturates UP TO ~5 r/s (was ~0.5 r/s sequential)** (2026-06-03, follow-up to DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 #436, operator: "parallelize the per-window fetch INSIDE a single (instrument, interval) series so a SINGLE-symbol spot pull saturates UP TO ~5 r/s"). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the ID `DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001` is the authoritative key; on current `main` the ledger carries a DUPLICATE **#436** (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 and DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001 both landed at #436 per their own numbering notes), and DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (PR #342) then merged at **#437** first, so this lands at the next free integer **#438** — the decision ID, not the number, is authoritative (same convention as #428/#430/#431/#432/#436/#437). **Problem #436 deliberately left open:** PR #436 parallelised only the OUTER `(instrument, interval)` / per-underlying loop; it explicitly kept the per-window spine of ONE series sequential. So a **single-symbol** pull (e.g. re-pulling just SENSEX, or any one index/stock) still issued its 90-day windows one-at-a-time, each waiting for the previous round-trip → **~0.5 r/s** (measured: SENSEX 2021→2026, 22 windows, ~43 s ≈ 0.5 r/s at ~2 s/call), leaving ~90% of Dhan's 5 r/s budget idle whenever the outer loop has only one job. **What shipped — parallelise the WINDOWS of one series, reusing the #436 infra (no reinvention, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py::ingest_spot` now maps its planned fetch windows through an injected `run_parallel: RunParallel | None` (default builds `PoolRunParallel(workers_to_saturate(<pace rps>))`), sharing the SAME thread-safe `DhanRateController` via the `pace` hook so the AGGREGATE issue rate across BOTH fan-out levels stays `≤ 5 r/s` (Rule #6). The per-window body was extracted **verbatim** into a private `_ingest_one_window(...)` returning a small `_WindowOutcome(bars_appended, transient, skipped)`; the caller thread sums these (addition is commutative → worker-completion order never changes the `IngestReport`, Rule #4/#7). Each worker RE-BINDS `pull_id` via `pull_id_scope(pull_id)` (the `ThreadPoolExecutor` does not inherit the contextvar — same #426/#436 fix) so every `ingest.*` event keeps its correlation id. A terminal `DhanError` is captured by `run_parallel` then **re-raised on the caller thread**, so the outer `run_dhan_spot_ingest` quarantine sees the exact same terminal error it did when the spine was sequential (`test_terminal_error_propagates` still green). `run_parallel` is injectable so tests drive a synchronous fake with zero threads (mirrors `run_dhan_spot_ingest` / `universe_phases.run_two_phase`). The default pool is sized from the live pace rate via a pure `_pace_rps(pace)` helper (reads `controller.current_rps` off a `DhanRateController`-bound `pace` method's `__self__`, else the 5.0 ceiling fallback — a sizing hint only; the shared bucket, not the worker count, is the real governor). **THE CRITICAL CORRECTNESS FIX (a real hazard #436's premise did NOT cover):** #436 reasoned "each pair writes a DISTINCT path-isolated partition → no write lock needed" — TRUE for different SERIES, but FALSE for the windows of ONE series. Adjacent 90-day windows straddle a MONTH boundary, so two windows of one series write the SAME `(symbol, interval, year, month)` Parquet partition (verified: SENSEX 2021→2026 has 20 of 22 windows sharing a month with an adjacent window, e.g. windows `[2021-04-01, 2021-06-30)` and `[2021-06-30, 2021-09-28)` both touch June). `ParquetWriter.write` does a read-modify-write merge (read stored month → union incoming bars by timestamp → atomic `os.replace`), so two threads merging the SAME file at once is a classic LOST UPDATE: both read the old file, each unions only its own bars, the later `os.replace` wins and silently DROPS the other window's bars for the shared month. Fixed with a `threading.Lock` **per destination path** (interned in `_PARTITION_LOCKS` under an `_PARTITION_LOCKS_GUARD` meta-lock) wrapping the existence-check + merge/create in `ParquetWriter.write`: same-file writers serialise (no lost update), different-partition writers NEVER contend (the fan-out keeps its parallelism). The lock is keyed by PATH (not writer instance) on purpose — the production fan-out may build one `ParquetWriter` per worker (the class docstring blesses that), so the lock MUST be shared across instances resolving to the same on-disk file. The merge unions by timestamp, so the stored bytes are identical regardless of which window acquires the lock first (order-independent merge-on-write — DEC-LAKE-MERGE-WRITE-001 — preserved). **Scope = SPOT ONLY (stated honestly).** The options rolling-option per-window fetch (`option_ingest.py` / `option_universe_ingest.py`) is NOT parallelised here: its write tail is the hash-chained single-writer `OptionBarSink`+`AuditWriter` (Rule #8, explicitly NOT thread-safe — #436 serialises it with a single-writer lock precisely because the audit chain must advance as one writer), so fanning out the option windows of one series is higher-risk and out of scope for this PR (a separate decision + its own §9 hostile review). The options OUTER per-underlying fan-out from #436 is unchanged. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10) — stated in the `ingest_spot` docstring, this entry, and the report:** this lets a SINGLE symbol's windows fan out so it saturates **UP TO ~5 r/s when Dhan is healthy** (single SENSEX pull ~43 s → toward ~10 s); it is **NOT a constant 5 r/s** — Dhan's hard cap + 429 backoff step-downs (`DhanRateController` 5→4→3) + per-call latency spikes lower the achieved rate, and on a SHORT 22-window series the 5-token burst means the raw admission count can momentarily read just above 5 while the burst-corrected steady-state rate never exceeds 5. Throughput here is **network-bound, NOT O(1)**; the fan-out is the *mechanism* that lets the shared rate bucket — not a single-threaded window loop — be the bottleneck. **MEASURED single-series speedup (real wall-clock, real `DhanRateController`, real `PoolRunParallel`, fake adapter sleeping the emulated round-trip — NO live network):** at the task's measured ~1.8 s/call SENSEX latency, **SEQUENTIAL (1 worker) = 22 windows in 39.6 s → 0.56 r/s** (reproducing the ~43 s / ~0.5 r/s baseline) vs **PARALLEL (`workers_to_saturate(5,1.8)`=9 workers) = 22 windows in 5.4 s → 4.07 r/s — a 7.3× wall-clock speedup** saturating toward the 5 r/s ceiling. (At a faster 0.5 s/call: 11.0 s→2.0 r/s sequential vs 4.0 s→5.5 r/s at 3 workers, 2.8×.) **Tests (deterministic — discrete-event timing simulator + real threads over a virtual clock, NO real network/sleep; CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/integration/test_dhan_spot_window_parallel.py` (new, 19 cases) — the `_SimPool` Little's-law harness (reused from #436's `test_dhan_spot_parallel.py` for COMMON consistency) proves ONE 22-window series fans out toward ~5 r/s with **peak in-flight == max_workers (10)** vs a 1-worker control at ~0.5 r/s (achieved 5.25 vs 0.50 r/s, > 5× over control); the burst-corrected steady-state rate never exceeds 5 even at the 32-worker cap (Rule #6 guard) incl. a REAL thread-pool run pacing 22 windows on a virtual-clock `DhanRateController`+`AdaptiveTokenBucket`; idempotent re-pull of one series issues ZERO net-new window fetches (Rule #7, coverage ledger byte-identical); **concurrent-window WRITE correctness** — the real `ingest_spot` window fan-out into a REAL `ParquetBarSink` on real threads (windows sharing month partitions) stores a lake byte-identical to a 1-worker run (the partition lock + order-independent merge ⇒ completion order never affects data); `pull_id` re-bound into every window worker (proven by running each in a FRESH `contextvars.Context`); a terminal `DhanError` re-raised from a worker; and the default-pool / `_pace_rps` sizing (controller-bound → live rps, plain callable / None → 5.0 fallback). `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py` (+3 whitebox cases) — `_partition_lock` interns the SAME lock per path + DISTINCT locks per path, and a 16-thread barrier-synced storm writing distinct timestamps into ONE month partition keeps ALL 16 bars (the lost-update guard). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` build):** `brutex.adapters.dhan.ingest` at per-module **100% line + 100% branch** (92 stmts / 22 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial) under the augmented CI gate (`test_dhan_ingest.py` + the new `test_dhan_spot_window_parallel.py` — the same gate-wiring fix #436 needed, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); `brutex.data.parquet_writer` new lock lines fully covered (the module clears its aggregate `--cov=brutex` 90% floor; its only uncovered lines are PRE-EXISTING polars-import/`_atomic_write`-cleanup paths, NOT this change); `run_dhan_spot_ingest` gate still **100%** (82/16); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean over `brutex tests`; `mypy --strict brutex` **0 errors** (164 files); `pyright brutex tests` **0 errors** (whitebox test files carry the DEC-P0-017 `# pyright: reportPrivateUsage=none` pragma; the 1 remaining pyright warning is the pre-existing `instrument_store.py:637`, untouched here); `bandit -r` clean (0 issues). The full affected suite (ingest / run_ingest / parquet_writer / rate_control / fetch_coverage / parallel wiring + the #436 parallel suites + smoke + redteam) is green; all 16 pre-existing `ingest_spot` unit tests pass UNCHANGED under the new default thread-pool path. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (#436, the OUTER-loop parallelisation + the thread-safe `DhanRateController`/`FetchCoverage`/`Catalog` + the `PoolRunParallel`/`workers_to_saturate` infra this reuses) · DEC-LAKE-MERGE-WRITE-001 (the order-independent merge-on-write this now serialises per-partition) · DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 (#426, the `pull_id` correlation preserved across the pool boundary) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip ledger, already thread-safe from #436) · DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 / DEC-DHAN-PULL-SCOPE-001 (#348, the 90-day-window 2021→today spot pull this accelerates) · CLAUDE.md §2 rules 6/7/8 · §4 · §9 (options deferral flagged for its own review) · §10 (honest envelope) · §11 COMMON (no reinvention — reuse `parallel.py` + the shared controller) · §12 (deterministic test types).

439. **DEC-DASHBOARD-COVERAGE-INVALIDATE-001 — the single-symbol `POST /api/v1/universe/pull` now invalidates the coverage `SummaryCache` so `/coverage` reflects a just-pulled symbol (was stuck at "0 series · 0 bars")** (2026-06-03, operator: "why coverage is not displaying anything ... check that"). **Root cause — a PR-A #437 regression:** DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (#437) added the O(1) `SummaryCache` for the `/coverage` spot+option polls, invalidated on every write tick by the BACKGROUND pull job (`BackgroundPullJob._on_progress` → `mark_dirty`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py:147`). But the SYNCHRONOUS single-symbol pull route (`api_universe_pull` → `pull_controller.pull_candles`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`) does NOT run through that job, so it never marked the cache dirty: after pulling ONE symbol (e.g. just SENSEX — the operator's exact case, 288,262 bars written per the live log) the cache kept serving its stale cold-start EMPTY snapshot, so `/coverage` showed "0 series · 0 bars" even though `/db` (which reads the lake LIVE, bypassing the cache) listed the bars. The bulk (`/pull-all`) and options (`/pull-options`) routes were UNAFFECTED — they run through the wired `BackgroundPullJob`. **What shipped (surgical one-line correctness fix + DI for a deterministic test):** (1) `api_universe_pull` calls `_summary_cache.mark_dirty()` after a successful `pull_candles` (O(1); the cache's 2 s TTL floor still bounds how often the next read actually rescans, so this can't become a scan storm); (2) `build_app(..., summary_cache: SummaryCache | None = None)` now accepts an INJECTED cache (CLAUDE.md §4 dependency injection) so the regression test can disable the TTL floor (`SummaryCache(ttl_floor_s=0.0)`) and assert the post-pull refresh DETERMINISTICALLY (in real use the 4 s page poll clears the floor). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this fixes the single-symbol path specifically; the bulk/options paths already invalidated. The robust bug-CLASS elimination (a lake-write-generation signal so ANY future writer auto-invalidates, instead of each route remembering to call `mark_dirty`) is a flagged follow-up, NOT claimed here. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage_invalidate.py` (new) — cold-start coverage caches EMPTY → a spot bar is written → the single-symbol pull route runs → the next `/coverage/spot` poll now reports `datasets == 1 · total_bars == 1`; PROVEN to guard the fix by a negative control (removing `mark_dirty` makes the test FAIL on the stale clean-hit). The existing dashboard e2e + responsive-under-write + universe-route suites pass UNCHANGED under the new `build_app` signature (31 green). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict brutex/dashboard/app.py` 0 issues. **Builds on:** DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (#437, the cache this completes the invalidation for) · DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-WIRING-001 (the background-job write funnel that already invalidates) · DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 (the spot summary the cache serves) · CLAUDE.md §2 rule 7 (idempotence — `mark_dirty` is safe to over-call) · §4 (DI, no global mutable state) · §10 (honest envelope) · §11 COMMON.

440. **DEC-DASHBOARD-REQUEST-LOGGING-001 — per-request structured dashboard logging (request_id + latency) + silence the uvicorn access-log firehose so the business events are readable again** (2026-06-03, operator: "what happened to our extensive professional-level logging mechanism ... logging with fix if there is any issues"). **The problem (operator-observed in the live log):** the dashboard's READ paths were observability-dark — a `GET /api/v1/...` produced only uvicorn's raw `"GET ... 200"` access line (no latency, no request id, no correlation with a concurrent pull), and the 1 s `/pull-progress` + 4 s coverage polls FLOODED that stream so the ~52 structured BUSINESS events (`rate.429`/`rate.stepdown`, `ingest.*`, `dhan.throughput`, `bloom_init`) were drowned. The structlog foundation itself was already professional-grade (JSON + rotating 10 MiB×5 file, the `/logs` viewer, `pull_id` correlation on writes/ingest/rate via `merge_contextvars`) — the gap was the READ path + the NOISE, not a missing mechanism. **What shipped (COMMON, CLAUDE.md §11):** (1) `brutex/observability/correlation.py` gains a `request_id` sibling to `pull_id` (`REQUEST_ID_KEY`, `new_request_id`, `current_request_id`, `request_id_scope`), sharing a single `_mint_id(width)` so id-generation lives in exactly one place (no copy-paste). (2) a NEW `brutex/dashboard/request_logging.py` owns the dashboard policy: `emit_request_log(...)` emits ONE structured `dashboard.request` event per request (`method` · `path` · `status_code` · `latency_ms` · `request_id` · `client`), at **DEBUG** for the high-frequency polls (`HIGH_FREQUENCY_POLL_PATHS` = `/pull-progress` + `/coverage/{spot,options,counters}`) and **INFO** otherwise, and `silence_uvicorn_access_log()` drops `uvicorn.access` to WARNING so its raw firehose stops duplicating what the structured event now records. (3) a thin `@app.middleware("http")` in `build_app` (FastAPI glue) binds the request_id (inbound `X-Request-ID` header else a fresh id) for the request's whole context — so any downstream event inherits it — times the handler, emits in a `finally` (a handler that RAISES is still logged as status 500 before the error propagates), and echoes the id in the `X-Request-ID` response header. (4) `cli.py` calls `silence_uvicorn_access_log()` once at dashboard startup. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this makes the read path observable + quiets the noise; it does NOT add multi-tenant log aggregation, sampling beyond the poll→DEBUG demotion, or a separate `access.log` file (flagged follow-ups, not claimed). The middleware is FastAPI glue (`# pragma: no cover`, like the rest of `app.py`'s glue) — its LOGIC (level policy, silencer, emit) is 100% unit-tested in `request_logging.py`, and its WIRING is proven by an integration test (the `X-Request-ID` header round-trips). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_request_logging.py` (NEW) — poll→DEBUG vs non-poll→INFO, field shape + 2-dp latency rounding, `client=None`, the silencer's default + custom level → `request_logging` **100% line+branch** (15 stmts / 2 branches); `tests/unit/test_observability_correlation.py` (+8) — the `request_id` mint/scope/unbind/coexist-with-pull_id mirror, keeping `correlation.py` **100%** (30 stmts); `tests/integration/test_dashboard_request_logging.py` (NEW) — a generated `X-Request-ID` is returned + an inbound one is echoed (the middleware glue is wired). Existing dashboard e2e + responsive-under-write suites pass UNCHANGED (30 green). New per-module 100% CI gates for `request_logging` + `correlation` added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12):** `ruff` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` 0 issues on the 3 changed sources. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 (#426, the `pull_id` correlation this mirrors) · DEC-RUN-LOG-CAPTURE-001 (the uvicorn→file routing this de-noises) · DEC-LOGS-VIEWER-001 (the `/logs` viewer that now shows readable events) · DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (#437, the O(1) cached routes the demoted polls hit) · CLAUDE.md §4 (DI, no global mutable state) · §10 (honest envelope) · §11 COMMON (one correlation module, one id minter) · §12 (test types).

441. **DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 — shared indicator + 52-condition vocabulary core in Rust, consumed by BOTH BruteX (Python via PyO3) and TickVault (Rust native), so a change to any indicator/condition reaches both bit-identically** (2026-06-03, operator-accepted: "build the common rust 52 vocab which can be used by both tickvault and brutex"). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the decision ID is authoritative; lands at the next free integer **#441** (main merged #437 DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 + #438 DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 + #439 DEC-DASHBOARD-COVERAGE-INVALIDATE-001 + #440 DEC-DASHBOARD-REQUEST-LOGGING-001 during this PR's review; main also carries pre-existing duplicate #434 + #436 from earlier racing PRs); renumbers if a sibling claims #441. **The decision (design proposal `docs/SHARED_CORE_DESIGN.md` + plain-English `docs/SHARED_CORE_EXPLAINED.md`):** **Option 1** of three — a standalone Rust crate (working name `trading-core`) holding the 5 indicators (EMA / pivots / Fib / day-extremes / prev-day-OHLC) + the 52-condition `evaluate_atoms`; BruteX binds it via **PyO3** (the existing `rust/fno-math` pattern, batched per chunk), TickVault links it **natively**. Rejected: Option 2 (two impls kept in sync by conformance vectors — does not deliver "write once") and Option 3 (codegen from a DSL — a generator to maintain forever). **Why (Correctness — Merge-Readiness priority #1):** the LIVE signal must equal the BACKTESTED signal or every backtest result is a lie about live; one compiled core makes them bit-identical by construction (not "verified equal", but *the same code*). **Reverses (deliberate scope expansion, Golden Rule #3 — done openly, never silently):** DEC-P0-026 (BruteX "self-contained … no co-development relationship to any other repo") + DEC-P0-025 (Rust indicators removed from `fno-math`); the reversal takes effect at **Phase 2** (when BruteX actually depends on the crate), where the paired `CLAUDE.md` amendments (here + in the TickVault repo) land. **Phased, mergeable, golden-vector-gated:** **Phase 0** (this PR) — freeze today's Python `evaluate_atoms` as the cross-language oracle; **Phase 1** — build the Rust crate, prove it reproduces the oracle bit-for-bit; **Phase 2** — BruteX delegates to it via PyO3 (its full suite stays green = proof of bit-identity); **Phase 3** — TickVault adopts it (needs TickVault repo access — currently outside this session's scope); **Phase 4** — crate semver + the shared golden-vector CI gate in both repos (the "always-latest, auto-reflect, can't-drift" guarantee, CI-enforced). **What shipped HERE (Phase 0 — pure-additive, reverses nothing yet):** `scripts/gen_vocab_golden_vectors.py` deterministically builds **400** diverse `input → u64` cases (fixed seed; prices int64 paisa; covering all 52 bits **set-somewhere AND clear-somewhere**) and freezes them to `tests/golden/fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json` — **language-neutral** (raw paisa inputs) so Python AND the future Rust crate read the *same* vectors; `tests/golden/test_vocab_golden.py` asserts the current Python `evaluate_atoms` reproduces every frozen `u64`, plus the full-52-bit-coverage + fixture-metadata invariants. This JSON is the **contract the Rust port must satisfy**. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** Phase 0 is groundwork only — the Rust crate, the PyO3 binding, the TickVault adoption, and the `CLAUDE.md` self-containment reversal are LATER phases, NONE claimed done here; today the vocab still runs in **Python** in BruteX, and "common Rust for both apps" is **in progress, not built**. The light-speed win is the hot-kernel-in-Rust + Python-glue split (the NumPy/Polars/PyTorch pattern), not "everything in Rust". **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean (generator + test); `mypy --strict` + `pyright` both **0 errors**; the generator is outside the CI bandit scope (`bandit -r brutex` only) and tests are excluded (`[tool.bandit] exclude_dirs`); the golden suite **3 passed**; fixture **400 cases / full 52-bit coverage both ways**. **§9 design pass:** `docs/SHARED_CORE_DESIGN.md` §6 carries the pre-authored 9-objection hostile-review table; the full 4-agent pass runs on the Rust crate at Phase 1 before it lands. **Builds on:** DEC-P0-025 / DEC-P0-026 (the decisions this reverses) · the existing `brutex/vocabulary/` + `brutex/indicators/` (the Python oracle source) · `rust/fno-math` (the PyO3 precedent) · CLAUDE.md §1 / §3 / §9 / §10 / §11 COMMON / §12. **Progress (appended; SAME decision, reusing #441 — Golden Rule #1):** **Phase 1 ✅ MERGED (PR #348)** — the `rust/trading-core/` crate (pure-Rust `rlib`; PyO3 behind an optional `python` feature so `cargo test` links no libpython) reproduces all 400 golden vectors bit-for-bit (`cargo test --release`, `overflow-checks=true`); the §9 4-agent hostile pass landed its findings (corrupt-OHLC always-on `assert!` so release fails loud like the Python `ValueError`; fractional-second floor; documented i64 paisa domain). **Phase 2a ✅ MERGED (PR #349)** — the maturin abi3 wheel + `trading_core.evaluate_from_raw` proven bit-identical FROM PYTHON across all 400 cases (`scripts/check_vocab_rust_parity.py`), wired into the isolated `rust-trading-core` CI job so a wheel-build issue can't destabilise the main pipeline. **Phase 2b ✅ (this PR) — THE CORE FLIP + the DEC-P0-025/026 reversal takes EFFECT:** `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py::evaluate_atoms` is now a thin marshalling **shim** delegating to the new `trading_core.evaluate_with_levels` (takes the PRE-BUILT pivot+fib levels, NO recompute — so a gap-day snapshot with hand-built `pdc == 0` levels flows through unchanged, which a `compute_pivot_levels` recompute would reject; this is why a SECOND entry point was added rather than reusing `evaluate_from_raw`). The Python 52-condition body + the `_is_near` / time-cutoff constants / `PriorBarHistory.all_bullish`·`all_bearish`·`alternating` helpers are DELETED — they now live ONCE, in Rust (COMMON / zero-duplication, CLAUDE.md §11); `PriorBarHistory` keeps only its `prior_n`/`flags`/`update()` state, passed straight through. 442. **DEC-STORE-READ-WRITE-SPLIT-001 — split the dashboard's `store.connection` reads onto a dedicated child READ cursor under a SEPARATE read lock so an uncached `/db` read NEVER waits behind the universe-pull writer** (2026-06-03, operator: "ultra fast extreme speed ... O(1) latency ... never slow/locked/hanged"). **The gap PR-A (#437) left:** DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 moved every blocking read OFF the event loop via `run_in_threadpool`, so one slow read no longer froze the server — but the read itself still WAITED behind the writer's single per-store `threading.RLock` (`_LockedReadConn` held that SAME RLock across `execute → fetch`); it just waited on a worker thread (PR-A's own note: an uncached `/db/tables` took 1005 ms during a held writer lock). **What shipped (lowest-risk split):** `InstrumentStore.__init__` now derives a child READ cursor `self._read_conn = conn.cursor()` (a SEPARATE DuckDB connection sharing the same in-process catalog) guarded by a SEPARATE `self._read_lock` (`RLock`); the `connection` property returns `_LockedReadConn(self._read_conn, self._read_lock)` instead of `(self._conn, self._lock)`. So the dashboard's raw `/db` + lake-summary reads run on a DIFFERENT connection under a DIFFERENT lock and never contend with the writer's RLock. The ~40 internal `self._conn.execute(...)` write/metadata call sites + every `@_synchronized` method are UNCHANGED (still on the writer connection + write RLock) — minimal blast radius. `close()` closes the child cursor first, then the parent. **Empirically verified BEFORE building (no illusion, DuckDB 1.5.3):** (a) `conn.cursor()` yields a usable separate connection; (b) a read on the child cursor DURING an open, uncommitted write transaction on the parent WORKS without blocking and sees the COMMITTED snapshot (MVCC — the uncommitted rows are invisible); (c) after the parent COMMITs, the child sees the new rows; (d) a second `read_only=True` connection is REFUSED while the process holds the file read-write, so the child cursor is the ONLY mechanism. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ an uncached dashboard read no longer waits for the writer — proven; the writer stays single-flight at the job level, this only frees concurrent READERS. 🟡 concurrent reads still serialize against EACH OTHER (one child cursor under one read lock) — fine for the single-operator dashboard, NOT unlimited reader parallelism (a read-only connection POOL is impossible while the process holds the file RW — a flagged follow-up). 🚫 the read itself is still O(rows scanned), NOT O(1) — this removes the WAIT, not the scan cost (the O(1) cached-summary path is PR-A's, unchanged). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/integration/test_instrument_store_read_write_split.py` (NEW, the headline oracle) — (1) while a background thread HOLDS the write `RLock` for seconds, an uncached `store.connection` read completes in < 0.3 s (it did NOT wait) returning the consistent committed snapshot; (2) during the writer's open uncommitted `DELETE` transaction, a reader sees the committed 2-row snapshot (MVCC), and the rows survive the rollback. PROVEN to guard the split by a negative control — reverting `connection` to `(self._conn, self._lock)` makes BOTH oracles FAIL (the read waits the full hold; the reader sees the dirty `0` rows). The `_RollbackConn` write-path double gains a `cursor()` method (mirrors the real connection interface). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + DuckDB 1.5.3):** `brutex.data.instrument_store` per-module **100% line+branch** (414 stmts / 58 branches) under the augmented CI gate (its two existing suites + the new oracle file); the dashboard e2e + responsive-under-write + coverage-invalidate suites pass UNCHANGED (29 green); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` 0 issues; `pyright` 0 errors (the 1 warning at `:637` is the PRE-EXISTING `_synchronized` self._lock access, untouched). **Builds on:** DEC-STORE-THREADSAFE-001 (the single RLock this splits) · DEC-STORE-LOCK-LEAK-FIX-001 (the idempotent `_release` the read view keeps — so a plain lock would not even deadlock; RLock chosen only to match the contract) · DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (#437, the off-loop offload this completes) · CLAUDE.md §2 rule 7 (idempotence — reads are pure SELECT) · rule 8 (audit chain untouched — `db_view` issues only SELECTs) · §10 (honest envelope) · §11 COMMON.

443. **DEC-DASHBOARD-RATE-PANEL-001 — surface the LIVE rate on the dashboard: `current_rps` (adaptive target) + `effective_rps` (measured) + recent 429s + p95 latency, via an O(1) `/api/v1/rate` route fed by a live-pull observer** (2026-06-03, operator: "is 5 r/s precisely working ... show me ... no illusion"). **The gap (Plan agent finding):** `DashboardState.update_rate_limit` existed but had NO live caller, and the MEASURED `effective_rps`/latency (already computed by `CallMeter.snapshot()` at the transport, logged as `dhan.throughput`) was never surfaced — so the rate panel rendered ZEROS. The operator's recurring "is 5 r/s working?" was answerable only from `/logs`. **What shipped (testable data plane + pragma'd live caller):** (1) `RateLimitPanel` gains `effective_rps` + `latency_ms_p95`; `DashboardState.update_throughput(...)` sets them. (2) `make_rate_observer(state)` (app.py) — a pure, tested factory returning a callback that maps a (`DhanRateController.snapshot()` → current_rps + recent_hits, `CallMeter.snapshot()` → effective_rps + latency_ms_p95) pair onto the panel (tolerates missing keys). The full dashboard e2e + responsive-under-write + coverage-invalidate + request-logging + pull_controller suites pass UNCHANGED (82 green). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12):** `ruff` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` 0 on app.py + pull_controller; `vulture` clean (the new methods have live callers); `pull_controller` stays 97.16% (aggregate-floor module; the only miss is the PRE-EXISTING `476-479`). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-CALL-LATENCY-LOGGING-001 (#419, the `CallMeter` effective_rps this surfaces) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001 (the `rate.*` events) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (#352, the [3..5] controller snapshot) · DEC-DASHBOARD-LIVE-1 (the `DashboardState` panel pattern) · DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (#437, the O(1) poll discipline) · CLAUDE.md §4 (DI) · §10 (honest envelope) · §11 COMMON · §12.

top:8px` — always visible while you scroll; (b) every row gets a multi-select **checkbox** that toggles a `selMulti` map; the checkbox `stopPropagation`s so the row BODY click still does single-select + expiries (the two interactions stay independent); 445. **DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001 — the brute-force funnel's first assembled vertical slice: `mask_to_entry_signals` (the missing Stage-1A→trade-sim seam) + `evaluate_combo` (one strategy combo → its `ResultMetrics`), with a configurable notional equity base for the signal-only percentage metrics** (2026-06-04, operator: "go ahead with the plan ... find the precise combo ... which made the massive profit + max win-rate"). **The gap (per the 4-agent roadmap audit, `docs/SHARED_CORE_COMPARISON.md`):** every brick of the funnel was built + unit-tested (Stage-1A `build_bar_bits`, `simulate_trades`, `compute_metrics`, `ResultsStore`, the supermask kernel, Bloom+LMDB dedup) but NOTHING connected them — there was no code that turned a strategy mask + real bars into a measurable result, because the seam converting a mask → the per-bar `entry_signals: bool[]` that `trade_sim` requires did not exist (`combo_mask` only had `count_supermasks` (aggregate counts) + `evaluate_mask` (one bar)). **What shipped:** (a) `brutex/engine/combo_mask.py::mask_to_entry_signals(bar_bits, mask) -> list[bool]` = `[(b & mask) == mask for b in bar_bits]` — THE seam, one AND+CMP per bar; (b) `brutex/engine/sweep_driver.py::evaluate_combo(bars, mask, *, direction, tf_minutes, sl, tp, start_equity_paisa, ...) -> ResultMetrics` chaining `build_bar_bits → mask_to_entry_signals → simulate_trades → build_equity_curve → compute_metrics` (a no-trade combo yields all-zero metrics, never an error); (c) `build_equity_curve(bars, trades, *, start_equity_paisa, tf_minutes)` maps each trade's realised P&L onto its exit bar (matched by `exit_ts`→bar `timestamp`), with a single-bar span floor so the `EquityCurve` `span_years > 0` invariant holds. **The modelling choice (recorded, not hidden — Golden Rule #1):** signal-only spot has NO real capital base, so the equity curve uses a configurable notional `DEFAULT_START_EQUITY_PAISA = 10_000_000` (₹100,000) as the percentage-metric denominator; absolute paisa P&L is unaffected, and the base is a parameter (the operator can set it per run). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_driver.py` 14 passed; the EXACT CI engine gate (`pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py`) reaches **100.00%** over the whole `brutex.engine` package incl. `sweep_driver.py` (42 stmts / 12 branches) + the `combo_mask` seam (212 passed); `mypy --strict brutex` 0 errors (167 files); `pyright` 0 errors; `ruff` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is the SINGLE-combo evaluator — ✅ you can now backtest one mask over real bars and get its win-rate / profit-factor / Sharpe. 🚫 NOT yet: the Stage-2 **ranking** (`brutex/ranking/__init__.py` is still spec-only — the 6 hard gates + the 7-term composite score), the **K-of-N mask loop** (`iter_masks_k_of_n` exists; the sweep over it does not), **`ResultsStore` persistence** + its top-K wiring, the Stage-1B coarse pre-filter (via the built `count_supermasks`), CPCV/DSR robustness, and a **`brutex sweep` CLI** (none exists). Each is the next increment and layers on `evaluate_combo`'s contract unchanged. **Builds on:** DEC-RUST-SUPERMASK-KERNEL-001 (the batched kernel for the later loop) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, `compute_metrics`) · the Stage-1A `build_bar_bits` + `trade_sim` + `ResultsStore` bricks · `docs/SHARED_CORE_COMPARISON.md` (the roadmap this executes) · CLAUDE.md §10 · §12.
446. **DEC-TF-MATERIALIZE-001 — MANUAL "derive timeframes": pre-materialise a symbol's STORED 1-minute bars into each SELECTED derived intraday timeframe as its OWN stored interval partition, so the brute-force sweep reads a 5m/15m/60m bar in O(1) (a direct Parquet read) instead of re-resampling 1m every time** (2026-06-04, operator-approved: a MANUAL trigger, storage is fine — external-drive-backed via `$BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT`). **Reconciles with DEC-UNIVERSE-MULTISELECT-001 (#444):** #444 correctly states the 19 intraday TFs *auto-derive from the 1m base at read time* (DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001) — that stays true and is the default. This entry adds an **opt-in pre-materialisation**: the same resample, run ONCE and written to the lake, so the sweep does not re-pay the resample ~33 billion times (CLAUDE.md §5 O(1) per read). It is **MANUAL only — never automatic** (no auto-trigger anywhere); the read-time auto-derive remains the fallback for any TF not materialised. **What shipped:** **(1)** NEW `brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py` — the pure, 100%-tested core `materialize_timeframes(*, tfs, read_1m, write_tf)`: de-dups `tfs` (`dict.fromkeys`, O(1) uniqueness, first-seen order), calls the **REUSED** `brutex.data.spot_resample.derive_intraday_tfs(read_1m())` (the single source of truth for session/DST/no-look-ahead bucketing — NOT re-implemented here), writes each requested TF present in the derivation via the injected `write_tf` (recording its bar count), and records requested-but-not-derived labels as `skipped`. Returns a frozen `MaterializeResult(written: dict[str,int], skipped: tuple[str,...])` + `total_bars`. `read_1m`/`write_tf` are INJECTED, so the whole control flow is unit-testable with NO lake / DuckDB / FastAPI. The module also owns the canonical `INTRADAY_TF_INTERVALS` map (TF label → `brutex.data.partition.VALID_INTERVALS` member, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — the ONE place that correspondence lives) for the **8 storable** TFs (`2m,3m,5m,10m,15m,30m,60m,240m`); the resampler's other derived labels (`4m,6m…14m,120m,180m`) have no canonical partition interval and are reported `skipped`. **(2)** Production glue in `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (`# pragma: no cover` — raw lake I/O, integration-tested not line-gated): `_make_read_1m` reads the symbol's stored `1minute` partitions → polars df (`ts_utc`+OHLCV, sorted); `_make_write_tf` converts the resampled frame rows → `CandleBar` (`open_interest=0` for spot) → `ParquetBarSink.append(interval=INTRADAY_TF_INTERVALS[tf], …)` (the sink snaps prices to the 2-dp tick grid + merges idempotently by `(year,month)`, DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 / CLAUDE.md §7). **(3)** Route `POST /api/v1/universe/derive-timeframes?symbol=&tfs=` (omitted `tfs` ⇒ all 8 materialisable TFs; unknown symbol → 400; comma-list parsed, blanks dropped) → JSON `{written:{tf:bars}, skipped:[...], total_bars}`; invalidates the coverage cache so the next poll rediscovers the new partitions. **(4)** UI in `templates/universe.html` — a "⚙ Derive timeframes" button + an 8-option multi-select (default `5m,15m,60m`), revealed when an instrument is selected; on click POSTs the route and renders the per-TF written counts (skipped TFs shown muted) in the existing live pull panel. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_timeframe_materialize.py` — `timeframe_materialize.py` at **100% line + 100% branch** via the REAL `derive_intraday_tfs` + a fake `write_tf`: requested-TFs-written-with-correct-counts, unknown-TF-skipped, duplicate-TF-deduped-once, empty-request-noop, all-storable-default, the `total_bars` property, and an `INTRADAY_TF_INTERVALS`-vs-`VALID_INTERVALS` drift guard; a NEW per-module strict-100 gate is wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. `tests/integration/test_timeframe_materialize_roundtrip.py` — the high-stakes oracle: writes ~120 one-minute bars to a tmp lake via `ParquetBarSink`, runs the materialise through the REAL app glue + `materialize_timeframes`, reads the derived `5minute` partition back via `db_view.query_candles`, and asserts the aggregation (5×1m → one 5m: open=first, high=max, low=min, close=last, volume=sum) AND idempotence (re-run ⇒ zero net-new rows + byte-identical Parquet). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the resampler is REUSED (not re-implemented) · the production lake round-trip + aggregation + idempotence are integration-proven · the materialise core is 100% line+branch tested + CI-gated. 🟡 the raw lake read/write glue (`_make_read_1m`/`_make_write_tf`) is `# pragma: no cover` — integration-tested, not line-gated (same pattern as the rest of `app.py`'s I/O glue) · only the **8** TFs that map to a `VALID_INTERVALS` partition are storable (the other 11 derived intraday labels stay read-time-only). 🚫 **MANUAL only, not automatic** (no auto-trigger) · this removes the per-read resample TAX, it does NOT change the physics — the production sweep is still **2–4 days** on the reference envelope (CLAUDE.md §8). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (the 1m-base resample this pre-materialises) · DEC-UNIVERSE-MULTISELECT-001 (#444, the /universe UI this extends) · DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the sink's 2-dp snap) · CLAUDE.md §5 (O(1) reads) · §7 (idempotence) · §11 COMMON (one resampler, one TF→interval map) · §12 (test types).

447. **DEC-RANKING-001 — Stage-2 composite ranking + the mask-sweep loop: turn a set of strategy combos into a gate-passed, z-scored, sorted leaderboard (Increment 2 of the brute-force funnel)** (2026-06-04, operator: "find the precise level where many conditions match + it achieved the highest, most-reliable profit ... this much possibility"). **What shipped:** (a) `brutex/ranking/__init__.py` implements the Track-1 ranking spec — `passes_gates(metrics)` (the 5 single-result hard rejection gates: `total_trades<30`, `profit_factor<1.2`, `max_drawdown_pct>30%`, `win_rate<25% AND win/loss<2.0`, `max_consecutive_losses>10`) + `rank_combos(candidates)` which z-score-normalises the 6 composite terms (`0.25·Sharpe + 0.20·Sortino + 0.15·Calmar + 0.15·(PF−1) + 0.10·Recovery + 0.10·(WinRate·WLR)`) across the surviving population, clamps each z to `[−3,+3]`, and sorts descending → a `list[RankedCombo]`; (b) `brutex/engine/sweep_driver.py::sweep_masks(bars, masks, ...)` backtests MANY masks, building the Stage-1A `bar_bits` matrix **ONCE** and reusing it across every mask (a shared `_metrics_for_mask` core — `evaluate_combo` refactored onto it, **zero behavioural drift**, pinned by a same-output test); (c) `rank_sweep(bars, masks, ...)` = `rank_combos(sweep_masks(...))` → the ranked leaderboard, head = the top combo. **The lockbox is deferred (Golden Rule #10):** the spec's 6th gate (overfit) + 7th composite term both need a train/test (CPCV/WFO) **lockbox Sharpe** that does not exist yet (Stage 3); this module implements the 5 single-result gates + 6 available terms and DROPS the 0.05 lockbox term until the Stage-3 split lands — the absolute score scale is irrelevant (z-scores are *relative*; used only for ORDERING a leaderboard), so dropping it changes ranking power, never correctness. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_ranking.py` **16 passed at 100% line+branch** on `brutex.ranking` (every gate branch + z-score zero-variance/clamp/None-term edges); the EXACT engine package gate reaches **100.00%** over `brutex.engine` incl. `sweep_driver.py` (52 stmts / 14 branches, 216 passed); a dedicated `--cov=brutex.ranking --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_ranking.py` gate added to `ci.yml` (mirrors `combo_mask`); `mypy --strict brutex` 0 errors (167 files); `pyright` 0 errors; `ruff` clean. **Honest envelope:** ✅ given a mask-set + 1m bars you now get a **ranked top-combo leaderboard** (gated + composite-scored) — the "which precise combo paid best, most reliably" answer. 🚫 NOT yet: the full **K-of-N enumeration sweep** over the millions of combos (`iter_masks_k_of_n` feeds `sweep_masks`, but a driver streaming all K=1..5 × the param grid × Bloom/LMDB dedup is Increment 3), **`ResultsStore` Parquet persistence** + top-K query, the **Stage-1B coarse pre-filter** (via the built `count_supermasks`), CPCV/DSR robustness, the lockbox, and a **`brutex sweep` CLI**. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001 (#445, `evaluate_combo` + the seam this loops over) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, the `ResultMetrics` the gates + composite read) · CLAUDE.md §10 · §11 COMMON (the shared `_metrics_for_mask`) · §12.

448. **DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001 — add the risk-efficiency (MAE/MFE excursion) term to the composite leaderboard score: rank tight-stop, big-run combos first (Increment 2.5 of the brute-force funnel)** (2026-06-04, operator: "always find the extreme tight SL and massive profit ... this one will decide the combinations and its conditions"). **Why:** the Increment-2 composite ranked on return-quality (Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar/PF/Recovery/WinRate·WLR) but had NO term rewarding *how tight the stop needed to be* — the operator's stated #1 objective ("extreme tight SL + massive profit"). **What shipped:** (a) `brutex/ranking/__init__.py::_risk_efficiency(m) = m.avg_mfe_paisa / max(m.avg_mae_paisa, 1)` — the favorable-to-adverse excursion ratio (avg Maximum Favorable Excursion ÷ avg Maximum Adverse Excursion, both already computed per-trade by `compute_metrics` and aggregated on `ResultMetrics`): HIGH ⇒ each trade tended to run far in our favour (big MFE = the move paid) for little adverse heat (small MAE = the effective stop never needed to be wide) — exactly "tight SL + massive profit". `avg_mae_paisa` is floored at 1 paisa so a never-adverse combo yields a large but FINITE ratio (z-scores require finite inputs), never a division by zero; (b) a 7th z-scored composite term `_W_RISK_EFFICIENCY = 0.15` added to `rank_combos` (co-equal with Calmar/PF, just under Sharpe's 0.25) — a strong first-class voice for the operator's priority, but BLENDED not dominant, so a single lucky huge-MFE trade cannot dictate the leaderboard (the anti-overfit / no-illusion choice, Golden Rule #10); (c) a `RankedCombo.risk_efficiency` read-only property exposing the raw ratio for leaderboard transparency ("this combo's MFE was N× its MAE"). **The excursion concept** is John Sweeney's Maximum Adverse/Favorable Excursion (1996); the raw avg-MFE/avg-MAE ratio here is an un-normalised cousin of the ATR-normalised Edge Ratio (Faith, *Way of the Turtle*, 2007) — NOT volatility-normalised, so it is described as a risk-efficiency ratio, not "the Edge Ratio" (Golden Rule #1, no over-claim). **Not a gate:** risk-efficiency is a RANKING term only — no arbitrary hard MFE/MAE floor is imposed (the existing 5 gates already reject losers); a hard floor can be added later if the operator wants one. **Also fixed (drive-by, operator "resolve any conflicts/issues"):** TWO duplicate ledger numbers that landed on main from parallel-session merges — (a) both #360 (DEC-RANKING-001) and #359 (DEC-TF-MATERIALIZE-001) merged as `446.` → DEC-RANKING-001 renumbered `446 → 447` (DEC-TF-MATERIALIZE keeps 446); (b) both #357 (DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001) and #358 (DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001) merged as `445.` → DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 renumbered `445 → 449` (DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER keeps 445, since this entry + #447 already cite it as #445). Unique monotonic numbering restored. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_ranking.py` (NEW cases: the avg-MFE/avg-MAE ratio, the avg-MAE-0 finite-floor path via the `risk_efficiency` property, and risk-efficiency driving the order with all else equal) at **100% line+branch** on `brutex.ranking`; the `brutex.engine` package gate stays **100.00%**; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` + `ruff` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the leaderboard now prioritises tight-SL/big-run combos as a co-top-tier signal, transparently exposed per combo. 🟡 the weight (0.15, blended) is a deliberate anti-overfit choice — it can be dialled up to dominate with one constant if the operator wants. 🚫 it does NOT make a backtest a guarantee of live profit — only the Stage-3 out-of-sample / lockbox / CPCV / DSR validation (NOT built yet) decides real-vs-illusion. **Builds on:** DEC-RANKING-001 (#447, the composite this extends) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, `avg_mfe_paisa`/`avg_mae_paisa`) · CLAUDE.md §10 (honest envelope) · §11 COMMON · §12.

## DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 (2026-06-04)

449a. **DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 — KEEP-FIRST conflict policy: when Dhan re-states a historical bar (same timestamp, different OHLCV/OI) the lake keeps the stored bar, records the discrepancy, and continues the pull — replacing the prior abort-on-conflict behaviour that killed the whole pull (real failure: NIFTY 2021-09-16 close 17513.80→17512.45 aborted the whole NIFTY ingest)** (2026-06-04, operator decision).

**The problem (verbatim from the failure log):** `WriterError: partition … CONFLICTING bar at 2021-09-16T03:45:00Z — stored close 17513.80, vendor close 17512.45` killed the entire NIFTY pull on a tiny re-statement. Dhan occasionally back-adjusts a bar (micro-correction, corporate action, or transport noise); the previous policy treated ANY such re-statement as a fatal error.

**The operator choice:** KEEP-FIRST + LOG + CONTINUE. The STORED bar wins unconditionally — once a bar is in the lake it is never overwritten (Golden Rule #7: reproducibility). The discrepancy is recorded as a `BarConflict` and surfaced as a WARNING so the operator sees exactly what the vendor changed. The pull finishes; the report counts every conflict across all windows.

**What shipped:**

- `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py` — `BarConflict(timestamp, stored, vendor)` frozen dataclass (DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 / Golden Rule #7 cited in NumPy docstring); `WriteResult.conflicts: tuple[BarConflict, ...] = ()` (defaulted so existing constructions are valid); `_merge_write` no longer raises on a value conflict — it appends a `BarConflict` to a local list, keeps `prev` in `merged` (stored bar wins), does NOT increment `added`, and propagates `conflicts` on BOTH the `added==0` early-return path (no rewrite needed) and the `added>0` rewrite path. The fresh-write path (no existing file) returns `conflicts=()`.

- `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py` — `_WindowOutcome.conflicts: int = 0`; `IngestReport.conflicts: int = 0`; `_ingest_one_window` iterates `result.write_results` and for each `wr.conflicts` emits one `ingest.conflict` WARNING per discrepancy (`pull_id`, `timestamp`, `stored_close`, `vendor_close`, `symbol`, `interval`) and counts them; `ingest_spot` sums `result.conflicts` across windows into the series total and includes it in the `ingest.series` DEBUG line.

- `tests/integration/test_data_lake_real.py` — `test_same_timestamp_different_value_raises` (which asserted the OLD abort behaviour) replaced by `test_same_timestamp_different_value_keep_first` asserting: no raise; `WriteResult.conflicts` has 1 entry; stored bar intact; on-disk Parquet is unchanged.

- `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py` — new `TestBarConflict` class (4 cases: pure conflict/added==0/no-rewrite, conflict-alongside-new-bar/added>0/rewrite-keeps-stored, identical-rewrite/empty-conflicts, fresh-write/empty-conflicts) + `TestWriterErrors` (empty-bars, multi-partition, atomic-write exception cleanup, polars-import error). Reaches 100% line+branch on `brutex.data.parquet_writer`.

- `tests/unit/test_dhan_ingest.py` — `_ConflictSink` fake + `TestIngestSpotConflicts` (4 cases: single conflict emits WARNING log with correct fields, conflict count in `ingest.series`, clean window emits no WARNING, multiple conflicts aggregated across windows). Reaches 100% line+branch on `brutex.adapters.dhan.ingest`.

**Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):**
- ✅ Keep-first is proven by the integration test (real Parquet round-trip + on-disk value asserted) and the unit tests (all paths at 100% line+branch).
- ✅ `ingest.conflict` WARNING is structlog-verified; the count surfaces in `IngestReport.conflicts` + `ingest.series`.
- 🟡 A gap-verifier that asserts COMPLETENESS (every stored bar has a hash-chain entry proving it was never overwritten) is a SEPARATE follow-up, not this PR — the keep-first invariant here is tested at the merge-write level, not end-to-end audit-chain level.
- 🚫 Does NOT change retry logic, skip logic, or rate-limiting — conflict detection is purely additive.

**Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-MERGE-WRITE-001 (the merge-on-write that this extends) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 (the per-partition lock under which `_merge_write` runs) · CLAUDE.md §2 Golden Rule #7 (idempotence) · §12 (100% coverage gate).

## DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 (2026-06-04)

449b. **DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 — /universe "⊕ tick its constituents": best-effort NSE index → constituent-stock auto-select (the follow-up #444 deferred)** (2026-06-04). **Why:** DEC-UNIVERSE-MULTISELECT-001 (#444) shipped the per-row multi-select + "⤓ Pull N selected" but explicitly deferred index→constituent auto-ticking because index membership is NOT in the Dhan instrument master. This PR adds it as the honestly-fragile, best-effort follow-up #444 named. **What shipped:** (1) NEW `brutex/dashboard/nse_constituents.py` — a metadata helper (NOT Dhan data): `INDEX_CSV_FILENAMES` (engine index symbol → NSE per-index CSV filename — NIFTY→`ind_nifty50list.csv`, BANKNIFTY→`ind_niftybanklist.csv`, FINNIFTY→`ind_niftyfinservicelist.csv`, MIDCPNIFTY→`ind_niftymidcapselect.csv`, NIFTYNXT50/NIFTY NEXT 50→`ind_niftynext50list.csv`, plus display-name aliases — DOCUMENTED "verify against NSE; may change", every unmapped index → unknown-index); `NSE_CONSTITUENTS_BASE_URL` (overridable via `BRUTEX_NSE_CONSTITUENTS_BASE_URL`); PURE `parse_symbols(csv_text)` (reads the `Symbol` column from the NSE CSV cols `Company Name, Industry, Symbol, Series, ISIN Code`, upper-cases, de-dups preserving order, survives `&`-bearing symbols like `M&M`/`GVT&D` + trailing blank lines); PURE `constituent_url(index_symbol)` (index→URL, None for unknown); `fetch_constituent_symbols(index, *, opener=None)` (resolve→fetch via injected opener→parse; default = real urllib opener with a browser UA + Accept headers + 10s timeout, `# pragma: no cover` live-only); `members_in_universe(index, fno_symbols, *, opener=None)` (intersect fetched constituents with the F&O-eligible stock symbols we hold, case-insensitive, INDEX order preserved, HELD casing returned). (2) NEW route `GET /api/v1/universe/index-constituents?symbol=…` in `dashboard/app.py` — resolves the index → reuses the COMMON `list_underlyings(kind="stock")` classifier to get our held F&O stock symbols → intersects → returns `{members, source, note}` where `source ∈ {"nse","unknown-index","unavailable"}`. On ANY fetch error (`OSError` — the urllib block/timeout superclass) it returns 200 `source:"unavailable"` with a note pointing at "Pull ALL F&O stocks" — **NEVER 500**. (3) UI in `templates/universe.html` — a "⊕ tick its constituents" button (enabled only when an INDEX row is selected); on click it GETs the route, on `source:"nse"` switches to the Stocks tab + ticks the returned members in the existing `selMulti` multi-select (reuses #444's `selMulti`/`toggleMulti`/`renderInstruments`), ready for "⤓ Pull N selected"; on `unknown-index`/`unavailable`/none-eligible it shows the honest note pointing at button ③. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the CSV **parser** + **index→URL mapping** + **universe intersection** + **graceful fallback** are 100% line+branch unit-tested (gated in CI) with a fixture CSV + an injected fake opener — NO hardcoded constituent list (membership rebalances semi-annually per CLAUDE.md §7, so a baked-in list would silently go wrong). 🟡 the **live NSE fetch is best-effort, runs ONLY on the operator's machine, and is UNVERIFIABLE in CI** — this build environment network-blocks `nseindia.com` ("Host not in allowlist") AND NSE actively bot-blocks those endpoints; the live urllib opener is the single `# pragma: no cover` surface. 🚫 this is **NOT Dhan data** — it is a metadata helper layered on top of the universe; the index→filename map is best-effort and may drift; the one-click ③ "Pull ALL F&O stocks" remains the superset fallback for any index whose constituents can't be fetched. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_nse_constituents.py` (NEW, 32 tests, 100% line+branch on the module sans the pragma'd opener — parser edges incl. `&`/blank/dup/whitespace-header, `constituent_url` known+unknown+alias, `fetch_constituent_symbols` success via fake opener + unknown→[] + error-propagation, `members_in_universe` case-insensitive/order-preserved/non-members-dropped/blank-skip/dup-casing); `tests/integration/test_dashboard_universe_constituents.py` (NEW, 3 route tests via TestClient — fake opener→200 `source:"nse"` with members, raising opener→200 `source:"unavailable"` no-500, unknown index→200 `source:"unknown-index"`). A per-module 100% gate is wired into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12):** 35 tests green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` 0 (nse_constituents.py + app.py); `pyright` 0 errors. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-MULTISELECT-001 (#444, the `selMulti` this ticks into + the deferred follow-up this closes) · DEC-UNIVERSE-DASHBOARD-001 (the explorer + the `list_underlyings` classifier reused) · DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the F&O-eligible set) · CLAUDE.md §1 (no-hallucination) · §10 (honest limits) · §11 (COMMON) · §12.

## DEC-COMBO-EXPLAIN-001 (2026-06-04)

450. **DEC-COMBO-EXPLAIN-001 — the strategy-mask explainer: decode a winning combo's u64 mask into its matched conditions, grouped by the 9 indicator families, so a leaderboard combo reads as a RULE not an opaque number** (2026-06-04, operator: "if we pick the combo based on our criteria ... it will check what are all the indicators and strategies got matched"). **Why:** the ranking leaderboard (DEC-RANKING-001 #447 / DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001 #448) surfaces the top combo as a u64 mask + score, but a mask number is not human-readable — the operator (rightly) wants to SEE which indicators/conditions a winning combo required. The brute-force premise IS explainability (CLAUDE.md §1, no black box): a combo *is* its set of required conditions. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/vocabulary/describe.py` (decode-only, no eval, no I/O): (a) `GROUP_RANGES` — the 9 indicator families (EMA Position, Pivot Proximity, PDH/PDL, Fibonacci, Candle Shape, Prior Bar Pattern, Day Structure, Time of Day, Day Type) mapped to their canonical contiguous bit ranges — the ONE place the family↔bit-range correspondence lives (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON), validated against the 52-bit `BIT_TO_NAME` vocabulary at import (`_check_group_invariants`: a clean `0..51` partition); (b) `describe_mask(mask) -> list[MaskGroup]` — decodes a mask into matched conditions grouped by family (only non-empty families, canonical order), so a combo reads as "EMA Position: close_above_ema20, ema20_above_ema200 · Fibonacci: near_fib_618 · Candle Shape: bar_bullish · Time of Day: early_morning"; (c) `matched_condition_names(mask) -> list[str]` — the flat matched-condition list in ascending bit order; (d) the `MaskGroup` frozen dataclass. Reserved bits `52..63` are ignored (forward-compatible — a wider future vocab never raises here). O(1) per mask (a bounded 52-bit scan, independent of bar count). Re-exported from `brutex.vocabulary`. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_vocabulary_describe.py` at **100% line+branch** on `brutex.vocabulary.describe` (18 stmts / 4 branches, 7 tests — multi-group decode, empty mask, reserved-bit ignore, name ordering, the partition-invariant raise); a per-module strict-100 gate (`19b2`) added to `ci.yml`; the existing `test_vocabulary.py` suite stays green (81 total); `mypy --strict` 0 (170 files); `pyright` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ every winning combo now decodes to its exact matched conditions grouped by strategy family — the "what indicators/strategies matched" answer, REAL + 100% gated. 🟡 it decodes the CURRENT 52-condition / 9-group vocabulary; expanding to MANY more indicators is a separate, larger change — the vocabulary is DYNAMIC by design (CLAUDE.md §11), but two honest limits apply: (i) the single-word mask is a **u64 = 64-condition ceiling** (a wider bitset is needed beyond that), and (ii) full brute-force is **K-of-N bounded, NOT 2^N** (you cannot enumerate every subset of hundreds of conditions — the winner is a precise FEW that align). 🚫 decode-only — it does NOT change ranking or evaluation. **Builds on:** DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001 (#448) + DEC-RANKING-001 (#447, the leaderboard this explains) · DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the shared 52-vocab `bits.py`/`BIT_TO_NAME` this decodes) · CLAUDE.md §1 (no black box) · §11 COMMON · §12.

## DEC-UNIVERSE-RENDER-O1-001 (2026-06-04)

451. **DEC-UNIVERSE-RENDER-O1-001 — /universe O(1)-per-interaction render: stop rebuilding all ~243 instrument rows on every click + kill the 7-second entrance-animation cascade** (2026-06-04, operator: *"why ... slow ... click the checkbox multiple times ... again and again loading"*). **Root cause (verified, not assumed):** `.inst { animation: fadeInUp .4s }` (universe.html:73) + `animationDelay = ix * 0.03s` (renderInstruments) → for 243 rows the last row's delay is **7.29 s**, and `animation … both` fill-mode keeps un-started rows at `opacity:0` (invisible, **unclickable**). `selectInstrument` (every row click) AND select-all/clear all called `renderInstruments()` — a full `innerHTML` rebuild that **restarted the 7-second cascade**, so clicks landed on opacity-0 / being-replaced nodes ("click multiple times") and the page looked like it was "loading again and again". **What shipped (frontend O(1)/O(visible) per interaction, CLAUDE.md §5):** (1) the entrance animation plays **ONCE per fresh load** via a `listAnimated` flag (reset only inside `loadInstruments`); every re-render sets `animation:none`; the stagger is capped at `min(ix,12)*0.03s` (< 0.4 s even for a full load). (2) `selectInstrument` swaps the `.sel` class on just the previously- and newly-selected rows (found via a new `data-symbol` attribute) — **no DOM rebuild**. (3) select-all / clear toggle the **visible** `.msel` checkboxes in place — no rebuild. The only remaining `renderInstruments()` calls are the initial load + the search-filter (necessary; now animation-free). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_perf.py` (NEW) pins all five fixes via rendered-template substring guards (the established dashboard-JS test pattern — the JS has no headless-DOM harness); the #355 sticky bar, #358 `tickconstbtn`, #359 `derivebtn` controls + the 6 existing `test_dashboard_universe_ux.py` tests stay green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the render hot paths are now O(1) (select) / O(visible) (select-all) per interaction and CI-guarded; the animation cannot re-cascade. 🟡 these are **template substring guards**, not a headless-DOM behavioural test (same pattern + limitation as `test_dashboard_universe_ux.py`) — they lock the markup/wiring, not a rendered click. 🚫 does NOT touch the engine, the adapter, or any data path — pure dashboard-render change. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-MULTISELECT-001 (#444, the `selMulti`/`renderInstruments` this optimises) · DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 (#358) · DEC-TF-MATERIALIZE-001 (#359) · CLAUDE.md §5 (O(1) discipline).

## DEC-DASHBOARD-PULL-ASYNC-001 (2026-06-04)

452. **DEC-DASHBOARD-PULL-ASYNC-001 — the single-symbol `/universe` pull no longer FREEZES the whole dashboard: offload the blocking pull off the asyncio event loop** (2026-06-04, operator: *"dashboard is slow ... webpage is slow loading slow when pull happens other webpages is fucking slow"*). **Root cause (verified from the operator's own logs, not assumed):** `POST /api/v1/universe/pull` is an `async def` route that called the blocking `pull_candles(...)` — a 20–30 s Dhan-rate-limited ingest — **directly on the event loop**. While it ran, EVERY other request queued behind the frozen loop: the logs show `GET /api/v1/db/tables latency_ms=32796` DURING a 32 s NIFTY pull (the read sat blocked for the pull's entire duration). The bulk routes (`pull-all` / `pull-options`) were already backgrounded via `BackgroundPullJob`; only this single-symbol route blocked. This is distinct from DEC-UNIVERSE-RENDER-O1-001 (#451), which fixed the *frontend* row-render thrash — this is the *backend* event-loop block. **What shipped:** wrap the `pull_candles(...)` call in `await run_in_threadpool(...)` — the SAME pattern 10+ other routes here already use (`/db`, `/coverage`, `/summary`, `/instruments`) — so the blocking pull runs on a worker thread and the event loop stays free to serve concurrent requests. **The pull's own duration is unchanged** (it is bound by Dhan's adaptive 5→3 r/s rate-limit + 10 s timeouts — a vendor limit, not our code), but it NO LONGER blocks the rest of the dashboard. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** the 16 existing dashboard pull-route tests stay green (the route contract is unchanged — it still awaits + returns the report); `ruff` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on `app.py`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the event-loop block is removed — other pages stay responsive DURING a pull, mirroring the proven `run_in_threadpool` pattern. 🟡 a single-symbol pull is still SYNCHRONOUS from the caller's POV (the POST still awaits the full pull); promoting it to a background job like the bulk pulls is a larger follow-up — but it no longer freezes other pages, which was the actual complaint. 🚫 does NOT change the pull's vendor-bound duration (Dhan rate-limit) or touch the engine/adapter logic. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-LIVE-001 (the `BackgroundPullJob` the bulk routes already use) · DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the `run_in_threadpool` read pattern this mirrors) · DEC-UNIVERSE-RENDER-O1-001 (#451, the sibling frontend-render fix) · CLAUDE.md §5 (O(1)/latency discipline) · §11.

## DEC-AUTOMERGE-ALLGREEN-001 (2026-06-04)

454. **DEC-AUTOMERGE-ALLGREEN-001 — no green = no merge: auto-merge now REFUSES if ANY check is failing + requires EVERY `CI OK (aggregate gate)` run to be success** (2026-06-04, operator decree: *"without green it should never ever be merged"*). **Root cause (the #366 merge hole):** a PR head carries TWO `CI OK (aggregate gate)` runs — a `push`-event run (which SKIPS the PR-only gates: bug-fix-regression, zplus, dec-id, no-hallucination, conv-commits → reports CI OK=success) AND a `pull_request`-event run (which RUNS them → can be FAILURE). The old `auto-merge.yml` ci-check did `<conclusions> | head -1` and merged on whichever it picked — so #366 auto-merged on the green push run while its pull_request run was RED (bug-fix-regression failed: a `fix:` PR with no `tests/` change). **What shipped:** `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` ci-check now reads EVERY check run on the PR's CURRENT head and (1) REFUSES the merge if ANY check conclusion is `failure`/`cancelled`/`timed_out`/`action_required`/`stale` (excluding the auto-merge workflow's own check), AND (2) requires the `CI OK (aggregate gate)` check to EXIST and EVERY instance of it to be `success` (a green push run can no longer mask a red pull_request run). The mergeability gate (DEC-AUTOMERGE-SAFETY-001) + the push-event acceptance / head re-resolution (DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-FIX-001) are untouched. **Also (closing the specific #366 gap):** added `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_async.py` — the regression test #366 merged WITHOUT (it pins that the single-symbol pull route offloads `pull_candles` via `run_in_threadpool`, never a direct call on the event loop). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/redteam/test_redteam_automerge_safety.py` (9, incl. the NEW `test_ci_check_requires_all_green_not_head_1` guard: no `head -1`, blocks on any failing conclusion, requires every CI OK success) + `test_dashboard_pull_async.py` (1) green; `auto-merge.yml` is valid YAML; `ruff` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a red check (required OR advisory) can no longer be auto-merged past — the exact #366 hole is closed + guarded; the async fix now has its regression test. 🟡 this hardens the AUTO-MERGE bot (the lever this repo actually uses); server-side branch-protection required-checks (G2) remain a separate admin step (per the DEC-AUTOMERGE-SAFETY-001 honest envelope). 🚫 does NOT change which jobs RUN — only that ANY red one now blocks the bot's merge. **Builds on:** DEC-AUTOMERGE-SAFETY-001 (G1 mergeability) · DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-FIX-001 (head re-resolution) · DEC-DASHBOARD-PULL-ASYNC-001 (#452, the fix whose test gap this closes) · CLAUDE.md §10 · §13 (merge-readiness charter — never merge over a red gate).

## DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 (2026-06-04)

456. **DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 — Stage-3 out-of-sample validation (first slice): split history at an IST day boundary into train (past) + test (unseen future), measure the SAME combo on both, and report whether it still clears the hard gates** (2026-06-04, operator: *"is this really achievable ... I need real guarantee and assurance ... no illusion ... even a single mismatch will defeat the system"*). **Why:** the sweep + ranking (DEC-RANKING-001 #447 / DEC-LEADERBOARD-EXPLAIN-001 #453) FIND a top combo on the full history, but an in-sample winner can be a **data-mining fluke** (the #1 risk). This is the first slice of the real-vs-illusion decider — re-measure the GIVEN combo on a held-out test period it never saw. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/engine/validation.py` (pure, no I/O): (a) `validate_out_of_sample(bars, mask, *, direction, tf_minutes, ..., train_frac=0.7) -> OOSValidation` — returns train + test `ResultMetrics`, the IST trading-day split, and `held_up` (the combo still clears the 5 hard rejection gates on the test period); (b) the `OOSValidation` frozen dataclass; (c) `_day_split` — the IST-day-boundary split primitive (train strictly before test; both periods keep ≥1 whole day; rejects `train_frac` ∉ (0,1) and <2 distinct days). **The careful, no-look-ahead design (the safety-critical part — Golden Rule #2/#5):** `bar_bits` is built ONCE over the FULL stream so every bar's prior-day anchors (pivots/Fib/PDH-PDL) come from its real prior IST day — including the test period's first day (whose prior is the last train day). The split is then applied to the *trade simulation* at an IST DAY BOUNDARY, so the test period opens on a fresh day — matching `build_bar_bits`'s per-day running-extreme reset. Building `bar_bits` per-segment instead would CLEAR the test period's first-day anchors (a subtle correctness leak this avoids). Reuses the shared `metrics_for_mask` core (**promoted private `_metrics_for_mask` → public this PR** — now shared by `evaluate_combo` + `sweep_masks` + the OOS validator, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) + the ranking `passes_gates`; it does NOT re-fit anything. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_validation.py` — the `brutex.engine` package gate reaches **100.00%** incl. `validation.py` (42 stmts / 10 branches; 231 tests across the engine suite), covering the `train_frac` range guard, the <2-day guard, the day-boundary split + clamping (both directions), the empty guard, the train/test split + `held_up` wiring, the no-trade combo (0 test trades → not held up), and determinism (same inputs → bit-identical, Golden Rule #7); `mypy --strict` 0 (172 files); `pyright` 0 (the public rename removes the private-usage warning); `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a GIVEN combo can now be measured on an unseen held-out period — the first real out-of-sample check, 100% gated, no look-ahead. 🟡 `held_up` is the BASIC OOS gate (test still clears the 5 hard gates); the fuller lockbox tolerance (test Sharpe within 30% of train, drawdown within 50% — `brutex.metrics.lockbox`) + CPCV pass-rate + DSR are the next refinements (the modules exist; wiring them is the next increment). The combo is GIVEN — the caller must select it on the TRAIN period only for the OOS verdict to be valid; the full train/test orchestration is the cascade's job. 🚫 it does NOT run on real data (the lake is empty — no Dhan creds); it validates whatever bars it is given. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001 (#445, the `metrics_for_mask` core this slices) · DEC-RANKING-001 (#447, `passes_gates`) · DEC-LEADERBOARD-EXPLAIN-001 (#453, the leaderboard whose top combo this validates) · DEC-STAT-LOCKBOX-MC-001 / DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001 (the fuller Stage-3/4 validators this is the holdout primitive for) · CLAUDE.md §2 (no look-ahead) · §10 · §11 COMMON · §12.

## DEC-OOS-LOCKBOX-TOLERANCE-001 (2026-06-04)

458. **DEC-OOS-LOCKBOX-TOLERANCE-001 — enrich the OOS verdict: `held_up` now ANDs the hard gates with the DEC-LOCK-001 Sharpe (30%) + drawdown (50%) degradation tolerances, applied at the OOS `ResultMetrics` level** (2026-06-04, operator: *"go ahead with the plan ... real guarantee and assurance ... no illusion"*). **Why:** DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 (#456) shipped the train/test holdout but its `held_up` was the BASIC gate (test still clears the 5 hard rejection gates). The institutional out-of-sample check (López de Prado / Bailey, DEC-LOCK-001) additionally requires the out-of-sample Sharpe + drawdown not to DEGRADE too far from training — the difference between *"still trades OK on unseen data"* and *"still performs comparably on unseen data."* **What shipped (`brutex/engine/validation.py`):** (a) `_sharpe_held(train, test)` — test Sharpe within 30% of a POSITIVE train Sharpe (`>= train_sharpe*(1-0.30)`); ``False`` if train had no positive in-sample Sharpe (no edge to hold) or the test Sharpe is undefined; (b) `_drawdown_held(train, test)` — test `max_drawdown_pct <= train*(1+0.50)`; (c) `OOSValidation` gains `gates_held` / `sharpe_held` / `drawdown_held` booleans (exposed like `LockboxResult`'s individual gates, so a failure is attributable), and `held_up = gates_held AND sharpe_held AND drawdown_held` — the full verdict. **Unit-safety (the careful part — Golden Rule #2):** the 30%/50% tolerances are applied to the train + test `ResultMetrics`, both produced by the IDENTICAL `compute_metrics` convention (same Sharpe formula, same `max_drawdown_pct` units) → directly comparable, NO unit mismatch. The tolerance VALUES mirror `brutex.metrics.lockbox`'s DEC-LOCK-001 spec constants (cited in-code); `lockbox` remains the trade-returns-level gate (500-trade floor, return-unit drawdown, window extension) for the Stage-4 cascade — this applies the SAME criteria at the metrics level for the OOS holdout. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_validation.py` — the `brutex.engine` package gate reaches **100.00%** incl. `validation.py` (60 stmts / 12 branches; 238 tests across the engine suite); NEW direct tests for `_sharpe_held` (None train, ≤0 train, None test, within-tolerance, below-tolerance) + `_drawdown_held` (within, worse) + the enriched `held_up` wiring; `mypy --strict` 0 (172 files); `pyright` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the OOS verdict now matches the institutional degradation criteria (gates + Sharpe-within-30% + drawdown-within-50%), attributable per-component, 100% gated. 🟡 still the metrics-level holdout — the trade-returns-level lockbox MODULE (500-trade floor) + CPCV pass-rate + DSR (the deflated-Sharpe multiple-testing penalty) remain the next refinements; the combo is GIVEN (caller selects on train only). 🚫 still NOT run on real data (lake empty — no Dhan creds). **Builds on:** DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 (#456, the holdout this enriches) · DEC-STAT-LOCKBOX-MC-001 (the DEC-LOCK-001 30%/50% tolerances mirrored here) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, the consistent `compute_metrics` Sharpe/MDD) · CLAUDE.md §2 (units/correctness) · §10 · §11 COMMON · §12.
## DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 (2026-06-04)

459. **DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 — in-run transient-window auto-retry + per-window failure visibility: a seconds-long network drop mid-pull now self-heals WITHIN the run** (2026-06-04, operator in Kumbakonam: *"sometimes in a day for seconds network is dropping and by that time our internet data pull from dhan will be interrupted right so this will also be taken care by our window finder right ... we never ever skipped it right"*). **Why:** the operator's region has intermittent seconds-long connectivity drops. The existing chain already made this SAFE — a transient drop wraps to a retryable `DhanTransportError`/`DhanTimeoutError` (`client.py:307-312`), the client fast-retries 3× in-call (`client.py:271-290`), and a window that still fails returns `_WindowOutcome(transient=1)` WITHOUT `mark_complete`, so it is NEVER skipped and is re-pulled on the NEXT pull (the no-skip guarantee: a window is recorded complete ONLY on a clean fetch+write). The gap: a transiently-failed window was deferred to the next pull, not re-attempted within the SAME run, and the bare `transient_failures=N` count hid WHICH window failed. **What shipped (ingest path only — `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py` + `run_ingest.py`):** (a) `_WindowOutcome` carries the window identity (`window`, `error_type`) on a transient outcome; (b) `ingest_spot` gains `max_retry_passes` (default **2**) + an injectable `retry_backoff` and, after the first fan-out pass, re-runs ONLY the windows that failed transiently as their own bounded passes (sorted worklists → deterministic report regardless of worker-completion order, Rule #4), with a seconds-scale exponential backoff (1s→2s, clamped 8s) between passes so a multi-second outage recovers; (c) a per-window `ingest.window.transient` WARNING (exact window + `error_type` + `in_run_retry`) — the visibility the count hid — plus an `ingest.retry_pass` INFO; (d) new `IngestReport` fields `retried_windows` + `still_failed_windows` (rolled up in `DhanIngestReport` + the per-instrument `ingest.underlying` INFO). **A 429 is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the in-run retry** (`window=None`) — mirroring `client._should_fast_retry`: the adaptive rate controller's step-down + the token bucket own 429 backoff (DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001), so retrying a 429 here would fight the limiter; a 429 window is still counted transient + deferred to the next pull (by when the stepped-down rate lets it through). Windows still failing after the budget stay UNMARKED (deferred — the guarantee is preserved). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_dhan_ingest.py` → `brutex.adapters.dhan.ingest` **100.00%** (137 stmts / 30 branch, 0 miss; 30 tests incl. drop→retry→succeed, drop-persists-left-unmarked, `max_retry_passes=0` disables retry, 429-not-retried-in-run, the WARNING/retry_pass logs, per-pass backoff, the bounded-exponential default); `run_ingest.py` back to **100.00%**; the 226-test ingest+pull slice green (the default-on retry did not regress the dashboard pull path); `mypy --strict` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a seconds-long network drop now self-heals within the same pull (bounded retry), each failed window is individually logged, and the no-skip guarantee is preserved + tested — a window is marked complete ONLY on a clean fetch, never on retry exhaustion. 🟡 a window still failing after `max_retry_passes` is deferred to the NEXT pull (unchanged guarantee) — the dashboard "incomplete windows / fill gaps" view + the hash-chained per-window audit + the lake-backfill of the skip-ledger are the NEXT two increments (designed, not yet shipped). 🚫 does NOT change the client's in-call retry, the rate limits, or the keep-first/idempotent sink; does NOT touch the engine. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 (the client's in-call fast-retry this layers above) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip-ledger whose no-skip guarantee this preserves) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the 429 controller this defers to) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 (the fan-out this re-runs) · DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 (keep-first makes a re-fetch safe) · CLAUDE.md §2 (Rule #4 determinism / Rule #7 idempotence) · §10 · §11 COMMON.
