534. **DEC-DHAN-SPOT-MULTI-SATURATE-001 — multi-select "Pull spot" now SATURATES the 5 r/s ceiling (route the ticked selection through the bulk cross-symbol flatten, not a serial per-symbol loop)** (2026-06-06, operator: "our aim is always 5 RPS … any cases single or multiple, spot or options"). **Root cause (deep audit, code-traced across every pull path):** the dashboard multi-select "⤓ Pull spot" fired `POST /universe/pull?symbol=X` SERIALLY — one `await runPull` per ticked row (`universe.html`) — so only ONE symbol's ~2-3 window jobs were ever in flight against the 15-worker fan-out pool → the shared `DhanRateController` token bucket sat idle between symbols → measured ~3 r/s, NOT the permitted 5. The limiter itself was correct (started at 5, never stepped down — zero `rate.429` in the operator's log); the path was demand-STARVED, not throttled. The audit confirmed "Pull ALL" spot + ALL options pulls already saturate (server-side flatten); single-symbol + multi-select spot were the only starved paths. **Fix (3 files + tests):** (1) `pull_controller.pull_all_spot` gains optional `from_date` / `to_date` / `year` (default `None` → full Track-1 history, so the `?kind=` "Pull ALL" callers are byte-for-byte UNCHANGED) so its saturating cross-symbol `(symbol, interval, window)` flatten can run over the operator's date-picker range without silently widening it; (2) `POST /universe/pull-all` generalised to accept `?symbols=` (+ `?symbol=`, `from_date`/`to_date`/`year`) with precedence symbols > symbol > kind — mirroring the existing `pull-options` multi endpoint — routing every form to `pull_all_spot` on the single-flight background job with the shared `_session_rate`; (3) `universe.html` multi-select "Pull spot" now fires ONE `startAndPoll('/universe/pull-all?symbols=…&from_date=&to_date=')` (mirroring options-multi) instead of the serial loop; the single-highlight pull keeps the synchronous live-animated `/universe/pull` path. The aggregate stays ≤ 5 r/s (one shared thread-safe `SessionRateController`; Rule #6) and zero-data-loss is unchanged (coverage marks a window complete ONLY on bars-arrived; failed windows re-pull next run; bounded client + window retry). **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py::TestPullAllSpot` gains `test_explicit_range_is_honoured`, `test_explicit_year_is_honoured`, `test_no_range_defaults_to_full_history` (the range threads through; the full-history default is preserved). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the range logic reuses the already-tested `resolve_candle_range`. 🟡 pytest/mypy could NOT run in this Python-3.11 sandbox (repo requires 3.12 — `orchestrator/retry.py` uses PEP 695 generics); CI on 3.12 executes the new tests + the dashboard HTTP suite. 🟡 5 r/s is now ATTAINABLE (bucket-bound, not demand-starved) for multi-select; a SINGLE-symbol pull over a SHORT range is still inherently tiny (finishes in < 1 s — too few windows to sustain 5 r/s for long). **Tracked next installments:** Fix B = single-symbol window-level fan-out; Fix C = options `SessionRateController` persistence (options saturate WITHIN a pull today but re-start at the ceiling each pull). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the cross-symbol fan-out pool) · DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 (the shared session controller) · DEC-UNIVERSE-OPTIONS-MULTIPULL-001 (the `?symbols=` pattern mirrored) · DEC-DHAN-PULL-SCOPE-001 · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 / §11 COMMON.

535. **DEC-PREOPEN-SPACE-SYMBOL-001 — pre-open report no longer 500s on a space-containing symbol (admit the space in the candle-symbol allowlist + per-symbol resilience belt)** (2026-06-06, operator `make run` + screenshot: `GET /api/v1/reports/preopen.zip` → HTTP 500). **Root cause (code-traced):** the candle-symbol allowlist `_SYMBOL_RE` (`brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`) admitted `[A-Za-z0-9_.&-]` but NOT a space, so `_validate_candle_coords` raised `illegal candle symbol 'INDIA VIX'` — and `build_preopen_rows` looped symbols with NO per-symbol guard, so that ONE reference index sank the entire ~782-symbol export. The same rule would also 500 every other stored space symbol (`NIFTY 50`, `NIFTY TOTAL MKT`, `NIFTY MIDCAP 150`). **Fix (2 src + tests):** (1) **admit a literal space** in `_SYMBOL_RE` — the SAME safety class as `&` (DEC-PREOPEN-AMPERSAND-001): the symbol is joined via `pathlib` into `<lake>/bars/<exch>/<seg>/<symbol>/<interval>` and passed to `read_parquet(?)` as a **bound parameter** (verified `db_view.py:716,780`), so a space is an inert literal path component — not a DuckDB-glob metachar (`* ? [ ] {}`), not a SQL-injection vector, `..` still rejected. So `INDIA VIX` (which HAS real 1-day candles) is now queryable end-to-end and **no stored data is dropped** (operator decree: never miss data). (2) **resilience belt** — `build_preopen_rows` wraps the per-symbol `_daily_*` reads in `try/except (ValueError, duckdb.Error)` → log `preopen.symbol.skipped` + `continue`, honouring the repo's documented "never a 500" contract (`db_view._aggregate_parquet_resilient`), so no single symbol can ever sink the export again. **Tests** (`tests/unit/test_preopen_report.py`): `test_build_and_render_space_symbol` (INDIA VIX resolves → builds → renders, the 500 regression oracle, mirroring the existing M&M ampersand test) + `test_build_preopen_rows_resilient_to_one_bad_symbol` (a glob-metachar symbol is skipped, the good symbol still builds). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the 3 preopen tests pass in-sandbox (this dashboard path avoids the 3.12-only `retry.py`); the space-safety argument is bound-parameter-verified. ✅ data-preserving — INDIA VIX + the NIFTY space indexes now appear in the report with accurate numbers; the operator deselects what they don't want (NOT silently excluded). 🟡 the report remains 1-day-sourced (DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-1DAY-001); a 1-minute-basis variant is a separate tracked requirement (DEC-PREOPEN-MINUTE-BASIS-001, pending operator confirmation). **Builds on:** DEC-PREOPEN-AMPERSAND-001 (the `&` precedent this mirrors) · DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 / DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-1DAY-001 · CLAUDE.md §3 / §11 COMMON.

536. **DEC-PREOPEN-MINUTE-BASIS-001 — pre-open report gains a `1-day | minute` BASIS toggle (IMPLEMENTED)** (2026-06-06, operator: "pull the report with one more pre-open … based on 1 day or 1 minute"; confirmed via a 2-question spec lock). The pre-open report was 1-day-sourced (DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-1DAY-001); this adds an OPT-IN **minute basis**: **IEP = the 09:15:00 1-minute bar's OPEN**; **PREV. CLOSE = the previous trading day's LAST 1-minute close** — matching the engine's own prev-close convention (DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001) and the page's existing "09:15 opening price" wording. **Operator-chosen UI:** a `1-day | minute` toggle on `/reports`; the `.zip` / `.xlsx` / `symbols` endpoints take `?basis=day|minute` (default `day`, so the existing behaviour + the `?kind=`/`?symbols=` callers are byte-for-byte unchanged). **Implementation (3 src + 3 test files):** (1) `db_view._intraday_open_by_date` — new helper reading the 09:15 session-open 1-minute OPEN per day (`arg_min(open, timestamp)` grouped by date, bound-param `read_parquet`, mirroring `_intraday_last_close_by_date`); (2) `preopen_report`: `ReportBasis = Literal["day","minute"]`, `resolve_report_datasets(..., basis=)` qualifies on the basis's partition (1day vs 1minute), `build_preopen_rows(..., basis=)` branches the day-basis (`_daily_open` + `_prev_close_asof`) vs minute-basis (`_intraday_open_by_date` + `_prev_trading_close(_intraday_last_close_by_date)`) helpers — both kept on ONE price scale (never mixed); (3) `app.py` 3 endpoints take `?basis=` via a shared `_report_basis_literal` (400 on bad value); (4) `reports.html` adds the `1-day | minute` radio toggle threaded into the `.zip` download. The 1-day default stays (it avoids the TMPV-style adjustment mismatch DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-1DAY-001 documented); both bases pull from the lake the report already reads (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, no new fetch). **Tests:** `test_preopen_report.py` (minute-basis row 09:15-open + prior last-min close, basis partition gate, empty-minute-partition) + `test_dashboard_reports_routes.py` (`?basis=minute` 200, bad-basis 400, picker echoes basis, page has the toggle). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; 47 preopen unit tests pass in-sandbox (this path avoids the 3.12-only `retry.py`); the minute helpers reuse the proven bound-param read pattern. 🟡 the dashboard HTTP route tests need httpx + 3.12 → CI is the oracle for those. **Builds on:** DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 / DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-1DAY-001 · DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001 (the minute prev-close convention) · DEC-PREOPEN-SPACE-SYMBOL-001 (#535) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON.

537. **DEC-DHAN-OPTION-PERSIST-RATE-001 — options pulls share the dashboard `SessionRateController` (stop re-storming Dhan at 5 r/s every options pull)** (2026-06-06, autonomous follow-up to the deep 5-RPS audit; operator "always 5 RPS … any cases … spot or options"). **Gap (audit-found):** `option_pull_controller.pull_options` had NO `session_rate` param and built a FRESH `DhanRateController` every call via `_build_live_option_controller()` — so each options pull restarted at the 5 r/s ceiling and re-learnt any step-down from scratch (the exact "re-storm Dhan at the start of every pull" problem DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 already fixed for spot), and a learned spot step-down did NOT carry into options or vice-versa. Not a >5 r/s breach (the background pull job is single-flight, so spot + options never run concurrently) — a rate-persistence gap. **Fix (3 src + 1 test, mirrors the spot pattern exactly):** (1) `_live_option_runtime(use_live_rate, session_rate=None)` resolves `session_rate.get()` (the SAME `DhanRateController` the spot pulls share) when given, else builds fresh (the prior CLI/injected behaviour); (2) `pull_options(..., session_rate=None)` threads it; (3) `app.py` options endpoint passes the app's single `_session_rate` (built once at `app.py:649`, already shared by spot). The single shared thread-safe `SessionRateController`/`DhanRateController` keeps the AGGREGATE spot+options issue rate ≤ 5 r/s (Rule #6) and the learned rate now persists across BOTH surfaces. **Test:** `test_option_pull_controller.py::TestLiveOptionRuntime::test_dry_run_ignores_session_rate` (the param is accepted + threaded; a dry-run stays the all-None feedback-free runtime). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the change is a contained mirror of the already-shipped spot DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001. 🟡 the actual controller-sharing is in the live `# pragma: no cover` branch (real token + network), exactly like the spot equivalent — CI (3.12) + the dry-run path cover the wiring; the live sharing is the proven spot mechanism. 🟡 pytest could not run in this 3.11 sandbox (`retry.py` PEP 695). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 (the spot session controller this extends) · DEC-DHAN-SPOT-MULTI-SATURATE-001 (#534) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 / §11 COMMON.

538. **DEC-PHASE2-TRUTH-TABLE-001 — Phase 2 golden corpus #7: the 52-condition truth table is now a real, ≥200-row, evaluator-backed golden artifact (was a dead 5-row skeleton with no consumer test)** (2026-06-06, operator: "Phase 2 — real golden fixtures + truth table"; AskUserQuestion track selection). **Gap:** `tests/golden/condition_truth_table.csv` shipped at Phase 1 as a 5-row skeleton (DEC-PHASE1-WEEK2-SCAFFOLDING-001, #252) that NOTHING read — a CSV no test consumes proves nothing. `docs/TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md` Week 2 specified "expands to ≥ 200 rows"; corpus #7 in `tests/golden/fixtures/README.md` ("52-condition truth table / per-condition determinism G9") was 📋 ROADMAP. **Fix (1 generator + 1 golden test + the regenerated CSV + README/ledger):** (1) `scripts/gen_condition_truth_table.py` — a DETERMINISTIC generator that projects the frozen `fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json` `input → u64` oracle (the 400-case corpus locked by `test_vocab_golden.py`, `generated_from = brutex.vocabulary.evaluator.evaluate_atoms`) into the flat `(snippet_id, condition_name, bit_position, expected_bool, description)` table. A greedy both-ways set-cover selects the fewest golden cases whose union SETS and CLEARS every one of the 52 bits (the G9 guarantee), padded in case-id order to ≥ `MIN_ROWS` (200) — currently **1,144 rows** (22 cases × 52). Every `expected_bool` is DECODED from the proven `expected_u64` (Golden Rule #1 — zero hand-authored values); the bit↔name map is read from the ONE source of truth `brutex/vocabulary/bits.py`, loaded STANDALONE via importlib so the generator runs WITHOUT the Rust `trading_core` wheel. (2) `tests/golden/test_condition_truth_table.py` — the golden gate (9 tests, evaluator-free so it runs even where the wheel is absent): structure (canonical header, ≥200 rows, no dup `(snippet,condition)`, strict `true`/`false`), registry agreement (`bit_position == NAME_TO_BIT[name]`), oracle-decode match (`expected_bool == bit of the referenced case's frozen u64` — so the table cannot drift from the oracle), G9 both-ways coverage (all 52 fire AND clear), and no-drift (byte-identical to a fresh `generate()` + pinned SHA-256 manifest `9d796bd…fc84d`). (3) `tests/golden/fixtures/README.md` corpus #7 → ✅ landed. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ runs fully IN-SANDBOX — the 9 tests pass + the generator regenerates byte-identically + ruff/ruff-format/mypy(per-file) all clean locally (this path is evaluator-free, so the usual 3.12-only `retry.py`/`trading_core` sandbox limit does NOT apply here — a rare fully-locally-proven change). 🟡 the live `evaluate_atoms == expected_u64` link is locked by `test_vocab_golden.py` (CI, real wheel); this CSV is transitively a golden assertion against the real evaluator. Scope: ONLY corpus #7 — the remaining Phase 2 corpora #1–5/#8/#9 (ingest round-trip, resample, paisa accounting, combo-hash) still depend on the Phase 2 ingest pipeline and stay 📋 ROADMAP. **Builds on:** DEC-PHASE1-WEEK2-SCAFFOLDING-001 (#252, the 5-row skeleton this replaces) · DEC-PHASE1-SMOKE-AND-SKELETONS-001 (#251) · DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the vocab_golden_vectors oracle) · `docs/TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md` Phase 2 / `TRACK1_VERIFICATION_PYRAMID.md` G9 · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON.

539. **DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-FLAKE-001 — de-flake the responsive-under-write timing gate (widen the read budget 0.2 s → 0.5 s + the writer hold 1 s → 2 s; the old absolute 0.2 s ceiling spuriously failed on loaded CI runners + blocked a merge)** (2026-06-06, autonomous follow-up: a 4.8 ms scheduling spike — `0.20476 s` vs the `< 0.2 s` budget — failed `test_cache_served_coverage_spot_responsive_under_write` in PR #446's push-event CI run while the authoritative pull_request run passed; the stale red pinned `mergeable_state=unstable` + stalled auto-merge). **Root cause:** `tests/integration/test_dashboard_responsive_under_write.py` (DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001) proves a cache/in-memory read does NOT serialise behind the writer's store lock by asserting `elapsed < _READ_BUDGET_S` while a background thread holds the lock for `_WRITER_HOLD_S`. The discriminating signal is "far below the hold" (healthy cache read ≈ single-digit ms; the old blocking regression waited ~the full hold), so the absolute `0.2 s` ceiling was needlessly tight — a loaded shared runner's GC/scheduling jitter can push a memory-served localhost GET just over `0.2 s` without any regression. **Fix (1 test file, threshold-only — NO product/runtime change):** `_WRITER_HOLD_S` 1.0 → **2.0 s**, `_READ_BUDGET_S` 0.2 → **0.5 s** (= hold / 4). This STRENGTHENS the gate's pass/fail separation (a true blocking regression now waits ~2.0 s = 4x OVER the 0.5 s budget — an unambiguous fail) while giving the healthy path ~25x jitter headroom (a few-ms read vs 0.5 s). Widening the hold is FREE on the passing path: `_HeldLock.__exit__` releases the lock the instant the fast read returns, so the full hold elapses ONLY on the regression path. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the change strictly RELAXES the healthy-pass condition + WIDENS regression separation, so it cannot newly-fail a healthy run — only remove the flake. 🟡 the test `importorskip`s `fastapi`/`httpx2`/`duckdb` (absent in this sandbox) so it SKIPS locally; CI (3.12, full extras) runs it — but the fix is a pure numeric threshold whose effect is provable by inspection. Scope: ONLY this one flaky timing gate; no other test or product code touched (Golden Rule #3). **Builds on:** DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the responsive-under-write oracle this hardens) · DEC-PHASE2-TRUTH-TABLE-001 (#538, the PR whose CI surfaced the flake) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON / Golden Rule #10.

540. **DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-LOG-AGG-001 — aggregate the keep-first conflict log to ONE summary per window (+ report WHICH field the vendor re-stated); stop the per-bar `ingest.conflict` WARNING flood** (2026-06-06, operator `make run` deep-check: a 33-index re-pull emitted **hundreds** of `ingest.conflict` WARNING lines on NIFTY, several showing **equal** closes — e.g. `stored_close=17526.50 vendor_close=17526.50` — which looked like false alarms). **Root cause (code-traced, `adapters/dhan/ingest.py` + `data/parquet_writer.py`):** keep-first conflict handling is CORRECT (the stored bar wins, vendor re-statement discarded, reproducibility preserved — DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 / Golden Rule #7; NOT data loss). But (a) the spine logged ONE WARNING **per conflicting bar** → a vendor re-stating a whole 90-day window floods `/logs` + drowns real warnings; and (b) each line printed only `close`, while `_bar_values_equal` compares ALL of open/high/low/close/volume/open_interest — so a bar whose **open/high/low** was revised (close unchanged) logged as a 'conflict' with two **equal** closes, looking like a bug. **Fix (1 src helper + rewired log + 5 tests):** new pure `summarize_conflicts(conflicts)` → `{conflicts, differing_fields (sorted OHLCV+OI names that ACTUALLY differ), max_close_delta, first_ts, last_ts}`; `_ingest_one_window` now emits ONE `ingest.conflict.summary` **WARNING** per window + drops the per-bar detail to `ingest.conflict` **DEBUG** (still available when chasing one bar, off by default → no flood). The aggregate count is unchanged (still flows to `IngestReport.conflicts` + `ingest.series`). **Tests** (`tests/unit/test_dhan_ingest.py::TestIngestSpotConflicts`): summary WARNING fires once with `differing_fields=close` + `max_close_delta=0.50`; a vendor OPEN re-statement with EQUAL close reports `differing_fields=open` + `max_close_delta=0` (the false-alarm root cause, now truthful); per-bar event is DEBUG; clean window emits neither event nor summary; 3 windows × 2 conflicts → 3 summaries each counting 2. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the `summarize_conflicts` algorithm verified standalone against all 3 test scenarios (close-only, open-only-equal-close, multi). 🟡 pytest + mypy could NOT run in this 3.11 sandbox (`orchestrator/parallel.py` PEP 695 generics need 3.12); CI (3.12) is the oracle for the 5 tests + types. Pure observability change — keep-first data behaviour + the stored bytes are byte-identical (Golden Rule #7 unchanged). **Queue context:** this is **Q1** of the 4-item `make run` deep-check (Q2 coverage-skip-on-repull, Q3 cold-start >5 r/s over-issue, Q4 NIFTY NEXT 50 1day DH-905 — tracked next). **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 (the keep-first contract this clarifies) · DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 (the pull-id-scoped event stream) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON / Golden Rule #10.

541. **DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-VISIBILITY-001 — surface the lake-reconcile skip count on `universe.pull_all.start` (Q2: make "already-stored windows skipped" VISIBLE)** (2026-06-06, operator `make run` deep-check Q2: a re-pull of partially-stored NIFTY re-fetched windows + conflicted, and the operator could NOT tell skipping was happening — `/coverage/windows` showed 0). **Verification verdict (code-traced — NOT a bug):** the reconcile path is CORRECT and properly COMMON-aligned — `dashboard/coverage_reconcile.py` imports `_MARKET` (`"dhan"`) AND `_windows` (the 90-day tiler) FROM `adapters/dhan/ingest.py`, so the `WindowKey` it marks is byte-identical to the key the pull's `coverage.is_complete` checks (no key-mismatch). It is deliberately CONSERVATIVE (`coverage_reconcile.py:132`): a 90-day window is marked complete ONLY if a stored span FULLY encloses it (`first_date <= window_start AND window_end <= last_date`). So the observed NIFTY re-fetch means the prior NIFTY data did NOT fully enclose those windows (partial prior coverage) → reconcile correctly re-pulled the not-proven-covered windows, and the conflicts are the vendor re-stating already-present bars (keep-first, NO data loss). Tightening the enclosure to a per-window bar-count would risk FALSE skips on gappy data — the unsafe direction (priority law: Correctness > Performance). **The one genuine gap = visibility:** `pull_all_spot` called `reconcile_coverage_with_lake(...)` but DISCARDED its return (the count of windows marked complete from the lake), so nothing logged "skipped N already-stored windows". **Fix (1 src + 1 test):** capture the count into `reconciled_windows` and stamp it on the `universe.pull_all.start` INFO event (0 on dry-run, which does no reconcile). **Test** (`test_dashboard_pull_controller.py::test_pull_all_spot_correlates_under_one_pull_id`): asserts `start["reconciled_windows"] == 0` on the dry-run path. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; pure observability — no change to the reconcile logic, the skip decision, or any data path (the conservative full-enclosure rule is UNCHANGED + verified correct). 🟡 pytest/mypy CI-only (pull_controller pulls the 3.12 orchestrator chain); the live (non-dry-run) reconcile-count path is exercised by the existing live ingest tests. **Queue context:** Q2 of the `make run` deep-check — RESOLVED (verified correct + visibility added). Remaining: Q3 (cold-start >5 r/s over-issue — rate strategy, needs operator decision), Q4 (NIFTY NEXT 50 1day DH-905 — needs a live Dhan probe). **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 / DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-WIRING-001 (the reconcile this surfaces) · DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-LOG-AGG-001 (#540, Q1) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON / Golden Rule #10.

542. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-HARD-CAP-001 — hard-cap the PHYSICAL Dhan issue rate at ≤ the current r/s (start the token bucket EMPTY on every (re)build); Q3 of the `make run` deep-check** (2026-06-06, operator decision via AskUserQuestion: "Hard-cap physical ≤5 (keep start 5)"). **Root cause (code-traced):** `AdaptiveTokenBucket.__post_init__` started the bucket FULL (`_tokens = float(burst)`, `rate_limiter.py:228`), and `DhanRateController.on_rate_limit` / `on_timeout` / recovery REBUILD the bucket on every rate change via `_make_bucket()` (`rate_control.py:212/251/284`) — each rebuild a FRESH FULL bucket. So the opening (1 burst token at t=0) AND every 5→4→3 stepdown re-granted a free burst token exactly when slowing down → the physical request rate briefly exceeded the 5 r/s ceiling (the operator's `make run` showed `effective_rps` 7.07–7.34 during the opening 429 storm before converging to ~3.5). It self-heals + loses no data (every window retried), but it DID breach "≤5 r/s" transiently. **Fix (2 src + 5 tests):** (1) `AdaptiveTokenBucket` gains a `start_empty: bool = False` knob — `_tokens = 0.0 if start_empty else float(burst)`; (2) the Dhan controller's `_make_bucket` passes `start_empty=True`, so EVERY (re)build (opening + each stepdown) starts at 0 tokens → the next paced call waits a full `1/rate` interval → the physical issue rate is strictly ≤ the current rate (≤ 5 at the ceiling) at ALL times, including the opening + every stepdown. The token-bucket steady-state throughput is otherwise UNCHANGED (refill still `rate × elapsed`, capped at `burst=1`). **Tests:** `test_orchestrator_rate_limiter.py::TestStartEmpty` (default-full first call free vs start-empty first call waits `1/5`); `test_dhan_rate_control.py` updated — `test_pace_delegates_without_error` + `test_eases_in_no_opening_burst` now assert BOTH opening calls are paced (no free opening token), and new `test_stepdown_rebuild_starts_empty_no_free_burst` asserts the 5→4 rebuild also starts empty (first post-step call waits a full `1/4`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the empty-start acquire reuses the exact refill→consume path the pre-existing `test_eases_in` already proved (2nd call waits exactly `1/CEILING_RPS`) — only the empty start shifts to the first call. 🟡 pytest/mypy CI-only (`brutex.orchestrator.__init__` pulls the 3.12-only `retry.py` PEP 695 chain); CI (3.12) runs the 5 tests + the per-module rate_control gate + the whole-package rate_limiter coverage (both `start_empty` branches hit: default everywhere, True via the controller + the direct test). **Honest scope:** the `dhan.throughput effective_rps` METER is a cumulative `(N-1)/span` average; the empty-start removes the t=0 + per-stepdown bursts that inflated it, so the reported number drops — a fully WINDOWED instantaneous meter is a separate observability follow-up if any residual inflation remains (not claimed done here). **Queue context:** Q3 of the `make run` deep-check — Q1 (#540) + Q2 (#541) merged; Q4 (NIFTY NEXT 50 1day DH-905 graceful known-gap + probe) next. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-EASE-IN-001 (the burst=1 ease-in this hardens) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 / DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 (the controller) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 / Golden Rule #10.

543. **DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 — classify a Dhan `DH-905` "no data" 400 as a visible KNOWN_GAP (not an alarming quarantine) + ship a daily-vs-intraday probe script; Q4 of the `make run` deep-check** (2026-06-06, operator decision via AskUserQuestion: "Graceful known-gap + probe script"). **Context:** an operator `make run` ended `failed=1` — `NIFTY NEXT 50` 1-DAY was rejected by Dhan with `DH-905` ("incorrect parameters or no data present") while its 1-MINUTE pulled fine (501,945 bars), so the engine `ingest.quarantine`d that one leg (isolated, pull continued — no crash, no corruption). DH-905 is AMBIGUOUS: a genuinely-empty range (an index whose daily history starts after the requested `fromDate`) OR a true param bug — Dhan does not distinguish. **Fix (3 src/script + 2 test files, SAFE — no data-masking):** (1) `errors.is_no_data_error(exc)` — detects the `DH-905` / "no data present" marker on a `DhanBadRequestError` (the single classification point, COMMON); (2) `run_dhan_spot_ingest`'s terminal-error path logs `ingest.known_gap` (INFO, with the reason + a "re-tried next pull, not masked" note) for a no-data 400 INSTEAD of the alarming `ingest.quarantine` WARNING — a genuine terminal error (real 400/404/auth) still logs the WARNING; EITHER way the pair stays in `failures` → isolated + NOT marked complete → re-tried next pull, so a transient/param case self-heals and a genuine gap is surfaced, never silently dropped (Golden Rule #1); (3) `scripts/dhan_daily_probe.py` — an operator-run diagnostic (their token) that fires the SAME daily (`/v2/charts/historical`) + 1-minute (`/v2/charts/intraday`) requests the spine fires for one `securityId` and prints each outcome (OK n-candles / NO_DATA / ERROR), so the operator can CONFIRM whether daily is a real Dhan gap, a range-too-early boundary, or a param mismatch — resolving the ambiguity empirically before any deeper change. **Tests:** `test_dhan_errors.py::TestIsNoDataError` (DH-905 + "no data present" → True; generic 400 → False; wrong-type → False) — 100% per-module errors gate; `test_dhan_run_ingest.py::...::test_no_data_logs_known_gap_not_quarantine` (DH-905 → `ingest.known_gap` INFO, NO `ingest.quarantine`, pair still `series_failed=1` → isolated + re-tried). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the `errors` tests run + pass IN-SANDBOX (pure stdlib path) — `is_no_data_error` both-branch covered. 🟡 the `run_ingest` test + the probe are CI/operator-only (orchestrator PEP 695 chain / live token). **Honest scope — NOT done here (deferred, gated on the probe result):** the **auto-narrow-daily-start retry** (re-fetch daily over a later start when DH-905 hits the full range) is intentionally NOT shipped blind — it needs the probe to confirm "range-too-early" is the cause, else it could waste quota or mask a param bug; this PR makes the gap VISIBLE + safe + diagnosable first. The pull report still counts the leg in `failed` (accurate — it fetched 0 this run); a `known_gaps` report field is a follow-up. **Queue context:** Q4 of the `make run` deep-check — Q1 (#540) + Q2 (#541) + Q3 (#542) merged; this closes the queue's safe-now scope. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the quarantine/isolation path this refines) · DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 / DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the re-try-next-pull guarantee) · CLAUDE.md §6 (Dhan facts) / §11 COMMON / Golden Rule #1.

544. **DEC-ENGINE-PAISA-ACCOUNTING-GOLDEN-001 — Phase 2 golden corpus #8: 12-fill paisa accounting (P-03 per-trade · P-04 Σ PnL exact int64)** (2026-06-07, engine roadmap, operator "go ahead"; continues the Phase 2 golden-fixtures track after corpus #7). **Gap:** `tests/golden/fixtures/README.md` corpus #8 ("12-fill paisa accounting / gross-net-Σ PnL, P-03/P-04") was 📋 ROADMAP — the per-trade `ClosedTrade` walker is golden-locked individually (`test_engine_trade_sim_golden.py`) but the AGGREGATE Σ-PnL-over-many-fills accounting (no float drift) had no golden. **Fix (1 golden test + README/ledger):** `tests/golden/test_engine_paisa_accounting_golden.py` runs the REAL `engine.trade_sim.simulate_trades` over a **correct-by-construction** 36-bar fixture = **12 identical back-to-back copies** of the already-hand-derived + golden-locked Fixture-A trade 1 (long, next-open entry 100.00, take-profit at the +50p level via high 100.60 → `pnl 50, mfe 60, mae 10, holding 2`), spaced 09:15-onward so the 15:20 forced-exit never fires. Asserts: (P-03) every fill emits one `ClosedTrade` with the exact proven paisa fields; (P-04) **Σ pnl == 12 × 50 == 600 paisa** as an EXACT `int` (never a float — int64-paisa discipline); net == gross (Track-1 spot is signal-only → NO brokerage, CLAUDE.md §7); all 12 round-trips are byte-identical in paisa (only timestamps differ). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean; the expected values are NOT fresh hand-math — they REUSE the already-golden-locked single-trade shape ×12 (correct by construction), so Σ=600 is certain without running. 🟡 the test is CI-only in this 3.11 sandbox (`brutex.strategies.types` import triggers `strategies/__init__` → `combo` → the `fno_math` wheel); CI (3.12, wheels built) is the oracle — the established pattern for every engine golden. **Honest scope:** "net == gross" reflects the CURRENT signal-only-spot reality (no cost model); when a cost model lands (options track) a net-vs-gross corpus follows. **Queue context:** Phase 2 golden corpora — #7 (#538) + #8 (this) landed; #1–5 (ingest round-trip / resample) + #9 (combo-hash, needs the Rust blake3 — not locally reproducible) remain ROADMAP. **Builds on:** DEC-TRADESIM-001 (the walker this aggregates) · DEC-PHASE2-TRUTH-TABLE-001 (#538, corpus #7) · DEC-PHASE1-SMOKE-AND-SKELETONS-001 (#251) · CLAUDE.md §4 (int64 paisa) / §7 (no brokerage) / §11 COMMON.

545a. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 — per-second physical Dhan rate ≤5 GUARANTEED (gate the client fast-retry through the bucket) + real-time ASSURANCE (windowed `rps_1s` gauge + breach alarm)** (2026-06-07, operator "I need the real-time guarantee and assurance"; priority law: correctness > observability). **Root-cause (traced, all physical-POST paths mapped):** with `BURST=1` + every (re)build `start_empty=True`, the token bucket already caps issuance at `current_rps` — EXCEPT one path: `DhanClient.post_json`'s bounded fast-retry (timeout/transport/5xx) called `_post_once` again WITHOUT re-acquiring a bucket token (the client is deliberately rate-agnostic). Under a parallel timeout storm (the operator's log: hundreds of `dhan.retry … DhanTimeoutError`, `latency_ms_max=20055`), 15 workers' un-gated retries could push the AGGREGATE issue rate over 5 r/s. The cumulative `effective_rps` meter (peaking 6.97 early) is the WRONG instrument — it is an `(N-1)/span` average, not an instantaneous gauge. **Fix (`client.py` + `run_ingest.py` + tests):** (a) **GUARANTEE** — `DhanClient` gains an injected `pace` hook (default no-op, same DI pattern as `transport`/`clock`/`sleep`); `post_json` calls `self.pace()` before each RETRY `_post_once` (the initial attempt stays paced by the ingest layer → no double-pace), so EVERY physical POST acquires a burst-1 token ⇒ rate ≤ `current_rps` ≤ 5. `run_dhan_spot_ingest._with_paced_client` injects `controller.pace` into the live `DhanMarketAdapter`'s client via `dataclasses.replace` (no-op for dry-run/non-Dhan adapters or unthrottled runs). (b) **ASSURANCE** — `CallMeter.record_issue(at)` tracks the trailing-1s POST-issue count (`rps_1s` / `rps_1s_max`) in `snapshot()`; `_post_once` logs a `rate.breach` WARNING if `rps_1s > 5` — so any breach is impossible to hide and `rps_1s_max <= 5` is the real-time PROOF the cap held. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ client + meter are wheel-free → 4 new sandbox tests (`tests/unit/test_dhan_rate_realtime_guarantee.py`) PROVE the retry pacing (2 stalls → pace called exactly twice; first-try success → zero client-pace) + the windowed gauge (5/s → `rps_1s_max==5`; 6-in-1s → 6 + eviction); existing `test_dhan_client.py` snapshot shape updated (+2 keys). 🟡 `run_ingest.py` wiring is CI-only here (imports `orchestrator.retry`'s PEP-695 generic, unparseable on the 3.11 sandbox). 🟡 **scope:** this PR gates the **spot parallel fan-out** (the operator's case + the only severe >5 vector — 15 workers); the **options** path (sequential, single-stream → retries already backoff-spaced ≤ ~5/s, far lower risk) gets the same wiring as the immediate follow-up. Does NOT claim options ≤5 guaranteed yet. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RATE-HARD-CAP-001 (#450, empty-start bucket) · DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 (the fast-retry being gated) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the shared bucket) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (5 r/s cap).

545b. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (addendum — options track gated + hostile-review residuals + coverage)** (2026-06-07, after a parallel hostile-review fleet + workspace audit on PR #453). **(1) Options ≤5 now closed:** the adversarial review found the options track's `post_json` fast-retry was still un-gated (same bug class, the one HIGH residual). Added `option_universe_ingest._with_paced_client` (the options analog of the spot helper) injecting `controller.pace` into the options `DhanClient` at the `run_dhan_options_ingest` entry — so BOTH spot AND options physical POSTs (initial + every retry) are now bucket-bounded ⇒ ≤ `current_rps` ≤ 5 for all in-process pulls. **(2) Coverage gate fixes:** the workspace audit found `brutex.adapters.dhan.client` (strict 100% gate, ci.yml line ~1200) was at 97.53% — lines 168 (meter eviction `popleft`) + 367 (`rate.breach` WARNING) uncovered by `test_dhan_client.py`; AND `run_ingest`/`option_universe_ingest` (also strict-100%, ci.yml ~1125/1130) had the `_with_paced_client` real-adapter branch uncovered (existing tests use fakes). Added: 2 tests to `test_dhan_client.py` (eviction + breach via 6-POST-in-1s with `capture_logs`), 1 direct-helper test each to `test_dhan_run_ingest.py` + `test_dhan_option_universe_ingest.py` (all 3 branches). Verified locally: client gate now 100.00%. **(3) Honest residual risks the review surfaced (NOT fixed here — documented, lower/out-of-scope):** (a) `auth.renew_token` POSTs un-paced — LATENT, no production caller wires it into a live pull; (b) `scripts/dhan_daily_probe.py` builds an un-paced client — diagnostic, 2 sequential requests; (c) **multi-process**: the bucket is per-`DhanRateController` (per-process); two processes against one Dhan account could aggregate >5 — inherent to the single-flight in-process design (operator runs ONE dashboard); (d) step-rebuild dual-bucket transient ~1 extra token at a rare rate-step instant — bounded, documented benign in `rate_control.py`. **Honest statement after this PR:** "no spot OR options fast-retry can bypass the 5 r/s bucket within a single process." The blanket cross-process claim remains out of scope. **Verification:** 2-agent hostile fleet (adversarial POST-path review + coverage/CI-gate audit); CI (3.12) is the runtime oracle for the run_ingest/option_universe wiring (3.11 sandbox can't import the PEP-695 `orchestrator.retry` chain).

547a. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-RESIDUAL-HARDEN-001 — close the two LATENT un-paced physical-POST residuals the #545b hostile review surfaced (renew_token + daily probe)** (2026-06-07, defence-in-depth follow-up to DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001, MIGRATION.md entries #545 / #545b). **Context:** #545b's hostile review found that after spot + options fast-retries were bucket-gated, two residual paths still issued physical Dhan POSTs WITHOUT acquiring a bucket token — both flagged as LATENT / out-of-scope at the time: (a) `brutex/adapters/dhan/auth.py::renew_token` POSTs `/v2/RenewToken` un-paced — **LATENT, no production caller wires it into a live pull today**; (b) `scripts/dhan_daily_probe.py` builds a `DhanClient` and fires 2 sequential POSTs un-paced — a diagnostic the operator runs by hand. This PR tightens BOTH so that EVERY physical Dhan POST from these paths is bucket-gated the moment they are ever threaded into a live pull, per CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (5 r/s cap). **Fix (2 src + 1 test file, NO behaviour change for current callers):** (1) `renew_token(client, *, pace=None)` gains an optional pace hook that gates the INITIAL physical POST (`(pace or client.pace)()` before `post_json`); `client.pace` (added in #545) continues to gate each fast-retry, so initial + retries are both bucket-bounded when wired. `pace=None` falls back to the client's own `pace` field — itself a no-op default — so byte-unchanged for today's callers. (2) `dhan_daily_probe._probe_one` calls `client.pace()` before each `post_json`, gating the initial POST through whatever the probe's `DhanClient.pace` carries (no-op default → diagnostic unchanged); the fast-retry path already self-gates inside `post_json`. **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_dhan_auth.py::TestRenewTokenPacing` — explicit pace fires BEFORE the POST (`order == ["pace","post"]`); default falls back to `client.pace` (fired exactly once). The strict-100% `brutex.adapters.dhan.auth` gate (ci.yml ~line 1205) stays at 100.00% line+branch (verified locally, 17 tests). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ both edits are wheel-free; `auth` 100% gate green locally; ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright all 0/0 on `auth.py`. ✅ This closes **LATENT (not active)** gaps — neither path had a production live-pull caller, so this is pure defence-in-depth, not a live-breach fix. 🟡 the daily probe is a `scripts/` diagnostic with no coverage gate; its one-line gate is exercised by the operator-run path, not a unit test. **Honest scope (unchanged from #545b):** the cross-process aggregation residual (bucket is per-`DhanRateController` / per-process) remains out of scope — inherent to the single-flight in-process design (operator runs ONE dashboard). **Honest statement after this PR:** "no physical Dhan POST on ANY in-process path — spot, options, renew_token, or the daily probe — can bypass the 5 r/s bucket within a single process when a controller is wired." **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (#545 / #545b, the pace-hook DI pattern + the residual list this closes) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-HARD-CAP-001 (#542, empty-start bucket) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (5 r/s cap) / Golden Rule #10.

546. **DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-LIVE-001 — Q-LIVE: /coverage/windows updates LIVE during a pull (incremental status flush)** (2026-06-07, operator: "the fetch window status is not getting continuously updated"). **Problem (confirmed in code + the operator's screenshots):** the per-window SUCCESS/EMPTY/FAILED log is loaded at `begin_pull_status` and only PERSISTED at `end_pull_status` (pull END) — so during a multi-minute 783-symbol pull the Fetch-windows page shows **"0 windows recorded"** the whole time and only jumps to the final table once the pull finishes, even while `/universe` shows live chunk progress and `/coverage/spot` shows growing datasets (those read the lake directly). **Fix:** `window_status_store.make_live_status_flush(log, lake_root, *, min_interval_s=2.0, clock=monotonic)` returns a THROTTLED callable that persists the in-memory status sidecar mid-pull; the spot ingest already fires `on_progress` once per completed `(symbol, interval)` pair on the controller thread, so `pull_controller.pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` wrap `on_progress` to also call the flush — the page now ticks up SUCCESS/EMPTY/FAILED as each pair lands. Throttled to ≤ once / 2s (`LIVE_FLUSH_MIN_INTERVAL_S`) so a multi-thousand-window JSON isn't rewritten on every one of ~1,500 pairs; `None` log (dry-run) → no-op; reuses the existing atomic `save_window_status` (tmp+`os.replace`), so a mid-pull flush is crash-safe and the final `end_pull_status` still runs. **Thread-safety:** workers `record()` under the log's lock; the flush reads `to_records()` (locked) on the single controller thread. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `make_live_status_flush` is wheel-free → `test_window_status_store.py` covers all 4 branches (None log, first-write, throttled-skip, post-interval write); the strict-100% `brutex.data.window_status_store` gate passes locally at 100.00%; ruff + pyright (0/0) clean. 🟡 the `pull_controller` wiring is CI-only here (imports the PEP-695 `orchestrator.retry` chain; `pull_controller` is under the global-90% gate, not strict-100%); CI (3.12) is the oracle. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (the sidecar this flushes) · DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-TRACKER-001 (the per-pair `on_progress` hook reused). **Follow-up:** an SSE/long-poll push so the page updates without its 4s poll is a separate observability nicety, not required for live correctness.

548a. **DEC-PHASE2-CORPORA-001 — Phase 2 golden corpora #1–5 + #9: NIFTY day / BANKNIFTY week / SENSEX forced-exit / INDIA VIX reference / cross-instrument resample / combo-hash distinct** (2026-06-07, engine roadmap, operator "go ahead"; completes the Phase 2 golden-fixtures track after #7 (#538) + #8 (#544)). **Gap:** `tests/golden/fixtures/README.md` corpora #1–5 + #9 were 📋 ROADMAP — the only landed Phase 2 goldens were the 52-condition truth table (#7) + the 12-fill paisa accounting (#8); the per-instrument engine drive (Stage-1A over a full day / a holiday-pruned week), the trade-sim end-of-session paths, the reference-only VIX guarantee, the resampler bucket math, and the byte-frozen combo-hash were all unlocked. **Fix (6 new byte-frozen golden tests + README/ledger):** each drives a REAL existing component over a small fixture whose expected values are hand-derived bar-for-bar (or translation-invariant / deterministic) and pinned by a SHA-256 / digest manifest (Golden Rule #1 — no hand-authored numbers without a justification): (#1) `test_engine_nifty_day_golden.py` — `engine.stage1a.build_bar_bits` over a 375-bar flat-doji NIFTY trading day; every `u64` mask is the closed form `{40 CLOSE_AT_DAY_HIGH, 41 CLOSE_AT_DAY_LOW} ∪ time_bit(i) ∪ ({38 PRIOR_N_BEARISH} if i≥3)` (flat doji ⇒ no EMA/candle bits, zero day-range, first-day anchors cleared), asserted bar-for-bar + SHA-256 pinned, plus the **reproducibility round-trip** batch==batch==stream (P-19) and the **2-dp ROUND_HALF_UP tick-rounding** seam `14025.7999→1402580` (P-21, DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001); (#2) `test_engine_banknifty_week_golden.py` — `calendars.nse.trading_days_between` prunes 2024-08-12→18 to 4 trading days (Independence Day 2024-08-15 + the weekend removed, P-23, CLAUDE.md §7) and `build_bar_bits` walks the pruned session-window feed across the IST day-rollover (P-22), masks hand-derived + SHA-256 pinned; (#3) `test_engine_sensex_forced_exit_golden.py` — `engine.trade_sim.simulate_trades` for the 15:20 **forced-exit override** (P-09, pnl 15/mfe 30/mae 20/holding 3) + the **end-of-data** close-at-last-CLOSE robustness path (pnl 30/mfe 50/mae 20/holding 2), both the proven Fixture-A windows from `test_engine_trade_sim_golden.py` translated +₹72900 to SENSEX scale (price-difference fields invariant under translation); (#4) `test_india_vix_reference_golden.py` — `data.tf_resampler` aggregates a VIX week to hand-derived daily bars (the reference data path) and `brutex.universe` proves INDIA VIX is `reference_only` AND `not is_in_brute_force_scope` (the "no signal bits" guarantee, DEC-ENGINE-ISOLATION-INVARIANT-001); (#5) `test_resample_cross_instrument_golden.py` — `data.tf_resampler.resample_1m_to_tf` 1m→5m at three instrument price scales (hand-derived buckets) + the **associativity** 1m→15m == (1m→5m)→15m (P-08); (#9) `test_combo_hash_distinct_golden.py` — byte-freezes the 9-field BLAKE3 `strategies.combo.combo_hash` over a base + nine single-field variants: determinism (P-01), distinct-inputs→distinct-digests + per-field sensitivity (P-02), param-order invariance. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ all 6 (24 tests) authored + PASS against a local **Python 3.12 venv with the `fno_math` + `trading_core` wheels built + polars installed** — the CI-equivalent oracle — so the hand-derived masks/trades/buckets/digests are verified, not asserted blind; ruff + ruff-format clean, mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors / 0 warnings) on all 6 files. 🟡 the standard 3.11 sandbox cannot import these (stage1a/trade_sim/combo pull the `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels + the PEP-695 `orchestrator.retry` chain; resampler needs polars) — CI (3.12, `golden` job `pytest tests/golden -x`) is the merge oracle. **Honest scope:** corpus #1's "375 bars × 4 instruments" pyramid note is realised as the single named NIFTY instrument × 375 bars (the cross-instrument dimension is covered by #5); these goldens lock the engine/resample/combo seams, NOT the Phase-2 ingest pipeline (still separate). **Builds on:** DEC-PHASE2-TRUTH-TABLE-001 (#538, #7) · DEC-ENGINE-PAISA-ACCOUNTING-GOLDEN-001 (#544, #8) · DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-001 / DEC-TRADESIM-001 (the components driven) · DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the trading_core evaluator) · DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (tick-rounding) · CLAUDE.md §1/§3 (VIX reference-only) / §7 (no brokerage) / §11 COMMON / Golden Rule #1/#4.

547b. **DEC-DASHBOARD-RPS1S-PANEL-001 — surface the real-time instantaneous Dhan issue rate (`rps_1s` / `rps_1s_max`) in the dashboard rate panel** (2026-06-07, operator "I need the real-time guarantee and assurance" — the observability companion to DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 #545/#545b). **Problem:** the transport `CallMeter.snapshot()` already exposes the instantaneous trailing-1s issue gauge (`rps_1s`) + its run peak (`rps_1s_max`) — the DIRECT real-time proof the 5 r/s cap held (`rps_1s_max <= 5` ⇒ no per-second breach, ever) — but the dashboard rate panel only showed the cumulative `effective_rps` AVERAGE (an `(N-1)/span` figure that reads high in the opening seconds without any true breach) + the controller target. The operator could SEE the per-second truth only by tailing `/logs` for the `rate.breach` WARNING; the panel hid it. **Fix (observability ONLY — no rate-control logic touched):** wired the two existing meter keys end-to-end through the read path: (a) `RateLimitPanel` gains `rps_1s: int` + `rps_1s_max: int` (default 0); (b) `DashboardState.update_throughput` gains matching `rps_1s` / `rps_1s_max` kwargs (default 0 → back-compat for any caller that omits them) and stamps them under the lock; (c) `make_rate_observer`'s `_observe` reads `int(meter.get("rps_1s", 0))` / `int(meter.get("rps_1s_max", 0))` from the same `CallMeter.snapshot()` it already consumes for `effective_rps` + `latency_ms_p95`; (d) the `asdict(rate_limit)` serialisation means BOTH `/api/v1/state` and the dedicated `/api/v1/rate` route expose the new fields automatically; (e) the rate-panel template adds `live: <rps_1s> rps · peak: <rps_1s_max> rps`, and the JS toggles a loud `.rps-breach` class (red + " ⚠ >5 r/s BREACH" suffix) on either span whenever the value exceeds the 5 r/s cap — which, with every physical POST now burst-1 bucket-gated (#545b), must NEVER fire. `pull_controller._observe_rate` already forwards the whole `meter.snapshot()` mapping, so no controller-side wiring change was needed (docstrings reconciled to mention the gauge). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the pure data plane is wheel-free → `test_dashboard_rate_panel.py` extended (panel defaults, `update_throughput`, `make_rate_observer` map + missing-key tolerance, `to_dict`, `/api/v1/rate` route) — 9 tests pass on a local 3.12 venv (sandbox is 3.11: the dashboard import chain pulls the PEP-695 `orchestrator.retry` generic + the `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels, so it is CI-only here; the wheels were built with `maturin develop` to verify locally). ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright (0/0) all clean on the touched modules. The JS/HTML breach visual is template text (not line-covered); `app.py` + `pull_controller.py` are under the global-90% coverage floor, not a strict-100% per-module gate, and the new executable lines (the two assignments + the two observer kwargs) are exercised by the added tests. **Scope:** observability only — the 5 r/s GUARANTEE itself is #545/#545b; this PR makes its real-time PROOF visible on the dashboard, not just in `/logs`. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (#545/#545b, the `rps_1s` / `rps_1s_max` meter this surfaces + the `rate.breach` alarm) · DEC-DASHBOARD-RATE-PANEL-001 (the `make_rate_observer` + panel this extends) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (5 r/s cap).

548b. **DEC-PROPERTY-INVARIANTS-LIVE-001 — promote five verification-pyramid ROADMAP stubs to LIVE hypothesis property tests against the real sandbox-safe components** (2026-06-07, verification-pyramid roadmap; continues the Phase-2 verification track after the golden corpus #8 work, #544). **Gap:** `docs/TRACK1_VERIFICATION_PYRAMID.md` §3 enumerates 24 property invariants, but `tests/property/test_invariants_catalog.py` still carried several as `pytest.skip("Phase 2 implementation pending …")` stubs even though their target modules already exist and are exercisable WITHOUT importing `brutex.orchestrator` (i.e., runnable in the 3.11 sandbox + the `property` CI job). **Fix (2 test files + catalog flip + this entry):** turned five stubs into real `hypothesis` tests and flipped their catalog rows from 📋 ROADMAP to ✅ IMPLEMENTED (each catalog `skip` now points at the live sibling file): **(P-03)** `test_p03_per_trade_pnl_sums_to_balance_delta` — drives the REAL `brutex.engine.trade_sim.simulate_trades` over random `(bars, entry, exit)` scenarios, builds an independent int64-paisa per-trade ledger / `EquityCurve`, and asserts Σ per-trade `pnl_paisa == final_balance − initial_balance` to the exact paisa AND that `brutex.metrics.compute.compute_metrics(...).net_pnl_paisa` agrees; **(P-04)** `test_p04_gross_minus_costs_equals_net` — asserts the cost-free identity `net_pnl == gross_profit − gross_loss` (Track-1 spot is signal-only → costs = 0, CLAUDE.md §7) with `net` the raw directional sum, exact `int`; **(P-09)** `test_p09_forced_exit_no_trade_survives_1520` — a 15:10-IST-anchored feed that straddles the 15:20 forced-exit boundary; every emitted trade opens strictly before, and exits on or before, the first `is_forced_exit_bar` bar (CLAUDE.md §7 forced 15:20 exit); **(P-13)** `test_p13_ema_is_contraction` — `brutex.indicators.ema.compute_ema` is an ℓ∞ contraction (`‖EMA(x)−EMA(y)‖∞ ≤ ‖x−y‖∞`, float-tolerance bounded); **(P-14)** `test_p14_pivot_levels_pure_no_state_leak` + `test_p14_fib_levels_pure_no_state_leak` — pivot / Fib levels (`brutex.indicators.{pivots,fib_levels}`, delegating to the shared Rust `trading_core` core, DEC-SHARED-CORE-001) are pure functions of the anchors: identical anchors → identical levels (determinism) and the levels never depend on the `trading_day` (no per-day state leak). P-03/P-04/P-09 live in `tests/property/test_engine_trade_sim_properties.py` (reusing its existing `_scenarios` generator — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, no duplication); P-13/P-14 in the new `tests/property/test_indicator_properties.py`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ all five run GREEN locally in a Python-3.12 venv with both Rust wheels built (`149 passed, 28 skipped` across `tests/property`; the 24-row catalog now reports 5 fewer "Phase 2 pending"); ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean, mypy `--strict` + pyright both 0/0 on the two touched test files. 🟡 the new tests are exercised by the dedicated `property` CI job (3.12, wheels built) — they import the `fno_math` wheel transitively via `brutex.engine.__init__` and `trading_core` via `brutex.indicators`, so a bare 3.11 interpreter without wheels cannot collect them; this matches every existing engine/indicator property test. **Honest scope:** P-04's "net == gross" reflects the CURRENT signal-only-spot reality (no cost model); the remaining ROADMAP invariants (P-06 instrumented accessor, P-08 resampler, P-11/P-24 u64-mask, P-21 parquet-writer, P-19/P-20 reproducibility, P-22/P-23 microstructure, P-07/P-10/P-12/P-15 cost/Track-2) stay 📋 pending their subjects — this PR does NOT weaken any existing test. **Builds on:** DEC-PHASE1-INVARIANT-CATALOG-001 (#250, the catalog this updates) · DEC-TRADESIM-001 (the walker P-03/P-04/P-09 drive) · DEC-ENGINE-PAISA-ACCOUNTING-GOLDEN-001 (#544, the golden-layer P-03/P-04 oracle these property-test) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, the aggregator) · DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the pivot/Fib core) · `docs/TRACK1_VERIFICATION_PYRAMID.md` §3.

550a. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-SINGLE-BUCKET-001 — eliminate the dual-bucket transient: change the controller rate IN PLACE instead of rebuilding the token bucket on every step** (2026-06-07, operator's live `make run` proof: `rate.breach … rps_1s=11` at the pull opening on `charts/intraday` + `charts/historical`, despite #542 burst-1 + #545 pace gating). **Root cause (confirmed by code read):** `DhanRateController.on_rate_limit` / `on_timeout` / `on_success` each did `self._bucket = self._make_bucket()` — REBUILDING the `AdaptiveTokenBucket` on every 5→4→3 step. `pace()` copies the current `_bucket` reference under the lock then `.acquire()`s OUTSIDE the lock (correct, so the lock is never held across the sleep). But during the rapid opening stepdown cascade, in-flight `pace` workers were still acquiring on the OLD bucket while new workers acquired on the freshly-built NEW one — TWO (or, across 5→4→3, up to THREE) independent token streams, each ≤ its own rate, whose COMBINED physical issue rate stacked into the trailing-1s window → `rps_1s` up to ~11 (≈ overlapping ≤5 streams). A single persistent bucket already caps at ≤5 (burst-1 + `start_empty` re-serialise concurrent sleepers via the second-critical-section while-loop); only the per-step REBUILD broke the single-stream invariant. **Fix (2 src + 2 test files, behaviour-preserving for the pacing math):** (1) `AdaptiveTokenBucket.set_rate(new_rps)` (new, O(1)) — under the bucket lock sets `initial_rps` + `downshift_rps` (= `new_rps/2`, kept `< initial` for the dormant internal ladder) + `_current_rps = new_rps`, then DRAINS `_tokens = 0.0` and re-stamps `_last_refill` (exactly mirroring the prior `start_empty=True` rebuild, so a downshift still can't release a stale higher-rate token); moving `initial_rps` WITH the rate keeps the bucket's own `_maybe_upshift_locked` a no-op (`_current_rps == initial_rps`) so it never fights the controller's chosen rate (the controller never feeds the bucket 429s — it owns its own ladder). Raises `RateLimiterError` on non-positive `new_rps`. (2) `DhanRateController.on_rate_limit/on_timeout/on_success` now call `self._bucket.set_rate(self._rps)` instead of `self._bucket = self._make_bucket()`; `_make_bucket` is retained for the ONE construction-time build. The object reference is therefore STABLE for the controller's whole life → exactly one ≤ `current_rps` token stream at all times, even mid-cascade. **Tests:** `test_orchestrator_rate_limiter.py::TestSetRate` (changes rate; rejects non-positive — both branches; drains a full bucket to 0; first call after a downshift waits a full `1/new_rps`; internal upshift stays dormant). `test_dhan_rate_control.py::test_steps_preserve_single_bucket_identity` — the ROOT-CAUSE regression: `ctl._bucket is original` across a 429 stepdown, a timeout stepdown AND a recovery stepup (with the old rebuild this assertion would FAIL); plus the renamed `test_stepdown_drains_to_empty_no_free_burst`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ both modules are wheel-free; the `brutex.adapters.dhan.rate_control` strict-100% gate passes locally at 100.00% (29 tests); `set_rate`'s two branches are covered by `TestSetRate` (the orchestrator module reaches 100% in the whole-package `--cov=brutex` run, not an isolated gate — the PyO3 double-init constraint documented in ci.yml ~#1155); ruff + ruff-format clean (0/0) on all four files; 107 rate tests pass on a local 3.12 venv. 🟡 the live end-to-end proof (`rps_1s_max <= 5` across a real opening cascade) is the operator's next `make run` — the `rate.breach` alarm (#545) + the `rps_1s_max` panel (#547) are the standing real-time assurance that confirms it. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RATE-HARD-CAP-001 (#542, the burst-1 `start_empty` bucket whose rebuild this removes) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (#545/#545b, the pace gating + `rps_1s` breach alarm that CAUGHT this) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the shared-controller fan-out the single bucket governs) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (5 r/s cap) / Golden Rule #10.

549. **DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 — sweep real-time GUARANTEE & ASSURANCE layer: 5 NEW standalone, 100%-tested engine modules (audit chain · progress · checkpoint · dedup cache · watchdog)** (2026-06-07, operator: "build the sweep real-time guarantee and assurance layer ... no illusion ... honest envelope"). **Context:** the brute-force sweep ENGINE exists (`engine/sweep_driver.py rank_sweep_over_bits`, `engine/stage1a.py`, `engine/trade_sim.py`, `engine/results_store.py`) and `brutex sweep` runs ONE ad-hoc sweep, but it had NO real-time guarantee/assurance layer — no per-combo audit chain (Golden Rule #8), no live progress/ETA, no crash-resume (Golden Rule #7), no re-run dedup, no hung-combo watchdog (§11 AUTOMATED). **What shipped (5 NEW source + 5 NEW test files, all wheel-free, each 100% line+branch):** (1) `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py` — per-combo append-only **BLAKE3** hash-chained JSONL (`SweepAuditWriter` + `verify_chain`), mirroring `orchestrator/audit.py`'s proven chain design (genesis prev-hash, `prev_hash[n]==entry_hash[n-1]`, recompute-and-compare) but BLAKE3 throughout per Golden Rule #4; a flipped byte / reordered / deleted line breaks the chain at the offending seq (Golden Rule #8). (2) `brutex/engine/sweep_progress.py` — O(1) thread-safe live tracker (enumerated / evaluated / survivors / skipped + percent + combos-per-sec + linear-extrapolation ETA), mirroring `dashboard/pull_progress.py`; one lock, injected clock, JSON-snapshot-able, reusable across re-runs (Rule 7). (3) `brutex/engine/sweep_checkpoint.py` — crash-safe resumable checkpoint (last-completed-combo index; atomic tmp + `os.replace`, mirroring `results_store._atomic_write`); monotonic high-water mark, sweep-id-scoped resume, so a killed sweep resumes where it left off (Rule 7). (4) `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py` — O(1) `(mask,instrument,tf,direction,params)` membership dedup via a Bloom L1 pre-filter (`orchestrator/bloom.py`) + an LMDB L2 exact store (`data/lmdb_membership.py`), keyed by the BLAKE3 combo digest, so a re-run skips already-evaluated combos (Rule 11 4-tier dedup). (5) `brutex/engine/sweep_watchdog.py` — heartbeat + hung-combo timeout, a thread-safe composition over the `observability/watchdog.py` primitive (DEC-WATCHDOG-001) with O(1) healthy/hung tallies. **Dependency:** adds `blake3>=0.4,<2.0` to core deps — the wheel-free BLAKE3 provider (prebuilt manylinux wheels, no local Rust build, unlike `fno_math.blake3_hash`) so the assurance layer runs + tests without the compiled kernel. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ all 5 modules are O(1) PER OPERATION + bounded/streaming memory, NOT O(1) total time/space for a whole sweep (the LMDB store + retained results grow O(N) — claiming otherwise would be physically impossible). ✅ each module hits 100% line+branch in its own `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_*.py` (89 tests; sandbox-verified on Python 3.12 = CI's interpreter, with hypothesis property tests + frozen golden hash/digest fixtures); ruff + ruff-format clean, pyright 0/0/0 on all 5, mypy --strict clean on the modules. 🟡 `sweep_cache` is a **membership** dedup tier (records WHICH combos were evaluated so the recompute is skipped) — it deliberately does NOT store the `ResultMetrics` VALUE (that is `results_store`'s job, and importing it would drag the Rust-wheel-bound `strategies`/`metrics` chain into this wheel-free module); returning the cached metrics on a hit is a documented Wave-2 extension on the same key space. **Out of scope (explicit, Golden Rule #3):** wiring these modules INTO `engine/sweep_driver.py` is a SEPARATE Wave-2 follow-up AFTER the parallel Phase-3 sweep-orchestrator session merges — this PR does NOT touch `sweep_driver.py` / `sweep_report.py` / `strategies/sweep.py` (avoids the merge conflict with that session). **Builds on:** `orchestrator/audit.py` (DEC chain design) · `dashboard/pull_progress.py` (DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-TRACKER-001) · `orchestrator/bloom.py` (DEC-P0-047) · `data/lmdb_membership.py` · `observability/watchdog.py` (DEC-WATCHDOG-001) · `engine/results_store.py` (DEC-RESULT-STORE-001) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #4/#5/#7/#8/#10/#11.

550b. **DEC-OPTIONS-LIVE-STATUS-001 — Q-LIVE (options): /coverage/options ticks LIVE during a single-underlying options pull (throttled per-series tick)** (2026-06-07, operator: apply the DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-LIVE-001 live-status pattern to the OPTIONS pull). **Investigation (confirmed in code):** unlike spot, the options pull records **no** per-window/per-series status log — `run_dhan_options_ingest` threads no `WindowStatusLog` and `pull_options` never calls `begin/end_pull_status`, so options never appears on `/coverage/windows`. Its ACTUAL live status surface is the lake-backed **`/coverage/options`** (Expired-options) page (+ the O(1) coverage headline counters + the pull-progress feed), which reads `summarize_option_datasets` through the `SummaryCache` (DEC-OPTIONS-COVERAGE-LAKE-001 / DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001). The option lake writer writes **incrementally per series** (`OptionParquetWriter`), so the lake holds mid-pull data — but the read surface only refreshes when something invalidates the cache (`mark_dirty`), and the ONLY invalidation trigger is `BackgroundPullJob._on_progress`, which for options fires **once per underlying** (`run_dhan_options_ingest` fires `on_progress` after each underlying's WHOLE fan-out), vs per `(symbol, interval)` pair for spot. So a **single-index options pull** (the common per-index "⛓ Pull options chain" button) fires `on_progress` exactly once, at the very end → `/coverage/options` stays frozen until the pull finishes: the same "stale-until-end" symptom spot's windows page had, on a different surface. **Fix (observability only — does not change fetch/parse/sink or rate logic):** (a) **generic throttle** — new `brutex/observability/throttle.py::make_throttled(callback, *, min_interval_s=2.0, clock=monotonic)`, the pure dependency-free essence of `make_live_status_flush` lifted out so a non-window-status surface reuses the SAME throttled-flush principle (first call fires, calls within the window are dropped, the first past the window fires again). (b) **per-series tick seam** — `run_dhan_options_ingest` gains an optional `on_series_tick: Callable[[], None] | None`, fired once per SERIES as each outcome is drained on the controller thread (the series' lake write already happened in the worker before the outcome was yielded), far finer than the per-underlying `on_progress`; `None` (the default) is a no-op so every existing caller is byte-unchanged. (c) **passthrough** — `option_pull_controller.pull_options` threads `on_series_tick` into the spine; `app.py`'s options `_work` passes `on_series_tick=make_throttled(_summary_cache.mark_dirty)` so the lake-backed `/coverage/options` recomputes mid-pull (the 2 s throttle matches the cache's 2 s TTL floor, so a 16k-series fan-out invalidates at most ~once / 2 s, never a scan storm — the cache's own TTL floor already bounds the O(files) recompute). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ wheel-free + import-light → `test_observability_throttle.py` covers all branches (first-fire, throttled-skip, post-window fire, no-throttle, default clock); strict-100% gates green LOCALLY on a real Python-3.12 venv + the `fno_math` release wheel (`maturin develop --release`) for `brutex.observability.throttle` (14 stmts / 2 br), `brutex.adapters.dhan.option_universe_ingest` (130 stmts / 30 br — the tick fires per drained series incl. quarantined), AND `brutex.dashboard.option_pull_controller` (113 stmts / 18 br — the passthrough), all 100.00%; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict brutex` (183 files, 0); `pyright brutex tests` 0 errors (the only warnings are pre-existing `reportPrivateUsage` in untouched test files); dashboard integration suite (`test_dashboard_coverage.py` + `test_dashboard_e2e.py`) green. 🟡 the `app.py` `_work` assembly line is `# pragma: no cover` (the job-thread body, like the spot equivalent) — the throttle helper + the controller/spine threading are fully covered; the final wiring is exercised end-to-end only on the live job thread. 🟡 **scope:** this makes the lake-backed `/coverage/options` surface live (the surface options actually uses); it deliberately does NOT add a window-status sidecar / `/coverage/windows` rows for options (that larger parity feature, per CLAUDE.md Rule #9, would need a hostile-review pass — out of scope here). The per-underlying `on_progress` still advances the pull-progress bar + counters as before; only the summary-cache refresh cadence is made finer. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-LIVE-001 (#546, the spot live-flush principle + `make_live_status_flush` this generalises) · DEC-OPTIONS-COVERAGE-LAKE-001 (the lake-backed `/coverage/options` surface) · DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the `SummaryCache` + TTL floor) · DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-TRACKER-001 (the per-underlying `on_progress` hook) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (rate untouched) / Rule 10 (honest envelope).

## DEC-MASK-IDENTITY-001 + DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 (2026-06-07)

551. **DEC-MASK-IDENTITY-001 — the brute-force u64 mask IS the strategy identity, encoded as `strategy_id = "mask:%016x"`** (2026-06-07, Phase 3 engine slice-1; reconciles the spec's `strategy_mask` field with the shipped `combo_hash` signature). **Gap (found by the 4-agent hostile review):** `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Identity":1010 + §"Result Row Schema":522-530 + CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #4 all name the FIRST run-identity input `strategy_mask` (the u64 bitmask), but the shipped `brutex.strategies.combo.combo_hash` (DEC-P0-060, 9-field BLAKE3) names its first field `strategy_id` (a free-form string) and has **no** `mask:int` slot — so the mask sweep had no canonical home for the u64 (the `"N/A"` placeholders + `# TODO(engine PR)` in `strategies/sweep.py:446-458` were exactly this hole). **Decision:** the u64 mask is serialised into the existing `strategy_id` field as `f"mask:{mask:016x}"` (16 lowercase hex chars, zero-padded) — deterministic, collision-free across masks, visually distinct from a grid-sweep `strategy_id`, and requiring **no** `combo_hash` signature change / spec re-lock. The mask-evaluation parameters that genuinely change the result — `sl_paisa`, `tp_paisa`, `prior_n`, `proximity_bps`, `start_equity_paisa` — go in the separate `params` field (canonicalised by `canonicalise_params`), per the spec's mask-vs-params separation. The three provenance fields (`data_snapshot_hash`, `indicator_version`, `code_commit_sha`) are **caller-injected real values — NEVER placeholders** (Golden Rule #1/#4): a fabricated snapshot hash would make the run-identity a lie. **Implemented:** `brutex.engine.sweep_run.mask_run_id(...)`. **Property-proven:** any change in {mask, direction, instrument, tf, mode, sl, tp, prior_n, proximity, snapshot, indicator_ver, commit} ⇒ a different run-id; identical inputs ⇒ identical id (`test_engine_sweep_run_properties.py` hypothesis suite). **Builds on:** DEC-P0-060 (the 9-field BLAKE3 `combo_hash`) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #4.

552. **DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 — Phase 3 slice-1: the persisted + deduped + audited single-(instrument, TF) sweep runner (`brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`)** (2026-06-07, Phase 3 kickoff; preceded by a full CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review — Audit/Architecture/Hostile/Reality). **What shipped:** the I/O-orchestration SEAM that turns *"sweep the K-of-my-chosen-conditions mask space for ONE (instrument, TF, direction, params)"* into a reproducible, idempotent, audited leaderboard on disk. It **composes** the already-golden-locked bricks and re-implements NONE of them (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON): `build_bar_bits` (Stage-1A, built ONCE) → `iter_masks_k_of_bits` → `has_conflict` prune → `mask_run_id`/`combo_hash` → `ComboDedup.seen` (Bloom→exact-confirm) → `count_supermasks` (Stage-1B min-hits prefilter) → `metrics_for_mask` → `rank_combos` → `ranked_combo_to_result_row` → `ResultsStore.append`/`flush`. **Public API:** `run_persisted_sweep(bars, cfg, *, store, dedup, audit) -> SweepRunSummary`, `SweepRunConfig`, `SweepRunSummary`, `ComboDedup` (a thin adapter COMPOSING the golden `OptionDedupIndex` two-tier engine — re-keys hex→bytes only, no re-implemented dedup logic), `mask_run_id`, `ranked_combo_to_result_row`. **Four review-driven correctness invariants (the hostile review's P0/P1 findings, all resolved):** (1) **dedup is Bloom→LMDB-confirm BEFORE evaluation** — a Bloom false-positive can NEVER cause a false skip (LMDB/exact is ground truth), so no silent data loss (Rules #4/#7); (2) **`ResultsStore` is a FINALIST sink** (its `flush` is O(N·log N)) — only the ranked top-`k` finalists are persisted; the per-combo journal is the Bloom+exact membership set; (3) **audit is per-sweep, never per-combo** — exactly THREE hash-chained lines (`SWEEP_START`/`SWEEP_FLUSH`/`SWEEP_COMPLETE`), O(1) in the combo count (Rule #8; `AuditWriter` fsyncs every line + isn't thread-safe, so per-combo would be an O(N) fsync storm); (4) **conflict-pair pruning is WIRED** — `vocabulary.has_conflict` filters degenerate masks pre-evaluation (it was previously dead code in the sweep path; VOCABULARY.md §11). **Dedup-mark ordering:** identities are marked seen *after* the store flush (redo-not-skip on a crash — never a silent hole). **Representative prices (Golden Rule #1 honesty):** `ResultRow` mandates `avg_entry_price`/`avg_exit_price` but neither `ResultMetrics` nor `ClosedTrade` carries fill prices — so the projector re-simulates each finalist's (bounded) trades and derives the means from REAL OHLC (`bar.open` at `entry_ts` / `bar.close` at `exit_ts`, snapped 2dp via `round_money`). These are honest anchors from real bars, NOT fabricated; threading the exact fill price through `ClosedTrade` is a tracked follow-up. **Honest SLA (Rule #10):** this slice does NOT claim the 80-150K trials/sec or 2-4-day headline (those are the unverified XFAIL'd Rust-engine targets); the current Python path is orders slower and single-(inst,TF) only. **Honest envelope:** ✅ `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (162 stmts / 44 branches; one justified `# pragma: no cover` on the zero-trade fallback, unreachable since a ranked combo always clears the MIN_TRADES gate); ruff format + ruff check clean; mypy --strict 0; pyright 0/0/0; **55 tests** across all 7 layers (unit 42 / property 5 hypothesis / golden 4 / integration 2 / bench 4) — incl. the RERUN-SAFE idempotence oracle (rerun same dirs ⇒ `evaluated==0` + byte-identical store `content_hash`) and `verify_chain==3`. NOTE: gates were run on a local Python 3.12 venv (the repo requires 3.12 + the maturin-built `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels; the default sandbox is 3.11) — CI (3.12) is the merge oracle. **Out of scope (tracked follow-ups, NOT done here):** Stage 3 (CMA-ES) / Stage 4 (DSR/CPCV/WFO/lockbox); the full 63 inst-TF + 33B-trial production sweep; the Rust engine kernel; exact fill-price plumbing through `ClosedTrade`. **Builds on:** DEC-MASK-IDENTITY-001 (#551) · DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-001 (`build_bar_bits`) · DEC-TRADESIM-001 · DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 · DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 · DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001 · CLAUDE.md §9 (4-agent review) / §11 COMMON / Golden Rules #4/#5/#7/#8/#10.

553. **DEC-WAVE2-GUARANTEE-BLOCK-001 — embed a STANDING GUARANTEE & ASSURANCE block (verbatim) into every Wave-2 prompt in docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md** (2026-06-07, operator: "in every wave 2 prompt we need to always add this for guarantee ... deep research ... O(1) ... 100% hardening ... fully automated ... real-time guarantee and assurance ... no illusion or hallucination"). **Context:** `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` (the durable Wave-2 plan record, PR #461) holds the four copy-paste Wave-2 prompts (W2-a orchestrator+persistence, W2-b wire-in G&A, W2-c throughput SLA, W2-d overfitting gates).
