## DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (2026-06-07)

554. **DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 — Wave-2a: the full multi-parameter sweep ORCHESTRATOR (`brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py`) + `brutex sweep-all` launch entry point** (2026-06-07, Wave-2a per `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-a; preceded by a CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review — Plan + Explore + 2×general-purpose). **What shipped:** the orchestration layer that lifts the single-slice `run_persisted_sweep` (DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 #552) up to a FULL grid sweep over the outer product **instrument × timeframe × direction × K × stop-loss × take-profit × proximity**. For every tuple it builds a `SweepRunConfig`, loads that tuple's bars, calls `run_persisted_sweep`, and persists every ranked finalist to that tuple's OWN Parquet `ResultsStore` — composing the golden-locked single-slice runner and re-implementing none of it (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). **Public API (`brutex.engine.sweep_orchestrator`):** `SweepGridConfig` (the 7-axis frozen config, every axis order-preservingly de-duped + fully validated at construction), `Timeframe` (label + minutes), `SweepTuple` (+ `to_run_config`), `SweepGridSummary` (scalar tallies only → O(1) memory in the tuple count T), `count_sweep_tuples` (O(1) product), `iter_sweep_tuples` (deterministic `itertools.product` generator, O(1) per step), `bloom_capacity_hint` (per-grid mask-identity upper bound for sizing the shared Bloom), `tuple_store_path` / `load_or_create_store` / `make_store_for` (deterministic, collision-proof per-tuple paths), and `run_sweep_grid(grid, *, bars_for, store_for, dedup, audit, skip_empty=True, on_tuple=None) -> SweepGridSummary`. **Launch entry point:** `brutex sweep-all` (in the coverage-omitted `cli.py`) pre-loads each `(symbol, interval)` slice via the same Catalog/ReplayFeed path `brutex sweep` uses, derives a REAL reproducibility context — git HEAD `code_commit_sha`, a `brutex+trading_core` `indicator_version`, and a BLAKE3 content fingerprint of the loaded bars as the `data_snapshot_hash` (NEVER placeholders, Golden Rule #1) — then drives `run_sweep_grid` with a shared Bloom→exact `ComboDedup`, a hash-chained `AuditWriter`, and one load-or-create store per tuple. **Five hostile-review-driven correctness invariants (all resolved):** (1) **idempotent re-run is LOSSLESS** — the hostile review's P0 data-loss finding: a resume against a populated dedup makes the runner flush an EMPTY store over good results; fixed by `load_or_create_store` PRE-LOADING each tuple's existing Parquet so a fully-skipped re-run re-flushes the IDENTICAL finalist rows (golden-proven byte-identical, `evaluated==0`); (2) **collision-proof per-tuple paths** — `<root>/<instrument>/<tf>/<direction>_k<k>_<blake3-16>.parquet`; the digest covers the FULL canonical tuple identity (incl. `sl=None` vs a value, proximity, provenance) so distinct tuples never share a file (property-proven injective); (3) **one store per tuple** — `ResultsStore.flush` re-serialises the whole dict, so a shared store would be O(T·finalists) quadratic; per-tuple keeps each flush O(its finalists); (4) **shared dedup + single audit chain are safe** — the 9-field run-identity already includes instrument/tf/direction/mode/params so no two tuples alias; the grid is bracketed by `GRID_SWEEP_START`/`GRID_SWEEP_COMPLETE` and the loop is STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL (the audit writer is not thread-safe; parallel tuples are a tracked W2-c follow-up); (5) **fail-fast guards** — HOLD direction, empty axes, k-out-of-range, per-tuple `max_combos` AND grid-wide `max_tuples` are all rejected at construction so a grid can never crash mid-run after persisting earlier tuples; a tuple with no bars is skipped+counted (`skip_empty=True`) or raises a clear tuple-named error (`skip_empty=False`). **The orchestrator never marks dedup / flushes itself** — it hands `store`/`dedup`/`audit` to the runner and respects its redo-not-skip ordering. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** every PER-OP is O(1) (`count_sweep_tuples`, each `iter` step, `ComboDedup.seen`, one config build); the grid as a whole is INHERENTLY O(T) tuples × O(N) masks each = O(Σ Nᵢ) work + O(Σ finalists) stored rows — **NOT O(1) total, which would be physically impossible and is FORBIDDEN**; a resume even re-pays mask enumeration + the BLAKE3 run-id + the dedup probe per mask (only the trade-sim is skipped). ✅ `brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (176 stmts / 54 branches) — verified IN the strict per-module `--cov=brutex.engine` CI gate (no ci.yml change needed; the new module + `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_orchestrator.py` fall under the existing `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` glob, whole-package still 100% = 1684 stmts / 400 branches); ruff + ruff-format clean; mypy `--strict brutex` (190 files, 0); pyright `brutex tests` 0 errors (only pre-existing `reportPrivateUsage` warnings in untouched test files); **60 new tests across all 7 layers** (unit 48 / property 4 hypothesis / golden 3 incl. the lossless-resume oracle / integration 1 end-to-end 16-tuple grid / bench 2 O(1)-ratio: `count`+`iter`-step 1M-vs-1K ≤ ratio_ceiling). The full unit suite (4224 passed) + smoke gate stay green. NOTE: gates run on a local Python-3.12 venv with both `maturin develop --release` wheels (`fno_math` + `trading_core`); the default sandbox is 3.11 — CI (3.12 + wheels) is the merge oracle. **Out of scope (tracked Wave-2 follow-ups, NOT done here):** wiring the W2-b G&A modules (`sweep_audit`/`sweep_progress`/`sweep_checkpoint`/`sweep_cache`/`sweep_watchdog`) into the loop; the W2-c throughput SLA on the real path; the W2-d overfitting gates (CPCV/SPA/DSR/PBO) into ranking; a dashboard launch route (the CLI is the entry point per WAVE2_PLAN §W2-a "and/or"); a cross-process LMDB-backed shared dedup for resume-skip across restarts (the in-memory dedup + load-or-create already make re-runs byte-identical + lossless; persistent dedup only adds recompute-skip). **Builds on:** DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 (#552, the single-slice runner this orchestrates) · DEC-MASK-IDENTITY-001 (#551) · DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 (the per-tuple sink) · DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (#549, the W2-b modules this leaves for the follow-up) · `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-a · CLAUDE.md §9 (4-agent review) / §11 COMMON / Golden Rules #1/#4/#5/#7/#8/#10.

## DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (2026-06-07)

555. **DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 — fail-fast on a dead Dhan token (one loud alert, no doomed-call flood) + proactive RenewToken at pull start** (2026-06-07, operator: a real `make run` whose 24h web access token EXPIRED mid-pull). **Root cause (the live bug):** when the operator's manual 24-hour Dhan web token expired part-way through a bulk spot pull, every remaining symbol failed — most with `DH-901` "Client ID or user generated access token is invalid or expired" (HTTP 401 → `DhanAuthError`) and a few with `DH-906` "Invalid Token" (HTTP 400 → `DhanBadRequestError`). Because auth errors are classified terminal-per-symbol, the engine quarantined ~400 symbols ONE BY ONE (each firing ~1-2 doomed 401 calls → ~800 wasted calls + ~10 min of per-symbol WARNING spam), with NO single loud "your token died" alert and NO renewal — `renew_token()` existed (`POST /v2/RenewToken`) but was LATENT, wired into nothing. **Scope (operator-chosen, exactly two pieces; NO TOTP, NO new stored secrets, NO change to the 5 r/s rate logic):** **Piece 1 — fail-fast.** A single-source-of-truth predicate `errors.is_auth_failure(exc)` (True for `DhanAuthError` 401/403 OR a `DhanBadRequestError` carrying `DH-906`/"Invalid Token" — the token-invalid 400 masquerading as a bad request; `is_retryable` UNCHANGED, auth stays non-retryable) + a new wheel-free thread-safe one-way latch `auth_guard.AuthGuard` (`trip(cause)` idempotent first-cause-wins / `tripped()` / `cause()`, all O(1) under one `threading.Lock`). `ingest.ingest_spot`/`_ingest_one_window` take an `auth_guard`: a window worker (a) short-circuits to a no-op `skipped` outcome BEFORE pacing/any vendor call once the guard is tripped (so in-flight windows drain instantly, ZERO further doomed 401s), and (b) trips the guard on the first `is_auth_failure` then RE-RAISES (auth is non-retryable, must surface). `run_ingest.run_dhan_spot_ingest` builds ONE `AuthGuard` per run, threads it into every `ingest_spot`, and in the quarantine drain: an auth failure STILL records the `PairFailure` (re-tried next pull, never masked) but emits the loud `ingest.auth_aborted` WARNING **exactly once** (carrying pull_id + cause + "regenerate the 24h token at web.dhan.co (or it will auto-renew while active next run)") instead of the 400-line per-symbol flood; subsequent auth failures are recorded silently. New `DhanIngestReport` fields `auth_aborted: bool` + `auth_cause: str | None` are set from the guard. **Piece 2 — proactive RenewToken.** `auth.maybe_renew_token(client, *, pace, log) -> TokenInfo | None` (best-effort: logs `auth.renewed` INFO + returns the token on success; logs ONE `auth.renew_failed` WARNING + returns None on any `DhanError`; NEVER raises) is called ONCE at the start of a LIVE spot pull from `dashboard/pull_controller` (`_maybe_renew_adapter_token`, same no-op guard style as `_with_paced_client` — dry-run / injected-factory / non-`DhanMarketAdapter` paths skip it), rebuilding the adapter's client with the fresh access token via `replace` on a successful renew. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** RenewToken only refreshes an ACTIVE token — it CANNOT revive a dead one, so fail-fast still requires the operator to re-paste once IF the token died with no active token to renew; the proactive renew pushes expiry +24h BEFORE a long pull crosses the wall to make that rare. The guard short-circuits NEW windows but does NOT hard-cancel threads already mid-call in the pool (those finish their current call, then drain at the next window-start check). NO TOTP added (so this is NOT the §11 "zero clicks/day" guarantee — that needs TOTP, explicitly out of scope); NO new stored secrets; the rate logic is byte-unchanged (renew's physical POST is paced through the shared ≤5 r/s bucket). Only the `AuthGuard.trip`/`tripped`/`cause` ops are O(1); the pull itself is network-bound, not O(1). **New public symbols:** `errors.is_auth_failure`; `auth_guard.AuthGuard`; `auth.maybe_renew_token`; `run_ingest.DhanIngestReport.{auth_aborted, auth_cause}`. **Coverage / gates (sandbox-verified on system python3.12 + pytest/structlog/lmdb/fastbloom; CI 3.12+wheels is the merge oracle):** `auth_guard.py` 100% line+branch, `errors.py` 100%, `auth.py` 100%, `ingest.py` 100%, `run_ingest.py` 100% (each via its own test file); `pull_controller.py` unchanged coverage (the new helper's live token construction is `# pragma: no cover`, its non-live no-op branch IS covered); ruff format + ruff check clean (`brutex tests`); pyright 0/0 on all six touched modules; mypy --strict clean on the wheel-free modules (`auth_guard.py`/`errors.py`/`auth.py`) — `ingest.py`/`run_ingest.py`/`pull_controller.py` could NOT be mypy-checked locally because they transitively import the PEP-695 `brutex.orchestrator` chain + `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels (the sandbox mypy runs under 3.11, which cannot parse PEP-695); CI (3.12 + wheels) is the merge oracle for those. A strict per-module 100% CI gate was added for `brutex.adapters.dhan.auth_guard` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, mirroring the existing `dhan.errors`/`dhan.auth` gates). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-CREDS-WIRING-001 (creds resolution) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 / DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the window/pair fan-out the guard drains) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (the `_with_paced_client` replace pattern mirrored by `_maybe_renew_adapter_token`) · DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 (the sibling quarantine-branch classifier) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 (no hallucination) / #5 (O(1) guard ops) / #6 (≤5 r/s) / #8 (audit/observability) / #10 (honest envelope).

## DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 (2026-06-07)

556. **DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 — Wave-2c: resident bar window reused across masks + retire the 33B-trial SLA xfail (honest M4-Pro-gated absolute, CI keeps the O(1) RATIO gate)** (2026-06-07, Wave-2c per `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-c; preceded by a CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review — Plan + 2×Explore + general-purpose — confirming the whole workspace builds + the 511-test `brutex.engine` strict gate is green before AND after). **Problem (verified, file:line):** the single-slice `run_persisted_sweep` (#552) rebuilt the Stage-1A `bar_bits` (the expensive per-bar 52-condition evaluation) AND re-marshalled it Python→Rust for the Stage-1B count on EVERY grid tuple (`sweep_run.py:628,659`), even though `bar_bits` depends ONLY on `(bars, proximity, prior_n)` — so it is IDENTICAL across every `(direction, K, sl, tp)` tuple sharing one `(instrument, tf, proximity)`. The SLA bench `test_projected_33b_within_sla` was a strict-`xfail` because its proxy re-marshalled the whole 50K-bar window on every `count_supermask_u64s` call (pessimistic ~80-160×, projecting ~23 days for 33B trials). **What shipped:** (a) **`brutex/engine/sweep_kernel.py`** — `ResidentSweepKernel` builds `bar_bits` ONCE for one `(instrument, tf, proximity, prior_n)` and holds a resident Rust `Vec<u64>` (`ResidentBarBuffer` → `fno_math.ResidentBars`), so a Stage-1B count over many mask batches marshals only the (small) masks, never the (large) bar window; `count_hits(masks)` is **byte-identical** to the free `count_supermasks(bar_bits, masks)` (both delegate to the one shared Rust `count_one`, or its numpy fallback) and `prefilter(masks, min_hits)` is the resident Stage-1B drop. `ResidentKernelCache` is the bounded LRU (keyed `(instrument, tf, proximity, prior_n)`, capacity = the grid's proximity fan-out) the grid threads through its tuples. (b) **`run_persisted_sweep(..., kernel=None)`** — when a kernel is supplied it reuses the pre-built `bar_bits` + the resident count (a bar-count mismatch raises); `kernel=None` is the unchanged inline path. (c) **`run_sweep_grid(..., reuse_bar_bits=True)`** — the grid now builds each bar window ONCE per distinct `(instrument, tf, proximity, prior_n)` instead of once per tuple; `reuse_bar_bits=False` restores the legacy rebuild path. The reuse is proven **byte-identical** to the rebuild path (same per-tuple `store_content_hash`, golden parity test) — it changes only WHEN work runs, never WHAT the answer is (Golden Rule #4). (d) **`tests/bench/test_full_sweep_extrapolation.py`** — the SLA gate is **no longer `xfail`**: it now measures the REAL resident + rayon-parallel batched mask-AND kernel (a 256-mask batch over a 50K-bar resident window crosses the production `PARALLEL_WORK_THRESHOLD` 2^20 arm — the §3.3 bandwidth-bound dominant cost) and, following the `test_throughput_absolute.py` convention (DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001), asserts the 4-day M4 Pro SLA as a REAL hard gate ONLY under `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS=1` (the self-hosted runner, wired in `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml`) and **skips** on shared GHA (absolute ops/s there chronic-flakes per DEC-P0-020) — where CI keeps the O(1) RATIO gate (`test_throughput_canary.py`) + a 10 ms/trial regression floor. The projection is PRINTED on every runner. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10) — NO ILLUSION:** ✅ each hot-path OP is O(1)/bounded — `count_hits`/`prefilter` are O(N_masks·N_bars) compute + O(N_masks) marshal (the O(N_bars) marshal paid ONCE at construction), the cache is bounded `O(capacity·N_bars)`; **NOT O(1) total** — a 33B-trial grid is INHERENTLY O(Σ Nᵢ) work + O(Σ finalists) rows, and claiming O(1)-total is physically impossible + FORBIDDEN. 🟡 the gate proves only the **bandwidth-bound mask-AND kernel** meets the SLA; the full sweep additionally walks a per-surviving-mask **Python trade-sim** (NOT batched here — a tracked follow-up), so this is explicitly NOT a claim that the whole real sweep hits the SLA. 🟡 the absolute SLA pass is asserted on the M4 Pro runner (which this sandbox is not) — measured here on a multi-core Linux runner it projects ~3.8 days < 4-day SLA at ~5000 M mask·bar/s, but the BINDING figure is the M4 Pro CI run; if it ever exceeds 4 days the spec's §5 claim is re-stated (Golden Rule #1 + §8 — we never lie about wall time). ✅ **`brutex/engine` whole-package at 100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (1744 stmts / 410 branches incl. the new `sweep_kernel.py` 52 stmts / 6 branches + the new `sweep_run`/`sweep_orchestrator` reuse branches) — verified in the strict per-module `--cov=brutex.engine` CI gate (no ci.yml change needed; the new `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_kernel.py` falls under the existing `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` glob); **511 engine tests pass** (incl. 23 new across unit + property-style parity + golden byte-identical reuse + integration grid + worst-case empty/zero/oversized/mismatch/LRU-evict); ruff + ruff-format clean; mypy `--strict` + pyright `brutex tests` 0/0 on every touched file. NOTE: gates run on a local Python-3.12 venv with both `maturin develop --release` wheels (`fno_math` + `trading_core`); the default sandbox is 3.11 — CI (3.12 + wheels) + the M4 Pro self-hosted bench are the merge oracles. **Out of scope (tracked follow-ups, NOT done here):** a batched/Rust trade-sim (the residual per-mask Python bottleneck); parallel grid tuples (the audit writer is still single-threaded, #554); wiring the W2-b G&A modules + the W2-d overfit gates. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (#554, the grid this accelerates) · DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 (#552, the runner the kernel threads into) · DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 (#473, the prefilter this serves resident) · DEC-RUST-RESIDENT-BARS-001 (the `ResidentBars` buffer) · DEC-RUST-RAYON-SUPERMASK-001 (the parallel arm) · DEC-RUST-SUPERMASK-KERNEL-001 (#411, the `count_one` kernel) · DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 (the M4-Pro-gated absolute convention) · DEC-P0-062 (#199, the SLA validator this retires the xfail on) · `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-c · CLAUDE.md §9 / Golden Rules #1/#4/#5/#7/#10.

## DEC-RANKING-OVERFIT-001 (2026-06-07)

557. **DEC-RANKING-OVERFIT-001 — Wave-2d: the Stage-3 multiple-testing OVERFIT gate (6th gate) + Deflated-Sharpe ranking term, wired into `brutex.ranking.rank_combos` and the persisted sweep** (2026-06-07, Wave-2d per `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-d; preceded by a CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review — Plan + Explore + 2×general-purpose, incl. a hostile statistical-honesty pass). **What shipped:** the originally-reserved Stage-3 "lockbox/overfit" gate + its 0.05 composite term, realised from leaderboard SCALARS via the **Deflated Sharpe Ratio** (Bailey & López de Prado 2014). New pure module `brutex/ranking/overfit.py` (`OverfitGateConfig`, `PoolDispersion`, `pool_sharpe_dispersion`, `deflated_sharpe_for`, `passes_overfit_gate`) — stdlib + the closed-form `brutex.metrics.deflated_sharpe` engine ONLY (no `numpy`/`cascade`/wheel into the ranking import graph), so it shares the SAME Bailey-LdP engine the Stage-4 cascade's filter #2 uses (COMMON, no drift). `rank_combos(candidates, *, overfit=None)` gains the **6th gate + 8th z-term**: when `overfit` is set, every gate-survivor's Sharpe is deflated against the WHOLE candidate pool (trial count `N = len(candidates)`, cross-trial Sharpe variance `V`), combos below `dsr_min` are REJECTED, and survivors are down-ranked by their Deflated-Sharpe z-term (weight 0.05); `RankedCombo` gains a `deflated_sharpe: float | None` field. Threaded through `SweepRunConfig`/`run_persisted_sweep` + `SweepGridConfig`/`SweepTuple.to_run_config` + a `brutex sweep-all --overfit-gate [--dsr-min]` opt-in flag, so W2-a's persisted `ResultsStore` output is, by construction, the overfit-gated leaderboard. **`overfit=None` (the default) is byte-identical legacy** (the 5 single-result gates + 7 composite terms unchanged; every existing call site is positional/keyword-default so none changed). **Hostile-review-driven correctness (all resolved, the no-illusion findings):** (1) **`N` is authoritative ONLY inline** — `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md:383-385` pins `N` to the per-(instrument, TF) leaderboard trial count (a wrong `N` corrupts the threshold: pool-wide `N=1e12`⇒impossible Sharpe-23 bar). After persistence only `top_k` finalists survive and `N` is destroyed, so a post-store re-deflation against `N=len(rows)` would FABRICATE significance — explicitly FORBIDDEN and NOT provided; the gate runs at ranking time where the true `N` exists. (2) **Real moments, not silent Gaussian** — the inline path uses each combo's real `skewness` + EXCESS `kurtosis` (converted to non-excess via `+ GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS`, the `with_stage4_statistics` convention); Gaussian (skew 0 / excess-kurtosis 0) is a FLAGGED fallback used only when a combo's own moment is `None`, because Gaussian is anti-conservative for negatively-skewed fat-tailed returns. (3) **Abstain, never fabricate** — when the pool cannot be deflated (`< 2` finite Sharpes or zero cross-trial variance ⇒ `SR_0=0`, no deflation), the gate ABSTAINS (no rejection, no DSR term; the leaderboard falls back to its 7 single-result terms) rather than report the un-deflated probability as an "overfit-cleared" pass. (4) **Only DSR is scalar-computable** — CPCV / SPA-Reality-Check / PBO / Romano-Wolf / WFO / Monte-Carlo all need each candidate's per-period RETURN SERIES, absent from the scalar `ResultRow`; reconstructing them from win/loss aggregates would fabricate significance (forbidden), so the full cascade remains a documented return-series-sidecar seam (the same adapter `cascade.py` already defers), not claimed as delivered. (5) **Per-trade i.i.d. caveat stated** — `sample_length = total_trades` on the per-trade non-annualised Sharpe is self-consistent for PSR; the mild serial-dependence inflation of the effective track length is documented, not hidden. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** every PER-OP is O(1) — one closed-form `deflated_sharpe_for` is two Normal-CDF/quantile calls whose cost is INDEPENDENT of the trial count `N` (bench-proven: N=1M vs N=1K ratio < ceiling). Ranking a leaderboard is inherently O(survivors) deflations + O(survivors·log) sort — **NOT O(1) total, which is physically impossible and is FORBIDDEN**. The composite score's absolute scale is irrelevant (relative per-leaderboard ordering only), so the enabled-path weight sum of 1.05 changes ranking power, never correctness. ✅ `brutex/ranking/overfit.py` + `brutex/ranking/__init__.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** in the strict `--cov=brutex.ranking` gate (134 stmts / 34 branches; the new `overfit.py` auto-folds into the existing ci.yml gate — no ci.yml change needed); `brutex.engine` stays **100.00%** (the `overfit` field threading + `rank_combos(pairs, overfit=cfg.overfit)` pass-through covered); ruff + ruff-format clean; mypy `--strict` 0 (only the pre-existing `dashboard/app.py` pydantic-stub errors remain, untouched); pyright 0 errors / 0 warnings on every touched file; **all 7 test types** — unit (37 new in `test_ranking.py` across config/dispersion/deflation/gate/rank), integration (2 end-to-end `run_persisted_sweep` overfit-threading tests + 1 orchestrator `to_run_config` forward), property/hypothesis (6 invariants: DSR∈[0,1]∪{None}, dispersion sanity, DSR-monotone-in-Sharpe, gate-monotone-in-threshold, the excess→non-excess `+3` identity, gate-only-shrinks-or-abstains), golden byte-equality (a frozen overfit-gated leaderboard, repr-exact), bench/O(1) (the N-independent deflation ratio gate), stress (a 30,000-combo deflated sweep — partial survivor set, deterministic re-run), and a mutation sanity pass (hand-applied boundary `>=→>` and deflatable `>0→>=0` mutations are caught by the boundary/abstain tests; the raw mutmut 2.x survivors are non-semantic — `frozen=`/`slots=` decorator flags, error-message text matched by `pytest.raises(match=...)` substrings, type-annotation defaults). NOTE: gates run on a local Python-3.12 venv with both `maturin develop --release` wheels (`fno_math` + `trading_core`); the default sandbox is 3.11 — CI (3.12 + wheels) is the merge oracle. **Out of scope (tracked follow-ups, NOT done here):** the series-dependent cascade filters (CPCV/SPA/PBO/WFO/MC) over a future return-series sidecar; persisting the per-row Deflated Sharpe onto `ResultRow`; threading `overfit` through the non-persisted `sweep_driver.rank_sweep_over_bits` / `sweep_report` CLI `sweep` path (the persisted W2-d target is `run_persisted_sweep`). **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (#554, W2-a, the persisted output this gates) · DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 (#552, `run_persisted_sweep`) · DEC-RANKING-001 (the 5 gates + 7 terms + the reserved 0.05 slot) · DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001 (`cascade.py`, the full Stage-4 the DSR is a scalar subset of) · DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 (`with_stage4_statistics`, the excess→non-excess + None-guard convention this mirrors) · `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-d · `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md`:383-385 (the per-leaderboard `N`) · CLAUDE.md §9 (4-agent review) / §11 COMMON / Golden Rules #1/#4/#5/#10.

## DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001 (2026-06-07)

558. **DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001 — Wave-2b: wire the 5 sweep guarantee-&-assurance modules (BLAKE3 audit chain · progress · checkpoint · dedup cache · watchdog) LIVE into the orchestrator loop via a new `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py`** (2026-06-07, Wave-2b per `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-b; preceded by a CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review — Plan + Explore + 2×general-purpose). **What shipped:** the supervisor that makes the real-time guarantee + assurance layer LIVE — `run_supervised_grid(grid, *, bars_for, store_for, dedup, ingest_audit, guards, skip_empty, on_tuple, on_progress, watchdog_poll_seconds)` drives the deterministic `iter_sweep_tuples` enumeration and, for every grid tuple, (1) audit-logs to a BLAKE3 hash-chain (`SweepAuditWriter`: `SUPERVISOR_START` / `TUPLE_DONE` / `TUPLE_SKIPPED_CACHE` / `TUPLE_SKIPPED_RESUME` / `TUPLE_NO_BARS` / `SUPERVISOR_COMPLETE` / `SUPERVISOR_ABORT`), (2) ticks `SweepProgress` (percent / ETA / tuples-per-sec / survivors / skipped) surfaced on the NEW dashboard `GET /api/v1/sweep-progress` route + a v29 panel, (3) records a crash-safe `SweepCheckpointStore` high-water mark so a killed sweep RESUMES from the next tuple, (4) dedup-skips an already-completed tuple via the Bloom→LMDB `SweepCache`, and (5) heartbeats `SweepWatchdog`. It COMPOSES the golden-locked engine bricks via a NEW shared `run_one_tuple(...)` body extracted from `run_sweep_grid` (both drivers now call it — `run_sweep_grid`'s public signature / `SweepGridSummary` return / 5-line GRID audit framing are UNCHANGED, W2-a tests stay green) and does NOT edit `run_persisted_sweep` (DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 #552 keeps its 3-line audit + redo-not-skip ordering). `brutex sweep-all` now runs supervised (publishes a live `sweep-progress.json` the dashboard reads) and `cmd_dashboard` points the panel at it (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). **Correctness invariants (all hostile-review-driven):** (P0-1) the `SweepCache` tuple key is the FULL tuple+grid identity — incl. `condition_bits`, `k`, `top_k`, `min_hits`, `max_combos` + the three reproducibility hashes — STRICTER than the per-tuple Parquet path digest, because the cache-skip path skips the run entirely with no preload-and-reflush safety net, so a re-run with ANY changed knob computes a different key and is never falsely skipped (property-tested); (P0-2) the resume-skip + cache-skip paths NEVER construct or flush a `ResultsStore`, preserving W2-a's lossless re-run; (crash window) the checkpoint is recorded AFTER `run_one_tuple` returns, so a `SIGKILL` mid-tuple leaves that index un-recorded → it is re-processed on resume where the shared `ComboDedup` skips every already-flushed mask and `load_or_create_store` re-flushes byte-identically (redo-not-skip; never a double persist); (abort) any in-band `Exception` records a best-effort `progress.fail` + `SUPERVISOR_ABORT` (suppressed so a disk-full can't mask the root cause) then re-raises unchanged, and the watchdog daemon is always stopped in `finally`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — no illusion):** the supervised unit is the grid TUPLE; **mask-level (per-u64-mask) dedup is ALREADY provided by the shared `ComboDedup` inside `run_persisted_sweep`** (Bloom→exact on the 9-field run-identity) — the new `SweepCache` adds a COARSER, content-addressed tuple-level fast-skip on top; W2-b requirement (4) is thus satisfied at the mask grain by `ComboDedup` and at the tuple grain by `SweepCache` (neither is an O(1)-total-dedup claim). Every per-tuple op is O(1) (one cache probe + one audit append + one atomic checkpoint write + one progress mutation + one watchdog beat); the grid as a whole is INHERENTLY O(T) tuples × O(Nᵢ) masks = O(Σ Nᵢ) work plus O(T) flushes/fsyncs — **NOT O(1) total, which is physically impossible and FORBIDDEN**. **Watchdog detection is INTER-TUPLE only:** with `watchdog_poll_seconds` set a daemon thread polls `check_once` on a cadence while the main thread beats per tuple, so a tuple running past the timeout is detected; a hang INSIDE one tuple's mask loop (inside the golden-locked runner) is NOT detectable at sub-tuple grain without modifying that runner — a tracked follow-up, stated plainly (no over-claim). There are TWO audit chains by design: the BLAKE3 `SweepAuditWriter` supervisor chain (canonical per Golden Rule #4/#8) and the per-tuple engine `AuditWriter` chain `run_persisted_sweep` already emits. ✅ `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py` engineered for 100% line + branch under the strict `--cov=brutex.engine` gate (the new `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_supervisor.py` rides the existing `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` glob — no ci.yml change needed); new tests across all 7 layers (unit run/no-bars/cache-skip/resume-skip/abort/watchdog-thread + both `_drive_watchdog` branches + progress publish/read bridge; integration end-to-end supervised grid; property knob-sensitivity P0-1 guard; golden frozen BLAKE3 byte-equality for `grid_identity` + `tuple_cache_key`; bench `tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_supervisor_o1.py` per-tuple `tuple_cache_key` O(1)-ratio ≤ `ratio_ceiling`); dashboard route + state covered by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_progress.py`; ruff + ruff-format clean. NOTE: gates requiring the `fno_math` + `trading_core` wheels + Python 3.12 (PEP-695) run on CI — the default sandbox is 3.11 without the wheels, so **CI is the merge oracle** (as W2-a documented). **Out of scope (tracked Wave-2 follow-ups):** the W2-c throughput SLA on the real path; the W2-d overfitting gates (CPCV/SPA/DSR/PBO) into ranking; sub-tuple (intra-`run_persisted_sweep`) watchdog detection; parallel tuple execution. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (#554, the grid this wires into) · DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (#549, the 5 standalone G&A modules) · DEC-PHASE3-SWEEP-SLICE-001 (#552, the per-tuple runner) · DEC-MASK-IDENTITY-001 (#551) · `docs/WAVE2_PLAN.md` §W2-b · CLAUDE.md §9 (4-agent review) / §11 COMMON / Golden Rules #4/#5/#7/#8/#10.

559. **DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 — continuous background 12h keepalive so the Dhan 24h web access token never expires while the app is running** (2026-06-07, operator-confirmed; builds on DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 #555). **Goal:** Piece 2 of #555 renews the token ONCE at pull start, which still lets a token cross the 24h wall during a long-idle dashboard (no pull → no renew) or a multi-hour pull. This adds a CONTINUOUS in-process keepalive: a single daemon thread polls the token's expiry and fires `RenewToken` when the remaining life drops below **12 hours** (operator-chosen, NOT 2h — a 24h token renewed at its half-life always retains ≥12h of buffer, resilient to a restart or a missed cycle). **The token-provider/holder seam (the load-bearing design):** `RenewToken` INVALIDATES the old token the instant it issues the new one, so a client still holding the captured string would 401 on its next call. The fix is ONE shared mutable cell read live on every request: (1) a new wheel-free `token_holder.TokenHolder` (`get()`/`set()`, both O(1) under one `threading.Lock`) is the single runtime source of the current token; (2) `client.DhanClient` gains an injected `token_provider: Callable[[], str] | None` field (mirrors the existing `pace` `field(default=None)` pattern) — `_headers()` reads the `access-token` value from `token_provider()` when set, else the static `access_token` (so EVERY existing caller is byte-unchanged); (3) the keepalive writes each fresh token into the holder via `holder.set`, so a mid-life renew propagates INSTANTLY to BOTH in-flight window workers AND the next pull. **`token_keepalive.py` (new, wheel-free):** `RENEW_BEFORE_EXPIRY_S = 12*3600` (the named tunable threshold), `MAX_SLEEP_S = 3600` (hourly wake cap), `RETRY_WHEN_DEAD_S = 3600` (retry interval after a failed renew / no learnable expiry); `parse_expiry_deadline(expiry_time, *, now, log)` parses Dhan's IST `expiryTime` (`"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000"`, ms + no-ms formats, docs/dhan-ref/02) to an epoch deadline and on ANY parse failure logs ONE `auth.keepalive.expiry_unparsed` WARNING and falls back to `now()+24h` (NEVER crashes); `class TokenKeepalive(client, holder, *, pace, now=time.time, sleep=time.sleep, log)` puts 100% of the decision logic in the synchronous, injected-clock `_tick() -> float` (remaining = deadline − now(); if < 12h → best-effort `renew_token` [on success `holder.set` + refresh deadline + `auth.renewed`; on `DhanError` log ONE `auth.renew_failed`, KEEP the old deadline, return `RETRY_WHEN_DEAD_S`]; else sleep `min(remaining − 12h, MAX_SLEEP_S)`; first tick with unknown deadline renews immediately to LEARN the expiry), with a THIN `start()`/`stop()`/`_run()` thread wrapper (one daemon thread looping `self._stop.wait(self._tick())` until stopped). **Wiring (best-effort, honest):** at dashboard startup (`app.py` `@app.on_event("startup")`) when live creds resolve, `pull_controller.start_token_keepalive(session_rate=...)` builds ONE `TokenHolder` seeded with the resolved token, INSTALLS it via `set_live_token_holder` (a process-wide live-path singleton mirroring the `_session_rate` holder pattern), builds a renew `DhanClient(token_provider=holder.get, ...)` paced through the session ≤5 r/s bucket, and starts ONE `TokenKeepalive` for the app's lifetime (stopped + holder cleared on `@app.on_event("shutdown")`); `_build_live_spot_adapter` now wires `token_provider=_LIVE_TOKEN_HOLDER.get` into every per-pull/per-worker client so a renew propagates instantly. Phase-1 `_maybe_renew_adapter_token` (renew-at-start) is KEPT (composes fine, belt-and-suspenders). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — NO illusion):** "never expires while running" holds ONLY while (a) the token is web-generated (RenewToken refuses TOTP-minted tokens), (b) the process is running to fire the timer (in-process, not a cron), and (c) the FIRST token is active (RenewToken cannot revive a dead one — physics). This is NOT the §11 "zero clicks/day across restarts/downtime" guarantee (that needs TOTP, explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here). NO TOTP, NO new stored secrets, NO change to the 5 r/s rate logic. Steady-state ≈ 2 RenewToken POSTs/day — negligible vs the 100,000/day quota, each paced ≤5 r/s. Only the per-op holder/keepalive work is O(1); nothing here is "O(1) total". **New public symbols:** `token_holder.TokenHolder`; `token_keepalive.{TokenKeepalive, parse_expiry_deadline, RENEW_BEFORE_EXPIRY_S, MAX_SLEEP_S, RETRY_WHEN_DEAD_S}`; `client.DhanClient.token_provider`; `pull_controller.{set_live_token_holder, start_token_keepalive}`. **Coverage / gates (sandbox-verified on system python3.12 + pytest/structlog; CI 3.12+wheels is the merge oracle):** `token_holder.py` 100% line+branch (14 stmts), `token_keepalive.py` 100% line+branch (60 stmts / 10 branches) — both proven locally with fake clock + fake transport (no real threads/sleeps); the new `token_provider` branch in `client.py` covered by `test_dhan_client.py` (provider-overrides-header + None→static); the `set_live_token_holder` install/clear seam covered in `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` (the live builder + `start_token_keepalive` + the FastAPI startup/shutdown glue are `# pragma: no cover`, matching existing live-path pragmas). 107 touched-area tests pass. Strict per-module 100% CI gates added for `brutex.adapters.dhan.token_holder` + `brutex.adapters.dhan.token_keepalive` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, mirroring the `dhan.auth_guard` gate). ruff format + ruff check clean (`brutex tests`); mypy --strict / pyright on the wheel-free modules locally — `pull_controller.py`/`app.py` transitively import the PEP-695 orchestrator chain + pydantic/fastapi absent in the 3.11 sandbox, so CI (3.12 + wheels) is the type/import oracle for those (honestly noted, per Golden Rule #10). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (#555, the fail-fast latch + `maybe_renew_token` + `_maybe_renew_adapter_token` this composes with) · DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 (the `SessionRateController` per-session holder pattern mirrored by the token holder + the pace bucket) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the shared-client worker fan-out the holder propagates to) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #5 (O(1) per-op) / #6 (≤5 r/s) / #8 (observability) / #10 (honest envelope) / #11 COMMON (one token source).

560. **DEC-AUDIT-VERIFY-UNIFY-001 — `brutex audit verify` auto-detects + verifies EITHER hash-chain format (SHA-256 ingest OR BLAKE3 supervisor); a valid supervisor chain is no longer falsely reported corrupt** (2026-06-07, operator operability bug; preceded by a CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review — Plan + Explore + 2×general-purpose). **Root cause (verified live):** BruteX writes two hash-chained, append-only `.jsonl` audit logs with an IDENTICAL line shape (the same 8 keys) but DIFFERENT chain algorithms — the ingest pipeline's **SHA-256** chain (`brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, e.g. the per-combo `sweep-all.jsonl`) and the sweep SUPERVISOR's **BLAKE3** chain (`brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py`, `sweep-all-supervisor.jsonl`, Golden Rule #4). `brutex audit verify` hard-wired ONLY the SHA-256 `verify_chain`, so running it on a perfectly valid BLAKE3 supervisor chain raised a FALSE `AUDIT CHAIN CORRUPT` (wrong verifier, not real corruption) — an operator could not verify the supervisor chain from the CLI. Reproduced before the fix (a 3-entry valid supervisor chain → `verify_chain` 3/VALID under `engine.sweep_audit`, yet `brutex audit verify` exited 2 with "corruption at seq=0 … content tampered"). **Fix (1 new module + a thin CLI shim, NO hash logic duplicated — §11 COMMON):** new top-level `brutex/audit_verify.py` REUSES both existing `verify_chain`s. `sniff_format(path)` reads only the FIRST non-empty JSONL line (O(1)) and recomputes its self-hash under each algorithm — because the two `compute_hash` preimages are byte-identical and differ ONLY in the hash function, EXACTLY one algorithm reproduces a genuine entry's stored `entry_hash`, naming the format (cross-algorithm preimage collision ≈ 2⁻²⁵⁶, treated as impossible). `auto_verify` then delegates to that format's own `verify_chain`; an empty file is trivially valid (`VerifyResult(None, 0)`); a first entry whose hash matches NEITHER algorithm is corruption carrying the entry's real `seq` (not a hard-coded 0). `brutex audit verify <file>` gains `--format {orchestrator,sweep,auto}` (default `auto`) and prints which format + entry count. **Exit codes preserved + hardened:** 0 OK, 1 user error (missing file / malformed JSON / wrong-shape line), 2 corruption — the CLI catches the corruption subclasses FIRST (each subclasses its base `*AuditError`, so base-first would mis-map corruption to exit 1; the prior handler also never caught the base error, so a malformed line crashed with a traceback — now a clean exit 1). The `audit_verify` import is done LAZILY inside the CLI handler so non-audit commands (`brutex version`, etc.) stay wheel-free. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — no illusion):** detection is O(1) (first line only) but **verification is inherently O(N)** over N entries (one O(1) hash-recompute + compare each) — NOT an O(1)-total claim, which is physically impossible. Both underlying verifiers require a **seq-0 origin**, so a legitimately rotated/truncated segment starting at seq ≥ 1 is reported corrupt by either format — pre-existing behaviour this module inherits, stated plainly. A genesis line whose `prev_hash` was hand-edited on an otherwise-valid chain sniffs as "matches neither" and is reported corrupt (correct verdict; the format is then undetermined — diagnosed honestly in the message). **Tests / gates:** `brutex/audit_verify.py` ships at **100% line + branch** (`tests/unit/test_audit_verify.py`: sniff for each format + empty + all-blank + leading-blank-skip + tampered-genesis + missing + malformed-first-line; explicit `verify` for each format + wrong-format-corrupt; `auto_verify` empty/each-valid/each-corrupt/genesis-indeterminate/malformed-later-line/missing; `verify_audit_file` auto + each explicit; a hypothesis property that any honest chain of either format auto-verifies and any single-byte tamper is caught; frozen golden self-hashes per algorithm; an O(1)-sniff bench; a 5,000-entry stress verify) plus `tests/integration/test_cli_audit_verify.py` (the original bug + the full exit-code contract + `--format` override; `brutex/cli.py` is coverage-omitted). A strict per-module 100% CI gate for `brutex.audit_verify` was added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (mirroring the `brutex.engine` gate). ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict brutex` (197 files) + `pyright` 0/0; bandit clean. Verified locally on a Python 3.12 venv with the `fno_math` + `trading_core` wheels built (CI 3.12 + wheels is the merge oracle, per the W2 precedent). **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001 (#558, the BLAKE3 supervisor chain this verifies) · DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (#549, `engine.sweep_audit`) · NFR-OBS-003 / Golden Rules #4 (BLAKE3) / #8 (audit trail) / #10 (honest envelope) / #11 COMMON (reuse, no copy-paste).

561. **DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-GET-001 — `RenewToken` is an HTTP GET (headers-only, NO body), not a POST** (2026-06-07, operator-confirmed). **Bug (proven, not a guess):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/auth.py::renew_token` called `client.post_json(ENDPOINT_RENEW_TOKEN, {})` — a POST with a JSON request body. The authoritative reference, the **official DhanHQ Python SDK** (`dhan-oss/DhanHQ-py`, `src/dhanhq/auth.py`), calls `RenewToken` as `requests.get(url, headers={"access-token": ..., "dhanClientId": ...})` — an **HTTP GET, headers-only, NO body**. Real Dhan rejects the wrong-method POST+body with `HTTP 400 DH-905` "Missing required fields, bad values for parameters", so proactive renew (#555) + the 12h keepalive (#559) ALWAYS failed and silently fell back. Our `DhanClient` was POST-only (`_post_once` + `urllib_transport` hardcoded `method="POST"`), so it physically could not issue the GET. The repo doc `docs/dhan-ref/02-authentication.md` also wrongly said `POST .../RenewToken` (a doc error — Dhan's real `curl` has no `-d`, i.e. a GET). **Fix (scope: make RenewToken a GET; everything else byte-identical):** (1) `client.DhanClient` generalised to support GET while keeping the POST path bit-for-bit: the `Transport` Protocol `__call__` + `urllib_transport` gain a keyword `method: str = "POST"` (default preserves every existing POST caller/fake-transport signature; the GET path passes `method="GET"` to `urllib.request.Request(..., method=method)`); the single physical-attempt method `_post_once` is refactored into a shared `_send_once(method, endpoint, body)` (same `_guard_url`, same `meter.record_issue` + `rate.breach` WARNING metered against the 5 r/s cap, same `_observe`, same status→errors map + JSON parse — a GET sends an empty `b""` body and `method="GET"`); the bounded latency-hygiene fast-retry loop is factored into a shared `_with_fast_retry(method, endpoint, body)` so BOTH `post_json` and the new `get_json` reuse the SAME pace + meter + breach + bounded-fast-retry path (DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 / DEC-DHAN-RATE-RESIDUAL-HARDEN-001 apply to GET identically); new `get_json(endpoint) -> dict[str, object]` runs that loop with `_send_once("GET", endpoint, None)` (no body). `post_json(endpoint, body)` is behaviour-byte-identical (POST + body) — every existing caller/test unchanged. (2) `auth.renew_token` swaps `client.post_json(ENDPOINT_RENEW_TOKEN, {})` → `client.get_json(ENDPOINT_RENEW_TOKEN)`; the `(pace or client.pace)()` initial-pace gating, the `accessToken`/`expiryTime` parse, and the `DhanAuthError` on a malformed response are unchanged; `maybe_renew_token` is unchanged (still best-effort, never raises). (3) Doc corrections (Golden Rule #1, no hallucination): `docs/dhan-ref/02-authentication.md` RenewToken `POST` → `GET` (headers `access-token` + `dhanClientId`, NO body; cites the official SDK as the source); CLAUDE.md §6 "Auth — default approach" row annotated GET-headers-only with the same SDK citation. **New / changed public surface:** `client.DhanClient.get_json(endpoint)` (new); `client.Transport.__call__` + `client.urllib_transport` gain `method: str = "POST"` (additive, default-compatible). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this makes renew actually WORK for an ACTIVE, WEB-GENERATED token — the case #555/#559 always intended. A non-web/TOTP-minted or already-EXPIRED token will now get Dhan's CORRECT error (RenewToken refusing it) instead of a misleading wrong-method DH-905; `maybe_renew_token` still swallows that to ONE `auth.renew_failed` WARNING and proceeds. TOTP `generateAccessToken` remains the separate restart-proof / post-expiry path (OUT OF SCOPE here, per §11 honest-envelope). NO change to the 5 r/s rate logic, the token bucket, or the bounded fast-retry budget; the GET is metered + paced exactly like a POST. **Coverage / gates (sandbox-verified on python3.12 + pytest/structlog via `pip --break-system-packages`; CI 3.12+wheels is the merge oracle):** `client.py` + `auth.py` are wheel-free and import on 3.12; strict per-module 100% line+branch on `brutex.adapters.dhan.client` AND `brutex.adapters.dhan.auth` (`--cov-fail-under=100`). New tests: `test_dhan_client.py` adds a method-aware fake transport + `TestGetJson` (GET verb + empty body + headers; issue-meter + `rate.breach` on a GET; GET timeout→`DhanTimeoutError`; POST still POST+body) and a GET fast-retry+pace test in `TestFastRetry`; `test_dhan_auth.py` renew tests now assert a GET with NO body (not a POST `{}`) and keep the malformed-response→`DhanAuthError` test. `urllib_transport` stays `# pragma: no cover` (thin urllib I/O shim). **Source:** official DhanHQ Python SDK `dhan-oss/DhanHQ-py` `src/dhanhq/auth.py` (`requests.get(url, headers=headers)`). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 (#559, the keepalive that fires RenewToken) · DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (#555, `maybe_renew_token`/proactive renew) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 / DEC-DHAN-RATE-RESIDUAL-HARDEN-001 (the metered+paced fast-retry loop now shared by GET) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 (no hallucination — cite the SDK) / #5 (O(1) — bounded attempts) / #6 (≤5 r/s — GET metered + paced) / #10 (honest envelope).

562. **DEC-SWEEP-WINNERS-BY-NAME-001 — persist the winning strategy mask as a readable surface (u64 `mask_bits` + decoded `condition_names`) + a `brutex results show` read-back leaderboard so an operator sees WHICH conditions won, by name** (2026-06-07, operator request; builds on DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 / W2-a + DEC-RESULT-STORE-001). **Problem (code-traced):** `brutex/engine/results_store.py` keyed each ranked finalist ONLY by the 9-field BLAKE3 `run_id`, with the 52-condition strategy mask folded INTO that hash and never stored as a readable column (the old module docstring called the readable-mask column a "future schema slot"). So a persisted sweep tree answered "what survived?" only as opaque hex keys — the explainability the brute-force search exists to deliver (CLAUDE.md §1) was unreachable without re-running the decoder. **Fix (2 src cols + 1 nullable metric + 1 read-back module + 1 CLI subcommand):** (1) `ResultRow` gains `mask_bits: int` (the u64 combo mask, validated `0 <= mask_bits <= MASK_BITS_MAX = 2**52-1` so reserved bits 52..63 are rejected and the value always fits Parquet `Int64`) and a DERIVED `condition_names: str` (`field(init=False)`, set in `__post_init__` to `" AND ".join(matched_condition_names(mask_bits))`) sourced bit-for-bit from the SINGLE source of truth `brutex.vocabulary.describe.matched_condition_names` (IMPORTED, never copy-pasted — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON), so the readable column can NEVER drift from the mask; (2) `ResultRow` also carries a nullable `deflated_sharpe: float | None` (the multiple-testing-adjusted Sharpe from DEC-RANKING-OVERFIT-001, `None` when the pool was not deflatable) for leaderboard transparency — finite-or-`None` validated, `-0.0`→`+0.0` canonicalised, round-trips as a Parquet null; (3) `sweep_run.ranked_combo_to_result_row` stamps `mask_bits=rc.mask` + `deflated_sharpe=rc.deflated_sharpe` at persist time (the orchestrator already holds `rc`); (4) new wheel-free `brutex/engine/results_report.py` discovers every per-tuple Parquet under a results root (`**/*.parquet`, sorted), merges them into one read-only `ResultsStore` (cross-file `run_id`s are globally unique → no alias), and renders a ranked leaderboard showing rank · instrument · tf · direction · condition NAMES · net P&L (`format_inr`, 2dp) · #trades · win-rate · Sharpe · Deflated-Sharpe · gate; (5) `brutex results show --results-root <dir> [--top N --sort-by {sharpe,sortino,calmar,pnl,win,trades,pf}]` (default `--top 20 --sort-by sharpe`) prints it. **Determinism preserved (Golden Rule #4/#7):** flush still sorts by `run_id` + pins the polars schema (new cols slot into the fixed column order: identity→mask→money→counts→metrics→deflated→prices), so the byte-identical re-flush + idempotent O(1) append/dedup are unchanged; but discovering + merging + ranking N finalists is inherently O(N) work + O(N) memory (sized for the funnel's 10²–10⁴ finalists, the same sizing `ResultsStore` assumes) — NO O(1)-total claim is made (that would be a hallucination). **Coverage / gates (sandbox-verified on python3.12 venv + built `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels; CI 3.12+wheels is the merge oracle):** `results_store.py` + `results_report.py` + `sweep_run.py` at 100% line+branch under the existing strict `--cov=brutex.engine` gate (572 engine unit tests pass — `brutex.engine.results_report` is auto-covered by the `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` glob, so NO new ci.yml gate is needed); ## DEC-SWEEP-RUST-TRADESIM-001 (2026-06-07)

563. **DEC-SWEEP-RUST-TRADESIM-001 — move the hot trade-sim + per-mask entry projection into a RESIDENT Rust kernel (`fno_math.ResidentSweepSim`), bars loaded ONCE per (instrument, tf) and reused across all masks; batch + rayon-parallel; bit-identical to the Python `TradeSimWalker`** (2026-06-07, follow-on to DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 #467 / W2-c; preceded by a CLAUDE.md §9 deep-research pass — Explore [CI/test-gate map] + general-purpose [hostile bit-identity port checklist of `trade_sim.py`]). Entry numbered **563** (560 = DEC-AUDIT-VERIFY-UNIFY-001, 561 = DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-GET-001, 562 = DEC-SWEEP-WINNERS-BY-NAME-001 all merged to main ahead of this; this takes the next free number to avoid an append collision). **Why:** W2-c made the Stage-2 SUPERSET *count* resident (`fno_math.ResidentBars`), but the per-surviving-mask TRADE-SIM still ran the Python `TradeSimWalker.push` state machine — O(1) per bar, but invoked ~33B× per full sweep, where the interpreter per-bar overhead dominates the measured end-to-end **~43–91 combos/s** (instrument-mix dependent, the honest envelope from this task's brief). This ports that per-bar SL/TP/forced-exit walker into a branch-predictable Rust loop over **resident `Vec<i64>` price columns**, so a whole mask grid is simulated without re-marshalling the bar window per combo. **What shipped (Rust, `rust/fno-math/src/trade_sim.rs`, registered in `lib.rs`):** a pure-Rust `Walker` that is a faithful port of `TradeSimWalker` (the hostile checklist's traps reproduced verbatim — exit precedence **pending-next-open → forced-15:20 → SL/TP → Mode-B signal → still-open**, so a pending next-open exit fills BEFORE forced is even checked; the three excursion folds — full `(high,low)` on a normal bar, `(open,open)` on a pending/forced exit, NOTHING on the end-of-data close; `finish()` silently closes a still-pending exit at the last bar's CLOSE; the exit bar consumes the entry signal; an entry landing on a forced bar is dropped), plus a `#[pyclass(frozen)] ResidentSweepSim` holding resident OHLC paisa + `is_forced` flags + `bar_bits`, exposing `simulate_masks(...) -> Vec<Vec<(pnl,mfe,mae,holding,entry_idx,exit_idx)>>` and a `count_trades(...)` throughput fast-path (both serial below the `1<<20` mask·bar threshold, order-preserving `par_iter` above — mirrors DEC-RUST-RAYON-SUPERMASK-001 #417). **Bit-identity design (Golden Rule #4) — the load-bearing decision:** the two seams a naive port gets wrong — the Decimal-rupee→int64-paisa rounding (`stage1a._price_to_paisa`, `ROUND_HALF_UP`) AND the tf-aware 15:20-IST forced-exit detection (`calendars.nse.is_forced_exit_bar`, UTC→IST) — STAY in Python (the single source of truth, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) and are computed ONCE per window; the kernel receives the resulting int64 columns + bool flags, so it depends on NEITHER and reproduces only the state-machine branch order. **Python seam (`brutex/engine/rust_trade_sim.py`, new):** `ResidentTradeSim(bars, bar_bits, *, tf_minutes)` derives the paisa columns + forced flags via those canonical seams, builds the resident kernel (or, when the maturin wheel is absent, transparently FALLS BACK to `trade_sim.simulate_trades` per mask — the SAME oracle, so never a silent divergence — mirroring `combo_mask.ResidentBarBuffer`); `.simulate_masks(masks, *, direction, stop_loss_paisa, take_profit_paisa, policy) -> list[list[ClosedTrade]]` maps the `FillPolicy` to the kernel's 3 flags and the per-mask trade tuples back to `ClosedTrade` (idx→bar timestamps). **Throughput / SLA (Golden Rule #10 — brutally honest, measured NOT fabricated):** `tests/bench/test_trade_sim_throughput.py` measures REAL combos/s of `count_trades` over a resident window and PRINTS it on every runner; the **O(1)-per-(mask·bar) ratio** gate (`tests/bench/_o1_tiers.ratio_ceiling`, 8× shared-CI / strict 1.1× M4-Pro) + a per-combo regression floor are the ACTIVE shared-CI gates; the **absolute ≥50 M mask·bar/s SLA assertion is gated to the M4 Pro self-hosted runner** (`BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS=1`, per DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 / DEC-P0-020) — which is currently OFFLINE (queues indefinitely), so this PR does NOT flip `test_projected_33b_within_sla` to a hard pass on shared CI; it documents the precise hardware envelope (the task's explicit "OR document" path) and the kernel measurement is the input that runner will gate once registered. **NOT claimed:** O(1)-total for a sweep (inherently O(N_masks·N_bars) — FORBIDDEN); that the full real sweep hits the SLA (the per-mask `compute_metrics` still runs in Python — a tracked follow-up); that the M4 Pro number is known (the runner is offline). **Testing (7 types):** Rust `cargo test --release` 23 new unit cases (every exit kind + same-bar tie BUY/SELL + next-open + forced + end-of-data + parallel-arm parity + construction validation via a pure `build()` returning `Result<_,String>` so no PyErr links under the no-libpython `cargo test`, mirroring `count_supermasks_scoped`) — **519/519 pass**, `cargo fmt`/`clippy -D warnings` clean; Python `tests/unit/test_engine_rust_trade_sim.py` (100% line+branch on `brutex.engine.rust_trade_sim` via the existing `--cov=brutex.engine` glob gate — Rust path AND forced-fallback AND the `except` import-shadow branch), `tests/property/test_trade_sim_rust_parity.py` (hypothesis: kernel == `simulate_trades` oracle field-for-field over random feeds/masks/params/policies incl. forced-crossing windows), `tests/golden/test_trade_sim_rust_golden.py` (frozen curated corpus kernel==oracle + one hand-computed absolute trade catching shared drift), `tests/bench/...` (throughput + O(1) ratio + regression floor). The `fno_math` `.pyi` stub + `__init__.py` re-export `ResidentSweepSim` (pyright/mypy strict). **Honest sandbox envelope:** Rust verified locally (cargo 1.94, 519 tests + fmt + clippy green); Python ruff format+check clean; the wheel can't be built on the local Py3.11/abi3-py312 sandbox and `combo_mask` imports `fno_math` at module top, so the Python tests + golden parity + bench run in CI (3.12 + wheels) — CI is the merge oracle, stated per Golden Rule #10. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 (#467, the resident `ResidentBars` count path this extends to the trade-sim) · DEC-RUST-RESIDENT-BARS-001 (#413, the resident-buffer + pure-core-no-PyErr pattern) · DEC-RUST-RAYON-SUPERMASK-001 (#417, the serial/parallel threshold + order-preserving collect) · DEC-TRADESIM-001 (the `TradeSimWalker` semantics ported) · DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 / DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 (the two-tier bench gate) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #4 (bit-identity) / #5 (O(1) per-op) / #10 (honest envelope) / #11 COMMON (one paisa/forced source).

564. **DEC-CATALOG-RECONCILE-WIRE-001 — register Parquet partitions in the DuckDB catalog so a real pull is sweep-able (no production ingest sink ever wired the catalog → `sweep-all` saw zero bars on every platform)** (2026-06-07, surfaced by a live end-to-end sweep run). **Bug (proven by a real run + repro, not a guess):** `brutex sweep-all` reads bars ONLY via `Catalog.get_bars` → `Catalog.list_partitions`, which queries the DuckDB `partitions` table. That table is populated ONLY by `ParquetBarSink.append` and ONLY when the sink holds a catalog (`sink.py:189` `if self._catalog is not None`). EVERY production sink construction passed NO catalog — `cli.py` `_build_live_dhan_spot` + the dry-run fetch, `dashboard/pull_controller.py:457`, and `dashboard/app.py:2358` all built `ParquetBarSink(writer=ParquetWriter(lake_root=...))` (the `catalog=None` default; the catalog's own docstring even noted "the live spot path passes `catalog=None` today, but tests wire one"). So `fetch`/pull wrote Parquet to disk but NEVER recorded partitions; `coverage_reconcile` reconciles the coverage LEDGER, not the `partitions` table; nothing else scans the lake into it. Net: after ANY real pull — including the operator's dashboard "Pull spot" on the M4 Pro — `brutex sweep-all` printed `[brutex] no bars … (lake=…)` and exited 1. The sweep integration tests passed only because they seed the catalog directly via `Catalog.upsert`, bypassing the real ingest path. Reproduced live: `fetch --dry-run` then `sweep-all` → "no bars"; the same lake with the fix → 2708 combos evaluated, Parquet results + both audit chains + checkpoint written. **Fix (operator chose BOTH halves; CLAUDE.md §9 hostile-review mindset + §11 COMMON — reuse `parse_partition_path` / `CatalogEntry`, no copy-paste):** (a) READ-side repair — new `brutex/data/catalog_reconcile.py` `reconcile_catalog_from_lake(*, lake_root, catalog, exchange=None, segment=None, symbol=None, interval=None)` globs the `bars/<exchange>/<segment>/<symbol>/<interval>/<year>/<month>.parquet` tree (each unset coord widening to `*`), reads only each file's `timestamp` column for `row_count`/`first_ts`/`last_ts`, sets `raw_hash = sha256(file bytes)` (bit-identical to what `ParquetWriter` records, so re-reconcile is a no-op upsert) + `fetched_at = file mtime` (deterministic), and upserts one `CatalogEntry` per partition; unparseable paths + zero-row files are skipped (counted). `cmd_sweep_all` now auto-runs it for the swept coordinates BEFORE reading, so an ALREADY-pulled lake (the operator's Mac lake) is sweep-able with NO re-pull; a new `brutex catalog reconcile [--lake-root]` command reconciles the whole lake on demand. (b) WRITE-side — `cli.py` `cmd_fetch` now opens a `Catalog` (under a `contextlib.nullcontext(None)` for `--inspect`, which persists nothing) and passes it into both the dry-run and live (`_build_live_dhan_spot(..., catalog=cat)`) sinks, so future CLI pulls self-register; the catalog's existing lock serialises upserts under the parallel-window fan-out (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — no illusion):** reconciliation is **O(P) one-time** over P partition files (each one O(1) sha256 + a single-column read), NOT in the per-combo hot loop and NOT an O(1)-total claim. It is additive (upsert-only): a partition whose Parquet was deleted leaves a stale catalog row (this append-only lake does not delete partitions). The DASHBOARD pull's write-time self-registration is intentionally NOT wired here — its `adapter_factory` seam + async pull are `# pragma: no cover` (untestable in CI) and threading a long-lived DuckDB connection through the concurrent path is a separate reviewed change; dashboard-pulled lakes are FULLY covered by the read-side auto-reconcile (the sweep rebuilds the catalog from the Parquet truth regardless of how it was pulled). The end-to-end sweep was exercised on SYNTHETIC `fetch --dry-run` bars (this run is a Linux cloud box with no real Dhan lake/creds) and produced 0 ranked winners — a degenerate-synthetic-data artifact, NOT real alpha; real winners require the operator's M4 Pro lake (out of scope for this fix). **Tests / gates:** `brutex/data/catalog_reconcile.py` ships at **100% line + branch** (`tests/unit/test_catalog_reconcile.py` — `_partition_files` missing-dir/globbed/coord-filter; reconcile register+counts, `raw_hash`==sha256(bytes), first/last-ts span, coord-filtered, idempotent, unparseable-path skip, zero-row skip, empty-lake no-op, get_bars-readable-after-reconcile; `_as_utc` tz-aware/tz-non-utc/tz-naive; a parametrized property that every written partition registers) + `tests/bench/test_catalog_reconcile_o1.py` (per-partition O(1)-in-P ratio gate). A strict per-module 100% CI gate for `brutex.data.catalog_reconcile` added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. `cli.py` is coverage-omitted; the dashboard builders are `# pragma: no cover`. ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict brutex` (198 files) + `pyright brutex tests` 0 new errors; verified on a Python 3.12 venv with the `fno_math` + `trading_core` wheels built (CI 3.12 + wheels is the merge oracle). **Builds on:** DEC-COVERAGE-CATALOG-001 (the 100% `catalog.py` this reads through) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the catalog lock that makes the wired sink concurrency-safe) · DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (the sibling coverage-ledger reconcile) · DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (#465, the `sweep-all` this unblocks) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #5 (O(1) per partition) / #7 (idempotent) / #9 (hostile review) / #10 (honest envelope) / #11 (COMMON).

## DEC-CASCADE-WIRE-001 (2026-06-07)

566. **DEC-CASCADE-WIRE-001 — auto-wire the Stage-4 nine-filter cascade onto every sweep's top-K winners (AUTOMATIC) + a manual `brutex cascade <run-id>` CLI subcommand and dashboard "Run cascade" button, both through one pure core so AUTO == MANUAL byte-for-byte** (2026-06-07; closes the #1 re-ranked gap of DEC-GAP-ANALYSIS-001 #565 — "cascade (manual+automatic)" — i.e. gap rows (4) "auto-wire the cascade into `sweep_orchestrator`" + (c) "no full-cascade CLI nor auto-on-sweep"). Entry numbered **566** (565 = DEC-GAP-ANALYSIS-001 landed ahead of this on the merge; next free number to avoid an append collision). **Why:** `brutex/metrics/cascade.py` (`run_stage4_cascade`, DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001 #436) chains all nine statistical filters (DSR/CPCV/SPA/PBO/Romano-Wolf/WFO/Lockbox/Monte-Carlo) but consumes hand-built `CandidateInput`s; its docstring explicitly deferred *"the production series-regeneration adapter (trade-sim + lake)"*. Nothing actually ran the cascade on a real sweep. **What shipped (new pure module `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py`, 100% line+branch under the strict `--cov=brutex.engine` gate):** (1) `build_candidate_input` re-simulates each persisted winning mask over the SAME bars (the golden-locked `simulate_trades` + `build_equity_curve` + `compute_metrics`) and fills the `CandidateInput` — per-**bar** equity-change returns as the equal-length pool axis (CPCV/WFO/SPA/PBO/RW), per-trade scalar moments (a `None` metric → `0.0`, the same documented choice as `ranked_combo_to_result_row`), and an injected Monte-Carlo exit closure returning the per-trade Sharpe of relocated entries; (2) the cascade runs **once per `(instrument, tf)` pool** because the pool-matrix filters require one shared returns length — pooling across slices (different bar counts) would crash `_pool_matrix`, so it is deliberately NOT done (honest envelope); (3) a `CascadeManifest` (the tuple params — sl/tp/prior_n/proximity/start_equity — that are folded into the `run_id` but NOT stored as `ResultRow` columns, so they are recorded, never re-derived) is the single source of truth BOTH paths consume. **AUTOMATIC:** `brutex sweep-all` builds the manifest from the grid + the persisted per-tuple stores after the grid completes and writes `<results-root>/cascade/{manifest.json,cascade-report.json}`. **MANUAL:** `brutex cascade <run-id>` (+ the dashboard `POST /api/v1/cascade/run` "Run cascade" button on `/reports`) reloads that manifest, re-reads the same lake bars, and re-runs the identical pure core → a **byte-identical** `cascade-report.json` (the golden test pins it). The existing `--overfit-gate` behaviour is UNCHANGED (it still runs per-leaderboard inside the sweep; the cascade is an additional Stage-4 pass). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** offline `O(K)` re-simulations over the top-K winners, NOT an O(1) per-bar hot path; small slices that cannot reach the Lockbox 500-floor / the CPCV/WFO window lengths are conservatively rejected at those stages (real, not papered over). **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_engine_cascade_wire.py` (100% line+branch — every validation/serialisation/error branch + reconstruction + the byte-identity assertion), `tests/golden/test_cascade_wire_golden.py` (AUTO==MANUAL on disk + manifest round-trip byte-stability), `tests/property/test_cascade_wire_properties.py` (manifest round-trip identity, per-bar-returns reconstruction, `_finite`/drawdown invariants). Refs: DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001 (#436, the cascade engine this wires), DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (#465), DEC-SWEEP-WINNERS-BY-NAME-001 (#562, the results read-back), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 (no hallucination — every param recorded, never guessed) / #4 (reproducible — deterministic seed from the sweep-id, byte-identical report) / #10 (honest envelope) / #11 (COMMON — one pure core for both paths).

567. **DEC-TELEGRAM-WIRE-001 — wire the built-but-unwired Telegram channel into the brute-force sweep + live pull: AUTOMATIC `watchdog-hung` / `rate.breach` / `auth.renew_failed` / `sweep complete` alerts + a MANUAL `brutex notify test` digest** (2026-06-07, gap-ledger row: `notifications/telegram.py` built but the SWEEP path emitted zero alerts). **Gap (verified):** the §11 AUTOMATED decree promises "watchdog + Telegram + auto-resume", and `brutex/notifications/telegram.py` (the async fire-and-forget notifier) + `brutex/notifications/wiring.py` (the INGEST `EventSubscriber` bridge) are both 100%-tested — but the **brute-force sweep supervisor** (`engine/sweep_supervisor.py`, `cmd_sweep_all`) and the **live Dhan pull** (`cmd_fetch`, `pull_controller`) never published a single operator alert: a hung sweep tuple, a Dhan 429 throttle, a `RenewToken` refusal, and a finished grid all passed silently. **Fix (1 new wheel-free module + thin pragma-omitted wiring at the existing seams — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, no hash/notifier logic duplicated):** new `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py` `SweepAlerter` maps each event to ONE best-effort `TelegramEvent` — `watchdog_hung`→`WORKER_HUNG`/CRITICAL, `rate_breach`→`RATE_LIMIT_DOWNSHIFT`/WARN (coalesced by the notifier's 60 s dedupe), `auth_renew_failed`→the new `AUTH_RENEW_FAILED`/ERROR kind (300 s dedupe), `sweep_complete`→`RUN_COMPLETE`/INFO, plus `test_digest`→`TEST` for the manual command. Two callback adapters plug into the UNCHANGED seams: `watchdog_hung_callback()` → `SweepWatchdog(on_hung=…)` in `cmd_sweep_all`; `rate_breach_callback(controller)` wraps `DhanRateController.on_rate_limit` in `cmd_fetch` (steps the rate down FIRST, then alerts). `sweep_complete(result)` fires after `run_supervised_grid` returns; `auth_renew_failed(...)` fires at the existing `pull_controller` `token is None` branch. New CLI surface `brutex notify test` (`cmd_notify_test`) is the MANUAL counterpart: reads the channel env, prints a clear hint + non-zero exit when disabled/misconfigured (never a traceback), else starts the singleton, publishes one digest, drains, prints the send stats. Every dynamic body is MarkdownV2-escaped (`escape_markdown_v2`) so a hyphenated symbol / decimal latency renders instead of a Telegram `HTTP 400`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — no illusion):** every emit is **best-effort, fire-and-forget** — it returns `True` iff a publish was attempted on a live (enabled) notifier, and EVERY exception (resolver raises / publish raises) is swallowed + logged, so an alert can **never** block, slow, or crash the sweep / pull; when Telegram is disabled (the default) every method is a silent no-op. Each emit is **O(1)** (one event build + one queue put; the notifier's own daemon thread does the network I/O off the caller's thread) — NOT an O(1)-total claim; sending N alerts is inherently O(N). The module is **wheel-free at import** (telegram channel → `brutex.models` only); the default lazy singleton resolver (`_resolve_singleton_notifier`, `# pragma: no cover`) delegates to the already-100% `brutex.notifications.wiring.get_or_start_notifier` and is the one spot that pulls the `fastbloom_rs`/`lmdb` chain — the same precedent as `observability/standard_monitor.py`. The watchdog seam is **inter-tuple only** (inherited from `SweepWatchdog`, stated plainly in `sweep_supervisor.py`). **Tests / gates:** `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py` ships at **100% line + branch** (`tests/unit/test_notifications_sweep_alerts.py` — resolver explicit/lazy/None/raising; publish ok/None/raising; each of the 4 alerts + the test digest with kind/severity/dedupe-key asserts; both callback adapters incl. "throttle still runs when the channel is disabled"; a hypothesis property + golden for the MarkdownV2 escaper; a stress burst that never raises) + `tests/bench/test_notifications_sweep_alerts_o1.py` (per-alert O(1)-in-N ratio gate) + `tests/integration/test_telegram_sweep_alerts_wire.py` (real-run proof: all 4 alerts + the manual digest through a REAL `TelegramNotifier` sync AND async daemon-thread path, and the on-hung callback firing through a real `Watchdog` HEALTHY→HUNG edge). `brutex.notifications.telegram` stays 100% after adding the `AUTH_RENEW_FAILED` kind + its dedupe window. A strict per-module 100% CI gate for `brutex.notifications.sweep_alerts` added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. `cli.py` is coverage-omitted; the `pull_controller` renew branch is `# pragma: no cover` (live token + network). ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` on the new module 0 errors; verified on a Python 3.12 venv (CI 3.12 + the `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels is the merge oracle — the sandbox is 3.11 and cannot load the engine wheels). **Builds on:** DEC-TELEGRAM-WIRING-001 (#238, the ingest `EventSubscriber` bridge) · DEC-STANDARD-MONITOR-001 (#243, the `get_or_start_notifier` lazy-singleton precedent) · DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001 (#558, the supervisor + `SweepWatchdog` this alerts on) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the `DhanRateController` 429 ladder) · DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (#555, the `maybe_renew_token` refusal this surfaces) · CLAUDE.md §11 (AUTOMATED + COMMON) / Golden Rules #1 / #8 (audit/observability) / #10 (honest, best-effort) / #11.

## DEC-OPTIONS-EXECUTOR-001 (2026-06-07)

568. **DEC-OPTIONS-EXECUTOR-001 — the options EXECUTOR / materializer: translate a winning Track-1 spot signal → an ATM±N option leg (via the existing 10-rule selector) → a priced, post-cost options PnL, with a manual `brutex options-sim <run-id>` trigger + an automatic post-winning-sweep hook** (2026-06-07, operator request; offset rules run by default, delta-target rules require a caller-supplied chain since the Greeks/BSM pipeline is Phase 4 — honest per Golden Rule #1), `materialize_trade` (loads the leg's entry + 15:20-forced-exit bars through an injected `OptionBarSource` seam, rejects on band-drift `NO_DATA` or §7.8 `TICK_FLOOR`, else prices via `compute_trade_cost` — NO pricing math re-implemented, pure composition per §11 COMMON), `run_rule_over_signals` + `execute_options_sim` (per-rule aggregation into `OptionsRuleResult` with an optional injected hash-chained `AuditAppend` sink — Golden Rule #8), and the `signals_from_spot_trades` replay seam (ClosedTrade-shaped trades → SpotSignals); (2) `brutex.money.rupees_to_paisa` — the shared forward complement of `paisa_to_rupees` (single-source rupees→paisa snap, `round_money` ROUND_HALF_UP × 100), so the executor never copy-pastes the lake-boundary conversion; (3) `brutex options-sim <run-id> --results-root --start --end [--lake-root --expiry --broker]` (manual) — resolves the run in the persisted results tree, replays its mask over the spot lake (Stage-1A matrix → `mask_to_entry_signals` → `simulate_trades`), prices every offset rule against the rolling-option lake, audits, prints the per-rule leaderboard; (4) `brutex sweep-all` auto-runs the same on its top winners by default (`--no-options-sim` to disable, `--options-expiry`/`--options-broker` knobs) — zero-touch + non-fatal, skipping cleanly when no rolling-option lake is present (MANUAL + AUTOMATIC both). **Honest O(1) envelope (Golden Rule #10):** `materialize_trade` is O(1) per trade (fixed strike ALU + one bar-source probe + one O(1) cost compute); the aggregators are O(N over signals) / O(rules × signals) for the sweep — inherent work over the input, NEVER an O(1)-total claim. **Scope honesty (Golden Rule #3 / #1):** the operator-confirmed conflicts were resolved BEFORE coding — the options 1m→TF resampler was SKIPPED (TRACK2_OPTIONS_SPEC §4 is locked at 1-minute-only, no resampling), and the 10-rule selector path was chosen over the 21-strike sweep (DEC-EXEC-001) per the task wording;
