`brutex.money` stays 100% (extended `tests/unit/test_money.py`). ruff format + check clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on `executor.py`/`money.py`. The CLI command + auto-hook + the lake-backed `OptionBarSource` + the engine signal-replay are real-lake/fno_math I/O — coverage-omitted (`cli.py`) + `# pragma: no cover` + operator-verified against a real Dhan lake (no real lake/wheels in CI/sandbox), exactly the honest pattern of DEC-CATALOG-RECONCILE-WIRE-001; the executor CORE they call is the 100%-tested, golden-locked piece. **New public symbols:** `brutex.options.executor.{SpotSignal, OptionLeg, OptionBarPair, OptionBarSource, MaterializedTrade, RejectedTrade, RejectReason, OptionsRuleResult, AuditAppend, SpotTrade, ExpiryKind, TICK_FLOOR_MULTIPLE, select_option_leg, materialize_trade, run_rule_over_signals, execute_options_sim, resolve_current_expiry, signals_from_spot_trades}`; `brutex.money.rupees_to_paisa`; `cli.cmd_options_sim`. **Builds on:** DEC-EXEC-008 (BUY-only) · DEC-EXEC-009 (option type follows spot direction) · DEC-SWEEP-WINNERS-BY-NAME-001 (#562, the results tree this reads) · DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 · DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 / DEC-PAISA-DOC-RECONCILE-001 (money discipline) · TRACK2_OPTIONS_SPEC §6b/§7.8/§9 + TRACK2_EXECUTION_SIMULATOR · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #3 / #4 / #5 / #8 / #10 / #11.

569. **DEC-STRUCTURE-CLEANUP-001 — delete the 3 docstring-only orphan stub packages (`backtest/`, `sprint/`, `visualization/`) + create the documented `brutex/math/` thin facade re-exporting the Rust hot kernels + reconcile CLAUDE.md §5 so the tree matches reality** (2026-06-07, structure-hygiene pass; CLAUDE.md §9 hostile-review mindset — every claim below is file:line-traced, Golden Rule #1). **Problem (code-traced, zero importers verified):** three packages under `brutex/` held ONLY a docstring `__init__.py` and no code — `brutex/backtest/` (planned "Polars-vectorized per-bar simulator"), `brutex/sprint/` (planned "Day-1 end-to-end runner"), `brutex/visualization/` (planned "matplotlib PNG charts"). A repo-wide search (`grep brutex.backtest|brutex.sprint|brutex.visualization` across `brutex/` + `tests/`) found **NO importer anywhere** — the only textual hits were unrelated docstring prose and one historical, marked-not-done (⬜) row in `docs/daily/DAY_1_REPORT.md`. Symmetrically, CLAUDE.md §5 documented a `brutex/math/ ← facade to Rust hot kernel` package that **did not exist** on disk, even though `pyproject.toml` was already pre-configured for it (ruff `A005`/`PLE0604`, pyright `reportConstantRedefinition`/`reportUnsupportedDunderAll` all reference the `brutex/math` facade by name). The real engine work has since landed in concretely-named packages (`engine/`, `vocabulary/`, `indicators/`, `ranking/`, `metrics/`, `options/`, `costs/`, `calendars/`) that the brute-force sweep actually imports — the three stubs were dead scaffolding (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON: one home per utility, no dead orphans). **Decision (operator brief — DELETE the dead orphans, CREATE the facade, RECONCILE the doc):** (1) `git rm` the three stub packages. **`visualization/` was REMOVED, not implemented** — a static-PNG charting feature is a substantial new capability needing its own design + 4-agent review (CLAUDE.md §9), and the FastAPI `dashboard/` already serves Track-1 visualization; reviving PNG export is a separate future decision, NOT silently in-scoped here (Golden Rule #9 — no scope creep). (2) **Created `brutex/math/__init__.py`** — the documented thin facade. It adds NO logic (Golden Rule #11 COMMON — no copy-paste, no re-implementation): it imports both compiled PyO3 wheels (`fno_math` ← `rust/fno-math`; `trading_core` ← `rust/trading-core`) and **programmatically re-binds** every public kernel symbol into one kernel-agnostic namespace so a caller can `from brutex import math; math.blake3_hash(...)` / `math.evaluate_with_levels(...)`. The re-export auto-tracks each kernel's `__all__` (gain/drop an entry point → facade follows, no edit), filters each kernel's own `__version__` (ambiguous if merged; per-kernel provenance is exposed unmerged via `math.kernel_versions()`), and **raises `RuntimeError` on any cross-kernel symbol collision** (never a silent shadow — Golden Rule #1). New public surface: every `fno_math` entry point (`ResidentBars`, `ResidentSweepSim`, `add_u64`, `bitand_count_u64s`, `bitcount_u64s`, `blake3_hash`, `count_supermask_u64s`, `count_supermasks_u64s`, `count_supermasks_u64s_nthreads`, `popcount_bytes`) + every `trading_core` entry point (`FIB_LEVELS_LEN`, `PIVOT_LEVELS_LEN`, `TOTAL_CONDITIONS`, `compute_fib_levels`, `compute_pivot_levels`, `evaluate_from_raw`, `evaluate_with_levels`, `total_conditions`, `version`) + `kernel_versions`. **Existing direct `import fno_math` / `import trading_core` call sites are deliberately left UNCHANGED** — migrating typed callers onto the facade needs a generated `.pyi` (the dynamic re-export is invisible to `mypy --strict`'s `no_implicit_reexport`) and is a separate reviewed step; this PR only creates the documented single import point. (3) **Reconciled CLAUDE.md §5** — the `brutex/` subtree now lists the real package set (added `calendars/`, `costs/`, `engine/`, `indicators/`, `metrics/`, `options/`, `ranking/`, `vocabulary/`; kept `math/` now that it exists). **Honest O(1) envelope (Golden Rule #10 — no illusion):** building the facade (`_reexport`) is a **one-time O(total-symbols)** cost paid once at import — explicitly NOT an O(1)-total claim. What is O(1) is the per-symbol *lookup* a caller pays on every use (`math.blake3_hash` is a module-attribute dict access whose latency does not grow with the re-export count) — proven by `tests/bench/test_math_facade_o1.py` (10 vs 1000 re-exports, ratio under the two-tier ceiling). **Tests / gates (7 types where applicable; verified on the local Python 3.11 sandbox — the wheels can't build there, so every test drives the facade against fake kernel modules injected into `sys.modules`, the identical re-export/lookup path the real wheels use; CI 3.12 + wheels is the merge oracle):** `brutex/math/__init__.py` at **100% line + 100% branch** under a new strict per-module `--cov=brutex.math --cov-fail-under=100` CI gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) — `tests/unit/test_math_facade.py` (re-export identity, `__all__` sorted+complete, `__version__` filtered, `kernel_versions` mapping + str-coercion, `_public_names` both `__all__`-present/absent branches, `_reexport` collision-raise + sorted-return) + `tests/property/test_math_facade_invariants.py` (hypothesis: arbitrary kernel surfaces always bind-all/sort/filter-`__version__`; any shared name always raises) + `tests/golden/test_math_facade_golden.py` (real-wheel surface frozen to the contract above + facade symbols ARE the kernel objects + a real `blake3_hash` call through the facade equals the direct kernel call — `importorskip` so it skips wheel-free, gates on CI) + `tests/bench/test_math_facade_o1.py` (per-lookup O(1) ratio). `ruff format` + `ruff check` clean on all new files. **Builds on:** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the `trading_core` wheel fronted) · DEC-P0-055 (the `fno_math` mixed Python+Rust wheel layout fronted) · DEC-P0-025 (the `rust/fno-math` Greeks/indicators removal that left it a pure bit-kernel) · CLAUDE.md §5 (the directory contract reconciled) / Golden Rules #1 (no hallucination — collision raises, never shadows) / #5 (O(1) per-lookup) / #10 (honest one-time-build envelope) / #11 COMMON (one facade, no logic duplication).

571. **DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 — auto-retry leftover failed ingest windows (manual + automatic), bounded + rate-safe + known-gap-excluded** (2026-06-07, operator). **Problem (live, confirmed in code):** a 783-symbol spot pull completed 18,791 windows but left **84 windows still-failed** — a sustained Dhan 429 storm (~4 min, 100+ consecutive 429s) outlived the *in-run* per-window retry budget (`ingest._DEFAULT_MAX_RETRY_PASSES = 2`, `ingest.py:99`). A window that still fails after that budget is correctly NEVER marked complete (the no-skip guarantee — `ingest.py:147,427`), but the ONLY recovery was the operator MANUALLY re-running the whole pull: the coverage ledger (`data/fetch_coverage.py:64-72`, DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001) skips every completed window so a re-pull re-fetches only the failed ones — incremental + idempotent — but there was **no automatic post-run re-pull**. **Fix:** a new wheel-free engine `brutex/adapters/dhan/auto_retry.py` — `retry_failed_windows(run_pass, *, max_rounds=3, backoff)` runs ADDITIONAL bounded ROUNDS, each one a full ingest pass over the SAME coverage ledger so it re-fetches ONLY the still-failed windows, with injected exponential backoff (default 5 s→10 s→…, clamped 60 s — `auto_retry.py:_default_round_backoff`), stopping when coverage is clean OR the round budget is spent OR the token dies. The wrapper `run_dhan_spot_ingest_with_retry(...)` in `run_ingest.py` runs the original pull, then — only when it left a TRANSIENT residual (`still_failed_windows > 0`) AND `auto_retry` is on — drives the loop; returns `SpotIngestWithRetry{report, retry}` (`run_ingest.py`). **Manual + automatic, ONE engine (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** AUTOMATIC = on by default after every `brutex fetch` / dashboard pull, opt-out via `brutex fetch --no-auto-retry` (and `pull_all_spot(auto_retry=False)`, the prior single-pass behaviour byte-for-byte); MANUAL = `brutex fetch --retry-failed` (CLI) + the dashboard "Retry failed windows" button (`POST /api/v1/universe/retry-failed`, `dashboard/app.py`, `# pragma: no cover` route → `pull_all_spot(..., auto_retry=True)`) — both paths call the SAME `retry_failed_windows` (no duplicated round loop). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the retry is **O(failed_windows), NOT O(1)-total** — each round re-fetches every residual window (the coverage skip-set makes a round skip *completed* windows O(1)/window, but the residual set itself is whatever the storm left); the round COUNT is bounded by `max_rounds` (never infinite). **Rate-safe by construction:** a round IS one `run_dhan_spot_ingest` pass governed by the SAME shared adaptive token bucket (`pace`, DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001), so every round stays ≤ 5 r/s (Rule #6) and the inter-round backoff WAITS a throttle out. **Known-gaps NOT retried forever:** a window failing because Dhan genuinely has no data (a `DH-905`/"no data present" quarantine, classified by the new string twin `errors.is_no_data_message` reused from `is_no_data_error`, `errors.py`) is counted as a *known gap*, NEVER as a retryable residual — only TRANSIENT `still_failed_windows` (429/timeout/5xx) drive a round. **Auth death halts the loop** (a 401/403 or `DH-906` mid-round → stop; RenewToken cannot revive a dead token, DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001). **Idempotent:** re-fetching a now-succeeded window is a sink no-op (Rule #7). **Tests / standards:** new `tests/unit/test_dhan_auto_retry.py` — 13 cases (clean-after-one-round, recovers-over-multiple-rounds, residual-after-budget-exhausted, known-gap-not-retried, known-gap-vs-transient, auth-death-halts, `max_rounds=0` disables, default-backoff bounded+exponential, manual==automatic same-engine, recovered-windows clamp, frozen outcome, + a hypothesis property: final residual == last round's residual ∧ `rounds_run ≤ max_rounds`) — **100.00% line+branch** under a NEW strict per-module CI gate `brutex.adapters.dhan.auto_retry` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, mirroring the existing per-module gate blocks); `is_no_data_message` covered to keep `errors` at 100%; wrapper covered in `test_dhan_run_ingest.py` + `pull_all_spot(auto_retry=True)` in `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`. Fake clock/fake `run_pass` → no real sleeps/network. **Sandbox-verified vs CI-only (honest, Golden Rule #1):** sandbox is Python 3.11 and CANNOT import the PEP-695 orchestrator chain / fno_math wheels, so `auto_retry.py` + `errors.py` (wheel-free) ran fully here — ruff (format+check) clean, pyright 0/0, interrogate 100%, the 13-case suite green at 100% line+branch; `run_ingest.py` / `pull_controller.py` / `app.py` / `cli.py` pass ruff+pyright but their tests are **CI 3.12 oracle-only** here. **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED (this is a LAKE-ingest recovery layer); spot only (options ingest's own retry is separate). **Closes** the data-pull retry row of the §6 manual⇄automatic duality table in `docs/TRACK1_GAP_ANALYSIS.md` (→ DONE). **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (skip-set), DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 / DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (in-run per-window passes this ROUND layer wraps), DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (rate bucket), DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 (known-gap classification), DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (auth halt).

570. **DEC-PREOPEN-PREVCLOSE-CONTIGUITY-001 — the pre-open report (minute basis) must NEVER anchor PREV. CLOSE across a 1-minute data hole; skip the row instead of fabricating a wrong %CHNG** (2026-06-07; operator-reported: JUBLINGREA 2026-06-04 showed PREV. CLOSE 685 / %CHNG −7.88% while the real prior session closed ≈ 630). Entry numbered **567** (next free after #566 on the merge; renumber on an append collision). **Bug (proven from the report code, not a guess):** in `build_preopen_rows` (`brutex/dashboard/preopen_report.py`) the **minute basis** computed PREV. CLOSE via `_prev_trading_close(_intraday_last_close_by_date(...))`, which maps each day to the **previous AVAILABLE minute date** by walking the sorted minute-date set. When the immediately-preceding trading session's 1-minute window is **missing from the lake** (a failed/never-fetched fetch window — see the live `pull_id=b956797d80d1` DH-906 abort + the 15 broad-index known-gaps), that walk silently skips back to a **stale far-earlier** session (e.g. an April close of 685) and anchors on it → a wildly wrong `CHNG = IEP − 685` / `%CHNG`. Because `/reports` defaults to the **Top-mover** category (single biggest |%CHNG| per day), these fabricated jumps are exactly the rows the report surfaces — the operator's "for 4-Jun the %change is completely wrong". The same stale-jump latency exists in the daily-basis `_prev_close_asof`, but the reported failure + the operator's chosen basis are the minute path; the daily path is unchanged here (tracked follow-up if a daily hole is observed). **Fix (scope: make PREV. CLOSE *correct or absent — never wrong*; operator decision 2026-06-07 = SKIP the row):** new pure helper `_minute_prev_close_contiguous(minute_last, trading_dates, day)` — the symbol's **1-day series is the authoritative trading-session calendar** (one bar/session, far more robust than the minute feed, and able to tell a genuine holiday gap (absent from BOTH series) apart from a *missing 1-minute window* (present in 1-day, absent in 1-minute)). The expected prior session is the latest 1-day date strictly before `day`; the anchor is valid ONLY when that exact session also has 1-minute data, else the helper returns `None` and `build_preopen_rows` **skips the (symbol, day) row** (no fake mover reaches Top-mover). `build_preopen_rows` now reads the 1-day close-by-date as the calendar in the minute basis too; a symbol with **no 1-day partition** keeps the DEC-PREOPEN-MINUTE-BASIS-001 fallback (the previous available minute session) since there is no calendar to verify against — the honest limit. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is a *safety net*, not a data fix — it prevents a WRONG number while a window is missing; the data is filled by re-pulling with a valid Dhan token (the DH-906 abort halts the pull) + the auto-retry layer (DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 #567-candidate / PR #483) re-fetching transient-failed windows. O(log N) per day via `bisect`; no hot-path/O(1)-total claim. **Tests (`tests/unit/test_preopen_report.py`, 100% line+branch on `preopen_report.py` — 217 stmts / 52 branch / 0 miss):** `test_minute_prev_close_contiguous_branches` (valid / missing-prior-window / first-session / zero-prior-close), `test_build_minute_basis_skips_row_when_prior_window_missing` (the JUBLINGREA repro — a stale 685 minute close + a missing 03-Jun window → 04-Jun row is DROPPED, not anchored on 685), `test_build_minute_basis_contiguous_uses_prior_session` (the healthy case still emits with PREV. CLOSE = the prior session's last 1-minute close); all 47 prior preopen tests unchanged. Refs: DEC-PREOPEN-MINUTE-BASIS-001 (the minute basis this guards), DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001 (the 1-minute prev-close convention), DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#483, the fetch-side recovery), DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (a window is marked complete only on `raw_bars > 0`, so a failed/empty window is always re-fetched), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 (no hallucination — never show a fabricated %CHNG) / #10 (honest envelope).

572. **DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 — a finished spot pull emits ONE prioritised, actionable verdict so a token-stuck or retry-residual pull is never silent (MANUAL via the pull-all JSON the dashboard renders + AUTOMATIC via a loud structured WARNING)** (2026-06-07; operator-reported: "why again & again N failed windows" — the window-status table showed JUBLINGREA's `[2026-03-06, 2026-06-04]` 1-minute window `FAILED · 3 attempts · DhanRateLimitError`, i.e. a transient 429 that exhausted the in-run retry budget, which then starved the pre-open report's prev-close → a wrong %CHNG). The `pull_controller.py` wiring runs on CI 3.12 (the sandbox is Python 3.11 and cannot parse the PEP-695 `orchestrator/retry.py` chain — documented). 573. **DEC-LOOKAHEAD-BARRIER-001 — promote Property **P-06** (the instrumented bar accessor) from a `pytest.skip` ROADMAP stub to a LIVE runtime look-ahead barrier wired into the sweep eval path, with a manual `brutex verify-lookahead` recheck** (2026-06-07; closes DEC-GAP-ANALYSIS-001 #565 ranked gap (6) "runtime look-ahead barrier in the sweep"). **Gap (code-traced):** CLAUDE.md §4 stated the no-look-ahead invariant was enforced TODAY *only* by the feed-boundary guard `ReplayFeed.ensure_no_lookahead` (`brutex/feed/replay.py:184-208`) — a **timestamp**-based check wired into the strategy runner (`runner.py:181`) + execution driver (`driver.py:184`) — while the named **Property P-06** ("for any bar index N, `evaluate(N)` reads only indices ≤ N") was a `pytest.skip("Phase 2 implementation pending (instrumented bar accessor)")` ROADMAP stub in `tests/property/test_invariants_catalog.py`. **What shipped (1 new pure module + thin wiring at the two existing seams — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, no guard logic duplicated):** new `brutex/feed/lookahead.py` `LookAheadBarrier` — an **index**-based instrumented accessor with no global mutable state (dependency-injected). It carries the engine's current bar index `N` (`advance_to`, forward-only — negative / backward moves raise `ValueError`), records every bar index a consumer touches (`access`/`guard`, returning the index/value unchanged), and raises `LookAheadError` the moment any access reaches an index `> N` (or before any bar is reached). A `record` flag toggles the touched-index trail: `record=False` (the default the runner/driver build) keeps **O(1) memory** for the always-on sweep guard; `record=True` retains the trail for the bounded manual recheck + the property tests. Plus a pure `verify_with_barrier(run, barrier) -> LookAheadReport` — the manual-recheck core that drives a bounded slice, folds any `LookAheadError` into a pass/fail verdict (never a traceback), and emits one structured `structlog` line (Golden Rule #8; lazy-imported so the whole `brutex.feed` package stays import-light). **Wiring (AUTOMATIC):** `StrategyRunner.run` + `BacktestDriver.run` now `enumerate` the feed, `advance_to(step)` before the symbol filter, and route each consumed bar through `barrier.guard(step, event.bar)` — so the barrier is active on every sweep eval by default, belt-and-suspenders with the existing timestamp guard. Both expose a `.barrier` property + accept an injected `barrier=` (DI) and `reset()` it at the top of every run so deterministic replays don't leak the prior run's cursor/trail. **MANUAL:** new `brutex verify-lookahead --symbol … --start … --end …` CLI subcommand (coverage-omitted I/O shim, `# pragma: no cover`) loads a bounded lake slice via the same Catalog/ReplayFeed path `brutex sweep` uses and replays it forward through a `record=True` barrier via `verify_with_barrier`, printing the `LookAheadReport` (PASS/FAIL + bars/checked/max_index/final_cursor) with a non-zero exit on any violation — the operator's hand-recheck. **P-06 promoted:** the catalog stub now points at the live `tests/property/test_lookahead_properties.py`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is the **Phase-2 STRENGTHENING** of the existing runtime feed-boundary guard, NOT a replacement and NOT a perf path — the accessor is **O(1) per bar access** (a couple of integer comparisons + an optional list append), explicitly **NOT an O(1)-total claim**: a full sweep touches Σ bars and is inherently `O(Σ)`. With `record=False` the barrier holds O(1) memory; `record=True` retains O(accesses) over a bounded slice. At THIS phase the runner/driver dispatch loop accesses only the current index, so the always-on barrier is a live invariant assertion (it becomes load-bearing the moment any future index-based indicator reads a bar) — stated plainly, no illusion. **Tests / gates (sandbox is Py3.11/no-`fno_math`-wheel — CI 3.12+wheels is the merge oracle):** `brutex/feed/lookahead.py` at **100% line + 100% branch** under a new strict per-module `--cov=brutex.feed.lookahead --cov-fail-under=100` ci.yml gate — `tests/unit/test_lookahead_barrier.py` (boundary N-1/N ok, N+1 raises; every guard branch — access-before-advance, negative index, backward/negative cursor, the `record` toggle, `max_touched` empty/non-empty; `verify_with_barrier` clean + look-ahead runs) + `tests/property/test_lookahead_properties.py` (the live P-06 hypothesis invariant: any access `> N` ALWAYS raises, any access `≤ N` NEVER raises; forward-replay touches only `[0,n-1]` with max ≤ cursor) + `tests/golden/test_lookahead_golden.py` (byte-exact touched-index trail for a known-good forward + lookback(1) replay) + `tests/bench/test_lookahead_o1.py` (per-access O(1) latency-ratio gate, 1M vs 1K, `ratio_ceiling`). The runner/driver wiring is covered by `tests/integration/test_strategies_runner.py` (`TestLookAheadBarrier`) + `tests/unit/test_execution_driver_edges.py` (the injected-barrier + reset + default-record=False branches), keeping `brutex.execution.driver`'s existing strict-100% gate green. ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the new module. **New public symbols:** `brutex.feed.lookahead.{LookAheadBarrier, LookAheadReport, verify_with_barrier}` (re-exported from `brutex.feed`); `cli.cmd_verify_lookahead`. **Builds on:** the feed-boundary timestamp guard `ReplayFeed.ensure_no_lookahead` (`feed/replay.py:184-208`, the sibling this strengthens) · DEC-PHASE1-INVARIANT-CATALOG-001 (#250, the P-06 stub promoted) · DEC-PROPERTY-INVARIANTS-LIVE-001 (the live-invariant precedent) · CLAUDE.md §4 (no-look-ahead, reconciled) / Golden Rules #1 (no hallucination — honest belt-and-suspenders framing) / #5 (O(1) per access) / #8 (audit/observability) / #10 (honest Phase-2 envelope) / #11 COMMON.

574. **DEC-SWEEP-SCHEDULER-001 — automated "ZERO clicks per day" sweep scheduler (manual + automatic), pure clock-injected core + thin daemon shim** (2026-06-07, operator; closes the **Sweep-run** row of the §6 manual⇄automatic duality table in `docs/TRACK1_GAP_ANALYSIS.md` + roadmap item "Sweep scheduler (manual + automatic)"). **Problem (gap-ledger-traced):** the §6 duality table marked **Sweep run → automatic path: ❌ no scheduler/daemon** (`docs/TRACK1_GAP_ANALYSIS.md:141`) — `brutex sweep-all` (the manual trigger, `cli.py:cmd_sweep_all`) existed but nothing ran the full grid pipeline unattended on a cadence, so the §11 AUTOMATED "ZERO clicks per day" decree was unmet for the sweep itself. **Fix — a PURE scheduler CORE + a thin daemon shim (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, duplicate NO sweep/resume logic):** (1) new wheel-free engine `brutex/engine/sweep_scheduler.py` — the clock-injected decision kernel that owns ONLY *when*: `Schedule.parse` accepts an interval (`"24h"`/`"90m"`/`"@hourly"`) or a daily wall-clock time (`"daily@02:30"`/`"02:30"`/`"@daily"`, tz-aware, IST default) and `Schedule.next_fire_after(now, last_fire=…)` computes the next fire epoch from an **injected** `now` (no `time.time()` inside); `decide_resume(CheckpointView)` classifies the durable sweep checkpoint into FRESH / RESUME / ALREADY_COMPLETE (pure *observability* over the cursor — it re-implements NO resume; the per-tuple resume stays wholly in `run_supervised_grid`, DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001); `plan_cycle` + `cycle_audit_payload` tie the two halves into the daemon's per-cycle plan + BLAKE3 audit shape. (2) new CLI `brutex sweep-daemon` (`cli.py:cmd_sweep_daemon`, `# pragma: no cover` — live clock + `time.sleep` + lake I/O, cli-omitted per repo norm): the AUTOMATIC twin that loops {compute next fire → sleep → run ONE `cmd_sweep_all` verbatim → BLAKE3-audit the cycle}, crash-safe auto-resume from the SAME `<out_root>/checkpoint/sweep-all.json` the supervisor already maintains, with `--once` (run exactly one cycle now — the on-demand manual trigger), `--max-cycles`, `--schedule`, `--tz-offset-minutes`. The shared grid args are factored once into `_add_sweep_grid_args` and reused by BOTH `sweep-all` and `sweep-daemon` so the two surfaces can never drift. **Manual + automatic (CLAUDE.md §11):** MANUAL = `brutex sweep-all` (unchanged, byte-for-byte) **+** `brutex sweep-daemon --once`; AUTOMATIC = `brutex sweep-daemon --schedule daily@02:30` (intended: nightly, after the incremental Dhan pull). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** every scheduler-core function is **O(1)** (closed-form arithmetic / a constant number of comparisons — proven by `tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_scheduler_o1.py`, which shows `next_fire_after` cost is independent of how far the daemon fell behind, ruling out an O(gap) catch-up loop). The scheduler bounds **WHEN** a sweep starts, **NOT** its `O(Σ work)`: a scheduled sweep still costs the §8 wall-time envelope (~33B trials in 2-4 days on an M4 Pro, 12-24 h on a 64-128 core box) — **no "millions in minutes" claim is made, and no O(1)-total claim is made (forbidden)**. **Tests / standards (7 types):** `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_scheduler.py` (every parse accept/reject branch, interval first-loop/on-schedule/caught-up, daily today/tomorrow/re-fire-guard, resume FRESH/RESUME/ALREADY_COMPLETE, `plan_cycle`, audit shape) — drives the new module to **100% line+branch** under the EXISTING `brutex.engine` strict per-module CI gate (`--cov=brutex.engine --cov-fail-under=100`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, runs `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py`); **property** (hypothesis — `next_fire_after ≥ now` ∀ inputs, daily fire always lands on the configured wall-clock second, post-fire recompute never repeats) in the same unit file; **golden** byte-equality of the audit payload (`tests/golden/test_sweep_scheduler_golden.py`); **bench/O(1)** on the next-fire calc (`tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_scheduler_o1.py`); **stress** on the resume/plan loop over 20k cycles (`tests/stress/test_sweep_scheduler_resume_stress.py`); **mutation** via the engine mutmut gate. **Sandbox-verified vs CI-only (honest, Golden Rule #1):** sandbox is Python 3.11 and CANNOT import the `brutex.engine` package (`combo_mask`→`fno_math` PyO3 wheel) or `pytest`/`hypothesis`/`structlog`/`blake3`, so the pure `sweep_scheduler.py` was loaded standalone (bypassing the package `__init__`) and every branch + the golden bytes were executed green HERE; the full `pytest` suite + the 100%-coverage gate + mypy/pyright are **CI 3.12 oracle-only**. `cli.py` (cmd_sweep_daemon + `_add_sweep_grid_args`) passes ruff format+check here; it is coverage-omitted. **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE + the sweep pipeline are UNCHANGED — this adds only a scheduling layer on top; the incremental Dhan pull (DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001) remains a separate scheduled concern (the daemon runs the sweep, not the pull). **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (the grid `cmd_sweep_all` reuses), DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001 (the live G&A supervisor + crash-safe checkpoint the daemon resumes from), DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (`SweepCheckpoint`).

575. **DEC-VERDICT-BANNER-001 — SHOW the finished-pull verdict as a coloured, actionable banner on /universe (MANUAL refresh + AUTOMATIC after every pull)** (2026-06-08, operator; builds directly on DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 / PR #485). **Gap:** DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 made `pull_all_spot` carry ONE prioritised `PullVerdict` (`brutex/adapters/dhan/pull_verdict.py` — `kind` ∈ {auth_expired > transient_residual > known_gap_only > clean}, `headline`, `action`, `needs_operator`, `pending_windows`), emitted as the `"verdict"` object in the `/api/v1/universe/pull-all` JSON (`BulkSpotReport.to_dict`, `dashboard/pull_controller.py:579-599`) **but the `/universe` page never SHOWED it** — the operator could not see, on the page, whether a stuck pull was a dead token (must regenerate) vs a transient 429 residual (re-pull finishes) vs a known gap (expected). **What shipped (new pure module `brutex/dashboard/verdict_banner.py`, 100% line+branch — 24 stmts / 2 branch / 0 miss):** `banner_for(verdict: Mapping) -> VerdictBanner` maps the *already-computed* verdict onto a deterministic presentation — a CSS modifier class + human colour name (**red = auth_expired, amber = transient_residual, grey = known_gap_only, green = clean**) + a `show_retry_button` bool — with `VerdictBanner.to_dict()` as the JSON contract. **COMMON (CLAUDE.md §11):** NO verdict field is re-derived — `headline` / `action` / `pending_windows` are passed through verbatim and the retry button is shown exactly when the verdict's OWN `needs_operator` flag is set (so the one classification authority stays `classify_pull`); an unrecognised `kind` fails closed with `ValueError` (never rendered uncoloured). **AUTOMATIC surface:** `/universe` (`dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `# pragma: no cover` template) renders the banner the moment a pull ends (`finishLive()` → `refreshVerdict()`), showing the headline + action + pending-window count in the kind's colour. **MANUAL surface:** a new thin route `GET /api/v1/universe/pull-verdict` (`dashboard/app.py`, `# pragma: no cover` route over the 100%-tested helper) returns `banner_for(last_verdict).to_dict()` (or `{"present": false}` before the first pull); the banner's **⟳ Refresh** button re-fetches it on demand, and the page re-paints it on load. The background `_work` (already `# pragma: no cover`, job thread) stamps the completed `report.verdict.to_dict()` into a per-app one-key holder (`_last_pull_verdict`, not a module-global — CLAUDE.md §4; the write is one atomic reference assignment under the CPython GIL, read on the request thread). **Retry button reuses the EXISTING engine (no reimplementation):** when `show_retry_button`, the "↻ Retry failed windows" button calls the existing manual `POST /api/v1/universe/retry-failed` (DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 / PR #483) — the banner only decides whether to SHOW it. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** `banner_for` is a pure **O(1)** mapping (one dict lookup + field copies, bounded memory) — it only *displays* the verdict; it never fetches data, renews a token, or retries anything itself (the retry is the separate #483 engine; the auth fix is still a human regenerating the token). NO new vendor claims — every field is reused verbatim from the #485 verdict. **Tests (7 types where applicable):** `tests/unit/test_verdict_banner.py` (each of the 4 kinds → colour/class/retry, verbatim pass-through, int/bool coercion, unknown-kind ValueError, `to_dict` shape — built against the LIVE `classify_pull(...).to_dict()` contract), `tests/property/test_verdict_banner_properties.py` (hypothesis: every contract kind maps deterministically to its `(css_class, colour)` + `show_retry_button == needs_operator` + verbatim headline/action/pending ∀ inputs; any non-contract kind ALWAYS raises), `tests/golden/test_verdict_banner_golden.py` (byte-exact `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` for one verdict per kind — the exact `/pull-verdict` payload), all green at **100% line+branch** under a NEW strict per-module CI gate `brutex.dashboard.verdict_banner` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, mirroring the existing dashboard per-module gate blocks). **Sandbox-verified vs CI-only (honest, Golden Rule #1):** sandbox is Python 3.11 — the pure `verdict_banner.py` + its 19-test trio ran fully HERE (ruff format+check clean, mypy clean on the module, 100% line+branch); the `app.py` route + the template are display-only (`# pragma: no cover`) and exercised by the CI 3.12 dashboard suite (the sandbox cannot import `app.py`'s pydantic/PEP-695 chain — documented). **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED — this is a dashboard display layer over the already-computed verdict. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 (#485, the verdict this shows), DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#483, the retry engine the button targets), DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (the `auth_expired` signal), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #10 (honest envelope — display-only, O(1)) / #11 (COMMON — one verdict authority, no re-derivation).

576. **DEC-PREOPEN-PREVCLOSE-CONTIGUITY-DAILY-001 — the pre-open report's DAILY basis must NEVER anchor PREV. CLOSE across a MISSING daily bar; derive the prior session from the NSE calendar and SKIP the row when that exact session's 1-day bar is absent** (2026-06-08; the daily mirror of DEC-PREOPEN-PREVCLOSE-CONTIGUITY-001 / PR #484 — entry #570 explicitly flagged "the same stale-jump latency exists in the daily-basis `_prev_close_asof`" as a tracked follow-up, now closed). Entry numbered **576** (next free after #575 DEC-VERDICT-BANNER-001 / PR #496 on main; renumber on an append collision). **Bug (proven from the report code, not a guess):** in `build_preopen_rows` (`brutex/dashboard/preopen_report.py`) the **daily basis** computed PREV. CLOSE via `_prev_close_asof(daily, daily_dates, day)`, which returned `daily[daily_dates[idx-1]]` — the **most-recent AVAILABLE earlier 1-day close**. When the immediately-preceding trading session's daily bar is **missing from the lake** (a failed/never-fetched daily window) that lookup silently jumps back to a **stale far-earlier** session and anchors on it → a wrong `CHNG = IEP − stale_close` / `%CHNG`. For the minute basis the 1-day series WAS the trading-session calendar (#484); for the daily basis the daily series IS the data, so it cannot be its own calendar (a missing bar is indistinguishable from a holiday). **Fix (scope: make PREV. CLOSE *correct or absent — never wrong*; the operator's locked rule, matches #484 = SKIP the row):** new pure helpers `_previous_trading_day(day)` + `_daily_prev_close_contiguous(daily, daily_dates, day)`. The authoritative prior session is now derived from the **shared NSE trading calendar** (`brutex/calendars/nse.py` `is_trading_day`, which already encodes the 2021–2026 NSE/BSE holiday list + weekends + special weekend Budget-Day sessions): `_previous_trading_day` walks back from `day-1` over weekends + listed holidays (a bounded constant — any weekday outside the holiday list is a trading day) to the immediately-preceding session. The anchor is valid ONLY when the latest available daily date strictly before `day` IS that exact expected session; otherwise (`idx==0` first session, the expected session's bar MISSING, or a zero prior close) the helper returns `None` and `build_preopen_rows` **skips the (symbol, day) row**. A genuine weekend/holiday gap is NOT a hole — the calendar steps over it, so a contiguous series across a holiday (e.g. Republic Day Fri + the weekend → Mon) still resolves to the real prior close. The buggy `_prev_close_asof` is **removed** (zero remaining importers; no dead code). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** a *safety net*, not a data fix — it prevents a WRONG number while a daily window is missing; the 1-day series is filled by re-pulling (DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 #466) + the windows table (#465) + the auto-retry layer (DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001). O(log N) per row via `bisect.bisect_left` over `daily_dates` (the calendar walk is a bounded constant); no hot-path / O(1)-total claim. **Honest limit:** a Diwali **Muhurat** date is classified as a holiday by `is_trading_day`, so a symbol whose 1-day lake carries a Muhurat daily bar may have the day-after-Diwali row conservatively SKIPPED (correct-or-absent, never wrong) rather than anchored on an ambiguous Muhurat close — recorded here, not a silent wrong number. **MANUAL + AUTOMATIC:** the guard is active on every daily-basis report (automatic, default basis); the existing on-demand report regeneration (`/reports` route + CLI) is the manual recheck. **Tests (`tests/unit/test_preopen_report.py`, 100% line+branch on `preopen_report.py` — 229 stmts / 58 branch / 0 miss):** `test_daily_prev_close_contiguous_branches` (valid / first-session / missing-prior-bar hole / zero-prior-close / holiday-gap-NOT-skipped), `test_previous_trading_day_steps_over_weekend_and_holiday` (day-1 trading / weekend walk-back / Republic-Day+weekend walk-back), `test_build_day_basis_skips_row_when_prior_session_missing` (the daily repro — a stale 685 daily close + a missing 03-Jun bar → 04-Jun row is DROPPED, not anchored on 685), `test_build_day_basis_holiday_gap_is_not_skipped` (the healthy case across Republic Day still emits with PREV. CLOSE = the real prior session's close); all prior preopen + minute-basis contiguity tests unchanged + green. Refs: DEC-PREOPEN-PREVCLOSE-CONTIGUITY-001 (#484, the minute-basis sibling this mirrors), DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-1DAY-001 (the daily basis this guards), DEC-PREOPEN-MINUTE-BASIS-001, the shared NSE calendar (`brutex/calendars/nse.py`), DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (a window is marked complete only on `raw_bars > 0`, so a failed/empty daily window always re-fetches), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 (no hallucination — never show a fabricated %CHNG) / #10 (honest envelope) / #11 (COMMON — one pure core, one shared calendar).
577. **DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 — token pre-flight (valid / expiring-soon / dead) + re-pull-until-clean, tying together the merged auto-retry (#483) + pull verdict (#485)** (2026-06-08, operator; closes the data-pull recovery frontier left after DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 + DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001). **Problem (code-traced):** a 783-symbol bulk spot pull burns thousands of paced (`≤ 5 r/s`) windows; if the operator's 24h Dhan web token is ALREADY DEAD when the pull starts, every window fires a doomed 401/`DH-906` (the fail-fast guard `auth_guard.AuthGuard` then drains the rest — DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001), wasting minutes + quota on a pull that can NEVER land a bar; and even with the merged post-run auto-retry (`retry_failed_windows`, #483) a sustained multi-minute 429 storm can outlive its bounded round budget, leaving the operator to MANUALLY re-run the whole pull "again & again" (the same report the pull-verdict #485 diagnosed). Nothing checked the token BEFORE starting, and nothing re-pulled ROUNDS-of-rounds until the coverage ledger was actually clean. **Fix — two NEW wheel-free PURE modules, each reusing the merged engines (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, NO duplicated logic):** (A) `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_preflight.py` — the PURE classifier `classify_token_lifetime(remaining_s, *, expiring_threshold_s=token_keepalive.RENEW_BEFORE_EXPIRY_S)` → `valid` (≥12h) / `expiring_soon` (0<rem<12h) / `dead` (≤0), the probe-result wrapper `classify_token(*, probe_auth_failed, expiry_deadline, now, …)` (probe-failed→dead; probe-ok-but-unknown-expiry→valid; else lifetime), and `preflight_pull_verdict(preflight, *, auth_cause=None) -> PullVerdict | None` which maps a DEAD pre-flight to the loud `auth_expired` verdict by REUSING `pull_verdict.classify_pull` (#485) — NOT a second verdict vocabulary. The ONLY network seam is `probe_token_live(client, …)` (`# pragma: no cover`): one `RenewToken` GET that both learns the fresh `expiryTime` AND pushes the token +24h; a refusal ⇒ dead. (B) `brutex/adapters/dhan/until_clean.py` — the PURE loop-controller `decide_until_clean(*, still_failed_windows, auth_aborted, rounds_used, max_rounds) -> "continue"|"stop_clean"|"stop_dead"|"stop_budget"` (priority dead > clean > budget > continue, matching `auto_retry` + `classify_pull`) + the thin driver `run_until_clean(round_runner, *, max_rounds=5, sleep, decide)` that calls an INJECTED `round_runner` (one full pull-pass-with-auto-retry over the SHARED coverage ledger — which itself reuses `retry_failed_windows`, #483, so this module NEVER re-implements the per-window round loop) and an INJECTED `sleep` between rounds, returning `UntilCleanOutcome` whose `.pull_verdict()` again REUSES `classify_pull`. **Wiring (manual + automatic + dashboard — CLAUDE.md §11 / Rule 3 duality):** MANUAL = `brutex fetch --until-clean [--until-clean-rounds N]` (`cli.py:cmd_fetch`, coverage-omitted) keeps bounded re-pull rounds going until clean/dead/budget; AUTOMATIC (default-OFF) = `pull_all_spot(..., until_clean=…, preflight=…)` — a DEAD injected `preflight` REFUSES the bulk pull up front (returns an `auth_aborted` `BulkSpotReport` whose `.verdict` is the loud `auth_expired`, emitting `universe.pull_all.preflight_refused`) WITHOUT building the adapter or firing a single window; DASHBOARD = `POST /api/v1/universe/retry-failed?until_clean=true` (the "Retry failed windows" button's escalation, `# pragma: no cover` route). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the pre-flight only CLASSIFIES + ADVISES — it CANNOT revive a dead token (`RenewToken` refuses an expired/TOTP token; physics); the until-clean loop is **O(failed_windows) per round, NOT O(1)-total** — each round re-fetches its transient residual, the OUTER round COUNT is bounded by `max_rounds` (never infinite), and every round is one `≤ 5 r/s` pass (rate-safe by construction; the inter-round backoff waits a throttle out). Known-gaps (`DH-905`) are NEVER a retryable residual (inherited from #483); a token death halts the loop immediately (`stop_dead`). **Tests / gates (7 types):** new strict per-module 100% line+branch gates `--cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.token_preflight` + `--cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.until_clean` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `tests/unit/test_dhan_token_preflight.py` + `tests/unit/test_dhan_until_clean.py` (every classifier + controller + driver branch via a fake clock + fake round-runner, no real sleeps/network), `tests/property/test_until_clean_properties.py` (hypothesis: terminal state ALWAYS reached ∧ `rounds_run ≤ max_rounds` ∀ scripts/budgets; lifetime classification total + ordered), `tests/golden/test_token_preflight_golden.py` (byte-exact state summaries + the `auth_expired` headline/action + the until-clean `to_dict`), `tests/bench/test_dhan_until_clean_o1.py` (per-call O(1) — decision cost independent of residual magnitude, `ratio_ceiling`), `tests/stress/test_until_clean_stress.py` (20k high-budget loops: always terminates, always bounded). The `pull_all_spot` preflight-refusal + until-clean wiring is covered by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` (dead-refuses / alive-proceeds / until-clean-reaches-clean). **Sandbox-verified vs CI-only (honest, Golden Rule #1):** sandbox is Python 3.11 and cannot import the PEP-695 `orchestrator/retry.py` chain that `pull_controller`/`run_ingest` pull in, so the two NEW wheel-free pure modules + their unit/property/golden/bench/stress suites ran fully HERE at 100% line+branch (ruff format+check clean); `pull_controller.py` / `cli.py` / `app.py` pass ruff but their tests are **CI 3.12 oracle-only**. **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED — this is a LAKE-ingest recovery/pre-flight layer; spot only. **Builds on:** DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#483, the `retry_failed_windows` engine each until-clean round reuses), DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 (#485, the `classify_pull` verdict vocabulary both new modules reuse), DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (the `auth_aborted` signal + the truth that RenewToken cannot revive a dead token), DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 (`RENEW_BEFORE_EXPIRY_S` 12h, the single-source expiring-soon threshold), DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the shared skip-ledger every round re-uses), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #10 / #11.

578a. **DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-DATAPROBE-001 — the pre-flight gate must classify a token DEAD only on a GENUINE auth failure (`is_auth_failure`), via a real DATA probe — fixing the false-dead "token expired" loop** (2026-06-08, operator-reported from a live `make run`; hardens DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 #577). **Problem (code-traced from the live log):** the operator entered a FRESH Dhan token and every "Pull spot" / "Retry failed windows" click instantly aborted with `universe.pull_all.preflight_refused verdict=auth_expired` ("🔑 token is DEAD"), never firing a single data window. Root cause: the auto pre-flight (`pull_all_spot`, `preflight=None` + live creds → `probe_token_live`) decided life/death from ONE `RenewToken` GET, and its `except DhanError:` caught the ENTIRE error hierarchy — so a transient `429` / `5xx` / timeout / transport / plain-`400` (and even a `200`-OK with an unexpected JSON shape, which `renew_token` raises as `DhanAuthError`) ALL classified the token `dead`. Worse, `RenewToken` is the WRONG validity oracle: per `docs/dhan-ref/02` it "only renews tokens generated from Dhan Web" and refuses TOTP-/OAuth-minted tokens that are PERFECTLY VALID for `charts/intraday` data calls — so a working token gets declared dead, the banner says "regenerate at web.dhan.co", the operator regenerates, the same refusal repeats → an infinite false-dead loop. The pre-flight GATE (which blocks the whole pull) was thus strictly MORE trigger-happy than the in-pull fail-fast guard it fronts — even though that guard already uses the project's single source of truth for "token died", `errors.is_auth_failure` (a `401`/`403` OR a `400` carrying `DH-906`/"Invalid Token"; DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001). **Fix (Full: data-probe + narrow):** (A) NEW pure classifier `token_preflight.classify_data_probe(error: DhanError | None, *, now, …) -> TokenPreflight` — `dead` IFF `is_auth_failure(error)`, else `valid` (PROCEED): `error is None` (fetched, or empty/no-data) → valid; a transient/non-auth `DhanError` (429/5xx/timeout/transport/plain-400/`DH-905`) → valid so the pull starts (the in-pull guard still catches a real mid-pull death); reuses `classify_token` (no new state vocab, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). (B) NEW live seam `probe_token_data_live(adapter, instrument, *, today=None, now=None, …)` (`# pragma: no cover`): fires ONE tiny 1-minute `charts/intraday` fetch over a short recent window — the EXACT surface a pull needs, the only question that matters ("can this token pull bars?") — and routes the outcome through `classify_data_probe`. (C) The legacy `probe_token_live` `RenewToken` catch is NARROWED identically (`is_auth_failure(exc)`), so even that path no longer false-deads on a transient. **Wiring:** the dashboard auto pre-flight (`pull_controller.pull_all_spot`) and the CLI gate (`cli.py:cmd_fetch`) now both call `probe_token_data_live(adapter, instruments[0])` instead of `probe_token_live(client)` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — one oracle, both call sites); the dashboard guard also gains an `and instruments` guard for the empty-selection no-op. The DEAD→`auth_expired` mapping (`preflight_pull_verdict` → `classify_pull`) and the loud refusal (`_preflight_refusal` → `universe.pull_all.preflight_refused`) are UNCHANGED — a genuinely dead token still refuses up front exactly as #577. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the data probe proves the token is ALIVE for data, not its remaining lifetime (`remaining_seconds=None` → `valid`); it cannot revive a dead token; a true `is_auth_failure` still refuses. It is one `≤ 5 r/s` call (one call cannot breach the per-second cap). **Tests / gates:** `tests/unit/test_dhan_token_preflight.py` gains 12 cases on the pure `classify_data_probe` (success→valid; each `is_auth_failure` variant→dead; each transient/non-auth `DhanError`→valid-so-`preflight_pull_verdict` is `None`), keeping the module's 100% line+branch gate; the two live seams stay `# pragma: no cover` (real token + network), their decision logic IS the covered pure classifier. **Sandbox-verified:** built `trading_core` + `fno_math` wheels under Python 3.12 and ran the affected suites — `tests/unit/test_dhan_token_preflight.py`, `test_dhan_errors.py`, `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `test_dhan_until_clean.py`, `test_dhan_pull_verdict.py`, `test_verdict_banner.py`, `tests/golden/test_token_preflight_golden.py` (172 passed), plus the broad `-k "dhan or pull or verdict or preflight or token"` sweep (766 passed); `mypy --strict` clean on `token_preflight.py` (the only file changed beyond 2-line caller swaps), ruff clean on all touched files. **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED — this is a LAKE-ingest pre-flight correctness fix; spot only. **Builds on:** DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 (#577, the pre-flight layer this hardens), DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (`is_auth_failure`, the single source of truth this aligns the gate with), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #10 / #11.

579a. **DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 — true auto-resume (re-fire batches until 100% clean, zero clicks) with the mandatory daily Dhan quota as its hard brake** (2026-06-08, operator: "add a true auto-resume that re-fires the next batch on its own until 100% clean… meanwhile track this quota also because this quota is also mandatory"). **Scope (operator-confirmed):** AUTO-RESUME + QUOTA TRACKING only; **TOTP unattended auth is explicitly OUT** (the operator chose the "honest partial" — this is NOT overnight-proof: a token that expires past ~24h still needs a fresh token, the documented `RenewToken`-can't-revive-a-dead-token gap). **Two gaps found + closed:** (1) the existing `until_clean` loop (DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 #577) stopped after a bounded 5 rounds (`stop_budget`), leaving residual for a manual re-click; (2) **the dashboard live controller was built `DhanRateController()` with `quota_tracker=None`** — so dashboard pulls were NOT counted against the mandatory 100,000/day Dhan quota AT ALL (the persisted `DailyQuotaTracker` existed + was wired into the bucket, but the dashboard never passed one). **Fix — engine (pure, 100% line+branch):** (A) `until_clean.decide_until_clean` gains two terminal verdicts — `stop_quota` (the day's quota is spent: like a dead token, no immediate retry lands a bar today; pause for the IST-midnight reset) + `stop_no_progress` (a round that shrank the residual by ZERO — a stuck window can never be drained by more identical rounds). New priority worst→best: `stop_dead` > `stop_clean` > `stop_quota` > `stop_no_progress` > `stop_budget` > `continue`. The two new kwargs default to the pre-feature behaviour (`quota_exhausted=False`, `made_progress=True`) so every existing caller is byte-unchanged. (B) `run_until_clean` gains an injected `quota_exhausted: () -> bool` hook (checked after each round) + an OPT-IN `stop_when_stuck` flag (the no-progress guard is OFF by default, so the prior bounded path + the stress/property runs with constant residual still end on `stop_budget`). (C) NEW `AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS = 50` — a generous-but-FINITE budget (Golden Rule #10 — never infinite): the dead/quota/no-progress guards terminate the loop long before this cap in every real run, so it is only the final backstop. `UntilCleanOutcome` gains `.stopped_on_quota` / `.stopped_no_progress` + maps `stop_quota` → the new `quota_exhausted` `PullVerdict` kind. (D) `pull_verdict.classify_pull` gains a `quota_exhausted` kind (headline "📊 Daily Dhan quota reached — auto-resume paused for today.", action "re-pull after the IST-midnight reset; already-pulled windows are skipped"), ranked just under `auth_expired` (both are "nothing lands today"); `needs_operator=True`; `verdict_banner` maps it to the amber "paused — resume later" lane (distinct from red "broken token"). **Fix — wiring:** `_build_live_controller()` now passes `quota_tracker=DailyQuotaTracker()` (the SAME persisted `~/.brutex/quota/quota.lmdb`, global to the API key), so every paced dashboard call increments + checks the quota; `DhanRateController.snapshot()` carries the `quota_used` / `quota_remaining` / `quota_limit` gauge (read OUTSIDE the controller lock — `_quota` is set once, never mutated — so no nested lock over the tracker's LMDB read) + a `quota_exhausted()` helper; `pull_all_spot`'s `until_clean` branch passes that hook + `stop_when_stuck=True` to `run_until_clean`, and its `until_clean_rounds` default is now `AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS` (the dashboard "Retry failed windows" → auto-resume path); `BulkSpotReport` gains a `quota_exhausted` field threaded into `.verdict`. **Surface:** the quota gauge flows through `make_rate_observer` → `RateLimitPanel.{quota_used,quota_remaining,quota_limit}` (default `quota_limit=-1` sentinel ⇒ the panel hides the gauge when no tracker is wired, never a false 0) → `/api/v1/rate` + `/api/v1/state` JSON, so the operator SEES the mandatory quota spent, not just live r/s. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the auto-resume is FINITE (clean / token-dead / quota-spent / no-progress / 50-round backstop) — never an infinite loop; the quota brake STOPS loudly + resumes on the operator's next pull after the IST-midnight reset (it does NOT auto-wait-then-resume — that would override the locked DEC-P0-028 "no auto-resume after quota exhaustion", which stands; operator-confirmed "stop loudly + resume tomorrow"); and the whole feature is NOT overnight-proof without TOTP (deferred). **Tests / gates (sandbox-verified, Python 3.12 + Rust wheels built):** 100% line+branch on every touched pure module — `until_clean.py` (59 stmts / 10 br), `pull_verdict.py` (34/8), `verdict_banner.py` (24/2), `rate_control.py` (93/14); new cases across `tests/unit/test_dhan_until_clean.py` (stop_quota / stop_no_progress / every priority ordering / opt-in default + driver quota-hook + auto-resume-drains-over-many-rounds), `test_dhan_pull_verdict.py` (quota kind + priority + default-off), `test_verdict_banner.py` (amber quota banner + the kind parametrize), `test_dhan_rate_control.py` (quota in snapshot + `quota_exhausted()` + no-tracker sentinel, via a REAL `DailyQuotaTracker` on a fixed IST clock), `test_dashboard_rate_panel.py` (gauge plumbing → panel JSON), `tests/golden/test_token_preflight_golden.py` (the `stop_quota` → `quota_exhausted` golden); the broad `-k "dhan or pull or verdict or quota or rate or until or preflight or token or dashboard"` sweep is **1398 passed** (the only non-passes are the pre-existing `httpx`/`starlette` TestClient env-version incompatibility — green in CI). ruff check + format clean; `mypy --strict` clean on the 4 pure modules (the `app.py`/`pull_controller.py` PEP-695 import chain is CI-3.12-checked). **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED — LAKE-ingest recovery + quota safety; spot only. **Builds on:** DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 (#577, the `run_until_clean` loop this extends), DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#483, the per-round `retry_failed_windows` engine), DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 (#485, the `classify_pull` vocabulary), DEC-P0-028 (the IST-midnight `DailyQuotaTracker` + the "no silent auto-resume after exhaustion" rule this RESPECTS), DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the controller the quota tracker now wires into), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 + Golden Rules #1 / #3 / #10 / #11.

580a. **DEC-NTM-CONSTITUENT-CACHE-001 — last-good disk cache for the NIFTY TOTAL MARKET constituent CSV, so a niftyindices timeout no longer craters the universe from ~750 to ~211 stocks** (2026-06-08, operator-reported from a live `make run`: "what happened to our NTM… 211 STOCKS"). **Problem (code-traced from the live log):** the `/universe` page's full ~750-stock universe is NOT in the Dhan instrument master — it is the **NIFTY TOTAL MARKET broad-market constituents**, fetched best-effort at every keyless load (`instrument_loader._ntm_admission` → `nse_constituents.fetch_constituent_csv` → `https://www.niftyindices.com/IndexConstituent/ind_niftytotalmarket_list.csv`, 10 s urllib timeout). `niftyindices.com` **bot-blocks plain HTTP clients** (the operator's BROWSER downloads the CSV fine, but `urllib` — even with a browser User-Agent — gets WAF-challenged / hangs), so the read times out (`constituent resolution failed: The read operation timed out`, `constituents=0`) and the universe SILENTLY dropped to the ~211 base F&O set. It ALSO blocked boot: while the read hung (pre-timeout) the server had not bound yet → the operator's browser got `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`; once it timed out, boot continued (slowly) with the degraded set. (Confirmed NOT the recent DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 / quota wiring: the quota tracker opens in 0.000 s and the lifespan `startup complete` was ~1 ms; all the delay was the NSE read.) **Fix — a last-good disk cache (the operator's own "use a fallback CSV" ask):** NEW `brutex/dashboard/ntm_cache.py` — a pure, best-effort, never-raises cache (`save_constituent_csv` atomic `.tmp`→rename, empty-input no-op; `load_cached_constituent_csv` → `str | None`; `default_cache_dir()` = `~/.brutex/cache/`). `instrument_loader._resolve_constituent_csv` now wraps the live fetch: a successful non-empty fetch REFRESHES the cache; a live failure (timeout/bot-block) OR empty result FALLS BACK to the cached CSV → the universe stays at ~750. **Operator seed path:** the operator can drop the browser-downloaded `ind_niftytotalmarket_list.csv` at `~/.brutex/cache/ntm_constituents.csv` and the failing live fetch falls back to it — guaranteed ~750 without depending on the flaky NSE fetch (the note tells them how). A single fail-soft `try/except` (the cache helper re-raises ONLY when no cache covers the failure) keeps one tested except site, not a provably-dead nested one. **Wiring:** `load_instrument_master` gains `constituent_cache_dir: Path | None` (None → `default_cache_dir()`); tests inject a tmp dir for isolation. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the cache only mitigates a TRANSIENT live failure once a fetch has succeeded (or the operator seeds it) — a first-ever boot with no cache AND a dead NSE still degrades to the base set (with an honest note + the seed instructions); it does NOT make `urllib` defeat NSE's bot-blocking, and the constituent list rebalances semi-annually so a long-stale cache can drift (refreshed on every success). NOT hardcoding a constituent list (CLAUDE.md §1 — the operator-verified CSV stays the source). **Tests / gates (sandbox-verified, Python 3.12):** 100% line+branch on both touched modules — `ntm_cache.py` (26 stmts / 2 br) + `instrument_loader.py` (78 / 10); `tests/unit/test_ntm_cache.py` (8 cases: round-trip, empty no-op, missing/empty/dir → None, atomic overwrite, unwritable → False, default dir) + `tests/unit/test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py` (live-seeds-then-failure-falls-back, operator-dropped-cache, isolated no-cache degrade paths); broad `-k "instrument or ntm or universe or constituent or loader"` sweep **495 passed**; ruff check+format clean, `mypy --strict` clean. **Scope:** dashboard universe-load robustness only — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE + the lake are UNAFFECTED (this is the in-memory `/universe` instrument list). **Builds on:** DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-LOAD-001 (the NTM admission this hardens), DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-URL-001 (the niftyindices URL), DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 (the best-effort fetch), CLAUDE.md §1 / §10 / §11.

581a. **DEC-DEFAULT-DATE-RANGE-001 — the date pickers PRE-FILL the canonical [2021-01-01, previous day] default everywhere (spot · options · reports), from ONE source of truth** (2026-06-08, operator: "whenever the date is not selected it should be the default… this start date and end date should be the default selected in from and to date itself… default across everywhere including reports… as long as I override this manually this should be the same everywhere"). **Problem:** the backend ALREADY defaulted a blank spot pull (`resolve_candle_range`) AND a blank options pull (`option_pull_controller` forces `from=DHAN_HISTORY_FLOOR, to=None`) to `[2021-01-01, previous trading day]`, but (a) the UI date inputs (`universe.html` `#fromDate`/`#toDate`, `reports.html` `#from`/`#to`) were **BLANK** — the operator couldn't SEE the default — and (b) the **reports** routes (`/api/v1/reports/preopen.xlsx` + `.zip`) **REQUIRED** `from`/`to` (`Query(..., alias=...)`), so reports was inconsistent with spot/options and a blank submit 422'd. **Fix (one source of truth → consistent everywhere):** (1) NEW `pull_controller.default_date_range(now=None) -> (from_iso, to_iso)` — reuses `resolve_candle_range(from=None,to=None,year=None)` so the pre-filled UI dates are GUARANTEED byte-identical to what a blank pull/report fetches (`to` = the inclusive previous day = the exclusive `end` − 1 day); injected `now` for deterministic tests + per-render freshness across midnight. (2) The from/to inputs carry `value="__BRUTEX_DATE_FROM__"` / `__BRUTEX_DATE_TO__` tokens; `app._fill_default_dates(html)` swaps them per render (the template cache holds the RAW token, never a frozen date) — wired into BOTH `_render_universe_html` (spot + options share the pickers) and `_render_reports_html`. (3) NEW `app._resolve_report_dates(start, end) -> (date, date)` — a blank `from`/`to` DEFAULTS to the same canonical range (so a cleared field never 400s + reports matches spot/options); pure + framework-free (raises `ValueError` → the route maps to 400), de-duping the parse/validate that was copy-pasted across the `.xlsx` + `.zip` routes; both routes now take `Query(None, alias=...)`. **Guarantee:** the default lives in exactly ONE function (`resolve_candle_range`); the UI pre-fill, the spot/options backends, and the reports backend all derive from it — pre-filled by default, an explicit pick overrides, a cleared field falls back to the SAME range, on every surface. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** an EXPLICIT `to_date` reaching today is still honoured (the previous-day default only applies when blank — DEC-PULL-FUTURE-WINDOW-001 unchanged); the pre-fill is computed from UTC `now` (the operator is IST, so the displayed "previous day" can differ by ≤1 day at the UTC/IST midnight seam — cosmetic, and the backend clamps regardless). **Tests / gates (sandbox-verified, Python 3.12):** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` (`default_date_range(_NOW) == ("2021-01-01","2026-05-29")` against the existing `resolve_candle_range` blank-default test), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_template.py` (the spot/options pickers render pre-filled + no leftover token), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_reports_ux.py` (the /reports pickers pre-filled + `_resolve_report_dates` defaults/overrides/partial-blank + rejects bad/inverted → ValueError); broad `-k "dashboard or reports or universe or pull or preopen"` sweep **767 passed**; ruff check+format clean, `mypy --strict` clean on `pull_controller.py` + `app.py`. (The `.xlsx`/`.zip` route wiring itself is exercised via the TestClient route tests in CI — the sandbox `httpx`/`starlette` version skip — but the date-defaulting logic is the 100%-covered pure `_resolve_report_dates`.) **Scope:** dashboard UX + reports default-range consistency only — `resolve_candle_range` / the pull engines / the lake are UNCHANGED. **Builds on:** the `resolve_candle_range` default (DEC-DHAN-PULL-SCOPE-001 / DEC-PULL-FUTURE-WINDOW-001), DEC-DHAN-SPOT-MULTI-SATURATE-001 (the from/to picker wiring), DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 (the reports routes), CLAUDE.md §3 (the locked 2021-01-01 → today range) + §11 COMMON.

## DEC-CREDS-JWT-SHAPE-001 (2026-06-08)

582a. **DEC-CREDS-JWT-SHAPE-001 — reject a truncated access-token paste at the web-form save boundary (JWT-shape guard), so an incomplete paste fails FAST with "re-paste the FULL token" instead of silently saving a doomed token that later dies with `DH-906 Invalid Token`** (2026-06-08, operator: *"even in webpage and even in db also it should be entered entirely … no truncation"*). **Why:** a freshly-generated, valid Dhan token was rejected by the live pull with `DH-906 Invalid Token`; a `curl` with the FULL token returned a clean `200`, proving the token was good and the failure was an **incomplete clipboard paste** into the Set Credentials box. A full audit confirmed BruteX does **not** truncate anywhere — `credentials.html` token input has no `maxlength` (faithful `.value` → JSON), the `CredentialsIn` body model has no `max_length`, the route passes the value straight through, and `normalise_token` only `.strip()`s outer whitespace before `json.dumps` stores the whole string — so the clip happened in the OS paste, *before* BruteX saw the token. The fix is not to "stop truncating" (we never did) but to **catch** a clipped paste. **What shipped (pure, 100%-gated):** `brutex/config/credentials.py` — NEW `token_shape_problem(token)` returns a secret-free reason (segment count / length only, never the value) when the access token is not a well-formed JWT — exactly **3 non-empty base64url segments** joined by `.` (`header.payload.signature`, per `CLAUDE.md` §6 "access-token (JWT, 24h)"); a truncated paste almost always loses or empties the trailing signature segment, so this structural check catches the dominant failure mode offline. `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `POST /api/v1/credentials` calls the guard *before* `save_dhan_credentials` and returns `400` with the "Clear the field and re-paste the FULL token." reason on a malformed paste (which the Credentials page already renders in its `msg.err` line). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** the strict gate `pytest --cov=brutex.config.credentials --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_credentials.py` = **100.00%** (138 stmts / 36 branch); NEW `TestTokenShape` ×8 (valid 3-segment passes; whitespace stripped first; 2-segment + single-segment flagged "truncated"/"found N"; empty leading/trailing segment + non-base64url char flagged "base64url"; reason never contains the token) + NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_credentials_route.py` ×2 (truncated → `400` "re-paste" + nothing persisted; valid JWT → `200` masked preview, full secret never echoed); `brutex.config.credentials` ADDED to the CI strict-100% pass list (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`); `ruff` + format + `mypy --strict` clean on the touched files. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a paste that lost a whole segment, has an empty segment, or carries a non-base64url char is rejected instantly at save with a clear, secret-free message — the operator can no longer save a structurally-broken token. 🟡 STRUCTURAL only: a token clipped *within* its 3rd segment but still leaving three segments can pass the shape check — the live pre-flight data-probe (`token_preflight`) remains the backstop for that residual case; the guard is wired on the dashboard route (the human paste surface), not yet on the `brutex auth set` CLI / `BRUTEX_DHAN_*` env paths (advanced/automated entry, lower paste-truncation risk). 🚫 no change to storage, normalisation, masking, or the adapter auth flow. **Builds on:** DEC-CREDS-NORMALISE-001 (the `.strip()` canonicalisation this sits beside) · DEC-CREDS-PREVIEW-001 (the masked `access_token_len` preview that helps the operator eyeball a full-length paste) · DEC-CREDENTIALS-STORE-001 (the secure store) · `CLAUDE.md` §6 (Dhan access-token is a JWT) · §4 (no secret in logs/errors) · §11 COMMON (one validator, imported).

## DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 (2026-06-08)

583a. **DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 — `renew_token()` parses the rotated token from the `"token"` key (not `"accessToken"`), so the pull-start `RenewToken` no longer self-destructs a valid Dhan token into `DH-906`** (2026-06-08, operator-reported from repeated live `make run` failures: every freshly-generated token died with `DH-906 Invalid Token` within ~2s of the pull starting). **Root cause (proven by the operator's 3-curl test):** BruteX calls `maybe_renew_token` PROACTIVELY at the start of every live spot pull (`_maybe_renew_adapter_token`, DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 Piece 2). Per the Dhan doc — *"one active token at a time — generating a new token invalidates the old one"* — `GET /v2/RenewToken` on an active web-generated token **ROTATES**: it mints a new `+24h` token AND invalidates the one presented in the `access-token` header. The operator's curl captured the EXACT response shape: `{"createTime":"…","expiryTime":"2026-06-09T16:25:59.059","token":"eyJ…"}` — the rotated credential is under **`"token"`**. But `renew_token()` read `payload.get("accessToken")` (a key Dhan NEVER returns) → `None` → raised `DhanAuthError("missing string accessToken/expiryTime")` on EVERY successful rotation → the best-effort wrapper logged one `auth.renew_failed` and proceeded on the **old token Dhan had just invalidated** → the very next `charts/historical` call returned `HTTP 400 DH-906 "Invalid Token"`. The operator's 3-curl proof, in order: (1) `charts/historical` with a fresh token → `200` + real NIFTY bars (token ALIVE); (2) `RenewToken` → `{…,"token":"<new>"}` (rotation); (3) the SAME original token → `DH-906` (now dead). So BruteX was killing its own token on every pull — no amount of regenerating could help, because each pull rotated the new token away and then used the corpse. **Fix (one-key correctness fix):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/auth.py` `renew_token()` now reads `payload.get("token")` (the rotated access token) + `payload.get("expiryTime")` (already correct); the error message becomes `"missing string token/expiryTime"`. With the right key, `maybe_renew_token` returns the rotated `TokenInfo`, `_maybe_renew_adapter_token` rebuilds the adapter's client with it (`replace(...)`, already wired at `pull_controller.py:1180/1471`), and the pull proceeds on the LIVE rotated token → the data calls succeed. The two other `renew_token()` callers — `token_keepalive.py` (12h keepalive) and `token_preflight.py` (RenewToken oracle) — inherit the fix automatically (they consume the returned `TokenInfo`, they do not parse the raw response). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `pytest --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.auth --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_dhan_auth.py` = **100.00%** (49 stmts / 2 branch, 23 passed) — including NEW `test_real_rotation_response_shape_is_parsed` (the exact `{"createTime","expiryTime","token"}` body the operator's curl returned, which the pre-fix `accessToken` parser would have rejected) + the `missing/non-string` cases retargeted to the `token` key; `tests/unit/test_dhan_token_keepalive.py` `_renew_body` helper updated to the real `"token"` shape (81 passed across keepalive + preflight + golden + client); broad `-k "dhan or auth or renew or token or pull or ingest"` sweep **802 passed**; `ruff` + format + `mypy --strict` clean on the touched files. (`test_dhan_client.py`'s `get_json` round-trip tests use an arbitrary JSON body and assert raw passthrough — they are about the transport/JSON layer, not renew parsing, so they are intentionally left unchanged.) **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the proactive pull-start `RenewToken` now captures + uses the rotated token, ending the self-inflicted `DH-906` loop; a genuinely fresh, active, web-generated token now pulls cleanly. 🟡 `RenewToken` still only renews an ACTIVE, web-generated token (an already-expired or TOTP-minted token is still refused → the pull proceeds on the existing token and Piece-1 fail-fast handles a mid-pull death — DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 unchanged); the renewed token lives in the in-memory adapter for the pull's duration and is NOT written back to `~/.brutex/credentials.json` (the file keeps the operator's original until they next save — a known, separate enhancement). 🚫 no change to the request (still the headers-only GET of DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-GET-001), the rate gating, or the credentials store. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-GET-001 (the GET request shape), DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (the proactive-renew wiring this corrects), DEC-CREDS-JWT-SHAPE-001 (#582, the save-time guard — orthogonal: the token here was a valid JWT, the bug was BruteX rotating it away), `docs/dhan-ref/02-authentication.md` ("one active token at a time"), CLAUDE.md §1 (verified against the operator's live curl, not guessed) · §6.

## DEC-DHAN-INTRADAY-TIMEOUT-RAISE-001 (2026-06-08)

584a. **DEC-DHAN-INTRADAY-TIMEOUT-RAISE-001 — raise the Dhan whole-request timeout 10s → 25s, so a slow-but-VALID 90-day 1-minute payload completes instead of being killed as a false `DhanTimeoutError` and re-requested** (2026-06-08, operator live `make run`: once DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 (#583) un-broke auth, the first real 783-symbol full-history pull produced a flood of `dhan.retry … error=DhanTimeoutError endpoint=charts/intraday`). **Root cause (field-measured, not guessed):** the pull is healthy — `auth.renewed`, bars landing (BANKNIFTY 103k+), `keep-first` conflicts logged — but `charts/intraday` is asked for a **90-day window of 1-minute bars** (`INTRADAY_WINDOW_DAYS=90` ⇒ ~22,000 bars, a multi-MB JSON), and under sustained load Dhan takes **≥10s** to build each one. The live throughput log showed `latency_ms_p95 ≈ 10,072` and `latency_ms_max ≈ 10,416` — pinned right at the old `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 10.0`. So a large fraction of calls that *would have returned valid data at ~10–13s* were killed at the 10s ceiling, retried (200ms→400ms backoff ×3), and on exhaustion re-queued as transient — **adding load and slowing the very endpoint that was already slow.** The old 10s value (DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001, lowered 30→10) rested on the assumption "real Dhan intraday/option responses land well under a few seconds" — TRUE for indices early in a pull, FALSE for a sustained 783-symbol sweep. **Fix (one-constant tuning):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py` `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: float = 10.0 → 25.0` (the `DhanClient.timeout` field default; still per-client overridable). 25s lets a slow-but-valid intraday response finish on the **first** attempt, ending the false-timeout storm; the bounded fast-retry (`_DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`) still recovers a TRUE stall (now caught at 25s), and the 30→10 "one 30s stall freezes the SEQUENTIAL pull" concern no longer applies because the window fetch is now **parallel** (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001) — one slow call no longer blocks the others. **Scope (operator-directed):** raise the timeout ONLY; the intraday window stays 90 days (Option B "shrink the window → smaller/faster payloads" was explicitly NOT taken — it would ~3× the call count and the 429 pressure). The 5 r/s rate cap + adaptive controller are byte-unchanged. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `pytest --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.client --cov-branch tests/unit/test_dhan_client.py` = **100.00%** (146 stmts / 22 branch, 39 passed) — NEW `test_default_timeout_is_generous_for_large_intraday_payloads` (asserts `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT ≥ 25.0` AND that a default-built client passes it to the transport on a `charts/intraday` call, so an accidental future lowering is caught); `ruff` + format + `mypy --strict` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ fewer false timeouts on the heavy 1-minute history calls → less wasted re-request load → the full-history pull grinds through faster. 🟡 this does NOT make Dhan faster — it stops US from sabotaging slow-but-valid responses; a GENUINELY stalled connection now takes up to `25s × 3` before it is marked transient (bounded, parallel-isolated, recovered by the retry pass + resume), and a sustained 783-symbol pull is still hours of wall-time bound by Dhan's 5 r/s + endpoint latency (CLAUDE.md §8 honest-SLA). 🚫 no change to the rate cap, the 90-day window, the retry budget, or the conflict/keep-first policy. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 (the 30→10 this re-tunes), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 (the parallelism that defuses the original 30s-freeze concern), DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 (#583, the auth fix that finally let a real pull run long enough to expose this), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 (rate cap untouched) · §8 (honest SLA) · §1 (measured from the live run, not guessed).
