## DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 (2026-06-08)

585a. **DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 — the expired-option `OptionParquetWriter` gets a per-PARTITION write lock + an `os.fsync` before the atomic rename, so its merge-on-write is correct on its OWN (no longer safe only by the coarse `OptionBarSink` audit lock) and a crash can't leave a truncated partition** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep #10 B-2). **Problem (code-traced):** `option_parquet_writer.py` `_merge_partition` did a read→`pl.concat`/`unique`→`os.replace` read-modify-write with **NO per-partition lock** — unlike the spot `ParquetWriter` (`parquet_writer.py:102-117`) which interns a `threading.Lock` per destination PATH (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001) — and its `_atomic_write_parquet` did `df.write_parquet(tmp)`→`os.replace` with **NO `os.fsync`** (vs the spot writer's `_atomic_write` at `parquet_writer.py:535`). The option write was therefore safe ONLY by the coarse process-wide `OptionBarSink._lock` (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001) that also serialises the audit-chain append — i.e. correctness was borrowed from a lock whose real job is the single-writer audit chain, and that global lock kills ALL option-write parallelism. Two writers to the SAME `options/<series>/<YYYY>-<MM>.parquet` (a 30-day option pull straddles a month boundary, so two windows of one series share a month partition) would race a lost-update: both read the old file, each unions only its own bars, the later `os.replace` wins and silently drops the other's bars. **Fix (mirror the spot writer, belt-and-braces):** (1) a process-wide `_PARTITION_LOCKS: dict[Path, threading.Lock]` + `_PARTITION_LOCKS_GUARD` + `_partition_lock(dest)` — interned lazily, keyed by resolved PATH (not writer instance, so one-writer-per-worker fan-out still shares the file's lock), O(1) get-or-create under the guard, the guard held ONLY for the dict op never across the write; `_merge_partition`'s existence-check→read→union→atomic-rename now runs `with _partition_lock(dest)`, so same-file writers serialise while different partitions never contend (parallelism preserved). The union is order-independent (keyed by `(side, timestamp)`), so the stored bytes are identical regardless of which window lands first (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 7). (2) `_atomic_write_parquet` now `os.open(tmp, O_RDONLY)`→`os.fsync`→`os.close` BEFORE `os.replace`, so the tmp's data is on stable storage before the rename publishes it (a crash between rename and the OS flushing the page cache can no longer surface a zero-length/truncated parquet — `os.replace` orders metadata, not data; `polars` owns the write so the fd is re-opened read-only purely to fsync, which Linux permits). This makes the writer correct independently so the option write can later be lifted out from under the global sink lock without a lost-update race. **O(1) discipline (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5):** the lock lookup is an O(1) dict get-or-create; per-bar work is unchanged (O(1) amortised union); the fsync is one syscall per flush, not per bar. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `pytest --cov=brutex.data.option_parquet_writer --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_option_parquet_writer.py` = **100.00%** (98 stmts / 18 branch, 17 passed) — NEW `TestPartitionLock` ×3 mirroring the spot writer: `test_same_path_returns_same_lock` (interning), `test_different_paths_get_distinct_locks` (no false contention), and `test_concurrent_same_partition_writes_lose_no_bars` (16-thread `threading.Barrier`, all 16 distinct-minute bars survive the merge → no lost update); the existing money-rounding / idempotent-repull / partial-merge / month-split / atomic-cleanup / path-safety cases unchanged; `ruff` check + format clean, `mypy --strict` clean on the module. This is the exact CI strict-100% gate at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1274`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the writer is now correct on its own (per-partition lock) AND crash-durable (fsync) — matching the spot writer; ✅ option-write parallelism is now SAFE at the writer layer (the global sink lock can be narrowed in a follow-up — NOT done here, out of scope). 🟡 the lock is in-PROCESS only (one host) — a multi-process pull would still need OS-level file locking (no such pull exists; the ingest is multi-thread, single-process per DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001); cross-RUN vendor-drift on the same `(side, ts)` is still keep-first (existing behaviour, a tracked follow-up). 🚫 no change to the merge semantics, the schema, the 2dp money rounding, or the `OptionBarSink` audit lock. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 (the spot per-partition lock this mirrors), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the coarse audit lock this de-couples correctness from), DEC-EXPIRED-OPTIONS-TABLE-001 (the option table), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1)) · Rule 7 (idempotence/order-independence) · §4 (no-look-ahead n/a; atomic-durable write) · §13 (merge-readiness: correctness > reliability > performance).

## DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001 (2026-06-08)

586a. **DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001 — add operator-configurable SPKI (SubjectPublicKeyInfo SHA-256) TLS public-key pinning to the Dhan production transport, with a SAFE opt-in fallback, a security-specific terminal error, and a never-silent audit+alert on mismatch** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep #9 E-1: `brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py` wired `urllib_transport` = default `urllib.request.urlopen`, which validates the `api.dhan.co` server certificate against the **system CA store ONLY**. A CA compromise / mis-issuance / corporate-proxy MITM presenting a *validly chained* cert for `api.dhan.co` would be accepted → the 24h bearer access-token JWT + every fetched bar would flow to the attacker). **Fix (defence-in-depth, second independent check ON TOP of CA validation):** new pure module `brutex/adapters/dhan/cert_pinning.py` (`DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001`): (1) `spki_sha256_pin(cert_der)` = `base64(SHA-256(DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo))` — the standard HPKP / mobile-pinning pin, computed by a minimal, self-contained DER walk (`_extract_spki_der`: Certificate→tbsCertificate→skip optional `[0]` version + the 5 RFC-5280 fields → SubjectPublicKeyInfo), so NO new runtime dependency and every malformed-input branch is testable; (2) `PinPolicy` (frozen, injectable) resolved from env via `from_env` — `BRUTEX_DHAN_TLS_PINS` (comma/whitespace pin set, optional `sha256/` prefix) + `BRUTEX_DHAN_TLS_PIN_DISABLE` (explicit break-glass opt-out); (3) `PinPolicy.verify(cert_der, host)` decision table — **opt-out** → WARNING + return; **no pins configured** → DEBUG + return (the SAFE fallback to system-CA validation, so a missing config NEVER breaks a live pull); **enforced + key matches any configured pin** (current+next ⇒ rotation-survivable) → DEBUG + return; **enforced + MISMATCH or absent/empty peer cert** → emit the CRITICAL `dhan.tls.pin_mismatch` audit line + fire the injected `alert` hook + raise the security-specific `DhanCertPinError` — **NEVER a silent fall-back** (a mismatch is treated as an active MITM, not a soft warning). `DhanCertPinError` is deliberately NOT in `is_retryable`, so an attacker-presented cert is never fast-retried/re-queued. **Wiring:** `client.make_pinning_transport(policy)` runs the request over `http.client` (returns status+body for 2xx AND 4xx/5xx like the old shim), extracts `getpeercert(binary_form=True)` and calls `policy.verify` BEFORE sending the token-bearing request (a MITM never even receives the JWT); `client.default_dhan_transport()` is the COMMON single wiring point (`make_pinning_transport(PinPolicy.from_env())`) now used by all 3 production builders (`cli.py` `_build_live_pull_adapter`, `pull_controller.py` `_build_live_pull_adapter` + `_start_token_keepalive`). With no pins configured this is byte-equivalent in behaviour to the prior `urllib_transport` wiring. **NO hardcoded pin** for `api.dhan.co` (a baked-in pin would brick every operator on Dhan's next key rotation, and Golden Rule #1 forbids unverifiable embedded facts) — pins are operator-supplied; a pin is a PUBLIC key hash, not a secret, so it is safe to log/echo (unlike the token). **O(1):** the pin check is O(1) per connection (one SHA-256 over the fixed-size SPKI + a frozenset membership test) — handshake-time, NOT a per-bar hot path; no O(1)-total claim. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** new `tests/unit/test_dhan_cert_pinning.py` (32 cases) + `test_dhan_client.py` factory tests → `pytest --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.cert_pinning --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.client --cov-branch` = **100.00% line+branch on BOTH** (cert_pinning 108 stmts/34 branch, client 151 stmts/22 branch, 0 miss); covers pin-MATCH, pin-MISMATCH (audit+alert+raise), ROTATION (multi-pin), missing-config fallback, explicit opt-out (all truthy/falsy spellings), absent/empty peer cert, and every malformed-DER branch — the real-cert SPKI cross-checked against `cryptography`'s `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` bytes (importorskip, NOT a runtime dep). `ruff` + `ruff format` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` + `bandit` (No issues identified) all clean; `semgrep` rule-registry fetch is blocked by this environment's network policy (HTTP 403) — bandit is the security gate that ran. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ when an operator configures `BRUTEX_DHAN_TLS_PINS`, a CA-compromise/MITM with a non-pinned key is REFUSED + audited + alerted before the token is sent. 🟡 pinning is **opt-in** — out of the box (no pins) the behaviour is unchanged (system-CA validation only); the operator must obtain + configure the real `api.dhan.co` SPKI pin(s) to enforce (the `pins_from_certs` helper derives them from trusted material). The `alert` hook defaults to a no-op; the always-on CRITICAL `dhan.tls.pin_mismatch` structlog line is the audit+alert surface (consistent with the `rate.breach` pattern), and production wiring can inject a Telegram bridge later. 🚫 no change to the request shape, rate gating, retry budget, credentials store, or any non-production transport. **Builds on:** the SSRF `_guard_url` (https + host allow-list, unchanged), DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-GET-001 (the GET/POST verbs the pinning transport preserves), DEC-CREDENTIALS-STORE-001 (the env-config pattern `from_env` mirrors), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (no hallucination — no baked pin) · Rule 5 (O(1) handshake check) · §11 COMMON (one wiring point) · Golden Rule #10 (honest opt-in envelope).

## DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001 (2026-06-08)

587a. **DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001 — rolling, NSE-calendar-anchored walk-forward mode for the brute-force engine (train 90d / test 5d / shift 1w), each combo scored per held-out fold then aggregated, so a seasonal overfit no longer hides in a single OOS block** (2026-06-08, closes audit Gap #4 — "only a single OOS split exists; rolling walk-forward is not implemented, so seasonal overfits (earnings, index reconstitution) slip through"). Entry numbered **587** (next free integer after #586 DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001; renumbered from #585 on the append collision with main's #585 DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 + #586 DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001 — the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative). Scope-locked to `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` + `brutex/engine/sweep_driver.py` + tests (no change to `rust/`, the Dhan adapter, `execution/`, mutation/coverage config). **What shipped.** `stage1a.py`: `trading_day_starts(bars)` (the canonical IST trading-day segmenter), the frozen `WalkForwardFold` / `WalkForwardSchedule` dataclasses, and `build_walk_forward_schedule(bars, *, train_days=90, test_days=5, step_days=5)` — which segments the stream into IST trading days, **reuses** the proven rolling-window arithmetic of `brutex/metrics/wfo.py::walk_forward_splits` (`ROLLING`, `embargo=0`; one source of truth for the `train_stop <= test_start` no-look-ahead stepping per CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON; lazy-imported so the engine module load stays numpy-free), maps each day-window to bar slices, and stamps a BLAKE3 `schedule_hash` (same `fno_math.blake3_hash` primitive + canonical-JSON rules as `strategies/combo.py::combo_hash`) over the window params, the stream shape (`n_trading_days` + `n_bars`), and every fold's bar bounds. `sweep_driver.py`: `FoldResult` / `WalkForwardResult`, `evaluate_combo_walk_forward(...)` and `walk_forward_sweep(...)` — both build `bar_bits` ONCE over the full stream (correct first-day pivots/Fib/PDH-PDL on every fold's first test day, exactly as the proven single-split `validation.validate_out_of_sample`) and slice the trade simulation at the fold IST day boundaries; `verify_walk_forward_no_lookahead(...)`, `_assert_trades_confined(...)`, and `_walk_forward_run_hash(...)`. **Reproducibility (Golden Rule #4):** the run-hash folds the `schedule_hash` in, so a walk-forward result is bound to the exact fold layout it was scored on (a golden test byte-locks the fold boundaries + the `schedule_hash`; property + integration tests prove determinism + schedule→run-hash binding). **Look-ahead safety (CLAUDE.md §4 / §11 COMPREHENSIVE / Golden Rule #5):** two complementary guarantees, honestly framed (Golden Rule #10). (1) The **substantive** guarantee is the build-once-then-slice causality — each bar's truth-vector reads only bars `<= N`, so a later fold's test window can never inform an earlier one; this is *proved* by a counterfactual property test (perturbing bars after a fold's `test_end_bar` leaves that fold's metrics byte-identical). (2) The named **P-06 `LookAheadBarrier`** (`brutex/feed/lookahead.py`) is reused as a belt-and-suspenders runtime guard in two places: `verify_walk_forward_no_lookahead` re-asserts the *schedule* keeps every training window before its test window (a structural regression guard — robustly maps a malformed hand-built schedule to `passed=False`, never an uncaught `ValueError`), and `_assert_trades_confined` drives the barrier over each fold's *realized test trades* to prove none escapes its window and that they are chronologically ordered (a genuine guard on the scoring OUTPUT); both fail-closed with `LookAheadError`. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9) ran on the diff** — architecture/causality · duplication/COMMON · correctness/edge-cases · test-adequacy/mutation — in the project venv (Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math`/`trading_core` `--release`). Findings acted on: the P-06 barrier was reframed from a (tautological) bounds re-check into the genuine trade-confinement guard + honest docstrings; the counterfactual no-look-ahead property test was added; the schedule hash now binds `n_bars` + `n_trading_days` (closing a length-aliasing gap) and the "iff collide" wording was corrected to assume BLAKE3 collision-resistance; the malformed-schedule `ValueError`-leak was fixed to `passed=False`; the aggregation layer gained direct `_aggregate_folds` unit tests (exact pass-rate, distinct-Sharpe min/mean, the `0.6` threshold boundary, all-`None` Sharpe) and the leaky-schedule fixture was tightened to a 1-bar leak — killing the surviving min→max / sum→max / threshold / barrier-cursor off-by-one mutants the review surfaced. **Tests (5 of 7 types — unit / property / golden / integration + the strict per-module self-test):** `tests/unit/test_engine_walk_forward.py`, `tests/property/test_engine_walk_forward_properties.py` (folds partition the range with no overlap/leak; exact window sizes; even stepping; `step==test` clean partition + `step<test` overlap; hash determinism + sensitivity; the counterfactual no-look-ahead proof), `tests/golden/test_engine_walk_forward_golden.py` (byte-stable fold boundaries + locked `schedule_hash`), `tests/integration/test_walk_forward.py` (full chain on fake bars). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12):** `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` + `brutex/engine/sweep_driver.py` at **100% line + 100% branch**; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` 0/0 on both modules; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; the broad engine/feed/metrics regression slice (validation + sweep_run + wfo + lookahead + cpcv/wfo properties + orchestrator) green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the aggregate `held_up` verdict (`WALK_FORWARD_PASS_RATE_THRESHOLD = 0.6`) is a SCREENING heuristic, NOT a spec-locked gate — the spec's positive-Sharpe WFO pass-rate gate stays in `brutex/metrics/wfo.py`; per-fold `train_metrics` is exposed as the standard in-sample-vs-out-of-sample WFO table (a deliverable a caller inspects), and the train-vs-test DEC-LOCK-001 degradation gating that `validate_out_of_sample` applies is a deliberate follow-up (not wired into the fold verdict here). **Tracked follow-up (out of scope per the locked task surface):** `validation.py::_day_split` still carries its own copy of the IST day-segmentation loop that `trading_day_starts` now owns — refactoring it to import the canonical segmenter is a §11 COMMON reconciliation deferred to its own PR (touching `validation.py` was outside this task's `stage1a + sweep_driver + tests` lock). **Builds on:** DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 (the single-split validator this generalises) · DEC-STAT-CPCV-WFO-001 (#428, the `metrics/wfo.py` rolling splitter reused) · DEC-EXTREME-001 (#202, the triple-variant WFO schemes) · DEC-LOOKAHEAD-BARRIER-001 (the P-06 barrier reused) · DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-001 (#423, the Stage-1A bitset producer sliced here) · DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001 (the per-mask metrics core) · DEC-P0-060 (#197, the `combo_hash` BLAKE3 primitive mirrored) · CLAUDE.md §4 / §5 / §9 / §11 COMMON / §12 / §2 r10 (honest envelope).

## DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (2026-06-08)

588a. **DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 — per-`(symbol, window)` retry-storm give-up guard + once-per-symbol 100%-window-failure Telegram alert + hash-chained give-up/alert audit rows (closes audit Gap #3)** (2026-06-08). Entry numbered **588** (next free integer after #587 DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001; renumbered from #585 on the repeated append collision with main's #585 DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 / #586 DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001 / #587 DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001 — the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative). **Problem:** a multi-hour continuous-429 storm across the parallel window fan-out (e.g. 100 symbols × 15 windows) loses bars *silently* until the run ends — `orchestrator/watchdog.py` (the heartbeat `Watchdog`, DEC-WATCHDOG-001) is a hung-worker detector, NOT a per-tuple give-up guard, so a window that keeps failing under the storm has no bounded "stop trying + tell the operator + record it" verdict; the only recovery was the operator hand-diffing the audit chain after the fact. **Fix (scope-locked to watchdog / notifications / cli flag wiring + tests):** new `brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py::RetryStormWatchdog` — a pure, no-thread, O(1)-per-tuple policy oracle poked by the caller. `record_failure(symbol, window)` times the *continuous-failure streak* per tuple against an injected monotonic clock and gives up the instant the streak reaches `max_retry_seconds`; `record_terminal_failure` is the immediate-give-up fast path for an already-exhausted window (the ingest progress stream's `failed=True`); `record_success` resets the streak. Each give-up marks the tuple terminally given-up (idempotent), stamps a hash-chained `RETRY_GIVE_UP` audit row via an injected `AuditSink` (`AuditWriter`-shaped), and counts toward its symbol; when a symbol reaches 100% window-failure it stamps one `SYMBOL_WINDOW_FAILURE` row and fires the operator alert **exactly once per symbol — never per window** (`== total` fires once, no unreachable double-alert branch). A failing audit write / buggy callback is swallowed + logged (Golden Rule #10) — the guard never crashes the ingest. `brutex/notifications/`: new `TelegramEventKind.SYMBOL_WINDOW_FAILURE` + `SweepAlerter.symbol_window_failure` / `symbol_failure_callback` (kept wheel-free via a structural `SymbolFailureLike` — no orchestrator import, so the strict per-module gate stays green). `brutex/cli.py`: `brutex fetch --max-retry-minutes N` flag (validated `>= 1`) → `_arm_retry_storm_guard` builds the guard (audit writer under `<lake>/audit/retry-storm-<pull_id>.jsonl`, `SweepAlerter` alert callback), registers the `(symbol_name, interval)` fan-out, and feeds the existing `run_ingest` `on_progress` stream into it (no `run_ingest` change). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** new `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_retry_storm_watchdog.py` + `tests/property/test_retry_storm_watchdog_props.py` + `tests/integration/test_retry_storm_watchdog_integration.py` + the `--max-retry-minutes` CLI tests + the `sweep_alerts` symbol-failure tests — give-up fires **exactly at the boundary** (and not one tick below), the alert fires **once per symbol not per window** (hypothesis property over random fan-outs), and give-up + alert audit rows are written and the real hash chain **verifies** (`verify_chain`); `brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py` + `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py` at **100% line + branch**; `ruff` + format + `mypy --strict` clean on the touched files. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the give-up guard, the once-per-symbol alert, and the hash-chained audit rows are fully implemented + tested; the live `fetch --max-retry-minutes` path drives the per-symbol 100%-window-failure **alert + audit** end-to-end via the `on_progress` terminal-failure feed. 🟡 the engine's real fan-out unit is `(instrument, interval)`, so "window" = that fan-out unit (not a date sub-chunk); the **time-based** per-attempt give-up (`record_failure` streak ≥ N min) needs the ingest retry loop to poke the guard on **each** attempt — that one-call adoption lives in the ingest spine (`ingest_spot`/`auto_retry`) and is intentionally **out of this PR's file scope** (the guard is complete + tested, ready to wire). 🚫 no change to `mutation.yml`, coverage config, `rust/`, or the dhan option path (L1-owned). **Builds on:** DEC-WATCHDOG-001 (the heartbeat `Watchdog` this complements), DEC-TELEGRAM-WIRE-001 (the `SweepAlerter` seam extended here), DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#571, the bounded-retry residual this turns from silent into audited), NFR-OBS-003 (the hash-chained `AuditWriter`), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1) per-tuple) · Rule 8 (audit trail) · Rule 10 (honest envelope) · §11 AUTOMATED (watchdog + Telegram).

## DEC-ORCH-LAZY-BLOOM-001 (2026-06-08)

589a. **DEC-ORCH-LAZY-BLOOM-001 — `brutex/orchestrator/bloom.py` imports `fastbloom_rs` LAZILY (on first `BloomFilter` construction), unblocking the standalone strict per-module 100%-coverage gate for the `brutex.orchestrator.*` modules** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep #12/#13). **Problem:** the strict per-module coverage gate (`ci.yml`, DEC-COV-001 ratchet) runs `pytest --cov=brutex.orchestrator.<mod> …` per module. For the orchestrator submodules this aborted at COLLECTION with `ImportError: PyO3 modules compiled for CPython 3.8 or older may only be initialized once per interpreter process` — the `fastbloom_rs` wheel is built `cp37-abi3`, and `coverage`'s source-package import of `brutex.orchestrator.<mod>` (which pulls the package `__init__` → `pipeline` → `store` → `bloom` → top-level `from fastbloom_rs import BloomFilter`) collided with the coverage machinery's own import, so PyO3's abi3≤3.8 single-init rule fired. The global `--cov=brutex` run was unaffected (one import), which is why these modules were covered at 100% via the aggregate but had their *standalone* strict gates commented out (`orchestrator.replay`) or never added (`orchestrator.retry` and the rest). **Fix:** `bloom.py` now defers the `fastbloom_rs` import to a one-line lazy loader `_load_rust_bloom()` called inside `BloomFilter.__post_init__` — mirroring the EXISTING lazy `fno_math` import in `_popcount_bytes`. Importing the orchestrator package no longer initialises the PyO3 extension, so the per-module coverage gate imports cleanly; the very first `BloomFilter()` still triggers exactly one init (behaviour byte-identical). The `_RustBloomFilter` type name moves under `TYPE_CHECKING` (annotations are strings via `from __future__ import annotations`), and the loader returns `cast("type[_RustBloomFilter]", …)` since `fastbloom_rs` ships no stubs. **Re-enabled gates:** `ci.yml` strict per-module 100% line+branch gates ADDED/re-enabled for `brutex.orchestrator.{replay, retry, audit, adaptive_rate_limiter}` — the four modules that reach 100% standalone with their dedicated test files (verified locally, Python 3.12). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the ABI3 import blocker is RESOLVED for ALL `brutex.orchestrator.*` modules (the import-time init is gone). 🟡 only the four named modules are gated NOW — `state` (98.6%), `store` (91.3%), `pipeline` (97.3%), `rate_limiter` (86.6%), `quota_tracker` (92.6%) and `bloom` (96.8%) carry RESIDUAL standalone-coverage gaps (lines exercised only by the aggregate `--cov=brutex` run / cross-module integration tests), a DISTINCT concern from the (now-fixed) import blocker — tracked as the next ratchet. 🚫 no runtime behaviour change; `mypy --strict` + `ruff` clean on `bloom.py`. **Verified:** `pytest --cov=brutex.orchestrator.{replay,retry,audit,adaptive_rate_limiter} --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` = 100.00% each (standalone). **Builds on:** DEC-COV-001 / DEC-L3-REPLAY-ORACLE-001 #241 (the deferred replay gate), DEC-COV-BACKFILL-LIMIT-001 #261 (the operator-accepted ABI3 limit this lifts), CLAUDE.md §4 (no-look-ahead lazy-import precedent) · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-MUTATION-GATE-RANKING-001 (2026-06-08)

590a. **DEC-MUTATION-GATE-RANKING-001 — extend the Python mutation gate (`mutation.yml`) to the ranking/metrics MATH, fix the broken job install, and harden the Sharpe/DSR/composite tests so a silent regression in strategy-selection math is caught** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep #12/#13). **Why:** the mutation gate mutated only orchestration/data plumbing (`state/retry/audit/rate_limiter/store/partition/parser`). A silent arithmetic regression in the leaderboard math — the per-trade Sharpe/Sortino/skew/kurtosis (`metrics/compute.py`), the Deflated-Sharpe engine (`metrics/deflated_sharpe.py`), or the composite ranking (`ranking/__init__.py`, `ranking/overfit.py`) — would corrupt strategy selection and slip past the gate. **Two infra bugs fixed first:** (1) the install line `pip install -e ".[dev]" mutmut>=2.5` was a shell-redirect bug (`>=2.5` redirected stdout to a file named `=2.5`, leaving `mutmut` UNPINNED → mutmut **3.x** resolved, whose CLI is incompatible with this workflow's `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate … --runner … --simple-output`) — now `"mutmut>=2.5,<3.0"`; (2) the job installed NEITHER the `fno_math`/`trading_core` Rust wheels NOR the `[data,ui]` extras, so the `pytest tests/unit` runner could not even COLLECT (the unit suite imports `brutex.strategies` → `import fno_math` and `brutex.vocabulary` → `trading_core`) — added the Rust toolchain + both `pip install ./rust/*` steps + `[data,ui]`, mirroring `ci.yml`'s test job. **Gate extension:** `brutex/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py` (the DSR / PSR Bailey-LdP engine) ADDED to `--paths-to-mutate` — verified to **ZERO surviving mutants** locally with a unit-only runner (mutmut 2.5.1, Python 3.12). **Hardening tests landed (kill real mutants):** `test_deflated_sharpe.py` (+sample-length / radicand boundaries, byte-exact `ValueError` text via `str(exc)` equality — a substring `match=` still passes mutmut's `"XX…XX"`-wrapped string mutant — and `frozen`/`slots` asserts → **0 survivors**); `test_ranking.py` (`MIN_TRADES == 30` boundary); `test_metrics_compute.py` (golden-value pins for `_percentile` interpolation, `_drawdown_stats` `drop>0`/`peak>0` boundaries, `_consecutive_runs` streak resets, exact `_skewness`/`_excess_kurtosis` moment math, floor-vs-true `//` integer division on avg-win/loss/expectancy/MFE/MAE, the all-zero `_empty_metrics` row, and `with_stage4_statistics` DSR/PBO gating + the `kurtosis + GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` offset) — these kill **172 of the 177** compute.py mutants measured. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `deflated_sharpe.py` (DSR) is now in the zero-survivor gate; Sharpe (`compute.py`) + composite (`ranking`) are heavily hardened by the new golden tests. 🟡 `compute.py` + `ranking` + `overfit` are NOT YET in the zero-survivor `--paths-to-mutate` set: under a deterministic UNIT-only runner they retain (a) provably-EQUIVALENT mutants — `float | None`→`float & None` annotation flips (annotations are never evaluated at runtime), `cast("float", …)` type-string edits (the runtime `cast` is a no-op), overwritten loop-init values, and `r < 0`→`r <= 0` where a zero return contributes zero to a sum-of-squares — which need documented `# pragma: no mutate`, and (b) `ranking`/`overfit` mutants currently killed only by PROPERTY tests (the gate runner is unit-only, matching the existing job). Folding them in (pragma sweep + a few more unit tests) is the tracked next ratchet. 🟡 DISCOVERED, not introduced: `tests/property/test_ranking_overfit_properties.py::test_dsr_monotone_in_observed_sharpe` is an over-strong property — the PSR/DSR is genuinely NON-monotone in observed Sharpe at large-negative Sharpe with a non-trivial deflation benchmark (the estimator-variance radicand grows faster than the numerator), so hypothesis can falsify it; a domain-restriction fix is a tracked follow-up (it does not affect this PR's unit-only gate). 🚫 `mutation.yml` is weekly / main-push only (not a per-PR `CI OK` gate), so this change is exercised by the weekly run, not this PR's CI. **Verified:** `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate brutex/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py` (unit-only runner) → 0 survivors; `ruff` + `mypy --strict` clean. **Builds on:** DEC-P0-001/002/003 (the mutmut 85% gate lineage), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 12 (mutation ≥ 85%) · §4 (no-pandas/typed) · §10 (honest limits).

Golden parity (all 400 cases) stays covered deterministically by the pre-existing `golden_vectors.rs` (strictly stronger than sampling). (2) **CI wiring** — `.github/workflows/mutation.yml` gains a `rust-mutation-trading-core` job (additive; coordinated with the parallel mutation.yml edit) running `cargo mutants --in-place …` from `rust/trading-core` — **`--in-place` is required** because the golden test reads the repo-root oracle at `../../tests/golden/fixtures/…` which is OUTSIDE the crate and absent from cargo-mutants' default scratch copy; `rust/trading-core/**` added to the push-path trigger; `.cargo/mutants.toml` `examine_re`/`exclude_re` now register the trading-core critical surface (evaluator + bits + indicators) and exclude its lib/python glue + tests. (3) **One behaviour-preserving src refactor** — `evaluate_atoms` now routes every `mask |= 1u64 << BIT_X` through a single `const fn bit(pos)` (DYNAMIC/COMMON: one shift site, not 52); this also eliminates the lone genuinely-equivalent mutant (`1u64 << 0` ⇔ `1u64 >> 0` at bit 0) by exercising the shift across all 52 positions, where `<<`→`>>` breaks bit 1+ and is killed. Masks are bit-identical (golden 400 + oracle prove it → **leaderboard-safe**). **O(1):** the evaluator is O(1) per bar (52 fixed branches, u64 mask, no allocation) — unchanged. **Verified locally (real `cargo` output, toolchain 1.94.1):** `cargo test` = **17 passed** (2 unit + 2 golden + 13 proptest/boundary/degenerate/panic), `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo mutants --in-place --file src/evaluator.rs` (the gated decision core) = **0 surviving mutants** — every viable evaluator mutant caught. A first whole-crate pass surfaced 4 evaluator survivors — one provably-EQUIVALENT (`total_range > 0` doji guard, subsumed by the strict `body*10 < total_range` since `body ≥ 0`; removed) and three LOAD-BEARING guards (`total_range`/`day_range`/`pdc` `> 0`) reachable only by degenerate out-of-domain bars (now killed by `degenerate_bars_fire_no_shape_or_gap_bits`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the SHARED 52-condition decision core (`evaluator.rs`) now has property coverage AND a zero-surviving-mutant CI gate that actually runs. 🟡 the gate is SCOPED to `evaluator.rs` (mirroring fno-math's scoped `examine_re`); `bits.rs` + the pivots/fib indicators are covered by the 400-case golden answer-key + property ordering/determinism/storage assertions (incl. the unused `r4`/`s4`/`ext_*_424` legs), but extending the *mutation* gate to those indicator modules — whose unused-field coefficient mutants (e.g. `r4 = pdh + 3·(p−pdl)`) need exact-value oracles — is a tracked FOLLOW-UP, NOT done here. 🟡 the mutation job runs on the **weekly schedule + push-to-main + manual dispatch** (mirroring the existing fno-math job) — it is NOT a per-PR required check, so it gates `main` + the nightly ratchet; the proptest layer (which IS in `cargo test`) is the per-PR guard. 🟡 `--in-place` precludes `-j` parallelism, hence the 120-min budget; local verification used the debug profile for speed (CI uses `--release`, which only adds the `overflow-checks` already on in dev). 🚫 no public-throughput / "millions in minutes" claim; no change to the 52-bit layout, the golden answer-key, or any mask value. **Builds on:** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the shared crate), DEC-PHASE1-WEEK2-SCAFFOLDING-001 (#252, the cargo-mutants config this extends), CLAUDE.md §4 (7 test types) · §11 COMMON/DYNAMIC · §12 (mutation ≥ 85% target) · §10 (honest envelope).

585c. **DEC-FUZZ-HOTKERNEL-001 — activate real `cargo-fuzz` targets for the Rust hot kernels (gap-sweep #6): `fno-math` mask-AND + SUPERSET-count, `trading-core` pivot/fib resolve + the 52-condition u64 evaluator** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep). **Problem:** `rust/fno-math/fuzz/` was a README-ONLY stub (7 planned cargo-fuzz targets, all unbuilt — DEC-PHASE1-WEEK2-SCAFFOLDING-001) and `rust/trading-core/` had **no `fuzz/` directory at all**, so the panic/overflow/UB safety of the hottest kernels (the Stage-1B/Stage-2 bit ops + the shared evaluate-time indicators + the 52-vocab evaluator) rested only on hand-picked unit/golden vectors, never on adversarial bytes. **What shipped:** four real libFuzzer targets (cargo-fuzz scaffolded by hand to preserve the existing README), built + run on nightly Rust 1.98 + cargo-fuzz 0.13.1 — (1) `fno-math/fuzz/fuzz_mask_and` over `bitand_count_u64s`: asserts total (never panics), commutative, and bounded by each operand's popcount — **7,646,580 runs, 0 crashes**; (2) `fno-math/fuzz/fuzz_supermask` over `count_supermask_u64s` / `count_supermasks_u64s`: asserts the SUPERSET count is bounded by `n_bars`, `mask==0` matches all, and the batch kernel equals the single kernel element-wise + positionally — **3,627,225 runs, 0 crashes**; (3) `trading-core/fuzz/fuzz_pivot_fib` over `compute_pivot_levels` + `compute_fib_levels`: asserts no panic + the documented monotone ladder (`R4≥R3≥PDH`, `S4≤S3≤PDL`, `PDL≤P≤PDH`, `range≥0`, midpoint in band) — **31,164,014 runs, 0 crashes**; (4) `trading-core/fuzz/fuzz_evaluator` over `evaluate_atoms`: asserts no panic, only bits 0..=51 set (reserved 52-63 always clear), and every mutually-exclusive condition pair (above/below the same level, bullish/bearish, gap-up/gap-down, inside/outside day, upper/lower third, ≤1 time-of-day bucket) — **7,719,702 runs, 0 crashes**. **Honest domain (Golden Rule #10, matching `trading-core/src/lib.rs`):** the `trading-core` fuzzers stay inside the DOCUMENTED realistic envelope — prices capped at `MAX_PAISA`=₹100,000,000 (far below the `~10¹⁷`-paisa overflow bound), OHLC ordered, `PDH≥PDL`, `PDC∈[PDL,PDH]`, proximity bps `∈[0,10000]` — because the crate INTENTIONALLY panics on corrupt OHLC (always-on `assert!`, mirrors Python `ValueError`) and on absurd `i64`-scale magnitudes (release `overflow-checks`); those are contract behaviour, not bugs, and the crate's own unit tests cover the panic path. The `fno-math` u64 mask ops are total, so those fuzz on truly arbitrary bytes. **Python⇆Rust / golden parity** is NOT re-asserted live inside libFuzzer (would need an embedded interpreter); it remains covered by `trading-core/tests/golden_vectors.rs` (400-case answer-key) + `tests/unit/test_fno_math_bridge.py`. These fuzz targets prove panic/overflow-freedom + structural invariants over the adversarial input space. **Build note (honest):** `fno-math` is a PyO3 `extension-module`, so its kernels are only reachable through the `#[pyfunction]` surface, which references Python C-API symbols; a fuzz EXECUTABLE (unlike a `cargo test` of the private cores) therefore needs libpython at link — the fuzz crate's `build.rs` resolves it via `python3.12-config` (the fuzzed code path is pure integer work and never initialises the interpreter, so symbol resolution alone suffices). `trading-core/fuzz` uses `default-features=false` → the dependency-free pure-Rust core, no libpython. Both fuzz crates are separate, non-published, NON-workspace packages — they never perturb the stable `cargo build` / `cargo test` / coverage gates of the parent crates. **NOT done (honest):** no CI fuzz workflow is wired yet (the README's "sibling workflow" remains a follow-up); the other README targets (`fuzz_combo_hash`, `fuzz_ema_update`, `fuzz_audit_chain`, `fuzz_parquet_reader`) stay ROADMAP until their kernels exist. **Builds on:** DEC-PHASE1-WEEK2-SCAFFOLDING-001 (#252, the README stub this activates), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the shared `trading-core` kernel), DEC-RUST-RAYON-SUPERMASK-001 / DEC-RUST-RESIDENT-BARS-001 (the SUPERSET kernel), CLAUDE.md §4 (Rust test stack: `cargo fuzz`) · §11 COMMON (one source of truth) · §10 honest limits.

Catalog P-18 row now points at it. **Verified locally (Py3.12 venv + kernels):** parser fuzz 3 passed; rate-limiter 2 passed; ruff + mypy --strict clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the fuzz proves *robustness* (no crash) not *vendor correctness* of the data; P-18 proves the *limiter's* cap, not end-to-end network rate (which also depends on the adaptive step-down on real 429s, separately unit-tested). **Builds on:** DEC-PHASE2-INVARIANTS-PROMOTE-001 (#501, the sibling promotion batch), DEC-VENDOR-VOLUME-NORMALIZE-001 (parser index-volume handling), the deep gap sweep (DEC-WORKSPACE-HEALTH-REPORT-001 follow-up), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #6 / #10.
582b. **DEC-INGEST-AUDIT-CHAIN-001 — wire the hash-chained AuditWriter into the spot ingest pull (Golden Rule #8)** (2026-06-08; closes the #1 finding of the deep data/reliability gap sweep — "spot ingest writes NO hash-chained audit"). **Gap (verified):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/run_ingest.py` + the `brutex fetch` CLI path emitted only `structlog` lines — `grep AuditWriter run_ingest.py` = 0 — so a spot data pull (a "material action" per CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #8) left NO hash-chained JSONL audit row, and the audit-replay oracle could not verify a pull. **What shipped (core capability, 100% line+branch under the EXISTING strict `--cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.run_ingest --cov-fail-under=100` ci.yml gate):** an optional injected `audit: AuditWriter | None = None` on `run_dhan_spot_ingest` + the `run_dhan_spot_ingest_with_retry` wrapper (default `None` = unchanged, so all 23 prior tests + every other caller are byte-identical). When wired, a new pure `_maybe_audit` helper appends a hash-chained trail — `INGEST_RUN_START` (worklist shape) → one `INGEST_PAIR_DONE` (bars/windows/still-failed) per succeeded pair OR one `INGEST_PAIR_FAILED` (error + `auth_failure`/`known_gap` classification) per quarantined pair → `INGEST_RUN_COMPLETE` (pairs ok/failed, total bars, auth_aborted). **Thread-safety (the key design constraint):** every append fires ONLY on the single controller thread that drains the parallel fan-out (`run_ingest.py` "single-threaded… need not be thread-safe"), so the not-thread-safe `AuditWriter` is never touched concurrently by the worker pool — no lock needed, no corruption possible. **Production activation:** `brutex fetch` (`cli.py:cmd_fetch`) now opens an `AuditWriter` at `<lake>/audit/spot-ingest.jsonl` (resume = append to the existing chain across runs) for LIVE pulls and threads it in; `--inspect`/`--dry-run` get a null context (no real data → no audit). The CLI wiring is `# pragma: no cover` (live token + network), consistent with the surrounding live-path code — the audit-WRITE core is 100%-tested via a fake-`ingest_spot` unit test asserting the 4-action chain + `verify_chain == 4`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this adds PAIR-level (symbol×interval) audit at the controller-thread serialization point — finer per-WINDOW audit from the worker threads would need a thread-safe audit sink and is a tracked follow-up; the OPTION-side audit (`OptionBarSink(audit=…)`, gap-sweep D-2) is a separate fast-follow. **Verified locally (Py3.12 venv + kernels):** `--cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.run_ingest` = 100% (139 stmts / 30 branch / 0 miss), 35 passed; `mypy --strict` + ruff clean; `import brutex.cli` OK. **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED — this is a lake-ingest observability layer. **Builds on:** DEC-L3-REPLAY-ORACLE-001 (the audit chain + replay oracle this feeds), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the controller-thread drain seam used as the serialization point), DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 / DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 (the failure classifications stamped into `INGEST_PAIR_FAILED`), the deep gap sweep (DEC-WORKSPACE-HEALTH-REPORT-001 follow-up), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #7 / #8 / #10.
583b. **DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 — Stage-2.5 Wald-SPRT early-stop is DESIGN-BLOCKED after a 4-agent hostile review; record the accepted design + 5 unblock items + fix the spec contradiction** (2026-06-08; the operator-authorized Lane G of the deep-gap-sweep program. Per CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #9 a major engine change gets a hostile review BEFORE code — this is that review's outcome). **What the review found (architect + hostile reviewer, both citing real code):** building Stage-2.5 SPRT as specified would ship a **subtly results-changing, non-deterministic** feature — the review PREVENTED that. Golden Rule #2 single-source-of-truth violated); **B2** NOT correctness-neutral — the Sharpe-percentile kill is not aligned with the 8-term composite leaderboard (`ranking/__init__.py:301-318`, which weights Risk-Efficiency/Calmar/PF) and pruning mutates the z-scores (`ranking/__init__.py:285-291`) + the Deflated-Sharpe trial-count `N` (`overfit.py:221-242`) of SURVIVING combos → a different leaderboard; the invariant is **probabilistic (β=0.10), not exact** like the `min_hits` prefilter; **B3** the `OPTIMIZATIONS.md` DashMap/Rayon design makes kills thread-scheduling-dependent → breaks reproducibility + the audit-replay oracle (mitigated by the adopted pure intra-backtest Layer-A design); **B4** the p95 kill percentile must track the real `cfg.top_k` fraction (`sweep_run.py:732`), not a hardcoded 95; **B5** the Rust `ResidentTradeSim.simulate_masks` (`rust_trade_sim.py:148`) is NOT wired into `run_persisted_sweep` (the production sweep is the Python `metrics_for_mask` loop, `sweep_run.py:715-730`), so the perf win needs Rust wiring first, and the "~61%" SLA has no honest no-prune worst case (a net slowdown). **What shipped (DOCS ONLY — zero code; the honest, no-illusion outcome):** `docs/adr/0006-stage2.5-sprt-design-block.md` (the accepted pure Layer-A design — a deterministic `sprt_decision` over a Welford `RunningSharpe` reusing `compute.py:134-145` + `deflated_sharpe.probabilistic_sharpe_ratio` verbatim, opt-in default-OFF, with the 7-test-type plan incl. the A/B top-3-recall oracle) + the 5-item unblock checklist; a ⚠️ DESIGN-BLOCKED banner on `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Stage 2.5". **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** Stage-2.5 stays UNBUILT — the "~61% faster / single overnight" SLA is NOT yet achievable; the engine backtests every Stage-2 survivor to completion. This decision prevents a FALSE speedup that would corrupt the leaderboard, rather than claiming one. **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED. **Builds on:** the deep gap sweep (DEC-WORKSPACE-HEALTH-REPORT-001), DEC-STAT-002 (#124, the project's own admission the Wald stack lacks an anytime-valid Type-I guarantee), the Stage-1B `min_hits` exact-prefilter precedent (`sweep_driver.py:264-272`), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #2 / #4 / #9 / #10.
584b. **DEC-SPRT-SPEC-RECONCILE-001 — lock the ONE canonical Stage-2.5 algorithm; resolve ADR-0006 blocker B1** (2026-06-08; the operator-authorized first unblock step for Lane G after DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 / PR #506). **Gap:** the 4-agent review found `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md §"Stage 2.5"` (≥50 *trades*, intra-backtest kill) and `TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §2` (≥50,000 *param-trials*, inter-backtest prune via a shared `Arc<DashMap>`) describe TWO different algorithms — Golden Rule #2 (single source of truth) violated. **Decision:** the **intra-backtest** definition is now the LOCKED canonical algorithm (cheaper, safer, and — critically — DETERMINISTic, since it's a pure function of one combo's own trade stream with no cross-trial/`DashMap` state). The OPTIMIZATIONS.md §2 inter-backtest/`DashMap` design is **SUPERSEDED** (it was rejected for the thread-scheduling determinism risk, ADR-0006 B3). **Docs:** added a `✅ B1 RESOLVED` block to the spec banner + a `🚫 SUPERSEDED` banner to OPTIMIZATIONS.md §2; the remaining open blockers are B2 (ranking-invariance / probabilistic envelope), B4 (`top_k`-tracked percentile), B5 (Rust production wiring + honest worst-case SLA). **Scope:** docs only; engine unchanged. **Builds on:** DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 (#583, ADR-0006), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #2 / #9.
585e. **DEC-SPRT-EARLY-STOP-CORE-001 — build the PURE, deterministic, INERT Stage-2.5 SPRT decision core (opt-in, default-OFF, NOT wired)** (2026-06-08; the second Lane-G unblock step — real SPRT code progress with ZERO risk of changing results, exactly because it is not wired into the sweep). **What shipped:** new `brutex/engine/early_stop.py` (100% line+branch under the EXISTING `--cov=brutex.engine` aggregate gate) — `SprtConfig` (frozen, fail-closed validation of α/β∈(0,1), min_trades≥1, kill_posterior∈(0,1)); `wald_bounds(cfg)` (the classic `A=ln(β/(1−α))≈−2.251`, `B=ln((1−β)/α)≈2.890` SPRT thresholds the spec asks to document); `RunningSharpe` (online Welford n/mean/m2 → O(1)-per-trade running Sharpe, `None` while undefined — reusing the `compute.py` recurrence, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); and the PURE `sprt_decision(stat, *, p95_threshold, cfg)` — CONTINUE below the 50-trade floor or while Sharpe is undefined, else KILL iff the **Gaussian** posterior `Pr(true_sharpe > p95_threshold)` (reusing `deflated_sharpe.probabilistic_sharpe_ratio` with normal skew/kurtosis — "Gaussian conjugate posterior" per spec, verbatim, no re-derivation) is below `kill_posterior`. **INERT (the whole point):** nothing in the production sweep imports or calls this module — it is opt-in, default-OFF, and NOT wired into `run_persisted_sweep`/`metrics_for_mask`, so it changes NOTHING. Wiring it stays BLOCKED on ADR-0006 B2/B4/B5. **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** `sprt_decision` is a pure function of the running stat + injected threshold (no I/O/clock/RNG/cross-combo state) → same stream + same p95 ⇒ same decision, worker-order-independent — proven by a hypothesis property. **Tests (unit + property):** `tests/unit/test_engine_early_stop.py` (every branch — floor, undefined-Sharpe, KILL, CONTINUE, all 7 config-validation rejections, the Welford-vs-offline Sharpe equality, the Wald-bound formulas) drives the module to **100% line+branch**; `tests/property/test_early_stop_properties.py` (determinism ∀ streams, KILL-never-below-floor ∀ streams, running-moment consistency). **Verified locally (Py3.12 venv + kernels):** `--cov=brutex.engine` aggregate = 100% (2432 stmts/566 branch/0 miss, 754 passed); the early_stop module alone 100% (58 stmts/18 branch); 21 early-stop tests pass; ruff + `mypy --strict` clean; **vulture PASS** (the inert module is not dead-code-flagged at min-confidence 80 — functions are 60% confidence < the gate). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is a TESTED BUILDING BLOCK, not a working early-stop — Stage-2.5 still does nothing in production (the "~61% faster" SLA remains unachievable until B2/B4/B5 + the Rust wiring land). **Scope:** the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE behaviour is UNCHANGED (the module is uncalled). **Builds on:** DEC-SPRT-SPEC-RECONCILE-001 (#584, the locked algorithm), DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 (#583, ADR-0006 Layer-A design), DEC-STAT-DSR-001 (`probabilistic_sharpe_ratio` reused), the `compute.py` Welford recurrence, CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #4 / #9 / #10 / #11.
586b. **DEC-SPRT-AB-ORACLE-001 — the Stage-2.5 A/B oracle: empirically pin down ADR-0006 blockers B2 + B4 against the REAL ranking (no production wiring)** (2026-06-08; the third Lane-G unblock step after DEC-SPRT-EARLY-STOP-CORE-001 / PR #511). **TEST-ONLY — zero `brutex/` code change; the early_stop module stays INERT.** **What shipped:** `tests/integration/test_stage2_5_ab_oracle.py` drives the inert `sprt_decision` over a deterministic 30-combo pool (3 strong winners / 7 moderates / 20 duds, seeded), ranks them with the REAL 8-term `brutex.ranking.rank_combos`, and compares the full-sweep top-K vs the top-K after dropping early-stop-killed combos. **Findings (real, measured — both tests green):** (1) **B4 characterized** — `test_naive_95th_percentile_threshold_is_unsafe` proves the LITERAL spec threshold (the pool's 95th-percentile Sharpe) is UNSAFE: it kills full-sweep top-10 combos → the leaderboard CHANGES. The safe bar is the `(1 − top_k/N)`-percentile Sharpe; the formula is now known (wiring it is the remaining B4 code). (2) **B2 empirically guarded** — `test_topk_tracked_threshold_preserves_the_leaderboard` proves that with the `top_k`-tracked bar, early-stop kills only clear duds and PRESERVES the leaderboard (top-3 recall 100%, top-10 recall ≥ 95%). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is a FIXTURE SPOT-CHECK, NOT a proof over the 33B-trial space, and does NOT cover the worst-case low-Sharpe-but-high-non-Sharpe-term combo (the hostile review's residual B2 risk). Early-stop therefore stays INERT/unwired until that case is bounded + B5 (Rust production wiring + honest worst-case SLA) lands. **Verified locally (Py3.12 venv + kernels):** 2 oracle tests pass; ruff clean. **Scope:** tests + ADR/ledger docs only; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED. **Builds on:** DEC-SPRT-EARLY-STOP-CORE-001 (#585, the inert decision core driven here), DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 (#583, ADR-0006 B2/B4), DEC-RANKING-OVERFIT-001 (the real `rank_combos` 8-term composite + DSR gate the oracle ranks against), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #4 / #9 / #10.
587b. **DEC-SPRT-B2-RESIDUAL-001 — PROVE the residual-B2 worst case is real: a Sharpe-only early-stop kill drops non-Sharpe top-K rankers (the leaderboard changes)** (2026-06-08; the honest conclusion of the Lane-G B2 investigation after DEC-SPRT-AB-ORACLE-001 / PR #515). **TEST-ONLY — the early_stop module stays INERT.** **What shipped:** `tests/integration/test_stage2_5_b2_residual.py` — an adversarial counterpart to the benign A/B oracle. It builds a deterministic pool that INCLUDES low-Sharpe / high-Risk-Efficiency (MFE≫MAE) "adversarial" combos, ranks with the REAL 8-term `rank_combos`, and proves that even the `top_k`-tracked early-stop (the "safe" bar from DEC-SPRT-AB-ORACLE-001) **drops gate-passing full-sweep top-10 combos**. **Verified (real, measured):** with seed 0, **4 of the baseline top-10 are adversarial combos (Sharpe 0.09–0.32, below the 0.629 kill bar) that rank top-10 via the composite's NON-Sharpe terms (Risk-Efficiency / Calmar / PF) yet are killed by the Sharpe-based criterion** → the ranked leaderboard CHANGES. This is the hostile review's ADR-0006 B2 worst case, CONFIRMED REAL (not theoretical) — the prior A/B oracle (benign winners+duds pool) only showed B2 is *avoidable on benign pools*, not that it's *safe*. **Decision (load-bearing):** early-stop **CANNOT be wired with a Sharpe-only kill** — the kill must be made **composite-aware** (never prune a full-composite top-K combo, or rank the full pool and prune only the bottom tail) before any B4-wiring/B5. **B4-wiring + B5 remain BLOCKED**; the merged inert core (#511), B1 spec-lock (#511), and A/B oracle (#515) stand. The test is a GUARDRAIL: it asserts the unsafe behaviour exists, so a future Sharpe-only wiring attempt is reminded why it must not. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is the no-illusion outcome — it proves the "61% faster" SLA cannot be claimed by wiring the current Sharpe-only criterion; it would corrupt the leaderboard. **Verified locally:** 1 test passes; ruff + mypy clean. **Scope:** tests + ADR/ledger docs only; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED. **Builds on:** DEC-SPRT-AB-ORACLE-001 (#586, the benign oracle this completes), DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 (#583, ADR-0006 B2), DEC-RANKING-OVERFIT-001 (the 8-term composite whose non-Sharpe terms are the attack surface), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #9 / #10.
588b. **DEC-SPRT-INFEASIBLE-001 — feasibility review verdict: a provably leaderboard-preserving Stage-2.5 SPRT early-stop is INFEASIBLE; ABANDON it as a sweep accelerator and redirect to the exact Stage-1B prefilter + the bit-exact GPU path** (2026-06-08; the honest conclusion of Lane G after DEC-SPRT-B2-RESIDUAL-001 proved the Sharpe-only kill unsafe). **Question investigated:** can the kill be made "composite-aware" to fix B2? **Verdict (structural, not a kill-statistic choice):** NO. (1) **No sound mid-flight bound for the non-Sharpe terms** — the leaderboard ranks on 8 full-backtest aggregates (`ranking/__init__.py:301-318`); `max_drawdown_pct` (`compute.py:262-307`), Calmar, and Risk-Efficiency (`ranking/__init__.py:165-177`) can be dominated by trades that have not happened at the 50-trade kill point, so none admits a sound bound from a prefix; the only mid-flight signal is the probabilistic PSR on Sharpe, already disproven (#587). (2) **The score is relative/pool-coupled** — z-scored across SURVIVORS (`ranking/__init__.py:180-193,285-291`) + DSR-deflated against pool `N`/`V` (`overfit.py:204-242`); pruning ANY combo perturbs every survivor's z-score AND the DSR bar; the only perturbation-free normalization (compute over the FULL pool) needs each killed combo's TRUE final metrics = the exact backtest early-stop exists to skip (closed circle). So a composite-aware kill is either UNSAFE (probabilistic) or NON-ACCELERATING (exact) — no safe-and-fast middle. This mirrors the only prune already proven safe: the EXACT Stage-1B `min_hits` prefilter (`sweep_driver.py:264-272`), safe precisely because it is exact not probabilistic. **Decision:** Stage-2.5 SPRT early-stop is **ABANDONED** as an accelerator (not merely blocked); **B4-wiring + B5 are CLOSED** (nothing safe to wire); the merged inert core (#511) + A/B oracle (#585/#515) + residual-B2 proof (#587/#516) STAY as documented building blocks + guardrails (not wired, must not be). **Redirect (leaderboard-safe, already in tree):** (a) the exact Stage-1B coarse prefilter (DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001) — the correct exact shape of the SPRT idea; (b) Phase-3.5 Metal GPU offload (`TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §3`, bit-exact parity + audit-replay gated). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the "~61% reduction / single overnight" SLA built on Stage-2.5 (`TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §1`) is NOT safely achievable and is RETIRED; the achievable leaderboard-safe speedup is Stage-1B + the bit-exact GPU path. **What shipped:** ADR-0006 "FINAL VERDICT" section + a 🚫 ABANDONED banner on `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Stage 2.5". **Scope:** docs only; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED. **Builds on:** DEC-SPRT-B2-RESIDUAL-001 (#587), DEC-SPRT-AB-ORACLE-001 (#586), DEC-SPRT-EARLY-STOP-CORE-001 (#585), DEC-SPRT-SPEC-RECONCILE-001 (#584), DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 (#583), DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 (the safe exact prefilter), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #9 / #10.
589b. **DEC-STAGE1B-CONFLICT-FIX-001 — fix a leaderboard-corruption bug in the Stage-1B conflict prune (it WRONGLY pruned bullish/bearish-doji masks) + add 4 verified candle conflicts + prove the prune is EXACT** (2026-06-08; the operator-chosen "Lane A — safe Stage-1B speedup". While tightening the exact prefilter, a correctness bug was found). **Bug (verified, not theoretical):** `brutex/vocabulary/conflicts.py` `CONFLICT_PAIRS` listed `(BIT_BAR_BULLISH, BIT_BAR_DOJI)` and `(BIT_BAR_BEARISH, BIT_BAR_DOJI)` as conflicts — but the shared evaluator defines **DOJI as a SMALL body** (`body*10 < total_range`, `rust/trading-core/src/evaluator.rs:239`), NOT `open==close`. So a bar with a tiny POSITIVE body is **both BULLISH and DOJI** (tiny negative → BEARISH+DOJI). Empirically ~**9% of random bars** are bullish/bearish dojis (1871/1897 of 20k). The Stage-1B prefilter (`sweep_run.py:676` `has_conflict`) therefore **WRONGLY dropped every mask requiring (bullish AND doji) / (bearish AND doji)** — strategies that CAN fire + rank — silently corrupting the leaderboard (the exact failure class the SPRT lane was abandoned to avoid). **Fix:** REMOVED the two false pairs (a tiny-bodied directional bar is genuinely both). **Tightening (the safe speedup):** ADDED 4 UNCONDITIONAL candle conflicts, each provable from the evaluator's body/range + wick/range bounds (`evaluator.rs:233-256`) AND verified to never co-occur across 20k random bars: `(DOJI, LARGE_BODY)` (body/range <0.1 ⊥ >0.7), `(LONG_UPPER_WICK, LONG_LOWER_WICK)` (upper+body+lower==range ⇒ two halves can't both exceed range/2), `(LARGE_BODY, LONG_UPPER_WICK)`, `(LARGE_BODY, LONG_LOWER_WICK)` (a >0.7 body leaves <0.3 for either wick). Net CONFLICT_PAIRS: 24 − 2 + 4 = **26**. **New proof test (the real assurance):** `tests/property/test_conflict_pairs_exact.py` drives the REAL `evaluate_atoms` over 600 randomized realistic bars and asserts the load-bearing invariant `has_conflict(evaluate_atoms(bar)) is False` ∀ bars — i.e. NO conflict pair is ever co-set on a real bar ⟺ pruning conflict-masks can never drop a fireable mask ⟺ the Stage-1B prune is **EXACT (leaderboard-preserving)**. This test would have CAUGHT the bullish-doji bug (a real bar sets both → fails) and now regression-guards both the removed pairs (must co-occur) and the added pairs (must never). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** net mask-count effect is roughly neutral (un-prune 2 false / prune 4 new); the WIN is CORRECTNESS (the leaderboard no longer silently loses bullish/bearish-doji strategies) plus a slightly tighter exact prune. The degenerate zero-range bar/day edge (which can trip the pre-existing `(at_day_high, at_day_low)` pair) is out of scope (real bars have range >= 1 tick). **Verified locally:** 128 tests pass incl. the 400-case vocab golden (evaluator unchanged) + the sweep goldens (conflict_pruned counts unchanged for their fixtures); ruff + mypy clean. **Scope:** the EVALUATOR + the 52-condition golden are UNCHANGED — only the mask-generation prune set + a new test. **Builds on:** DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 (the prefilter), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (the authoritative evaluator semantics), the SPRT-abandon redirect (DEC-SPRT-INFEASIBLE-001, which pointed here as the safe exact speedup), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #4 / #10.
590b. **DEC-OPTION-AUDIT-WIRE-001 — wire the hash-chained option-ingest audit into the live option pull (Golden Rule #8 parity with spot; closes gap D-2)** (2026-06-08; the next safe item after DEC-STAGE1B-CONFLICT-FIX-001 / PR #521). **Gap (re-verified by the fresh gap sweep):** `OptionBarSink` fully supports an injected `audit=` sink and emits one hash-chained `OPTION_BARS_WRITTEN` row per written series (`brutex/data/option_sink.py:107,170-172`, 100%-tested in `tests/unit/test_option_sink.py:84` `test_writes_survivors_and_audits` via `_FakeAudit`) — but the production builder `_build_live_options` (`brutex/dashboard/option_pull_controller.py:277`) constructed the sink WITHOUT `audit=`, so live option pulls left NO audit chain (the spot side got wired in #582/DEC-INGEST-AUDIT-CHAIN-001; the option side was its explicitly-deferred fast-follow). **What shipped:** `_build_live_options` now opens an `AuditWriter` at `<lake>/audit/option-ingest.jsonl` (resume = append to the existing chain) and passes it as `audit=` to the sink. `AuditWriter.append` satisfies the `OptionAuditSink` protocol (mypy --strict confirms). The `AuditWriter` is **flush-per-entry** (every row persists without an explicit close), and the sink's existing single write-lock keeps the hash chain single-writer (no concurrency issue under the parallel option fan-out). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the change is the LIVE wiring only — `_build_live_options` is `# pragma: no cover` (needs real Dhan creds + network), consistent with the spot CLI wiring; the audit-WRITE core it activates is already 100%-tested. The dry-run path (`_build_dry_run_options` → `NullOptionBarSink`) and the injected-factory test path are UNCHANGED. **Verified locally:** ruff + `mypy --strict` clean on `option_pull_controller.py`; `import brutex.dashboard.option_pull_controller` OK; 27 option_pull_controller + option_sink tests pass (dry-run path unaffected). **Scope:** dashboard live-builder wiring only — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE + the option sink/writer are UNCHANGED. **Builds on:** DEC-INGEST-AUDIT-CHAIN-001 (#582, the spot audit this mirrors), the `OptionBarSink` audit design (`option_sink.py`), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the single-lock that keeps the chain single-writer), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #8 / #10.

591b. **DEC-DOC-STANDARDS-RECONCILE-001 — reconcile CLAUDE.md §2 rule 12's stale "~22% enforced" envelope to the real "~71% enforced" (G4 of the 4-gap audit; doc-only)** (2026-06-08; the first gap-closure PR after the 4-agent deep workspace audit). **Gap:** a parallel-agent audit found that `CLAUDE.md:174` claimed the CI enforcement matrix was "**9 of 21 sub-rows ✅ ENFORCED + 4 🟡 + 5 📋 + 3 👁️** (~22%)" — a verbatim 2026-05-16 snapshot taken BEFORE the DEC-STANDARDS-AUDIT-001 → DEC-CROSSWALK-001 → DEC-PYLINT-DROP-001 → DEC-DOCTOR-001 → DEC-STRESS-001 ratchet arc closed 6 rows. The authoritative summary count at `docs/STANDARDS_100PCT.md:67-86` has read "**15 🟢 / 2 🟡 / 1 📋 / 3 👁️ → 71% / 10% / 5% / 14%**" since 2026-05-24. 592a. **DEC-O1-BENCH-GAPS-001 — close the 3 un-benched O(1) hot-path gaps with isolated ratio gates: Bloom probe, BLAKE3 combo-hash, raw Parquet lake-write (G1 of the 4-gap audit)** (2026-06-08; the follow-on after DEC-DOC-STANDARDS-RECONCILE-001 / PR #528). **Gap:** the O(1) audit agent found that of the five Golden-Rule-#5 hot paths, three had NO dedicated bench: (a) the **Bloom probe** `BloomFilter.might_contain` was only exercised inside the composite option-dedup gate, never alone (`brutex/orchestrator/bloom.py:346`); (b) the **BLAKE3 combo-hash** `combo_hash`→`fno_math.blake3_hash` (`brutex/strategies/combo.py:91,180`) was architecturally O(1) per fixed-size identity but unbenched; (c) the **raw Parquet lake-write** `ParquetWriter.write` (`brutex/data/parquet_writer.py:224`) had only the in-memory results-store append gated, not the real file write. All three were YELLOW ("plausible, not proven"). **What shipped:** three new bench modules under `tests/bench/`, each a ratio gate routed through the existing two-tier `_o1_tiers.ratio_ceiling` (robust shared-CI ceiling, decreed 1.1× on the M4-Pro strict tier): `test_bloom_o1.py` (probe latency independent of inserts, 100k vs 1k, < 5×), `test_blake3_combo_hash_o1.py` (per-call latency independent of call count — guards against accidental growing state, 100k vs 1k, < 5×), `test_parquet_write_o1.py` (fresh-write latency independent of existing partition count, 500 vs 50, < 8×; each write targets a unique symbol → a new partition file, isolating the create-write from any merge). **Real-run proof (local .venv):** all 10 tests pass in ~10s; measured ratios Bloom 1.03×, hash ~1.0×, write ~1.0× — all far under their ceilings, and an O(n) regression (scan-on-probe / growing hash state / lake-scan-on-write) would blow the ratio and fail the gate. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this does NOT force the decreed strict 1.1× on shared CI (that stays M4-Pro-tier only, per DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 / DEC-P0-020 shared-runner flake reality) — it converts three previously-unbenched O(1) claims into machine-checked regression gates at the same noise-tolerant ceilings the existing O(1) benches use. Test-only; no `brutex/` runtime code changed; CI scopes mypy to `brutex/` and jscpd to `brutex/`, so the new test modules add gates without touching either. **Builds on:** the 4-agent audit (this session), DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 (the `_o1_tiers` two-tier helper), `test_lmdb_membership_o1.py` / `test_option_dedup_o1.py` (the sibling O(1) gates this mirrors), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #4 (reproducibility) / #5 (O(1) discipline) / #10 (honest limits).
592b. **DEC-OPTION-429-RECOVERY-001 — make the rolling-option series ingest TRANSACTIONAL (resume-cursor in-run retry + commit-all-or-nothing) so a 429 mid-pagination never leaves a page-holed partition (closes audit Gap #2)** (2026-06-08; the option-path parity for the spot in-run 429 retry DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 + the `until_clean` recovery #571). **Gap (verified in code):** `ingest_rolling_option_series` (`brutex/adapters/dhan/option_ingest.py`) tiled a series into 30-day windows (the "cursors" of a multi-page option chain) and, on a RETRYABLE error (429 / 5xx / timeout), **DEFERRED** that cursor to the next pull (`continue`) while still fetching + WRITING the later cursors (the old `option_ingest.py:288-297` "a failed window is DEFERRED, NOT retried in-run as the spot path does"). So a 429 landing mid-pagination left the lake partition with a HOLE — a missing page between written pages. Keep-first dedup (`data/option_sink.py` + `data/option_dedup.py`) collapses a duplicate timestamp on a re-pull but can NEVER fill a missing page, so the partition could sit PARTIAL until a manual re-run (the audit's Gap #2). The spot path already had BOTH the in-run per-window 429 retry (DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 / `ingest.py`) AND the outer `until_clean` round loop (`until_clean.py`); the option path had neither. **What shipped (1 source file — `option_ingest.py`):** the series ingest is now **transactional** with two mechanisms: (1) **resume-cursor in-run retry** — a retryable cursor is re-fetched IN-RUN after a bounded seconds-scale exponential backoff (`_default_retry_backoff`, 1 s→2 s→…→8 s ceiling), up to `max_retry_passes` (default **2**) EXTRA attempts, paced by the SAME `≤ 5 r/s` bucket (Rule #6) so the retry waits the limiter out (mirrors the spot 429-retry rationale: the opening burst is over + the governor has stepped down by then); (2) **commit-all-or-nothing** — every cursor's session-filtered bars are STAGED in a phase-1 buffer and the sink is written + coverage marked only in a phase-2 COMMIT pass that runs AFTER every cursor has been fetched cleanly. If a cursor outruns its retry budget (or a TERMINAL error raises mid-fetch), the whole series ABORTS having committed NOTHING — the partition stays EMPTY and the un-committed windows are deferred to the next pull (coverage untouched ⇒ a re-pull re-fetches them). So the lake partition for a series is always WHOLE or ABSENT, **never a page-holed partial**. New `OptionIngestReport` fields `retried_windows` + `still_failed_windows` (mirroring the spot `IngestReport`) + a `complete` property (`still_failed_windows == 0`). The rate-feedback routing (429→`on_rate_limit`, 5xx/timeout→`on_timeout`, clean→`on_success`; DEC-DHAN-TIMEOUT-BACKOFF-001) is preserved per attempt. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the staging buffer is **O(session-bars in the series) SPACE, NOT O(1)** — an all-or-nothing commit cannot be O(1) space without a sink-side rollback (out of this path's scope); the O(1) guarantees that DO hold are per-bar (the coverage probe, the dedup probe, the coverage-key build). The retry COUNT is bounded by `max_retry_passes` (never infinite) and every fetch is paced ≤ 5 r/s; a terminal / token-death error is non-retryable and raises straight out (quarantined upstream, partition empty). Behaviour change vs the old spine: a transient cursor now ABORTS the series (commit nothing) instead of deferring just that one window with the others written — that is the whole point (no more partial partitions). **Tests (100% line+branch on `option_ingest.py` — 110 stmts / 24 branch / 0 miss, verified locally in a 3.12 venv with the `fno_math`+`trading_core` kernels built):** `tests/unit/test_dhan_option_ingest.py` — the resume-heals-on-retry (partition COMPLETE), permanent-429-leaves-EMPTY (NOT even the already-fetched cursor 0 committed), abort-does-not-mark-coverage, complete-marks-every-window-in-one-commit, backoff-zero-based-indices, terminal-mid-series-commits-nothing, + the updated transient/feedback-routing cases (now assert clean abort, `sink.batches == []`) + the bounded-exponential backoff math (worst-case clamp, no real sleep via injected hook); a NEW property test `tests/property/test_dhan_option_429_recovery_properties.py` drives randomized chain length × failing-cursor position × heal-vs-permanent × retry budget and asserts the load-bearing invariant `committed_windows ∈ {0, N}` (never 1…N−1) ∧ `complete ⇔ failing cursor recovers within budget`; a NEW integration test `tests/integration/test_dhan_option_429_recovery.py` proves the guarantee against the REAL lake-write stack (real `OptionBarSink` + `OptionDedupIndex` + recording partition writer + a real hash-chained `AuditWriter`): a resumed 429 commits the whole partition with one audit row per window and `verify_chain` passes, a permanent 429 leaves ZERO writes / ZERO audit rows and the chain still verifies. Existing `test_dhan_option_universe_ingest` / `_parallel_wiring` / `option_pull_controller` / audit-chain tests pass unchanged (the universe fan-out calls the series spine with the defaults; its terminal-quarantine + success paths are unaffected). **Scope:** the Dhan option ingest path only — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE, the option sink/writer/dedup, and the spot path are UNCHANGED; `option_universe_ingest` / `option_pull_controller` signatures are untouched (the resume-cursor guard is fully contained in the series spine, default-on). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 / DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 (the spot in-run retry this brings to options), DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#571) + `until_clean` (the outer round-loop recovery), DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip-ledger now advanced all-or-nothing), DEC-DHAN-TIMEOUT-BACKOFF-001 (#494, the per-attempt rate feedback), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the single-writer sink the integration test exercises), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #7 / #8 / #10 / #11.

## DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 (2026-06-08)

592c. **DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 — make the 12h `TokenKeepalive` the SINGLE token renewer (renews ONLY when <12h, learning expiry OFFLINE from the JWT `exp`), and DELETE the ungated per-pull `RenewToken` that rotated + then lost a healthy live token** (2026-06-08, operator: *"why always this renew token is hitting even in that case [>12h] ... it is wiping the current active token and trying to fetch the stale token ... one and only when the current active token is less than 12 hours alone right then this renew token should hit"*). Entry numbered **592** (renumbered 587→592 on the MIGRATION append collision with main's #587–#591; the decision ID is authoritative). **Root cause (two coupled defects, code-traced — distinct from #583 which only fixed reading the rotated `token` key):** (a) `pull_controller.py::_maybe_renew_adapter_token` fired a `RenewToken` at the START OF EVERY live pull / repull / retry (call sites `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles`), with **NO <12h gate** — exactly the operator's "why is it always hitting" complaint. `RenewToken` **ROTATES** (mints a new token and INVALIDATES the presented one — DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 #583), so firing it on a healthy >12h token needlessly killed it. (b) On success the helper wrote the new token into `replace(adapter.client, access_token=...)` — but the live client reads its token from the shared `TokenHolder` via `token_provider` (`client.py:_headers`: `token_provider() if token_provider is not None else access_token`), so the rebuilt `access_token` field is **IGNORED** and the holder was **never updated**. Net effect: the pull kept reading the **just-invalidated** token from the holder → `HTTP 400 DH-906 "Invalid Token"` → the loud `auth_expired` verdict, on a token that was **never actually expired**. (The 11:37 full pull succeeded because the per-pull `RenewToken` was *refused* that time, a no-op; the 13:15 "Retry failed windows" *succeeded* at rotating and self-destructed the live token.) The correct renewer already existed: the background `TokenKeepalive` renews ONLY at the 12h half-life AND writes the fresh token into the holder the client reads. **What shipped:** (1) `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_keepalive.py` — NEW pure `decode_jwt_expiry(token)`: reads the access-token JWT's standard `exp` claim (RFC 7519, base64url middle segment) **offline, with no network and no rotation**, so a freshly-pasted >12h token triggers **ZERO** `RenewToken` calls until it is genuinely inside the 12h window; returns `None` on ANY untrusted shape (not a 3-segment JWT / bad base64url / non-JSON / non-object claims / missing-or-non-numeric `exp`, `bool` rejected though it subclasses `int`) so a non-JWT token degrades to the prior learn-by-renew path — never a crash, never a guess. `_tick` now LEARNS expiry from the JWT on the first tick instead of an immediate rotating `RenewToken`; only a token actually <12h is renewed. (2) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — DELETE `_maybe_renew_adapter_token` + both call sites + the now-unused `replace` import; a breadcrumb comment at each former call site records WHY no per-pull renew exists. The keepalive is the sole renewer. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all four changed files; the FULL `pytest`/`mypy --strict`/`pyright`/strict-100%-coverage gate is enforced by CI (the dev container is Python 3.11 without the runtime deps, so the suite runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, NOT fabricated here). NEW tests: `TestDecodeJwtExpiry` ×9 (every decode branch) + `TestTick` ×2 (first-tick JWT >12h ⇒ 0 RenewToken calls, token untouched, `auth.keepalive.expiry_learned` logged; <12h ⇒ renews); the obsolete `TestMaybeRenewAdapterToken` removed with the helper. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ RenewToken now fires ONLY when the active token is genuinely <12h — never on a normal pull/repull/retry — and when it does fire (the keepalive) the fresh token propagates through the holder the client reads. 🟡 the keepalive keeps a token alive only while the PROCESS runs AND the first token is an ACTIVE web-generated JWT; a non-JWT/TOTP-minted or `exp`-less token degrades to one learn-by-renew at startup (best-effort, not a crash). The per-pull Telegram `auth_renew_failed` alert is removed with the per-pull renew; the keepalive still logs `auth.renew_failed`. 🚫 no change to the rate caps, ingest spine, or engine. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 (#583) · DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 · DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 · §6 · §10 · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (2026-06-08)

593. **DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 — make the one-click "Pull spot" DRIVE ITSELF to a clean lake: turn the (already-built, already-100%-tested) re-pull-until-clean loop ON by default in the dashboard pull route** (2026-06-08, operator: *"once you finish the entire chunks then at last automatically retry until it fetched all the windows ... until every window gets finished this process should be repeated ... that too until or unless our quota is not yet exceeded ... until everything is clean it should always pull/retry, automated"*). Entry numbered **593** (renumbered 588→593 on the append collision; the decision ID is authoritative). **Root cause (capability existed but wired OFF):** `until_clean.run_until_clean` loops bounded re-pull rounds until `stop_clean` (every window fetched) / `stop_quota` (daily 100k Dhan quota spent) / `stop_dead` (token died) / `stop_no_progress` / budget, reusing the shared coverage ledger so each round re-fetches ONLY still-failed windows, rate-safe (DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001; `until_clean.py` is 100% line+branch + property + stress + O(1) bench tested). But `pull_all_spot(auto_retry=False, until_clean=False)` defaults it OFF, and the dashboard's main `POST /api/v1/universe/pull` route (`app.py::api_universe_pull._work`) passed NEITHER flag — so the one-click "Pull spot" ran a **single pass**, left whatever a transient 429/timeout storm failed (the operator's 125 residual windows), and STOPPED with the "⏳ Re-pull to finish" banner, requiring a MANUAL "Retry failed windows" click (which then independently died on the token-rotation bug fixed by DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 #592). The failures were never auto-retried-to-completion — not "tried and failed", but "never auto-tried". **What shipped (one wiring change):** `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the main pull route's background `_work` now calls `pull_all_spot(..., auto_retry=True, until_clean=True)`, engaging `run_until_clean` with the persisted-quota hook (`_rate_controller.quota_exhausted`) + `stop_when_stuck=True` over the bounded `AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS` (50) budget. The one-click pull now self-drives to a clean lake — zero manual "Re-pull" clicks (CLAUDE.md §11 AUTOMATED) — and stops cleanly on quota (resume after the IST-midnight reset) or token-death (re-auth), never an infinite or quota-burning loop. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** the changed `_work` route body is `# pragma: no cover — runs on the job thread` (the underlying `pull_all_spot(until_clean=True)` path, `run_until_clean`, the quota hook, and the no-progress guard are each already 100% line+branch covered by `tests/unit/test_dhan_until_clean.py` + `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` + `tests/property/test_until_clean_properties.py` + `tests/stress/test_until_clean_stress.py` + `tests/bench/test_dhan_until_clean_o1.py`); no route test pins the prior single-pass kwargs. `ruff` + `ruff format --check` clean; the full gate runs on CI. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the one-click pull retries every failed window automatically until the lake is clean OR the daily quota is spent, with the 50-round bound + the no-progress guard + the quota brake making it safe. 🟡 each round is O(failed_windows), NOT O(1)-total — a sustained throttle still costs wall-time; the loop pauses (not fails) on quota and resumes after IST midnight. This complements DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (#588), which audits/alerts a per-symbol 100%-failure storm. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s / 100k-day caps, the ingest spine, or the engine; the `/retry-failed` button + its `?until_clean=` escalation are unchanged. **Builds on:** DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 · DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 · DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 (#592) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 · DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (#588) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 · §10 · §11 AUTOMATED.
