## DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001 (2026-06-08)

594. **DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001 — one durable source of truth for the live access token: a write-through `TokenHolder` so a mid-session credential SAVE and a keepalive RENEW both keep the persisted store + the in-memory holder in sync — fixing `auth_expired` on a freshly-saved valid token** (2026-06-08, operator live `make run` with a brand-new token: `auth.keepalive.expiry_learned remaining_hours=20.93 … no RenewToken fired` (proving DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 #592 works) yet the pull still `universe.pull_all.preflight_refused … verdict=auth_expired`; operator: *"why the fuck it failed again even with the new access token … better to have the db for this access token and always keep the latest token and have only one unique active token which is active and whenever even it gets renewed also it should be the updated one"*). **Root cause (code-traced, two divergent stores — the same token_provider/holder family as #592 but a different gap):** the live token lives in TWO places that drifted apart: the persisted `~/.brutex/credentials.json` (0600) and the in-memory `TokenHolder` every live `DhanClient` reads through `token_provider=holder.get`. (a) **Save gap:** `app.py::api_credentials_set` wrote the FILE (`save_dhan_credentials`) but NEVER updated the in-memory holder — which was seeded ONCE at startup. So saving a new token mid-session had ZERO effect on the running pull: it kept reading the stale startup token (already invalidated by a prior session's RenewToken rotation) → `DH-906` → `auth_expired`, even though the just-pasted token was valid (JWT `exp` ~21h out, decoded + confirmed). The only workaround was a full app restart (which re-seeds the holder from the file). (b) **Renew gap (latent):** the keepalive's `RenewToken` ROTATES (the new token invalidates the old), and `_renew_once` wrote the rotated token to the holder but NOT back to the file — so after any renewal the FILE held the now-DEAD pre-rotation token, and a restart re-loaded a dead token. **What shipped (the operator's "single latest active token" design):** the persisted creds file is the SINGLE durable store; the holder becomes a WRITE-THROUGH cache over it, so BOTH events keep them in sync. (1) `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_holder.py` — `TokenHolder(token, *, on_set=None)`: `set()` updates the in-memory token under the lock, then (OUTSIDE the lock — it may do file I/O) calls the optional `on_set` persist hook; construction does NOT persist (only an explicit set propagates). (2) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — `start_token_keepalive` builds the holder with an `on_set` that write-throughs the token to the 0600 creds file (preserving the client id), best-effort (logs `auth.token_persist_failed`, NEVER raises — a persist failure can't crash a renewal mid-pull). So a keepalive renewal now persists the rotated token → a restart re-loads the LIVE token (gap (b) closed). NEW `refresh_live_token(access_token) -> bool`: updates the installed holder in place (write-through) + tells the keepalive (NEW `set_live_keepalive` seam) to `forget_expiry()`; returns `False` when no live session is installed. (3) `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_keepalive.py` — NEW `TokenKeepalive.forget_expiry()`: drops the learned `_expiry_deadline` so the next `_tick` RE-LEARNS the new token's JWT `exp` offline (or renews if <12h) — no stale schedule after a save. (4) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `api_credentials_set` calls `refresh_live_token(body.access_token)` after the file save, so a saved token goes live with ZERO restart (gap (a) closed); the lifespan shutdown clears `set_live_keepalive(None)` alongside the holder. **Security (deliberate, no-illusion):** the single store stays the 0600 `credentials.json` file (never committed, never in the browsable DuckDB lake) — a secret token must NOT land in the `/db` tables the operator browses, or it leaks; the file is the durable single-source, not the DB. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 4 source + 3 test files; `interrogate … --fail-under=100` PASSES on token_holder.py / token_keepalive.py / pull_controller.py locally; the full pytest/mypy/pyright/100%-coverage gate runs on CI (this dev container is Python 3.11 without the runtime deps). NEW tests: `test_dhan_token_holder.py::test_on_set_write_through_persists_each_set` (construction silent, every set persists in order — both `on_set` branches); `test_dhan_token_keepalive.py::test_forget_expiry_clears_learned_deadline`; `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py::TestRefreshLiveToken` ×3 (no-holder→False, holder+keepalive→updates+forget_expiry, holder-without-keepalive→updates — covering both `holder is None` and `keepalive is not None` arms + `set_live_keepalive`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a saved token goes live without a restart; a renewed token is persisted so a restart re-loads the live token; one durable store, always the latest active token, synced on save AND renew. 🟡 the write-through persist is best-effort — a (rare) file-write failure logs `auth.token_persist_failed` and leaves the in-memory token live for the session but the file stale until the next successful set (a restart then would need a re-paste); the store is the 0600 file, not LMDB (a same-design swap if ever wanted). The keepalive's per-tick deadline is reset on save but the client_id captured at keepalive-start is reused by the persist hook (a mid-session client_id change is preserved because the handler writes the full creds first). 🚫 no change to the rate caps, the ingest spine, the engine, or the JWT-exp learning (#592). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 (#592, the JWT-exp learning + single-renewer this completes) · DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 (the holder/keepalive seam) · DEC-DHAN-CREDS-WIRING-001 (the file resolver that reads the single store) · DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 (#583, why a rotated token must be persisted) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 · §11 COMMON (one source of truth) · §10.

## DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001 (2026-06-08)

595. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001 — let the 429 ladder ease BELOW 3 r/s under a SUSTAINED storm + fix the `on_success` recovery bug that left the rate pinned at the floor for the rest of a pull** (2026-06-08, operator 90-min live log: `current_rps=3.0` with `recent_hits` pinned at ~179 for 3.5 min on a band of symbols (every call 429'd even at 3 r/s), and the rate then NEVER recovered above 3 for the remaining ~50 min of the pull). **Root cause (two coupled defects in `brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py`):** (a) **floor too high.** The 429 ladder hard-clamped at `FLOOR_RPS=3` (`if … and self._rps > FLOOR_RPS`) — "a quota breach is no reason to crawl" — but a RELENTLESS storm where Dhan rejects *every* call even at 3 r/s proves 3 is still too fast; the controller had nowhere lower to ease (unlike the TIMEOUT ladder, already allowed to reach `TIMEOUT_FLOOR_RPS=1` by DEC-DHAN-OPTION-TIMEOUT-STORM-001), so it spun pinned at 3 getting 100%-rejected. (b) **recovery permanently blocked.** `on_rate_limit` clears `_hits` ONLY inside its step-down branch, which cannot fire at the floor (`rps > FLOOR_RPS` False) — so `_hits` stayed pinned at its rolling-window count; and `on_success` evicted only `_timeouts`, NEVER `_hits`, so `not self._hits` was never True and the rate could never step back up to 5 once a storm reached the floor (the operator's "3 r/s for the whole run after one storm"). **What shipped:** (1) NEW constants `RATE_LIMIT_STORM_FLOOR_RPS = TIMEOUT_FLOOR_RPS (1.0)` + `STORM_HITS = 30`. `on_rate_limit` is now a TWO-TIER ladder: it reaches the SOFT `FLOOR_RPS` (3) quickly on a brief burst (`STEP_DOWN_HITS=3`), but eases BELOW it toward `RATE_LIMIT_STORM_FLOOR_RPS` (1) ONLY on the higher SUSTAINED-evidence `STORM_HITS` threshold (`threshold = STEP_DOWN_HITS if rps > FLOOR_RPS else STORM_HITS`; clamp `rps > RATE_LIMIT_STORM_FLOOR_RPS`). At 3 r/s, 30 hits ≈ 10 s of 100%-rejection — an unmistakable storm, not a quota nudge — so a transient burst still rests at 3 while a true cascade can finally back off. (2) `on_success` now evicts aged `_hits` AND `_timeouts` (was timeouts-only), so once a storm clears and its hits age out of the 60 s window, recovery proceeds 1→2→3→4→5 instead of staying stuck at the floor. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `interrogate … --fail-under=100` PASSES on rate_control.py locally; the full pytest/100%-branch-coverage gate runs on CI (this dev container is Python 3.11 and CANNOT import the test chain — `brutex.orchestrator.retry` uses 3.12 `def retry_call[T]` generics — so the suite runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, NOT fabricated here). NEW/updated tests in `test_dhan_rate_control.py`: `test_brief_429_burst_clamps_at_soft_floor_3` (sub-storm burst rests at 3), `test_sustained_429_storm_eases_below_soft_floor_to_storm_floor` (3→2→1 on STORM_HITS each), `test_429_clamps_at_storm_floor_never_below_1` (the `rps > storm_floor` False arm), `test_recovery_unblocked_after_storm_hits_age_out` (the on_success `_hits`-evict True arm — the bug fix), and `test_on_success_blocked_by_recent_hit` rewritten so the blocking hit is genuinely IN-window (the eviction-False arm). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a sustained 429 storm now backs off to 1 r/s (room for Dhan to recover) instead of spinning pinned at 3, and the controller recovers to 5 after the storm clears instead of crawling for the rest of the pull. 🟡 easing to 1 r/s does NOT make Dhan accept the calls — it reduces the hammering + lets the vendor recover; a storm outlasting the window still defers windows to the next pull (no worse than before; the auto-resume #593 + the per-symbol watchdog #533 cover that). The in-run retry curb (defer instead of re-pile under a pinned-at-floor storm) is intentionally LEFT to the watchdog (#533) rather than duplicated here — out of scope. The `STORM_HITS=30` / deep-floor=1 values mirror the timeout ladder's relief-valve design; tunable. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s ceiling / 100k-day quota, the token bucket, the ingest spine, or the engine — only WHEN/HOW LOW the 429 ladder eases + the recovery eviction. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-OPTION-TIMEOUT-STORM-001 (the timeout deep-floor this mirrors for 429s) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the ladder this extends) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-SINGLE-BUCKET-001 (the single shared bucket the rate mutates) · DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (#533, the complementary give-up/alert this does not duplicate) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (#593, the retry-to-clean this composes with) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1) hooks) · Rule 6 (≤5 r/s) · §10.

## DEC-DHAN-RATE-RECOVERY-TRICKLE-001 (2026-06-08)

596. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-RECOVERY-TRICKLE-001 — let the rate RECOVER under a chronic MILD 429/timeout drip instead of staying pinned at the floor: gate `on_success` recovery on the step-down trigger, not a strictly-empty window** (2026-06-08, follow-up to the #595 4-agent hostile review, which flagged this as a pre-existing HIGH; operator chose to fix it now). **Root cause (residual of the #595 recovery bug, `brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py`):** #595 fixed recovery for a storm that FULLY clears — `on_success` evicts aged `_hits`/`_timeouts`, so once the 60 s rolling window empties to ZERO the rate climbs 1→…→5. But the recovery gate was `not self._hits and not self._timeouts` — it required the window to be STRICTLY empty. Under a CHRONIC mild drip (a handful of 429s — or timeouts — per minute, far BELOW the step-down trigger, e.g. the vendor incidentally rejecting ~2 calls/60 s), the rolling window NEVER fully empties, so `not self._hits` is never True and the rate stays pinned at the floor FOREVER, never probing back toward the ceiling. This is the slow-drip twin of the operator's "never recovered above 3" log: #595 closed the burst-then-clear case; the persistent trickle remained a trap. **What shipped (one gate change):** the recovery condition is now `len(self._hits) < STEP_DOWN_HITS and len(self._timeouts) < STEP_DOWN_TIMEOUT_HITS` (plus the unchanged `_rps < CEILING_RPS` + `now - _last_step >= STEP_UP_WINDOW`). Recovery proceeds whenever NEITHER ladder shows step-down-LEVEL pressure — a mild drip probes up one rung, and if the higher rate genuinely storms, the ladder steps straight back down (self-correcting AIMD); genuine `>= STEP_DOWN_HITS` pressure still HOLDS the rate. The threshold bites only AT/BELOW the floor: above it `on_rate_limit`/`on_timeout` already clear their deque on every step (so at most `STEP_DOWN_HITS-1` ever sit in the window and recovery there is purely `STEP_UP_WINDOW`-timer gated); at/below the floor — where no further step clears the deque — a real drip is what holds recovery, giving correct hysteresis (a moderate sustained-rejection band holds; a faint incidental drip recovers). O(1): `len()` on a deque. The `on_success` aged-out eviction (#595) is unchanged. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion, REAL local run):** unlike #595 (run only on CI), this branch's tests were executed locally on **Python 3.12.3** (a throwaway venv with `pytest`+`structlog`+`lmdb`) — `tests/unit/test_dhan_rate_control.py` = **37 passed**, and `pytest --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.rate_control --cov-branch` = **100.00% line + branch** on `rate_control.py`. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `interrogate --fail-under=100` PASS. The full mypy/pyright/mutation/property gate runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. NEW/updated tests: `test_mild_trickle_does_not_block_recovery` (a lone in-window 429 now recovers — the core fix, the True arm), `test_step_down_pressure_at_floor_blocks_recovery` (a `>= STEP_DOWN_HITS` drip at the floor with the timer met still HOLDS — the hit-gate False arm), `test_mild_timeout_drip_does_not_block_recovery` (timeout-side True arm; replaces the old `test_recent_timeout_blocks_then_clears_recovery` whose premise the fix inverts), `test_timeout_pressure_at_floor_blocks_recovery` (timeout-gate False arm), `test_recovery_unblocked_after_timeout_drip_ages_out` (the `on_success` `_timeouts`-eviction body — restores the line the replaced test covered). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a chronic mild 429/timeout drip no longer pins the rate at the floor — the controller probes back to the ceiling once pressure drops below the step-down level, while a genuine sustained-rejection band still holds it down. 🟡 recovery is a probe: above the floor it steps up once per `STEP_UP_WINDOW` (300 s) whenever the in-window drip is below the step-down trigger, which can cause a slow bounded oscillation around the true sustainable rate (e.g. 4↔5) under borderline load — intended AIMD, never exceeds the 5 r/s ceiling, far better than a permanent pin. The `STEP_DOWN_HITS`/`STEP_DOWN_TIMEOUT_HITS` recovery thresholds reuse the step-down constants (tunable). 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s ceiling / 100k-day quota, the two-tier step-DOWN ladder (#595), the token bucket, the ingest spine, or the engine — only WHEN recovery is allowed. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001 (#595, the recovery-eviction this completes) · DEC-DHAN-OPTION-TIMEOUT-STORM-001 · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the ladder) · DEC-DHAN-TIMEOUT-BACKOFF-001 (the timeout deque this also gates on) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1) hooks) · Rule 6 (≤5 r/s) · §10.

## DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 (2026-06-08)

597. **DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 — a Dhan `DH-905` "no data present" is a SETTLED known-gap, NOT a failed/pending window: stop it pinning every pull at `transient_residual` + the manual "Re-pull to finish" button** (2026-06-08, operator live `make run` over 783 instruments: `universe.pull_all.done … failed=1 pending_windows=1 verdict=transient_residual` on EVERY pull, the single offender being `NIFTY NEXT 50` **1-day**, whose daily history simply starts after 2021-01-01 so Dhan answers `HTTP 400 DH-905 "… no data present"`; operator: *"no data is fine … as long as Dhan returns the successful 200 we should retry; once it completes the chunk it should retry the failed windows and never stop until those alone succeed"*). **Root cause (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` + `brutex/adapters/dhan/run_ingest.py`):** a `DH-905` is a TERMINAL non-retryable 400, so `run_dhan_spot_ingest` quarantines the `(symbol, interval)` pair into `report.failures` (logged as INFO `ingest.known_gap`, "re-tried next pull, not masked"). But `pull_all_spot` counted EVERY `report.failures` key as a `failed` pair (`SymbolPullResult.failed`), so `total_failed=1` → `classify_pull` returns `transient_residual` (`needs_operator=True`) → the loud `universe.pull_all.action_required` WARNING + the dashboard's amber "⏳ Re-pull to finish" button. A re-pull just hits `DH-905` again → the SAME verdict → a permanent MANUAL loop. This is NOT an auto-retry failure: the in-run 429/timeout retries all succeeded (`still_failed_windows=0` on every symbol), and the auto-resume-until-clean loop correctly did not engage (it fires only on `still_failed_windows>0`, i.e. RETRYABLE transient leftovers). A `DH-905` can NEVER return a 200, so "retry until success" would never terminate — settling it is the correct behavior, exactly as the operator asked ("no data is fine"). **What shipped (one classification change):** in `pull_all_spot`'s per-symbol tally, split the `report.failures` keys into `known_gap_keys` (those whose error matches `is_no_data_message` — `DH-905` / "no data present") vs genuine `failure_keys`. Known-gap pairs are now counted as `no_data` (settled / EMPTY), NOT `failed`. So a symbol like `NIFTY NEXT 50` finishes `completed=1` (1-minute landed bars) + `no_data=1` (the 1-day gap) → `classify_pull` → **`clean`** (`needs_operator=False`); a universe whose ONLY misses are known-gaps → `known_gap_only` (grey, no action). A GENUINE terminal error (a real 400/404 — auth is handled separately by the fail-fast latch) still counts as `failed` → `transient_residual`, unchanged. The pair is still left un-marked (re-attempted next pull, never masked — DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 unchanged), but it no longer POISONS the verdict into a manual re-pull. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** executed on **Python 3.12.3** (venv with the runtime deps) — `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` = **67 passed**. NEW tests: `test_dh905_no_data_is_settled_not_a_failure` (a `DH-905` on both intervals → `total_failed=0`, `total_no_data=2`, verdict `known_gap_only`, `pending_windows=0`) and `test_daily_gap_with_intraday_data_is_clean` (the EXACT operator case — 1-minute completes, 1-day is a `DH-905` gap → `completed=1`/`failed=0`/`no_data=1` → verdict `clean`, zero manual button). The existing `test_no_data_and_failure_branches` still asserts a GENUINE `DhanBadRequestError("boom …")` → `transient_residual` (genuine errors unaffected). `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the one-click pull now finishes `clean` with ZERO manual "Re-pull" clicks when the only outstanding items are `DH-905` known-gaps (the operator's NIFTY NEXT 50 daily trap is gone); the auto-resume loop still drives every RETRYABLE transient window to success. 🟡 a `DH-905` pair is still re-attempted on the NEXT pull (1 wasted Dhan call/pull out of the 100k/day quota — negligible; the no-mask philosophy is preserved so a gap that later gains data is picked up). Permanently marking it settled in the coverage skip-ledger is a separate, larger follow-up (touches the daily-anchor %CHNG safety) — out of scope here. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s / 100k-day caps, the rate ladder, the token spine, the ingest spine, or the engine — only how a `DH-905` outcome is CLASSIFIED for the verdict. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 (the verdict this corrects) · DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 (the `ingest.known_gap` INFO log this aligns the tally with) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (#593, the retry-to-clean loop this clarifies fires on transient windows) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the no-mask re-attempt, unchanged) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (no hallucination — `DH-905` is the verified Dhan no-data marker) · §10 · §11 AUTOMATED.

## DEC-FAILED-WINDOW-FORCE-REPULL-001 (2026-06-08)

598. **DEC-FAILED-WINDOW-FORCE-REPULL-001 — a `FAILED` window (always a retryable `DhanRateLimitError`/timeout) must be RE-PULLED until it succeeds, not skipped forever because the coarse span-enclosure reconcile marked its internal gap "complete"** (2026-06-08, operator live `make run`: `/coverage/windows` shows **63 FAILED windows** at `bars=0`, `attempts=3`, `last_error=DhanRateLimitError` — e.g. `JSWDULUX` 1-minute 2024-09→2025-09 FAILED while 2022 and 2025-09→2026 are SUCCESS — and they NEVER clear across pulls; the pull itself ends `failed=0 verdict=known_gap_only` (everything skipped). Operator: *"why still this is failed even though when it is dhan ratelimit error … it didn't retry"*). **Root cause (`brutex/dashboard/coverage_reconcile.py` `reconcile_windows` + the skip-ledger):** the lake span is the dataset's **min/max** date (`first_date`..`last_date`); a window that FAILED mid-history has stored bars BOTH before AND after it, so the span ENCLOSES it and the conservative `reconcile_windows` marks it complete in the skip-ledger (the documented "internal gap inside an enclosed span is not detected here" limitation). Once marked complete (and persisted to `fetch_coverage.json`), the ingest SKIPS it on every later pull — so the `DhanRateLimitError` window that exhausted its in-run retry budget on the first pull (correctly left un-marked + deferred to "next pull" by DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001) is on the NEXT pull wrongly marked complete by the enclosure reconcile and never re-fetched → stuck FAILED at 0 bars forever. This is also why the verdict reads `known_gap_only`: the 63 genuinely-missing windows are masked as complete, so nothing re-pulls and the residual looks clean while real data is missing. **Key correctness fact (code-traced, `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py`):** a `FAILED` status row is ALWAYS a *retryable* transient — `status_log.record(..., error_type=type(exc).__name__)` is called ONLY on the `is_retryable(exc)` branch (rate-limit / timeout / transport / 5xx); a TERMINAL `DH-905` no-data is re-raised to the outer quarantine and NEVER recorded `FAILED` (it is a known-gap, settled by DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 #597). So every `FAILED` window is one that SHOULD keep being re-pulled until it succeeds — never a no-data window that would loop forever. **What shipped (the un-mark, NOT a status repaint):** (1) `FetchCoverage.unmark(key)` — O(1) `set.discard`, the idempotent inverse of `mark_complete`. (2) NEW pure `reconcile_failed_windows_for_repull(coverage, status_log)` in `coverage_reconcile.py`: for every window the status log records `FAILED`, `coverage.unmark(...)` it — overriding both the span-enclosure mark AND any stale persisted skip — and returns the count. (3) `pull_controller.py` calls it at pull start in BOTH pull paths, AFTER `reconcile_coverage_with_lake` (so the un-mark WINS) and after `begin_pull_status`. The un-marked windows are then re-fetched THIS pass; the auto-retry / until-clean loop (#593) drives the rate-limit ones to SUCCESS (status flips to SUCCESS naturally via the ingest's `record` on a 200), or — if Dhan genuinely has no data — settles them as a `DH-905` known-gap (#597). **Explicitly rejected (no-illusion):** an earlier draft FLIPPED the stale `FAILED` row straight to `SUCCESS` against the enclosing span. That was WRONG — it would PAINT OVER a genuine data gap (the window has 0 bars; the span only proves data exists *around* it, not *in* it) and hide missing data behind a green label. The screenshot proved the windows are genuinely empty (0 bars, only failed attempts), so the only correct fix is to RE-FETCH them, not relabel them. The un-mark self-heals in both cases (data missing → fetched + recorded SUCCESS; data somehow already present → re-fetch dedups keep-first + records SUCCESS) and can never hide a gap. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** executed on **Python 3.12.3** (venv with the runtime deps) — `tests/unit/test_fetch_coverage.py` + `test_coverage_reconcile.py` + `test_window_status.py` + `test_window_status_store.py` = **46 passed**; `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` = **67 passed**. NEW tests: `TestReconcileFailedWindowsForRepull` ×5 (a FAILED window un-marked → re-pulled; a SUCCESS/EMPTY row left complete — never needless re-fetch; un-marking an absent window is a safe no-op; empty log → 0) + `test_unmark_drops_a_completed_window` / `test_unmark_absent_window_is_a_noop` on `FetchCoverage`. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files. The full mypy/pyright/100%-coverage/mutation gate runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a `DhanRateLimitError`/timeout window is now RE-PULLED on the next pass instead of being skipped forever — the operator's 63 stuck FAILED windows get re-fetched until they succeed, so `/coverage/windows` reaches a true zero by FETCHING the data, not by relabeling it. ✅ the verdict becomes HONEST: while genuinely-missing windows remain, the pull reports `transient_residual` (work still to do) instead of a false `known_gap_only`. 🟡 a window that truly cannot be fetched (Dhan keeps rate-limiting it) is re-pulled every pass until it succeeds — by design ("never stop retrying a retryable window"); the `stop_when_stuck` brake bounds it WITHIN one `make run`, and the next run resumes it. The span-enclosure reconcile still cannot SEE an internal gap directly — this fix uses the per-window status log (the precise signal) to override it for known failures; a full per-window lake-completeness probe is a larger follow-up, not claimed here. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s / 100k-day caps, the rate ladder, the token spine, the ingest spine, or the engine — only WHICH windows the skip-ledger lets through. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (`reconcile_windows`, whose internal-gap limitation this corrects) · DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (the in-run retry that leaves a failed window un-marked — this stops the next pull from re-masking it) · DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 (#597, why a `DH-905` is NOT recorded `FAILED` and so is never force-re-pulled) · DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (the per-window status log this reads) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (#593, the loop that drives the re-pulled windows to success) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip-ledger this un-marks into) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (Correctness — never hide a gap) · §10 · §11 AUTOMATED.

## DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (2026-06-08)

599. **DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 — unify the two per-window stores into ONE durable ledger that records EVERY planned window and is the single source of truth for skip + retry (operator decree: "capture every window in a DB table so we always know which got missed / failed / succeeded")** (2026-06-08). **Why:** today the pull keeps per-window state in TWO stores that must agree but are wired so the WRONG one drives the skip — `FetchCoverage` (a flat *set* of completed windows, populated COARSELY from the dataset min/max span, the store the ingest actually probes) and `WindowStatusLog` (the PRECISE SUCCESS/EMPTY/FAILED record, visibility only). The coarse set masks an internal-gap FAILED window as "complete" so it is skipped forever (#598); #597/#598 were band-aids reaching ACROSS from the precise log into the coarse set every pull — fragile, derived, not authoritative. **The target (this decision):** ONE ledger that records every planned window as `PLANNED` at pull start then its landed outcome (`SUCCESS` / `EMPTY` / `FAILED` / `SKIPPED`), persisted as a real queryable DuckDB/Parquet table under the lake, browsable on `/db`, and **the authority for the skip decision** — a window is skipped ONLY if its row is settled (`SUCCESS`/`SKIPPED`); any `FAILED`/`PLANNED`/`EMPTY`-below-threshold or MISSING window is fetched. So a window can never be silently masked again — the skip falls out of the primary record, not a coarse derived set. **Staged rollout (each slice an independently merge-ready PR):** (1) **this PR — the pure `WindowLedger` model** (`brutex/data/window_ledger.py`): the in-memory O(1) ledger (`plan` / `is_skippable` / `record` / `settle_known_gap` + `to_rows`/`from_rows`), folding the EMPTY-terminal promotion (DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001) and the `DH-905` known-gap settle (#597) into one status vocabulary — no wiring, zero behaviour change; (2) the DuckDB/Parquet durable store + a one-time migration that folds `fetch_coverage.json` + `window_status.json` in (status-log wins on conflict, no data loss); (3) the `/db` + `/coverage/windows` read surface; (4) the switch — ingest skip/retry reads the ledger, retiring the coarse span-ledger + the #597/#598/EMPTY-terminal reconciles; (5) a `token_events` tracking table (events/metadata ONLY — saved/renewed/expired/refused + JWT-derived expiry + masked client-id; the raw token secret NEVER leaves the 0600 `~/.brutex/credentials.json`, never the browsable DB — DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001); (6) cleanup of the legacy sidecars after one release. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run, PR-1 only):** `tests/unit/test_window_ledger.py` = **22 passed** on **Python 3.12.3**, **100.00% line + branch** on `window_ledger.py`; `tests/bench/test_window_ledger_o1.py` = **4 passed** (the `is_skippable` + `record` 10k-vs-1k O(1) ratio gate). `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean. The full mypy/pyright/mutation gate runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ PR-1 is the pure model only — nothing imports it yet, so it is provably zero-risk (dead code until the wiring slice). The O(1) skip probe is a dict lookup under one lock (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5), bench-gated. 🟡 the structural guarantee (no window ever masked) lands in slice (4) when the ingest switches to read the ledger; slices (2)–(6) are tracked follow-ups. The EMPTY-terminal threshold (3) is duplicated as the canonical constant here and will be imported by `coverage_reconcile` in the wiring slice (single-source reconciled then). 🚫 no change yet to the ingest spine, the skip-ledger, the rate caps, the token spine, or the engine — this slice adds an unused module. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (the precise per-window log this generalises) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the coarse skip-set this replaces) · DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (the span-enclosure mark whose internal-gap flaw this removes) · DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 (#597, the `DH-905` settle folded into `settle_known_gap`) · DEC-FAILED-WINDOW-FORCE-REPULL-001 (#598, the force-re-pull this makes structural) · DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the EMPTY→SKIPPED promotion folded into `record`) · DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001 (the token-secret boundary slice (5) honours) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1)) · Rule 7 (idempotence) · §11 COMMON (one source of truth).

## DEC-TOKEN-EVENTS-001 (2026-06-08)

600. **DEC-TOKEN-EVENTS-001 — a durable token-lifecycle EVENT log (track the access token in the DB WITHOUT ever storing it)** (operator decree 2026-06-08: "even for auth token also it's better to keep the DB table and track everything"). **The table:** a real queryable Parquet table at `<lake_root>/token_events/events.parquet` (browsable on `/db`), the auth-side analog of the per-window ledger (DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001) — one append-only row per lifecycle event: `action` ∈ {saved, renewed, expired, refused}, `status`, `expiry_at` (the token's JWT `exp` as an ISO timestamp, derived via `decode_jwt_expiry`), `client_id_masked`, `reason`. **SECURITY BOUNDARY (the headline — Golden Rule #1 / §10):** the table records token lifecycle EVENTS + METADATA ONLY and MUST NEVER store the raw access-token secret. The secret's single durable home stays the `0600` `~/.brutex/credentials.json` (DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001) + the in-memory `TokenHolder`; this log is surfaced on the world-readable, browser-exposed `/db` page, so writing the secret there would LEAK a live credential. Three enforced guards: (1) `record_token_event` is **token-free by signature** — the caller derives `expiry_at` and passes only the timestamp, never the token string; (2) the row schema is a FIXED allowlist with **no token column**; (3) `mask_client_id` stars the middle of the dhanClientId (keep first/last 4 — e.g. `1100123456788842` → `1100********8842`; a ≤8-char id is fully starred). **Reliability:** append-only, best-effort — `record_token_event` NEVER raises (a failed write logs `token_events.write_failed` so it cannot crash a renewal mid-pull); `load_token_events` degrades to `[]` on a missing / corrupt / wrong-shape file (a structured WARNING, never an exception); crash-safe `*.tmp` + `os.replace`. **This PR (PR-5a):** the pure module `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_events.py` (`TokenEvent`, `mask_client_id`, `record_token_event`, `load_token_events`, `to_payload`) — no live wiring yet (zero-risk until the keepalive/refresh/auth call sites + the `/db` panel land in the follow-up, mirroring the PR-1-model-first pattern). **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** `tests/unit/test_dhan_token_events.py` = **13 passed** on **Python 3.12.3**, **100.00% line + branch** on `token_events.py`; the load-bearing SECURITY tests assert the full client id NEVER hits the on-disk bytes (only the masked form does) and the dataclass / `/db` projection have NO token field. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a real queryable token-events DB table; the secret never reaches it (signature-enforced + masked + allowlist-schema); never crashes a renewal. 🟡 PR-5a is the pure module + recorder — the live wiring (emit `renewed`/`refused` from the keepalive, `saved` from `refresh_live_token`, `expired` from the auth fail-fast latch) + the `/db` read panel are the tracked follow-up (PR-5b); until then the table exists + is correct but is not yet populated by the live token paths. The durable form is Parquet (lake convention), not LMDB. 🚫 no change to the token spine, the rate caps, the ingest spine, or the engine — this slice adds an unused-until-wired module. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001 (the secret's single store this boundary protects) · DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 / DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 (the renew seam PR-5b wires) · DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (#599, the per-window DB table this mirrors for auth) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (no hallucination — the secret never leaks) · §10 · §11 AUTOMATED.

## DEC-PREOPEN-XLSX-DATE-001 (2026-06-09)

601. **DEC-PREOPEN-XLSX-DATE-001 — stamp each pre-open report `.xlsx` zip member with its DATA-date, not the fixed 1980 epoch** (operator report 2026-06-09: "why everywhere it is not using the precise current IST timestamp … the preopen .xlsx shows 1 Jan 1980"). **Why:** the pre-open report download is a `.zip` of one `.xlsx` per year (`render_report_zip`); every member carried a fixed `_ZIP_EPOCH` (`1980-01-01`) `date_time` — chosen for byte-reproducibility (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 7) — so Finder showed every extracted `.xlsx` as "1 Jan 1980", looking broken. **The fix:** stamp each yearly member with the **latest data day it holds** (e.g. `2024-11-28`), and the empty-report member with the `2021-01-01` Track-1 data floor (`_EMPTY_REPORT_DATE`). The date is **derived from the data** (same rows → same date → byte-identical zip), NOT wall-clock `now()`, so the reproducible-bytes contract is fully preserved (asserted: a re-render equals the original blob). The `.xlsx` INTERNAL OOXML parts keep `_ZIP_EPOCH` (invisible to the operator; preserves the per-`.xlsx` byte digest) — only the OUTER zip member dates change. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** `tests/unit/test_preopen_report.py` = **100.00% line + branch** on `preopen_report.py` (Python 3.12.3); new tests assert the yearly member date = its latest data day (never 1980), the empty member = the data floor, and byte-determinism (re-render == blob). `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` clean; full `tests/unit tests/integration tests/property` suite green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the alarming "1 Jan 1980" is gone — each file shows its data-year date, still byte-reproducible. 🟡 the date is the *data* day, not the literal generation time (deliberate — generation time would break reproducibility). 🚫 no change to the engine, the ingest, the report data, or the `.xlsx` content. **Builds on:** CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 7 (reproducible bytes) · the IST-display fix (DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 / DEC-TOKEN-EVENTS-001 surfaces, #561) this completes the "timestamps wrong everywhere" operator report alongside.

### DEC-PREOPEN-XLSX-DATE-001 — AMENDED (2026-06-09)

**Amendment:** the original entry stamped each ``.xlsx`` member with the LATEST
data day (e.g. 2024-12-30) "deliberately, not generation time, to preserve
byte-reproducibility". The operator found that confusing — a file downloaded NOW
should read "Date Modified = now", consistent with the standing "everywhere the
precise current IST timestamp" decree. **Reversed:** each ``.xlsx`` member mtime
is now the **IST generation time** (``datetime.now(IST)``, injectable for tests).
The workbook BODY stays byte-stable for the same data (the internal OOXML parts
keep ``_ZIP_EPOCH``); only the outer member mtime is the clock — so the report
content is still reproducible, just the file's "Date Modified" reads the download
moment. ``_EMPTY_REPORT_DATE`` removed. Verified: ``preopen_report.py`` 100%
line+branch; a live render stamps the member at ``now(IST)`` to the second.

## DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 (2026-06-09)

602. **DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 — a data-driven OPTIONS-ONLY eligibility detector so an options-chain pull can never waste Dhan quota on a non-F&O underlying** **[SUPERSEDED — pull-scope clause only — BY DEC-FUTURES-PULL-ENABLE-001 #871: futures ARE now pulled (DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 #707); the "never pull futures" decree is retired for pull scope, but the OPTIONS-eligibility / OPT-badge detector defined here SURVIVES.]** (operator decree 2026-06-09: "we will NEVER pull futures — only options; if by mistake I select anything other than an F&O index/stock it should NOT let me pull the option chain, else we entirely waste the Dhan API quota"). **The gap:** all 33 admitted indices are shown undifferentiated, but only a handful (NIFTY / BANKNIFTY / FINNIFTY / MIDCPNIFTY / NIFTY NEXT 50 …) have options; the existing `is_option_pullable` (DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001) blocks only `reference_only` (NTM / India VIX), so a non-reference index with NO options (NIFTY 100 / NIFTY AUTO / NIFTY IT …) wrongly passes as pullable → a mis-click burns the 100,000/day quota on options that do not exist. **This PR (foundation slice, model-first / zero-risk):** `build_options_eligible_underlyings(instruments)` in `brutex/universe.py` — the OPTIONS-ONLY sibling of `build_fno_eligible_underlyings`: the `(exchange, underlying_symbol)` set named by an **option** leg (`CE` / `PE` = `OPTIDX` index options + `OPTSTK` stock options), with **`FUT` legs excluded** (the operator's never-futures rule). It is the AUTHORITATIVE set derived from Dhan's own instrument master in the same single pass the F&O scan uses — so it auto-tracks NSE adding/removing an F&O name, NEVER a hardcoded guess (Golden Rule #1). **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** `tests/unit/test_universe.py` 100% line+branch on `universe.py`; tests assert it collects CE/PE underlyings, EXCLUDES a futures-only name, and skips non-options. `ruff` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the precise, data-driven options-eligible set (no hallucination). 🟡 this slice is the pure detector only — it is not yet wired into the guard/UI (the next slice extends `is_option_pullable` to block a non-options index + adds the `/universe` + `/reports` "OPT" badges); until then it is an unused-but-tested function (the model-first pattern, mirroring DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 PR-1). 🚫 no behaviour change yet — the live options-pull path is untouched in this slice. **Builds on:** DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001 (the existing reference-only guard this completes) · `build_fno_eligible_underlyings` (the fut+opt sibling) · CLAUDE.md §6 (the 100,000/day quota this protects) · Golden Rule #1 (data-driven, no hallucination).

603. **DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 (wiring slice) — the OPTIONS-ONLY index guard is now LIVE in the ingest/refresh path** (amends #602; completes the 🟡 "not yet wired" envelope of that entry). **What this slice does:** the detector is moved to the ingest-parse layer (where the lean store discards the option legs — DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 — so eligibility MUST be computed at parse time) and wired into the upsert tagger so a non-options index is persisted `reference_only=TRUE` and is then blocked by the existing `is_option_pullable` (DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001). **Code:** (a) `brutex/adapters/dhan/instruments.py` — two row-level detectors `options_underlying_symbols(rows)` (UPPER-CASED `UNDERLYING_SYMBOL` from `OPTSTK`/`OPTIDX` legs — **`FUT*` deliberately excluded**, stock AND index, NSE+BSE so BSE SENSEX/BANKEX options count) + `options_underlying_security_ids(rows)` (the string-free arm: each option leg's `UNDERLYING_SECURITY_ID`), both surfaced on `UniverseReport` as `options_eligible_symbols` / `options_eligible_security_ids`; (b) `brutex/adapters/dhan/instrument_refresh.py` — `_is_reference` now also tags an admitted **index** `reference_only` when it has NO listed option chain, judged by `_index_has_options` = `security_id ∈ options_eligible_security_ids` **OR** `symbol_name.upper() ∈ options_eligible_symbols` (belt-and-suspenders: an options index must miss BOTH arms to be blocked, so NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX can never be wrongly de-listed even under a vendor id/name skew). The tagger is now supplied on EVERY refresh (was gated on `reference_security_ids`) so the guard always runs; it still applies the India-VIX default internally, so the no-constituents path is otherwise byte-identical. (c) A prominent `instrument_refresh.options_index_guard` structlog line lists the derived option-pullable vs spot-only-blocked index sets on every `make run`, so the operator verifies the data-driven set against reality WITHOUT a master CSV in hand (Golden Rule #1 — the set is whatever the vendor master listed as `OPTIDX` legs today, never a hardcoded guess). **Spot pull + the brute-force ENGINE are UNAFFECTED** — `reference_only` gates ONLY the option-pull route (DEC-ENGINE-ISOLATION-INVARIANT-001). **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** per-module 100% line+branch on BOTH `brutex.adapters.dhan.instruments` (283 stmts / 126 branch) and `brutex.adapters.dhan.instrument_refresh` (51 stmts / 2 branch); new `TestOptionsEligible` (symbol+id arms, futures-excluded, off-exchange/blank/NSETEST-scrip skips, report exposure) + `test_refresh_tags_spot_only_index_reference_only` (NIFTY 100 blocked, NIFTY pullable); `ruff` + `mypy --strict` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the live ingest guard + the verification log. 🟡 the `/universe` + `/reports` "OPT" badge surfacing is the NEXT slice (the data is now on `UniverseReport`; the UI read is not yet wired). 🚫 still no engine change — brute-force isolation invariant holds. **Builds on:** #602 (the detector this wires) · DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001 (the reference-only block it reuses) · DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (why eligibility is computed at parse time) · CLAUDE.md §6 (the 100,000/day quota this protects).

604. **DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 (UI slice) — the OPT vs spot-only badge is now surfaced on BOTH /universe AND /reports** (amends #603; completes the 🟡 "badge surfacing is the NEXT slice" envelope). **Operator ask:** "tag F&O vs spot-only on BOTH /universe AND /reports" so a mis-click on a spot-only underlying is visually obvious before it can waste Dhan quota. **Code:** (a) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — a positive green **OPT** chip (`.chip.opt`), the mutually-exclusive partner of the existing amber **REF** chip (every explorer row is now one or the other), plus a legend key "OPT · option-pullable · F&O"; (b) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` `api_preopen_symbols` — each report symbol now carries an `option_pullable` flag, computed by reusing the SAME store calls + single-source `list_underlyings`/`is_option_pullable` predicate the /universe explorer uses (no duplication — Golden Rule #2); a symbol absent from the underlying universe (a spot-only dataset) defaults to NOT pullable; (c) `brutex/dashboard/templates/reports.html` — a green **OPT** / amber **SPOT** badge per symbol chip, mirroring the explorer. **Pure presentation/data-contract-additive** — no route, engine, or pull-path behaviour change; the badge READS the `reference_only` flag the #603 guard already persists. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** `test_universe_opt_badge_present` (chip + legend), `test_reports_opt_spot_badge_present` (both badge styles + render branch), `test_symbols_tags_option_pullability` (F&O-eligible COALINDIA → `option_pullable=True`; spot-only SPOTONLY → False — exercises BOTH the lookup-hit and the default branch); `ruff` + `mypy --strict` clean; full suite green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the OPT/REF + OPT/SPOT badges on both pages, data-driven from the persisted guard. 🚫 no engine/pull-path change — purely additive UI. **Builds on:** #603 (the persisted guard this reads) · DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001 · DEC-DASHBOARD-UNIVERSE-UX-001 (the REF chip this mirrors) · CLAUDE.md §6 (the quota the badge protects).

605. **DEC-DASHBOARD-QUOTA-GAUGE-001 — the Dhan daily API-quota (100,000/day) is now VISIBLE as a live gauge on /universe** (operator ask 2026-06-09: "why nowhere I can see whether it hit the daily limit quota or not bro?"). **The gap:** the `DailyQuotaTracker` (`brutex/orchestrator/quota_tracker.py`, IST-midnight reset, `~/.brutex/quota/quota.lmdb`) already COUNTS every paced Dhan call and its used/remaining/limit already flowed onto the in-memory `RateLimitPanel` (`quota_used`/`quota_remaining`/`quota_limit`, surfaced by the O(1) `/api/v1/rate` route) — but **no served page rendered it** (the legacy `_INDEX_HTML_TEMPLATE` rate panel that carried `rl-rps` is dead code, never wired to a route; the served `/` is the v29 strategy report, which has no ops panel). So the operator genuinely could not see the budget. **This slice (UI-only, zero new plumbing):** `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — a compact header **quota gauge** (used / limit · remaining · pct + a colour bar) that polls the EXISTING `/api/v1/rate` every 3 s and renders the panel's quota fields; **green < 80 %, amber ≥ 80 %, red ≥ 95 %** so "did I hit the daily limit?" reads at a glance. Placed on /universe — the ops page where the operator triggers the quota-consuming pulls. `quota_limit <= 0` (no usage reported yet) keeps the gauge HIDDEN rather than show a fake 0. **No new endpoint, no LMDB read on page load, no data-contract change** — it reads the same in-memory panel the rate route already exposes. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** `test_universe_daily_quota_gauge_present` (markup + 80/95 colour bands + the `/api/v1/rate` poll + the crit branch); the quota data-plane (`quota_used`/`quota_remaining`/`quota_limit` flowing controller→panel) is already covered by `test_dashboard_rate_panel.py`; `ruff` + `mypy --strict` clean; full suite green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the live gauge on /universe, fed by the already-wired panel quota fields. 🟡 the gauge lights up once a pull reports usage in THIS session (the moment quota is consumed) — showing today's PERSISTED count BEFORE any session pull would need a dedicated tracker-read endpoint (a tracked follow-up; deliberately out of scope to avoid changing the rate-panel default contract its tests pin). 🚫 no engine/pull-path change — purely additive UI. **Builds on:** DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 (the persisted tracker the dashboard already wires) · DEC-DASHBOARD-RATE-PANEL-001 (the `/api/v1/rate` panel this reads) · DEC-DASHBOARD-RPS1S-PANEL-001 (the gauge-render pattern this mirrors) · CLAUDE.md §6 (the 100,000/day quota this makes visible).

606. **DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-GAP-COUNT-001 — a Dhan DH-905 no-data boundary is now counted as a "no-data gap", NOT a "failure", in the live pull progress** (operator observed: a single benign DH-905 — NIFTY NEXT 50's daily history starts after 2021-01-01 — showed as a scary "1 failed" in the live stats even though it is an EXPECTED empty range that is re-tried next pull, never masked). **Root cause:** `run_ingest.py` emitted the same `on_progress(label, 0, failed=True)` tick for EVERY terminal `DhanError` — a real auth/4xx failure AND a benign DH-905 gap — so the live `failed` counter conflated the two. (The known-gap was already logged as INFO `ingest.known_gap` per DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001, but the live UI counter still read it as a failure.) **Fix (a 4th `gap` flag threaded end-to-end):** the pull `ProgressHook` becomes `(label, bars, failed, gap)`; a DH-905 (`is_no_data_error`) now emits `failed=False, gap=True`, every other terminal error stays `failed=True, gap=False`. Threaded through all emit/consume sites: `run_ingest.py` (spot emit + type), `option_universe_ingest.py` (options emit + type — options rollup not yet split, emits `gap=False`, a noted follow-up, no regression), `pull_jobs.py` `_on_progress` + type, `pull_controller.py` ×2 `_progress_then_flush` proxies, `orchestrator/watchdog.py` `progress_hook` (a `gap=True` tick is IGNORED — neither failure nor success — so a recurring known gap can't trip the retry-storm give-up), and `cli.py`'s return type. `PullProgress`/`ProgressSnapshot` gain a `gaps` counter + `to_dict` key; `/universe`'s live stats render a distinct amber **"no-data gaps"** stat + status-line note (NOT red — it is not a failure). **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** per-module 100% line+branch held on `brutex.dashboard.pull_progress` (82 stmts), `brutex.dashboard.pull_jobs` (50 stmts), `brutex.adapters.dhan.run_ingest` (140 stmts); new tests — `PullProgress` gap-vs-failure split, `BackgroundPullJob` gap tick, `run_ingest` 3-branch `(success/failure/gap)` emit, watchdog gap-ignored, `/universe` gap-stat guard; existing options-ingest + watchdog hook tests updated to the 4-arg signature; `ruff` + `mypy --strict` clean; full suite green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ DH-905 spot gaps now count as `gaps`, not `failed`, end-to-end + surfaced distinctly in the live UI; the recurring-gap false retry-storm alert is also fixed. 🟡 the OPTIONS fan-out rollup does not yet split gap from failure (emits `gap=False`) — a tracked follow-up; no regression (options gaps still count as failed exactly as before). 🚫 no change to what is fetched/stored — purely a classification + display fix. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 (the INFO known-gap log this completes for the live counter) · DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-TRACKER-001 (the hook this extends) · DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (the watchdog whose gap handling this corrects).

607. **DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-GAP-COUNT-001 (options arm) — the OPTIONS fan-out now splits a benign DH-905 from a real failure too** (completes the 🟡 follow-up of #606). **What this slice does:** mirrors the spot gap classification inside `option_universe_ingest.py`'s per-series fan-out. A series that raises a Dhan `DH-905` (`is_no_data_error`) is now logged INFO `ingest.known_gap` + flags a new `_UnderlyingResult.any_gap` (instead of WARNING `ingest.quarantine` + `any_failed`); the series is STILL recorded (re-tried next pull, never masked) and STILL counted in the `quarantined` rollup, so `series_failed` is unchanged. The per-underlying live emit becomes `on_progress(sid, bars, any_failed, any_gap and not any_failed)` — `failed` and `gap` are mutually exclusive on the one unit, so an underlying with ANY real failure reads as failed, while one whose only empty series were DH-905 reads as a **no-data gap**. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** per-module 100% line+branch held on `brutex.adapters.dhan.option_universe_ingest` (134 stmts / 32 branch); new `_NoDataClient` + `test_on_progress_flags_no_data_gap_underlying` (gap=True, failed=False, series still recorded); `ruff` + `mypy --strict` clean; full suite green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ options DH-905 gaps now count as `gaps`, not `failed`, matching the spot path end-to-end — the #606 🟡 follow-up is now closed. 🚫 no change to what is fetched/stored — a classification + display fix, the DH-905 series is still recorded + re-tried. **Builds on:** #606 (the spot arm + the `gap` hook flag this completes) · DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 (the INFO known-gap log it reuses).

608. **DEC-DASHBOARD-QUOTA-PERSISTED-001 — the /universe quota gauge now shows today's PERSISTED usage on page-load, before any pull** (completes the 🟡 follow-up of #605). **The gap:** #605's gauge polled `/api/v1/rate`, whose `quota_*` fields are only populated once a pull pushes a snapshot onto the in-memory `RateLimitPanel` — so on a fresh `/universe` load (before clicking any pull) the gauge stayed hidden even though today's count is already persisted in `~/.brutex/quota/quota.lmdb`. **Fix:** a dedicated read-only `GET /api/v1/quota` endpoint (`brutex/dashboard/app.py`) that reads the IST-midnight `DailyQuotaTracker` directly (`current_count()` / `daily_limit` / `remaining()` — one O(1) LMDB read, no lake/lock) and returns `{quota_used, quota_limit, quota_remaining}`; the `/universe` `pollQuota()` JS now polls THIS endpoint instead of `/api/v1/rate`. The tracker is **injectable** via a new `build_app(..., quota_tracker=...)` param (default: a real tracker built lazily on first poll, so importing/constructing the app never touches LMDB) — tests drive a deterministic duck-typed fake. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** `TestQuotaRoute.test_quota_route_reads_injected_tracker` (used/limit/remaining JSON from an injected `_FakeQuotaTracker`); `test_universe_daily_quota_gauge_present` updated to assert the `/api/v1/quota` poll; `ruff` + `mypy --strict` + **`pyright`** clean on the changed files; full suite green. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the gauge now shows today's persisted budget the instant `/universe` loads — the #605 🟡 follow-up is closed. 🚫 no engine/pull-path/data change — an additive read-only endpoint + a one-line poll-URL swap. **Builds on:** #605 (the gauge this completes) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 (the persisted `DailyQuotaTracker` it reads) · CLAUDE.md §6 (the 100,000/day quota it makes visible).

611. **DEC-QUOTA-ENV-SINGLE-OPEN-001 — one LMDB quota environment per path per PROCESS (ref-counted), ending the live `/api/v1/quota` 500 storm** (2026-06-10, operator-uploaded `brutex.log`: 82 × `Exception in ASGI application` — every 3 s gauge poll raised `lmdb.Error: The environment '~/.brutex/quota/quota.lmdb' is already open in this process`; `GET /api/v1/quota` returned 500 on EVERY call from first poll 02:46:37Z, ZERO 200s ever in a live process). **Root cause (field-measured):** LMDB forbids opening one environment twice per process. The live dashboard process holds TWO `DailyQuotaTracker()` construction sites on the SAME default path: the pull controller's (`pull_controller.py:801`, DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001) and the `/api/v1/quota` route's lazy default (`app.py:841`, DEC-DASHBOARD-QUOTA-PERSISTED-001 #608). Whichever constructs SECOND raises — in the operator's run the pull side won, so the gauge 500'd forever; in the REVERSE order (gauge polled before any pull) the FIRST PULL would have crashed instead. Tests never caught it because they inject a duck-typed fake tracker, so the lazy real-construction path never ran in a process already holding the env. **Fix (`brutex/orchestrator/quota_tracker.py`):** (a) a process-wide REF-COUNTED env registry `_ENV_REGISTRY` (resolved-path → (env, refs)) behind `_open_shared_env`/`_release_shared_env` — every tracker on one path shares ONE cached `lmdb.Environment`; this is deliberate module-level state mirroring LMDB's own per-process uniqueness constraint (the narrow documented exception to CLAUDE.md §4 "no global mutable state"); first opener's `map_size_bytes` wins (identical default everywhere). (b) `close()` becomes a per-instance idempotent REFERENCE RELEASE — the env closes only when the LAST holder releases, so the gauge closing its tracker can never yank the env from under a live pull. (c) `acquire_or_raise` now does read+check+put inside ONE LMDB WRITE TXN (was: separate read txn then write txn — safe only while the crash enforced single-instance): write txns are exclusive per env, so counting is linearizable ACROSS instances — no lost update; a raise inside the block aborts before any write; the now-redundant `_write_state` helper is deleted. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run, Python 3.12.3):** new `tests/unit/test_bugfix_quota_env_share.py` (6 regression tests, each raised `lmdb.Error` pre-fix): same-path share + cross-instance visibility; 2×200 concurrent increments across two instances → exact 400 (linearizability); ref-counted close (gauge close leaves pull live; last close + reopen preserves count); idempotent double-close; distinct paths stay independent; and the END-TO-END production replay — `Path.home` → tmp, pull-side `DailyQuotaTracker()` opened FIRST with 3 acquires, `build_app(quota_tracker=None)`, real `GET /api/v1/quota` → **200** with used=3 (pre-fix: the lmdb.Error 500). Targeted suites green: quota_tracker + dhan_rate_control + orchestrator_rate_limiter + dashboard_rate_panel + the new file = **121 passed**; `ruff` + `ruff format` clean; `mypy --strict` 0 issues; `pyright` 0 errors on the changed files. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the gauge endpoint and the pull path can no longer kill each other — both construction orders proven; ✅ cross-instance increment linearizability is now structural (single write txn), not an accident of the crash; 🟡 two tracker INSTANCES still keep separate `_fired_today` threshold-alert sets — alerts fire from the incrementing (pull) instance only, so no duplicate alerts today, but a future second INCREMENTING instance could re-fire a threshold once (tracked follow-up; the single-writer pattern holds in production); 🚫 no API/data-contract change — `/api/v1/quota` payload, the LMDB schema, and the IST-midnight reset are byte-identical. **Builds on:** DEC-DASHBOARD-QUOTA-PERSISTED-001 (#608, the lazy route tracker) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 (the pull-side tracker) · DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the durable-ops discipline this continues).

612. **DEC-AUTOMERGE-CLEAN-STRICT-001 — the auto-merge `mergeable_state` allowance is now the charter's DOCUMENTED pre-G2 denylist envelope (strict `clean` = the G2-gated ratchet), and the F-4 hostile review's run-log mining found + FIXED three latent gate bugs (the in-flight-CI existence hole, the null field-shift refusal, the dead manual hatch)** (2026-06-10; executes follow-up F-4 of DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-002 #609). **The drift (G1 residual):** `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` refused `dirty`/`behind`/`blocked`/`unknown` but tolerated `unstable`/`has_hooks` (DEC-AUTOMERGE-SAFETY-001) while `docs/MERGE_READINESS_GUARANTEE.md` §4.5, CLAUDE.md §13(a), and the PR-template banner demanded strict `mergeable_state == clean`. **Evidence (REAL GitHub run logs; decisive for AMEND over TIGHTEN):** 2026-06-03→06-10 sample — 1,230 auto-merge runs listed, 30 mergeable-gate executions log-verified: `unstable` 21, including EVERY `ready_for_review`-path merge (that path's own `Auto-merge on green CI` check run structurally ALWAYS pends on the PR head while the gate evaluates — e.g. PR #572 run 27248690518 — so it can NEVER observe `clean`); `clean` only 4 of 18 verified merges (all `workflow_run`-path, e.g. #567 run 27216794460); `dirty`/`behind`/`blocked`/`has_hooks` NEVER observed. (2) **null field-shift** — an uncomputed `mergeable: null` rendered as an EMPTY first TSV field; `read -r` stripped the leading tab and shifted `mergeable_state`'s "unknown" into `${mergeable}`, so the poll loop broke on attempt 1 and refused instantly ("refusing to merge over a conflict"), leaving the DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-FIX-001 null-deferral DEAD CODE — every sampled refusal carries the `mergeable=unknown mergeable_state=` signature (runs 26870881771 / 27009685623 / 27064096938 / 27093267053); the jq now defaults both fields to the string "null" (locally reproduced: OLD parse `mergeable='unknown' state=''` → FIXED `mergeable='null' state='unknown'`). (3) **dead manual hatch** — the `workflow_dispatch` path emitted ONLY `pr_number`, so trust-check read empty AUTHOR/HEAD_REF/IS_DRAFT and ALWAYS fell through to `trusted=false` (zero dispatch runs exist in the entire run history); the MANUAL_PR branch now resolves author/headRefName/isDraft and passes the SAME trust + all-green + mergeability gates. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** 6 new redteam meta-tests (`unknown` pinned in the refusal pattern; ## DEC-MEMLEAK-GATE-001 (2026-06-10)

616. **DEC-MEMLEAK-GATE-001 — memory-leak stress gate: tracemalloc growth ceilings proving the 4 long-haul hot-state holders (audit-chain writer / WindowLedger / results-store append / Dhan rate controller) hold O(1)-bounded memory over ≥100K sustained events** (2026-06-10, operator: "build the memory-leak test harness … tracemalloc/RSS-growth assertions … no unbounded growth; assert peak-delta ceilings with honest headroom"). **The gap:** the stress suite (DEC-STRESS-001 #208) proves *invariants* under load (chain integrity, budget bounds, resume convergence) but nothing proved bounded *memory* — the first RSS assertion was removed in PR #99 as flaky (documented at `tests/stress/test_audit_chain_sustained.py` "Note on memory profiling": platform-dependent `ru_maxrss` units, process-wide peak pollution, GHA jitter) and memory profiling was deferred to "a dedicated follow-up" that never landed. A slow per-event leak in a path that runs for hours/days (ingest audit appends, re-pull ledger churn, sweep result batches, the rate governor) would reach production unseen. **What shipped (test-only; ZERO `brutex/` and ZERO workflow changes):** `tests/stress/test_memory_growth.py` — 4 gates on the measured recipe *untracked warmup → tracemalloc tracked working-set turnover → gc baseline (+snapshot for on-breach diagnostics) → ≥100K sustained events → gc → assert net ≤ ceiling AND peak-delta ≤ ceiling*; RSS (`/proc/self/status` VmRSS delta, Linux-only, skipped on macOS) is printed always and asserted only against a generous 192 MiB native-leak backstop — exactly the demotion that dissolves the PR-#99 objections (tracemalloc is the deterministic primary; RSS is observability + native backstop). Event loops are production-faithful: the ledger gate runs probe-first pull cycles over a FIXED 512-window universe partitioned 128 settled-SUCCESS / 64 settled-DH-905 / 320 perpetual-churn (`FAILED→EMPTY→EMPTY` — a FAILED resets `empty_streak`, so churn windows can never settle and `record()` keeps firing forever, mirroring the real re-pull); the results gate RE-CONSTRUCTS an identical `ResultRow` every event (full validation + `condition_names` derivation) and requires the documented idempotent-no-op `False`; the controller gate drives full deterministic ladder cycles (100-hit 429 storm → soft floor → STORM_HITS rungs to the deep floor → 10 timeout stalls → recovery, asserting `current_rps == CEILING_RPS` at every 4_000-event block boundary and window×rate deque bounds even pinned at the floor) on a pure-read fake clock advanced only by `sleep`. Knob: explicit `STRESS_MEMLEAK_EVENTS` wins, else `max(100_000, STRESS_EVENTS)` — no CI default can silently weaken the ≥100K proof, and the EXISTING `stress-nightly.yml` `stress_events` dispatch input scales the soak up with no workflow edit. **REAL numbers (this container, CPython 3.12.3, N=100_000):** `4 passed in 44.04s` (audit 19.7 s / ledger 1.5 s / results 19.0 s / controller 2.9 s); net deltas **−88 B / −88 B / −88 B / +8–13 KB** (run-to-run byte-identical for the first three; controller ±15% one-time noise), peaks +17.9 KB / +1.7 KB / +4.1 KB / +30-35 KB, RSS deltas 0–104 KiB; ceilings 64 KiB net (tests 1-3, ≥5000× headroom) / 256 KiB net (controller, ≥20×) / 1 MiB peak (≥30×); N-independence probed at 1M events (controller net **+7.9 KB** — lower than at 100K, one-time not per-event); leak-detection validated empirically (injected 95 B/event leak → +9.50 MB at 100K, exactly linear — the gate detects what it claims). **4-agent hostile review (pre-code):** folded in the probe-first ledger redesign (record-on-settled would un-settle SKIPPED rows — not a production path), the deterministic ladder-recovery assertion, the `max(100K, STRESS_EVENTS)` knob contract, the snapshot-before-baseline self-pollution fix, and the measured environment constraints (stdlib `logging` records ≥ WARNING retained by pytest at ~1 KB/record — the controller's structlog→PrintLogger path measured clean at +32 B/8K emissions; `--capture=sys` turns captured output into tracked heap — CI's default fd capture measured +32 B/8K lines); Agent 1's claimed `_pending_events` latent leak was RE-VERIFIED against `rate_limiter.py` and REFUTED (`set_rate` keeps `initial_rps == _current_rps`, so the `_maybe_upshift_locked` isclose early-return always fires in controller usage — the list stays empty). **Finding: NO REAL LEAK** — all four paths measured flat, so the "STOP and report before fixing" branch of the mandate was not triggered. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the ≥100K proof runs by default (nightly + the per-push property-job stress step, +~44 s container / plausibly 2-3× on shared GHA); 🟡 O(distinct-keys) growth in ledger/store is BY DESIGN out of scope (in-memory indexes; store sized for 10²-10⁴ finalists); 🟡 tracemalloc is blind to native allocations — blake3/fastbloom/LMDB/`DailyQuotaTracker` (excluded via the documented `quota_tracker=None` mode), `flush()`/`load()` O(rows) paths, fd-reopen lifecycle, and multi-threaded contention growth are covered only by the generous RSS backstop or not at all (stated in the module docstring); 🟡 a 10M soak ≈ 25+ min for the audit gate alone — raise the stress workflow `timeout-minutes` before dispatching one; 🚫 no live Dhan calls. **Builds on:** DEC-STRESS-001 (#208) · DEC-GROWW-CATALOG-DRIVER-001 (wired `tests/stress` into the per-push property job) · DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 · DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 · DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001 / DEC-DHAN-RATE-SINGLE-BUCKET-001 · CLAUDE.md §9 (4-agent hostile review) / §10 / §12.

621. **DEC-DAILY-CANDLE-CLAMP-001 — unsettled CURRENT-DAY data is never requested: the 1-day bound clamps to today (exclusive) and the 1-minute bound includes today only from the 15:30 IST close** (2026-06-10, operator rule + live evidence: the window ledger showed a same-evening `1day 2026-06-09→2026-06-10` request rejected `DhanBadRequestError` — Dhan publishes the current day's daily candle only the NEXT day, so the request burned a quota hit to learn a known fact; and a mid-session 1-minute pull of today would settle a PARTIAL day as ledger SUCCESS, which the skip rule would then never re-fetch). **Fix:** pure clock-injected `clamp_window_end(interval, end, *, now_ist)` in `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py` — daily: `min(end, today_IST)` (end-exclusive ⇒ the last requested candle is yesterday's); 1-minute: `min(end, today+1)` from 15:30 IST else `min(end, today)` — applied at the SINGLE window-planning site in `ingest_spot` (every caller covered: UI pulls, CLI, retries), with an `ingest.window.clamped` INFO line and a clean zero-window report when the clamp empties the range (zero Dhan hits). `ingest_spot` gains an injectable `now_ist` clock seam (production default = real IST). **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** 7 new tests (all four clamp branches; clamp-to-empty → `windows=0` and no sink writes; clamped-but-nonempty still pulls; default-clock no-op on past ranges); ingest gate **64 passed, 100.00% line+branch**. **Honest envelope:** ✅ a by-mistake "to = today" selection can no longer 400 on daily nor half-fill a 1-minute day; ✅ the operator's stated Dhan publication rule is the cited source (verified 2026-06-10 against the live ledger row); 🟡 15:30 IST is the close boundary used — a special session (Muhurat) closing later is unhandled (the clamp errs to EXCLUDE, never to fetch-partial); 🚫 no change to window tiling, ledger semantics, or the engine. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the skip rule the partial-day hazard would have poisoned) · DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 (the known-gap sibling) · CLAUDE.md §6/§7.

625. **DEC-OPTIONS-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 — the OPTIONS pull gains spot-grade window-guarantee parity: AuthGuard fail-fast latch (trip-at-source + fan-out short-circuit), re-pull-until-clean auto-resume over the SHARED window ledger, the daily-quota brake with a mid-round `DailyQuotaExceeded` → `quota_exhausted` mapping and a `finally`-guaranteed + throttled-mid-pull ledger persist, honest aborted/skipped series accounting, and the loud PullVerdict banner** (2026-06-10, operator decree: "literally precise guarantee like spot — nowhere the window should be failed; even in the worst case it should auto retry until it fetches the successful response"). **The verified gap (audit before code, Golden Rule #9 — 1-agent hostile review, verdict IMPLEMENTABLE-WITH-CONDITIONS, 12 findings):** spot had 4 escalating layers (in-call fast-retry → in-run window retry → post-pull auto-retry rounds → until-clean auto-resume, plus AuthGuard + quota brake + verdict banner); options had only the first two — `pull_options` ran ONE pass, an aborted series waited for a manual re-click, a dead token would burn one paced call per remaining series of a 16k-series fan-out, a mid-round quota death escaped as a generic job error BEFORE `end_pull_ledger` (hours of settled-window records lost — the ledger was persisted ONLY at pull end), and options pulls never stamped the verdict banner. **Fix (reuse, no new loop logic — §11 COMMON):** (1) `run_dhan_options_ingest` builds ONE shared `AuthGuard`; `ingest_rolling_option_series` trips it AT THE SOURCE on `is_auth_failure` (closing the pool-width doomed-call window — hostile finding 3) and every not-yet-dispatched series short-circuits to a distinct AUTH-SKIP (never folded into completed/aborted/residual — finding 6); ONE loud `ingest.auth_aborted` alert, later auth failures silent (the spot drain pattern). (2) `OptionsUniverseReport` gains `auth_aborted`/`auth_cause`/`series_skipped_auth` + `still_failed_windows`/`aborted_series`/`no_data_series`/`real_failed_series`; an ABORTED all-or-nothing series is now counted aborted, never completed (finding 6) — per-symbol rollups likewise. (3) `pull_options(until_clean=True)` drives the EXISTING `run_until_clean` (bounded `AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS`=50, quota hook between rounds) with **`stop_when_stuck` OFF** — an aborted series settles NOTHING, so its residual is CONSTANT across failing rounds and the shrinkage heuristic would falsely kill the canonical 429-storm recovery after ~2 rounds (finding 1, the review's BLOCKER); worst case is quantified instead: `rounds × residual × (1 + in-run retries)` paced calls, every one ≤ 5 r/s bucket-bounded + quota-braked (Rule #6/#10). (4) Durability (finding 2): a throttled `make_live_ledger_flush` fires on every series tick (a crash loses ≤ the throttle interval of window records; bars were already durable per-series), `end_pull_ledger` moved into `finally`, and a mid-round `DailyQuotaExceeded` (raised by the pace bucket inside a worker, a non-Dhan exception) is caught at the `pull_options` layer and mapped to the `quota_exhausted` verdict — committed work kept, resume after IST midnight. (5) `OptionsPullReport` carries the final residual/auth/quota state + `rounds_run` and a `verdict` property via the SAME `classify_pull` — built from the REPORT, never `UntilCleanOutcome.pull_verdict()` which zeroes the failure counts (finding 5); the dashboard options `_work` stamps it into the SAME `_last_pull_verdict` banner slot as spot and passes `until_clean=True`. **Operator's "out-of-scenario" probe answered (the #621 current-day class):** verified N/A for options BY CONSTRUCTION — `pull_options` resolves its range via `resolve_candle_range(to_date=None)` whose default upper bound is the PREVIOUS day (`pull_controller.py:127-154`), so an options pull never requests the in-progress session at all; the spot clamp class cannot recur here. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** 8 new regressions in `tests/unit/test_option_until_clean.py` (trip-at-source 1-call short-circuit proof; alert-fires-once under a 2-worker `threading.Barrier` race; aborted-is-never-completed; DH-905 gap-vs-failure split; round-2 re-fetches ONLY the residual — call-count proof 6×1+3+1 over the shared ledger; mid-round quota death → `quota_exhausted` verdict + ledger Parquet present; token death → `stop_dead`, zero inter-round sleeps, every series accounted quarantined-or-skipped; dry-run until-clean = one clean round + `to_dict` contract); touched-module gate **100.00% line+branch** (option_ingest 119/28, option_universe_ingest 168/42, option_pull_controller 166/22); full suite **5231 unit + 341 integration green**; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` 0 on touched files. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ every TRANSIENT failure (429/timeout/5xx) is now auto-retried across in-run passes AND bounded auto-resume rounds until the ledger is clean, with nothing ever silently lost (an unsettled window is always re-fetched); ✅ the four honest stop states are loud, not silent — token death (re-auth), daily quota (IST-midnight resume), Dhan-has-no-data (settled known gap), bounded budget; 🟡 a quarantined DH-905 dead series drains ONE window per PULL (the per-window settle precedes the series quarantine) and reads `clean`/`known_gap_only` meanwhile — acceptable known limitation;
