634. **DEC-OPTION-DH905-CONTINUE-001 — a DH-905 option cursor settles SKIPPED and the series CONTINUES: a fully-dead series drains in ONE paced pass (was ~67 pulls), with the all-or-nothing transient invariant preserved EXACTLY and auth outranking no-data** (2026-06-10; renumbered #629→#632→#633→#634 per the P-1 parallel rule — #629–#633 were claimed on main by PRs #589–#592 + #594 while this PR was in flight, the ID not the number being authoritative; executes the tracked follow-up from DEC-OPTIONS-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 #625 hostile finding 4 — this entry SUPERSEDES the `DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001` Stage-c2 settle-then-quarantine semantics). **The defect:** a Dhan DH-905 "no data" on ONE cursor settled that single window as a known gap then re-raised, quarantining the WHOLE series — so a fully-dead series (e.g. a far weekly expiry code that never listed; the [2021-01-01, today] range is ~67 thirty-day windows) drained ONE window per pull, needed ~67 paced pulls to settle, and read `clean`/`known_gap_only` meanwhile. **Hostile review BEFORE code (Golden Rule #9, 1-agent):** verdict IMPLEMENTABLE-WITH-CONDITIONS, 9 findings; the BLOCKER (finding 1): `is_no_data_error` and `is_auth_failure` are NOT disjoint — a token-death 400 carrying BOTH markers (DH-906 + DH-905) would, under continue, mass-settle real windows SKIPPED forever on a dead token (today's re-raise capped damage at one window; CONTINUE is what weaponizes it). **Fix:** (1) `option_ingest` Phase-1: a cursor failing `is_no_data_error(exc) and not is_auth_failure(exc)` settles `SKIPPED` (reason = truncated `str(exc)` so the browsable ledger row self-explains — finding 5) and CONTINUES as a 0-bar known-gap cursor; AUTH OUTRANKS NO-DATA — a both-marker 400 re-raises un-settled (latch tripped at source); any other terminal error re-raises unchanged. The settle lands mid-Phase-1 exactly where the old settle-before-raise did — ledger state only, never bars, surviving a later abort (strictly more forward progress). (2) `OptionIngestReport.no_data_windows` (threaded into BOTH return sites + the `ingest.series`/`ingest.series.aborted` events — finding 4); the abort residual becomes `windows − skipped − no_data` (settled gaps are vendor answers, never failures; `transient_failures == still_failed_windows` preserved); a continued-with-gaps series is COMPLETE. (3) `option_universe_ingest`: drain reordered AUTH-FIRST (finding 1); the kept DH-905 drain branch is DEFENSIVE-ONLY (no production arrival path — fake-runner tested + disclosed, finding 8); gap-only series (complete ∧ 0 bars ∧ ≥1 gap window) keep the per-series INFO `ingest.known_gap` + the per-underlying `series_gap_only` rollup field; new `no_data_windows`/`gap_only_series` report properties; `no_data_series` now excludes both-marker auth deaths via the NEW string-twin `errors.is_auth_failure_message` (the auth analog of `is_no_data_message`, same `_TOKEN_INVALID_MARKERS` source — §11 COMMON). (4) Verdict interplay (`option_pull_controller`): `OptionSymbolResult.series_gap_only` + `OptionsPullReport.gap_only_series`; `verdict` passes `no_data = no_data_series + gap_only_series` and `completed = total_series_completed − gap_only_series` (never negative — gap-only ⊆ complete), so an ALL-dead pull reads `known_gap_only` ("Dhan has no data"), never a lying `clean`, and any real first-pass bars keep it `clean`. Until-clean: a dead series's residual is 0 after round 1 → `stop_clean` in ONE round; a mixed gap+429-storm series settles its gaps in round 1 and rounds 2+ re-fetch ONLY the transient residual (the gap windows skip O(1) off the ledger). **Rule #6/#10 universe-scale envelope (finding 3):** per-series cost is `windows` paced calls ONCE (lifetime calls IDENTICAL to the status quo — front-loaded into one pull instead of ~67); universe-scale worst case: one dead weekly code across the 3 indices = 21 strikes × 2 types × 3 = 126 series × ~67 windows ≈ **8.4k paced calls (~28 min at 5 r/s)**; four dead codes ≈ **33.8k ≈ ~34% of the 100k/day quota in ONE pull** — every call ≤ 5 r/s bucket-bounded, the quota brake fires mid-round, and settles made before a quota death persist via the throttled flush + `finally` persist (regression-tested: quota-death-preserves-settles + skip-after-reset). **Mass-settle amplification disclosed (finding 2):** Dhan's DH-905 conflates "incorrect parameters" with "no data" (`errors.py:83-88`), so a systematic request bug (the DEC-OPTION-SECURITY-ID-FIX-001 class) can now poison every fetched window in ONE pull (~67× faster than the old one-window-per-pull drip) — recovery is the NEW verified runbook `docs/runbooks/option-ledger-gap-unsettle.md` (scoped ledger surgery via the public `to_rows`/`from_rows` round-trip; snippet REAL-run tested), and the failure is LOUD (gap-only verdict + INFO logs + `last_error` carries the vendor message), never silent. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run, Python 3.12.3):** per-module gates **100.00% line+branch** — option_ingest **127/30** (its dedicated `tests/unit/test_dhan_option_ingest.py`: settle-and-continue, one-pass drain + O(1) re-pull skip, mixed commit+settle, gap-then-transient-abort keeps the gap settled + excludes it from the residual, BOTH-MARKER-is-auth-not-gap, ledger-less continue, known-gap log nook), option_universe_ingest **187/46** (gap-only INFO + rollup, defensive drain branch via fake runner, drain auth-outranks-no-data), option_pull_controller **169/22** (all-gap-only → `known_gap_only`, mixed → `clean`, dead-universe until-clean drains in ONE round = 7 calls/7 series/0 sleeps), errors **45/16** (`is_auth_failure_message` incl. the both-marker blocker case); NEW Hypothesis property `tests/property/test_dhan_option_dh905_continue_properties.py` pins the window partition over randomized gap/transient/success/pre-settled interleavings (`windows == skipped + no_data + committed` ∕ `+ still_failed`, gap-never-in-sink, abort-commits-nothing, pre-settled-never-calls — finding 4); full unit suite green; `ruff` + `ruff format` clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` 0 errors on touched files. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a dead series drains in ONE paced pass and is never re-fetched; ✅ the all-or-nothing commit invariant for TRANSIENT failures is byte-for-byte intact (gap settles write ledger state only, never bars); ✅ auth outranks no-data at BOTH the spine settle and the drain; 🟡 the verdict's `completed` is FIRST-pass-sourced (the pre-existing spot until-clean contract), so a pass-0-aborted series whose bars land in round 2 still reads `known_gap_only` when only dead series coexist — this misclassification EXISTS TODAY (verified) and is not widened here (finding 6); 🟡 per-symbol SEMANTIC CHANGE disclosed: a dead underlying now reads `series_completed=N, series_gap_only=N, bars=0` instead of `series_failed=N` (finding 5) — honest (it IS settled) but dashboards keying on `series_failed` for dead underlyings see 0; 🟡 the SHOULD-grade pass-level mass-settle circuit breaker (refuse settles when 100% of fetched windows universe-wide are DH-905) is NOT implemented — tracked follow-up; the runbook + loud verdict are the recovery surface meanwhile; 🟡 the SPOT twin (`ingest.py` settles-then-raises with the same both-marker inversion, damage capped at ONE window per pull by the re-raise) is NOT fixed here — tracked follow-up (findings 1/7; options-scoped PR per Golden Rule #3); 🟡 mid-series settles are memory-only until the next throttled flush (a crash loses ≤ the throttle interval — the #625 finding-2 envelope; re-answered next pull, nothing lost); 🚫 no Rule-#5 CI hot path touched (the settle is O(1) per window; no O(1)-total claim); 🚫 the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED (options stay LAKE-only/REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063). **Builds on:** DEC-OPTIONS-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 #625 (the follow-up this executes + the until-clean loop this completes) · DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the settle/skip authority; Stage-c2 semantics superseded) · DEC-OPTION-429-RECOVERY-001 (the all-or-nothing invariant preserved exactly) · DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 #597 (the original known-gap settle) · DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-GAP-COUNT-001 (gap-not-failure classification) · DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 (the latch auth-outranks-no-data protects) · DEC-OPTION-SECURITY-ID-FIX-001 (the param-bug class the runbook recovers from) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1/#3/#6/#9/#10 + §11 COMMON.

the EXHAUSTIVE `denormalize(normalize(p)) == p` round-trip over all 90 Mode-A grid points; the documented round-half-to-even tie pinned on an exact-binary axis; the condition-3 proof that `canonicalise_params` over denormalized output emits int literals only; 629. **DEC-WINDOW-OPTION-DECODE-001 — /coverage/windows shows OPTION windows PRECISELY: the dhan-option ledger rows decode to the operator's coordinates (`BANKNIFTY · NSE_FNO` / `WEEK#1 ATM+3 CALL · 1m`) instead of the raw folded vendor key (`25|NSE_FNO` / `OPT|WEEK|1|ATM+3|CALL`), and the page gains an All/Spot/Options market filter so option rows are findable above 20k+ spot rows** (2026-06-10, operator's live make-run + screenshots: a 3-index options pull in flight — notably running the just-merged #586 until-clean loop, `until_clean=True` visible in the live log — while /coverage/windows showed only 360ONE spot rows; "why is the precise options pull chain not showing the windows precisely?"). **Diagnosis (two stacked causes, both verified):** (1) TIMING — an option series commits ALL its windows at once (the all-or-nothing invariant, DEC-OPTION-429-RECOVERY-001), so ~2 minutes / ~350 calls into a pull of 67-window series ZERO series had committed → zero option rows existed yet (by design, now explained in the page's empty-state copy); (2) PRECISION — when option rows DO land, `_window_row` rendered `record.security_id`/`record.interval` VERBATIM, i.e. the coverage key's folded coordinates (`option_ingest._coverage_key`: id+segment, `OPT|flag|code|strike|type`), and the ledger's sorted record order puts `dhan-option` rows AFTER every `dhan` spot row — vendor ids, bottom of a 20k-row table. **Fix (display-only, data untouched):** `db_view._decode_option_window` — parse the folded key, map the numeric id to the engine symbol via an optional `symbol_for_id` map (built in the route from `store.list_index_equity_instruments()` on the SAME threadpool worker, DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001), render `SYMBOL · SEGMENT` + `FLAG#code strike type · 1m`; ANY non-parsing shape falls back to the raw row (never an exception, never hidden; an unknown id keeps the numeric id). `fetch_windows.html` gains the All/📈Spot/⛓️Options filter chips (client-side, re-renders the cached payload — no extra fetch) and an options-specific empty-state explaining the all-or-nothing batching. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** 5 new regressions in `test_dashboard_db_view.py` (decode; unknown-id fallback; no-map still decodes series; malformed-key raw fallback; spot rows byte-unchanged with/without the map); dashboard sweep **437 unit + 86 integration green**; `ruff`+`mypy --strict`+`pyright` 0 on touched files. **Honest envelope:** ✅ what the operator sees is now the precise series coordinate; ✅ `market` stays raw in the JSON (the filter key + API back-compat); 🟡 option windows still APPEAR only at series commit — that is the #586 correctness invariant, not a display bug (the empty-state now says so); 🟡 the /db expired-options DATASET names still carry the numeric id (`NSE_FNO__25__…`) — same legibility class, separate surface, tracked follow-up; 🚫 ledger schema, keys, and ingest untouched. **Bundled hook hardening (found while SHIPPING this fix):** the commit-msg hook ran `check-conventional-commits.sh HEAD~1 HEAD`, which at commit-msg time validates the PREVIOUS commit — never the message being written — so the moment PR #588's dual-type squash title (`fix(coverage)+feat(engine): …`) landed on main, EVERY subsequent local commit failed regardless of its own message. Process lesson recorded: PR titles BECOME squash-commit titles — keep them single-type conventional. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the unified ledger + its folded option key) · DEC-OPTIONS-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 #625 (the live pull this was observed under) · DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the one-thread store rule).

630. **DEC-OPTIONS-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 — the OPTIONS pull gains the spot token pre-flight twin: `pull_options` verifies the Dhan token with the EXISTING pre-flight engine BEFORE any paced fan-out call — a dead token now costs ZERO vendor fan-out calls (was: one doomed paced call + the AuthGuard drain) and returns the loud `auth_expired` verdict with `rounds_run=0`** (2026-06-10; executes the 🚫-disclosed follow-up from DEC-OPTIONS-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 #625 — "token preflight before an options pull (spot's `DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001` twin) is NOT added here"). **The gap (#625's own honest envelope, code-traced):** spot refuses a dead-token bulk pull up front (DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 — the injected-`preflight` gate + the live `probe_token_data_live` auto-probe, both funnelling into `_preflight_refusal`); options had only the in-pull AuthGuard — a LIVE options pull with an already-dead 24h token still built the live client, opened the ledger, fanned out, burned ONE doomed paced 401/DH-906 call at the first dispatched series, tripped the latch, and drained every remaining series as AUTH-SKIPs. The pull could never land a single bar; the doomed call + the pool-wide drain were pure waste. **Fix (reuse, ZERO new pre-flight logic — §11 COMMON):** (1) `pull_options` gains `preflight: TokenPreflight | None = None` — an injected DEAD classification short-circuits BEFORE the client factory is even invoked (and before `begin_pull_ledger` — zero side effects), returning an `auth_aborted` `OptionsPullReport` with `rounds_run=0` whose `.verdict` is the SAME `classify_pull` `auth_expired` spot stamps (no second vocabulary), and emits ONE loud `universe.pull_options.preflight_refused` WARNING — the spot `_preflight_refusal` pattern, options-report-shaped (`_options_preflight_refusal`). (C2 — BLOCKER) `make_live_ledger_flush` throttle is now ADAPTIVE: ``max(min_interval, 5 × last_save_duration)`` — the fixed 2 s throttle under a 3.94 s save degenerated to flush-per-tick (a 12.5k-outcome drain ≈ **13.7 h of pure Parquet rewriting**); factor 5 caps flush overhead at ~20%, fake-clock-tested. (C3 — BLOCKER) `/api/v1/coverage/windows` + `build_window_payload`: ``market``/``status`` filters, severity-first cap (FAILED → EMPTY → SUCCESS → SKIPPED → PLANNED; the cap can NEVER hide actionable rows), counts always complete over every record, ``PLANNED`` rows shipped ONLY on explicit ``?status=PLANNED``, and an mtime-keyed records cache (any flush invalidates; the 4 s poll stops re-paying the 13.6 s load); `fetch_windows.html` chips now drive the query params + a "planned (pending)" KPI. logged ``universe.pull_options.planned``); rebased over the parallel #590 (token preflight, same function — gates re-run green post-merge) and #591. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** new tests — C1 trio (abort records the failing cursor with its type; (3) the per-symbol rollup falls back to an EMPTY `DhanIngestReport` when no pass completed and claims nothing for an unknown pair (`pairs.get` → skip) — the verdict carries the actionable state; this also fixes the `until_clean_rounds=0` IndexError; (4) `BulkSpotReport.auth_cause` is now `final_auth_cause` — on until-clean it prefers the FINAL round's dead-token cause (`until_outcome.auth_cause`) over the first pass's (the options contract; previously a round-3 token death reported `auth_cause=None`); (5) the spot controller joins the strict per-module CI gate (the `option_pull_controller` twin): `--cov=brutex.dashboard.pull_controller --cov-fail-under=100` over `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` + `test_dashboard_pull_pool_sizing.py`. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** 5 new regressions in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` — mid-pull quota death (single-pass) → `quota_exhausted` verdict + ledger Parquet `{SUCCESS, PLANNED}` (count 2, the settled window survives, the never-run window stays PLANNED) + status sidecar present + the loud warning, with a `threading.Event` ordering scaffold (the 1day death waits for the 1minute pair's collection-loop progress tick) so the parallel fan-out outcome is deterministic, never racy; `until_clean_rounds=0` is a safe all-zeros no-op (was IndexError); `pull_candles` `on_progress` per-pair forwarding (the module's last uncovered line). Touched-module gate **100.00% line+branch (336 stmts / 68 branches)**; full suite **5813 unit+integration green** (8 pre-existing documented skips, post-merge with main through PR #593); `mypy --strict` clean on all 216 package files; `pyright` 0 errors on touched files; `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a mid-round spot quota death now keeps every committed bar + window record and reports the SAME actionable verdict as the between-round brake — the next pull (after the IST-midnight reset) resumes incrementally over the SAME ledger; ✅ behaviour on every green path (clean / auth-death / transient-residual / DH-905 known-gap) is unchanged — the full suite pins it; 🟡 a quota death before ANY pass completed rolls every symbol up as zeros (per-pair outcomes are unknowable once the pass aborts — the report-level counters, not the ledger, lose the partial pass; 636b. **DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001 — trailing-window ledger orphans STOP accumulating: plan time now prunes every SUPERSEDED trailing row (the end-clipped tail key the advancing daily `end` re-tiles away — ~4.4M orphan rows/year at universe cadence), with a no-mask-by-construction guarantee and a measured 0.48 s universe-scale scan** (2026-06-10, executes the tracked follow-up ④ of DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001 #632). **The orphan mechanism (two sources, both verified):** the ledger keys a window by its exact 5-tuple (market/sid/interval/start/end) while the tiler clips the trailing window of `[start, end)` to `end` — every daily `end` advance mints a NEW trailing key (options ~12.5k series/day + spot 783 instruments × {the 1minute trailing tile + the whole-range 1day window}/day) and yesterday's settled row becomes a permanently-unreachable orphan (the tiler re-emits that key only for the SAME end — an identical re-pull — never a later one); second source: the planners plan with the UNCLAMPED `end` while the spot fetch clamps (DEC-DAILY-CANDLE-CLAMP-001), stranding the planned trailing row PLANNED forever whenever they diverge. **Design choice — GC over canonical key (1-agent hostile review FIRST, Golden Rule #9; verdict IMPLEMENTABLE-WITH-CONDITIONS, 11 findings, all five conditions implemented):** option (i) (a stable full-tile trailing key, clip only the HTTP request) was REJECTED on three review-verified mask mechanisms (a settled SUCCESS partial under a stable key masks the tile remainder forever; EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD=3 over a long weekend + holiday would SKIPPED-settle the whole 90-day tile; `settle_known_gap` would stamp a DH-905 verdict about `[b, today)` onto `[b, b+span)`) — fixing those needs an `as_of` probe-signature ripple or a `settled_through` schema column, it saves ZERO vendor calls (the trailing tile must stay unskippable until full, so it re-fetches daily either way), and the on-disk orphan backlog needs a GC regardless. **What shipped:** `WindowLedger.prune_superseded(planned_tiles)` — one O(rows) scan under the existing lock (doomed keys collected first, deleted after; never mid-iteration, no nested lock — hostile F2), keyed by a {(market, sid, interval) → {tile_start_iso: tile_end_iso}} index built INSIDE both planners from the very keys/tiles they already enumerate (hostile F3 — O(series + tiles) ≈ 1.4 MB at universe scale, NOT an O(P) per-window prefix map; the option index rides `coverage_key` itself so planner/GC can never drift, the #632 C4 rule); a row is pruned iff its series is planned AND its start is on the tiling AND its end is STRICTLY shorter than the tile's planned end — equal-end rows (a same-day re-pull's settled trailing row: the preserved skip) and longer-end rows (shrunk-range history) always survive; wired into `window_ledger_store.plan_windows` (spot — all three call sites inherit) + `plan_option_pull_windows` (options), structlog `window_ledger.pruned_superseded`, zero call-site changes; the four stale "every window ever planned" doc invariants amended in the same PR (hostile F1). **No-mask THEOREM (the review's core attack, upheld):** an absent row is never skippable (`is_skippable(absent)=False` → fetch) and GC only deletes — so pruning can only turn would-be skips into re-fetches (the idempotent keep-first sink absorbs them), NEVER a fetch into a skip; every retry surface re-derives its worklist from the tiling (in-run `_drain_pass` tuples, post-run auto-retry full re-tile, until-clean re-pass), never from FAILED ledger rows (review A2), and the ONLY deletion→insert coupling (`reconcile`/`seed_lake_success` seed-on-absent) targets exclusively current-plan keys, which the equal-end rule never prunes (review A3 — pinned by a dedicated regression, hostile F5). **Verified (HONEST — REAL local runs):** 9 prune unit tests + 4 store-level plan→prune tests (incl. the F5 reconcile-coupling pin + the same-day-replan skip pin + the logged-only-when-pruning pin) + the options-planner trailing-orphan test + a hypothesis property suite driving random multi-day advancing-end pull histories against FOUR invariants (no-mask monotonicity: skippable-after ⇒ skippable-before for every key; plan completeness; zero sub-planned-end survivors on the tiling; idempotent fixed point); per-module gates **100.00% line+branch** (window_ledger 104/16, window_ledger_store 143/46, option_universe_ingest 194/48) — window_ledger + window_ledger_store had NO standalone ci.yml gates until now (both ADDED, hostile A10); full sweep **5,462 unit + 710 integration/property/smoke/golden green**; `mypy --strict` 216 files clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `ruff`+format clean. **Measured (Linux container, Python 3.12.3 — NOT the M4 Pro reference):** pruning 364,182 orphans from a 1,205,568-row ledger = **0.477 s** (idempotent second pass 0.187 s, 0 pruned), index ~1.4 MB, RSS delta ~3 MB beside the ~480 MB ledger itself. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the daily orphan mint stops and the existing backlog drains on the next pull of each series; 🟡 NOT O(1) — one O(rows) scan per planner invocation at pull start (measured above; the per-window plan/probe/record stay O(1)); 🟡 GC reduces /coverage/windows FAILED counts by DELETION of unreachable orphans, not by recovery (hostile F6 — the replacement key starts PLANNED); 🟡 a pruned key CAN be re-fetched redundantly when the fetch tiling diverges from the plan tiling — only explicit `to_date=today` pulls (1day always, 1minute pre-close; DEFAULT pulls NEVER diverge — review A6 verified the clamp arithmetic across the IST/UTC date rollover), bounded ≤1 window per (instrument × interval) ≈ ≤1,566 calls vs the 100k/day quota ≈ 1.6% (hostile F4 — sized on the 783 live spot instruments, not the 241-row lean instruments table); 🟡 concurrent pulls share the ledger Parquet last-save-wins (pre-existing class) — a clobbered save can resurrect orphans until the next pull re-prunes them, so "gone after ONE pull" is NOT guaranteed under concurrent operation (hostile F8); 🚫 out of scope: grid-shift orphans from a CHANGED pull `start` (off-tiling rows deliberately untouched), orphans of series absent from the current plan (they drain when that series next pulls — universe cadence covers all), and the legacy `window_status.json` sidecar which still accumulates the same trailing churn (hostile F7 — TRACKED FOLLOW-UP: fold or GC the status sidecar; display-only, never drives skip). **Builds on:** DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001 #632 (follow-up ④ executed; pre-plan amplified the class) · DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (plan/record/skip semantics UNCHANGED) · DEC-DAILY-CANDLE-CLAMP-001 #621 (the clamp-divergence second source) · DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 #597 / the #598 no-mask arc (the guarantee this preserves by construction) · the 2026-06-10 1-agent hostile review (this entry is its record).

639. **DEC-PLAN-CLAMP-PARITY-001 — the spot window PLANNER tiles the SAME settled-data clamp the fetch does, and plan-time GC now also deletes the longer-end PLANNED ghosts the old mismatch minted: the operator's 783 "pending which never got auto-retried" rows were planner artifacts the fetch could NEVER record, not missed work** (2026-06-10, operator live /coverage/windows screenshots + uploaded `make run` log: 783 spot `1day` rows PLANNED `2021-01-01 → 2026-06-11`, attempts 0 — exactly one per universe instrument — while the SAME log shows `universe.pull_all.done … failed=0 verdict=clean pending_windows=0`; operator: "how come still I can see these many pending and planned items which didn't get auto retried … everything should receive SUCCESS"). **Root cause (code-traced):** `plan_windows` (`window_ledger_store.py`) tiled the RAW pull end (`today+1` from the default range) while `ingest_spot` tiles the `clamp_window_end` bound (`DEC-DAILY-CANDLE-CLAMP-001` #621: daily → `today`; intraday → `today+1` only from the 15:30 IST close) — so every (instrument, 1day) pull planned a key (`…→2026-06-11`) the fetch NEVER fetches (it fetches+records `…→2026-06-10`), leaving one permanently-PLANNED ghost per instrument per pull. The `DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001` #636b prune could not touch them: its shorter-end rule deletes rows the advancing end superseded, but the ghost's end is LONGER than every later clamped plan, and its longer-end rule kept ALL longer rows ("shrunk-range history"). This also falsifies #636b's "DEFAULT pulls NEVER diverge" disclosure — the live default universe pull diverges on `1day` ALWAYS and on `1minute` pre-close; the divergence cost is not a bounded redundant re-fetch but a permanent false-pending row the operator reads as missed work. **What shipped (one PR, three surfaces):** (1) **clamp parity** — `plan_windows` clamps per interval via the SAME `clamp_window_end` (+ the same `start < clamped_end` empty-range guard as `ingest_spot`), clock-injected (`now_ist` param, production default `_now_ist()`); planned keys == fetched keys by construction, so the ghost class can NEVER be minted again. (2) **ghost GC** — `WindowLedger.prune_superseded` additionally deletes a row whose series is planned and whose start is on the tiling when its end is STRICTLY LONGER than the planned tile end AND the row is `PLANNED` with `attempts == 0` (PURE INTENT: zero fetch history, unfetchable under the clamp, invisible to the shorter-end rule) — so the operator's existing 783 ghosts self-heal on the NEXT pull's plan→prune cycle, no manual migration. Longer-end rows with ANY recorded attempt (genuine shrunk-range history) are kept exactly as before; equal-end (current-plan) keys are always kept; a `PLANNED` row was never skippable, so the no-mask theorem is unchanged — deletion can only re-fetch, never skip. (3) **the page tells the truth** (`DEC-WINDOW-KPI-MARKET-SCOPE-001` + `DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-VISIBLE-001`, same operator report): the /coverage/windows KPI tiles now scope to the selected Spot/Options chip (only the All chip sums both buckets — the server's per-bucket `counts` were always complete; the page summed both regardless), and every EMPTY row shows its CONSECUTIVE clean-empty streak vs the promotion bound (`empty_streak` per row + `empty_threshold` in the payload, rendered `EMPTY 1/3`) — answering "why is attempts 5-6 still EMPTY": R1 promotes on the consecutive streak, interleaved rate-limit FAILEDs reset it (the uploaded log shows 2,168 `rate.429`/transient lines), so those rows are BY-DESIGN still retrying, not stuck. The third screenshot class (~30,739 options PLANNED) needed NO fix: the log timestamps show the snapshot was minutes into a planned-30,954-window until-clean run — the options planner/fetcher share one enumeration + key builders (golden-pinned, `DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001` C4), so options windows drain to SUCCESS/SKIPPED with no ghost class. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run, Python 3.12.3):** new tests — planner clamp trio (daily clamps to today; intraday follows the 15:30 close both sides; fully-clamped interval plans nothing) + the LIVE-STATE regression `test_operator_ghost_self_heals_on_next_plan` (ghost pruned, settled clamped row stays skippable) + ghost-prune pair on the ledger (longer-end PLANNED+0 pruned; defensive PLANNED-with-attempts kept via `from_rows`) + a NEW property invariant over NON-monotonic end histories (clamp flapping: after every plan→prune, surviving pure-intent rows sit EXACTLY on the current tiling; plan completeness + fixed point hold) + payload/page pins (`empty_streak` row field, `empty_threshold` top-level, streak-reset e2e). Binding gates ALL **100.00% line+branch**: `window_ledger` 108/18, `window_ledger_store` 145/46, `db_view` 423/138; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the three touched modules; `ruff` + `ruff format` clean; full unit battery green (see PR proof). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the ghost class is dead at the source (parity) AND the live backlog self-heals on the next pull; ✅ KPI tiles match the selected market exactly ("when spot is selected it should display only spot alone … only for All, all the counts"); 🟡 the prune scan stays O(rows) once per pull start (#636b's measured envelope; per-window plan/probe/record stay O(1)); 🟡 a plan→fetch clock race across the 15:30 IST boundary inside ONE pull can still strand ≤1 trailing key per (instrument × 1minute) — it self-heals on the next plan→prune cycle (shorter-end rule), disclosed not hidden; 🟡 off-tiling-start ghosts (changed pull `start`) remain out of scope exactly as in #636b — they heal when the range re-covers them; 🚫 no change to the options ingest spine, the all-or-nothing commit invariant, the 5 r/s / 100k-day caps, or the engine. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001 #636b (the prune this completes; its F4/A6 divergence disclosure corrected by live evidence) · DEC-DAILY-CANDLE-CLAMP-001 #621 (the clamp now applied at BOTH ends of the pipe) · DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001 #632 (the pre-plan surface + C4 parity that kept options ghost-free) · DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (plan/record/skip semantics unchanged) · DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 / R1 (the streak rule now made visible) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (no illusion: the fix deletes FALSE pending, never real work) · Rule 7 (idempotent re-plan) · §11 AUTOMATED (self-healing, zero operator clicks).

645. **DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 — every /coverage spot dataset row gains an HONEST fetch-window completeness chip sourced from the unified window ledger (SETTLED / PENDING n / FAILED m / derived / no-ledger-record / ambiguous) — PARTIALLY executes the DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 #397 follow-up: ledger-settledness over planner-planned ranges, NOT a trading-day gap audit** (2026-06-10/11). **The gap (#397's own disclosure):** the spot coverage page showed `bars + first_date/last_date` per dataset and explicitly did NOT assert any range complete. Since then the unified window ledger became exactly that record — per-window PLANNED/SUCCESS/EMPTY/FAILED/SKIPPED with clamp parity + GC (#639) — so the honest move is to PROJECT the ledger, never to re-derive gaps from lake spans (the #598 internal-gap lesson: a span ENCLOSES holes). **Hostile review FIRST (Golden Rule #9, 1-agent): verdict IMPLEMENTABLE-WITH-CONDITIONS, 10 findings/conditions — ALL implemented**, including two course corrections: (F1) the chip belongs on `spot_coverage.html` (the per-row table moved there in the COVERAGE-SPLIT; #397's text predates it) — `coverage.html` (the hub) is BYTE-UNTOUCHED, preserving its pinned headline; (F6) the green state is named **SETTLED, deliberately NOT "complete"** — and this entry says "partially executes #397" because ledger-settledness covers ONLY windows a pull ever planned (an explicit narrow-range pull reads SETTLED while older years are absent from the lake; with full-history default pulls + clamp parity + GC the planned tiling does span Track-1, but that is an operational property, not a guarantee the chip may assert). **What shipped:** (1) `brutex/data/window_ledger.py` exports `SETTLED_STATUSES` (a public alias of the ledger's OWN `_SKIPPABLE` skip authority) so consumers never mint a third hand-typed status list (C5; `pull_verdict.classify_pull` was evaluated and is the WRONG source — it classifies per-pull tallies, no PLANNED/EMPTY axis). (2) `brutex/dashboard/db_view.spot_window_rollup(lake_root)` → `(symbol, interval) → (settled, pending, failed)`: filters `market == "dhan"` EXACTLY (`_SPOT_WINDOW_MARKET`, mirrored against `ingest._MARKET` per the `_OPTION_WINDOW_MARKET` precedent — `_window_market_bucket` is a display bucket, not a join identity, C3); settled = `SETTLED_STATUSES`, failed = `FAILED`, everything else (PLANNED + below-threshold EMPTY) = pending — the exact complement of the skip rule; `is_file()` guard (no `FileNotFoundError` on a fresh lake) and deliberately NO `window_status.json` fallback (a frozen, write-retired snapshot #641 — a stale completeness claim is worse than an honest unknown); the GROUPING carries its own `(path, mtime_ns)`-keyed cache beside `_ledger_records_cached` (C7 — the endpoint is polled every 4 s by TWO pages; an O(~1M-row) Python loop per poll at universe scale is not acceptable; O(rows) once per ledger flush, O(datasets) per request between flushes). (3) `coverage_view.build_spot_coverage_payload(rows, rollup=None)` annotates each row (`completeness` + `windows_settled/pending/failed`, `int | None`) via the pure `_classify_completeness` ladder: non-fetch intervals → **derived** (resampled from 1minute, DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 — the fetch ledger does not apply; counts `None`, never `0`, and NEVER inheriting the 1minute state: materialisation is MANUAL so a derived partition can be stale relative to a later 1m pull — inheriting would be the textbook illusion, C2); duplicate `(symbol, interval)` across (exchange, segment) directories → **ambiguous** (the ledger key carries neither exchange nor segment — counts cannot be attributed without guessing; surfaced as its own state, C4 — the known envelope hole: a segment/exchange migration leaves one ledger series joined by two dataset rows); fetch interval with no rows → **no_ledger_record** (e.g. an externally-copied lake — honest unknown); else FAILED>0 → failed, pending>0 → pending, else settled. `FETCH_INTERVALS` is mirrored in `coverage_view` against `pull_controller.DHAN_FETCH_INTERVALS` (mirror-constant chosen over importing the adapter stack into a pure viewer; stated per C2). (4) The route (`/api/v1/coverage/spot`) joins PER REQUEST OUTSIDE the SummaryCache (C8 — ledger flushes never bump that cache's generation; fusing the rollup into `_recompute` would freeze the chips until the next LAKE write), inside the existing threadpool worker, data flowing db_view → app → coverage_view as plain arguments (C9 — no new cross-imports, no cycle). (5) `spot_coverage.html` renders the chip column + the subtitle/status disclaimers updated to the new envelope wording. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run, Python 3.12.3):** binding gates ALL **100.00% line+branch** — `coverage_view` (32 passed), `db_view` (189 passed over both gate files), `window_ledger` (43 incl. the new authority-equivalence pin `SETTLED_STATUSES == is_skippable`); NEW tests — the full chip ladder (settled / pending / failed-outranks-pending / derived / no-record / ambiguous / rollup-omitted / headline-unchanged), the rollup grouping with option-market exclusion, the no-ledger-file guard, the rollup's own mtime-cache invalidation (mirrors the C3 cache test), and the e2e integration pins (full-row dict equality WITH the new fields on a no-ledger lake + a settled-chip e2e against a real written ledger); `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean; `ruff` + format clean; full battery green (see PR proof). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the operator finally SEES per dataset whether the fetch ledger has outstanding work — sourced from the single authority, zero new scans, zero new claims; 🟡 **SETTLED ≠ complete** — scoped to planner-planned ranges (disclosed on the page itself, in the subtitle AND the chip vocabulary); 🟡 the ambiguous state surfaces (not solves) the ledger-key envelope hole — widening the key with exchange/segment is a SEPARATE decision, not smuggled in here (C4); 🟡 the rollup is O(rows) once per ledger flush — NOT an O(1)-total claim (the per-request join is O(datasets)); 🚫 no change to the ledger semantics, the skip rule, the pull paths, the hub page, or the engine. **Builds on:** DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 #397 (the follow-up partially executed — trading-day gap audit REMAINS open) · DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the authority projected) · DEC-PLAN-CLAMP-PARITY-001 #639 + DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001 #636b (why the planned tiling is trustworthy) · DEC-STATUS-SIDECAR-WRITE-RETIRE-001 #641 (why there is no sidecar fallback) · DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001 #632 (the records cache reused) · DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (why non-fetch intervals are derived) · the 2026-06-10 1-agent hostile review (this entry is its record) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 · Rule 10 · §11 COMMON.

`Σ evals_total ≥ unique trials`); `Stage3PassReport` gains `sidecars_written` and the `STAGE_3_PASS_COMPLETE` payload carries it; (condition 5) every sidecar binds `_tuple_digest` + the flush `content_hash`; (condition 9) the F11 A/B oracle's tree hash now covers `*.trials.json` alongside `*.parquet` — two full enabled runs remain byte-identical INCLUDING sidecars and the idempotent third run appends nothing and changes no bytes. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local runs, Linux container Python 3.12.3):** the three F4 crash corners are each a dedicated test — resumed-completed-tuple PRESERVES (a sentinel-corrupted sidecar survives a full-resume byte-untouched), partial-mark subset NEVER writes (one pre-marked mask ⇒ `skipped_dedup == 1` ⇒ no file), flush-then-die redo REWRITES byte-identical (fresh-dedup re-run ⇒ identical sidecar bytes); Bailey-LdP V); 🟡 grid trials are correlated and Stage-3 CMA-ES trials adaptive — raw-N deflation is conservative for the former, the i.i.d. expected-max benchmark under-models the latter (stated, unquantified, per the ADR §5); 🚫 RC/SPA/PBO/RW/CPCV/WFO/MC remain pool-only (they need return SERIES; unpersisted trials cannot enter them — DSR is the only filter whose multiplicity input is scalar-computable at full N); 🚫 the partial-`mark_many` redo hole is NOT touched by this slice — tracked next row (#650, condition 10). **Builds on:** ADR-0008 #642 conditions 3/6/7/9 · `DEC-TRIAL-STATS-FREEZE-001` #647 (the frozen records consumed) · `DEC-TRIAL-STATS-WRITE-001` #646 · `DEC-TRIAL-STATS-CORE-001` #643 · `DEC-PBO-SIDECAR-001` (the additive-key + three-state display precedents).

650. **DEC-MARK-MANY-REDO-HOLE-001 — TRACKED FOLLOW-UP (open, not fixed): the PRE-EXISTING partial-`mark_many` redo hole gets its own decision row per ADR-0008 condition 10 — a crash INSIDE the dedup mark loop can let a re-run re-rank a SUBSET of a tuple's combos** (2026-06-11; recorded as part of the slice-4 PR per `DEC-CASCADE-N-DESIGN-LOCK-001` #642 condition 10 — "this design must not silently absorb or mask it"). **The hole, precisely:** `run_persisted_sweep` flushes the store, writes the trial-stats sidecar, then calls `mark_many` to record the tuple's combos in the Bloom+LMDB dedup; a crash partway through the mark loop leaves SOME combos marked and some not, so a redo re-enumerates only the UNMARKED subset and re-ranks THAT subset: under `--overfit-gate` the subset's differing `deflated_sharpe` values raise the store's append conflict (loud, but a wedge); with `top_k` truncation the subset's own top-K can append EXTRA rows and silently break tree byte-identity. **What the cascade-N arc guarantees about this window (and no more):** slice 2's condition-2 write policy (`flush → sidecar → mark`; overwrite iff `skipped_dedup == 0`, PRESERVE otherwise) keeps the trial-stats SIDECAR safe across the crash window — the redo of a partially-marked tuple sees `skipped_dedup > 0` and preserves the original whole-population sidecar rather than overwriting it with subset moments; the N the cascade deflates against stays honest even while the STORE itself can be wedged/inflated by the hole. NOTHING about the hole itself is fixed, claimed fixed, or masked. **Candidate remedies for the fix PR (to be hostile-reviewed, not pre-decided here):** transactional mark (LMDB write-txn over the whole tuple batch) · mark-then-verify-store reconciliation on resume · per-tuple completion sentinel consulted before re-ranking. **Follow-up:** its own PR + decision row; until then this row is the single source of truth for the hole's existence, blast radius, and the slice-2 sidecar-preservation boundary.
651. **DEC-REPORT-FILENAME-001 — the pre-open report downloads get SELF-DESCRIBING filenames: every selection knob (mode + top-mover threshold · price basis · selected symbols · date range) is encoded in the download name, replacing the selection-blind static `preopen_report.zip` / date-only `.xlsx` name** (2026-06-11, operator: "whenever we download based on selected indices and top movers percentage of all symbols, everything should become the file name — precise clear reference instead of some static name"). **The gap (code-confirmed):** `/api/v1/reports/preopen.zip` hardcoded `preopen_report.zip` regardless of mode/min_pct/symbols/basis/range; `/api/v1/reports/preopen.xlsx` carried dates only. Two reports with different selections downloaded as the SAME name — zero reference value, silent overwrite risk in the browser's download folder. **What shipped:** (1) NEW pure `preopen_report.report_filename(extension, start, end, basis, symbols, mode=None, min_pct=None)` — ONE builder for both endpoints (§11 COMMON; the routes stay thin wrappers, the function is 100% offline-testable). Name grammar: `preopen` · mode (`all` / `topmover-minNpct` — the threshold rendered ONLY where it applies; `Decimal.normalize` display so `2.0`→`2pct`, `2.5`→`2.5pct` — threshold display formatting, NEVER money rounding, DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 is money-only) · basis (`day`/`minute`) · symbols (spelled out up to 5 then `+Nmore`; `all-symbols` when unfiltered) · `from`_`to`. Examples: `preopen_day_all-symbols_2026-06-01_2026-06-11.xlsx`, `preopen_topmover-min2.5pct_minute_NIFTY-BANKNIFTY_2026-06-01_2026-06-11.zip`. (2) `_filename_token` sanitizer — every token collapses non-`[A-Za-z0-9-]` runs to `-` (NSE's `M&M` → `M-M`) so a symbol can never smuggle a quote/path-separator/whitespace into the quoted `Content-Disposition` header; an all-unsafe token degrades to `X`, never empty. (3) Both routes wired (`preopen.xlsx` + `preopen.zip`). **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run, Python 3.12.3):** `brutex.dashboard.preopen_report` gate **100.00% line+branch** (65 passed); NEW `TestReportFilename` ×8 (xlsx no-mode/no-symbols exact name · zip topmover threshold exact name · `2.0`→`2pct` normalize · mode=all ignores min_pct · topmover-without-threshold falls back to plain mode token · 8-symbol overflow → `SYM0..SYM4+3more` · `M&M`/quote sanitization · all-unsafe→`X`); BOTH route pins updated to the exact new names (the old static-name pin deleted); reports routes + ux suites 100 passed; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean; `ruff` + format clean; unit+integration+smoke battery green (see PR proof). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ every download now names its exact selection — no two different selections share a filename (within the 5-symbol spell-out cap, beyond which the count disambiguates); 🟡 the symbol spell-out caps at 5 (+`Nmore`) — a deliberate filesystem-name-length tradeoff, so two DIFFERENT >5-symbol selections of the same size/range/mode CAN share a name (disclosed; the in-file content remains the authority); 🟡 in-zip member names (`preopen_all_2024.xlsx` per year) are UNCHANGED — this decision names the outer download only; 🚫 report content, row building, rendering, and all other endpoints untouched. **Builds on:** DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 (the report this names) · DEC-REPORTS-EXCEL-CATEGORIES-001 (the zip export) · DEC-PREOPEN-MINUTE-BASIS-001 (the basis knob encoded) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON (one builder, two consumers) · Golden Rule #10 (the cap disclosed).
652. **DEC-PROGRESS-WINDOW-UNITS-001 — the /universe pull card and /coverage/windows finally speak ONE language: the card's coarse unit counter is labelled honestly ("units", not "chunks") and gains a live WINDOW-scale line read from the SAME ledger counts the windows page renders — closing the operator's "15/43 chunks vs 1,956 planned windows" confusion** (2026-06-11, operator live screenshots: the 360ONE options pull showed "15/43 chunks" while /coverage/windows showed 1,956 PLANNED rows — "as per planned it should show all of them right, but how are the window chunk numbers different?"). **Root cause — two honest scales, zero shared vocabulary:** the progress card counts COARSE units (options: one unit = one ALL-OR-NOTHING series commit of ~dozens of 30-day windows, 42 series + 1 spot unit = 43 for one stock per DEC-OPTIONS-PROGRESS-SERIES-001; spot: symbol×interval chunks) while the windows page counts fine-grained per-window ledger rows — both correct, neither page SAYING which scale it speaks, and the static "chunks" label actively wrong for the options flavor. The PLANNED count being smaller than the full fan-out (1,956 < 42×~67) is the SKIP working: previously settled windows of re-pulled ranges never re-plan ("no wasted Dhan hit"), which the card also never said. **What shipped (display-only):** (1) the card's unit label reads `units` (flavor-neutral, never wrong); (2) a `windowsline` under the stat grid polls `/api/v1/coverage/windows` every 5 s (the mtime-cached counts read — no new backend surface, no extra ledger load) and renders `fetch windows (<bucket>, all recorded): settled · pending · failed · total`, with settled = SUCCESS+SKIPPED (the ledger's own skip authority, DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 vocabulary), pending = PLANNED+EMPTY, failed = FAILED; (3) the bucket binds at pull start (options paths → `options`, spot pulls → `spot`) and refreshes immediately. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run, Python 3.12.3):** template-only change; coverage + pull-controller + smoke suites 118 passed; the counts contract this line consumes is already pinned by the windows-page suites (DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001 C3 + DEC-WINDOW-KPI-MARKET-SCOPE-001). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ both surfaces now share the window-scale vocabulary live during a pull; 🟡 the line is BUCKET-GLOBAL (all recorded spot or options windows), NOT per-pull — the counts API has no per-pull axis; said verbatim in the rendered label ("all recorded") and the template comment, never implied otherwise; 🟡 the coarse counter stays coarse by design (the series unit IS the commit unit — DEC-OPTION-429-RECOVERY-001's all-or-nothing invariant); 🚫 no backend, ledger, or pull-path change. **Builds on:** DEC-OPTIONS-PROGRESS-SERIES-001 (the series unit explained) · DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001 C3 (the cached counts read) · DEC-WINDOW-KPI-MARKET-SCOPE-001 (the bucket vocabulary) · DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 (the settled/pending classification reused) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON (one counts source, three consumers).
653. **DEC-PLAN2-OPTION-SELL-BACKLOG-001 — the intraday option-selling strategy idea is RECORDED as an explicitly NOT-AUTHORIZED Track 2 backlog item (`docs/track2/TRACK2_OPTION_SELLING_BACKLOG.md`), preserving the 2026-06-11 design discussion without expanding scope** (operator: "forget about Plan 2 — just document this, meanwhile go ahead with the remaining process"). **What the doc preserves:** the sell-the-spike thesis (top-volume current-expiry stock-option premium spikes → IV-crush/theta mean-reversion → intraday SELL with SL/TP, square-off by close) with its honest negative-skew risk framing; the four data-feasibility findings established in-session — (1) the lake's banded Dhan rollingoption data already holds the near-ATM fuel (DEC-P0-063 REFERENCE_ONLY), (2) the relative-strike MOVING-window semantics (`ATM±N` is a slot, not a contract — per-contract series reconstruct via the per-bar `strike[]` column), (3) the WINNER-CENSORING hazard (a sold strike drifts out of the ±3 band exactly on winners — any backtest must censor, never fabricate, band-exited trades or it is biased optimistic), (4) Groww is NOT the historical source per ADR-0002's verified n/a — the operator-reported "Groww 1m from 2020" claim is marked UNVERIFIED with a Phase-0 hard-gate probe as the first slice IF ever authorized; plus the if-authorized spec-slice order ending in hostile review. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ nothing is lost, nothing is authorized — the doc's banner + this entry both say NOT AUTHORIZED in capitals; 🚫 no scope, lake, engine, or schedule change. **Builds on:** DEC-P0-063 (the REFERENCE_ONLY lake fuel) · DEC-GROWW-DHAN-REVERT-001/ADR-0002 (the verified Groww facts) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 3 (scope lock — the rule this document honors by existing) · Rule 9 (the review the future decision must run).

654. **DEC-MARK-MANY-SENTINEL-001 — the partial-`mark_many` redo hole (#650) is CLOSED: per-tuple COMPLETION SENTINELS are now the redo authority and the dedup marks are demoted to advisory — a crash anywhere in a tuple's write sequence forces a FULL-population re-run with dedup probes BYPASSED, so a subset re-rank (the overfit-gate wedge / the silent `top_k` row inflation) is impossible by construction** (2026-06-11; executes the ADR-0008 condition-10 tracked follow-up recorded at #650). **Hostile review FIRST (Golden Rule #9, 1-agent, 42 tool-use evidence pass):** verdict — candidate B (mark-then-verify-store reconciliation) **INFEASIBLE** (the unconditional `store.flush()` at `sweep_run.py` satisfies "store exists with a valid flush" from the flush→sidecar crash window onward, so naive B declares a W2-crashed tuple complete and permanently orphans its trial-stats sidecar → that leaderboard falls back to pool-N forever — the exact regression the #643→#649 arc closed); candidate A (transactional LMDB mark) **FEASIBLE-WITH-CONDITIONS but inferior** (LMDB batch-txn atomicity is sound, but the Bloom tier cannot join the transaction and `seen()` treats Bloom-negative as definitive — a partially-updated Bloom re-creates the subset redo in-session, and correctness would still DEPEND on mark completeness, the precise property the hole exploits); candidate C (completion sentinel) **RECOMMENDED with one amendment** — never wipe stale marks (no unmark API exists; Bloom cannot unmark), BYPASS them instead. The review also delivered three corrections to #650's framing, all verified file:line: (P1) the hole is LATENT in every shipped cross-process crash path — the production launcher's dedup is in-memory (`cli.py` builds `OptionDedupIndex` with no LMDB injection; Bloom persistence "does NOT ship in V1"), so a `kill -9` mid-mark erases all marks and the redo was safe-by-amnesia; the hole armed only same-process (a caught mid-mark exception, e.g. `BloomCapacityExceeded` FAIL_CLOSED) or under the DESIGNED future persistent Bloom+LMDB tier — this fix closes the contract before that tier ships; (P2) `sweep_supervisor.py`'s crash-safety docstring claimed resume "skips every already-flushed mask" via ComboDedup — FALSE cross-process (corrected in the same PR); (P3) on post-#646 trees the `top_k` inflation was not silent forever (the preserved sidecar's `store_content_hash` pairing raises at cascade-build), but pre-#646 trees were fully silent. **What shipped:** (1) NEW `brutex/engine/tuple_complete.py` — `TupleCompletionSentinel` (frozen/slots, construction-validated: 16-hex tuple digest + 64-hex store sha256 pairing identity, bool `sidecar_written`, `n_marked >= 0`; hex validation DELEGATED to the slice-1 trial-stats validator, §11 COMMON), `<store>.parquet.complete.json` path helper (the sidecar suffix discipline), deterministic sorted-key render, atomic write (`_atomic_write`, the ONE tempfile+fsync+replace source), typed reader with every error arm (`TupleCompletionError`); (2) `run_persisted_sweep` — write ordering per tuple is now **append → flush → sidecar → mark_many → sentinel STRICTLY LAST**; at entry on the digest path `_sentinel_resume` decides: PAIRED sentinel (digest match ∧ sha256(store bytes) == recorded ∧ sidecar paired-or-recorded-absent) → **short-circuit** (no eval, no flush, no writes, dedup untouched; ONE `SWEEP_RESUMED` audit line instead of the usual three; `SweepRunSummary.resumed_complete=True` echoing the recorded store hash); sentinel absent/unpaired → **full redo with `dedup.seen` probes BYPASSED** (`skipped_dedup == 0` by construction) → byte-identical rewrite of store + sidecar + sentinel (self-healing, loud `sweep_run.sentinel_unpaired` warning per failure arm); legacy no-digest callers keep probe semantics verbatim; `SweepRunSummary` gains additive `resumed_complete`/`sentinel_written`; (3) ADR-0008 condition 2's preserve-on-skips sidecar arm REMOVED as structurally unreachable on the digest path (bypass ⇒ the population is always FULL; a subset population can no longer exist to be preserved against — the policy contract in `trial_stats.write_tuple_trial_stats` amended accordingly); (4) the supervisor crash-safety docstring corrected (P2); (5) the stage3-wire A/B byte-identity tree oracle extended to `*.complete.json`. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local runs, Linux container Python 3.12.3):** `brutex.engine` glob gate **true 100.00% line+branch (3,493 stmts / 868 branches, 1,033 tests)** incl. `tuple_complete.py` (64/14) and `sweep_run.py` (238/68) at 100.00%; THE two hole regressions land as named tests (`test_overfit_wedge_regression` — pre-marked subset + overfit-gate redo raises NOTHING and the store is byte-identical; `test_topk_inflation_regression` — `top_k=1` redo persists exactly 1 row, never inflated); the W4 ordering pin (`_MarkCrashDedup` dies mid-mark-loop ⇒ NO sentinel ⇒ next run fully redoes and heals); every `_sentinel_resume` arm value-pinned (corrupt sentinel / digest mismatch / missing store / tampered store / corrupt sidecar / valid-but-mispaired sidecar / sidecar-less record / paired success incl. exactly-one-audit-line + `verify_chain` + dedup-never-consulted); goldens updated honestly (`test_golden_idempotent_resume_is_lossless` now pins the sentinel short-circuit, `skipped_dedup == 0`, files byte-identical — the prior dedup-skip pin documented inline); full goldens (360) + property + integration (352) + chaos (18) + smoke green; `mypy --strict` clean (220 files); `pyright` 0 errors on every changed file; `ruff check`+`format` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ crash windows W1-W6 all converge to byte-identical trees (enumerated in the test suite; W4 — the hole — closed regardless of dedup backing, persistence, or same-process reuse); 🟡 the sentinel-absent redo is an O(N_masks) full re-evaluation paid ONLY on crash recovery (the prior all-skip resume was cheaper but unsound; the sentinel-present path is CHEAPER than before: one JSON read + one sha256 over a ≤top_k-row Parquet vs O(N_masks) BLAKE3+probes); 🟡 the in-memory `set`/Bloom tiers stay non-transactional and the mask dedup stays volatile in production — demoted to an explicit optimization, never load-bearing on the digest path (documented, not removed); 🚫 PRE-FIX trees where the `top_k` inflation already fired and the tuple then completed are NOT healed (append-only stores cannot shed rows; post-#646 trees self-detect via the sidecar-pairing raise, pre-#646 trees are undetectable by the sweep) — the remedy is the ADR-0008 §3-D deterministic-recount `sweep-verify` doctor command, a TRACKED FOLLOW-UP for its own PR + decision row, per the review's scoping default; 🚫 multi-process concurrent sweeps over one root remain out of contract (unchanged); 🚫 the optional LMDB `add_many` batch-mark defense-in-depth was NOT shipped (no correctness reliance on it; smallest-diff discipline). **Builds on:** #650 (the hole's record) · ADR-0008 #642 conditions 2/5/10 · `DEC-TRIAL-STATS-WRITE-001` #646 (the write ordering extended) · `DEC-TRIAL-STATS-FREEZE-001` #647 (the pairing-identity discipline reused).

655. **DEC-O1-CACHE-TIER-001 — strict-tier O(1) ratio gates split into SAME-FOOTPRINT (keep the decreed 1.1×) vs CROSS-CACHE-TIER (measured 3.0× constant allowance): the first REAL M4-Pro run proved 1.1× physically unsatisfiable when the big workload spills L2/SLC into DRAM** (2026-06-11; amends `DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001` #381's single strict ceiling; evidence from the 2026-06-11 bench-m4pro certification run on the operator's self-hosted M4-Pro runner). **The evidence (REAL hardware, not simulation):** with `BRUTEX_M4PRO_STRICT=1` live for the first time, 11/11 absolute-throughput gates and 4/4 33B-SLA gates PASSED (mask-AND ≈ 2.0 BILLION ops/s — 40× the 50 M/s floor; 33B-trial sweep extrapolates inside the §8 2-4-day envelope), but exactly 3 of the strict 1.1× ratio gates failed: throughput-canary mask-AND 2.43× (0.20→0.49 ns/elem, 100K-elem arrays fit the M4's private L2 while 1M-elem arrays stream from SLC/DRAM), dict-lookup 2.11× (24→51 ns under the same footprint jump), primed rate-limiter window 1.20× (5,000-hit deque spans more cache lines than an empty one). Per-element cost is bounded by a CONSTANT memory-tier factor at every N — the paths remain O(1) in the algorithmic sense the decree protects; the 1.1× literal is a cache-hierarchy impossibility for tests whose two sizes BY DESIGN straddle a cache tier. **What shipped:** `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py` gains `CACHE_TIER_STRICT_CEILING = 3.0` + `cache_tier_ceiling(shared_ci_default)` — strict tier returns `min(3.0, shared_default)` (can only TIGHTEN, never loosen), shared CI returns the caller's default UNCHANGED (zero behaviour change, zero new flake surface); exactly 3 call sites switch to it (`test_rate_limiter_o1.py` acquire-ratio 5.0, `test_throughput_canary.py` mask-AND 8.0 + dict 10.0), each with an inline cache-tier comment; `test_throughput_canary.py`'s evaluate_atoms ratio KEEPS the strict 1.1× (same-footprint — it passed on the M4); `tests/bench/test_o1_tiers.py` gains 3 tests pinning shared-unchanged / strict-3.0 / never-looser. **Verified (HONEST — local Linux container):** touched bench files 22/22 green on BOTH tiers (`BRUTEX_M4PRO_STRICT=1` and unset); smoke 15/15; `ruff check`+`format` clean; `mypy --strict` clean on `_o1_tiers.py`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ same-footprint hot paths keep the decreed 1.1× strict gate; ✅ the `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS` absolute floors still gate raw speed independently (a cache-tier excuse cannot hide a real slowdown — 2.0B ops/s is also asserted absolutely); 🟡 3.0× is a MEASURED allowance (max observed 2.43× + ~23% headroom), not a derived hardware model — if a future runner measures higher, the constant gets ITS OWN decision, never a silent bump; 🟡 the M4 gate itself is re-armed but the post-merge fully-green bench-m4pro run is pending the operator's browser re-run (workflow dispatch is 403 for this integration token); 🚫 the decree's literal 1.1× for cross-cache-tier comparisons is documented as physically unsatisfiable on cache-hierarchy silicon — this is a measured-constant refinement of the O(1) gate, NOT a bypass (CLAUDE.md §2 r5's O(1) discipline is what the constant bound preserves). **Builds on:** `DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001` #381 (the two-tier pattern) · the 2026-06-11 M4-Pro runner certification (runner `m4pro`, actions-runner 2.334.0).
656. **DEC-SWEEP-VERIFY-001 — the `sweep-verify` doctor's pure core ships (slice 1 of 2): the two BARS-FREE verification tiers — Tier-1 STRUCTURAL (every artifact's self-described pairing, tree-only) and Tier-2 IDENTITY (expected-path + per-row 9-field run-id re-derivation under the tree's RECORDED context) — including the killer cheap check that detects the pre-#646 `top_k` inflation #654's envelope called "undetectable by the sweep", without bars** (2026-06-11; executes the #654 tracked follow-up / ADR-0008 §3-D. P-1 note: #655 was claimed by open PR #615 `DEC-O1-CACHE-TIER-001` while this slice was in flight; this entry takes #656). **Hostile review FIRST (Golden Rule #9, 1-agent, 32 tool-use evidence pass):** verdict IMPLEMENTABLE-WITH-CONDITIONS as a three-tier doctor, REPORT-ONLY — auto-healing REJECTED outright on three verified grounds: (a) wrong-inputs-condemn-good-data (a recount under a mistyped grid flag or re-ingested lake would condemn a healthy tree; only a Tier-3 CORRUPT under an exact three-way recorded-context match is ever heal-grade); (b) **the naive heal is a verified no-op trap (P0)** — deleting a divergent tuple's store+sidecar+sentinel does NOT make the next sweep redo it, because two skip tiers sit ABOVE `run_one_tuple` (the checkpoint resume skip and the `SweepCache` tuple skip, neither of which has a delete API; the Bloom tier cannot unmark — the same fact that killed #654's candidate A), so a sound future heal must also wipe `checkpoint/` + `dedup-cache/` wholesale — affordable post-#654 since intact tuples short-circuit at their sentinels; (c) quarantine-not-delete (append-only stores cannot shed rows; `os.replace` into `<root>/quarantine/<ts>/` is the only correct repair). Tier-3 (the full recount = a SHADOW RE-SWEEP composing the existing `run_sweep_grid` into a scratch root and byte-diffing — never a hand-rolled mirror, §11 COMMON) + the CLI shim are slice 2; the recount is an oracle ONLY under matched recorded context (ADR-0008's two drift channels: min-hits is lake-state-sensitive, `has_conflict` vocabulary-version-sensitive) — any mismatch → refuse-or-INCONCLUSIVE, never condemn. **What shipped (NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py`):** typed findings (`VerifyFinding` corrupt/warn/info; corrupt is verdict-grade, warn/info honest narration — `TreeVerifyReport.clean` ignores warns) + deterministic render; `recorded_context_from_audit` (review condition 2a — the three reproducibility strings read from the tree's own `SWEEP_START` audit payloads, refusing loudly on inconsistency; the operator's memory is never the source); **Tier 1 `verify_structural`** — store loadability (every row construction-revalidated; `ResultsStore.load` now wraps corrupt/truncated/foreign Parquet bytes into its OWN `ResultsStoreError` so every reader handles damage uniformly — previously a raw polars `ComputeError` escaped), sidecar readability + (filename-digest, store-sha256) pairing (the cascade-build check, runnable without a cascade), sentinel readability + pairing + recorded-sidecar cross-check, the post-#654 tally invariant (a sentinel'd tuple bypassed dedup ⇒ `n_enumerated − pruned − dropped − backtested == 0`, nonzero is impossible-by-construction), orphan sidecars/sentinels; **Tier 2 `verify_identity`** — `plan_expected_stores` re-derives every expected path from the grid (Stage-3 refined cells attributed via the cascade manifest's recorded coordinates + train hash, condition 2c — never guessed; manifest absent ⇒ honest `unattributed_store` warn), the GRID-MISMATCH refusal (condition 2b — fully disjoint expected/found digest sets ⇒ one tree-level verdict, per-file judgments withheld: wrong flags must never read as tree-wide corruption), per-row label/mask-membership/`run_id` re-derivation through the SAME `canonical_trade_params` + `mask_run_id` the sweep persists with, the opt-in `vocabulary_trusted` conflict check (off by default — valid only under matched code), missing-expected-store as info (mid-sweep/no-bars, never condemned), and **`rows > top_k` ⇒ CORRUPT** — the hostile review PROVED this signature sound and complete for the silent #650 inflation class (silent requires no overfit gate; extras append only when the original store already held exactly `top_k` rows; post-#654 the digest path always rewrites the full population) — so the pre-#646 inflation IS detectable bars-free, on sidecar-less trees. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local runs, Linux container Python 3.12.3):** `brutex.engine` glob gate **true 100.00% line+branch (3,710 stmts / 950 branches, 1,073 tests)** with `sweep_verify.py` (214/82) at 100.00%; every tier arm value-pinned over a REAL swept tree (module-scoped clean fixture, per-test copies surgically damaged): all 6 structural pairing arms + tally invariant + orphans + legacy-tree warn-only; identity clean/grid-mismatch/unattributed/missing/labels/mask/run-id/conflict-trust arms; THE inflation regression (`test_topk_inflation_signature` — a real `top_k=1` sweep inflated then stripped to pre-#646 shape, flagged bars-free); the Stage-3 cell exemption from the `top_k` bound; goldens (360) + integration (352) + smoke green; `mypy --strict` clean (221 files); `pyright` 0 errors; `ruff` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the two shipped tiers are evidence-grade for pairing drift, foreign/tampered rows, and the `top_k` inflation class — bars-free, O(artifacts + total rows) offline work, no O(1)-total claim; 670. **DEC-MUTATION-GATE-COMPUTE-001 — the `compute.py` fold-in (#590's "next ratchet", restated by #615/#624) EXECUTED: `brutex/metrics/compute.py` (Sharpe / Sortino / drawdown / Welford-Pébay moments — the last ranking-math module outside the zero-survivor mutation gate) joins `mutation.yml`'s per-module loop at ZERO surviving mutants** (2026-06-12). **Measured BEFORE (mutmut 2.5.1, Python 3.12.3, focused runner `pytest tests/unit/test_metrics_compute.py -x -q --no-header` wrapped `sh -c '… || exit 1'` per #624):** 357 mutants — 341 killed, **16 SURVIVED, 3 untested** (leftovers of an interrupted first pass; resolved by the fresh full AFTER run). Survivor triage, each against the real code path: **5 KILLABLE** — the two Stage-4 dataclass defaults `None → ""` (real field corruption), `sum_mfe = 0 → 1` (floor division hides it except at n=1), `largest_loss = 0 → 1` (visible exactly when there are no losers), the ruin-boundary `<= 1` flip (a 1-paisa terminal equity is observably NOT ruin); **11 PROVABLY EQUIVALENT** — 4 annotation-only `| None → & None` flips (PEP 563 / local annotations never evaluated), 2 dead-store inits (`current_dd_bars`: first loop iteration always has drop == 0, the else-branch reassigns before any read), `max_holding = 0 → 1` (dominated by the ClosedTrade `holding_bars >= 1` invariant + the non-empty-trades guard), `end_equity <= 0 → < 0` (at the boundary the else-branch computes growth 0.0 → exactly -100.0, identical to the ruin clamp), the dead CAGR lower clamp `max(-100.0, ·)` (positive annualised growth ⇒ argument ≥ -100.0 after rounding), the Sortino filter `< → <=` (an admitted r == 0.0 contributes r·r == 0.0), and the unreachable `if n_trades else 0.0` arm (zero-trade rows return earlier). **What shipped:** (1) **7 new targeted tests** in `tests/unit/test_metrics_compute.py` (Stage-4 defaults `is None` on both construction paths; n=1 exact MFE/MAE pins; no-losers `largest_losing_trade_paisa == 0`; the 1-paisa-terminal-equity boundary pinned byte-exact `cagr_pct == 100.0 * (1/1_000_000 - 1.0)` and `!= -100.0`; the end-equity-zero ruin pin `== -100.0`; a byte-exact `==` Sortino pin replicating the implementation's own expressions over a scratch+positive mix — named protection for the filter-threshold mutants, upgrading the prior `pytest.approx`; a ResultMetrics slots pin); (2) **observability restructures instead of blanket pragmas** (the #615 cast-extraction precedent): the ruin condition re-phrased `<= 0` → `< 1` (identical on ints; EVERY comparison mutant of it is now killable — both flips clamp a 1-paisa row to -100.0 and die on the boundary test), the CAGR cap arithmetic extracted to its own mutable line so only the dead `max(-100.0, ·)` carries a pragma, the Sortino RMS arithmetic split onto an unmarked line with only the equivalence-carrying filter pragma'd, and the dead `else 0.0` guard REMOVED outright; (3) **line-scoped `# pragma: no mutate` markers with in-code proof comments** for the remaining equivalent classes, real line-mates named to their pinning tests in the comments (the #615 convention); the 3 previously-untested IDs resolved in-run). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12.3):** 81 tests in the focused file; full unit suite 5951 passed (1 pre-existing skip); smoke 14 passed; `ruff` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict brutex` 0 issues / 224 files; `pyright` 0 errors; `--cov=brutex.metrics` shows compute.py at 100.00% line+branch (235 stmts / 44 branches / 0 miss). **DISCOVERED, tracked, not fixed here (Golden Rule #10):** `scripts/ci/validate_no_hallucination.py` pairs original vs code-stripped paragraphs BY INDEX, but stripping a fenced code block deletes a whole paragraph and misaligns every later pairing — proven live on PR #628's first body revision (the flagged "uncited" paragraph was a bare section header); 672. **DEC-SCANNER-PARAGRAPH-ALIGN-001 — (renumbered 671→672 pre-merge: open PR #631's DEC-GROWW-ADAPTER-LEAF-001 claimed and merged #671 first, P-1 protocol) the no-hallucination citation scanner's paragraph-pairing defect FIXED: fenced code blocks no longer shift the keyword-paragraph / citation-paragraph alignment** (2026-06-12; executes the follow-up tracked in #670 after the defect was proven LIVE on PR #628 — a fully-cited body was MERGE BLOCKED with the "uncited" finding pointing at a bare section header). **The defect (scripts/ci/validate_no_hallucination.py):** `find_uncited_external_claims` split the ORIGINAL text and the code-STRIPPED text into paragraphs separately and zipped them BY INDEX; `strip_code_spans` deletes fenced blocks entirely, so a fence that was its own paragraph vanished from the stripped list and every later pairing shifted — a keyword hit in stripped paragraph i was citation-checked against original paragraph i, which after the shift was an UNRELATED block. The function's own comment claimed "both versions produce the same paragraph count + order" — false for fenced blocks. Reproduced under the OLD script (preserved via git): the PR-#628-shaped body (fence + a Dhan claim cited per CLAUDE.md §6 + an innocent header) exits 1 with the FENCE flagged as the uncited paragraph; the NEW script exits 0. **The fix:** remove fenced blocks FIRST (`strip_fenced_blocks`, which also handles fences CONTAINING blank lines that would otherwise leak their innards into prose paragraphs), split ONCE, then check each paragraph against itself — keywords on the inline-code-stripped view (`strip_inline_code`), citations on the paragraph as written. Single-split alignment is structural, not assumed. **Deliberate behaviour change, pinned by test:** a citation that exists ONLY inside a fenced block no longer satisfies the citation duty for prose claims (a quoted log is not a source); citations in INLINE backticks still count. **Tests:** 6 new regressions in `tests/unit/test_ci_no_hallucination_scanner.py` (`TestFencedBlockAlignment`, subprocess-invoking the REAL script like the CI job): the #628 reproduction passes; the same shape UNCITED stays blocked (no detection weakening); keywords inside single- and multi-paragraph fences don't trigger; inline-code citations count; fence-only citations don't. 12/12 file total. **Verified:** ruff + `ruff format` + `mypy --strict` + pyright clean on both files; smoke 14 passed; the fixed scanner re-run over the real PR #628 and #630 bodies still passes both. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the false-positive class is closed with the true-positive direction explicitly re-pinned; 🟡 the scanner remains a HEURISTIC (presence, not correctness, of citations — row 17 stays partial automation); 🟡 `validate_dec_ids.py` keeps its own `strip_code_spans` copy, which is SAFE there (global search, no paragraph pairing) but is a §11 COMMON duplication smell — consolidation is a tracked nicety, not a defect; 🚫 no other gate logic touched. **P-1 note:** at write time open PR #631 claimed ledger #670 (already consumed on main by DEC-MUTATION-GATE-COMPUTE-001 via PR #630); #631 then renumbered to #671 and MERGED first, so this unmerged entry moved to the next free #672 (the standing protocol, the #628→#629 race precedent). **Builds on:** #670 (the discovery + tracking) · DEC-HONESTY-AUDIT-RECONCILE-001 (the scanner's test-file lineage) · DEC-DEFINITION-OF-READY-001 / DEC-P0-005 (the PR-body gate family this hardens).

684. **DEC-SWEEP-CACHE-DEADLINE-001 — the 20%-flaky sweep-cache property test fixed at root cause: the missing `deadline=None` on an LMDB-on-disk hypothesis test (P-1 note: this entry takes #684 because open PR #643 claims #683)** (2026-06-12; closes the flake first observed by the DEC-COV-APP-BACKFILL-001 baseline run — then dismissed after a 5/5 green probe, an honest mistake this entry corrects: the sample was too small). **Measured:** a 20-run stress probe of `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_cache.py::test_property_recorded_combos_always_seen` produced **4 failures (20%)**, with failing runs at 4.2–7.7 s vs 2.6–3.2 s passes — the signature of hypothesis's default **200 ms per-example deadline**: the test carries `@given` with NO `@settings`, and every example opens a `SweepCache` (an LMDB environment ON DISK — env create + mmap), which routinely exceeds 200 ms under machine load (hypothesis then re-runs the slow example to confirm, producing the long failing runtimes and the `DeadlineExceeded` flake). Sitting in the unit suite that gates EVERY merge, this randomly blocked ~1 in 5 future PRs. **The fix (one decorator + the measured justification comment):** `@settings(deadline=None)` — exactly the established house convention for I/O-touching property tests (`tests/property/test_audit_chain_properties.py`, `test_bloom_invariants.py`, et al. all carry `deadline=None`); correctness is untouched (every example still runs and asserts; only the per-example wall-clock guard is lifted, which guards nothing meaningful for a disk-backed test). **Verified:** 25/25 stress runs of the whole file green post-fix (14 tests each); ruff + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the flake is reproduced, root-caused, and the fix is the named house convention, not a suppression — a genuine assertion failure still fails; 🟡 load-induced flakes are probabilistic — 25/25 post-fix vs 16/20 pre-fix is strong but not exhaustive proof; if it ever flakes again the failure mode will be different (not DeadlineExceeded) and gets its own diagnosis; 🚫 no production code, no other test semantics touched. **Builds on:** #678 (the observation) · the tests/property deadline=None convention · DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 (the P-1 numbering above).
