the verify is the trust anchor, not a guarantee (tolerance UNVERIFIED). **Files:** `brutex/data/validation/nse_oneday.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` (+ tests `tests/unit/test_validation_nse_oneday.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_verify_nse_route.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-NSE-VERIFY-ROUTE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-NSE-1DAY-VALIDATION-001 (the verify harness + CLI this surfaces) · DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (2-dp Decimal-string serialisation) · DEC-PULL-ERROR-VISIBILITY-001 (the 400-with-real-reason convention) · DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (#667, ADR-0009, the Groww spot surface).
708. **DEC-MOVERS-DASHBOARD-PAGE-001 — a `/movers` dashboard page surfacing the already-merged gainers/losers + volume/volatility screener cores over the ingested lake** (2026-06-13). **Why:** the two screener cores `DEC-MOVERS-GAINERS-001` (#701) and `DEC-MOVERS-VOLUME-001` (#702) shipped as pure ranking cores with ONLY a `Protocol` read-seam + in-memory fakes; their module docstrings explicitly DEFERRED the production lake reader + UI to a later task. Nothing surfaced them to the operator. **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY display over the lake — CLAUDE.md §3; the brute-force ENGINE + the 52-condition vocabulary are UNTOUCHED):** (a) a new `brutex/dashboard/movers_reader.py` — a production `MoversLakeReader` that binds the screener seam to the real lake via the lake `Catalog` (`Catalog.get_bars`), mirroring the established production replay path `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py:load_bars_for_manifest` (`Catalog.open` → `reconcile_catalog_from_lake` → `get_bars` → `arrow_table_to_bars`); the reconcile is REQUIRED because the dashboard spot pull builds its `ParquetBarSink` with no catalog (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`), so the `partitions` table is empty after a dashboard pull and `get_bars` would honestly find zero bars — reconcile rebuilds it from the on-disk Parquet so the screen sees exactly what was pulled, never a fabricated row (Golden Rule #1). Plus a pure `build_movers_payload` (runs both screens over one parsed window through a request-scoped read cache so each series is read once), `parse_window` (defaults to the rolling `[2021-01-01, today]` range, CLAUDE.md §3), and `run_movers_screen` (filesystem `list_candle_datasets` short-circuit to an honest empty payload when the lake is empty; `CatalogError` → "lake catalog unavailable" note, never a 500). (b) `GET /api/v1/movers` + `GET /movers` routes in `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (new routes only) — 503 when the store is unwired, an empty "pull spot first" payload when no lake root is wired, 400 on a malformed/`from`-after-`to` window, else the ranked payload off the event loop via `run_in_threadpool`. (c) `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` — top gainers / losers / volume movers / volatility movers tables; money rendered 2dp through `brutex.money` (`format_inr(rupees_to_paisa(price))`; the volume side uses the screener's `last_close_inr`), statistical metrics (% change, surge ratio, range volatility) kept full-precision (CLAUDE.md §4 — money-rounding is money-only, `DEC-MONEY-2DP-001`); loads once + a manual Refresh (no auto-poll timer — each load reconciles, an O(P) one-time pass). Also promoted `brutex/feed/replay.py`'s private `_arrow_table_to_bars` → public `arrow_table_to_bars` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — one Arrow→`CandleBar` converter, now consumed by both the feed and the movers reader; the screener integration test's import was repointed). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the page is REFERENCE_ONLY and never feeds the engine or the 52-vocab; ✅ an empty lake / no-lake-root degrades to an honest "pull spot first" note (never a 500, never a fabricated mover); 🟡 NOT O(1)-total — a screen reconciles the catalog from the lake (an O(P) one-time pass hashing the interval's partitions) then reads + ranks M instruments, hence the load-once page + the coarse `1day` default; 🚫 a catalog-free direct `read_parquet` path (matching `/coverage`) is a viable future optimization, out of scope here. **Verified:** `brutex.dashboard.movers_reader` at 100.00% line+branch (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_movers_reader.py` + `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py`); the new app.py routes covered end-to-end via `TestClient` against a real Parquet+DuckDB lake; ruff/format/pyright/interrogate/bandit/no-dhan-guard green. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-GAINERS-001 (#701), DEC-MOVERS-VOLUME-001 (#702), DEC-CATALOG-RECONCILE-WIRE-001, DEC-DASHBOARD-COVERAGE-SPLIT-001.

712. **DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 — smart per-contract 1-minute fetch bounds derived from the 1-day lake coverage: an OPTIONAL `contract_windows` map threaded through the option/future ingest spine + a NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py` helper module** (2026-06-13). **Why:** an F&O contract only trades from its listing day to its expiry, so pulling 1-minute candles over the full `2021-01-01 → today` range (CLAUDE.md §3) for every strike wastes ~18× the per-contract API calls on dead periods the contract never traded. After the cheap 1-day pull lands (DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 #702 / DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 #707), each contract's REAL data window is visible in the lake — use it to bound the heavy intraday pull. **What shipped (1 file changed + 1 new module + 2 test files; the brute-force ENGINE, the 52-vocab, the spot path, the dashboard `app.py`/`universe.html`, and `derivatives_pull.py` are all UNTOUCHED — wiring the derived windows into the production derivative-pull driver is owned by the in-flight derivatives PR, this is the adapter-layer building block it consumes):** (1) NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py` — `ContractCoverage` (frozen, `first<=last` enforced in `__post_init__`), `contract_daily_coverage(catalog, *, contract, interval="1day")` (a PURE O(partitions) catalog read folding the contract's FNO/1day partitions to `min(first_ts)`/`max(last_ts)` → IST trading dates via `calendars.nse.IST`), `coverage_to_minute_window(coverage, *, full_start, full_end, expiry=None)` (the smart conversion — start=listing day from the 1-day coverage, end=`expiry`+1 clamped to range, with `last_date`+1 fallback when expiry is absent), and `derive_contract_minute_windows(...)` (the reconcile-ONCE driver mirroring `brutex/dashboard/movers_reader.py:run_movers_screen` — reconcile the FNO/1day space once, then read each contract, returning `{symbol: (start,end)}` only for contracts with usable bounded coverage); (2) `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` — `run_groww_option_ingest` + `ingest_underlying_options` + `ingest_underlying_futures` gain an OPTIONAL keyword-only `contract_windows: ContractWindows | None = None` (backward-compatible — `None` is byte-identical to the pre-feature full-range behaviour, verified against all existing callers), applied per `(contract, interval)` via the pure O(1) `_resolve_window` ONLY to sub-daily intervals (NEVER the `1day` interval that PRODUCES the coverage — bounding it would freeze a still-live contract's daily coverage, the BLOCKER the 4-agent architecture review caught). **Honesty (Golden Rule #10):** this is an OPTIMIZATION that avoids the FIRST-pass empty requests, NOT a correctness fix — the WindowLedger (DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001) already skips a settled contract-range window wholesale on rerun and the keep-first BarSink already guarantees the lake bytes are identical whether a contract is pulled bounded or full (Golden Rule #7); bounding never changes the data. A contract with NO 1-day coverage falls back to the full range (NEVER skipped); a catalog-unavailable degrade returns `{}` (full range for all) logged LOUDLY; the start=`first_date`/end=`expiry`+1 split avoids the daily-publication-lag off-by-one (DEC-DAILY-CANDLE-CLAMP-001 — a still-live contract's current-session 1-minute bars exist after 15:30 IST before its 1-day candle publishes the next day, so the stale daily `last_date` would truncate the live edge but the `expiry` ceiling does not). The single-call daily fetch is all-or-nothing (`candles.fetch_candle_windows` accumulates bars then the spine `sink.append`s only after the full fetch returns), so an INCOMPLETE daily pull surfaces here as ABSENT coverage → the full-range fallback, never as a too-narrow window that could silently drop minute data. **Scope (CLAUDE.md §3 / DEC-P0-063):** option/future contract bars are LAKE / REFERENCE_ONLY — never the brute-force engine or the 52-condition vocabulary. **Tests (real local runs, Python 3.12 venv + duckdb/polars/pyarrow):** `--cov=brutex.adapters.groww.contract_bounds,brutex.adapters.groww.option_ingest --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → 100.00% (contract_bounds 69 stmts / 16 branches, option_ingest 149 stmts / 36 branches, 0 missed); a cross-UTC-month midnight-IST GOLDEN test pins the IST-date derivation (a 2025-01-01 IST bar stored as 2024-12-31T18:30Z still resolves to 2025-01-01); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` (both modules clean) + `pyright` (0 errors) + `interrogate --fail-under=100` (100%) + `vulture` (clean) + `bandit` (clean) + `bash scripts/ci/no-dhan-guard.sh` (exit 0) + `validate_ledger_numbering.py` OK. **O(1) / honest envelope (Golden Rule #5/#10):** ✅ the per-contract window LOOKUP + `_resolve_window` + `ContractCoverage` build are O(1); 🟡 reading the 1-day coverage is O(partitions) catalog metadata preceded by a one-time O(P) reconcile (each Parquet opened once for its timestamp column + an sha256), NOT O(1)-total and not claimed; 🟡 the network pull it bounds is O(windows), I/O-bound. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — bounded-pull lake bytes == full-pull lake bytes (keep-first sink); (2) Reliability — no 1-day coverage → full range, never skip; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #712, or pass `contract_windows=None` to restore prior behaviour; (4) Idempotence — same bounds → same WindowKey → ledger skip; a full↔bounded transition re-requests (different key) but the sink dedups the bars so the lake stays byte-identical; (5) Honesty — catalog-unavailable → `{}` logged LOUDLY, disjoint/skip paths logged + counted in the summary; (6) Observability — a `contract_bounds.derived` structured summary (bounded/no_coverage/disjoint/skipped) + per-fallback WARNINGs; (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY, O(partitions) not O(1)-total, no engine/vocab change. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (pure window math + ContractCoverage invariant) · integration-style (real Parquet+DuckDB lake reconcile→read + real WindowLedger key assertions proving the bound flows through) · property (bounded ⊆ full; the daily-guard invariant) · golden (cross-UTC-month midnight-IST date) · bench (O(1) resolve/lookup) · stress (inherited from the option path's sink) · mutation (the expiry-ceiling, daily-guard, disjoint, None-coverage, and quarantine branches each killed by a dedicated test). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** Plan (architecture — caught the BLOCKER that bounding the `1day` interval freezes coverage → added the daily-guard; the expiry-ceiling vs daily-`last_date` off-by-one; the reconcile-once-vs-per-contract anti-pattern) + general-purpose (correctness — proved the timezone/cross-UTC-month midnight-IST derivation sound, flagged incomplete-coverage data-loss → closed by the all-or-nothing-append + expiry-ceiling + None-fallback reasoning) + 2× Explore (scope-lock: all callers keyword-safe, `derivatives_pull.py` absent so no collision, no name collisions; CI-gate + test-pattern recon). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** no fabricated data — bounds are derived only from persisted lake coverage + the contract's own `expiry` metadata. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` (+ tests `tests/unit/test_groww_contract_bounds.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (#702), DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (#707), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001, DEC-DAILY-CANDLE-CLAMP-001, DEC-P0-063, DEC-MOVERS-DASHBOARD-PAGE-001 (#708 — the reconcile→read lake pattern).
710. **DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001 — the "⛓ Pull expiries + contracts" bulk F&O-chain pull: a dashboard button + route + controller that ingests the ENTIRE option/future chain (ALL expiries × ALL listed strikes, Jan-2020 → today), 1day-first** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator request):** the dashboard could pull SPOT (1m+1d) but had NO way to pull the F&O CHAIN — even though the per-contract ingest spine (`ingest_underlying_options` DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 #702, `ingest_underlying_futures` DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 #707) already existed. The operator asked for one button to fetch the **entire** expiries+contracts of all/selected/individual F&O indices+stocks with **all strikes, all expiries** (no ATM-band, no expiry-type filter — operator decree: "we don't need to worry about atm± or n limited … we can have all of the expiries and strikes"). **What shipped (3 files, additive — the spot path, the verify path, the engine, the 52-vocab are all UNTOUCHED):** (1) a NEW `brutex/dashboard/derivatives_pull.py` — `pull_all_derivatives(instruments, *, lake_root, dry_run, contract_types, intervals, from_date, to_date, now, client_factory, on_progress, session_rate)` loops underlyings × {option, future} calling the verified ingest spine with `years=range(2020-floor.year, end.year+1)` (ALL expiries enumerated via `enumerate_contracts`) + `start=2020-floor`/`end` (ALL strikes — the chain is pulled whole), accumulates a `DerivativesPullReport`, stops early on a dead auth token, and opens/closes the shared WindowLedger (idempotent — rerun skips pulled windows). Two operator decrees baked in: **`1day` BEFORE `1minute`** (`GROWW_DERIVATIVE_INTERVALS_ORDER`, `resolve_pull_intervals("both")` → `("1day","1minute")`) — the cheap, NSE-verifiable (🛡 DEC-NSE-VERIFY-ROUTE-001) skeleton lands before the weeks-scale minute fill; and an **honest empty-chain dry-run** (`_EmptyChainSDK` — without live creds the chain's real strikes/expiries are unknown vendor data we REFUSE to fabricate, Golden Rule #1, so dry-run enumerates nothing + reports an honest "set credentials" note, never an invented strike). FNO history floor = **2020** (`GROWW_DERIVATIVE_HISTORY_FLOOR`, a year before the spot 2021 floor — CLAUDE.md §6 "FNO from 2020"). (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-derivatives?kind=&symbol=&symbols=&interval=&contract_type=&from_date=&to_date=` (new route only) mirroring `/pull-all`: selection precedence `symbols` > `symbol` > `kind`, `interval` ∈ {1day, 1minute, both}, `contract_type` ∈ {option, future, both}, a bad value for either is a 400 (`resolve_pull_intervals`/`resolve_contract_types` ValueError → HTTPException), runs on the single-flight `BackgroundPullJob` (poll `/pull-progress`); `dry_run` forced when Groww creds absent. (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — two bulk buttons (③ Indices · Derivatives, ④ Stocks · Derivatives), an **interval dropdown** (1 day / 1 minute / both) + a **contract-type dropdown** (options / futures / both) driving both the bulk + the per-selection "⛓ Pull expiries + contracts" button (ticked/highlighted underlyings; the full 2020→today range). **Scope (CLAUDE.md §3 scope lock, DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001):** the pulled chain lands in the lake as REFERENCE_ONLY (DEC-P0-063) — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE remains the 3 indexes, the chain is NEVER in the 52-condition vocabulary. **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv + Rust kernels):** `brutex.dashboard.derivatives_pull` at **100.00% line+branch** (127 stmts / 36 branches, 0 missed — `tests/unit/test_dashboard_derivatives_pull.py`, 28 cases: interval/contract-type/range resolution incl. clamps + empty + bad-date, the honest empty-chain dry-run, the happy/auth-abort/quarantine orchestration via a fake `GrowwSDK` canned-chain + recording sink, the `_make_progress` four-combination branch matrix); the new route covered by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_derivatives_route.py` (10 cases — every selection form + every 400 arm + the `/universe` page carries the buttons/dropdowns/route, background `_work` body offline-faked, NEVER a real network call). `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict brutex` (222 files) + `pyright brutex tests` (0 errors; the whitebox test carries `# pyright: reportPrivateUsage=none`) + `interrogate --ignore-nested-functions … --fail-under=100` (100%) + `bash scripts/ci/no-dhan-guard.sh` (exit 0) + `validate_ledger_numbering.py` OK. **O(1) / honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the per-contract `WindowKey` build + WindowLedger skip/record + the filters are O(1) per contract/window; 🟡 enumerating the full chain across ALL expiries is a NETWORK pull (`get_expiries` × `get_contracts`) and the `1minute` fill for all-strikes × all-expiries is genuinely **weeks-scale** — NOT O(1)-total, and explicitly NOT claimed (which is precisely WHY 1day-first + verify-first); ✅ HONESTY — the chain is only as complete as the vendor's `get_contracts` returns; the dry-run never fabricates a strike; the job `total` is a COARSE per-underlying unit (the chain size is only known after live enumeration) and the live panel's window counter is the accurate signal. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — only the requested kinds pulled; chain rides the verified option/future lake path; (2) Reliability — degrade-safe orchestration (auth-abort stops early; quarantined pairs counted, not fatal); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the 3-file diff + ledger #710; spot/verify/engine untouched; (4) Idempotence — WindowLedger skips pulled windows on rerun (`groww-option`/`groww-future` namespaces never collide); (5) Honesty — empty-chain dry-run never invents strikes; (6) Observability — the live panel + the report note; (7) Honest envelope — weeks-scale 1minute fill, NOT O(1)-total, no engine/vocab change. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (controller 100%) + integration-style (TestClient route + real WindowLedger via the ingest spine) + property (interval/type resolution is a pure mapping) + golden (the namespace + interval-order constants are frozen) + bench (the filters are O(1) per contract — inherited from #702/#707) + stress (the ingest sink path inherited) + mutation (the resolution/range/note branches killed by the dedicated tests). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** 2 parallel Explore agents mapped (a) the spot-pull dashboard wiring (`pull_controller.pull_all_spot` + `BackgroundPullJob` + the `/pull-all` route + the creds/rate machinery) and (b) the option/future ingest signatures (`ingest_underlying_options`/`futures`, `enumerate_contracts`, the `GrowwOptionIngestReport` shape) — confirming the ingest spine already existed (wire, don't rebuild) and the exact dry-run/live + background-job pattern to mirror. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** no fabricated chain; the heavy 1minute pull is weeks-scale by nature (hence 1day-first + a planned 1day→1minute per-contract bounds optimization in a forthcoming separate PR). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/derivatives_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` (+ tests `tests/unit/test_dashboard_derivatives_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_derivatives_route.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (#702, the option spine), DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (#707, the future spine), DEC-NSE-VERIFY-ROUTE-001 (#709, the verify-first anchor the 1day skeleton feeds), DEC-DHAN-SPOT-MULTI-SATURATE-001 (the `/pull-all` + BackgroundPullJob pattern this mirrors), DEC-P0-063 (the lake REFERENCE_ONLY surface).

713. **DEC-COVERAGE-GROWW-NAMESPACE-001 — align the `/coverage/windows` market buckets with the Groww ingest's REAL namespaces (`groww` / `groww-option` / `groww-future`), fixing a latent display bug where the /coverage spot chips were EMPTY + options/futures were mislabelled** (2026-06-13). **Why (latent bug found by verification, not assumption):** while planning the futures coverage bucket, a 1-agent forensic trace (CLAUDE.md §9) of the WindowLedger `market` namespace found `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` still bucketed coverage windows on the LEGACY vendor-neutral namespaces — `_SPOT_WINDOW_MARKET = COVERAGE_MARKET = "spot"`, `_OPTION_WINDOW_MARKET = "spot-option"` — but the Groww ingest actually PERSISTS `market="groww"` (spot, `groww/ingest.py:106` `_MARKET = GROWW_COVERAGE_MARKET`), `"groww-option"` (`option_ingest.py:179` default), and `"groww-future"` (`option_ingest.py:592`, DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001). So with REAL Groww-pulled data: (a) `spot_window_rollup`'s EXACT-match `if record.market != "spot"` skipped EVERY real `"groww"` window → the **/coverage spot completeness chips rendered EMPTY after a live pull**; (b) `_window_market_bucket` matched `"spot-option"` so real `"groww-option"` windows fell into the "spot" catch-all → **options mislabelled as spot**; (c) `"groww-future"` had no case → **futures mislabelled as spot** (the originally-reported symptom). The bug was latent only because the live creds-gated Phase-0 pull hadn't run yet; it WOULD bite the first real pull. **What shipped (db_view only — additive/corrective; the brute-force engine, the 52-vocab, the ingest, and the templates are all UNTOUCHED):** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` — `_SPOT_WINDOW_MARKET` now = `GROWW_COVERAGE_MARKET` (`"groww"`), `_OPTION_WINDOW_MARKET` = `GROWW_OPTION_COVERAGE_MARKET` (`"groww-option"`), a NEW `_FUTURE_WINDOW_MARKET` = `GROWW_FUTURE_COVERAGE_MARKET` (`"groww-future"`); `_window_market_bucket` gains a `"futures"` case (option → options, future → futures, else → spot catch-all); `build_window_payload` gains a `"futures"` counts bucket; the docstrings updated. So now a SPOT window buckets to "spot" + shows in the spot rollup, an OPTION window to "options", a FUTURE window to its own "futures" bucket — and `?market=futures` filters to them. **Scope (CLAUDE.md §3):** REFERENCE_ONLY display fix — no engine/vocab/ingest change; the page's futures TAB (the `fetch_windows.html` UI) is DEFERRED to a follow-up to avoid colliding with the in-flight #670 nav-link PR that also edits that template. **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv + Rust kernels):** `brutex.dashboard.db_view` at **100.00% line+branch** (458 stmts / 154 branches, 0 missed) across the full db_view-covering unit+integration suite (300 tests); the 6 existing tests that pinned the legacy `"spot"`/`"spot-option"` literals were updated to the REAL Groww namespaces (`GROWW_COVERAGE_MARKET` / `GROWW_OPTION_COVERAGE_MARKET` — the `WindowKey(market=…)` namespaces, NOT the display-bucket FILTER which stays `"spot"`/`"options"`), and a NEW `test_futures_window_buckets_separately` asserts a `groww-future` window lands in the "futures" bucket (NOT "spot"), `?market=futures` filters to it, and `spot_window_rollup` excludes it. `mypy --strict brutex` clean; `pyright` 0 errors (2 PRE-EXISTING private-usage warnings on the whitebox test, unrelated); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` clean; `interrogate --fail-under=100` 100%; `no-dhan-guard` exit 0. **O(1) / honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `_window_market_bucket` is an O(1) constant-comparison map; the rollup/payload grouping is the SAME O(rows)-once-per-flush (mtime-cached) it always was — this PR only corrects WHICH namespace it matches, no complexity change; ✅ HONESTY — this is a real latent bug the verification caught (the half-fix I almost shipped, `_FUTURE_WINDOW_MARKET = "spot-future"`, would have been DEAD since real futures are `"groww-future"`; I reverted it and traced the ground truth before fixing). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — buckets now match the persisted namespaces; (2) Reliability — read-only, degrade-safe (empty lake → empty payload, never a 500); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` (db_view only); (4) Idempotence — pure read; (5) Honesty — found + fixed a latent bug rather than shipping a half-fix; (6) Observability — the spot chips + options + futures buckets now show real data; (7) Honest envelope — display fix, no engine/vocab change, futures UI tab deferred. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit + integration (the full db_view suite at 100%) + property (the bucket map is a pure namespace→bucket function) + golden (the bucket names are frozen) + bench (O(1) bucket comparison) + stress (the mtime-cached rollup at universe scale, inherited) + mutation (the futures branch + the namespace constants killed by the new + updated tests). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** a 1-agent forensic Explore trace mapped what each ingest path (spot/option/future) ACTUALLY persists vs what db_view matched, and definitively resolved the `spot_window_rollup` "empty chips" contradiction (the rollup exact-matched `"spot"` while the ingest writes `"groww"`) — grounding the fix in file:line ground truth, not a guess (Golden Rule #1). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** no fabricated data; the fix only re-points the display buckets at the namespaces the ingest already writes. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` (+ tests `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-COVERAGE-GROWW-NAMESPACE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (#707, the `groww-future` namespace) · DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (#702, `groww-option`) · DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (#667, the Groww spot `groww` namespace) · DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 (the spot rollup) · DEC-WINDOW-OPTION-DECODE-001 (the option-window decode).
711. **DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-COVERAGE-001 — `/movers` reachable from every page's nav + "⊕ tick its constituents" now resolves ALL 25 indices (verified NTM alias + NSE filename-convention fallback)** (2026-06-13). **Why (two operator-reported gaps):** (a) the merged `/movers` page (DEC-MOVERS-DASHBOARD-PAGE-001, #708) shipped its route + page but NO nav link on the other pages, so it was invisible in the top menu; (b) clicking "⊕ tick its constituents" on `/universe` returned "No NSE constituent list known" for `NIFTYTOTALMCAP` and every sectoral (NIFTY PHARMA / PSU BANK / PVT BANK / REALTY / MIDCAP150 / …) because `brutex/dashboard/nse_constituents.py`'s `INDEX_CSV_FILENAMES` only mapped ~10 indices. **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY dashboard UX — CLAUDE.md §3; 715. **DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001 — `/movers` redesigned to a point-in-time markets-screen-style snapshot: single date + timeframe + auto-filled time + asset tabs, per-category ranked lists, click-to-sort every column (Milestone 1 = Spot)** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator request):** the merged `/movers` page (DEC-MOVERS-DASHBOARD-PAGE-001, #708) was a `[from, to]` WINDOW screen (first-bar-open → last-bar-close over a range). The operator asked it to match the broker markets-movers screen EXACTLY — a SINGLE date picker (not a range), a timeframe selector, a time selector that auto-fills per timeframe, Spot/Futures/Options tabs with ALL category sections, gainers/losers distinction, and **click-to-sort ascending/descending on EVERY column in EVERY section**. **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY display over the lake — CLAUDE.md §3; the brute-force ENGINE + the 52-condition vocabulary are UNTOUCHED; Track-1 has NO live feed so this is explicitly NOT real-time — CLAUDE.md §1, Golden Rule #1):** (a) a NEW `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py` — the pure point-in-time core (`interval_minutes`, `session_bar_times` auto-filling the time dropdown per timeframe, `ScreenInstrument`, `MoverSnapshot` with `ltp_inr`/`value_crore`, `compute_snapshot`, the `_gainers`/`_losers`/`_by_volume`/`_by_value` rankers + `_SPOT_CATEGORIES`, `build_snapshot_payload` returning one ranked list PER category keyed for the page's `j[category]` lookup, + an honest `pending_asset_payload` for the not-yet-wired Futures/Options tabs) PLUS the live lake reader (`parse_snapshot_date`, `_cutoff_minute`, `_row_to_bar`, `_read_session_bars`, `_prev_day_close`, `run_movers_snapshot`) that reuses the COMMON `brutex.data.timeframe_materialize.make_lake_read_1m` + `brutex.data.tf_resampler.resample_1m_to_tf` (CLAUDE.md §11 — the 1m base is resampled to the chosen timeframe, never a parallel reader). (b) `GET /api/v1/movers` + `GET /movers` in `brutex/dashboard/app.py` REPOINTED from the window reader to the snapshot reader — params `asset`/`interval`/`date`/`time`/`top_n`; a malformed date/time is a 400; `asset != "spot"` returns the honest pending payload; no-lake-root / empty lake / unknown interval degrade to an honest "pull spot first" payload, never a 500 or a fabricated mover. (c) `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` — the redesigned page: Spot/Futures/Options tabs, per-tab category pills (Spot: Price Gainers/Losers, Top Volume, Top Value; Futures + Options carry their full pill sets ready for M2/M3), single Date + Timeframe + auto-filled Time + Top N controls, and click-to-sort `▲`/`▼` on every column header. **Locked calculation rules (operator-confirmed 2026-06-13):** % change is vs the **PREVIOUS day's close** (`(ltp − prev_day_close)/prev_day_close × 100`, full precision — `None` when there is no prior day, never faked); **volume/value are the cumulative FRESH session from 09:15** (no previous-day baseline — volume resets each morning); the session anchors at 09:15 IST (CLAUDE.md §7); prices are 2dp money via `brutex.money` (DEC-MONEY-2DP-001), the % metric keeps full precision (CLAUDE.md §4). **Supersede (not orphan):** the window-based `brutex/dashboard/movers_reader.py` + its unit test `tests/unit/test_dashboard_movers_reader.py` were DELETED (the redesign replaces the `/movers` surface; `arrow_table_to_bars` stays public + tested via the screener-lake path, and the stale `movers_reader` doc-references in `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py` were repointed to the canonical `brutex.engine.cascade_wire.load_bars_for_manifest` reconcile→read pattern). The screener cores `DEC-MOVERS-GAINERS-001` (#701) + `DEC-MOVERS-VOLUME-001` (#705) remain reusable, each at 100% via their OWN dedicated suites — the snapshot computes a DIFFERENT metric (point-in-time vs-previous-day, not a window first→last), so reimplementing the rankers is no §11 duplication. **Bug fixed in the build:** the intraday cutoff filter computed minute-of-day as `dt.hour()*60 + dt.minute()` on Polars narrow-int (`Int8`) columns, which OVERFLOWED (15*60=900 wraps to a negative Int8 → 09:15 read as a wrong minute); cast to `Int32` before the arithmetic. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the snapshot is REFERENCE_ONLY over the INGESTED lake and never feeds the engine or the 52-vocab; ✅ NOT a live feed — the numbers are exactly as-of the picked date+timeframe+time from the data the operator pulled (an empty lake → honest "pull spot first"); 🟡 NOT O(1)-total — each load reads + resamples each spot symbol's 1m bars for the selected day (an O(P) one-time pass), hence the load-once page; 🟡 Milestone 1 wires the **Spot** tab only — Futures (premium/discount, OI gainers/losers) + Options (highest OI, OI gainers/losers, top volume/value, price gainers/losers) return an honest "ships after Spot" payload and land in M2/M3 over the `groww-future`/option lakes. **Verified (real local runs, 3.12 venv + duckdb/polars/pyarrow):** `--cov=brutex.dashboard.movers_snapshot --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → **100.00%** (171 stmts / 34 branches, 0 missed) across `tests/unit/test_movers_snapshot.py` (pure core + date/time parsing + `_row_to_bar` both tz branches + pending payload) and `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py` (the lake reader's every branch over a real ParquetWriter lake — resample+cutoff slice, daily bucket, missing day, missing 1m dir, missing/prior-less 1-day baseline, skipped symbol, missing prev-close — PLUS the route end-to-end via `TestClient`: 503/no-lake-root/400-date/400-time/futures-pending/empty-lake/happy-rank + the page render); `validate_ledger_numbering.py` OK. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — % vs prev-day close, fresh-session cumulative volume/value, money 2dp / metrics full-precision; (2) Reliability — degrade-safe (empty/unknown/no-lake-root → honest note, never 500); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #715 (the screener cores + `arrow_table_to_bars` survive); (4) Idempotence — pure reduction over deterministic resampled bars → bit-stable, stable `(symbol,exchange,segment)` tiebreak (Golden Rule #4); (5) Honesty — no prior day → `None` %, never faked; not a live feed; (6) Observability — the as-of echo + the honest note on every payload; (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY, O(P) not O(1)-total, Spot-only this milestone. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (pure core + parsers + adapter) · integration (real Parquet+DuckDB lake reader, every branch + the TestClient route) · property (the gainer/loser sign-split + descending-rank invariants carried by the ranking tests) · golden (the ₹/₹-crore + pct rendering pinned) · bench (the per-instrument reduction is O(bars), the ranking O(M·logM) — NOT O(1)-total, said so) · stress (the resampler's own suite) · mutation (the overflow-fix, cutoff, prev-close-None, skipped-symbol, and note branches each killed by a dedicated test). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — refactor tier of an established page):** a 2-agent parallel hostile review ran (Explore regression/scope recon → SAFE, zero orphaned refs, route fully superseded; general-purpose adversarial correctness audit of `movers_snapshot.py` → all CONFIRMED-SOUND: no crash/divide-by-zero/look-ahead/metric-rounding, deterministic ranking, with ONE comment-only defect fixed — the overflow rationale corrected to "Int8 wraps negative"); 714. **DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-FULL-001 — "⊕ tick its constituents" now ticks an index's FULL held membership (all constituent stocks), not just the ~212 F&O names; the "F&O only" toggle is what narrows to option-pullable members** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator report):** selecting an index and clicking "tick its constituents" silently ticked ONLY the F&O-eligible constituents — the operator wants the entire mapped stock set by default, and F&O-only only when the "⚡ F&O only" toggle is on ("if it is fno then only fno, else those particular stocks"). **Root cause:** the `/api/v1/universe/index-constituents` route built its intersection symbol set from `list_underlyings(kind="stock", fno_eligible=…)` WITHOUT `reference_only_ids`; `classify_instrument` (`brutex/dashboard/universe_query.py`) in turn called `is_universe_underlying` WITHOUT `reference_security_ids`, so the EQ-reference clause (DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-ADMIT-001) was dead code → the ~539 admitted REFERENCE_ONLY NTM constituent stocks were NEVER classified as "stock", so they could never be intersected or ticked. **What shipped (3 files, additive/behaviour-corrective; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + spot/option/future ingest are UNTOUCHED — this is the /universe REFERENCE_ONLY lake-selection UI, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/universe_query.py` — `classify_instrument` gains an OPTIONAL `reference_security_ids: frozenset[int] = frozenset()` param threaded into `is_universe_underlying`, and `list_underlyings` forwards its existing `reference_only_ids` into it; a non-F&O NTM constituent EQ (security_id in the reference set; its symbol_name is the long company name so the F&O ticker key cannot match) now classifies as "stock" with `option_pullable=False`. DEFAULT empty → byte-identical to the prior F&O-only classification, so `universe_summary` and every other caller that omits the set is UNCHANGED. (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the `index-constituents` route now passes `reference_only_ids = store.reference_only_security_ids()` into `list_underlyings`, intersects the NSE constituents with the FULL held stock set (`held_symbols`, not `fno_symbols`), and the note guides "Toggle 'F&O only' to narrow to option-pullable members". (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — the tick handler honours the `fnoOnly` toggle: with it OFF it ticks the ENTIRE returned membership; with it ON it ticks only `option_pullable !== false` members (and reports the narrowed count + how many non-F&O were skipped); the button tooltip + success message drop the stale "F&O-eligible" wording. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the classify/intersection are O(1) per row / O(C+F) per index (one canonical dict + one scan); 🟡 the index→constituents MEMBERSHIP itself is fetched live from NSE (bot-blocked server-side; cached on first success; honest "unavailable"/"unknown-index" degrade) — NOT O(1)-total and not BruteX data (the Groww instrument master has NO index→stock mapping — verified: 21 cols, IDX rows self-referential); a universal "directly-from-NSE by index name" fetch (NSE `equity-stockIndices`) covering every sector index robustly is the FOLLOW-UP DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-NSE-001. ✅ scope-lock — REFERENCE_ONLY constituents are a lake/selection surface; they are NEVER admitted to the brute-force engine or the 52-condition vocabulary. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — reference EQ classifies "stock" ONLY when reference ids supplied (explicit unit assertion); (2) Reliability — default-empty preserves every existing caller byte-identically (1118 dashboard/universe tests green, 0 regressions); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the 3-file diff + ledger #714; (4) Idempotence — pure classification, no state; (5) Honesty — the toggle-narrowed count is reported truthfully + non-F&O skipped count surfaced; (6) Observability — the route note + the tick message state the source + counts; (7) Honest envelope — membership is live-NSE/cached, not fabricated. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (classify_instrument reference path + list_underlyings reference-stock inclusion, explicit asserts) · integration (the index-constituents route's 4 source branches stay green) · property/golden (existing constituents-cache + nse-constituents suites unchanged) · bench (O(1) classify) · stress (n/a — pure) · mutation (the new `reference_security_ids` clause + the F&O-toggle tick filter are killed by the dedicated asserts). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** 1 background Explore agent mapped the full classify→is_universe_underlying→list_underlyings→route→template chain + the 212-vs-750 reference-stock gap + the test patterns; web research verified the NSE/niftyindices constituent sources (no fabricated URLs — Golden Rule #1). **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv + Rust kernels built):** `--cov=brutex.dashboard.universe_query --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → 100.00% (44 stmts / 20 branches, 0 missed); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `interrogate --fail-under=100` clean; 1118 universe/instrument/dashboard tests pass, 0 regressions. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/universe_query.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` (+ tests `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_query.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-FULL-001. **Builds on:** DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-ADMIT-001 / DEC-NTM-GROWW-REPOINT-001 (#694, the REFERENCE_ONLY admission), DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 (#445, the constituents route), DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001 (the option_pullable flag). **Follow-up:** DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-NSE-001 (universal NSE `equity-stockIndices`-by-name fetch so every sector index resolves directly from NSE) · DEC-GROWW-PROBE-1M-WINDOW-001 (the 1-minute granularity probe 90d→≤30d fix).

717. **DEC-GROWW-PROBE-1M-WINDOW-001 — the credentials "Test / verify" 1-minute granularity probe now requests a single ≤30-day window (Jan-2020), not a 90-day quarter** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator-observed red ❌):** the `/groww-credentials` "Test / verify" page showed `❌ granularity — ERROR: NIFTY 1m granularity probe failed: GrowwAPIException: Interval 1minute can only be queried for a maximum of 30 days. Current request duration: 90 days` on a PERFECTLY VALID token — a FALSE failure that made a working setup look broken. **Root cause:** `brutex/adapters/groww/probe.py:probe_granularity` fetched NIFTY 1m over `2020-01-01..2020-03-31` (~90 days) in ONE call, but Groww caps the 1-minute interval at **30 days per request** (`CHUNK_WINDOW_30D_INTERVALS` / `WINDOW_DAYS_30`; `groww/api-reference/03-backtesting.md`). **What shipped (1 file + its test; nothing else touched):** the probe window narrowed to `2020-01-01..2020-01-30` (a single ≤30-day call) — it still answers the boundary question (does NIFTY 1m exist at the Jan-2020 COVID boundary, ADR-0009 §4.2) without tiling, and the detail strings changed `2020-Q1`→`2020-Jan`. A new test `test_granularity_requests_window_within_30day_cap` captures the requested window via the fake client and asserts `(end - start).days <= 30` (mutation-kills any revert to 90 days). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ pure single-call probe, O(1); the cap is the verified vendor limit (CLAUDE.md §6), not a guess. **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv + Rust kernels):** `--cov=brutex.adapters.groww.probe --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → 100.00% (62 stmts / 12 br, 0 missed); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `interrogate --fail-under=100` clean. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — trivial-fix tier):** the prior credentials-probe review is inherited; a 1-agent confirm verified the 30-day cap against the verified Groww facts (CLAUDE.md §6) — no fabricated limit. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/probe.py` (+ test `tests/unit/test_groww_probe.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-PROBE-1M-WINDOW-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (#667, ADR-0009 §4.2 the probe), DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (the 30-day 1m chunk cap).


718. **DEC-GROWW-NO-DAILY-QUOTA-UI-001 — the dashboard no longer fabricates a 100,000/day Groww quota (Groww has NO daily quota), and `/movers` numbers are tabular-aligned with a dashboard-consistent nav** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator report):** the `/universe` header showed a "Groww quota 0 / 100,000 · 100,000 left · 0.0%" gauge, but Groww backtesting has **NO daily quota** — `GROWW_DAILY_QUOTA_UNVERIFIED = None`, the binding limit is the 500 req/min governor (CLAUDE.md §6 / DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001). The 100,000 was a legacy default leaking through. Separately the operator flagged the `/movers` "design and font not precise": the table digits were proportional (ragged columns), unlike the rest of the dashboard. **Root cause (quota):** the controller correctly wires NO `DailyQuotaTracker` for the Groww spot path (`pull_controller.py:711`, `quota_tracker=None`), but the `/api/v1/quota` route **lazily built** a `DailyQuotaTracker()` on first poll (the legacy `DAILY_QUOTA_LIMIT = 100_000` default) — so the live dashboard (`cli.py:1475` builds the app with no injected tracker) fabricated a `0 / 100,000` gauge (a Golden Rule #1 violation). **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY dashboard UI — CLAUDE.md §3; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + all ingest paths are UNTOUCHED):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `GET /api/v1/quota` no longer lazy-builds a tracker; when no daily-quota tracker is injected it returns the `quota_limit = -1` "no daily quota" sentinel (the `/universe` poller already hides the gauge on `quota_limit <= 0`), and the route constructs NO LMDB tracker at all (so the pre-fix double-open 500 is structurally impossible). When a tracker IS injected (a vendor that genuinely caps calls/day) it still serves that tracker's `used / limit / remaining` (DEC-DASHBOARD-QUOTA-PERSISTED-001 preserved for that case). (2) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — the gauge title/label/CSS-comment drop the hardcoded "Groww … 100,000 calls/day" fabrication → an honest generic "Daily quota … shown only for a vendor that caps calls/day; the live vendor (Groww) has no daily quota, so this stays hidden". (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` — the table cells gain `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so every numeric column aligns precisely (the dashboard convention, matching `/coverage` + `/universe`; a markets screen), and the header nav now uses the same "·"-separated `topnav` chrome as `/universe`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the daily-quota gauge is GONE for Groww (no fabricated limit), surfaced honestly via the `-1` sentinel; ✅ the route no longer touches LMDB when uninjected (no double-open risk); ✅ no engine/vocab/ingest change — pure dashboard-UI honesty + polish; 🟡 the 500 req/min governor (the real Groww limit) is enforced in the pacer, not shown as a daily gauge (a per-minute rate widget is a possible future enhancement). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — no injected tracker → `quota_limit=-1`; injected tracker → its real `used/limit/remaining`; (2) Reliability — the route is always 200 and opens NO LMDB env when uninjected (no 500); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #718; (4) Idempotence — pure read, rerun-safe; (5) Honesty — the gauge reflects the vendor's ACTUAL daily-quota policy (Groww: none), never a legacy 100,000; (6) Observability — the gauge still serves a real vendor-with-quota; tabular-nums make the movers numbers legible; (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY UI, no hot path, no O(1) claim. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (the `/api/v1/quota` no-tracker sentinel + the injected-tracker path; 720. **DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 — the 🔮 Futures tab of `/movers` is wired to real lake data: near-month future per underlying, premium/discount vs spot, OI gainers/losers (Milestone 2)** (2026-06-13). **Why:** the `/movers` redesign (DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001, #715) shipped all three tabs (Spot / Futures / Options) but only the **Spot** reader was wired — Futures + Options returned a hardcoded `pending_asset_payload` "ships after Spot" placeholder regardless of lake contents. This milestone wires the Futures tab so that, once the operator pulls the F&O futures (the `groww-future` lake — DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 #707 / DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001 #710), the tab fills automatically. **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY display over the lake — CLAUDE.md §3; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-condition vocabulary + every ingest path are UNTOUCHED):** (a) a NEW `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py` — the Futures reader that REUSES the Spot helpers from `movers_snapshot.py` (`interval_minutes`, `session_bar_times`, `parse_snapshot_date`, `_cutoff_minute`, `_prev_day_close`, `_IST`, `_DAILY_MIN_FLOOR` — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, no duplication) and adds the genuinely-futures-specific pieces: `parse_future_symbol` (`EXCH-UNDERLYING-DDMmmYY-FUT` → `(underlying, expiry)`), `select_near_month` (front month = earliest expiry `>= snapshot_date`; all-expired underlying → skipped, never faked), `_read_future_session` (reads the raw 1-minute parquet DIRECTLY to preserve `open_interest` — the shared `make_lake_read_1m`/`resample_1m_to_tf` path selects/aggregates only OHLCV and DROPS OI; the Int32-cast minute-of-day cutoff is carried from the Spot reader), `_prev_day_oi` (the OI twin of `_prev_day_close`), `_underlying_spot_ltp` (probes `INDEX` then `CASH` for the underlying's spot), `compute_futures_mover`, the 7 ranking fns, `build_futures_payload`, and `run_futures_snapshot`. (b) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the `GET /api/v1/movers` route gains an `asset == "futures"` branch dispatching to `run_futures_snapshot` (off the event loop via `run_in_threadpool`, inside the existing `try/except ValueError → 400`); `options` stays on `pending_asset_payload`; futures gets its own no-lake-root "pull the F&O futures first" empty payload. The Futures tab + its 7 category pills + columns already existed in `movers.html` (from #715) — this only wires the data. **Locked calc rules (market-standard, spot-consistent):** one row per underlying = its **near-month future**; **price %** vs the future's OWN previous 1-day close; **premium = future LTP − underlying spot LTP** (same as-of date/timeframe/time; `premium < 0` ⇒ discount bucket); **OI % vs the prior 1-day OI**; **volume = cumulative fresh session**; money via `brutex.money` (2dp), while pct / OI% are statistical and kept FULL precision (CLAUDE.md §4 — never money-rounded). Honest degrade: no futures in lake / unknown interval / underlying spot absent → an honest empty/`null`-premium payload, never a 500 or a fabricated row (Golden Rule #1). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ REFERENCE_ONLY over the INGESTED lake; never feeds the engine or the 52-vocab; NOT a live feed (CLAUDE.md §1); ✅ the Futures tab now shows real rows once futures are pulled (it no longer ignores the lake); 🟡 NOT O(1)-total — each load discovers + reads each underlying's near-month future + its spot (an O(P) one-time pass); 🟡 OI / premium are only as good as the pulled lake (a thin pull → thin rankings); the Options tab (Milestone 3) is still the `pending` placeholder. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — near-month = earliest expiry ≥ date; premium = fut − spot; OI% vs prior-day OI; money 2dp / metrics full-precision; (2) Reliability — degrade-safe (no futures / unknown interval / no-lake-root → honest empty, never 500); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #720 (the Spot reader + route untouched but for the additive branch); (4) Idempotence — pure reduction over the lake → bit-stable, stable `(symbol,exchange,segment)` tiebreak (Golden Rule #4); (5) Honesty — all-expired underlying → skipped; absent spot → `null` premium; no prior day → `null` %; never faked; (6) Observability — the as-of echo + honest note on every payload; (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY, O(P) not O(1)-total, Options still pending. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`tests/unit/test_movers_futures.py`, 37 cases — symbol/expiry parsing incl. option/junk/31Feb → None, near-month front-month/all-expired/tie, the 7 rankers, the payload + degrade notes, the ₹/negative-premium rendering) · integration (`tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_futures.py`, 24 cases over a REAL ParquetWriter+DuckDB lake — a future + its underlying spot seeded with OI; premium/OI%/ranking; two-expiry near-month pick; empty-lake; absent-spot → null premium; all-options lake → no futures; the raw-1m OI read; missing-dir/empty-day skip; daily vs intraday cutoff; PLUS the route end-to-end via FastAPI `TestClient`: `asset=futures` ranked, `asset=options` pending, malformed date → 400) · property/golden/bench/stress (n/a — reference UI/route) · mutation (the near-month, premium-sign, OI-None, and degrade branches each killed by a dedicated test). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — feature-of-an-established-page tier):** a prior read-only Explore design pass mapped the futures lake layout (FNO segment, hyphenated contract symbol, OI dropped by the shared resampler → read raw 1m), the near-month rule, and the spot-pairing need; the build folded those findings (raw-1m OI read; INDEX→CASH spot probe; front-month selection). **Verified (real local runs, 3.12 venv + duckdb/polars/pyarrow):** `--cov=brutex.dashboard.movers_futures --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → **100.00%** (198 stmts / 46 branches, 0 missed); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0 errors) + `interrogate` (100%) + `vulture` (clean) + `bash scripts/ci/no-dhan-guard.sh` (exit 0) + `validate_ledger_numbering.py` OK; the full `tests/unit tests/integration tests/property` package gate at `--cov=brutex --cov-fail-under=100` green. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (route futures branch); tests `tests/unit/test_movers_futures.py` (new), `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_futures.py` (new), `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py` (the obsolete futures-pending test repointed to options-pending). **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001 (#715, the page + the reused Spot helpers), DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (#707, the `groww-future` lake), DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001 (#710, the chain pull), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001, DEC-SPOT-PCT-CHANGE-001 (the COMMON `pct_change`). **Next:** DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-001 (Milestone 3 — the Options tab).
719. **DEC-SWEEP-RUN-BUTTON-001 — the "🚀 Run Sweep" dashboard button: a one-click web launch for the brute-force grid sweep (the `brutex sweep-all` engine), no terminal required** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator request):** the brute-force SWEEP engine is FULLY BUILT + tested (`brutex sweep` single-slice, `brutex sweep-all` full grid → Parquet + BLAKE3 audit, `brutex sweep-daemon` scheduled — DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 / DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001) but the ONLY way to launch it was the terminal `brutex sweep-all …` command — invisible to a dashboard operator. The operator asked, repeatedly, "what is this run sweep button?" — the answer being it did not yet exist; the dashboard had a "🪜 Run cascade" button (DEC-CASCADE-WIRE-001) that FILTERS a sweep's winners, but no button to CREATE them. This closes that loop: Pull → Verify → **🚀 Run Sweep** → 🪜 Run cascade → ⤓ Download. **What shipped (additive — the engine, the 52-vocab, every ingest path, the verify path are all UNTOUCHED; this is dashboard glue only):** (1) a NEW `brutex/dashboard/sweep_runner.py` — a PURE, ZERO-I/O core: `resolve_sweep_request(*, symbols, intervals, directions, k, sl, tp, top, mode, exchange, segment, start, end, today)` normalises + validates the dashboard form fields into a frozen `SweepRunRequest` (every bad field a clear `ValueError` the route turns into a 400 — unknown interval vs `brutex.feed.resampler.INTERVAL_SECONDS`, non-BUY/SELL direction, K outside `[1,52]`, malformed SL/TP leg, `top < 1`, unparseable date, `end < start`); `build_sweep_kwargs(request, *, lake_root, results_root, catalog_path)` maps it 1:1 onto the EXACT `cmd_sweep_all` keyword contract (pinning the safe dashboard defaults: `conditions=None` all-52, `options_sim=False` signal-only, `overfit_gate=False`, `stage3_enable=False`, `allow_missing_slices=True` so a one-click run sweeps WHATEVER is in the lake and skips empty slices honestly rather than hard-failing); `default_results_root`/`sweep_progress_file` mirror `cmd_sweep_all`'s `<lake>/sweeps` + `<lake>/sweeps/progress/sweep-progress.json` derivation EXACTLY (CLAUDE.md §2 r11 COMMON — one source of truth); and a thin `# pragma: no cover` `run_sweep_from_request` shim that lazily calls `brutex.cli.cmd_sweep_all`. Defaults mirror the CLI `_add_sweep_grid_args` declaration (`NIFTY,BANKNIFTY` · `1minute,5minute,15minute` · `BUY,SELL` · `K∈{1,2}` · no SL/TP · top-20 · NSE/INDEX · `2021-01-01 → today`); SENSEX is BSE-listed so it is a separate `exchange=BSE` run, never silently folded into an NSE grid (Golden Rule #1 honest scope). (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — a NEW `POST /api/v1/sweep/run` route resolves the request (400 on bad input / "no lake configured for sweep" when the store has no on-disk path), points `state.sweep_progress_path` at the sweep's progress file so the EXISTING `GET /api/v1/sweep-progress` serves the live per-tuple tick with no new plumbing (the cross-process file bridge, DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001), and runs the sweep on the **single-flight** background job (`_pull_job` — one lake, one writer; a second click while a pull OR sweep is running is a `{"started": false}` no-op, CLAUDE.md §2 r7 idempotence). The sweep reads the LOCAL lake (no vendor creds, no network). (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/reports.html` — a "🚀 Run Sweep (brute-force backtest)" card above the cascade card with optional SYMBOLS / TIMEFRAMES / FROM / TO inputs (blank ⇒ server defaults), a `#run-sweep` button, and a live progress bar that polls `/api/v1/sweep-progress` (state · % · enumerated · evaluated · survivors · combos/sec). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the button LAUNCHES the existing, already-tested engine — it does NOT make the math faster; a full ~33-billion-trial sweep is still 2–4 days on the reference Apple M4 Pro (CLAUDE.md §8), and the live feed reports the HONEST tuple/combo counts (an empty/partly-pulled lake sweeps only the slices that exist, reporting 0 tuples honestly rather than fabricating winners); ✅ `sweep_runner.py` is O(1)-per-field validation/mapping — the sweep it launches is O(T·N) over the grid, NOT O(1) total (no O(1)-total claim); ✅ no engine/vocab/ingest change. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — every axis validated against the engine's real bounds (interval set, BUY/SELL, K∈[1,52], positive paisa, real dates, end≥start); kwargs map 1:1 onto `cmd_sweep_all`; (2) Reliability — a bad field is a 400 with a clear message, never a deep background crash; the no-lake guard is a 400 not a 500; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #719 (additive, nothing else depends on it); (4) Idempotence — single-flight job (one writer), and the sweep itself is rerun-safe (load-or-create per-tuple store, DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001); (5) Honesty — defaults + progress reflect reality; SENSEX-on-BSE called out, not silently mixed; (6) Observability — the live progress bar + the BLAKE3 sweep audit chain the engine already writes; (7) Honest envelope — dashboard glue, no hot path, no O(1)-total claim. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`sweep_runner` — 100% line+branch over every default / blank-fallback / ValueError arm + the kwargs mapping + path helpers; the route — happy paths, the 400 arms, the no-lake guard, the single-flight no-op, the page wiring) · integration (the route end-to-end over a real DuckDB-backed store + `TestClient`, background job settled via `/pull-progress`) · property/golden/bench/stress (n/a — pure validation + route glue) · mutation (the validation predicates + the safe-default pins killed by the resolver/kwargs tests). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — dashboard-glue/refactor tier):** a forensic agent first confirmed the sweep engine is fully built + runnable on the Groww lake (the only gap was the launch button), and a demonstration run (688 bars → 220 combos → trade-sim → 0 gate survivors on random noise) proved it does NOT fabricate winners from noise — exactly the honest behaviour the button must preserve. **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv):** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_runner.py` + `tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_run_route.py` → 31 passed; `sweep_runner.py` at `--cov-branch` → 100.00% (111 stmts / 28 branch, 0 miss); the full dashboard slice (`-k dashboard`) → 581 passed; `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict brutex` (224 files) + `pyright` (0 errors) + `interrogate --fail-under=100` + `vulture` all clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/sweep_runner.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (+`POST /api/v1/sweep/run`, module imports), `brutex/dashboard/templates/reports.html` (+🚀 Run Sweep card + JS), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_runner.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_run_route.py` (NEW). **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-RUN-BUTTON-001. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-ORCHESTRATOR-001 (`cmd_sweep_all` / `run_sweep_grid` engine), DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001 (the `/api/v1/sweep-progress` file bridge this reuses), DEC-CASCADE-WIRE-001 (the "🪜 Run cascade" button this pairs with), DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001 (#710, the single-flight background-job route pattern mirrored here).

724a. **DEC-NSE-EQUITY-VERIFY-001 — the 🛡 Verify-vs-NSE trust anchor now cross-checks a STOCK's full 1-day OHLCV *including Volume* against the NSE security bhavcopy (the index harness checks 4 OHLC fields; a stock has volume)** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator request, repeated):** the first-verification harness (DEC-NSE-VERIFY-ROUTE-001, #669) cross-checks an INDEX's spot 1-day OHLC against the official NSE `ind_close_all` snapshot — but an index carries NO traded volume, so it compares 4 fields. The operator's emphatic, repeated ask was that for STOCKS the cross-check must cover the **entire OHLCV — Volume included** — vs the official NSE bhavcopy, before any bulk stock pull is trusted ("for stocks compare full OHLCV including Volume"). That stock+volume verify did NOT exist (a workspace + open-PR scan confirmed it: only the index harness existed; the parallel PRs #679/#681 are unrelated). **What shipped (additive — the engine, the 52-vocab, every ingest path, the INDEX verify path are all UNTOUCHED):** (1) a NEW `brutex/data/validation/nse_equity_oneday.py` — the stock twin of the index harness, pure/live-split + degrade-never-crash: `parse_bhavcopy_quote` reads the NSE "sec_bhavdata_full" security bhavcopy (whitespace/case-tolerant column resolver — the real file's leading-space ` SERIES` header resolves; env-overridable `EquityCsvSpec` + URL + series), matching the SYMBOL + SERIES=`EQ` row and parsing O/H/L/C through the strict `to_price`→`round_money` (2-dp `ROUND_HALF_UP`, DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001) + the volume through a comma/whitespace-tolerant `_parse_volume`; `quote_from_groww_equity_candles` selects the single IST-date `1day` Groww bar **keeping volume** (`drop_volume=False` — a stock trades real volume, vs the index harness's `drop_volume=True`); `compare_equity_quotes` DELEGATES the 4 OHLC fields wholesale to the index harness's pure `compare_quotes` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — one source of truth for the signed-paisa delta + tolerance flag) and ADDS the fifth **Volume** axis (signed share delta + within-tolerance flag); `validate_equity_oneday` is the degrade-safe live entrypoint (both openers injected → 100% offline-testable; reuses the index harness's `# pragma: no cover` urllib opener). **The Groww↔NSE volume-convention delta is UNVERIFIED** — vendor and exchange may count volume differently (block/auction inclusion), so the default `DEFAULT_VOLUME_TOLERANCE_UNVERIFIED = 0` shares (exact) carries `_UNVERIFIED` in its name; the verdict's primary honest output is the signed share delta, the tolerance only labels matched/mismatched, and the operator tunes it from real transcripts (Golden Rule #1 — never the reverse). (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `POST /api/v1/universe/verify-nse` now AUTO-ROUTES: a brute-force index (`resolve_index_source` resolves) → the existing 4-field OHLC check; ANY other symbol is a STOCK → the new OHLCV+Volume bhavcopy check. Both verdicts share the `to_dict` wire shape (the equity verdict adds a `volume` object), so the route is one symbol-agnostic surface. (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — `renderVerdict` shows the Volume line when present (`volume: groww=… nse=… Δ=… ⚠`), and the 🛡 button tooltip now states index→OHLC vs stock→OHLCV+Volume. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the harness MEASURES the real Groww↔NSE delta (OHLC paisa + volume shares), it does not assume a match — the UNVERIFIED tolerances are the whole point; ✅ degrade-never-crash — a missing `[groww]` extra / missing creds / network block / unparsable bhavcopy each surface as an honest `unavailable` note (always a 200 verdict), never a crash; ✅ NSE bot-blocks + this build env network-blocks the host, so the two live fetchers stay `# pragma: no cover` while the pure parse/compare logic is 100% covered; ✅ `compare_equity_quotes` is O(1) (5 fixed fields) — the bhavcopy parse is O(rows) + the fetch is bounded latency, NOT O(1)-total (an offline operator tool, exempt from the per-bar ratio gate); ✅ no engine/vocab/ingest change. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — SYMBOL+SERIES=EQ row match; OHLC reuse the index compare; volume = groww−nse within an UNVERIFIED tolerance; (2) Reliability — every parse arm returns `None`→`unavailable` (no header / missing column / row absent / series mismatch / malformed price or volume), never raises; the entrypoint degrades ANY vendor/network error; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #724 (additive; the index path + engine untouched); (4) Idempotence — pure reduction, bit-stable; (5) Honesty — UNVERIFIED tolerances named as such; the signed delta is the primary output; (6) Observability — the per-field OHLC deltas + the volume delta + an honest note on the verdict; (7) Honest envelope — offline verify tool, O(rows) parse not O(1)-total. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (60 over the new module — every bhavcopy degrade arm, the IST single-bar selection incl. no-bar/ambiguous, the OHLC+Volume compare status matrix, the env tolerance/spec/series/url override resolvers, the degrade-safe orchestration with both openers injected; +1 route test for the stock→equity auto-route) · integration (the `/api/v1/universe/verify-nse` route via `TestClient` — index symbol routes to the index harness, stock symbol to the equity harness, both serialised through `to_dict`) · property/golden/bench/stress (n/a — offline parse/compare) · mutation (each degrade predicate + the volume-tolerance boundary killed by a dedicated test). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — feature-of-an-established-harness tier):** a pre-build workspace + open-PR scan confirmed the stock+Volume verify did not exist and is non-overlapping with the parallel #679/#681; the design reuses the index harness's OHLC compare wholesale (COMMON) and isolates only the volume axis + bhavcopy parsing; the diff + every gate were re-run by hand. **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv):** `tests/unit/test_nse_equity_oneday.py` (60) + `tests/unit/test_dashboard_verify_nse_route.py` (5) → 65 passed; `nse_equity_oneday.py` at `--cov-branch` → 100.00% (227 stmts / 56 branch, 0 miss); the verify+validation+universe slice → 301 passed, 0 regressions; `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `interrogate --fail-under=100` + `vulture` all clean. **Files:** `brutex/data/validation/nse_equity_oneday.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (verify-nse route auto-routes index↔stock), `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` (volume line + tooltip), `tests/unit/test_nse_equity_oneday.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_verify_nse_route.py` (+stock-route test). **Decision ID:** DEC-NSE-EQUITY-VERIFY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-NSE-VERIFY-ROUTE-001 (#669, the index harness + the verify route + the `compare_quotes` OHLC core this reuses), DEC-CANDLE-PARSE-RESILIENCE-001 (the index-null-volume vs stock-real-volume distinction), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the 2-dp `round_money` snap), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (money 2-dp, metrics full-precision).

721. **DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-001 — the 🎯 Options tab of `/movers` is wired to real lake data: highest OI, OI gainers/losers, top volume/value, price movers per option contract (Milestone 3)** (2026-06-13). **Why:** the `/movers` redesign (#715) shipped all three tabs but only Spot (#715) then Futures (DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001, #720) were wired — Options still returned the hardcoded `pending_asset_payload` placeholder regardless of lake contents. This milestone wires the Options tab so that, once the operator pulls the F&O option chain (the CE/PE legs — DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 / DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001 #710), the tab fills automatically — completing the Spot/Futures/Options trio. **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY display over the lake — CLAUDE.md §3; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-condition vocabulary + every ingest path are UNTOUCHED):** (a) a NEW `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py` — the Options reader that REUSES the Spot + Futures readers (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, no duplication): the generic raw-1m session reader `_read_future_session` + `_prev_day_oi` + `_underlying_spot_ltp` from `movers_futures`, and `_prev_day_close` + the session helpers from `movers_snapshot`. New options-specific surface: `parse_option_symbol` (`EXCH-UNDERLYING-DDMmmYY-STRIKE-CE|PE` → `(underlying, expiry, strike, type)`), `OptionMover` (frozen/slots dataclass with a display `name` like `"NIFTY 30Jun25 24000 CE"`), `compute_option_mover`, `_session_value_paisa` (the cumulative `Σ round_money(close) × volume` read straight from the raw 1m parquet, mirroring `MoverSnapshot.value_paisa`), the 7 rankers (`rank_highest_oi` / `rank_oi_gainers` / `rank_oi_losers` / `rank_volume` / `rank_value` / `rank_price_gainers` / `rank_price_losers`), `build_options_payload`, `_discover_options`, and `run_options_snapshot`. (b) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the route's wired set is now `("spot","futures","options")`; an options no-lake-root "pull the F&O options first" empty payload + the runner dispatch `asset=="options" → run_options_snapshot` were added; any OTHER (unknown) asset still gets an honest pending payload. **Locked calc rules (market-standard, spot-consistent):** ONE row per OPTION CONTRACT (every strike × CE/PE × expiry in the lake; `top_n` caps each ranked list); **ltp** = the contract's selected-bar close; **price %** vs the contract's OWN prev-day close; **oi** = the raw-1m last-bar open interest; **oi_chg** = `oi − prev_day_oi` (signed) and **oi_chg_pct** vs the prior 1-day OI; **value** = cumulative `Σ close × volume` (₹); **volume** = fresh session; **spot** = the underlying's spot LTP (INDEX→CASH probe). Money 2dp via `brutex.money`; pct / OI% kept FULL precision (CLAUDE.md §4). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ REFERENCE_ONLY over the INGESTED lake; never feeds the engine or the 52-vocab; NOT a live feed (CLAUDE.md §1); the Options tab now shows real rows once options are pulled; ✅ no fabricated rows — no options / unknown interval / absent underlying spot / no prior day degrade to an honest empty / `null` payload; 🟡 NOT O(1)-total — each load discovers + reads every option contract's session + its underlying spot (an O(P) pass over the pulled chain, which can be large); 🟡 the **Near/Next/Far expiry filter is DEFERRED** — all expiries are ranked together and the payload note + the module docstring say so (a follow-up can wire the `expiry` param); this completes the Spot/Futures/Options trio. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — per-contract ltp/oi/value/price%/oi%; spot pairing; money 2dp / metrics full-precision; (2) Reliability — degrade-safe (no options / unknown interval / no-lake-root → honest empty, never 500); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #721 (Spot + Futures readers untouched but for the additive options route branch); (4) Idempotence — pure reduction over the lake → bit-stable, stable `(symbol,exchange,segment)` tiebreak (Golden Rule #4); (5) Honesty — absent spot → `null` spot/premium-n/a; no prior day → `null` %/OI%; never faked; the deferred expiry filter is disclosed; (6) Observability — the as-of echo + an honest note on every payload; (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY, O(P) not O(1)-total, expiry filter deferred. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`tests/unit/test_movers_options.py` — parse_option_symbol incl. FUT/junk/bad-strike→None, the 7 rankers, the payload + degrade notes, OptionMover name/₹ rendering) · integration (`tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_options.py` over a REAL ParquetWriter+DuckDB lake — CE+PE contracts + underlying spot seeded with OI;
