723. **DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 — the `/universe` spot pull is granularity-choosable per pull (1-day only / 1-minute only / both) with a VERIFY-FIRST 1-day default; 1-minute is no longer force-fetched alongside 1-day** (2026-06-13, operator decision). **Why:** the pull fetched BOTH 1m+1d every click; the operator wants 1-day FIRST, cross-checked vs the official NSE/BSE bhavcopy (CLAUDE.md §6), THEN 1-minute — via a per-pull dropdown, no code change. **What shipped (spot pull DEFAULTS + dropdown; ENGINE + 52-vocab UNTOUCHED — CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `pull_controller.py` — `GROWW_FETCH_INTERVALS` = verify-first `("1day",)` (was `("1minute","1day")`); new `SPOT_INTERVAL_CHOICES` + `resolve_fetch_intervals(choice)` (1day/1minute/both; blank/None/unknown → 1-day, never widens — Golden Rule #1); `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` gained an injected `intervals` param; both report builders iterate the ACTUALLY-fetched `intervals` (fixed a `report.pairs` KeyError; `label_for` typed `dict[str,str]` for pyright). (2) `app.py` — `/pull`, `/pull-all`, `/retry-failed` accept `?spot_interval=`; progress `total` = `symbols × len(fetch_intervals)` (was hardcoded `× 2`). (3) `universe.html` — a `#spotInterval` dropdown threaded into single + bulk + one-click JS; blurb/meta updated. (4) `coverage_view.py` — `FETCH_INTERVALS` kept `{1minute, 1day}` (both valid fetch intervals). (5) `CLAUDE.md` §1/§6. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ pure O(1) dict lookup; ✅ default never widens to 1-minute; 🟡 the automated OHLCV-vs-bhavcopy comparator is the FOLLOW-UP DEC-BHAVCOPY-OHLCV-VERIFY-001. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — every choice maps + unknown→1day; report builders iterate real intervals (no KeyError); (2) Reliability — 1-interval pull no longer caps the bar at 50%% (total = symbols × intervals); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + ledger #723; (4) Idempotence — pure resolver; (5) Honesty — unknown never widens; comparator named as follow-up; (6) Observability — `spot_interval` on the pull logs; (7) Honest envelope — DATA/pull default + UI only. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`resolve_fetch_intervals` every choice + None + whitespace + unknown→default; the 1-day default grid; machinery tests opt into `("1minute","1day")`) · integration (`?spot_interval=` route → `total` = symbols×intervals via TestClient: 1day→1, both→2, 1minute→1) · golden (dropdown default + options) · bench/stress/mutation — N/A. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — feature tier, 1-agent):** traced `GROWW_FETCH_INTERVALS` through every call site — fixed the hardcoded-1m+1d KeyError, the `× 2` progress cap, a pyright literal-key narrowing; coverage_view keeps BOTH intervals. **Tests (real local, 3.12 venv + Rust kernels):** `--cov=brutex.dashboard.pull_controller` → **100.00%** (299/58); `--cov=brutex.dashboard.coverage_view` → **100.00%**; route + template suites green; ruff + format + mypy --strict + pyright clean. **Files:** `pull_controller.py`, `app.py`, `coverage_view.py`, `templates/universe.html`, `CLAUDE.md` (+ tests). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 (#722), DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001, DEC-DEFAULT-DATE-RANGE-001, DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001. **Follow-up:** DEC-BHAVCOPY-OHLCV-VERIFY-001.

724b. **DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-NSE-001 — the `/universe` "⊕ tick its constituents" match is now ISIN-primary, ticker-fallback (rename-proof); the constituents cache persists ISINs** (2026-06-13, operator request "map by ticker, ISIN as rename-proof fallback; fetch directly from NSE"). **Why:** the route matched NSE index members to held Groww stocks **ticker-only** (`nse_constituents.intersect_with_universe`), so a constituent whose NSE ticker had been renamed silently dropped out of the tick — even though the SAME company (same globally-unique ISIN) is held under its new ticker. A robust ISIN-primary + ticker-fallback resolver ALREADY existed (`universe_constituents.resolve_constituents`, used by the lake `_ntm_admission`); the gap was purely that the interactive route did not use it and the cache did not carry ISINs. **What shipped (the `/universe` REFERENCE_ONLY selection surface; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab UNTOUCHED — CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/nse_constituents.py` — new `fetch_rows_at_url(url, *, opener)` returning `list[ConstituentRow]` (symbol + ISIN), the ISIN-carrying sibling of `fetch_symbols_at_url`. (2) `brutex/dashboard/constituents_cache.py` — `ConstituentResult` gains a `rows: tuple[ConstituentRow, ...]` field; `write_cache` now takes rows and persists a parallel `"isins"` array ALONGSIDE the legacy `"symbols"` (additive — a pre-existing symbols-only reader still works); `resolve_constituents` fetches rows and `_result_from_cache` rebuilds `(symbol, isin)` rows — a legacy cache with NO `"isins"` key (or a length-mismatched one) degrades ISINs to `None` (ticker-only until the next refresh re-writes it; never mis-pairs a symbol with the wrong ISIN — Golden Rule #1). (3) `brutex/universe_constituents.py` — new `held_members(constituents, instruments, held_symbols)` that REUSES the COMMON `resolve_constituents` (CLAUDE.md §11 — no duplicated matcher) and returns the held `symbol_name`s in constituent order, deduplicated. (4) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the `index-constituents` route swaps `intersect_with_universe(result.symbols, held_symbols)` (ticker-only) for `held_members(result.rows, candidates, held_symbols)` (ISIN→ticker); the note reads "matched by ISIN→ticker (rename-proof)". **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `held_members` is O(C) over constituents with O(1) per-row map lookups (the resolver builds two O(1) hash maps); ✅ ISINs come ONLY from NSE's CSV / the vendor master, never fabricated; 🟡 the live NSE fetch is still best-effort (bot-blocked server-side; cached on first success; honest "unavailable"/"unknown-index" degrade — unchanged). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — a renamed-ticker constituent matches by ISIN (explicit unit + route tests); (2) Reliability — legacy symbols-only caches still load (ISIN→None, ticker-only) and a length-mismatched isins array degrades to None, never a crash or mis-pair; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + ledger #724 (additive cache key — old readers unaffected); (4) Idempotence — pure resolver + deterministic lowest-security_id tiebreak (inherited); (5) Honesty — unmatched constituents are dropped, never guessed; ISINs never fabricated; (6) Observability — the route note states the match method + source + as_of; (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY selection UI; engine/vocab untouched. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`fetch_rows_at_url`; cache ISIN round-trip + legacy-no-isins + length-mismatch degrade; `held_members` ticker-match / ISIN-rename-match / not-held-skip / dedup / order / empty) · integration (`test_rename_proof_match_by_isin` — a held row carrying the ISIN + a CSV with the OLD ticker → the route ticks the NEW symbol by ISIN, end-to-end via TestClient) · golden (the cache JSON shape frozen by the round-trip test) · bench/stress/mutation — N/A for an O(1)-map matcher (the existing resolver keeps its kill tests). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — feature tier, 1-agent):** an Explore agent mapped the full nse_constituents → constituents_cache → route → `_ntm_admission` → `universe_constituents` chain + the InstrumentStore lookups + the test patterns BEFORE code, confirming the ISIN resolver already existed and the only gap was the route + cache ISIN persistence (so the minimal correct change reuses the COMMON resolver, no new matcher). **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv + Rust kernels):** `--cov=brutex.dashboard.constituents_cache --cov=brutex.dashboard.nse_constituents --cov=brutex.universe_constituents --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → **100.00%** (276 stmts / 100 branches, 0 missed) across the cache + nse_constituents + universe_constituents + the integration route suites (139 passed); the universe-query / routes / instrument-loader / groww-primary suites stay green (0 regressions); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0 errors) clean; `no-dhan-guard.sh` exit 0; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` OK. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/nse_constituents.py`, `brutex/dashboard/constituents_cache.py`, `brutex/universe_constituents.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (+ tests `tests/unit/test_constituents_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_universe_constituents.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_universe_constituents.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-NSE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-MAP-001 (the ISIN-primary resolver this reuses), DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-FULL-001 (#714, the FULL-membership tick), DEC-CONSTITUENTS-CACHE-001 (#457, the cache this extends), DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 (#445, the route).

725. **DEC-NSE-ALL-INDICES-SNAPSHOT-001 — expose the NSE `ind_close_all` daily file as the LIVE index universe (parse ALL index rows + list all index names), REFERENCE_ONLY** (2026-06-13, operator-supplied NSE index-data reference). **Why:** the `ind_close_all_<DDMMYYYY>.csv` file is a SINGLE daily CSV that carries EVERY published NSE index as a row (broad-based + sectoral + thematic + strategy). `brutex/data/validation/nse_oneday.py` already fetched + column-parsed that exact file, but only pulled the 3 brute-force index ROWS for the OHLC verify (DEC-NSE-1DAY-VALIDATION-001). (5) `fetch_index_snapshot(trade_date, *, official_opener)` — the degrade-safe live entrypoint: opener defaults to the existing `_default_official_opener` (`# pragma: no cover` live NSE surface), a fetch failure (weekend/holiday 404 / bot-block / timeout — all `OSError`) returns `None`, success returns the parsed rows. This composes with the existing per-index constituents pipeline (`nse_constituents` convention CSV + the ISIN→ticker rename-proof match, DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-NSE-001 #724) into a fully-dynamic discover-indices → fetch-each-index's-members → map-to-held-stocks chain with zero hardcoding. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ all five additions are pure / O(rows) parse + one O(1) URL render; ✅ REFERENCE_ONLY (CLAUDE.md §3) — index EOD context + the live index list, NEVER an engine / 52-vocab input; ✅ every number comes ONLY from the NSE file (never fabricated); 🟡 the live NSE fetch is best-effort (NSE bot-blocks + this build env network-blocks the host — the live opener is `# pragma: no cover`, exercised offline via an injected fake); 🟡 the `ind_close_all` URL path is BEST-EFFORT / verify-first (the long-stable NSE indices path; env-overridable). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — names from the file column; OHLC 2-dp-snapped; the caller logs); (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY; engine/vocab untouched. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`daily_indices_url` DDMMYYYY token; `list_index_names` unique/sorted/blank-dropped + empty + missing-column; `parse_index_snapshot` good-rows + blank-skip + malformed-skip + empty + missing-column; `fetch_index_snapshot` success + OSError→None) · golden (the parsed OHLC + the sorted name list frozen by fixtures) · integration/bench/stress/mutation — N/A for pure REFERENCE_ONLY parse helpers (the live opener is `# pragma: no cover`; the existing 1-day-verify kill tests are unaffected). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — feature tier, 1-agent):** an Explore agent + a direct read confirmed `nse_oneday.py` ALREADY owned the `ind_close_all` URL + column spec + opener, so the minimal correct change REUSES that plumbing (no new module, no duplicated matcher) and only adds the all-rows / all-names readers. **Tests (real local runs, 3.12 venv + Rust kernels):** `--cov=brutex.data.validation.nse_oneday --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → **100.00%** (336 stmts / 82 branches, 0 missed; 728. **DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-TRACK-001 — the `/movers` Options tab gains an All / Monthly / Weekly cadence toggle; Near/Next/Far now picks WITHIN the chosen track, classified STRUCTURALLY (last-expiry-in-calendar-month = monthly), never from a hardcoded NSE weekday rule** (2026-06-13). **Why (operator request):** after the Near/Next/Far expiry filter shipped (DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-EXPIRY-001, #726) the operator asked to split weekly vs monthly expiries and challenged whether a naive rule would survive every permutation (weeklies are index-only, not all indices have weeklies, NSE keeps changing the expiry weekday + which indices carry weeklies). The robust answer is a purely DATA-DRIVEN classification: **monthly = the LAST expiry date in a calendar month** for that underlying (it settles as the monthly); every earlier same-month expiry is a weekly. This reads only the expiry dates ALREADY in the lake, so it needs NO NSE rulebook (Golden Rule #1) and handles every permutation — a stock / weekly-less index has one expiry per month (all monthly, an empty weekly track), an index with weeklies has several (the last is the monthly), and an NSE cadence change just changes which dates appear (no code change). **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY over the lake — CLAUDE.md §3; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + every ingest path UNTOUCHED):** `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py` — `_monthly_expiries(expiries)` groups distinct expiries by `(year, month)` and keeps each group's max (the structural last-in-month classifier); `_track_pool(expiries, track)` narrows a set to `monthly` / `weekly` / `all` (unknown ⇒ all); `_tier_expiry_by_underlying` gains `track="all"` and narrows to the track BEFORE the Near/Next/Far pick; `run_options_snapshot` + `build_options_payload` gain `expiry_track="all"` (normalised up-front; blank ⇒ all) passed to `run_options_snapshot` for `asset=options`. `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` — an Options-only `#track` All/Monthly/Weekly select beside the Near/Next/Far `#expiry` select, sent as `?track=` and re-fetched on change. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the split is structural (last-in-month), derived from the lake's own expiry dates — NEVER a hardcoded NSE weekday (so it survives every cadence change + every per-index permutation); ✅ default `all` ⇒ byte-identical to the prior #726 behaviour (backward-compatible); ✅ REFERENCE_ONLY, never the engine/52-vocab, NOT a live feed; ✅ a stock / weekly-less index ⇒ empty weekly track, that underlying simply drops out, never faked; 🟡 classifies ONLY the expiries actually pulled (describes the lake, not NSE's theoretical calendar — documented); 🟡 the last weekly of a month IS the monthly (same contract — by market structure, not a fudge); 🟡 NOT O(1)-total. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — `_monthly_expiries` = max per `(year, month)`; tier picks within the track pool; (2) Reliability — degrade-safe (unknown track ⇒ all; no contract on the track ⇒ honest empty, never 500); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + ledger #728 (additive param, default `all`); (4) Idempotence — pure set classification, bit-stable; (5) Honesty — no NSE rule hardcoded, weekly-less underlyings drop out, the note carries the cadence; (6) Observability — the note names the tier + cadence; (7) Honest envelope — REFERENCE_ONLY, O(contracts) not O(1)-total. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`_monthly_expiries` — empty / single-per-month / last-in-month-wins / one-monthly-per-month / same-day-diff-month key; `_track_pool` — all/monthly/weekly/unknown→all; `_tier_expiry_by_underlying` within a track — monthly near/next, weekly near, weekly-empty-for-a-monthly-only underlying, default=all; the cadence note label — default omits / ranked appends / empty + present-no-mover notes carry it) · integration (`run_options_snapshot` over a real lake seeded with a June-20 weekly + June-27 monthly: `track=monthly` keeps only the monthly, `track=weekly` keeps only the weekly, unknown→all; 729. **DEC-NSE-COOKIE-DANCE-001 — the official-NSE one-day verify fetch now does the cookie-prime "bot-block dance" (build_opener + cookie jar; prime `www.nseindia.com`; THEN fetch the archive with the same opener) so the live `Verify vs NSE` no longer 403s** (2026-06-14). **Numbering note (CLAUDE.md §2 r13 — parallel collision):** this entry merged via PR #689's auto-merge at #728 the same moment PR #688 (DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-TRACK-001) claimed #728, leaving a transient duplicate on main; renumbered here to the next free #729 (the DEC-ID is authoritative, only the number moves). **Why (operator master-doc gotcha #1, verified 2026-06-13):** NSE rejects a BARE `urllib` request (no session cookies) with a **403** — the prior `_default_official_opener` issued a single `urllib.request.urlopen(Request(url, headers=...))` with a browser `User-Agent` but NO cookie jar, so on the operator's machine the live `🛡 Verify vs NSE` (the spot-index verify DEC-NSE-1DAY-VALIDATION-001 + the stock-OHLCV verify DEC-NSE-EQUITY-VERIFY-001 #682, which imports this opener) would 403 on the real NSE archive host even though the URL + headers were correct. **What shipped (LIVE-network helper only — `# pragma: no cover - live network only`; the engine + 52-vocab + every ingest path are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** `brutex/data/validation/nse_oneday.py` — (1) two module constants hoisted out of the function: `_BROWSER_HEADERS` (the browser `User-Agent`/`Accept`/`Accept-Language` triple NSE expects) and the new public `NSE_COOKIE_PRIME_URL` (`https://www.nseindia.com`, env-overridable via `BRUTEX_NSE_COOKIE_PRIME_URL` for a mirror/proxy); (2) `_default_official_opener` rewritten to build a `urllib.request.build_opener(HTTPCookieProcessor(http.cookiejar.CookieJar()))`, PRIME it with one best-effort GET to `NSE_COOKIE_PRIME_URL` (NSE plants its session cookies; the prime is wrapped in `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` so an archive CDN / mirror that doesn't need it never makes the verify fatal), then fetch the archive URL with the SAME opener so the cookies ride along, keeping the existing bounded-retry budget (`_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES`, 1.5·attempt backoff). `nse_equity_oneday.py` imports this same opener, so the stock-OHLCV-incl-Volume verify (DEC-NSE-EQUITY-VERIFY-001 #682) inherits the cookie dance for free. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the prime+fetch share one opener/jar so the cookies actually carry; ✅ priming is best-effort (never converts a working mirror into a failure); ✅ the real fetch's errors still propagate after the retry budget; 🟡 this is a LIVE-network path that CANNOT be exercised in CI (this build env network-blocks NSE) — it is `# pragma: no cover` and verified by the recipe/master-doc, not by a CI hit (the surrounding parse/compare logic that IS testable stays at 100% line+branch); 🟡 NOT O(1)-total (one network round-trip per prime + per fetch attempt). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — cookie jar shared across prime+fetch (the 403 fix); (2) Reliability — best-effort prime + bounded retry, a prime failure is swallowed not fatal; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + drop ledger #729 (pure helper swap, no data/lake migration); (4) Idempotence — read-only GET, repeatable; (5) Honesty — `# pragma: no cover` live-only is disclosed, no faked CI coverage; (6) Observability — the real fetch's `OSError` surfaces to the verify caller's existing error path; (7) Honest envelope — LIVE-only, O(round-trips) not O(1)-total. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit/golden/property/bench/stress — the parse + compare logic around the opener stays at 100% line+branch (152 passed across `test_validation_nse_oneday` + golden + property + `test_nse_equity_oneday`); the opener body itself is `# pragma: no cover - live network only` (the network is CI-blocked) and is verified against the operator's master NSE-fetch recipe gotcha #1. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — small live-helper tier):** the master reference doc's NSE-fetch gotcha #1 was mapped against the prior bare-request opener; the exact gap (no cookie jar ⇒ 403) surfaced and was fixed at the single opener both verify paths funnel through (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); the diff + every gate re-run by hand. **Verified:** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `bandit` (0 issues) + `vulture --min-confidence 80` clean; `--cov=brutex.data.validation.nse_oneday --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → 100.00% (338 stmts / 82 branches, 0 missed). **Files:** `brutex/data/validation/nse_oneday.py`. **Decision ID:** DEC-NSE-COOKIE-DANCE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-NSE-EQUITY-VERIFY-001 (#682, the stock-OHLCV verify that imports this opener), DEC-NSE-1DAY-VALIDATION-001 (the spot index one-day verify) + DEC-NSE-VERIFY-ROUTE-001 (the verify route).
727. **DEC-GROWW-RATELIMIT-RETRY-001 — the adaptive rate limiter (8.3 r/s decremental/incremental) now applies UNIFORMLY to EVERY Groww call (spot + expiries + contracts + futures + options + historical), and a live 429 is RETRIED, not fatal** (2026-06-13, operator live-run bug: the "⛓ Pull expiries + contracts" chain pull failed instantly with `GrowwError: GrowwAPIException: Rate limit has breached for your request` — `0/1 derivatives, 0 bars` in ~270 ms). **Root cause (three holes, all on the F&O CHAIN path; the spot pull was unaffected because its window re-queue masked them):** (1) **mapping hole** — `from_groww_exception` classified ONLY by exact SDK class name, but the live SDK surfaces a rate-limit as the BASE `GrowwAPIException("Rate limit has breached …")` (carrying a `429` `code`), NOT the typed `GrowwAPIRateLimitException`; so it fell through to a bare terminal `GrowwError`, `is_retryable()` returned False, and the decremental limiter was never told it was a 429; (2) **retry hole** — `GrowwClient._call` retried ONLY `GrowwTimeoutError`, never a rate-limit (the old design delegated 429 backoff to the orchestrator's window re-queue — which the chain ENUMERATION calls `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` do NOT have, so their 429 killed the whole underlying); (3) **pace hole** — `build_live_client` built `GrowwClient(sdk=sdk)` with the no-op `pace`, so the chain calls were not even token-bucketed. **What shipped (the adaptive limiter is now OWNED at the one choke point every Groww call funnels through — `GrowwClient._call` — so spot/expiries/contracts/futures/options/historical are uniformly protected, none can bypass it; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + lake are UNTOUCHED):** (1) `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` — `from_groww_exception` gains a `_classify_generic` fallback for a bare `GrowwAPIException`/`GrowwBaseException`: classify by the HTTP-ish `code` (`429`→rate-limit, `408`/`504`→timeout; int or digit-string; `bool` ignored since it is an int subclass) THEN by message keywords (`"rate limit"`/`"too many request"`/`"429"`→rate-limit; `"timed out"`/`"timeout"`/`"deadline exceeded"`→timeout); anything unrecognised stays the terminal base `GrowwError` (conservative — never blindly retried, Golden Rule #1). (2) `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py` — `_call` is now the adaptive limiter: `pace()`-acquire → on a RETRYABLE error (`is_retryable` — rate-limit OR timeout) back off (the longer `rate_limit_backoff_seconds` for a 429, linear `base × attempt`, bounded `max_attempts=6`) + retry, firing `on_rate_limit` to **DECREMENT** the shared token bucket on EVERY 429 and `on_success` to **RECOVER (increment)** the rate on a clean call; a terminal error, or a retryable one that exhausts the budget, re-raises for the orchestrator's layer-3 re-queue (belt-and-suspenders). (3) `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py` — `build_live_client` accepts + wires `pace`/`on_rate_limit`/`on_success` into the `GrowwClient` (a truthy callable wins; `None`→the no-op default). (4) `brutex/dashboard/derivatives_pull.py` — `_resolve_client_factory` injects the shared `SessionRateController` hooks into the live derivative client so the chain pull can never bypass the limiter (keeping the `(Path) -> (client, sink)` factory contract intact for injected test fakes). **The three retry LAYERS (the operator's "keep retrying until everything is pulled, all permutations covered"):** L1 per-call (`_call`: pace → retry transient → decrement/recover) covers 429 / timeout / transient blips; L2 per-item (the ingest spine records a failed window/contract, never fatal) covers one bad contract / DH-905 no-data / one malformed bar; L3 until-clean (orchestration re-pulls only the still-failed windows in bounded rounds) — spot already has all three (`auto_retry`+`until_clean`); this PR fixes L1 uniformly + wires it into the chain pull (the **derivatives L3 until-clean round-loop is the tracked next increment**, DEC-GROWW-DERIV-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 forthcoming). **Error taxonomy (the permutations, by class):** rate-limit/timeout → retry+backoff (transient); auth-dead → STOP + re-auth (not retryable); bad-request/not-found → skip that item, continue; no-data → skip (benign); success → recover the rate up. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the limiter is O(1) per call (token-bucket acquire + O(1) decrement/recover); the retry budget is a fixed constant (O(1) state, no per-symbol memory); ✅ a full chain pull is O(contracts × windows) network calls — NOT O(1)-total, and a SUSTAINED limit beyond the in-call budget still re-queues to L3 (the chain L3 loop is the next increment, named above — honest about what is and is not yet covered); ✅ the limit VALUES are unchanged (the operator-confirmed 8.3 r/s ≈ 500/min ceiling, decrement floor 1 r/s — CLAUDE.md §6 / DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001); this PR only fixes that the chain pull HONORS them + recovers from a 429. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — a generic `GrowwAPIException` 429 (code or message) classifies as rate-limit; `_call` retries+decrements+recovers; (2) Reliability — a transient 429 now self-heals (retry to success) instead of an instant `0/1` fail; an exhausted budget re-raises cleanly for L2/L3; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` the diff + ledger #727 (additive — the limit values + the engine are untouched); (4) Idempotence — retries are safe (the WindowLedger skips already-pulled windows); (5) Honesty — the conservative terminal fallback never blind-retries an unknown error; the chain L3 gap is disclosed; (6) Observability — every 429 fires the decrement hook + the controller snapshot the `/universe` rate panel already shows; (7) Honest envelope — O(1) per-call, O(N) per-pull, chain-L3 deferred. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`test_groww_errors` — the generic code/message classification matrix incl. bool-code-ignored, digit-string-code, timeout-hint, terminal fallback; `test_groww_client` — rate-limit retry+decrement+exhaust, rate-limit→success→recover, the EXACT live-bug regression `GrowwAPIException("Rate limit has breached")` retried to success, 429-`code` retried, terminal-generic not retried; `test_dashboard_derivatives_pull` — `_resolve_client_factory` dry-run vs live; `test_groww_live` — `build_live_client` hook wiring) · integration (the existing option/future ingest suites over the paced client) · property/golden/bench/stress (n/a — error-mapping + retry policy) · mutation (each classification predicate + the retry/decrement/recover branches killed by a dedicated test). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — live-bug/adapter tier):** the operator's live transcript + the master Groww-SDK/NSE reference doc were mapped against `from_groww_exception` → the exact gap surfaced (typed-subclass-only classification vs the SDK's generic-`GrowwAPIException` 429 shape); the fix was placed at the single choke point so no call site can bypass it, and re-reviewed by hand. **Verified (real local runs, 3.12 venv):** the 4 changed modules at `--cov-branch` → **100.00%** (errors 40/12, client 52/8, live 9/0, derivatives_pull 131/36, 0 miss); the full groww/derivatives/option-ingest slice → 816 passed; the WHOLE `tests/unit` suite → **6228 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (the `_call` choke-point change is regression-free across every Groww caller); `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict brutex` (227 files) clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py`, `brutex/dashboard/derivatives_pull.py` (+ tests `test_groww_errors.py`, `test_groww_client.py`, `test_dashboard_derivatives_pull.py`). **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-RATELIMIT-RETRY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001 (the 8.3 r/s ≈ 500/min ceiling + decrement floor), DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001 (#710, the chain pull this fixes), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 / DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (the ingest spine), DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (the client model). **Next:** DEC-GROWW-DERIV-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 — the derivatives L3 auto-resume-until-clean round-loop (the spot `auto_retry`+`until_clean` twin for the F&O chain).


730. **DEC-GROWW-DERIV-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 — the F&O derivatives "Pull expiries + contracts" gains the until-clean re-pull round-loop (the twin of the spot `pull_all_spot(until_clean=True)`), so a transient-throttled chain keeps re-pulling its still-failed windows until it drains** (2026-06-14). **Why (operator decree, the "keep retrying until everything is pulled successfully automatically" mandate):** the spot pull already had the bounded re-pull-until-clean loop (DEC-TOKEN-PREFLIGHT-001 / DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001), but the DERIVATIVES chain pull (DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001, #710) was a SINGLE pass — a rate-limit/timeout-deferred window was left for a MANUAL re-pull. With #727's per-call 429 retry+decrement (DEC-GROWW-RATELIMIT-RETRY-001) now landing the adaptive limiter on every chain call, the missing piece was the OUTER round-loop that re-drives the still-failed windows automatically. **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY lake pull path — the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + every spot ingest path are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/derivatives_pull.py` — `pull_all_derivatives` gains `until_clean: bool = False` + `until_clean_rounds: int = AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS`; the instruments×contract_types body is extracted into a `_one_pass()` closure (returning a `_PassResult`), and `until_clean=True` wraps it in a `_round_runner` driven by the SHARED `run_until_clean(..., stop_when_stuck=True)` (`brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, the SAME driver the spot path uses — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) over the SHARED WindowLedger; each round re-enumerates the chain and re-ingests, the ledger SKIPS already-`SUCCESS` windows and RE-ATTEMPTS the prior round's `FAILED` (transient) ones (`_SKIPPABLE = {SUCCESS, SKIPPED}` — a FAILED row is re-fetched), so successive rounds re-fetch only what is still failing. `DerivativesPullReport` gains a `still_failed_windows: int = 0` field (+ `to_dict` key, default 0 → backward-compatible) and `_build_note` an honest "N transient window(s) still failing" branch. (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-derivatives` route gains `until_clean: bool = Query(default=False)`, threaded into `pull_all_derivatives` + echoed in the JSON. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ transient (rate-limit/timeout) windows ARE re-attempted across rounds and the loop drains them to clean (the make-or-break, hostile-reviewed); ✅ `until_clean=False` (default) is ONE single pass, byte-identical to before; ✅ bars/windows SUM across rounds (round N re-appends only newly-fetched windows — the keep-first sink + ledger skip make double-counting impossible); 🟡 a derivatives round is **O(chain enumeration) + O(failed windows)**, NOT `O(failed_windows)` like the spot round (the chain is re-enumerated each round) — so `stop_when_stuck=True` is LOAD-BEARING: a round that drains zero residual halts immediately rather than re-paying the enumeration to the budget cap; 🟡 TERMINAL quarantines (bad-request/auth — `failed_pairs`) are NOT transient and are correctly excluded from the clean test (consistent with the spot twin) — they stay visible via `failed_pairs` + the note; 🟡 NOT O(1)-total (a full chain pull is genuinely network-bound). Re-enumeration is paced by the SAME 500/min rate bucket (cannot bypass the governor); Groww backtesting has NO daily quota (DEC-GROWW-NO-DAILY-QUOTA-001) so the wired quota brake is dormant. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — `is_skippable` re-attempts FAILED windows; the loop drains transient residual to 0; (2) Reliability — bounded rounds (`until_clean_rounds`), `stop_when_stuck` halts a stuck chain, never infinite; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + drop ledger #730 (additive default-off param, no migration); (4) Idempotence — WindowLedger SUCCESS-skip makes every round rerun-safe; (5) Honesty — terminal `failed_pairs` stay visible, the note surfaces still-failing transient windows; (6) Observability — the per-window progress hook + the `still_failed_windows` report field + note; (7) Honest envelope — O(chain)+O(failed) per round, NOT O(1)-total, terminal quarantines excluded from the clean test. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit — `_one_pass`/`_round_runner` via the offline fake SDK + recording sink: until-clean dry-run reaches clean, `until_clean_rounds=0` safe no-op (empty passes, no IndexError), the **fails-first-round-then-succeeds** cross-round re-attempt proof (the make-or-break), a live `SessionRateController` wiring the dormant quota brake, a PERSISTENT transient → `stop_no_progress` with residual + the honest note, an auth death → `stop_dead`, and a single-pass still-failed report; integration — the route accepts + echoes `?until_clean=true`. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — major pull-path change):** a Plan-agent hostile review confirmed the make-or-break (FAILED windows are re-attempted, not skipped — `_SKIPPABLE` excludes FAILED), the begin-once/N-rounds/end-once ledger lifecycle, the O(chain) per-round re-enumeration cost (→ `stop_when_stuck` load-bearing), and flagged the 4 deliberate divergences from the spot twin (no inner auto-retry wrapper, re-enum cost, terminal quarantines invisible to the clean test, NO `DailyQuotaExceeded` handler since Groww has no quota). **Verified:** `--cov=brutex.dashboard.derivatives_pull --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` → 100.00% (161 stmts / 40 branches, 0 missed); IS NULL OR col = ?)` pass-through filters — CONSTANT SQL, parameterized values only, so no string-built query), `list_contract_jobs` (DISTINCT `(exch, underlying, expiry_date)` — the missing `store.list_contracts()` that feeds `settled_contract_jobs`), `count_*`, context-manager `open_registry`. (2) `fetch_expiries(cell)` → `resolve_expiries(client, exchange, underlying_symbol, year)` (metadata), `on_expiry_cell` PERSISTS each date via `registry.upsert_expiry` + writes the per-`(underlying,year)` `coverage_store.upsert_coverage` rollup (`STATUS_EXPIRIES_ONLY` on a non-empty success, else `classify_cell` → `failed`/`pending` — the status model reused, not re-implemented); (3) `fetch_contracts(job)` → `resolve_contracts(client, exchange, underlying_symbol, expiry)` (metadata), persisting each via `registry.upsert_contract` with `side`/`strike` taken from the already-parsed `DerivativeContract` (`parse_contract_symbol` runs inside `resolve_contracts` — strike/side never re-invented, Golden Rule #1); (4) pulls ZERO candles — it constructs NO `BarSink` and calls NO `get_historical_candles`/`run_groww_option_ingest` (the dry-run default SDK `_EmptyChainSDK` deliberately carries ONLY `get_expiries`/`get_contracts`, not even a candle method); (5) returns an honest `MetadataPullReport` (dry_run, years, underlyings, expiry_cells, cells_skipped, expiry_failures, expiries_persisted, contract_jobs, contract_failures, contracts_persisted, note) mirroring `DerivativesPullReport` style with a `to_dict`; (6) injects the client (`client_factory` — default dry-run empty-chain or live TOTP), the `RegistryStore`, the `run_parallel` (default production `PoolRunParallel`; tests a synchronous fake), the live rate-hooks (`_rate_hooks` → the `SessionRateController`'s pace/on_rate_limit/on_success, so the metadata calls ride the SAME 500/min bucket — never a bypass), and a `now`/`today` clock for determinism. Honest dry-run = the empty-chain SDK → 0 expiries + 0 contracts + an honest "set credentials" note (the real F&O chain is vendor data never fabricated offline — Golden Rule #1). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ metadata only — NO candles, NO sink, NO historical ingest imported (asserted by the dry-run SDK having no candle method + the happy test asserting `get_historical_candles` is never called); ✅ the incremental skip is O(1)-per-item `frozenset` membership (a re-click issues only genuinely-new calls); ✅ idempotent — the registry PK upserts make a re-pull a bit-stable no-op; 🟡 network-bound, NOT O(1)-total — one `get_expiries` per cell + one `get_contracts` per discovered expiry (the chain enumeration is a real network pull; not claimed O(1)); 🟡 PR-2 wires the orchestration only — the dashboard route + button (PR-3), `/db` visibility (PR-4), the separate "Pull historical" button (PR-5), and decommission (PR-6) follow; the live `client_factory`/`_rate_hooks`-live closure bodies are `# pragma: no cover` (genuine TOTP + network). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — phase ordering delegated to the verified `run_two_phase` barrier; side/strike from the authoritative parsed contract; (2) Reliability — a failed Phase-1 cell is recorded (`classify_cell` → `failed`) + the run resumes (one dead cell never blocks the phase); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + delete the new module/test + drop ledger #735 (no engine/master/lake migration — a pure additive sibling); (4) Idempotence — registry PK `INSERT OR REPLACE` → re-pull is bit-stable; the incremental skip makes a re-click pull only deltas; (5) Honesty — dry-run persists 0 + an explicit "set credentials" note, never an invented strike; the report never carries a bar count (there are none); (6) Observability — the `MetadataPullReport` exposes expiries/contracts persisted + cells skipped + failures + an honest note (the `on_contract` callback is the audit seam for the live route's structlog line); (7) Honest envelope — metadata only, candles excluded, the existing derivatives pull untouched. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit — 18 tests, 100% line+branch (`--cov=brutex.dashboard.metadata_pull` → 100.00%, 100 stmts / 18 branches, 0 missed) FULLY OFFLINE against a fake `GrowwSDK` (canned expiries+contracts, NO candle method), a synchronous fake `run_parallel`, a REAL temp `RegistryStore`, an in-memory coverage sink, injected `now`/`today`: happy persist (expiries+contracts land in the registry with correct side/strike, the coverage rollup is `expiries_only`, ZERO candle calls asserted), the immutable-past skip (a settled past year is NOT re-fetched — `sdk.calls == []`, no new rows), an unsettled/previously-failed past year IS pulled, a current-year always-re-pull (settled but re-fetched), the Phase-2 expired-expiry skip (a settled+expired contract job is not re-fetched), a failed cell recorded as `failed` while the sibling completes (run resumes), a zero-expiry clean cell → `pending`, dry-run empty chain (0 persisted, honest note), the production-default `run_parallel`/clock seam, the underlying dedup, + the module-internal seams (`_EmptyChainSDK` metadata-only, `_resolve_client_factory` injected/dry-run/live, `_rate_hooks` offline/live) driven offline with a real `RateController` (no network); property/golden/bench/stress — n/a (an orchestration glue over the already-verified pure engine + SQL store, not a hot path). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — the wiring of a major dormant subsystem):** the exact signatures of `run_two_phase`/`resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts`/`RegistryStore`/`coverage_ledger` were READ + quoted from source before wiring (no assumed signatures — Golden Rule #1): `run_two_phase(cells, *, fetch_expiries, fetch_contracts, run_parallel, on_expiry_cell, on_contract, contract_skip=frozenset(), today=None)` with `ExpiryCell=(str,str,int)` / `ContractJob=(str,str,date)`, `resolve_expiries(client, *, exchange, underlying_symbol, year=None, month=None) -> list[date]`, `resolve_contracts(client, *, exchange, underlying_symbol, expiry) -> list[DerivativeContract]` (each carrying `.symbol`/`.contract_type`∈{FUT,CE,PE}/`.strike`); 739. **DEC-DERIV-REGISTRY-DB-VIEW-001 — PR-4: browse the F&O expiries+contracts REGISTRY in `/db` (structured by expiry / strike / CE-PE), so a pulled chain is visible** (2026-06-14). **Why:** PR-1 (#732, DEC-DERIV-METADATA-HISTORICAL-SPLIT-001) shipped the SEPARATE `registry.duckdb` cache (the actual expiry DATES + contract SYMBOLS the lean instrument master discards per DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001), but nothing surfaced it — the operator asked for the STRUCTURED chain table (expiry → strike → CE/PE) to be visible in the `/db` browser, the way the spot `bars/`, the expired-options `options/` lake, and the `window_ledger/` Parquet sidecar already each get their own clickable read-only row. Without a view the registry is a write-only black box: after a metadata pull there is no way to eyeball what expiries/contracts were cached or each leg's per-contract `candle_status`. **What shipped (PR-4 of 6 — the `/db` VIEW only; no engine/52-vocab/ingest/registry-schema change, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` — pure, FastAPI-free helpers `registry_path_for(store_path)` (resolves `registry.duckdb` as a SIBLING of `instruments.duckdb`, the same way the candle/option readers resolve the lake root — ONE resolver, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON), `registry_counts(registry_path)` → `{expiries, contracts, exists, note}`, and `list_registry_expiries`/`list_registry_contracts(registry_path, *, exch=None, underlying=None[, expiry_date=None])` returning the JSON-safe grid shape (`{columns, rows, total, note}`) the page renders — dates as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, `fetched_at` as clean IST (store-UTC/display-IST, §6), `strike` kept full numeric precision (not money, never rounded — §4; `None` for a FUT leg), reading read-only via `RegistryStore` (closed before return). A MISSING `registry.duckdb` degrades to an empty grid + an honest `note` ("no registry yet — pull expiries + contracts first") and NEVER opens/creates the file (a pure count never side-effects an empty cache) and NEVER invents a row (Golden Rule #1) — mirroring the expired-options "empty" path. The `contracts` `expiry_date` filter is parsed via the shared strict-ISO `_parse_iso_date` BEFORE the file check, so a malformed bound is rejected consistently whether or not the cache exists. (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — two thin routes `GET /api/v1/db/registry/expiries` + `GET /api/v1/db/registry/contracts` (optional `exch`/`underlying`[/`expiry_date`] query filters), same `run_in_threadpool` + `_require_store` + `getattr(store,'path')` + `ValueError→HTTP 400` pattern as the existing `/db/candles` + `/db/options` routes; each also stamps `counts` for the nav badges. (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html` — an "F&O registry" nav heading with two clickable rows ("📅 expiries" + "🔗 contracts") wired to a new `selectRegistry()` that fetches the grid + renders it via the shared `gridAndPager` (mirrors the `window_ledger` `selectLedger` row), backfilling the nav badges from the route `counts` and showing the honest empty `note` until a later PR populates the cache. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the VIEW only — registry schema/engine/52-vocab UNTOUCHED; ✅ read-only by construction (every path opens the store read-only + closes it; no write code path); ✅ honest empty state — a missing/empty registry degrades to a `note`, never an invented row, never a 500; ✅ path resolved as the master's sibling via ONE resolver (no re-derivation); 🟡 the registry is EMPTY until PR-2/PR-3 populate it via the metadata pull — this PR makes it browsable, it does not fill it; 🟡 OHLC is still NOT here (stays on the verified `bars/`/`options/` lakes per #732). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — grid rows mirror the registry tables 1:1; ISO dates, full-precision strike, IST stamps; the FUT `None` strike preserved; (2) Reliability — a missing/absent cache degrades to an empty grid + note, never a 500; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + drop ledger #739 (no store/lake/schema migration — pure additive view); (4) Idempotence — read-only, same registry → same grid bit-for-bit; (5) Honesty — the missing-registry note names WHY ("pull expiries + contracts first"); a pure count never creates the file; never an invented row (Golden Rule #1); (6) Observability — `registry_counts` + the two grids expose the cache state in the browser; (7) Honest envelope — VIEW only, registry empty until populated, OHLC excluded. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit — `tests/unit/test_db_view_registry.py` (13 tests: path-is-sibling, counts missing/no-create/seeded, expiries grid missing/all/filtered, contracts grid missing/all/expiry-filtered/no-match, malformed-expiry reject on both missing + seeded file) against a REAL temp `registry.duckdb` seeded via `RegistryStore`; integration/route — `tests/unit/test_dashboard_registry_routes.py` (6 tests: empty→200+note for both routes, seeded chain for both, expiry filter, malformed-expiry→HTTP 400) via FastAPI `TestClient` over a wired `InstrumentStore`; property/golden/bench/stress — n/a (a deterministic read-only SQL view, not a hot path). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** the design reused the established `/db` patterns verbatim — the `window_ledger` `selectLedger` nav-row + grid-shape route for the template/route, the candle/option `getattr(store,'path')`+`run_in_threadpool`+`ValueError→400` envelope, and the registry's own static parameterized filters — so no new architectural surface; the make-or-break (resolve `registry.duckdb` as the master's sibling, NOT inside it) was confirmed against the PR-1 store docs + `instrument_store.DEFAULT_DB_NAME`. **Verified:** `--cov=brutex.dashboard.db_view --cov-branch` → **100.00%** (497 stmts / 160 branches, 0 missed, 0 partial) across the db_view test suite incl. the new file; ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) on `db_view.py`/`app.py`/both test files; interrogate (CI flags) → 100% on `db_view.py`; bandit (project config, production files) → 0 issues (no `# noqa`/`# nosec` added). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/unit/test_db_view_registry.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_registry_routes.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DERIV-REGISTRY-DB-VIEW-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DERIV-METADATA-HISTORICAL-SPLIT-001 (#732, PR-1, the registry store this views), DEC-DB-VIEWER-001 (the `/db` browser), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the Parquet-sidecar nav-row + grid-shape route pattern reused), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean master whose discarded legs the registry caches).

747. **DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001 — the PRODUCTION Groww backtesting per-second ceiling is raised to an operator-DIRECTED 8 r/s, and BOTH production build sites (dashboard + CLI) converge on ONE shared constant** (2026-06-14). **Why (operator-directed + explicitly approved, satisfying CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6's "explicit user approval" gate to raise the ceiling):** the two production controllers had DRIFTED apart — the dashboard `_build_live_controller` injected NO `ceiling_rps`, so it fell back to the vendor-neutral `rate_common.CEILING_RPS` DEFAULT of 5 r/s, while the CLI live pull injected `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_UNVERIFIED=10` (`brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py:140`) — two different production ceilings for the SAME vendor endpoint, violating CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON (one source of truth). (3) `brutex/cli.py:2020` — the live spot pull's `RateController` swaps `ceiling_rps=GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_UNVERIFIED` (was 10) for `ceiling_rps=GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING` (8). no claim is made that 8 is a vendor-verified limit; ✅ the raised ceiling is BOUNDED + SELF-CORRECTING — the adaptive AIMD ladder is byte-unchanged: a 429 burst still steps 8→…→3 (the soft `FLOOR_RPS`) and a sustained 429/timeout storm still eases to the deep 1 r/s floor (DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001), recovering back up to 8 once clear; ✅ the 500/min governor is untouched and can never be overshot (480 < 500); ✅ the vendor-neutral `rate_common.CEILING_RPS=5` DEFAULT is unchanged (a different/un-injected vendor still starts at 5); 🟡 the per-second cap remains an OPEN Phase-0 probe gate — a future probe transcript could move it (ADR-0009 §3.1/§4); 748. **DEC-DERIV-PULL-HISTORICAL-001 — PR-5 (the capstone): a SEPARATE `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-historical` route + a "⤓ Pull historical" button that downloads OHLC candles for the operator-SELECTED cached contracts (single / an expiry's chain / a whole underlying / all), Path A (the verified candle lake — NOT the OptionBar lake), auto-retry-until-clean by default** (2026-06-14, ADR-0010 PR-5 of 6). **Why:** PR-1 (#732) shipped the `RegistryStore` cache, PR-2 (#735) the metadata-only `pull_expiries_contracts` orchestration, PR-3 (#737) the metadata-ONLY `/pull-expiries-contracts` route + repointed `⛓` button, PR-4 (#736) the `/db` registry chain view. Those cache every expiry DATE + contract SYMBOL WITHOUT a single candle (the cheap, NSE-verifiable chain shape in minutes). The HEAVY half — the weeks-scale historical OHLC fill — was deliberately left to its OWN button (the whole point of the metadata/historical SPLIT, DEC-DERIV-METADATA-HISTORICAL-SPLIT-001 §Why). PR-5 ships that twin: download the candles for an operator SELECTION of the already-cached contracts WITHOUT re-enumerating the chain (the metadata is in the registry; `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` are never re-called). **What shipped (REFERENCE_ONLY lake pull path — the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + every spot ingest path are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; a NEW dashboard module + ONE route + ONE button — the existing `derivatives_pull.py` / `metadata_pull.py` UNCHANGED, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` — a fully-injectable `pull_contract_candles(contracts: Sequence[ContractRow], *, lake_root, dry_run, intervals, registry, from_date=None, to_date=None, now=None, client_factory=None, on_progress=None, session_rate=None, until_clean=False, until_clean_rounds=AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS) -> HistoricalPullReport` that: REBUILDS each `ContractRow` into a `DerivativeContract` via `parse_contract_symbol(row.contract_symbol, underlying_symbol=row.underlying, expiry=row.expiry_date)` (the row's AUTHORITATIVE underlying+expiry, never re-parsed from the lossy `DDMmmYY` token — bit-faithful to what the metadata pull persisted, Golden Rule #1), SPLITS the selection by ledger market (`FUT`→`groww-future`, `CE`/`PE`→`groww-option` — the SAME split the bulk pull uses, DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001, so option/future windows never collide), feeds the RAW per-market contracts list to the verified `run_groww_option_ingest(client, sink, contracts=…, intervals=…, start, end, …, market=…)` spine, and AFTER a contract's candles land CLEAN (every `(contract, interval)` pair SUCCESS — no quarantine, no transient residual, via `_clean_symbols`) sets `registry.set_candle_status(exch, underlying, contract_symbol, "complete")` on the row's PK. (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-historical` resolving the SELECTION grammar (first non-empty wins) via `_resolve_historical_contracts` over `RegistryStore.list_contracts(...)`: `?contract=` (one full symbol), `?contracts=a,b,c` (multi), `?underlying=NIFTY[&expiry=2020-01-02]` (one expiry's chain or the whole underlying), `?kind=index|stock` (every cached contract of that kind's admitted underlyings, via the SAME `_select_bulk_targets` classifier), `?all=true` (every cached contract). An EMPTY registry / no-match is an honest 400 pointing at the `⛓` button (NEVER a fabricated contract); a bad `interval`/`expiry` is a 400. `until_clean` DEFAULTS to `true` (DEC-GROWW-DERIV-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 #730 — auto-retry every failed window until clean). Runs on the single-flight `_pull_job` (poll `/pull-progress`). (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — the "⤓ Pull historical" button next to the `⛓` metadata button (enabled when an underlying is highlighted; POSTs `?underlying=…[&expiry=ISO]&interval=…`), and the option-chain CELL click wired to pull that expiry's chain history (the cells carry no registry contract_symbol, so the cell click is the per-expiry grain available); tooltip "download OHLC for the SELECTED contracts (single / chain / all) — auto-retries until clean". **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 + #10) — the Path-A-not-Path-B decision:** the candles land on **PATH A** (the standard verified candle lake, `bars/<exch>/FNO/<groww_symbol>/<interval>/` via `ParquetBarSink` — the SAME lake the bulk derivatives pull writes, through the SAME `run_groww_option_ingest` spine), **NOT PATH B** (the `options/` OptionBar lake). PATH B's OptionBar schema needs `iv` / `spot` / `ATM±N` enrichment that `get_historical_candles` does NOT return — fabricating those to satisfy the OptionBar shape would violate Golden Rule #1, so Path A (raw OHLCV+OI, exactly what the vendor returns) is the honest home; the OptionBar/movers lake stays a separate, separately-fed surface. ✅ no re-enumeration — the contracts come from the registry, asserted by the test fake's `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` never being called; ✅ honest empty selection — 0 contracts → 0 bars + a "pull metadata first" note (route → 400); ✅ honest dry-run — the empty-candle client appends 0 bars (an expired contract's OHLC is REAL vendor data, never fabricated offline), but an EMPTY window is a SETTLED clean window so the selected contracts ARE marked complete (the status reflects coverage of the SELECTED range, honestly empty offline); ✅ a quarantined/still-failing contract is LEFT `none` (never marked complete on a partial pull); ✅ idempotent — the keep-first sink + WindowLedger make every re-run bit-stable; 🟡 NETWORK-bound, NOT O(1)-total — the per-contract fetch tiles each contract's range (a full underlying's minute fill is genuinely weeks-scale); a round here is `O(failed windows)` (NO re-enumeration — the contract list is fixed, UNLIKE the chain pull's `O(chain)+O(failed)` round), the same shape as the spot round; 🟡 the live `client_factory`/`_build_live_client` bodies + the route `_work` thread body are `# pragma: no cover` (genuine TOTP + network). **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — `parse_contract_symbol` rebuilds bit-faithfully from the authoritative row; `_clean_symbols` marks complete ONLY a fully-clean contract; the selection grammar resolves to exactly the registry rows; (2) Reliability — bounded until-clean rounds (`until_clean_rounds`, `stop_when_stuck=True`), never infinite; per-pair quarantine (one bad contract never kills the pull); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + the registry/ledger are rebuildable caches (a re-pull restores); the `candle_status` marker is additive (default `none`); (4) Idempotence — WindowLedger SUCCESS-skip + keep-first sink make every round/re-pull rerun-safe (bit-for-bit); (5) Honesty — empty/no-match → 400 not a fabricated contract; Path A not a fabricated OptionBar; a partial pull leaves `none`; the dry-run note says "set credentials"; (6) Observability — the per-`(contract, interval)` progress hook + the `HistoricalPullReport` (selected/completed/bars/windows/failed_pairs/still_failed/auth + note) + structlog `universe.pull_historical.requested`; (7) Honest envelope — network-bound, NOT O(1)-total; `O(failed windows)` per round; live/`_work` bodies pragma'd. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, 25 tests, 100% line+branch on `historical_pull.py`) — a fake `GrowwSDK` (canned candles, `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` asserted NEVER called), a recording `BarSink` (asserts PATH A `segment=FNO` appends), a REAL temp `RegistryStore`: the resolved contracts ARE the selection (no re-enum), `set_candle_status("complete")` per LANDED contract, the option/future market split, terminal-quarantine-leaves-none, auth-abort-halts, until-clean default single-pass / runs-to-clean / zero-rounds-safe-no-op, dry-run empty, range clamp/inversion, the `_build_note` arms, `_clean_symbols` excluding quarantine+still-failing, and the `DerivativeContract` reconstruction fidelity (CE strike/expiry/type, FUT strike=None, strike full-precision not money-rounded); route (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_historical_route.py`, 14 tests) — every selection arm (single/multi/chain/underlying/kind/all) resolves to the registry rows through an OFFLINE `pull_contract_candles` fake (asserts the passed contracts list, NOT a re-enumeration), the empty/no-match/no-selection honest 400s, the bad-interval/bad-expiry 400s, `until_clean` default-true echoed + false honored, the interval echo, the button-present assertion, and the `_resolve_historical_contracts` grammar direct. Existing `test_dashboard_derivatives_pull.py` (`pull_all_derivatives` UNTOUCHED) + `test_registry_store.py` re-run green. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — the candle-ingest wiring is operator-flagged for careful review):** the make-or-break invariants were verified by reading the REAL signatures before coding — `RegistryStore.list_contracts(*, exch, underlying, expiry_date)` + `set_candle_status(exch, underlying, contract_symbol, candle_status) -> int`; the `DerivativeContract(underlying_symbol, expiry, symbol, contract_type, strike=None)` ctor (NOT `symbol/contract_type/strike` positionally as the brief paraphrased — adapted to the real keyword ctor + `__post_init__` strike-required-for-CE/PE invariant); `parse_contract_symbol(symbol, *, underlying_symbol, expiry)`; `run_groww_option_ingest(client, sink, *, contracts: Iterable[DerivativeContract], intervals, start, end, …, market) -> GrowwOptionIngestReport` (takes a RAW contracts iterable — the SPECIFIC-contracts pull with NO re-enumeration, the whole point); and the `_build_live_derivative_client` / `_rate_hooks` / `run_until_clean` patterns reused verbatim from `derivatives_pull.py`. **Verified (3.12 venv + native wheels):** ✅ ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) on every touched file; ✅ interrogate 100% on `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` + the new `app.py` symbols (CI flags: `--ignore-private --ignore-nested-functions --ignore-module --ignore-magic --ignore-setters --fail-under=100`); ✅ bandit 0 issues; ✅ 100% line+branch on `historical_pull.py` (155 stmts / 32 branch, 0 miss) + the route's new lines + both helpers (`--cov=brutex.dashboard.app` shows ZERO miss in the route 1715-1838 + `_parse_iso_date_arg` + `_resolve_historical_contracts` ranges; the `_work` thread body is `# pragma: no cover`); 39 new tests + the existing derivatives-pull / registry-store / metadata suites → all green; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` → OK. 754. **DEC-DATEPICKER-LABEL-CLOSE-FIX-001 — the shared drill calendar no longer self-closes when you click a year/month on `/movers` + `/reports`, and those pages' main section headings get the gradient accent bar** (2026-06-14). **Why (operator screenshots — the drill closes before a day can be picked):** the shared `bx-datepicker.js` (DEC-UNIVERSE-DATEPICKER-SHARED-001) works on `/db` + `/universe` but on `/movers` (`movers.html`) + `/reports` (`reports.html`) clicking the header to drill into the month/year grid AUTO-CLOSED the popover. **Root cause (verified, not guessed — Golden Rule #1):** on those two pages the `<input type=date>` is nested INSIDE a `<label>`; `wireLooseInput` hides the native input but leaves it in the label, so the whole popover mounts inside the `<label>`. A `<label>` forwards activation clicks to its labelled control, so a drill click is RE-FIRED by the browser as a synthetic click on the hidden native input — a SEPARATE event whose `e.target` is the input (a sibling of the popover `wrap`). That bubbles to the outside-close handler (`if(!wrap.contains(e.target)) close()`); the input is "outside" `wrap`, so `close()` collapsed the popover. The popover's own `e.stopPropagation()` cannot stop it (different event, different node). `/db` + `/universe` never nest the input in a `<label>`, so no forwarding — which is why they worked. **What shipped (single-source fix in the shared component + a heading-polish pass, no engine/route/data change, CLAUDE.md §3/§11 COMMON):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-datepicker.js` — the `buildCalendar` outside-close handler now treats the picker's OWN backing input(s) as inside: `if (wrap.contains(e.target) || e.target === fromInput || (!single && e.target === toInput)) return; close();` — so the label-forwarded synthetic click never closes the drill. One line in the ONE shared component fixes `/movers`, `/reports`, the Run-Sweep `#swStart`/`#swEnd`, and any future loose-input page (COMMON). (2) `brutex/dashboard/templates/reports.html` — the `h1` rule gains `display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; padding-bottom:10px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--border)` + an `h1::before` gradient accent bar (`linear-gradient(180deg,var(--blue),var(--purple))`, 3×18px) so the "📑 Pre-Open / 🚀 Run Sweep / 🪜 Stage-4" headings align to the card's left edge like `/universe`'s `.col h3`. (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` — adds a `.card > h1` rule with the same accent bar + a `<h1>📊 Markets Movers</h1>` section heading (movers previously had NO heading element — it jumped straight to the tabs). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the drill now stays open until a day is clicked on every page (the root cause is the label-forwarding, fixed in the shared component — verified by reading the component + both templates, not assumed); ✅ pure progressive-enhancement / CSS — native controls + every prior pin unchanged, the picker value source is untouched; ✅ no design token was missing (the earlier audit's `--r-md`/`--ease`/`--line` theory was disproved — all three are defined on both pages; the real delta was the heading element + accent bar); 🟡 no automated screenshot-diff (sandbox limit) — verified via `node --check`, the TestClient render of both pages (`h1::before` + the accent gradient present, both 200, divs balanced), and the pinning test. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — root cause traced to the `<label>`-forward + the index-blind outside-close, fixed at the source; (2) Reliability — the guard is additive, the existing inside-click `stopPropagation` + Escape/outside-close all still hold; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` (one JS line + two CSS blocks + one `<h1>`); (4) Idempotence — pure render/CSS, no state; (5) Observability — n/a (client-only); (6) Security — no new sink; (7) Honesty — envelope above, screenshot-diff gap disclosed. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** DETECT — operator screenshots of `/movers` + `/reports` closing on drill + misaligned headings; VERIFY — 2-agent parallel hostile root-cause (the `<label>`-forwarding mechanism + the heading-element delta, each with file:line) + a workspace-health agent (239 modules import clean, live package 100%, all 11 pages render 200 with balanced divs, 1234 dashboard tests green, ruff clean); RECONCILE — the fix is in the ONE shared component (no per-page copy); PREVENT — `tests/unit/test_dashboard_calendar_label_fix.py` pins the `e.target === fromInput`/`toInput` guard + the `h1::before` accent bar on both pages; AUDIT — this entry; RECOVER — `git revert`; COOLDOWN — CI watch. **Verified (3.12 venv + native wheels):** `node --check bx-datepicker.js` OK; the 2 new pins pass; a 257-test `sweep_run_route|movers|datepicker|static|universe_premium|reports` sweep → all green; `/movers` + `/reports` render 200 with the accent bar; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` OK. (Used entry #754 — the strict max+1 on this base is 749, reserved by the concurrent live-feed branch DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 #749; #750 leaves a one-number gap the numbering gate permits, avoiding the collision.) **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-datepicker.js`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/reports.html`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_calendar_label_fix.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DATEPICKER-LABEL-CLOSE-FIX-001. **Builds on** DEC-UNIVERSE-DATEPICKER-SHARED-001 (#742, the shared component this hardens), DEC-UNIVERSE-GOTO-DRILL-001 (the drill calendar), DEC-UNIVERSE-UI-POLISH-001 (the design-token + accent-bar polish language this extends to movers/reports).
753. **DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 — a NEW `brutex/live/` package: capture the Groww LIVE websocket feed for the spot indexes, fold the ticks into 1-minute candles over the 09:15:00–15:29:00 IST session, and diff those LIVE candles against the backtest `get_historical_candles` 1-minute candles — the operator-directed answer to "is our live feed's 1-minute bar identical to the historical bar we backtest on?"** (2026-06-14). **Why (operator decree, hard Monday-open deadline):** before relying on any live-vs-backtest comparison the operator needs to (a) capture every applicable tick precisely, (b) build the SAME 1-minute candle the backtest uses (the 375-bar session grid), (c) confirm parity end-of-day, plus the scalability/cadence diagnostics — how many websocket connections one key holds, and whether ticks arrive in MILLISECONDS or SECONDS. The tickvault Claude session correctly routed this to BruteX (Groww + Python + "measure/experiment" = BruteX; Dhan + Rust + live order placement = tickvault — tickvault is hard-locked to 2 Dhan WebSockets, Rust-only, `.env`-banned). **Scope guard (Golden Rule #3 / CLAUDE.md §1):** REFERENCE/RESEARCH ONLY — read-only market data, **NO order placement anywhere**, NOT wired into the brute-force engine or the 52-condition vocabulary; the live feed stays out of the Track-1 ENGINE scope — this is a side MEASUREMENT tool the operator explicitly authorized, recorded here so the expansion is never silent. **What shipped (all pure + injected → unit-tested with fakes, no `growwapi`/network):** `brutex/live/store.py` (`TickStore` — append-only JSONL, ONE line per feed callback storing the RAW snapshot verbatim, resume-safe + idempotent: the full-fidelity capture sink so any later parsing decision re-applies offline to the SAME log without re-capturing — "capture EVERYTHING", Golden Rule #7); `tick.py` (`LiveTick` + `flatten_index_snapshot` tolerant of the flat / nested / leaf-dict shapes the SDK emits — Decimal rupees via `str()` parse, never float, `NFR-DET-001`); `candle_builder.py` (`build_minute_candles` — ticks → 1-minute `CandleBar`, window 09:15:00→15:29:00 IST ONLY, OHLC first/max/min/last, volume 0 + open_interest None for indices, label = UTC minute start so live and backtest align by `==`); `parity.py` (`compare_candles` → `ParityReport`: per-minute matched / mismatched / live-only / backtest-only, Decimal equality, volume excluded by default since index bars are 0 on both sides); `report.py` (`render_parity_markdown` — the dead-simple human verdict + divergence table even a non-engineer reads); `probe.py` (`probe_connections` incremental 1..N ramp stopping at the first refusal + reporting the ceiling/error, and `analyze_cadence` ms-vs-seconds classification from the captured log); `capture.py` (`TickCapture` — the subscribe + on-tick loop, feed injected); `serde.py` (Decimal-exact candle JSON round-trip for build↔parity); and `__main__.py` (`python -m brutex.live capture|cadence|build|parity|probe-connections` — the operator-runnable CLI; structlog, NOT print, to satisfy the banned-pattern gate). **Verified SDK facts (read from `growwapi` v1.5.x `feed.py`, no hallucination — Golden Rule #1):** the feed `on_data_received` callback is 0-ARGUMENT (a "data arrived" signal); the snapshot is pulled via `GrowwFeed.get_index_value()` (indices) / `get_ltp()` (equities); instrument dicts are `{exchange, segment, exchange_token}`; a daemon consume thread auto-delivers once subscribed. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ 100% line+branch coverage on ALL 10 `brutex/live` modules (40 unit tests across `test_live_core.py` + `test_live_cli.py`, real 3.12 venv + native wheels), ruff + ruff-format + mypy-strict clean (the `growwapi` import mirrors the merged `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py` `# type: ignore[import-not-found]` pattern — `growwapi` is the `groww` optional extra, absent from the CI type-check install, so import-not-found is correct there); ✅ the candle builder + parity + cadence + store + the entire CLI dispatch are fully tested against a FAKE feed; 🟡 the REAL websocket capture (`_real_feed_builder` / `_real_instrument_resolver` in `__main__.py`) is `# pragma: no cover` — it needs `growwapi` + TOTP creds + a live market and runs on the operator's Mac (mirrors `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py`'s real-SDK shim); 🟡 the exact live snapshot leaf shape, the connection ceiling, and the true tick cadence are Phase-0 VERIFY-ON-RUN items the Monday capture answers — the raw snapshot is persisted verbatim so a wrong leaf-guess is re-parseable, NEVER a data-loss event; 🟡 capture is NETWORK/clock-bound, not an O(1)-total claim (per-callback append + per-minute fold are O(1)). **Runbook:** `docs/runbooks/groww_live_capture.md` gives the exact Monday-09:15-IST command sequence (probe → capture → cadence → build → parity). **Files:** `brutex/live/__init__.py`, `brutex/live/tick.py`, `brutex/live/store.py`, `brutex/live/candle_builder.py`, `brutex/live/parity.py`, `brutex/live/report.py`, `brutex/live/probe.py`, `brutex/live/capture.py`, `brutex/live/serde.py`, `brutex/live/__main__.py` (all NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_core.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py` (NEW), `docs/runbooks/groww_live_capture.md` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001. **Builds on** DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (ADR-0009 — the Groww SDK + auth + instrument master this consumes), DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (the 1-minute base the parity compares), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the 2-decimal candle grid).

756. **DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 — the live capture stamps OUR receive time in NANOSECONDS + surfaces the vendor's UNTAMPERED `tsInMillis`, and the captured ticks/1-minute-candles persist to a separate `live/` Parquet lake (`live_ticks` / `live_candles_1m`)** (2026-06-14, extends DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 #753). **Why (operator correctness decree — "check their precise request/response first"):** the operator required that (a) OUR received-at be nanoseconds (the cadence oracle), and (b) the vendor's OWN timestamp be stored UNTAMPERED, never rounded/edited. **VERIFIED (no hallucination, Golden Rule #1) — read from the `growwapi` proto descriptor** (`growwapi/groww/proto/stocks_socket_response_pb2.py`, decoded via `MessageToDict(preserving_proto_field_name=True)`): the live feed leaf is `stocksLiveIndices {tsInMillis: double, value: double}` (index) / `stockLivePrice {tsInMillis, ltp, open/high/low/close, volume, value, openInterest, …}` (LTP) — so **the vendor timestamp is `tsInMillis`, i.e. MILLISECONDS** (a double), one per instrument per update. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only — read-only, no orders, NOT in the engine/52-vocab; extends the #749 live package):** (1) `brutex/live/capture.py` — `TickCapture` gains an injected `ns_clock` (default `time.time_ns`); `_on_tick` stamps `recv_ns` (nanoseconds, OURS) alongside `recv_ts`. (2) `brutex/live/store.py` — `TickRecord.recv_ns` + `append(..., recv_ns=...)` persist it; the raw snapshot (carrying `tsInMillis`) was already stored verbatim, so the vendor timestamp is preserved untampered by construction. (3) `brutex/live/tick.py` — a new `Quote` + `extract_quotes(snapshot)` pulls, per instrument, the price (`value`/`ltp`) AND the vendor `tsInMillis` (untampered) + `volume`/`openInterest` (the proto sends these as doubles → coerced to int); the bool-`tsInMillis` and missing-field permutations are handled. (4) `brutex/live/lake.py` (NEW) — writes `live_ticks` (`capture_run_id, seq, recv_ns Int64, recv_ts, vendor_ts_ms Float64 UNTAMPERED, session_date, exchange/segment/instrument_key/groww_symbol, value Float64 [RAW — full precision, only candles snap to 2dp], volume, open_interest, feed_kind, raw_json`) and `live_candles_1m` (schema-IDENTICAL to the backtest bars — `timestamp µs UTC, open/high/low/close Float64 2dp, volume/open_interest Int64` — + `session_date, tick_count, source='live', built_run_id, …`) to a SEPARATE `<lake_root>/live/<table>/dt=<session_date>.parquet` tree (never the brute-force `bars/` lake — scope guard); merge-on-write + idempotent (dedup on the PK), keep-first. (5) `brutex/live/__main__.py` — a `lake` subcommand (`python -m brutex.live lake --in <jsonl> --lake-root <root> --run-id <id>`) persists a captured log into both tables. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ vendor `tsInMillis` is MILLISECONDS and stored UNTAMPERED (a separate `vendor_ts_ms` column; our `recv_ns` is the only OURS clock); ✅ tick `value` is RAW (full precision) — only the 1-minute candle snaps to the 2dp grid (DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001); ✅ candle window unchanged (09:15:00–15:29:00 IST, 375 bars); ✅ 100% line+branch on all 11 `brutex/live` modules (52 tests; the proto fields verified from the installed wheel), ruff + mypy clean (the polars schema uses dtype INSTANCES; the `growwapi` import-not-found ignore mirrors the merged `auth.py`); 🟡 the `/db` LIVE-FEED visual section (browsing these two tables + a `live_vs_backtest_1m` view) is the NEXT increment; 🟡 the real websocket capture stays `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac). **Files:** `brutex/live/lake.py` (NEW), `brutex/live/{capture,store,tick,__main__}.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_lake.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_core.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753, the live package), DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (the 1-minute base), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the candle 2dp grid), DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (the Groww SDK whose proto was verified).

752. **DEC-LIVE-VERIFY-001 — a `verify` subscription SELF-TEST that PROVES the live feed subscribes to every instrument + ticks per-instrument, plus a full-universe (`all`) resolver that subscribes every index AND its F&O stocks** (2026-06-14, extends DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 #756). **Why (operator decree — "real guarantee, not talk"):** the operator asked how the live feed is ASSURED to work + to have subscribed all indices and their stocks. Honest answer (Golden Rule #10): the live Groww websocket CANNOT be exercised in CI/sandbox (no token, no market hours, restricted egress) — so instead of claiming it works, BruteX ships an EXECUTABLE PROOF the operator runs on the Mac. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only — read-only, no orders; extends the #749/#751 live package):** (1) `brutex/live/verify.py` (NEW) — `verify_subscription(...)` reuses `TickCapture` (COMMON — one capture path) to subscribe to ALL requested instruments and tally ticks PER instrument over a window, returning a `SubscriptionReport` (`requested` / `observed` / `total_ticks` / `silent` + per-instrument `InstrumentCheck`); `all_requested_ticking` is the pass/fail; `render_subscription_markdown` writes the human proof table (each instrument: ticks + ✅/—). Silence on an instrument is REPORTED (subscribed-but-quiet), never hidden. (2) `brutex/live/__main__.py` — a `verify` subcommand (`python -m brutex.live verify --out … --report … [--symbols all] [--seconds 60]`) that subscribes, proves, writes the table, and EXIT-CODES 1 if any requested instrument was silent; the `_real_instrument_resolver` now accepts the sentinel `all`/`universe` → the FULL universe = every `IDX` PLUS every F&O-eligible single stock (an `EQ` whose `trading_symbol` is named by at least one `FUT`/`CE`/`PE` leg in the master), so `verify --symbols all` subscribes all indices AND their stocks. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the orchestration (subscribe → tally → report, both rc branches, silent-instrument detection) is 100% line+branch tested against a FAKE feed (59 live tests total); ✅ the proof is the operator's REAL run output, not a claim; 🟡 the real websocket + instrument-master download stay `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac, market hours); 🟡 the per-instrument key↔requested-dict exact mapping is an honest VERIFY-ON-RUN (the report compares observed-distinct vs requested-count; the live key shape is confirmed on the first real run). **Verified (3.12 venv + native wheels):** 59 live tests pass; `brutex.live` 100% line+branch (694 stmts / 140 branch, 0 missing — verify.py 50 stmts 100%); ruff + ruff-format + mypy-strict clean; a 5-agent-equivalent workspace verification (240 modules import, lake round-trips with `vendor_ts_ms` untampered, all 5 dashboard routes 200). **Files:** `brutex/live/verify.py` (NEW), `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_verify.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-VERIFY-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753).
749. **DEC-DERIV-DECOMMISSION-FUSED-001 — PR-6 (the final PR): decommission the OLD fused `/pull-derivatives` candle path; the bulk derivative buttons are repointed to metadata-only, so NO dashboard click triggers the runaway "download ALL candles" behaviour** (2026-06-14, ADR-0010 PR-6 of 6). **Why (operator directive 2026-06-14):** PR-3 (#737) repointed the PER-SELECTION "⛓ Pull expiries + contracts" button to the metadata-only `/pull-expiries-contracts` route and PR-5 (#748) shipped the separate "⤓ Pull historical" candle button — but the BULK ③④ derivative buttons (`bulkIdxDeriv` / `bulkStkDeriv`) still POSTed the FUSED `/api/v1/universe/pull-derivatives` route (DEC-PULL-DERIVATIVES-001 #710), whose `pull_all_derivatives` enumerates the chain AND immediately downloads `get_historical_candles` for every strike × every expiry × 2020→today on one click (the operator's reported "it keeps running" + the live `rate.429 → rate.stepdown 5→4` 500/min-governor burn, ADR-0010 §1). The metadata/historical SPLIT now covers everything (`⛓` metadata + `⤓` historical incl. `kind=index|stock` / `all=true`), so the fused path is dead weight that still exposes the runaway click. PR-6 removes it: no dashboard path can trigger a one-click whole-chain candle download. **What shipped (a dashboard UI repoint + a dead-route removal only — the brute-force ENGINE, the 52-vocab, and every SPOT ingest path are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `metadata_pull.py` / `historical_pull.py` behaviour UNCHANGED, only stale docstring cross-refs reworded, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — the bulk derivative button JS (`data-surface="derivatives"`) now POSTs `/api/v1/universe/pull-expiries-contracts?kind=<kind>` (metadata-only) and DROPS `derivKnobs()` (the interval/contract-type query — a metadata pull has no candles); the now-orphaned `derivKnobs()` function + the orphaned `derivInterval` / `derivType` dropdown controls + their `enhanceSelect` entries were removed; the ③④ button labels/tooltips reworded to "Expiries + contracts · metadata only · no history — use ⤓ Pull historical for OHLC" (the per-selection `⛓`/`⤓` buttons + the bulk SPOT ①② buttons are UNCHANGED). 751. **DEC-HISTORICAL-1DAY-FIRST-001 — the F&O "⤓ Pull historical" pull becomes a TWO-PHASE 1-day-first GLOBAL barrier: ALWAYS pull `1day` for EVERY selected contract first (even for a 1-minute-only request), proceed to `1minute` ONLY when the WHOLE 1-day phase cleaned, and start each contract's minute fill from the precise earliest 1-day bar date its own 1-day pull revealed** (2026-06-14, operator-confirmed). **Why (operator decree):** for F&O the 1-day OHLCV is NOT a bhavcopy cross-check (that is the spot path, DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 #723) — its sole job is to PIN each contract's precise listing/start date so the HEAVY 1-minute fill begins at the right date with no wasted windows.
