An F&O contract only trades from its listing day to its expiry, so blindly starting every contract's minute pull at the `2020-01-01` floor (`GROWW_HISTORICAL_FLOOR`) wastes the bulk of the per-contract API calls on dead periods the contract never traded. The fix: pull 1-day FIRST (cheap — one window per contract per the 180-day daily tier), and only after the ENTIRE 1-day phase settles clean, read each contract's REAL earliest 1-day bar date back off the just-written lake and START its 1-minute fill there. **What shipped (1 module changed + 2 test files; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + spot ingest + metadata pull are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; the `/api/v1/universe/pull-historical` route contract is UNCHANGED — it already passes `intervals`, the phasing lives INSIDE `pull_contract_candles`, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` — `pull_contract_candles` is re-shaped into two phases over the SAME fixed market buckets (FUT→`groww-future`, CE/PE→`groww-option`; the barrier applies to BOTH leg types, NOT special-cased): (1) **Phase 1 — `1day` ONLY, ALWAYS** via the extracted single-call-site `_run_phase(interval, …, contract_windows)` helper (the existing per-market `run_groww_option_ingest` + `_clean_symbols` + bounded `run_until_clean` loop, now parameterised by ONE interval) — run even when the operator requested only `1minute` (`minute_requested = "1minute" in intervals` decides ONLY whether Phase 2 runs; `1day` is de-duped so it is NEVER pulled twice). (2) **GLOBAL barrier** — `_PhaseResult.clean` is True iff EVERY selected contract symbol is in the phase's clean-landed union (`selected_symbols <= complete` — no quarantine, no still-failing, no auth death). If Phase 1 did NOT fully clean, the pull STOPS: `minute_skipped=True`, 1-minute is NOT started, and `_build_note`'s new `minute_skipped` arm reports "1-day phase INCOMPLETE — N/M cleaned; 1-minute SKIPPED (global barrier)". (3) **Phase 2 — `1minute` (only if requested AND barrier passed)** — `_discover_start_dates` reads each contract's earliest 1-day bar date from the just-written lake via the SHARED `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py` primitives (`Catalog.open` → `reconcile_catalog_from_lake(FNO, "1day")` → `contract_daily_coverage` → `coverage_to_minute_window`, DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 #712) — whose returned window `start` IS the discovered listing date (`max(full_start, coverage.first_date)`) and whose `end` clamps to the contract's expiry; that `{symbol: (start, end)}` map is passed as `run_groww_option_ingest`'s `contract_windows` so each contract's minute pull begins at its real date. A contract with ZERO 1-day bars (it never traded in range) is ABSENT from the map → EXCLUDED from Phase 2 (its 1-minute would be empty too), honestly reported via its absence from `start_dates`. The `HistoricalPullReport` gains `phase1_clean` / `phase1_complete` / `start_dates` (each contract's discovered ISO start) / `minute_requested` / `minute_skipped` (all surfaced in `to_dict`); `candle_status=complete` keys on the Phase-1 completion set (the 1-day pins ARE the historical-completion gate; Phase 2 is the optional heavy fill on top). **Why `_discover_start_dates` does NOT reuse `derive_contract_minute_windows` verbatim:** that convenience driver ALSO omits a contract whose bounded window collapses to the full range (the optimisation-only disjoint case) — here the map is the AUTHORITATIVE Phase-2 contract set, so a contract with REAL data but a full-range window must still be pulled (just from its discovered start), and ONLY a truly-no-coverage contract may be excluded; so the helper composes the lower-level `contract_daily_coverage` + `coverage_to_minute_window` directly, keeping every contract that has ANY 1-day coverage. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ 1-day ALWAYS first, even for a 1-minute-only request (mandatory Phase 1); ✅ GLOBAL barrier — 1-minute skipped entirely if ANY 1-day contract fails (no partial start), reported; ✅ Phase-2 start = the discovered 1-day MIN date, read from the lake, never fabricated (a zero-1-day contract is honestly excluded, not invented); ✅ Path A only (`bars/<exch>/FNO/…` via `run_groww_option_ingest` — never the OptionBar lake; no fabricated iv/spot); ✅ FUT + CE/PE both covered (the barrier is leg-type-agnostic); 🟡 NETWORK-bound, NOT O(1)-total — the phasing OPTIMISES the 1-minute window set (starts at each contract's real date), it does NOT make the pull O(1); the per-contract skip + dedup stay O(1) (frozenset membership + WindowLedger), the start-date map is O(contracts) memory; 🟡 the live `client_factory` / `_build_live_client` bodies stay `# pragma: no cover` (genuine TOTP + network), consistent with the existing module; a catalog-unavailable / per-contract-malformed start-discovery degrades to an EMPTY-or-partial map (logged loudly via `structlog`, every excluded contract reported), the honest conservative choice. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — `selected_symbols <= complete` is the exact barrier; the discovered start equals the lake's earliest 1-day IST date (asserted bit-exact against the fake's listing dates through a REAL `ParquetBarSink`+`Catalog`); 1-day is pulled exactly once under `both`; (2) Reliability — each phase runs the SAME bounded `run_until_clean` (`stop_when_stuck=True`, never infinite); per-pair quarantine survives (one bad contract quarantines, the barrier then withholds Phase 2); (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + the WindowLedger/keep-first sink make every re-pull rerun-safe (a re-pull re-derives the same start dates from the same 1-day lake); (4) Idempotence — Golden Rule #7: the bounded windows produce a lake byte-identical to a full-range pull (the ledger skips done windows); (5) Honesty — empty selection → honest 0-bar no-op; barrier-failed → 1-minute skipped + reported (never a silent partial); zero-1-day → excluded + reported; (6) Observability — the new report fields (`phase1_clean`/`phase1_complete`/`start_dates`/`minute_requested`/`minute_skipped`) + the `historical.start_discovery.*` structlog degrade events; (7) Scalability — the phasing is O(contracts) memory + O(1) per-contract window lookup; the heavy fill is unchanged in shape, only its window set is tightened to each contract's live span. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, +14 tests → 50 total, 100% line+branch on `historical_pull.py`, 220 stmts / 42 branch, 0 miss) — a two-phase fake `_PhasedSDK` (per-symbol 1-day listing dates + recorded 1-minute `start_time`s) over a REAL `ParquetBarSink`+`Catalog`: 1-day pulled FIRST for every contract even on a 1-minute-only request; the global barrier (a contract whose 1-day fails → ZERO minute calls for ANY contract, `minute_skipped` + the note); Phase-2 minute START == each contract's discovered 1-day date (bit-exact); a zero-1-day contract EXCLUDED from Phase 2; `intervals=["1day"]` runs only Phase 1 (no minute, never skipped); `both` pulls 1-day exactly once then 1-minute; dry-run 1-minute honest empty (no lake → no discovered starts → nothing to pull); and the `_discover_start_dates` degrade branches (catalog-open raises, reconcile raises, per-contract malformed-symbol skip, no-coverage exclude); route (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_historical_route.py`, the offline `pull_contract_candles` fake updated for the new report fields — 14 tests green). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 — the candle-ingest phasing is operator-flagged):** the make-or-break invariants were verified by reading the REAL signatures before coding — `run_groww_option_ingest(…, contract_windows: ContractWindows | None)` (the existing per-contract bounds hook this drives, DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001), `contract_daily_coverage(catalog, *, contract, interval="1day") -> ContractCoverage | None` (returns `None` on zero coverage — the exclusion signal), `coverage_to_minute_window(coverage, *, full_start, full_end, expiry)` (start=listing day, end=expiry+1 clamped), and the `_run_phase` extraction preserves the prior single-pass / until-clean / zero-rounds behaviour byte-for-byte (the 25 pre-existing tests pass unchanged). **Verified (3.12 venv + native wheels):** ✅ ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy --strict (whole `brutex`, 230 files) + pyright (0 errors on the 3 changed files); ✅ interrogate 100% on `historical_pull.py` (CI flags `--ignore-private --ignore-nested-functions --ignore-module --ignore-magic --ignore-setters --fail-under=100`); ✅ bandit 0 issues; ✅ vulture `--min-confidence 80` clean (exit 0); ✅ 100% line+branch on `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` (220 stmts / 42 branch, 0 miss); 50 pull-historical + 14 route + 328 pull/derivative-related tests green; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` → OK. (Used entry #751 — the strict max+1: #750 was taken by DEC-FNO-INDEX-MATCH-DIAG-001 on the post-squash main; pylint is a CI-only gate not installed in this venv, ruff's `PL` subset is enabled + green.) **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_historical_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-HISTORICAL-1DAY-FIRST-001. **Builds on** DEC-DERIV-PULL-HISTORICAL-001 (#748, the `pull_contract_candles` selection-based pull this phases), DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#723, the spot 1-day-first VERIFY-FIRST default this mirrors for F&O — but for F&O the 1-day pins the start date, NOT a bhavcopy check), DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 (#712, the `contract_bounds` coverage→window primitives this consumes for the per-contract start), DEC-GROWW-DERIV-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 (#730, the until-clean round-loop each phase reuses), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (the `run_groww_option_ingest` Path-A candle spine + its `contract_windows` hook).
750. **DEC-FNO-INDEX-MATCH-DIAG-001 — an OBSERVE-ONLY diagnostic that surfaces F&O indices silently dropped to REFERENCE_ONLY (losing their OPT badge) by a vendor symbol mismatch between the index's `IDX` spot row and the `underlying_symbol` Groww stamps on its option legs** (2026-06-14). **Why:** the OPT-vs-REF badge keys on an EXACT `(exchange, symbol_name)` match — `is_spot_only_index` (`brutex/universe.py`) tags an `IDX` row REFERENCE_ONLY iff it is NEITHER a brute-force index (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX) NOR in the options-eligible set built by `build_options_eligible_underlyings` (which keys on the option leg's `underlying_symbol` column — CLAUDE.md §6 "Instrument master schema", the 21-column Groww master with the `underlying_symbol` key; DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001). The `IDX` row's `symbol_name` comes from the CSV `trading_symbol` column; the leg's key comes from the `underlying_symbol` column. When those two strings differ for the SAME real index (e.g. the operator reports a `trading_symbol` like `NIFTYNEXT50` against a leg `underlying_symbol` like `NIFTY NEXT 50`), the exact match fails and a genuinely options-bearing index is mis-tagged REFERENCE_ONLY — and the operator could not tell WHICH string differed without reading the raw master by hand. This diagnostic REPORTS the real vendor strings so the operator can drive a SEPARATE data-fix; it hardcodes NO per-index alias (Golden Rule #1 — never invent a `NIFTYNEXT50 → NIFTY NEXT 50` map). **What shipped (DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — ZERO classification/behavior change; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + every spot/derivatives ingest path are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; only observability ADDED, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — one new pure function + one new structlog line, the existing `is_spot_only_index` / `build_options_eligible_underlyings` / the `reference_only` tagging all BYTE-UNCHANGED):** (1) `brutex/universe.py` — a frozen-dataclass `OptionUnderlyingGap(exchange, underlying_symbol, matched_index_symbol_name, nearest_index_symbol_name)`; a pure total `normalize_underlying_symbol(symbol) -> str` (uppercase + remove ASCII spaces and `-`, nothing more — it folds `"NIFTY NEXT 50"` ≈ `"NIFTYNEXT50"` but NEVER bridges a genuine abbreviation `"MIDCPNIFTY"` ≠ `"NIFTY MIDCAP SELECT"`); and `diagnose_unmatched_option_underlyings(instruments) -> list[OptionUnderlyingGap]` that, for every distinct NSE option `underlying_symbol` in the master, reports ONLY those with NO exact `IDX` `symbol_name` match AND that are NOT a known NSE `EQ` `symbol_name` (a stock option's spot row is its EQ row, not an index — so it is correctly excluded). For each reported gap, `matched_index_symbol_name` is always `None` (by construction — a gap exists precisely because nothing matched exactly) and `nearest_index_symbol_name` is the admitted `IDX` `symbol_name` whose normalized form equals the underlying's normalized form (a pure CASE/SPACE mismatch — operator just needs to align spelling) else `None` (a genuine abbreviation mismatch — needs a real data map elsewhere). The result is sorted deterministically by `(exchange, underlying_symbol)`; NumPy docstrings on every public symbol. (2) `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py` — wired into `load_instrument_master` right after `build_options_eligible_underlyings(index.universe)` (the diagnostic runs over the SAME full `index.universe` that still carries the option legs, before the lean ingest discards them), via a `_log_fno_index_gaps(gaps)` helper that emits exactly ONE structlog line `universe.load.fno_index_unmatched` with `count=<n>` and `gaps=[{underlying, nearest_index, exchange}, …]` (the inlined list capped at `_FNO_INDEX_GAP_LOG_CAP=50` so a pathological master cannot bloat one line; the full count is always carried by `count`). The line is emitted ONLY when `count > 0` (silent in the healthy steady state — sits next to the existing `universe.load.groww` / `universe.load.ntm_*` lines). The `reference_only` upsert predicate, the OPT badge, and the lean-store admission are all byte-unchanged. (Per the task's optional §3 a read-only `/api/v1/universe/fno-index-gaps` route was DELIBERATELY SKIPPED — it would touch `app.py` + add route tests + scope/risk; the structlog line fully satisfies the operator-visibility requirement, and the §3 directive was "if it adds risk/scope, SKIP it and just do the structlog line".) **Honesty + envelope (Golden Rule #1 + #10):** the diagnostic ONLY observes — running it against the test master confirmed `NIFTYNEXT50` STAYS `reference_only=True` (the bug is reported, NOT fixed), and the matched FINNIFTY STAYS option-pullable (no badge moved). It reports the REAL strings + a normalization-only nearest match; it never fabricates an alias. The scan is O(rows) over the in-memory master (a single pass the load already makes for `build_options_eligible_underlyings` — no extra network, no extra master read); NOT an O(1)-total claim. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — exact `symbol_name` match excludes correctly-matched indices; the EQ-name exclusion drops stock options; `normalize_underlying_symbol` flags case/space without bridging abbreviations; deterministic sort; (2) Reliability — pure, total, no I/O, no exceptions — cannot fail the load; an empty / index-only / leg-only master returns `[]`; (3) Recoverability — purely additive (a new function + a conditional log line); `git revert` removes it with zero state to unwind; (4) Idempotence — same master → same gap list bit-for-bit (sorted, set-deduped); the log line is a deterministic function of the master; (5) Honesty — reports real vendor strings + a normalization-only nearest; no invented alias; the bug is surfaced not silently fixed; (6) Observability — the single `universe.load.fno_index_unmatched` line (`count` + capped `gaps`) is the whole deliverable; (7) Honest envelope — observe-only, O(rows) single-pass, NOT O(1)-total; no classification touched. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit (`tests/unit/test_fno_index_diagnostic.py`, 18 tests, 100% line+branch on the new `universe.py` symbols + the loader change) — the pure layer covers the four required master shapes (an exactly-matched index → NOT reported; a case/space-only mismatch → reported with `nearest_index` set; a genuine-abbreviation mismatch → reported with `nearest_index=None`; an F&O-eligible equity underlying → NOT reported), plus a PE leg, a non-NSE leg, an empty iterable, a FUT leg (the option-branch False arm), duplicate legs collapsing to one gap, deterministic sort, and the `normalize_underlying_symbol` arms; the loader layer asserts (via `structlog.testing.capture_logs`, mirroring `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`) that a master with both mismatch kinds emits ONE `universe.load.fno_index_unmatched` line with `count=2` and exactly `[{MIDCPNIFTY,None,NSE},{NIFTY NEXT 50,NIFTYNEXT50,NSE}]`, that a no-gap master is SILENT, and that FINNIFTY keeps its non-reference badge (behavior unchanged). The existing `test_universe.py` + `test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py` suites re-run green (129 tests, no regression). **Verified (3.12 venv at `/home/user/bruteX/.venv` — the repo's PEP-695 generics need 3.12, NOT the sandbox 3.11):** ✅ ruff check + ruff format --check on the 3 touched files; ✅ mypy --strict (`brutex/universe.py` + `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py` + the test) → 0 issues; ✅ pyright → 0 errors / 0 warnings; ✅ interrogate `brutex` at the CI flags (`--ignore-private --ignore-magic --ignore-nested-functions --ignore-module --ignore-setters --fail-under=100`) → PASSED 100.0%; ✅ bandit -r brutex -ll → 0 issues; ✅ vulture `brutex scripts/ci/vulture_whitelist.py --min-confidence 80` → no findings; ✅ 100.00% line+branch on BOTH `brutex/universe.py` (128 stmts / 48 branch, 0 miss) and `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py` (109 stmts / 18 branch, 0 miss) over the new+existing tests; ✅ `validate_ledger_numbering.py` → OK. (pylint is a CI-only gate not installed in this venv; ruff's `PL` subset is enabled + green.) **Files:** `brutex/universe.py` (the `OptionUnderlyingGap` dataclass + `normalize_underlying_symbol` + `diagnose_unmatched_option_underlyings` + `__all__`), `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py` (the import + `_FNO_INDEX_GAP_LOG_CAP` + `_log_fno_index_gaps` + the one wired call), `tests/unit/test_fno_index_diagnostic.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-INDEX-MATCH-DIAG-001. **Builds on** DEC-NON-OPTION-INDEX-REFTAG-001 (the `is_spot_only_index` exact-match REF tagging this diagnostic instruments without changing), DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 (the `build_options_eligible_underlyings` option-underlying scan this mirrors), DEC-NTM-GROWW-REPOINT-001 (the keyless Groww load + `instrument_loader` structlog surface this adds one line to). **NOTE:** the actual REF→OPT data fix (aligning the mismatched strings) is a SEPARATE follow-up the operator authorizes ONCE this diagnostic reports the real strings from the live master — this PR adds ONLY the observability.

758. **DEC-SKIP-REF-METADATA-001 — the `⛓ Pull expiries + contracts` metadata route SKIPS reference-only underlyings BEFORE any `get_expiries` call, so a mistaken REF selection is a TRUE zero-call no-op (reported, never silently dropped)** (2026-06-14, operator-approved). **Why:** the metadata pull (DEC-DERIV-METADATA-ROUTE-001) calls `get_expiries` per selected underlying. A REFERENCE_ONLY underlying — a spot-only index (INDIAVIX / MIDCAP50 / NIFTY100 …) or a non-F&O NTM constituent (DEC-NON-OPTION-INDEX-REFTAG-001 / DEC-NTM-GROWW-REPOINT-001) — has NO F&O chain, so `get_expiries` returns empty and persists nothing (already SAFE — never fabricates), but it still costs ONE wasted empty network call per REF underlying. The operator approved closing that gap so a mistaken REF tick costs ZERO calls. **What shipped (a route-level pre-filter; ZERO change to `pull_expiries_contracts` itself; the engine / 52-vocab / spot ingest UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** in `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-expiries-contracts` (`brutex/dashboard/app.py`), AFTER the `symbols`/`symbol`/`kind` selection resolves into `instruments`, the route PARTITIONS on `store.reference_only_security_ids()` (the SAME set the `/universe` REF badge uses — CLAUDE.md §6): `tradable` = instruments whose `security_id` is NOT reference-only; `skipped_reference_only` = the rest (by `symbol_name`). Only `tradable` is passed to `pull_expiries_contracts` (a REF underlying never reaches `get_expiries`). If `tradable` is EMPTY (every selected underlying was reference-only), NO job starts — the route returns `started=False` + an honest note `"all N selected are reference-only (no F&O chain) — nothing to pull"` (never a fabricated pull). The `skipped_reference_only` list + count are echoed in the JSONResponse AND on the `universe.pull_expiries_contracts.requested` structlog line, so the operator SEES exactly what was dropped + why (never silently masked). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a mistaken REF selection is now a zero-call no-op (the wasted empty `get_expiries` is eliminated); ✅ TRADABLE (F&O) behaviour is byte-unchanged — only REF underlyings are filtered; ✅ the skipped set is REPORTED, never silently dropped; this is an efficiency + observability guard, NOT a behaviour change for F&O underlyings. 🟡 a REF selection was ALREADY safe (it persisted nothing); this PR only removes the wasted call + reports the skip. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — `reference_only_security_ids` is the authoritative REF set; `tradable` excludes exactly it; (2) Reliability — an all-REF selection is a clean `started=False` 200, never a started-then-empty job; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + drop ledger #758 (a route-level filter; trivially reversible); (4) Idempotence — the filter is a pure partition, deterministic given the store; (5) Honesty — the skipped REF symbols are echoed + logged, never silently dropped; an all-REF selection returns an honest note, never a fabricated pull; (6) Observability — `skipped_reference_only` / `skipped_count` in the response + the structlog line; (7) Honest envelope — efficiency/observability guard, F&O behaviour unchanged. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit — `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_expiries_contracts_route.py` (the skip-REF arms: a REF instrument in the selection is SKIPPED — the monkeypatched `pull_expiries_contracts` fake receives ONLY the tradable instruments + the skipped set is echoed; a MIX → only tradable passed; an ALL-REF selection → honest "nothing to pull" note + the pull fake NOT called; a fully-tradable selection → unchanged) via the offline TestClient + a real temp `InstrumentStore` seeded with a reference_only instrument; property/golden/bench/stress — n/a (route glue over the already-verified metadata pull). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** the `reference_only_security_ids() -> frozenset[int]` signature + that it is the SAME set the `/universe` REF badge surfaces were read from `brutex/data/instrument_store.py` before wiring (no assumed API — Golden Rule #1); the filter sits at the ROUTE (the store is available via `_require_store()`), leaving `pull_expiries_contracts` byte-unchanged. **Verified (3.12 venv):** ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) on `app.py` + the route test; interrogate(100% CI flags) on `app.py` → 100%; bandit -ll → 0 issues; the new skip-REF route lines are 100% covered by the route test (the full-package coverage gate keeps `app.py` at 100%); the 16 route tests → green; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` → OK. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_expiries_contracts_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SKIP-REF-METADATA-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DERIV-METADATA-ROUTE-001 (#737, the metadata route this filters), DEC-NON-OPTION-INDEX-REFTAG-001 + DEC-NTM-GROWW-REPOINT-001 (the reference_only tagging this reads), DEC-FNO-INDEX-MATCH-DIAG-001 (#750, the sibling diagnostic on the same REF/OPT boundary).
755. **DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 — O(1) instrument↔connection mapping + sharding for scaling the live feed (`brutex/live/plan.py`), and the `/db` live-table browse backend (`brutex/dashboard/live_db_view.py`)** (2026-06-14, extends DEC-LIVE-VERIFY-001 #752). **Why (operator decree — precise mapping + O(1) scaling for many security-IDs across multiple websocket connections):** with indices + their F&O stocks + futures/options (each its own `(exchange, segment, exchange_token)` security identity), scaling past one websocket's subscription cap needs MULTIPLE connections with a PRECISE, O(1) instrument↔connection mapping. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only; extends the #749 live package):** (1) `plan.py` — `Instrument` (composite `key = exchange:segment:exchange_token`, hashable) + `build_plan(instruments, per_connection_cap=1000) -> ConnectionPlan` that DEDUPS on the key (O(1) set membership — never subscribe twice), packs the unique instruments into `ceil(N/cap)` shards of ≤cap each, and builds the O(1) indexes `by_key` (instrument→connection) + `by_underlying` (underlying→legs inverted index); `connection_of(key)`/`legs_of(underlying)`/`connection_count(n)` are all O(1). Routing an incoming tick to its instrument is O(1) because the feed snapshot self-identifies (no reverse map needed). (2) `live_db_view.py` — `query_live_table(lake_root, table, limit, offset)` surfaces `live_ticks`/`live_candles_1m` as the SAME `{table, columns, rows, total, limit, offset}` payload the rest of `/db` uses, REUSING the lake readers (no new `read_parquet` glob → zero SQL/path-injection surface) + the shared `clamp_limit`/`clamp_offset` bounds. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — the O(1) claim, precisely):** every LOOKUP / dedup / route / assign is **O(1)** (dict/set); BUILDING the plan is **O(N)** one pass and the maps are **O(N)** space — you must touch each of N distinct instruments once and store its assignment, which is NOT an O(1)-total claim (impossible for N distinct instruments). The per-connection-vs-per-account 1000 cap stays UNVERIFIED until the `verify`/`probe` run. **Verified (3.12 venv + native wheels):** 16 new tests; `plan.py` + `live_db_view.py` 100% line+branch; ruff + ruff-format clean; mypy clean (the only errors are the transitive growwapi-install artifacts in `auth.py`/`live.py`, absent in CI). 🟡 the `/db` LIVE-FEED route + template + JS wiring (browsing these via `query_live_table`) is the next increment; 🟡 the multi-connection RUNTIME (opening N real sockets from `ConnectionPlan.shards`) is `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac). **Files:** `brutex/live/plan.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/live_db_view.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_plan.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_db_view.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-VERIFY-001 (#752), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753).

759. **DEC-FNO-INDEX-GROWW-SYMBOL-MATCH-001 — a genuine F&O index whose spot `IDX` row carries a VERBOSE `trading_symbol` (MIDCPNIFTY → "NIFTY MID SELECT", NIFTYNXT50 → "NIFTY NEXT 50") now keeps its OPT badge via the vendor-canonical `groww_symbol` bridge, instead of silently dropping to REFERENCE_ONLY** (2026-06-14, operator-directed; the live `make run` ground truth). **Why:** the OPT-vs-REF badge (`is_spot_only_index`, DEC-NON-OPTION-INDEX-REFTAG-001) keys on an EXACT `(exchange, symbol_name)` match between an `IDX` row's `symbol_name` (← the CSV `trading_symbol`) and the option legs' `underlying_symbol` set (`build_options_eligible_underlyings`). The operator's `make run` proved this drops two GENUINE F&O indices: `universe.load.fno_index_unmatched count=2 gaps=[{underlying: MIDCPNIFTY, nearest_index: None}, {underlying: NIFTYNXT50, nearest_index: None}]` (DEC-FNO-INDEX-MATCH-DIAG-001, #750 — the diagnostic that surfaced it). `nearest_index: None` = the option legs name the COMPACT F&O symbol (`MIDCPNIFTY` / `NIFTYNXT50`) while the spot `IDX` row's `trading_symbol` is the VERBOSE display name (`NIFTY MID SELECT` / `NIFTY NEXT 50`), and normalization (uppercase + strip spaces/`-`) cannot bridge `NXT`↔`NEXT` or `MIDCP`↔`MIDCAP SELECT`. So both indices lost their OPT badge → could not pull expiries/contracts/historical even though they have live option chains. **The vendor-canonical bridge (Golden Rule #1 — reads the vendor's OWN identity, NEVER a hardcoded per-index alias):** for an `IDX` row the Groww `groww_symbol` key is the two-part `"EXCH-SYMBOL"` (`"NSE-MIDCPNIFTY"`), whose SYMBOL component IS the vendor's F&O symbol — the SAME string the option legs stamp as `underlying_symbol`. The brute-force universe PROVES this convention: the `NSE-NIFTY` spot row ↔ its option legs' `underlying_symbol` `"NIFTY"` (CLAUDE.md §6 — `BRUTE_FORCE_INDEX_SYMBOLS` = `NSE-NIFTY`/`NSE-BANKNIFTY`/`BSE-SENSEX`). FINNIFTY already matched only because its `trading_symbol` HAPPENS to equal its F&O symbol; MIDCPNIFTY/NIFTYNXT50 fail solely because their `trading_symbol` is the verbose name. **What shipped (a load-time tagging fix — the brute-force ENGINE, the 52-vocab, every SPOT ingest path UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `is_spot_only_index` itself is BYTE-UNCHANGED):** (1) `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py` — new pure `index_symbol_of(groww_symbol)` returns the SYMBOL component (`"NSE-MIDCPNIFTY"` → `"MIDCPNIFTY"`; a `-`-less key → `""`, matches nothing). (2) `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py` — new `_groww_symbol_index_bridge(index, options_eligible)` reads each `IDX` row's `groww_symbol` F&O symbol and returns `(options_eligible_bridged, index_alias_symbols)`: `options_eligible_bridged` = `options_eligible` UNION the `(exch, symbol_name)` of every `IDX` whose F&O symbol IS options-eligible (so the UNCHANGED `is_spot_only_index` symbol_name check now matches the verbose-named index → keeps OPT), and `index_alias_symbols` = `(exch, F&O symbol)` for EVERY `IDX` row. `load_instrument_master` passes the bridged set to `_reference_only_of` and `index_alias_symbols` to the diagnostic. (3) `brutex/universe.py` — `diagnose_unmatched_option_underlyings` gains an optional `index_alias_symbols` arg: an underlying the bridge already resolved is no longer reported (the diagnostic stays HONEST — no permanent false `count` after the fix; `None` default preserves the original behaviour). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the bridge reads the vendor's own `groww_symbol` identity — no hardcoded alias; ✅ ZERO change to the brute-force engine / 52-vocab / spot ingest; ✅ `is_spot_only_index` byte-unchanged (the union happens in the loader); ✅ FINNIFTY + every already-matched index is unaffected (the union is additive); ✅ a TRUE orphan underlying (no `IDX` spot row at all) is STILL reported by the diagnostic. 🟡 the structural premise — an `IDX`'s `groww_symbol` SYMBOL component equals its option legs' `underlying_symbol` — is grounded in the verified brute-force convention (CLAUDE.md §6) but the SPECIFIC strings for MIDCPNIFTY/NIFTYNXT50 are confirmed by the operator's NEXT `make run` (gaps→0 + both badged OPT on `/universe`); if a vendor ever names an index's `groww_symbol` differently from its option `underlying_symbol`, the bridge simply does not fire (the index stays REF, NO regression — same as today) and the diagnostic re-surfaces the real strings. **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix:** (1) Correctness — the bridge matches the vendor's own F&O symbol; the union only ADDS verbose-named F&O indices, never removes a REF tag; (2) Reliability — a `-`-less/garbage `groww_symbol` yields `""` → skipped, never raises; (3) Recoverability — `git revert` + drop ledger #759 (load-time tagging only; the next load re-tags); (4) Idempotence — pure functions over the parsed index, deterministic; (5) Honesty — the diagnostic stops crying about bridged indices but STILL reports true orphans; (6) Observability — `universe.load.fno_index_unmatched` now reflects only RESIDUAL gaps; (7) Honest envelope — load-time OPT/REF tagging fix, engine untouched, specific strings proven by the next `make run`. **Z+ 7-layer audit:** unit — `tests/unit/test_groww_instruments.py` (`index_symbol_of` across NIFTY/MIDCPNIFTY/NIFTYNXT50/SENSEX/INDIAVIX + the `-`-less empty case); `tests/unit/test_fno_index_diagnostic.py` (the `index_alias_symbols` arg suppresses a bridged underlying + still reports an orphan + `None` default unchanged; `_groww_symbol_index_bridge` bridges a verbose IDX, ignores non-IDX rows, adds an alias-but-no-bridge for an option-less sectoral index, skips a `-`-less key; loader end-to-end: MIDCPNIFTY + NIFTYNXT50 verbose-named rows keep OPT (`reference_only` FALSE) + the diagnostic is SILENT, while a true orphan is still logged) via the offline loader + a real temp `InstrumentStore`; property/golden/bench/stress — n/a (load-time tagging glue over the verified parser). **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** the `groww_symbol` "EXCH-SYMBOL" format + that an index's option `underlying_symbol` equals its spot row's F&O symbol were read from `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py` (`BRUTE_FORCE_INDEX_SYMBOLS`) + the brute-force resolution before wiring (no assumed API — Golden Rule #1); the bridge sits in the loader, leaving `is_spot_only_index` byte-unchanged. **Verified (3.12 venv):** ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) on the 3 source files + the 2 test files; interrogate(100% CI flags) → 100%; bandit -ll → 0 issues; per-module 100% line+branch on `brutex.universe` (test_universe + test_fno_index_diagnostic), `brutex.adapters.groww.instruments` (test_groww_instruments), and `brutex.dashboard.instrument_loader` (test_fno_index_diagnostic + test_dashboard_instrument_loader); `validate_ledger_numbering.py` → OK. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py`, `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`, `brutex/universe.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_instruments.py`, `tests/unit/test_fno_index_diagnostic.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-INDEX-GROWW-SYMBOL-MATCH-001. **Builds on:** DEC-NON-OPTION-INDEX-REFTAG-001 (the symbol_name-exact OPT/REF badge this bridges), DEC-FNO-INDEX-MATCH-DIAG-001 (#750, the diagnostic that surfaced the two gaps), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean ingest that discards the legs after this load-time harvest).
757. **DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 — remove the one dashboard-coupled live file (`brutex/dashboard/live_db_view.py`) so the live-feed measurement surface is PURELY `brutex/live/`, with ZERO coupling to the existing dashboard/backtest code** (2026-06-14, extends DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 #756). **Why (operator decree):** the live feed will be verified manually on the operator's MacBook, then MOVED to TickVault (and on to AWS) — so it must be kept ENTIRELY SEPARATE: it may USE existing modules (read-only) but must never be imported BY, or modify, the existing backtest engine or dashboard. The merged #706 left `brutex/dashboard/live_db_view.py` (a `/db` browse-backend that imported `clamp_limit`/`clamp_offset` from `db_view`) — the ONLY live file coupled to the dashboard package; the `/db` LIVE-FEED route that would have consumed it was deliberately NOT added (it would have modified `app.py`), leaving the file consumed only by its own test. **What shipped:** delete `brutex/dashboard/live_db_view.py` + `tests/unit/test_live_db_view.py`. After this, the entire live-feed feature is the self-contained `brutex/live/` package (`store, tick, capture, candle_builder, parity, report, probe, lake, serde, plan, verify, __main__`) which READS only `brutex.data.models` (`CandleBar`), `brutex.calendars.nse` (IST/session), `brutex.money` (`round_money`), and the Groww SDK/adapter — and is imported by NOTHING in the engine or dashboard. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ verified nothing imports the removed module (grep), `brutex.live` imports clean with no dashboard dependency, ruff clean, `brutex.live` still 100% line+branch (69 tests); ✅ zero change to any existing backtest/dashboard file — a pure deletion of two additive files; 🟡 the `/db` LIVE-FEED browse UI is intentionally NOT built (it would couple the live feed to the dashboard) — if ever wanted it is a SEPARATE BruteX-side feature, not part of the portable core. **Migration note:** `brutex/live/` is the unit that lifts to TickVault → AWS; its read-only deps (`CandleBar`/IST/`round_money`/Groww adapter) re-point at the destination. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_db_view.py` (DELETED), `tests/unit/test_live_db_view.py` (DELETED), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753), DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 (#755).
762. **DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-001 — the REAL dashboard "Live" tab: an ON/OFF websocket-capture toggle (subprocess) + a read-only browse of the two live Parquet tables, with `brutex/live/` still imported-by-nothing** (2026-06-14, operator decree — "it should be real in our dashboard, not a mockup"). **Why (operator decree + the answered design question):** the operator chose the **subprocess + read-lake** model (over importing the live package or a background thread) so the live feed stays portable to TickVault → AWS. This lands the real `/live` tab the v28/v29-style mockup previewed. **What shipped (purely additive; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; read-only market data, no orders):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py` (NEW) — `LiveRunner` start/stop/status of the capture **subprocess** via a JSON state file + `brutex.config.runtime.is_pid_alive`: exactly-once start (idempotent), reap-or-report on `status`, SIGTERM→SIGKILL on `stop`; it SPAWNS `python -m brutex.live capture …` and **never imports `brutex.live`** (DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757), credentials inherited from the env (never on argv, so `ps` stays clean). (2) `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` (NEW) — reads the SEPARATE `live/` Parquet lake (`live_ticks` + `live_candles_1m`, DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 #756) DIRECTLY via DuckDB `read_parquet(?, union_by_name=true)` (bound-parameter, no path-traversal/glob-injection surface; mirrors `db_view`) — again **without importing `brutex.live`**. (3) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — a `/live` page + `GET /api/v1/live/status` (process state + JSONL tick count), `POST /api/v1/live/start` / `stop`, `GET /api/v1/live/tables`, `GET /api/v1/live/table/{name}`; `build_app` gains an injected `live_runner` (a fake-backed runner in tests → no real subprocess). (4) `brutex/dashboard/templates/live.html` (NEW) — the wired page: ON/OFF toggle, status/uptime/tick cards, and the two-table browser (every cell `esc()`-escaped — XSS on vendor-origin values). (5) the **Live** nav link added to all 11 templates that carry the nav. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `live_runner` + `live_lake_view` are 100% line+branch tested against fakes (no real process/signals/network); the `/live` routes are TestClient-tested with a fake runner + a seeded lake; ruff + ruff-format clean; mypy clean on the new modules (the only notes are the transitive `growwapi` import-not-found artifacts, absent in CI); 🟡 the watchdog (heartbeat-silence auto-restart), the cross-process OS lock, and the `(pid, start_time)` identity check (PID reuse) are the explicit Phase-1 hardening follow-ups from the 4-agent review; 🟡 the live PARQUET tables fill once the capture JSONL is materialised (`python -m brutex.live lake`) — the status card shows the live JSONL tick count meanwhile; 🟡 the real subprocess/feed stays operator-Mac-only. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/templates/live.html` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, 11 nav templates, `tests/unit/test_live_runner.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756), DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001 (#760).
760. **DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001 — the live capture/verify/probe CLI gains a heartbeat progress-log + a durable JSONL log file, and `capture` now defaults to the FULL universe via a feed-aware `all`/`everything` resolver** (2026-06-14, operator decree — "where are the logs… why logging/tracking/monitoring didn't happen… it should be our entire indices and entire stocks"). **Why:** an unattended `python -m brutex.live capture --seconds 23400` logged `live_capture_start` then went SILENT for the whole window (the `run_for` keep-alive loop only logged start+done) and wrote NOTHING to a file — so the operator could not tell ticks were flowing (the uploaded `brutex.log` was the DASHBOARD's `.brutex-logs/brutex.log`, a different process). And plain `capture` subscribed only the 4 parity instruments, not the whole universe. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only — read-only, no orders, NOT in the engine/52-vocab, CLAUDE.md §3; PURELY `brutex/live/`, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757):** (1) `brutex/live/capture.py` — `TickCapture.run_for` emits a `live_capture_progress` heartbeat every `heartbeat_interval` s (default 30) carrying `captured`/`since_last`/`elapsed_s`/`ticks_per_s` (a `since_last=0` beat IS the feed-went-quiet signal); a `heartbeats` counter property; the keep-alive loop restructured to stay deterministic under the injected monotonic. (2) `brutex/live/__main__.py` — a `configure_logging` LiveDeps hook (no-op default; the real `_real_configure_logging` tees structlog JSON to console AND `--log-file`, default `.brutex-logs/brutex-live.log`) called by `capture`/`verify`/`probe-connections`; `probe-connections` now logs `connection_opened ordinal=N` per successful open (so the ramp is visible live + persisted, not just the Groww SDK's "Ready to Groww!" prints — CLAUDE.md §6); `capture` gains `--heartbeat`/`--log-file`; `capture --symbols` default flips to the FULL universe `all` and `--feed` default to `ltp` (the parity-subset 4 indices are `--feed index --symbols NSE-NIFTY,NSE-BANKNIFTY,BSE-SENSEX,NSE-INDIAVIX`, the `PARITY_SYMBOLS` constant). (3) the `_real_instrument_resolver` is now FEED-AWARE over the Groww instrument master (CLAUDE.md §6): `all`/`universe` → every `IDX` on `--feed index`, PLUS every F&O-eligible `EQ` on `--feed ltp` (stocks are never subscribed on the index-value feed, where they would be silent); a new `everything`/`all-equity` sentinel adds every NSE/BSE equity (the ~750 the dashboard shows). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ heartbeat + per-connection log + log-file hook are 100% line+branch tested against fakes (70 live tests; `brutex.live` 100% line+branch); ✅ logs now persist to a JSONL file AND console; ✅ the live tick/candle tables remain the SEPARATE `live/` Parquet lake (DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 #756), deliberately NOT in the dashboard `/db` (DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757) — browse them via `brutex.live.lake.read_live_ticks` / `read_live_candles`; 🟡 the real feed/instrument-master/socket paths stay `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac, market hours); 🟡 the per-connection instrument cap + whether the LTP feed carries index values stay VERIFY-ON-RUN (the `verify` per-instrument table reports any silence, never hides it). **Files:** `brutex/live/capture.py`, `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757), DEC-LIVE-VERIFY-001 (#752), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756), DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 (#755), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753).
761. **DEC-LIVE-ROBUSTNESS-001 — capture-store crash durability + tick price/schema hygiene + nanosecond cadence (Phase-0 fixes from the 4-agent live-feed hostile review)** (2026-06-14, extends DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001 #760). **Why (operator decree — "did you really cover all extreme permutations/combinations of worst cases?"):** a 4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9) of the `brutex/live/` Groww websocket feed surfaced real defects the green 100%-coverage hid. This entry lands the self-contained, fully-offline-testable subset (durability + data hygiene); the structural items (no `feed.consume()`, wire the 1000-cap sharding, vendor-`tsInMillis` candle binning, the dashboard ON/OFF subprocess + watchdog) are tracked as follow-ups. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only — read-only, no orders, NOT in the engine/52-vocab, CLAUDE.md §3; purely `brutex/live/`, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757):** (1) `store.py` — **B3** `TickStore.read` now tolerates a torn final line (a crash/`SIGKILL`/disk-full mid-`flush` leaves a partial last line with no newline) and skips it, while still RAISING on real mid-file corruption (a malformed non-final or newline-terminated line) — a single truncated byte no longer poisons `cadence`/`build`/`lake`/`parity`; **B4** resume now `_repair_and_count` TRUNCATES the torn tail back to the last complete newline before appending and counts only complete records, so `next_seq` is exact and a restart never duplicates/drops a sequence number (Golden Rule #7). (2) `tick.py` — **L1** a negative index/LTP value (vendor sign-flip glitch) is dropped via `_coerce_price` (finite AND ≥ 0), skipped not raised so one bad tick never aborts a build; **H-a** a feed leaf carrying `tsInMillis` but an UNKNOWN price key (schema drift — a renamed/added vendor field) is SKIPPED with a `live_tick_unknown_price_key` warning instead of recursed-into, so it never mints phantom instruments (e.g. a `…:tsInMillis` key whose "value" is the timestamp). The Groww proto fields are per CLAUDE.md §6 / `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md`. (3) `probe.py` — **M4** `analyze_cadence` now measures inter-arrival gaps on OUR nanosecond `recv_ns` clock (the documented cadence oracle) when present, falling back to µs `recv_ts` only for pre-`recv_ns` logs. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ all four fixes are 100% line+branch tested (79 live tests; `brutex.live` 100%), ruff + ruff-format + mypy-strict clean; ✅ torn-tail truncation is safe under the single-writer capture invariant (the cross-process lock is the Phase-1 watchdog item); 🟡 the structural blockers from the review (B1 `consume()`, B2 vendor-ts candle binning, B6 sharding wiring, the lifecycle/watchdog) are explicit follow-ups, NOT in this PR; 🟡 the real feed remains `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac, market hours). **Files:** `brutex/live/store.py`, `brutex/live/tick.py`, `brutex/live/probe.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_core.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-ROBUSTNESS-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001 (#760), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756).
763. **DEC-LIVE-PROBE-CONCURRENT-001 — the connection-scaling probe now HOLDS connections open CONCURRENTLY (the per-account ceiling), not opened-then-dropped** (2026-06-14, operator decree — "scaling is about CONNECTIONS not subscriptions; if they have the limit they auto-close the connections, that's why I want to check connection scaling now"). **Why (correctness):** the binding scaling constraint is the **concurrent** websocket-connection ceiling — a per-account limit makes the vendor REFUSE/auto-close the N+1-th socket while the first N are still open. Subscribing the entire live universe (indices + F&O stocks + their futures + options legs) needs `connections × 1000` ≥ total instruments (the Groww 1000-instruments-per-subscription cap, `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md`, CLAUDE.md §6), so the concurrent-connection ceiling is what gates "can we subscribe everything live". The pre-fix `probe_connections` (`brutex/live/probe.py`) **discarded** each opened connection (`held = ordinal` was a bare counter), so the held references were GC'd → it measured SEQUENTIAL reopen capacity, NOT the concurrent hold the operator asked about. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only — read-only, no orders, NOT in the engine/52-vocab; purely `brutex/live/`, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001):** `probe_connections` now **retains** every opened connection in a list (kept referenced → kept open) for the whole ramp, reports `max_held = len(held)` (the max held CONCURRENTLY), and releases them best-effort via an injected `close` callback in a `finally` (a close error is logged `probe_connection_close_failed` + swallowed so it never masks the result). The CLI's `open_connection` already returns the feed (DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001 #760 per-connection logging), so `python -m brutex.live probe-connections --max 100` now ramps + HOLDS, printing `connection_opened ordinal=N` live and a final `connection_probe max_held=… failed_at=…` — the real concurrent ceiling. This pairs with the `plan.py` O(1) sharding (DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 #755: `ceil(N/1000)` connections): once the probe reports the concurrent ceiling C, the max subscribable universe is `C × 1000`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the hold-then-close lifecycle + the empty-cleanup + the close-error-swallow paths are 100% line+branch tested against fakes (`brutex.live.probe` 100%); ruff + ruff-format + mypy-strict clean; 🟡 the ACTUAL per-account concurrent ceiling is irreducibly VERIFY-ON-RUN (the operator runs the probe on the Mac — it needs no market data, so it runs any day); 🟡 wiring the shard plan into the real `subscribe` path (so `C × 1000` instruments are actually subscribed across C connections) is the named follow-up B6 from the 4-agent review. **Files:** `brutex/live/probe.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_core.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-PROBE-CONCURRENT-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 (#755), DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001 (#760), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753).
791. **DEC-LIVE-REALTIME-FOLD-001 — the dashboard "Live ON" toggle now MATERIALISES the live Parquet lake CONTINUOUSLY (micro-batch, ~every 5s), so the `/live` + `/db` `live_ticks` / `live_candles_1m` tables fill AUTOMATICALLY in near-real-time while the feed runs — no manual `brutex.live lake` command** (2026-06-15, operator: click Live ON → ticks + candles flow into the tables automatically). **Why (the operator-visible bug):** the Live-ON toggle spawned `python -m brutex.live capture-all` which wrote ticks to `runs/live-ticks.jsonl` (the durable JSONL write-ahead log) but NEVER folded them into the Parquet lake; the dashboard reads the lake (`<lake_root>/live/ticks/dt=*.parquet` + `.../candles_1m/dt=*.parquet`), so both pages showed **0 rows** even though thousands of ticks were captured (the operator saw 12,445 captured / 0 in the tables). This is the industry-standard WAL→micro-batch→columnar pattern: the JSONL is the durable WAL, the fold is the columnar batch sink, and this PR adds the TIME trigger so the sink flushes on a cadence rather than only when a segment fills. **What shipped (purely `brutex/live/` + the dashboard WIRING — REFERENCE/RESEARCH only, read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; REUSES PR #748's `RollingTickStore`/`make_fold_on_rotate`/`fold_segment` — the fold is NEVER duplicated, Golden Rule #11 COMMON):** (1) `brutex/live/rolling.py` — `RollingTickStore` gains a **time trigger**: an optional `max_seconds: float | None = None` + an injected `monotonic: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic` clock on `open`/`__init__`. `append` now rotates (and so FOLDS the just-closed segment via the existing `on_rotate`) when the active segment is full OR aged: a NON-EMPTY active segment older than `max_seconds` of monotonic wall-clock rotates even far below its size/line cap, so the lake materialises within a few seconds on a quiet feed. The age clock restarts on every `_rotate`. **An EMPTY active segment NEVER time-rotates** — there is nothing to fold, so a quiet feed produces no empty-segment folds (the `self._lines > 0` guard). (2) `brutex/live/__main__.py` — `capture-all` gains `--lake-root` (optional), `--roll-max-seconds` (default 5.0), `--run-id` (default `live`), `--roll-max-bytes`, `--roll-max-lines`. When `--lake-root` is given, `_cmd_capture_all` writes into a `RollingTickStore.open(..., on_rotate=make_fold_on_rotate(lake_root=…, capture_run_id=run_id, feed_kind="both"), max_seconds=…)` instead of the plain `TickStore` and `flush_active()`s the tail at end-of-session; ABSENT → unchanged plain `TickStore` capture. The `_cmd_capture_all` body stays `# pragma: no cover` (real websockets, operator's Mac), but the PARSER additions + the time-rotation logic ARE 100% tested. (3) `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py` — `LiveRunner.start(...)` gains `lake_root: str | None = None`; when given it appends `--lake-root <root> --roll-max-seconds 5 --run-id live` to the spawned `capture-all` argv and persists `lake_root` in `_last_start` so the watchdog re-spawn carries it. (4) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the `/api/v1/live/start` handler resolves the SAME lake root the dashboard READS (`_live_lake_root()` = `instrument_store.path.parent`) and passes it as `start(lake_root=…)`, so the capture writes EXACTLY where `/live` + `/db` read (the empty-tables fix); `None` when no instrument store is wired (plain capture, no crash). **Crash-honesty + idempotence (Golden Rule #7):** the time fold reuses the verified-before-delete prune + the lake PK `(capture_run_id, seq, instrument_key)`, so a re-fold unions to a byte-identical row set; the watermark/seq machinery (#790) is untouched. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/live/rolling.py` + `brutex/live/__main__.py` + `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py` are **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (`pytest test_live_rolling test_live_cli test_live_core test_live_runner test_dashboard_live --cov=brutex.live.rolling --cov=brutex.live.__main__ --cov=brutex.dashboard.live_runner --cov-branch` → 560 stmts / 70 branch / 0 miss; 169 passed), and the changed `app.py` `/api/v1/live/start` handler lines are line+branch covered by `test_dashboard_live.py`; ✅ tests cover the time-rotate-at-interval fold, time-trigger-not-before-the-interval, the **empty-active-segment-never-time-rotates** worst case, `max_seconds=None` disabling the trigger, the clock reset across two rotations, the default `time.monotonic` wiring, the capture-all parser additions (exact dashboard-shaped argv parsed via the REAL `_build_parser`), the runner appending the flags (the EXACT spawned argv fed back through the real parser → `command == "capture-all"` with `lake_root` set — the #743/#744 "rejected flag crashes the launch" guard), the watchdog re-spawn carrying the remembered lake root, and the dashboard toggle forwarding the dashboard's READ lake root (capture-write-root == dashboard-read-root); ✅ `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; ✅ `mypy --strict` clean on the changed files (only the PRE-EXISTING transitive `growwapi` import-untyped notes in `_real_feed_builder`/`auth.py`/`live.py`, untouched + absent in CI); ✅ `pyright` 0 ERRORS on all changed files (the only notes are pre-existing `reportPrivateUsage` warnings on unchanged import/test patterns); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — no `brutex.live` import added to `brutex/dashboard/` (the dashboard only spawns the subprocess with `--lake-root` + resolves the root from the already-available `instrument_store.path`). 🟡 the REAL websocket/feed build stays the operator's-Mac-only `# pragma: no cover` boundary (`_cmd_capture_all` body, unchanged); 🟡 the actual at-market TICKS remain the 09:15-IST gate (ADR-0009 Phase-0, UNVERIFIED — not claimed); 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change. **Files:** `brutex/live/rolling.py`, `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_rolling.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-REALTIME-FOLD-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-AUTOROLL-001 (#790, the `RollingTickStore`/`make_fold_on_rotate`/`fold_segment` REUSED), DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 (the `capture-all` spawn + manifest + watchdog), DEC-DB-LIVE-TABLES-001 (#789, the `/db` live-table browse this fills), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756, the live lake schema), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the imported-by-nothing invariant); Groww tick/candle schema CLAUDE.md §6.

793. **DEC-LIVE-LEG-RESOLUTION-001 — POPULATE the F&O contracts registry from a live CLI `pull-contracts` command (`get_expiries` → `get_contracts` → upsert) so `build_leg_rows` emits the option/future legs, the live subscription universe crosses the 1000/conn cap, and the N-connection sharding ENGAGES automatically (was always 1 connection because `legs=[]`)** (2026-06-15, the named follow-up that activates DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 #755's `ceil(N/1000)` sharding). **Why (the operator-visible gap):** the live capture only ever subscribed the ~779 SPOT instruments, so `plan_connections` (`brutex/live/multiconn.py`) always built ONE connection (779 < the 1000/conn cap) and the operator never saw the N-connection scaling. The root cause was upstream: `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` `build_leg_rows` reads the F&O `contracts` registry (`brutex/data/registry_store.py` `RegistryStore.list_contracts`) but on the LIVE setup that registry was **never populated** — the dashboard's `metadata_pull.pull_expiries_contracts` (#732) populates it only when an operator clicks the dashboard button, never on the headless live path — so `build_leg_rows` degraded to `legs=[]` (`live_manifest.py:205`) and the legs never reached the manifest. The Groww adapter ALREADY had the resolution primitives (`contracts.py` `resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts`); this PR wires "pull contracts → populate the registry" on the live CLI path so the legs flow `registry → build_leg_rows → manifest → plan_connections → N connections`. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only — read-only market data, no orders; the F&O legs are LAKE / live-subscription REFERENCE_ONLY mirroring DEC-P0-063; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + trading universe + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3 — the engine stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** (1) NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_pull.py` — `pull_contracts_to_registry(client, registry, *, targets, expiries_per_underlying, now, today, run_id)`: for each `PullTarget (exchange, underlying)` it resolves the chain's expiry dates across the CURRENT + NEXT year (so a December run still discovers the January chain), keeps the **nearest N** (operator-tunable; `select_nearest_expiries` prefers UPCOMING-nearest, backfills with the most-recent EXPIRED if short — never invents a future expiry), then for each kept expiry calls `resolve_contracts` and UPSERTS the expiry + each CE/PE/FUT leg into the `RegistryStore` (REUSING the existing `resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts` + `upsert_expiry`/`upsert_contract` — never re-implemented, Golden Rule #11 COMMON; the LIVE-path twin of the dashboard's `metadata_pull`). It lives in the ADAPTER layer (not `brutex/live/`) so it can import `RegistryStore` while keeping `brutex/live/` itself imported-by-nothing (DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757). A per-underlying TERMINAL Groww error is QUARANTINED (recorded on `UnderlyingPullResult`, the run CONTINUES to the next underlying — one bad/delisted symbol never aborts the whole pull); a non-Groww exception (a real bug) is NOT swallowed. (2) `brutex/live/__main__.py` — a NEW `pull-contracts --registry <path> [--expiries N] [--run-id …]` command + handler `_cmd_pull_contracts` that resolves its targets (the F&O-eligible single stocks + the indices) via an injected `LiveDeps.contract_target_resolver`, builds the LIVE credentialed Groww client paced by the shared 8 r/s + 500/min `RateController` via `LiveDeps.client_builder`, opens the `RegistryStore`, and runs the pull. The handler exits 0 on a partial/full success (legs landed) and 1 ONLY when EVERY underlying was quarantined (a credential/connectivity failure). The two NETWORK boundaries (`_real_contract_targets` downloads the SSRF-allowlisted instrument master + parses the 212-stock F&O-eligibility set, CLAUDE.md §6; `_real_groww_client` mints the TOTP token + wires the rate controller) are the only `# pragma: no cover` lines — the handler, the pull loop, the registry upsert, the nearest-N selection, and the idempotence are 100%-tested with a FAKE adapter. **Pacing (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6):** every `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` rides the injected `client.pace` — the SAME adaptive token bucket + 500/min governor the spot/option pulls use (8 r/s ceiling, `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`/`GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`); NO hardcoded rate. **Idempotence + crash-safety (Golden Rule #7):** the upserts are per-contract `INSERT OR REPLACE` on the contract PK, so a re-pull yields the SAME rows (proven byte-stable in a re-run test) and a process killed mid-pull leaves a VALID registry of exactly the contracts already written — never an all-or-nothing rollback that loses prior underlyings. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_pull.py` + the changed `brutex/live/__main__.py` are **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (`pytest test_groww_contract_pull test_live_cli_pull_contracts test_live_cli test_live_manifest --cov=brutex.adapters.groww.contract_pull --cov=brutex.live.__main__ --cov-branch` → 337 stmts / 32 branch / 0 miss; 89 passed); ✅ the FEATURE PROOF test asserts spot-only (779) shards to 1 connection but spot+pulled-legs (1259 > 1000) shards to 2 — the sharding ENGAGES — and that `build_leg_rows` returns the legs from a POPULATED registry vs `[]` from an empty/absent one; tests also cover the nearest-N selector (upcoming-first / expired-backfill / `limit<=0` / oversize / today-counts-as-upcoming), the current+next-year query, the quarantine on a failing underlying (run continues, good legs survive) AND on an expiry-phase failure (never reaches the contract phase), the idempotent re-pull, the report aggregation, and the CLI exit codes (0 partial-success, 1 all-quarantined, 0 empty-targets); ✅ `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; ✅ `mypy --strict` clean on `contract_pull.py` (the only `__main__.py` notes are the PRE-EXISTING transitive `growwapi` import-untyped artifacts in `_real_feed_builder`, untouched + absent in CI); ✅ `pyright` 0 ERRORS on all new/changed files (the only `__main__.py` note is the pre-existing `reportPrivateUsage` on the unchanged `_utc_now` import); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — `brutex/live/__main__.py` calls the ADAPTER `contract_pull` exactly as it already calls other Groww adapter primitives, imports nothing from `brutex/dashboard/`, and `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing; ✅ `validate_ledger_numbering.py` → OK. 🟡 the two network boundaries (`_real_contract_targets` master download + `_real_groww_client` TOTP) stay the operator's-Mac-only `# pragma: no cover`; 🟡 the SDK contract-row shape is the verified `EXCH-SYMBOL-DDMmmYY[-STRIKE]-TYPE` (03-backtesting.md:33-35) parsed by the existing `parse_contract_symbol`; 🟡 the actual at-market subscription/ticks remain the 09:15-IST gate (ADR-0009 Phase-0, UNVERIFIED — not claimed). 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change; the F&O legs are NOT added to the trading universe (live-subscription/lake REFERENCE_ONLY only). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_pull.py` (NEW), `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_contract_pull.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_cli_pull_contracts.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-LEG-RESOLUTION-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 (#755, the `ceil(N/1000)` sharding this activates), DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 (the `build_leg_rows`/manifest contract this fills), DEC-DERIV-METADATA-HISTORICAL-SPLIT-001 (#732, the `RegistryStore` + the dashboard `metadata_pull` twin this mirrors on the live path), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (the `resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts` primitives REUSED), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean master that DISCARDS these legs, recovered here), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the imported-by-nothing invariant); Groww expiry/contract addressing CLAUDE.md §6.

789. **DEC-DB-LIVE-TABLES-001 — the two LIVE lake tables (`live_ticks` + `live_candles_1m`) are now browsable PRIMARILY under the `/db` Database page, in their own "LIVE LAKE" sidebar section, with the SAME columns+rows grid the other `/db` tables use** (2026-06-15, operator request — "surface the live tick/candle tables under /db, not only on /live"). **Why:** the two live Parquet tables (`live_ticks` + `live_candles_1m`, the SEPARATE `live/` lake the capture writes — DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 #756; the Groww tick/candle schema per CLAUDE.md §6) were reachable only from the `/live` page's own browser. The operator wants them ALSO (primarily) on the `/db` instrument-master browser so every lake is in one place. **What shipped (dashboard-only; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; read-only market data, no orders; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing — DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html` — a new **"Live lake"** sidebar section renders `live_ticks` + `live_candles_1m` as clickable `data-live` rows (mirroring the existing Candle-lake / Window-ledger / F&O-registry sections), each with a row-count badge filled by `loadLiveTables()` from the live counts route; clicking one browses it through the SAME table mode + `gridAndPager` columns/rows grid + structured query builder the other `/db` tables use (the table-query path is parameterised by an `apiBase` per row — `DB_API` `/api/v1/db` for the DuckDB master tables, `LIVE_API` `/api/v1/db/live` for the two live tables — so ONE code path renders both, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); the `/db` header count now reads `tables.length + LIVE_TABLES.length` (includes the two live tables). (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — thin `/api/v1/db/live/tables`, `/api/v1/db/live/table/{name}`, `/api/v1/db/live/columns/{name}`, `/api/v1/db/live/query/{name}` routes that DELEGATE to the SAME 100%-tested `brutex.dashboard.live_lake_view` reader (`live_table` / `live_columns` / `live_tables_summary` / `query_live_table`) the `/live` page already uses — NO duplicate reader. The table name is allowlisted to `LIVE_TABLES` (`{live_ticks, live_candles_1m}`) INSIDE `live_lake_view` (an unknown name raises `ValueError` → HTTP 400 here, never reaching the Parquet `read_parquet` glob); an absent/empty lake degrades to an empty page + honest note, never a 500 (the lake root is `instrument_store.path.parent`, resolved by the existing `_live_lake_root`). The `/live` page + its `/api/v1/live/*` routes are UNCHANGED (still working). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the four new `/db/live/*` routes are 100% line+branch covered by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_live.py` (table list + counts, a browse page with the live columns+rows when the lake holds partitions, an honest empty page when absent, the allowlist 400 on an unknown name, and a malformed-filter 400); ✅ the `db.html` "LIVE LAKE" markup + wiring is guarded by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_ux.py::test_live_lake_section_present_and_wired`; ✅ `ruff check brutex/dashboard tests` clean (no SIM300), `mypy --strict` clean on the changed files (only the known transitive `growwapi` import-untyped notes in the adapter modules, absent in CI); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — no `brutex.live` import added to the dashboard (`live_lake_view` reads the Parquet lake via DuckDB). 🟡 the live tables fill only once the capture has written the `live/` lake (the 09:15-IST market gate); an empty lake renders an honest empty page. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_live.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_ux.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-LIVE-TABLES-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-001 (#762, the `/live` page + `live_lake_view` reader this reuses), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756, the live lake schema), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the imported-by-nothing invariant), DEC-DB-VIEWER-001 / DEC-DB-QUERY-001 (the `/db` browse + structured-query surface this extends); Groww tick/candle schema CLAUDE.md §6.

788. **DEC-LIVE-DELTA-CAPTURE-001 — O(1) delta tick capture: write only the instrument(s) whose value CHANGED since the previous callback, not the full 779-instrument snapshot verbatim** (2026-06-15, operator's live open run: `brutex/live/capture.py` `TickCapture._on_tick` wrote the ENTIRE 779-instrument snapshot verbatim on every ~140/sec callback → **4.33 GB in 4 minutes** of almost-pure redundancy, since the vast majority of each snapshot is unchanged from the previous callback). **Why:** each persisted `TickRecord` held the raw nested snapshot verbatim (`brutex/live/store.py`), but callback-to-callback only a handful of the 779 instruments actually move; re-writing the other ~775 every 7 ms is the bloat. **What shipped (lowest-risk NESTED-PRUNE design — downstream UNCHANGED; purely `brutex/live/`, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) NEW pure helper `brutex/live/tick.py` `prune_unchanged(snapshot, last_obs) -> (pruned_snapshot, updated_last_obs)` — walks the raw snapshot the SAME way `extract_quotes`/`flatten_index_snapshot` do (REUSING `_leaf_quote`/`_leaf_price` + the `"prefix:key"` instrument-key rule + the `_is_drifted_leaf` guard + `_coerce_price`, factored into a `_prune_into` recursive worker + a `_changed` baseline check — NO duplication of the key rule, Golden Rule #11 COMMON), KEEPS a leaf only if its **FULL-leaf `Quote` signature** (coerced price **AND** the vendor `tsInMillis` **AND** volume / openInterest) differs from `last_obs[instrument_key]` (a never-seen instrument is always kept), and rebuilds the SAME nested shape holding only changed instruments' FULL RAW leaves (so `tsInMillis`/volume/openInterest survive verbatim for every kept instrument — no downstream parser change needed). **Full-leaf, NOT price-only — "save ALL the ticks" (operator decree 2026-06-15):** a liquid REFERENCE_ONLY equity prints many trades at the SAME price, each carrying a fresh `tsInMillis` (+ rising cumulative volume); a price-only delta would drop those same-price reprints as "unchanged" and silently lose ticks, so the dedup keys on the whole `Quote` and drops ONLY a byte-for-byte re-read of the identical leaf. Indices (the brute-force trio NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX) carry no volume and re-stamp `tsInMillis` on every print, so the full-leaf key is exact for them too. (2) `brutex/live/capture.py` `_on_tick` now prunes against `self._last_obs` (seeded `{}`): an UNCHANGED callback prunes to EMPTY → writes NOTHING (no record, the counter is frozen, the baseline untouched — O(1), no redundant 779-line); a changed callback `store.append`s the pruned delta + adopts the new baseline. `recv_ts`/`recv_ns`/`seq` semantics are identical; `seq` advances only on a written record. **O(1) SPACE (Golden Rule #5):** `prune_unchanged` mutates `last_obs` IN PLACE and returns the SAME dict (NOT a `dict(last_obs)` copy), so a ~140/sec callback over ~779 instruments costs only O(kept-leaves) extra space, never an O(n) full-dict copy every callback — the 4-agent hot-path hostile review flagged the prior per-callback copy as the one remaining O(n), and this closes it; the idle path keeps nothing → mutates nothing → the baseline is left byte-for-byte untouched. **NESTED-PRUNE chosen over the flat `{key: leaf}` alternative** because it needs ZERO downstream change — `iter_ticks`/`flatten_index_snapshot`/`build_minute_candles` all consume the pruned nested snapshot unmodified. **The no-data-loss subtlety (caught + fixed):** the candle builder emits a 1-minute bar for an instrument ONLY if a tick arrived in that minute (a missing live minute is itself a parity signal — `candle_builder.py`), so an instrument that stays QUIET across a minute boundary would, under a naive prune, lose its carry-forward bar that the full-snapshot stream produces. Fixed by a **per-minute KEYFRAME**: `_on_tick` CLEARS the baseline at each `recv_ts` minute boundary, so the first callback of every new minute re-writes a full keyframe for every present instrument while the within-minute prune still strips the ~140/sec redundancy. This is what makes the candles byte-identical. **GOLDEN no-data-loss proof:** `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py::test_golden_delta_candles_identical_to_full` (one hand-built sequence with repeats, an intra-minute rise-then-fall, and an instrument quiet across a minute boundary) PLUS `test_golden_delta_candles_identical_randomized` (12 pseudo-random seeds, 3 instruments, 40-90 callbacks spanning many minute lines) both capture the SAME snapshot stream (a) full + (b) delta, build 1-minute candles from each, and assert the candle dicts are EQUAL — so the delta is proven to lose no tick: **downstream candles are byte-identical**. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `capture.py` + the new `tick.py` functions are 100.00% line+branch tested (`prune_unchanged`: first→all-kept, identical→empty, partial→only-changed, **same-price-new-`tsInMillis`→KEPT** (the save-ALL-ticks guard), **byte-identical-leaf→dropped**, kept-leaf preserves volume/OI/`tsInMillis`, empty-nested-branch dropped, drift/junk skipped, **baseline mutated IN PLACE + returned as the SAME object** (the O(1)-space contract), **idle callback leaves the baseline byte-untouched**; capture: sequence of unchanged+partial callbacks writes only changes / no record when nothing changed / counter == written records); the GOLDEN candle-identity holds across all 12 randomized seeds + the hand-built case; `ruff check brutex/live tests` + `ruff format --check` clean (no Yoda conditions); `mypy --strict brutex/live/capture.py brutex/live/tick.py` clean (the known transitive `growwapi` import-untyped notes in `__main__.py`/`auth.py` are pre-existing + acceptable, nothing in the changed files). 🟡 the real websocket/feed stays `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac, market hours) — the unit+golden tests prove the prune correctness offline. **Files:** `brutex/live/tick.py` (`prune_unchanged`/`_prune_into`/`_changed`), `brutex/live/capture.py` (`_on_tick` delta + per-minute keyframe), `tests/unit/test_live_core.py` (prune unit tests), `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py` (capture-sequence + GOLDEN no-data-loss), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DELTA-CAPTURE-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-TICK-CALLBACK-META-001 (#787), DEC-LIVE-ROBUSTNESS-001 (#761), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757); market facts CLAUDE.md §6/§7.
787. **DEC-LIVE-TICK-CALLBACK-META-001 — the Groww feed invokes the tick callback WITH a `meta` arg, but `TickCapture._on_tick` took 0 args → EVERY live tick crashed at the open** (2026-06-15, operator open-bell `make run`: the capture launched + planned 779 instruments on connection #0 + subscribed, but `.brutex-logs/brutex-live.log` filled with `Error: TickCapture._on_tick() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given`, so ZERO ticks were persisted). **Why:** `brutex/live/capture.py` documented + defined the feed callback as **0-argument** (`def _on_tick(self): ...`), per an earlier reading of the SDK. The LIVE feed disproved it: Groww's daemon thread calls `on_data_received(meta)` with ONE positional argument on every update (`def on_data_received(meta): ...` — `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md`; CLAUDE.md §6), so the bound method received `(self, meta)` = 2 positional and raised `TypeError` on every callback — silently swallowed by the SDK's per-callback try/except, which only logged the error and dropped the tick. This is the THIRD live-feed input-format bug after DEC-LIVE-CAPTURE-ALL-FEED-FIX-001 (#784, the `--feed` launch crash) and DEC-LIVE-MANIFEST-FEED-FORMAT-001 (#785, the index feed-token format), all of which the spot+launch fixes UNBLOCKED to reach — the feed now launches + subscribes 779; this is the last gate before real ticks persist. **What shipped (`brutex/live/capture.py` + its test, no other module):** `_on_tick(self, *_args: Any)` now accepts AND ignores the meta (the snapshot is pulled from `read_snapshot` — the full current feed state — not the per-callback meta), staying robust to BOTH the 1-arg (Groww) and 0-arg feed-callback conventions; the module/`SubscribeFn`/`subscribe` docstrings that wrongly asserted "0-argument" are corrected to the verified-live behaviour. **Regression guard:** `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py::test_tickcapture_on_tick_accepts_groww_meta_arg` fires the callback BOTH with the meta (`_on_tick({"feed_type":...})`) and with no arg and asserts both capture a record — the exact crash, now locked. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `capture.py` 100% line+branch; ruff + mypy clean; the fix is verified against the operator's live error + `07-feed.md`. 🟡 real end-to-end tick PERSISTENCE is the operator-Mac live confirmation (the websocket itself stays `# pragma: no cover`); the unit test proves the callback contract. **Files:** `brutex/live/capture.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-TICK-CALLBACK-META-001. **Completes the live-launch arc** DEC-LIVE-CAPTURE-ALL-FEED-FIX-001 (#784) + DEC-LIVE-MANIFEST-FEED-FORMAT-001 (#785); feed-callback fact `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md` + CLAUDE.md §6.
785. **DEC-LIVE-MANIFEST-FEED-FORMAT-001 — the dashboard live-manifest emitted BruteX-INTERNAL ids, not Groww feed tokens → indices could never tick** (2026-06-15, operator `make run` + the live-manifest.json inspection: index rows carried `segment:"INDEX"` + a numeric surrogate, e.g. `935205938`). **Why:** the manifest (`dashboard/live_manifest.py`) was built from the persisted `instruments` table, which deliberately normalises Groww's raw identifiers into engine-internal ones — indices get the internal `Segment.INDEX` (PK-disambiguation, DEC-INDEX-SEGMENT-PK-FIX-001) and a blake2b SURROGATE `security_id` (because a non-numeric index token like `"NIFTY"` cannot be the model's `int` security_id). But Groww's live websocket feed addresses instruments by the RAW CSV `exchange_token` on `segment:"CASH"` — `subscribe_index_value` wants `{"exchange":"NSE","segment":"CASH","exchange_token":"NIFTY"}` and BSE SENSEX `…"exchange_token":"1"`; `subscribe_ltp` wants `{"exchange":"NSE","segment":"CASH","exchange_token":"2885"}` (`docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md:54,132`). So equities (numeric token survives) were fine but every index was unaddressable. The manifest also wrote only the in-scope spot (`list_in_scope`, ~4 brute-force rows) instead of the full 775. **What shipped:** (1) **persist the raw feed token** — new `Instrument.feed_token` field + `instruments.feed_token VARCHAR` column (SCHEMA_VERSION 6→7, append-only so the column-order invariant across `_INSTR_COLUMNS`/`_instrument_to_params`/`_row_to_instrument` is shift-free; the bump drop+recreates `instruments`, which the dashboard auto-reloads on next `make run`), populated by the Groww loader from the literal CSV `exchange_token` (`groww/instruments.py`); (2) `live_manifest._spot_row` now emits the GROWW feed row — `segment:"CASH"` (the feed segment for BOTH index-value and ltp, never the internal `INDEX`) + `exchange_token = feed_token` (the raw token, fallback `security_id` for legacy/numeric rows); (3) `build_spot_rows` reads `list_index_equity_instruments()` (the full 775 = 25 indices + 750 equities), not `list_in_scope`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the spot index + equity feed rows now match the official Groww doc exactly (asserted in tests against `07-feed.md`); the F&O **leg** feed-token format (`_leg_row` emits the contract addressing string, but `subscribe_ltp` wants the numeric CSV token — `07-feed.md:54`) is a SEPARATE remaining defect that only bites once the `contracts` registry is pulled (legs are `[]` today), tracked as the next follow-up;
