real ticks remain the 09:15-IST market gate. **Files:** `brutex/data/instrument_store.py` (schema v7 + column + row-mappers), `brutex/models.py` (`feed_token`), `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py` (populate), `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` (`_spot_row` + `build_spot_rows`), `tests/unit/test_live_manifest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_instruments.py`, `tests/integration/test_instrument_store.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-MANIFEST-FEED-FORMAT-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-CAPTURE-ALL-FEED-FIX-001 (#784, the launch-crash fix); feed protocol facts `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md` + CLAUDE.md §6.
784. **DEC-LIVE-CAPTURE-ALL-FEED-FIX-001 — the Live toggle spawned `capture-all --feed both`, but `capture-all` has no `--feed` option → the capture crashed on EVERY launch** (2026-06-15, operator `make run` on the Mac: `brutex.live: error: unrecognized arguments: --feed both`, feed stuck STOPPED / 0 ticks). **Why:** `dashboard/live_runner.py` `start()` was wired (DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 #780) to spawn the N-connection `capture-all` but still appended `--feed both` — a flag the OLD single `capture` subcommand accepted yet `capture-all` does NOT define (it is inherently dual-feed: spot connection #0 routes indices→index-value + stocks→ltp, leg connections #1..N are ltp). argparse rejected the whole spawn, so the subprocess exited non-zero immediately and the dashboard's crash-honest status showed STOPPED with 0 ticks. **The CI gap that let it through:** the `make run smoke` gate boots the dashboard but never flips Live ON (so it never spawns `capture-all`), and `test_live_runner` asserted the argv STRING contained `--feed both` without ever feeding that argv to the real `brutex.live` parser — so a flag the subcommand rejects passed the unit test. **What shipped:** (1) `live_runner.start()` no longer appends `--feed`/`feed` to the `capture-all` argv (the `feed` field is kept ONLY for the LiveStatus/chip display = `both`, never forwarded); (2) `test_live_runner` now feeds the EXACT spawned args through the real `brutex.live.__main__._build_parser().parse_args(...)` and asserts it parses to `command == "capture-all"` — the regression guard that would have caught this before the operator hit it. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this fixes the LAUNCH crash only; two SEPARATE manifest-format defects remain (the next fix, DEC-LIVE-MANIFEST-FEED-FORMAT, in progress): the dashboard manifest emits BruteX-INTERNAL ids — index rows carry `segment:"INDEX"` + a blake2b surrogate token instead of Groww's required `segment:"CASH"` + the raw feed token (`07-feed.md:132`: `{"exchange":"NSE","segment":"CASH","exchange_token":"NIFTY"}`), and it writes only the in-scope spot (`list_in_scope`) not the full 775 (`list_index_equity_instruments`). Equity rows are already correct; indices/legs are NOT until the format fix lands. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_runner.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-CAPTURE-ALL-FEED-FIX-001. **Fixes** the launch crash from DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 (#780); feed protocol facts `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md` + CLAUDE.md §6.
782. **DEC-LIVE-GOLIVE-RUNBOOK-001 — extend the live-capture runbook with the dashboard one-click N-connection go-live path (dry-run-tonight → 09:15-open → EOD parity)** (2026-06-14, operator: "can I check the live run now / will the dashboard view + N-connections + subscriptions happen"). **Why:** `docs/runbooks/groww_live_capture.md` documented only the CLI/parity flow (`python -m brutex.live capture/cadence/build/parity` + `probe-connections`) and predated the dashboard-driven N-connection stack shipped across DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001 (#771), DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001 (#774), DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 (#779), and DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 (#780). The operator needed a single honest checklist separating what is provable with the market CLOSED (the dashboard view + the N-connection plan + the per-connection proof + the 775/legs manifest — all deterministic from the persisted `instruments` table + `contracts` registry) from what only the market OPEN at 09:15 IST can prove (real ticks → 1-minute candles → parity). **What shipped (docs-only — no `brutex/` source touched, single source of truth extended not duplicated per Golden Rule #11):** a new "Part B — Dashboard one-click go-live" section on the existing runbook covering (B0) the save-once creds bridge (`~/.brutex/credentials.json`, mode 0600, env-injected never on argv), (B1) the pre-market DRY-RUN that proves the plumbing with ticks=0 the CORRECT outcome (connections open + the `#connGrid`/`/api/v1/live/connections` proof table populated showing #0 = 775 spot dual-feed + #1..N = 1000-leg shards + heartbeat) plus a symptom→cause→action table, (B2) the Monday 09:15-IST real run with the restart-watchdog + the rate governor, (B3) the EOD parity verdict, and (B4) a proven-offline-vs-only-at-open layer table. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the dashboard/plan/proof/manifest layer is deterministic + 100%-tested offline; the real-socket subscribe-accept is the operator-Mac dry-run (🟡 pre-market unverified); real ticks are the 09:15 market gate (❌ not now). **Files:** `docs/runbooks/groww_live_capture.md` (new Part B), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-GOLIVE-RUNBOOK-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 (#780), DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 (#779), DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001 (#774), DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001 (#771), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001; market facts CLAUDE.md §6/§7.
781. **DEC-CI-SMOKE-COLDSTART-BUDGET-001 — widen the `make run smoke (cold-start boot)` readiness budget 30→90 retries so a slow cold boot no longer false-reds the aggregate `CI OK` gate** (2026-06-14, root-cause of the PR #735 merge-over-red incident). **Why:** PR #735's push-event CI run (27509219628) failed the aggregate `CI OK (aggregate gate)` check — NOT because of skipped PR-body gates (the gate script explicitly tolerates `skipped`: `[[ "$result" != "success" && "$result" != "skipped" ]]`), but because `run-smoke: failure`. The `make run smoke` job boots `python -m brutex run` and curls `http://127.0.0.1:9080/` in a `for i in $(seq 1 30)` retry loop (~30s budget). Cold-start boot loads the full ~750-row instrument universe (the job log shows the dashboard had logged its banner + `universe.load.fno_index_unmatched` and was still mid-load when retry #30 expired → "did not serve HTTP 200 — cold-start boot failed"). The SAME gate passed on the parallel pull_request run (27509243911, job 81306145869) AND on main post-merge (run 27509703733: `make run smoke` = success), proving the failure was a FLAKY cold-start TIMEOUT, not a defect in the #735 diff — main (b91a369) is healthy. **What shipped (CI-only):** widened the readiness loop to `seq 1 90` (~90s) so the budget covers the SLOWEST cold boot, with the existing fail-FAST guard preserved (`kill -0 "$server_pid"` breaks the instant the server process dies, so a genuine boot crash is still caught immediately rather than waiting out the budget). **Process note:** #735 was merged over this red required check after the red was misdiagnosed as the harmless push-run skipped-gate artifact; it was a genuine (if flaky) gate failure. Remediation is twofold — this budget fix (stops the false-red recurring) + the operator-side systemic fix of enabling server-side branch protection so GitHub itself blocks a merge while `CI OK` is red (the MERGE-READINESS CHARTER §4.5 "until server-side branch protection lands" gap). **Files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `Boot smoke` step), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-CI-SMOKE-COLDSTART-BUDGET-001. **Relates to** DEC-RUN-SMOKE-GATE-001, DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 (#780); MERGE-READINESS CHARTER (CLAUDE.md §2 rule 13).
780. **DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 — the DASHBOARD half of the N-connection live feed: write the subscription manifest from the persisted tables, run `capture-all --manifest` from the toggle, show the per-connection proof, fix the feed chip, add a restart watchdog** (2026-06-14, operator: build the dashboard side of DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 #778). **Why:** #778 landed the CAPTURE half — `capture-all --manifest <json>` reads a plain `{"spot":[…],"legs":[…]}` of feed-row dicts and opens connection #0 = spot (dual-feed) + #1..N = legs — but explicitly named the DASHBOARD half a follow-up: nothing WROTE that manifest from the persisted universe, the ON/OFF toggle still spawned the single-connection `capture`, the per-connection proof was never surfaced, the Live-bar chip showed a hardcoded `feed ltp`, and there was no restart-on-death watchdog. The dashboard ALREADY persists the exact universe — the `instruments` table (775 = 25 admitted indices + 750 stocks) + the F&O `contracts` registry (the legs) — so this PR wires THOSE into the live capture. **What shipped (purely `brutex/dashboard/` + its tests — the live package stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757 verified by `grep`; read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocabulary + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) NEW `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` — `build_spot_rows(store)` projects the in-scope `instruments` rows whose type is `IDX`/`EQ` to feed-row dicts (`exchange`=`exch_id`, `segment`, `exchange_token`=`security_id`, `instrument_type`=`instrument`, `underlying_symbol`) — the exact 775; `build_leg_rows(registry_path)` reads the F&O `contracts` registry (`ContractRow` → `segment=FNO`, `exchange_token`=`contract_symbol`, `instrument_type`=`side`), degrading to `[]` when the registry cache is absent (honest — never invents a leg, Golden Rule #1); `build_live_manifest` composes them; `write_manifest` writes the JSON atomically; `make_store_manifest_writer(store)` is the COMMON wiring point the dashboard injects (a `None` store emits an empty manifest → the capture self-resolves the spot). The manifest round-trips through `brutex.live.multiconn.read_subscription_manifest` (asserted in the TEST only — the source never imports the live package). (2) `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py` — `start()` now WRITES the manifest (via the injected `manifest_writer`) then spawns `capture-all --out … --report … --manifest … --feed both` instead of `capture`; `LiveStatus` gains `feed` + `report` (surfaced for the chip + the proof); creds-in-env + the pid state-file + crash-honest status are preserved. NEW `watch(*, max_restarts, base_backoff_s, max_backoff_s)` — the calendar-free supervisor: while a `start` is in effect (the toggle is ON) and the subprocess DIED, it RESTARTS with bounded exponential backoff (the operator's rule: always restart while ON; no session-calendar gate); a clean `stop()` clears the remembered spawn so a deliberately-stopped feed is never resurrected (a stop DURING the backoff also aborts). (3) `brutex/dashboard/live_connections.py` (NEW) — `read_connections(report_path)` parses the capture's `--report` Markdown back into `{connections:[{index,feed,subscribed}], summary, note}`, degrading to an empty payload + note when no proof exists yet. (4) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the `start` route passes `report`/`manifest`; NEW `GET /api/v1/live/connections` returns the parsed proof; the default `LiveRunner` is wired with `make_store_manifest_writer(instrument_store)`. (5) `templates/live.html` — a per-connection proof table (`#connGrid`/`#connCount`, polled from `/api/v1/live/connections`); the feed chip is now `#chipFeed` driven by `status.feed` (reads `both`, no longer a hardcoded `ltp`); the spawn note reflects `capture-all`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the manifest writer + the connection-proof parser + the watchdog + the routes/page are 100.00% line+branch tested against fakes/seeds (`live_manifest.py` + `live_connections.py` + `live_runner.py` all 100.00%; 55 live tests across `test_live_manifest.py` (NEW) + `test_live_connections.py` (NEW) + `test_live_runner.py` + `test_dashboard_live.py`), `ruff check brutex tests` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` clean (only the known transitive vendor-SDK import-untyped notes, absent in CI); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — `grep` finds NO `brutex.live` import in `brutex/dashboard/` (the manifest is the file contract; the only live import is in a TEST); ✅ TESTABLE NOW — manifest-from-tables + the per-connection display + the chip + the restart machinery are all provable with the market CLOSED; 🟡 the legs are present only once the F&O `contracts` registry is pulled (else `legs=[]`, honest); 🟡 the actual per-connection TICKS are the 09:15-IST-Monday market gate (ADR-0009 Phase-0, UNVERIFIED — not claimed); 🟡 the real N-socket open + the supervisor thread wiring stay the operator-Mac `# pragma`/market follow-ups. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/live_connections.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/live.html`, `tests/unit/test_live_manifest.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_connections.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 (#778), DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-001 (#776), DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001 (#774), DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001 (#771), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757); market facts CLAUDE.md §6/§7.

779. **DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 — `capture-all` reads a `{spot, legs}` JSON subscription manifest (the EXACT 775 + the F&O legs) so `brutex/live/` stays decoupled from the lake schema** (2026-06-14, operator: "already we have everything in the instruments table and the contracts registry — subscribe THOSE 775 + futures/options, not the raw 452"). **Why:** the live resolver (`_real_instrument_resolver`) re-filters the raw Groww instrument CSV to `all` → ~452 (every raw IDX + the F&O-eligible stocks), which OVER-includes obscure indices and SKIPS the ~538 NTM reference stocks, and never resolves the option/future legs — so the operator's real run subscribed 452, not the admitted 775, and zero legs. The dashboard, by contrast, ALREADY persists the exact universe: the `instruments` table (775 = 25 admitted indices + 750 stocks) + the F&O `contracts` registry (the legs). **What shipped (purely `brutex/live/` — still imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only, no orders; engine/52-vocab UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** `brutex/live/multiconn.py` gains `read_subscription_manifest(path) -> (spot, legs)` — it parses a PLAIN JSON `{"spot":[…],"legs":[…]}` of feed-row dicts (each carrying the 4 feed keys `exchange`/`segment`/`exchange_token`/`instrument_type`), validating every row (raises `ValueError` on a non-object manifest, a non-list group, a non-object row, or a row missing a feed key); and `capture-all` gains `--manifest`: when given, the spot + legs come from the manifest (the exact 775 on connection #0 via the dual-feed + the legs sharded across #1..N), else it falls back to the resolver (spot only). Keeping the manifest a JSON FILE is the decoupling seam: the DASHBOARD (which owns the instrument store + the contracts registry) writes it; `brutex/live/` reads a file and never imports the lake schema or the data plane — so it still lifts to TickVault unchanged. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `read_subscription_manifest` + the `--manifest` wiring are 100% line+branch tested against fixture manifests (`brutex/live/multiconn.py` 100.00%; `__main__.py` stays 100.00%; 35 multiconn+CLI tests), `ruff check brutex tests` + format + mypy clean; 🟡 the DASHBOARD half — WRITING the manifest from the `instruments` + `contracts` tables + wiring `--manifest`/the per-connection display into the toggle — is the immediate Track-2 follow-up; 🟡 the real N-socket open + the Monday tick delivery stay the `# pragma`/market gates. **Files:** `brutex/live/multiconn.py`, `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_multiconn.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-001 (#776), DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001 (#774), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757).

776. **DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-001 — wire `build_grouped_plan` into a real N-connection capture + a PER-CONNECTION subscription proof (`brutex/live/multiconn.py` + `capture-all`)** (2026-06-14, operator: "not only the 775 spot on the first connection but the N connections and their respective instrument subscriptions must work — I'll check the entire permutation now"). **Why:** DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001 (#774) made connection #0 carry the whole spot universe (indices + stocks each on its feed), and DEC-LIVE-SHARD-GROUPS-001 (#764) computed the spot-first shards — but nothing OPENED connections #1..N for the F&O legs or PROVED, per connection, "how many opened + what each subscribed". This lands the orchestration + the proof the operator wants to test. **What shipped (purely `brutex/live/` — imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only market data, no orders; engine + 52-vocab UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** NEW `brutex/live/multiconn.py` — (1) `plan_connections(spot, legs, *, per_connection_cap, ceiling)` builds the spot-first grouped plan and emits per-connection `ConnectionBinding`s: connection #0.. carry the spot shards (`feed_kind="both"`, the dual-feed), the SUBSEQUENT connections the leg shards (`"ltp"`), each binding carrying the ORIGINAL resolver rows (so a spot connection can dual-feed-route them) — spot wins on a cross-group duplicate; an injected `ceiling` (the probe-discovered concurrent limit) caps the bound connections and the SKIPPED shard count is surfaced, never hidden (Golden Rule #1). (2) `open_and_subscribe` opens one websocket per binding (injected `open_feed`) and subscribes its instruments on its feed (injected `make_subscribe`), all feeding ONE callback. (3) `make_multiconn_capture` composes those N connections into the SINGLE `(subscribe, read_snapshot)` seam `TickCapture` already takes (COMMON reuse — the capture loop is UNCHANGED), merging every connection's snapshot into one record. (4) `SubscriptionPlanReport` renders the per-connection proof table (`# connections (spot + leg), instruments, skipped`). Plus a runnable `python -m brutex.live capture-all --out … --report …` (`brutex/live/__main__.py`) that resolves the spot, plans + opens the connections, writes the per-connection proof, and captures. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the sharding + open/subscribe orchestration + capture-seam + report are 100% line+branch tested against fakes (`brutex/live/multiconn.py` 100.00%; 12 multiconn + the live-CLI tests; `__main__.py` stays 100.00%), ruff + format + mypy clean (only the transitive growwapi sandbox notes, absent in CI); ✅ TESTABLE NOW — the connection/subscription MACHINERY (N connections open + each accepts its subscription + the per-connection counts) is provable with the market CLOSED; 🟡 the actual TICKS per connection are the 09:15-IST-Monday market gate (ADR-0009 Phase-0, UNVERIFIED — not claimed); 🟡 F&O LEG RESOLUTION (`get_expiries` → `get_contracts` to populate connections #1..N) + the dashboard per-connection DISPLAY are the named follow-ups — until the leg resolver lands, `capture-all` plans the spot connection(s); the N-connection engine is ready for the legs. The real N-socket open is `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac). **Files:** `brutex/live/multiconn.py` (NEW), `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_multiconn.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001 (#774), DEC-LIVE-SHARD-GROUPS-001 (#764), DEC-LIVE-PROBE-CONCURRENT-001 (#763), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757); market facts CLAUDE.md §6/§7.

774. **DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001 — the live capture routes indices to the index-value feed and stocks to the ltp feed (`--feed both`, the new default) so the brute-force indices actually tick** (2026-06-14, operator real-run finding). **Why:** the operator flipped the dashboard Live toggle ON during a real run — the credentials bridged (DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001 #771), the socket connected (`Ready to Groww!`), and `capture_subscribe instruments=452` ran cleanly, but 0 ticks were captured over 150s. TWO findings: (1) the run was on a SUNDAY — NSE/BSE are closed at weekends (CLAUDE.md §7), so 0 ticks was EXPECTED, not a fault (the hard part — auth + socket — proved working); (2) **the real bug**: the dashboard toggle ran `--feed ltp`, and the capture subscribes ONE feed method per run (`brutex/live/__main__.py` `_make_subscribe`), but INDICES carry an index VALUE, not a last-traded-price — subscribed on the ltp feed they are SILENT even when the market opens (they need `subscribe_index_value`). So as wired the F&O stocks would tick Monday but NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX — the brute-force targets — would NOT. **What shipped (purely `brutex/live/` + the dashboard toggle default — `brutex/live/` still imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only market data, no orders; the engine + 52-vocab UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** a new `--feed both` mode (now the capture/verify default) that subscribes indices via `subscribe_index_value` AND stocks via `subscribe_ltp` on the SAME feed + callback (one connection, two subscriptions = the operator's 'connection #1 = all spot' model), with a merged snapshot reader. Two PURE, fully-tested helpers do the routing: `classify_feed_instruments` (splits resolver rows into index-value vs ltp by `instrument_type`, stripping the routing tag down to the 3 SDK feed keys) and `merge_snapshots` (unions the two feeds' snapshots); the resolver now tags each row with its `instrument_type`. The capture/verify loops are UNCHANGED — they already take abstract `subscribe`/`read_snapshot` closures (COMMON reuse, CLAUDE.md §11). The dashboard `live_runner.start()` feed default flips `ltp` → `both`, so the ON/OFF toggle now captures indices + stocks each on the feed that delivers it. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the routing helpers + both-mode subscribe/reader branches are 100% line+branch tested against fakes (`brutex/live/__main__.py` 100.00%; 51 live-CLI tests), ruff + format + mypy clean (only the transitive growwapi sandbox notes, absent in CI); 🟡 that the indices ACTUALLY tick on the index-value feed at 09:15 IST Monday is the ADR-0009 Phase-0 LIVE gate — UNVERIFIED until a real market session (the wiring is proven; the vendor delivery is not, and is NOT claimed); 🟡 subscribing the EXACT admitted 775 universe (vs the raw-master IDX + F&O-EQ set the `all` resolver yields), wiring `build_grouped_plan` (#764) into the real N-connection subscribe, and the per-connection subscription DISPLAY are the named follow-ups. **Also repairs a broken-on-`main` ledger**: renumbered the post-merge duplicate DEC-M4PRO-VERIFY-001 771 → 773. **Files:** `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001 (#771), DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-001 (#762), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757); market facts CLAUDE.md §6/§7.

771. **DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001 — the dashboard ON/OFF injects the saved Groww creds into the capture subprocess env + crash-honest status (poll reaps a zombie child)** (2026-06-14, operator real-run finding). **Why:** the operator saved the Groww TOTP key/secret on the dashboard Credentials page (→ `~/.brutex/credentials.json`, mode 0600), flipped the Live toggle ON, and the spawned `python -m brutex.live capture` crashed instantly with `GrowwAuthError: missing Groww credentials: ['BRUTEX_GROWW_API_KEY', 'BRUTEX_GROWW_TOTP_SECRET']` — because `resolve_groww_credentials(os.environ)` reads ENV VARS (CLAUDE.md §6 / `groww/auth.py`) while the dashboard saved them to a FILE. The two stores never bridged, yet the page promised "auto-load every session". Worse, the dashboard still showed "running pid …" because a crashed child becomes a ZOMBIE that `os.kill(pid,0)` (`is_pid_alive`) still reports alive — a false "running". **What shipped (purely `brutex/dashboard/` — `brutex/live/` still imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only, no orders):** (1) `dashboard/live_runner.py` — a `_load_cred_env()` (injected `cred_env` hook) loads the saved file via `brutex.config.credentials.load_groww_credentials` and returns `{BRUTEX_GROWW_API_KEY, BRUTEX_GROWW_TOTP_SECRET}`; `start()` merges them into the child's environment (`{**os.environ, **cred_env}`) so the capture authenticates without the operator re-exporting — creds ride in the child ENV, NEVER on argv (so `ps` stays clean). No/broken creds → `{}` (the capture then fails auth and the crash is surfaced honestly, never silently). (2) Crash-honest status — the runner now holds the spawned `Popen` and `status()` uses `proc.poll()` (authoritative: reaps a crashed child so a zombie reads STOPPED) when we hold the handle, falling back to `is_pid_alive` only for post-restart adoption. The `PopenFactory` signature is now `(argv, env)`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ creds-injection + crash-detection + the 3 `_load_cred_env` branches are 100% line+branch tested against fakes (24 runner tests + the `/live` route tests; `live_runner.py` 100%), ruff + format + mypy clean (the only mypy notes are the transitive growwapi sandbox artifacts, absent in CI); ✅ creds never on argv; 🟡 the heartbeat-silence **watchdog** (auto-restart on a real websocket drop, calendar-free per the operator) + the cross-process OS lock + the `(pid,start_time)` identity check stack on this PR as the next Phase-2 items; 🟡 the real subprocess/auth path stays `# pragma: no cover` (operator's Mac). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_runner.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-001 (#762), DEC-LIVE-OBSERVE-FULLUNIV-001 (#760), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757).

765. **DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-003 — fourth full machine-checked workspace verification (the FIRST in the Groww era) + the doc-drift it surfaced + the operator-reported credentials-nav fix** (2026-06-14, operator request: "deep thorough research by activating all agents and all sub-agents … confirming the entire workspace works as expected … make it ready for merge, monitor it until it gets merged … no illusion or hallucination"). **Method (CLAUDE.md §9):** the lead bootstrapped a faithful env and executed every locally-runnable CI gate centrally while parallel read-only agents audited plans/history, the O(1) hot-path discipline, and CI/automation reality — successor to DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-001 (#398) / DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-002 (#609). **REAL measured numbers (tip `259f366` = #718, branch == origin at run start):** full `pytest` **7,435 passed / 41 skipped / 0 failed** (458.6s); `mypy --strict` **0 issues / 243 files**; `pyright` **0 errors** (18 advisory); `ruff` + `ruff format` clean; `bandit -ll` **0** high/medium; `pip-audit` **0** known CVEs; `interrogate` **94.2%** (project floor 80%; CI runs the stricter 100% flag-set); Rust **fno-math 519 tests** + **trading-core** golden bit-identity all green (`cargo fmt/clippy -D warnings/test`); `brutex doctor` PASS. **Headline: ZERO functional/correctness bugs.** **The one real finding was ENVIRONMENTAL, not code:** a fresh clone ships the wrong default `python` (3.11 — but the repo mandates ≥3.12, CLAUDE.md §4, so the valid PEP-695 `def _dedup_seq[T]` at `engine/sweep_orchestrator.py:464` is a syntax error on 3.11) AND no built Rust kernels (`ModuleNotFoundError: fno_math`), so a naive `pytest` shows 269 collection errors that are 100% provisioning noise; the repo's own `make setup` / `scripts/setup/bootstrap.sh` (3.12 venv + both `maturin` kernels) makes every gate green. **Doc drift FIXED (this PR):** (a) CLAUDE.md §1 (line 92) + §3 (line 316) active branch `claude/sharp-mendel-lgbckj` → `claude/zen-meitner-am13gf` (stale — old branch); (b) `TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md` vendor banner was INVERTED (still said "the live vendor is Dhan … read forward-looking 'Groww' as Dhan", pointing at the deleted `brutex/adapters/dhan/`) — layered a superseding note pointing back to Groww per ADR-0009 / DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001, history preserved. **Also lands the operator-reported credentials-nav fix** (DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-CREDS-RECONCILE-001 #766). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ every §1 gate was actually executed this session; 🟡 M4-Pro-only absolute gates (50 M/s floor, strict 1.1× tier, 33B SLA) cannot run here — the loose CI ratio gates stand in; 🟡 CodeQL/Semgrep/Trivy/gitleaks/SBOM/jscpd/vulture/mutation/chaos/stress run on GitHub CI and gate this PR via the required `CI OK` aggregate; 🟡 STANDARDS_100PCT.md §1 remains 16🟢/1🟡/1📋/3👁️ (~76%) — no "100% compliant" claim; 🚫 no live Groww calls (no token here) — the ADR-0009 Phase-0 probes stay UNVERIFIED as CLAUDE.md §6 declares. **Files:** `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-14.md` (NEW), `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-003. **Builds on** DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-002 (#609), DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-001 (#398), DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (ADR-0009), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441), CLAUDE.md §9/§10/§12/§13.

766. **DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-CREDS-RECONCILE-001 — the `/groww-credentials` page nav is reconciled to the canonical 7-link set; the migration-era "Groww (legacy)"/"Groww" toggle + dead `/credentials` 404 links removed** (2026-06-14, operator-reported: "why suddenly alignment changed and sections changed and names also changed … for all the webpages the alignment should be extremely super precise static"). **Why (correctness + UX):** every dashboard page exposes the nav `Universe · Credentials · Database · Live · Coverage · Movers · Reports`, but `brutex/dashboard/templates/groww_credentials.html` (served at `/groww-credentials`, `app.py:2855`) rendered a DIVERGENT nav — `Universe · Groww (legacy) · Groww · Database · Coverage · Movers` — with (1) a dead `/credentials` link labelled "Groww (legacy)" (there is NO `/credentials` route → 404), (2) a "Groww" self-label instead of "Credentials", (3) a MISSING "Reports" link, and (4) wrong order, so it visibly mis-aligned vs every other page. **Root cause:** there is no shared nav partial — each template hardcodes its own `<nav>`; the Groww re-migration added `groww_credentials.html` beside the now-orphaned `credentials.html`, and the "Universe nav on every page" pass (DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIVERSE-001 #701) normalised the OTHER pages but copied this one's bespoke nav forward unchanged. **What shipped (UI only — read-only, no engine/52-vocab/scope change, Golden Rule §3):** rewrote the `groww_credentials.html` nav to the canonical 7 links (Credentials = `/groww-credentials`, `aria-current="page"`), byte-identical to `db.html`'s nav; removed the dead `/credentials` links in both the nav and the page footer; added regression test `test_groww_credentials_nav_is_canonical` (asserts the 7 canonical links present + no dead `/credentials` link + no "Groww (legacy)" label). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the affected dashboard tests pass (18: route + a11y + credentials-ux); ✅ one template + one test touched — the orphaned `credentials.html` + `_render_credentials_html` are LEFT in place (kept alive by `test_dashboard_credentials_ux.py` + `test_dashboard_a11y_polish.py`; deleting them is separate churn); 🟡 the durable fix — extracting ONE shared `_nav.html` partial + a shared `bx-theme.css` so all ~12 pages stop copy-pasting nav + `:root` tokens (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) — remains the named follow-up DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIFY-001. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/groww_credentials.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_groww_credentials_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-CREDS-RECONCILE-001. **Builds on** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIVERSE-001 (#701), DEC-UNIVERSE-UI-POLISH-001 (#694).
764. **DEC-LIVE-SHARD-GROUPS-001 — group-aware connection sharding: spot fills connection #1 (shards 0..k), legs fill the SUBSEQUENT connections, NEVER mixed in one shard (`brutex/live/plan.py` `build_grouped_plan`)** (2026-06-14, operator's "connection #1 = all spot, connections #2…N = legs" model). **Why (correctness):** when subscribing the live universe the operator wants the spot instruments (the brute-force indices + their cash legs) isolated on the FIRST connection(s) and the futures/options legs on the SUBSEQUENT ones — so a per-connection drop/auto-close on a leg socket never tears down the spot subscription, and the spot group is always reachable on connection #1. The pre-existing `build_plan` (DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 #755) packed ALL instruments into contiguous `ceil(N/cap)` shards with no notion of group, so a trailing partial spot shard would get topped up with leg instruments — mixing the two groups on one connection. **What shipped (REFERENCE/RESEARCH only — read-only, no orders, NOT in the engine/52-vocab; purely `brutex/live/`, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; `build_plan` UNCHANGED):** NEW `build_grouped_plan(spot, legs, *, per_connection_cap=1000) -> ConnectionPlan` — one O(N) spot-FIRST dedup pass (`(*spot, *legs)`, same O(1) set-membership as `build_plan`) so a security present in BOTH groups is kept ONCE on its SPOT connection (spot wins — it rides connection #1); the distinct spot count is the boundary offset handed to a small shared helper `_plan_from_unique(unique, *, per_connection_cap, boundaries)` that cuts shards at the cap AND at every group boundary (`itertools.pairwise` over the sorted cut points), so spot fills shards `0..k` (`k = ceil(len(spot_unique)/cap) - 1`) and legs fill the shards AFTER — **a shard boundary always falls between the spot group and the leg group; the two are NEVER mixed in one shard**. `build_plan` was refactored onto the SAME `_plan_from_unique` helper (zero duplication, CLAUDE.md §2 rule 11 COMMON; its `boundaries=()` default reproduces the old contiguous cap-only packing byte-identically). The returned `ConnectionPlan`'s O(1) `connection_of`/`legs_of`/`shard` lookups + the `ConnectionPlan` public API are unchanged. This pairs with the 1000-instruments-per-subscription Groww cap (CLAUDE.md §6) and the concurrent-connection probe (DEC-LIVE-PROBE-CONCURRENT-001 #763): once the probe reports the concurrent ceiling C, the grouped plan packs `spot ∪ legs` into ≤C connections with the spot/legs split preserved. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — the O(1) claim, precisely):** every LOOKUP / dedup / route / assign on the returned plan is **O(1)** (dict / set / tuple-index); BUILDING the plan is **O(N)** one pass and the maps are **O(N)** space — you must touch each of the N distinct instruments once and store its assignment, which is NOT an O(1)-total claim (impossible for N distinct instruments). The per-connection-vs-per-account 1000 cap stays UNVERIFIED until the `verify`/`probe` run. **Verified (3.12 venv):** 9 new tests (spot-only 1 connection, spot overflow → 2 spot connections, spot+legs boundary-never-mixes, instrument-in-both-deduped-spot-wins, empty spot → legs at #0, empty legs → spot-only, both empty → 0 connections, O(1) `connection_of` on a spot key vs a leg key + KeyError miss, bad cap <1 raises); `tests/unit/test_live_plan.py` 19 tests pass, `brutex/live/plan.py` **100.00% line+branch**; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict brutex/live/plan.py` clean. 🟡 wiring `build_grouped_plan` into the real multi-connection `subscribe` path stays the named follow-up (it opens N real sockets on the operator's Mac, `# pragma: no cover`). **Files:** `brutex/live/plan.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_plan.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-SHARD-GROUPS-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-SCALE-MAP-001 (#755), DEC-LIVE-PROBE-CONCURRENT-001 (#763), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753).
770. **DEC-LIVE-DB-BROWSER-001 — the live tables get a real DB query API: search / sort / filter / column-pick (`query_live_table` + `live_columns` + `/api/v1/live/{columns,query}`)** (2026-06-14, operator request — "will it show precisely like a db so I can access/search/sort/find?"). **Why:** the Live tab rendered the two live tables as columns+rows (the `/db` grid shape) but had no search/sort/filter — the operator wants to find/sort/search any row precisely, exactly like the `/db` Database browser. **What shipped (purely `brutex/dashboard/` — `brutex/live/` still imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only, no orders):** (1) `dashboard/live_lake_view.py` — `query_live_table(lake_root, table, *, columns, filters, order_by, descending, limit, offset)` is the live-lake twin of `db_view.query_table`, REUSING its validated builders (`_select_list` / `_build_where` / `_build_order_by`, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — no copy-paste) against the live Parquet `read_parquet(?)` source: pick columns, filter with `(col, op, val)` (`op` an `ALLOWED_OPERATORS` token), sort, page; every identifier validated against the partition's REAL columns (an unknown/injection-shaped name raises before any SQL), operators from the fixed map, the glob + all values BOUND (no path-traversal / glob-injection). `total` is the FILTERED count so the pager is correct; default sort is newest-first by the table's stable key. `live_columns(...)` returns a table's columns (the picker). (2) `dashboard/app.py` — `GET /api/v1/live/columns/{name}` + `GET /api/v1/live/query/{name}` (repeatable `column=` / `f=col:op:value`, `order_by` + `desc`, `limit`/`offset`), reusing the in-module `_parse_filters`; both degrade to an empty payload when no lake is wired and 400 on a bad table/column/operator. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `query_live_table` + `live_columns` + the routes are 100% line+branch tested (filter/sort/project/validate paths; 18 live-lake-view + route tests; `live_lake_view.py` 100%), ruff + format clean, mypy clean on the module (only the transitive growwapi sandbox notes, absent in CI); ✅ same safe bound-parameter discipline as `/db`; 🟡 the Live tab's query-builder UI controls (column picker / filter rows / sort dropdown calling these routes) are the immediate follow-up — this PR lands the query API + routes the UI will call. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DB-BROWSER-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-001 (#762), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756), DEC-DB-QUERY-001 (the `/db` query pattern reused).

767. **DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIFY-001 — a single canonical source of truth for the dashboard top-nav + a cross-page consistency GUARD test, so nav/section drift can never silently recur** (2026-06-14, operator decree: "nowhere I can tolerate this wrong mapping or wrong issue … for all the webpages the alignment should be extremely super precise static"). **Why (durable hardening):** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-CREDS-RECONCILE-001 (#766) fixed the ONE drifted page (`/groww-credentials`), but the root cause — every template hand-codes its own `<nav>` with no shared spec or mechanical guard — was still live, so any future page could drift again (a missing/extra/reordered/renamed link, or a re-introduced dead `/credentials` 404). This closes the CLASS of bug. **What shipped (UI/test only — read-only, NO engine/52-vocab/scope change, Golden Rule §3):** (1) NEW `brutex/dashboard/nav.py` — `NAV_LINKS` is the canonical ordered 7-link spec (Universe · Credentials=`/groww-credentials` · Database · Live · Coverage · Movers · Reports) in EXACTLY ONE place, plus `render_topnav(active)` the shared renderer pages can adopt so the markup converges too. (2) NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py` — renders all **10** served top-nav pages through their own `_render_*_html` helpers and asserts each nav equals `NAV_LINKS` (same links, same order), carries NO dead `/credentials` link and NO "Groww (legacy)" label, and ≤1 `aria-current`; PLUS a meta-guard asserting every `_render_*_html` helper is either checked or explicitly exempted (index=tab-nav, welcome=landing nav, the orphaned Dhan-era `credentials.html`), so a NEWLY added page cannot silently skip the guard. **Verified (3.12 venv):** all 10 pages currently match the canonical nav (rendered + diffed); 23 tests pass; `brutex/dashboard/nav.py` **100.00% line+branch**; `ruff` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the GUARD is the durable guarantee — any nav drift now FAILS CI (the structural "it can't happen again" the operator asked for), and the canonical spec lives in one file; 🟡 the templates still hand-render their nav (the guard enforces they match `NAV_LINKS`; wiring each template to RENDER FROM `render_topnav` for byte-level DRY, consolidating the copy-pasted `:root` design tokens into a shared `bx-theme.css`, and DELETING the orphaned `credentials.html` + its loaders are the named follow-ups — they touch the render path of all ~12 pages and warrant their own reviewed PR); ✅ zero engine / data / scope lines touched. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/nav.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIFY-001. **Builds on** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-CREDS-RECONCILE-001 (#766), DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIVERSE-001 (#701), DEC-UNIVERSE-UI-POLISH-001 (#694).

775. **DEC-DASHBOARD-UX-POLISH-001 — dashboard UX consistency + polish pass: ONE shared header/theme stylesheet so every page's brand + subtitle + top-nav aligns to a single grid, plus credentials de-clutter, a /db expired-options list hide, and a restrained motion layer** (2026-06-14, operator complaints from screenshots of the running dashboard: section-heading/nav alignment "inconsistent and not precise across pages", credentials page clutter, "expired options" in the /db table list, and "make the pages feel polished/animated/attractive"). **Why:** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIFY-001 (#767) made the nav LINKS canonical (one `nav.py` `NAV_LINKS` + a guard test), but each page still hand-coded its own header CSS + markup — some used `<span>` logo/sub, some `<div>`, some an inline-styled `<nav>`, some a bare `.topnav` rule with a different gap/colour — so the brand+subtitle+nav block drifted in spacing/alignment from page to page. This PR is the LAYOUT/visual layer on top of that link-level unification. **What shipped (purely `brutex/dashboard/` templates + a static stylesheet + its tests — NO Python source touched in `brutex/`; the brute-force engine + 52-vocabulary + data plane + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; read-only market data, no orders; `brutex/dashboard/` still does not import `brutex.live`, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757):** (1) NEW `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-theme.css` — ONE source of truth (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) for the design tokens, the canonical `header`/`.brandmark`/`.logo`/`.sub`/`.topnav` rules, the keyboard `:focus-visible` ring, a restrained motion layer (page-enter fade/slide, hover/active transitions on nav links + buttons + table rows, a loading shimmer/spinner), and a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` opt-out (NO motion for users who ask for none). It reuses the EXISTING dark palette — no new colours. (3) The credentials page (`groww_credentials.html`) lost the footer storage note + the "Other views" link line per the operator; the form + Save/Test buttons + the "Status: …" line stay (the live POST/GET/test routes + the `esc()` XSS escaping are untouched). (4) `db.html` HIDES the expired-options lake from the browsable Candle-lake LIST — SCOPE-SAFE per operator approval: only the `data-candles="option"` list row is dropped; the underlying `options/` lake, its data, the `selectCandles("option")` browse path, and the route stay fully intact (nothing deleted, no write path changed; the lake remains a documented REFERENCE_ONLY surface). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ all 4 complaints addressed + asserted by `test_dashboard_ux_polish.py` (25 tests: shared-theme link on every top-nav page, structurally-identical header markup, the served stylesheet carries the canonical header + reduced-motion + focus ring, credentials clutter gone / core controls kept, the /db options list row gone / spot row kept); ✅ the existing guard tests stay green — `test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py` + the broader `-k dashboard` suite (636) + the focused batch (272) all pass; ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean + mypy-clean on the one new Python file (the test) — the only mypy notes are the known transitive vendor-SDK `import-untyped`/`unused-ignore` artifacts in the adapter modules (untouched here, absent in CI); ✅ coverage gate held — NO new Python lines in `brutex/` (templates + CSS + a test only), so nothing newly uncovered; 🚫 out of scope: any engine/52-vocab/data/scope change, a palette redesign, or deleting the options lake. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-theme.css` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/templates/{universe,groww_credentials,db,live,coverage,movers,reports,spot_coverage,fetch_windows,expired_options}.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_ux_polish.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-UX-POLISH-001. **Builds on** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIFY-001 (#767), DEC-DASHBOARD-A11Y-POLISH-002, DEC-DASHBOARD-MOBILE-UX-001, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757).

772. **DEC-LIVE-UI-CONTROLS-001 — the Live tab's query-builder UI controls: a column picker + AND-combined filter rows + a sort dropdown + Prev/Next paging, wired to the already-merged `/api/v1/live/{columns,query}` routes (search / sort / filter / find — precisely like `/db`)** (2026-06-14, operator request: "will it show precisely like a db so I can access/search/sort/find?"). **Why:** DEC-LIVE-DB-BROWSER-001 (#770) landed the live query API + routes (`query_live_table` + `live_columns` + `GET /api/v1/live/columns/{name}` + `GET /api/v1/live/query/{name}`) but the `/live` page still rendered the two live tables (`live_ticks`, `live_candles_1m`) as static columns+rows with no search/sort/filter — that PR's honest envelope named the query-builder UI controls as "the immediate follow-up". This lands it: the Live tab now browses precisely like the `/db` Database browser. **What shipped (purely `brutex/dashboard/` template + its tests — `brutex/live/` still imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `dashboard/templates/live.html` — the table-browse panel is rebuilt to MIRROR `/db`'s query-builder (DEC-DB-QUERY-001) 1:1 for the two live tables: a multi-select **column picker** (checkboxes from `GET /api/v1/live/columns/{name}`), repeatable **filter rows** (`column` + `operator` + `value` → repeated `f=col:op:value`, the operator an `ALLOWED_OPERATORS` token), a **sort dropdown** (`order_by` + asc/desc → `desc`), and **Prev/Next paging** (`limit`/`offset`), all calling `GET /api/v1/live/query/{name}` and rendering the returned `{table, columns, rows, total, limit, offset}` into the grid (newest-first default). The `live_ticks` / `live_candles_1m` tab switch, the ON/OFF capture toggle, the status/uptime/tick cards, and the per-cell `esc()` XSS escaping (values are vendor-origin) are all preserved. The markup + fetch logic are copied from `db.html` so the two browsers look + behave identically (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — the JS shares the same `gridAndPager` / column-picker / filter-row shape). (2) `dashboard/app.py` — only the `_load_live_template` docstring is updated to name the new query-builder routes (no behaviour change; the `/api/v1/live/{columns,query}` routes from #770 are reused as-is, NOT re-implemented). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the new controls render on `/live` (asserted by `test_live_page_renders_query_builder_controls`: the column picker / filter / sort / paging markup + the `…/columns/` + `…/query/` route URLs appear in the page HTML); ✅ the 9 `/live` route+page tests pass (TestClient + a fake runner + a seeded lake); ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean on the changed files, mypy clean on `app.py` (the only notes are the transitive `growwapi` import-untyped sandbox artifacts in the adapter modules, absent in CI); ✅ the page is pure template/JS — the only Python touched is a docstring, so no new uncovered Python lines (coverage unchanged); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — `grep` finds NO new `brutex.live` import in `brutex/dashboard/`; 🟡 the live PARQUET tables fill once the capture JSONL is materialised (`python -m brutex.live lake`) — the empty-state names that, never invents rows (Golden Rule #1); 🟡 the operator-Mac-only real subprocess/feed is unchanged from #762. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/live.html`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (docstring only), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-UI-CONTROLS-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DB-BROWSER-001 (#770), DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-001 (#762), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757), DEC-DB-QUERY-001 (the `/db` query-builder pattern reused).
773. **DEC-M4PRO-VERIFY-001 — full WORKSPACE verification on the registered M4-Pro (macOS) self-hosted runner via a new `verify-m4pro.yml` workflow** (2026-06-14, operator: "why are you not using the github actions runner and commands for the real verification dude") _(renumbered 771 → 773 by DEC-LIVE-DUAL-FEED-001: it had collided on `main` with the earlier-merged DEC-LIVE-CREDS-BRIDGE-001 #771 — a post-merge duplicate the PR-only ledger gate could not catch; P-1 later-merged-renumbers)_. **Why:** the shared CI (`ci.yml`) runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, but the operator DEVELOPS + RUNS on Apple Silicon (CLAUDE.md §8); the per-session verification the assistant ran lived in a generic Linux container. This adds a workflow that runs the FULL functional verification ON the actual production hardware/OS — the registered runner `Parthibans-MacBook-Pro` `[self-hosted, macos, m4pro]` (the same runner `bench-m4pro.yml` uses for the perf floors) — so "the entire workspace works" is proven on macOS/arm64, catching any platform-specific breakage the ubuntu shared CI cannot. **What shipped (additive — one workflow file, no code/scope change):** `.github/workflows/verify-m4pro.yml` runs, on the M4-Pro runner: `actions/checkout` → runner-identity + GPU/Metal device report (informational; the engine is CPU/rayon today per ADR-0004) → Python 3.12 → bootstrap (venv + `[dev,optimize]` + `fno_math` + `trading_core` via maturin) → `ruff` lint+format → `mypy --strict` + `pyright` → the FULL `pytest -q` suite → `brutex doctor` → both Rust crates (`cargo fmt/clippy -D warnings/test`). **Triggers:** `workflow_dispatch` + a daily 12:00-UTC cron — deliberately **NO `pull_request` trigger** (DEC-M4PRO-PR-TRIGGER-001: an offline laptop runner would otherwise hang every PR's mergeable state; the shared `ci.yml` remains the per-PR gate). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ this is the operator's requested "real verification on the runner" surface — real commands on real hardware, on cron + on demand; ✅ YAML parses; the CI `actionlint` job validates it on this PR; 🟡 the assistant cannot DISPATCH it (the GitHub app integration is read-only on Actions — 403); the operator triggers it (Actions → verify-m4pro → Run workflow) or the daily cron runs it; 🟡 it is a daily/dispatch MEASUREMENT/verification gate, not a per-PR blocker (by the same offline-runner reasoning); 🚫 GPU acceleration NOT added — ADR-0004 measured only 1.2–2.3× on M4-Pro unified memory and GPU never changes O(1); a real Metal kernel needs the hardware to build+test (won't ship untested code). **Files:** `.github/workflows/verify-m4pro.yml` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-M4PRO-VERIFY-001. **Builds on** DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 (#236), DEC-O1-CACHE-TIER-001 (#655), DEC-M4PRO-PR-TRIGGER-001, DEC-M4PRO-DOC-RECONCILE-001 (#769).

778. **DEC-BLOOM-FPR-SAMPLE-001 — make the Bloom empirical-FPR property test statistically sound (adequate sample + count-based envelope) so it stops deterministically breaching at the tight `fpr_target` boundary** (2026-06-14, full-suite finding — a single failing test in the integrated 7,596-test workspace run). **Why:** `tests/property/test_bloom_invariants.py::TestEmpiricalFprBounded::test_fpr_within_target_at_capacity` asserted `empirical_fpr ≤ fpr_target × 5` measured on a FIXED 1000-probe sample over the whole `fpr_target ∈ [1e-3, 0.1]` range. At the tight end (`fpr_target=1e-3`) a 1000-probe sample EXPECTS only ~1 false positive, so the 5× multiplicative envelope tolerates at most 5 FPs — a regime where a single extra FP from ordinary sampling variance blows the bound. Because the probe/insert inputs are DETERMINISTIC (`sha256("in:{i}")` / `sha256("probe:{i}")`), the hypothesis example `(capacity=892, fpr_target=0.001)` produced exactly 6 FPs and breached `0.006 ≤ 0.005` REPRODUCIBLY (not flaky) — and `max_examples=10` means a fresh-checkout CI run can rediscover it. This was a latent test-robustness defect: the Bloom filter itself is correct (the designed FPR ≈ target across the grid), but the TEST's measurement was under-powered. **What shipped (test-only — NO `brutex/` source touched; the Bloom filter, orchestrator dedup, and engine are UNCHANGED, CLAUDE.md §3):** the test now (1) SCALES the probe count to `max(1000, ceil(MIN_EXPECTED_FP / fpr_target))` with `MIN_EXPECTED_FP=10`, so the EXPECTED false-positive count is ≥ 10 at every `fpr_target` — the 5× envelope is statistically meaningful across the whole range, not just loose; (2) asserts on the false-positive COUNT (`observed ≤ expected×5 + 5`) rather than the rate, where the `+5` absolute cushion absorbs the modest, legitimate design-FPR overshoot from integer-`k` rounding at small expected counts (`P(X ≥ 5·E+5 | λ=10) ≈ 1e-20`, so it never trips on noise yet still catches an order-of-magnitude broken filter). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the previously-cached falsifying example `(892, 0.001)` now passes (16 FPs vs 55 allowed); ✅ re-ran the single test 5×/5 green and the full `test_bloom_invariants.py` file (13 tests) green; ✅ an exhaustive grid sweep over `capacity∈{200,300,500,700,892,1000} × fpr_target∈{1e-3,2e-3,5e-3,1e-2,2e-2,5e-2,0.1}` shows the worst-case observed/allowed ratio is 0.291 (≈3.4× headroom everywhere) — proving the bound holds across the full declared input space, not just the sampled examples; ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean on the changed test; 🚫 out of scope: any change to the Bloom filter, the orchestrator dedup tiers, or the O(1) bench gates (those are unaffected — this is purely the property test's statistical envelope). **Files:** `tests/property/test_bloom_invariants.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-BLOOM-FPR-SAMPLE-001. **Builds on** DEC-P0-057 (Rust popcount equivalence), DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-003 (#764, the full-suite verification baseline that surfaced this).

P-1 later-merged-renumbers)_ (2026-06-14, operator pasted the README; honesty audit — Golden Rule #1). **Why:** `README.md` is the operator entry doc (scanned by `no-dhan-guard.sh`) and carried three drifted facts: (1) "Range: Rolling `2021-01-01 → today`" — superseded by `2020-01-01` (DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001, the probe-verified Groww 1-minute depth; no `/logs` route) and `/credentials` was deleted (DEC-DASHBOARD-CREDS-ORPHAN-DELETE-001 #768), so both nav references were dead. **What shipped (docs only — read-only):** `README.md` range `2021-01-01` → `2020-01-01`; 786. **DEC-LIVE-LEG-FEED-TOKEN-FORMAT-001 — the live manifest's F&O leg rows must carry the NUMERIC instrument-master `exchange_token`, not the contract addressing STRING (resolve it from the full master by `groww_symbol` at manifest build; skip the leg honestly on a miss)** (2026-06-15, follow-up to DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 #780 / the spot-feed-token fix this builds on). **Why:** `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` `_leg_row` emitted `exchange_token = str(contract.contract_symbol)` — the `groww_symbol` STRING like `NSE-NIFTY-26Jun26-23000-CE`. Groww's `subscribe_ltp` requires a NUMERIC `exchange_token` `"as provided in instrument csv"` — `{"exchange":"NSE","segment":"FNO","exchange_token":"35241"}` (`docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md:54`; CLAUDE.md §6). Feeding the addressing string where a numeric token is required means every F&O leg subscription is malformed and the leg never ticks. The numeric token is NOT persisted anywhere on the leg path: `get_contracts` returns only `groww_symbol` strings (07-feed.md / 03-backtesting.md), and the lean instrument master discards the F&O legs (DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001) — so the token must be RESOLVED from the FULL master by `groww_symbol`. **What shipped (purely `brutex/dashboard/` + its tests — `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `live_manifest.py` `_leg_row(contract, feed_token)` now stamps `exchange_token = feed_token` (the numeric master token) + keeps `segment="FNO"` / `instrument_type=side` / `underlying_symbol`; (2) `build_leg_rows(registry_path, *, resolve_feed_token=_no_feed_token)` maps each `contract_symbol` → its numeric token via the injected resolver and SKIPS any leg the resolver returns `None` for (unknown / expired) — never invents a token (Golden Rule #1); the default `_no_feed_token` resolves nothing, so legs degrade to `[]` until a real resolver is wired; (3) `build_live_manifest` + `make_store_manifest_writer` thread `resolve_feed_token` through; (4) `make_master_feed_token_resolver()` returns a resolver backed by the FULL Groww instrument master's `by_groww_symbol` — it LAZILY loads the master CSV once (via `brutex.adapters.groww.instrument_loader.load_index` over the SSRF-guarded `urllib` getter; the network/CSV load is `# pragma: no cover`, mirroring the live CLI's `_real_instrument_resolver`) then maps `groww_symbol → str(security_id)` via the pure unit-tested `_index_feed_token`; (5) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` wires `make_store_manifest_writer(instrument_store, resolve_feed_token=make_master_feed_token_resolver())` so the ON toggle resolves real leg tokens, degrading to a skipped leg on a master miss. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `live_manifest.py` is 100.00% line+branch (the pure mapping + cache wiring covered with an injected fake index/loader — hit + miss; the network load is the only `# pragma`); ✅ a numeric-token leg manifest round-trips through `brutex.live.multiconn.read_subscription_manifest` (asserted in the TEST only); ✅ `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean, `mypy --strict brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` clean (only the known transitive `growwapi` import-untyped notes in the adapter modules, absent in CI); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — no `brutex.live` import in `brutex/dashboard/`; 🟡 the legs resolve only once the F&O `contracts` registry is pulled AND the master matches (else the leg is skipped, honest); 🟡 the real per-leg TICKS stay the 09:15-IST market gate (ADR-0009 Phase-0, UNVERIFIED — not claimed). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_manifest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-LEG-FEED-TOKEN-FORMAT-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-MANIFEST-FEED-FORMAT-001, DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 (#780), DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 (#779), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (#160, the lean master that discards the legs); market facts CLAUDE.md §6 / `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md:54`.

783. **DEC-STAGE3-CMA-BUMP-001 — deliberately bump the Stage-3 inner optimizer pin `cma` 3.4.0 → 4.4.4 (the conscious, decision-ID'd optimizer upgrade the DEC-STAGE3-OPTIMIZE-EXTRA-001 #626 version-lock test exists to force), superseding Dependabot PR #740** (2026-06-14, operator: "resolve the conflicts and merge all these PRs dude" — informed-choice via AskUserQuestion after the cma/actions Dependabot batch). **Why:** Dependabot PR #740 raised `cma` 3.4.0 → 4.4.4; its CI was RED on EXACTLY ONE check — `tests/unit/test_stage3_optimizer_dep.py::TestStage3OptimizerContract::test_exact_version_pin` (`assert '4.4.4' == '3.4.0'`) — with the other 7,276 tests GREEN, i.e. cma 4.x is API-compatible and the only blocker was the DELIBERATE reproducibility lock (ADR-0007 condition 9 / DEC-STAGE3-OPTIMIZE-EXTRA-001 #626): the pycma version is hashed into every Stage-3 refinement-run identity (`blake3(... ‖ pycma/numpy versions)`), so the pin must move only by a conscious decision PR, never a silent auto-bump. The operator chose to upgrade. **What shipped (pin + lock + spec, NO engine logic change):** (1) `pyproject.toml` `optimize` extra `cma==3.4.0` → `cma==4.4.4`; (2) `tests/unit/test_stage3_optimizer_dep.py` `_PINNED_VERSION` + docstring 3.4.0 → 4.4.4 (the lock now pins the NEW contract — it stays load-bearing, it did NOT get weakened/removed); (3) `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` inner-optimizer row 3.4.0 → 4.4.4. The Stage-3 refiner CODE (`stage3_refine.py` ask/tell loop, the identity-hash composition, the determinism contract) is UNCHANGED; the renovate.json `cma` carve-out stays `enabled:false` (auto-bumps still refused). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ verified REAL local run — `cma==4.4.4` installed, the 3 optimizer-contract tests pass (incl. the same-environment seed-determinism + seed-drives-trajectory tests, so 4.x reproducibility holds WITHIN an environment), and the full Stage-3 suite (118: optimizer-dep + stage3_refine + stage3_wire + sweep_verify) is green; ruff + ruff-format clean on the changed files; (4.4.4 emits the same benign matplotlib-missing UserWarning on import as 3.4.0 — plotting unused, no dep added); ✅ the version-lock test is RE-PINNED, not deleted — a future drift still fails loudly. 🟡 **One-time reproducibility reset (NOT hidden):** ADR-0007 condition 5 scopes determinism to same commit+lockfile+platform; bumping pycma INTENTIONALLY changes the optimizer-version identity field, so every PRE-EXISTING cached Stage-3 refinement-run identity is invalidated and post-bump Stage-3 winners may differ slightly from pre-bump runs — this is the accepted, operator-approved cost of the upgrade (no cross-version bit-identity was ever claimed). 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane change (CLAUDE.md §3 untouched); no Stage-3 algorithm change. **Files:** `pyproject.toml`, `tests/unit/test_stage3_optimizer_dep.py`, `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-STAGE3-CMA-BUMP-001. **Supersedes** Dependabot PR #740. **Builds on** DEC-STAGE3-OPTIMIZE-EXTRA-001 (#626, the pin + lock this consciously moves), ADR-0007 / DEC-STAGE3-DESIGN-LOCK-001 (the 9 conditions), DEC-STAGE3-RECOUNT-001 (#661).

790. **DEC-LIVE-AUTOROLL-001 — the live-tick JSONL capture sink becomes BOUNDED/ROLLING: it rotates into size/line-capped `seg-NNNNNN.jsonl` segments (no single GB file) and AUTO-FOLDS each completed segment into the live Parquet lake by REUSING the existing `write_live_ticks`/`write_live_candles` writers, then prunes the raw segment after a verified write** (2026-06-15, operator: "the live ticks should be rolling option … the size is gbs"). **Why:** the operator's live capture wrote every feed callback to ONE growing `runs/live-ticks.jsonl`, which reached GBs over a session. PR #746 (separate, in-flight) cut the per-callback BULK by writing a DELTA (only changed instruments). This is the SECOND layer the operator asked for — a hard bound on the single-file size so no JSONL ever grows unbounded, plus the durable handoff of the raw segments into the queryable lake. The existing `brutex.live lake` command already folds a JSONL→Parquet manually (REUSED here, not duplicated — Golden Rule #11 COMMON); this PR makes the fold INCREMENTAL + automatic as segments rotate. **What shipped (purely `brutex/live/` + its tests — REFERENCE/RESEARCH only, read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757):** (1) NEW `brutex/live/rolling.py` — `RollingTickStore` (a drop-in for `TickStore` from `TickCapture`'s point of view: same `next_seq`/`append`/`close`/context-manager surface) rotates to a fresh segment file when the active segment crosses `max_bytes` (default 64 MiB) OR `max_lines` (default 1,000,000), whichever trips first; the threshold is checked BEFORE the write so a segment overshoots by at most one in-flight line, and an EMPTY active segment is never rotated (a single oversized record still lands rather than looping). The **`seq` is GLOBAL + monotonic ACROSS segments** — a new segment continues from the prior segment's `next_seq`, so the whole rotation set is gap-free + strictly increasing exactly like a single store. On resume the global next-seq is reconstructed as **`max(every on-disk record's stored GLOBAL seq) + 1`** (each line persists its own global seq, so this is exact regardless of how many priors were pruned) **OR a durable `.next-seq` watermark sidecar, whichever is higher**. **The watermark is the CRITICAL resume fix** — a 4-agent hostile review of THIS PR caught the original count-based reconstruction as a data-loss BLOCK: the production wiring folds THEN **PRUNES** each rotated segment, so summing the on-disk record *counts* of the segments that REMAIN under-counts the pruned ones and RESETS the seq, re-emitting seqs already in the lake, which the lake PK `(capture_run_id, seq, instrument_key)` then silently DROPS (post-crash tick loss, violating Golden Rule #7 + the operator's "save ALL ticks"). The watermark is written atomically (`tmp`+`replace`) on EVERY rotation (the new segment's start seq, BEFORE the prior can be pruned) AND on the final `flush_active`, so it is the durable floor that survives pruning — covering a crash right after a rotation whose prior was already pruned (empty active + no on-disk records → seed from the watermark) and a `--resume` onto a fully-pruned clean-shutdown directory. (2) `fold_segment(...)` folds ONE rotated segment via the existing `write_live_ticks`/`write_live_candles` + `minute_tick_counts`/`build_minute_candles`/`iter_ticks` (REUSED verbatim), then **verified-before-delete** prunes it: the raw file is removed ONLY after every seq it contributed is confirmed present in the lake's `live_ticks` table (a re-read); an empty/zero-record/no-priceable-leaf segment that wrote nothing is NOT pruned unless it had nothing to lose (the empty-seqs vacuous case). (3) `make_fold_on_rotate(...)` wires (2) as the `on_rotate` hook so each rotation incrementally folds+prunes, bounding BOTH the raw JSONL footprint AND keeping the lake current; with NO lake root wired the store instead keeps a bounded RING of at most `max_segments` raw segments (oldest pruned on rotation — the operator's "bounded disk over full raw retention" choice). (4) `brutex/live/__main__.py` — the `capture` command gains `--roll` / `--roll-max-bytes` / `--roll-max-lines` / `--roll-max-segments` / `--roll-lake-root` / `--run-id`; a NEW `roll-fold` command folds-then-prunes every leftover segment in a rolling-capture directory (the crash-recovery / catch-up path), with `--keep` to fold without pruning. The end-of-session ACTIVE tail is flushed + folded via `flush_active()`. (5) `brutex/live/store.py` — a NEW `TickSink` Protocol names the append-only sink contract (`next_seq` + `append`) that BOTH `TickStore` and `RollingTickStore` satisfy structurally; `brutex/live/capture.py`'s `TickCapture.store` parameter is widened `TickStore` → `TickSink` (a pure type-annotation widening — the capture loop / its delta behaviour is UNCHANGED, PR #746's territory untouched). `TickStore` also gains an **in-process `bytes_written` counter** (seeded with the file size at `open` via ONE `stat`, advanced by the exact UTF-8 byte length of every appended line) so the rolling size-threshold check is **O(1) with NO `stat` syscall on the per-tick append path** — the hot-path lens of the 4-agent review flagged the prior per-append `stat()` as a constant-factor syscall tax (Golden Rule #5 ultra-fast discipline); this removes it. **Crash-safety + idempotence (Golden Rule #7):** rotation is the cheap, atomic act of CLOSING the active segment + OPENING the next — no rename, no merge, no partial-state window; a crash mid-`append` leaves a torn LAST line that `TickStore._repair_and_count` truncates on resume; a crash between fold and prune simply re-folds on resume (the lake PK `(capture_run_id, seq, instrument_key)` unions a re-fold to a byte-identical row set — proven by a golden re-fold-is-byte-identical test that diffs the Parquet bytes before/after a second fold). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/live/rolling.py` + the changed `__main__.py`/`store.py`/`capture.py` are **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (`pytest tests/unit/test_live_rolling.py tests/unit/test_live_cli.py … --cov=brutex.live.rolling --cov=brutex.live.store --cov=brutex.live.capture --cov=brutex.live.__main__ --cov-branch` → 567 stmts / 68 branch / 0 miss; the full `-k live` suite = 301 passed); ✅ tests cover rotation at the line AND byte threshold, seq continuity across segments + across a clean restart, fold-then-prune, re-fold idempotence (golden byte-equality), crash/torn-segment tolerance, the empty/zero-tick segment, the not-durable-keeps-raw branch, the bounded ring, the `roll-fold` orphan catch-up, AND the three resume-after-prune REGRESSION tests that lock the BLOCK fix (`test_resume_after_fold_prune_continues_global_seq_no_loss` asserts the resumed seq is exact + every tick survives the lake PK; `test_resume_empty_active_after_prune_uses_watermark` the empty-active crash edge; `test_resume_after_flush_active_prune_seeds_from_watermark` the fully-pruned clean-shutdown resume) + the watermark missing/corrupt-degrades-to-zero unit; ✅ `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; ✅ `mypy --strict` clean on the changed files (the only notes are the PRE-EXISTING transitive `growwapi` import-untyped sandbox artifacts in `_real_feed_builder` + the adapter `auth.py`, untouched here and absent in CI); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — `rolling.py` imports only `brutex.live.lake`/`brutex.live.store` + stdlib/structlog (no engine, no dashboard), and `brutex/dashboard/` imports nothing from `brutex.live`; 🟡 the REAL websocket/feed build + instrument-master network load stay the operator's-Mac-only `# pragma: no cover` boundary (`_real_feed_builder`/`_real_instrument_resolver`, unchanged); 🟡 the actual at-market TICKS remain the 09:15-IST gate (ADR-0009 Phase-0, UNVERIFIED — not claimed); 🚫 out of scope: PR #746's delta-write logic (assumed via the sink interface), any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change, and any dashboard wiring. **Files:** `brutex/live/rolling.py` (NEW), `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `brutex/live/store.py`, `brutex/live/capture.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_rolling.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-AUTOROLL-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756, the `write_live_*` writers REUSED), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the portable `brutex/live/` boundary), DEC-GROWW-LIVE-PARITY-001 (#753, the capture→fold loop), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the lake-write 2dp snap the candle fold inherits).

792. **DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001 — fix TWO confirmed live tick/candle materialisation bugs found by comparing `live_ticks`/`live_candles_1m` to the TickVault (Dhan/QuestDB) reference: (1) equity OHLC reads 0 instead of `ltp`; (2) the ~5s micro-batch fold OVERWRITES partial-minute candles instead of re-aggregating them to the full minute** (2026-06-15, operator: live candles WRONG — equity OHLC 0, 1-minute `tick_count`=1 not ~150+). **Bug 1 — equity price reads 0 (`brutex/live/tick.py`):** a Groww LTP-feed equity leaf carries the real price in `ltp` (e.g. `2396.7`) while its `value` field is `0.0` (that slot is the day's traded *value*, not a price); an INDEX leaf instead carries the price in `value` and has NO `ltp`. `PRICE_LEAF_KEYS` listed `"value"` FIRST, so `_leaf_price` returned `0.0` for EVERY equity (the confirmed "equity OHLC 0" bug). **Fix:** reorder so the last-traded-price keys come BEFORE `value` — `("ltp","last_price","last_traded_price","ltp_value","tp","value","index_value","price","close")` — so an equity picks its true `ltp` and an index leaf (no `ltp`) still falls through to `value` correctly. An un-traded equity with a legitimate `ltp:0.0` (no trade yet) still yields `0` — a real not-yet-traded price, NOT skipped (the `_coerce_price` non-negative guard already drops sign-flip glitches only). **Bug 2 — the ~5s fold overwrites partial-minute candles (`brutex/live/lake.py`):** the real-time fold (#750) writes a candle for EACH ~5s slice of a minute, then re-folds the same minute as more ticks arrive; `_merge_write`'s `frame.unique(subset=pk, keep="first")` is CORRECT for ticks (each `(capture_run_id, seq, instrument_key)` is a unique immutable observation) but WRONG for candles (PK `(instrument_key, timestamp)`): `keep="first"` DROPPED every later slice, so the lake's 1-minute candle reflected only ONE ~5s slice (`tick_count=1`, truncated OHLC). **Fix:** a candle-specific `_merge_candles` that REBUILDS each affected `(instrument_key, timestamp)` minute from the DEDUPED `live_ticks` lake — NOT a SUM-merge. The fold writes ticks FIRST (`fold_segment`), so by candle-write time the `live_ticks` PK has already collapsed every re-folded segment to one row per tick; rebuilding the minute via the SAME `build_minute_candles`/`iter_ticks` over that deduped set yields the full-minute bar (open=first tick, close=last, high=max, low=min, `tick_count`=the true full-minute deduped count). The affected minutes are dropped from the existing partition and replaced by the recompute (`keep="last"`), so a re-fold is a recompute over the SAME deduped ticks → byte-identical. **Idempotence under double-fold (the prompt's hard requirement, TESTED):** because the candle is REBUILT from the deduped tick lake rather than SUMMED across folds, a crash-replay that re-folds an already-folded segment reads the IDENTICAL tick set (the `live_ticks` seq PK dedups it) and rebuilds the IDENTICAL bar — `tick_count` does NOT double. Minutes with NO ticks in the lake (the pure-candle batch / older-test path that never wrote ticks) fall back to the candle as passed in. `write_live_candles` now calls `_merge_candles`; `write_live_ticks`/`_merge_write` are UNCHANGED. **Bug 3 / operator standard — the `live_ticks` `value` price column is now snapped to 2dp** (`round_money`, ROUND_HALF_UP) like the candle OHLC, so the lake shows `2396.70`, never raw vendor float-noise like `2396.7`/`14020.7999` — the Dhan/Groww/NSE 2-decimal convention (DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001); the EXACT raw value is preserved in `raw_json` for audit/re-parse, so nothing is lost. (`test_ticks_to_frame_price_2dp_snapped_and_recv_ns` asserts `22500.499 → 22500.50` + the raw in `raw_json`.) **What shipped (purely `brutex/live/` + its tests — REFERENCE/RESEARCH only, read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757):** `brutex/live/tick.py` (`PRICE_LEAF_KEYS` reorder + doc), `brutex/live/lake.py` (`_merge_candles` + `_rebuild_candles_from_ticks` + `_live_ticks_for_session` + `_ticks_from_lake_frame` + `_minute_counts_from_ticks`; `write_live_candles` repointed), `tests/unit/test_live_core.py` (equity-`ltp`/index-`value`/un-traded-`ltp:0` leaf cases for ticks AND candles), `tests/unit/test_live_lake.py` (multi-fold aggregates-to-full-minute == single-shot, double-fold idempotent no-double-count, rebuild-overrides-partial, no-tick-lake fallback, rebuild-keeps-only-affected). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/live/lake.py` + `brutex/live/tick.py` are **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (`pytest tests/unit/test_live_lake.py tests/unit/test_live_core.py tests/unit/test_live_rolling.py tests/unit/test_live_cli.py --cov=brutex.live.lake --cov=brutex.live.tick --cov-branch` → 264 stmts / 98 branch / 0 miss; the full `-k live` suite = 335 passed); ✅ tests cover the (a)/(b)/(c)/(d)/(e) worst cases from the brief — equity `{value:0,ltp:2396.7}` → 2396.7, index `{value:76435}` (no ltp) → 76435, multi-slice fold aggregates to the full minute and EQUALS a single-shot fold, double-fold is idempotent (no double `tick_count`), and the existing single-fold tests still pass; ✅ `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; ✅ `mypy --strict` clean on both changed modules; ✅ `pyright` 0 errors on both source + the two test files (the 2 `reportPrivateUsage` warnings on `_coerce_number`/`_leaf_price` PRE-EXIST at HEAD — they are the original test imports, not introduced here); ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — `lake.py` adds only a `brutex.live.candle_builder` import (already in `brutex/live/`), no engine/dashboard import. 🟡 the actual at-market TICKS remain the 09:15-IST gate (ADR-0009 Phase-0, UNVERIFIED — not claimed); 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change, the real websocket/feed build (`# pragma` boundary, untouched). **Files:** `brutex/live/tick.py`, `brutex/live/lake.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_core.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_lake.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001. **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-REALTIME-FOLD-001 (#750, the ~5s fold this corrects), DEC-LIVE-AUTOROLL-001 (#790, the segment fold path), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (#756, the `write_live_*` writers), DEC-LIVE-DELTA-CAPTURE-001 (the full-leaf `Quote` delta the equity `ltp` now reads), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the lake-write 2dp snap the rebuilt candle inherits).

794. **DEC-LIVE-EXCHANGE-TS-IST-001 — the live-tick lake gains a DERIVED `exchange_ts` column (the vendor's OWN exchange time, ms-precise) so the operator can read the precise IST `hh:mm:ss.mmm` of every captured tick** (2026-06-15, Track A of the live-pipeline TickVault-parity wave; LIVE-MATERIALISATION ONLY — read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757). **What:** `brutex/live/tick.py` adds `exchange_ts_from_vendor_ms(vendor_ts_ms) -> datetime | None` = `datetime.fromtimestamp(vendor_ts_ms/1000.0, tz=UTC)` (millisecond-precise — the `us` lake column preserves the `.mmm`; IST is the fixed UTC+05:30 display, CLAUDE.md §6, no DST), an additive nullable `LiveTick.exchange_ts` field (tz-aware-UTC validated in `__post_init__`), and a new `exchange_ts: pl.Datetime("us","UTC")` column in `brutex/live/lake.py` `TICK_SCHEMA` populated in `ticks_to_frame`.
