The untampered raw `vendor_ts_ms` (`tsInMillis`) AND OUR `recv_ns`/`recv_ts` are KEPT verbatim alongside — `exchange_ts` is purely ADDITIVE + DERIVED. **The fallback rule (skip-not-raise, mirrors `_coerce_price`):** `exchange_ts` is `None` (and the candle path falls back to `recv_ts` for that tick) when `vendor_ts_ms` is `None` OR implausible — **non-finite** (`nan`/`inf`; the upstream `_coerce_ms` does NOT reject these, so a bare `< floor`/`> ceiling` pair would let a `nan` reach `datetime.fromtimestamp` and RAISE — caught by a 4-agent hostile self-review as a CRITICAL and fixed with an explicit `math.isfinite` guard BEFORE push), negative, before `2015-01-01` (`_MIN_PLAUSIBLE_VENDOR_TS_MS`), or more than +1 day past "now" (`_FUTURE_VENDOR_TS_SLACK`). One bad tick is dropped, never raised — the whole fold never aborts. **Idempotence preserved:** `exchange_ts` is a pure deterministic function of the persisted `vendor_ts_ms`, and the future-slack guard only ever RELAXES the upper bound, so a fixed past timestamp accepted at capture is always accepted on rebuild — re-deriving on a re-read of the deduped tick lake yields the identical value (DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001 #792 rebuild stays byte-identical). **Files:** `brutex/live/tick.py` (`exchange_ts_from_vendor_ms`, `effective_clock`, `LiveTick.exchange_ts`, `iter_ticks` now built from `extract_quotes` so the vendor ts survives), `brutex/live/lake.py` (`TICK_SCHEMA` + `ticks_to_frame` + `_ticks_from_lake_frame` read-back), `tests/unit/test_live_core.py` + `tests/unit/test_live_lake.py` (100% line+branch on all three modules). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅REAL — derivation + ms precision + IST display + the full fallback ladder are implemented + tested; the per-second backtesting cap and the live leaf shape remain Phase-0 VERIFY-ON-RUN items (CLAUDE.md §6) — the raw snapshot is persisted verbatim so a wrong leaf guess is re-parseable offline.

795. **DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-BUCKET-IST-001 — live 1-minute candles now bucket by the EXCHANGE minute (`exchange_ts` truncated to the minute) instead of OUR receive minute, aligning live bars to exchange minute boundaries (09:15:00 IST = 03:45:00 UTC) so they are schema- AND semantics-identical to the backtest bars** (2026-06-15, Track A of the live-pipeline TickVault-parity wave; builds on #794; LIVE-MATERIALISATION ONLY, engine/52-vocab/scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why:** OUR `recv_ts` is a snapshot-cadence clock — a tick the exchange stamped at 09:15:58 IST can be RECEIVED by us in the 09:16 wall-clock minute (GC pause / ~1-per-sec snapshot lag), spilling a 09:15 trade into a phantom 09:16 bar. Bucketing by the vendor's own exchange time fixes the boundary so a 09:15:30-IST and a 09:15:59-IST tick land in the SAME 09:15 exchange minute even when `recv_ts` crosses a wall-clock minute. **The fallback rule:** per-tick, the bucketing clock is `exchange_ts` when present-and-plausible, else `recv_ts` (a single helper `brutex.live.tick.effective_clock(tick) -> datetime`, the ONE source of truth, Golden Rule #11 COMMON). **No-look-ahead clamp:** `effective_clock` returns `min(exchange_ts, recv_ts)` so a vendor `exchange_ts` skewed into OUR future (a clock glitch the +1-day plausibility slack still admits) is clamped to `recv_ts` and can NEVER push a tick into a minute we had not yet received (CLAUDE.md §4 look-ahead invariant) — flagged by the 4-agent hostile self-review as a LOW parity artifact and closed BEFORE push; the intended exchange-EARLIER-than-recv case is preserved (`min` keeps the earlier exchange instant). **Threaded through EVERY bucketing site so batch-fold, micro-batch-fold, and the lake rebuild AGREE minute-for-minute:** `candle_builder.build_minute_candles` (bucket + open/close ordering), `lake._minute_label`, `lake.minute_tick_counts` (the raw-record batch counter — switched from the timestamp-less `flatten_index_snapshot` to `extract_quotes` so it sees `tsInMillis`), `lake._minute_counts_from_ticks` (the rebuild counter, via `effective_clock`), and `lake._ticks_from_lake_frame` (reads `exchange_ts` back from the lake so the rebuild re-buckets by the SAME clock). **Idempotence preserved (the #792 contract):** the rebuild reads the deduped `live_ticks` (now carrying `exchange_ts`), re-folds with the same `effective_clock`, and the `affected` minute set (candle timestamps) is the exchange minute on both the write and the rebuild — so a double-fold of the same segment re-reads the identical deduped tick set and rebuilds the byte-identical bar (tick_count NOT doubled). A late-received-but-exchange-earlier tick correctly re-opens its exchange minute via the `affected` drop-and-replace. **Files:** `brutex/live/candle_builder.py`, `brutex/live/lake.py`, `brutex/live/tick.py` (`effective_clock`), `tests/unit/test_live_core.py` + `tests/unit/test_live_lake.py` (the 09:15:30/09:15:59-same-minute case, double-fold idempotence, multi-slice == single-shot, index-leaf-by-exchange vs no-ts-leaf-by-recv; 100% line+branch). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅REAL — exchange-minute bucketing + the per-tick fallback + idempotence are implemented + tested; 🟡PARTIAL — within a single minute that mixes exchange-clock and recv-clock ticks the open/close ordering interleaves two clocks (a schema-drift edge; in practice a feed-shape carries `tsInMillis` consistently per instrument, and the rebuild is still byte-identical because `exchange_ts` is persisted + re-read).
796. **DEC-LIVE-PREVDAY-OHLCV-001 — a prev-day OHLCV reference layer so the live dashboard can show each instrument's prior-session Open/High/Low/Close/Volume + prev-close (a TickVault/QuestDB-parity reference)** (2026-06-15, operator request for the live-pipeline TickVault-parity wave — Track D). **Why:** the live tape (`live_ticks` / `live_candles_1m`, DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001 #792) shows the CURRENT session; TickVault/QuestDB surfaces a prior-session OHLCV strip beside it (prev O/H/L/C/V + prev-close) and the operator asked BruteX to match. There was no artifact the dashboard could read for "the previous completed trading day's daily bar per instrument". **What shipped — a NEW module `brutex/live/prevday.py` (purely additive; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing from the dashboard, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757 — the dashboard later reads the Parquet artifact, never imports this module; read-only market data, NO vendor network, NO orders):** (1) a frozen `PrevDayOHLCV` dataclass (`instrument_key`, `session_date`, `open/high/low/close` as 2dp-snapped `Decimal`, `volume` int, `open_interest int|None`). (2) a PURE `load_prev_day(lake_root, instrument_keys, as_of_date, *, resolve_previous=True)` that resolves the previous COMPLETED trading day STRICTLY before `as_of_date` via `brutex.calendars.nse.is_trading_day` (`previous_trading_day` — walks back one calendar day at a time, skipping weekends + NSE/BSE holidays, so a Monday → prior Friday and a post-holiday session → past the holiday AND the weekend behind it), reads that session's `1day` bar per instrument from the HISTORICAL lake — `<lake_root>/bars/<exchange>/<segment>/<symbol>/1day/<yyyy>/<mm>.parquet` (FR-CAT-001; CLAUDE.md §6 / DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 — the `1day` candle is the VERIFY-FIRST default spot pull granularity) via the COMMON `brutex.data.partition.build_partition_path` (no path duplication) — and returns an O(1) dict keyed by `instrument_key`. The lake stores instrument identity in the PARTITION PATH (no `instrument_key` column), so a key here is the lake coordinate triple `"<EXCH>:<SEGMENT>:<SYMBOL>"` (e.g. `"NSE:INDEX:NSE-NIFTY"`), parsed by the COMMON `brutex.live.lake.split_instrument_key`. The reader reads ONLY the single targeted month-partition file per instrument (one `pl.read_parquet` + a bounded ≤~23-row filter — NOT a whole-lake glob), and the partition is built from the RESOLVED session date so a cross-month / cross-year prev day (e.g. as-of 2026-01-01 → 2025-12-31) reads the correct prior partition. The bar's trading day is its IST date (`_bar_ist_date`, `.astimezone(IST)` — mirrors `dashboard/db_view._bar_ist_date`, DEC-DB-CANDLE-DERIVED-001), so a session-instant or IST-midnight stamp resolves correctly. (3) a `write_prev_day(lake_root, rows, as_of_date)` that persists to `<lake_root>/live/prevday/dt=<as_of_date>.parquet` with a stable schema (`instrument_key Utf8`, `session_date Date`, `open/high/low/close Float64` 2dp, `volume Int64`, `open_interest Int64|null`, `prev_close Float64` = the prior session close, surfaced as its own column for a direct dashboard read) — idempotent overwrite-by-PK (dedup on `instrument_key` `keep="last"` + sort, written with the SAME reproducible Parquet options as the bars-lake `ParquetWriter` — `zstd`/`ZSTD_LEVEL`/`ROW_GROUP_SIZE`/`statistics=False` — so a rerun on the same inputs is byte-identical, Golden Rule #7). Plus a `read_prev_day` (the read half a downstream reader/dashboard uses) and `rows_to_frame`. **The 2dp rule (DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 / DEC-MONEY-2DP-001):** prices are snapped to the 2-decimal tick grid via `brutex.money.round_money` (ROUND_HALF_UP) at this write boundary, mirroring the spot lake; **volume + open_interest are NEVER rounded** (raw integer passthrough). **Graceful degrade (Golden Rule #1/#10):** a malformed key, an unknown coordinate (partition rejects → `PartitionError` caught), a missing partition, or a missing prior-day bar is OMITTED from the dict (debug-logged via structlog, never raised); an empty daily lake yields `{}` and a schema-correct EMPTY Parquet — the layer never invents data. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/live/prevday.py` is **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (`pytest tests/unit/test_live_prevday.py --cov=brutex.live.prevday --cov-branch` → 84 stmts / 16 branch / 0 miss, 21 passed); ✅ tests cover prev-trading-day resolution across a weekend AND a holiday (2026-01-27 → 2026-01-23, skipping Republic Day + the weekend) AND a cross-year boundary (2026-01-01 → 2025-12-31), a present instrument's 2dp-snapped OHLCV, a missing instrument / missing day omitted (not raised), a malformed key skipped, an unknown coordinate skipped, an empty lake → `{}` + empty schema-correct Parquet, idempotent rewrite (byte-identical on reversed-order rerun), `prev_close == close`, volume NOT rounded, FNO `open_interest` integer passthrough + non-FNO `null` passthrough, an IST-date-≠-UTC-date stamp, and the `resolve_previous=False` direct-date read; ✅ `ruff check brutex` + `ruff format --check` clean; ✅ `mypy --strict brutex/live/prevday.py` clean; ✅ `pyright` 0 errors on the module + its test; ✅ DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 holds — the module imports only `brutex.calendars.nse`, `brutex.data.errors`, `brutex.data.parquet_writer`, `brutex.data.partition`, `brutex.live.lake`, `brutex.money` (no `brutex.dashboard`, no `brutex.engine`/`strategies`/`vocabulary`). 🟡 the dashboard SURFACING of this artifact is a SEPARATE PR (a concurrent agent owns the dashboard); this PR ships only the module + writer + tests. 📋 a thin CLI hook was deliberately SKIPPED — `brutex/live/__main__.py` is owned by a concurrent agent and editing it is out of territory; downstream code calls `load_prev_day`/`write_prev_day` directly. 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change; the dashboard surfacing; a live websocket/feed. **Files:** `brutex/live/prevday.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_live_prevday.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-PREVDAY-OHLCV-001 (ledger #796). **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001 (#792, the live tape this references beside), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the read-Parquet-only dashboard boundary), DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#723, the `1day` default the prev-day bar reads), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 / DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the 2dp price snap), and the FR-CAT-001 partition layout (`brutex/data/partition.py`).

803. **DEC-LIVE-DASH-PROBE-001 — surface the live N-connection plan / probe + a per-instrument "ticks flowing" indicator on `/live`, and render the live-lake table timestamps as clean IST (drop the `+05:30` offset)** (2026-06-15, operator: the `/live` page should SHOW the connection plan + whether ticks are actually flowing, and the live tables read `2026-06-15T15:34:41.335741+05:30` — "it should be clean"). **Why:** two operator gaps on the Live page. (1) Visibility — the page already showed the per-connection subscription proof (DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 #762, the `--report` Markdown) but NOT the PLANNED N-connection count + cap + spot/leg summary from the manifest, no account-level connection-probe ceiling, and no honest answer to "are ticks FLOWING right now?"; worse, `/live` showed "TICKS CAPTURED 0" (a JSONL write-ahead-log line count, often 0 once folded) while `/db` showed tens of thousands of live-lake rows — the captured-vs-lake mismatch. (2) The live `live_ticks.recv_ts`/`.exchange_ts` + `live_candles_1m.timestamp` rendered the raw `isoformat()` with the `+05:30` offset suffix and microseconds, where `/db`'s spot candle viewer already had a clean-IST formatter wired ONLY to spot candles. **What shipped (purely `brutex/dashboard/*` + ONE manifest-writer field; read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing — the dashboard reads the Parquet lake + the manifest JSON ONLY, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757):** **Part 1 (surfacing, dashboard READER side):** (a) new `brutex/dashboard/live_plan_view.py` `read_connection_plan(manifest_path)` — parses the `{spot, legs, meta}` manifest the ON toggle wrote and re-derives the plan locally (`ceil((spot+legs)/cap)`, cap from `meta.plan.per_connection_cap`), surfaced via `GET /api/v1/live/plan`; it also passes through a `meta.probe` ceiling block IF present (a future `probe-connections` wiring stamps it) — honestly `None` + a note otherwise, never a fabricated ceiling (Golden Rule #1); the plan arithmetic is re-implemented locally so it never imports `brutex.live.plan`. (b) `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` `ticks_flowing(lake_root, *, now)` — reads ONLY the NEWEST `live/ticks/dt=*.parquet` partition (a BOUNDED, O(1)-in-history read, Golden Rule #5) for the max `recv_ts`/`exchange_ts` + tick count + last-tick age per instrument, surfaced via `GET /api/v1/live/ticks-flowing`; it reads the SAME lake the `/db` tables show, reconciling the "captured 0 vs tens-of-thousands of rows" mismatch; an absent/empty lake → `flowing=False` + an honest "no ticks yet" note. (c) the `/live` template gains a plan band (planned conn / cap / spot / legs / total / probe ceiling) + a "ticks flowing" panel (per-instrument freshness table) + a card, polling the two new routes. **Part 2 (clean IST, DISPLAY-ONLY):** new shared sibling `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` `format_clean_ist_millis(value)` (the millisecond-trimmed twin of the spot viewer's `_format_candle_timestamp`); `live_lake_view` routes the `recv_ts`/`exchange_ts`/`timestamp` columns through it so the live tables render `2026-06-15 15:34:41.335` (clean IST, no `+05:30`, ms-trimmed) — a null `exchange_ts` still renders its `recv_ts`; the underlying storage stays UTC `Datetime("us","UTC")` (CLAUDE.md §6 "stored UTC, displayed IST"); the spot candle viewer's existing clean formatting is UNCHANGED. **The ONE manifest-WRITER change (clearly the writer side, NOT the read side):** `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` `build_manifest` now stamps a `meta.plan` block (cap + spot/leg counts) so the read-side plan is always present; `read_subscription_manifest` (in `brutex/live/multiconn.py`) only reads `spot`/`legs` and IGNORES `meta`, so the capture subscribe path is unaffected and DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 still holds (the dashboard READ side imports nothing from `brutex.live`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ both new reader modules at 100.00% line+branch (real local run); ✅ ruff + ruff-format + mypy `--strict` (source) + pyright (source+tests, 0 errors) clean; ✅ empty-lake / stale-feed / no-legs / many-legs(2-conn) / null-`exchange_ts` / minute-boundary / clean-timestamp-format edges all tested (FastAPI TestClient + fake lake/manifest). 🟡 the `meta.probe` ceiling is surfaced when present but no probe-WRITING wiring ships here (the `probe-connections` CLI logs the ceiling; stamping it into the manifest is a named follow-up — until then the dashboard shows "probe not run" honestly). 🚫 out of scope: any engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change; a live websocket/feed; editing `brutex/live/` (a concurrent agent owns the live tick/lake/capture modules). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_plan_view.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/live_manifest.py` (the manifest-WRITER `build_manifest`), `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` (`format_clean_ist_millis`), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (two new read routes), `brutex/dashboard/templates/live.html`, `tests/unit/test_live_plan_view.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_manifest.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DASH-PROBE-001 (ledger #803). **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the read-Parquet/JSON-only dashboard boundary, STILL HELD), DEC-LIVE-DASHBOARD-WIRE-001 (#762, the per-connection proof this surfaces beside), DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 (#779, the `{spot, legs}` manifest contract), DEC-LIVE-EXCHANGE-TS-IST-001 (#756, the vendor `exchange_ts` the indicator + clean formatter read), and DEC-DB-CANDLE-DERIVED-001 (the spot viewer's `_format_candle_timestamp` this milli-second twin mirrors).
801a. **DEC-LIVE-RAM-RING-001 — an in-RAM ring buffer for the live-capture hot path so the per-tick callback is a zero-disk-latency O(1) append, with the bound enforced by spill-to-sink (never silent eviction)** (2026-06-15, Track B of the live-pipeline TickVault-parity wave; builds on DEC-LIVE-AUTOROLL-001 (the `.next-seq` watermark lineage) + DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001 (#792); LIVE-MATERIALISATION ONLY — engine/52-vocab/scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing from the dashboard, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757; read-only market data, NO vendor network, NO orders, NO socket-protocol change). **Why:** before this the Groww feed callback (`docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md`; CLAUDE.md §6, verified 2026-06-15 — the SDK invokes our callback on its OWN daemon thread) wrote ONE durable JSONL line per tick (`TickStore.append` + `flush()`) INSIDE the callback, so a slow write or a folding rotation could add latency to the feed's own thread. **What shipped — a NEW module `brutex/live/ring.py` (purely additive):** (1) a frozen `RingItem` dataclass holding the capture PAYLOAD only (the delta-pruned snapshot + OUR `recv_ts`/`recv_ns`) — deliberately NOT a `TickRecord`, because `seq` is the sink's to assign at flush time, so the ring never owns a sequence number and never races the sink's counter. (2) a `TickRing` bounded in-memory ring: O(1) `append` (one `collections.deque.append` under a short `threading.Lock`, the per-tick hot path — never touching disk), O(1) `drain_pending` (an atomic buffer SWAP under the lock — steal the deque, install a fresh empty one — so the caller writes the batch OUTSIDE the lock and a concurrent append never waits on disk), and a consistent `snapshot()` observer read. **The zero-loss bound (Golden Rule #7):** a `deque(maxlen=N)` would DROP the oldest un-flushed entry on overflow — a silent data-loss violation flagged by the 4-agent hostile review (durability + concurrency agents BOTH caught it) — so the ring never evicts; `append` instead RETURNS `True` at/over `capacity` so the owner (`RingFlusher`, #798) spills the overflow SYNCHRONOUSLY to the durable sink, degrading to the prior per-tick durability under sustained burst rather than dropping. **Thread-safety (honest envelope):** safety rests on CPython's per-method `deque` atomicity under the GIL for the primitives PLUS the single lock held only across the O(1) swap (released before any disk write); `seq` is assigned exclusively by the single-threaded drainer inside the sink, so there is no race on the sequence counter — argued from CPython semantics + corroborated by a NON-GATING real-thread stress test, not a deterministic concurrent test. **O(1) hot path (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5):** `tests/bench/test_live_ring_o1.py` proves `TickRing.append` latency at 1M-deep == 1K-deep occupancy under the `ratio_ceiling` (DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/live/ring.py` is **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (`pytest --cov=brutex.live.ring --cov-branch` → 83 stmts / 12 branch / 0 miss); ✅ ring append/drain/snapshot/capacity-validation + the spill-never-drop path + the property multiset-preservation + the ring-full stress + the crash-restart (un-flushed tail lost, sink resumes gap-free) are tested with fakes + injected clocks; ✅ ruff + ruff-format + bandit clean; ✅ pyright 0 errors on the module + its tests; ✅ mypy --strict clean on the module (the only mypy noise is the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub `unused-ignore` on UNTOUCHED `auth.py`/`live.py`/`__main__.py:111`, present identically on origin/main). 🟡 thread-safety is argued, not deterministically tested (the non-gating producer-thread check is evidence). 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / scope change; a live websocket/feed; the dashboard surfacing. **Files:** `brutex/live/ring.py` (new), `brutex/live/__init__.py` (export), `tests/unit/test_live_ring.py` (new), `tests/bench/test_live_ring_o1.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-RAM-RING-001 (ledger #801).

802. **DEC-LIVE-FLUSH-LOOP-001 — a periodic (~1s) + on-shutdown drain of the in-RAM ring to the EXISTING durable sink, wired cooperatively into the capture loop, with the honest durability bound stated** (2026-06-15, Track B of the live-pipeline TickVault-parity wave; the flush half of DEC-LIVE-RAM-RING-001 #801; LIVE-MATERIALISATION ONLY — engine/52-vocab/scope UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757 holds; read-only, NO orders, NO socket-protocol change). **What shipped — a `RingFlusher` in `brutex/live/ring.py` + the capture/CLI wiring:** (1) `RingFlusher` owns a `TickRing` (#797) + the EXISTING durable `TickSink` (`TickStore`/`RollingTickStore` — REUSED verbatim, the WAL writer + the Parquet fold are NOT duplicated, Golden Rule #11 COMMON): `capture(snapshot, recv_ts, recv_ns)` is the per-tick hot path (ring append + capacity-spill), `flush_due(now)` is the cooperative periodic drain (injected `flush_interval` + injected monotonic clock; below the deadline a no-op, at/after it drains the ring and advances the deadline by exactly one interval so a long pause does not burst a backlog), and `drain()` is the full shutdown flush. (2) `brutex/live/capture.py` `TickCapture` gains an optional injected `flusher`: when set, `_on_tick` buffers through `flusher.capture(...)` instead of the per-tick `store.append(...)`, and `run_for` calls `flush_due(now)` every poll (mirroring the existing heartbeat schedule — NO dedicated flush thread, so the whole drain is deterministic under the injected clock) and does a FULL `drain()` on loop exit (graceful-shutdown zero-loss); `on_record` is NOT fired on the ring path (there is no per-callback `TickRecord` — `seq` is the sink's at flush time). (3) `brutex/live/__main__.py` gains `--ring` / `--ring-capacity` (default 10,000) / `--flush-interval` (default 1.0) on the `capture` command (via `_add_ring_args` + `_make_flusher`), wired into BOTH the plain-`TickStore` and the `--roll` `RollingTickStore` branches; absent → the prior per-tick durable path is UNCHANGED (so `verify` and the default capture keep flush-every-line durability). **seq continuity + idempotence (preserved):** `seq` is assigned by the SINK at flush time in FIFO drain order, so the gap-free global sequence, the `.next-seq` watermark (DEC-LIVE-AUTOROLL-001), and the lake PK `(capture_run_id, seq, instrument_key)` idempotence are all unchanged — a resumed `TickStore`/`RollingTickStore` continues the global seq, tested across a simulated crash. **The honest durability bound (Golden Rule #10 — architecturally significant; chosen after a genuine 4-agent-style hostile review whose durability + concurrency agents both flagged the naive ring-as-primary + `deque(maxlen)` design as a SILENT-loss regression):** the ring is NOT an unconditional zero-loss layer — it is a hot-path latency buffer with three regimes: (a) **graceful shutdown → ZERO loss** (`run_for` fully drains before the caller closes the sink); (b) **capacity overflow → ZERO loss** (spilled synchronously to the durable sink, never dropped); (c) **hard crash (SIGKILL / power loss) → BOUNDED loss** — only the items still in RAM (drained no later than `flush_interval` ago, ≤ `capacity`) can be lost, a window of at most one flush interval of un-flushed ticks. This is a DELIBERATE, NAMED weakening of the prior flush-every-line guarantee on the `--ring` path; it is NOT claimed as unconditional "zero loss". **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/live/ring.py` + the changed `capture.py`/`__main__.py` are **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (`pytest --cov=brutex.live.ring --cov=brutex.live.store --cov=brutex.live.rolling --cov=brutex.live.capture --cov=brutex.live.__main__ --cov-branch` → 0 miss across all five); ✅ `flush_due` cadence / overflow-spill / shutdown-drain / seq-continuity-through-resumed-sink / crash-restart-gap-free / the `RollingTickStore` global-seq drain are tested with fakes + injected clocks; ✅ ruff + ruff-format + bandit clean; ✅ pyright 0 errors on source + tests; ✅ mypy --strict clean on the changed modules (the only noise is the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub `unused-ignore` on UNTOUCHED files). 🟡 thread-safety is argued from CPython semantics + a non-gating real-thread check, not a deterministic concurrent test. 🚫 out of scope: any engine / 52-vocab / scope change; a live websocket/feed; the dashboard surfacing; `fsync`-level durability (the live path uses `flush()`, a pre-existing page-cache exposure unchanged here). **Files:** `brutex/live/ring.py` (`RingFlusher`), `brutex/live/capture.py`, `brutex/live/__main__.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_ring.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-FLUSH-LOOP-001 (ledger #802).
799. **DEC-LIVE-TICK-FIELDS-PARITY-001 — the live-tick lake gains additive TickVault-parity vendor fields: an `avg_price` (the leaf's average/VWAP price, 2dp) and a `payload_hash` (a `blake3` fingerprint of the raw leaf for audit/dedup)** (2026-06-15, Track C of the live-pipeline TickVault-parity wave; LIVE-MATERIALISATION ONLY — read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757). **What shipped (purely additive):** `brutex/live/tick.py` adds (1) `AVG_PRICE_LEAF_KEYS = ("avgPrice","average_price","avg_price","vwap")` + a `_leaf_avg_price(mapping) -> Decimal | None` helper (mirrors `_leaf_price`'s skip-not-raise / non-negative discipline), (2) a `payload_hash(raw_leaf) -> str` = `blake3(json.dumps(raw_leaf, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), default=str))` — the repo's canonical hash (Golden Rule #4), hashing the IDENTICAL canonical bytes `brutex/live/lake.py` `ticks_to_frame` stores in the `raw_json` column so the digest faithfully fingerprints the PERSISTED record (order-independent dedup + drift-detectable audit), and (3) two new optional fields on the frozen `Quote` dataclass — `avg_price: Decimal | None = None` and `payload_hash: str | None = None` — stamped by `_leaf_quote`. `brutex/live/lake.py` `TICK_SCHEMA` gains `avg_price: pl.Float64()` (2dp money snap via `brutex.money.round_money`, ROUND_HALF_UP — DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001/DEC-MONEY-2DP-001; null-preserving so an absent avg is never a fabricated 0) and `payload_hash: pl.String()`, populated in `ticks_to_frame`. The existing columns + `_TICK_PK` (`capture_run_id, seq, instrument_key`) are UNTAMPERED; the new columns are NOT in the PK (per-leaf attributes, not identity), so `_merge_write` dedup is unchanged. **EVIDENCE, not assumption (Golden Rule #1 no-hallucination):** `avg_price` is the SAME observed-leaf-harvest pattern already shipped for `volume` / `open_interest` (parse-when-present, honest-`None`-when-absent) — `avgPrice` appears in the repo's own observed Groww equity-leaf fixture (`tests/unit/test_live_core.py` equity leaf: `avgPrice`, `bidQty`, `volume`, `ltp`, `tsInMillis`, `open/high/low/close`). It is **OBSERVED / Phase-0 VERIFY-ON-RUN**, NOT in the documented snapshot response tables — the official `get_ltp` leaf is `tsInMillis`+`ltp` and the index leaf is `tsInMillis`+`value` (CLAUDE.md §6; `docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md:105-110,180-185`), so every index leaf + a minimal LTP leaf carries NO avg field and yields `avg_price = null` (honest, never fabricated), and the raw snapshot is persisted verbatim (`raw_json` + `payload_hash`) so a renamed vendor avg field is re-parseable offline by extending `AVG_PRICE_LEAF_KEYS`. **Deliberately OMITTED — `last_qty` / last-traded-quantity (honest scope cut):** the documented Groww live SNAPSHOT streams (`get_ltp` / `get_index_value`) carry NO last-traded-quantity field (`docs/groww/api-reference/07-feed.md:105-110,180-185`); the `qty` / `filledQty` / `avgFillPrice` fields exist ONLY in the ORDER-UPDATE streams (`07-feed.md:394-407`), which BruteX does NOT capture (it captures `get_ltp` / `get_index_value` only). Inventing a `last_qty` from the snapshot would be a Golden Rule #1 fabrication, so it is left OUT — a flat numeric leaf likewise has no avg field and no raw mapping, so it yields `avg_price = null` AND `payload_hash = null` (the scalar value itself is the content). **Idempotence (Golden Rule #7):** `payload_hash` is a pure deterministic (`sort_keys`) function of the persisted raw leaf; `avg_price` is a pure function of the leaf — a re-fold re-reads the deduped tick lake and re-derives the identical values. **Files:** `brutex/live/tick.py`, `brutex/live/lake.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_core.py` + `tests/unit/test_live_lake.py` (100.00% line + 100.00% branch on `tick.py` + `lake.py`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅REAL — avg/VWAP harvest + 2dp money snap + null-when-absent + the blake3 payload hash (order-independent, drift-sensitive, raw_json-byte-consistent) are implemented + tested; 🟡 `avgPrice` presence on the LIVE `get_ltp` leaf is a Phase-0 VERIFY-ON-RUN item (observed in a fixture, not in the documented snapshot table) — the raw leaf is persisted verbatim so a wrong leaf guess is re-parseable offline; 🚫 out of scope: `last_qty` (no documented/observed snapshot field — honestly omitted), the dashboard surfacing (a concurrent agent owns the dashboard), any engine / 52-vocab / scope change. **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-TICK-FIELDS-PARITY-001 (ledger #799). **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-EXCHANGE-TS-IST-001 (#794, the additive-tick-column pattern), DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001 (#792, the deduped-tick-lake rebuild), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 / DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the money 2dp snap), and Golden Rule #4 (the `blake3` canonical hash).

800. **DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-DERIVED-PCT-001 — live 1-minute candles gain additive DERIVED percentage columns `pct_from_open` (intraday) and `pct_change` (vs the prior-session close), kept at FULL precision (NEVER 2dp — they are statistics, not money)** (2026-06-15, Track C of the live-pipeline TickVault-parity wave; LIVE-MATERIALISATION ONLY — read-only market data, no orders; the brute-force engine + 52-vocab + scope are UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3; `brutex/live/` stays imported-by-nothing, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757). **Why:** TickVault/QuestDB surfaces an intraday %-change strip beside the live tape; BruteX had only raw OHLC. **What shipped (purely additive):** `brutex/live/lake.py` `CANDLE_SCHEMA` gains `pct_from_open: pl.Float64()` = `(close - open) / open * 100` and `pct_change: pl.Float64()` = `(close - prev_close) / prev_close * 100`, computed at candle-build by two new helpers — `_pct(numerator, denominator) -> float | None` (the math, with the divide-by-zero guard) and `_derived_pcts(bar, prev_close) -> tuple[float|None, float|None]`. The math runs on EXACT `Decimal` rupees and is floated LAST (`float(numerator / denominator * 100)` — never float-then-divide), so the statistic keeps its full tail; **NEITHER percentage is ever passed through `round_money` / any 2dp snap** — DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 forbids rounding non-money (Sharpe/DSR/iv keep full precision; these percentages join them). The existing OHLC/volume/tick_count columns + `_CANDLE_PK` (`instrument_key, timestamp`) are UNTAMPERED; the new columns are NOT in the PK (derived, not identity). **prev_close source (reuse, not recompute — Golden Rule #11 COMMON):** `prev_close` is threaded in as an optional `prev_closes: Mapping[str, Decimal] | None` parameter on `candles_to_frame` (and `write_live_candles`), sourced by the caller from the existing `brutex/live/prevday.py` `load_prev_day(...).close` (merged #796, DEC-LIVE-PREVDAY-OHLCV-001) — this module does NOT recompute the prior day. `candle_builder.py` is OFF-LIMITS territory, so the prev-close threads through the lake layer at `candles_to_frame` time (the owned file), NOT through the candle builder. **Divide-by-zero + null discipline (Golden Rule #1/#10 — honest, no fabrication):** a 0-rupee `open` → `pct_from_open = null`; a missing prev_close (instrument absent from the `prev_closes` map, or a `None` map) OR a 0-rupee prev_close → `pct_change = null` — never a fabricated 0, never an `inf`/`nan`, never a divide-by-zero raise. `pct_from_open` is intraday so it is computed even when prev_close is absent. **Idempotence (Golden Rule #7):** `prev_closes` is threaded through BOTH the passed-in candle path AND the deduped-tick-lake REBUILD path (`write_live_candles` → `_merge_candles` → `_rebuild_candles_from_ticks` → `candles_to_frame`), so a double-fold of the same segment re-reads the identical deduped ticks, rebuilds the identical bar, and recomputes the identical percentages — byte-identical (verified by a double-fold read-back-equal test). The no-tick-lake fallback path writes the passed candle (already carrying its pcts) verbatim. **Files:** `brutex/live/lake.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_lake.py` (100.00% line + 100.00% branch on `lake.py`; `tick.py` unchanged by this entry but co-covered). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅REAL — both percentages, the exact-Decimal-then-float math, the full-precision (never-2dp) rule, the divide-by-zero + missing-prev-close null guards, and the rebuild-path idempotence are implemented + tested (including an explicit `pct != round(pct, 2)` full-precision assertion + both zero-denominator branches + the fallback-path pct assertion); 🟡 only `pct_from_open` + `pct_change` ship in this PR — any further intraday % (e.g. pct-from-prev-high) is a deliberate future add, not claimed here; 🚫 out of scope: the dashboard surfacing (a concurrent agent owns the dashboard), any engine / 52-vocab / scope change, any change to the off-limits `candle_builder.py` / `prevday.py`. **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-DERIVED-PCT-001 (ledger #800). **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-PREVDAY-OHLCV-001 (#796, the prev_close source it reuses), DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001 (#792, the rebuild it threads through), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757), and DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the money-only-2dp rule these full-precision statistics deliberately do NOT obey).
797. **DEC-DASHBOARD-INSTANT-LAUNCH-001 — the dashboard binds its port INSTANTLY: the (up-to-~90 s niftyindices-blocked) instrument autoload moves OFF the bind path into a background daemon thread, killing the cold-start `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` window** (2026-06-15, operator real-run: `make run` → banner + `universe.load.fno_index_unmatched` logged, then the browser sat on `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` at 127.0.0.1:9080). **Why:** `cmd_dashboard` ran the startup instrument autoload SYNCHRONOUSLY before `uvicorn.run` bound the port. That autoload calls `load_instrument_master` → `_ntm_admission`, which best-effort fetches the NIFTY-Total-Market constituents from niftyindices.com — a host that bot-blocks / slow-first-bytes non-browser clients, so `nse_constituents.fetch_constituent_csv` burns its full bounded budget (`_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES=3` × 30 s read-timeout + backoff ≈ 90 s) before degrading to the base set. For that entire ≈90 s the port was unbound and `cmd_run` had ALREADY opened the browser (it opens best-effort before the bind, cli.py docstring), so the operator saw a connection-refused screen and reasonably thought it was broken. **What shipped (purely `brutex/cli.py` + its test — NO engine / dashboard-app / instrument_loader / scope change, CLAUDE.md §3):** the inline autoload block in `cmd_dashboard` is extracted to two module-level seams — `_autoload_instrument_master(store, log)` (the exact same best-effort load + auto-heal + autopull-disabled logic, unchanged) and `_start_instrument_autoload(store, log)` (spawns a `daemon=True` `brutex-instrument-autoload` thread) — and `cmd_dashboard` now calls `_start_instrument_autoload(store, _log)` and proceeds straight to `build_app` + `uvicorn.run`, so the port binds in milliseconds. Concurrency is SAFE by construction: `InstrumentStore` already runs a read/write split (child read cursor + separate RLocks, DEC-STORE-READ-WRITE-SPLIT-001) with DuckDB MVCC giving route reads a consistent committed snapshot WHILE the loader thread writes — already covered by `test_store_concurrency` + `test_dashboard_responsive_under_write`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ verified — `test_dashboard_autoload_runs_off_the_bind_path` proves `uvicorn.run` is reached while the (threaded) autoload is still blocked (the bind no longer waits on the load); the existing `cmd_dashboard` tests stay green by stubbing `_start_instrument_autoload` to run the body synchronously + offline (`should_reload` stubbed, so the network `load_instrument_master` is never hit); 107 cli+dashboard+store-concurrency tests pass; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` clean on `brutex/cli.py`; the two new seams are `# pragma: no cover` (daemon-thread + live-network/server glue, mirroring the pre-existing `uvicorn.run` + autoload pragma) and the covered call site keeps the package-wide 100% gate intact. 🟡 the FIRST cold start still does the live niftyindices fetch in the background — the ~540 REFERENCE_ONLY NTM names appear once it lands (or instantly next launch from the `~/.brutex/cache/ntm_constituents.csv` cache); the dashboard + the core universe (indices + F&O stocks from the keyless Groww master) are usable IMMEDIATELY. 🚫 out of scope: the niftyindices fetch budget / cache behavior itself (unchanged), any engine / 52-vocab / data-plane change. **Files:** `brutex/cli.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_run.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-INSTANT-LAUNCH-001. **Builds on** DEC-STORE-READ-WRITE-SPLIT-001 (the concurrency-safe store this relies on), DEC-INDEX-PARSE-FIX-001 (the startup autoload), DEC-ONECLICK-RUN-001 (`make run`).

801b. **DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-CLEAN-001 — the auto-merge job that LOSES a concurrent merge-race reports SUCCESS, not a scary red ✗ (the PR still merged GREEN; a lost race is not a failure)** (2026-06-15, operator: "how come #753 merged without becoming green" — a red ✗ on a cleanly-merged PR). **Why (investigated from the real run):** PR #753 (DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-PRECISION-001) merged with EVERY required gate GREEN — `CI OK (aggregate gate)` ✅, `Unit tests + coverage (100% gate)` ✅, mypy/pyright ✅, benchmarks ✅, all 30+ jobs ✅ — confirmed in the run logs (the auto-merge job itself logged `Merging PR #753 (ci-ok is green)`). The ONE red ✗ was the `Auto-merge on green CI` helper job, which failed with `GraphQL: Merge already in progress (mergePullRequest)` → exit 1: a SECOND merge trigger (a later-push auto-merge run and/or the operator clicking Merge) won the race, so the loser's `gh pr merge` errored even though the PR had merged correctly. No gate was bypassed; the merged code is fully green. The defect was purely COSMETIC — a benign race surfaced as a red failure, which (rightly) alarmed the operator. **What shipped (CI governance only — `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`; NO code/engine/scope change):** the `Squash-merge + delete branch` step now wraps `gh pr merge` — on failure it inspects the PR state + stderr, and if the PR is already `MERGED` or the error matches the race signatures (`already in progress` / `already merged` / `already been merged` / `not mergeable`) it emits a `::notice::` and `exit 0` (the lost race is success); only a genuine non-race merge failure still `exit 1`s (red). The green-`ci-ok` + `mergeable_state` gates UPSTREAM are UNCHANGED — this never merges anything that wasn't already green (DEC-AUTOMERGE-CLEAN-STRICT-001 / DEC-AUTOMERGE-ALLGREEN-001 still bind); it only stops the duplicate-trigger loser from FALSELY reporting red. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ root cause proven from the #753 run logs (ci-ok green + `Merge already in progress` on the loser); ✅ the YAML parses + the merge-step bash passes `bash -n`; ✅ the merge SAFETY gates are untouched — a red/!clean PR still cannot merge; the change ONLY reclassifies an already-merged race-loser from failure→success; 🟡 GitHub Actions workflows are validated by the CI `actionlint` job (not unit-testable in pytest); 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane change, and the UPSTREAM stranded-PR race (that is DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-FIX-001's domain — this is its sibling for the OPPOSITE symptom: the loser, not the straggler). **Files:** `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-CLEAN-001. **Builds on** DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-FIX-001 (the stranded-PR race sibling), DEC-AUTOMERGE-CLEAN-STRICT-001 (the mergeable-state gate, unchanged), DEC-AUTOMERGE-ALLGREEN-001 (the ci-ok green gate, unchanged).

804. **DEC-LEDGER-DEDUP-801-001 — disambiguate the duplicate bare ledger #801: two PRs (DEC-LIVE-RAM-RING-001 / PR #758 and DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-CLEAN-001 / PR #761) each independently claimed a bare `801.` header in parallel and merged without suffix-disambiguation, so `scripts/ci/validate_ledger_numbering.py` failed on main (Rule 2: a (number,suffix) pair may appear at most once)** (2026-06-15, caught by a workspace-verification agent run after the live-parity wave merged). **What shipped (docs/MIGRATION.md ONLY — no code/engine/scope change, CLAUDE.md §3):** the two colliding headers are renumbered `801.` -> `801a.` (DEC-LIVE-RAM-RING-001) and `801.` -> `801b.` (DEC-AUTOMERGE-RACE-CLEAN-001) per the DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 disambiguation mechanism (letter suffixes; both keep entry number 801, each (801,suffix) pair now unique); existing #801 prose/docstring references remain valid (both are entry 801). No DEC-ID changes; the decisions themselves are untouched. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the validator passes after the suffix; purely a ledger-numbering repair, zero behavioural/code impact. **Files:** `docs/MIGRATION.md` (the two suffixes + this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LEDGER-DEDUP-801-001. **Builds on** DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 (the suffix-disambiguation gate this executes).
805. **DEC-LIVE-PROBE-MANIFEST-001 — wire the connection-probe result into the live subscription manifest so the dashboard's N-connection panel shows a REAL account concurrent-connection ceiling instead of "probe not run"** (2026-06-15, the named follow-up to DEC-LIVE-DASH-PROBE-001 #803, which surfaced `meta.probe.max_held` when present but shipped no probe-WRITING wiring — until now the `/live` panel always showed the honest "connection probe not run" placeholder because nothing stamped the ceiling). **Why:** the merged dashboard reader (`brutex/dashboard/live_plan_view.read_connection_plan`, surfaced via `GET /api/v1/live/plan`, PR #760) already CONSUMES `meta.probe = {"max_held": int, "failed_at": int|None, "reached_ceiling": bool}` and degrades honestly to `None` + a note when it is absent/malformed (Golden Rule #1); the `probe-connections` CLI already MEASURES that concurrent ceiling (`brutex/live/probe.ConnectionProbeResult.max_held`) but only LOGGED it. This closes the gap by stamping the measured ceiling into the manifest in the EXACT shape the reader expects, so the panel surfaces the account ceiling with ZERO dashboard-reader change. **What shipped (live/WRITER side only — read-only market data, NO orders, NO engine/52-vocab/scope change, CLAUDE.md §3; the dashboard imports NOTHING from `brutex.live`, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757 HELD):** (1) `brutex/live/multiconn.py` gains three pure/IO functions — `probe_meta_block(probe_result)` projects a `ConnectionProbeResult` to the reader's `{max_held, failed_at, reached_ceiling}` block (the `failure` reason string is deliberately NOT carried — the reader keys only on the int ceiling, and the human reason already lands in the `connection_probe` log line); `merge_probe_into_manifest(manifest, probe_result)` is a pure DEEP-MERGE that PRESERVES every existing block (`spot` / `legs` / `meta.plan` from #803) and sets only `meta.probe` (a malformed non-mapping `meta` is replaced by a fresh `meta` carrying only `probe`); `stamp_probe_manifest_file(manifest_path, probe_result)` reads the manifest, deep-merges, and rewrites it with canonical sort-stable JSON. **Honesty (Golden Rule #1):** a MISSING / unreadable / non-object manifest is LEFT UNTOUCHED and `False` returned (the dashboard keeps "probe not run") — never a fabricated/default ceiling; the stamp is invoked ONLY after a REAL probe ran. **Idempotence (Golden Rule #7):** the canonical `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` rewrite makes re-stamping the SAME probe byte-identical. (2) `brutex/live/__main__.py` `probe-connections` gains a `--manifest <path>` option; after the real ramp the CLI calls `stamp_probe_manifest_file` and logs `probe_manifest_result {stamped, max_held}`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/live/multiconn.py` + `brutex/live/__main__.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (Python 3.12 venv, `pytest --cov --cov-branch` → 0 miss on both); ✅ stamp-present / missing-manifest(untouched) / unreadable-JSON(untouched) / non-object(untouched) / OSError(untouched) / deep-merge-preserves-`meta.plan` / replaces-malformed-meta / replaces-existing-probe / byte-idempotent-rewrite / a round-trip proving the REAL `read_connection_plan` surfaces the stamped ceiling — all tested with fakes + injected `ConnectionProbeResult`s (no socket/network; the real opener stays `# pragma: no cover`); ✅ ruff + ruff-format + bandit clean; ✅ `mypy --strict` clean on the changed SOURCE (the 2 residual `mypy --strict brutex` notes — `stage3_refine.py` `cma` stub, `prevday.py:190` — are byte-identical to origin/main, pre-existing, NOT in this changeset); ✅ pyright 1.1.410 **0 errors** on changed source + tests (the `reportPrivateUsage` items are config-`"warning"`, pre-existing); ✅ ledger numbering validator OK. 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change; a live websocket/feed; editing the dashboard reader contract (UNCHANGED — the stamp matches its expected `meta.probe.max_held` shape exactly). **Files:** `brutex/live/multiconn.py` (the 3 new stamp/merge/project functions + exports), `brutex/live/__main__.py` (`--manifest` option + `_cmd_probe_connections` stamp call), `tests/unit/test_live_multiconn.py` (probe→manifest stamp/merge/honest-absence/idempotence/round-trip tests), `tests/unit/test_live_cli.py` (`--manifest` CLI stamp + missing-manifest tests), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-PROBE-MANIFEST-001 (ledger #805). **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DASH-PROBE-001 (#803, the reader that consumes `meta.probe`, UNCHANGED), DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the dashboard-imports-nothing-from-`brutex.live` boundary, STILL HELD — the stamp is on the live/WRITER side), DEC-LIVE-MULTICONN-MANIFEST-001 (#779, the `{spot, legs}` manifest contract this extends with `meta.probe`), and DEC-LEDGER-DEDUP-801-001 (#804, the immediately-preceding ledger entry).

806. **DEC-LIVE-DASH-MOVERS-PARITY-001 — the dashboard Movers panel gains a "Live" tab that surfaces the newly-merged live derived percentages (`pct_change` / `pct_from_open`) + the prev-day reference (`prev_close`), previously visible only in the `/db` browser** (2026-06-15, the dashboard-surfacing follow-up to DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-DERIVED-PCT-001 #800/#759 (the derived %s) and DEC-LIVE-PREVDAY-OHLCV-001 #796/#755 (the prev-day reference), both of which shipped the LAKE columns but explicitly deferred the dashboard surfacing to a concurrent agent — this is that surfacing). **Why:** the live 1-minute candle lake (`live/candles_1m`) now carries `pct_change` (vs the prior-session daily close) + `pct_from_open` (intraday), and the `live/prevday` lake carries the prior-session OHLCV + `prev_close` — but the operator could only see them by hand-browsing the raw `/db` tables. The Movers panel (top gainers/losers) is the natural home for a %-ranked view; the prev-day close is the natural reference column beside it. **What shipped (dashboard READ side only — read-only, NO orders, NO engine/52-vocab/scope change, CLAUDE.md §3; the dashboard imports NOTHING from `brutex.live` — it opens the Parquet lake DIRECTLY via DuckDB, DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757 HELD):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` gains `live_movers(lake_root, *, top_n=25)` — a BOUNDED, O(1)-in-history read that mirrors the merged `ticks_flowing` (#760): it reads ONLY the NEWEST `live/candles_1m` partition (via a generalised `_latest_partition(base)` helper the tick reader now also delegates to — Golden Rule #11 COMMON, no copy-paste), takes each instrument's LATEST minute candle (`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY instrument_key ORDER BY timestamp DESC)`), LEFT-JOINs the newest `live/prevday` partition for the AUTHORITATIVE prev-day reference `prev_close` (on the shared `instrument_key`, the flattened `<EXCH>:<SEGMENT>:<SYMBOL>` feed key both lakes write), and returns the top `top_n` gainers (desc) / losers (asc) by `pct_change`. Each row carries `{instrument_key, groww_symbol, timestamp (clean IST), close, pct_change, pct_from_open, volume, prev_close}` — the derived %s at FULL precision (NEVER 2dp — they are statistics, not money; DEC-MONEY-2DP-001). Plus `clamp_top_n` ([1,100]) + `MOVERS_EMPTY_NOTE`. **prev_close join-miss resilience (Golden Rule #1 — exact, never fabricated; the hostile-review CRITICAL fix):** the empty-reference CTE is `CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR/DOUBLE)`-typed so the no-prevday-partition LEFT JOIN is type-safe (an untyped `NULL AS instrument_key` is INTEGER and the `USING` join would 500 trying to coerce the VARCHAR candle key — a 4-agent hostile review caught this; fixed pre-push); and `prev_close` falls back via `COALESCE` to `close / NULLIF(1 + pct_change/100, 0)` — the EXACT prior daily close the candle's OWN `pct_change` was computed against (reconstruction to float precision, never an invented number), with the `NULLIF` guard degrading the impossible `pct_change == -100` to honest `None`. So the reference column is populated whenever the candle has a `pct_change`, even on a fresh session before the prev-day backfill (a routine real state), and honestly `None` only when neither source is derivable. **Honesty (Golden Rule #1/#10):** an absent/empty candle lake → empty gainers/losers + the honest note, NEVER fabricated movers; an instrument with a NULL `pct_change` (no prior close) is counted in `total_instruments` but EXCLUDED from the ranked lists (it cannot be ranked honestly). The DuckDB read uses a fixed lake-schema column list + BOUND-parameter Parquet paths (no glob/SQL-injection surface; the `# nosec B608` markers carry the static-SQL/bound-path justification). No side-effecting calls inside `assert` (the #758 CodeQL lesson — every query result is hoisted to a variable first). (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` gains `GET /api/v1/live/movers?top_n=` (Query-bound [1,100]) mirroring the `ticks-flowing` route — thin wrapper over `live_movers`, honest empty payload when no store is wired. (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` gains a "💧 Live" tab beside Spot/Futures/Options: it fetches `/api/v1/live/movers`, renders Symbol · Close · Prev Close · Change % · From Open % · Volume · Last (IST) with click-to-sort, formats the RAW numeric live cells (the historical tabs already arrive pre-formatted), hides the historical-only date/interval/time/exchange/expiry controls in Live mode, and degrades to a clearly-labelled PREVIEW sample layout when the backend is absent. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (Python 3.12 venv, `pytest --cov=brutex.dashboard.live_lake_view --cov-branch` → 0 miss; the new `/api/v1/live/movers` route lines in `app.py` are exercised by the dashboard route tests); ✅ empty-lake(honest-note) / present-data-ranked / prevday-join-present(authoritative) / prevday-partition-absent(reconstructed prev_close, route-level too) / total-wipeout(pct=-100 → null prev_close via NULLIF) / null-pct_change-excluded / top_n-clamp / newest-partition-only / latest-minute-per-instrument / route-without-store-empty / route-reads-the-lake / route-top_n-out-of-range-422 / movers-page-ships-Live-tab — all tested with fake lake fixtures seeded via `brutex.live.lake` + `brutex.live.prevday` (the TEST may seed via `brutex.live`; only the dashboard MODULE is decoupled) + FastAPI `TestClient`; ✅ ruff + ruff-format clean (bandit `# nosec` markers in place); ✅ `mypy --strict` clean on the changed SOURCE (`live_lake_view.py`); ✅ pyright 1.1.410 **0 errors** on changed source + tests (the `reportPrivateUsage` items are config-`"warning"`, pre-existing, matching the file's existing private-import convention); ✅ ledger numbering validator OK; ✅ **4-agent hostile self-review (correctness / invariants-security / template-UI / test-quality) → SHIP** after fixing the ONE CRITICAL it surfaced (the untyped-NULL empty-CTE no-prevday-partition 500, + the prev_close join-miss now reconstructed) and the MINOR notes (the `top_n=500` request hoisted out of its `assert` per #758; live money cells now render `₹` + Indian grouping for parity). 🟡 the existing 3 historical Movers tabs (Spot/Futures/Options) are UNCHANGED — this adds a 4th Live tab, it does NOT retrofit the live %s into the historical-lake snapshot (a different data source; forcing the two together would be a misfit). 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change; a live websocket/feed; the Reports panel (the prev-day reference fit MORE naturally beside the live %-ranked movers than in the pre-open-export Reports form, so BOTH datasets are surfaced together in ONE Live Movers tab — stated honestly per the task's "surface where it fits" instruction). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` (`live_movers` + `_query_movers` + `_mover_row` + `_latest_partition`/`_latest_candle_partition`/`_latest_prevday_partition` + `clamp_top_n` + `MOVERS_EMPTY_NOTE`), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (the `/api/v1/live/movers` route + import), `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` (the Live tab + fetch + render), `tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py` + `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py` (the view + route + page tests), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DASH-MOVERS-PARITY-001 (ledger #806). **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-DERIVED-PCT-001 (#800, the `pct_change`/`pct_from_open` columns it surfaces), DEC-LIVE-PREVDAY-OHLCV-001 (#796, the `prev_close` reference it joins), DEC-LIVE-DASH-PROBE-001 (#803, the `ticks_flowing` bounded-read + clean-IST pattern it mirrors), and DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the dashboard-imports-nothing-from-`brutex.live` boundary, STILL HELD — the Parquet lake is read directly via DuckDB).
808. **DEC-LIVE-DB-SCHEMA-WHEN-EMPTY-001 — show the live `live_ticks` / `live_candles_1m` COLUMN SCHEMA (names + types) on the `/db` + `/live` browser even when the live lake is EMPTY (0 rows / no partitions), so the operator can verify the merged columns exist** (2026-06-15, operator-hit gap: the live-lake browser rendered "0 cols · 0 rows" when no ticks were captured yet — market closed / feed off — which HID the column DEFINITIONS, so there was no way to confirm the newly-merged columns (`exchange_ts` / `avg_price` / `payload_hash` on ticks; `pct_change` / `pct_from_open` on candles) had actually landed). **Why:** the reader (`brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view`) derived columns from the Parquet `cursor.description`, which is empty when no partition file exists, so the no-partition branch short-circuited to `columns: []`. **What shipped (read-only dashboard surface — NO orders, NO engine/52-vocab/scope change, CLAUDE.md §3; DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 #757 HELD — the dashboard runtime still imports NOTHING from `brutex.live`):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` gains a DECOUPLED canonical `_CANONICAL_SCHEMA` (an ordered `(name, DuckDB-type)` mirror of `brutex.live.lake.TICK_SCHEMA` / `CANDLE_SCHEMA` — `VARCHAR` / `BIGINT` / `DOUBLE` / `DATE` / `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`), plus public `live_table_schema(table)` (→ `[{name,type}]`) and `schema_only_page(table, columns=…, limit, offset)` helpers; the no-partition branches of `live_table` / `query_live_table` / `live_columns` now return the canonical column DEFINITIONS + a `schema` block + an honest `note` "schema only — no data yet (market closed / feed off)" + 0 rows (NEVER a fabricated row — Golden Rule #1). With data present the behaviour is UNCHANGED (columns derived from the REAL Parquet, so a future schema migration shows through verbatim). (2) The `/api/v1/live/{table,columns,query}` + `/api/v1/db/live/*` routes' `lake is None` branches likewise surface the schema (an unknown table / projected column → 400, matching the with-lake path). (3) `db.html` + `live.html` `gridAndPager` render the column header + the note when 0 rows but columns are present, so the grid visibly shows the columns. **Decoupling held + drift-guarded:** the dashboard never imports `brutex.live`; instead the canonical constant is duplicated in the dashboard layer and a drift-guard test (`tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py::test_canonical_schema_matches_real_lake_schema`) builds an empty Parquet FROM the real `brutex.live.lake` schema, reads its DuckDB description, and asserts byte-equality with `_CANONICAL_SCHEMA` — so any add/rename/retype/reorder of a live-table column fails CI (the test MAY import `brutex.live`; tests are not the dashboard runtime). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (Python 3.12 venv, `pytest tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py --cov --cov-branch` → 154 stmts / 34 branch, 0 miss); ✅ the new `app.py` `lake is None` schema branches are 100% covered by the live route tests (no new uncovered lines in `app.py`); ✅ empty-lake → schema columns + note returned / populated → real columns unchanged / projection honoured + validated on the empty path / unknown-table + unknown-column → 400 / the drift-guard — all tested via FastAPI `TestClient` + fake empty/seeded lakes (the seed uses `brutex.live.lake`, the reader never does); ✅ ruff + ruff-format + bandit clean (no print / no bare except / deps injected); ✅ `mypy --strict brutex` clean on the changed SOURCE (`live_lake_view.py` + `dashboard/app.py` 0 errors — the 6 residual `mypy --strict brutex` errors are all in `growwapi`-stub files `adapters/groww/{auth,live}.py` + `live/__main__.py`, a pre-existing venv artifact NOT in this changeset); ✅ pyright 1.1.410 **0 errors** on changed source + tests (the `reportPrivateUsage` items are config-`"warning"`, the established pattern); ✅ ledger numbering validator OK (#808 unique; #806/#807 reserved by concurrent PRs). 🚫 out of scope: any brute-force engine / 52-vocab / data-plane / scope change; a live websocket/feed; fabricating rows; changing the populated-path payload shape. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` (`_CANONICAL_SCHEMA` + `live_table_schema` + `schema_only_page` + the three no-partition branches), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (the six `lake is None` route branches), `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html` + `templates/live.html` (`gridAndPager` schema header + note), `tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py` (schema-when-empty + projection + drift-guard tests), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_live.py` + `tests/unit/test_dashboard_live.py` (no-store schema-only route tests), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-DB-SCHEMA-WHEN-EMPTY-001 (ledger #808). **Builds on** DEC-LIVE-DECOUPLE-001 (#757, the dashboard-imports-nothing-from-`brutex.live` boundary, STILL HELD), DEC-LIVE-LAKE-SCHEMA-001 (the live-lake schema), DEC-LIVE-TICK-FIELDS-PARITY-001 + DEC-LIVE-CANDLE-DERIVED-PCT-001 (the merged columns this surfaces), DEC-DB-LIVE-TABLES-001 (the `/db` live-table routes), and DEC-LIVE-DASH-PROBE-001 (#803, the clean-IST live-table rendering this leaves untouched).

809. **DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-RATELIMIT-001 — a 429/timeout PRESERVES the genuine-EMPTY streak (only a SUCCESS resets it), so the full historical pull CONVERGES under a rate-limit storm instead of re-fetching pre-listing windows forever** (2026-06-15, operator: the full 779-symbol Groww pull "gets stuck / never finishes"). **Why:** the unified `WindowLedger` (DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001) settles a clean-EMPTY window to `SKIPPED` only after `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD=3` genuine empties in a row (the transient-empty guard, DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001). But `record()` RESET that streak to 0 on ANY non-EMPTY outcome — including a `FAILED` (429 / timeout). Hundreds of the 779 symbols listed in 2023-2024, so their 2020-2023 windows are genuinely EMPTY; under Groww's 429 throttling those windows kept getting rate-limited BETWEEN clean empties, so the streak never reached 3 → they were re-fetched on EVERY pull forever → the `pending` count never dropped and the pull never finished (the operator-observed "stuck", with `/coverage` showing a flood of `EMPTY 1/3` that never advanced). **What shipped (`brutex/data/window_ledger.py` — pure model, no engine/scope change):** `record()`'s streak transition is now per-outcome — EMPTY bumps, **SUCCESS resets to 0** (the window has data → not empty), **FAILED PRESERVES** (a rate-limit / timeout is NOT evidence the window has data, so it must not throw away the genuine-empty progress). The `_threshold` is UNCHANGED, so a real-data window is still never masked before 3 GENUINE empties — the pull-until-success contract holds: a window that errors (FAILED) or is EMPTY-below-threshold is NEVER skippable, so it re-fetches until it returns bars or is confirmed genuinely empty `_threshold` times. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ verified offline (pure model) — the exact operator scenario (`test_pull_converges_under_a_429_storm`: EMPTY, 429, EMPTY, 429, EMPTY → `SKIPPED`) now converges; `test_real_data_after_empties_is_never_masked` proves EMPTY×2 then bars → `SUCCESS` (never a premature skip); 1,154 groww / ledger / coverage / pull / ingest tests pass; ruff + mypy --strict clean. 🟡 a window that has data but Groww FALSELY returns clean-EMPTY 3× running would still settle (the irreducible cost of converging at all — retrying empties forever IS the stuck bug); the listing-date / earliest-success guard that would make even that impossible is a named follow-up. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope change. **Files:** `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-RATELIMIT-001. **Builds on** DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the unified ledger + R1 streak), DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the 3-empty threshold this hardens).

810. **DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001 — every historical `get_historical_candles` SDK call is bounded by a 45 s wall-clock deadline so a stalled connection can never FREEZE the pull** (2026-06-15, operator: the historical pull "freezes / hangs" with multi-minute zero-progress stretches). **Why:** `GrowwClient._call` retries a RETRYABLE error (429/timeout, `is_retryable`) up to `max_attempts=6`, but it can only react to a RAISED exception. The SDK call `self.sdk.get_historical_candles(...)` carried NO wall-clock bound, so a half-open socket / non-responding server would block the pull worker FOREVER — the retry loop never even runs (a hung call never raises), and the whole historical pull is frozen on that one window. **What shipped (`brutex/adapters/groww/client.py` + `constants.py` + `live.py`):** new `run_with_deadline(fn, seconds)` runs the SDK call in a daemon thread and, if it has not returned within the deadline, raises a `TimeoutError` carrying the `deadline exceeded` hint → `from_groww_exception` classifies it a retryable `GrowwTimeoutError` → the existing bounded retry loop re-issues it; a persistently-stalled window finally FAILS (and re-attempts next pull, never skippable) instead of hanging. `GrowwClient.call_timeout_seconds` (default `None` = unbounded for unit tests / dry-runs) is injected with the new `GROWW_PULL_CALL_TIMEOUT_S=45.0` at the SINGLE shared live build seam `build_live_client` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — both the CLI and dashboard pull paths flow through it). The abandoned worker is a daemon — it dies with the process, never blocks shutdown. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ verified offline — `test_stalled_call_times_out_instead_of_freezing` (a hanging fake SDK + a 0.05 s deadline) raises `GrowwTimeoutError` after the bounded retries instead of blocking; the fast-path + error-propagation paths are pinned; 1,154 tests pass; ruff + mypy --strict clean (the live build seam stays `# pragma: no cover` — real TOTP + network). 🟡 the abandoned daemon worker leaks until its socket dies at the OS level (bounded, harmless — never blocks the pull or shutdown); 45 s is generous for one ≤180-day daily window yet caps a dead socket to seconds, NOT a vendor-documented limit. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope change; the live websocket feed is untouched (this is the REST historical path). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_client.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001. **Builds on** DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the client's adaptive retry/limiter), DEC-GROWW-RATELIMIT-RETRY-001 (the retryable classification this reuses).

811. **DEC-SPOT-CROSS-SYMBOL-FANOUT-001 — the bulk spot pull fans ONE bounded pool ACROSS symbols (serial windows per symbol) instead of nesting a per-symbol window pool inside every outer worker, so the full 779-symbol pull saturates the rate bucket instead of crawling** (2026-06-15, operator: the full 779-symbol Groww 1-day pull "crawls / is stuck" — ~23 symbols in 19 min). **Why (measured, not assumed):** `run_groww_spot_ingest` mapped `_run_pair` over the (instrument×interval) jobs through the live rate-sized OUTER pool (`workers_to_saturate(8 r/s, 3 s)` = 24), but `_run_pair` did NOT forward that pool to `ingest_spot`, which then built its OWN per-symbol WINDOW pool from the `_pace_rps` fallback (`GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_UNVERIFIED=10.0` → `workers_to_saturate(10, 3)` = 30). So the live shape was outer 24 × inner 30 = up to **720 threads** — a thread explosion that only thrashed the GIL on the Parquet write render (a sub-agent micro-benchmark measured the lake WRITE path — polars `DataFrame`/`write_parquet` + per-bar `Decimal` reconstruction in `parquet_writer.py`, GIL-bound — as the true serializer: swapping a no-op sink in restored 25× concurrency; the ledger + per-partition lock were ruled out). Net: the achieved fetch concurrency collapsed far below the 8 r/s ceiling → the operator's hours-long crawl. **What shipped (`brutex/orchestrator/parallel.py` + `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py` — concurrency model only, no engine/scope change):** new `SerialRunParallel` (the in-thread twin of `PoolRunParallel`, same exception-capture contract, zero worker threads). `run_groww_spot_ingest` now hands a MULTI-pair (bulk) pull a `SerialRunParallel` as the per-symbol window runner, so concurrency comes ENTIRELY from the ONE bounded outer pool fanned ACROSS symbols (one in-flight call per symbol, 24 symbols concurrent) — no nested pool, ≤ 24 threads. A SINGLE-pair pull (the /universe per-symbol button or the CLI) still hands its one pair the full outer pool for its WINDOWS, so single-symbol window parallelism is preserved. The shared rate token bucket stays the sole issue governor — **no ceiling is raised** (Rule #6). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ verified offline — a probe over the REAL `run_groww_spot_ingest` (48 symbols × 14 windows, fake adapter) measured **effective concurrency 23.0×, max 24 concurrent fetches, 24 distinct worker threads** (down from the 720-thread nest); `brutex/orchestrator/parallel.py` + `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py` at 100% line+branch; 263 parallel / run_ingest / ingest / pull-controller / universe-phase tests pass. 🟡 ASSUMED (cannot measure offline — no live token): the exact production speedup; with real ~3 s Groww latency, 24 in-flight ÷ 3 s = ~8 r/s = the bucket ceiling, so the full 1-day pull is bucket-bound (~20–40 min) instead of effectively serial (~16 h). 🟡 the GIL-bound Parquet write ceiling (~257 writes/s, measured) sits far above the 8 r/s fetch bucket, so writes do not bottleneck a real latency-bound pull; moving the parquet render off the GIL (Rust/pyarrow) is a named future follow-up, out of scope here. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope change. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/parallel.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_parallel.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SPOT-CROSS-SYMBOL-FANOUT-001. **Builds on** DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the shared-bucket fan-out + Little's-law pool sizing), DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-8RPS-001 (`workers_to_saturate`), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001 (the 8 r/s ceiling this saturates).

812. **DEC-SPOT-POOL-WIDTH-15S-001 — size the SPOT fan-out pool for Groww's REAL ~15 s/call latency (a wider, env-tunable budget + 96 concurrent-socket cap) so the 8 r/s bucket — not the pool — is the binding gate; measured 3.07× over the prior 24-wide pool** (2026-06-15, operator: after #811 merged + the operator restarted on fresh code, the pull STILL crawled at ~1.6 windows/s, 24/779, zero 429s). **Why (MEASURED — corrects #811's "~3 s latency" ASSUMPTION):** #811 fixed the 720-thread nest and made bulk concurrency = the OUTER pool width across symbols. But that pool is sized `workers_to_saturate(8 r/s, DEFAULT_LATENCY_BUDGET_S=3 s) = 24`, provisioned for the ~3 s expiry/contract call. A faithful offline reproduction (the REAL `run_groww_spot_ingest` + REAL `ParquetBarSink`/`ParquetWriter` + REAL `RateController(8 r/s)` + REAL 24-wide pool, only the network swapped for a latency-controlled fake) proved Groww's `get_historical_candles` actually serves **~15 s/call**: at a 15 s latency a 24-wide pool achieves exactly `24/15 ≈ 1.57` windows/s (reproducing the operator's 1.6), with `max_in_flight = 24` and **eff_concurrency 23.6/24** — i.e. the pool is FULLY saturated yet Little's-law-capped (rate = workers/latency = 24/15), never reaching the 8 r/s bucket (hence zero 429s). The GIL-bound write was quantified and RULED OUT as the primary cause (~42–49 writes/s single-thread, ~18% concurrency tax at 3 s, negligible at 15 s; a dedicated-writer-thread prototype gave ≈0 gain). So the bottleneck is purely **pool width vs real latency**, NOT rate, NOT the GIL, NOT #811. **What shipped (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — sizing seam only, no engine/scope change):** `_spot_run_parallel` now sizes from a SPOT-specific Little's-law budget `_SPOT_LATENCY_BUDGET_DEFAULT_S=15.0` (env `BRUTEX_SPOT_LATENCY_BUDGET_S`) and a wider cap `_SPOT_FANOUT_CAP_DEFAULT=96` (env `BRUTEX_SPOT_FANOUT_CAP`) — `workers_to_saturate(8, 15, cap=96) = 96` in-flight at the ceiling — instead of the global 3 s/24. New `_env_positive` reader makes both operator-tunable with a hardened fallback (a malformed / ≤0 value can never zero-size or crash the pool). The global `DEFAULT_LATENCY_BUDGET_S=3.0` is UNTOUCHED (correct for the ~2.9 s expiry/contract pulls). **Rate safety (Rule #6):** the per-second issue rate is UNCHANGED — the shared token bucket still caps the AGGREGATE at 8 r/s; a wider pool only fills idle latency, it never raises the rate. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ MEASURED — pool 24→96 lifted the real spine from 1.95→5.98 windows/s at a 12 s latency (3.07×), the 8 r/s bucket becoming the binding gate; `pull_controller.py` at 100% line+branch (198 tests); the spine correctly hits ~8 r/s at ≤3 s latency. 🟡 ASSUMED: Groww's true per-call latency ≈15 s is back-derived (24÷1.6) + reproduced, not measured against the live API (no token); if the real value differs the env knobs retune without a redeploy. 🟡 UNKNOWN: whether ~96 concurrent sockets trips an undocumented Groww connection limit — the env cap can be dialled DOWN and the adaptive 429 ladder + retries absorb a rejection. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-ceiling change. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_pool_sizing.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SPOT-POOL-WIDTH-15S-001. **Builds on / corrects** DEC-SPOT-CROSS-SYMBOL-FANOUT-001 (#811 — same pull, the pool-width half its 3 s assumption missed), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001, DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-8RPS-001 (`workers_to_saturate`'s `cap` param), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001.

813. **DEC-SPOT-POOL-UNIFORM-001 — REVERT #812's spot-only 96-wide pool: the ONE shared GrowwAPI SDK hangs at ~96 concurrent connections, so the spot/historical pull now uses the SAME modest pool as every other Groww pull (expiries/contracts)** (2026-06-15, operator: after #812 merged + restart, the pull HUNG — 8 min, 0/779, 0 bars, 0 events, no errors). **Why (this is #812's own flagged 🟡 UNKNOWN coming true):** #812 widened ONLY the spot pool to 96 in-flight, on the offline-measured assumption that more concurrency = faster. It explicitly flagged as UNKNOWN "whether ~96 concurrent sockets trips an undocumented Groww connection limit." It did. Evidence: the live log shows `universe.pull_all.start` then **zero** worker events for 8 minutes — not a network timeout (#766's 45 s deadline would have logged one), not `pace()` (re-verified: it correctly throttles 96 threads to 8 r/s, no deadlock), but the **shared `GrowwAPI` SDK** (`GrowwClient.sdk`, built once in `build_live_client`, shared across ALL worker threads) blocking at ~96 simultaneous connections. The decisive cross-check the operator pointed out: the **expiry + contract pulls go through the SAME SDK and never hang** — because they use the default `PoolRunParallel()` = **8 workers** (`metadata_pull.py`); #811's spot pool was 24 (worked, crawled); ONLY #812's 96 exceeded what the shared SDK tolerates. The backtesting docs (`docs/groww/api-reference/03-backtesting.md`, re-read) document NO special limit for `get_historical_candles` vs expiries/contracts — so there is no reason historical should be special-cased. **What shipped (full revert of #812's sizing seam + per-call measurement):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — `_spot_run_parallel` now returns the IDENTICAL default `PoolRunParallel()` (`DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS`=8) the expiry/contract pulls use against the SAME shared SDK — no rate-based widening, no spot-special 15 s budget, no 96 cap, no env knobs; `_env_positive` + the `_SPOT_*` constants + `import os` + the `workers_to_saturate`/`DEFAULT_LATENCY_BUDGET_S` imports removed. Historical now behaves byte-for-byte like the pulls that have always worked. (2) `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py` — **per-call latency logging (DEC-GROWW-CALL-LATENCY-LOG-001):** every successful Groww REST call (`historical_candles` / `get_expiries` / `get_contracts`) logs `groww.call` at INFO with `method` + `attempt` + `elapsed_ms` (injectable `clock` for deterministic tests), so the operator SEES the REAL per-call response time live in `/logs` — the measurement that ends the "is it 15 s or stuck?" guessing. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the hang is removed (spot = the proven-safe 8-worker default expiries/contracts use); per-call latency is now measured, not assumed; `pull_controller.py` + `client.py` 100% line+branch (208 tests); ruff clean. 🟡 this restores RELIABILITY first — the pull works but is throughput-limited by what the shared SDK safely allows; the REAL latency is now what the next live run will print (no more back-derivation). 🟡 UNKNOWN (to be resolved from the NEW `groww.call` logs on the operator's next run, NOT guessed): the true per-call latency + the SDK's safe concurrency. 📋 ROADMAP: read the `groww.call` latency from a live run; then, if the shared SDK serializes, a **per-thread Groww client** (each worker its own connection) for true safe parallelism. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-ceiling change. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_pool_sizing.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_client.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision IDs:** DEC-SPOT-POOL-UNIFORM-001 + DEC-GROWW-CALL-LATENCY-LOG-001. **Reverts** DEC-SPOT-POOL-WIDTH-15S-001 (#812). **Builds on** DEC-SPOT-CROSS-SYMBOL-FANOUT-001 (#811), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001, DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001.

814. **DEC-INSTRUMENT-SKIP-NO-GSYM-001 — one malformed/stale row in the Groww instrument master can no longer abort the whole load: the parser isolates+skips ANY un-parseable in-scope row (counted + logged) and loads every valid row, so "Load instruments" never returns the empty-universe HTTP 502 again** (2026-06-16, operator: clicking "Load instruments" returned HTTP 502 and the app started with 0 instruments). **Why (Verified against the operator's real master CSV):** the dashboard route `api_universe_load_instruments` (`brutex/dashboard/app.py`) catches `(InstrumentFormatError, OSError)` → 502. `parse_instrument_csv` parsed each in-scope row but let the FIRST row-level failure propagate, aborting the entire ~162k-row parse. Analysis of the operator's actual `instrument.csv` (162,256 rows, 111,700 in-scope) found EXACTLY ONE offending in-scope row — `"BSE FOCUSED IT"` (BSE / `IDX` / `CASH`, `exchange_token` 93) with a **BLANK `groww_symbol` + blank `trading_symbol`** — which is genuinely un-pullable (every Groww `get_historical_candles` / `get_expiries` / `get_contracts` call keys on the `groww_symbol`; per the instrument-master schema `docs/groww/api-reference/02-instruments.md:119` `groww_symbol` IS the vendor identity key).
