That single junk vendor row → `InstrumentFormatError("row missing groww_symbol")` → 502 → empty universe → the dashboard auto-heal re-loaded on every startup. **Future/stale hardening (the operator's explicit ask — "not only now even in the future if there is a stale or any kinds of issues"):** the fix is GENERAL, not a one-row special-case. `parse_instrument_csv` now wraps each in-scope row in `try/except _ROW_PARSE_ERRORS`, where `_ROW_PARSE_ERRORS = (InstrumentFormatError, ValueError)` — the TWO families a malformed/stale *cell* can raise: (a) `InstrumentFormatError` from our explicit field guards (blank `groww_symbol`, unparseable `lot_size`/`tick_size`/`strike_price`/`expiry_date`, unmappable `segment`); (b) `ValueError` from enum coercion of a drifted `exchange`/`instrument_type` AND from the `Instrument.__post_init__` invariants — including the realistic stale case of an `EQ` row whose `lot_size` cell is blank → parses to `0` → "lot_size must be positive". Skipped rows are collected, **counted, and logged at WARNING** (`instrument_master.skipped_unparseable_rows` with a 3-sample reason list) so the drop is visible in `/logs`, never silent. **What it deliberately does NOT do (honest boundary):** it is NOT `except Exception` — a structural fault still fail-louds: the HEADER schema contract (the 21-column check, Golden Rule #1) is verified ONCE above the loop and still raises on drift, and a genuine CODE bug (`AttributeError`/`TypeError`) surfaces loudly instead of being swallowed row-by-row. We harden against bad DATA, never mask bad CODE. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py` at 100% line+branch (31 tests), ruff + ruff-format clean, bandit clean; new tests cover the exact `BSE FOCUSED IT` reproduction, the stale-blank-`lot_size` `ValueError` arm, an all-rows-malformed→empty-list (not raise) out-of-box case, the WARNING-log path, and the preserved row-level `parse_instrument_row` fail-loud + header-drift fail-loud. ✅ the dashboard route now returns 200 with the valid universe (the one junk row dropped). 🟡 a skipped row means that instrument is absent from the universe until the vendor fixes its master — surfaced honestly via the WARNING count, NOT invented. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate change; pure parser resilience. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_instruments.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-SKIP-NO-GSYM-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-ADAPTER-LEAF-001 (the instrument-master parser this hardens), the §6 verified instrument-master schema (`docs/groww/api-reference/02-instruments.md`).

815. **DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001 — the bulk SPOT pull advances its bar + flushes /coverage per WINDOW, so a long backfill never LOOKS "stuck at 24/779" between minutes-apart symbol completions** (2026-06-16, operator: across three runs the `/universe` bar + `/coverage/windows` sat FROZEN at `24/779` for 7+ min even though the `groww.call` logs prove the pull WAS progressing — ~130 ms/call, ~200 calls/min, zero 429s/errors — i.e. NOT a hang, NOT #813's pool). **Why:** both the units bar (`PullProgress.advance`) and the live ledger flush (`make_live_ledger_flush`) were driven SOLELY by `on_progress`, which `run_groww_spot_ingest` fires once per fully-completed `(symbol, interval)` PAIR — a whole symbol's multi-year backfill. With the modest 8-worker pool (DEC-SPOT-POOL-UNIFORM-001, #813) sharing one adaptively-stepped-down bucket, a wave of symbols takes minutes, so for minutes at a time NEITHER surface moved even while windows kept landing in memory (the metadata expiries/contracts pull never looks stuck precisely because its unit is one cheap call — the operator's exact cross-check). **What shipped (ADDITIVE — no rate / pool / concurrency / engine / scope change):** a new idempotent O(N) `WindowLedger.progress_counts()` → `LedgerProgress(total, settled, failed, bars, current)` (settled = the SAME `SETTLED_STATUSES` the /coverage headline uses); `PullProgress.sync()` (absolute, not cumulative — repeated polls never double-count windows the retry rounds re-touch) + `set_current()`; `BackgroundPullJob.sync_from_ledger()` + a `ledger_synced` start-mode where the per-pair hook only refreshes the label; a throttled, thread-safe `make_live_sync()` fired once per fetched window via a new optional `on_window` tick threaded `ingest_spot → run_groww_spot_ingest(_with_retry) → pull_all_spot`; the dashboard `/universe/pull-all` route wires it (`ledger_synced=True`) so the bar advances per settled WINDOW (re-scaling from the symbol placeholder to the window total on the first ~1 s sync) and a FINAL unthrottled push in the `finally` lands the exact end state — even on a crash/abort, so the operator SEES how far the pull got (the screenshot's "5,819 settled"). The live-sync OWNS the ledger flush in that mode (single writer, no race). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `window_ledger` / `pull_progress` / `pull_jobs` / `pull_controller` / `ingest` / `run_ingest` each at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright clean, the `/universe` route smoke test green. 🟡 the per-window bar reflects REAL fetch activity, so it still moves slowly when the pull is genuinely throughput-limited (DEC-SPOT-POOL-UNIFORM-001, #813) — it makes progress HONEST + visible, it does NOT raise throughput. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-ceiling / pool change. **Files:** `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_progress.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, the matching `tests/unit/*` files, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001. **Builds on / complements** DEC-SPOT-POOL-UNIFORM-001 (#813 — the throughput half; this is the visibility half), DEC-GROWW-CALL-LATENCY-LOG-001 (#813), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001, DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-WIRING-001, and the sibling crash fix #816 (DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ABSENT-SKIP-001) shipped in the same PR.

816. **DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ABSENT-SKIP-001 — a Groww candle with a `null` OHLC price can no longer CRASH the whole 779-symbol spot pull: the shared assembler skips the un-storable partial bar, and the ingest quarantines a parse error to the ONE symbol** (2026-06-16, operator: a spot pull hard-failed `✕ 779 symbols spot failed: CandleParseError: unparseable open price: None` after `5,819` windows had already settled). **Why:** DEC-CANDLE-EMPTY-BAR-001 made a partially-absent bar (e.g. Groww's `open: None` alongside a real high/low/close) a hard `CandleParseError`; that non-`GrowwError` propagated out of `run_groww_spot_ingest` (whose "non-GrowwError ⇒ re-raise as a real bug" guard never anticipated vendor `null` prices) and aborted ALL 779 symbols on ONE bad candle from ONE symbol — distinct from #814 (that was the instrument-master *load*; this is a *candle* during the pull). **What shipped (ADDITIVE):** Layer 1 — `assemble_candle` now SKIPS a partially-absent bar (any required OHLC price ABSENT but not all) as a graceful `EmptyCandleRow` (the parser's `except EmptyCandleRow: continue`), never fabricating the missing price (Golden Rule #1) — so the production `open: None` case drops just the un-storable bar and the symbol COMPLETES; a price PRESENT-but-unparseable (`"abc"`/`inf`) still hard-errors (a genuine malformation is never masked). Layer 2 — `run_groww_spot_ingest` now quarantines a `CandleParseError` like a terminal `GrowwError` (the ONE symbol is isolated + re-tried next pull) instead of crashing the whole bulk pull. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `candle_fields` / `run_ingest` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; new tests cover the partial-absent skip across every OHLC field, the present-but-unparseable hard-error, and the `CandleParseError`-quarantines-not-crashes path. 🟡 a skipped partial bar / a quarantined unparseable symbol means that bar/symbol is absent until the vendor fixes its data — surfaced honestly (the skip is logged; the quarantine emits `ingest.quarantine`), never invented. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate change; pure parser + ingest resilience. **Files:** `brutex/data/candle_fields.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_candle_fields.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_parser.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ABSENT-SKIP-001. **Builds on** DEC-CANDLE-EMPTY-BAR-001 (the no-trade-bar skip this extends), DEC-INSTRUMENT-SKIP-NO-GSYM-001 (#814 — the sibling instrument-master skip), and the per-window progress fix #815 (DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001) shipped in the same PR.

818. **DEC-GROWW-RATE-SNAPSHOT-LOG-001 — a throttled periodic `rate.snapshot` makes a HOLDING (stepped-down, non-changing) rate visible in /logs, closing the "why does it sit at ~3 r/s?" blind spot** (2026-06-16, operator throughput investigation: a 12-min spot pull held at ~3.3 r/s — ≈ the 3 r/s soft floor — with **2.4× headroom** to the 8 r/s ceiling, but the live log had NO `rate.*` events to show why). **Why:** the existing rate telemetry (`rate.429` / `rate.stepdown` / `rate.timeout` / `rate.stepup`) fires ONLY on a rung CHANGE. A pull that has already stepped down and is HOLDING at a floor emits nothing, so /logs cannot show the current rate or the pressure (recent 429s / timeouts) pinning it — the operator could only see ~3.3 r/s indirectly via the achieved call rate. **What shipped (ADDITIVE — observability only, no pacing change):** `RateController.pace` now calls a throttled `_maybe_log_snapshot` that emits one `rate.snapshot` INFO at most once per `SNAPSHOT_LOG_INTERVAL_S` (15 s) of ACTIVE pacing, carrying the SAME gauges `snapshot()` already exposes to the dashboard rate panel (`current_rps`, `recent_hits`, `recent_timeouts`, `recent_minute`, `ceiling_per_min`). Driven by `pace`, it ticks only while the pull is issuing calls (no background thread; stops when the pull stops); the throttle CLAIM is O(1) under the lock, the snapshot read + log run OUTSIDE it. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `rate_common.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) clean; new tests cover the warm-up-grace skip, the post-interval emit, the post-log throttle, and a stepped-down HOLDING rate surfacing in the snapshot. ✅ changes NO pacing decision (Rule #6 untouched). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-ceiling change; pure telemetry. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-SNAPSHOT-LOG-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-CALL-LATENCY-LOG-001 (#813 — the sibling per-call latency log, same measure-don't-guess pattern), DEC-DASHBOARD-RATE-PANEL-001 (the `snapshot()` gauges this reuses), DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001.

819. **DEC-GROWW-RATE-RECOVER-8-001 — the INCREMENTAL recovery ladder now climbs the soft floor back to the operator-DIRECTED 8 r/s ceiling within a pull (one rung per clean 60 s window, ~5 min for 3→8) instead of 300 s/rung (~25 min — longer than a pull), so a stepped-down pull actually REACHES 8 r/s; the DECREMENTAL back-off is untouched** (2026-06-16, operator directive: "ensure to achieve the rate limiter of 8 rps incremental and decremental approach"). **Why:** the AIMD controller's ceiling is already the operator-DIRECTED 8 r/s (`GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`, DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001) and it already steps DOWN on 429/timeout pressure (decremental) and UP after a clean window (incremental). But the step-UP window was `STEP_UP_WINDOW=300 s` — so recovering the soft floor (3) to the ceiling (8) took 5 rungs × 300 s = ~25 min, longer than most pulls' wall time, leaving a once-stepped-down pull pinned near 3 r/s with 2.4× headroom unused (the throughput symptom DEC-GROWW-RATE-SNAPSHOT-LOG-001 now makes visible). **What shipped (a SINGLE contained tuning — no ladder/floor/trigger logic change):** `STEP_UP_WINDOW` is set to ONE `STEP_DOWN_WINDOW` (60 s) — symmetric with the rolling window the step-DOWN ladder watches: after a single clean 60 s window the controller probes UP one rung, climbing 3→8 in ~5 clean windows. **Safety is unchanged (Rule #6):** the DECREMENTAL ladder still steps DOWN immediately on a 429/timeout storm AND the soft (3) / storm (1) floors are untouched, so a too-eager probe self-corrects (AIMD never exceeds the sustainable rate — it only reaches it sooner). The `rate.snapshot` telemetry (#818) makes the real climb/back-off trajectory observable. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `rate_common.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + mypy --strict + pyright clean; a new test drives an 8-ceiling controller down to the floor and asserts it recovers 3→4→5→6→7→8 and clamps at 8; every existing step-down/floor/storm test is unchanged (they key off the constants). 🟡 8 r/s is the CEILING the controller now reaches WHEN the vendor sustains it; if Groww's backtesting endpoint genuinely 429s above ~3 r/s the decremental ladder will correctly hold it lower — the `rate.snapshot` telemetry (#818) reveals the vendor's REAL sustainable rate on the next live run, so this is "able to reach 8", not "forced to 8" (no illusion). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pool / ceiling-VALUE change; only the recovery SPEED. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-RECOVER-8-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001 (the 8 r/s ceiling this now reaches), DEC-GROWW-RATE-SNAPSHOT-LOG-001 (#818 — the telemetry that proves the trajectory), DEC-DHAN-RATE-RECOVERY-TRICKLE-001 (the recovery gate this speeds up), DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001, DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001.
817. **DEC-LIVE-TICKS-PARTIAL-PARQUET-001 — the `/live` ticks-flowing indicator can no longer 500 when the newest live-tick partition is mid-write: a partial / zero-byte Parquet degrades to the honest empty-state instead of crashing** (2026-06-16, operator: a `/live` page load logged `Exception in ASGI application ... _duckdb.InvalidInputException: ... 'live/ticks/dt=<date>.parquet' too small to be a Parquet file`). **Why:** `ticks_flowing` (`brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py`) guards the ABSENT-partition case (`_latest_tick_partition is None` → honest empty), but when the live capture has CREATED today's `dt=<date>.parquet` yet not flushed a valid Parquet footer, `_latest_tick_partition` (which picks the newest by ISO-date NAME, not content) returns it and the bounded `read_parquet(?)` aggregate raises DuckDB `InvalidInputException` ("too small to be a Parquet file") — the freshly-opened-feed first-second race — which propagated out of the FastAPI route as a 500. This is UNRELATED to the spot pull (#815/#816); it is the `/api/v1/live/ticks-flowing` endpoint reading a partial live-tick lake. **What shipped (ADDITIVE — pure read resilience, no schema/behaviour change):** the `read_parquet` read is wrapped to catch `(duckdb.InvalidInputException, duckdb.IOException)` — the two a partial / zero-byte / corrupt / locked Parquet raises — and degrade to the SAME honest empty payload the no-partition branch returns (`flowing=False`, empty instruments, the partition's session date still surfaced) with a NEW distinct `TICKS_PARTIAL_NOTE` ("the live-tick lake is being written … refresh in a moment"), logged LOUDLY (`live.ticks_flowing.partition_unreadable` WARNING). The SQL is static + the path is bound, so a DuckDB error here is only ever a bad/partial FILE, never a code bug — a schema-drift `BinderException` still surfaces (harden against bad DATA, never mask bad CODE — DEC-INSTRUMENT-SKIP-NO-GSYM-001's philosophy). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) clean; new regression tests cover the too-small-content partition AND the 0-byte partition (both would 500 before this PR). 🟡 the sibling `live_table` / `live_movers` reads (over a multi-partition glob) carry the same latent risk if a partition is mid-write; that broader hardening is a noted follow-up, not in this focused fix. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate / pull change; pure `/live` read resilience. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/live_lake_view.py`, `tests/unit/test_live_lake_view.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-TICKS-PARTIAL-PARQUET-001. **Builds on** DEC-INSTRUMENT-SKIP-NO-GSYM-001 (#814 — the same degrade-on-bad-data philosophy), DEC-LIVE-DB-SCHEMA-WHEN-EMPTY-001 (the schema-when-empty sibling), DEC-LIVE-DASH-PROBE-001 (the ticks-flowing indicator this hardens).

821. **DEC-MOVERS-DAILY-DIRECT-001 — the `/movers` DAILY timeframe now reads the stored `1day` partitions DIRECTLY instead of requiring a `1minute` series, so a VERIFY-FIRST 1-day-only pull (DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001) finally shows movers instead of "No spot data in the lake yet"** (2026-06-16, operator: after a 1-day-only spot pull the `/movers` page — which opens on the `1day` timeframe — showed no spot data even though the `1day` lake was populated). **Why:** `run_movers_snapshot` (`brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`) discovered instruments via `list_candle_datasets(...) if d["interval"] == "1minute"` and read every series through `_read_session_bars` → `make_lake_read_1m` (1-minute → resample). The 1-day-only pull writes ONLY the `1day` partitions, so the `1minute` discovery list was EMPTY and the function returned the honest-but-wrong "pull spot first" payload — the daily timeframe (the page DEFAULT, `DEFAULT_INTERVAL="1day"`) needed 1-minute data it would never have under the VERIFY-FIRST default. **What shipped (the timeframe now picks its own read path):** (a) a daily snapshot (`minutes >= _DAILY_MIN_FLOOR`, i.e. `1day`) DISCOVERS the `1day` datasets and reads the selected day's stored 1-day bar DIRECTLY via the new `_read_daily_bars` (no resample — "the bar IS the day"); (b) an intraday snapshot (`1minute … 4hour`) keeps the existing `1minute` discovery + `_read_session_bars` resample. A new COMMON `_read_daily_partition` is the single place that opens the `1day` partitions; `_prev_day_close` is refactored to use it too (no duplicated path — CLAUDE.md §11). The prev-day close, the rank/skip/None-prev semantics, and the money-2dp / full-precision-metric rules are UNCHANGED — only the discovery + current-day read for the daily timeframe. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `movers_snapshot.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) clean; new tests: `_read_daily_bars` (missing 1day dir / selected-day read / no-bar-on-day), the daily snapshot discovers `1day` + skips a symbol absent on the day, and the seed now writes the snapshot-day 1-day bar. 🟡 a daily snapshot needs the stored `1day` partition for the snapshot day (the 1-day-only pull writes it); a 1-minute-only pull with no stored `1day` partition still uses an intraday timeframe — surfaced honestly via the existing "pull spot first" note, never fabricated. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate change; pure dashboard read-path fix (REFERENCE_ONLY lake view, CLAUDE.md §3). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-DAILY-DIRECT-001. **Builds on** DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001 (the snapshot view this fixes), DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#723 — the 1-day-only default pull that exposed the gap), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the lake price grid the read honours).
820. **DEC-GROWW-QUARANTINE-BRUTEX-001 — every Groww candle-ingest spine (spot AND option) now quarantines a per-symbol `BruteXError` DOMAIN error instead of re-raising it, so NO single bad / unresolvable symbol can ever crash a bulk pull; a genuine CODE bug (a Python builtin) still surfaces** (2026-06-16, operator: a 779-symbol spot pull progressed to 8,019/10,906 then hard-failed `✕ 779 symbols spot failed: OutOfScopeError: symbol not in Groww universe: BAJAJ-AUTO` — the THIRD such whole-pull abort after a `GrowwError` and a `CandleParseError`). **Why:** `run_groww_spot_ingest` (post-#816) quarantined only `(GrowwError, CandleParseError)` and re-raised everything else as "a genuine bug" — but `OutOfScopeError` (raised by `groww/adapter.py` when a niftyindices→Groww-matched constituent like `BAJAJ-AUTO` does not resolve to a Groww instrument) is ALSO a `BruteXError`, so it propagated out of the fan-out and aborted ALL 779 symbols after thousands of windows had settled. `GrowwError`, `CandleParseError`, AND `OutOfScopeError` are ALL `BruteXError` subclasses (every explicit `raise` in the spine is), so the precise, general line is: quarantine the `BruteXError` BASE. **What shipped (ADDITIVE — the unified per-symbol resilience):** (1) `run_groww_spot_ingest` (`brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`) — `isinstance(exc, (GrowwError, CandleParseError))` → `isinstance(exc, BruteXError)`; (2) `run_groww_option_ingest` (`brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`) — the per-contract `except GrowwError` → `except BruteXError`, so the option candle pull gets the SAME resilience (it had the identical latent crash). Both keep `auth_failed = isinstance(exc, GrowwError) and is_auth_failure(exc)` (only a `GrowwError` can be an auth death; a scope/parse error never is). **One carve-out — the GLOBAL-stop quota signals** (`DailyQuotaExceeded` / `QuotaInvariantError`, both `BruteXError` subclasses) are RE-RAISED before the per-symbol quarantine (`_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` in `run_ingest.py`; an `except (DailyQuotaExceeded, QuotaInvariantError): raise` ahead of `except BruteXError` in `option_ingest.py`): a quota signal means the day's budget is spent / a quota-ledger invariant broke, so EVERY remaining symbol would fail the same way — it is NOT one symbol's problem and must PROPAGATE to the controller's `except DailyQuotaExceeded` to raise the loud `quota_exhausted` verdict + resume after the IST-midnight reset (DEC-SPOT-QUOTA-MIDROUND-001). Without this carve-out the broad `BruteXError` quarantine swallowed `DailyQuotaExceeded` and the quota verdict never fired (caught in CI by `TestQuotaDeathMidRound`; the regression this carve-out closes). A genuine CODE bug (`ValueError` / `RuntimeError` / `AttributeError` — a Python builtin, NOT a `BruteXError`) STILL propagates loudly — the harden-against-bad-DATA-never-mask-bad-CODE line (DEC-INSTRUMENT-SKIP-NO-GSYM-001's philosophy). **The metadata (expiries+contracts) pull was already robust** — `run_two_phase` captures every per-cell exception and classifies it "failed" (never re-raises), and the route already pre-filters reference-only / non-F&O underlyings (DEC-SKIP-REF-METADATA-001) — so "Pull expiries + contracts" already pulls ONLY F&O and never crashes on a non-F&O selection (verified, no change needed). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `run_ingest.py` + `option_ingest.py` BOTH at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict clean; new regression tests: the spot path quarantines an `OutOfScopeError` (BAJAJ-AUTO) while the other 778 land, the option path quarantines an `OutOfScopeError` per contract, a `ValueError`/`RuntimeError` still propagates in both, AND a `DailyQuotaExceeded`/`QuotaInvariantError` PROPAGATES (is NOT quarantined) in both spines so the `quota_exhausted` verdict still fires. 🟡 a quarantined symbol is absent until the vendor/match resolves it — surfaced honestly (the `ingest.quarantine` / `option.ingest.quarantine` WARNING + the failed-pair count), never masked; a future follow-up can pre-filter the selection to drop Groww-unresolvable constituents before the pull (an efficiency win on top of this safety net). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate / pool change; pure per-symbol error resilience. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-QUARANTINE-BRUTEX-001. **Builds on** DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ABSENT-SKIP-001 (#816 — the spot CandleParseError quarantine this generalises), DEC-INSTRUMENT-SKIP-NO-GSYM-001 (#814 — the degrade-on-bad-data philosophy), DEC-SKIP-REF-METADATA-001 (the metadata reference-only pre-filter), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001.

822. **DEC-GROWW-RATE-ACHIEVED-METER-001 — a real ACHIEVED-throughput meter (`CallMeter`) measures the TRUE calls/s from actual call-completion instants, so the dashboard + `/logs` show what the pull is REALLY doing instead of the controller's self-reported target; this closes the "how are you even telling it's hitting 8 r/s?" blind spot** (2026-06-16, operator throughput audit: a live 779-symbol spot pull was claimed to "hit 8 r/s" on the strength of the controller's `current_rps=8.0`, but a measurement of the real `groww.call` timestamps showed the ACHIEVED rate was **3.40 calls/s** with avg **0.49** calls in flight — the single shared `GrowwAPI` SDK connection serialising the 8 workers, invisible because NO instrument reported the achieved rate). **Why:** `current_rps` is the controller's CEILING (the rate it is *allowing*), NOT the rate achieved; the dashboard rate panel already reads `adapter.client.meter.snapshot()` for `effective_rps`/`rps_1s`/`rps_1s_max`/`latency_ms_p95`, but the `CallMeter` it expects was a Dhan-era class DELETED in the Groww remigration, so those gauges were permanently 0 and the only visible number was the (misleading) target. **What shipped (Stage 0 — observability only, ZERO pacing/behaviour change):** a vendor-neutral `brutex/adapters/call_meter.py` `CallMeter` that brackets every physical SDK call (`GrowwClient._call` fires `meter.start()` before the call + `meter.stop(completed=True|False)` after) and reports, from true completion instants: `effective_rps`/`rate_achieved` (a trailing-10 s rolling average — ramps from 0, never over-reads), `rps_1s` + `rps_1s_max` (the instantaneous gauge + run peak — the live PROOF the cap held), `latency_ms_p95`, and `in_flight` (the live concurrency — the gauge that makes the 0.49-serialised-SDK problem VISIBLE). A throttled `rate.achieved` INFO (≤ once / 15 s, mirroring the controller's `rate.snapshot`) surfaces it in `/logs` next to the target. A failed attempt releases its in-flight slot but is NOT counted as achieved throughput (achieved = SUCCESSFUL calls). Every gauge is **O(1) amortized** (deque append + bounded evict, no pandas, no scan) and the meter is thread-safe so a future multi-connection pool records into one aggregate instrument. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `call_meter.py` + `client.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright (0 errors) clean; new tests cover in-flight balance, the rolling window + eviction, the rps_1s peak ratchet, latency-p95 (empty / populated / ring-bounded), the success-only completion rule, the throttled log (warm-up grace / post-interval emit / re-throttle / off), AND the parallel-hostile-review hardening: the `_call` bracket is a `try/finally` so a **BaseException** (Ctrl-C mid-call / a futures cancellation that `except Exception` would miss) STILL releases the in-flight slot (never a leaked gauge), `in_flight` floors at 0 (a stray stop can never go negative), the meter is thread-safe (an 8×250-bracket concurrency stress asserts it returns to exactly 0), and `dataclasses.replace` preserves the SAME meter instance (so the pool aggregates into one, pinned by a test). ✅ this is the HONEST number (counts what completed, from real timestamps, never the controller's target). 🚫 NO pacing/engine/scope change — pure observability; it does not RAISE the achieved rate (that is the multi-client-pool fix, DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001, Stage 1) — it MEASURES it so the next fix is provable. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/call_meter.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `tests/unit/test_call_meter.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-ACHIEVED-METER-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-CALL-LATENCY-LOG-001 (#813 — the per-call latency log this records alongside), DEC-GROWW-RATE-SNAPSHOT-LOG-001 (#818 — the controller's target snapshot this is the achieved twin of), DEC-DASHBOARD-RATE-PANEL-001 / DEC-DASHBOARD-RPS1S-PANEL-001 (the dashboard gauges this re-lights). **Precedes** DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001 (Stage 1 — the multi-client pool that uses this meter to PROVE the achieved rate rises toward 8).

823. **DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001 — an EMPTY (no-data) window is RESOLVED for completion/progress reporting even below the 3× skip-promotion threshold, and the "re-pull to finish" verdict fires ONLY on PLANNED or FAILED windows — so a COMPLETE historical pull stops reporting itself ~73% done and crying "re-pull"; the skip authority is byte-for-byte unchanged** (2026-06-16, operator throughput audit: a finished 779-symbol 1-day pull over 2020-01-01→2026-06-15 — entirely in the PAST — showed THREE divergent "pending" numbers for the same complete pull: the universe widget "2,887 pending · re-pull to finish", the verdict banner "2 pending windows", the /coverage ledger "28 planned"). **Why:** "pending" meant three different things in three modules that were never reconciled. (1) The universe progress widget + the `/api/v1/coverage/windows` JS counted `pending = PLANNED + below-threshold EMPTY` — so on pull #1 every genuinely-empty pre-listing window (e.g. 360ONE / AADHARHFC not listed in 2020-2022, shown "EMPTY 1/3") was counted "pending" (≈2,859 EMPTY + 28 PLANNED = 2,887), and the bar numerator was `settled = SUCCESS+SKIPPED` only, reading "8,019/10,906". (2) `PullVerdict.pending_windows = still_failed_windows + failed_pairs` mislabeled the 2 quarantined SYMBOLS (BAJAJ-AUTO / NAM-INDIA — not on Groww) as "windows", and `classify_pull` fired the amber `transient_residual` "Re-pull to finish" whenever `failed_pairs > 0` — but a re-pull can NEVER recover a symbol that isn't on Groww, and the date range is wholly PAST so the EMPTY windows will NEVER gain data: "re-pull to finish" was dishonest. (3) The /coverage ledger KPI counted PLANNED-only (28). **What shipped (REPORTING-ONLY — zero fetch/skip behaviour change):** one honest four-bucket model derived from the same ledger authority — RESOLVED = SUCCESS+SKIPPED+EMPTY (the progress-bar numerator), NO_DATA = EMPTY (its own bucket, never "pending"), PLANNED (re-pull WILL try), FAILED (re-pull SHOULD retry). Specifically: (a) `WindowLedger` adds `RESOLVED_STATUSES` (DELIBERATELY WIDER than the unchanged skip set `SETTLED_STATUSES`) + `LedgerProgress.resolved`/`no_data`/`planned`; `progress_counts` folds them; the live-sync bar numerator switches `settled` → `resolved` (`make_live_sync` + the final finally-sync). (b) `classify_pull` fires `transient_residual` ONLY on `still_failed_windows > 0`; a quarantine-only pull gets a NEW grey `quarantined_symbols` verdict (`needs_operator = False`, no retry button, "No re-pull needed — these symbols are not on Groww"); `pending_windows` now counts WINDOWS (`still_failed_windows`) not pairs. (c) the universe `/coverage/windows` JS line recomputes `resolved / no-data / pending(=PLANNED) / failed`. **CRITICAL — the skip authority is untouched:** `is_skippable` / `SETTLED_STATUSES` / the EMPTY→SKIPPED 3× promotion (DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001) / `empty_streak` preservation-across-FAILED (DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-RATELIMIT-001) are byte-for-byte unchanged — a below-threshold EMPTY is STILL re-fetched on the next pull (no data ever masked); we changed only what the REPORTS count, never what the skip decides. The honestly-rejected alternative (Option B: settle historical empties to SKIPPED on pull #1) would risk silently dropping real data on a transient vendor EMPTY (the exact case the 3× threshold guards) — a Golden Rule #1 violation. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `window_ledger.py` + `ingest_common.py` + `verdict_banner.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; new tests cover the EMPTY-is-resolved fold, the all-empty pull reading 100%, the `quarantined_symbols` verdict + grey banner + golden, and the transient-outranks-quarantine ordering. ✅ this is a reporting RECONCILIATION only — no fetch/skip change; an EMPTY window is still re-fetched next pull. 🟡 the /coverage SPOT-COVERAGE chip (`spot_window_rollup` / `_classify_completeness`, a separate page) still classifies an all-EMPTY dataset's chip with the old 3-bucket lumping — a noted follow-up applying the SAME four-bucket model; this PR reconciles the universe page (the operator's reported surface). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate change. **Files:** `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, `brutex/dashboard/verdict_banner.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, tests, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001. **Builds on** DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the 3× skip-promotion threshold kept), DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-RATELIMIT-001 (the all-empty throttle kept), DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 / DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the status set, unchanged), DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 (the verdict this amends), DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001 (the bar numerator switched), DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 (the chip follow-up).

824. **DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 — a clean 0-bar (EMPTY) response is now RE-FETCHED in-pull up to 3 attempts before it is trusted as no-data, so a TRANSIENT vendor empty (Groww returns `{}` under load for a range that DOES have data) is RECOVERED ("pull until a successful response") instead of silently recorded as a false EMPTY** (2026-06-16, operator: "since we pull from Jan-2020 we can never know if a 0-bar response really fetched or was a glitch/hallucination — make 3 retry attempts to be sure"). **Why:** the spine treated a clean 0-bar `200` as a "successful" no-data answer and recorded EMPTY on the FIRST call (the transient/error retry only covered 429/timeout EXCEPTIONS, never a clean-but-empty body). On a Jan-2020→today historical range a 0-bar response is genuinely AMBIGUOUS on one call — it is EITHER a real empty (pre-listing / holiday / no data) OR a vendor glitch on a range that has data — and accepting the first empty risked recording real, fetchable data as permanently no-data. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, bounded):** `_ingest_one_window` (`brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`) now wraps the fetch in an EMPTY-retry loop — up to `empty_retry_attempts` (default **3**, `_DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`) TOTAL attempts; the FIRST attempt that returns bars WINS (the window is recorded SUCCESS, the glitch recovered), and only an ALL-empty run falls through to record genuine no-data WITH confidence. Each attempt is paced by the shared rate bucket (~125 ms at the 8 r/s ceiling spaces the re-fetches), so the default `empty_retry_backoff` is a **no-op** (an injectable hook — a recorder in tests, or a real pause at a live site — without a pointless per-window sleep on a bulk pull's thousands of empties). The retry is BOUNDED (a truly-empty window fires exactly `empty_retry_attempts` calls, never loops forever) and ORTHOGONAL to BOTH the transient-error retry (429/timeout, unchanged) AND the ledger's across-pull EMPTY→SKIPPED 3× threshold (DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001, unchanged — a genuine empty still stays re-fetchable across future pulls for late-arriving recent data). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `ingest.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; new tests prove the glitch-recovery (empty→empty→DATA records SUCCESS in 3 calls), the bounded genuine-empty (always-empty → exactly 3 calls → EMPTY, backoff fired between attempts not after the last), and the no-retry happy path (data on attempt 1 → 1 call). ✅ never masks data — an EMPTY that survives 3 tries is recorded EMPTY and STILL re-fetched next pull. 🟡 cost: a genuinely-empty window costs up to `empty_retry_attempts`× the calls (the operator-accepted "be sure" trade-off on a Jan-2020+ range); the rate bucket + the 500/min governor still cap the issue rate. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / reporting change (the EMPTY→resolved REPORTING is DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001 #823; this is the FETCH side). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001. **Builds on** DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001 (#823 — the reporting twin: this RECOVERS/confirms the empty, that REPORTS the confirmed no-data honestly), DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the across-pull 3× threshold kept), DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001 (the per-call freeze guard each attempt still rides).

825. **DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001 — the live spot historical pull fans its worker threads across a `ClientPool` of K INDEPENDENT Groww SDK connections (one shared rate controller + one shared achieved-rate meter), so the workers stop SERIALISING on a single shared SDK socket — the measured avg-0.49-in-flight → ~3.4 r/s starve that pinned achieved throughput far below the 8 r/s ceiling** (2026-06-19, operator throughput logs: 31,881 real `groww.call` events over a 779-symbol pull showed `effective_rps` mode **3** / max **5** / never 8, with `in_flight` dominantly 0–1 and a smoking-gun `{"effective_rps": 0.1, "in_flight": 7}` line — 7 worker threads simultaneously past `pace()` yet near-zero completions, i.e. all blocked on ONE connection). **Why:** the fan-out (`ingest_spot` → `PoolRunParallel`) already issues windows concurrently, but every worker funnelled its physical `get_historical_candles` through ONE injected `GrowwAPI` SDK socket, so the calls serialised on that single connection (`CallMeter` recorded avg **0.49** in-flight). By Little's Law `throughput = in-flight ÷ latency ≈ 0.49 ÷ 0.15 s ≈ 3.4 r/s` — exactly the observed ceiling — and to reach 8 r/s you need only ~1.2 calls overlapping, which one connection cannot sustain. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, config-gated):** (a) a new `brutex/adapters/groww/pool.py` `ClientPool` holding K leaf `GrowwClient`s — duck-compatible with a single client via the new `GrowwClientProtocol` (`client.py`) so it drops into the adapter's `client` slot with ZERO change to the adapter / candle / contract fetchers (their `client:` params widened `GrowwClient` → `GrowwClientProtocol`); dispatch is O(1) thread-affinity (each worker bound to one leaf on first call via `threading.local`, lock-free thereafter) so K worker threads spread across K connections AND each keeps its socket warm. (b) `build_live_pool` (`live.py`) mints the TOTP token ONCE and builds K SDKs from it, all sharing ONE `pace`/decrement/recover hooks AND ONE `CallMeter` (the aggregate the dashboard reads — `in_flight` now rises toward K, `effective_rps` toward the ceiling). (c) `_with_paced_client` (`run_ingest.py`) now wires pace via the `with_pace()` protocol seam (re-fans into EVERY leaf) instead of a raw `dataclasses.replace` (which would have skipped the pool's leaves). (d) the dashboard spot builder `_build_live_spot_adapter` builds a pool sized by `resolve_pool_size()` (`constants.py`: `GROWW_CLIENT_POOL_SIZE` default **2**, hard clamp `GROWW_CLIENT_POOL_MAX` **4**, env override `BRUTEX_GROWW_POOL_SIZE`). **CRITICAL — rate safety unchanged (Golden Rule #6):** the SHARED `RateController` still paces EVERY physical call at the per-window `pace` gate, so the AGGREGATE issue rate stays ≤ the ceiling — the pool adds CONCURRENCY, never extra rate; K connections cannot exceed the shared bucket or the 500/min governor. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `pool.py` + `client.py` + `live.py` + `constants.py` + `adapter.py` + `candles.py` + `contracts.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + ruff-format clean, mypy --strict clean on all touched files; the pool tests PROVE the speed-up deterministically (a shared `threading.Barrier(K)` releases ONLY when K calls are truly simultaneously in-flight — K independent connections pass it; a single connection driven by 4 threads pins observed concurrency to **1**, the documented starve) plus thread-affinity, shared-meter aggregation, `with_pace` re-fanning, delegation, and the constructor guards; the build_live_pool composition + `resolve_pool_size` env/clamp/fail-safe matrix are 100% covered with injected fakes (no `growwapi`, no network). 🟡 **8 r/s is NOT vendor-sustainable** — the SAME logs show **421** `rate.429` events with the AIMD floored to 3.0 r/s for 413 snapshots, and 429s persisting even at current_rps=3 (recent_hits 18–20), i.e. a per-minute cap (~300/min ≈ 5 r/s) is the REAL binding limit; the pool's honest win is reaching the vendor's true ~5 r/s ceiling STEADILY (the `CallMeter` proves the real number live, DEC-GROWW-RATE-ACHIEVED-METER-001), NOT a fictional sustained 8. Tuning the 500/min governor toward the vendor's real ~300/min is a NOTED follow-up requiring operator sign-off (Golden Rule #6 — not changed here). 🟡 concurrent use of one TOTP token across K SDK connections is vendor-UNVERIFIED (ADR-0009 §3); each leaf is a SEPARATE SDK session (no interleaving) and the AIMD + bounded retry absorb any vendor pushback (429 → step down → recover), and the operator falls straight back to a 1-connection pool via `BRUTEX_GROWW_POOL_SIZE=1` (today's exact behaviour) — observable + reversible, no code change. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / reporting change; the per-second 8 r/s ceiling + 500/min governor constants are UNTOUCHED. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/pool.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/adapter.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/candles.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/contracts.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_pool.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_groww_live.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_constants.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-RATE-ACHIEVED-METER-001 (#822 — the meter that DIAGNOSED the 0.49-in-flight starve and now PROVES the pool's real achieved rate), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001 (the 8 r/s ceiling the pool lets the workers actually approach), DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001 (the 500/min governor that still caps the aggregate), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the fan-out the pool now feeds independent connections), DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 / ADR-0009 (the Groww SDK client this pools).

826. **DEC-EMPTY-RETRY-EVERYWHERE-001 — the "pull until a successful (non-empty) response" retry is generalised from the spot candle pull to EVERY empty-prone Groww call (historical candles, `get_expiries`, `get_contracts`) via one shared `fetch_until_nonempty` primitive — so a transient empty can never silently DROP a newly-listed weekly/monthly expiry or its strike chain** (2026-06-19, operator: "this retry is applicable for entire expiries contracts and historical data pull everywhere right dude … especially for expiries alone every week or month it can be newly added — how will you check/fetch those new expiries and contracts"). **Why:** the in-pull EMPTY-retry of DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 (#824) covered ONLY the spot candle window (`ingest.py:_ingest_one_window`). The option/future chain RESOLUTION calls — `resolve_expiries` (`get_expiries`) and `resolve_contracts` (`get_contracts`) — trusted a clean 0-length array on the FIRST call. New expiries are listed continuously (weekly + monthly), so the option pull is RE-RUN to pick them up (`enumerate_contracts` re-calls `get_expiries` per year every run; the `WindowLedger` O(1)-skips already-pulled contract windows and fetches only the new ones — the incremental-discovery spine). But a single transient empty `get_expiries` on a re-run would make the system conclude "no new expiries" and SILENTLY MISS a freshly-listed weekly expiry (and an empty `get_contracts` would drop a new expiry's entire strike chain) — the exact ambiguity (genuine no-data vs vendor glitch) the candle retry already guards, left unguarded on the most important discovery calls. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, COMMON):** a single vendor-neutral primitive `fetch_until_nonempty(fetch, *, is_empty, attempts=DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS, backoff)` in `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — one source of truth, PEP-695 generic, O(1) fixed-attempt state): call `fetch`; if `is_empty(result)`, re-fetch up to `attempts` TOTAL; the FIRST non-empty result wins (the glitch recovered), only an all-empty run returns the (confidently) empty result; BOUNDED so a truly-empty call fires exactly `attempts` times, never loops. `resolve_expiries` + `resolve_contracts` (`contracts.py`) now wrap their client-call+parse in this primitive (`is_empty = not result`, default 3 attempts, opt-out via `empty_retry_attempts=1`). The default `DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=3` mirrors the spot candle default. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `ingest_common.py` (the 6-file strict gate) + `contracts.py` at 100% line+branch, ruff + mypy --strict + pyright clean; new tests prove the helper (happy 1-call, glitch-recovery 2-call, genuine-empty bounded-to-N, attempts=1 opt-out, backoff-fires-before-each-refetch) AND `resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts` (glitchy-empty recovers in 2 calls, genuine-empty bounded to exactly 3, opt-out single call). ✅ never masks data — an empty that survives the budget is recorded empty and re-discoverable on the next re-pull; the WindowLedger across-run skip authority is UNCHANGED. 🟡 cost: a genuinely-empty resolution call (e.g. a pre-listing year's `get_expiries`) now costs up to `attempts`× the calls — the operator-accepted "never miss a new expiry" trade-off, bounded + rate-gated. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope change; the option candle empty-retry (`ingest_option_contract`) + the options connection pool are SEPARATE follow-ups (the options-pull parity series). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/contracts.py`, `tests/unit/test_ingest_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_contracts.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-EMPTY-RETRY-EVERYWHERE-001. **Builds on** DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 (#824 — the spot candle empty-retry this generalises), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (the expiries→contracts resolution it hardens), DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 (#711 — the listing→expiry bounds the new contracts ride), DEC-INGEST-COMMON-001 (the shared vendor-neutral home).

827. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-SCOREBOARD-001 — a Data Completeness Scoreboard (per-symbol + aggregate, indices vs equities-cash SEPARATELY) answering "of all our symbols, how many have the COMPLETE 6-year (2020→today) dataset?" across four dimensions — 1-day spot, 1-minute spot, option expiries, option contracts — exposed at `/api/v1/completeness/scoreboard`** (2026-06-19, operator: "in webpage and even as reports I need to clearly know how many symbols from indices and equities cash separately have full entire 6 years … one day and one minute spot data … and how many have entire expiries and entire contracts … even per symbols also"). **Why:** the existing `/coverage` surfaces showed per-(symbol,interval) spot rows and aggregate option coverage, but there was NO consolidated "how many symbols are COMPLETE on each dimension" rollup — neither the aggregate counts nor a per-symbol side-by-side 1-day vs 1-minute view, and nothing splitting the count by category. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, REUSE — read-only):** a new pure module `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` (`build_completeness_scoreboard` + `categorize_instruments`) that RE-AGGREGATES the EXISTING ledger classification (it consumes the annotated spot rows from `build_spot_coverage_payload` — which already carry the `spot_window_rollup` settled/pending/failed verdict — and the option `CoverageRecord` rows, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON: no re-derivation). For each spot symbol it folds the 1-day + 1-minute chip into a per-dimension verdict (`full` = ledger-settled / `partial` = PLANNED outstanding / `failed` / `none` = no record) + an overall verdict, and counts per category (`index` / `equity` / `reference`, classified by the injected `is_in_brute_force_scope` + `is_reference_only`); for each option underlying it sums expiries/contracts across years and folds the per-year cell statuses into the HONEST verdict. The route `/api/v1/completeness/scoreboard` (`# pragma: no cover` — live store+lake) delegates to the pure engine. **CRITICAL — honest options (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** spot completeness is EXACT (the window ledger knows every expected trading-day window), but option **expiries/contracts have NO knowable expected total** — Groww only returns the set that EXISTS when asked — so the scoreboard does NOT fabricate a percentage: it reports the pulled-count + a `stable` / `growing` / `partial` / `failed` verdict where **`stable` = every currently-listed expiry pulled AND nothing new outstanding** (the only honest "complete" for options, made trustworthy by the `get_expiries` empty-retry of DEC-EMPTY-RETRY-EVERYWHERE-001 #826). A delisted / no-longer-listed symbol is judged on the windows it HAS (the ledger never planned past its real lifetime), so it reads complete-up-to-lifetime, never penalised. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ Verified — `completeness.py` at 100% line+branch via `tests/unit/test_completeness.py` (per-symbol full/partial/failed/none verdicts, overall fold, unmapped + derived-interval skips, sorting, the option stable/growing/partial/failed/none fold, the aggregate count tables, the category buckets, and a drift guard pinning the duplicated cell-status strings to `coverage_ledger`); ruff + mypy --strict + pyright clean; the app factory builds with the route registered (dashboard app-build suite green). The pure engine is offline-testable (no lake/store/network); the route is the thin live wiring. 🟡 this PR delivers the ENGINE + the JSON API (the data); the HTML webpage rendering it + a CSV export are the immediate follow-up (the payload is the contract). 🟡 option expiries/contracts completeness is a stability signal, NOT an exact %, because the vendor exposes no total (stated, not hidden). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pull change — read-only reporting over the existing ledger. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (route + imports), `tests/unit/test_completeness.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-SCOREBOARD-001. **Builds on** DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 + DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001 (the spot rollup it reuses), DEC-EMPTY-RETRY-EVERYWHERE-001 (#826 — makes the option "stable" signal trustworthy), DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 (the `/coverage` route pattern it mirrors), the option coverage ledger (CoverageRecord) it folds.

coverage sub-nav + a "Download CSV report" link + the `/coverage` hub link) that polls `/api/v1/completeness/scoreboard` and renders one summary card PER category (each showing full-1day / full-1minute / full-both spot counts out of total + the option stable/growing/failed counts) and the two drill-down tables (per-symbol spot 1day/1minute/overall verdict chips; nav-consistency guard extended to the new page; ruff + mypy --strict + pyright clean (the lone `cma` import-stub note is a pre-existing env gap in `engine/stage3_refine.py`, not this change). 🟡 the CSV is the per-symbol/per-underlying DETAIL + the per-category SUMMARY counts (the "how many"); spot completeness stays EXACT (window-ledger) and option status stays the honest `stable`/`growing`/`partial`/`failed` — NO fabricated % (CLAUDE.md §6, the vendor exposes no expected total). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pull change — read-only reporting over the #827 payload. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` (CSV builder), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (page route + CSV route + shared builder + template loader/render helper + import), `brutex/dashboard/templates/completeness.html` (new), `brutex/dashboard/templates/coverage.html` (hub card), `tests/unit/test_completeness.py` (CSV tests), `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py` (page+JSON+CSV tests), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py` (new page classified), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-PAGE-001. **Builds on** DEC-COMPLETENESS-SCOREBOARD-001 (#827 — the engine + JSON payload this renders), DEC-DASHBOARD-COVERAGE-SPLIT-001 (the focused-page + hub pattern it mirrors), DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIFY-001 (the cross-page nav guard it joins), DEC-REPORT-FILENAME-001 (the attachment-download pattern).

829. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001 — a per-symbol completeness strip on the `/universe` pull page: right where the operator clicks Pull, each symbol row now shows whether it has the ENTIRE 2020→today set — the EXPLICIT first→last bar dates + a from-2020 flag for spot 1-day & 1-minute, plus the honest option status + year span — backed by a new `/api/v1/universe/completeness` per-symbol map** (2026-06-19, operator: "when I click pull expiries and contracts and historical fetch, I can't see or identify whether this symbol has entire data starting 2020 — even for spot 1 day or 1 minute or expiries or contracts — that's where I need to see and identify all these … per symbols also"; placement + explicit-dates both operator-chosen via AskUserQuestion). **Why:** the Data Completeness Scoreboard (#783/#784) answered "how many symbols are complete" on a SEPARATE `/completeness` page with full/partial CHIPS — but at PULL time, on `/universe`, the operator had no per-symbol signal at all, and a chip doesn't show the explicit "does it start 2020-01-01" boundary they need to eyeball. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, REUSE — read-only):** (1) a new pure `per_symbol_completeness(spot_rows, spot_categories, option_records, option_categories)` in `completeness.py` returning `{symbol_name: {category, exchange, spot:{1day,1minute,overall}, options:{status,expiries_pulled,contracts_pulled,years,first_year,last_year}}}` — per spot dimension it carries the verdict + the REAL earliest/latest bar date (from the annotated `build_spot_coverage_payload` rows, which already carry `first_date`/`last_date`) + a `from_2020` boolean (earliest bar `< 2021-01-01` ⇒ data begins in the GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR year, year-granular so it is robust to which exact Jan-2020 trading day the vendor serves; never a magic threshold); it reuses the shared verdict helpers (no re-derivation, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); (2) the route `/api/v1/universe/completeness` delegating to it over the SAME lake+ledger read the scoreboard uses — refactored into ONE shared `_completeness_inputs(store, lake)` so the scoreboard, the CSV, AND the per-symbol map share a single lake read (COMMON, no duplication); no lake root → empty `{}` (page degrades to "not yet pulled"), unwired store → 503; (3) the `/universe` page (`templates/universe.html`) overlays a compact strip on EVERY `.inst` row — `1d 2020-01-01→2026-06-18 ✓ · 1m 2021-03-04→… ⚠ · opt 2020–2025 stable` — green ✓ = full AND from-2020, amber ⚠ = partial OR starts later, red ✕ = failed, dim — = never pulled; the map is fetched once on bootstrap + polled every 15 s and re-renders ONLY when it actually changes (so a landed pull updates the strip live without churning ~750 rows), escape-before-innerHTML throughout (XSS). **Performance (Golden Rule #5 / charter):** the engine is O(spot_rows + option_records) — two single passes, dict-grouped; the page join is O(1) per row (`COV[i.symbol]`); the 15 s poll re-renders only on a changed signature. NOT an O(1)-total claim (it is O(rows) to build the map — honestly stated). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `completeness.py` (incl. `per_symbol_completeness`) at 100% line+branch via `tests/unit/test_completeness.py` (25 tests: both-intervals-with-dates from_2020 True, from_2020 False on a 2021 start, missing-dates/no-record defaults, unmapped + derived-TF skips, option year-span fold, options-only/spot-only merges, unmapped-underlying skip); the new route + the no-lake-root + 503 paths integration-tested in `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py` (no `# pragma: no cover`); the page wiring guarded by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_template.py`; ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; nav/a11y/mobile guards green. 🟡 spot dates are EXACT (lake first/last bar); option year span is the pulled coverage, status is the honest stable/growing/partial/failed (CLAUDE.md §6 — no fabricated %). 🟡 a symbol legitimately listed after 2020 reads ⚠ (it never HAD 2020 data) — correct + the explicit date disambiguates a late-listing from a gap. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pull change — read-only over the existing ledger. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` (the engine fn), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (route + shared `_completeness_inputs` + import), `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` (strip + fetch + CSS), `tests/unit/test_completeness.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_template.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001. **Builds on** DEC-COMPLETENESS-SCOREBOARD-001 (#783 — the engine + verdict helpers it reuses), DEC-COMPLETENESS-PAGE-001 (#784 — the page/CSV sibling), DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 (the first/last date source), DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 (the 2020 floor the from-2020 flag tests against), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the `/universe` instrument feed it overlays).

830. **DEC-OPTION-EMPTY-RETRY-001 — the in-pull "pull until a successful (non-empty) response" retry is extended to OPTION CANDLES (`ingest_option_contract`), closing the LAST remaining gap: spot candles (DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 #824) + `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` (DEC-EMPTY-RETRY-EVERYWHERE-001 #826) already had it; the option/future candle leaf did NOT — a clean 0-bar `200` on a listed strike chain was recorded EMPTY on the FIRST call, with no re-fetch** (2026-06-19, operator: "especially to pull until it fetches successful response … cover all kinds of extreme permutations/combinations of exceptions errors situations"). **Why:** `ingest_option_contract` had a transient-error retry (`while True` + `max_attempts`) but a SUCCESSFUL fetch returning 0 bars broke immediately and recorded EMPTY — the exact genuine-no-data-vs-vendor-glitch ambiguity the spot spine already guards, left unguarded on the option/future candle pull (the same leaf used by `run_groww_option_ingest` → `ingest_underlying_options`/`ingest_underlying_futures`). **What shipped (ADDITIVE, mirrors the spot `_ingest_one_window`):** `ingest_option_contract` now wraps its inner transient-retry fetch in a bounded OUTER `for empty_attempt in range(empty_retry_attempts)` loop — a 0-bar SUCCESS is re-fetched up to `empty_retry_attempts` times; the FIRST attempt with bars WINS (a glitched empty recovered), only an all-empty run falls through to record genuine no-data WITH confidence; bounded, so a truly-empty window can never loop. New params `empty_retry_attempts: int = DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` (the COMMON canonical 3, imported from `ingest_common`) + `empty_retry_backoff` (default the new module-local `_noop_empty_backoff` — the per-call token-bucket `pace()` already spaces the calls, mirroring the spot default). PRODUCTION inherits it automatically: `run_groww_option_ingest` calls the leaf without overriding, so every option/future candle pull now empty-retries at 3 with ZERO driver-signature change (minimal-risk: the leaf-only change, not threaded through every driver). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `option_ingest.py` at 100% line+branch via `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py` (42 tests; explicit empty-retry cases: empty-then-data recovers in 2 fetches, persistent-empty bounded to EXACTLY 3 with the 0-based backoff firing on rounds 0+1 — mirroring the spot spine's `empty_retry_backoff(empty_attempt)`, `empty_retry_attempts=1` opt-out single fetch, `empty_retry_attempts=0` clamps to ONE fetch via a `max(1, …)` guard that HARDENS over the spot mirror's bare `range(N)`, an empty→transient→data interleave proving the shared transient counter spans empty rounds correctly, default-is-3-with-noop-backoff); a hostile-review pass (verdict SHIP) drove the two cross-mirror fixes (0-based backoff + `max(1,…)` guard) + the interleave test; ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; all 36 pre-existing option-ingest tests still green (no regression — data-returning fetches break on the first attempt; the existing quarantine test's empty contract now fetches 3× but asserts no call-count). 🟡 the in-pull retry confirms "empty right now" within ONE pull; the WindowLedger's CROSS-pull empty-streak threshold (3 pulls) is a SEPARATE, complementary guard — a single confirmed-empty window (`empty_streak=1`) is recorded but still re-checked on future pulls until the streak confirms a durable empty (both guards documented + tested). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit change — the pace/governor are untouched; this only adds bounded re-fetches of a window that returned 0 bars. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-OPTION-EMPTY-RETRY-001. **Builds on** DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 (#824 — the spot candle empty-retry this mirrors), DEC-EMPTY-RETRY-EVERYWHERE-001 (#826 — the expiries/contracts generalisation), DEC-INGEST-COMMON-001 (the `DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` canonical it imports), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (the option ingest leaf it hardens).

831. **DEC-CLAUDE-AUTOMATION-001 — the build→review→CI→merge loop is codified as checked-in `.claude/` artifacts so every Claude Code session inherits the parallel hostile-review + workspace-health pass + the ship-to-merge discipline WITHOUT per-session re-instruction** (2026-06-19, operator: "are we really using the latest Claude Code features … make everything completely fully comprehensively automated with real time guarantee and assurance … yes everything should be always automated"). **Why:** the parallel-review + ship loop has been run BY HAND on #783–#786 (spawn hostile-reviewer + workspace-health agents, write the Z+/DoR markers, monitor→merge); nothing in the repo captured it, so a new session relied on discipline + this transcript. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, config/docs only — no Python/engine change):** (1) `.claude/agents/hostile-reviewer.md` — the adversarial diff reviewer (correctness, security, O-complexity honesty, and the recurring `# pragma: no cover` coverage-honesty failure mode), Read-only, opus; (2) `.claude/agents/workspace-health.md` — the independent evidence-based whole-repo verifier (the import-smoke + unit/integration/property + ruff/mypy/pyright + Rust sweep that just proved 7,747 Python + 532 Rust tests green), Read-only, sonnet; (3) `.claude/skills/ship-pr/SKILL.md` — the repeatable ship→merge loop (pre-flight CI-exact gates → parallel review → the 6 Z+ + 5 DoR PR-body markers → draft→ready → monitor-without-churn → post-merge health); (4) `docs/runbooks/claude_automation.md` — the full playbook tagging each surface Verified / Documented / Manual, including the opt-in `anthropics/claude-code-action` cloud auto-fix snippet (job-gated off by a `CLAUDE_AUTOFIX_ENABLED` repo variable so it stays dormant until enabled). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — the EXISTING automation is real + proven (CI 60+ gates, the Auto-merge-on-green workflow merged #783–#786 hands-free, the SessionStart + PreToolUse + PostToolUse hooks in `.claude/settings.json` run); the new files are valid Claude Code config (correct subagent/skill frontmatter). 🟡 Documented-not-Verified: whether a given REMOTE/web session auto-discovers repo-defined subagent *types* is runtime-dependent and was NOT verifiable from inside a session — the files are additive + harmless if a runtime ignores them, and the parallel-review pattern is ALSO invoked explicitly each PR regardless (no reliance on auto-discovery). 🟡 Manual (cannot be automated by a session): the cloud auto-fix needs a repo-admin to add the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret + flip `CLAUDE_AUTOFIX_ENABLED=true` — surfaced explicitly, never silently assumed working. 🚫 no gate is weakened — automation only ADDS verification + removes manual clicks; no `brutex/` Python / engine / scope change. **Files:** `.claude/agents/hostile-reviewer.md` (new), `.claude/agents/workspace-health.md` (new), `.claude/skills/ship-pr/SKILL.md` (new), `docs/runbooks/claude_automation.md` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CLAUDE-AUTOMATION-001. **Builds on** DEC-SESSION-START-HOOK-001 (#237 — the existing SessionStart hook this complements), the Z+ PR-body guard (DEC-P0-015) + Definition-of-Ready gate (DEC-DEFINITION-OF-READY-001) the ship-pr skill satisfies, and the Auto-merge-on-green + pre-merge-gate workflows it documents.

832. **DEC-GROWW-OPTION-POOL-001 — the option/future candle pull is un-deferred from a SEQUENTIAL loop to the SAME cross-contract parallel fan-out the spot pull uses (8-RPS parity): `run_groww_option_ingest` now maps one job per `(contract, interval)` pair through an injected `RunParallel`, and the dashboard historical pull builds a multi-connection `ClientPool` + derives a rate-sized `PoolRunParallel` so option contracts fan across K SDK connections instead of serialising on one socket** (2026-06-19, the K2 wiring the `option_ingest` module docstring had explicitly deferred — "Parallel outer fan-out … is a K2 wiring concern; the LAKE reference pull is not the brute-force hot path"). **Why:** the spot pull already reaches ~8 r/s via `PoolRunParallel` over a `ClientPool` (DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001), but the option/future candle driver stayed a sequential paced loop over a SINGLE connection — so a heavy whole-underlying chain pull (genuinely weeks-scale) crawled at the measured ~3.4 r/s single-socket ceiling (Little's Law: avg 0.49 in-flight ÷ ~0.15 s) no matter the controller rate. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, the proven spot template):** (1) `run_groww_option_ingest` gained `run_parallel: RunParallel | None` and now builds a deterministic `[(contract, interval) …]` worklist drained through the runner — quarantine (terminal `BruteXError`), GLOBAL-stop propagation (`DailyQuotaExceeded`/`QuotaInvariantError` via the new `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` carve-out), code-bug re-raise (non-`BruteXError`), and `on_progress` ALL fire on the single CONTROLLER thread (so the hook need not be thread-safe), mirroring `run_groww_spot_ingest` exactly; each worker re-binds `pull_id_scope` (context-vars don't cross the pool). The DEFAULT is a LAZY `SerialRunParallel` that is **byte-identical** to the prior nested loop (same contract-major order, same early-stop-on-quota), so all 36 pre-existing option tests + every non-wired caller keep the exact prior behaviour with ZERO churn — the safer choice over mirroring spot's pool-DEFAULT (which would have changed quota-stop semantics and forced 32 test edits). Concurrency is purely CROSS-contract (one in-flight call per contract — `fetch_candle_windows` tiles each contract's windows serially, no nested window pool, simpler than spot). The `client` params (+`ingest_option_contract`/`fetch_option_candles`/`ingest_underlying_options`/`ingest_underlying_futures`) widened `GrowwClient` → `GrowwClientProtocol` so a `ClientPool` drops in. (2) `historical_pull._build_live_client` now builds a `ClientPool` via `build_live_pool(resolve_pool_size())` (was a single `build_live_client`); a new pure `_option_run_parallel(dry_run, session_rate)` (the option twin of `pull_controller._spot_run_parallel`) derives a `PoolRunParallel` for a LIVE pull / `None` (→ the serial default) for dry-run, threaded through `_run_phase` → `run_groww_option_ingest`; an explicit `run_parallel` (a test fake) always wins. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #6 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `option_ingest.py` + `historical_pull.py` at 100% line+branch (`tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py` + `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`: injected-runner worklist order, real-`PoolRunParallel` quarantine-keeps-others, pool global-stop propagates + shuts down without hang, both `ingest_underlying_*` forward `run_parallel`, `_option_run_parallel` both branches, the live-derive + explicit-runner wins paths); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; all pre-existing option + historical tests green (no regression — the serial default is byte-identical). 🟡 the SHARED `RateController` (the `pace` token bucket + 500/min governor) is UNCHANGED and remains the SOLE issue governor — the pool adds CONCURRENCY, never extra rate (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 untouched); the true sustainable rate is still the vendor's (live 429s above ~5 r/s), so the realistic win is reaching the vendor ceiling STEADILY, not a fictional sustained 8 r/s. 🟡 concurrent use of one TOTP token across K connections stays vendor-UNVERIFIED (ADR-0009 §3); a `build_live_pool` failure degrades to a 1-connection pool, and `BRUTEX_GROWW_POOL_SIZE` falls straight back to size 1 (no code change). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope change — option bars remain LAKE / REFERENCE_ONLY (DEC-P0-063); this is pull-throughput only. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-OPTION-POOL-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001 (#319-area — the spot `ClientPool` + `build_live_pool` + `resolve_pool_size` this reuses), DEC-SPOT-CROSS-SYMBOL-FANOUT-001 (the spot cross-symbol fan-out template `run_groww_spot_ingest` set), DEC-GROWW-QUARANTINE-BRUTEX-001 (the per-pair quarantine + global-stop carve-out it mirrors), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (the option ingest leaf it parallelises), DEC-DERIV-PULL-HISTORICAL-001 (the historical pull it wires the pool into).

833. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-INDEX-CATEGORY-001 — the /completeness asset-class split now categorises by the TRUE instrument type (`instrument_type == IDX`), not brute-force membership: a real index that is not one of the 3 brute-forced ones (e.g. FINNIFTY) is correctly shown as an INDEX, never "equity (cash)"** (2026-06-19, operator: "how the fuck under coverage completeness check finnifty is showing as equity cash … why wrong mapping?"). **Why (the bug):** the `/completeness` route built its `symbol → category` map with `categorize_instruments(is_index=is_in_brute_force_scope, …)` — but `is_in_brute_force_scope` is the ENGINE-tier test (True only for NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). FINNIFTY is a genuine NSE `IDX` instrument that is NOT brute-forced, so it failed the index test, was not reference-only, and fell through to `CATEGORY_EQUITY` — displayed under "EQUITIES (CASH)" with category `equity`. The `/universe` page categorises by the real instrument type, so it correctly showed the `index` badge — the SAME instrument read two different ways on two pages (the operator's screenshots). The mapping itself was already O(1) (a dict lookup); the defect was the WRONG predicate (wrong key logic), not complexity. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, minimal):** (1) new pure `is_index_instrument(instrument) -> bool = instrument.instrument == InstrumentType.IDX` in `universe.py` (the by-TYPE / asset-class index predicate, O(1) one enum compare; exported), DISTINCT from the engine-tier `is_in_brute_force_scope`; (2) `categorize_instruments` (`completeness.py`) now checks **reference-only FIRST**, then index, then equity — because a reference-only index (India VIX) satisfies BOTH the by-type index AND reference predicates, so reference must win to keep VIX in REFERENCE (for the legacy brute-force `is_index` the two sets are disjoint, so this precedence is a behaviour-preserving no-op there); (3) the `/completeness` route (`app.py`) passes `is_index=is_index_instrument` (the now-unused `is_in_brute_force_scope` import dropped). Result: all 4 pulled indices (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX/FINNIFTY) read INDEX, India VIX stays REFERENCE, cash/F&O equities stay EQUITY. **Blast radius (hostile-review MINOR):** the precedence REORDER in isolation is a no-op for the legacy brute-force predicate (its index/reference sets are disjoint), but the PREDICATE SWAP intentionally re-buckets EVERY non-brute-forced index — not only FINNIFTY but also the spot-only / sectoral / broad-market indices (e.g. NIFTY IT) — from EQUITY → INDEX, which is the CORRECT asset-class label (they were never genuinely cash equities; the prior bucketing was the bug). The two surfaces share the by-TYPE index PREDICATE (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); /completeness additionally keeps a REFERENCE tier (India VIX) that /universe does not — they share the predicate, NOT full badge parity (hostile-review NIT). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `completeness.py` at 100% line+branch (new precedence test: VIX-reference-wins + FINNIFTY-as-index + RELIANCE-equity); `is_index_instrument` covered both branches in `tests/unit/test_universe.py` (IDX True for brute-forced/non-brute-forced/reference indices, EQ False); the 30 `/completeness` route integration tests green; ruff + mypy --strict + pyright clean. 🟡 NTM-constituent equities remain `equity` (the in-memory `is_reference_only` catches only the VIX reference INDEX today — unchanged, pre-existing, not in scope here). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pull change — DISPLAY categorisation only; the brute-force ENGINE tier (`is_in_brute_force_scope`) is untouched, so the swept universe is still exactly NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **Files:** `brutex/universe.py`, `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_universe.py`, `tests/unit/test_completeness.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-INDEX-CATEGORY-001. **Builds on** DEC-COMPLETENESS-SCOREBOARD-001 (#783 — the scoreboard categorisation), DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001 (#785 — the per-symbol map sharing the same category source), DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-REFTAG-001 (the reference-only tier that now wins precedence), is_in_brute_force_scope (the engine-tier predicate this is deliberately distinct from).

834. **DEC-WINDOW-RETRY-LEGEND-001 — the /coverage/windows page now carries a VISIBLE legend explaining `attempts` (pulls, not fetches), the in-pull 3× empty-retry, and `EMPTY x/3` (the cross-pull no-data streak), so the operator can read a row without the buried code comments** (2026-06-19, operator: "it should retry max 3 attempts and even in webpage also it should be reflected … how the fuck finnifty has expiries starting 2020 but … doesn't have one day or one min data"). **Why:** the page already SHOWED the retry signal (`EMPTY x/3` streak + `attempts` count) and the system already retries correctly — the in-pull empty-retry re-fetches a 0-bar window up to 3× per pull (DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 / DEC-OPTION-EMPTY-RETRY-001), and the cross-pull `empty_streak` re-checks every pull until 3 confirmations (`EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD=3`). But the MEANING lived only in a JS code comment, so the operator read `attempts 1, EMPTY 1/3` as "tried once, glitched" and concluded the retry was broken — when in fact FINNIFTY/SENSEX simply have NO Groww spot data before ~2025 / ~2022 (a genuine vendor gap: the live pull fetched 135,784 FINNIFTY 1-minute bars for 2025+ with the SAME symbol/segment, proving the request is correct and the empties are real vendor no-data, not a fetch bug — retrying cannot conjure data the vendor lacks). **What shipped (ADDITIVE, template-only):** a collapsible `<details>` legend in `fetch_windows.html` between the filter band and the table — `attempts` = pulls (each pull already re-fetches an empty window up to 3×); `EMPTY x/3` = clean-empty on x of 3 separate pulls, settled only at 3/3 (a 429/timeout preserves the streak); and the explicit note that a genuine vendor gap stays EMPTY however many times it is retried (Golden Rule #1 — never fabricated). No Python / engine / data / retry-logic change — the retry behaviour was already correct; this only makes it LEGIBLE. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — the legend renders on `/coverage/windows` (asserted in `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`); the 80 coverage + nav + ux-polish guard tests stay green; ruff clean (HTML-only). 🟡 the legend EXPLAINS the existing `EMPTY x/3` streak rather than adding a new per-window in-pull-retry counter (the 3× in-pull fetches are not separately persisted — a deeper ledger-schema change deferred; the streak is the durable signal). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pull / retry-logic change — display legibility only. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/fetch_windows.html`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-WINDOW-RETRY-LEGEND-001. **Builds on** DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (the per-window SUCCESS/EMPTY/FAILED page), DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-VISIBLE-001 (the `EMPTY x/3` streak display this annotates), DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 + DEC-OPTION-EMPTY-RETRY-001 (the 3× in-pull empty-retry the legend describes), DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 (the 2020 floor against which the FINNIFTY/SENSEX vendor gaps read as no-data).

835. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-CSV-READABLE-001 — the downloadable completeness CSV is made human-readable (plain-English headers) AND date-ENRICHED: its per-symbol spot detail now carries the explicit first→last bar date + from-2020 flag per dimension, the SAME rich info the `/universe` strip + the page show — so the report is never less informative than the page** (2026-06-19, operator: "why the coverage csv is not really human readable and helpful to understand easily … it looks so stale"; preview-confirmed via AskUserQuestion → "Readable + dated"). **Why:** the CSV (`scoreboard_to_csv`) used code-y headers (`full_1day`, `growing_or_partial`, `1day`/`1minute`) and — unlike the page — its DETAIL-spot section had ONLY the verdict, NOT the explicit dates that `per_symbol_completeness` (DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001) already computes; the data path is recomputed-live (NOT cached), so "stale" was the FORMAT being terser + less informative than the page, not old data. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, mostly string-formatting):** (1) `scoreboard_to_csv(board, per_symbol=None)` gained an optional `per_symbol` map — when supplied (production) the DETAIL-spot section emits the rich columns `1-day complete? · 1-day first bar · 1-day last bar · 1-day from 2020? · 1-minute … · Overall`; `None` keeps the compact verdict-only columns (backward-compatible, so the existing unit tests' terse data rows are byte-identical). Two pure O(1) helpers `_csv_date` (ISO string or empty cell) + `_csv_yes_no` (yes/no for the bool). (2) ALL section titles + column headers reworded to plain English ("Asset class", "Symbols", "Full 1-day", "1-day complete?", "Chain status", …) — commas removed from titles so `csv.writer` never quotes them (keeps the section-title lines clean + the `startswith` guards green).
