(3) the `/api/v1/completeness/scoreboard.csv` route builds BOTH the board AND the per-symbol map from ONE shared `_completeness_inputs` lake read (`_build_completeness_csv` / `_completeness_csv`; CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — no second read), passing `per_symbol` so every live download is date-enriched. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `completeness.py` at 100% line+branch (the rich path + both helper branches: dates-present, None-date→empty cell, from-2020 yes/no; the terse path stays covered by the pre-existing CSV tests); the live CSV route asserts the date columns + the no-lake CSV + the 503 paths (`tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`); ruff + mypy --strict + pyright clean. 🟡 the option DETAIL section keeps its existing year-span (no per-expiry dates — the vendor exposes no expected total, CLAUDE.md §6). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pull change — report serialisation only; the underlying scoreboard data is byte-identical (recomputed live, never cached). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_completeness.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-CSV-READABLE-001. **Builds on** DEC-COMPLETENESS-PAGE-001 (the CSV report this enriches), DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001 (the `per_symbol_completeness` date map it now reuses), DEC-COMPLETENESS-SCOREBOARD-001 (the board it serialises), DEC-COMPLETENESS-INDEX-CATEGORY-001 (#833 — the corrected asset-class categories the CSV groups by).

836. **DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 — the SPOT 1-minute fill now STARTS, per symbol, from that symbol's DISCOVERED 1-day start date (read from the lake's 1-day coverage), instead of blindly pulling 1-minute from the 2020 floor — the spot twin of the proven option/future 1-day-first pattern, so an index that only has Groww data from a later year (SENSEX ~2022, FINNIFTY ~2025) no longer plans + fetches years of never-fillable empty 1-minute windows** (2026-06-19, operator: "what about our auto one day pull at first and only from auto pull of one day starting date alone our one min will be generated … this one day required and one min entirely should be applicable across spot expiries contracts historical pull everywhere"). **Why:** the option/future pull already does this (DEC-HISTORICAL-1DAY-FIRST-001 / DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 #711 — a cheap 1-day pull PINS each contract's listing→expiry, and the heavy 1-minute fill runs only across that real life), but the SPOT pull (`pull_all_spot` / `pull_candles`) blindly planned + fetched 1-minute over the full `[2020-01-01, end)` range for EVERY symbol. A spot index does not begin on the same calendar day across vendors, so for SENSEX/FINNIFTY this planned thousands of pre-listing 1-minute windows that can only ever come back EMPTY — the operator-observed "stuck at partial / 2020→2024 empties". (Spot is the LAST **dashboard** candle-pull gap: options + futures already 1-day-first; expiries/contracts are metadata with no interval, N/A. SCOPE-HONEST caveat — the CLI live spot pull `cli.py` is NOT yet 2-phased: it still pulls 1-minute unbounded with `symbol_windows=None` — correct but un-optimised — so this PR scopes the fix to the dashboard `pull_all_spot`/`pull_candles`; the CLI parity is a deferred follow-up below.) **What shipped (ADDITIVE, the proven options template — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** (1) a new leaf `brutex/adapters/groww/spot_bounds.py` — `spot_daily_coverage(catalog, *, instrument, interval="1day")` reads a spot symbol's inclusive `[first,last]` 1-day coverage from the lake (the EXACT `exch_id`/`segment`/`symbol_name` coords `ingest_spot` writes under), folding global `min(first_ts)`/`max(last_ts)` to IST trading days; `spot_coverage_to_minute_window(coverage, *, full_start, full_end)` maps it to the half-open minute window where **start MOVES to the discovered listing day but end STAYS `full_end`** — the SPOT≠OPTION divergence: a spot index never expires, so its minute fill runs to the requested upper bound, NOT clamped to an expiry (a degenerate start≥end → the full-range never-skip fallback); `discover_spot_minute_windows(catalog, *, lake_root, instruments, full_start, full_end)` reconciles the catalog ONCE per DISTINCT spot segment present (never the giant FNO tree) and reads each symbol's coverage, OMITTING any symbol with NO 1-day data — the **3c rule** (operator-chosen 2026-06-19 via AskUserQuestion): a symbol the lake holds zero 1-day bars for has no anchor, so its 1-minute is SKIPPED + reported (never pulled blindly from 2020, never a fabricated start — Golden Rule #1); reuses the shared `ContractCoverage` (COMMON). (2) `run_groww_spot_ingest`(+`_with_retry`) gained `symbol_windows: SpotWindows | None` threaded via the new `_resolve_spot_window` (the spot twin of options' `_resolve_window`): applied to SUB-DAILY intervals ONLY (never `1day` — the coverage that produces the bound must keep advancing) and only for a symbol IN the map; absent symbol / `None` map → the global `(start,end)` (O(1) one dict lookup). (3) `plan_windows` + `reconcile_ledger_windows` + `reconcile_ledger_with_lake` (`window_ledger_store.py`) gained the SAME `symbol_windows` so the ledger PLANS + cold-start-SEEDS the bounded per-symbol minute windows — the planned/reconciled keys EQUAL the bounded fetched keys, so there are NO phantom pre-listing PLANNED rows AND no orphan SUCCESS seeds (a global-tiled seed anchored at 2020 would land a key the bounded plan never created — explicitly guarded). (4) `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` (`pull_controller.py`) now PHASE the pull (mirroring options' `pull_contract_candles`): 1-day FIRST over all symbols, then `_discover_minute_windows` reads the just-written (or pre-existing) 1-day coverage, then 1-minute runs over ONLY the symbols with coverage, each from its discovered start; the no-coverage symbols are logged + excluded (3c); a phase-1 auth/quota death skips phase 2 (global stop); ONE shared ledger spans both phases so live progress is continuous; the DEFAULT `1day`-only mode is byte-identical (only phase 1 runs, `symbol_windows=None`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #5 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `spot_bounds.py` + `run_ingest.py` + `window_ledger_store.py` + `pull_controller.py` at 100% line+branch via unit + property tests (coverage fold, start-moves/end-stays mapping, degenerate-window fallback, reconcile-unavailable + per-symbol-skip degrades, the daily-never-bounded + absent-symbol + None-map spine branches, the ledger bounded-tiling parity, and the controller phasing: 1day-only unchanged / 1minute-only derives-from-existing / both = 1day→derive→minute / 3c skip reported / global-stop skips phase-2 / dry-run no-catalog → {} → honest skip); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; existing pull/ledger/ingest suites green. O(1) per-symbol window lookup (one dict `get`); the discovery is O(partitions) catalog reads after a one-time O(P) reconcile (NOT O(1)-total — stated, not hidden). 🟡 this is a CORRECTNESS bound presented as an optimisation: the keep-first sink + WindowLedger already make the lake bytes identical (Golden Rule #7); bounding avoids the dead-period FIRST-pass requests AND the phantom ledger rows — it never narrows real data. 🟡 a spot symbol legitimately listed after 2020 now correctly starts its 1-minute at its listing day (not 2020); a symbol with no 1-day yet is skipped + reported (re-run after a 1-day pull). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit change — the pull throughput, pace bucket + 500/min governor are untouched; spot bars stay the 3 brute-force indices + the reference-only universe. 🟡 a 3c-/global-stop-skipped minute interval is reported `skipped` (we deliberately refused to query — no anchor), NEVER `no_data` (which means "vendor queried, returned empty") — the honest distinction; `pull_candles` was fixed to match `pull_all_spot` (hostile-review MINOR-1, Golden Rule #1 no-illusion). 🟡 DEFERRED follow-ups (hostile-review, both non-corrupting): (a) thread `symbol_windows` into the CLI live spot pull (`cli.py`) for full 1-day-first parity with the dashboard; (b) a one-shot prune of any stale phantom PLANNED minute rows a PRE-PR "both" pull may have left for a now-3c-skipped symbol (idempotent + no bad data today — only the `/coverage/windows` count is cosmetically affected). **Verification gates:** parallel hostile-reviewer (verdict **SHIP** — no BLOCKER/MAJOR; key-parity plan==fetch==seed, 3c skip, coverage-honesty, O-complexity, default byte-identity all confirmed) + workspace-health (**7805 Python tests + 534 Rust green**, ruff/format/pyright clean, mypy only the known `cma` env gap). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/spot_bounds.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py` (public `DAILY_INTERVAL` alias), `tests/` (spot_bounds + run_ingest + window_ledger + pull_controller suites), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001. **Builds on** DEC-HISTORICAL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (the option/future 2-phase 1-day-first→minute pattern this mirrors for spot), DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 (#711 — the `ContractCoverage` + `coverage_to_minute_window` shared core), DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#723 — the verify-first 1-day-only default this completes), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the ledger plan/reconcile it bounds), DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 (the 2020 floor the discovered start clamps to).

837. **DEC-GROWW-FORMING-BAR-PARSE-001 — the Groww candle parser now ACCEPTS the 6-element row the vendor returns for the CURRENT not-yet-finalised trading day's intraday bars (`[ts, open, high, low, close, volume]` — no trailing `open_interest` slot), padding `open_interest=None`, instead of HARD-requiring exactly 7 elements and quarantining the WHOLE symbol's intraday series** (2026-06-19, operator: pulled NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/FINNIFTY/SENSEX 1-minute with `to_date=today` and all 4 quarantined — `verdict: quarantined_symbols`, the live `brutex.log` showing `candle row 6300 must be a 7-element array, got ['2026-06-19T09:15:00', 23991.2, 23991.2, 23951.6, 23959.55, None]`). **Why:** `parse_candle_rows` (`brutex/adapters/groww/parser.py`) required `len(row) == 7` and unpacked `ts, o, h, l, c, volume, open_interest`. Settled historical bars are 7-element, but the CURRENT day's intraday bars come back 6-element (the `open_interest` slot is dropped + `volume` is typically `None`) until the vendor's EOD settlement — so a `to_date=today` 1-minute pull hit a `CandleParseError` on the first bar of today (row ~6300 = `2026-06-19T09:15:00`), which the spine quarantines as a TERMINAL per-`(symbol, interval)` failure (DEC-GROWW-QUARANTINE-BRUTEX-001) → the entire 1-minute series for ALL 4 indices was dropped (0 bars), the windows left `PLANNED (pending)` → the /completeness page read 1-minute "partial". NB this is ORTHOGONAL to + downstream of DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#836), which worked correctly (the log's `spot_bounds.derived: bounded=4` + the 1-day phase's 1614/364/1614/937 bars prove the 1-day-first discovery + 1-day pull succeeded); the quarantine was purely the parser rejecting the live-edge row shape. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, hardening — Golden Rule #1 "tolerate every vendor data shape", never drop a recoverable pull):** the parser accepts `len(row) in {6, 7}` (`_ACCEPTED_ROW_LENS`); a 6-element row unpacks `ts, o, h, l, c, volume` with `open_interest=None`; a 7-element row is unchanged. An index/spot row carries null volume/OI regardless, so accepting the shorter shape NEVER loses data — it only stops the still-settling live edge from quarantining the series. Rows of any OTHER length (≤5 or ≥8) STILL raise `CandleParseError` (fail-loud on a genuinely malformed/unexpected shape — the tolerance is exactly the documented 6-element current-session variant, nothing else). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `parser.py` at 100% line+branch (`tests/unit/test_groww_parser.py` +4: the exact log 6-element row parses with `open_interest=None`, a mixed 7-then-6 batch, a 5-element row still raises, an 8-element row still raises); the exact `brutex.log` crasher row reproduced + now parses; ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; 113 Groww ingest/candle/parser tests green (no regression — the change is purely additive). 🟡 a current-session bar pulled mid/just-post-session is stored with `volume`/`open_interest` as the vendor returns them at that moment (null for indices anyway); the default pull range still EXCLUDES today (previous-day end) so this only applies when the operator EXPLICITLY picks `to_date=today` (DEC-PULL-FUTURE-WINDOW-001). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit change — candle-parse robustness only. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/parser.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_parser.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-FORMING-BAR-PARSE-001. **Builds on** DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#836 — the 1-minute pull this unblocks at the live edge), DEC-GROWW-QUARANTINE-BRUTEX-001 (the per-`(symbol, interval)` terminal quarantine this stops a recoverable row from tripping), DEC-VENDOR-VOLUME-NORMALIZE-001 (the index null-volume rule that makes the shorter shape lossless), DEC-CANDLE-EMPTY-BAR-001 (the sibling graceful-skip the parser already had).

838. **DEC-CSV-FORMULA-INJECTION-001 — the downloadable completeness CSV report now NEUTRALISES spreadsheet formula-injection: any cell whose text starts with `= + - @` (or a leading TAB / CR) is prefixed with a single quote so Excel / Google Sheets / LibreOffice render it as literal text instead of EVALUATING it as a formula** (2026-06-19, the #791 hostile-review NIT-1 deferred follow-up — CSV/formula injection, OWASP). **Why:** `scoreboard_to_csv` (`brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`) wrote symbol / status / date cells straight through `csv.writer`. `csv` correctly RFC-4180-escapes commas + quotes, but does NOT defuse the SEPARATE "CSV injection" vector — a cell like `=HYPERLINK(...)` / `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` / `+...` / `-...` / `@...` is run as a FORMULA when the downloaded report is opened in a spreadsheet app, which can exfiltrate data or run a command. A symbol field is the realistic injection point (the lake admits vendor-supplied tickers). **What shipped (ADDITIVE, defense-in-depth — one source of truth):** a pure `_csv_safe(cell)` helper (a STRING cell whose first char is in `_CSV_INJECTION_LEADERS = frozenset("=+-@\t\r")` is prefixed with `'`; non-string / empty / non-leading cells pass through UNCHANGED so numeric columns + ISO dates stay numeric/plain) + a thin `_FormulaSafeWriter` wrapper around `csv.writer` whose `writerow` runs every cell through `_csv_safe`. Wrapping the writer ONCE neutralises EVERY one of the ~15 `writerow` call sites with a single-line change (`writer = _FormulaSafeWriter(csv.writer(...))`) — no per-call-site sprinkling, so a future row can never bypass the guard (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). The underlying `csv` comma/quote escaping is unchanged (the two guards compose). The hostile-review (verdict SHIP) NIT — a LEADING-WHITESPACE bypass (`" =cmd"`, which some apps strip-then-evaluate) — was folded in: `_csv_safe` ALSO prefixes a cell whose first NON-whitespace char is in `_CSV_FORMULA_FIRST_CHARS = frozenset("=+-@")` (the out-of-box edge; not exploitable on this report's only attacker field — symbols are EXCH-prefixed — but covered for completeness). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `completeness.py` at 100% line+branch (`tests/unit/test_completeness.py`: `_csv_safe` prefixes each of the 6 leaders + the leading-whitespace `" =cmd"` / `"  @SUM"` variants + passes through plain string / ISO date / int / None / empty / all-whitespace / whitespace-then-non-formula; an end-to-end `scoreboard_to_csv` with a `=HYPERLINK(0)` symbol round-trips to the quoted `'=HYPERLINK(0)` through a strict CSV reader); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; the 28 pre-existing completeness/CSV tests stay green (plain symbols/dates/counts are byte-unchanged — only a genuinely dangerous leader is altered). 🟡 a legitimate (non-malicious) value that happens to start with one of these chars is also quoted — harmless for this report (no spot cell legitimately leads with `=+-@`; counts are int, dates start with a digit). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / data change — report-serialisation hardening only; the scoreboard data is byte-identical (recomputed live, never cached). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`, `tests/unit/test_completeness.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CSV-FORMULA-INJECTION-001. **Builds on** DEC-COMPLETENESS-PAGE-001 (the CSV report this hardens), DEC-COMPLETENESS-CSV-READABLE-001 (#835 — the human-readable CSV whose hostile-review raised this NIT).

839. **DEC-WINDOW-INPULL-FETCHES-001 — the /coverage/windows (and /db) ledger now PERSISTS + DISPLAYS the in-pull vendor-fetch count, so the operator can SEE that the in-pull 3× empty/transient retry fired — previously it was DEBUG-only and the page showed `attempts 1` with no sign the retry ran** (2026-06-19, operator, after a clean 279/279 spot pull: "see if it retried three times means then why this is not displayed in the webpage why why why?"). **Why:** the in-pull empty-retry (DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001) re-fetches a clean 0-bar window up to `_DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 3` times WITHIN a single pull (`brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py` `_ingest_one_window`; the option twin in `option_ingest.py`), but it only logged `ingest.window.empty_retry` at DEBUG and recorded nothing — so on the operator's INFO-level log AND on /coverage/windows the genuine-gap EMPTY rows (FINNIFTY/SENSEX early years per DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001) showed `EMPTY 1/3 · attempts 1` with the 3 re-fetches invisible. `attempts` counts PULLS (one per `WindowLedger.record`), not the network fetches inside one. **What shipped (ADDITIVE — one new ledger column, backward-compatible):** (1) `WindowLedgerRecord` gains `in_pull_fetches: int = 0` — the LAST pull's vendor-fetch count (1 = first-try win, >1 = the retry fired up to `empty_retry_attempts`, 0 = a never-fetched PLANNED row); OVERWRITTEN per pull (NOT accumulated), so re-running the SAME pull is bit-identical (Golden Rule #7). (2) `WindowLedger.record` gains an `in_pull_fetches=1` param (the default keeps every legacy single-fetch caller honest); `plan`→0, `seed_lake_success`→1, `settle_known_gap`→1. (3) `to_rows`/`from_rows` carry it as the 13th tuple element; `window_ledger_store` appends the `in_pull_fetches` Parquet column LAST — exactly as `empty_streak` was (DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 R1) — so a legacy Parquet WITHOUT it loads cleanly (`_derive_in_pull_fetches`: PLANNED→0, else 1; the legacy status-log migration derives the same floor). (4) the spot + option spines count the fetches and thread them into BOTH the transient-FAILED and the SUCCESS/EMPTY `record` calls; each emits ONE INFO `…empty_after_retries {fetches:N}` when the retry fired AND the window stayed empty (the per-attempt log stays DEBUG), so the retry is visible in the log too. (5) /coverage/windows gains a "Fetches" column (muted `1`, amber `↻ N` when >1, `—` for a never-fetched row) + an updated `winhelp` legend; the /db `window-ledger` grid gains the matching column. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `window_ledger.py`, `window_ledger_store.py`, `ingest.py`, `option_ingest.py` all at 100% line+branch (a 3× empty retry records `in_pull_fetches == 3`; a first-try win records 1; a transient FAILED records its fetch count; the legacy-Parquet derive covers PLANNED→0 + non-PLANNED→1; the save→load round-trip preserves a >1 count; the INFO summary fires once on retry-then-empty and is silent on a first-try win); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean. 🟡 the count is the LAST pull's value (overwrite, not cumulative) — by design, mirroring `last_error`/`last_attempt_at`; the cross-pull history stays in `attempts` + `empty_streak`. 🟡 a legacy pre-feature pull's TRUE in-pull retry count is unrecorded — the derive shows the honest floor (1) until the next pull stamps the exact count. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / data change — observability + ledger-schema only; the lake bars are untouched. **Files:** `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/fetch_windows.html`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger.py`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-WINDOW-INPULL-FETCHES-001. **Builds on** DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 (the 3× in-pull retry this exposes), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the unified ledger + its append-a-column-LAST backward-compat pattern), DEC-WINDOW-RETRY-LEGEND-001 (#834 — the winhelp legend this extends), DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#836 — the per-symbol 1-day-first bounds that produce the genuine-gap EMPTY rows).
840. **DEC-FNO-ONECLICK-HISTORICAL-001 — the one-click multi-select F&O historical pull: ticking many F&O symbols + clicking "⤓ Pull historical" now runs, per F&O-eligible selected underlying, the GUARDED metadata refresh (enumerate expiries + contracts) THEN the contract candle pull over the freshly-cached registry rows — futures AND options — by COMPOSING the two existing spines (never a new fused engine); this ALSO formally SUPERSEDES the stale "never pull futures" decree DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 (#602) for the historical-lake pull** (2026-06-19, operator decree). **Why:** the metadata/historical split shipped two power-user buttons — "⛓ Pull expiries + contracts" (metadata-only, multi-select OK; DEC-DERIV-METADATA-ROUTE-001) and "⤓ Pull historical" (candles for an ALREADY-cached single underlying / chain / contract / all; DEC-DERIV-PULL-HISTORICAL-001) — so a multi-select historical pull required the operator to click metadata first, then historical, per name. The operator asked for the one-click fusion over the multi-select: tick many F&O names, click once, and for each have the chain enumerated then its contracts' candles pulled (both FUT and CE/PE). Separately, the old never-futures decree #602 (a Dhan-era quota-protection rule) is contradicted by the later Groww futures-ingest work (DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 #707, DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 #720) and this spec; it is hereby SUPERSEDED for the historical-LAKE pull (the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX only; this is the lake, CLAUDE.md §3). **What shipped (ADDITIVE — a thin orchestrator + a route branch + UI wiring; the two existing buttons are byte-unchanged, the metadata/candle split is preserved):** (1) a NEW `brutex/dashboard/composite_pull.py` — `pull_historical_for_underlyings(instruments, *, reference_only_ids, registry, coverage_store, lake_root, dry_run, intervals, years, …)` + a `CompositePullReport` carrying BOTH sub-reports. It partitions the selection with the SAME reference-only guard the metadata route uses (DEC-SKIP-REF-METADATA-001 — index / India VIX / non-F&O NTM are SKIPPED before any network call, a TRUE zero-call no-op, REPORTED never dropped), then for the tradable subset runs phase (a) `pull_expiries_contracts` (the metadata enumerator — FUT + CE + PE, no side filter) THEN phase (b) `pull_contract_candles` over the FRESHLY re-read `ContractRow` rows (`_select_fresh_contracts`). The two spines are COMPOSED, not fused — the candle engine receives a CONCRETE registry selection and NEVER re-enumerates (the decommissioned fused `pull_all_derivatives` anti-pattern is NOT resurrected). A tradable name with an empty chain (dry-run / no live contracts) honestly skips phase (b) (no fabricated contract, Golden Rule #1). (2) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-historical` route gains `?symbols=a,b,c` + an `enumerate=true` flag that dispatch to a new `_start_composite_historical_pull` closure (resolve symbols → 400 on unknown/empty; partition + report the reference-only skip; ALL-reference-only is an honest `started: False` no-op; run the composite on the single-flight `_pull_job`). The single-underlying / contract / kind / all grammar is byte-unchanged (back-compat preserved). (3) `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` — the "⤓ Pull historical" button now drives BOTH modes: a multi-select sends `?enumerate=true&symbols=…` (the composite over the same selection the spot / metadata buttons use); a single highlight keeps the original `?underlying=…` cached-chain pull. `updateMultiBtn` enables + count-labels the button on any ticked rows OR a single highlight. The two existing buttons + the `auto-retries until clean` tooltip survive. **Safety (the operator's explicit ask):** selecting ALL symbols including an index / India VIX / a non-F&O name enumerates + pulls ZERO contracts for every reference-only underlying (the partition runs before any `get_expiries`); proven by a test that asserts the reference-only names trigger no vendor call and never reach the registry. **Idempotence (Golden Rule #7):** phase (b) shares the WindowLedger, so a second composite run over the same selection skips already-settled windows (`is_skippable`) and re-fetches ONLY non-settled ones — proven by a test where the second run fetches zero candles. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `composite_pull.py` at 100% line+branch (9 unit cases: phase-a-before-phase-b ordering + both spines invoked; reference-only zero-call no-op in a mixed AND an all-ref selection; FUT + CE + PE all pulled; the second-run window skip; the empty-chain honest degrade; `to_dict` both-present and null-sub-report shapes; the public surface) and the new app.py route lines at 100% line+branch (route tests: `?symbols=` starts the job with the reported skip set; `enumerate=true` without `?symbols=` is a 400; unknown symbol is a 400; all-reference-only is an honest no-op; bad `from_date` is a 400; single-underlying back-compat preserved; the page sends the composite query); ruff + ruff format --check + mypy --strict (changed modules) + pyright (changed modules) clean. 🟡 NOT O(1)-total — both phases are network-bound (one `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` per cell + one `get_historical_candles` per contract-window); the composite optimises the work set (reference-only skip + incremental window skip), it does NOT make the pull O(1)-total. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope change — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; futures + the multi-select composite are LAKE / REFERENCE_ONLY only (CLAUDE.md §3). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/composite_pull.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (route branch + `_start_composite_historical_pull`), `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` (button wiring); tests `tests/unit/test_composite_pull.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_historical_route.py` (composite-branch cases), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-ONECLICK-HISTORICAL-001. **Supersedes (for the historical-lake pull):** DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 (#602, the Dhan-era never-futures rule). **Builds on:** DEC-DERIV-PULL-HISTORICAL-001 (the candle spine this composes), DEC-DERIV-METADATA-ROUTE-001 (the metadata spine this composes), DEC-SKIP-REF-METADATA-001 (the reference-only guard reused as the safety partition), DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (#707, the futures ingest path), DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 (#720, the futures-in-scope precedent), DEC-HISTORICAL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (the 1-day-first phase the candle pull runs), DEC-GROWW-DERIV-UNTIL-CLEAN-001 (the until-clean default).
841. **DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 — a genuine-gap fetch window that is EMPTY after the FULL in-pull retry AND is OLD enough that vendor data can never appear now settles SKIPPED after ONE pull, instead of needing the conservative 3 separate EMPTY pulls; RECENT windows keep the 3-pull EMPTY-streak** (2026-06-19, operator-locked decision). **Why:** the across-pull EMPTY→SKIPPED promotion (DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 / DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 R1) requires `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD = 3` SEPARATE pulls before a genuinely-empty window stops costing a re-fetch. That conservatism is correct for a RECENT window (a just-missed backfill or still-settling edge MUST be allowed to fill on a later pull), but it is WASTED on an OLD genuine gap (e.g. a FINNIFTY/SENSEX pre-listing early-year window, DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001): Groww serves a stable 2020+ history and any backfill lag is DAYS, not months (CLAUDE.md §6), so a window whose `window_end` is months in the past that came back empty across the in-pull 3× retry will be empty FOREVER — re-fetching it on two more whole pulls only burns quota + leaves it "pending" on /completeness in the meantime. **What shipped (ADDITIVE — a transient per-call decision, NO new stored field / NO serialisation change):** (1) `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py` gains `OLD_GAP_HORIZON_DAYS: int = 60` (a window whose `window_end` is > 60 days in the past can never gain vendor data — comfortably wider than any observed Groww backfill lag, so it never fast-settles a gap that could still legitimately fill) + `CONFIRMED_EMPTY_MIN_FETCHES: int = 2` (the COMMON "the in-pull retry must have re-hit the window ≥2× and stayed empty" threshold — a single glitch-prone fetch is NOT enough, which also excludes the degenerate `empty_retry_attempts <= 1` single-fetch case). (2) `WindowLedger.record` gains a keyword `settle_empty: bool = False` — when the classified status is EMPTY and `settle_empty` is True it sets `status = SKIPPED` + `empty_streak = self._threshold` (terminal in ONE pull, the SAME persisted shape a normal threshold settle leaves); when True on a SUCCESS / FAILED it is IGNORED (a no-op — never settle real data or an error as empty). The default False is byte-identical to today; the resulting SKIPPED status + streak persist through the existing columns (no Parquet/round-trip change). (3) the spot spine (`ingest._ingest_one_window`) computes `confirmed_empty_after_retry = (not raw_bars) and fetch_count >= CONFIRMED_EMPTY_MIN_FETCHES` and `is_old = window_end < old_cutoff` (where `old_cutoff = now_date − OLD_GAP_HORIZON_DAYS`, derived ONCE in `ingest_spot` off the `now_ist` clock — **production uses the REAL IST wall clock by design** (`_now_ist`; a window's "old"-ness must be judged against the real today, never an injected range-reference), the clock is injectable ONLY so tests can FREEZE it for determinism — threaded down via a new `old_cutoff` param), and passes `settle_empty = confirmed_empty_after_retry and is_old` to the SUCCESS/EMPTY `record` (the transient-FAILED `record` does NOT — errors are not empties). (4) the option spine (`option_ingest.ingest_option_contract`) does the same using the contract window's `clamped_end` + the `now_ist` clock it already threads — an expired contract's old windows are permanent gaps. (5) the `…empty_after_retries` INFO log (DEC-WINDOW-INPULL-FETCHES-001) gains a `settled=True/False` field so the log is honest about whether the empty window became terminal SKIPPED this pull. **Idempotent + monotonic (Golden Rule #7):** a window only ages INTO "old", never back, so re-runs are stable; the SKIPPED+streak shape is identical to a normal settle. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `window_ledger.py`, `ingest.py`, `option_ingest.py` all at 100% line+branch (ledger: `settle_empty=True` settles an EMPTY in one record with streak==threshold + is_skippable True; `settle_empty=True` on a SUCCESS / FAILED is a no-op; default False keeps the conservative 1/3 streak. spot: an OLD genuine-empty window with an injected 2026 clock settles SKIPPED in ONE pull, in_pull_fetches==3; a RECENT empty window stays EMPTY 1/3; an OLD window with `empty_retry_attempts=1` (one fetch, not confirmed) is NOT fast-settled. option: an OLD expired-contract empty window settles SKIPPED in one pull; a recent one stays EMPTY); ruff + ruff format --check + mypy --strict (changed modules) + pyright (changed modules) clean. The pre-existing `test_empty_windows_are_recorded_empty` was updated to the new age-gated reality (a 2020→2026 backfill yields {EMPTY, SKIPPED} — old gaps fast-settle, recent ones stay EMPTY) AND now **monkeypatches `ingest._now_ist` to FREEZE the gate clock** to its fixed `_BULK_NOW`, so the boundary assertion is deterministic and can never become a wall-clock time-bomb (the hostile-review FIX-FIRST finding — the spot production path reads the real clock, so the test must freeze it rather than key the assertion off a `now=` the gate ignores); the conservative-EMPTY tests gained an injected RECENT clock so they still pin the unchanged across-pull behaviour. 🟡 the 60-day horizon is a deliberately-conservative heuristic, NOT a vendor-documented backfill SLA — it only ever turns an in-pull-confirmed-empty OLD window terminal one pull sooner; it never masks a window with data (the `settle_empty` no-op on SUCCESS guards that) and never fast-settles a RECENT window. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-data change — ledger skip-timing + observability only; the lake bars are untouched. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001. **Builds on** DEC-WINDOW-INPULL-FETCHES-001 (#839 — the `in_pull_fetches` count this fast-settle keys its "confirmed across the in-pull retry" decision on, + the `…empty_after_retries` log it adds `settled` to), DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 (the in-pull 3× empty retry that produces the confirmed empty), DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 / DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the across-pull EMPTY→SKIPPED threshold this fast-settles past for OLD gaps while preserving it for RECENT ones), DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#836 — the per-symbol 1-day-first bounds that surface the genuine-gap early-year EMPTY windows).

842. **DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 — when a `1day` spot window comes back EMPTY from Groww but the lake holds the matching `1minute`, the missing daily bars are now DERIVED by resampling the 1-minute (midnight-IST stamped to match the vendor daily convention) and the window is recorded SUCCESS — instead of being settled SKIPPED forever; this RECOVERS the recent ~6-month daily gap Groww serves at 1-minute but not 1-day for cash equities** (2026-06-19, operator-locked decision; the locked Fix #1 of the post-#798 plan). **Why:** a deep log analysis of a clean universe pull found ~83 `1day` windows EMPTY (zero `1minute`), 48/50 stocks on the IDENTICAL `2025-11-30 → 2026-05-29` window, while the SAME range IS served at `1minute` and the `IDX` indices' `1day` is unaffected — i.e. Groww's `get_historical_candles(candle_interval="1day", segment="CASH")` does not serve the most-recent ~6 months of DAILY bars for single stocks. A retry can never fix a SYSTEMATIC vendor empty (DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 #841 would even fast-settle those old gaps SKIPPED, permanently dropping daily coverage the 1-minute can supply). The daily data EXISTS — it is derivable. **The linchpin (verified, not assumed):** a vendor `1day` bar is stamped at **midnight IST** (00:00 IST = 18:30 UTC of the PRIOR calendar day) — confirmed by `brutex/adapters/groww/spot_bounds.py` ("a Jan-1-IST bar lives in the December UTC partition") + the `test_daily_coverage_cross_utc_month_midnight_ist_golden` / `test_load_prev_day_ist_date_differs_from_utc_date` golden tests — whereas the shared `tf_resampler.resample_1m_to_tf` labels its daily bucket at 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC). So the fix REUSES that resampler ONLY for the OHLCV aggregation (open=first/high=max/low=min/close=last/volume=sum — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, never re-implemented) then RE-STAMPS every derived bar to midnight IST with the SAME fixed +05:30 offset the Groww parser uses, so a resampled daily bar's UTC instant is byte-identical to a vendor-parsed `00:00:00 IST` bar (the dedup identity). **What shipped (ADDITIVE — a new pure module + a quarantined post-phase glue; no engine/schema/scope change):** (1) a NEW `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` — `resample_1m_to_daily(df_1m, *, before)` (reuse + midnight-IST re-stamp + a forming-session guard that DROPS any session whose IST date >= today, so today's still-forming session is never written as a final bar — no look-ahead; `open_interest=None` to match a vendor spot daily); `fill_daily_from_minute(*, read_1m, write_1day, before)` (pure, injected I/O — an EMPTY 1-minute slice is an honest no-op, NEVER an invented bar, Golden Rule #1); `plan_daily_resample_windows(records, *, daily_interval)` (selects `1day` windows the ledger settled EMPTY/SKIPPED via the empty path — `empty_streak > 0`); `reconcile_daily_from_minute(...)` (drives the per-window fill over the SHARED WindowLedger, recording a filled window SUCCESS with `in_pull_fetches=0` — the honest "a resample made zero vendor calls" provenance, which RESETS `empty_streak` so a now-has-data window is never re-promoted SKIPPED — quarantining EACH window so one bad slice never blanks the pass); + the `# pragma: no cover` window-bounded `make_lake_read_1m_window` (returns an EMPTY frame when no 1-minute exists, never raises) + `make_lake_write_1day` (writes through the SAME ParquetBarSink the vendor spine uses, so the bar is byte-indistinguishable + 2-dp-snapped + keep-first-merged). (2) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — a NEW `_resample_daily_after_pull` glue (the twin of `_autoderive_after_pull`) called at the END of the spot pull's try block (AFTER both phases, BEFORE the `finally`'s `end_pull_ledger` so a fill's SUCCESS persists with the ledger) for live pulls only; binds the per-window builders + runs the reconcile, wrapped so NO failure here can ever fail the pull. **Idempotent (Golden Rule #7):** a re-run re-resamples the same 1-minute → identical bars → keep-first merge adds 0; a filled window is SUCCESS → excluded from the next plan; a later REAL vendor `1day` fetch shares the timestamp → dedups keep-first (never a double bar per session). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `spot_daily_resample.py` at 100% line+branch (19 unit cases: midnight-IST stamp == 2025-11-27T18:30Z for a 2025-11-28 IST session + OHLCV oracle; multi-session ascending; the forming-guard both arms; empty-frame + no-minute no-op with NO write call; float-noise kept full-precision; the planner's every exclude arm (non-daily / SUCCESS / FAILED / PLANNED / SKIPPED-streak-0) + full-ISO date parse + custom interval; the reconcile filled/no-minute/errored arms with SUCCESS+in_pull_fetches=0+empty_streak-reset asserted) + a 4-case integration round-trip (real sink + the pragma builders: cross-UTC-month partition placement Dec/Jan, OHLCV read-back via `query_candles`, window-bounded exclusion, byte-identical idempotent re-run, keep-first dedup vs a pre-seeded vendor daily); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict (changed modules) + pyright (changed modules + tests) clean. 🟡 the midnight-IST convention is verified from 3 repo tests, NOT re-confirmed against the live API offline — but the reconcile only fills windows the vendor returned EMPTY (no vendor bar exists to mismatch against) and any future divergence surfaces as a logged BarConflict (keep-first, visible, never silent), and the exact UTC instant is pinned by a golden so a convention drift fails CI loudly rather than corrupting the lake. 🟡 the verify-first `1day`-only default self-heals NOTHING unless 1-minute was also pulled — surfaced honestly via the structured log, never invented. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit change — lake daily backfill only; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **Files:** `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` (glue + call site + TYPE_CHECKING imports), `tests/unit/test_spot_daily_resample.py` (new), `tests/integration/test_spot_daily_resample_roundtrip.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001. **Supersedes (for any window 1-minute can supply):** DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 (#841 — an old empty daily gap is now RECOVERED from 1-minute, not just fast-settled SKIPPED). **Builds on:** DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#836 — the 1-day-first phase model whose EMPTY daily windows this fills), DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 + DEC-RESAMPLE-ANCHOR-002 (the canonical resampler reused), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the write-boundary 2-dp snap), DEC-TF-MATERIALIZE-001/002 (the injected-I/O materialiser pattern reused), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the SUCCESS-resets-streak ledger record).

843. **DEC-GROWW-CANDLE-TS-SPACE-001 — the `get_historical_candles` request now sends Groww's DOCUMENTED `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` SPACE-separated timestamp format instead of the ISO `T` separator the window tiler emits** (2026-06-19, ships WITH DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 #842). **Why:** windows are tiled with `datetime.isoformat()`, which emits `2025-11-30T00:00:00` (a `T`), but the API reference (`docs/groww/api-reference/03-backtesting.md`) specifies `start_time`/`end_time` as `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss` with a SPACE — and a parser that silently returns empty on a slightly-off datetime is a plausible secondary contributor to the empty-daily symptom #842 addresses. **What shipped (ADDITIVE — a one-line normalization at the single vendor boundary):** `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py` `historical_candles` now passes `start.replace("T", " ")` / `end.replace("T", " ")` to the SDK — the ONE funnel every candle call (spot + options) shares (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON), so the request side is aligned to the documented contract in one place. The `DateWindow` keys + the ledger ISO form are UNCHANGED (only the SDK call string is normalized). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — the client test asserts the SDK receives `start_time="2025-11-30 00:00:00"` (space, no `T`) AND that an epoch-seconds bound (no `T`) is unchanged by the replace (a safe no-op); ruff + mypy --strict + pyright clean. 🟡 whether the space form is strictly REQUIRED by the live SDK is UNVERIFIED offline — our own parser already accepts both (`parse_timestamp_ist` strips the `T`), so the change is a documented-contract ALIGNMENT that is correct either way and cannot regress a working call (the replace is a no-op when there is no `T`). 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-data change — request-format alignment only. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_client.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-CANDLE-TS-SPACE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (the Groww client this normalizes), DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 (#842 — the daily-empty fix this ships alongside).

844. **DEC-UNTIL-CLEAN-ALL-OUTSTANDING-001 — the cross-pull until-clean loop now re-pulls EVERY genuinely-outstanding window (PLANNED + FAILED + EMPTY-below-threshold) until each is SUCCESS or SKIPPED, instead of stopping the instant the TRANSIENT failures clear — the "pull until it fetches a successful response" guarantee** (2026-06-19, operator-locked; the Fix #2 of the post-#798 plan). **Why:** the operator saw a pull report "done" with PLANNED / EMPTY windows still unfetched ("why the fuck even planned or failed or empty also didn't get included in this attempt"). The cross-pull `run_until_clean` loop keyed its `stop_clean` decision EXCLUSIVELY on `GrowwIngestReport.still_failed_windows` (`decide_until_clean`, `ingest_common.py`), which sums only the TRANSIENT per-window FAILED count across successful pairs — it does NOT count PLANNED (never-fetched) windows or EMPTY-below-threshold windows (which need up to `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD = 3` pulls to settle to SKIPPED). So the loop hit `still_failed_windows == 0` and returned `stop_clean` while PLANNED + EMPTY windows remained outstanding in the ledger. **The deeper finding (the fix is cheap, not a re-architecture):** the window SELECTION was already correct — `ingest_spot` re-tiles the FULL `[start, end)` range every round and skips a window only when `ledger.is_skippable` (SUCCESS / SKIPPED only), so PLANNED + FAILED + EMPTY-below-threshold are ALL re-fetched every round automatically, and each EMPTY re-fetch bumps `empty_streak` toward the SKIPPED promotion. The spine does the right work each round; the LOOP just exited too early. So this is a LOOP CONTINUE-CONDITION change, not a selection change. **What shipped (ADDITIVE — back-compat by an opt-in signal; every legacy caller byte-identical):** (1) `UntilCleanRound` gains three optional fields (`outstanding_windows`, `settled_windows`, `streak_total`), all `None` for legacy rounds (the CLI, the options path, `historical_pull`) so positional construction `UntilCleanRound(0, False)` is unchanged. (2) `decide_until_clean` gains a keyword `outstanding_windows: int | None = None` — when provided, the `stop_clean` test keys on `outstanding_windows == 0` (`total - settled`: PLANNED + FAILED + EMPTY) instead of `still_failed_windows == 0`; `None` falls back to the legacy test (byte-identical). Priority order (auth > clean > quota > no_progress > budget) unchanged. (3) `run_until_clean` re-keys the `made_progress` measure on the outstanding path to **`settled` strictly rose OR (`settled` flat AND the summed `empty_streak` rose)** — the SECONDARY streak signal is essential: a round that only advanced an EMPTY window toward its SKIPPED threshold (settled still flat) must count as progress, else `stop_no_progress` would halt the loop BEFORE a recent EMPTY window settles in 3 rounds. `settled` is monotonic (a SUCCESS/SKIPPED row is never un-settled), so it never falsely flags progress; the legacy `still_failed`-decreasing measure is preserved when `outstanding_windows is None`. (4) only the ledger-backed `pull_all_spot._run_phase._round_runner` populates the new fields (from `ledger.progress_counts()` + a once-per-round single-lock O(N) `ledger.streak_total()` fold (no sort)); a dry-run (`ledger is None`) leaves them `None` → legacy behaviour. **Termination (proven):** `settled` is monotonic non-decreasing and bounded by `total`; a productive round strictly raises `settled` or the streak-sum; when neither moves (`stop_when_stuck=True`, the auto-resume path) the round trips `stop_no_progress` — so a genuinely-stuck window (a quarantined / unresolvable symbol's PLANNED windows, e.g. BAJAJ-AUTO) self-terminates the loop within a few rounds (once the good symbols settle and the streak-sum plateaus), NEVER churning to the budget cap. The bounded outer budget (`max_rounds`) is the final backstop. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `ingest_common.py` at 100% line+branch (8 new cases: `decide` continues when only PLANNED remain + `outstanding==0` is clean regardless of stale transient + `None` falls back; `run_until_clean` drives PLANNED to clean via settled-rise, the EMPTY-streak-as-progress case that would otherwise stop one round too early, the all-flat `stop_no_progress` futile-window termination at round 2 not 50, and the `stop_when_stuck=False` budget bound) + `pull_controller.py` round-runner at 100% line+branch; ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; the 137-case until-clean + controller back-compat suite is byte-unchanged. 🟡 the per-symbol FUTILE-EXCLUSION (dropping a permanently-quarantined symbol like BAJAJ-AUTO from the worklist) is DEFERRED to Fix #3 (DEC owns symbol resolution/exclusion); Fix #2's termination already bounds the futile case via `stop_no_progress` (it does not spin), so the exclusion is an efficiency/cleanliness follow-up, not a correctness gap. 🟡 the "pull until successful" guarantee holds for the `until_clean=True` path (the dashboard retry / auto-resume); the one-click single-pass default (`until_clean=False`) is unchanged — flipping that default is a separate operator UX decision, not folded here. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-data change — loop continue-condition + observability only. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_ingest_common_until_clean.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-UNTIL-CLEAN-ALL-OUTSTANDING-001. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the `progress_counts`/`settled`/`is_skippable` authority this keys on), DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 (the `run_until_clean` / `stop_when_stuck` driver extended), DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the 3-pull EMPTY→SKIPPED settle the loop now runs long enough to reach), DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 (#841, the 1-round fast-settle that interacts), DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 (#842, whose resampled-fill SUCCESS records raise `settled`, helping this measure). **Relates to:** Fix #3 (BAJAJ-AUTO unresolved-symbol resolution — the upstream owner of worklist exclusion).

845. **DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001 — a HYPHENATED single-stock ticker (`BAJAJ-AUTO`, `M&M`…) now resolves to its Groww `groww_symbol` instead of erroring `OutOfScopeError` every pull; resolution is MASTER-AUTHORITATIVE (by the vendor's own `(exchange, trading_symbol)` / `groww_symbol` index keys), never reconstructed off a hyphen guess** (2026-06-19, operator-locked; the Fix #3 of the post-#798 plan). **Why:** `GrowwMarketAdapter.fetch_ohlcv` (`brutex/adapters/groww/adapter.py`) built the groww_symbol with `symbol if "-" in symbol else f"{exchange}-{symbol}"` — a guard meant to detect an ALREADY-PREFIXED contract groww_symbol (e.g. `NSE-NIFTY-25Aug26-FUT`) and not re-prefix it. But a hyphen INSIDE a single-stock ticker (`BAJAJ-AUTO`, the vendor `trading_symbol`) tripped the same guard, so the adapter looked the BARE ticker up in `by_groww_symbol` (which is keyed on the prefixed `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO`), missed, and raised `OutOfScopeError("symbol not in Groww universe: BAJAJ-AUTO")` — quarantining every hyphenated F&O stock on every pull (perpetually PLANNED, never fetched). This is the concrete futile case DEC-UNTIL-CLEAN-ALL-OUTSTANDING-001 (#844) deferred. **The fix is master-authoritative (Golden Rule #1 — no invented mapping):** (1) `fetch_ohlcv` now resolves by the vendor's OWN keys — a bare spot/index trading symbol (incl. a hyphenated stock) resolves via the `(exchange, trading_symbol)` index `by_exchange_symbol` (its `symbol_name` was loaded verbatim from the master's `trading_symbol`, so it is resolvable by construction) and the groww_symbol handed to the vendor is the master's REAL `groww_symbol_by_pair` value (a NEW O(1) `InstrumentIndex` map built in lockstep with `by_exchange_symbol`), NEVER a reconstructed `EXCH-symbol` — so a VERBOSE-symbol index like `MIDCPNIFTY` (`trading_symbol` `"NIFTY MID SELECT"` ≠ the `MIDCPNIFTY` component of `NSE-MIDCPNIFTY`) sends the correct `NSE-MIDCPNIFTY`, not a garbage `NSE-NIFTY MID SELECT` (the hostile-review BLOCKER: reconstruction would have downgraded a loud `OutOfScopeError` to a silent wrong-fetch for the verbose-index class the repo already documents). An already-prefixed contract groww_symbol (whose `trading_symbol` is the un-hyphenated `NIFTY25Aug26FUT`) misses the `(exchange, symbol)` index and falls through to `by_groww_symbol`, used AS-IS. No `"-" in symbol` heuristic, no reconstruction off a guess. (2) `brutex/data/validation/nse_equity_oneday.py` `normalize_equity_symbol` strips ONLY a leading exchange prefix (`NSE-` / `BSE-`), not every hyphen — the prior `split("-", 1)[1]` mangled `BAJAJ-AUTO` → `AUTO`, breaking the bhavcopy cross-check + the verify fetch for every hyphenated stock; now `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO` → `BAJAJ-AUTO` and a bare `BAJAJ-AUTO` is kept whole. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `adapter.py` at 100% line+branch (a hyphenated `BAJAJ-AUTO` resolves to `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO` CASH + returns bars; an ampersand `M&M` resolves to `NSE-M&M`; a VERBOSE-symbol index `NIFTY MID SELECT` sends the master `NSE-MIDCPNIFTY` not a reconstructed `NSE-NIFTY MID SELECT`; an already-prefixed `NSE-NIFTY-25Aug26-FUT` is used as-is on the FNO segment; a genuinely-unknown hyphenated ticker raises `OutOfScopeError` naming the symbol) + `instruments.py` at 100% line+branch (the `groww_symbol_by_pair` map) + `nse_equity_oneday.py` at 100% line+branch (the parametrized normalize cases gain `BAJAJ-AUTO`→`BAJAJ-AUTO`, `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO`→`BAJAJ-AUTO`, `bse-m&m`→`M&M`); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean; the 72-case adapter + equity-verify suite is byte-unchanged. 🟡 the EXACT Groww-master spelling of `BAJAJ-AUTO`'s groww_symbol cannot be confirmed OFFLINE (no Groww instrument-master fixture for a hyphenated stock exists in-repo) — the fix is deliberately MASTER-AUTHORITATIVE (it sends the vendor's OWN `groww_symbol` column verbatim via `groww_symbol_by_pair`, never reconstructs by guess), so it is correct for whatever the real vendor spelling is — hyphenated stock OR verbose-symbol index alike. 🟡 the genuinely-unresolvable-symbol EXCLUSION-from-the-worklist (so a symbol that is in NO master spelling is reported + not retried) is the remaining half of #844's deferred futile-exclusion — once this fix lands, `BAJAJ-AUTO` RESOLVES and is no longer the futile case, and #844's `stop_no_progress` already BOUNDS any genuinely-stuck symbol (it never spins to the budget cap); a dedicated pre-flight worklist partition is a follow-up, not a correctness gap. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-data change — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; the F&O single stocks are lake / REFERENCE_ONLY (CLAUDE.md §3). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/adapter.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py` (the `groww_symbol_by_pair` map + `build_index`), `brutex/data/validation/nse_equity_oneday.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py` (quarantine-comment honesty), `tests/unit/test_groww_adapter.py`, `tests/unit/test_nse_equity_oneday.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001 (the Groww adapter + instrument index this resolves through), DEC-UNTIL-CLEAN-ALL-OUTSTANDING-001 (#844 — whose deferred futile-exclusion this completes for the hyphenated-symbol case), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean universe whose F&O stocks include the hyphenated tickers).

846. **DEC-CLAUDEMD-ADAPTER-CITE-RECONCILE-001 — CLAUDE.md §6 symbol-resolution rows refreshed after the Track-1 data-quality fix series (#799/#800/#801) merged: the stale `groww/adapter.py` line citations + the now-incomplete "resolved via `by_groww_symbol`" wording corrected to the master-authoritative `by_exchange_symbol` + `groww_symbol_by_pair` resolution** (2026-06-19, post-merge consistency-audit follow-up). **Why:** DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001 (#845, PR #801) restructured `GrowwMarketAdapter.fetch_ohlcv` — a BARE trading symbol (incl. a hyphenated stock or a verbose-symbol index) now resolves via `by_exchange_symbol` + the master's `groww_symbol_by_pair` (the REAL groww_symbol, never reconstructed), with `by_groww_symbol` the FALLBACK for an already-prefixed FUT/CE/PE contract. A read-only post-merge consistency/drift audit (all-agent workspace verification) found three §6 rows left citing stale `adapter.py` line ranges (the methods moved) and the `Symbol/key format` + `Track 1 brute-force universe` rows still describing resolution as "via `by_groww_symbol`" — an INCOMPLETE description of the new contract (Golden Rule #1 / the §12 honesty discipline: a doc that drifted from the code it cites). **What shipped (docs-only — NO code/behavior change):** (1) §6 `Historical OHLC` row: `adapter.py:88-129` → `adapter.py:129` (the relocated `fetch_ohlcv` → `fetch_candle_windows`). (2) §6 `Symbol/key format` row: the "O(1) `by_groww_symbol` lookup" wording → the full master-authoritative resolution (bare/hyphenated/verbose via `by_exchange_symbol` + `groww_symbol_by_pair`; already-prefixed contract via `by_groww_symbol`), citing `adapter.py:162-174` + the DEC-ID. (3) §6 `Track 1 brute-force universe` row: "resolved via `by_groww_symbol`" → "resolved master-authoritatively via `by_exchange_symbol` + `groww_symbol_by_pair`", `adapter.py:45-58` → `adapter.py:162-174`. (4) the `_Last updated` line + the §1/§3 `Active branch` pointers refreshed (the prior `claude/zen-meitner-am13gf` pointer was stale — a pre-existing NIT the audit also flagged). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — docs-only; the post-merge consistency audit confirmed NO BLOCKER/MAJOR drift (MIGRATION numbering intact, every changed-symbol caller in sync, no stale code lies, the scope guard holds — zero engine import of any changed module); ledger numbering validates. 🟡 the `Active branch` pointer is inherently per-session ephemeral — refreshed to the current branch, the next session updates it again (the standing discipline). 🚫 NO substantive §6 FACT changed (intervals, price unit, rate limits, scope are untouched) and NO code/behavior change — the merged trio is lake/adapter/ingest only, the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **Files:** `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CLAUDEMD-ADAPTER-CITE-RECONCILE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001 (#845 — the resolution restructure that drifted the citations), DEC-CLAUDEMD-SPEC-LINE-RECONCILE-001 (the prior §-citation reconciliation precedent), DEC-WORKSPACE-VERIFY-002 (the all-agent workspace-verification discipline that surfaced the drift).

847. **DEC-PHASEPLAN-TF-COUNT-RECONCILE-001 — `TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md` Phase-4 first-sweep row corrected from the stale `3 inst × 15 TF` to the locked `3 inst × 21 TF`** (2026-06-19, engine-readiness-briefing follow-up). **Why:** the all-agent engine readiness map flagged an internal inconsistency: the Phase-4 deliverable table (`TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md:277`) described the first production sweep as `full 5-year × 3 inst × 15 TF × ~33B trials`, but the SAME doc's Stage-1B row (`:234`) states `63 inst-TF = 3 brute-force inst × 21 TFs` (and 3 × 15 ≠ 63), and every other authoritative source locks 21: `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md:160` (`21 timeframes (1m, 2-15m every minute, 30m, 60m, 120m, 180m, 240m, 1d)`) + `:322` (`63 matrices = 3 instruments × 21 TFs`), CLAUDE.md §3 (`21 timeframes (1m base + 19 derived intraday + 1d)`), and the engine code (`brutex/data/timeframes.ALL_TF_MINUTES` = 21). The `15` was a stale typo contradicting the doc's own arithmetic — a Golden-Rule-#1 honesty drift (a spec lying about the locked scope). **What shipped (docs-only, one cell):** `TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md:277` `15 TF` → `21 TF`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified against four primary sources (the doc's own #234, the spec ×2, CLAUDE.md, the engine constant) — the corrected value is the locked scope, not a guess. 🚫 NO code / behavior / scope change — the brute-force engine already sweeps the 21 timeframes (`ALL_TF_MINUTES`); this only fixes the doc cell that under-counted them. **Files:** `docs/TRACK1_PHASE_PLAN.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PHASEPLAN-TF-COUNT-RECONCILE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-CLAUDEMD-ADAPTER-CITE-RECONCILE-001 (#846 — the sibling post-merge doc-drift reconciliation), DEC-TF-VOCAB-21-001 (the 21-timeframe lock this doc cell must match).

848. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-HONEST-EMPTY-001 — a NON-terminal `EMPTY` spot window no longer counts toward the /coverage + /completeness "full" chip (it reports PENDING — the next pull WILL re-fetch it), and the per-symbol completeness table now shows the actually-covered `start → end` date range per `1day` / `1minute` dimension so a human sees in ONE view which interval is partial and exactly what span it holds** (2026-06-20, operator-locked; PR-A of the post-real-pull data-quality plan). **Why:** a deep line-by-line analysis of a real Groww universe pull (operator log, 14,269 lines) found recent `1day` windows (`2025-11-30 → 2026-05-29`, `2026-05-29 → 2026-06-20`) returned `EMPTY` during a 1-day-only run — recorded HONESTLY as `EMPTY` (`settled:false`) because the vendor publishes the most-recent daily bars a day or two late — yet the per-underlying SPOT completeness chip read **"full"**. Root cause (confirmed in code, not guessed): `spot_window_rollup` (`brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`) folded `EMPTY` into the RESOLVED bucket via `RESOLVED_STATUSES = {SUCCESS, SKIPPED, EMPTY}` (DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001 — that projection was DESIGNED for a genuinely-empty PRE-LISTING window that can never gain data, but it ALSO swallowed a recent maybe-late empty that a later pull DID fill — the operator's screenshot shows those exact windows `SUCCESS` with 120/16 bars at `attempts 4`). So a symbol with genuinely-missing recent data reported "full" — a dishonest headline. The operator also could not see WHICH dimension was partial nor its covered date range ("why in completeness start date and end date as well has not been added"). **What shipped (ADDITIVE — chip-classification + a display column; no data/schema/scope change):** (1) `spot_window_rollup` now re-buckets a NON-terminal `EMPTY` (status still `EMPTY`, below the terminal threshold) into PENDING for the completeness CHIP — it is OUTSTANDING work the next pull re-fetches — while a TERMINAL empty (`SKIPPED` — promoted at the threshold, OR fast-settled as an old pre-listing gap per DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001) stays RESOLVED, so an all-empty PRE-LISTING dataset still reads complete (its old windows fast-settle `SKIPPED`); only a RECENT maybe-late empty reads pending (the fix). The LIVE progress-bar numerator (`RESOLVED_STATUSES`, `window_ledger.py:541` — still `SUCCESS+SKIPPED+EMPTY` so the bar never freezes mid-pull) is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: completion-chip honesty and progress-bar liveness are intentionally DIFFERENT authorities (the rollup uses `SETTLED_STATUSES` for resolved now, not `RESOLVED_STATUSES`). (2) `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` `_per_symbol_spot` carries the covered `start`/`end` (the lake's earliest/latest bar date, already computed by `summarize_spot_datasets`) per `1day` / `1minute`; `completeness.html` `renderSpot` renders new "1-day covered" + "1-minute covered" columns (`start → end` or `—`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `db_view.py` rollup branch (the new `elif status == EMPTY` → pending) + `completeness.py` (the per-dimension covered-date fields) at 100% line+branch; the rollup test updated (`(3,1,0)` SUCCESS+SKIPPED+EMPTY-resolved → `(2,2,0)` SUCCESS+SKIPPED-resolved, PLANNED+EMPTY-pending); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean. 🟡 a genuinely-empty dataset reads "growing/partial" for the first pulls until its windows fast-settle (old) or hit the threshold (recent) — the honest "still confirming empty" state, then settles "full". 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-DATA change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; this is a /coverage + /completeness reporting honesty change only. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` (`spot_window_rollup` re-bucket + docstring), `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` (`_per_symbol_spot` covered dates), `brutex/dashboard/templates/completeness.html` (covered columns), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-HONEST-EMPTY-001. **Supersedes (the CHIP half only):** DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001 — a non-terminal EMPTY is pending for the completeness CHIP; the PROGRESS-BAR half of that decision (EMPTY counts as progress) is retained. **Builds on:** DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 (the chip this corrects), DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 (the old-empty `SKIPPED` fast-settle that keeps pre-listing datasets reading complete), DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the terminal-vs-non-terminal `EMPTY`/`SKIPPED` distinction this keys on), DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001 (the per-symbol date detail reused).

849. **DEC-RETRY-PERSIST-10-001 — the cross-pull `EMPTY → SKIPPED` terminal threshold (3 → 10) and the until-clean OUTER round budget (5 → 10) are raised so a recent maybe-late vendor bar gets far more "pull until it fetches a successful response" chances before a window is ever settled empty** (2026-06-20, operator-directed: "is it better to keep max 10 retry attempts… the data is available so why the fuck at first it failed"; the recommended scope of PR-D of the post-real-pull plan). **Why:** the real-pull log showed recent `1day` windows return `EMPTY` at the in-pull `fetches:3` during a 1-day-only run, then `SUCCESS` at window-`attempts:4` once the vendor published the data a pull later — i.e. the data EXISTS and a re-pull recovers it, but the cross-pull `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD = 3` would settle such a window `SKIPPED` after only 3 separate empty pulls, too few for a bar the vendor publishes a day or two late. Raising the terminal threshold to 10 gives a recent maybe-late window many more whole-pull confirmations before it is treated as a durable no-data gap; raising the manual until-clean `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS` 5 → 10 matches (the dashboard auto-resume path already uses `AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS = 50`). **Why this is safe (verified, not assumed):** (a) genuinely-OLD pre-listing windows still fast-settle on the FIRST empty via the old-gap settle path (`window_ledger.py` `settle_empty`, DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 — `empty_streak` forced straight to the threshold → `SKIPPED`), so raising the threshold NEVER re-hammers an ancient dead window; only RECENT maybe-late windows (not old enough to fast-settle) get the extra chances. (b) a 429 / timeout still PRESERVES (never bumps, never resets) the streak (`window_ledger.py:369-374`, DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-RATELIMIT-001), so a rate storm can never push a window toward `SKIPPED` — the deep-dive on the same log proved a throttled response is structurally incapable of being recorded `EMPTY` (`classify_window_status` gates `EMPTY` behind `error_type is None`; a 429 raises `GrowwRateLimitError → FAILED`). (c) the until-clean `decide_until_clean` guards (clean / dead / quota / no-progress) terminate the loop long before the round cap. **What shipped (two constants + the matching UI legend; in-pull budget UNCHANGED):** `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` 3 → 10 (`brutex/data/window_ledger.py`), `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS` 5 → 10 (`brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`), and the `fetch_windows.html` legend `EMPTY x/3` → `EMPTY x/10` (+ the JS `empty_threshold ?? 10` fallback). The IN-PULL per-window EMPTY re-fetch budget (the `↻ 3` `fetches`, `_DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 3`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py:156`) is DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 3 — raising it would multiply re-fetches of legitimately-empty windows WITHIN one pull without addressing late publication (which is a CROSS-pull phenomenon the terminal threshold handles); the two "3"s are different layers and the legend distinguishes them (`the 3× retry` in-pull text is unchanged). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — the constants + every threshold-pinned test updated (the promotion / migration / 429-storm-convergence tests now drive `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` empties SYMBOLICALLY so they survive a future re-tune; `empty_threshold` payload + UI assertions 3 → 10; `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS == 10`); the full unit + integration suite green; ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright clean. 🟡 a genuinely-dead RECENT window (not old enough to fast-settle) now re-pulls across up to 10 pulls before settling `SKIPPED` — a bounded quota cost (old windows fast-settle in 1; the no-progress guard bounds the loop), the deliberate trade for never settling a real-but-late bar empty. 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope change; the per-second 8-RPS ceiling + 500/min governor + the adaptive token bucket are UNTOUCHED (the same log confirmed the controller already absorbs storms with zero window failures — there was no rate bug to fix). **Files:** `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/fetch_windows.html`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger.py`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_ingest_common_until_clean.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-RETRY-PERSIST-10-001. **Builds on:** DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the threshold raised), DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 (the fast-settle that keeps old dead windows cheap), DEC-EMPTY-STREAK-RATELIMIT-001 (the 429-preserves-streak guard that makes raising the threshold safe under a storm), DEC-UNTIL-CLEAN-ALL-OUTSTANDING-001 (#844 — the until-clean loop whose round budget this raises), DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 (the auto-resume round budget this aligns with).

850. **DEC-METADATA-LIVE-PROGRESS-001 — the options expiries+contracts METADATA pull now emits LIVE incremental progress the `/universe` bar already polls (it no longer freezes at `0/N` for the whole pull), and the misleading `contracts pulled = 0` is made HONEST as "metadata-only by design" rather than "broken"** (2026-06-20, operator-observed: the `⛓ Pull expiries + contracts` button's progress bar sat frozen at `0/51` for the entire pull even though the registry was filling). **Why:** the `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-expiries-contracts` route ACCEPTED the background job's `on_progress` hook then immediately `del on_progress`'d it (threw it away), and `metadata_pull.pull_expiries_contracts` took NO progress hook at all — it only persisted + logged in its `on_expiry_cell` / `on_contract` callbacks. So the `BackgroundPullJob` bar the page polls at `/api/v1/universe/pull-progress` never advanced: it showed the placeholder `0/instrument-count` until the whole pull finished (`done`). The SPOT pull (`pull_all_spot`) does NOT have this bug — it wires `on_progress` + `on_ledger_sync` into the job and the bar advances per settled WINDOW (DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001). Separately, the per-underlying OPTIONS completeness view showed `contracts pulled = 0` for an `expiries_only` underlying, which READS like a failure but is BY DESIGN — the lean universe PARSES then DISCARDS the ~89k FUT/CE/PE legs (DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001); the metadata pull persists only the chain SHAPE (expiry dates + contract symbols), never the legs. **What shipped (smallest honest set; the lean-universe behaviour is UNCHANGED — no leg is ever stored):** (1) `metadata_pull.pull_expiries_contracts` gains an `on_progress: MetadataProgressHook | None = None` parameter — an ABSOLUTE `(completed, total, current)` hook (no `bars` arg: this pull has no candles). It fires once per Phase-1 (underlying, year) expiry cell as it settles, once at the phase boundary to RE-SCALE `total` from cells-only to `cells + contract_jobs` (the Phase-2 job count, computed by REUSING the engine's own `contract_jobs_from` + `contract_jobs_to_pull` so the denominator is exactly the jobs `run_two_phase` then runs — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON), and once per Phase-2 contract job. `completed` climbs 1 → total so the bar fills 0→100%. `None` (every non-dashboard caller) is a silent no-op — behaviour byte-unchanged when no hook is wired. (2) The `pull-expiries-contracts` route STOPS deleting `on_progress`: its `_work` now maps the metadata pull's absolute hook onto the SAME `BackgroundPullJob.sync_from_ledger(completed, total, bars=0, failed=0, current)` resync the spot pull uses, and starts the job `ledger_synced=True` — so `/api/v1/universe/pull-progress` reflects the metadata pull LIVE (the exact spot-pull shape, reused not reinvented). (3) Honest `contracts pulled` label: `completeness.py` gains `OPT_CONTRACTS_BY_DESIGN_NOTE` + `_contracts_note(status, contracts_pulled)` — a `contracts_note` annotation attached (in BOTH `_per_underlying_options` and the per-symbol `/universe` strip `_fold_per_symbol_options`) ONLY when the verdict is `expiries_only`/`OPT_PARTIAL` AND `contracts_pulled == 0`, reading "metadata-only by design — option legs are discarded (DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001), only the chain shape is kept"; empty for every other row so no false claim is attached. `completeness.html` renders it as a "by design" tooltip beside the 0, and the downloadable scoreboard CSV gains a `Notes` column carrying the same note. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — `metadata_pull.py` + `completeness.py` at **100% line+branch** (per-module `--cov-fail-under=100`, NO `# pragma: no cover` added to dodge the gate; the route's `_work` body stays under the SAME pre-existing `# pragma: no cover — runs on the job thread` every pull route uses, and its route-level `start(...)` line is covered); new tests prove the metadata pull EMITS incremental progress (a fake collector sees `completed` climb 1→total across cells then contract jobs, with the phase-boundary total re-scale, a failed cell ticking-but-adding-no-job, and the zero-cells no-emit edge) and the honest label (the by-design note attaches ONLY to `expiries_only`/0-contract rows, in the per-underlying + per-symbol + CSV payloads); ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright all clean on the changed modules. 🟡 the initial `total` is the instrument count (a placeholder the first cell-settle resync re-scales within the first callback) — identical to the spot pull's placeholder-then-resync pattern; the metadata pull is network-bound, not O(1)-total (one `get_expiries` per cell + one `get_contracts` per discovered expiry, unchanged). 🚫 NO lean-universe change — the ~89k option legs are STILL parsed-then-discarded; no leg is persisted; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-DATA change. This is a dashboard progress-wiring + display-label change only. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py` (`on_progress` param + `MetadataProgressHook` + per-cell/per-job emission + phase-boundary re-scale), `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (route stops `del on_progress`, wires `sync_from_ledger` + `ledger_synced=True`), `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` (`OPT_CONTRACTS_BY_DESIGN_NOTE` + `_contracts_note` + `contracts_note` in the per-underlying / per-symbol / CSV payloads), `brutex/dashboard/templates/completeness.html` (by-design tooltip + `.note` style), `tests/unit/test_metadata_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_completeness.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-METADATA-LIVE-PROGRESS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DERIV-METADATA-ORCHESTRATION-001 (the metadata pull this adds progress to), DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001 (the `sync_from_ledger` absolute-resync shape reused), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean-universe leg-discard the honest 0-contracts label explains), DEC-DERIV-METADATA-ROUTE-001 (the route wired), DEC-COMPLETENESS-SCOREBOARD-001 (the options completeness view annotated).
851. **DEC-SPOT-INTERVAL-DECOUPLE-001 — the SPOT 1-minute pull is FULLY DECOUPLED from the 1-day coverage: the `1day` phase pulls its full `[start, end]` range and the `1minute` phase INDEPENDENTLY pulls its full `[start, end]` range (the configured floor → today) for EVERY requested symbol — no coverage discovery, no per-symbol filtering, no minute-start bounding** (2026-06-20, operator-locked). **Why:** the prior 1-day-first model (DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 #836 / DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 #723) made the heavy `1minute` phase (a) DISCOVER each symbol's landed `1day` coverage off the lake, (b) FILTER OUT any symbol with ZERO `1day` data (the "3c skip" — reported, never pulled), and (c) BOUND each symbol's `1minute` start up to `max(full_start, coverage.first_date)`. The operator wants the two granularities pulled INDEPENDENTLY over the SAME full range: a symbol whose `1day` series is absent on Groww but whose `1minute` IS served (the operator's recurring "1day gap, 1minute lands" case — the inverse of the empty-daily DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 #842) was being SILENTLY EXCLUDED from the `1minute` fill it could have completed. The verify-first **1-day-only DEFAULT** (the operator picks granularity per pull via the `/universe` dropdown — `resolve_fetch_intervals`) is RETAINED; only the 1-minute↔1-day COUPLING is removed. **What shipped (a removal — the minute phase now runs over ALL requested instruments with `symbol_windows=None`):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — BOTH spot pull paths (`pull_all_spot` bulk + `pull_candles` single-instrument) dropped the `_discover_minute_windows` discovery call, the `minute_instruments = [inst for inst in instruments if inst.symbol_name in symbol_windows]` 3c filter, and the `minute_skipped_no_1day` logging; the minute phase now plans (`plan_windows`) / reconciles (`reconcile_ledger_with_lake`) / runs (`_run_phase`) over EVERY requested instrument with `symbol_windows=None`, so the spine's `_resolve_spot_window` returns the global `(start, end)` for every symbol. The `1day` phase is UNCHANGED (`_run_phase((_PHASE1_DAILY,), instruments, None)`); the auth/quota GLOBAL-STOP guard that skips the minute phase on a dead Phase-1 token is RETAINED (it is not the coverage coupling). (2) DELETED the now-dead `_discover_minute_windows` helper + its `Catalog`/`CatalogError`/`cast` imports (the `cast`-narrow-the-ledger trick is gone — a clean `if ledger is not None:` guard mirrors the `1day` phase). (3) `brutex/adapters/groww/spot_bounds.py` — DELETED `discover_spot_minute_windows` (the coupled discovery driver), `spot_coverage_to_minute_window` (the pure coverage→window mapper), and `spot_daily_coverage` (the lake-read helper, now dead); the module is reduced to the surviving `SpotWindows` type alias (still threaded — always `None` on the SPOT path — through the ingest spine + window ledger as the opt-in never-narrow fallback). (4) `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py` — `_resolve_spot_window` KEPT verbatim (it already returns the global range when `symbol_windows is None`, which is exactly the decoupled behavior); only its docstring + the `symbol_windows` param docstrings refreshed to describe the opt-in fallback. (5) docstring-only reference fixes in `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py` (`plan_windows`) + `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` (repointed the midnight-IST partition-order note to `contract_bounds.contract_daily_coverage`, which retains the identical note). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — all five changed modules at 100% line+branch (`pull_controller.py` 376/86 with the pre-existing `test_dashboard_pull_pool_sizing.py` pairing, `spot_bounds.py` 4/0, `run_ingest.py` 142/28, `window_ledger_store.py` 170/50, `spot_daily_resample.py` 84/20); ruff check (`brutex tests`) + ruff format + mypy --strict (changed modules) + pyright (changed modules + tests) clean; new tests prove a `both` and a `1minute`-only pull plan + fetch the FULL `[start, end]` minute window for EVERY instrument INCLUDING a symbol with ZERO `1day` coverage (the `_DailyGapAdapter` — previously skipped, now `completed=1`, NOT skipped, and the earliest planned `1minute` window starts at the global start date for every symbol), and that `symbol_windows=None` flows to the minute phase (no `minute_skipped_no_1day` log ever emitted); the 175-case spot-pull + ledger + run-ingest suite is green (the coupling tests were updated/removed: `_EmptyAdapter`/`_FailingAdapter` now hit BOTH intervals → 2 no-data / 2 failed, not 1+1-skipped). 🟡 the per-second Groww backtesting cap stays UNVERIFIED (unchanged);
