the decoupled `1minute` pull issues MORE first-pass requests for a no-`1day` symbol than the old skip did — but every window is rate-paced by the shared token bucket (Rule #6, unchanged) and idempotent (Golden Rule #7), and a genuinely-no-`1minute` symbol settles EMPTY→SKIPPED via the existing 3-pull threshold, so the worst case is bounded, not a runaway. 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-schema change — adapter/ingest/dashboard pull-orchestration only; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (CLAUDE.md §3). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/spot_bounds.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py` (docstrings), `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py` (docstring), `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` (docstring), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_spot_bounds.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py` (docstrings), `tests/unit/test_window_ledger_store.py` (docstrings), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SPOT-INTERVAL-DECOUPLE-001. **Supersedes:** the 1-minute-bounded-to-1-day-coverage COUPLING of DEC-SPOT-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#836) / DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#723 — the verify-first 1-day-only DEFAULT is RETAINED; only the coupling is removed). **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#723 — the operator-chosen-granularity dropdown this keeps), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the `plan_windows`/`reconcile_ledger_with_lake` full-range planning this funnels through), DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (the 1-minute base from which the 19 intraday TFs resample), DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 (#842 — the complementary empty-`1day`-from-`1minute` fill, now that `1minute` always lands for a no-`1day` symbol).

852. **DEC-REALDATA-ONLY-NO-1M-TO-1D-001 — REAL Groww vendor data ONLY: the 1-minute→1-day daily resample-on-empty feature is REMOVED (a recent-stock `1day` window the vendor does not serve stays honestly EMPTY, never computed from the stored 1-minute), and the EMPTY-retry persistence raised for it is REVERTED — `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` 10 → 3 and `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS` 10 → 5** (2026-06-20, operator decree). **Why:** the operator FORBIDS generating/computing 1-day OHLC from 1-minute — Track 1 must hold REAL Groww `1day` data ONLY (Golden Rule #1 — no invented bar). DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 (#842) had derived the recent missing-`1day` cash-equity bars from the 1-minute already in the lake (midnight-IST stamped); that is now a forbidden synthesis, so the feature is deleted in full. With the resample gone there is nothing for a recent-stock `1day` empty to wait for, so the 5 → 10 / 3 → 10 retry persistence DEC-RETRY-PERSIST-10-001 (#849) raised SPECIFICALLY to keep grinding those empties long enough for the resample to fill them is now FUTILE — it is reverted to the prior 5 rounds / 3-empty terminal threshold so the now-honestly-terminal empties settle FAST instead of a 10-round grind. **What shipped (a removal + a 2-constant revert; the INTRADAY resamplers are UNTOUCHED):** (1) DELETED the module `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` and its tests `tests/unit/test_spot_daily_resample.py` + `tests/integration/test_spot_daily_resample_roundtrip.py` (the whole 1m→1d daily reconcile core + lake read/write builders). (2) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — removed the `_resample_daily_after_pull(...)` call from the spot pull try-block (the resample was the LAST step before the `finally`'s `end_pull_ledger`; the try/finally is intact), the `_resample_daily_after_pull` function def + its inner `spot_daily_resample` import, the `DailyResampleWindow` TYPE_CHECKING import, and the now-orphaned `polars as pl` + `CandleBar` TYPE_CHECKING imports it alone used. (3) `brutex/data/window_ledger.py` — `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` 10 → 3 (+ docstring restored to describe 3, noting the 10→3 revert). (4) `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py` — `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS` 10 → 5 (+ docstring restored to 5; the invariant `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS >= EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` still holds — 5 >= 3). (5) the #849 test/UI literals pinned to 10 reverted: `empty_threshold` payload/UI assertions 10 → 3 (`test_dashboard_db_view.py`, `test_dashboard_coverage.py`), the `empty_streak == 10` fast-settle "forced to threshold" cases 10 → 3 (`test_groww_ingest.py`, `test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `test_window_ledger_store.py`), `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS == 10` → `== 5` (`test_ingest_common_until_clean.py`, invariant guard kept), and the `fetch_windows.html` legend `EMPTY x/10` → `EMPTY x/3` (+ the JS `empty_threshold ?? 10` → `?? 3` fallback). The symbolic `range(EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD)` tests auto-adapt. **CRITICAL — NOT touched:** the INTRADAY resamplers `brutex/data/spot_resample.py` + `brutex/data/tf_resampler.py` (they build the engine's 19 intraday timeframes 1m → 5m/15m/… — core, NOT in scope); ONLY the 1m→1d DAILY resample is removed. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — recent-stock `1day` now stays honestly EMPTY (reported partial on the coverage view, never a synthesized bar); stocks keep their REAL 1-minute (the decoupled minute pull of DEC-SPOT-INTERVAL-DECOUPLE-001 #851 is unaffected); `pull_controller.py` / `window_ledger.py` / `ingest_common.py` all at 100% line+branch and the package TOTAL stays 100.00% (deleting the module + its tests is net-neutral; the removed `_resample_daily_after_pull` glue carried `# pragma: no cover`); the full unit + integration suite green (7612 passed, 7 pre-existing skips); ruff check (`brutex tests`) + ruff format + pyright (changed modules) clean; mypy --strict clean on the changed modules. 🟡 a recent-stock `1day` gap that the vendor genuinely never publishes is now a permanent honest EMPTY rather than a 1-minute-derived fill — the deliberate trade for real-data-only; the bar is surfaced, never invented. 🚫 the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX indices) is UNAFFECTED — index `1day` is REAL vendor data (the resample only ever targeted recent cash-equity gaps); no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-schema / intraday-resample change. **Files:** `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` (DELETED), `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/fetch_windows.html`, `tests/unit/test_spot_daily_resample.py` (DELETED), `tests/integration/test_spot_daily_resample_roundtrip.py` (DELETED), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_ingest_common_until_clean.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-REALDATA-ONLY-NO-1M-TO-1D-001. **Supersedes:** DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 (#842 — the 1m→1d resample-on-empty, REMOVED) and reverts the threshold/rounds of DEC-RETRY-PERSIST-10-001 (#849 — `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` and `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS` back to 3 / 5). **Builds on:** DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (the threshold reverted), DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 (the FIRST-empty fast-settle that keeps old dead windows cheap, unchanged), DEC-SPOT-INTERVAL-DECOUPLE-001 (#851 — the decoupled 1-minute pull that keeps real 1-minute landing for a no-`1day` symbol), DEC-DHAN-1M-ONLY-001 (the 1-minute base + the INTRADAY 1m→5m/15m/… resample that is explicitly OUT of scope here).

853. **DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 — 1-MINUTE is the ONLY granularity FETCHED from Groww (spot + futures + options); 1-DAY (and every other timeframe) is DERIVED from the 1-minute and written to the lake, never vendor-fetched; the "Verify vs NSE" feature is REMOVED in full; and the F&O historical DEFAULT window becomes per-contract `expiry − 3 calendar months → expiry` at 1-minute** (2026-06-20, operator decree). **Why:** the operator wants ONE source of truth for OHLC — pull only 1-minute, then DERIVE the 1-day (PDH/PDL daily anchor) + the 19 intraday timeframes from it. This deliberately REVERSES DEC-REALDATA-ONLY-NO-1M-TO-1D-001 (#852, the "never compute 1-day from 1-minute" decree) but CLEANLY: 1-minute is now the single fetched granularity, so a derived 1-day is not a gap-fill synthesis competing with a vendor bar — there IS no vendor 1-day to compete with, the 1-day is an OPENLY-derived bar by design (Golden Rule #1 — it is labelled derived, not passed off as vendor data). It also SUPERSEDES DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001 (#723, the verify-first 1-day-default dropdown) + its DEC-HISTORICAL-1DAY-FIRST-001 F&O twin: with 1-minute the sole granularity there is no granularity choice + no 1-day-first barrier, so the `/universe` granularity dropdown + the whole NSE/BSE-bhavcopy cross-check ("Verify vs NSE") are removed. **What shipped (5 changes — spot + F&O fetch becomes 1-minute-only with derived 1-day; ENGINE + 52-vocab UNTOUCHED, CLAUDE.md §3):** **(A) Fetch 1-minute only.** `pull_controller.py` — `GROWW_FETCH_INTERVALS` = `("1minute",)`; `resolve_fetch_intervals(choice)` now IGNORES `choice` and ALWAYS returns `("1minute",)` (the legacy `SPOT_INTERVAL_DAY/MINUTE/BOTH` + `SPOT_INTERVAL_CHOICES` tokens stay importable only for the vestigial CLI `--interval` alias map). `universe.html` — the `#spotInterval` granularity `<select>` + its `&spot_interval=` JS threading are REMOVED (a static "granularity · 1-minute (1-day derived)" label replaces it); the "Pull the Universe" help text reworded to 1-minute-only + derived-1-day. The route `spot_interval` query param is retained but VESTIGIAL (resolves to 1-minute regardless). **(B) Derive 1-day always-on, written to the lake.** RESTORED `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` (the module #852 deleted — `resample_1m_to_daily` midnight-IST-stamped 1m→1d, `fill_daily_from_minute`, `make_lake_read_1m_window`/`make_lake_write_1day`) and ADDED an ALWAYS-ON driver `derive_daily_for_targets(targets, build_read_1m, build_write_1day, before)` + `DailyDeriveTarget`/`DailyDeriveReport` (UNCONDITIONAL full-range derivation, distinct from the retained ledger-EMPTY-window `reconcile_daily_from_minute` arm). `pull_controller.py` — both spot pull paths (`pull_all_spot` bulk + `pull_candles` single) call a new `_resample_daily_after_pull(...)` AFTER the 1-minute phase, deriving the 1-day partition over the FULL pulled `[start, end)` range (quarantined `# pragma: no cover` glue; the derive CORE is 100%-unit-tested). The engine + preflight (`prev_day_ohlc.lookup_prev_day_ohlc`, `sweep_preflight._FETCHED_INTERVALS = {"1minute","1day"}`) are UNCHANGED — they read the now-derived 1-day partition. **(C) F&O default = per-contract `expiry − 3mo → expiry`, 1-minute.** `contract_bounds.py` — new pure `subtract_calendar_months(anchor, months)` (hand-rolled, day-clamped to month-end — `python-dateutil` is NOT a declared dep, only transitive; Golden Rule #1 no hidden deps) + `default_fno_minute_window(expiry, full_start, full_end)` → `[max(full_start, expiry−3mo), min(full_end, expiry+1day))` + `DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_MONTHS=3`. `historical_pull.py` — `pull_contract_candles` RESTRUCTURED from the two-phase (1-day-discover-then-1-minute) barrier to a SINGLE 1-minute phase bounded per contract by its own window (explicit operator dates OVERRIDE → the resolved range for all; else the per-contract `expiry−3mo` default via the new `_resolve_minute_windows`), then a quarantined per-contract `_derive_daily_from_minute` writes the `FNO/<symbol>/1day` partition. `_discover_start_dates` (the lake-read 1-day-coverage pin) + the global 1-day barrier + `minute_skipped` arm are DELETED. The `HistoricalPullReport` fields are RETAINED but repurposed for the single 1-minute phase (`minute_requested` always True, `minute_skipped` always False, `phase1_clean`/`phase1_complete` describe the 1-minute phase, `start_dates` = each contract's resolved window start). `app.py` — the historical route `interval` default `1day` → `1minute`; `universe.html` `histInterval()` → `"1minute"`. **(D) Remove "Verify vs NSE" entirely.** DELETED the `brutex/data/validation/` package (`nse_oneday.py` + `nse_equity_oneday.py` + `__init__.py`), the `POST /api/v1/universe/verify-nse` route + its lazy imports (`app.py`), the "🛡 Verify vs NSE" button + `#verifymsg` div + the verify JS handler/enable logic (`universe.html`), the CLI `validate-nse-1day` subcommand + `cmd_validate_nse_1day` handler + dispatch (`cli.py`), and ALL nse-validation tests (unit/golden/property/stress/bench/integration). `bhavcopy` / `verify-first` / `DEC-PULL-1DAY-FIRST-001` references reconciled to the 1-minute-only framing across the touched modules + tests (NOT an exhaustive repo sweep — a follow-up under DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 reconciled the residual stale docstrings the hostile review flagged in `movers_snapshot.py` / `coverage_view.py` / `spot_bounds.py` / `prevday.py`). **(E) Docs.** `CLAUDE.md` §1/§3/§6 + `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 / #10):** ✅ Verified — the derive CORE (`spot_daily_resample.derive_daily_for_targets`/`fill_daily_from_minute`/`resample_1m_to_daily`) + the new pure helpers (`subtract_calendar_months`/`default_fno_minute_window`/`_resolve_minute_windows`) at 100% line+branch with direct tests (month-end clamp incl. Feb leap/non-leap, year-borrow, expiry−3mo window, clamp-to-floor, none-expiry full-range); `resolve_fetch_intervals` always returns `("1minute",)`; the F&O pull fetches 1-minute ONLY (asserted the SDK is never called at `1day`) with the per-contract default + explicit-override windows; the raw lake-I/O glue (`_resample_daily_after_pull`) carries `# pragma: no cover` (integration-shaped) but is behaviorally tested (writes a midnight-IST 1-day partition from seeded 1-minute; no-1-minute is a clean no-op). (Follow-up: the F&O `_derive_daily_from_minute` had its whole-function `# pragma: no cover` REMOVED + was refactored to DELEGATE the quarantine loop to the tested `derive_daily_for_targets` driver, so its window-skip / contract-skip / per-target-error branches are now honestly unit-measured — DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 FIX-1/FIX-4.) ruff check (`brutex tests`) + ruff format + mypy --strict (clean on changed modules; the pre-existing `cma` import-not-found in `stage3_refine.py` is unrelated + untouched) clean. The 1-day derivation is QUARANTINED end-to-end (a derive error NEVER fails the pull — the authoritative 1-minute candles are already in the lake). 🟡 the 1-day OHLC is a 1-minute aggregation (first-minute open / summed volume / last-minute close), which need NOT equal an official exchange daily (call-auction open / settlement close can differ) — it is an openly-derived bar, surfaced as derived, never claimed as vendor-official; the per-second Groww backtesting cap stays UNVERIFIED (unchanged). 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-schema change — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (CLAUDE.md §3); India VIX stays REFERENCE_ONLY; the 8-RPS ceiling + 500/min governor + adaptive token bucket are UNTOUCHED; the INTRADAY resamplers (`spot_resample.py` + `tf_resampler.py`, the 19 intraday TFs) are UNTOUCHED (the derive reuses `tf_resampler.resample_1m_to_tf` for the daily OHLCV aggregation). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py`, `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` (RESTORED + extended), `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_ux.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_template.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_premium.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_groww_primary.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_app_backfill.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py`, the deleted nse-validation tests (`test_dashboard_verify_nse_route.py`, `test_validation_nse_oneday.py`, `test_nse_equity_oneday.py`, `test_validation_nse_oneday_golden.py`, `test_validation_nse_oneday_properties.py`, `test_validation_nse_oneday_stress.py`, `test_validation_nse_oneday_o1.py`, derive), DEC-SPOT-1DAY-RESAMPLE-ON-EMPTY-001 (#842 — the midnight-IST resample core restored + generalized to always-on), DEC-SPOT-INTERVAL-DECOUPLE-001 (#851 — the decoupled-phase plumbing the 854. **DEC-POSTPULL-DATAQUALITY-BATCH-001 — post-real-pull data-quality + universe-classification batch (5 fixes, one PR): (A) remove the dead 1-day dimension from `/completeness`; (B) show the REAL enumerated contracts count; (C) an empty-body `JSONDecodeError` is RETRYABLE, not a terminal "not on Groww" quarantine; (D) the niftyindices NTM fetch is cache-on-success + bounded-retry + cache-fallback; (E) the F&O OPT/REF classification gains a vendor-canonical token-join (numeric-token stocks/BSE indices) + a SOURCED, env-extensible NSE-index alias (`NIFTYJR`→`NIFTYNXT50`, `NIFTYMIDSELECT`→`MIDCPNIFTY`) + a reconciliation audit diagnostic** (2026-06-20, operator-locked after a deep line-by-line analysis of the FIRST full real-data Groww universe pull + the 11,823-line operator `make run` log; the brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + rate-limit + lake-schema are UNCHANGED, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why:** the first real pull surfaced five operator-visible data-quality defects: (1) `/completeness` showed a `1-DAY` column permanently `none` for every symbol — 1-day is DERIVED, never fetched (DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853), so its fetch-ledger is always empty — making every symbol read `OVERALL partial` despite full 1-minute coverage; (2) the options `CONTRACTS PULLED` column read `0 by design` even while the live pull enumerated thousands of contracts; (3) two genuine F&O stocks (TITAN, SHRIRAMFIN) were terminally quarantined as "not on Groww" on a transient empty/throttled body (`JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`); (4) a transient niftyindices `404` collapsed the universe from ~752 to the ~211 F&O base ("no last-good cache"); (5) two genuine NSE F&O indices — Nifty Next 50 (`NIFTYNXT50`) + Nifty Midcap Select (`MIDCPNIFTY`) — were tagged REFERENCE_ONLY (REF) not option-pullable (OPT) because the spot rows spell them `NIFTYJR`/`NIFTYMIDSELECT`, which the symbol bridge cannot match to the option legs' `underlying_symbol`. **What shipped:** **(A) completeness 1-day removed (VIEW only).** `completeness.py` `SPOT_DIMENSIONS=("1minute",)`; `_overall_spot` = the 1-minute verdict alone; the per-symbol `1day*` keys, the `full_1day`/`full_both` summary buckets, the `1-DAY`/`1-DAY COVERED` table columns + `FULL 1-DAY`/`FULL 1D+1M` tiles + the CSV 1-day columns are removed; downstream JSON consumers (`coverage.html`, `universe.html`) reconciled. The DERIVED 1-day STAYS in the lake (the engine reads it) — only the misleading fetch-keyed completeness view is removed. **(B) real contracts count.** `metadata_pull.py` folds each successful Phase-2 contract job's count into `(exchange, underlying, year)` and re-upserts the Phase-1 coverage cell with the real integer count (≥1 ⇒ `complete`); only the COUNT is persisted (legs still discarded — lean-universe, DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001); `_contracts_note` drops "by design" automatically once a count is present. **(C) empty-body retry.** `errors.py` new `GrowwEmptyResponseError(GrowwError)`; `from_groww_exception` maps a `json.JSONDecodeError` (empty/non-JSON body = transient throttle) → `GrowwEmptyResponseError` (`is_retryable=True`) — NARROW (only `JSONDecodeError`, not every `ValueError`, so a real code bug stays terminal, Golden Rule #1); the until-clean/auto-retry loop re-pulls it; a genuine 404 stays `GrowwNotFoundError` (terminal). **(D) NTM cache resilience — regression-test PIN only (NO production change in this PR).** The niftyindices fetch ALREADY had bounded retry+backoff (browser UA/Referer), cache-on-success, and a live→cache→honest-degrade order on `main` (`nse_constituents.py` + `ntm_cache.py` are UNCHANGED in this batch); this PR only ADDS a regression test (`test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py`) that PINS the cache-on-success, so a transient 404 falling back to the last-good 752 (instead of collapsing to 211) can never silently regress. **(E) OPT/REF classification.** `instrument_loader.py` — (i) a vendor-canonical token-join (`_option_underlying_security_ids` ∩ spot `security_id`, gated on a numeric `feed_token` so the blake2b-surrogate NSE-index string tokens are EXCLUDED) marks numeric-token stocks/BSE-indices OPT, symbol-agnostic (immune to spelling drift); (ii) a SOURCED, env-extensible alias `_SOURCED_FNO_INDEX_ALIASES={"NIFTYJR":"NIFTYNXT50","NIFTYMIDSELECT":"MIDCPNIFTY"}` (NSE product naming cited in the constant; `BRUTEX_FNO_INDEX_ALIASES` JSON override merged on top — DYNAMIC, mirrors `BRUTEX_INDEX_CSV_FILENAMES`) marks the 2 NSE indices OPT; (iii) a new `universe.load.opt_reclassified` diagnostic enumerates every REF→OPT rescue by mechanism (`token_join`/`alias`/`symbol_bridge`) + the residual `still_unmatched` count — the operator's comprehensive audit. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ all changed modules at 100% line+branch on their suites (`completeness.py`, `metadata_pull.py`, `errors.py`, `nse_constituents.py`, `ntm_cache.py`, `instrument_loader.py`); ruff + ruff-format + mypy --strict clean on changed modules (the pre-existing `cma` import-not-found in `engine/stage3_refine.py` is unrelated + untouched). 🟡 LIVE-vendor behavior — the real niftyindices fetch + the real Groww master classifying the full 752-stock universe + the 2 NSE indices — is OPERATOR-verified on the operator's Mac, NOT sandbox-verified (this build bot-blocks NSE/niftyindices; all tests use synthetic schema-faithful rows). The stock token-join is exercised at the CLASSIFICATION/AUDIT level; persisting a spot-symbol-mismatched stock ROW additionally needs a symbol-keyed `is_universe_underlying` change (OUT of scope — flagged for a follow-up). 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-schema change — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; India VIX + NTM constituents stay REFERENCE_ONLY; the 8-RPS ceiling + 500/min governor + adaptive token bucket are UNTOUCHED. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`, `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/{completeness,coverage,universe}.html`, + tests (`test_completeness.py`, `test_metadata_pull.py`, `test_groww_errors.py`, `test_groww_client.py`, `test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py`, `test_fno_index_diagnostic.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`), `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-POSTPULL-DATAQUALITY-BATCH-001. **Builds on:** DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 (#853), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001, DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001, DEC-NTM-GROWW-REPOINT-001, DEC-FNO-INDEX-GROWW-SYMBOL-MATCH-001, DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001.

855. **DEC-POSTPULL-DQ-REMEDIATION-001 — pre-merge `hostile-reviewer` FIX-FIRST remediation of the #854 batch + ledger-anchoring of the batch's granular sub-decision IDs** (2026-06-20). **Why:** the pre-merge adversarial review of #854 returned **FIX-FIRST** — one MAJOR correctness defect + two MINOR honesty issues — and the batch's code cited granular per-fix DEC IDs that needed ledger anchors (Golden Rule #1: every DEC ID traces to a ledger entry). **What shipped:** **(1) [MAJOR] contract-count year-key fix** (`metadata_pull.py`): the enumerated-contract count is now folded by the FULL `(exchange, underlying, expiry)` key, and `_rewrite_contract_counts` sums each Phase-1 cell over ITS OWN discovered expiries — so a cross-year expiry (a `get_expiries(year=2025)` returning a Jan-**2026** expiry; the vendor does NOT year-filter its returned expiries, `adapters/groww/contracts.py:165-181`) is credited to the discovering cell instead of being silently dropped to `expiries_only`/`contracts_pulled=0` (which, being a SETTLED status, never self-healed on re-run — defeating the #854 part-B fix). Regression tests `test_year_boundary_expiry_credits_discovering_cell` + `test_shared_expiry_credits_every_discovering_cell` (verified fail-before / pass-after). **(2) [MINOR] EQ token-join audit honesty** (`instrument_loader.py`): an `EQ` row surfaced by the token-join is now logged in a SEPARATE `token_join_diagnostic` bucket (EXCLUDED from the rescue `count`) labelled "classification UNCHANGED" — because a stock's `reference_only` is decided by F&O-eligibility membership, NOT the IDX-only bridged set (`universe.is_spot_only_index` returns False for any non-IDX row); only `IDX` token-join hits are real REF→OPT rescues. The operator still SEES every symbol-mismatched stock in the audit, but is no longer told its flag changed when it did not. **(3) [MINOR] changelog honesty**: #854 part (D) reworded to "regression-test pin only — no production change" (the niftyindices cache/retry predates the batch; `nse_constituents.py`/`ntm_cache.py` are UNCHANGED). **Granular sub-decision IDs anchored here** (each cited in the #854 batch's code): `DEC-METADATA-CONTRACTS-COUNT-001` (the real-contracts-count persistence, #854 part B), `DEC-GROWW-EMPTY-BODY-RETRY-001` (the empty-body `json.JSONDecodeError` → retryable `GrowwEmptyResponseError`, #854 part C), `DEC-FNO-INDEX-EQ-TOKEN-JOIN-AUDIT-001` (the EQ-token-join audit split, above). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ `metadata_pull.py` + `instrument_loader.py` at 100% line+branch post-fix; ruff (check + format) clean; mypy `--follow-imports=silent` clean on both modules (the bare-mypy `cma` import-not-found in `engine/stage3_refine.py` is the pre-existing, unrelated optional-dep Limitation); the touched suites (metadata_pull 26, instrument_loader+fno_index_diagnostic 65, composite_pull consumer) all green. 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-schema change. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`, `tests/unit/test_metadata_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py`, `tests/unit/test_fno_index_diagnostic.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-POSTPULL-DQ-REMEDIATION-001. **Remediates:** DEC-POSTPULL-DATAQUALITY-BATCH-001 (#854).

856. **DEC-TF-PRECISION-PROOF-001 — timeframe-OHLCV-precision proof pyramid: 13 new tests that PROVE the existing 1m→21-TF resampler derives every bar of every timeframe EXACTLY (no production change — the resampler was already correct; no imprecision found)** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "guarantee … every timestamp of every timeframe of OHLCV will be precisely calculated … how bro how?"). **Why:** the operator wanted a GUARANTEE (not an assumption) that every O/H/L/C/V + timestamp of all 21 timeframes derived from the 1-minute base is precise. A survey found `brutex/data/tf_resampler.py` already correct — a 09:15-IST **fixed-arithmetic** grid (`bucket = session_open + floor((ts−session_open)/tf)·tf`), **selection** aggregation (open=first, high=max, low=min, close=last, volume=Σ), the session window **[09:15:00 inclusive, 15:30:00 exclusive)** — with 10/13 proof invariants already tested. This PR closes the remaining 3 + strengthens the rest so precision is PROVEN. **What shipped (TEST-ONLY; 3 files, 13 new tests, all pass; 39 incl. the 26 existing dedicated `tests/unit/test_tf_resampler.py` tests, 0 regression):** **(1) per-bar tiling** (`tests/property/test_tf_resampler_tiling_properties.py`, hypothesis) — every 1-minute bar maps to EXACTLY ONE bucket of each of the 21 TFs (Σ per-bucket member-counts == #1m bars; label-set == independently-derived bucket-set), none dropped or double-counted; **(2) associativity over ALL 88 divisor pairs** — `resample(1m→T)` equals `resample(T'→T) ∘ resample(1m→T')` bit-for-bit (`DataFrame.equals`) for every `(T',T)` with `T%T'==0 ∧ T'<T` over `ALL_TF_MINUTES`, incl. the daily-target pairs `(1,375)(3,375)(5,375)(15,375)`; **(5) independent oracle** — a pure-Python dict reference resampler (no polars, in-test helper) matches production OHLCV + `ts_utc` exactly (two independent implementations agree); **(3) session-bound + truncated last bar** (`tests/unit/test_tf_resampler_session_bounds.py`) — every `bar_start` ∈ [09:15:00, 15:30:00) IST for all 21 TFs, count == `ceil(375/tf)`, the truncated final bucket verified (60m→7 bars last-label 15:15, 30m→13, 120m→4, 180m→3, 240m→2) incl. its clipped-`[start,15:30)`-window OHLCV; **(4) half-day / short session** — Muhurat (120 bars) + early-13:00 (225 bars) sessions clamp to the real last bar, no synthetic bars past the short close; **(6) O(1) bench** (`tests/bench/test_tf_resampler_o1.py`, repo `_o1_tiers.ratio_ceiling`) — per-1m-bar cost ratio ≈ 0.81 across a 5× dataset jump (469K vs 94K bars) under the ceiling, + a 30 s wall-clock catastrophe gate. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ all 13 new tests pass; ruff + `mypy --strict` clean; no `# pragma: no cover`; NO production code touched (the proof FOUND no bug). 🟡 the bench proves **O(n)-total / O(1)-amortised-per-output-bar** + a catastrophe ceiling, NOT an absolute throughput SLA (machine-dependent) and NOT "O(1) total" (a resample inherently reads every bar once); the lake-derived TF path is **spot OHLCV only** — the TF resampler carries NO open-interest column (F&O `OI=last` is handled by the separate live `feed` resampler, out of scope here); the resampler is **polars-based** (fast + deterministic), NOT a Rust kernel. 🚫 NO production / engine / 52-vocab / scope / lake-schema change — pure verification hardening. **Files:** `tests/property/test_tf_resampler_tiling_properties.py`, `tests/unit/test_tf_resampler_session_bounds.py`, `tests/bench/test_tf_resampler_o1.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **CI hotfix (post-hostile-review):** the 3 new files imported polars at module top (`import polars as pl`), which errors at COLLECTION on the lean `.[dev]`-only property/bench CI jobs (polars is the optional `[data]` extra). Replaced with the repo-standard `pl = pytest.importorskip("polars")` (matching `tests/property/test_derived_daily_properties.py` + 16+ siblings) so the suites SKIP — not error — when polars is absent, and still RUN in the `[data]`-equipped unit/full env. Confirmed by the `hostile-reviewer` agent (BLOCKER → resolved) — the proofs themselves were rigorous, mutation-killed, and honestly documented (SHIP-after-fix). **Decision ID:** DEC-TF-PRECISION-PROOF-001. **Builds on:** DEC-RESAMPLE-ANCHOR-002 (the 09:15 fixed-arithmetic grid being proven), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 (#853 — 1-minute is the sole fetched granularity; all TFs derived).

857. **DEC-FNO-EQ-TOKEN-JOIN-PERSIST-001 — persist symbol-mismatched F&O stocks as TRADABLE universe underlyings (the follow-up that closes the #855/#854 EQ-token-join audit-only split)** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "the same issues can happen even for some other indices and stocks symbols also … marked wrongly as simple ref instead of opt right so even check all these"). **Why:** a genuinely F&O-eligible NSE stock whose SPOT row's `trading_symbol` is spelled differently from its option leg's `underlying_symbol` (e.g. spot `BAJAJ-AUTO` vs leg `BAJAJAUTO`) misses the ticker-keyed `fno_eligible` set, so `is_universe_underlying` DROPPED it from the lean store (or, if it was ALSO an NTM constituent, persisted it wrongly as `reference_only=TRUE` — losing its option chain). DEC-FNO-INDEX-EQ-TOKEN-JOIN-AUDIT-001 (#855) deliberately surfaced such a stock in the `token_join_diagnostic` audit ONLY and named the persist fix the out-of-scope follow-up — this is that follow-up. The token-join evidence (the stock's GENUINE numeric vendor token == an option leg's `underlying_security_id`) is the same vendor-canonical signal already used for BSE indices (DEC-FNO-INDEX-TOKEN-JOIN-001; Golden Rule #1 — never an invented alias). **What shipped (lake/ingest only — the brute-force ENGINE is UNCHANGED, still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** **(1)** `brutex/universe.py` `is_universe_underlying` gains a 4th id-keyed arm `fno_eligible_security_ids: frozenset[int] = frozenset()` (default empty → byte-identical to the prior F&O-only rule), OR'd into the EQ clause so a token-join F&O stock is ADMITTED for persistence; the `is_option_pullable` invariant doc updated ("every persisted non-reference equity is F&O-eligible — by ticker OR token-join"). **(2)** `instrument_loader.py` `_classify_option_pullable` now also RETURNS the EQ token-join `security_id` set (a 4th tuple element; it already computed the membership for the diagnostic) — the EQ rows are STILL kept out of the index-only `options_eligible_bridged`/reclassification `count` (no INDEX flag flips) and STILL listed in `token_join_diagnostic`. **(3)** `_lean_universe` threads the set into `is_universe_underlying` (the persist filter). **(4) precedence — F&O-tradable WINS over NTM-reference:** `_ntm_admission` subtracts the token-join set (alongside the existing ticker-keyed `fno_security_ids`) from `reference_security_ids`, so a symbol-mismatched F&O stock that is ALSO an NTM constituent is never tagged `reference_only` (it keeps its options). The query layer SELF-HEALS — once persisted, `store.fno_eligible_underlyings()` returns the stock by `symbol_name`, so `universe_query.classify_instrument` counts it as a stock with NO token-join propagation needed (verified by test, not assumed); `classify_instrument`/`is_in_fetch_scope` are deliberately left unchanged (lean ingest only consumes `is_universe_underlying`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ `brutex/universe.py` + `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py` + `brutex/dashboard/universe_query.py` all at **100.00% line+branch** (measured); ruff (check + format) + `mypy --strict` (the sole error is the pre-existing unrelated `cma` optional-dep limit in `engine/stage3_refine.py`) + `pyright` (0 errors) clean; the touched suites (test_universe, test_dashboard_instrument_loader, test_dashboard_universe_query, test_fno_index_diagnostic — 197) all green; new tests cover the admit arm (True/BSE-reject/derivative-reject branches), the persist-as-tradable loader path, and the F&O-AND-NTM precedence. 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-schema change — the admission is keyed on vendor-canonical numeric token-join evidence, widening only WHICH EQ rows the lake persists as tradable. **Files:** `brutex/universe.py`, `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`, `tests/unit/test_universe.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py`, `tests/unit/test_fno_index_diagnostic.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-EQ-TOKEN-JOIN-PERSIST-001. **Builds on / completes:** DEC-FNO-INDEX-EQ-TOKEN-JOIN-AUDIT-001 (#855, the audit-only split), DEC-FNO-INDEX-TOKEN-JOIN-001 (the vendor-canonical token-join), DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-ADMIT-001 (the id-keyed admission template), DEC-OPTIONS-PULL-GUARD-001 (F&O stays tradable over NTM-reference).

858. **DEC-UNIVERSE-CONSTITUENTS-TICK-IN-PLACE-001 — `/universe` "⊕ tick its constituents" selects the mapped stocks IN PLACE, no navigation to the Stocks screen** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "when I select nifty from indices and tick its constituents it should NOT be navigated to stocks symbols screen … without navigation all of its mapped symbols should be selected but the webpage screen should not be navigated"). **Why:** the prior handler (`brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`) force-switched the active tab — `filter = "stock"; …toggle .tab active… ; await loadInstruments();` — because the tick loop looked up each member in `UNIV` (the currently-loaded list), so it had to LOAD the stock list (replacing the visible view) before ticking. That yanked the operator off the index view to the Stocks screen on every tick. **What shipped (FRONTEND-ONLY, template JS; no backend / route / Python change):** the constituents handler now fetches the stock instruments in the BACKGROUND (`GET /api/v1/universe/instruments?kind=stock`) into a LOCAL list (never replacing `UNIV` nor re-assigning `filter`), builds a `symbol → inst` map, adds the (F&O-only-honoring) members to `selMulti`, and re-renders the CURRENT view — so only the selection count + "⤓ Pull spot" button update; the operator stays on the index screen. The ticked stocks still show their checkboxes if/when the operator later switches to the Stocks tab (`renderInstruments` reads `selMulti.has(symbol)`). The `/api/v1/universe/index-constituents` route + the F&O-only toggle semantics (DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-FULL-001) are UNCHANGED. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ template renders (route 200); a `/universe`-render regression test pins the in-place behavior — asserts the in-place marker + the `?kind=stock` background fetch are present AND the navigating `filter = "stock"` re-assignment is GONE; ruff clean; the touched universe-page suite green. 🟡 this repo has NO JS-runtime test harness, so the guard is at the rendered-template level (the strongest available without adding a browser-test stack — stated honestly, not claimed as a DOM test). 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / backend change — pure dashboard UX. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_app_backfill.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-CONSTITUENTS-TICK-IN-PLACE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 (the tick-its-constituents button), DEC-INDEX-CONSTITUENTS-FULL-001 (the F&O-only membership semantics), DEC-UNIVERSE-SELECTION-PRECISE-001 (the shared visibility/selection model).

859. **DEC-OPTIONS-COMPLETENESS-REAL-YEARS-001 — the /completeness OPTIONS table shows only the years that ACTUALLY have expiries + an honest `partial` for late-listed underlyings (no more fake 2020→2026 span, no more perpetual `growing`)** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "for some stocks the starting expiries are only from 2023/2024 but why are you showing 2020 till 2026 and even showing it as growing … make it partial and only the expiries year which is getting started"). **Why:** the F&O metadata pull calls `get_expiries(year=Y)` for EVERY year 2020→now; a year that returned ZERO expiries (a pre-listing year of a recently-listed F&O underlying — JIOFIN listed Aug-2023, ETERNAL ~2024 — or a gap) is recorded by Phase 1 as status `pending` with `expiries_pulled=0` (`metadata_pull.py:_rewrite_contract_counts` leaves the empty cell intact). `completeness.py` then (a) appended EVERY year — including those 0-expiry pending ones — to the displayed `years`, so a late-listed underlying FALSELY showed `2020,2021,…,2026`; and (b) `_option_verdict` returned `growing` if ANY cell was `pending`, so those empty pre-listing years kept the underlying **perpetually `growing`** (it could never stabilise). Both are dishonest (Golden Rule #1/#10). **What shipped (READ/ROLLUP side only — `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`; NO pull/registry/engine change):** **(1) real years only** — `_per_underlying_options` + `_fold_per_symbol_options` append a year to `years` ONLY when `expiries_pulled > 0`, so JIOFIN shows `[2023,2024,…]`, never the empty pre-listing years; `first_year`/`last_year` default to `None` when there are no real years. **(2) honest verdict** — `_option_verdict` now folds per-year `(status, expiries_pulled)` cells (not bare statuses): any `failed` → `failed`; else NO year has expiries → `none`; else a year that HAS expiries but is still `pending` → `growing` (DEFENSIVE / forward-compat, see the honesty note); else any requested year with ZERO expiries → **`partial`** (late-start / gap — the option history does not span the full requested range; honest, never a fabricated %); else any `expiries_only` (with expiries) → `partial`; else all-complete-non-empty → `stable`. A 0-expiry pre-listing year therefore NO LONGER forces `growing` (the stuck-growing bug). **Honesty note (hostile-review #859, Golden Rule #10):** the `growing` arm is currently UNREACHABLE in production — the ledger's `coverage_ledger.classify_cell` invariant is `pending ⟺ expiries_pulled == 0` (a year with discovered expiries is `expiries_only`/`complete`, never `pending`), so a `(pending, n>0)` cell is never emitted; a still-filling current year reads `expiries_only` → `partial` until it completes. The arm + its synthetic `(pending, n>0)` unit fixtures are retained as a DEFENSIVE / forward-compat fold (mirroring the existing defensive `OPT_NONE` aggregate case), NOT claimed as a live verdict; consequently the `growing_or_partial` aggregate bucket is effectively partial-only in real data. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (measured); ruff (check + format) + `pyright` (0 errors) + `mypy --strict` clean (the sole error is the pre-existing unrelated `cma` optional-dep limit in `engine/stage3_refine.py`); 38 completeness tests pass incl. the new `test_late_listed_underlying_shows_real_years_and_partial_not_growing` (JIOFIN: 2020-2022 zero-expiry → `years==[2023,2024]` + `partial`, not stuck growing) + the verdict-signature update. The "options have no knowable expected total" stance is preserved — `partial` here means "real history that doesn't span the full requested range", never a fabricated coverage %. 🚫 NO pull / registry / metadata_pull / engine / 52-vocab / scope change — purely the completeness DISPLAY rollup. (Optional follow-up noted for review: a 0-expiry pre-listing year could be recorded as a SETTLED "no-options-that-year" status in `metadata_pull.py` so re-pull skips it — but the completeness-side fix alone makes the DISPLAY honest.) **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`, `tests/unit/test_completeness.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-OPTIONS-COMPLETENESS-REAL-YEARS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-METADATA-LIVE-PROGRESS-001 (the options stable/growing/partial honest-status model), DEC-METADATA-CONTRACTS-COUNT-001 (the per-year coverage cells), DEC-COMPLETENESS-PAGE-001.

860. **DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 — make every `/movers` interaction feel INSTANT: split the expensive `top_n`-independent lake scan from the cheap rank, cache it per coordinate, bound the cold per-symbol read to the day's month Parquet, and make the sub-filter pill switch a zero-round-trip client re-render** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "the /movers page is SLOW on every interaction … make EVERY section feel INSTANT — O(1)-latency … with zero correctness change … be HONEST about what's achievable"). **Why:** every control change (tab / sub-filter / date / timeframe / time / top-N / exchange / Refresh) re-ran `run_{spot,futures,options}_snapshot`, which (a) walked the WHOLE `bars/` tree via `list_candle_datasets` and (b) for EACH screened symbol/contract called `pl.read_parquet(.../**/*.parquet)` — reading the ENTIRE multi-year partition into memory then filtering to one day in Python — i.e. **O(N_instruments × N_all_bars)** per click; the sub-filter pills (Gainers/Losers/Top Volume/Top Value …) re-fetched even though the payload already carried every category, and the exchange `<select>` was a no-op that the route IGNORED yet still triggered a full re-scan. **What shipped (lake/dashboard READ-only — the brute-force ENGINE is UNCHANGED, still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; the 52-vocab/scope/rate-limit/lake-schema all UNTOUCHED):** **(1) split scan from rank** — `movers_snapshot`/`movers_futures`/`movers_options` each grew a `compute_{spot,futures,options}_candidates(...) -> {Spot,Futures,Options}Candidates` core (the expensive, `top_n`-INDEPENDENT product of one lake scan: the per-instrument mover list + skipped count + normalised date [+ canonical tier/track for options]); the public `run_*_snapshot` are now thin `compute_* ∘ build_*_payload` composes — **behaviour byte-identical** (all 191 pre-existing movers tests pass unchanged). **(2) keyed snapshot cache** — NEW `brutex/dashboard/movers_cache.py` `MoversSnapshotCache` (thread-safe, capacity-bounded **LRU** [default 64 → O(capacity) space], generation-stamped) caches the candidate set per `candidate_key(asset, exchange, interval, date, time[, tier, track])`; it reuses the EXISTING coverage `SummaryCache.generation` as its write-invalidation signal (a pull/materialize bumps it → every cached snapshot is dirty → recompute, so the page never serves pre-pull data — zero new wiring at the write sites). Re-clicking a sub-filter, nudging `top_n`, or re-selecting a viewed coordinate is now an **O(1) cache hit + a cheap O(candidates·log candidates) re-rank**, never a re-scan. **(3) cold-path read bound** — NEW `brutex/data/lake_day_glob.py` `read_day_intraday_frame` reads ONLY the day's `1minute/<yyyy>/<mm>.parquet` for the intraday session readers (`_read_session_bars`/`_read_future_session`/`_session_value_paisa`): a SESSION-FILTERED IST trading day's 1-minute bars all live in that ONE monthly file (the 09:15–15:30 IST session is 03:45–10:00 **UTC**, never crossing a UTC month boundary — `partition_for_timestamp` partitions by UTC, verified), so the slice is **byte-equivalent for session-filtered symbols** but **O(one month)** not **O(all-bars)**. **SESSION-EXEMPT symbols (GIFT Nifty, ~21h — `session.SESSION_EXEMPT_SYMBOLS`) FALL BACK to the whole partition** (the hostile-review fold): their full-day series CAN cross a UTC month boundary, so an IST-month-1st bar can sit in the PRIOR UTC month's file; the symbol-aware `read_day_intraday_frame(..., symbol=)` reads the whole partition for them to stay exactly byte-equivalent — GIFT Nifty is rare/not-yet-admitted so the slow path never touches the hot NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX set, and F&O contract symbols are session-filtered unconditionally at ingest so they always take the fast month-bound path. (The DERIVED `1day` partition is midnight-IST = 18:30 UTC the prior day, so it can sit in the prior UTC month's file — the daily/prev-close readers are therefore deliberately LEFT whole-partition [a daily series is tiny]; mis-applying the month-bound there would drop month-boundary days, documented in the module.) **(4) exact exchange scope** — the route now accepts `?exchange=NSE|BSE` and threads it into discovery (`compute_*_candidates` filter datasets by exchange → an EXACT per-exchange top-N, fewer partitions scanned), part of the cache key; any other value ranks every exchange. **(5) frontend zero-round-trip sub-filter** (`templates/movers.html`) — the fetched payload (which already holds EVERY category for the coordinate) is cached client-side; switching the sub-filter pill re-renders the other category list IN THE BROWSER with NO server round-trip (falls back to a fetch only on first paint / preview); the exchange selector is now actually SENT. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — stated, not hidden):** ✅ the per-interaction HIT (the dominant interaction after the first view of a coordinate, + every sub-filter switch) is **O(1)** in the lake size — `tests/bench/test_movers_cache_o1.py` pins it flat (1000-instrument hit 563 ns ≈ 10-instrument 567 ns, ratio ≈ 1.0 under `_o1_tiers.ratio_ceiling`). 🟡 the FIRST computation of a coordinate (a miss, or the first read after a pull) STILL pays the real **O(N_instruments × N_bars-read)** lake scan — this is NOT claimed away; the month-bound caps the per-symbol read but ranking top-N inherently scans the candidate rows once, so it is **O(rows-scanned)**, NOT "O(1) total". The cache bounds how OFTEN that cost is paid (once per coordinate per write-generation). 🟡 two concurrent COLD misses of the same key both compute (no cross-thread wait — deliberately simple; the scan is a deterministic function of the coordinate so it is idempotent, last-write-wins); rare for a click-driven page, the cost is stated. 🟡 the **Futures/Options** tabs depend on the F&O historical-candle store as it exists today (a separate in-flight PR creates the dedicated F&O table); this PR makes them fast over whatever FNO `1minute` partitions are present and does not block on it — the **Spot** tab is fast unconditionally. The **Live** tab is being removed in a separate PR and was NOT touched (the client payload-cache applies to it generically, no Live-specific code added). 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / lake-schema change — pure read-path latency. **Coverage/gates:** `movers_cache.py` + `lake_day_glob.py` + the three `movers_*` modules at **100.00% line+branch** (measured); the new `api_movers` route region fully covered by the movers route tests; ruff (check + format) + `mypy --strict` (no new errors; the pre-existing `growwapi`/`cma` optional-dep notes are env artifacts of the local install, absent in CI's mypy job) + `pyright` (0 errors) + `bandit` clean; interrogate 100% under the CI flags. New tests: `tests/unit/test_movers_cache.py` (hit/miss, generation invalidation, LRU eviction, capacity guard, key building, raise-propagation, concurrent idempotence), `tests/unit/test_lake_day_glob.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_selectors.py`, `tests/integration/test_movers_exchange_cache.py` (spot/futures/options exchange scope + end-to-end cache hit→`mark_dirty`→recompute), `tests/bench/test_movers_cache_o1.py`. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_cache.py` (new), `brutex/data/lake_day_glob.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `tests/unit/test_movers_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_lake_day_glob.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_selectors.py`, `tests/integration/test_movers_exchange_cache.py`, `tests/bench/test_movers_cache_o1.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001 (the point-in-time movers page), DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 / DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-001 (the Futures/Options tabs), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 (#853 — 1-minute the sole fetched granularity, 1day derived), DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the `SummaryCache` generation signal reused for invalidation).
