863. **DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001 — `/db` + `/universe` per-interaction latency made flat (O(page)/O(visible)); zero correctness change** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "Two dashboard pages lag on every interaction … make BOTH feel INSTANT — O(1)/O(page)-latency … zero correctness change"). **Why (the REAL bottleneck per a 3-agent file:line diagnosis — not the assumed one):** (a) `/db` candle pager — `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py::query_candles` ALREADY did SQL `COUNT(*)` + `LIMIT/OFFSET` + `read_parquet` partition-pruning for the PAGE, but it then appended the derived `change_pct`/`open_gap_pct` columns (DEC-DB-CANDLE-DERIVED-001) by aggregating the **WHOLE multi-year 1-minute partition** (`_intraday_last_close_by_date` → `arg_max(close, ts) GROUP BY day`, NO bound) on EVERY paging/sort/apply click — so a click on a 6-year symbol scanned hundreds of thousands of rows just to baseline the page. (b) `/db` FRONTEND — `renderCandleView`/`renderTableView` rebuilt the ENTIRE control bar + grid (`dataEl.innerHTML = head + controls + grid`) on every interaction, which destroyed + recreated the date inputs and triggered the `bx-datepicker.js` `MutationObserver` to re-scan the whole document and rebuild the calendars on each click, AND blanked the panel to "loading…" (flash-to-empty). (c) `/universe` — the index/stock TAB SWITCH refetched `/api/v1/universe/instruments` every time (no client cache; the backend recomputes 3 latest-snapshot self-joins + serialises ~750 rows per call), the SEARCH box fired a full ~750-row rebuild per keystroke (no debounce), and the 15s completeness poll rebuilt the whole list on every change. **What shipped:** *(backend, fully gated — `db_view.py`)* a page-bounded intraday baseline: `_page_ist_dates` extracts the page's distinct IST dates and `_intraday_prev_close_by_page_date` reads the last-1-minute-close per day for ONLY the page's own `[min,max]` span (`WHERE timestamp` between IST-midnight instants — row-group-pruned) PLUS the single bar immediately before it (`ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1` — the one baseline outside the page), then reuses `_prev_trading_close`. A page's dates are a contiguous run of trading days, so prepending their shared predecessor makes the result **byte-for-byte identical** to the old full-partition scan for every page date (Golden Rule #7). The 1-DAY view keeps its full `_daily_close_by_date` scan (intrinsically tiny — ≤ one row per trading day, ~1.5k rows for 6 years, flat as the lake deepens). The brute-force ENGINE + the engine store are UNTOUCHED — this is the read-only viewer. *(frontend, template JS — `db.html`)* a controls-once / grid-per-interaction split: paging / sort / apply / limit route through `updateCandleGrid`/`updateTableGrid` which replace only `#dbgrid` + the row-count sub, leaving the control bar + date pickers in the DOM (no MutationObserver re-scan), and the grid is **dimmed in place** (`#dbgrid.is-loading`) instead of flashed to "loading…"; a dataset switch (column set can change) still does the full render. *(frontend, template JS — `universe.html`)* a per-tab instrument cache (`UNIV_CACHE[kind]` — only successful non-empty sets pinned; busted + force-refetched on a master reload), a ~140ms debounce on the search box, and `refreshCov()` which patches ONLY the per-row `.cov` strip on a completeness-poll change instead of rebuilding the list. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the per-interaction cost is **O(page date-span)** for `/db` (a dense intraday page ≈ 1–2 trading days regardless of stored years; DuckDB still reads each matched Parquet file's footer metadata, so this is flat in the ROW count, NOT a literal O(1)-total claim) and **O(visible)** for the `/universe` filter (one debounced render of the matching rows) + **O(1)-network** for a cached tab flip — explicitly NOT claimed as true O(1)-total where a bounded scan/footer read is unavoidable. ✅ proven: `query_candles` derived columns byte-identical under exhaustive contiguous-window equivalence + tiny-chunk paging vs single-page (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py`, 13 new cases); a flat-latency bench (`tests/bench/test_db_candle_query_o1.py`) — page latency 1.27× for a 12× deeper partition (vs the old O(rows) scan); `db_view.py` at 100.00% line + 100% branch; a live `TestClient` smoke (the page-bounded baseline correctly reads across a weekend gap); ruff + pyright clean; the rendered-template guards (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_latency_o1.py`, 6 cases) pin the frontend wiring. 🟡 this repo has NO JS-runtime/DOM test harness, so the frontend half is guarded at the rendered-template level (the established `test_dashboard_*_ux.py` pattern — stated honestly, not claimed as a DOM test). 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / data-contract change. **Coordination:** a separate session makes `/movers` fast + another REMOVES the Live feature — this PR deliberately did NOT touch Live or the movers route. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_latency_o1.py`, `tests/bench/test_db_candle_query_o1.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-QUERY-001 (the candle pager), DEC-DB-CANDLE-DERIVED-001 / DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001 / DEC-DB-CANDLE-PERINTERVAL-001 (the derived %-columns + their per-interval basis), DEC-UNIVERSE-RENDER-O1-001 (the prior frontend O(1) row-render fixes), DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001 (the per-row completeness strip).

864. **DEC-DB-VIEWER-PAGINATE-ALL-001 — EVERY `/db` tab is now O(page): the last two whole-table reads (F&O registry expiries/contracts + the window-ledger sidecar) are SQL-`LIMIT`/`OFFSET` paginated, completing the candle/option/F&O/DuckDB-table pages already bounded** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "even these pagination and all scenarios should be entirely applicable for all tables under database webpage … always I need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … O(1) latency … by covering all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions … common runtime dynamic scalable approach"). **Why:** after DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001 (#863) made the candle pager flat, two `/db` tabs STILL loaded every row: (a) the F&O **registry** — `db_view.list_registry_expiries`/`list_registry_contracts` called `RegistryStore.list_*` with NO bound + returned `total: len(rows)`, so a contracts chain of tens of thousands of legs was materialised + serialised + DOM-rendered whole; (b) the **window-ledger** route loaded `load_window_ledger(lake).to_rows()` entirely + returned `total: len(rows)`. The other tabs (DuckDB master tables via `query_table`/`sample_rows`, spot candles via `query_candles`, expired options via `query_option_candles`, F&O candles via the shared candle path) were ALREADY `COUNT(*)` + `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` bounded — these two were the remainder. **What shipped (COMMON pagination, reusing the existing `gridAndPager` + grid-split contract — no copy-paste):** *(registry — fully SQL-bounded)* `RegistryStore.list_expiries`/`list_contracts` gain optional `limit`/`offset` (a STATIC `" LIMIT ? OFFSET ?"` literal appended, bind-parameter values — the no-injection discipline preserved) + FILTERED `count_expiries`/`count_contracts` (the same `(? IS NULL OR col = ?)` pass-through, so a paged tab's `total` is the rows matching ITS filter, not the whole table); `db_view.list_registry_*` thread `limit`/`offset` (clamped `[1,500]`/`[0,∞)`) + return the FILTERED `COUNT(*)` total; the `/api/v1/db/registry/{expiries,contracts}` routes take `limit`/`offset`; `db.html` pages the registry grid in place (prev/next refresh only `#dbgrid`). *(window-ledger — bounded-read + page-slice)* the route takes `limit`/`offset`, loads the ledger (a SMALL bounded sidecar — one row per fetch window), slices `[offset:offset+limit]` BEFORE IST-formatting (only the page's rows are coerced/serialized), and returns the real (full) `total`; the slice preserves the canonical `WindowLedger.to_rows()` sort + derived columns (`empty_streak`/`in_pull_fetches`) byte-for-byte; `db.html` pages it like the registry. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the registry is fully **O(page)** (DuckDB `LIMIT/OFFSET` over the `(exch,underlying,expiry_date)` index — bench: first-page latency 1.04× for 10× more legs, flat) with an O(rows) FILTERED `COUNT(*)` for the total (cheap on the indexed cache); the window-ledger is **O(page) render + O(page) serialize** but the underlying *read* stays **O(windows)** — deliberately NOT rewritten to SQL-paginate, because the ledger is a small bounded sidecar (thousands of fetch windows, not the millions a candle partition holds) and replicating its `to_rows()` sort + legacy-file derived-column logic in SQL is high-risk for negligible gain (stated honestly, NOT claimed as an O(page)-read). So "every /db tab is O(page)" is true for the operator-visible render + serialize on ALL tabs, and O(page)-read on every tab EXCEPT the bounded ledger sidecar. ✅ proven: `brutex/data/registry_store.py` + `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` at **100.00% line+branch**; new store tests (filtered counts, limit/offset pages, last-partial-page, offset-past-end empty), db_view tests (page total is the FILTERED count not the page length, filter-aware total), an integration test (`test_paginates_with_limit_offset` — contiguous non-overlapping pages == the full read's slices, offset-past-end clean empty, byte-for-byte `to_rows()` order), a frontend guard (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_pagination.py`), a flat-latency bench (`tests/bench/test_registry_pagination_o1.py`); ruff + pyright clean; db.html JS re-parses. Worst cases covered: empty/missing registry (honest note, no invented row — Golden Rule #1), filtered-empty, offset past end, malformed date (→ HTTP 400 unchanged), no-lake-root. 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / data-contract change — read-only `/db` viewer only; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **Files:** `brutex/data/registry_store.py`, `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/unit/test_registry_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_db_view_registry.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_pagination.py`, `tests/bench/test_registry_pagination_o1.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-VIEWER-PAGINATE-ALL-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001 #863 (the candle pager + grid-split), DEC-DB-QUERY-001 (the SQL-bounded table/candle pages), DEC-DERIV-REGISTRY-DB-VIEW-001 (the registry `/db` tabs), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the ledger sidecar).

865. **DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 — derive per-option MONEYNESS (ITM/ATM/OTM) + a signed ATM±N strike offset for the ENTIRE F&O universe, surfaced on the options-movers screen (as-of snapshot) AND the `/db` F&O candle viewer (per-bar), from a shared DYNAMIC-grid engine** (2026-06-20, operator request: "for every option … whether that strike is atm or itm or otm like plus or minus … applicable for the entire fno symbols … O(1) … common/dynamic/scalable … no hallucination"). **Why:** the lake stores every F&O contract bar (DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 #861) but never said, for a given option at a given instant, whether it was in/at/out of the money or how many strikes it sat from the at-the-money rung — the single most-asked option attribute. Moneyness is **time-varying** (the strike is fixed but the underlying spot moves, so the same `24000 CE` reads OTM in the morning and ITM in the afternoon), so it MUST be **DERIVED at read time, never stored** (O(1) extra space, can never go stale — Golden Rule #1). **What shipped (lake/dashboard READ-only — the brute-force ENGINE is UNCHANGED, still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO new storage, NO write-path/scope/vocab/rate change):** **(1)** NEW pure `brutex/data/moneyness.py` — the ONE source of truth (stdlib + `Decimal`, NEVER raises): `classify(option_type, strike, spot, *, atm_band)` (CE: spot>strike→ITM / spot<strike→OTM; PE the mirror; non-option→`NA`; absent/≤0/non-finite spot|strike→`UNKNOWN`), `derive_strike_step(strikes)` (the **DYNAMIC** grid = the smallest positive gap of the distinct sorted strike ladder — so it works for EVERY F&O underlying [all ~212 single stocks AND the indices], where `options/strike_grid.py` only knows the 3 index grids and would `KeyError` on a stock — never a hardcoded NSE rule, Golden Rule #1), `atm_offset(strike, spot, step)` (signed `round((strike−spot)/step)`, ROUND_HALF_UP, anchor-independent), and `moneyness_view(...)` bundling the bucket + ATM±N + a compact label (band = `step/2` so the rung nearest spot reads ATM). **(2)** `dashboard/movers_options.py` — `OptionMover` gains `moneyness` + `atm_offset`; `compute_option_mover(..., strike_step=)` derives them vs the as-of snapshot spot; `compute_options_candidates` derives the step ONCE per `(underlying, expiry)` from the screened strike ladder and threads it in; `_option_row` emits the two payload fields. **(3)** `dashboard/templates/movers.html` — two new Options columns ("Moneyness" tinted green/red/muted · "ATM±N" signed). **(4)** `dashboard/db_view.py` — `query_candles` appends per-bar `moneyness` + `atm_offset` to every `segment="FNO"` page (stable column set on empty + populated): `_fno_moneyness_rows` parses the contract via `parse_fno_symbol`, derives the step from the SIBLING strike glob (`_fno_strike_step`), reads the underlying spot keyed by **bar timestamp** (`_underlying_spot_close_by_ts` — probes INDEX then CASH, BOUNDED to the page's `[min,max]` instant so it never materialises more than a page of spot bars), and classifies each bar against the spot at THAT instant; a FUTURE reads `NA`, an option whose underlying spot is absent reads `UNKNOWN` (never faked). **(5)** `data/fno_candle_lake.py` — the descriptor's `FNO_CANDLE_COLUMNS` gains the two `source="derived"` columns (the `/db` schema + `schema_meta` now advertise them as READ-time-derived, never stored). **(6)** `dashboard/templates/db.html` — the candle grid tints the `moneyness` cell + signs the `atm_offset` cell. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `moneyness.py` + `fno_candle_lake.py` + `db_view.py` + `movers_options.py` all at **100.00% line+branch** (measured); ruff (check + format) clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` 0 errors on all touched files; `vulture` (full-package, 80%) + `bandit` clean. The per-bar / per-row classification + ATM±N is **O(1)**; the per-query setup (derive step from the sibling glob, build the bounded spot map) is **O(siblings)** + **O(page)** ONCE, then O(1) per bar — NOT an O(1)-total claim. The 7 test types present: unit + property (Hypothesis: `moneyness_view` NEVER raises on arbitrary junk; the CALL/PUT mirror; the step is positive + minimal) + golden (a frozen CE/PE × ITM/ATM/OTM decode table) + integration (end-to-end movers snapshot with a real 3-strike lake → derived step → ATM±N; `query_candles` FNO page → per-bar moneyness vs the joined spot). 🟡 `movers.html` / `db.html` ride the dashboard suite's coverage (no JS-runtime harness — the tint/sign is a display-only concern asserted at the payload + rendered level). 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / write-path / storage change — moneyness is a read-time derivation over data ALREADY stored. **Files:** `brutex/data/moneyness.py`, `brutex/data/fno_candle_lake.py`, `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/unit/test_moneyness.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_fno_moneyness.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_fno.py`, `tests/unit/test_fno_candle_lake.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_options.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_options.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_datasets.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 (#861 — the F&O candle lake + `parse_fno_symbol` this derives over), DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-001 (the options-movers screen), DEC-DB-CANDLE-DERIVED-001 (the per-bar derived-column pattern `query_candles` already uses for `change_pct`/`open_gap_pct`), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the 2-dp spot grid moneyness classifies against), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (money 2dp display vs full-precision metrics).

866. **DEC-UNIVERSE-BACKEND-CACHE-001 — the `/universe` BACKEND summary + instruments reads are cached behind a content-revision token of the `instruments` table, so a repeat poll between two instrument loads is an O(1) dict handoff instead of an O(candidates) re-read + re-classification** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "go ahead with all the future PRs … always I need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) uniqueness O(1) deduplication O(1) mapping O(1) latency with O(1) time + space complexity … common runtime dynamic scalable approach … cover all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions bugs … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001 (#863) made the `/universe` FRONTEND instant (per-tab client cache + debounce + in-place completeness patch) but left the BACKEND recomputing on every poll that DID reach it: `api_universe_summary` + `api_universe_instruments` each re-ran three lean store reads — `fno_eligible_underlyings()` (a SQL `DISTINCT`), `list_index_equity_instruments()` (the ~hundreds of IDX+EQ candidate rows, materialised as `Instrument` objects), `reference_only_security_ids()` — then re-classified them via `universe_query` on EVERY call. The page re-polls on first paint, the "F&O only" toggle, the kind tab, and the 30s completeness refresh; the master changes only when a pull / keyless instrument-load lands, so the SAME deterministic `O(candidates)` scan (measured ~25 ms over ~750 underlyings; ~108 ms at 4000) was paid over and over. **What shipped (read-only dashboard accelerator — the brute-force ENGINE is UNCHANGED, still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO store/schema/scope/vocab/rate change):** NEW `brutex/dashboard/universe_cache.py` `UniverseSnapshotCache` (thread-safe, single-resident) — it memoises the three base reads + the derived `summary` dict + the per-`kind` (`None`/`index`/`stock`) instrument row lists, keyed by a **content-revision token** = `(count(*), max(fetched_at))` over the **`instruments`** table ITSELF (the exact table the cached reads project from). Every `upsert_many` stamps a fresh `fetched_at = datetime.now(UTC)` on every written row, so ANY master change strictly advances `max(fetched_at)` and/or moves `count(*)` → the token moves → the cache rebuilds; an empty store keys at the stable `(0, "")`. The token is keyed off `instruments` content directly — NOT the `instrument_runs` audit sidecar, which is written by a SEPARATE `record_run` call and can lag an upsert (a stale-illusion trap that keying off the content table AVOIDS — Golden Rule #1). The token probe is a `COUNT`+`MAX` aggregate DuckDB answers from row-group statistics (measured FLAT: 615 µs at 50 rows ≈ 640 µs at 5000), strictly cheaper than the `list_index_equity_instruments` read it guards. Wired into `build_app` as a `universe_cache` param (mirrors the `summary_cache`/`movers_cache` injection; defaults to a fresh production instance); the two routes now call `_universe_cache.summary(store)` / `.instruments(store, kind=)` (a bad `kind` still raises `ValueError` → HTTP 400, BEFORE any caching — no poison). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10 — stated, not hidden):** ✅ a cached HIT (the dominant interaction between two loads) is **O(1)** in the universe size — a flat token probe + a dict handoff under one lock; `tests/bench/test_universe_cache_o1.py` pins it flat (hit-latency ratio **1.02×** for a 100× deeper universe, 40 → 4000 underlyings, vs the cold read scaling 13×→166×). 🟡 the FIRST read after a load (a miss) STILL pays the real **O(candidates)** base read + classification — NOT claimed away; the cache bounds how OFTEN that cost is paid (once per revision), it does not make the scan O(1). 🟡 two concurrent COLD misses each recompute (no cross-thread wait — deliberately simple, mirrors `MoversSnapshotCache`; the reads are a deterministic function of the revision so the duplicate is idempotent, last-write-wins, and the `_current`/`summary` re-checks ADOPT a peer's already-memoised payload). 🟡 a residual stated honestly: two DISTINCT-content writes within the SAME microsecond that ALSO preserve the exact row count would share a token — impossible for a click-driven dashboard fed by network pulls seconds apart, and a re-read (the conservative direction), never a corruption. 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / store-schema change — `build_app`-layer read cache only; `InstrumentStore` is untouched. **Coverage/gates:** `brutex/dashboard/universe_cache.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (`tests/unit/test_universe_cache.py` — empty-store stable token, summary/instruments hit identity, per-kind independent memo, bad-kind ValueError-not-cached, master-change invalidation + rebuild, the defensive `_revision` `None`-row / `None`-count branches, and the two concurrent-install re-check branches via deterministic side-effect fakes — no flaky threads); `mypy --strict brutex` clean (the sole error anywhere is the pre-existing unrelated `cma` optional-dep stub note in `engine/stage3_refine.py`, an env artifact absent in CI's `[optimize]` job); `pyright` 0 errors / 0 warnings; ruff (check + format) + bandit clean; the 42 existing `/universe` route + backfill tests pass unchanged (byte-identical payloads). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/universe_cache.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_universe_cache.py`, `tests/bench/test_universe_cache_o1.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-BACKEND-CACHE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001 (#863, the `/universe` FRONTEND O(1) work this completes on the backend), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean base reads it caches), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 (#860, the `MoversSnapshotCache` injection + honest-envelope pattern mirrored here), DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the `SummaryCache` build_app-param precedent).

867. **DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001 — the `/db` candle-pager TOTAL (`COUNT(*)` over `read_parquet(glob)`) is memoised behind a generation-stamped cache, so a prev/next paging click within one dataset reuses the cached total instead of re-reading every Parquet footer** (2026-06-20, operator decree: "go ahead with all the future PRs … always I need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … by covering all worst cases … no illusion or hallucination" — option "Ship the built COUNT cache (honest)" chosen via AskUserQuestion after the measurement below). **Why + the HONEST finding first (Golden Rule #1/#10):** the candle pager (`db_view.query_candles`) computes the page `total` as `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM read_parquet(?, union_by_name=true)` on EVERY paging click; DuckDB answers a `COUNT(*)` over a Parquet glob from each file's FOOTER, so it is **O(files)** (measured 1.24 ms at 3 monthly files → 3.92 ms at 72 — ~0.05 ms/file, growing as the lake deepens). The total is INVARIANT across paging / sort / column-subsetting of one `(coords, start, end)` — only a pull changes it — so re-reading every footer per click is pure waste. **A measured caveat that bounds the claim (stated, not hidden):** the COUNT is NOT the dominant paging cost — the page DATA query (`SELECT … ORDER BY "timestamp" DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` over the same glob) is itself **O(files)** and ~2.4× larger (3.74 ms → 9.56 ms across the same depths) because it too opens every file's footer to plan the scan. So this cache removes ONE of the two O(files) footer scans (the COUNT, ~16% of a deep-partition click); it does **NOT** make paging O(1) — true O(page) paging needs a write-time lake manifest (file → timestamp-range + row-count) so the read narrows the glob to the page's file(s), scoped here as explicit FUTURE work, NOT claimed. **What shipped (read-only `/db` viewer accelerator — the brute-force ENGINE is UNCHANGED, still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO store/schema/scope/vocab/rate/write-path change):** `db_view.query_candles` gains an OPTIONAL `count_cache` + `generation` (a structural `CandleCountCache` `Protocol` + the pure `candle_count_key(exchange, segment, symbol, interval, start, end)` helper — the key excludes `limit`/`offset`/`descending`/`columns`, the invariance the cache exploits); when injected, the `COUNT(*)` runs through `count_cache.get_or_compute(key, generation, compute=…)`, else it runs inline (the pure-function default — behaviour byte-identical, all 159 existing `query_candles` tests pass unchanged). `build_app` instantiates `_candle_count_cache` by REUSING the COMMON generation-stamped LRU `MoversSnapshotCache` (CLAUDE.md §11 — it is a generic keyed cache; no movers coupling, just the shared implementation, so no jscpd duplication) and the `/api/v1/db/candles` route passes it + `_summary_cache.generation`. Invalidation is the SAME write-generation signal the movers cache uses — a pull/materialize bumps `_summary_cache.generation` → the cached total is dirty → recount (never a stale total — Golden Rule #1). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a cached-total HIT (the dominant interaction — every paging click after the first view of a dataset) is **O(1)** in the partition depth: `tests/bench/test_db_candle_count_cache_o1.py` pins the cached-total retrieval FLAT (hit ratio ~1.0 at 72 vs 6 months, under `ratio_ceiling`), and `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_candle_count_cache.py` proves the `COUNT(*)` executes exactly ONCE across paging clicks of one (dataset, generation) via a COUNT-counting connection. 🟡 the FIRST view of a (dataset, filter) per generation STILL pays the real O(files) `COUNT(*)` — the cache bounds how OFTEN, not the scan itself. 🟡 paging is NOT O(1) overall — the page DATA query remains O(files) (the larger residual); this cache is a ~16%-on-deep-partitions constant-factor win + a step toward O(1), explicitly NOT the whole fix. 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate / write-path / store-schema change — `query_candles` stays the pure owner of the query (cache is an optional injected accelerator); the empty/not-yet-pulled partition early-returns `total: 0` WITHOUT touching the cache. **Coverage/gates:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (259 db_view unit tests incl. the 9 new count-cache cases — key format/None-bounds/distinct, byte-identical cached==uncached total, COUNT-once-across-pages, generation-bump recount, distinct-dataset independence, empty-partition no-cache, pure default); `mypy --strict brutex` clean (sole error the pre-existing unrelated `cma` stub in `engine/stage3_refine.py`); `pyright` 0 errors/0 warnings; ruff (check + format) + bandit clean; the candle route + e2e dashboard tests pass unchanged. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_candle_count_cache.py`, `tests/bench/test_db_candle_count_cache_o1.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001 (#863, the candle pager + the page-bounded derived-column baseline), DEC-DB-QUERY-001 (the SQL-bounded candle pager), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 (#860, the `MoversSnapshotCache` generation-stamped LRU reused here), DEC-UNIVERSE-BACKEND-CACHE-001 (#866, the sibling generation/content-token cache pattern). **Future work (NOT this PR):** a write-time lake manifest for true O(page) paging (narrows BOTH the COUNT and the data query to the page's file(s)).

868. **DEC-SPOT-COMPLETENESS-2020-FLOOR-001 — the `/completeness` + `/universe` SPOT 1-minute verdict is HONESTLY downgraded `full` → `partial` when the symbol's covered data does NOT begin in JANUARY 2020 (a late listing / late vendor data — even one that starts later WITHIN 2020), so only symbols with the solid full-2020 history read `full`** (2026-06-21, operator decree: "even when we have started our start date starting Jan 1 2020 … TMPV and etc symbols still have the data starting only from 2023 … this also needs to be marked as partial … only then we need to understand which one has the solid data especially starting 2020 for strong evidence in our deep drill brute force backtesting" + the follow-up AskUserQuestion decree "must have Jan-2020 data": a within-2020-but-late start like TATACONSUM 2020-02-27 / MAXHEALTH 2020-08-21 is ALSO `partial`). **Why (Golden Rule #1/#10):** the spot pull starts at the `GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR` (2020-01-01), so the window ledger PLANS a window for every trading day from 2020. A LATE-listed / late-data symbol (JIOFIN `2023-08-21`, SHRIRAMFIN `2022-12-20`, TMPV `2025-10-24`, and within-2020-but-late starts like TATACONSUM `2020-02-27` / MAXHEALTH `2020-08-21`) has NO vendor bars before its first bar — but those pre-start windows still RESOLVE (the vendor honestly returns empty under DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001's window-ledger), so EVERY planned window is `settled` and the prior verdict read `full` even though the covered range begins after the start of 2020. That over-claimed "complete 2020→today" coverage and made it impossible to tell, at a glance, WHICH symbols actually hold the strong 2020-anchored evidence the deep-drill brute-force backtest needs. This is the SPOT analog of the OPTIONS real-years fix (DEC-OPTIONS-COMPLETENESS-REAL-YEARS-001, #859). **What shipped (read/rollup-side only — `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`; NO pull/registry/engine/store/schema/scope/vocab change; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** one COMMON helper `_spot_dimension_verdict_with_floor(completeness, first_date)` (CLAUDE.md §11 — single source of truth for BOTH rollups) that takes the base `_spot_dimension_verdict` and, ONLY when it is `full` AND `_from_2020(first_date)` is False (the earliest bar is after January 2020, OR there are no bars at all — `first_date` None), returns `partial` instead; `partial`/`failed`/`none` already carry no positive 2020 claim and pass through byte-identically. Wired into the scoreboard rollup (`_per_symbol_spot`) AND the per-symbol detail (`_spot_dimension_detail`, the `/universe` strip), so the `OVERALL` + `1-MINUTE` columns, the per-category `full_1minute` count (`_aggregate_spot`), and the downloadable CSV all reflect the honest downgrade; the explicit first→last bar dates + the `from_2020` flag (already carried) disambiguate WHY a row is `partial`. The January-2020 floor bar (`_FROM_2020_EXCLUSIVE_UPPER = 2020-02-01`, operator decree "must have Jan-2020 data") is MONTH-granular — TATACONSUM 2020-02-27 + MAXHEALTH 2020-08-21 start in 2020 but AFTER January, so they are correctly `partial`; month-granular (not exact-day) is robust to which exact January-2020 trading day the vendor serves (Jan-1 is a market holiday), never a brittle single-date threshold. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (43 completeness tests, +5 new — the JIOFIN late-start scoreboard downgrade, the settled-but-no-bars first_date-None edge, the TMPV per-symbol-detail downgrade, the within-2020-late TATACONSUM/MAXHEALTH `partial` case, the Jan-31-full vs Feb-1-partial boundary — plus the two existing `full` tests updated to a January-2020 first_date so they stay genuinely full); ruff (check + format) clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (sole error the pre-existing unrelated `cma` stub in `engine/stage3_refine.py`). 🚫 NO new false `none`: a genuinely-never-pulled dimension stays `none`; only a `settled`-but-not-2020 dimension moves `full`→`partial` (it HAS data, just not from the floor). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py`, `tests/unit/test_completeness.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SPOT-COMPLETENESS-2020-FLOOR-001. **Builds on:** DEC-OPTIONS-COMPLETENESS-REAL-YEARS-001 (#859, the options real-years/`partial` analog), DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001 (the per-symbol `from_2020` flag + first/last dates), DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 (the window-ledger that resolves empty pre-listing windows), DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 (#722, the 2020-01-01 `GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR`), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 (#853, 1-minute the sole scored spot dimension).

869. **DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-LABEL-001 — show the option moneyness + strike-distance as ONE combined cell ("ITM -1" / "OTM +10" / "ATM"), replacing the split bucket + ATM±N columns the operator could not read at a glance** (2026-06-21, operator: "for otm or itm it should clearly display itm -1 or itm -10 or otm +1 or otm +10 like plus or minus numbers also — why is that missing"). **Why:** DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 (#865) shipped moneyness as TWO separate columns — a bare bucket ("Moneyness" = ITM/ATM/OTM) and a raw signed strike offset ("ATM±N" = -8/+8) — so the single glanceable "in/out of the money by N strikes" reading the operator wanted ("ITM -10", "OTM +1") was split across two cells and easy to miss. **What shipped (lake/dashboard READ-only — the brute-force ENGINE is UNCHANGED, still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO storage/scope/vocab/rate change):** **(1)** `brutex/data/moneyness.py` `_format_label` reformatted to the trader-facing **`"<bucket> <signed depth>"`** string: `"ITM -1"` / `"ITM -10"` (in the money by N strikes) · `"OTM +1"` / `"OTM +10"` (out by N strikes) · `"ATM"` · `"ITM"` / `"OTM"` (no strike grid → bucket only) · `"—"` (a future) · `"?"` (spot absent). The sign tracks the **BUCKET** (ITM negative, OTM positive), so it reads identically for calls AND puts — a deep-ITM put still shows `"ITM -N"`, never `"ITM +N"` (the raw `atm_offset` strike-vs-spot sign would flip for puts; the label deliberately does not). Depth = `|atm_offset|` strikes from the at-the-money rung. **(2)** Options-movers screen — `OptionMover` gains `moneyness_label`; `compute_option_mover` sets it from `moneyness_view().label`; `_option_row` emits it as the `"moneyness"` payload key (the raw bucket moves to `"moneyness_bucket"`, `atm_offset` stays for sorting); `movers.html` collapses the two columns to ONE "Moneyness" column reading the label + tints by the leading bucket (ITM green / OTM red). **(3)** `/db` F&O candle viewer — `db_view._fno_moneyness_rows` now returns the single combined label per bar; `FNO_MONEYNESS_COLUMNS` + `fno_candle_lake.FNO_CANDLE_COLUMNS` collapse the `(moneyness, atm_offset)` derived pair into ONE `source="derived"` `moneyness` column (the label); `db.html` tints by the leading bucket. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `moneyness.py` + `db_view.py` + `movers_options.py` + `fno_candle_lake.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (measured); ruff (check+format) + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0 errors) + `vulture` (full-package, 80%) clean. Pure DISPLAY reshape over the SAME derived values of #865 — moneyness is still read-time-derived, never stored; the per-bar/per-row O(1) classification is unchanged. 🟡 `movers.html` / `db.html` ride the dashboard suite's coverage (no JS-runtime harness — the single-column reshape + tint asserted at the payload + rendered level). 🚫 NO engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-limit / write-path / storage change. **Files:** `brutex/data/moneyness.py`, `brutex/data/fno_candle_lake.py`, `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/unit/test_moneyness.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_options.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_fno_moneyness.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_fno.py`, `tests/unit/test_fno_candle_lake.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_options.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_datasets.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-LABEL-001. **Builds on:** DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 (#865 — the moneyness engine + the two-column surfacing this reshapes into one).
870. **DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-RECONCILE-001 — a real-time, self-checking GREEN/RED audit that proves the core spot↔options mapping is precise: every options-eligible spot underlying must actually have pulled its option expiries, or it is flagged — no "trust me", no hallucination** (2026-06-21, operator: "how confident or guaranteed … that these spot underlying symbols and their mapping of futures and options are precisely extracted and mapped … without hallucination or illusion or acting like it's mapped correctly … I need real-time guarantee and assurance" — option "Both F6 then F2" chosen via AskUserQuestion). **Why (Golden Rule #1/#10):** the spot↔F&O mapping uses 3 bridges (direct `underlying_symbol`==`trading_symbol`, the index-alias map, and the numeric token-join) and is HIGH-confidence for indices + plain stocks — but the M&M (0 expiries) / BAJAJ-AUTO (2024-only) gaps PROVE it is not 100%: the options FETCH (`adapters/groww/contracts.py` `resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts`) hands the vendor the spot `trading_symbol` VERBATIM with no normalization, so `M&M`'s `&` — the HTTP query-string separator, sent un-encoded — silently returns empty. (The operator's `instrument.csv` later CONFIRMED the mapping/extraction itself is EXACT for both: M&M token 2031 + BAJAJ-AUTO token 16669 each match their FUT/CE/PE legs on BOTH `underlying_symbol` string AND `underlying_exchange_token`; BAJAJ-AUTO's legs use `BAJAJ-AUTO` with the hyphen, NOT `BAJAJAUTO` — so BAJAJ-AUTO's 2024-only is a SEPARATE shortfall, NOT a symbol mismatch, to be confirmed on a clean re-pull. F2 fixes the `&`-encoding for M&M.) There was NO surface that turns "is the mapping precise?" into a number you can WATCH. **What shipped (the DETECTOR — read-only; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** a NEW PURE module `brutex/data/mapping_integrity.py` (`reconcile_mapping_integrity` + `coverage_years_from_records` + `report_to_dict`, frozen `EligibleSpot`/`UnderPulledSpot`/`MappingIntegrityReport`) that, in ONE O(eligible) pass over O(1) dict/set lookups (NO 89k legs — the lean store discards them, so it reads the store-level `fno_eligible_underlyings()` + the coverage ledger, NOT a leg re-scan), flags every options-eligible spot that pulled ZERO expiries (`reason="none"` — the GATING red, e.g. M&M) or only PART of the expected 2020→today span (`reason="partial"` — amber, e.g. BAJAJ-AUTO's 2024-only; partial does NOT gate because telling a genuine late listing from a bug is the vendor-bounded completeness verdict's job, never a fabricated total). `is_green` ⟺ no non-whitelisted zero-coverage eligible spot. Surfaced as a NEW `GET /api/v1/universe/mapping-integrity` route (thin glue over the 100%-tested core) + a green/red `/universe` panel (`#mappanel` + `loadMappingIntegrity`, 15s live poll). The whitelist (documented genuine late listings) defaults EMPTY — we do NOT hardcode NSE listing dates (Golden Rule #1); red therefore fires only on genuinely-zero coverage (M&M), while a late listing that pulled SOME years reads amber. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `brutex/data/mapping_integrity.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (13 unit + 3 integration tests: full/none(M&M)/partial(BAJAJ-AUTO)/whitelisted/empty-span/empty-universe/dedup/both-input-shapes/route-red/route-green/503); ruff + ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean. ⚠️ this module DETECTS, it does not FIX — M&M reads RED here until **F2 (DEC follow-up)** normalises the options-fetch symbol (route the vendor F&O underlying via the token-join + encode `&`); that red is the honest, intended pre-fix proof, after which the panel flips GREEN. 📋 FOLLOW-UPS (NOT this PR): F2 the options-fetch fix; a downloadable CSV report + a CI gate over a committed fixture; an ingest-time orphan-leg capture (every leg maps to a spot) — the lean store discards legs, so that needs an ingest hook. **Files:** `brutex/data/mapping_integrity.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_mapping_integrity.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_mapping_integrity.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_template.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-RECONCILE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-SPOT-COMPLETENESS-2020-FLOOR-001 (#868, the completeness honesty sibling), DEC-COMPLETENESS-UNIVERSE-001 (the per-symbol pull-page surface this panel joins), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean store whose discarded legs shape the store-fed inputs), DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001 (#845, the spot-side special-char resolve F2 extends to the options fetch).

871. **DEC-FUTURES-PULL-ENABLE-001 — formally ENABLE futures pulling: supersede the retired "we will NEVER pull futures" decree so the docs match the code, which already pulls FUT into the reference lake** (2026-06-21, operator: "Add futures pulling also in the plan queue … enable futures pulling too"). **The HONEST finding first (Golden Rule #1/#10):** futures pulling is NOT new — it was ALREADY built + wired by DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (#707) + DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 (#720): `contracts.py` `future_contracts` (the FUT-only sibling of `option_contracts`), `option_ingest.py` `ingest_underlying_futures` (the FUT mirror, `market=GROWW_FUTURE_COVERAGE_MARKET`), `metadata_pull._fetch_contracts` persists EVERY leg (FUT+CE+PE, no side filter), `composite_pull` pulls FUT + CE/PE candles, and `historical_pull._contract_market` routes a `FUT` leg to the `groww-future` coverage namespace. The pull paths scope on the FUT-inclusive `build_fno_eligible_underlyings` + the reference-only partition, NOT on the options-only `build_options_eligible_underlyings` (which is the OPT-badge DETECTOR, never a pull gate). **The gap this closes (a real Golden-Rule-#3 contradiction):** the `build_options_eligible_underlyings` docstring (`universe.py:349`) STILL quoted the Dhan-era decree "we will NEVER pull futures — only options" (DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001, #602 — the prior vendor's options-CHAIN quota guard), and the `/coverage/windows` Futures-tab empty hint implied a non-existent "Type: futures or both" selector — so the DOCS said the opposite of what the CODE does. The operator's `/coverage/windows` Futures tab read `0 windows` only because no FUT *candle* pull had been run/recorded yet (metadata persists FUT legs to the registry; the candle windows fill when `Pull historical`/composite runs over them) — a DATA/run gap, not a code gap. **What shipped (DOCS/honesty reconciliation — NO behaviour change; futures already pulled):** (1) `universe.py` `build_options_eligible_underlyings` docstring rewritten — strike the "never pull futures" decree quote, mark the pull-scope clause of #602 SUPERSEDED, clarify the set is the OPT-badge detector only (NOT a pull gate) and that futures ARE pulled per #707/#871; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX — futures are LAKE/REFERENCE_ONLY, NEVER in the 52-condition vocab. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the futures-pull path is comprehensively pre-existing-tested — `tests/unit/test_groww_contracts.py` `test_future_contracts_keeps_only_fut` (FUT-only filter), `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py` `test_ingest_underlying_futures_full_path` (FUT leg ingested via the shared driver), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py` (the `groww-future` window namespace bucket), `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py` `test_contract_market_split` (`_contract_market(FUT)==groww-future`); index futures (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY) carry no such risk. 🚫 NO new pull capability, NO engine/scope/vocab change — futures were already enabled by #707; this entry formalises it + fixes the contradicting docs. **Files:** `brutex/universe.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/fetch_windows.html`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-PULL-ENABLE-001. **Supersedes:** the pull-scope clause of DEC-OPTIONS-ELIGIBLE-GUARD-001 (#602). **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (#707, the futures-pull engine this formalises), DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 (#720, futures on /movers), DEC-COVERAGE-GROWW-NAMESPACE-001 (the `groww-future` window namespace).

872. **DEC-ONE-CLICK-PIPELINE-001 — a single "▶ Pull EVERYTHING" button that runs the whole data pull as ONE gated chain: spot → expiries+contracts → historical, each phase starting only once the previous one finishes clean** (2026-06-21, operator: "provide one button which should do all the process in a single shot instead of clicking everything manually one by one … started from pull spot once it is successfully completed then pull expiries and contracts and when it is successfully completed and then pull historical"). **Why:** the `/universe` page exposed the pull as THREE separate buttons the operator clicked in sequence, manually waiting on each to finish before starting the next — exactly the per-step manual toil the operator asked to collapse into one click, and a violation of CLAUDE.md §11 AUTOMATED (zero clicks per day). **What shipped (a THIN sequencer over the three EXISTING, separately-tested spines — NO new pull engine, NO behaviour change to the individual pulls):** a NEW PURE module `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py` — three concrete-typed gates (`spot_phase_ok` = not `auth_aborted` AND not `quota_exhausted` AND `still_failed_windows == 0`; `metadata_phase_ok` = `expiry_failures == 0` AND `contract_failures == 0`; `historical_phase_ok` = a `None` candle sub-report is a no-op, else not `auth_aborted` AND `still_failed_windows == 0` AND `failed_pairs == 0`), a frozen-style `PipelinePullReport` (each phase's real report or `None` + `stopped_after` + `note` + an `ok` property + `to_dict`), and `run_full_pipeline(*, run_spot, run_metadata, run_historical)` that calls three INJECTED callables in order, applying the gate BETWEEN phases so a failed earlier phase STOPS the chain (fail-CLOSED — the later phases never make a doomed vendor call and are reported `None`, never falsely "complete"). The gates/runner read the REAL report fields of `BulkSpotReport` (`pull_controller.py`), `MetadataPullReport` (`metadata_pull.py`), and `CompositePullReport`/`HistoricalPullReport` (`composite_pull.py`/`historical_pull.py`) — verified against the dataclasses, not guessed (Golden Rule #1). Wired as `POST /api/v1/universe/pull-pipeline` (a thin route that binds the three callables to `pull_all_spot` / `pull_expiries_contracts` / `pull_historical_for_underlyings` over the WHOLE admitted universe — every index+stock spot for phase 1; every F&O-eligible underlying for phases 2+3 with reference-only names a true zero-call no-op — and runs `run_full_pipeline` on the SAME single-flight `BackgroundPullJob` the other pulls use; the `_work` body is `# pragma: no cover` exactly like its sibling routes since it runs on the job thread) + a green hero "▶ Pull EVERYTHING — one click, full pipeline" button on `/universe` (`#pullPipelineBtn`, reusing the existing `startAndPoll` + `setBulkDisabled` single-flight machinery). **Why injected callables (the testability seam):** the sequencer takes plain `Callable[[], Report]`, so the ENTIRE control flow — every gate, every stop-early branch, the note synthesis, the `ok` property, `to_dict` — is unit-testable offline with trivial fakes that return the real report dataclasses (ZERO network; CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON+AUTOMATED). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (27 unit tests over the gate matrix + sequencing + `ok`/`to_dict`/notes) + a route test with all three spines faked offline (2 tests); ruff + ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean on both `pipeline_pull.py` and `app.py`. ✅ the sequencer itself is O(1) (three calls + three gate checks); ❌ NO throughput claim — the WORK it triggers is the real multi-hour full-history vendor fill (network-bound, NOT O(1)-total — stated, not hidden). ✅ idempotent — phase 3's composite re-runs the metadata enumeration internally but incrementally (skips the cells phase 2 already settled, Golden Rule #7), so the separate phase-2 gate is preserved without a wasteful re-pull. 🚫 NO engine/scope/vocab change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; this is pure dashboard orchestration over already-tested pull paths. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_pipeline_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-ONE-CLICK-PIPELINE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DERIV-METADATA-ROUTE-001 (the metadata phase), DEC-DERIV-PULL-HISTORICAL-001 + DEC-FNO-ONECLICK-HISTORICAL-001 (the historical/composite phase), DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-UNIFY-001 (the spot phase), DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 (the spot verdict the pipeline surfaces), DEC-FUTURES-PULL-ENABLE-001 (#871, futures ride phase 3's composite).

874. **DEC-INSTRUMENT-MASTER-INTEGRITY-001 — a parse-time STRUCTURAL audit over the WHOLE instrument.csv master proving every futures/option leg maps to exactly ONE index/equity spot (by symbol AND numeric token), captured at ingest BEFORE the lean store discards the ~89k legs; surfaced green/red + downloadable CSV** (2026-06-21, operator: "this instruments csv will be thoroughly checked tracked monitored audited reviewed logged captured … especially to do the precise mapping for indices equities spot futures options … always I need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) uniqueness/dedup/mapping/latency … covering all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions bugs … common runtime dynamic scalable … completely fully comprehensively automated with real time checks … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** the `instrument.csv` master is the single source of truth for ALL instrument types (IDX/EQ/FUT/CE/PE), but there was NO check that each derivative leg actually maps to a real spot underlying — and the lean ingest (DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001) DISCARDS the ~89k FUT/CE/PE legs straight after parse, so ingest is the ONLY moment the leg→spot mapping can be verified. This is the documented follow-up #3 of DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-RECONCILE-001 (#870, "an ingest-time orphan-leg capture"). It is the STRUCTURAL sibling of #870 (which is the COVERAGE audit — did each eligible spot PULL its expiries); #874 is the MAPPING audit — does each leg MAP to a spot. **What shipped (READ-ONLY; DETECT-only; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; legs are SUMMARISED, never re-stored, so the lean-store decree stands):** (1) a NEW PURE `brutex/data/master_integrity.py` `audit_master_integrity(instruments, *, index_aliases, now, run_id, csv_source_sha256)` — TWO linear sweeps over the parsed universe (O(rows) time, O(1) per lookup, O(spots) space, NO nested scan): pass 1 builds `spot_by_symbol[(exch,symbol)]` + `spot_by_token[(exch,security_id)]` (only GENUINE numeric-token spots — a non-numeric NSE-index token is a blake2b surrogate that can never joinably equal a leg token, the same `_has_genuine_numeric_token` rule as the loader, replicated self-contained so `data/` imports no `dashboard/`), pass 2 resolves every leg into EXACTLY one bucket — `resolved_both` / `resolved_symbol_only` (NSE-index surrogate token) / `resolved_token_only` (the special-char case: M&M / BAJAJ-AUTO whose spot symbol differs but the numeric token agrees) / or a GATING failure `orphan` / `ambiguous` (two spots share a symbol) / `disagreement` (symbol→A, token→B) / `empty_underlying`; PLUS a non-gating `test_instrument` bucket for EXCHANGE TEST legs (`*NSETEST*`/`*BSETEST*` — every NSE/BSE master injects fake test contracts that have no real spot; counted + reported, EXCLUDED from the verdict so they are never a perpetual false-RED, never silently dropped — injectable markers, DYNAMIC); plus per-type counts, dedup-collision count, spots-with-no-legs, special-char underlyings (BOTH the orphan AND special-char SAMPLES are CAPPED at 200 with exact full counts, so the persisted summary never bloats). The injected `{spot_symbol: fno_underlying_symbol}` alias map (reversed) resolves NIFTYJR↔NIFTYNXT50 etc. `is_green` ⟺ zero gating failures. `report_to_dict`/`report_from_dict` round-trip. (2) an INGEST HOOK `instrument_loader._persist_master_integrity` — runs the audit against the FULL leg-bearing `index.universe` while it is still in memory (between `_classify_option_pullable` and the lean discard), emits a structlog counts line, and PERSISTS the bounded JSON summary to `schema_meta` via a NEW generic `InstrumentStore.set_meta`/`get_meta` (the legs are gone by the time the routes run, so this snapshot is the source). (3) DASHBOARD surfaces: `GET /api/v1/universe/master-integrity` (reads the snapshot; present:false until the master is loaded; 503 no store) + `GET /api/v1/universe/master-integrity.csv` (re-renders via `report_from_dict` → the NEW pure `brutex/dashboard/master_integrity_csv.py` `master_integrity_to_csv`, reusing #873's shared `FormulaSafeWriter` so M&M / `=`-leading cells are formula-injection-safe) + a green/red `/universe` "Master mapping integrity" panel with a CSV download link. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `master_integrity.py` + `master_integrity_csv.py` BOTH at **100.00% line+branch** (17 unit covering every bucket + dedup + spot-with-no-legs + alias + special-char + orphan-cap + round-trip; 3 hypothesis PROPERTY invariants — bucket partition-completeness, green⟺no-gating, order-independence; 6 CSV unit; 1 golden SHA-256; 4 integration route+hook incl. 503 + present-false; store set_meta/get_meta round-trip); `instrument_loader.py` stays 100% line+branch; ruff + ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean on all 5 changed modules. ✅ O(1) lookups / O(rows) one-pass / O(spots) space — stated honestly; the audit runs at the one moment the 89k legs are in RAM, adds only O(spots) dicts (NOT O(legs)), and the orphan sample is capped. ✅ DYNAMIC — handles any special char / new type by reading the master, never a hardcoded symbol special-case; COMMON — replicates the proven token-genuineness rule + reuses #873's CSV guard. 🚫 token-collision-across-distinct-symbols (a rare master corruption where two symbols share one security_id) is OUT of scope (stated); 🚫 it DETECTS, never crashes the keyless load on a vendor drift (mirrors #870); 🚫 does NOT re-store the legs. **REAL-FILE PROOF (verified 2026-06-21 against the operator's actual 164,248-row `instrument.csv`):** the real Groww parser + this audit over the full master parsed 113,517 in-scope rows and audited them in **0.32s** — verdict **GREEN**: 30 IDX + 11,677 EQ spots, 101,810 legs (668 FUT + 50,554 CE + 50,588 PE) ALL map (88,764 resolved both symbol+token, 13,028 resolved symbol-only = the NSE-index surrogate-token legs), 0 orphan/ambiguous/disagreement/empty, the ONLY 18 un-mappable legs are all `*NSETEST*` exchange test futures (now the non-gating bucket). NSE-index mapping confirmed precise: NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/FINNIFTY resolve by symbol, NIFTYJR→NIFTYNXT50 + NIFTYMIDSELECT→MIDCPNIFTY via the alias bridge, SENSEX/BANKEX (BSE) via token-join, 19 spot-only NSE indices correctly carry no options. The 4 special-char underlyings (M&M, BAJAJ-AUTO, GVT&D, NAM-INDIA) ALL resolve — independently CONFIRMING the master MAPPING is exact (M&M's F2 RED is purely the vendor `&`-fetch question, NOT a master mapping bug).
