875. **DEC-INSTRUMENT-ECONOMICS-INTEGRITY-001 — a parse-time ECONOMICS audit proving lot_size is uniform PER (underlying, expiry) across the whole instrument.csv, with cross-expiry lot revisions shown as legitimate informational data (not errors); surfaced green/red + downloadable CSV** (2026-06-21, operator: "even lot size tick size freeze quantity etc everything should be entirely checked and mapped right dude am I right bro" — chosen as the next item via AskUserQuestion). **Why:** the operator asked that the contract economics (lot_size/tick_size/freeze_quantity) be checked + mapped too, alongside the #874 leg→spot MAPPING audit. This is the ECONOMICS sibling of DEC-INSTRUMENT-MASTER-INTEGRITY-001 (#874). **The HONEST design (grounded in the real 164k-row master — NOT assumed; Golden Rule #1):** two "obvious" checks were verified WRONG/redundant against the operator's actual `instrument.csv` and are therefore deliberately NOT done — (a) lot/tick POSITIVITY is already guaranteed upstream by `Instrument.__post_init__` (fail-CLOSES on a non-positive lot/tick for any non-index row, `models.py:206-209`), so re-checking it would be dead untestable code; (b) tick_size is NOT uniform within an expiry — it legitimately varies by strike/premium band (e.g. 360ONE 0.05 vs 0.10 — 350 such groups in the real master), so tick uniformity is NOT checked. The ONE real invariant the per-leg validator can't see, and that #875 adds: **lot_size is uniform PER (underlying, expiry)** — one expiry's whole chain (every strike, CE+PE, + the future) shares ONE lot; a lot that DIFFERS within a single expiry is a genuine bug → GATING. lot_size legitimately REVISES across expiries (NSE quarterly / post-split — e.g. AMBUJACEM 1050→1200, 45 names in the real master), so cross-expiry variation is reported as **informational** (`underlyings_with_lot_revisions`), never gated. **What shipped (READ-ONLY; DETECT-only; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** (1) a NEW PURE `brutex/data/economics_integrity.py` `audit_economics_integrity(instruments, *, test_underlying_markers, now, run_id, csv_source_sha256)` — ONE O(legs) sweep, O(1) per lookup, O(expiry-groups) space: collects the distinct lot per (underlying, expiry) and per underlying, derives the gated within-expiry lot mismatches + the informational cross-expiry revisions; exchange `*NSETEST*` legs excluded (reuses #874's `DEFAULT_TEST_UNDERLYING_MARKERS`, DYNAMIC); samples capped at 200 with exact counts; `is_green` ⟺ zero within-expiry mismatch; `report_to_dict`/`report_from_dict` round-trip. (2) an INGEST HOOK `instrument_loader._persist_economics_integrity` (sibling of #874's) — audits the FULL leg-bearing `index.universe`, structlog counts, persists bounded JSON to `schema_meta` (NEW economics META key) after the lean upsert+prune. (3) DASHBOARD: `GET /api/v1/universe/economics-integrity[.csv]` (CSV via NEW pure `brutex/dashboard/economics_integrity_csv.py`, reusing #873's shared `FormulaSafeWriter`) + a green/red `/universe` "Economics integrity (lot size)" panel. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `economics_integrity.py` + `economics_integrity_csv.py` BOTH at **100.00% line+branch** (8 unit + 2 hypothesis property + 3 CSV unit + 1 golden SHA-256 + 3 integration route+hook incl. 503 + present-false); `instrument_loader.py` stays 100%; ruff/ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean. ✅ REAL-FILE PROOF: ran the actual 164,248-row `instrument.csv` → **GREEN**, 101,792 legs over 684 (underlying, expiry) groups, **0 within-expiry lot mismatches**, 45 underlyings with legitimate cross-expiry lot revisions (AMBUJACEM 1050→1200 etc.) correctly surfaced as informational. ✅ no false positives — the naive per-underlying check would have flagged 45 lot + 350 tick "inconsistencies" that are all LEGITIMATE (revisions / premium bands); #875 gates only the true invariant (no illusion). 🚫 positivity is upstream-guaranteed (not re-checked); tick uniformity deliberately not checked; freeze_quantity is NOT collected by this audit (lot_size is the only gated invariant — the freeze is already folded onto each underlying by DEC-GROWW-LEG-ECONOMICS-001 and is out of scope here); assurance/observability tool, NOT a backtest-pull blocker. **Files:** `brutex/data/economics_integrity.py`, `brutex/dashboard/economics_integrity_csv.py`, `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_economics_integrity.py`, `tests/unit/test_economics_integrity_csv.py`, `tests/golden/test_economics_integrity_csv_golden.py`, `tests/property/test_economics_integrity_property.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_economics_integrity.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-ECONOMICS-INTEGRITY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-MASTER-INTEGRITY-001 (#874, the MAPPING sibling + the test-marker/CSV-guard reuse), DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (the lean discard forcing the ingest hook), DEC-GROWW-LEG-ECONOMICS-001 (the leg-economics fold this audit's invariant complements), DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-EXPORT-001 (#873, the shared CSV-injection guard).

876. **DEC-MOVERS-COMPLETENESS-001 — the `/movers` page now defaults Top-N to 100 and offers ALL 21 Track-1 timeframes (1m + 19 derived intraday + 1d), every one derived on-the-fly from the stored 1-minute (NO pre-materialised partition needed)** (2026-06-21, operator: "make the default topn as minimum 100 always … i need all these timeframe which will be entirely generated from 1 min timeframe … all those 19 or 20 timeframes … even with its respective time … as long as we have data in candles and fno candles … O(1) latency … common runtime dynamic scalable … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** the Markets-Movers timeframe dropdown listed only 6 of the 21 timeframes (1day/1hour/30min/15min/5min/1min) even though the movers backend ALREADY supports all 21 — `_INTERVAL_MINUTES` (movers_snapshot.py) is built from the single-source-of-truth `brutex.data.timeframes.LAKE_INTERVAL_LABELS` and `resample_1m_to_tf` resamples the stored 1-minute to ANY of the 21 on-the-fly (DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001), so the gap was purely the FRONTEND list (the other 15 TFs were silently unreachable). The Top-N default of 50 was also shallower than the operator-directed "minimum 100". **The HONEST finding (verified in code — no illusion, Golden Rule #1):** for movers, NO timeframe needs to be pre-materialised to the lake — the only prerequisite is 1-minute spot candles + 1-minute F&O candles; movers derives every TF live (the pre-materialisation of all 21 TFs is a SEPARATE optimisation for the sweep engine + `/db`, NOT a movers prerequisite). The per-metric formulas (Price Gainers/Losers, Top Volume, Top Value, Premium/Discount, OI Gainers/Losers, Highest OI) were independently re-verified correct (snap-then-multiply value, prev-day-close baseline, premium = future_ltp − spot_ltp, OI%-change None on zero prev-OI). **What shipped (READ-ONLY display polish; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `DEFAULT_TOP_N` / `DEFAULT_FUTURES_TOP_N` / `DEFAULT_OPTIONS_TOP_N` 50 → **100** (the three tabs stay aligned, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); (2) the `/api/v1/movers` route Top-N cap raised `le=200` → `le=500` (deeper screens; the candidate set is computed once per coordinate then ranked cheaply, so a larger N costs only the in-memory sort — O(candidates·log candidates), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001); (3) `templates/movers.html` Timeframe dropdown expanded from 6 to all **21** options + the `TF_MIN` JS map expanded to all 21 (both mirror `LAKE_INTERVAL_LABELS` — the labels can never drift from the backend vocab) + the Top-N input `value="50"`→`100`, `max="200"`→`500`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `movers_snapshot.py` + `movers_futures.py` + `movers_options.py` all stay at **100.00% line+branch**; ruff + ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean. ✅ NEW tests pin the new behaviour: `tests/unit/test_movers_completeness.py` (the three 100 defaults; EVERY one of the 21 `LAKE_INTERVAL_LABELS` resolves via `interval_minutes` AND is in the resampler's `ALL_TF_MINUTES`; an unknown label is honestly `None`) + `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py` (route default top_n=100, accepts top_n=500, rejects 501 with 422, a 2hour/3hour/7minute/14minute interval is 200 not 422, the `/movers` page lists all 21 TF options + the 100 default). ✅ O(1)/cheap — no new lake scan; the deeper N is a bigger in-memory sort only. 🚫 NO backend/TF-materialisation work was needed (the backend already supported all 21 — the change is the dropdown + the defaults), so NO illusion of new compute. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `tests/unit/test_movers_completeness.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-COMPLETENESS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 (the snapshot-cache + cheap-rerank the deeper N rides on), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 (the 1m-only fetch + on-the-fly TF derivation), DEC-TF-VOCAB-21-001 (the 21-timeframe single source of truth `LAKE_INTERVAL_LABELS` the dropdown mirrors), DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001 (the movers page this completes).

877. **DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 — the one-click pull pipeline now also runs over ONLY the ticked instruments (dedicated "▶ Pull selected — full pipeline" button), and `run_full_pipeline` gains a GATED post-pull movers-warm phase that runs ONLY after a fully-successful fetch** (2026-06-21, operator: "pull everything is fine but still it should work for only selected … only when the successful of all these pull fetches successfully only then go ahead with movers calculation automated in the same process … until/unless successful fetches happens never ever run this movers … O(1) … common runtime dynamic scalable … cover all extreme permutations/exceptions … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** the one-click pipeline (DEC-ONE-CLICK-PIPELINE-001 #872) ran ONLY over the whole universe — the selected-only flow existed merely as the THREE separate buttons. The operator wanted a one-click pipeline scoped to the ticked watchlist, AND for movers to be (re)computed automatically after — but ONLY on a clean fetch. **What shipped (NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) a NEW SHARED `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` `resolve_pull_targets(*, symbols, symbol, lookup, whole_universe)` — the ONE selection resolver (precedence `symbols` > `symbol` > whole-universe; O(1) per id via the store `get`; de-dupes + preserves order via `resolve_pull_symbols`; fail-CLOSED on an empty/unknown selection → the route maps it to 400, Golden Rule #1) — replacing the byte-identical `if symbols … elif symbol … else` block that `/pull-pipeline` + `/retry-failed` each inlined (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, both now call the shared resolver); (2) the `/api/v1/universe/pull-pipeline` route gains optional `?symbols=` / `?symbol=` (no selection → the WHOLE universe — backward-compatible with the "▶ Pull EVERYTHING" hero) + echoes `target_source` (`selection`/`single`/`universe`); (3) a NEW `/universe` "▶ Pull selected · N — full pipeline" button (active only when ≥1 row is ticked) that POSTs the SAME route with `?symbols=<ticked ids>` via `startAndPoll`; (4) `pipeline_pull.run_full_pipeline` gains an OPTIONAL gated 4th phase `run_movers` + `PipelinePullReport.movers_warmed` (a NEW `PHASE_MOVERS`): the warmer runs ONLY when `historical_phase_ok` passes (spot + metadata already passed to reach there), so a partial/broken fetch leaves `movers_warmed = None` (the operator's hard rule "never run movers unless the fetch succeeded"); `0` is an honest "ran, warmed nothing" distinct from `None` "did not run"; the pull's own `ok`/`stopped_after` is NEVER affected by the warm. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `pipeline_pull.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (34 cases incl. 5 new gated-movers tests: warm-on-clean, zero-is-honest-not-None, skip-when-historical-not-clean, skip-when-stopped-early, no-phase-when-not-injected); `resolve_pull_targets` fully covered (5 unit + 4 route integration: selection/single/whole-universe/unknown→400); ruff/ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean. ⚠️ **The gated movers WARMER is NOT yet bound in the route** — a warm pinned to the DEFAULT (today) coordinate would cache EMPTY snapshots right after a historical pull (the lake fills only to the PREVIOUS trading day, and `compute_spot_candidates` reads the EXACT requested date — verified, no latest-date fallback), which would be exactly the illusion this codebase forbids. Movers already auto-refresh on the next `/movers` open (the pull bumps the `SummaryCache` generation, invalidating the movers cache, DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001). The gate INFRASTRUCTURE is delivered + proven; the latest-available-date warm BINDING is the explicit, stated follow-up (DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001, not claimed here). 🚫 the sequencer is O(1) (four calls + gate checks); the WORK is the real multi-hour vendor fill (no throughput claim). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_pipeline_route.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_ux.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-ONE-CLICK-PIPELINE-001 (#872, the whole-universe pipeline this scopes + the gated sequencer it extends), DEC-UNIVERSE-OPTIONS-MULTIPULL-001 (`resolve_pull_symbols` + the `?symbols=` selection mechanism reused), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 (the generation-invalidated movers cache the warm phase will prime), DEC-MOVERS-COMPLETENESS-001 (#876, the movers page the warm targets).

878. **DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001 — bind the gated phase-4 movers warmer in the pull-pipeline route: after a fully-successful fetch, pre-compute the default movers snapshots for the LATEST AVAILABLE day (never 'today' → never empties)** (2026-06-21, operator: "when I click [pull selected] and even when everything is entirely successful then our movers entire sections and its webpages also will be calculated right … only when the successful of all these pull fetches successfully … until/unless successful fetches happens never ever run this movers … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 (#877) shipped the gated phase-4 HOOK (`run_full_pipeline(run_movers=…)`) + proved the gate, but deliberately did NOT bind a warmer — a warm pinned to the DEFAULT (today) coordinate would cache EMPTY snapshots right after a historical pull (the lake fills only to the PREVIOUS trading day, and `compute_spot_candidates` reads the EXACT requested date — no latest-date fallback). This PR closes that follow-up by binding a warmer that targets the LATEST day WITH DATA, so the operator's first `/movers` open after a clean pull is an O(1) cache hit (not a cold scan) AND never an empty illusion. **What shipped (READ-ONLY post-pull accelerator; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) a NEW PURE `brutex/dashboard/movers_warm.py`: `latest_movers_date(lake_root)` — the MAX spot `1day` IST date across the INDEX+CASH partitions (a bounded `1day`-only read, self-contained DuckDB; `None` on an empty lake → warm nothing, never a fabricated "today" snapshot) + `warm_movers_snapshots(jobs)` — runs each warm job (compute+cache one default snapshot) and returns how many warmed NON-EMPTY; **best-effort** (a job that raises is structlog-logged + counted 0, NEVER re-raised — a warm hiccup never fails the already-successful pull; Correctness of the pull > the warm's latency benefit). (2) the `/pull-pipeline` route's `_work` binds `run_full_pipeline(run_movers=_warm_movers)`: `_warm_movers` resolves the latest date, then warms the spot/futures/options DEFAULT snapshots (`1day` · latest day · all-exchange · near/all for options) into the SAME `MoversSnapshotCache` at the post-pull generation, REUSING the EXACT `candidate_key` + `compute_*_candidates` the `/api/v1/movers` route uses (no drift, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). The gate is inherited from #877 — the warmer runs ONLY after spot+metadata+historical all pass. (3) **the `/movers` route now defaults a MISSING `?date=` to the latest-available spot day** (`latest_movers_date`), NOT today — so the default landing open (a) SHOWS DATA (a historical pull fills only to the PREVIOUS trading day, so a today-default rendered an empty snapshot) AND (b) keys on the SAME day the warm pre-computed → a cache HIT, not a miss (this is the hostile-review MAJOR fix that makes the "first open is O(1)" claim actually hold; an explicit malformed date still 400s; an empty lake falls back to today → honest empty). (4) the whole `_warm_movers` body (the `latest_movers_date` resolve INCLUDED) is best-effort — a transient lake-read race is logged + returns 0, NEVER failing the already-successful pull (the hostile-review MINOR fix). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `movers_warm.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (7 tests: latest-date over a real seeded Parquet+DuckDB lake — newest day, INDEX+CASH span, empty-lake→None, FNO-only→None; warm counts only non-empty, empty job-list→0, a raising job logged+counted-0); ruff/ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean. ✅ targets the LATEST day WITH DATA — never caches an empty "today" snapshot (the illusion #877 flagged is now closed honestly). ✅ best-effort — a warm failure NEVER fails the successful pull; movers also still auto-refresh on the next `/movers` open (the generation bump, DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001) so correctness never depends on the warm. ✅ O(1) per warmed coordinate (a generation-keyed cache store); the `latest_movers_date` read is bounded to the tiny `1day` partitions. 🚫 the route-side `_warm_movers` closure is DI wiring inside the existing `# pragma: no cover` `_work` job-body (the warm LOGIC — `latest_movers_date` + `warm_movers_snapshots` — is the 100%-tested part; the compute fns it binds are already tested); warms only the DEFAULT landing coordinate (other coordinates compute lazily on selection — stated, not claimed exhaustive). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_warm.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_warm.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py` (the no-date→latest-day default test), `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 (#877, the gated phase-4 hook this binds), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 (the generation-invalidated `MoversSnapshotCache` + the `candidate_key`/`compute_*_candidates` reused), DEC-MOVERS-COMPLETENESS-001 (#876, the movers page warmed), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 (the derived `1day` partition `latest_movers_date` reads).

879. **DEC-FNO-WINDOW-PLAN-001 — the F&O (options + futures) pull now PRE-PLANS every contract window as `PLANNED` before any fetch, so the `/coverage/windows` Options + Futures tabs show a real planned total + units, exactly like spot** (2026-06-21, operator: "why planned items are not available for futures and options dude i mean even including units also dude why bro? … always I need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … covering all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions bugs … make everything as common runtime dynamic scalable approach … completely fully comprehensively automated with real time guarantee and assurance … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** `/coverage/windows` buckets every ledger row into spot/options/futures (`db_view._window_market_bucket`), and a `PLANNED` row is only ever created by `plan_windows` (`window_ledger_store.py`) — which the audit confirmed is called ONLY for the SPOT pull (all 4 call sites pass `market=GROWW_COVERAGE_MARKET`). The option ingest (`option_ingest.py`) wrote a ledger row ONLY at fetch time (`ledger.record(...)`), so options + futures had NO pre-fetch `PLANNED` rows → both tabs read "0 PLANNED" (their units were genuinely 0). Spot's expected set is enumerable up front (fixed symbols × 21 TFs × `2020→today`), so it pre-seeds every window; F&O's grid is only knowable after `get_expiries`→`get_contracts` resolves it AT pull time (CLAUDE.md §6), so it was never pre-planned. **What shipped (NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; the F&O lake is REFERENCE_ONLY, DEC-P0-063):** (1) a NEW shared `option_ingest._clamped_window_key(contract_symbol, *, interval, start, end, market, now_for_clamp)` — the ONE source of truth for a derivative ledger key (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON), returning `WindowKey | None` (`None` for an empty clamped range, exactly the case the fetch returns `windows=0` for and never touches the ledger). `ingest_option_contract` was REFACTORED onto it (its inline clamp + empty-guard + `WindowKey(...)` build replaced by one call; `clamped_end = key.end` keeps the rest byte-identical — proven by the 50 pre-existing tests staying green), so the planner's key is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the fetched key — the "planned == fetched" invariant that keeps a `PLANNED` row from being a permanent ghost it can never settle (the spot-spine guarantee of `window_ledger_store.plan_windows`). (2) a NEW `option_ingest.plan_contract_windows(ledger, *, contracts, intervals, start, end, market, contract_windows, now_ist)` — the F&O twin of spot's `plan_windows`: for each resolved `(contract, interval)` pair it derives the SAME key (via `_resolve_window` → `_clamped_window_key`) and `ledger.plan`-s it (idempotent — a settled prior-pull row is NEVER reset), then `prune_superseded` GCs any orphan of an advancing range (DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001). (3) WIRED into `run_groww_option_ingest` — it materialises `contracts` ONCE, then (when `ledger is not None`, i.e. not a dry-run) pre-plans before the parallel drain; this auto-covers BOTH `ingest_underlying_options` (`groww-option`) AND `ingest_underlying_futures` (`groww-future`) since both delegate here, each with its own namespace. **The VIEW layer needed ZERO change** — `db_view.build_window_payload` already computes `counts` (status × spot/options/futures) over every record, so the Options + Futures `PLANNED` total + units now simply populate. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `option_ingest.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (59 unit cases — the 50 pre-existing all green after the refactor + 9 new: seeds-planned, default-clock plans a past range, empty-range-not-planned, byte-identical-to-fetch [plan-then-fetch leaves ONE row, no ghost], idempotent-keeps-settled, prunes-superseded, futures-namespace, driver-pre-plans-quarantined-stays-PLANNED, ledger=None-does-not-plan); a NEW end-to-end integration (`test_groww_option_ingest_pipeline.py`) persists a planned options+futures ledger and asserts `build_window_payload` shows `counts["options"]["PLANNED"]==1` + `counts["futures"]["PLANNED"]==1` + the units listed on `status="PLANNED"`; ruff/ruff-format clean; `pyright` 0 errors; `mypy --strict` clean. ✅ `PLANNED == fetched` key parity is the load-bearing invariant — a quarantined/un-reached contract correctly STAYS `PLANNED` (genuinely-outstanding, the no-mask guarantee #598), a fetched one settles its OWN row IN PLACE (no orphan). ✅ idempotent (a re-pull never resets a settled row → no re-fetch; the existing idempotency integration test stays green) + the advancing-range orphan is pruned (worst case covered). ✅ O(contracts × intervals) plan (each plan O(1)) + one O(rows) prune scan — NOT an O(1)-total claim (honest). 🚫 a F&O cold-start `seed_lake_success` (the spot-style "lake already has bars on a fresh ledger" bridge) is NOT added here — a fresh-ledger F&O re-pull already re-fetches (idempotent, keep-first sink absorbs it), so planning does not regress it; that bridge is a separate, explicitly-out-of-scope follow-up. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/integration/test_groww_option_ingest_pipeline.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-WINDOW-PLAN-001. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the unified per-window ledger + `plan`/`prune_superseded`/`is_skippable` reused), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 + DEC-GROWW-FUTURE-INGEST-001 (the option/future ingest spines pre-planned), DEC-COVERAGE-GROWW-NAMESPACE-001 (the `groww-option`/`groww-future` buckets the planned rows land in), DEC-SPOT-COVERAGE-COMPLETENESS-001 (spot's `plan_windows` this mirrors for F&O), DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 (the `contract_windows` bounds the plan resolves through, identical to the fetch).

880. **DEC-DB-FNO-CASCADE-001 — the `/db` F&O candle picker is now a lazy O(1) symbol → expiry → contract cascade instead of one flat thousand-row dropdown** (2026-06-21, operator: "if I need to see the data plainly as a human directly from database, how can I filter or view the precise strikes easily … it's best to first select symbols and then based on symbols expiries and then based on expiries then contracts … always I need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … make everything as common runtime dynamic scalable approach … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** the `/db` F&O dataset selector was ONE flat `<select>` of every `[F&O] NIFTY · 2020-02-06 · 12250 PE · 1minute` partition — thousands of rows, impossible to navigate to a precise strike (the operator's screenshot). **What shipped (READ-ONLY viewer; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; F&O lake is REFERENCE_ONLY):** (1) a NEW pure `brutex/dashboard/fno_cascade.py` — `build_fno_cascade(datasets)` groups the decoded F&O datasets (`list_fno_candle_datasets`, which decodes each partition via `parse_fno_symbol`) into a THREE-LEVEL `FnoCascadeIndex` with O(1) `underlyings()` / `expiries(underlying)` / `contracts(underlying, expiry)` reads into pre-sorted tuples (futures-first, then ascending NUMERIC strike, CE before PE); a contract leaf aggregates its (≥1) intervals; an undecodable partition is surfaced in `unparsed`, never hidden (Golden Rule #1). Derived from the LAKE partitions that truly have data — NOT the `contracts` registry table (frequently empty — the operator's screenshot showed `contracts: 0`), so the cascade can never offer a phantom strike. (2) a generation-stamped `FnoCascadeCache` (rebuilds only when a pull bumps `_summary_cache.generation`; otherwise every cascade click is an O(1) cached handoff) + 3 NEW lazy routes `GET /api/v1/db/fno/{underlyings,expiries?underlying=,contracts?underlying=&expiry=}` behind ONE shared `_fno_cascade_or_none` helper (COMMON; threadpool dir-walk; no-lake-root → empty shape, never a 500). (3) the `/db` frontend (`db.html`) replaces the flat F&O dropdown with three dependent selects (underlying → expiry → contract) + an interval sub-pick — a later level disabled until its parent is chosen, so an impossible combination is unreachable; the contract pick MATERIALISES the dataset descriptor so the SHARED candle query path (`curDataset`/`buildCandleUrl`) is byte-unchanged. Spot + option keep the flat dropdown (only the F&O branch changed). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `fno_cascade.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (14 unit: empty/sorted-underlyings/scoped-expiries/futures-first-numeric-strike-sort/interval-aggregation/unparsed-surfaced/partial-decode/fractional-strike + cache hit-same-gen / rebuild-on-bump + JSON projection) + 8 route+frontend integration (data / unknown cell / no-lake-root every branch / unparsed-surfaced / `/db` page wires all 3 endpoints + handlers + `cund`/`cexp`/`ccon` elements); the broader `/db` suite (229 tests) stays GREEN — no regression to the spot/option viewer; ruff/ruff-format clean, `mypy --strict` clean, `pyright` 0 errors. ✅ O(1)-per-step (pre-sorted-tuple dict lookups; the `O(datasets)` build is once per generation) — tiny lazy payloads (hundreds of names / dozens of expiries / dozens of contracts), never the flat thousand-row list. 🚫 the richer F&O columns (`days_to_expiry` / `spot` / `intrinsic` / `time_value`) the operator also asked about are the explicit, stated NEXT PR — NOT claimed here (the cascade is the navigation fix); the frontend JS is asserted by a Python template-presence test (consistent with the repo — JS is not Python-coverage-gated). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/fno_cascade.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/unit/test_fno_cascade.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_fno_cascade.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-FNO-CASCADE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 (the `list_fno_candle_datasets` decode this groups), DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 (the per-bar moneyness column the contracts then show), DEC-DB-VIEWER-001 (the `/db` candle viewer this re-pickers), DEC-UNIVERSE-BACKEND-CACHE-001 (the generation-stamped content-token cache pattern reused).

881. **DEC-DB-FNO-COLUMNS-001 — the `/db` F&O candle view gains four read-time derived value columns (`spot` · `intrinsic` · `time_value` · `days_to_expiry`) so an option's worth reads at a glance** (2026-06-21, operator: "along with that what other columns can be easily or particularly needed to be added even in database fno candles … always I need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … make everything as common runtime dynamic scalable approach … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** the stated NEXT-PR follow-up to the #880 cascade (the operator's two-part `/db` ask — part 1 was the navigation cascade, part 2 "what other columns"). The F&O candle grid showed OHLCV + OI + moneyness, but not the option's underlying spot / intrinsic / time-value / days-to-expiry — the numbers a human reads an option by. **What shipped (READ-ONLY viewer; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab change — ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY):** four NEW columns appended after `moneyness`, ALL riding the SAME single per-bar underlying-spot join `moneyness` already does (**no extra read** — the O(1)/no-waste bar): `spot` (underlying close at the bar, 2-dp ₹), `intrinsic` (`max(0, spot−strike)` CE / `max(0, strike−spot)` PE, 2-dp ₹), `time_value` (`close − intrinsic`, 2-dp ₹), `days_to_expiry` (pure `(expiry − bar IST date).days`, no I/O — resolves for a future too). `db_view._fno_moneyness_rows` was REPLACED by `_fno_derived_rows` (returns the 5-tuple `(moneyness, spot, intrinsic, time_value, days_to_expiry)` from ONE spot join) + a pure `_option_intrinsic` helper; `FNO_VALUE_COLUMNS`/`FNO_DERIVED_COLUMNS` constants + `fno_candle_lake.FNO_CANDLE_COLUMNS` advertise the four as `source="derived"`; the candle grid renders them automatically (column-generic). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ a future/undecodable contract reads `moneyness="—"` + `None` value columns (no spot read) but still gets `days_to_expiry` when its expiry decodes; an option with no spot reads `"?"` + `None` values — never a fabricated price. The early-return guard narrows `strike` so the option branch + `_option_intrinsic` have NO dead/unreachable branch (the defensive guard removed). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): the `/db` F&O moneyness/schema/datasets/candle-lake suites GREEN (44 + broader); the new `_fno_derived_rows`/`_option_intrinsic` lines fully covered (CE/PE intrinsic, ITM/OTM, no-spot, no-timestamp, future, undecodable, spot-present-but-close-not-projected); ruff/ruff-format/mypy --strict/pyright clean. ✅ statistical/price honesty: money columns 2-dp (DEC-MONEY-2DP-001); JSON-native cells. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/data/fno_candle_lake.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_fno_moneyness.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_fno.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_datasets.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-FNO-COLUMNS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-FNO-CASCADE-001 (#880, the cascade this completes — the operator's two-part `/db` ask), DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 (the per-bar spot join + moneyness these value columns extend), DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 (the `FNO_CANDLE_COLUMNS` schema advertised), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the 2-dp money display rule).

882. **DEC-OPTIONS-LAKE-READER-001 — the options executor's `OptionBarSource` seam now has a PRODUCTION implementation that reads real option bars from the F&O candle lake (gap-analysis item 1, the highest-value engine step)** (2026-06-21, operator: "item 1 … the options lake reader … if real data not needed then build it now … always O(1) … make everything common runtime dynamic scalable … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** `brutex/options/executor.py` prices a winning Track-1 spot signal into a real options trade through an INJECTED `OptionBarSource` seam — but the only implementation was a `Protocol` stub, so no sweep could ever price a leg from the lake (the #1 blocking gap in the spot→options mapping per the readiness analysis). **What shipped (the F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY, DEC-P0-063; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3):** a NEW `brutex/options/lake_source.py` `LakeOptionBarSource` (the production `OptionBarSource`): given a leg's `(instrument, expiry_date, strike, option_type, entry_ts, exit_ts)` it (1) DISCOVERS the contract `groww_symbol` by scanning + `parse_fno_symbol`-matching the `bars/<exch>/FNO/` partition dirs on `(expiry, strike, option_type)` — cached per `(exchange, underlying)`, robust to format quirks (NOT a fragile reconstructed string); (2) reads that contract's `1minute` bars into a cached `{utc_instant → OptionBar}` map; (3) returns the entry + forced-exit `OptionBarPair` matched on the EXACT UTC minute, or `None` when the contract / either bar is absent — **never a fabricated price** (Golden Rule #1). The `OptionBar` carries `side`/`strike` from the query; `spot`/`iv` are honest `None` (the F&O candle lake stores neither — the executor's `iv_at_entry` is already documented `None` when omitted). Exchange map NIFTY/BANKNIFTY→NSE, SENSEX→BSE. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ O(1) per `load_pair` after the per-contract read (the symbol index + bar map are cached, so a sweep pays the lake read ONCE per contract, then dict lookups); the first touch is O(bars-in-contract) (one small partition) — NOT an O(1)-total claim. ✅ entry/exit matched on the exact minute — a minute the option did not trade is an honest `None`, never the nearest-prior bar. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `lake_source.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (76→77 stmts / 22 branches; 13 unit cases — happy CE/PE, SENSEX-under-BSE, absent contract, missing entry/exit bar, empty lake, contract-dir-without-parquet, future/undecodable/file/other-underlying excluded from the index, caching) + 2 executor-INTEGRATION tests proving it prices a real round-trip (₹150→₹210 = 15000→21000 paisa, `iv_at_entry=None`) through the REAL `materialize_trade`→`compute_trade_cost` path + an honest `RejectedTrade(NO_DATA)`; the options suite (53) + F&O-lake smoke (77) GREEN; ruff/ruff-format clean, `mypy --strict` clean, `pyright` 0 errors. **4-agent hostile review** (hostile-reviewer + workspace-health, parallel) caught ONE BLOCKER — mis-coded `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on the `int()` casts that mypy raised as `[call-overload]` (+ `warn_unused_ignores`) — FIXED by typing the polars row `Mapping[str, Any]` like the sibling `movers_snapshot._row_to_bar` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) + deleting both ignores; re-verified mypy-clean. Everything else verified solid (protocol conformance genuine, symbol resolution exact-underlying, caching collision-free, real 100% coverage). 🚫 NOT built here (stated, parked): the options TF resampler (item 2) + Greeks/delta strikes (item 5); a futures underlying-spot column. **Files:** `brutex/options/lake_source.py`, `brutex/options/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/test_options_lake_source.py`, `tests/integration/test_options_lake_executor.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-OPTIONS-LAKE-READER-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 + DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 (the F&O candle lake this reads), DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 / `fno_symbol` (the `parse_fno_symbol` decode the discovery matches on), DEC-OPTIONS-EXECUTOR-001 (the executor + `OptionBarSource` seam this fills), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 (the cached-read pattern + the `movers_snapshot._row_to_bar` row-typing mirrored).

883. **DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001 — a transient Groww 5xx server error is now a RETRYABLE `GrowwServerError`, not a terminal quarantine (resilience gap #1 of the critical-risks batch)** (2026-06-21, operator: "Firstly cover all these gaps dude because this is the critical risks … always real time guarantee with assurance … no hallucination or illusion … just go ahead"). **Why:** a multi-agent resilience audit (the data-pull/lake/adapter "heart") found that the Groww error taxonomy had NO server-error class — a generic `GrowwAPIException` carrying a `500`/`502`/`503` `code` (or an "internal server error" / "bad gateway" / "service unavailable" message) fell through `_classify_generic` to the terminal base `GrowwError` and was QUARANTINED instead of retried, so a momentary upstream blip TERMINALLY dropped a real symbol — the exact class of bug DEC-GROWW-EMPTY-BODY-RETRY-001 fixed for empty bodies, still open for 5xx. **What shipped (`brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` ONLY — additive classification; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** a NEW `GrowwServerError(GrowwError)` (retryable); `_CODE_TO_ERROR` extended `500`/`502`/`503` → `GrowwServerError` (`504` gateway-timeout deliberately KEPT as `GrowwTimeoutError` — already retryable, the timeout ladder governs it, no behaviour change); a NEW phrase-only `_SERVER_ERROR_HINTS` (`"internal server error"`, `"bad gateway"`, `"service unavailable"`, `"server error"` — NO bare numeric substrings that would false-match) checked in `_classify_generic` AFTER the rate-limit + timeout hints (priority preserved: a 429/timeout that also mentions a server never mis-reads as a plain 5xx); `GrowwServerError` added to `is_retryable` + `__all__`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ deliberately NOT a `GrowwRateLimitError` — a 5xx is not a quota signal, so `is_rate_limit` stays `False` for it and it rides the GENTLE timeout ladder (`on_timeout`), never stepping the per-second rate ceiling down; verified the three consumption sites (`client.py:213` in-call retry, `ingest.py:579`, `option_ingest.py:363`) pick it up via `is_retryable`/`is_rate_limit` with ZERO extra code. ✅ a genuine `404` stays terminal `GrowwNotFoundError`; an unknown code/message stays the terminal base (conservative — an unknown failure is never blindly retried). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `errors.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (48 stmts / 16 branches; code-classified 500/502/503 + digit-string, message-sniffed, priority-ordering rate-limit/timeout-wins, the not-rate-limit assertion, unknown→terminal); the broader groww client/ingest/retry suites (140) GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-EMPTY-BODY-RETRY-001 (the empty-body retryable-classification twin), DEC-GROWW-RATELIMIT-RETRY-001 (the generic-`GrowwAPIException` code/message classifier extended), DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001 (the rate ladder a 5xx must NOT step). **Part of:** the operator's critical-risks resilience-hardening batch (this is gap #1; remaining: live-ledger CLI checkpoint, disk-full/OOM halt, lake process-lock, Telegram alerting, plus the audit-discovered engine map-full/Bloom-capacity/poison-combo isolation + the corrupt-file `/movers` skip).

884. **DEC-CLI-LEDGER-CHECKPOINT-001 — the `brutex fetch` CLI now checkpoints the durable window ledger MID-pull (per window), not only at pull end, so a crash recovers in seconds instead of re-pulling the whole span (resilience gap #2 of the critical-risks batch)** (2026-06-21, operator: "cover all these gaps … critical risks … always real time guarantee with assurance … no illusion or hallucination … just go ahead"). **Why:** a grounded audit found the CLI fetch path saved the durable ledger SOLELY via `end_pull_ledger` (run-END), passing only `storm_progress` as `on_progress` — no mid-pull flush. The dashboard pull already checkpoints live per window, but a CLI crash after N completed windows (e.g. deep into a single symbol's multi-year 1-minute backfill — ONE pair, ~75 windows, so `on_progress` never even fires until the pair finishes) lost every SUCCESS row and the next run re-pulled the entire span. **What shipped (`brutex/cli.py` wiring + ONE new COMMON helper; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** `cmd_fetch` now threads the SAME throttled `make_live_ledger_flush` the dashboard uses (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — no copy-paste) as the ingest engine's per-WINDOW `on_window` hook. Because `on_window` fires from the PARALLEL `PoolRunParallel` worker threads and the throttled flush is not itself thread-safe, it is wrapped in a NEW minimal `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.make_locked_flush` (a single-flight `threading.Lock` wrapper). The CLI wants the flush ONLY (not the dashboard bar push), so it deliberately does NOT use `make_live_sync` (which no-ops without an `on_ledger_sync`). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ recovery is bounded to ONE throttle interval of windows, NOT bit-for-bit mid-window resume — a re-pull of an un-flushed window simply re-fetches (the save is tmp→atomic-rename; the keep-first sink is idempotent, so a duplicate is absorbed). ✅ a `None` ledger (`--dry-run` / `--inspect`) makes the flush a no-op (the lock wraps a no-op), so neither touches disk — the persistence-free `--inspect` contract is preserved. ✅ O(1) lock acquire per window; the existing adaptive flush throttle (`_FLUSH_DUTY_FACTOR`) still bounds the write RATE so the checkpoint can never dominate wall time. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `window_ledger_store.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (177 stmts / 50 branches — incl. a new `make_locked_flush` forward test + an 8-thread concurrency single-flight test); a new CLI test proves a mid-pull `on_window()` fire flushes the durable ledger BEFORE `end_pull_ledger`, and a `--inspect` test proves the None-ledger checkpoint never saves; the CLI fetch + window-ledger suites (72) GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_retry_storm.py`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger_store.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CLI-LEDGER-CHECKPOINT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-OPTION-WINDOW-PLAN-001 (the adaptive-throttle `make_live_ledger_flush` reused), DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001 (the per-window `on_window` / `make_live_sync` checkpoint pattern this mirrors for the CLI), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the durable ledger as the sole skip authority). **Part of:** the critical-risks resilience-hardening batch (gap #2 of: 5xx-retry #883 ✅, this CLI checkpoint, disk-full/OOM halt, lake process-lock, Telegram alerting, + the audit-discovered engine map-full/Bloom-capacity/poison-combo isolation + the corrupt-file `/movers` skip).

885. **DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 — disk-full / OOM at the lake-write boundary now HALTS the pull gracefully (a `LakeWriteHalt` global stop) instead of crashing raw or quarantining per-symbol, via a shared `atomic_io` write helper (resilience gap #3 of the critical-risks batch)** (2026-06-21, operator: "cover all these gaps … critical risks … cover all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions … always real time guarantee with assurance … no illusion or hallucination … just go ahead"). **Why:** a multi-agent audit found the two lake Parquet writers (`parquet_writer.ParquetWriter._atomic_write` + `option_parquet_writer._atomic_write_parquet`) re-raised a full-disk `OSError(ENOSPC)` raw and never caught a `MemoryError` from a huge `df.write_parquet` — so a full disk either crashed the worker uncontrolled OR (being a `BruteXError`? no — a raw `OSError`) propagated unpredictably, and the near-identical tmp→fsync→`os.replace`→cleanup dance was DUPLICATED (a COMMON-rule drift, one of 7 atomic-write copies the audit flagged). A full disk is not one symbol's problem — it fails every remaining window identically, so it must halt the pull, not be quarantined per-symbol (which would keep hammering a full disk). **What shipped (NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** a NEW `brutex/data/errors.py` `LakeWriteHalt(DataLakeError)` carrying a non-secret `reason` (`"disk_full"` = `ENOSPC`, `"out_of_memory"` = `MemoryError`); a NEW shared `brutex/data/atomic_io.py` with `lake_write_guard()` (the ONE place mapping `ENOSPC`/`MemoryError` → `LakeWriteHalt`, every OTHER error propagating UNCHANGED) + `atomic_write_via(dest, write_to)` (the ONE tmp→fsync→`os.replace`→cleanup implementation). BOTH lake writers now delegate to it, and EVERY allocation/failure site on the boundary is guarded (a 4-agent hostile review caught + folded two MAJOR gaps in the first cut — the merge-read OOM + the `mkstemp` ENOSPC): the spot FRESH render (`_render_bytes`) AND the steady-state MERGE READ (spot `_read_existing_bars` + the option read/concat — the re-pull path that loads the WHOLE existing partition, the largest allocation) run inside `lake_write_guard`, and `mkstemp` ITSELF runs inside the guard (on a full volume the inode/first-block alloc is frequently the FIRST call to fail). `LakeWriteHalt` is added to BOTH ingest spines' `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` (`run_ingest.py` + `option_ingest.py`) so it propagates past the per-symbol / per-contract quarantine and halts gracefully — never a half-written partition (the temp is always cleaned before the halt; `dest` is untouched until the atomic `os.replace`), never fabricated data (Golden Rule #1). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ this is graceful DETECTION + halt, NOT a memory CAP — a true RSS ceiling needs OS-level `setrlimit`/cgroups (explicitly OUT OF SCOPE); recovery is a clean re-pull (durable ledger + keep-first sink), not an in-place resume. ✅ a non-`ENOSPC` `OSError` (e.g. `EACCES`) is NEVER mis-escalated to a halt — it re-raises as-is (fail-closed but never over-broad). ✅ this consolidates only the TWO data-lake writers; the other 5 atomic-write copies (engine `results_store`/`sweep_checkpoint`, `config/credentials`, the two ledger stores) remain as noted COMMON debt for a follow-up (NOT claimed done). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `atomic_io.py` + `errors.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (incl. ENOSPC/OOM mapping, non-ENOSPC re-raise, the `mkstemp`-ENOSPC `tmp-is-None` branch, tmp-cleanup on every path); `parquet_writer.py` / `option_parquet_writer.py` / `run_ingest.py` / `option_ingest.py` all stay **100.00% line+branch** (the writer cleanup tests repointed to the shared helper + NEW merge-read-OOM tests for both writers; the global-stop propagation parametrized to also cover `LakeWriteHalt("disk_full")` + `("out_of_memory")` on BOTH spines; the spot-writer CHAOS suite updated to the new ENOSPC→`LakeWriteHalt` contract while keeping every no-corruption invariant); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/data/errors.py`, `brutex/data/atomic_io.py`, `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `brutex/data/option_parquet_writer.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_atomic_io.py`, `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_option_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/chaos/test_parquet_writer_chaos.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-MERGE-WRITE-001 + DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 (the atomic-write dance now centralised), DEC-GROWW-QUARANTINE-BRUTEX-001 + DEC-SPOT-QUOTA-MIDROUND-001 (the `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` carve-out `LakeWriteHalt` joins). **Part of:** the critical-risks resilience-hardening batch (gap #3 of: 5xx-retry #883 ✅, CLI ledger checkpoint #884 ✅, this disk-full/OOM halt, + remaining: lake process-lock, Telegram alerting, the audit-discovered engine map-full/Bloom-capacity/poison-combo isolation, the corrupt-file `/movers` skip, + the remaining 5-copy atomic-write COMMON consolidation).

887. **DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 — a cross-process advisory `flock` now serialises concurrent writers to the SAME lake month partition, closing a silent data-LOSS race (resilience gap #5 of the critical-risks batch)** (2026-06-21, operator: "cover all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions … O(1) … always real time guarantee with assurance … no illusion or hallucination … just go ahead"). **Why:** a multi-agent audit (the data-pull/lake "heart", Correctness > Reliability priority law) found the two lake Parquet writers do a READ-modify-WRITE on a month partition (read stored bars → union incoming keyed by timestamp → atomic `os.replace`) guarded ONLY by a per-partition `threading.Lock` — which serialises threads WITHIN one interpreter but NOT across PROCESSES. Two pulls sharing `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT` (a CLI `brutex fetch` + a dashboard pull, or two CLI runs) writing the same month partition therefore lost-update SILENTLY: P1 reads `[T1,T2,T3]`, P2 reads `[T1,T2,T3]`, P1 writes `[…,T4]`, P2's `os.replace` clobbers it with `[…,T5]` → **T4 is gone**, no error, no conflict — the exact opposite of "real guarantee / no illusion" (Golden Rule #1). The keep-first idempotent merge does NOT save it: it only applies WITHIN one process's merge; across processes the LAST `os.replace` wins. **What shipped (NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** a NEW `brutex/data/partition_lock.py` (`partition_write_lock(lake_root, dest)` + `partition_lock_path`) takes a blocking exclusive `fcntl.flock` held ACROSS the whole read-modify-write, so the later process reads AFTER the earlier writer's `os.replace` and its union INCLUDES the earlier bars. BOTH writers nest it inside their existing per-partition `threading.Lock` critical section (`parquet_writer.ParquetWriter.write` + `option_parquet_writer._merge_partition`), in the SAME lock ORDER everywhere (threading → flock → `lake_write_guard`), so no cross-partition deadlock. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ the lock is on a STABLE sidecar `<lake_root>/.locks/<sha256(dest)>.lock`, NEVER the partition file — `os.replace` swaps the partition's inode on every write, so an flock on the partition fd would guard an orphaned inode (no mutual exclusion); the `.locks` dir is OUTSIDE `bars/`+`options/` and is not a `*.parquet`, so no dataset glob / lake scanner sees it (verified: 134 ingest + lake-scan tests green). ✅ PER PARTITION — writers to DIFFERENT partitions hash to DIFFERENT lock files and never contend, so the per-window fan-out keeps its parallelism; only same-partition cross-process writers queue. ✅ NO stale-lock recovery needed — an `flock` is released by the kernel on fd-close OR process death, so a crashed pull never leaves a stuck lock (unlike a PID-file). ✅ O(1) per partition write (one open+flock+close — NOT per bar); a disk-full at lock creation maps to `LakeWriteHalt` (reuses #885's `lake_write_guard`, consistency preserved). ✅ POSIX (Linux + macOS, the Track-1 hardware envelope); Windows OUT OF SCOPE. ✅ This serialises CONCURRENT writers to one partition; it is NOT a cross-partition transaction and does NOT replace the crash-safe `atomic_write_via` rename (they compose). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-21): `partition_lock.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (6 unit cases — under-`.locks` path, per-partition determinism, hold-then-release, release-on-body-error, different-partitions-don't-contend, disk-full→`LakeWriteHalt`); `parquet_writer.py` (125/22) + `option_parquet_writer.py` (87/16) stay **100.00% line+branch** with NEW deterministic regression tests for EACH writer that probe a SEPARATE fd (≈ another process) DURING the writer's merge READ and assert the lock is HELD — these FAIL without the cross-process flock (the precise lost-update regression); chaos/sink/atomic_io (26) + ingest + lake-scan (134) suites GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/data/partition_lock.py`, `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `brutex/data/option_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_partition_lock.py`, `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_option_parquet_writer.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 + DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 (the intra-process per-partition `threading.Lock` this extends across processes), DEC-LAKE-MERGE-WRITE-001 (the read-modify-write merge serialised), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 (the `lake_write_guard` reused for the disk-full-at-lock-creation case). **Part of:** the critical-risks resilience-hardening batch (gap #5 of: 5xx-retry #883 ✅, CLI ledger checkpoint #884 ✅, disk-full/OOM halt #885 ✅, corrupt-file `/movers` skip #886 ✅, this lake process-lock, + remaining: Telegram alerting, the audit-discovered engine map-full/Bloom-capacity/poison-combo isolation, + the remaining 5-copy atomic-write COMMON consolidation).

a disk-full is NOT mis-escalated into a `LakeWriteHalt`. ✅ a small durability IMPROVEMENT folded in: the shared core's `finally` cleans the temp on ANY error (the old `except OSError` leaked a temp on a non-`OSError`); `results_store.py` + `sweep_checkpoint.py` stay **100.00% line+branch** (the engine cleanup-on-replace-failure tests repointed to `brutex.data.atomic_io.os.replace` + the `.brutex-write-*` temp prefix); a disk-full is NOT mis-escalated. ✅ TWO free improvements folded in everywhere: an `fsync` before the rename (none of the four had one — real durability gain) + temp-cleanup on ANY error (the window-ledger copy in particular previously LEAKED its `.tmp` on a mid-write failure). ✅ the credential 0600 security boundary is PRESERVED (and arguably tightened — `mkstemp` is owner-only from creation). ✅ DEFERRED (NOT claimed): the `window_ledger_store` ENOSPC→`LakeWriteHalt` **graceful-halt upgrade** — it CHANGES error semantics and the `end_pull_ledger` call-path (outside the ingest spine's global-stop handler) needs verification that the halt propagates gracefully, so this PR keeps the SAFE guard-free dedup (raw `OSError`) and flags the guard-extend as a separate verified follow-up. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `atomic_io.py` (NEW `chmod` test) + `config/runtime.py` + `dashboard/ntm_cache.py` + `data/window_ledger_store.py` all **100.00% line+branch**; `config/credentials.py` **100.00% line+branch** (via `test_credentials.py` + `test_groww_credentials.py`); the runtime cleanup test repointed to `brutex.data.atomic_io.os.replace` + `.brutex-write-*` prefix;
