892. **DEC-NTM-CACHE-FIRST-001 — the `/universe` NTM-constituent load is now CACHE-FIRST + fail-fast, so every load after the first is INSTANT instead of re-blocking ~30–160 s on the slow niftyindices.com host (the operator's "why is this taking so much time / why AGAIN" fix)** (2026-06-22, operator: "always i need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … latency … covering all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions … make everything as common runtime dynamic scalable … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** the operator's `make run` showed `POST /api/v1/universe/load-instruments` at `latency_ms=162854.5` (≈163 s) and a page stuck at "0 INDEX 0 STOCKS / loading instrument master". Root cause: `instrument_loader._resolve_constituent_csv` was **LIVE-FIRST** — it ALWAYS attempted the live niftyindices fetch (`_default_opener`, a fixed 30 s timeout × 3 retries + backoff ≈ 90 s worst case) and used the on-disk last-good cache ONLY when that live fetch FAILED. So even with a perfectly good cache present, EVERY `/universe` load re-paid the full slow live fetch (the niftyindices host is slow-to-first-byte / bot-blocks non-browser clients), and the whole load runs under `_LOAD_LOCK` — hence the repeated multi-minute "stuck" page. The NTM ~750-name universe is REFERENCE_ONLY and rebalances only semi-annually (CLAUDE.md §7), so re-fetching it on every load is pure waste. **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard load; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** `_resolve_constituent_csv` is rewritten CACHE-FIRST and now returns `(csv_text, source)` with `source ∈ {cache_fresh, live, cache_stale, none}`: (1) a cache YOUNGER than a TTL (`_ntm_cache_ttl_seconds`, env `BRUTEX_NTM_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, default 7 days) is served INSTANTLY with ZERO network call — the O(1) ultra-fast hot path that fixes the repeated slowness; (2) only a cold/stale cache hits ONE bounded live fetch (now env-tunable — `nse_constituents._fetch_timeout_seconds` / `_fetch_max_retries`, env `BRUTEX_NSE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` / `BRUTEX_NSE_FETCH_MAX_RETRIES`), and crucially that fetch is now paid AT MOST ONCE per TTL, not on every load. The headline win is the cache-first ORDERING, NOT a timeout cut: the per-attempt timeout DEFAULT stays the operator-validated 30 s (the prior code's comment recorded that a 10 s attempt read-TIMED-OUT on this exact host and 30 s was the deliberate fix), so the ONE cold fetch stays patient enough to SUCCEED-once and seed the cache → instant forever (a cut-and-FAILED fetch would crater a cold boot to the ~211 F&O base — the worse outcome); retries are trimmed 3 → 2 so the worst case is 30 s × 2 ≈ 61.5 s, down from the old 30 s × 3 ≈ 90 s; an operator who prefers a HARDER fail-fast lowers the env knobs; (3) a live failure/empty with a stale cache falls back to it (`cache_stale` — universe stays full); (4) no fresh cache + live fail/empty + no stale cache → `("", "none")` honest degrade to the F&O base set. A NEW `ntm_cache.load_cached_constituent_with_age` (+ `CachedConstituents`) reads the body and its mtime once (age clamped ≥ 0 for clock skew); the `_ntm_admission` note now carries the honest `source` + `from_cache` for the operator audit. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ this is O(1)-latency on the STEADY-STATE load (a fresh-cache hit = one small stat+read, no network), NOT a literal O(1) on the first-ever boot — the cold/post-TTL refresh still pays the bounded live fetch ONCE (explicitly bounded + env-tunable, never the old unbounded 90 s); after one success it is cache_fresh for the whole TTL. ✅ correctness unchanged — the SAME constituent CSV is parsed/matched; only the ORDER (cache before live) + the live timeout bound changed; a non-positive TTL explicitly DISABLES the fast path (always refresh) yet still serves a stale cache, so worst case is "as patient as before", never worse. ✅ no background threads / no new global mutable state — fully synchronous + deterministic. ✅ the operator's manual "drop ind_niftytotalmarket_list.csv at ~/.brutex/cache/ntm_constituents.csv" now makes the VERY NEXT load instant (cache_fresh), not just a failure-fallback. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `ntm_cache.py` + `nse_constituents.py` at **100.00% line+branch**, `instrument_loader.py` at **100.00% line+branch** across its covering files; NEW tests — fresh-cache served with a `_must_not_fetch_opener` that ASSERTS the network is never called, stale-cache refreshed-by-live / covered-by-empty / covered-by-raise (TTL=0 forces stale), no-cache+empty→`none` degrade, the age helper (text+age, future-mtime clamp, default wall-clock, absent/empty/dir/stat-vanish → None), + the three env-tunable bound helpers (absent/valid/malformed/non-positive); 262 universe/constituents/loader tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict brutex`/`pyright brutex tests` clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`, `brutex/dashboard/nse_constituents.py`, `brutex/dashboard/ntm_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py`, `tests/unit/test_nse_constituents.py`, `tests/unit/test_ntm_cache.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-NTM-CACHE-FIRST-001. **Supersedes the ORDERING of:** DEC-NTM-CONSTITUENT-CACHE-001 (the last-good disk cache stays — it is now the PRIMARY fast path, not just a failure fallback). **Builds on:** DEC-NTM-GROWW-REPOINT-001 (the NTM admission this accelerates), DEC-NTM-CONSTITUENT-CACHE-001 (the cache it reads first), DEC-ATOMIC-WRITE-FINISH-001 #891 (the `atomic_write_simple` the cache save uses). **Part of:** the operator's ultra-fast/O(1)/cover-all-worst-cases mandate applied to the literal cause of the "stuck dashboard" — the slow NTM constituent fetch on every load.

893. **DEC-COVERAGE-WINDOWS-O1-001 — the `/coverage/windows` "Fetch windows" page is now O(page): DuckDB `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` + a generation-cached `GROUP BY` replace the unconditional O(340,330) Python count+filter+sort that ran on EVERY tab/filter click + 4 s poll (the operator's "navigating from one section to another is really very slow … O(1) latency everywhere")** (2026-06-22, operator: "always i need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … latency … covering all worst cases … make everything as common runtime dynamic scalable … no illusion or hallucination"). **Why:** a 3-agent investigation + the operator's attached `brutex.log` PROVED it: `db_view.build_window_payload` built `counts` with a full Python loop over EVERY record (`for r in records`), then filtered with a full list-comprehension over EVERY record, then `.sort()`, then sliced `[:limit]` — all O(N=340,330) on every request, regardless of filter (the mtime `_ledger_records_cached` saved the READ, never the PROCESSING). There was NO SQL `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` or `WHERE` pushdown (unlike `query_candles`). The log showed it degrade **tens-of-ms early → 1.5–4 s sustained** (peak 4008 ms) as the ledger grew over an 80-min pull, once per minute in lockstep with the page poll. **What shipped (READ-ONLY viewer; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** modelled exactly on the proven `/db` (DEC-DB-VIEWER-PAGINATE-ALL-001 + DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001) + `/movers` (DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001) + `/universe` (DEC-UNIVERSE-BACKEND-CACHE-001) patterns: a NEW `_build_window_payload_duckdb` reads the ledger Parquet (`<lake>/window_ledger/ledger.parquet`) via DuckDB — the ROW page is a `WHERE` (market-bucket + status, PLANNED excluded unless `?status=PLANNED`) + severity-first `ORDER BY` (a CASE built from `_WINDOW_STATUS_ORDER`, the ONE order source) + `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` query (O(page)); the `counts` come from ONE `GROUP BY market, status` (`_window_counts_total`) memoised behind the COMMON generation-stamped `MoversSnapshotCache` (NEW dedicated `_window_counts_cache`, keyed by `_summary_cache.generation` — a repeat click within one generation is O(1), a pull bumps the generation → recompute), and `matched` is DERIVED from those cached counts (NO extra scan). `build_window_payload` gains optional `conn`/`offset`/`count_cache`/`generation`; the `/api/v1/coverage/windows` route injects `store.connection` + the cache + generation + a NEW `offset` query param. The per-row projection REUSES the shared `_window_row` (ONE shape with the legacy path — `_decode_option_window`/`format_ist_clock` already handle each field). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ a cached-counts HIT is O(1) in partition depth + the row page is O(page) (DuckDB still reads Parquet footers/row-groups, NOT a literal O(1) total); the FIRST read after a pull (new generation) pays one real `GROUP BY` scan — true O(page) WRITE-side would need a write-time manifest (NOT claimed). ✅ a `None` `conn` (every existing caller/test) OR no ledger Parquet keeps the LEGACY pyarrow path byte-for-byte (back-compat + the `window_status.json` fallback) — ZERO behaviour change there. ✅ the DuckDB path returns the SAME payload dict (proven by a fast-path-equals-legacy-path test on a mixed spot/option/future ledger). ✅ this fixes the SERVER `latency_ms` the log measured; a frontend in-place-`<tbody>`/client-cache/debounce pager (the 2,244-row full-DOM re-render) is a flagged FAST-FOLLOW, NOT claimed here, as is the even-slower `/completeness` 7–9 s endpoint (same O(windows) family). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `db_view.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (675/212, 322 covering-file tests) with a NEW `TestBuildWindowPayloadDuckDB` (equals-legacy, market/status filters, PLANNED-only-on-request, offset paging + capped, severity order, generation cache memoise+invalidate, empty Parquet, the helpers direct); the `/api/v1/coverage/windows` route integration (31) GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_view.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COVERAGE-WINDOWS-O1-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001 (the `CandleCountCache` Protocol + generation-cache pattern this mirrors as `WindowCountsCache`), DEC-DB-VIEWER-PAGINATE-ALL-001 (the `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` pushdown — it had left the window-ledger as the one deliberately-O(windows) read; this closes it), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the durable ledger Parquet read here via DuckDB). **Part of:** the operator's "nowhere in the product should ever be slow" / O(1)-everywhere mandate — queue item #1 of the coverage/db latency batch (next: the `/completeness` 7–9 s endpoints + the `/db` spot-candles cascade + the frontend window pager).

894. **DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 — the F&O default historical-pull lookback is now SPLIT by contract type: FUTURES default to 3 calendar months, OPTIONS to a tighter 30 days (the operator's "only for futures by default try to fetch it for 3 months but for options only one month, that is max 30 days")** (2026-06-22, operator: "only for futures by deafult try to fetch it for 3 months dude but for otpions only one month thats is max 30 days"). **Why:** when the operator passes NO explicit from/to dates, `default_fno_minute_window` defaulted EVERY F&O contract — future AND option — to the last `DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_MONTHS = 3` calendar months of its trading life (DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853). An option's liquid life is short and the option chain is huge (every listed strike × CE/PE per expiry), so a 3-month default over-pulls illiquid early-life option bars and inflates the pull; the operator wants options bounded to a 30-day tail while futures keep the 3-month "recent life of the contract" window. **What shipped (pull-PLANNING window only; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3 — the F&O lake is REFERENCE_ONLY):** (1) `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py` gains `DEFAULT_OPTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS: Final[int] = 30` (a fixed-30-DAY cap, not a calendar month, per the operator's "max 30 days"; added to `__all__`) alongside the existing `DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_MONTHS = 3`; `default_fno_minute_window` gains an `is_option: bool = False` keyword and branches the lookback START — `expiry − timedelta(days=DEFAULT_OPTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS)` for an option vs `subtract_calendar_months(expiry, DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_MONTHS)` for a future — with the SAME `max(full_start, lookback_start)` / `min(full_end, expiry + 1 day)` clamp + the SAME `start >= end → (full_start, full_end)` empty-window guard + the SAME `expiry is None → (full_start, full_end)` early return as before (only the START formula forks; the end-EXCLUSIVE `+ 1 day` expiry-day inclusion is unchanged). (2) `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py::_resolve_minute_windows` passes `is_option=contract.contract_type in {"CE", "PE"}` (the contract types are exactly `FUT`/`CE`/`PE` per `adapters/groww/contracts.py` — CE/PE → option, FUT → future; explicit operator from/to dates still take the `explicit_dates` branch and override either default). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ this changes ONLY the DEFAULT planning window when the operator gives no dates — an explicit from/to range is byte-for-byte unchanged (the `explicit_dates` branch is untouched). ✅ 30 days is a fixed day-count, NOT one calendar month (the operator said "max 30 days" — a calendar month varies 28–31 days); the future side keeps the calendar-month helper. ✅ both bounds stay clamped INTO the resolved `[full_start, full_end)` envelope so the default never widens past the historical floor → previous-day ceiling, and the empty/`None`-expiry guards are preserved (no new failure mode). ✅ pull-side only — no lake schema, no stored-bar, no rate, no vocab, no engine change; the F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `contract_bounds.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (87 stmts/20 branches, 32 tests — NEW: 30-day constant, option uses expiry−30d, future-vs-option differ for the same expiry, option clamps start to full_start) and `historical_pull.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (210 stmts/46 branches, 40 tests — the two minute-window-default tests updated for the per-type split since the NIFTY fixture mixes CE/PE/FUT at one expiry); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_contract_bounds.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853 (the 1-minute-only F&O pull whose default window this refines), DEC-FNO-WINDOW-PLAN-001 #879 (the per-`(contract, interval)` planning this window feeds). **Refines (does NOT supersede):** the "F&O historical DEFAULT window is per-contract `expiry − 3mo → expiry`" fact of #853 — futures keep 3 months; options narrow to 30 days. **Part of:** the operator's pull-tuning requests (bound the option-chain over-pull).

895. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-O1-LATENCY-001 — the `/completeness` endpoints (scoreboard + CSV + `/universe/completeness`) are now O(1) on a repeat load: the O(datasets) full-lake spot scan is routed through the SAME generation-stamped `_summary_cache` SPOT entry `/coverage/spot` already uses, instead of the prior UNCACHED direct call that re-ran the whole Parquet-footer aggregate on every load (the operator's 7–9 s page)** (2026-06-22, operator: "always i need ultra fast extreme speed to achieve O(1) … latency … covering all worst cases situations scenarios errors exceptions … make everything as common runtime dynamic scalable … no illusion or hallucination"; queue item #3 of the coverage/db latency batch, the flagged FAST-FOLLOW of DEC-COVERAGE-WINDOWS-O1-001 #893). **Why:** the three completeness endpoints share ONE helper `app._completeness_inputs(store, lake)`, which built the spot rows via `build_spot_coverage_payload(summarize_spot_datasets(store.connection, lake), spot_window_rollup(lake))` — calling `summarize_spot_datasets` (db_view.py: it iterates EVERY discovered spot dataset and runs a per-dataset `COUNT(*)`/`MIN`/`MAX` `read_parquet` footer aggregate — O(datasets), each reading Parquet footers across all year/month partitions) DIRECTLY with NO cache. Yet the sibling `/coverage/spot` route wraps the BYTE-IDENTICAL `summarize_spot_datasets(store.connection, lake)` call inside `_summary_cache.get_or_refresh(SPOT, recompute=…)`. So every scoreboard / CSV / `/universe` completeness load re-ran the full O(datasets) scan from scratch while `/coverage/spot` served it cached — the asymmetry that made completeness the slow page. **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** a one-expression DRY fix in `_completeness_inputs` — the spot scan now goes through `_summary_cache.get_or_refresh(SPOT, recompute=lambda: summarize_spot_datasets(store.connection, lake))`, sharing the SAME per-kind SPOT cache entry `/coverage/spot` populates (open either page and the other is warm). The ledger rollup `spot_window_rollup(lake)` (its OWN mtime-keyed cache) stays PER-REQUEST and OUTSIDE the SummaryCache — exactly the hostile-C8 freshness contract `/coverage/spot` uses — so a ledger flush with no lake write still refreshes the completeness chips between scans. The two other reads in the helper (`store.list_index_equity_instruments()` for the category map + `store.list_coverage()` for the option records) are single-table SELECTs, far cheaper than the per-dataset footer scans, and stay per-request so option/instrument state is never stale. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ a repeat load is O(1) on the SPOT lake scan (served from the shared cache), NOT a literal O(1) total — the FIRST read after a pull (the cache marked dirty past the TTL floor) still pays ONE real O(datasets) scan, and the cheap option/instrument SELECTs run every request; ✅ correctness unchanged — the SAME `summarize_spot_datasets` output feeds the SAME `build_spot_coverage_payload` projection; only the cache ORDERING changed (proven by a fast-path test: the scan runs EXACTLY ONCE across two `/completeness/scoreboard` loads + one `/coverage/spot` load, and the two completeness payloads are byte-identical); ✅ the chips stay fresh on a ledger flush because the rollup is deliberately kept outside the cache (C8); ✅ a pull marks `_summary_cache` dirty so the next eligible completeness read recomputes (inherited from the already-100%-covered `SummaryCache`). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `brutex/dashboard/app.py` stays at **100.00% line+branch** (the change adds no new app.py branch — the hit/miss/throttle decision lives inside the 100%-covered `SummaryCache`; the new lambda is exercised on the first completeness load); NEW integration test `test_spot_scan_shared_cache_across_completeness_and_coverage` (spy proves one scan across three loads + identical payloads); the `TestCompletenessScoreboard` + coverage route suites (83) GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Folded hostile-review MAJOR (cold-start race hardening — the operator's "cover all worst cases / errors / exceptions / 500s with real-time guarantee, no illusion"):** because this PR is the FIRST to SHARE the per-kind SPOT cache entry across TWO concurrently-polled routes (`/coverage/spot`'s 4 s poll + the completeness loads), it widened the cold-start exposure of a LATENT race in `SummaryCache._plan`: the `kind in self._refreshing` branch returned `None` (→ `get_or_refresh` then dereferenced `self._entries[kind]`) even on a COLD cache where no entry had EVER been written — a `KeyError` → 500 during the multi-second first scan when two readers hit the same uninitialised kind. FIX (in `brutex/dashboard/summary_cache.py`): the in-flight short-circuit now fires only when `entry is not None and kind in self._refreshing` (the warm-entry fast path is byte-unchanged — the existing `test_in_flight_refresh_serves_current_entry_no_double_scan` still seeds first, so it still serves the stale entry with NO double scan); on a COLD cache the reader deliberately FALLS THROUGH and recomputes too — a transient, idempotent double-scan on the very first concurrent access, far better than a 500. NEW unit test `test_cold_concurrent_refresh_recomputes_instead_of_keyerror` drives it deterministically (the first-ever refresh re-enters `get_or_refresh` for the same kind while the cache is still cold → the re-entrant reader recomputes its OWN fresh scan, never a `KeyError`); `summary_cache.py` stays at **100.00% line+branch** (80 stmts/10 branches, 21 tests). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/summary_cache.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `tests/unit/test_summary_cache.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-O1-LATENCY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-COVERAGE-WINDOWS-O1-001 #893 (which flagged the `/completeness` 7–9 s endpoint as the next FAST-FOLLOW in the same O(latency) family), DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the `_summary_cache` + threadpool-worker store-connection pattern this reuses), DEC-COVERAGE-SPOT-001 (the `/coverage/spot` cached scan this shares). **Part of:** the operator's "nowhere in the product should ever be slow" / O(1)-everywhere mandate — queue item #3 (next: the `/db` spot-candles cascade + the frontend window pager).

896. **DEC-DB-TAB-SWITCH-O1-001 — the `/db` candle tab switch (spot ↔ F&O ↔ option) is now O(1): the `/api/v1/db/candles/datasets` discovery endpoint — which walked the WHOLE `bars/` tree THREE times on EVERY tab switch — is memoised behind the shared write generation, so a switch within one generation is a cached handoff instead of a triple full-lake dir-walk (the operator's "to navigate from F&O candles to candles also taking so much time")** (2026-06-22, operator: "even to naviaget from section fromfno cnaldes to cnadles also takign som uch time … why … O(1) latency"; queue item #4a of the coverage/db latency batch). **Why:** an Explore-agent diagnosis traced the slow tab switch to `app.api_db_candle_datasets` (`/api/v1/db/candles/datasets`), the endpoint the `/db` frontend re-hits on every spot/F&O/option candle tab switch. Its `_datasets()` builder ran THREE O(files) `bars/` dir-walks with NO cache — `list_candle_datasets(lake)` for the spot list (db_view.py: walks `bars/<exch>/<seg>/<symbol>/<interval>/` and `rglob("*.parquet")`s every interval dir), `list_fno_candle_datasets(lake)` (which itself calls `list_candle_datasets` + `parse_fno_symbol` per F&O set), and `list_option_datasets(lake, …)` over `options/`. On a multi-year lake that is thousands of filesystem stats PER tab switch. The already-merged O(page) work (#817/#818/#821) fixed within-tab PAGING but never the tab-SWITCH discovery — the gap this closes. **What shipped (READ-ONLY viewer; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** the three discovered lists are invariant between lake writes, so `_datasets()` is now wrapped in `_db_datasets_cache.get_or_compute("db_candle_datasets", generation=_summary_cache.generation, compute=_datasets)` — REUSING the COMMON generation-stamped `MoversSnapshotCache` (the SAME generic memo `_candle_count_cache` + `_window_counts_cache` use, CLAUDE.md §11 — one keyed cache, no movers coupling, NO new class / NO copy of `FnoCascadeCache`). A repeat tab switch within one generation is an O(1) cached handoff; a pull/materialize bumps `_summary_cache.generation` → the next switch rediscovers. The build still runs on the threadpool worker on a cache MISS (the store read + dir-walks stay off the event loop). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ a repeat tab switch is O(1) in the lake dir depth (cached lists), NOT a literal O(1) total — the FIRST switch after a pull (new generation) still pays ONE real triple dir-walk; ✅ correctness unchanged — the SAME `_datasets()` output (spot + fno + fno_schema + options) is served, only the discovery ORDERING changed (proven by a spy test: `list_fno_candle_datasets` runs EXACTLY ONCE across three `/api/v1/db/candles/datasets` loads, and all three payloads are byte-identical); ✅ the no-lake-root empty-shape path is unchanged (never a 500); ✅ this fixes the BACKEND discovery cost the diagnosis measured — the frontend full-DOM-rebuild-on-switch (vs an in-place `#dbgrid` refresh) is a flagged FAST-FOLLOW, NOT claimed here, as is the spot-candle symbol→interval CASCADE picker (queue item #4b, the F&O-cascade twin). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `brutex/dashboard/app.py` stays at **100.00% line+branch** (the change adds the cache lookup + a compute lambda, exercised by the new + existing datasets tests; the hit/miss decision lives in the 100%-covered `MoversSnapshotCache`); NEW integration test `test_datasets_discovery_cached_across_tab_switches` (proves BOTH halves at this call site with an INJECTED `SummaryCache`: the discovery runs ONCE across three tab-switch loads with byte-identical payloads, AND a `mark_dirty` generation bump forces exactly ONE re-discovery — never a stale dataset list, the folded hostile-review NIT); the `/db` datasets + F&O-candle-lake + db-ux + movers-cache suites GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_datasets.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-TAB-SWITCH-O1-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001 #867 / DEC-COVERAGE-WINDOWS-O1-001 #893 (the generation-stamped `MoversSnapshotCache` memo pattern reused), DEC-DB-FNO-CASCADE-001 #880 (the F&O cascade whose `_fno_cascade_cache` uses the same generation signal), DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 #861 (the `list_fno_candle_datasets` discovery cached here). **Part of:** the operator's "nowhere in the product should ever be slow" / O(1)-everywhere mandate — queue item #4a (next: #4b the `/db` spot-candle symbol→interval cascade picker).

897. **DEC-DB-SPOT-CASCADE-001 — the `/db` SPOT candle picker is now a symbol→interval CASCADE (the spot twin of the F&O cascade), replacing the flat ~750-row dropdown so the operator can actually pick an underlying symbol + a stored timeframe (the operator's "even for candles i can't select the underlying symbol or timeframe")** (2026-06-22, operator: "even for candles also i cant select the udnerlyign symbol or timefrmae or from or to date right dude even there also inside database inside candle also we need to have the same where we have implemented for fno candle"; queue item #4b of the coverage/db latency batch, the stated FAST-FOLLOW of DEC-DB-TAB-SWITCH-O1-001 #896). **Why:** the `/db` SPOT candle tab rendered ONE flat `<select>` of every spot partition — the ~750-name NIFTY-Total-Market reference universe × the stored intervals — an unnavigable list (the operator couldn't find a symbol/timeframe), while the F&O tab already had a clean underlying→expiry→contract cascade (DEC-DB-FNO-CASCADE-001 #880). **What shipped (READ-ONLY viewer; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** a faithful 2-level mirror of the proven F&O cascade. NEW pure `brutex/dashboard/spot_cascade.py` (`build_spot_cascade` → `SpotCascadeIndex.symbols()` O(1); `SpotSymbol` leaf carrying its STORED `intervals` inline; `symbol_to_json`) groups the discovered non-F&O datasets (`list_candle_datasets` filtered to the `INDEX`/`CASH` segments — exactly the `spot` list the datasets endpoint builds, DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001) by `(exchange, segment, symbol)`, sorted **indices-first then alphabetical** (the `INDEX` segment floats NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX to the top, DATA-DRIVEN — no hardcoded symbol list). ONE new route `GET /api/v1/db/spot/symbols` (the symbols-with-intervals payload is small, so unlike F&O's huge contracts-per-expiry it needs NO lazy second level) via a `_spot_cascade_or_none()` helper memoised behind `_summary_cache.generation` in a dedicated `_spot_cascade_cache` (REUSING the COMMON `MoversSnapshotCache`, the spot twin of `_fno_cascade_cache` — NO new cache class). The `db.html` frontend gains a `cstate.spot` substate + `loadSpotCascade`/`onSpotSymbolChange`/`spotCascadeHtml` + a `csym` symbol select wired in `renderCandleView`; a symbol pick MATERIALISES the per-interval `{kind:"spot", exchange, segment, symbol, interval}` descriptors so the SHARED `query_candles` candle path (`dsKey`/`buildCandleUrl`) is BYTE-UNCHANGED — the cascade is purely the picker. The interval sub-pick reuses the F&O `cintv` handler. **Stored-only intervals (Golden Rule #1 — no phantom TFs):** the interval level offers ONLY the intervals with a real on-disk partition (in practice `1minute` + the derived `1day`, DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001), because `query_candles` reads a physical partition and returns an EMPTY page for an absent one (it does NOT resample on-the-fly) — offering all 21 TFs would render an empty grid, an illusion; this mirrors F&O exactly. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the cascade index is O(1)-cached per generation (a pull rebuilds it, every picker open is a handoff), NOT a literal O(1) first build (the cold build is one O(datasets) walk); ✅ the query path is unchanged — the cascade only changes the PICKER, the candle read is the same `query_candles` spot path; ✅ only the expired-OPTIONS lake keeps the flat dropdown (it is a genuinely different, decoded-label surface); ✅ the spot cascade is independent of the F&O cascade (separate leaf shapes — a shared base would be a leaky abstraction), but the generation MEMO is the COMMON `MoversSnapshotCache`, NOT a copy of `FnoCascadeCache`; `spot_cascade.py` imports nothing from `dashboard.*`/`data.*` (the route does the lake read), so no import cycle (CodeQL `py/cyclic-import`, mirroring `fno_cascade.py`). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `brutex/dashboard/spot_cascade.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (32 stmts/2 branches, 6 unit tests — empty/index-sort/interval-aggregate/exchange-tie/label/json); `brutex/dashboard/app.py` stays **100.00% line+branch** (the new route + helper exercised by the cascade integration tests); NEW `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_spot_cascade.py` (4 — indices-first + intervals-inline, F&O-segment-excluded, no-lake degrade, frontend wiring); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/spot_cascade.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/unit/test_spot_cascade.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_spot_cascade.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-SPOT-CASCADE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-FNO-CASCADE-001 #880 (the F&O cascade this mirrors), DEC-DB-TAB-SWITCH-O1-001 #896 (which flagged this as the next FAST-FOLLOW + cached the datasets discovery), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853 (the stored 1m + derived 1d partitions the interval level offers), DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 #861 (the non-F&O segment filter reused). **Part of:** the operator's "/db candle navigation is hard + slow" batch — #896 made the tab SWITCH O(1), this makes the spot PICKER navigable (next: the frontend in-place-grid refresh on tab switch).

898. **DEC-GROWW-AMPERSAND-FALLBACK-001 — F&O expiries/contracts for `&`-containing underlyings (M&M, M&MFIN, L&TFH, GVT&D, J&KBANK, ARE&M, GMRP&UI) now TRY a second `%26`-encoded symbol form when the plain form returns empty, so the whole-underlying chain failure (the operator's "M&M fails for entire expiries and contracts") is recovered instead of silently dropped** (2026-06-22, operator: "why still M&M is failing for entire expiries and contracts … maybe expiries and contracts are specifically expecting the different name … do a deep through check"; queue item #5; operator-chosen "try-both-forms fallback"). **Why (root-caused by a deep multi-file investigation + MIGRATION.md #870):** `metadata_pull` hands the F&O-eligible underlying's NSE `trading_symbol` (e.g. `M&M`) VERBATIM to `contracts.resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts` → `client.expiries`/`contracts` → the third-party `growwapi` SDK's `get_expiries`/`get_contracts`. The `&` is the HTTP query-string separator; the SDK's request builder sends it UN-ENCODED, so the vendor returns a clean-but-EMPTY `200`. Because the break is at the chain-discovery ROOT (`get_expiries` returns empty → zero expiries discovered → zero `get_contracts` calls → zero contracts), the ENTIRE underlying's expiry+contract set is missed — there are no legs to quarantine because none are ever enumerated, and `/completeness` reads `expiries_pulled=0` as `failed`/`none`. RULED OUT (with code evidence): NOT a master-lookup miss (the mapping is EXACT — M&M token 2031 matches its legs on `underlying_symbol` + `underlying_exchange_token`, #870), NOT a parse failure (`parse_contract_symbol`/`parse_fno_symbol` split on `-`; `&` is never a delimiter and the canonical symbol parses fine), and NOT fixed by #845 (which only fixed the SPOT candle path). This is the named-but-unshipped "F2" the repo's `mapping_integrity.py` documents as intentionally-deferred (M&M reads RED there as honest pre-fix proof). **What shipped (adapter resolution-layer only; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3 — the F&O lake is REFERENCE_ONLY):** NEW pure `contracts.underlying_symbol_forms(underlying_symbol)` → `(symbol,)` for a plain symbol, `(symbol, symbol.replace("&", "%26"))` for an `&` symbol (plain FIRST, then the standard `%26` encoding of `&`) + NEW generic `contracts._fetch_first_nonempty_form[T](forms, fetch, *, is_empty)` (tries each form in order, first non-empty wins, returns the LAST form's empty result if all empty — O(forms): exactly 1 call for a no-`&` symbol, at most 2 for an `&` symbol). `resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts` now wrap their per-form fetch in this BEFORE the existing transient-glitch `fetch_until_nonempty` budget (the two retry axes compose); `resolve_contracts` keeps `parse_contract_symbol` on the ORIGINAL `underlying_symbol` (the vendor returns the canonical `&` symbol — only the FETCH arg is encoded). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — explicitly NOT an illusion):** ✅ the EXACT correct encoding is an UNVERIFIED vendor/SDK behaviour — the `growwapi` SDK's internal URL construction needs a live Groww probe (CLAUDE.md §6 Phase-0 probe discipline; the SDK call sites are `pragma: no cover`) — so this is a HYPOTHESIS grounded in the #870 diagnosis, NOT a probe-confirmed fix; ✅ try-both is the no-worse-than-before contract: a non-`&` symbol is byte-for-byte unchanged (one form, no extra call), an `&` symbol where the vendor ALREADY handles plain `&` never regresses (plain non-empty → encoded never tried), and if neither form yields data (e.g. the SDK double-encodes `%26`→`%2526`, or a genuine pre-listing year) we record the SAME empty as today — never a fabricated chain; ✅ a confirmed encoding can replace `replace("&","%26")` once the probe lands (the helper is the single COMMON funnel both resolvers use); ✅ BAJAJ-AUTO's separate 2024-only `partial` shortfall is NOT conflated (it is a real coverage gap, not a symbol-encoding bug, per #870). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `brutex/adapters/groww/contracts.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (92 stmts/34 branches, 37 tests — NEW: `underlying_symbol_forms` plain/`&`, the expiries fallback empty-plain→encoded-data + plain-data-no-encoded, the contracts fallback empty-plain→encoded-chain parsed off the real `&` symbol); 148 contracts+option-ingest+metadata-pull+client tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/contracts.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_contracts.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-AMPERSAND-FALLBACK-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-RECONCILE-001 #870 (the root-cause diagnosis + the documented-deferred "F2"), DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001 #845 (the SPOT-path sibling — this is the OPTIONS-path twin it did not reach), DEC-EMPTY-RETRY-EVERYWHERE-001 (the `fetch_until_nonempty` transient-glitch retry this composes with on the orthogonal symbol-form axis). **Part of:** the operator's F&O data-completeness requests — recovers the `&`-underlying chains the `/completeness` screen showed failing.
899. **DEC-MOVERS-VWAP-VALUE-001 — the `/movers` "Top Value" (turnover) metric now uses the per-bar HLC3 typical price `(high+low+close)/3 × volume` instead of `close × volume`, so the ranking tracks a broker's intraday turnover far more closely (the operator's "for top value alone it is not precise to broker right? if yes then solve this")** (2026-06-22, operator-greenlit "yes pick this"; queue item #6). **Why:** the "Top Value" screen (Spot + Options; futures has no value tab) ranked instruments by `Σ over session bars (round_money(close) × volume)` — pricing a WHOLE minute's volume at that minute's CLOSING tick. A broker's true turnover is `Σ (actual trade price × qty)` over every tick; within a 1-minute bar trades span the `[low, high]` range, so pricing all of it at the close systematically over/under-states turnover whenever the close sits away from the minute's volume-weighted average — a SYSTEMATIC (not random) divergence summed over a session. The duplicated `close × volume` loop lived in BOTH `movers_snapshot.compute_snapshot` AND `movers_options._session_value_paisa` (a COMMON copy-paste). **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard ranking; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** NEW ONE COMMON helper `movers_snapshot.session_traded_value_paisa(rows)` (CLAUDE.md §11 — `rows` = an iterable of `(high, low, close, volume)`; computes `Σ round_money((high+low+close)/3) × volume` → int64 paisa) used by BOTH the spot snapshot (`compute_snapshot` now calls it with `(bar.high, bar.low, bar.close, bar.volume)`) AND the options screen (`_session_value_paisa` now also selects `high`/`low` from its 1-minute frame and delegates to the SAME helper) — killing the two duplicated loops. HLC3 = the standard "typical price" VWAP proxy. Money discipline (DEC-MONEY-2DP-001): each bar's typical price is `round_money`-snapped to the 2dp tick grid BEFORE the `× volume`, so every bar's contribution stays on the grid and the paisa total is exact. Ranking/display (`_by_value`/`rank_value`/`value_crore`) are UNCHANGED — they ride the now-more-accurate `value_paisa`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — explicitly NOT bit-exact):** ✅ this is a precision IMPROVEMENT — the CLOSEST-to-broker turnover obtainable from 1-minute OHLCV, NOT a bit-exact match: a broker sums actual trade price×qty per TICK; without tick data the HLC3×volume sum is the best volume-weighted-price approximation, and a residual divergence (the unknown intrabar volume distribution) remains and is NOT claimed away; there is NO Dhan/broker turnover spec in the repo to validate against, so this is framed "closer to broker", not "matches broker"; ✅ it degenerates to the OLD `close×volume` answer for a zero-range bar (`high==low==close`) — so a flat/illiquid bar is unchanged; ✅ scope: Spot + Options only (futures has no "Top Value" tab — a futures value metric would be a separate change). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py` + `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py` BOTH at **100.00% line+branch** (210/46 + 216/46); NEW golden `test_compute_snapshot_value_uses_hlc3_typical_price` proves the formula is active + DISTINCT (bars high=102/low=98/close=100/vol=10 + high=112/low=106/close=110/vol=20 → typical 100.00×10 + round_money(109.3333)=109.33×20 = ₹3186.60 = 318660 paisa, vs the OLD close×volume 320000); the `_bar` test helper gained optional `high`/`low` (defaulting to close so existing zero-range callers are unchanged); 304 movers tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_snapshot.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-VWAP-VALUE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001 (the spot snapshot whose value metric this refines), DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-001 (the options movers screen sharing the formula), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the 2dp tick-grid rounding the per-bar typical price obeys). **Part of:** the operator's "Top Value should match the broker precisely" request — the precision-improvement honest answer (closest-from-OHLCV, not tick-exact).

900. **DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-VALUE-001 — the `/movers` Futures tab gains a "Top Value" (turnover) ranking + a "Value (Cr)" column, completing the value metric across all three asset tabs (spot + options already had it; futures was the gap)** (2026-06-22, operator: "along with resilience hardening take futures top value tab also"). **Why:** the spot + options movers tabs ranked by traded value ("Top Value"), but the Futures tab had NO value metric — its session reader returned only `(ltp, volume, oi)` and `_FUTURES_CATEGORIES` had no `value` ranker. The operator asked for the futures value tab too. **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard ranking; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `FuturesMover` gains a `value_paisa: int` field + a `value_crore` property; (2) NEW `rank_value` ranker (turnover desc, zero-turnover excluded — the futures twin of the spot/options ranking) + `"value": rank_value` in `_FUTURES_CATEGORIES`; (3) `_futures_row` emits `value_cr`; (4) `_read_future_session` now ALSO computes the turnover from the SAME day-frame it already reads (one read, no extra pass) via the SHARED `movers_snapshot.session_traded_value_paisa` (the HLC3 typical-price × volume VWAP-proxy turnover of DEC-MOVERS-VWAP-VALUE-001) — returning `(ltp, volume, value_paisa, oi)`; `compute_futures_mover` + the candidate loop thread it through; (5) the `movers.html` Futures tab gains the `["value","Top Value"]` pill + the `["Value (Cr)","value_cr","num"]` column (mirroring spot). (6) COMMON: the `value_crore` ₹-crore formatter — previously inline in `MoverSnapshot.value_crore` — is extracted to ONE shared `movers_snapshot.value_crore_str(value_paisa)` used by BOTH the spot AND futures `value_crore` (no 2nd copy; CLAUDE.md §11). The options caller of the shared `_read_future_session` unpacks the new 4-tuple and ignores the `value_paisa` field (options keeps its own `_session_value_paisa` reader; the pre-existing options double-frame-read is unchanged — a deliberately-minimal touch, NOT a forced options refactor). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ same precision envelope as DEC-MOVERS-VWAP-VALUE-001 — the futures turnover is the CLOSEST-to-broker value from 1-minute OHLCV (HLC3 × volume), NOT a tick-exact match; ✅ it degenerates to `close × volume` for a zero-range bar; ✅ the value metric now spans spot + options + futures (full parity); ✅ READ-ONLY ranking, no engine/lake/scope change. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `movers_futures.py` + `movers_options.py` + `movers_snapshot.py` ALL at **100.00% line+branch** (226/48 + 216/46 + 212/46); NEW tests — `rank_value` (turnover desc, zero excluded), `compute_futures_mover` value pass-through + `value_crore`, `_futures_row` `value_cr`, the `_FUTURES_CATEGORIES` `value` key, `_read_future_session` value (full-day + cutoff-sliced) + an HLC3 distinguisher (real-range bar → 218660 ≠ the old close×volume 220000); 307 movers tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `tests/unit/test_movers_futures.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_futures.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-VALUE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-VWAP-VALUE-001 #899 (the HLC3 turnover helper this reuses for futures), DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 (the Futures tab this extends), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the 2dp crore formatter). **Part of:** the operator's "futures top value tab also" request — completing the "Top Value" metric across all three movers tabs.

901. **DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-WRITE-HALT-001 — a disk-full / OOM during the durable window-ledger save now HALTS the pull gracefully (a pull-wide `LakeWriteHalt`) instead of propagating a raw `OSError`, closing the last deferred gap of the lake-write-halt resilience arc** (2026-06-22, operator: "along with resilience hardening take futures top value tab also"; the resilience half of the paired request). **Why:** the durable window ledger lives under `<lake_root>/window_ledger/ledger.parquet` — it IS a lake write — yet `save_window_ledger` (`brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py`) used the guard-FREE `atomic_write_simple`, so a disk-full (`ENOSPC`) / out-of-memory during a save propagated a RAW `OSError`/`MemoryError`. A raw `OSError` is NOT a `BruteXError`, so on the mid-pull `on_window` flush path it would either crash the worker or be swept past the per-symbol quarantine UN-classified; a full disk fails every remaining window identically, so it must HALT the pull (the SAME semantics the spot + option Parquet writers already get from `atomic_write_via` per DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885). This was the EXPLICITLY-deferred follow-up flagged in DEC-ATOMIC-WRITE-CONSOLIDATE-001 #890 / DEC-ATOMIC-WRITE-FINISH-001 #891 ("the ENOSPC→LakeWriteHalt graceful-halt upgrade is a deliberately-deferred follow-up … the end_pull_ledger call-path's halt handling needs verification"). **What shipped (lake-write resilience; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `save_window_ledger` now writes through the lake-guarded `atomic_write_via` (`brutex/data/atomic_io.py`) instead of `atomic_write_simple`, so a save-time `ENOSPC` → `LakeWriteHalt("disk_full")` and a `MemoryError` → `LakeWriteHalt("out_of_memory")`, with EVERY other error UNCHANGED (a non-`ENOSPC` `OSError` such as `EACCES` still propagates raw — never mis-escalated). (2) the `atomic_write_simple` docstring drops "the window ledger" from its non-lake-caller list (it was promoted to the guarded variant — keeps the COMMON doc honest, CLAUDE.md §11). **Call-path verification (the deferral blocker, now COMPLETE — proven by a read-only Explore map + a hostile review):** `LakeWriteHalt` is ALREADY a member of BOTH ingest spines' `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` (`run_ingest.py` / `option_ingest.py`), so it propagates past the per-symbol/per-contract quarantine to the outer halt handlers ALREADY in place — the CLI `cmd_fetch` `_pull_halt_errors` (DEC-TELEGRAM-PULL-HALT-001 #888) + the dashboard `BackgroundPullJob._run` `_is_pull_halt` (DEC-TELEGRAM-PULL-HALT-DASHBOARD-001 #889), both of which fire the CRITICAL Telegram alert. All THREE save sites propagate cleanly: the mid-pull `on_window()` flush is called UN-wrapped in the ingest drain loop (`brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`); the dashboard's `make_live_sync._sync` lets the flush raise out of its `with lock:` (a `threading.Lock.__exit__` never suppresses); and `end_pull_ledger` runs in a `finally`. The dry-run / `None`-ledger path never reaches `save_window_ledger`, so it is unaffected. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ a graceful DETECTION + halt, NOT a memory CAP (a true RSS ceiling needs OS `setrlimit`/cgroups — out of scope, unchanged from #885); ✅ ONLY `ENOSPC` + `MemoryError` are mapped — a non-`ENOSPC` `OSError` propagates raw (proven), so an ordinary write error is never over-escalated to a pull-wide stop; ✅ recovery is a clean re-pull (the durable ledger + keep-first idempotent sink), not an in-place resume; ✅ strictly IMPROVES the disk-full path on every save site (the alert now fires where a raw `OSError` previously did not) with ZERO raw-`OSError` dependency broken (no test or caller expected a raw error). ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22): `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (177/50, 53 tests) + `brutex/data/atomic_io.py` stays **100.00% line+branch** (42/6, 13 tests); NEW regression tests `TestSaveDiskFullHalts` — `ENOSPC`→`disk_full` halt (+ asserts NO `.tmp` leak), `MemoryError`→`out_of_memory` halt, a non-`ENOSPC` `EACCES` propagating raw (never `LakeWriteHalt`), each driving the REAL `atomic_write_via`→`lake_write_guard` path by patching `pyarrow.parquet.write_table`; 904. **DEC-ENGINE-TUPLE-SKIP-RESILIENT-001 — when one grid TUPLE errors mid-sweep the engine now SKIPS it, finishes every remaining tuple, and exits NON-ZERO with a `tuples_failed` count + a `TUPLE_FAILED` audit line naming the exact offending combo (operator-chosen "Resilient: skip + continue")** (2026-06-22, operator: "work on everything else" → resilience hardening; AskUserQuestion: "Resilient: skip + continue"). **Why:** the brute-force sweep's per-combo evaluation loop (`sweep_run.py` `run_persisted_sweep`) was a list comprehension with NO exception isolation — one `metrics_for_mask` raise aborted the WHOLE grid (the `run_one_tuple` raise propagated uncaught through both `sweep_orchestrator.run_sweep_grid` and `sweep_supervisor.run_supervised_grid`), losing a multi-day grid to one bad tuple. A 4-agent hostile DESIGN review (Rule #9) established the fault model: every input to `metrics_for_mask` is TUPLE-INVARIANT (direction/tf/sl/tp/bar-window), so a raising combo is provably a tuple-wide BUG or corrupt bar window, NEVER a transient single combo — so **per-COMBO isolation was ruled OUT** (silently skipping one combo would be an illusion, Golden Rule #1, and risk a non-reproducible leaderboard, Rule #4). The genuine choice — the blast radius of a raising TUPLE — was put to the operator, who chose RESILIENT (vs strict abort). **What shipped (4 layers; brute-force ENGINE behaviour change — failure-path only, success path BYTE-IDENTICAL, scope still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** (1) `sweep_run.py`: NEW `SweepComboError(BruteXError)` — the combo loop became an explicit `for` that wraps each `metrics_for_mask` in `try/except Exception` and re-raises `SweepComboError` naming the offending `mask` (hex) + `run_id` + `instrument/tf/direction/k` (fail-loud-WITH-fingerprint, NOT swallowing; success `pairs` byte-identical). (2) `sweep_orchestrator.py`: `run_sweep_grid` catches ONLY `SweepComboError` → bumps a NEW `SweepGridSummary.tuples_failed`, appends a `TUPLE_FAILED` audit line (`{tuple,error}`), WARNING-logs, `continue`s; threaded into the summary + `GRID_SWEEP_COMPLETE` payload. (3) `sweep_supervisor.py`: `run_supervised_grid` catches `SweepComboError` → bumps `SupervisedGridSummary.tuples_failed` + `TUPLE_FAILED` audit (`{index,tuple,error}`) + advances progress as non-survived/non-skip, and CRITICALLY does NOT `cache.record`/`checkpoint.record` the failed tuple (the sweep_heal "C5" lesson — so a resume RE-RUNS it, never a permanent silent hole); the outer record-then-reraise ABORT path (genuinely-fatal infra errors) is unchanged. (4) honesty surface: NEW `cli.EXIT_SWEEP_TUPLE_FAILED = 6` + pure `sweep_all_exit_code(tuples_failed)` wired into `cmd_sweep_all` (prints `failed=…`, loud stderr WARNING, non-zero exit when >0); `notifications.sweep_alerts.sweep_complete` downgrades ✅→⚠️ + appends "N tuples FAILED" (MarkdownV2-escaped). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#4/#7/#10):** ✅ a failed tuple is left UN-sentineled (`run_persisted_sweep` raises BEFORE its flush/mark/sentinel) AND UN-cached/UN-checkpointed → a DETERMINISTIC bit-for-bit redo next run (reproducibility preserved); ✅ NEVER silent — the count is in BOTH grid summaries + a `TUPLE_FAILED` audit line naming the combo + a structured WARNING + a non-zero CLI exit + a ⚠️ alert (no illusion: a skipped tuple cannot masquerade as a complete sweep); ✅ ONLY `SweepComboError` is caught at the drivers (a genuine infra failure — disk-full `ResultsStoreError`, audit/flush error, `MemoryError` — is NOT a `SweepComboError` and still ABORTS globally, never mis-skipped); ✅ per-combo isolation explicitly REJECTED as an illusion; ✅ the success path is byte-identical (the golden suite proves the leaderboard + content hashes + clean-run audit lines unchanged); the `cmd_sweep_verify` shadow-resweep discards its grid summary so `tuples_failed` was not natural there (left, spec-permitted). ✅ REAL (independently verified 2026-06-22 via the repo `.venv`): `sweep_run.py` **100% line+branch** (246/70), `sweep_orchestrator.py` **100%** (217/66), `sweep_supervisor.py` **100%** (167/20), `notifications/sweep_alerts.py` **100%** (119/10), `cli.py` **100%** (539/102, the `sweep_all_exit_code` helper covered; `cmd_sweep_all` is a `# pragma: no cover` orchestration shim); NEW tests — `SweepComboError` subclass + raise-names-the-combo + no-store/sidecar/sentinel-written + dedup-unmarked; `run_sweep_grid` one-tuple-fails-others-run + audit + unsentineled + non-SweepComboError-propagates; `run_supervised_grid` skip-WITHOUT-cache/checkpoint-record (real-guard spies) + unsentineled + non-SweepComboError-aborts; the CLI exit helper; the ⚠️ alert branch; golden suite 42/42 GREEN (success path byte-identical); 374+278+123 broad engine/golden/alerts/cli/dashboard/scheduler/stage3/cascade/chaos passes, no regression; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (255 files)/`pyright` (0 errors) clean. **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_run.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_orchestrator.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_supervisor.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_backfill.py`, `tests/unit/test_notifications_sweep_alerts.py`, `tests/integration/test_telegram_sweep_alerts_wire.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-ENGINE-TUPLE-SKIP-RESILIENT-001. **Builds on:** the per-symbol/per-contract ingest quarantine pattern (`_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS`, DEC-GROWW-QUARANTINE-BRUTEX-001) this mirrors at the tuple grain, DEC-MARK-MANY-SENTINEL-001 (the completion-sentinel that makes an aborted tuple's redo deterministic), the `sweep_heal` C5 "never permanently skip a non-completed tuple" lesson. **Part of:** the operator's "resilience hardening … cover all extreme exceptions/errors/situations" mandate — the brute-force ENGINE's tuple-grain resilience capstone.

905. **DEC-FNO-PULL-ORDER-LOOKBACK-001 — the historical F&O pull now (1) pulls every FUTURES (FUT) contract BEFORE the CE/PE options, and (2) defaults ALL F&O contracts to a UNIFORM 30-day lookback (futures dropped from 3 months to 30 days, matching options)** (2026-06-22, operator: "always try to pull the futures at first one and only then options" + "even for futures also make it as only one month"). **Why (part 1 — order):** the historical-contract phase grouped rebuilt contracts into `by_market` (`GROWW_FUTURE_COVERAGE_MARKET` vs `GROWW_OPTION_COVERAGE_MARKET`) and iterated `by_market.items()` in dict INSERTION order — the option bucket was inserted first, so OPTIONS pulled before FUTURES (the live `/coverage` Futures tab read 0 windows while options churned; the first `option.ingest` log events were all `-PE`/`-CE`). **Why (part 2 — lookback):** `default_fno_minute_window` SPLIT the default lookback by type — FUT `expiry − 3 calendar months` (DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 #894), OPT `expiry − 30 days` — and the operator wants futures tightened to 30 days too. **What shipped (pull-PLANNING + ORDER only; NO lake/schema/stored-bar/rate/vocab/engine change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY):** (1) `historical_pull.py`: NEW module-level `_MARKET_PULL_ORDER = {GROWW_FUTURE_COVERAGE_MARKET: 0, GROWW_OPTION_COVERAGE_MARKET: 1}`; the phase loop now iterates `sorted(by_market.items(), key=lambda kv: (_MARKET_PULL_ORDER.get(kv[0], 99), kv[0]))` — FUTURES first, OPTIONS second, any unknown market LAST, with a stable name tie-break (reorders only the two market BUCKETS, never the contracts within a bucket; both leg types still pulled — only the order changed). (2) `contract_bounds.py`: `default_fno_minute_window` lost its `is_option` parameter — the lookback COLLAPSES to a single `lookback_start = expiry − timedelta(days=DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_DAYS)` for ALL F&O; `DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_MONTHS` (=3) + `DEFAULT_OPTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (=30) are replaced by ONE `DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_DAYS: Final[int] = 30`; the now-dead `subtract_calendar_months` function + the `from calendar import monthrange` import are REMOVED (zero remaining refs in `brutex/`); the caller `_resolve_minute_windows` drops the `is_option=` kwarg. SUPERSEDES the futures-3-month half of DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 #894 (the 30-day options half is unchanged; F&O is now uniform). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the same `max(full_start,…)` / `min(full_end, expiry + 1 day)` clamp + the `None`-expiry + collapsed-span fallbacks are byte-IDENTICAL (the options path was already 30 days, so it is unchanged; only the FUTURES default narrows 3mo→30d); ✅ the lookback is PER-CONTRACT (each contract's own expiry), never a global window; ✅ an explicit operator from/to range still overrides the default (the default path only runs when no dates are given); ✅ pull-PLANNING + ORDER only — no stored-bar/lake/rate/granularity change (still 1-minute-only per DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001), and FUT legs were already pulled (DEC-FUTURES-PULL-ENABLE-001) — this only fixes WHEN + HOW-FAR-BACK. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22 via `.venv`): `historical_pull.py` 100% line+branch (211/46) + `contract_bounds.py` 100% line+branch (79/20, branch count DROPPED with the simpler code); NEW tests — a spy asserting `run_groww_option_ingest` runs the FUTURE market BEFORE the OPTION market + the unknown-market-last tie-break; the window tests rewritten to the uniform 30-day (FUT/CE/PE all `expiry − 30d`); the 5 `subtract_calendar_months` tests + the 3-month + option-split tests REMOVED (the code they covered is gone); 132 F&O pull tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (255 files)/`pyright` clean; hostile-reviewer + workspace-health PENDING. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_contract_bounds.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-PULL-ORDER-LOOKBACK-001. **Supersedes:** the futures-3-month half of DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 #894. **Builds on:** DEC-FUTURES-PULL-ENABLE-001 (FUT legs already pulled — this orders them first), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853 (1-minute-only, unchanged), DEC-COVERAGE-GROWW-NAMESPACE-001 (the FUT/OPT market namespaces this orders). **Part of:** the operator's F&O pull-priority + bounded-lookback requests.

906. **DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-5-001 — the production Groww per-second rate ceiling is LOWERED 8 → 5 r/s, cutting wasted 429-retries with ZERO throughput loss (the AIMD ladder, the 500/min governor, and the floors are all unchanged)** (2026-06-22, operator: "add Rate-ceiling tuning (8→5?)"). **Why:** a live-log audit of a full F&O backfill (`brutex.log`, the operator's "check whether the rate limiter is really working") showed the adaptive controller spent almost the entire pull stepped DOWN at the soft floor (~3 r/s) absorbing the vendor's 429s — **~870 `rate.limited` 429-retries over the run with 0 data loss** — while the ceiling sat at the operator-DIRECTED 8 r/s (DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001). The vendor 429s even at 3–5 r/s, so the headroom between 5 and 8 was never usable throughput — it only let the controller probe UP into a wall and pay another wasted 429-retry ladder each time it cleared. An in-repo note already observed "vendor 429s above ~5 r/s anyway (live logs)" (`constants.py:196`), so the 8 ceiling already contradicted the repo's own measurement; this reconciles it. **What shipped (adapter + dashboard CONFIG + tests only; NO engine/lake/vocab/scope change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** the single source-of-truth constant `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING` (`brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`) drops `8.0` → `5.0`; BOTH production injection sites already read the CONSTANT (no literal touched) — the dashboard `_build_live_controller` (`pull_controller.py:861`) + the CLI `cmd_fetch` live pull (`cli.py:2120`) — so the new ceiling propagates with no wiring change. All surrounding prose is reconciled to the new value AND rationale: `constants.py` docstring (5×60 = 300/min < the 500/min governor; the 8→5 supersession), `cli.py` + `app.py` + `pull_controller._build_live_controller`/`SessionRateController` docstrings (all "8 r/s"→"5 r/s", "8×60=480"→"5×60=300"), `rate_common.py` STEP_UP recovery-window note (climb soft-floor-3 → ceiling-5 in ~2 clean windows / ~2 min, was ~5/~5 min), `ingest.py` empty-retry spacing (~200 ms at 5 r/s, was ~125 ms at 8), and the `GROWW_CLIENT_POOL_SIZE` Little's-Law comment (~0.75 concurrent calls reach 5 r/s at ~150 ms latency, so pool=2 stays sufficient). Genuinely-historical past-run measurement prose (the 3.4-r/s-while-8 meter note, 2.75-r/s expiries-run figures, "old serial loop ~3 r/s") is deliberately LEFT INTACT — rewriting a dated measurement would falsify it (Golden Rule #1). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10, §2 Rule 6):** ✅ a cap-LOWERING is intrinsically SAFE — the rate ceiling can only ever LOWER the issue rate (the §2 Rule-6 "never raise a ceiling without operator approval" invariant is satisfied; this is a lowering, and the operator directed it); ✅ the per-second backtesting cap STAYS officially UNVERIFIED (`GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_UNVERIFIED`) — 5 is an OPERATOR decision fed as the controller's CEILING into the existing adaptive token-bucket MECHANISM, NOT a vendor-confirmed limit (no fabricated "verified 5 r/s" claim); ✅ the safety invariant `5×60 = 300 ≤ GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN (500)` is property-TESTED (not just the literal pinned), so the per-second ceiling stays the binding gate without fighting the per-minute governor; ✅ the AIMD ladder + governor + floors are PROVABLY unchanged (the `rate_common.py` diff is comment-only — `FLOOR_RPS=3.0`, `TIMEOUT_FLOOR_RPS=1.0`, `RATE_LIMIT_STORM_FLOOR_RPS=1.0`, `STEP_RPS=1.0`, `STEP_UP_WINDOW==STEP_DOWN_WINDOW==60.0` all unchanged at runtime), so a 429 burst still steps DOWN to the soft floor 3 and a sustained storm to 1, recovering UP to the new 5 ceiling; ✅ the pool-size constant `GROWW_CLIENT_POOL_SIZE=2` is unchanged (only its Little's-Law comment), and 2 ≥ 0.75 so the pool stays sufficient at the lower ceiling; ✅ a near-O(1) per-call config read — no new state, no new branch. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22 via the repo `.venv`): `constants.py` **100% line+branch** (49/4), `rate_common.py` **100%** (140/36), `pull_controller.py` **100%** (across its covering set), `cli.py` covering suites green; NEW/updated assertions pin `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING == 5.0`, `ceiling×60 == 300`, and the `≤ GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN` safety property; 191 rate/constants/pull-controller/cli-retry tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (255 files)/`pyright` (0 errors) clean; hostile-reviewer **SHIP** (0 BLOCKER/MAJOR; 2 cosmetic NITs — a stale "8 r/s" docstring in the generic `test_rate_common.py` AIMD-ladder test FOLDED to say "the INJECTED ceiling … deliberately decoupled from production", and a harmless `<`→`<=` invariant relaxation already over-determined by the sibling `== 300`, left as the correct safety boundary), workspace-health **HEALTHY**. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_constants.py`, `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_retry_storm.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-5-001. **Supersedes:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001 (the prior operator-directed 8 r/s ceiling). **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001 (the 500/min governor this stays under), DEC-GROWW-RATE-RECOVER-8-001 (the STEP_UP recovery window, mechanism unchanged), DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the AIMD token-bucket controller). **Part of:** the operator's "check whether the rate limiter is really working" audit + the "add Rate-ceiling tuning (8→5?) into the plan" directive.

907. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-RECONCILE-DIAG-001 — an OBSERVE-ONLY `/completeness` diagnostic that PINPOINTS why a specific stock (the operator's "M&M") reads empty on the scoreboard: a lake-symbol-key ↔ scored-symbol-key divergence, surfaced as ONE structured WARNING naming both sides via `repr()`** (2026-06-22, operator: "see still why M&M is still empty what is the issue … you need to thoroughly check this also"; AskUserQuestion: "Ship a diagnostic to pinpoint it"). **Why:** the `/completeness` scoreboard showed `M&M` empty/`none` despite bars on disk, and an earlier GUESSED fix (`.replace("&amp;","&")`) was REJECTED as an illusion (Golden Rule #1). A read-only reproduce-agent proved the engine join handles `&` correctly, so the operator chose a DIAGNOSTIC (surface the real cause) over a blind fix. ROOT MECHANISM (now made visible, not yet repaired): `_per_symbol_spot` drops any lake-coverage row whose `symbol` key is absent from the scored `categories` map (`category = categories.get(symbol); if category is None: continue`) — so a lake partition keyed on a near-identical form has DATA yet is INVISIBLE on the board, while the scored `M&M` reads `none`; either side alone is invisible, together they pinpoint the exact drift. HONEST (the hostile-review MINOR, folded): the EXACT divergent on-disk form is UNVERIFIED — the production pull keys BOTH the lake partition AND the scored map on the same stripped `instrument.symbol_name`, so a same-pull divergence should not occur; a real drift would be a legacy / foreign / regression partition or an encoding artefact. The forms `"M&M "` (trailing space) / `"NSE-M&M"` (exchange prefix) are ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT asserted — the diagnostic SURFACES whatever drift actually exists and the `repr()` names the true on-disk key in the live box. **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard observability; NO engine/lake/vocab/rate/scope change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3; the scoreboard payload is BYTE-UNCHANGED):** NEW pure `reconcile_symbol_coverage(*, lake_symbols, scored_symbols) → SymbolReconcileReport` in `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` — two `set` builds + two difference scans (O(symbols), O(1) membership), returning `stray_lake_symbols` (lake keys NOT scored — data present, unscored) + `unmatched_scored_symbols` (scored keys with NO lake row — they read `none`), each with the FULL count plus a sorted SAMPLE capped at `_RECONCILE_SAMPLE_CAP=10` (counts are the true totals; and the COMMON wiring point `log_symbol_reconcile_from_board(spot_rows, spot_categories)` deriving the lake set from the SAME annotated `spot_rows` the scoreboard scores — filtered to the single fetched `SPOT_DIMENSIONS` (a derived intraday-TF row is NOT a distinct lake symbol) **AND to the spot segments `SPOT_PROBE_SEGMENTS` (`INDEX`/`CASH`, the COMMON `brutex/data/partition.py` constant)**: an F&O contract partition is ALSO stored at `1minute` but is NEVER a scored spot underlying, so without the segment filter every backfilled F&O contract would be mis-counted as a stray and fire the WARNING on EVERY load, drowning the real signal (the hostile-review MAJOR, folded) — plus the scored set from `categories.keys()`. deliberately deferred so the fix is grounded in the live `repr()` evidence, not a guess); ✅ SILENT in the healthy state AND on a pure F&O backfill (the segment filter — no false-alarm spam); ✅ the sample cap truncates only the inlined lists, never the counts; ✅ near-O(symbols), runs once per `/completeness` load with O(1) lookups, internally guarded so it adds NO new failure surface. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-22 via the repo `.venv`): `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` at **100% line+branch** (257/86, 0 missing);
