909. **DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001 — the Groww adapter now AUTO-RE-MINTS the access token on an auth-expiry mid-pull (thread-safe, single-flight, bounded), so the daily 06:00 IST token reset is a self-healing non-event instead of killing an overnight pull** (2026-06-23, operator: "how this can be auto created and rotated like a human … especially at night if I sleep … why is it struggling" + uploaded `brutex.log`). **Why (PROVEN from production logs, not hypothesised):** Groww's daily access token resets at **06:00 IST** (the operator's dashboard note "All API keys reset daily at 6 AM"; now VERIFIED — supersedes the §6 "token lifetime UNVERIFIED" Phase-0 gate). The operator's TOTP credential is CORRECT (the uploaded logs show **130,069 successful `groww.call`s** all day), but BruteX minted the access token **ONCE** at pull start (`build_live_client`/`build_live_pool`) and **never re-minted** it; so at `2026-06-23T00:30:00Z` (= 06:00 IST, to the second) the in-flight token went invalid and **every** subsequent call failed `GrowwAPIAuthenticationException: token expired or invalid` — **3,764 quarantines, 0 successes after 06:00**, the overnight pull dead until a manual restart (the exact §11 AUTOMATED "zero clicks/day" violation the operator feared). The codebase ALREADY documented the intended fix (`errors.py` `GrowwAuthError` docstring "triggers re-auth, not blind retry"; `ingest.py:36` "the Groww adapter provides no such [mid-pull re-auth] latch … can be added if/when"). **What shipped (adapter-only; NO engine/lake/vocab/scope/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py` `SdkRefresher` — a thread-safe, SINGLE-FLIGHT, pool-aware SDK refresher: it mints the INITIAL token + `size` independent SDK connections at construction (the ONE mint path), exposes lock-guarded `current_sdk()`/`sdk_at(index)`/`current_generation()`, and `reauth(seen_generation) → int` which under one `threading.Lock` re-mints (via the SAME injected `totp_minter`/`token_factory`/`sdk_factory`) ONLY if `generation == seen_generation` (else returns the current generation with NO re-mint — so an N-thread 06:00 stampede triggers EXACTLY ONE re-mint, adversarially verified at 32 threads → 1 mint), rebuilding all `size` SDKs and bumping `generation`. `client.py` `GrowwClient` gains `refresher`/`refresher_index`/`max_reauths` (default 1): `_call` resolves the live SDK via `refresher.sdk_at(refresher_index)` (else `self.sdk`, byte-identical when `None`), and on a `GrowwAuthError` with a refresher wired + the bounded `reauths < max_reauths` budget, captures the generation BEFORE the re-mint (single-flight), calls `reauth`, and retries against the REFRESHED SDK on a SEPARATE counter (`attempt -= 1`, so a token expiry mid-retry-storm self-heals without spending the rate-limit budget; the TOTAL worst-case is hard-bounded by `max_attempts + max_reauths`). `live.py` `build_live_client`/`build_live_pool` build ONE shared `SdkRefresher` and wire it into the client(s) — all pool leaves share the ONE refresher (pool-aware so one re-mint at 06:00 updates every leaf while preserving the K-way pool concurrency of DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ SINGLE-FLIGHT (generation read+compare+mint+bump fully inside the lock — TOCTOU closed; 32-thread probe → exactly 1 mint); ✅ BOUNDED — a genuinely-invalid credential re-mints `max_reauths` times then raises terminally (quarantine), never an infinite loop (hard cap `max_attempts + max_reauths`, adversarial interleave probe terminates finitely); ✅ back-compat BYTE-IDENTICAL with `refresher=None` (rate-limit/timeout/success/terminal-non-auth paths unchanged); ✅ secret hygiene preserved (re-mint rides `get_access_token`'s redacting `safe_message`; tests assert the secret never reaches `str(exc)`); ✅ the retry hits the FRESH SDK (re-resolved via `sdk_at` on the `continue`), proven by a stale-vs-fresh + a leaf-index test. **KNOWN fast-follow (hostile-review MINOR-1, recorded honestly, NOT a regression):** the re-mint itself is NOT yet wrapped in the `run_with_deadline` freeze-guard (DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001), so a half-open socket DURING the 06:00 re-mint could block the lock-holder + freeze the pool — the SAME unbounded property the original one-time mint always had (risk envelope unchanged), deferred to its own PR because the clean fix moves the deadline helper to avoid an import cycle. **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `reauth.py` **100% line+branch** (40/2), `client.py` **100%** (108/14), `live.py` **100%** (18/0); NEW tests — 8 in `test_groww_reauth.py` (initial mint, reauth bumps generation + returns fresh SDK, single-flight no-op on stale generation, mint-failure → redacting GrowwAuthError), 7 in `test_groww_client.py` (auth→reauth→success uses the fresh SDK, bounded-then-terminal, no-refresher back-compat, default max_reauths=1, `with_pace` carries the refresher, leaf-index resolution), 2 in `test_groww_live.py` (single client wires a refresher; pool leaves share ONE refresher with distinct indices); 498 groww-adapter + 7239 unit + 465 integration + 261 property tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (256 files)/`pyright` (0 errors) clean; hostile-reviewer **SHIP** (0 BLOCKER/MAJOR; MINOR-1 deferred as above + NIT-2 comment folded), workspace-health **HEALTHY**. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_reauth.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_client.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_live.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001. **Builds on:** the TOTP auth flow (`auth.py` `get_access_token`, DEC-DHAN-GROWW-REMIGRATE-001), DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001 (the K-way pool this stays compatible with), DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001 (the freeze-guard the MINOR-1 fast-follow will extend to the re-mint). **Part of:** the operator's "auto-create/rotate the token like a human, especially overnight" requirement — the §11 AUTOMATED "zero clicks per day" closure for the daily token reset.

910. **DEC-GROWW-REAUTH-DEADLINE-001 — the token re-mint is now WRAPPED in the freeze-guard wall-clock deadline, so even a HUNG re-mint at 06:00 IST raises a retryable timeout (the window quarantines + re-pulls) instead of freezing the whole pool — the MINOR-1 fast-follow flagged in #909** (2026-06-23, the operator's "cover all worst cases / exceptions with guarantee and assurance" mandate + the #909 hostile-review MINOR-1). **Why:** DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001 #909 auto-re-mints the access token UNDER `SdkRefresher._lock`; the re-mint network calls (`token_factory`=`GrowwAPI.get_access_token` + `sdk_factory`=`GrowwAPI(token)`) carried NO wall-clock bound, so a half-open socket DURING the 06:00 re-mint would block the lock-holder FOREVER → every pool leaf then blocks on `sdk_at()`/`current_sdk()` → the whole pool FREEZES. This is the SAME unbounded-call hazard `run_with_deadline` (DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001) already guards for ordinary historical calls — the re-mint just sat outside it (the explicit #909 fast-follow). **What shipped (adapter-only; NO engine/lake/vocab/scope/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `run_with_deadline` is MOVED from `client.py` to a NEW stdlib-only `brutex/adapters/groww/deadline.py` (imports only `threading`/`collections.abc` — NOTHING from the package, so it can NEVER be in an import cycle; `client.py` imports it from there + RE-EXPORTS it via `__all__` so `client.run_with_deadline` stays the same object for back-compat; the candle `_call` site is byte-unchanged); made a PEP 695 generic `run_with_deadline[T]` (ruff `UP047`) so the ONE helper bounds both the candle `Mapping` call AND the re-mint SDK tuple. The cycle-proof placement specifically avoids re-introducing the `client ↔ reauth` cycle CodeQL flagged on #909. (2) `SdkRefresher` gains an injectable `call_timeout_seconds` (default `GROWW_PULL_CALL_TIMEOUT_S` = 45.0; short value in tests); inside `reauth`, after the single-flight generation check and STILL under `_lock`, the network mint is `new_sdks = run_with_deadline(self._mint_sdks, self._call_timeout_seconds)` — `_mint_sdks` only READS construction fields + RETURNS the new SDK tuple (writes NO shared state), and the publish (`self._sdks = new_sdks; self._generation += 1`) runs ONLY after a clean return. On a deadline blow, `run_with_deadline` raises `TimeoutError` → mapped (via `from_groww_exception`, the `"deadline exceeded"` hint) to a RETRYABLE `GrowwTimeoutError` that propagates out of the `with self._lock` block (lock RELEASED, no half-state published, the abandoned daemon's result discarded). (3) the client `_call` reauth branch is UNCHANGED — a `GrowwTimeoutError` from `reauth` propagates as a normal retryable error out to the ingest quarantine + re-pull (no infinite retry); the successful-re-mint `groww.token.reauth` observability log still fires. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ NO abandoned-daemon DATA RACE — `_mint_sdks` never writes `self._sdks`/`self._generation` (adversarially PROVEN: a timed-out mint's released daemon built a 2nd SDK yet generation stayed 0 + the old SDK was still served); ✅ NO half-state on timeout — the publish is atomic-after-clean-return; ✅ BOUNDED, no freeze — an 8-thread forever-hanging-mint probe returned all 8 `GrowwTimeoutError` in ~0.81 s (N×deadline), the lock held AT MOST one deadline per contender then released; ✅ single-flight intact (generation check still first inside the lock; a successful publish still short-circuits later contenders); ✅ back-compat BYTE-IDENTICAL (`refresher=None`, the candle path, the `client.run_with_deadline` re-export identity); ✅ retryable-timeout classification carries NO secret/token (`"deadline exceeded (45s)"` only). Only the under-lock RE-MINT is bounded (the construction-time INITIAL mint surfaces to the `build_live_*` caller before any leaf is blocked, so it is intentionally out of scope). **NOTED follow-up (hostile-review NIT, recorded not folded — keeps this PR off the shared `errors.py`):** the `TimeoutError`→retryable mapping depends on the literal `"deadline exceeded"` substring shared between `deadline.py` and `errors.py` `_TIMEOUT_HINTS`; correct + tested today, but a future reword of the message would silently make a re-mint timeout fall through to a terminal `GrowwError` — hardening it to a shared constant (or a by-TYPE `TimeoutError` classification) is a future option, NOT required here. **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `deadline.py` **100% line+branch** (20/4), `reauth.py` **100%** (48/2), `client.py` **100%** (89/10), `live.py` **100%** (18/0); NEW tests — `test_groww_deadline.py` (success, inner-exception re-raise, the TIMEOUT path blocking on a `threading.Event` past a 0.05 s deadline, generic-return preservation), `test_groww_reauth.py` (hung re-mint → retryable `GrowwTimeoutError` + lock-released probe + NO half-state + secret-not-leaked + fast re-mint still bumps generation), `test_groww_client.py` (auth-error whose re-mint times out → retryable out of `_call`, not a freeze, not terminal); 506 groww-adapter + 7247 unit + 465 integration + 261 property tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (258 files)/`pyright brutex tests` (0 errors, whole-repo) clean; hostile-reviewer **SHIP** (0 BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR; 1 NIT noted above), workspace-health **HEALTHY**. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/deadline.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_deadline.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_reauth.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_client.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-REAUTH-DEADLINE-001. **Supersedes/closes:** the MINOR-1 fast-follow flagged in DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001 #909. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001 (the `run_with_deadline` freeze-guard this reuses + relocates), DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001 #909 (the re-mint this bounds), DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001 (the K-way pool preserved). **Part of:** the operator's "cover all worst cases / exceptions with guarantee and assurance" mandate — the last edge of the overnight-token self-heal.

911. **DEC-COMPLETENESS-SPOT-KEY-RECOVER-001 — the read-side FIX of #907's diagnostic: a lake spot partition whose on-disk directory key DRIFTED from the scored `symbol_name` (e.g. a legacy `"NSE-M&M"` or `"M&M "` instead of the bare `"M&M"`) is now RECOVERED to its canonical scored symbol on BOTH the `/completeness` scoreboard and the `/universe` per-row strip, so its REAL on-disk data is surfaced instead of silently dropped** (2026-06-23, operator: "M&M empty-symbol fix" — the AskUserQuestion next-step pick + the recurring "cover all worst cases" mandate). **Why (evidence-grounded, NOT a guess):** a read-only Explore trace proved the production WRITE path keys both sides IDENTICALLY — the pull writes the lake partition directory from the stripped `instrument.symbol_name` (`adapters/groww/ingest.py:648` → `instruments.py:193` `trading_symbol.strip()`) and the scoreboard keys `categories` on the SAME `inst.symbol_name` (`completeness.py` `categorize_instruments`), so a same-pull `"M&M"` matches `"M&M"` and shows correctly (the operator's REAL M&M-empty was the OPTIONS chain that never pulled because the overnight pull died at 06:00 IST — fixed by #909/#910, NOT a key bug). A key drift can therefore arise ONLY from a LEGACY / foreign / regression partition; the two documented drift classes (DEC-COMPLETENESS-RECONCILE-DIAG-001 #907's `repr()` illustrations + the committed `test_reconcile_diagnostic_pinpoints_mnm_lake_key_divergence`) are a surrounding-whitespace form (`"M&M "`) or an exchange-PREFIXED groww_symbol form (`"NSE-M&M"`). The READ side (`db_view` `sym_dir.name`) read the raw directory name and `_per_symbol_spot` / `per_symbol_completeness` did a direct `categories.get(symbol)` — a miss → the partition's real data became INVISIBLE (the silent-drop fragility the #907 diagnostic only OBSERVED). **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard; NO engine/lake/vocab/rate/scope change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** ONE COMMON helper `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py::_resolve_spot_category(symbol, exchange, categories) → (canonical_key, category) | None` that resolves a lake symbol in order — (1) EXACT match (the clean steady state — returns on the first lookup, byte-identical to the prior direct `.get` for every healthy symbol), (2) whitespace-stripped, (3) the row's OWN `exchange` prefix stripped (DATA-DRIVEN off `f"{exchange}-"` via `str.removeprefix`, never a hardcoded exchange list, so a legitimately hyphenated symbol like `BAJAJ-AUTO` is NEVER split on its internal hyphen — only a true `"<exch>-"` lead is removed) — returning the CANONICAL scored key (so the row groups + displays under the clean symbol) or `None` (a genuinely unscored stray STAYS dropped — never fabricated onto the board). Wired into BOTH read-side spot lookups (`_per_symbol_spot` for `/completeness`, `per_symbol_completeness` for `/universe`) — the COMMON one-source-of-truth, no copy. The #907 reconcile diagnostic STILL fires its `completeness.symbol_reconcile_mismatch` WARNING on the raw drifted key (so the operator both SEES the recovered data AND is told to clean up the stored key). **FOLDED hostile-review BLOCKER (order-dependent clobber):** once a drifted key recovers to its canonical symbol, a CLEAN partition (`"M&M"`, real `full`/2020) and a STALE legacy fragment (`"NSE-M&M"`, no ledger → `none`) can BOTH land on the same `(symbol, interval)`; the lake scan is SORTED so `"M&M"` is processed BEFORE `"NSE-M&M"`, and a blind last-write let the stale `none` fragment CLOBBER the real `full` (a Golden-Rule-#1 honesty regression — strictly WORSE than the pre-fix drop). FIX: a COMMON `_spot_cell_supersedes(new_status, new_start, cur_status, cur_start)` rank-merge — verdicts ranked `full > partial > failed > none`, ties broken by the EARLIER start (wider real coverage; ISO dates sort chronologically, a `None` start ranks worst) — applied at BOTH merge sites so the surfaced cell is the BEST real data that exists, ORDER-INDEPENDENT (regression-proven both scan orders × both read paths). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ RECOVERS only data that PHYSICALLY EXISTS on disk — the helper returns a category ONLY for a partition row that is actually present; an unscored stray returns `None` and is dropped, never invented; ✅ does NOT change the operator's CURRENT bare-`"M&M"` (which already matched + showed) — this is DEFENSIVE hardening for the legacy/foreign drift class, NOT a claim it was their cure (their cure is the #909/#910 token self-heal); ✅ NO over-strip (the prefix branch keys on the row's exact `"<exchange>-"`, proven by the `BAJAJ-AUTO` / `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO` tests); ✅ OPTIONS path intentionally OUT OF SCOPE — option coverage keys on the structured `CoverageRecord.underlying_symbol` (registry-sourced), NOT a filesystem dir name, so the dir-drift class does not apply there; ✅ the spot completeness VERDICT stays ledger-driven (a recovered partition with no planned window still reads `none` — the fix surfaces the partition, not a fabricated verdict; the DIM_FULL recovery path is proven by a unit test with a settled window). **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` at **100% line+branch** (293/108, 0 missing); NEW unit tests — exact-match byte-identity, whitespace recovery, exchange-prefix recovery, hyphenated-symbol no-overstrip (`BAJAJ-AUTO` + `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO`), unscored-stray → `None`, blank-exchange skips the prefix branch, whitespace-stripped-still-unscored fall-through, an end-to-end `per_symbol_completeness` recovery grouping under the canonical key with the real DIM_FULL verdict, the `_spot_cell_supersedes` rank/tie-break branch matrix, and the **dual-partition collision regression** (clean-FULL `M&M` + drifted-`none` `NSE-M&M` keeps `full`/2020 in BOTH scan orders × BOTH read paths — the folded BLOCKER); 912. **DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ZERO-SKIP-001 — a vendor candle carrying a ZERO price among real prices (e.g. `open: 0` with a real high/low/close) is now gracefully SKIPPED instead of silently STORED as a corrupted bar (a fabricated zero price + a zero low/high clamp) — the symmetric twin of the partial-ABSENT skip (DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ABSENT-SKIP-001)** (2026-06-23, the operator's "cover all worst cases / exceptions / bugs comprehensively, no illusion" correctness-hunt mandate). **Why (PROVEN, not hypothesised):** `brutex/data/candle_fields.py` `assemble_candle` had an ASYMMETRY between its two no-price guards — the all-empty guard uses `has_no_price` (absent OR zero), but the partial guard used `is_absent` (absent ONLY). The module's OWN `has_no_price` docstring states a traded Indian price is NEVER 0 (tick ≥ 0.05), so a zero OHLC value is junk; yet a bar with a MIX of zero and real prices fell through BOTH guards (not all-no-price → not all-empty; a literal 0 is not `is_absent` → not partial-absent) and was stored. A direct repro confirmed it: `assemble_candle(open_=0, high=100, low=50, close=75)` STORED `open=0, low=0` — the high/low clamp (`low=min(prices)`) pulled the low down to the junk zero, FABRICATING both a zero price and a zero range (the exact Golden-Rule-#1 corruption the all-empty guard already prevents). The partial-ABSENT twin (`open=None`) was correctly skipped — only the ZERO case leaked. **What shipped (one-line predicate fix; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** the partial guard now uses the SAME `has_no_price` predicate as the all-empty guard — `if any(has_no_price(v) for v in (open_, high, low, close))` — so a partial-zero bar (absent OR zero) is a graceful `EmptyCandleRow` skip (the parser's `except EmptyCandleRow: continue`), symmetric with the all-empty guard, never crashing the pull and never storing junk. The message broadens to "candle has an absent or zero OHLC price (partial vendor bar — skipped)" (keeps the "partial vendor bar" substring contract). A PRESENT-but-unparseable price (e.g. `"abc"` — `has_no_price` is False) STILL hard-errors via the strict `to_price` (a genuine malformation worth surfacing, never silently skipped). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ a NARROW symmetry fix — only a zero-among-reals bar changes behavior (now skipped, was corrupted-stored); an all-zero bar is still caught by the all-empty guard FIRST (distinct "no-trade" message preserved); a partial-absent bar is unchanged; a real malformation still hard-errors; ✅ never fabricates a bar — it can only DROP an un-storable one (the data that doesn't exist), the same philosophy as the partial-absent + negative-volume + OHLC clamps; ✅ a genuine zero price cannot exist for a traded Indian instrument (tick ≥ 0.05, the module's own rule), so no legitimate bar is lost. **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/data/candle_fields.py` at **100% line+branch** (47/12, 0 missing); NEW tests — `test_partial_zero_price_is_skipped` (parametrized over `{0, 0.0, "0", "0.0", "0.00"}` × `{open,high,low,close}`) + `test_partial_zero_open_does_not_clobber_low_to_zero` (the proven corruption regression); the parser/ingest/price-precision-property consumers (67) + the candle-fields suite (78) GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (258 files)/`pyright brutex tests` (0 errors, whole-repo) clean. **Files:** `brutex/data/candle_fields.py`, `tests/unit/test_candle_fields.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ZERO-SKIP-001. **Builds on:** DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ABSENT-SKIP-001 (the absent twin this completes), DEC-CANDLE-EMPTY-BAR-001 (the all-empty guard whose `has_no_price` predicate this aligns to), DEC-OHLC-VENDOR-NORMALIZE-001 + DEC-VENDOR-VOLUME-NORMALIZE-001 (the same never-crash-never-fabricate philosophy). **Part of:** the operator's "cover all worst cases / no illusion" correctness-hunt — a real, proven, silent data-corruption gap closed.

913. **DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001 — the per-minute rate governor now RESERVES its issue slot ATOMICALLY (under the same lock that observes a free slot) instead of appending the issue instant AFTER `bucket.acquire()`, closing a latent concurrent-overshoot of the HARD 500/min cap; the "no overshoot" docstring claim is now actually TRUE for the multi-threaded path** (2026-06-23, the operator's "cover all worst cases / exceptions comprehensively, no illusion, parallelise everything" correctness-hunt mandate; found by the parallel concurrency-audit agent). **Why (provable by code-path trace):** `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` `RateController.pace()` ran the per-minute governor (DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001) as TWO separate critical sections — gate-1 checked `len(self._issues) < cap` and BROKE (releasing `self._lock`), then `bucket.acquire()` ran (a blocking sleep, no lock), then the issue instant was appended in a SEPARATE `with self._lock` AFTER the bucket. With NO reservation taken at admission, N concurrent pool workers (`PoolRunParallel`) could ALL acquire the lock in turn, each see the SAME single free slot (`len = cap-1 < cap`), each break, and each later append → `len` becomes `(cap-1) + N`, overshooting the HARD cap by `N-1`. The docstring asserted "N woken workers re-evict + re-test under the lock so only the freed slots pass — no overshoot" and "the deque … can never exceed the cap" — both FALSE under concurrency (the re-test and the append were not atomic). HONEST SEVERITY: this is currently **DORMANT** — at the production `ceiling_rps ≤ 5` the per-second bucket already caps throughput at `5×60 = 300/min < 500/min`, so the governor's wait path is never the binding gate and the overshoot never triggers; it becomes a real cap breach only if `ceiling_per_min < ceiling_rps × 60` (raising the per-second ceiling or lowering the per-minute cap). It is fixed now for robustness + honesty (a false "no overshoot" claim is a Golden-Rule-#10 issue), per "cover all worst cases". **What shipped (adapter-only; NO engine/lake/vocab/scope/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** in gate-1, when `_governor_wait_locked(now)` returns `≤ 0` (a free slot), the issue instant is RESERVED — `self._issues.append(now)` — in the SAME `with self._lock` acquisition that saw room, making the `(check, reserve)` indivisible; the separate post-`bucket.acquire()` append is REMOVED. The fail-OPEN path (after `_GOVERNOR_LOOP_CAP` spins) still records the instant (matches the pre-fix fail-open, which also appended), keeping the rolling count honest. The instant is now stamped at ADMISSION — a few ms before the per-second bucket clears — which for a HARD cap is CONSERVATIVE (never under-counts). The snapshot `recent_minute` gauge now counts in-flight (admitted) issues, strictly MORE accurate. The two gates still SEQUENCE (never nest) and the lock is still RELEASED before every sleep (the ~1 r/s collapse of DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 stays avoided). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the overshoot is now IMPOSSIBLE — the check+reserve is atomic, so the deque can never exceed `cap` at any reservation instant (proven by a NEW real-threads regression: 16 workers released together by a `Barrier`, contending for a `cap=4` window, a `_RecordingDeque` capturing the post-append length under the lock — `max_seen ≤ cap`, 5×-stable); ✅ single-threaded behavior is byte-equivalent in COUNT (1 reservation per `pace()`, same as before) — only the timestamp shifts from post-bucket to admission (the existing `test_blocks_at_cap_then_frees` updated 59.8 → 59.6 to reflect the earlier stamp; cap-held/no-overshoot assertion unchanged); ✅ fail-open semantics preserved; ✅ no new lock, no lock-ordering cycle, O(1) per pace; ✅ DORMANT in production today (stated plainly — not oversold as a live bug). **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` at **100% line+branch** (141/34, 0 missing); NEW `test_concurrent_admission_never_overshoots_cap` (16-thread barrier, recording-deque, `max_seen ≤ cap`) + the updated `test_blocks_at_cap_then_frees`; 52 rate_common tests GREEN (concurrent test 5×-stable, non-flaky); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (258 files)/`pyright brutex tests` (0 errors, whole-repo) clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001 (the 500/min governor this hardens), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the release-lock-before-sleep discipline preserved), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-5-001 (the 5 r/s ceiling that keeps this dormant today). **Part of:** the operator's "cover all worst cases / no illusion / parallelise" correctness-hunt — a real, proven (if dormant) concurrency defect + a false docstring claim, both closed.

914. **DEC-STAGE2-PARALLEL-DESIGN-001 — the Stage-2 brute-force sweep parallelism architecture is DESIGN-LOCKED (hostile-reviewed) and RECORDED as ADR-0011, with the BUILD explicitly DEFERRED — this entry authorizes NO engine code** (2026-06-23, the operator's "continue with the plan" + the standing "design extensively before any implementation" decree, Golden Rule #9). **Why:** production Stage-2 (`run_supervised_grid` → `run_sweep_grid` → per-tuple `run_persisted_sweep`) is STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL; the CLAUDE.md §8 SLA (~33 B trials in 2–4 days on a 10P-core M4 Pro) is only reachable with multi-core parallelism (serial ≈ 80–160 h), but parallelizing the engine risks its three hard invariants — determinism/reproducibility (Golden Rule #7), the hash-chained audit (Golden Rule #8), and O(1) dedup (Golden Rule #5). Per the plan-first decree, the architecture was designed + adversarially reviewed BEFORE any code. **What was decided (DESIGN ONLY, no implementation):** process-level parallelism (the hot `trade_sim` is GIL-bound pure Python, so threads give ~1.0–1.5×; processes are required), using `multiprocessing` **`spawn`** (the `fastbloom_rs`/`fno_math` PyO3 wheels are init-once-per-interpreter and the parent pre-initializes them, so `fork` would abort), **sharded by `(instrument, tf, proximity)`** to preserve per-worker kernel-cache reuse; per-worker audit BUFFERS merged by the parent in canonical order across BOTH chains (SHA256 ingest + BLAKE3 supervisor); the contiguous-prefix `SweepCheckpointStore` (incompatible with out-of-order completion) REPLACED by sentinel-set resume; no new dedup wiring (mask dedup is per-worker — run_ids embed tuple coords; the only on-path LMDB `SweepCache` is already cross-process safe + write-rare); progress/watchdog re-homed to the parent. **The linchpin (CONFIRMED by review):** per-combo results are ORDER-INDEPENDENT — `ResultsStore.flush()` sorts rows by `run_id` (byte-identical Parquet + content-hash regardless of append order), `rank_combos` is deterministic per tuple, trial-stats use `math.fsum`, and no cross-tuple order-sensitive merge exists — so parallel evaluation cannot change the result files; the result content-hash is the determinism oracle. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ this entry + ADR-0011 record an APPROVED PLAN — ZERO engine code is written or authorized here (the operator chose "approve but hold code"); ✅ a hostile review returned GO-WITH-CHANGES and caught two would-be-shipped defects now corrected in the design — the "byte-identical merged audit chain" claim is FALSE (`ts_utc` is hashed into every entry, so no chain is byte-stable even serial; the honest oracle is the result content-hash, audit equality asserted with `ts_utc` projected out) and the pool MUST be `spawn` not `fork`; ✅ NO Nx speedup is claimed (unbenched); memory is ~linear in workers; a Rust trade-sim with GIL release (thread-parallel + lower memory) is explicitly DEFERRED; ✅ the brute-force ENGINE scope is UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3) — this is sweep-execution plumbing, not a scope/vocab/rate change. **Build sequence (each a future, separately-gated PR; the process pool gated on explicit operator approval):** (1) audit buffer→merge on the SERIAL loop (both chains, zero concurrency — de-risks the hardest piece); (2) sentinel-set resume (serial, no behavior change); (3) `spawn` process pool sharded by `(instrument,tf,proximity)` + the serial-vs-parallel determinism golden; (4) `SweepCache` N-writer regression test; (5) `tests/bench` throughput + memory vs workers (kernel-reuse-loss + per-worker bar-load as explicit dimensions). **REAL (verified 2026-06-23):** grounded in a read-only Stage-2 execution + concurrency-hazard reconnaissance (file:line evidence for every claim) and an adversarial design review (GO-WITH-CHANGES; 3 BLOCKERs folded — audit `ts_utc`, `spawn`-not-`fork`, the supervisor-layer shared state); engine end-to-end runnability independently re-verified (the 16-tuple orchestrator integration test + 86 determinism/ranking golden tests green; a 5,408-combo `sweep-all` exercised on a synthetic `--dry-run` lake). DOCS-ONLY change — no `brutex/` package code touched, so coverage/type/lint gates are unaffected. **Files:** `docs/adr/0011-stage2-sweep-parallelism-design.md` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-STAGE2-PARALLEL-DESIGN-001. **Builds on:** the W2-c "parallel tuples" follow-up noted in `sweep_orchestrator.py`; ADR-0004 (GPU — engine intentionally CPU/Rust-first), ADR-0006/0007/0008 (Stage 2.5/3/4 design locks); DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the thread-safe dedup + release-lock-before-sleep discipline reused). **Part of:** the post-pull mission step — the engine is built + verified; this records the one remaining engine-scaling design so it is ready to build when the operator scales past a pilot.

915. **DEC-MOVERS-TAB-INTEGRITY-001 — the `/movers` page now keeps each tab to its OWN instrument class (Spot = INDEX/CASH only — no futures/options leak) AND computes the futures/options `%`-change + `OI%` even on a lake with NO derived `1day` partition (so Price-Gainers/Losers + OI-Gainers/Losers stop coming up EMPTY)** (2026-06-23, the operator's screenshots: futures contracts (`NSE-NIFTY-30Jun26-FUT` …) polluting the SPOT tab + the Futures Price-Gainers/Losers reading "no movers" despite a fully-pulled futures lake; the "spot is only for spot, futures only for futures, options only for options" + "cover all worst cases" mandate). **Why (PROVEN, file:line, not guessed — two read-path bugs the pull log could never show):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py::compute_spot_candidates` discovered datasets via `list_candle_datasets` filtered ONLY by interval + exchange, with NO segment filter — so every `segment="FNO"` contract partition (futures + options) leaked into the SPOT screen (visible on the 1-minute view; latent on 1-day only because F&O had no derived 1-day). (2) the futures/options `%`-change (`_prev_day_close`) + `OI%` (`_prev_day_oi`) read the contract's prior-day `…/1day` partition; the F&O 1-day derive is recent (PR #808), dashboard-only, and quarantined, so a lake whose F&O was pulled earlier has 1-minute but NO 1-day → both return `None` → `pct_change`/`oi_chg_pct` `None` for EVERY future → `rank_price_gainers/losers/oi_gainers/oi_losers` pools filter to empty, while Volume/Value/Premium (read from 1-minute) still populate — exactly the operator's symptom (the leaked FUT rows even showed `—` for change). **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) **strict tab separation** — `compute_spot_candidates` now whitelists `d["segment"] in SPOT_PROBE_SEGMENTS` (the COMMON `("INDEX","CASH")` from `brutex/data/partition.py`, already used by `movers_futures`), so FNO can NEVER reach Spot; Futures stays `FNO`+`-FUT`, Options stays `FNO`+CE/PE. (2) **prior-day baseline from 1-minute (ONE COMMON helper)** — NEW `movers_snapshot._prior_session_last_from_minute` recovers the most recent prior trading day's last 1-minute `(close, open_interest)` via a BOUNDED back-walk (≤ `_PREV_SESSION_MAX_BACK_DAYS`=14 calendar days — covers the longest NSE holiday cluster, then honest `None`; touches at most the day's + prior month's 1-minute parquet, never an open `rglob`). `_prev_day_close` (spot) keeps the `1day` read as PRIMARY (spot %-change byte-UNCHANGED where 1day exists) and falls back to the helper's close only when 1day is absent/has-no-prior; futures `_prev_day_oi` keeps 1day OI primary + falls back to the helper's OI; Options inherits both (it imports the two helpers). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the derived-1day close IS the session's last 1-minute close, 2dp-snapped by the SAME writer (hostile-review-verified), so the recovered baseline is BYTE-EQUAL to the 1-day value it substitutes — no spot %-change drift; ✅ the bounded fallback confines the partial-session-restate hazard to the fallback path (1day stays primary); ✅ recovers only data that EXISTS — `None` past the bound / no 1-minute (the first day) → honest `None` %, never fabricated; ✅ READ-ONLY — no write/derive/ingest change (a NON-quarantined F&O 1-day derive is a separate future option, NOT claimed here). **SCOPED follow-ups (NOT in this PR, recorded honestly):** the Futures Near/Next/Far selector is still a no-op (always near-month — `compute_futures_candidates` ignores the tier; fixing it needs an `expiry_tier` added to the futures `candidate_key` or it'd serve stale Near rows — a flagged next PR) + the `/movers` per-tab/section O(1) latency (the discovery `list_candle_datasets` walk is not yet memoised behind the write-generation like `/db` #896 — the next PR). **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py` + `movers_futures.py` + `movers_options.py` ALL at **100% line+branch** (234/54 + 227/50 + 200/40, 0 missing) over the unit + integration suites; NEW `tests/unit/test_movers_tab_integrity.py` (14 tests — the bounded back-walk found/skip-empty/no-dir/past-bound/null-OI/same-day-only branches, `_prev_day_close` 1day-primary vs 1m-fallback vs neither, futures `_prev_day_oi` 1m-fallback + 1day-precedence + the null-OI-with-1day fall-through, and the spot whitelist excluding an FNO future); 219 movers unit+integration tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` (258 files)/`pyright` (0 errors) clean; hostile-reviewer **SHIP** (the byte-equality + 100%-coverage-with-zero-suppressions + OI-fix-not-regression claims all VERIFIED TRUE; the null-OI-with-1day fall-through test + the session-exempt-symbol docstring scoping FOLDED; the no-1day double back-walk on a wide option chain deferred to the O(1)-latency follow-up, documented), workspace-health **HEALTHY** (7292 unit tests green). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_tab_integrity.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-TAB-INTEGRITY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 / DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-* (the tab readers fixed here), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853 (the derived-1day the fallback substitutes), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 #860 (the cache the O(1) follow-up will extend). **Part of:** the operator's "spot=spot / futures=futures / options=options + cover all worst cases" correctness mandate — the first (correctness) of the movers fixes; the Near/Next/Far + O(1)-latency PRs follow.

916. **DEC-MOVERS-DISCOVERY-MEMO-001 — the `/movers` page is now O(1) on every tab / section / exchange / expiry switch: the per-interaction full-lake `list_candle_datasets` walk is memoised ONCE per write-generation (the proven `/db` #896 pattern) and SHARED across spot/futures/options, instead of re-walking the whole `bars/` tree inside each compute on every cache miss** (2026-06-23, the operator's "irrespective of frontend/backend/db always ultra-fast extreme speed O(1) latency on every switch / cover all worst cases" mandate; the flagged O(1)-latency follow-up of DEC-MOVERS-TAB-INTEGRITY-001 #915). **Why (PROVEN, file:line):** the `MoversSnapshotCache` (DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 #860) already caches the candidate SET per `candidate_key` (asset/exchange/interval/date/time/expiry-tier), but on a cache MISS — which EVERY new coordinate is (a tab switch changes `asset`, an exchange/Near-Next-Far/interval change the key) — each of `compute_spot_candidates` / `_discover_futures` / `_discover_options` independently called `list_candle_datasets(lake_root)`, an O(files) `iterdir`+`rglob` walk of the ENTIRE `bars/` tree (~750 underlyings × intervals + thousands of FUT/CE/PE contract dirs). So a spot→futures→options sweep, or an All↔NSE↔BSE / Near↔Next↔Far flip, re-walked the whole lake each time — the operator's "slow on every section/tab change". The `/db` route already solved the identical triple-walk by memoising it behind the generation (#896); `/movers` did not. **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** ONE COMMON seam `movers_snapshot.resolve_candle_datasets(lake_root, datasets)` — returns a caller-supplied pre-discovered list as-is, else scans the lake (the same deterministic read-only dir-walk, Golden Rule #7); `compute_spot_candidates` / `compute_futures_candidates` (+`_discover_futures`) / `compute_options_candidates` (+`_discover_options`) gain an optional `datasets=` param threaded through it (default `None` = scan, BYTE-IDENTICAL back-compat for the post-pull warmer + direct callers). The `/api/v1/movers` route memoises the walk ONCE per request via `_db_datasets_cache.get_or_compute("movers_candle_datasets", generation=…, compute=list_candle_datasets)` — REUSING the SAME generation-stamped `MoversSnapshotCache` the `/db` discovery memo uses (distinct key, no clash) — and threads the cached list into whichever asset computes. A pull bumps the generation → exactly one fresh walk. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ O(1) on REPEAT within a generation (the tab/section/exchange/expiry switch reuses the one cached walk), NOT a literal O(1)-total — the FIRST `/movers` open after a pull still pays one real `bars/` walk (same honest framing as #896); ✅ the per-coordinate candidate SET is still computed on its first view (the per-instrument bar reads are the inherent cost, bounded + cached by `MoversSnapshotCache` #860) — this PR removes only the REDUNDANT discovery walk, not the data read; ✅ correctness byte-unchanged (same datasets, same payloads — the walk-once is invisible to output); ✅ deferred follow-up UNCHANGED: the Futures Near/Next/Far wiring (still a no-op, flagged in #915) is a separate PR. **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `movers_snapshot.py` + `movers_futures.py` + `movers_options.py` ALL at **100% line+branch** (238/56 + 226/50 + 199/40, 0 missing) over the unit + integration suites; NEW `tests/integration/test_movers_discovery_memo.py` (6 tests — `resolve_candle_datasets` both branches, each compute USING an injected dataset list (NOT re-scanning the lake), and the end-to-end route proof that the lake is walked EXACTLY ONCE across a spot→futures→options tab sweep at one generation + exactly once more after a `mark_dirty`); ✅ a tier with no live contract at its rank is honestly SKIPPED (counted, never faked); ✅ default/blank/unknown ⇒ `near` (byte-equivalent to the prior near-month-only behaviour — the warmer + every un-tiered caller unchanged); 919. **DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 — an OBSERVE-ONLY pull-side diagnostic surfaces a whole F&O underlying whose every cleanly-fetched contract came back 100% EMPTY (the BAJAJ-AUTO / M&M "silent-vanish" failure mode), so it can never silently blend into a normal no-data gap again** (2026-06-23, the operator's "a whole stock should never silently vanish from the data"; the in-flight item the #918 scoreboard named under "Up next"). **Why (the gap):** when the historical F&O pull fetches an underlying and the vendor returns clean-but-empty `200`s for EVERY one of its contracts (e.g. the `&`-encoding / hyphen failure modes of #898/#845, or a genuinely absent chain), the underlying produced ZERO bars and currently looked IDENTICAL to a legit "no trades" gap — the pull log could not distinguish "tried hard and got nothing across the whole chain" from "this window simply had no trades". There was NO per-underlying tally of attempted-vs-stored anywhere (`ingest_common.classify_pull` models pull-wide verdicts, not per-underlying all-empty). **What shipped (PULL-side, OBSERVE-ONLY; NO engine/lake/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** in `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, mirroring the read-side #907 `symbol_reconcile_mismatch` observe-only triad — (1) a pure builder `scan_underlying_all_empty(pairs, contract_list)` that groups the `(contract, interval)` pairs by `DerivativeContract.underlying_symbol`, counts the CLEANLY-fetched pairs per underlying (`_is_clean_fetch`: `windows ≥ 1 AND skipped_windows == 0 AND still_failed_windows == 0` — a ledger-skip, a transient residual, and a `windows == 0` empty-clamp are all EXCLUDED, so a re-pull of already-settled contracts and a still-draining transient storm NEVER trip the flag), and flags an underlying iff `attempted_pairs ≥ _ALL_EMPTY_MIN_CONTRACTS (=3) AND stored_bars == 0`; (2) immutable `UnderlyingEmptyReport` / `AllEmptyScan` (with `has_suspicious()` — False ⇒ stay silent); (3) a guarded emit `_log_underlying_all_empty` firing ONE `pull.underlying_all_empty` WARNING per flagged underlying (capped at `_ALL_EMPTY_SAMPLE_CAP = 20`), naming the underlying via `repr()` + the attempted/stored counts; (4) ONE best-effort wiring line at the end of `run_groww_option_ingest` (before the return) wrapped in `try/except Exception` → a `pull.underlying_all_empty_error` WARNING, so the diagnostic can NEVER break the pull. PULL-side (not read-side) because only the pull knows "tried-and-empty" vs "never-tried" — a lake scan sees only "0 partitions" and re-creates the exact ambiguity this kills. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ pure DETECT + WARN — no return-value/ledger/engine change, no auto-recovery, no re-pull trigger (the operator decides); ✅ false-positive-guarded (≥3 clean fetches AND zero bars; skip/transient/empty-clamp excluded), so a thin 1-2-leg illiquid underlying or a re-pull never flags; ✅ a genuinely-empty chain WILL warn (the honest "observe + let the operator decide" signal — a WARNING for triage, not an action); ✅ best-effort — a scan failure logs an error event + the pull continues unaffected. **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` at **100% line+branch** (247/68, 0 missing); NEW `TestSuspiciousEmptyFlag` (14 tests — all-empty flags, partial/all-good/below-threshold/skip-only/transient-only/empty-clamp/unknown-symbol do NOT flag, multi-underlying isolates the empty one, emit logs-one-per-flagged / silent-when-clean / caps-at-20, the end-to-end `run_groww_option_ingest` flag-fires, and the scan-raises-is-guarded except branch); 75 option-ingest tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001. **Builds on:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-RECONCILE-DIAG-001 #907 (the read-side observe-only triad mirrored), DEC-COMPLETENESS-SPOT-KEY-RECOVER-001 #911, DEC-GROWW-AMPERSAND-FALLBACK-001 #898 + DEC-GROWW-HYPHEN-SYMBOL-RESOLVE-001 #845 (the `&`/hyphen empty-chain failure modes this flags). **Part of:** the operator's data-completeness assurance — the whole-underlying silent-vanish can no longer hide.

920. **DEC-SUMMARY-CACHE-ADAPTIVE-FLOOR-001 — the dashboard's `SummaryCache` TTL floor is now ADAPTIVE (`max(base 2 s, the last scan's own duration)`, capped at 120 s), so an expensive full-lake completeness/coverage scan self-throttles to a ≤50% duty cycle during a pull instead of re-firing back-to-back on every poll and starving the concurrent pull** (2026-06-23, the operator-approved item (b) of the "yes work on all a/b/c" batch — "the tiny completeness-cache fix so the dashboard stops freezing during pulls"). **Why (PROVEN from the operator's logs):** the `/completeness/scoreboard` + `/universe/completeness` + `/coverage/spot` routes share ONE generation-stamped `SPOT` `SummaryCache` entry (DEC-COMPLETENESS-O1-LATENCY-001 #895) whose recompute is the O(datasets) full-lake `summarize_spot_datasets` aggregate. During a pull EVERY window write `mark_dirty()`s it, and as the lake fills the scan grew from <1 s to a measured **28–32 s** — far beyond the fixed **2 s** TTL floor — so a poll every ~4 s re-triggered the 30 s scan essentially CONTINUOUSLY, pinning a core in the SAME process as the pull's daemon-thread fan-out. A per-bucket re-analysis of the operator's run showed the pull's fetch rate **halving from ~6 RPS to ~3 RPS exactly as the dashboard scan latency climbed past ~8 s into the options phase** — the dashboard was starving its own pull (the "groww pull should never collide with the local product" concern). **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard cache; NO engine/lake/pull/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** `brutex/dashboard/summary_cache.py` — `_Entry` gains `compute_duration` (the measured clock-delta across each `recompute`, clamped ≥ 0 for a non-monotonic injected clock); `get_or_refresh` times the scan; `_plan`'s throttle now uses an ADAPTIVE floor `min(max(self._ttl_floor_s, entry.compute_duration), MAX_ADAPTIVE_FLOOR_S=120 s)` — so a CHEAP scan (`< base`) keeps the snappy 2 s floor (idle/fast behaviour byte-unchanged) while a 30 s scan auto-throttles to re-fire at most once per ~30 s (a ≤50% duty cycle), freeing the other half of the CPU for the pull; the 120 s cap bounds worst-case staleness. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the live coverage HEADLINE is unaffected — it is driven by the O(1) `CoverageCounters` write-funnel, NOT this scan; only the DETAILED per-dataset aggregate goes up to its-own-duration stale during a pull (the explicit trade: a slightly-staler detail table vs a pull starved by 30 s scans); ✅ idle/clean-cache behaviour is BYTE-UNCHANGED (the floor only bites while dirty = during writes; a fast scan keeps the 2 s floor); ✅ this REDUCES the collision (a ~50% CPU-duty recovery for the pull during the options phase) but does NOT eliminate disk-IO contention or fully isolate the pull (process isolation was DESIGNED in #919-era discussion then DROPPED by the operator as not worth it — NOT claimed here); ✅ self-tuning — no magic constant to set, the floor tracks the real scan cost. **REAL (verified 2026-06-23 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/dashboard/summary_cache.py` at **100% line+branch** (86/12, 0 missing); NEW adaptive-floor tests (`_SlowRecompute` advancing the injected clock — slow-scan self-throttle, the 120 s cap, `ttl_floor_s=0` still bounding a slow scan, and the non-monotonic-clock duration clamp); 25 summary-cache tests GREEN; 299 coverage/completeness/dashboard regression tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/summary_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_summary_cache.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SUMMARY-CACHE-ADAPTIVE-FLOOR-001. **Builds on:** DEC-COMPLETENESS-O1-LATENCY-001 #895 (the shared SPOT entry this throttles), DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the SummaryCache + the O(1) CoverageCounters headline that keeps the live tick fresh). **Part of:** the operator's "the pull must never collide with the local product" investigation — the dashboard's full-lake rescans no longer starve the concurrent pull.

921. **DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 — the Groww pull was achieving only ~3.2 r/s against a held 5.0 ceiling; Lever 2 (raise the default connection pool 2 → 4) ships first as the PROVEN fix to consume the slack, with Lever 1 (a fetch/write OVERLAP primitive to unlock 8) designed + adversarially reviewed and gated on a write-rate benchmark** (2026-06-24, the operator's "why not always hit 5 RPS when there's no major rate-limiting — what is the precise logic/architecture change needed — can you make it 8 — cover all extreme cases with real-time guarantee", verified by a 9-agent deep-research workflow). **Why (PROVEN from the fresh log `cf1afd97-brutex.log`, 3.33 h, 37,381 fetches, re-derived independently TWICE):** the throttle is OUR code, not Groww — the controller's time-weighted rate was **4.96 r/s** (held at 5.0 for 96.3% of the run; only **65** 429s / 3 stepdowns, ALL 65 at `current_rps=5.0`, never reaching the 3.0 floor), the bucket burst to `rps_1s_max=10`, yet achieved was only **3.20 r/s** — a **1.76 r/s SLACK** a binding limiter cannot have. The mechanism: only **2 SDK connections** (`GROWW_CLIENT_POOL_SIZE=2`), each on a ~625 ms per-contract cycle = ~185 ms fetch + ~440 ms serial non-fetch work (DOMINATED by the lake Parquet append — whole-month read-modify-write + zstd + fsync, ONCE per contract). 2 workers × (1/0.625 s) = 3.2 r/s demand < 5 allowed = exactly the slack. The earlier `constants.py` "Little's Law → 2 is sufficient" comment was WRONG (it used the 185 ms FETCH latency, not the 625 ms full cycle); `L = λ·W` ⇒ reaching 5 needs ≥ 3.1 concurrent calls. **What shipped in THIS commit (Lever 2 — PROVEN, low-risk, within the already-sanctioned 4-connection envelope; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3, Rule 6 per-second ceiling UNTOUCHED at 5.0):** `GROWW_CLIENT_POOL_SIZE` 2 → 4 (4/0.625 = 6.4 r/s demand > 5 → the SHARED rate controller binds at the 5.0 ceiling, consuming the slack with ZERO new concurrency-correctness surface — K connections add concurrency, never extra rate); `GROWW_CLIENT_POOL_MAX` stays 4 (one shared TOTP token; raising it is vendor-UNVERIFIED, ADR-0009 §3); the stale Little's-Law comment is corrected with the proven 625 ms-cycle arithmetic + the log evidence. **What is DESIGNED + gated (Lever 1 — the NEXT step, NOT in this commit):** a COMMON `write_consumer` producer/consumer primitive that moves the ~440 ms append+record OFF the fetch worker so each connection fetches near-continuously (shrinking the 625 ms cycle toward the 185 ms fetch) — the only lever that unlocks 8 (2 connections could then demand ~10.8 r/s). The hostile review caught that a SINGLE writer would serialize all appends at ~2.8–3.0 r/s (AT/BELOW today's 3.2 → a NET REGRESSION) and would remove the existing cross-partition write parallelism, so Lever 1 must ship as a SHARDED W≥2 consumer and merges ONLY if `bench_write_rate(W) > 3.20/s` is proven; it folds the back-channel-block fix for the #919 false-positive (`report.bars_appended` must be real before the drain reads it), the one-consumer-per-`_run_one_interval` lifecycle, and the ledger-settles-only-after-durable-write invariant. **The 5 → 8 ceiling flip** is then ONE constant (`GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`, injected at `pull_controller.py:861` + `cli.py:2120` into the fully-parametric `RateController`), gated on a clean overlap-at-5 run then KEPT only if a measured 8 run nets HIGHER throughput (not merely tolerable 429s — the #906 trap); `8×60 = 480 < 500/min` governor is PROVEN-safe (a HARD atomic reserve-under-lock, DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001 #913). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ Lever 2 is PROVEN by arithmetic + the verified worker/cycle model (reaches ~5, NOT 8); ✅ 4 is within the already-sanctioned MAX=4 token-sharing envelope (the default moves, the cap does not); ✅ Lever 1 + the 8-flip are EMPIRICAL — only a measured run proves the overlap clears 3.2/s and that the vendor tolerates 8 (the log shows Groww 429ing AT the 5.0 ceiling, so headroom above 5 is UNPROVEN); ✅ a sub-agent that claimed the gap was the rate-limiter at a stepped-down 3 r/s was REFUTED by the time-weighted-rate evidence (it assumed a step-down that never happened) — recorded for honesty. **REAL (verified 2026-06-24 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py` ruff + `mypy --strict` clean; `tests/unit/test_groww_constants.py` 21 tests GREEN (incl. NEW `test_pool_size_default_is_four_for_saturation` pinning the default + the slack arithmetic); 58 groww constants/pool/live/reauth tests GREEN. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_constants.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001 (the multi-connection pool this resizes), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-5-001 #906 (the 5.0 ceiling + the "8 wasted 429-retries" lesson the 8-flip gate respects), DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001 #913 (the 500/min governor that bounds the 8-flip), DEC-SUMMARY-CACHE-ADAPTIVE-FLOOR-001 #920 (the sibling pull-collision fix). **Part of:** the operator's "always hit the ceiling when not rate-limited / make it 8 / real-time guarantee" saturation work — Lever 2 (reach 5) ships now; Lever 1 (reach 8) is benchmark-gated next.

922. **DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 — the production Groww per-second rate ceiling RAISED 5 → 8 r/s (operator-directed), now that DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 Lever 2 (pool 2→4) gives the pull enough connections to generate demand toward the ceiling** (2026-06-24, the operator's explicit, repeated "make it as 8 RPS and our incremental/decremental will work automatically … everything should work precisely"). **Why:** at the prior 2 connections the achieved rate capped at ~3.2 r/s (DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921), so the 5–8 range was pure waste — the exact reason DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-5-001 #906 LOWERED 8 → 5. Lever 2 (now MERGED, #883) raised the default connection pool to 4, generating ~6.4 r/s of demand (4/0.625 s cycle), so for the FIRST time the controller can actually push toward a ceiling above 5 — making 8 a FAIR test of whether the vendor serves above 5, instead of the #906 probe-into-a-wall. **What shipped (ONE constant + its pin test + docs; NO engine/scope/vocab change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING` 5.0 → 8.0 (`constants.py`), read by BOTH live build sites (`pull_controller.py` + `cli.py`) into the fully-parametric `RateController`; the pin test `test_operator_directed_per_second_ceiling_stays_under_the_per_minute_governor` updated to assert `== 8.0` and `8×60 == 480 ≤ 500`; the Lever-2 pin test's honesty assertion updated (6.4 demand < 8 ceiling ⇒ demand-limited at ~6.4, NOT ceiling-limited at 8). **Safety (why a raise is acceptable here despite Rule 6):** (1) EXPLICIT, repeated operator approval (Rule 6 satisfied); (2) `8×60 = 480/min < 500/min` HARD governor (DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001 #913) — the per-minute cap can NEVER be overshot, proven by the property test; (3) a CEILING raise only ALLOWS a higher rate — it does NOT force it: the AIMD ladder still steps DOWN on a 429 burst (soft floor 3, deep floor 1) and recovers UP only as far as the vendor tolerates, so the worst case at 8 is IDENTICAL to 5 (the controller self-corrects); the floors/ladder/governor are UNCHANGED. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the change is SAFE + reversible (one constant; revert to 5 if 8 only burns 429-retries — the #906 trap); ✅ SUSTAINED 8 is UNVERIFIED — the `cf1afd97` log showed the vendor 429ing AT the 5.0 ceiling, so headroom above 5 is NOT proven; the controller will SETTLE wherever the vendor allows (the operator's "incremental/decremental works automatically"); ✅ with pool=4 the pull is demand-limited at ~6.4 r/s (4/0.625), so 8 will likely NOT be fully reached until the per-contract cycle is shortened — reaching a true 8 needs a shorter cycle, NOT more connections (MAX=4 token cap) and NOT the append-overlap (Lever 1, which a write-rate benchmark REFUTED: a fresh ParquetBarSink append is ~30 ms, not the assumed ~440 ms — the per-contract residual is elsewhere, to be measured by per-contract instrumentation next). **REAL (verified 2026-06-24 via the repo `.venv`):** `constants.py` ruff + `mypy --strict` clean; 99 groww constants/rate-common/pool/live tests GREEN (incl. the updated `== 8.0` / `480 ≤ 500` pin + the honest demand-vs-ceiling assertion). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_constants.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002. **Supersedes:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-5-001 #906 (which had superseded the original DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-001). **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (Lever 2, the connections that make 8 a fair test), DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001 #913 (the 480 < 500 governor proof). **Part of:** the operator's "make it 8 / the AIMD self-corrects / real-time guarantee" directive — the ceiling now ALLOWS 8; 923. **DEC-ENGINEERING-CHARTER-001 — the operator's full ultra-deep drill-down engineering-requirements dump is captured as a SCOPE-TAGGED repo doc (`docs/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS_CHARTER.md`) instead of pasted verbatim into Project custom instructions, so the intent is preserved without becoming an illusion** (2026-06-24, the operator's "make it full ultra-deep drill-down requirements … can I paste this into the project"). **Why:** the operator supplied a comprehensive reliability/automation/observability/merge requirements set and wanted it "in the project". 924. **DEC-FETCHES-COL-HONESTY-001 — the /coverage/windows FETCHES column is RELABELLED "EMPTY-retries" and its legend is corrected to state it is NOT the total vendor calls, so a FAILED window reading `1` can no longer be mis-read as "barely retried" when it actually burned the deeper timeout/429 in-call retry ladder** (2026-06-24). **Why:** the column rendered `in_pull_fetches` — the durable per-window count of the in-pull EMPTY-retry loop's re-issues (1-3, OVERWRITTEN per pull, `window_ledger.py:188-198` "OVERWRITTEN each pull… NOT cumulative", DEC-WINDOW-INPULL-FETCHES-001 #839). That count is honest for an EMPTY/SUCCESS window, but it is NOT the total vendor calls a FAILED window makes: inside EACH `adapter.fetch_ohlcv` the Groww client retries up to `max_attempts = 6` on a timeout / 429 (`brutex/adapters/groww/client.py:98`, the in-call ladder), and the whole window is re-attempted across `max_retry_passes = 2` (`ingest.py:126`) and `_DEFAULT_MAX_RETRY_ROUNDS = 3` (`run_ingest.py:102`) — so a FAILED `GrowwTimeoutError` window can burn far more vendor calls (~6 in-call × passes × rounds) than the `1-3` the column shows. `ingest._ingest_one_window` records `in_pull_fetches=fetch_count` on the transient-FAILED path (`ingest.py:608`), where `fetch_count` only counts the EMPTY-retry loop iterations, NEVER the in-call ladder. The operator could read a deeply-retried FAILED row as "tried once". **What shipped (DISPLAY-ONLY; template + one test assertion; NO Python/engine/payload-schema change):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/templates/fetch_windows.html` — the column header is renamed `Fetches` → **`EMPTY-retries`** with a corrected `title` tooltip ("in-pull EMPTY-retry depth of the LAST pull … NOT the total vendor calls: a FAILED window also burns the deeper timeout/429 in-call retry ladder (up to 6× per fetch) across passes/rounds, which is not counted here"); (2) the `<details>` "How to read a row" legend's `fetches` paragraph is rewritten to define it as the in-pull EMPTY-retry DEPTH and to state explicitly, in bold, that **This is NOT the total vendor calls** — naming the 6× in-call ladder × passes/rounds a FAILED window also burns, and that only the EMPTY-retry depth is persisted per window; (3) the inline `winFetches` JS comment is annotated with the same caveat. The payload key `in_pull_fetches` is UNCHANGED, so the `/db` generically-rendered window-ledger grid and every API consumer are byte-unchanged. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ this is the LEAST-INVASIVE honest fix — it removes the read-as-total-calls illusion by RELABEL + legend, without fabricating a number; the TRUE total-vendor-call count is NOT separately tracked per window (the in-call ladder count is not persisted — surfacing it would need new ledger-schema tracking, deliberately NOT added per the task's "do NOT add heavy new tracking just for display"); ✅ the 6×/2/3 figures are sourced from the in-repo constants cited above (no external claim); 🚫 no engine / 52-vocab / scope / pull / retry-logic / lake-data change — display legibility only; the retry behaviour is already correct, this only makes the column honest. **Real-run proof:** `pytest tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py -q` (the page asserts `EMPTY-retries` + `NOT the total vendor calls` render). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/fetch_windows.html`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FETCHES-COL-HONESTY-001. **Builds on** DEC-WINDOW-INPULL-FETCHES-001 #839 (the `in_pull_fetches` column this relabels for honesty), DEC-WINDOW-RETRY-LEGEND-001 #834 (the winhelp legend this corrects), DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (the per-window page).
