933. **DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-LATENCY-001 — the three remaining UNCACHED dashboard pollers (`/api/v1/coverage`, `/api/v1/universe/completeness`, `/api/v1/universe/mapping-integrity`) are now memoised behind a COMPOSITE (write-generation, instrument-master-revision) token, so a repeat poll is an O(1) handoff instead of a full O(datasets)+ledger projection — the LOW-RISK nav-latency wins (the dominant full-page-reload→in-place-swap lag is a separate larger follow-up, NOT in this PR)** (2026-06-26, the operator's "navigating section to section is slow / O(1) latency everywhere" — the cheap wins that the prior O(1) work (#860/#863/#866/#893/#895/#896) had not yet reached). **Why:** three routes re-ran their whole projection on EVERY poll — `/api/v1/coverage` (the 4 s headline+grid: a `list_index_equity_instruments` scan + `build_coverage_payload` over the ledger), and `/api/v1/universe/completeness` + `/api/v1/universe/mapping-integrity` (the 15 s polls: `categorize_instruments` + `per_symbol_completeness` and `fno_eligible_underlyings` + `reconcile_mapping_integrity` over the coverage ledger). The inner SPOT lake scan was already `_summary_cache`-cached (DEC-COMPLETENESS-O1-LATENCY-001 #895), but the residual classification + ledger reconciliation re-ran each poll. **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) a NEW COMMON public helper `master_revision(store)` in `brutex/dashboard/universe_cache.py` — the ONE source of truth for the instrument-master content fingerprint `(count(*), max(fetched_at))` over the `instruments` table — extracted from the existing `UniverseSnapshotCache._revision` (which now DELEGATES to it, zero duplication); (2) three dedicated `MoversSnapshotCache` instances in `build_app` (`_coverage_cache` / `_universe_completeness_cache` / `_mapping_integrity_cache`) — REUSING the COMMON generation-stamped LRU the `/db` discovery + candle-count caches already use (NO new class); (3) a `_nav_latency_key(name, store, *extra)` closure that folds BOTH freshness signals into the cache KEY — the dashboard write-generation (`_summary_cache.generation`, bumped by every pull / materialize) AND `master_revision` (which a keyless `load-instruments` moves WITHOUT bumping the generation) — and the three routes call `get_or_compute(key, generation=0, compute=…)`; the JSON + CSV mapping-integrity routes share ONE cached report via `_build_mapping_integrity_report_cached`; (4) `defer` added to the render-blocking `html2canvas` CDN `<script>` in `brutex/dashboard/templates/v29.html` (+ the `docs/dashboard/mockups/v29.html` copy) so it no longer blocks first paint — `html2canvas` is only used inside the PNG-export click handler (`typeof html2canvas === 'undefined'`-guarded), so `defer` is safe and the `onerror` fallback is preserved. **Freshness contract (Golden Rule #1 — no stale illusion):** folding BOTH the generation AND the master revision into the KEY (with a fixed `generation=0`) means a HIT fires ONLY when neither the coverage ledger NOR the instrument master has changed since the entry was stored — a pull (generation bump) OR an instrument load (master-revision move) yields a NEW key → recompute, so a poll can NEVER serve pre-pull / pre-load data; the LRU bounds memory (stale keys evict). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a repeat poll within one generation + master revision is O(1) in the lake/ledger depth (a dict handoff + a cheap COUNT+MAX token probe), NOT a literal O(1) total — the FIRST poll after a pull / load still pays one real O(datasets)+ledger projection (the cache bounds HOW OFTEN, not the build cost); ✅ READ-ONLY accelerator — same payloads, byte-identical to the uncached path (proven by a payload-equality assertion across two polls), only memoised; ✅ these are the CHEAP nav-latency wins — the DOMINANT remaining nav lag (the full-page reload on every section switch → an in-place DOM swap) is a SEPARATE larger PR, deliberately NOT attempted here. **REAL (verified 2026-06-26 via the repo `.venv`, Python 3.12):** `brutex/dashboard/app.py` + `brutex/dashboard/universe_cache.py` ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean (0 errors); `universe_cache.py` 100% line+branch (65/12); NEW `tests/integration/test_dashboard_nav_latency_cache.py` (4 tests — hit/generation-miss/master-miss + payload-identity per route + JSON↔CSV shared report) + a NEW `master_revision` unit test in `tests/unit/test_universe_cache.py` (11 green); 491 dashboard integration tests green. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/universe_cache.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/v29.html`, `docs/dashboard/mockups/v29.html`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_nav_latency_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_universe_cache.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-LATENCY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-BACKEND-CACHE-001 #866 (the `master_revision` token + `UniverseSnapshotCache` this extends), DEC-COMPLETENESS-O1-LATENCY-001 #895 (the inner SPOT scan cache these wrap), DEC-DB-TAB-SWITCH-O1-001 #896 (the generation-stamped `MoversSnapshotCache.get_or_compute` memo reused here), DEC-COVERAGE-WINDOWS-O1-001 #893 (the sibling O(page) coverage work). **Part of:** the operator's "O(1) latency everywhere" nav-speed series — the cheap per-poll cache wins; the in-place-nav-swap is the next, larger step.
934. **DEC-RAW-DATA-INTEGRITY-001 — a real-time, provable RAW-DATA INTEGRITY LAYER: a content hash (`blake2b`) of EXACTLY what Groww sent is captured per fetched window BEFORE any transform and persisted to an append-only sidecar, so any later tampering / drift of a re-fetched window is caught by a hash mismatch — purely ADDITIVE, changing NOTHING about existing storage** (2026-06-26, the operator's top-priority "provide a real-time provable guarantee that the stored lake derives from EXACTLY what Groww sent"). **Why (the gap):** the lake's bars ARE a deterministic function of the raw vendor payload (2dp `ROUND_HALF_UP` snap DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 + `high`/`low` clamp + IST→UTC + non-negative clamps + skip-empty + keep-first), but NOTHING recorded what the vendor actually sent — `ParquetWriter.raw_hash` is a `sha256` of the STORED Parquet FILE bytes (`parquet_writer.py:344,399,411`), which proves only the file did not change on disk, NOT that the file derives from the un-tampered response. **What shipped (ADDITIVE only; the parser + the writer value path + the 2dp rounding are UNTOUCHED; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) NEW PURE `brutex/data/raw_integrity.py` — `canonicalize_payload` (the `candles` row-of-arrays serialised compact JSON sorted-keys/no-whitespace, so envelope noise can never flip an identical series; a missing key → `[]`), `hash_payload` (`hashlib.blake2b` digest_size=32 → 64-hex; stdlib because the repo's `blake3` run-identity hash is not guaranteed importable pure-python — the record stamps `algorithm` so a future native-`blake3` migration coexists), the immutable `RawIntegrityRecord` (keyed by `(exchange,segment,groww_symbol,interval,window_start,window_end)` + `payload_hash`+`row_count`+`captured_at`), `build_record`, and `verify_record` (re-hash + compare → `VerifyResult`); (2) NEW `brutex/data/raw_integrity_store.py` — the durable APPEND-ONLY JSON-lines sidecar at `<lake_root>/raw_integrity/records.jsonl` (OUTSIDE `bars/`/`options/` — the candle lake schema is NEVER touched; append-only over an in-place rewrite is the lower-risk additive option, justified: extending the load-bearing window-ledger Parquet schema would be strictly riskier) with latest-wins load + a degrade-to-empty on missing/unreadable/malformed, plus `make_capture_hook` — the BEST-EFFORT `RawPayloadHook` that hashes+persists and SWALLOWS every error (a `RawIntegrityError`/`OSError` is logged + swallowed, so a hash failure can NEVER halt or corrupt a pull — the hash is additive PROOF, not a gate); (3) the capture seam: `candles.py::fetch_candle_windows` (the ONE COMMON tiling-fetch primitive BOTH spot+option paths funnel through) gains an optional `on_raw_payload` callback fired per window with the RAW payload BEFORE `parse_candle_rows`, `None`-default ⇒ byte-identical to the pre-feature path; threaded SPOT via new `GrowwMarketAdapter` fields (`capture_hook_factory` for the live per-symbol path + `on_raw_payload` for single-symbol tests, both eq/repr-excluded — observability state, NOT a `MarketAdapter` protocol change) and OPTION via a pass-through param on `fetch_option_candles`/`ingest_option_contract`/`run_groww_option_ingest` plus a `capture_hook_factory` per-contract builder on `run_groww_option_ingest`; **(3b) the capture is now BOUND at the LIVE pull build sites — the FIX that makes the guarantee REAL, not dormant. (Honesty correction: the original wording above said "ingest wiring", but NO production caller bound the hook, so the capture ran on ZERO real pulls; this entry now describes the post-fix reality.) NEW per-symbol `make_capture_hook_factory(lake_root)` — one live adapter / ingest run pulls MANY symbols through ONE object, so a single pre-bound `make_capture_hook` (which fixes one `groww_symbol`) would MIS-attribute every window; the factory builds the correctly-attributed per-symbol hook AT the call site where the symbol is resolved (spot: inside `fetch_ohlcv`; option: per contract in `run_groww_option_ingest`). The CLI builder `cli._build_live_groww_spot`, the dashboard builder `pull_controller._build_live_spot_adapter`, AND the live F&O `historical_pull._run_one_interval` (non-dry-run only — a dry-run has no real vendor bytes to attest) each now construct the adapter/ingest with `capture_hook_factory=make_capture_hook_factory(lake_root)`, so EVERY real spot + futures + option pull captures; the lake root uses the same seam the rest of the pull uses (never hardcoded). The factory + every per-symbol hook stay best-effort, so binding them can NEVER make a pull fail. Because the capture is now LIVE, a CLI `brutex fetch` + a dashboard pull can share one `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT` and append concurrently, so `append_record` now nests a cross-process advisory `fcntl.flock` (`LOCK_EX`) around the write on top of the in-process `threading.Lock` (mirrors DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887; the sidecar is append-only / never `os.replace`d so the held fd's inode is stable; POSIX-only — Linux + macOS, the Track-1 envelope);** (4) the VERIFY path: NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/integrity_verify.py` `verify_one` (re-issue `historical_candles` with the recorded coords + compare) + `verify_lake_records` (load every sidecar record, verify each → a `VerifyRun` summary, mismatch logged WARNING) — the `brutex verify-integrity` core; the live re-fetch CLI is a thin layer over this pure summary; (5) the design doc `docs/observability/RAW_DATA_INTEGRITY.md`. **Integration point (file:line):** `brutex/adapters/groww/candles.py::fetch_candle_windows` line 97 (`payload = client.historical_candles(...)`) — the raw row-of-arrays in hand BEFORE `parse_candle_rows`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ this proves (a) the RECORDED hash matches the raw payload AT CAPTURE TIME and (b) the lake is a deterministic function of that exact payload — so drift/tampering of a re-fetched window is caught; ✅ it does NOT retroactively prove pre-existing lake data (no historical raw payloads exist for windows pulled before this layer — `verify_record` attests captured-forward only, stated plainly); ✅ it does NOT distinguish a legitimate vendor RESTATEMENT from tampering (both surface as a mismatch — the operator investigates); ✅ the verbatim raw-payload archive for full offline replay is DESIGNED-ONLY (future, gated — storing every payload is heavy); ✅ best-effort capture can NEVER break a pull (every hook error swallowed + logged); ✅ the candle lake schema / stored bytes / `raw_hash` / 2dp rounding are byte-UNCHANGED. **REAL (verified 2026-06-26 via the repo `.venv`, Python 3.12):** the NEW + changed modules at **100% line+branch** (`raw_integrity_store.py` 86/14, `adapter.py` 43/6, `option_ingest.py` 251/70, `historical_pull.py` 213/46 — 0 missing each; the live build-site lines in `cli.py` + `pull_controller.py` are inside `# pragma: no cover` builders — `pull_controller.py` stays 100% across its suite); NEW `tests/unit/test_raw_integrity.py` (unit + hypothesis property: same payload→same hash / 1-byte change→different hash + a frozen golden digest) + `tests/unit/test_raw_integrity_store.py` (append/load round-trip, latest-wins, degrade-to-empty, best-effort swallow, the per-symbol `make_capture_hook_factory` attribution + the cross-process `flock` spy + an 8-thread concurrent-append no-interleave) + `tests/integration/test_raw_integrity_wiring.py` (hook fires through `fetch_candle_windows`/`fetch_ohlcv`/`fetch_option_candles`; the factory attributes per-symbol/per-contract; the CLI + dashboard build sites BIND the factory and write a real record on a pull; verify match + drift) + `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py` (the live F&O pull threads a non-None factory; the dry-run threads None); 184 covering tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on src AND tests. **Files:** `brutex/data/raw_integrity.py`, `brutex/data/raw_integrity_store.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/integrity_verify.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/candles.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/adapter.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_raw_integrity.py`, `tests/unit/test_raw_integrity_store.py`, `tests/integration/test_raw_integrity_wiring.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `docs/observability/RAW_DATA_INTEGRITY.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-RAW-DATA-INTEGRITY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the 2dp snap the verifier treats as part of the deterministic transform), DEC-GROWW-OPTION-INGEST-001 (the `fetch_candle_windows` COMMON primitive the seam lives in), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the per-window coordinate keying mirrored by the sidecar), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (the additive-never-halt discipline the best-effort capture follows), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the cross-process advisory-`flock` pattern the live append now mirrors). **Part of:** the operator's data-trust priority — provable lake provenance.

935. **DEC-PULL-HEALTH-WIRING-001 — the live pull-health monitor (shipped DORMANT in PR #893 / DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001) is now BOUND at the dashboard live-pull build site, so it actually WATCHES every real pull and fires its `pull_degraded` Telegram alert on a breach edge — the same dormancy fix just applied to the raw-data-integrity layer (#934)** (2026-06-26, the operator's "wire the pull-health monitor into the LIVE pull so it actually runs"). **Why (the gap):** #893 shipped `brutex/observability/pull_health.py::PullHealthMonitor` (the five SLA rules `pull.achieved_below_allowed` / `pull.pool_idle_high` / `pull.write_latency_spike` / `pull.rate_storm` / `pull.stalled`) PLUS the `_observe_rate(..., monitor=None)` seam in `pull_controller.py`, but NO production build site constructed a monitor — its own #893 entry honestly flagged "the monitor's production binding at the live build site is a flagged FAST-FOLLOW". So on a real pull the seam passed `None` and the monitor watched NOTHING (the identical dormant-feature failure mode #934 just closed for the integrity hook). **What shipped (ADDITIVE, best-effort; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) NEW `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py::_build_pull_health_monitor(controller)` — a GUARDED best-effort builder that, for a LIVE controller, constructs a `PullHealthMonitor` wired to the process-global `MetricRegistry` (`get_registry()`, so `/metrics` carries the live pull-health gauges), a `SweepAlerter.pull_degraded` `on_degraded` callback (so a breach reaches the operator's phone — a silent no-op when Telegram is disabled, the default), and the resolved connection-pool width (`resolve_pool_size()`, used by `pull.pool_idle_high`); it returns `None` for a dry-run / injected-factory pull (no controller — `_observe_rate`'s `monitor is None` arm stays a no-op), and the whole body is wrapped so an import / construction error is swallowed + logged and yields `None` — binding the monitor can NEVER block, slow, or crash the pull; (2) BOTH live-pull functions (`pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles`) build the monitor right after `_live_rate_runtime` resolves the controller and thread it into their `_observe_rate(rate_observer, _rate_controller, adapter, _pull_health_monitor)` tick. **Integration point (file:line before→after):** `pull_controller.py` — `pull_all_spot`'s `_observe_rate(rate_observer, _rate_controller, adapter)` and `pull_candles`'s identical call both gained the 4th `_pull_health_monitor` arg (built one line after each `_live_rate_runtime(use_live_rate, session_rate)` site); the seam at `_observe_rate` already accepted `monitor` (#893), so the change is the BINDING, not the seam. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the thresholds are operator-tunable HEURISTICS, NOT vendor-verified limits, and a breach is an OBSERVATION + alert, NOT auto-remediation — the pull runs identically whether or not the monitor fires; ✅ best-effort throughout — the builder swallows construction errors → `None`, and the monitor's own `observe` swallows malformed snapshots / callback raises (#893), so the monitor is structurally incapable of harming a pull; ✅ this wires the DASHBOARD pull path (the `_observe_rate` tick), which is the only path with a rate-observe seam — the CLI `brutex fetch` path has NO `_observe_rate` tick (it drives the ingest spine directly with pacing hooks but never periodically snapshots the rate), so a CLI-path monitor is a SEPARATE follow-up requiring a new tick seam, NOT claimed here; ✅ the `pull.stalled` dwell rule needs K consecutive samples — the dashboard seam ticks `_observe_rate` once per pull-phase end, so `pull.stalled` realistically fires only on a multi-phase pull (the WARN rules fire on a single tick) — an honest limitation of the existing tick cadence, not changed here. **REAL (verified 2026-06-26 via the repo `.venv`, Python 3.12):** `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean (0 errors on the file; the only `mypy`/`cma` noise is a pre-existing env-stub artifact on the clean origin/main baseline, NOT this change); the NEW `_build_pull_health_monitor` is at 100% line+branch (all three branches — `None` controller, live build, construction-raises → `None`); 936. **DEC-GROWW-NETWORK-ERROR-RETRY-001 — a transient host NETWORK / DNS failure (`ConnectionError` / `NameResolutionError` / `socket.gaierror` / `ConnectionResetError`, the live `"Failed to resolve api.groww.in"` shape) is now classified RETRYABLE (`GrowwNetworkError`), not a terminal quarantine, so a contract that hit a momentary connectivity blip is RETRIED / re-queued instead of being permanently dropped — the direct twin of DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001 #883 (5xx) and the never-headed `DEC-GROWW-EMPTY-BODY-RETRY-001` empty-body retry shipped under DEC-POSTPULL-DATAQUALITY-BATCH-001 #854** (2026-06-27, operator forensic of a 28h pull). **Why (the gap):** a 28h F&O pull forensic found **218 option contracts permanently lost** to a raw transport exception — a host DNS / connection failure the SDK surfaces (`requests.exceptions.ConnectionError` / `urllib3.exceptions.NameResolutionError` / `socket.gaierror` / `ConnectionResetError`) carries NO Groww `code` and matched none of the existing rate-limit / timeout / 5xx / empty-body hints, so it fell through `_classify_generic` to the terminal base `GrowwError` and was QUARANTINED — the exact data-loss class DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001 #883 closed for 5xx, still open for a network blip. **What shipped (`brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` ONLY — additive classification; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** a NEW `GrowwNetworkError(GrowwError)` (retryable); a NEW frozen `_NETWORK_ERROR_NAMES` transport class-name set (`ConnectionError`, `NameResolutionError`, `NewConnectionError`, `MaxRetryError`, `ConnectionResetError`, `ConnectionRefusedError`, `gaierror`) matched in `from_groww_exception` AFTER the typed-SDK map (so a `GrowwAPINotFoundException` 404 still WINS and stays terminal); a NEW phrase-only `_NETWORK_ERROR_HINTS` (`"failed to resolve"`, `"name or service not known"`, `"connection refused"`, `"connection reset"`, `"temporary failure in name resolution"` — NO bare numeric substrings) checked in `_classify_generic` AFTER the rate-limit + timeout + server hints (priority preserved: a 429 / timeout / 5xx that also mentions a connection never mis-reads as a plain network blip); `GrowwNetworkError` added to `is_retryable` + `__all__`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10 — no illusion):** ✅ deliberately NOT a `GrowwRateLimitError` — a network blip is not a quota signal, so `is_rate_limit` stays `False` and it rides the GENTLE timeout ladder (`on_timeout`), never stepping the per-second rate ceiling down (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6); the two consumption sites (`client._call` retry arm + the `ingest`/`option_ingest` quarantine-vs-defer branch) pick it up via `is_retryable` / `is_rate_limit` with ZERO extra code. ✅ this AUTO-RECOVERS FUTURE transient network failures (retried / re-queued so the scenario can NEVER permanently lose data again) — it does NOT itself re-pull the already-lost 218 contracts from the past run (those need a separate operator re-pull / the next until-clean pass; stated, not claimed). ✅ a genuine `404` stays terminal `GrowwNotFoundError`; an unknown class/message stays the terminal base (conservative — an unknown failure is never blindly retried). ✅ the reauth-path MINOR (a network error during the 06:00 IST token re-mint → terminal `GrowwAuthError`) is a flagged FOLLOW-UP, not fixed here. ✅ REAL (verified 2026-06-27): `errors.py` at **100% line+branch** (55/20); `client.py` 100% (89/10), `option_ingest.py` 100% (251/70); a 15-row classification matrix (transport class-name rows + message-hint rows + priority/collision rows + the parametrised `is_retryable` row in `test_groww_errors.py`) + a 7-row resilience matrix (DNS-then-success retried · DNS exhausted → raises retryable / deferred `still_failed` · whole-pull DNS → 0 terminal quarantines · real 404 STILL terminally quarantines); the broader groww client/ingest/retry suites GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_client.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-NETWORK-ERROR-RETRY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001 #883 (the 5xx retryable-classification twin — same additive-subclass / classified-by-name-or-phrase / preserved-hint-priority / not-a-rate-limit pattern), DEC-POSTPULL-DATAQUALITY-BATCH-001 #854 (the empty-body retryable classification, cited in #883 as the never-headed `DEC-GROWW-EMPTY-BODY-RETRY-001`), DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001 (the rate ladder a network blip must NOT step). **Part of:** the operator's data-trust / resilience priority — a momentary connectivity blip can no longer terminally lose a real contract.

927. **DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001 — the lake `ParquetWriter`'s merge-read (`_read_existing_bars`) rebuilds the stored month partition into `{timestamp: CandleBar}` by extracting each column ONCE via `polars.Series.to_list` instead of allocating one Python dict PER ROW with `df.iter_rows(named=True)`; a byte-PRESERVING speed cut of the GIL-bound merge read** (2026-06-26, the "4a" byte-preserving pull-write speed fix — the design + measurement done up front, the SAFE modest win that does NOT touch the stored bytes). **Why (measured):** a steady-state re-pull's largest per-window cost is the merge read-modify-write — the writer reads the WHOLE existing month partition, unions the incoming bars by timestamp, and (only if changed) re-renders. The read's reconstruction looped `df.iter_rows(named=True)` (one Python dict allocated per row) then rebuilt `Decimal(str(float))` + `_tick_round` per row — a per-row, GIL-bound rebuild. **What shipped (READ-PATH ONLY; the stored bytes / `raw_hash` / idempotence are UNCHANGED; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py::_read_existing_bars` now does one `Series.to_list()` per column (`timestamp`/`open`/`high`/`low`/`close`/`volume`/`open_interest`) and `zip(..., strict=True)`s the per-row scalars, dropping the per-row dict allocation. `Series.to_list()` yields the SAME Python scalar types per cell as `iter_rows(named=True)` — `float` for the OHLC columns, the SAME `datetime` (UTC `ZoneInfo`) dict key, `int`/`None` for volume/open_interest — so the `Decimal(str(float))` reconstruction, the `round_money` `ROUND_HALF_UP` 2dp snap, the keep-first/latest-wins merge decision, and the resulting partition file are BYTE-IDENTICAL. The float→`Decimal` math (the byte contract) is DELIBERATELY unchanged — a switch to float math would change the stored bytes and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here (that is the riskier "4b", not done). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ byte-PRESERVING — proven by a golden parity oracle + a hypothesis property test that run a verbatim copy of the LEGACY per-row reader alongside the NEW columnar reader and assert the two writers leave a BYTE-IDENTICAL Parquet file + identical `raw_hash` + identical reconstructed frame across empty/partial-append/idempotent-re-touch/out-of-order/exact-dup/same-ts-diff-value-keep-first/latest-wins/4dp-vendor-noise/OI-None-vs-int/large-partition (and 120 random fuzzed bar sets); ✅ the win is MODEST, not a 5× — the read/rebuild is only a FRACTION of the total write (the Parquet decode + the merge + the zstd re-encode + the atomic fsync write are all UNCHANGED), so the bench measures a real but small improvement; ✅ idempotence (CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #7) is preserved — same inputs → same stored bytes. **REAL (measured 2026-06-26 via the repo `.venv`):** a `tests/bench/test_write_latency.py` micro-bench seeds a deep 8,000-row month partition and times a real merge re-pull (re-read + rewrite-decision) BEFORE (per-row reader rebound on the writer) vs AFTER (production columnar reader), 25 trials each — **BEFORE p50 ≈ 110.2 ms / p99 ≈ 134.8–155 ms → AFTER p50 ≈ 101.9 ms / p99 ≈ 124–135 ms (~1.08× p50, ~1.09–1.15× p99)**; the bench asserts AFTER ≤ BEFORE (×1.15 jitter tolerance). `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py` at **100% line+branch** (131/22, 0 missing); the existing writer unit + chaos suites (31) + the new parity golden (10) + property (1) + bench (1) all GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `tests/golden/test_writer_columnar_parity.py`, `tests/property/test_writer_columnar_parity_properties.py`, `tests/bench/test_write_latency.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-MERGE-WRITE-001 (the merge-on-write read-modify-write this accelerates), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 (the `round_money` 2dp snap the read path preserves byte-for-byte), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (the `lake_write_guard` the read still runs inside), DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (the pull-write-cost investigation this is the byte-safe first cut of). **Part of:** the pull-write speed work — 4a is the SAFE byte-preserving read/rebuild cut; the larger fetch/write-overlap levers are tracked separately and gated on their own benchmarks.

## DEC-PIPELINE-SEGMENT-MOVERS-001 (2026-06-27)

951. **DEC-PIPELINE-SEGMENT-MOVERS-001 — the one-click pull pipeline now warms the `/movers` snapshots PER SEGMENT, the moment that segment fully succeeds (SPOT the instant the spot phase passes its gate — even if a later phase fails — and FUTURES + OPTIONS the instant the historical phase passes), instead of one combined warm gated on the WHOLE fetch; a segment that did NOT fully succeed is NEVER warmed (no illusion). PLUS an end-to-end regression PIN that the Futures/Options CHANGE / CHANGE% / OI columns compute from the REAL stored 1-minute table (the operator's blank-columns screenshot), with an explicit assertion that NO materialised view / pre-materialised table is created** (2026-06-27, the operator's "compute movers precisely AS EACH SEGMENT FINISHES" + "fix the blank Futures/Options CHANGE/CHANGE%/OI columns"). **PART 1 — per-segment movers gating (the change).** Before, `pipeline_pull.run_full_pipeline` ran ONE combined `run_movers` warm gated on `historical_phase_ok` (DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001 #878 / DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 #877) — spot/futures/options all warmed together, only after the WHOLE fetch (spot→metadata→historical) succeeded, so a clean SPOT pull whose metadata/historical later failed warmed NOTHING. **What shipped (ADDITIVE seam, NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** `run_full_pipeline`'s single `run_movers` param is REPLACED by three per-segment warm callables `warm_spot_movers` / `warm_futures_movers` / `warm_options_movers`, each fired at its OWN segment's success gate: (a) `warm_spot_movers` fires the moment `spot_phase_ok(spot)` passes — BEFORE the metadata phase even runs — so a clean spot pull warms its movers even if a LATER phase fails (the spot data is already clean + usable; this is the headline new behaviour); (b) `warm_futures_movers` + `warm_options_movers` fire the moment `historical_phase_ok(historical)` passes. The historical phase pulls FUTURES-BEFORE-OPTIONS (DEC-FNO-PULL-ORDER-LOOKBACK-001 #905), but its COMBINED `HistoricalPullReport` does NOT split FUT vs CE/PE success counts, so BOTH gate honestly on the SAME historical success — claiming a futures-only verdict the report cannot prove would FABRICATE one (Golden Rule #1; documented in the docstring + this ledger). `PipelinePullReport` gains `segment_movers_warmed: dict[str,int]` (the per-segment warmed-count map — a segment is in the map IFF its warmer was injected AND its own gate passed; ABSENT means "did not warm", `0` means "ran, warmed nothing" — the honest None-vs-0 distinction preserved at the segment level) + `movers_warmed` stays the SUM (`None` only when no segment warmed); the complete-note names each warmed segment in `spot → futures → options` order. The dashboard `/pull-pipeline` route (`app.py`, in the `pragma: no cover` background-job body) splits its one `_warm_movers` closure into three per-segment closures sharing a COMMON `_warm_for_date()` (the best-effort `latest_movers_date` + post-pull generation resolver — never 'today', so a prev-day pull never caches an empty 'today' snapshot), each reusing the EXACT `candidate_key` + `compute_spot/futures/options_candidates` + `MoversSnapshotCache.get_or_compute` the `/api/v1/movers` route uses (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — no drift), wrapped in the existing best-effort `warm_movers_snapshots` so a warm that raises is logged + counted 0 and NEVER fails the already-successful segment. **PART 2 — the blank Futures/Options columns (the GROUNDING + the PIN).** The operator's screenshot showed Futures/Options CHANGE / CHANGE% / OI columns blank ("—") while VALUE + VOLUME populated. GROUNDING (verified empirically + by reading the code): the helper fix already LANDED in PR #877 (`movers_snapshot._prior_session_last_from_minute` recovers the prior trading day's close + OI from the stored **1-minute** bars when the derived `1day` partition is absent — or its OI is null, which `spot_daily_resample` ALWAYS writes — and `movers_futures._prev_day_oi` falls back to that minute OI), and `_read_future_session` reads the CURRENT bar's OI from the real 1-minute. So the columns compute CORRECTLY from the real minute table whenever the lake holds the prior day's 1-minute bars (the production sink APPENDS prior + current day into the SAME month parquet) — VERIFIED end-to-end (a 1-minute-only F&O lake → futures `pct_change=+1.0%` / `oi_chg_pct=+20%`, options `pct_change=+30%` / `oi_chg=+150` / `oi_chg_pct=+30%`); the operator's blank is the HONEST blank of a contract whose prior trading day is genuinely absent (e.g. the first day of the 30-day OPTIONS lookback window, DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 #894). HONESTLY (Golden Rule #1/#10): PART 2 is therefore NOT a new code fix — fabricating a fix for already-working code would be the illusion this rule forbids; the value-add is an END-TO-END regression PIN at the `compute_futures_candidates` / `compute_options_candidates` level (the symptom the operator actually saw, vs the existing helper-level tests in `test_movers_tab_integrity.py`) over a lake that has ONLY the real `1minute` partitions (NO `1day` anywhere): the Futures CHANGE% + OI-gainers and the Options CHANGE% + OI-change/gainers are NON-blank from the real minute table; a contract with no prior day shows an HONEST blank (current OI still reads from the real minute bar); and — the operator's HARD RULE — the readers create NO materialised view / pre-materialised table (the on-disk tree is byte-unchanged across both snapshots and every data file is a real `1minute` partition Parquet; the `.locks/` write-time flock sidecars of DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 are from the seed WRITES, excluded). **IMPORTANT DEPENDENCY (stated, NOT hard-depended):** full OI correctness for the DERIVED daily path relies on the F&O OI-derivation branch (`claude/fno-tf-derive-oi-jlzt1n`) landing; until then OI reads from the real 1-minute (which always carries true OI), so the OI columns are correct NOW from the real minute table, and the daily path becomes correct once that lands. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ PART 1 is a read-only POST-SUCCESS accelerator over the just-filled lake — the pull's own success (`stopped_after`/`ok`) is NEVER affected by any warm (each is best-effort at its own call site); ✅ futures + options share the historical-phase gate because the combined report cannot honestly split FUT vs CE/PE — no fabricated per-segment verdict; ✅ PART 2 is a PIN of already-correct behaviour, NOT a claimed new fix — stated plainly per this rule; ✅ NEVER a materialised view — every read goes to the real stored 1-minute partitions (+ the stored 1-day where present); the only acceleration is the transient generation-invalidated `MoversSnapshotCache`, which always reflects the real table; ✅ ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py` at **100% line+branch** (76/0 stmt + 20/0 branch, 0 missing); `tests/unit/test_pipeline_pull.py` rewritten for the per-segment seam (36 tests — each segment warms as it finishes / spot-only success warms spot only + a later metadata failure leaves spot warmed / futures+options warm only after historical success / the hard gate: historical-not-clean never warms futures-options but keeps spot / early spot stop warms nothing / segment-0 honest-vs-absent / no-warmer back-compat + the full gate + `ok` + `to_dict` matrix); NEW `tests/integration/test_movers_fno_columns_from_minute.py` (5 tests — futures + options non-blank from the real minute table, the honest-blank-when-prior-absent case, and the NO-materialised-view assertion); 41 touched-file tests + 167 movers/pipeline regression tests GREEN; ruff + ruff-format --check + `pyright` (0 errors) clean on every touched file (`mypy --strict` clean on `pipeline_pull.py` + the new tests — the only `mypy` noise is the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub artifact in untouched `auth.py`/`reauth.py`, transitively imported by `app.py`, reproducing on the clean origin/main baseline). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline_pull.py`, `tests/integration/test_movers_fno_columns_from_minute.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PIPELINE-SEGMENT-MOVERS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001 #878 (the combined post-pull warm this supersedes with per-segment warming), DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 #877 (the gated phase-4 `run_movers` seam this replaces + the futures/options %/OI-from-1-minute fix this pins), DEC-FNO-PULL-ORDER-LOOKBACK-001 #905 (the futures-before-options historical pull order), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 #860 (the `MoversSnapshotCache` + `candidate_key` the warm reuses), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the `.locks/` write-time sidecar the no-view assertion accounts for), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853 (the 1-minute-only fetch + derived-1day-OI-null reality the minute fallback handles). **Part of:** the operator's `/movers` per-segment freshness + the data-trust priority — each segment's movers appear the moment its data is real, never an illusion.

## DEC-PULL-SCALE-HARNESS-001 (2026-06-26)

929. **DEC-PULL-SCALE-HARNESS-001 — a TESTS-ONLY at-scale pull harness drives the REAL production pull stack against a deterministic offline `FakeGrowwSDK`, plus a CI "slack/idle" gate that proves the pull SATURATES the rate it is allowed (issued-token slack < 15 %, pool idle ≤ 25 %) instead of trusting the controller's self-report** (2026-06-26). **Why:** the rate controller reports its TARGET (`current_rps`), but the ACHIEVED throughput can lag it badly when the worker pool serialises on a shared connection (the live 0.49-in-flight / ~3.4 r/s-at-8-ceiling starve `call_meter.py` documents). A regression that re-introduces such a starve would pass every unit test yet halve a real overnight pull. There was no automated guard that the whole stack — adaptive limiter + governor + multi-connection pool + parallel ingest + lake writer — actually keeps the rate bucket BUSY end-to-end. **What shipped (TESTS-ONLY; NO `brutex/` change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `tests/fakes/fake_groww_sdk.py` — a `FakeGrowwSDK` satisfying the real `GrowwSDK` Protocol that returns synthetic row-of-arrays candle payloads (`{"candles":[[ts,o,h,l,c,v,oi],...]}`) at a configurable seeded REAL latency (5-20 ms default), with injectable 429/timeout bursts by 1-based call index + configurable `candles_per_window`/`empty_rate`; it flows through the REAL parser/assemble/session-filter path (NOT a shortcut). (2) `tests/bench/pull_harness/` (`scenario.py`/`runner.py`/`report.py`) — wires the REAL `RateController` (ceiling 8 r/s + 500/min governor), REAL `ClientPool`/`GrowwClient` (pool 4) sharing ONE `CallMeter` via the real `build_live_pool` `sdk_factory` seam, REAL `ingest_spot` + `PoolRunParallel`, REAL `ParquetBarSink`/`ParquetWriter` to a tmp lake; drives N contracts × deep partitions across an outer thread pool, samples the shared meter (per-window `on_window` hook for the ALLOWED rate + a short-interval background poller for the live in-flight the post-completion hook cannot see), and produces a frozen `PullHarnessReport` (achieved/allowed/slack, in-flight p50/max, pool_idle_pct, write p50/p99, rps_1s_max, 429/timeout/empty counts, wall_s, seed). (3) `tests/bench/test_pull_at_scale_gate.py` — Gate 1 (40 contracts × 12 mo, pool 4, no bursts) asserts RATIO-based: issued-token slack < 15 %, pool idle ≤ 25 %, rps_1s_max ≤ ceiling + tolerance, every planned window pulled. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ TESTS-ONLY — no `brutex/` code touched (no coverage/engine/scope impact); ✅ the slack denominator is the ISSUED-token rate (the controller's governed unit) because production legitimately consumes the bucket TWICE per window (per-window pace + client-retry pace) — `physical_call_rps` is reported as the honest second number (~half); ✅ the pool-busy (idle ≤ 25 %) property only holds in the SATURATION regime where the per-call latency ≈ `pool_size / window_rate` (~1 s) — at the fast-socket 5-20 ms default the rate ceiling binds with near-zero concurrency by Little's law (in-flight ≈ rate × latency), which is correct physics NOT a defect, so Gate 1 drives the saturating latency while a cheap fast-vendor smoke asserts ONLY the latency-independent slack; ✅ deterministic seed; ✅ real-run measured (reference env): slack_ratio 0.009, pool_idle 0.0 %, in_flight_p50 4.0, rps_1s_max 10, 62 400 bars, 132 s wall (< 3 min). **Real-run proof:** `pytest tests/bench/test_pull_at_scale_gate.py -m bench` (Gate 1 + smoke pass; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on the touched files). **Files:** `tests/fakes/fake_groww_sdk.py`, `tests/bench/pull_harness/__init__.py`, `tests/bench/pull_harness/scenario.py`, `tests/bench/pull_harness/runner.py`, `tests/bench/pull_harness/report.py`, `tests/bench/test_pull_at_scale_gate.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-SCALE-HARNESS-001. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-RATE-ACHIEVED-METER-001 (the `CallMeter` the harness samples), DEC-GROWW-CLIENT-POOL-001 (the `ClientPool`/`build_live_pool` it drives), DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (the pool-2→4 lever whose effect this gate measures), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 #922 (the 8 r/s ceiling under test).
926. **DEC-AUDIT-FSYNC-DURABILITY-001 — the hash-chained audit log's writer now (1) `os.fsync`-es each record to stable storage before the action is considered committed (was flush-only, page-cache-durable but crash-losable) and (2) serialises payloads as RFC 8259-valid JSON (`allow_nan=False`), refusing a `NaN`/`Infinity` value with a clear `AuditPayloadError` instead of silently emitting the bare non-RFC tokens a strict reader rejects** (2026-06-26, the top Med-risk item the audit-log deep-verify flagged). **Why (the two confirmed gaps, file:line on pre-change `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`):** (1) **flush-not-fsync** — `append` did `self._fp.write(line)` then `self._fp.flush()` ONLY (lines 433-440), no `os.fsync`; `flush()` pushes bytes into the OS page cache, not durable disk, so a power loss / host crash after flush but before the kernel writes back could lose the last record and break the chain — even though the class docstring (lines 259-261) claimed the last write is "either fully persisted or absent" and `close()` (lines 366-371) ALREADY fsync'd best-effort, so the per-record durability was inconsistent with both the doc and the close path. (2) **non-RFC JSON on NaN/Inf** — `_canonical_json` (lines 138-143) called `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False)` with Python's default `allow_nan=True`, so a `NaN`/`Inf` metric value (e.g. a degenerate Sharpe) would serialise to the bare tokens `NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity` — invalid per RFC 8259 §6 — poisoning both the on-disk line AND the entry hash (a value that cannot be round-tripped). **What shipped (writer-only; NO engine/lake/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `append` now `os.fsync(self._fp.fileno())` after `flush()`, guarded by `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` — the SAME best-effort pattern `close()` already uses, since a few filesystems / sandboxes reject fsync on an append-only fd, where the flush has still reached the kernel — ONE fsync per append (O(1) per record, NOT per byte); (2) NEW `AuditPayloadError(AuditError)` + `_canonical_json` now passes `allow_nan=False` and maps the resulting `ValueError` to it. **Design choice — RAISE, not coerce (Golden Rule #1):** the audit log is tamper-evident + bit-reproducible; silently coercing `NaN→0`/`null` would hide a real data anomaly and break auditability, so the writer REFUSES the append at serialise time (BEFORE any byte is written — `to_json_line` raises, the file + chain are never advanced), keeping the on-disk chain RFC-valid and the rejected append non-mutating (the next good append takes the same seq). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ fsync is best-effort (suppressed `OSError`) — on a fsync-rejecting fs the flush still reaches the kernel, so durability degrades to the prior flush-only behaviour rather than crashing (NOT a claim of fsync on every host); ✅ a crash can still leave a TORN final line (write started, process died mid-line) — that is DETECTED by the reader (an incomplete final line → `AuditError`, never a corrupt committed prefix), and the durable newline-terminated prefix verifies + resumes unbroken (the kill-recovery test); ✅ NaN/Inf rejection is RECURSIVE (json.dumps walks the structure) and finite floats are byte-unchanged (the golden compute_hash/to_json_line pins still pass). **REAL (verified 2026-06-26 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` at **100% line+branch** (150/28, 0 missing); NEW `TestRfcSafeJson` (6 — each non-finite rejected, rejection does-not-corrupt-chain, nested NaN, byte-exact message pin, finite-still-serialises) + `TestKillRecovery` (5 — torn-tail detected, durable-prefix recovers+resumes, fsync-per-record spy, fsync-OSError suppressed) + property `TestRfcSafeJsonInvariant` (random good/bad append mix always verifies to the GOOD count with dense seq); 93 audit unit+property+chaos tests GREEN; 27 engine-sweep-audit + sustained-stress regression tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_audit.py`, `tests/property/test_audit_chain_properties.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-AUDIT-FSYNC-DURABILITY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (the `atomic_io` fsync-before-rename durability pattern this mirrors per-record for the append-only log; the audit log is append-only so it uses the append+fsync variant, NOT the tmp→rename whole-file variant), NFR-OBS-003 (the hash-chained audit contract). **Part of:** the audit-log deep-verify hardening — the tamper-evident record is now crash-durable per record + RFC-valid.
