932. **DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001 — the live Groww pull now SELF-INSTRUMENTS its own health: a `PullHealthMonitor` watches the rate-controller + call-meter snapshots already produced each `_observe_rate` tick, mirrors them as Prometheus gauges, and fires a best-effort Telegram `pull_degraded` alert on a degraded / stalled pull — WITHOUT a new background thread** (2026-06-26, the operator's "build the live pull-health self-instrumentation"). **Why:** the dashboard rate panel SHOWED `current_rps` / `effective_rps` / `latency_ms_p95` / `in_flight` but nothing WATCHED them — a pull achieving only ~3.2 r/s against a 5 r/s ceiling (the DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 slack), or one stalled under a 429 storm, produced no signal beyond the chart the operator had to read. **What shipped (reuses the EXISTING rails, minimal new surface; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** NEW `brutex/observability/pull_health.py` — `PullHealthMonitor` holds an `SLADetector` (the hysteresis-aware rule engine, UNCHANGED — only an OK↔BREACH edge fires, a steady state is silent), mirrors every observed gauge into a `MetricRegistry`, and routes a breach/recovery to a `pull_degraded` callback + structlog. Five rules read value-provider closures over the LAST-observed snapshot pair: `pull.achieved_below_allowed` (effective/current < 0.6 — OUR pipeline), `pull.pool_idle_high` (1−in_flight/pool_size > 0.5), `pull.write_latency_spike` (latency_ms_p95 > 1500 ms), `pull.rate_storm` (recent_hits > 20 — VENDOR-gated), `pull.stalled` (effective_rps < 0.5 for 5 consecutive samples → CRITICAL). The stall rule uses a NEW `DwellProvider` closure that returns the value ONLY after the predicate dwells K samples and `None` otherwise — so the dwell requirement layers on TOP of the detector via the documented None-skip contract with ZERO change to `SLADetector`. `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py` gains ONE method `pull_degraded(*, rule, achieved, allowed, detail)` mirroring `rate_breach` (dedupe_key=`pull-degraded:<rule>`); the message carries the *detail* string that DISTINGUISHES "OUR pipeline is the limiter — check write latency / pool width" from "VENDOR 429-gated — expected; the pull continues". `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py::_observe_rate` gains an optional `monitor` param and feeds it the SAME `(controller_snap, meter_snap)` it already sends the dashboard observer — best-effort (`observe` is wrapped so it can never block/crash the pull), no new thread, stops when the pull stops. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the thresholds are operator-tunable HEURISTICS, NOT vendor-verified limits — a breach is an OBSERVATION, never an auto-remediation; ✅ `pull.rate_storm` is explicitly labelled VENDOR-gated (a 429 burst is expected and the adaptive controller already handles it), so the operator never chases our code for a vendor signal; ✅ the monitor is NOT yet bound at the live build site (the `_observe_rate` seam accepts it; wiring it into the production pull-controller construction is a flagged FAST-FOLLOW so the monitor's alert cadence can be operator-reviewed first) — the SEAM + the WATCH logic ship here, the production binding does not, and this is stated not claimed. **REAL (verified 2026-06-26 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/observability/pull_health.py` at **100% line+branch** (130/28, 0 missing) + `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py` at **100% line+branch** (122/10, 0 missing); NEW `tests/unit/test_observability_pull_health.py` (dwell streak, each rule fire/clear with hysteresis, each provider None branch, gauge mirroring, the on_degraded-raises swallow, the observe-swallow, a breach→`pull_degraded`→fake-notifier wiring + dedupe test) + NEW `pull_degraded` / vendor-detail tests in `test_notifications_sweep_alerts.py` + `_observe_rate` active-path + monitor-branch tests in `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` (the file CI's per-module `pull_controller` 100% gate runs — an initial CI failure at 97.52% on the new `_observe_rate` body (lines 931-937) was traced to those tests originally living in `test_dashboard_rate_panel.py`, which is NOT in that gate's scoped set; moved to the gated file → `pull_controller.py` 100% line+branch (390/0/94/0) under the EXACT CI command); 66+ covering-file tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **Files:** `brutex/observability/pull_health.py`, `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_observability_pull_health.py`, `tests/unit/test_notifications_sweep_alerts.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_rate_panel.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001. **Builds on:** DEC-SLA-DETECTOR-001 #239 (the hysteresis SLADetector reused unchanged), DEC-DASHBOARD-RATE-PANEL-001 / DEC-DASHBOARD-RPS1S-PANEL-001 (the `_observe_rate` seam + the snapshot contracts this watches), DEC-TELEGRAM-WIRE-001 #567 (the SweepAlerter best-effort channel), DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (the achieved-below-allowed slack this rule detects). **Part of:** the §11 AUTOMATED observability promise (watchdog + Telegram + alerting) — the pull now tells the operator when it is degraded, instead of leaving them to read the chart.

940. **DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-LEVER1-001 — Lever 1 (a sharded parallel write-consumer that decouples the Groww fetch from the lake write) is a benchmark-proven NO-GO on the Track-1 hardware envelope: the consumer is BUILT, fully-tested, and SHIPPED DORMANT (not enabled at the live site), because the A/B bench REFUTED a throughput gain — the GIL-held deep-merge write does not parallelise across pure-Python shard threads, and settle-after-durable forbids fetch-ahead, so it cannot beat the synchronous path** (2026-06-27, the operator's #1-priority "decouple the fetch from ALL internal write/dedup/db work so the ONLY limiter is Groww — ships ONLY if it beats the gate, else a documented NO-GO like #922"). **The hypothesis (verified Design B):** the #910 deep-partition bench PROVED the lake write is O(month-depth) per save (12 ms → 213 ms over 500 → 15,000 rows) and runs serially on the fetch worker under the per-partition lock, so each connection idles ~74% waiting on its own write — capping achieved at ~2.8-3.2 r/s. Lever 1's plan: a `ShardedWriteConsumer` (W worker threads, each draining its own bounded `queue.Queue`, requests routed to a shard by `blake2b(series) % W` so all writes to one `(exchange,segment,symbol,interval)` series land on ONE shard — preserving the per-partition `threading.Lock` + `partition_write_lock` flock, NO single-serializer regression of the #886/#921 trap) hands the write OFF a background thread; the fetch worker enqueues then BLOCKS on a one-shot `ResultBox` until the durable `atomic_write_via` returns the REAL `WriteResult`, so the ledger settles ONLY after the durable write (Golden Rule #7), while OTHER connections fetch during the wait. **What was BUILT (correct, fully-tested infrastructure — kept DORMANT):** NEW `brutex/data/write_consumer.py` (`ShardedWriteConsumer` + `WriteConsumerSink` (a drop-in `BarSink` that routes `append` through the pool, preserving the spine's byte-identical settle-after-durable ledger ordering) + immutable `WriteRequest` + `ResultBox` + `resolve_write_pool_size`), stdlib-only at import (`queue`/`threading`/`hashlib`); the OPTIONAL `write_pool` param wired through BOTH ingest spines (`run_ingest.py` spot + `option_ingest.py` F&O) — `write_pool=None` (the default, and what the live build site passes) reproduces TODAY's synchronous path BYTE-IDENTICALLY (no thread, no queue, no behaviour change). The full failure matrix is handled + tested: settle-after-durable (a SUCCESS box is set ONLY on the line after `append` returns); bounded-queue back-pressure (a full shard queue blocks the producer — throttles fetch to the write rate, never OOM); disk-full/OOM at the consumer → `LakeWriteHalt` captured into the box + re-raised on the producer (a member of both spines' `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` → graceful halt) + a pool-wide fail-fast flag so the rest of the pull stops hammering a full disk; a consumer thread that fails mid-write → the exception is captured + surfaced, NEVER a fabricated success, and the shard stays alive to drain the rest; graceful `drain()` (poison-pill + join every shard so every queued request is durable BEFORE `end_pull_ledger`); a hard-exit request stays UN-settled → re-fetched (idempotent keep-first sink); keep-first order-independence (property-tested); crash mid-write (`atomic_write_via` untouched); 2-dp tick grid + partial/zero-price handled upstream on the fetch worker; clock-skew (durability = the `os.replace` return, not a timestamp). **THE HARD GATE — REFUTED (NO fake win, Golden Rule #10):** the A/B bench (`tests/bench/test_write_consumer_overlap_bench.py`) drives the REAL `ShardedWriteConsumer` against the REAL `ParquetWriter` over a deep ~7,500-row steady-state month, 4 connections, median of 3 repeats. MERGE required `achieved_rps(W≥2) > 3.20/s AND > achieved_rps(None) AND byte-parity`. **MEASURED (verbatim, repo `.venv`, 2026-06-27):** `achieved_rps(None) = 9.89 r/s` (raw 9.68/10.06/9.89) · `achieved_rps(W=2) = 10.06 r/s` (raw 10.06/9.90/10.09) · `achieved_rps(W=4) = 10.03 r/s` (raw 10.03/10.01/10.08). The consumer clears the 3.20 floor but does NOT beat sync by any reproducible margin (within ±0.3 r/s = pure noise; W=2 < None on 1 of 3 repeats). **ROOT CAUSE (measured, the honest reason — corroborates #922's "Lever 1 refuted" note + deepens it):** the deep merge write is ~78 ms of GIL-HELD Python (the `_read_existing_bars` zip-reconstruction loop over the stored month) + ~18 ms of GIL-released polars render; a pure-Python shard worker STILL holds the GIL for that 78 ms, so moving the merge to a shard thread does not parallelise it (Python threads cannot run bytecode concurrently) — the write-bound ceiling `1/0.096 ≈ 10 r/s` binds in BOTH arms. AND settle-after-durable (the #1 correctness invariant) REQUIRES the producer to block on the result box until the write is durable, so a connection cannot fetch ahead during its OWN write; the "overlap" of other connections fetching during one's wait ALREADY happens in the synchronous path (the connections are separate threads), so the consumer reproduces it exactly with no extra gain. **The byte-parity oracle PASSES** (the stored Parquet is BIT-IDENTICAL across None/W=2/W=4 — the merge is order-independent, so the decouple would change throughput, never the bytes) and **settle-after-durable PASSES** (the producer's result is the REAL durable `WriteResult`, partition on disk before the box settles) — the infrastructure is correct, it simply does not pay off on this envelope. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ NO regression shipped — the live build site is NOT wired to a pool, `write_pool=None` keeps the byte-identical synchronous path, so production is UNCHANGED; ✅ the dormant code is proven harmless if ever enabled (within noise of sync, byte-parity holds); ✅ the real unlock is named explicit FUTURE work, NOT claimed — escaping the GIL needs either a PROCESS-pool write worker (pickling cost + cross-process partition-lock coordination to evaluate) or moving the merge-read into the Rust kernel (a `trading_core`/`fno_math` columnar merge that releases the GIL), at which point the SAME `ShardedWriteConsumer` seam + `write_pool` param can be flipped on and re-benchmarked against THIS gate; ✅ ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/data/write_consumer.py` at **100% line+branch** (114/26, 0 missing); `run_ingest.py` + `ingest.py` at 100% line+branch under their covering suites, `option_ingest.py` at 100% line+branch under its full covering set; NEW `tests/unit/test_write_consumer.py` (32 — unit + property order-independence + chaos: halt-mid-queue re-raise + pool-wide fail-fast, consumer-failure-never-fakes-success, back-pressure saturation, drain-flushes-non-empty-queue, settle-after-durable gating) + the wired-spine tests in `test_groww_run_ingest.py` / `test_groww_option_ingest.py` (write_pool wraps the sink / None leaves it untouched / retry forwards it / F&O routes durably through the pool) + the bench's NO-GO A/B + byte-parity + settle-after-durable + no-leaked-threads; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/data/write_consumer.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_write_consumer.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/bench/test_write_consumer_overlap_bench.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-LEVER1-001. **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (Lever 2 pool 2→4; this is the Lever-1 follow-up it flagged "benchmark-gated NEXT"), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 #922 (whose entry already noted "Lever 1, which a write-rate benchmark REFUTED" — this is the full, instrumented refutation), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (`atomic_write_via` + `LakeWriteHalt`, untouched), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the per-partition flock the shard routing preserves), DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001 #927 (the merge-read whose GIL-held cost is the root cause). **Part of:** the operator's "decouple fetch from internal work" #1 priority — the answer is an HONEST NO-GO with the mechanism explained: a pure-Python write-consumer cannot help while the GIL-held merge-read is the dominant write cost; the seam is ready for the GIL-escaping (process-pool / Rust) follow-up.
948. **DEC-PULL-STALL-DETECTION-001 — a HUNG or STALLED dashboard pull is now DETECTED + alerted in REAL TIME, never silent: a heartbeat watchdog declares a wedged background pull HUNG (fires a CRITICAL pull-halt Telegram alert + releases the stuck single-flight flag so future pulls are not silently refused), and the live pull-health monitor's `observe()` is now fed PER WINDOW (not only at pull boundaries) so the dwell-gated `pull.stalled` rule can actually accumulate and fire mid-pull** (2026-06-27, the operator's "the fetch must never silently stall / real-time guarantee"; the two MAJOR stall-detection gaps a failure-hunt found, hardened through a hostile review). **Why (the two gaps, verified file:line):** **GAP 1** — `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py::BackgroundPullJob._run` cleared its single-flight `_running` flag ONLY on return/raise, so a HUNG worker (e.g. wedged on the no-timeout partition `flock` at `partition_lock.py:126`, a deadlocked socket) never reached the `finally` → `_running` stayed `True` FOREVER → the single-flight guard then SILENTLY REFUSED every future pull. The proven `brutex/observability/watchdog.Watchdog` heartbeat primitive existed but was wired ONLY into the sweep engine, NEVER the dashboard pull. **GAP 2** — `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`'s `PullHealthMonitor.observe()` was fed ONLY at pull/instrument BOUNDARIES (the post-loop `_observe_rate` call), so the dwell-gated `pull.stalled` rule (needs K=5 consecutive samples, `pull_health.py:296-308`) could NEVER accumulate → a mid-pull stall was undetectable; the `_observe_rate` "watches every tick" comments were misleading. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, best-effort; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) GAP 1 — NEW `brutex/dashboard/pull_stall.py` `PullWatchdog` (a thin, value-adding wrapper over the proven `observability.Watchdog`, mirroring `engine.sweep_watchdog.SweepWatchdog`): `start()` registers ONE worker HEALTHY + spawns a daemon timer that `check_once()`s on a `timeout/3` cadence; the pull worker `beat()`s on REAL progress (per fetched window) so a slow-but-progressing pull never false-positives; an operator-tunable timeout (`resolve_stall_timeout_seconds`, env `BRUTEX_PULL_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 600 s, fail-safe to the default on a bad value). `BackgroundPullJob` builds one per run (injected `watchdog_factory`, default builds the real one), beats it from `_on_progress` + `sync_from_ledger`, and stops it in the worker's `finally`; on the HEALTHY→HUNG edge the job's `_on_hung` fires a best-effort CRITICAL pull-halt alert via the COMMON `emit_pull_halt_alert`, marks the progress error, and CLEARS `_running`. **Per-RUN IDENTITY GATE (the hostile-review BLOCKER fix, hardened twice):** the per-run watchdog OBJECT is the run-identity token — BOTH `_on_hung` and the worker's `finally` clear `_running` ONLY when `self._watchdog is` THEIR run's watchdog (under the lock), so a stale (later-unwedged) worker, or a late-fired duplicate timer for an already-superseded run, can NEVER clobber a freshly-started newer run (the shared-flag design the first cut used was racy: a new run reset the flag → the stale finally cleared a live run → single-flight violated; the identity gate has no shared mutable flag to reset). CRUCIALLY the run-identity token is PUBLISHED ATOMICALLY with the single-flight flag — `start()` builds the watchdog BEFORE the lock (side-effect-free; `.start()` is not called on the `return False` path → no leaked timer) and assigns `self._watchdog = watchdog` INSIDE the SAME `with self._lock` block that sets `self._running = True`, closing a residual TOCTOU the second hostile review found: publishing the token AFTER releasing the lock left a window where a stale worker A's `finally` could acquire the just-released lock, still read `self._watchdog is wd_A`, clear `_running`, and admit a third pull C concurrently with B. `_on_hung` ALSO calls its run's `watchdog.stop()` (so the daemon timer cannot leak on the one path it exists for) and wraps its whole body in its own best-effort `try/except` (a raising `progress.fail` can never kill the timer). (2) GAP 2 — NEW `pull_controller.make_window_observer` wraps the per-window `on_window` callback so each PROCESSED window ALSO pushes the live rate/throughput snapshot to the panel + the monitor via `_observe_rate`; threaded into BOTH `pull_all_spot` (wrapping the existing `live_sync`) AND `pull_candles` (wrapping a no-op inner), so the `pull.stalled` dwell now accumulates on the pull's own activity cadence and a sustained near-zero-throughput stall trips the CRITICAL `pull.stalled` alert. (3) the misleading "watches every _observe_rate tick" comments corrected to the honest per-window + boundary reality. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ this DETECTS + alerts a stall (the real-time guarantee) — it does NOT itself PREVENT the underlying hang (the no-timeout `flock` is a separate MINOR follow-up, NOT claimed); ✅ the stall timeout is an operator-tunable HEURISTIC, not a vendor limit; a breach is an OBSERVATION + alert + single-flight release, NOT auto-remediation of the wedged I/O; ✅ best-effort throughout — every callback is swallowed (the underlying watchdog's narrow catch PLUS `_on_hung`'s own blanket `try/except`), so the watchdog can NEVER block or crash the pull; ✅ single-flight is PRESERVED across the dangerous hung→new-run→stale-finally ordering by the per-run identity gate (no shared mutable latch), proven by a regression test that FAILS without the gate; ✅ a slow-but-PROGRESSING pull keeps beating and is never falsely declared hung (proven by a test that beats just before each timeout); ✅ POSIX-applicable (the daemon timer is stdlib threading — no `flock` here). **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/dashboard/pull_stall.py` at **100% line+branch** (61/8), `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py` at **100% line+branch** (94/16), `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` at **100% line+branch** (416/98) across its full suite; NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_stall.py` (28 tests — env-override fail-safe matrix · watchdog hung-on-timeout / beat-keeps-healthy / recovery-logged-only / drive-loop / poll-cadence · BackgroundPullJob beat-per-window / hung-edge alerts + clears `_running` + STOPS its watchdog / on_hung-swallows-a-raising-progress-fail / future-pull-accepted-after-hung / the DANGEROUS hung→new-run→stale-finally ordering does NOT clobber (fails without the identity gate) / the residual TOCTOU — a stale finally INTERLEAVED at run-B's lock-release boundary does NOT clobber (fails without the under-lock token publish) / a late duplicate hung edge for a superseded run does NOT clobber / normal-finish clears + allows next / per-window observe accumulates the `pull.stalled` dwell → BREACH); two standalone repro scripts (`repro_race`/`repro_concurrent`) now exit 0 against the fix; 328+ pull + watchdog + health regression tests GREEN; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on the touched files. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_stall.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_stall.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-STALL-DETECTION-001. **Builds on:** DEC-WATCHDOG-001 #240 (the `Watchdog` heartbeat primitive this wraps), DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 (the `SweepWatchdog` + `_drive_watchdog` daemon-poll pattern mirrored here), DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001 #932 (the `PullHealthMonitor` + dwell-gated `pull.stalled` rule GAP 2 feeds), DEC-PULL-HEALTH-WIRING-001 #935 (the per-pull monitor binding this extends to per-window), DEC-TELEGRAM-PULL-HALT-DASHBOARD-001 #889 (the `emit_pull_halt_alert` CRITICAL path the hung edge reuses), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the no-timeout `flock` that motivates GAP 1, whose timeout is the flagged MINOR follow-up). **Part of:** the operator's "the fetch must never silently stall" real-time guarantee + the §11 AUTOMATED observability promise (watchdog + Telegram + alerting).
941. **DEC-DB-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 — a single corrupt / version-incompatible Parquet file in a `/db` candle partition now SKIPS (logged `db.parquet_skip` + counted out) instead of 500-ing the WHOLE candle pager on EVERY paging click until the file is manually quarantined — the `/db` candle-pager twin of the shipped `/movers` corrupt-skip (DEC-MOVERS-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 #886)** (2026-06-27, the failure-hunt's MAJOR `/db` corrupt-Parquet gap). **Why (the gap, file:line on pre-change `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`):** `query_candles` issued bare `conn.execute(read_parquet(glob))` reads with NO `try/except` — the page `COUNT(*)`, the page cursor, AND the derived-column baseline helpers (`_intraday_prev_close_by_page_date` / `_daily_close_by_date` / `_intraday_last_close_by_date` / `_daily_open_by_date` / `_intraday_open_by_date` / `_underlying_spot_close_by_ts`). The route `app.py` caught only `ValueError`→400, NOT `duckdb.Error`. So a corrupt / version-incompatible Parquet in the partition glob (seen in the wild as DuckDB *"No magic bytes found at end of file"* / `don't know what type: \r`) raised an uncaught `duckdb.Error` → FastAPI 500 on EVERY paging click until the operator manually quarantined the file — even though the SIBLING coverage readers (`summarize_spot_datasets` / `summarize_option_datasets`) already routed through the resilient `_aggregate_parquet_resilient` probe-and-skip (DEC-COVERAGE-PARQUET-RESILIENT-001); `query_candles` simply omitted it. **What shipped (READ-ONLY viewer; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) the COMMON unreadable-Parquet skip set `brutex/dashboard/movers_resilient.movers_read_skip_errors()` now ALSO includes `duckdb.Error` (was `(PolarsError, OSError)` — polars covers the `/movers` reads, duckdb covers the `/db` `read_parquet` reads, OSError covers file faults) so ONE source-of-truth set spans BOTH engines (no copy-pasted set, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); adding `duckdb.Error` is harmless to `/movers` (polars never raises it). (2) NEW `db_view._execute_parquet_resilient(conn, base, sql, extra_params, *, source, skip_event, unreadable_event)` — the ONE COMMON probe-and-skip primitive: fast path binds the `<base>/**/*.parquet` glob + extra params once (byte-identical to a direct query); on an unreadable-Parquet error it probes each file via the shared NEW `_readable_parquet_subset` (logs `db.parquet_skip` per bad file + path/reason, OMITS it, never a fabricated bar), re-runs over the readable LIST, or logs `db.parquet_unreadable` + returns `[]` when nothing is readable. (3) NEW `db_view._execute_candle_page_resilient` returns `(out_columns, raw_rows)` (the page cursor needs the column description) over the SAME resolver — a degraded all-corrupt page returns `([], [])` so the caller renders an empty (degraded-but-correct) page. (4) `_aggregate_parquet_resilient` is REFACTORED to delegate to `_execute_parquet_resilient` (keeping its own `coverage.*` log namespace via the event-name params), so the coverage + candle surfaces share ONE logic with ZERO behaviour change to the coverage tests (their `coverage.parquet_skip` / `coverage.parquet_unreadable` event names are byte-unchanged). (5) `query_candles`' COUNT + page reads + ALL six derived-column helpers route through the resilient helpers; the empty-partition guard (the no-files case) is unchanged. (6) **ADJACENCY GUARD — hostile-review BLOCKER folded (Golden Rule #1):** the prior-day-close %-change baseline (the TWO `_prev_trading_close`-fed paths — the intraday `_intraday_prev_close_by_page_date` predecessor read + the 1-day `_daily_close_by_date`) must NOT, after a corrupt file is skipped, BRIDGE across the gap to a NON-ADJACENT earlier day's close and render a confidently-WRONG `change_pct`/`open_gap_pct` (reproduced end-to-end: April shown as −46.34% baselined on February's 205 when the true predecessor March=105 was corrupt; truth +4.76%, honest answer BLANK). That would trade a *visible 500* for a *silent wrong number* — the exact failure the skip must never cause. FIX: `_readable_parquet_subset` now also returns `any_omitted`, and `_execute_parquet_resilient` reports it via an optional `skip_sink`; the two adjacency-sensitive baseline readers pass a sink and, on ANY skip, return `{}` → every affected bar gets an HONEST BLANK %-change (`None`), never a fabricated number. The other four derived helpers (`_intraday_last_close_by_date`, `_intraday_open_by_date`, `_daily_open_by_date`, `_underlying_spot_close_by_ts`) are per-key GROUP BY/BETWEEN with NO adjacency assumption, so a skip there already degrades to an honest blank — UNCHANGED. (The `duckdb.Error` catch stays deliberately BROAD — DuckDB has no version-stable unreadable-file subclass — but a genuine SQL bug is STILL never swallowed: every file probes readable so the degraded re-run RE-RAISES the original error as a 500, proven by a test.) **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ NARROW catch — a genuine code bug (`ValueError`/`KeyError`/…) STILL propagates, never silently swallowed as a "skip"; ✅ a skipped file is OMITTED + logged, never a fabricated bar — the corrupt file stays on disk for the operator to quarantine; ✅ a degraded page is HONEST (`total` counts only readable bars; an all-corrupt partition is an empty page + a `db.parquet_unreadable` error log, never a 500; a corrupt PREDECESSOR yields a BLANK %-change, never a wrong number); ✅ the fast path stays a single bound-glob query (per-file probing is paid ONLY when a read actually fails — Golden Rule #5 O(1) steady-state); ✅ the COVERAGE summaries (`summarize_spot_datasets`/`summarize_option_datasets`) now also skip on the COMMON `(PolarsError, duckdb.Error, OSError)` set via the shared `_execute_parquet_resilient` — byte-unchanged `coverage.*` log namespace; ✅ pure read-time DETECT-and-skip — no write surface, no engine/lake/scope change. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` at **100% line+branch** (712/0 stmt + 230/0 branch) + `brutex/dashboard/movers_resilient.py` at **100% line+branch** (9/0, 0 missing) across the full covering set; NEW tests in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py` — the corrupt-skip group (one-corrupt COUNT+page skip, all-corrupt empty-page-not-500, direct `_execute_parquet_resilient` fast-path, `_execute_candle_page_resilient` all-corrupt, `_readable_parquet_subset` mixed + all-readable, `_aggregate_parquet_resilient` coverage-namespace, genuine-SQL-error-propagates) PLUS the BLOCKER VALUE-asserting tests (a corrupt PREDECESSOR month → `change_pct is None` for BOTH the 1-minute AND 1-day views, with a clean-baseline control asserting the TRUE `+1.00%` — these FAIL with the wrong number `1.51%` WITHOUT the adjacency guard, PASS blank WITH it, closing the line-coverage-masking the prior len-only test left) — each writes a GOOD month + corrupt month(s) so the REAL `read_parquet` raises a `duckdb.Error`; 170 db-query tests + 487 full-covering-set tests GREEN; ruff + ruff-format --check + `pyright` (0 errors) + `bandit` (0 issues) clean on the touched files (`mypy --strict` clean on the two touched `brutex/` modules — the only `mypy` noise is the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub artifact in untouched `auth.py`/`reauth.py`). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_resilient.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-CORRUPT-SKIP-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 #886 (the `/movers` corrupt-skip + the `movers_read_skip_errors` COMMON skip set this extends with `duckdb.Error`), DEC-COVERAGE-PARQUET-RESILIENT-001 (the `_aggregate_parquet_resilient` probe-and-skip pattern this generalises + the coverage readers now share), DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001 #867 (the `query_candles` COUNT path this wraps), DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 #865 / DEC-DB-FNO-COLUMNS-001 #881 (the F&O derived-column spot join now resilient). **Part of:** the critical-risks resilience-hardening arc (#883–#887, #901, #919) — a single corrupt lake file can never again 500 a whole read-only viewer page.
946. **DEC-DEEP-PARTITION-BENCH-001 — a TESTS-ONLY deep-partition write-cost-vs-depth at-scale bench measures the REAL synchronous lake-write per-append cost (`append_ms`) + the derived single-lane `achieved_rps` at increasing partition depths (500 / 2,000 / 7,500 / 15,000 rows), producing the achieved-rps-vs-partition-depth CURVE that is the PROVE-FIRST evidence gate for the parallel write-consumer (Lever 1) — with a None-only A/B seam left for the future W∈{2,4} byte-parity run** (2026-06-27, the remaining half of scalability fix #1 — the instrumentation half (`lake.partition.write` event + `pull.pool_size`) being the separate landing). **Why:** the scalability audit confirmed the lake write (`parquet_writer._merge_write` / `option_parquet_writer._merge_partition`) is **O(month-partition-size)** per straddling append — it reads + rebuilds + (on any change) re-encodes + atomically rewrites the WHOLE month, on the FETCH worker, under the per-partition lock. The old "440 ms uniform per write" figure was REFUTED (DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 — a FRESH append is ~30 ms; DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001 #927 measured a deep 8,000-row merge at p50≈102 ms). To responsibly decide whether Lever 1 (overlap the append OFF the fetch worker) is worth building — without falling into the #886/#906 trap of shipping a "fix" that doesn't net more throughput — we need the achieved-rps-vs-depth curve, the HARD merge gate input (`achieved_rps(W≥2) > 3.20/s`). **What shipped (TESTS-ONLY; NO `brutex/` change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** NEW `tests/bench/test_deep_partition_write_cost.py` — seeds a deep month partition (`_deep_bars` — distinct in-range 1-minute bars in ONE 2021-01 partition), then times exactly ONE straddling `ParquetWriter.write` merge per trial (the seed write is UNTIMED) at each depth, in BOTH steady-state re-pull modes: `rewrite` (a straddling batch of NEW bars past the partition end → full read+rebuild+zstd-re-encode+atomic-fsync-rewrite — the worst case, the #927 8,000-row analogue) and `noop` (a straddling batch of already-stored bars → keep-first no-op: full read+rebuild, NO rewrite — proving even an idempotent re-pull pays the O(depth) READ). It derives `achieved_rps = 1 / append_p50_s` (the single synchronous lane's write-bound throughput ceiling), PRINTS the recorded curve, and asserts SANE MONOTONICITY (cost rises with depth / single-lane rps falls with depth, ≥0.80 jitter tolerance + a ≥3× deepest-vs-shallowest floor) — NOT a brittle absolute SLA (the absolute ms is CI-disk-bound, CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 10). **The measured curve (reference env, 2026-06-27, Python 3.12, 15 trials/point):** `rewrite` mode — depth 500: append_p50≈12.83 ms / p99≈16.11 ms / achieved≈77.9 r/s · 2,000: 35.61 / 68.96 / 28.1 · 7,500: 106.05 / 142.25 / 9.43 · 15,000: 215.88 / 286.09 / 4.63; `noop` mode — 500: 7.72 / 9.38 / 129.6 · 2,000: 24.75 / 36.24 / 40.4 · 7,500: 83.70 / 113.23 / 12.0 · 15,000: 169.74 / 199.57 / 5.9. **The read (the Lever-1 decision):** `append_ms` grows ~LINEARLY with partition depth (rewrite ~14 ms per 1,000 rows; a 30× depth jump is a ~17× per-write cost), so a single write-bound lane caps at ~10 r/s at a 5-day-deep partition (7,500 rows) and ~5 r/s at a 10-day-deep one (15,000) — BELOW the 5–8 r/s ceiling, exactly the slack #921 attributed to the serial append. With the #921 lane analysis putting the append as the DOMINANT ~440 ms of the ~625 ms per-contract cycle, this is the quantitative case that Lever 1 is LIKELY TO PAY OFF — and it names the bar Lever 1 must clear: `achieved_rps(W≥2) > 3.20/s` on this SAME deep scenario, with a byte-parity oracle. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ MEASUREMENT ONLY — no `brutex/` production change, this is the PROVE-FIRST gate NOT the Lever-1 implementation; ✅ records the curve + asserts only monotonicity, never a hard absolute SLA (the ms is host-disk-dependent); ✅ a SINGLE-lane synchronous measurement — the rps is one lane's write-bound ceiling, the load-bearing Lever-1 input; ✅ the `write_consumer` (Lever 1) does NOT exist yet — the `write_consumer_workers` A/B param is `None`-only with an explicit `NotImplementedError` + TODO referencing #921 (a non-None W raises, never a silent fake number; a pinning test proves the seam stays synchronous-only this PR), and when the primitive lands the SAME deep scenario reruns at W∈{None,2,4} with the byte-parity oracle + the 3.20 gate; ✅ the #908-instrumentation half (`lake.partition.write` event + `pull.pool_size`) is the separate landing — this bench times `ParquetWriter.write` directly (the task-sanctioned alternative), so it stands alone on this clean origin/main base. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** ruff + ruff-format --check + `pyright` (0 errors) + `mypy --strict` (no issues) all clean on the touched file; `pytest tests/bench/test_deep_partition_write_cost.py -m bench` — 3 passed (the rewrite curve, the noop curve, the Lever-1 seam pin), curve printed verbatim. **Files:** `tests/bench/test_deep_partition_write_cost.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DEEP-PARTITION-BENCH-001. **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (Lever 1 designed + the ~3.2 r/s serial-append slack this bench quantifies vs depth; the 3.20 gate threshold), DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001 #927 (the deep-8,000-row merge measurement this curve extends across depth; the byte-preserving read path), DEC-PULL-SCALE-HARNESS-001 #929 (the at-scale pull harness this complements — that gate proves the rate BINDS, this curve proves the write COST vs depth), DEC-LAKE-MERGE-WRITE-001 (the O(partition) read-modify-write under measurement). **Part of:** scalability fix #1 — the PROVE-FIRST gate for the parallel write-consumer (Lever 1); the bench is the merge gate, the consumer is the next (separately reviewed + benchmark-gated) step.
953. **DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001 — the pull can no longer STALL on its own internal locks: the cross-process partition `flock` is now a BOUNDED acquire that DEFERS the window (transient, like a 429) instead of pinning a worker until the 600 s watchdog force-kills the pull; the raw-integrity sidecar is SHARDED per `groww_symbol` with a bounded `flock` (distinct symbols never contend, exhaustion is a logged skip); and a process-global liveness beat fired by the lock-wait poll + the rate pacer keeps a slow-but-progressing pull's watchdog heartbeat alive — so the ONLY thing that limits the pull is the rate limiter** (2026-06-27, the anti-stall / contention hardening batch — GAP #3 MAJOR + GAP #14/#15 MINOR). **GAP #3 (MAJOR) — bounded partition lock (`brutex/data/partition_lock.py`):** the prior acquire was an unconditional blocking `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` held across the whole Parquet read-modify-write (DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887), so a WEDGED peer (stuck mid-`write_parquet` on a hung volume) pinned a fetch worker until the 600 s `PullWatchdog` killed the entire pull. FIX: `_acquire_bounded` loops `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` catching `BlockingIOError`, short-sleeps, until a tunable deadline (`BRUTEX_PARTITION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S`, default `120 s` — well under 600 s; non-positive / non-finite `nan`/`inf` fall back to the default so a bad value can never re-disable the bound), then raises the NEW transient `PartitionLockTimeout(DataLakeError)` (NOT a `LakeWriteHalt` — a window defer, never a pull-wide stop). Both ingest spines (`ingest.py::_ingest_one_window`, `option_ingest.py::ingest_option_contract`) catch it around `sink.append`, record the window `FAILED` in the ledger, and return a TRANSIENT outcome (`transient=1` / `transient_failures=1` + `still_failed_windows=1`) — the window is DEFERRED to the next pull exactly like a 429/timeout, NOT a symbol/contract-wide quarantine and NOT a rate-controller step (it is OUR contention, not vendor pressure). Both writers ride the SAME `partition_write_lock`, so the option-writer `enter_context` site is fixed identically with ZERO copy (COMMON); the per-process `threading.Lock` + `lake_write_guard` are byte-unchanged. **GAP #14 (MINOR) — sharded raw-integrity sidecar (`brutex/data/raw_integrity_store.py`):** the capture hook serialised EVERY window completion across all ~750 symbols behind one process-global lock + a no-timeout `flock` on one shared `records.jsonl`, blocking the fetch worker. FIX: append to a per-symbol shard `<lake_root>/raw_integrity/<sha256(groww_symbol)>.jsonl` (distinct symbols → distinct files + locks → never contend); `load_records` globs ALL `*.jsonl` shards (and the legacy `records.jsonl`, so old sidecars still load, one unreadable shard skipped not fatal); the cross-process `flock` is BOUNDED (`LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` retried under a short deadline) and exhaustion is the EXISTING best-effort skip (log `raw_integrity.append_lock_timeout` + swallow — the hash is additive proof, a dropped record only costs a re-verify, never data). **GAP #15 (MINOR) — liveness beat (`brutex/observability/progress_beat.py`):** `PullWatchdog` beat only on a COMPLETED window, so a pull genuinely progressing-but-slow under lock contention could be FALSELY declared hung. FIX: a NEW decoupled process-global seam — the bounded lock-wait poll + the rate controller's `pace()` return fire `emit_progress_beat()`, and `BackgroundPullJob._run` registers its `_beat` for the run's lifetime (removed in `finally`); single-flight guarantees one pull, a beat is pure liveness so even a stray beat only keeps a heartbeat alive. The hot paths import ONLY `emit_progress_beat` (no import edge up into the dashboard); a raising beat is swallowed + logged (never crashes the worker). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ GAP #3 is the real ROOT-CAUSE fix (the pull never blocks on the partition lock — only the rate limiter limits it); ✅ GAP #15 is defence-in-depth against a FALSE-POSITIVE kill, not the root fix; ✅ a deferred window is re-pulled next pass / next pull (the peer making real progress finishes and the window succeeds), never masked, never fabricated; ✅ POSIX (`fcntl.flock`, Linux+macOS — the Track-1 envelope), Windows out of scope; ✅ NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change — ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (CLAUDE.md §3). **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** all 8 touched `brutex/` files at **100% line+branch** (`partition_lock.py` 53/6 · `errors.py` 14/0 · `raw_integrity_store.py` 106/20 · `progress_beat.py` 24/2 · `rate_common.py` 143/34 · `ingest.py` 177/48 · `option_ingest.py` 260/74 · `pull_jobs.py` 97/16, 0 missing) captured via `pytest --cov`; NEW tests — `_acquire_bounded` retry/timeout/beat + env fail-safe (incl. nan/inf) + a public-CM wedged-peer timeout, the spot + option `PartitionLockTimeout`-defers-window regressions (FAILED-ledger + no-block), the per-symbol shard + bounded-flock-timeout-skips-record + legacy-file-loads + retry-then-acquire, the progress-beat seam (register/emit/unregister + best-effort swallow) + a watchdog-alive-under-contention integration test, and a property test (timeout always bounded+finite+positive · shard path deterministic+per-symbol); ruff + ruff-format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on all touched source + test files. **Files:** `brutex/data/partition_lock.py`, `brutex/data/errors.py`, `brutex/data/raw_integrity_store.py`, `brutex/observability/progress_beat.py`, `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py`, `tests/unit/test_partition_lock.py`, `tests/unit/test_progress_beat.py`, `tests/unit/test_raw_integrity_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_stall.py`, `tests/property/test_partition_lock_property.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the cross-process partition `flock` this bounds), DEC-RAW-DATA-INTEGRITY-001 (the sidecar this shards), DEC-PULL-STALL-DETECTION-001 #945 (the `PullWatchdog` this keeps alive), DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001 #883 (the transient-defer / FAILED-preserve path this mirrors), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the rate pacer the liveness beat hooks). **Part of:** the anti-stall / contention hardening — the pull must never block on internal locks; only the rate limiter limits it.
960. **DEC-RANKING-TIEBREAK-001 — the composite-ranking leaderboard is now a DETERMINISTIC TOTAL ORDER: tied composite scores break on the combo's unique `mask` (ascending), so a leaderboard ranks bit-identically regardless of the order the sweep enumerated its candidates in — closing an order-dependent-output defect that violated idempotence/reproducibility (Golden Rules #4/#7)** (2026-06-27, the `brutex/ranking/` deep-audit + hardening pass). **Why (the defect, file:line on pre-change `brutex/ranking/__init__.py`):** `rank_combos`'s final sort was `ranked.sort(key=lambda rc: rc.composite_score, reverse=True)` — keyed on the SINGLE float `composite_score`. Two distinct combos can produce an IDENTICAL composite (e.g. byte-identical metrics, or any z-term blend that collides), and `list.sort` is STABLE, so tied combos kept their INPUT relative order. A leaderboard is a SET of candidates, so permuting the candidate enumeration permuted the output for any score tie — reproduced end-to-end: three combos with identical metrics ranked `[10,20,30]` forward but `[30,20,10]` when the same set was passed reversed. That violated **Golden Rule #7** (same inputs → same outputs bit-for-bit) and **Golden Rule #4** (reproducibility): the existing golden fixture froze only ONE fixed input order and the stress test re-ran the SAME order, so the gap was untested. **What shipped (ranking-only, `brutex/ranking/__init__.py`; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) the sort key becomes the strict TOTAL order `key=lambda rc: (-rc.composite_score, rc.mask)` — primary composite score DESCENDING (via negation, in ONE `reverse=False` sort), unique `mask` ASCENDING as the final tie-break. `mask` is the per-(instrument, TF) combo identity, so two distinct survivors can never compare equal; the negation is well-defined because every composite sort key is FINITE — a non-finite metric field DOES reach `_zscores`, but the `[-_Z_CLAMP, +_Z_CLAMP]` min/max clamp maps any non-finite z to a finite bound, so the composite (and thus `-composite_score`) is never `NaN` (a `NaN` key would itself make `list.sort` nondeterministic — audited + confirmed empirically). (2) the unique-`mask` precondition the total order depends on is now ENFORCED (post-hostile-review MINOR-1): the two callers (`engine.sweep_run` / `sweep_driver`) pass the sweep's `(mask, metrics)` pairs VERBATIM with no dedup, so a duplicate mask would silently reintroduce the input-order-dependent ordering the tie-break removes — `rank_combos` now detects a duplicate among the gate-SURVIVORS (via `collections.Counter`) and FAILS LOUD with a `ValueError` naming the offending mask(s), converting latent silent nondeterminism into a deterministic, auditable error (a duplicate among gate-REJECTED combos never reaches the sort and is correctly ignored). The `rank_combos` docstring's Returns section documents the deterministic mask tie-break and a new Raises section documents the precondition. (3) `passes_gates` is now FAIL-CLOSED on non-finite metrics (post-hostile-review follow-up): a `NaN`/±`inf` in any float-valued gate input (`profit_factor`, `max_drawdown_pct`, `win_rate`, `win_loss_ratio`) would silently PASS a `<`/`>` comparison (`NaN < x` / `NaN > x` are both `False`, and `-inf` slips through the drawdown gate) — a silent wrong-ACCEPT on malformed data — so a NEW COMMON `_non_finite_gate_input` helper (`math.isfinite`-based, `None`-preserving) rejects any present non-finite input up front, while behaviour for every FINITE value and for `None` stays byte-identical (the integer gates `total_trades`/`max_consecutive_losses` cannot be non-finite). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the BEHAVIOUR change is CONFINED to the previously-undefined tie case — a strict improvement (the prior order was input-dependent / undefined); every NON-tied ordering is byte-identical, so the byte-frozen overfit golden fixture (`tests/golden/test_ranking_overfit_golden.py`) passes UNCHANGED; ✅ the opt-in overfit path inherits the same key (proven by an abstain-pool tie-break test); ✅ NO materialised view, NO new threshold/weight, NO scope/vocab/rate/engine change — one sort-key change; ✅ the audit also confirmed the gate boundaries (`>=`/`>` per spec), the COMMON single-source thresholds, the honest O(n log n)/O(1)-per-op complexity claims, and the no-input-mutation discipline were already correct; ✅ the NaN-in-a-gate-input wrong-ACCEPT the audit FLAGGED is now CLOSED in this same entry by the fail-closed guard (point 3) rather than left as a producer-contract observation — a `NaN`/±`inf` gate input now REJECTS, with finite + `None` behaviour byte-identical. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv, Rust wheels built via maturin):** the only MODIFIED source file is `brutex/ranking/__init__.py` — `brutex/ranking/overfit.py` is UNCHANGED (audited clean, no edit), it is only CO-MEASURED by the `--cov=brutex.ranking` package target; both read **100% line+branch** (`__init__.py` 99 stmt / 26 branch, `overfit.py` 47 stmt / 12 branch — 146 stmt / 38 branch total, 0 missing) via `pytest tests/unit/test_ranking.py --cov=brutex.ranking --cov-branch`; NEW tests — `TestTieBreakDeterminism` (identical-metrics→ascending-mask, tied-scores input-order-independent, score-dominates-mask, partial-tie-groups, overfit-path tie-break, duplicate-survivor-mask-RAISES with a byte-exact message, duplicate-among-rejected-does-NOT-raise, unique-mask-path-unaffected — 8 unit), `TestNonFiniteGatesFailClosed` (NaN profit_factor / +inf & -inf drawdown / ±inf win_rate / NaN win_loss_ratio all REJECT, finite + None byte-identical — 8 unit), a hypothesis permutation-invariance property (`test_ranking_is_a_permutation_invariant_total_order` — shuffling the candidates yields a byte-identical ranking + masks strictly increase within every equal-score run, with deliberate duplicate Sharpes forcing real ties), and two 100k stress cases (`test_huge_all_tied_pool_is_permutation_stable_no_quadratic` — all-tied pool ranks ascending-mask, permutation-stable, sorts in <5 s = no O(n²); `test_huge_distinct_pool_is_permutation_stable`); 113 ranking tests (unit/golden/property/stress/bench) GREEN; ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict brutex/ranking` + `pyright brutex/ranking` all clean on every touched source + test file. **Files:** `brutex/ranking/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/test_ranking.py`, `tests/property/test_ranking_overfit_properties.py`, `tests/stress/test_ranking_overfit_sustained.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-RANKING-TIEBREAK-001. **Builds on:** DEC-RANKING-001 (the composite ranking + gates this hardens), DEC-RANKING-OVERFIT-001 (the opt-in 6th-gate/8th-term path that inherits the tie-break), DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001 (the risk-efficiency term in the composite). **Part of:** the per-package deep-audit + hardening arc — every ranking output must be bit-stable regardless of input order.

964. **DEC-ENGINE-DEDUP-NAN-CANON-001 — the sweep dedup digest now REJECTS a non-finite float in the combo params (a defensive one-NaN-policy guard, byte-stable for every FINITE digest), and the engine's tuple-skip resilience + the dedup hot path's O(1)/bounded-memory contracts are PINNED across the 7 test types — so a NaN can never silently enter a membership key the run-identity hash would refuse, and an operator Ctrl-C can never be silently downgraded to a single-tuple skip** (2026-06-27, an engine-only hardening of the brute-force dedup canonicalisation + the resilient-skip seam, from a deep adversarial audit of `brutex/engine/`). **Why (the two consistency/regression gaps, file:line):** **GAP O1 (NIT→fixed)** — `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py::combo_digest` canonicalised the combo identity with a bare `json.dumps(...)`, which SILENTLY emits the non-standard `NaN` / `Infinity` JSON tokens for a non-finite float param. The two SIBLING canonicalisers REJECT a non-finite float — `brutex/strategies/combo.py::canonicalise_params` ("NaN floats are not hashable", the run-identity hash, rejecting NaN only) and `brutex/engine/tuple_complete.py::render_completion_sentinel` (`allow_nan=False`, the completion sentinel, rejecting ALL non-finite) — so the membership-DEDUP key would silently ACCEPT a NaN the run-IDENTITY key forbids: divergent canonicalisation policy across the three engine paths (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 11 COMMON). **GAP H1 (missing regression guard)** — the combo loop's per-tuple `except SweepComboError` re-raises `MemoryError` bare (regression-tested), but NO test pinned the `BaseException` twin: an operator `KeyboardInterrupt` (Ctrl-C) propagating BARE past the `except Exception` catch was CONFIRMED-correct behaviour but UNGUARDED, so a future refactor widening the catch to `except BaseException` would silently downgrade a fatal Ctrl-C into a single-tuple skip + continue over a 33B-trial sweep — exactly the failure the `MemoryError` test guards. **What shipped (3 items; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO storage/vocab/rate/scope change):** **(1) SOURCE** — `combo_digest`'s `json.dumps` gains `allow_nan=False` + a new `except ValueError` arm raising a `SweepCacheError` whose message is truthful for BOTH `ValueError` causes — `json.dumps(allow_nan=False)` raises `ValueError` for a non-finite float AND for a circular reference — "combo params are not JSON-serialisable as a canonical digest (non-finite float such as NaN/inf, or a circular reference): …". `combo_digest` now matches the tuple-completion sentinel canonicaliser EXACTLY — both `combo_digest` and `brutex/engine/tuple_complete.py::render_completion_sentinel` use `allow_nan=False`, so both reject ALL non-finite (NaN / inf / -inf) — at the ONE dedup-key canonicalisation point. It is therefore marginally STRICTER than the run-identity hash `brutex/strategies/combo.py::canonicalise_params` (which rejects only NaN, not ±inf) — a harmless TIGHTENING: any param the run-identity hash refuses, the dedup key also refuses, never the reverse. The guard is DEFENSIVE (the engine feeds no non-finite params today) and `allow_nan=False` only ever REJECTS a non-finite float — it NEVER reshapes a finite value's serialisation — so for any FINITE combo the digest is BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to before (proven: the pre-change and post-change hex of a fixed finite combo are equal; pinned as a golden). **(2) TUPLE-SKIP RESILIENCE PINS** — `KeyboardInterrupt` (and a generic non-`Exception` `BaseException` subclass) is now regression-tested to escape the per-tuple `except Exception` BARE at every grid level — the single-tuple runner (`run_persisted_sweep`), the resilient grid (`run_sweep_grid`), and the supervised grid (`run_supervised_grid`) — with NOTHING written (no store / sidecar / completion-sentinel), `tuples_failed` NOT bumped, no `TUPLE_FAILED` / `GRID_SWEEP_COMPLETE` audited, no cache/checkpoint recorded, and the grid ABORTED (the sibling tuple never runs). **(3) O(1) + BOUNDED-MEMORY BENCHES** — the per-mask AND-evaluation (`combo_mask.evaluate_mask` / `mask_to_entry_signals`) and the per-dedup digest (`combo_digest`) latency ratios are pinned ≤ the two-tier O(1) ceiling (5× shared-CI / strict 1.1× M4-Pro), and `combo_digest`'s stateless heap footprint is proven FLAT across N=1k vs 100k via the `tracemalloc` recipe. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ a DEFENSIVE guard — the engine feeds no non-finite params today, so this closes a latent consistency gap, not a live defect; ✅ FINITE digests are byte-for-byte UNCHANGED (the golden + a byte-stability proof pin it — `allow_nan=False` only rejects, never reshapes); ✅ the Ctrl-C behaviour was ALREADY correct (a `BaseException` never matched `except Exception`) — this PINS it against a future-refactor regression, it does not change runtime behaviour; ✅ the O(1) benches assert a 10×-scale latency RATIO + an absolute, N-independent memory ceiling, NOT a literal O(1)-total or an absolute SLA (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 10); ✅ ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — `stage3_refine.py` untouched, no storage/vocab/rate/scope change. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the repo `.venv`):** `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py` at **100% line+branch** (81/0 stmt + 10/0 branch), the whole `brutex.engine` package at **100% line+branch** (4090/0 + 1104/0) under `pytest tests/unit/test_engine_*.py --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch` (1183 passed); NEW tests across the 7 types — unit (`test_engine_sweep_cache.py`: NaN/inf/-inf → `SweepCacheError`, finite → 64-hex; `test_engine_sweep_run.py`: KeyboardInterrupt + a `BaseException`-subclass escape bare, nothing written; `test_engine_sweep_orchestrator.py` + `test_engine_sweep_supervisor.py`: KeyboardInterrupt aborts the grid, no `tuples_failed`/cache/checkpoint), property (`tests/property/test_engine_sweep_cache_properties.py`: digest deterministic + key-order-insensitive, non-finite always raises), golden (`tests/golden/test_engine_combo_digest_golden.py`: pinned finite-combo hex), integration (`tests/integration/test_engine_sweep_keyboard_interrupt.py`: a real grid where one tuple raises Ctrl-C aborts, not skips), bench (`tests/bench/test_engine_combo_mask_o1.py` per-mask ratio + `tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_cache_o1.py` per-dedup ratio + bounded memory), stress (`tests/stress/test_engine_sweep_cache_bounded_memory_stress.py`: ≥100K digests bounded + deterministic); ruff + ruff-format clean on `brutex/engine` + `tests`; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py`. **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_run.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_orchestrator.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_supervisor.py`, `tests/property/test_engine_sweep_cache_properties.py`, `tests/golden/test_engine_combo_digest_golden.py`, `tests/integration/test_engine_sweep_keyboard_interrupt.py`, `tests/bench/test_engine_combo_mask_o1.py`, `tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_cache_o1.py`, `tests/stress/test_engine_sweep_cache_bounded_memory_stress.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-ENGINE-DEDUP-NAN-CANON-001. **Builds on:** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 #441 (the 52-vocab combo identity the digest keys), DEC-MARK-MANY-SENTINEL-001 #650 (the dedup/sentinel redo authority the tuple-skip pins protect), DEC-ENGINE-TUPLE-SKIP-RESILIENT-001 #904 (the `SweepComboError` resilient-skip seam this guards against a `BaseException` widening), DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 (the two-tier `ratio_ceiling` the new benches route through), DEC-MEMLEAK-GATE-001 #616 (the `tracemalloc` bounded-memory recipe the dedup bench/stress reuse). **Part of:** the engine-hardening / 100%-standards arc — the brute-force dedup canonicalisation is now COMMON across all three engine paths, and the resilient-skip seam's "only `SweepComboError` is a skip" contract is regression-pinned.

## DEC-COSTS-HARDEN-PAISA-001 (2026-06-27)

963. **DEC-COSTS-HARDEN-PAISA-001 — the Track-2 options cost calculator (`brutex/costs/`) is HARDENED on its latent / forward-compat paths while the live NORMAL_CLOSE long path stays BYTE-IDENTICAL: a non-NORMAL trade outcome now FAILS LOUD instead of silently returning premium-based NORMAL_CLOSE numbers, the post-slippage fill can no longer collapse to ₹0.00, the integer rounding helpers are correct ROUND_HALF_UP for negatives too, and the short-side slippage sign ambiguity is PINNED with a byte-exact test rather than guess-fixed** (2026-06-27, the costs deep-audit hardening batch — audit MAJOR-1 + MINOR-3 + MINOR-4 + NIT-1). **Why:** a `brutex/costs/` deep correctness audit confirmed the live Track-2 NORMAL_CLOSE long_call/long_put path is correct + 100% covered, but flagged four latent defects hiding behind a green gate (the never-used forward-compat branches were executed but under-asserted). **CHANGE 1 (MAJOR-1) — fail-loud on unsupported outcomes:** `compute_trade_cost` previously ran the NORMAL_CLOSE math REGARDLESS of `trade_outcome`, so a caller passing `EXPIRY_EXERCISE` / `EXPIRY_ASSIGN` / `EXPIRY_WORTHLESS` got SILENTLY WRONG premium-based costs (the `CALCULATOR_SPEC §4.2` intrinsic-based state machine is not implemented). VERIFIED SAFE: the ONLY production caller (`brutex/options/executor.py:490`) always passes `"NORMAL_CLOSE"` (DEC-EXEC-008 / DEC-RISK-011 intraday-only), so a guard breaks no consumer. NEW `UnsupportedTradeOutcomeError(ValueError)` in `types.py` (a custom, TESTED exception — NOT `NotImplementedError`, which is coverage-excluded); a Step-0 guard in `compute_trade_cost` raises it (message naming the outcome + citing "CALCULATOR_SPEC §4.2 not yet implemented") for any non-NORMAL outcome; `used_exercise_branch` is now a literal `False` (the guard makes the exercise branch unreachable). The `intrinsic_value` field + `stt_exercise_rate_*` helpers stay (still constant-tested). **CHANGE 2 (MINOR-3) — tick-floor the fill:** a ₹0.05 (1-tick) long exit slipped to a ₹0.00 sell fill (a "free" sale); `_apply_slippage` now floors EVERY returned fill at `max(fill, TICK_PAISA)` — economically correct (nothing trades below one tick) and only affecting the degenerate tick-boundary case (normal path ≥ 2 ticks BYTE-UNCHANGED). **CHANGE 3 (NIT-1) — correct negative ROUND_HALF_UP:** `_round_to_paisa` / `_round_to_rupee` used floor-division half-up (correct for non-negative, but rounding negatives toward +∞); both now branch on sign to round half AWAY from zero for negatives (`-0.5 → -1`, matching `brutex.money.round_money` Decimal `ROUND_HALF_UP`), with the POSITIVE path proven byte-identical to the old formula via a direct property test (the live calculator only ever feeds non-negative products — this is FUTURE-caller hardening, not a live-result change). **CHANGE 4 (MINOR-4) — short-side slippage sign PINNED:** the short SELL (entry) leg is a documented spec CONTRADICTION — `CALCULATOR_SPEC §8` table says `entry_open − 1 tick` (adverse) but the §4 pseudocode says "SELL at entry+1tick" and is itself flagged "# CHECK SIGN". Track 2 is BUY-only so the short path is never exercised; per the audit + Golden Rule #1 the current behaviour (`entry_open + tick`) is PINNED with a byte-exact test + a code comment naming the ambiguity, NOT guess-changed. **CHANGE 6 (hostile-review NIT-1) — realized-fill slippage:** the informational `slippage_paisa` was the NOMINAL `2 × TICK_PAISA × n_shares`, which OVER-STATED the slippage when CHANGE 2's 1-tick floor fired (a 5-paise long exit floored to 5 actually moved the sell leg 0 paise, so its slippage is 1 tick not 2); `_apply_slippage` now ALSO returns the realized per-share delta (`|buy_fill − buy_raw| + |sell_raw − sell_fill|`) and `compute_trade_cost` derives `slippage_paisa = realized × n_shares`, so the line is always internally consistent with the notionals/PnL — the NORMAL path (fills ≥ 2 ticks) stays BYTE-IDENTICAL (`2 × tick × shares`; the §12.1 fixture's 650 paisa is unchanged), only the degenerate floored case reads `1 × tick × shares`. **CHANGE 7 (extreme-edge MAJOR) — fail-loud runtime validation of the Literal enum fields:** `TradeInput`'s `instrument` / `option_type` / `side` / `broker` / `gst_split` / `trade_outcome` fields are typed `Literal[...]` but a static annotation is NOT a runtime guard, so a typo'd enum string (e.g. `side="banana"`) was SILENTLY ACCEPTED and routed into the short-leg / inverted-PnL forward-compat branch, producing a silently-WRONG cost instead of an error — the same fail-loud class as CHANGE 1. FIX: `__post_init__` now runtime-validates each Literal-typed field is a member of its allowed set (after the existing numeric guards), raising `ValueError` naming the field, the bad value (`repr`), and the allowed set. The allowed sets are derived ONCE from the Literal aliases themselves via `typing.get_args` (frozen module-level `_*_VALUES` constants — a SINGLE source of truth, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, never a hand-maintained duplicate list that could drift). Every VALID member of every field still constructs (the canonical fixture + every prior test unchanged); only a non-member fails loud. **CHANGE 5 — 7-test-type coverage:** named regression tests per change (audit-ID-traced), boundary LOTS (1 / 10,000) + PRICES (1-tick floor / exactly-on-tick / 5-paise degenerate), STT regime-boundary timestamps (Oct-2024 + Apr-2026 flips), direct rounding ties (positive/negative/exact/just-below/just-above half), a `@pytest.mark.property` Hypothesis test over random valid NORMAL_CLOSE long trades (total == Σ components · net == gross − total · every component ≥ 0 · fills ≥ 1 tick · rupee-rounding idempotence), and the `__post_init__` guard gaps (negative lots/strike, equal entry==exit, min-valid boundaries). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the live NORMAL_CLOSE long_call/long_put path is BYTE-IDENTICAL (the canonical §12.1 fixture + all prior fixtures pass unchanged — positive rounding + ≥2-tick fills are untouched); ✅ CHANGE 1 is a fail-loud GUARD, NOT the §4.2 state machine (still deferred — a wrong outcome now ERRORS instead of mis-pricing); ✅ CHANGE 4 PINS an ambiguous unused path, it does NOT resolve the spec contradiction (resolve before any short-side track relies on it); ✅ NO engine / scope / vocab / rate change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (CLAUDE.md §3). **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** all 4 `brutex/costs/` files at **100% line+branch** (`__init__.py` 4/0 · `calculator.py` 63/10 · `constants.py` 59/12 · `types.py` 81/14 — 207 stmt / 36 branch, 0 missing) captured via `pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=100`; 67 tests pass, ZERO warnings (`-W error`); ruff / ruff-format --check / `mypy --strict brutex/costs/` / `pyright brutex/costs/` all clean; the executor consumer suite (`test_options_executor.py`, 38 passed) green (the polars/`fno_math`-wheel collection errors + the 2 `cli_backfill`/`instrument_loader` failures are PRE-EXISTING environment gaps, reproduced on the clean tree, unrelated to this change). **Files:** `brutex/costs/calculator.py`, `brutex/costs/types.py`, `brutex/costs/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/test_costs_calculator.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (`constants.py` UNCHANGED). **Decision ID:** DEC-COSTS-HARDEN-PAISA-001. **Builds on:** DEC-COST-001/002/003/004 (the locked rate/rounding decisions this preserves), DEC-EXEC-008 (the BUY-only policy that makes the short-side path unused), DEC-RISK-011 (the intraday-only NORMAL_CLOSE lock that makes the outcome guard safe), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the `brutex.money` ROUND_HALF_UP semantics the helpers now match). **Part of:** the costs deep-audit hardening — close the latent/forward-compat defects without touching the live NORMAL_CLOSE numbers.
