## DEC-RESAMPLE-BOUND-GLOB-001 (2026-06-27)

939. **DEC-RESAMPLE-BOUND-GLOB-001 — the post-pull 1-day derivation read is BOUNDED to ONLY the `<yyyy>/<mm>.parquet` month partitions the pulled window covers, instead of EAGERLY reading each symbol's WHOLE 1-minute partition tree and filtering in memory — `O(lake-depth)` per symbol → `O(pulled-window)`, byte-identical output** (2026-06-27, scalability fix #2 — the always-on 1m→1d derive must not re-read years of minute history on every pull). **Why (verified file:line):** `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py::make_lake_read_1m_window._read` did an eager `pl.read_parquet(base.as_posix() + "/**/*.parquet")` over the ENTIRE `<lake_root>/bars/<exch>/<seg>/<sym>/1minute/**` tree and THEN filtered to the derive target's IST `[start, end)` span in memory. So `_resample_daily_after_pull` (`pull_controller.py`, one `DailyDeriveTarget(start=start, end=end)` per pulled instrument) re-read each symbol's full multi-year minute history every pull just to derive a few days of `1day` — the scan cost scaled with total stored depth, not the pulled window. **What shipped (READ-SIDE ONLY; NO write/schema/engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) NEW pure `ist_span_partition_months(start, end)` — the UTC `(year, month)` partitions an IST `[start, end)` span can touch. The 1-minute lake partitions by **UTC** `(year, month)` (`partition.partition_for_timestamp`) while the reader filters by each bar's **IST trading date** `(ts_utc + 05:30).date()`; an intraday spot bar (09:15–15:30 IST = 03:45–10:00 UTC) keeps the SAME calendar day in both zones, so its UTC partition month equals its IST month, and the covering partitions are exactly the UTC months the IST date range covers. The span is PADDED one calendar day on each side before the month set is collected, so even a hypothetical future / non-spot bar sitting within 05:30 of a UTC month boundary (IST date ≠ UTC month) is never globbed out — the pad adds at most the immediately-adjacent month, so the result stays `O(pulled-window)`. An empty/inverted span (`end <= start`) → `[]`. (2) NEW `ist_span_partition_files(base, start, end)` — the EXISTING `<base>/<yyyy>/<mm>.parquet` files for those months as POSIX strings ready for `polars.read_parquet`; an absent month is skipped cleanly. (3) `make_lake_read_1m_window._read` now reads ONLY `ist_span_partition_files(...)` (a no-covered-file result returns the SAME empty schema-frame as before — a clean no-op), with the in-memory IST-date `[start, end)` filter kept as the precise final cut. **Byte-correctness (the latest-wins safety net):** the derived `1day` partition is written `merge_mode="latest-wins"` (DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 / FIX-2), so a narrowed re-derive that re-reads only the pulled months still self-heals a daily an earlier partial-session pull wrote — AND, because intraday bars never cross the UTC midnight, the narrowed read sees EVERY minute bar whose IST date lands in the span (no daily bar ever needs minute bars from an untouched month), so the resampled `1day` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the old whole-tree read. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ `O(lake-depth)` → `O(pulled-window)` on the post-pull DERIVATION read only (the pull's own fetch + the lake-write are unchanged); ✅ byte-IDENTICAL output — proven by a multi-month + cross-year fixture comparing the bounded reader's `resample_1m_to_daily` bars against a verbatim replica of the old whole-tree read across single-day / cross-year / single-month / absent spans; ✅ read-side only — no stored-bar / schema / idempotence / engine / scope / vocab / rate change; ✅ the one-day pad is a cheap correctness belt-and-suspenders, NOT a perf cost (≤ 1 extra adjacent month). **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad venv, Python 3.12):** `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py` ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean; the module at **100% line+branch** (137/34, 0 missing); NEW unit tests `TestIstSpanPartitionMonths` (single/multi-month, cross-year rollover, empty/inverted, first-of-month pad, Jan→prior-Dec pad) + `TestIstSpanPartitionFiles` (existing-covered-only, absent-month skip, empty span, cross-year, missing base) + NEW integration `test_bounded_read_reads_strictly_fewer_files_than_whole_tree` (spies `polars.read_parquet`: a single-day span reads STRICTLY fewer files than the 5-month tree, never the far-past 2024 month) + `test_bounded_read_byte_identical_to_whole_tree`; 42 module tests + 217 related (daily-resample / partition) suites GREEN. **File-count evidence:** on a 5-month fixture the whole-tree read globbed all 5 partition files for EVERY span; the bounded read touches 1 (single-month), 2 (single-day / cross-year), or 0 (absent span) — never the whole tree. **Files:** `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py`, `tests/unit/test_spot_daily_resample.py`, `tests/integration/test_spot_daily_resample_roundtrip.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-RESAMPLE-BOUND-GLOB-001. **Builds on:** DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853 (the always-on 1m→1d derive + the latest-wins write merge this narrows safely), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 #860 (the same month-bounded-read pattern on the `/movers` cold read, `lake_day_glob`), DEC-DB-UNIVERSE-O1-LATENCY-001 #863 (the date-span-bounded read pattern on the `/db` candle pager). **Part of:** the pull-side scalability work — the post-pull derivation no longer re-scans the whole lake per symbol.
937. **DEC-LAKE-WRITE-INSTRUMENT-001 — the lake-write / append boundary now emits structured telemetry so the pull's serial-write cost (the throughput bottleneck DOWNSTREAM of fetching the 28-hour pull-log forensic could only INFER) becomes a measurable fact: `ParquetWriter.write` emits one `lake.partition.write` event per successful partition write (`append_ms` / `lock_wait_ms` / `rows` / `partition_rows` / `partition`), and the resolved connection-pool width is logged once at pull start as `pull.pool_size` — INSTRUMENTATION ONLY, it does NOT itself speed up the pull** (2026-06-27, the operator's "instrument the lake-write so we can SIZE the write-overlap fix honestly", the forensics-recommended #1 next fix supporting DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP Lever 1 sizing). **Why (the gap):** the 28-hour pull-log forensic proved the achieved rate (~2.8 r/s) sat well under the allowed ceiling (~4.6 r/s) with a 1.74 r/s slack 94% of the time and connections idle 74% — a DOWNSTREAM serial-write bottleneck — yet the writer emitted ZERO append/latency/lock telemetry (0 such events across 343,914 log lines), so the lake-write cost could only be inferred, and the forensic even mis-inferred the pool width ("pool=2" from `in_flight` peaks that actually reached 7) because the resolved pool size was never logged. Without a measured per-write cost the `write_consumer` (DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP Lever 1) could not be sized or gated honestly. **What shipped (ADDITIVE instrumentation only; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py::ParquetWriter.write` (the writer `ParquetBarSink` uses for BOTH spot AND F&O candles) now emits ONE `lake.partition.write` structlog `info` per successful partition write carrying `append_ms` (the serial read-modify-write wall time, lock-wait EXCLUDED), `lock_wait_ms` (lock-acquire time), `rows` (bars appended in this batch), `partition_rows` (the FULL merged partition size — the disk-write-cost signal), and `partition` (the path); the event is emitted AFTER both locks are released (timed via `time.perf_counter` deltas, no I/O in the critical section), so it can NEVER extend the serialised write — the lock order/scope (ExitStack: cross-process `flock` nested in the per-partition `threading.Lock`) is byte-UNCHANGED, and the merge / keep-first / 2dp-snap semantics + the stored bytes + the existing `raw_hash` are byte-identical; (2) NEW `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py::_emit_pull_pool_size` logs the resolved `resolve_pool_size()` once at pull start as `pull.pool_size`, wired into BOTH `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles`; the emission is GUARDED (`try/except` logs `pull.pool_size_emit_failed` and continues) so a `resolve_pool_size()` error can never crash the pull. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** 🟡 PARTIAL — this is INSTRUMENTATION ONLY; it does NOT itself speed up the pull or change throughput. It makes the serial lake-write cost MEASURABLE so the `write_consumer` (DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP Lever 1) can be sized + benchmark-gated honestly; the actual overlap is a SEPARATE, benchmark-gated PR (the `bench_write_rate(W) > 3.2/s` gate of #921), NOT claimed here. ✅ O(1): one `info` per PARTITION write (never per bar); ✅ a multi-partition `ParquetBarSink` batch emits one event per physical partition write; ✅ an idempotent re-pull (no rewrite) STILL emits one event reporting the unchanged partition; ✅ best-effort `pull.pool_size` emission can never crash the pull; ✅ does NOT touch the separate `OptionParquetWriter` (the F&O CANDLE lake already rides the instrumented `ParquetWriter` via `ParquetBarSink(segment="FNO")`); ✅ a CLI-pull `pull.pool_size` emission + the `write_consumer` overlap primitive are deferred FOLLOW-UPS. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27):** `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py` at **100% line+branch** (143/0 stmt + 22/0 branch) + `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` at **100% line+branch** (415/0 stmt + 96/0 branch), captured via `pytest --cov`; NEW unit tests `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py::TestLakePartitionWriteTelemetry` (fresh / merge / no-op / multi-partition — captures real structlog output from a real `ParquetWriter.write` against a tmp lake) + `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py::TestEmitPullPoolSize` (happy + env-override + swallowed-failure), 7 new tests GREEN; 189 ingest/sink/F&O-smoke tests GREEN; ruff check + ruff format --check + pyright clean on all 4 touched files; `mypy --strict` clean on the two touched `brutex/` modules (the residual mypy noise is pre-existing `growwapi`-stub artifacts in untouched `auth.py`/`reauth.py`). **Files:** `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-LAKE-WRITE-INSTRUMENT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (the serial-write slack this telemetry sizes for Lever 1), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the cross-process `flock` + per-partition lock whose order/scope this leaves byte-unchanged), DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001 #932 (the pull-health observability surface these events feed). **Part of:** the §11 AUTOMATED observability promise (logging pillar) — the lake-write bottleneck is now a measured fact, not an inference.

## DEC-SWEEP-DEDUP-LMDB-001 (2026-06-27)

957. **DEC-SWEEP-DEDUP-LMDB-001 — sweep recoverability + reproducibility hardening (engine): (GAP #2) the production grid sweep's exact-confirm combo dedup is now the OFF-HEAP `LmdbMembership` (not an unbounded in-memory `set()` that OOMs the 48 GB envelope), (GAP #16) an out-of-range condition bit is rejected at CONFIG TIME instead of failing late as a bare `ValueError` aborting the whole grid, and (GAP #17) `-0.0` collapses to `+0.0` in param canonicalisation so two mathematically-equal params hash to ONE run-identity** (2026-06-27, the sweep recoverability/reproducibility batch). **Why (verified file:line):** (#2) `brutex/cli.py::cmd_sweep_all` (and the `cmd_sweep_verify --recount` shadow re-sweep) built `ComboDedup(OptionDedupIndex(...))` with the DEFAULT in-memory `set()` exact tier — a production grid enumerates `O(combos)` BLAKE3 run-identities, so the set grows unbounded and OOMs (the SAME `SweepCache.open` already wires LMDB for the tuple tier). (#16) `SweepRunConfig.__post_init__` validated `k <= count(condition_bits)` but NOT that each bit is in `[0, 64)`; an out-of-range bit slipped past to the LAZY `iter_masks_k_of_bits` generator and raised a bare `ValueError` mid-enumeration, which the grid loop does NOT catch (only `SweepComboError` is a tuple-skip) → the whole grid aborts. (#17) `strategies/combo._canonicalise_value` did `return repr(value)` for floats — `repr(-0.0)` is `"-0.0"` but `repr(0.0)` is `"0.0"`, so a `-0.0` param split one run into two distinct run-identities (breaks reproducibility / Golden Rule #4). **What shipped (ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change, CLAUDE.md §3):** (#2) BOTH production launch sites now open `LmdbMembership.open(out_root / "combo-dedup")` (recount: `scratch / "combo-dedup"`) inside the existing `with`-block and inject it as `OptionDedupIndex(exact=...)` — the env is closed deterministically by the context manager, mirroring the `SweepCache.open` tuple-tier pattern; DEFENSIVELY, `sweep_run.run_persisted_sweep` now SKIPS the unconditional advisory `dedup.mark_many` when `bypass_dedup` is true (the digest path never consults the probes, so marking is a pure wasted `O(survivors)` write to the off-heap LMDB tier — the completion sentinel is the redo authority, so `n_marked` honestly reads 0). (#16) `SweepRunConfig.__post_init__` AND `SweepGridConfig.__post_init__` now validate every condition bit `∈ [0, MAX_VOCAB_BITS=64)` and raise a config-time `ValueError` (the CLI already catches it → clean `EXIT_USER_ERROR`), so a bad bit can never reach the lazy enumeration. (#17) `_canonicalise_value` normalises signed zero with `value = value + 0.0` (exact / bit-unchanged for every other finite double — only the sign of zero changes) BEFORE `repr`, mirroring the `results_store.py:303` / `trial_stats.py:209` precedent. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ off-heap LMDB membership keeps per-op RAM `O(1)` regardless of combo count (the OOM this removes); ✅ the bit-range check is a pure config-time fail-fast — an in-range grid is byte-unchanged; ✅ the `-0.0 → +0.0` collapse is NOT rounding (only the sign of zero is normalised), proven byte-equal to the `+0.0` form; ✅ the `bypass_dedup` mark-skip changes only an ADVISORY write on the sentinel-authoritative digest path (resume correctness unchanged — the paired completion sentinel still short-circuits a redo); ✅ the CLI shims (`cmd_sweep_all` / `cmd_sweep_verify`) are `# pragma: no cover` orchestration shims, so the wiring is validated FUNCTIONALLY by a new end-to-end integration test. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad venv, Python 3.12):** `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py` + `brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py` + `brutex/strategies/combo.py` ALL at **100% line+branch** (251/72, 220/68, 56/38; 0 missing) captured via `pytest --cov`; ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on all touched files (the residual mypy noise is pre-existing `growwapi`-stub artifacts in untouched `auth.py`/`reauth.py`). NEW tests: `test_engine_sweep_run.py` bit-range rejection (`[0,1,99]` / boundary 64 / negative / top-in-range) + the `bypass_dedup`-skips-`mark_many` regression (a crash-on-mark dedup is NEVER invoked) + `n_marked == 0` on the digest path; `test_engine_sweep_orchestrator.py` grid-level bit-range rejection; `test_strategies_combo.py` signed-zero collapse (flat / nested / list / run-identity); NEW `tests/integration/test_cli_sweep_all_dedup.py` drives the REAL `cmd_sweep_all` against a tiny lake and asserts the injected exact tier is an `LmdbMembership` (NOT a `set`) + the `combo-dedup` LMDB dir is created. **Files:** `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py`, `brutex/strategies/combo.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_run.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_orchestrator.py`, `tests/unit/test_strategies_combo.py`, `tests/integration/test_cli_sweep_all_dedup.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-DEDUP-LMDB-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MARK-MANY-SENTINEL-001 (the completion-sentinel redo authority the `bypass_dedup` mark-skip relies on), DEC-ENGINE-TUPLE-SKIP-RESILIENT-001 #904 (the `SweepComboError`-only tuple-skip the config-time bit check fronts), DEC-MASK-IDENTITY-001 (the 9-field run-identity the signed-zero collapse keeps reproducible). **Part of:** the sweep recoverability + reproducibility hardening (engine) — the production sweep no longer OOMs on combo dedup, no longer aborts mid-grid on a bad bit, and no longer splits an equal param into two run-identities.

## DEC-ORCH-AUDIT-RATE-HARDEN-001 (2026-06-27)

968. **DEC-ORCH-AUDIT-RATE-HARDEN-001 — the orchestrator audit hash-chain, FSM rate-limiter and quota tracker are hardened against four confirmed defects a deep-audit found: (B) a `|`-delimiter collision could make two distinct audit triples flatten to ONE hash-preimage; (D) a tampered NON-FINITE (NaN/Infinity) payload surfaced as a raw `AuditPayloadError` instead of the documented `AuditChainCorruption`; (G) the rate-limiter upshift was gated on the WRONG (`downshift_window`) timer instead of the documented `upshift_recovery` window; (J) a corrupt-state construction failure leaked the shared LMDB env refcount — all fixed with no hash-byte change and no engine/scope/vocab/rate change** (2026-06-27, orchestrator deep-audit batch). **Why (the four confirmed defects, verified file:line):** **FIX B (audit `|`-collision, MAJOR)** — `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py::AuditEntry.compute_hash` joins `actor`/`action`/`subject` into the BLAKE-preimage with a literal `b"|"`, so any `|` INSIDE a free-form field made the encoding non-injective (`action="A|B", subject="C"` and `action="A", subject="B|C"` both flatten to `…|A|B|C|…` → ONE hash) — a latent forgery/collision surface. **FIX D (NaN-payload tamper, MAJOR)** — `verify_chain` re-parses each on-disk line; a tampered payload carrying a non-finite `NaN`/`Infinity` raised the LOW-LEVEL `AuditPayloadError` straight out of `from_json_line`, so a corrupt chain looked like a parse bug instead of the documented `AuditChainCorruption(seq)` the doctor/CLI catch. **FIX G (rate-limiter upshift gate, MAJOR)** — `brutex/orchestrator/rate_limiter.py` gated the recovery upshift on the `downshift_window` timer (dead/wrong) rather than the documented `upshift_recovery` window keyed off `_last_429_at`, so the limiter could upshift too eagerly after a 429 (or never, depending on the two windows' relation). **FIX J (quota env-refcount leak, MINOR)** — `brutex/orchestrator/quota_tracker.py::__post_init__` incremented the shared-`_ENV_REGISTRY` refcount BEFORE `_read_state`, which raises `QuotaInvariantError` on a corrupt persisted state; the constructor then re-raised so the instance never bound, `close()` was unreachable, and the `(env, refcount)` entry leaked — growing on every corrupt load. **What shipped (orchestrator hardening; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change):** (1) FIX B — a NEW `AuditFieldError(BruteXError)` + an `AuditEntry.__post_init__` guard that REJECTS any `|` in `actor`/`action`/`subject` at construction (the field alphabet is constrained so the sole preimage delimiter can never appear inside a field), naming the offending field + value; `append` and `from_json_line` raise it before the chain is touched, so a `|`-bearing row is refused, never silently stored, and the BLAKE preimage stays injective — proven byte-for-byte UNCHANGED for all conforming rows (the golden hash is identical). The one in-scope production audit-subject that joined a `(symbol, window)` pair with `|` (`brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py::_record_give_up`) now uses `~` (a deliberate, readable, non-delimiter separator), and the matching best-effort `_fire_give_up` log message format was switched `|`→`~` for consistency (a structlog message, NOT an audit field). (2) FIX D — `verify_chain` now maps a non-finite/`NaN` tampered-payload `AuditPayloadError` to `AuditChainCorruption(seq)` so the documented corruption type reaches the doctor/CLI verifiers unchanged (no edit to either caller). (3) FIX G — the upshift now honors the documented `upshift_recovery` window via `_last_429_at` (the dead `downshift_window` gate removed). (4) FIX J — `__post_init__` wraps the post-refcount body and RELEASES the shared env reference on any construction failure (mirroring `close()`'s teardown exactly) before re-raising, so a corrupt-state construction never orphans the refcount. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ FIX B constrains the field ALPHABET (reject `|`) rather than adopting a formal length-prefixed encoding — sufficient because `|` is the SOLE preimage delimiter, so forbidding it inside a field restores injectivity with zero hash-format change (a length-prefix is a larger, breaking re-design, NOT done); ✅ a `verify_chain` over the whole log stays O(n) by nature — each link's hash recompute + compare is O(1), the WHOLE-LOG verify is O(number-of-rows), stated as such (not an O(1)-total claim); ✅ FIX D maps the type at verify-time only — it does not change what bytes are written or the live hash; ✅ FIX B re-verified hash-byte-IDENTICAL for every conforming triple (the golden); ✅ the IDENTICAL `b"|"`-join recipe in `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py::SweepAuditEntry` has the SAME latent collision and is a flagged COMMON follow-up deliberately left UNTOUCHED (out of orchestrator scope, Golden Rule #3). **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, `brutex/orchestrator/rate_limiter.py`, `brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py` and `brutex/orchestrator/quota_tracker.py` each at **100% line+branch**, the full orchestrator test set 1895 passing; ruff + ruff-format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the touched files; NEW regression tests — `test_golden_hash_unchanged_by_the_guard` (FIX B byte-identity), the `|`-collision rejection tests (historical collision pair both rejected + pipe-in-actor/action/subject + the error names field+value + a property test that distinct pipe-free triples never collide), `test_chain_corruption_is_not_payload_error` + the parametrized NaN/Infinity/-Infinity tampered-payload → `AuditChainCorruption` (FIX D), `test_upshift_gated_on_upshift_recovery_not_downshift_window` + the recovery-edge tests (FIX G), and the quota env-leak tests (`test_corrupt_construct_releases_env_refcount` + repeated-corrupt-constructs-do-not-grow-registry + good-tracker-coexists-after-corrupt-release, FIX J) — each FAILS without its fix. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, `brutex/orchestrator/rate_limiter.py`, `brutex/orchestrator/quota_tracker.py`, `brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py`, `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_audit.py`, `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_rate_limiter.py`, `tests/unit/test_quota_tracker.py`, `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_retry_storm_watchdog.py`, `tests/unit/test_audit_verify.py`, `tests/integration/test_retry_storm_watchdog_integration.py`, `tests/property/test_audit_chain_properties.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-ORCH-AUDIT-RATE-HARDEN-001. **Builds on:** the orchestrator audit/rate/quota modules. **Part of:** the orchestrator deep-audit hardening.

## DEC-FNO-TF-DERIVE-OI-001 (2026-06-27)

954. **DEC-FNO-TF-DERIVE-OI-001 — the F&O (futures + options) internal timeframes — the derived `1day` AND the 19 intraday TFs — are now derived from the stored F&O 1-minute the SAME way spot already is, but OPEN-INTEREST-CORRECT: the ONE canonical session-anchored resampler (`brutex/data/tf_resampler.py::resample_1m_to_tf`) is generalized to carry an OPTIONAL `open_interest` column with carry-last (snapshot) semantics, so 5m / daily / multi-day F&O buckets carry the bucket's LAST source bar's OI (NEVER summed), while spot output stays byte-identical (no OI column added)** (2026-06-27). **Why (the grounded gap):** the F&O 1m→1day derive ALREADY existed and was wired (`historical_pull._derive_daily_from_minute` → the shared `spot_daily_resample.derive_daily_for_targets`), but it LOST open interest by construction — `resample_1m_to_tf` aggregated only OHLCV (no OI in its `.agg()`), `resample_1m_to_daily` HARDCODED `open_interest=None` (correct for cash spot, WRONG for F&O), and `make_lake_read_1m_window` never read the OI column — so the derived F&O `1day` stored `OI=None` while only the fetched 1-minute carried true OI (`movers_futures._read_future_session` had to BYPASS the shared reader specifically because it "DROPS open_interest"). **What shipped (lake/derive-only; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY, the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX — CLAUDE.md §3; NO fetch/scope/vocab/rate change):** (1) `tf_resampler.resample_1m_to_tf` gains a `has_oi = "open_interest" in df.columns` gate that conditionally appends `pl.col("open_interest").last()` — the EXACT carry-last rule `feed/resampler.py:237` already proves ("snapshot semantics"), a STOCK not a FLOW; a null source OI yields a null bucket OI (preserved, never fabricated as 0); the spot 6-column path is byte-identical. (2) NEW `brutex/data/fno_daily_resample.py::resample_1m_to_fno_daily` — the F&O twin of `resample_1m_to_daily`, identical OHLCV aggregation + midnight-IST re-stamp + forming-session `before` guard, EXCEPT it reads the carry-last OI (`None if absent/null else int(...)`, with a defensive `"open_interest" in columns` guard) instead of hardcoding `None`. (3) NEW `brutex/data/fno_resample.py::derive_fno_intraday_tfs` (the F&O twin of `spot_resample.derive_intraday_tfs` — `resample_all_21_tfs` then drop `{1m, 1d}`, OI carried) + `resample_session_to_tf` (the on-the-fly /movers read path: RENAMES the lake `timestamp -> ts_utc` the resampler requires, resamples OI-aware, and DROPS the trailing FORMING/partial bucket whose `bucket_start + M > cutoff` — no look-ahead, Property P-06). (4) `spot_daily_resample.make_lake_read_1m_window(include_oi=True)` appends `open_interest` to BOTH the `.select(...)` AND the empty-schema fallback frame (`pl.Int64`); the shared daily driver gains an injectable `resample_fn` seam (default = spot OI-None, F&O injects the carry-last positional adapter) so ONE driver serves both — NO second resampler (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). (5) `historical_pull._derive_daily_from_minute` binds `include_oi=True` + `resample_fn=resample_1m_to_fno_daily_positional`, so the stored derived F&O `1day` partition now carries true last-of-day OI. **OI convention (operator-confirmed default, stated HONESTLY — Golden Rule #10):** OI = LAST value in the bucket / last-of-day for daily — the standard in-repo convention (`feed/resampler.py:237` + `movers_futures._read_future_session` both carry last) AND the only OI derivable from 1-minute candles; true exchange end-of-session SETTLEMENT OI is a SEPARATE vendor field we do NOT fetch and is OUT OF SCOPE — NEVER fabricated. HONEST edge (pinned by a golden + integration test): if the LAST 1-minute bar of a session has a null OI, the derived daily OI is null even though earlier bars carried real OI (consistent with carry-last, no fabrication). **Backfill HONESTY (Golden Rule #10):** this does NOT retroactively rewrite on-disk derived F&O `1day` partitions written before this change (they carry `OI=None`); they self-HEAL on the NEXT pull via the existing `merge_mode="latest-wins"` overwrite (`_bar_values_equal` compares `open_interest`, so a re-derive with real OI supersedes the stale None). A one-time re-derive backfill was deliberately NOT shipped (it is not small/self-contained — it would re-scan every stored F&O 1-minute partition); heal-on-next-pull is explicitly accepted. **O(1) / streaming (HONEST):** per contract the resample is a SINGLE linear pass with O(1) memory per open bucket (one running open/high/low/close/volume/last-OI accumulator); the per-bar/per-bucket hot-op cost is FLAT as bars scale 1K→1M (bench gate). This is explicitly NOT an O(1)-TOTAL claim — total work is O(Σ bars) = O(total stored 1m), stated as such. **Scope of the on-the-fly read:** the stored `1day` OI fix lands immediately (a physical partition); the `/movers` as-of session snapshot is documented as the honest partial-as-of (corrected_point #1b) and the TRUE per-TF resampled F&O bar is the new COMMON `resample_session_to_tf` (corrected_point #1a, trailing forming bucket dropped); on-the-fly intraday F&O in `/db` is OUT OF SCOPE (a flagged fast-follow — `db_view` does not import the resampler today). **Tests (7 types):** `tf_resampler` / `fno_daily_resample` / `fno_resample` / `spot_daily_resample` ALL 100% line+branch; an OI-last golden (5m + 1day, OI = last NOT sum/first/max); a sparse/illiquid-minute gap (empty bucket → NO bar); an expiry partial-session day; an IST↔UTC month-boundary derive; a hypothesis idempotence/byte-identity property test (re-derive == bit-identical, prices Decimal-exact, OI int-exact); the specific "real OI all session, null only on the FINAL bar → daily OI null" case (corrected_point #5); an O(1)-streaming bench (per-bar cost flat 1K→1M, p99 ratio ≤ ceiling); and a real-lake integration test proving the wired derive carries last-of-day OI end-to-end (incl. month-boundary + partial-session self-heal). 7 touched source files at 100% line+branch; ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on the touched files; 1366 related tests green.
