## DEC-METRICS-NONFINITE-GUARD-001 (2026-06-27)

969. **DEC-METRICS-NONFINITE-GUARD-001 — defense-in-depth non-finite (NaN/±inf) INPUT guards across the Stage-4 statistical-validity leaves (`brutex/metrics/`), so each function honors its own documented "no NaN/inf in result rows" contract (spec line 746) at its OWN boundary instead of relying on the caller to pre-screen; plus two docstring/comment accuracy fixes — READ-ONLY robustness, byte-identical for every in-domain input, every formula independently verified CORRECT (no correctness bug found)** (2026-06-27). **Why (the gaps, verified file:line; each was a real path that returns/leaks a non-finite value where the docstring promises a clean degrade):** (1) `deflated_sharpe.probabilistic_sharpe_ratio` — the `radicand <= 0.0` guard is BYPASSED by a NaN moment (`nan <= 0` is `False`) and by `observed_sharpe = +inf` (which makes the radicand `+inf`, also passing the guard), so a NaN/inf `observed_sharpe`/`benchmark_sharpe`/`skew`/`kurtosis` silently returned `NaN` from the final CDF, contradicting the function's own "surfaced rather than silently returning NaN" docstring. (2) `cpcv.sharpe_of_returns` + `cpcv._combine_moments` — the inputs are individually finite (so `_validate_returns` admits them), but for `|returns| ≳ 1e154` the squared-deviation accumulation OVERFLOWS to `inf`/`nan`; the bare `variance <= 0.0` guard is `False` for `inf` (→ wrong `mean/sqrt(inf) == 0.0` from `sharpe_of_returns`) and `False` for `nan` (→ `mean/sqrt(nan) == nan` LEAKED into the `cpcv_pass_rate` fold count from `_combine_moments`). (3) `pbo._validate` — a NaN/inf cell in the performance matrix would fabricate a finite mid-rank (the CSCV ranking silently corrupts), with no validation reject despite the module's explicit validation philosophy. (4) `types.EquityCurve.__post_init__` — the float `span_years` guard `<= 0.0` is `False` for `nan` (a NaN span would later annualise CAGR to NaN) and for `+inf` (silently flattens CAGR), the one genuine gap mypy cannot catch (the int paisa fields are already statically NaN-proof by the `int` type contract + `mypy --strict`). (5) `monte_carlo` — the docstring + inline comment CLAIMED a non-finite permuted statistic is "treated as did not beat", but `+inf >= observed` is `True`, so a `+inf` permutation IS counted as beating the observed (which only RAISES the p-value — the conservative direction); only NaN/`-inf` are did-not-beat. **What shipped (READ-ONLY robustness; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX — CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) `probabilistic_sharpe_ratio` raises `ValueError("PSR inputs must be finite; …")` after the `sample_length` check and before the radicand, when any of the four moment inputs is non-finite. (2) `sharpe_of_returns` + `_combine_moments` change `if variance <= 0.0` → `if not math.isfinite(variance) or variance <= 0.0` → honest `None` (degrade), byte-identical for every in-domain input. (3) `pbo._validate` adds a finiteness sweep (after the raggedness check, before the modulo check) raising `ValueError("performance matrix has a non-finite entry at [r][c]: …")`. (4) `EquityCurve.__post_init__` changes `if self.span_years <= 0.0` → `if not math.isfinite(self.span_years) or self.span_years <= 0.0` (existing error message kept verbatim, so any `match=` test still passes); the int paisa fields are documented as relying on the `int` type contract for finiteness, NOT runtime-guarded (an isfinite check on an `int` adds an unreachable branch). (5) `monte_carlo` docstring + comment reworded to state the CORRECT behaviour (NaN/`-inf` did-not-beat; `+inf` counts as beating → p-value up, conservative); the `>=` comparison + `pvalue < alpha` logic UNCHANGED. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ every guarded path is UNREACHABLE in production today — the Stage-4 callers pre-screen their inputs — so this is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH so each leaf honors its OWN contract at its OWN boundary, NOT a fix for an observed production failure; ✅ every formula was independently re-verified CORRECT against its cited source (Bailey & LdP 2012/2014 PSR/DSR; López de Prado AFML CPCV; Bailey et al. 2017 CSCV; Phipson & Smyth 2010 permutation p-value) — there is NO correctness bug, only the missing non-finite REJECT/DEGRADE; ✅ byte-identical for all in-domain inputs (the in-domain unit/golden/property suites are unchanged and green); ✅ READ-ONLY metrics — no lake/pull/engine/scope/vocab/rate change. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** all FIVE touched `brutex/metrics/` files at **100% line+branch** captured via `pytest --cov=brutex.metrics --cov-branch` (`deflated_sharpe.py` 43/12, `cpcv.py` 124/40, `pbo.py` 105/42, `types.py` 48/20, `monte_carlo.py` 42/18 — 0 missing each); NEW/extended tests across the 7 types — unit (PSR non-finite parametrize; `sharpe_of_returns` overflow→None; `cpcv_pass_rate` overflow-magnitude→finite; PBO NaN/inf cell at `[1][2]`; `EquityCurve` NaN/inf span; monte_carlo `+inf` beats / `-inf` did-not-beat), property/hypothesis (PSR rejects any non-finite moment; `sharpe_of_returns` never non-finite; `cpcv_pass_rate` finite in [0,1] + determinism; WFO index-level no-look-ahead `max(train)<min(test)`; PBO all-logits-finite + determinism), golden (`sharpe_of_returns` fixed-series population-Sharpe constant `0.3234983196103152` full-precision + overflow→None); ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict brutex/metrics` + `pyright brutex/metrics` clean on every touched source + test file; the full metrics-related suite (`-k "metric or cpcv or wfo or pbo or spa or lockbox or monte_carlo or cascade or deflated_sharpe"`) 802 passed / 3 skipped (the 3 skips are an unrelated missing optional `cma` dep). **Files:** `brutex/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py`, `brutex/metrics/cpcv.py`, `brutex/metrics/pbo.py`, `brutex/metrics/types.py`, `brutex/metrics/monte_carlo.py`, `tests/unit/test_deflated_sharpe.py`, `tests/unit/test_cpcv.py`, `tests/unit/test_pbo.py`, `tests/unit/test_metrics_compute.py`, `tests/unit/test_monte_carlo.py`, `tests/property/test_deflated_sharpe_properties.py`, `tests/property/test_cpcv_wfo_properties.py`, `tests/property/test_pbo_properties.py`, `tests/golden/test_cpcv_wfo_golden.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-METRICS-NONFINITE-GUARD-001. **Part of:** the robustness-hardening arc — each statistical leaf honors its own "no NaN/inf in result rows" contract at its own boundary (defense-in-depth, not a caller-trust assumption).

## DEC-CORRUPT-PARTITION-READ-RESILIENT-001 (2026-06-27)

950. **DEC-CORRUPT-PARTITION-READ-RESILIENT-001 — a single corrupt / unreadable EXISTING Parquet partition can no longer crash a whole pull, a whole sweep load, or the `/movers` default poll: the four unguarded existing-partition reads (spot merge, option merge, catalog reconcile, latest-movers-date) are wrapped over the COMMON unreadable-Parquet skip set and either QUARANTINE that one symbol/contract or DEGRADE that one read, while every other unit proceeds; the unbounded per-partition lock intern is also capacity-bounded; PLUS the no-op spot merge no longer re-reads the partition a second time** (2026-06-27, the corrupt-existing-partition read-resilience hardening batch — the read-side twin of the corrupt-file skips already shipped for the `/movers` candidate loops #886 and the `/db` coverage aggregate). **Why (the four unguarded reads + two adjacent gaps, verified file:line):** **GAP 1 (MAJOR)** — `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py::ParquetWriter._read_existing_bars` (`pl.read_parquet(dest)`) and `brutex/data/option_parquet_writer.py::OptionParquetWriter._merge_partition` (`pl.read_parquet(dest)`) read the EXISTING month partition UNGUARDED on every steady-state re-pull, so ONE corrupt / version-incompatible Parquet on disk raised a `PolarsError` out of the merge and crashed the WHOLE pull (every other symbol's window died with it). **GAP 9 (MAJOR)** — `brutex/data/catalog_reconcile.py::reconcile_catalog_from_lake`'s per-file `pl.read_parquet(path, columns=["timestamp"])` (+ `.min()`/`.max()`/`read_bytes()`) was UNGUARDED and runs at the START of EVERY sweep load + F&O window derivation, so one corrupt partition aborted the entire reconcile. **GAP 4 (MAJOR)** — `brutex/dashboard/movers_warm.py::latest_movers_date`'s DuckDB `MAX` over the spot 1day glob was UNGUARDED and backs the DEFAULT (no-date) `/api/v1/movers` poll, so a corrupt 1day Parquet 500'd the whole page; it was ALSO called BLOCKING on the event loop (`app.py:3306`) and re-run on every default poll. **GAP 11 (MINOR)** — the spot no-op merge path (`added == 0 & not rewrite`) did `dest.read_bytes()` + `dest.stat()` a SECOND time OUTSIDE `lake_write_guard` purely to hash a partition it had ALREADY loaded — an unguarded OOM site on a deep partition. **GAP 19 (NIT)** — both writers' `_PARTITION_LOCKS` dict interned one `threading.Lock` per partition path FOREVER, so a full multi-year pull accumulated 10^5–10^6 `Lock` objects. **What shipped (READ-SIDE / lock-side resilience; NO write-schema / stored-bar / engine / scope / vocab / rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) NEW COMMON `brutex/data/errors.py::parquet_read_skip_errors()` — the ONE data-layer source of truth for the unreadable-Parquet skip set (`polars.exceptions.PolarsError` + `OSError`, NARROW so a real code bug still propagates, Golden Rule #1); the dashboard twin `brutex/dashboard/movers_resilient.movers_read_skip_errors` now DELEGATES to it and WIDENS with `duckdb.Error` (no copy-pasted set). (2) GAP 1 — both writers wrap the existing-partition parse in `try/except parquet_read_skip_errors()` → raise a QUARANTINABLE `WriterError` / `OptionWriterError` naming the corrupt path (NOT in either ingest spine's `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS`, so the spine skips that one symbol/contract and proceeds); the parse stays INSIDE `lake_write_guard` so `MemoryError`/ENOSPC still escalate to a pull-wide `LakeWriteHalt` (never demoted to a quarantine — `LakeWriteHalt` is a `DataLakeError`, not in the skip set), and a non-ENOSPC `OSError` reading the spot partition bytes also quarantines (`unreadable existing partition`). (3) GAP 9 — the reconcile per-file read is wrapped, logging `catalog.reconcile.parquet_skip` (path + error), incrementing `skipped`, and continuing. (4) GAP 4 — `latest_movers_date` wraps the DuckDB read in `try/except (duckdb.Error, OSError)` returning `None` (degrade = empty/today payload, never a 500); the call is MOVED off the event loop INTO the `_resolve` threadpool closure AND memoised behind `_summary_cache.generation` in a dedicated `_latest_movers_date_cache` (REUSES the COMMON `MoversSnapshotCache`), so a repeat default poll is an O(1) handoff and a pull invalidates it. (5) GAP 11 — `_merge_write` reads the partition's raw bytes ONCE via a new guarded `_read_existing_bytes`, parses the bars from those same bytes, and the no-op path reuses the bytes for the hash/size (no second full read; matches the option writer's no-second-read no-op). (6) GAP 19 — NEW COMMON `brutex/data/partition_lock.py::BoundedLockRegistry` (capacity-bounded LRU intern, refcounted so an IN-USE lock is NEVER evicted — correctness independent of the cap); both writers replace their hand-rolled `_PARTITION_LOCKS` dict + guard + `_partition_lock` with one `BoundedLockRegistry` (`.acquire(dest)` context manager). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ pure DETECT-and-skip / degrade — a corrupt file is QUARANTINED (writers) or the read DEGRADES (reconcile counts it `skipped`; latest-date returns `None`), never a fabricated bar/price and never a silently-swallowed code bug (NARROW skip set); ✅ `MemoryError`/ENOSPC stay a pull-wide `LakeWriteHalt`, never demoted; ✅ GAP 4 memoisation is O(1) on REPEAT default polls only (the first poll after a pull pays one real scan), and the explicit-date path NEVER pays the latest-date scan; ✅ the bounded lock registry caps only IDLE locks — the live in-use set is bounded by the concurrent-writer count, never the partition count, so a held lock is never dropped + re-created (mutual exclusion preserved); ✅ READ-SIDE/lock-side only — no stored-bar / schema / idempotence (byte-parity oracle re-verified) / engine / scope / vocab / rate change. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** all seven touched source modules at **100% line+branch** (`parquet_writer.py` 147/20, `option_parquet_writer.py` 82/14, `catalog_reconcile.py` 58/8, `errors.py` 13/0, `partition_lock.py` 70/6, `movers_warm.py` 29/6, `movers_resilient.py` 9/0 — 408 stmt / 54 branch, 0 missing), captured via `pytest --cov`; NEW regression tests — `TestCorruptExistingPartition` + `TestNoOpReusesExistingBytes` (spot writer: corrupt → `WriterError`, vanished-bytes → `WriterError`, no-second-read, no-op OOM → `LakeWriteHalt`), `TestCorruptExistingPartition` (option writer: corrupt → `OptionWriterError`, one corrupt series does not block a distinct series), `test_corrupt_partition_is_skipped_others_reconcile` (reconcile: good + garbage → reconciled==1 / skipped==1 + the skip log), `test_latest_movers_date_none_on_corrupt_lake` + the `/api/v1/movers` route degrade-not-500 + latest-date-memoised-once-per-generation integration, `TestBoundedLockRegistry` (constructor / serialise / distinct-keys / idle-eviction / in-use-never-evicted / concurrent mutual-exclusion), and the COMMON skip-set delegation test; the parity golden/property/bench legacy-reader stubs updated to the GAP #11 single-read signature (byte-parity preserved); 100% line+branch maintained; ruff / ruff-format --check / `mypy --strict brutex` / `pyright` clean on the touched files. **Files:** `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `brutex/data/option_parquet_writer.py`, `brutex/data/catalog_reconcile.py`, `brutex/data/errors.py`, `brutex/data/partition_lock.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_warm.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_resilient.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_option_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_catalog_reconcile.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_warm.py`, `tests/unit/test_partition_lock.py`, `tests/unit/test_parquet_read_skip_errors.py`, `tests/integration/test_movers_latest_date_resilient.py`, `tests/golden/test_writer_columnar_parity.py`, `tests/property/test_writer_columnar_parity_properties.py`, `tests/bench/test_write_latency.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CORRUPT-PARTITION-READ-RESILIENT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 #886 (the `/movers` candidate-loop corrupt-file skip + the `movers_read_skip_errors` set this generalises into the data layer), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (the `lake_write_guard` ENOSPC/OOM→`LakeWriteHalt` mapping these reads preserve), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the per-partition lock whose intern this bounds), DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001 #878 (the `latest_movers_date` this guards + memoises), DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001 #927 (the columnar merge read this keeps byte-identical). **Part of:** the resilience-hardening arc — one bad on-disk file must never crash a whole pull, a whole sweep load, or the `/movers` page.
## DEC-EXEC-REPRO-RESILIENCE-001 (2026-06-27)

962. **DEC-EXEC-REPRO-RESILIENCE-001** (2026-06-27) — the signal-only Track-1 execution simulator (`brutex/execution/`) is hardened for REPRODUCIBILITY + bad-stream RESILIENCE, with every new guard firing ONLY on bad/duplicate/out-of-order/corrupt data so a VALID sorted positive-price feed stays BYTE-IDENTICAL (the frozen golden oracle passes WITHOUT regeneration — the proof the hardening is non-invasive). FIVE in-scope fixes, all within `brutex/execution/`: (1) REPRODUCIBLE RE-RUN (latent BLOCKER): `BacktestDriver.run()` reset state+barrier+feed but NOT the `ExecutionSimulator`, so a second `run()` on the SAME driver silently concatenated fills/equity + carried cash forward → a non-reproducible result (violated NFR-DET-001). NEW `ExecutionSimulator.reset()` (restores `_cash` to the recorded `_initial_cash`, clears positions/fills/equity) is now called at the top of `run()` → `r1 == r2` for a same-driver re-run. (2) OUT-OF-ORDER / DUPLICATE bar guard (latent BLOCKER): no monotonicity guard existed, so a single mis-sorted or duplicated lake row (`heapq.merge` assumes each per-symbol input is pre-sorted) silently rewound time and was traded as a stale bar. `run()` now enforces STRICTLY-INCREASING per-symbol bar timestamps via a per-run local `last_ts_by_symbol`, raising the NEW typed `NonMonotonicBarError` on a backwards OR equal (duplicate) within-symbol timestamp — while ALLOWING equal timestamps ACROSS symbols (the legit multi-symbol interleave). Loud + deterministic → the engine tuple-skip layer quarantines it (never silent, Golden Rule #1/#7). (3) NON-TRADEABLE PRICE guard (MAJOR): a zero/negative `bar.close` raised a cryptic uncaught `ValueError` from the cost model and a NaN/inf a `decimal.InvalidOperation`, either crashing the whole run on ONE corrupt vendor bar. NEW `_require_tradeable_price` (checks `is_finite()` BEFORE `<= 0` so a NaN never reaches a comparison) is wired into `execute()` + `mark_to_market()` and raises the NEW typed `InvalidPriceError` (an `ExecutionError`), consistent with how the simulator already raises `InvalidLotSizeError`/`InsufficientFundsError` for invalid orders. (4) IMMUTABLE RESULT (MINOR): `_freeze_positions` was a shallow dict copy holding the LIVE mutable `Position` objects, so a later `run()`/mark mutated a previously-returned `BacktestResult`; it now snapshots each `Position` via `dataclasses.replace` (values identical → byte-stable). (5) DETERMINISTIC COST ROUNDING (MINOR): `IndianCostModel._quantise` rounded via the process-global ambient `decimal.getcontext().rounding`; it now pins `rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN` explicitly (= the current effective default → byte-identical output), removing the cross-module non-determinism vector (NFR-DET-001). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): VIX `vix_at_entry`/`vix_at_exit` stamping, the forced 15:20 IST exit, and the blake3 run-identity hash are correctly ABSENT from `brutex/execution/` — they live in `brutex/engine/` (`trade_sim.py`/`sweep_run.py`) + `brutex/strategies/combo.py` and are OUT of this package's scope (verified, not changed). The monotonic guard + price guard are O(1) per bar (one dict lookup / a few Decimal predicate checks), NOT an O(1)-total claim. All 6 `brutex/execution/` files at 100% line+branch; 7 test types (unit + integration + property + golden byte-stable + a regression test per fix); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change.
## DEC-DASHBOARD-XSS-HARDENING-001 (2026-06-27)

949. **DEC-DASHBOARD-XSS-HARDENING-001 — the `/movers` dashboard page is hardened against TWO frontend XSS sinks: (A) a STORED XSS where vendor-derived row cells (the symbol name + the moneyness label) were interpolated into `innerHTML` UNescaped, and (B) a REFLECTED XSS where the note (which echoes the raw `?asset=` query param) was set via `innerHTML` with server text — both closed without changing the engine, scope, vocab, or rate caps** (2026-06-27, dashboard XSS hardening batch; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why (the two gaps, verified file:line):** **GAP A (stored)** — `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`'s `renderRows` loop built each cell as `` `<td class="${cls}">${v}</td>` `` and assigned the joined string to `tb.innerHTML`, so a vendor-derived string cell (`name` / `moneyness`) like `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` rendered as a LIVE tag (numeric cells are coerced via `toLocaleString`/`toFixed` and are safe, but the two string columns are not). **GAP B (reflected)** — the note was set as `$("note").innerHTML = "<b>Note:</b> "+(j.note||"")` (and a sibling preview branch), and the server note in `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py::pending_asset_payload` formats the raw `?asset=` query param verbatim (`f"{asset.title()} movers ship after Spot …"`), so `GET /api/v1/movers?asset=<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` reflected an executable tag straight into `innerHTML`. **What shipped (FRONTEND + a server defense-in-depth layer; READ-ONLY dashboard, NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change):** (1) GAP A — the COMMON `esc()` HTML-escaper that `db.html` / `universe.html` / `completeness.html` already ship (the SAME five-replacement body — `&`→`&amp;`, `<`→`&lt;`, `>`→`&gt;`, `"`→`&quot;`, `'`→`&#39;`; one source of truth, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) is added to `movers.html` and the cell interpolation becomes `` `<td class="${cls}">${esc(v)}</td>` `` — every cell value (string OR coerced-number) is escaped before it touches `innerHTML`; a clean numeric/`₹`-formatted string passes through unchanged. (2) GAP B (frontend) — the note's bold prefix is now a STATIC node `<b>Note:</b> <span id="noteText"></span>` and ONLY the dynamic text is set via `noteText.textContent` (`$("noteText").textContent = (j.note||"")`), so the reflected server note can NEVER become live HTML; the "Loading…" + preview branches set `textContent` on the same span (no `#note` `innerHTML` write remains). (3) GAP B (server defense-in-depth) — `pending_asset_payload` HTML-escapes the reflected `asset` AT THE SOURCE before formatting (`html.escape(asset.title())` — title-case FIRST then escape, so `.title()` cannot mangle the entities and the JSON payload is byte-clean), so even a future non-`textContent` consumer of the payload is safe; a `<img …>` label comes back as inert `&lt;Img …&gt;` text. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ both XSS sinks are closed — no literal `<`/`>` survives into the reflected note (proven by the route test), and the row cells are escaped (proven by a template + a unit-render test); ✅ READ-ONLY display hardening — no change to the ranked numbers, the lake, the engine, the 52-vocab, or the rate caps; ✅ COMMON — reuses the existing `esc()` helper body, no copy-paste of a new escaper; ✅ defense-in-depth, not a single point of failure — the server escapes AND the frontend uses `textContent`, so either alone would already neutralise the reflected note. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad venv, Python 3.12):** `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py` at **100% line+branch** (240/0 stmt + 56/0 branch) across the full movers suite; ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on every touched file (`movers_snapshot.py` + the three test files); NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_movers_template_xss.py` (4 static-template tests: the shared `esc()` helper is present, the cell is `esc(v)` not raw `${v}`, the note is a static label + `textContent` span with no `#note` innerHTML write, and no `j.note` reaches any `innerHTML`) + NEW `tests/unit/test_movers_snapshot.py::test_pending_asset_payload_escapes_reflected_asset` (the reflected asset is escaped at the JSON source — no literal angle bracket survives) + NEW `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py::TestMoversApi::test_reflected_asset_note_carries_no_unescaped_tag` (end-to-end `GET /api/v1/movers?asset=<img …>` carries no unescaped tag); 324 movers + 84 dashboard-template/e2e tests GREEN. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_movers_template_xss.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_snapshot.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-XSS-HARDENING-001. **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-TIER-001 / DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 #865 (the moneyness cell now escaped), DEC-MOVERS-SNAPSHOT-VIEW-001 (the `/movers` page + `pending_asset_payload` this hardens). **Part of:** the dashboard frontend security hardening — the read-only viewer can never reflect or store a live tag from vendor data or a query param.
956. **DEC-PULL-HEALTH-CONCURRENCY-001 — the live `PullHealthMonitor.observe()` body is now ATOMIC across the up-to-8 parallel Groww pool workers via ONE `threading.Lock`, closing a shared-state race in the per-window pull-health observe wiring; plus a regression that PINS the deadline-guard daemon bound — no engine/scope/vocab/rate change** (2026-06-27, pull-health concurrency hardening batch; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why (GAP #8 MAJOR, verified file:line):** the dashboard live pull threads the monitor into a per-window `on_window` tick (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` `make_window_observer` → `_observe_rate` → `monitor.observe`, ~ll. 977-981 / 1402-1404 / 1474), and the ingest spine fires that tick from up to 8 parallel SDK pool workers concurrently. `PullHealthMonitor.observe()` mutated shared state with NO lock — the `self._last_controller`/`self._last_meter` snapshot assignment, the `_mirror_gauges()` write, the `DwellProvider._streak` increment (`pull_health.py` ll. 156-165), and the `SLADetector._state` OK↔BREACH transition (`sla.py` `check_once`, ll. 229-275) — so two ticks could interleave: a torn snapshot read, a double-counted dwell streak, or a `pull.stalled` edge that flips more than once. **What shipped (observability hardening; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, READ-side monitor only):** (1) GAP #8 — `PullHealthMonitor` gains ONE `threading.Lock` (`_observe_lock`, added to `__slots__`, built in `__init__`) held around the WHOLE `observe()` body (snapshot assignment + `_mirror_gauges` + `_detector.check_once`), so every per-window tick is atomic across the parallel workers; the dwell increment and the OK↔BREACH transition can no longer interleave. The `on_degraded` Telegram alert fires inside `check_once` under the lock but only ENQUEUES an async, best-effort alert (no synchronous network I/O is ever held under the lock — `SweepAlerter.pull_degraded` is fire-and-forget). The now-false `DwellProvider` docstring line ("the detector evaluates rules synchronously on the caller's thread, so no lock is needed") is CORRECTED to document the monitor-provided serialisation. (2) GAP #18 NIT — `run_with_deadline` (`brutex/adapters/groww/deadline.py`) gains a comment noting its abandoned-daemon bound depends on the SDK's finite socket timeout (ADR-0009 §3), NO production logic change; a NEW regression in `tests/unit/test_groww_deadline.py` fires 20 timed-out calls through the guard (each blocking on a per-call release event standing in for a short socket timeout), releases every "socket", and asserts `threading.active_count()` returns to its pre-storm baseline — pinning the "a daemon dies with its call" bound so a sustained timeout storm cannot accumulate daemons unboundedly. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ GAP #8 closes the interleave class — proven by a NEW `Barrier`-driven 8-thread test asserting `pull.stalled` fires EXACTLY once (not N times) under maximal overlap, plus a repeated-storm test asserting the mirrored gauges end at the exact un-torn last-snapshot values; ✅ the lock holds only the cheap in-memory rule evaluation (no I/O), so it can never block/slow/crash a pull (the `observe()` best-effort try/except is unchanged); ✅ GAP #18 is a TEST + COMMENT only — no production logic change, the bound was ALREADY correct (a daemon is finite-lived), the regression just makes it explicit; ✅ no engine/scope/vocab/rate change — the monitor is a read-side observer, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad venv, Python 3.12):** `brutex/observability/pull_health.py` at **100% line+branch** (133/0 stmt + 28/0 branch) and `brutex/adapters/groww/deadline.py` at **100% line+branch** (20/0 stmt + 4/0 branch) across the touched suites; ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on every touched file; NEW `tests/unit/test_observability_pull_health.py::TestObserveConcurrency` (2 Barrier-storm tests: `pull.stalled` fires once + no lost gauge updates) + NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_deadline.py::test_daemon_threads_drain_after_a_timeout_storm` (the 20-call daemon-drain regression); 64 pull-health + deadline + wiring + SLA tests GREEN. **Files:** `brutex/observability/pull_health.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/deadline.py`, `tests/unit/test_observability_pull_health.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_deadline.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-HEALTH-CONCURRENCY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001 #932 (the monitor + the `_observe_rate` seam this makes thread-safe), DEC-PULL-HEALTH-WIRING-001 #935 (the dashboard binding that fires the per-window tick from parallel workers), DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001 / DEC-GROWW-REAUTH-DEADLINE-001 #910 (the freeze guard whose daemon bound is now pinned). **Part of:** the concurrency-correctness hardening of the live-pull observability path.
967. **DEC-STRATEGIES-CANONICAL-HARDEN-001 — the `brutex/strategies/` combo-identity layer (the 9-field BLAKE3 `combo_hash` + param canonicaliser in `combo.py` and the `ParamGrid` Cartesian enumeration + LMDB dedup cache in `sweep.py`) is hardened against six adversarially-confirmed collision/footgun/honesty defects with REJECT-ONLY guards — every guard raises `StrategyError` for NEVER-VALID input before any byte is produced, so NO valid digest moves (the frozen golden `_BASE` digest `c48b382d…453ecd6` is byte-unchanged — the safety proof)** (2026-06-27, strategies canonicalisation hardening; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why (six confirmed findings; a 5-lens multi-agent audit surfaced 32, each re-proven with a runnable repro, 31/32 confirmed):** (A) `combo_hash` joins its 9 identity fields with the `\x1f` unit-separator but validated the 8 raw fields only for non-emptiness, so a raw `\x1f` inside any field shifted the join boundary and let two DISTINCT 9-tuples (`instrument="NIFTY\x1fX",tf="Y"` vs `instrument="NIFTY",tf="X\x1fY"`) forge the IDENTICAL payload → identical digest (a real dedup collision; `canonical_params` itself is immune — `ensure_ascii=True` escapes `\x1f`→``); (B) the float branch guarded only `math.isnan`, so `±inf` and (unconditional `str()`) `Decimal('NaN'/'Infinity'/'sNaN')` were silently accepted, contradicting the module's own "NaN values are rejected" contract; (C) `canonicalise_params` (typed `Mapping`) silently canonicalised a non-Mapping top level (`None`→`"null"`, `[1,2]`→`"[1,2]"`) instead of rejecting; (D) `numpy.float64` (a genuine `float` subclass whose NumPy-2.x `repr` is `'np.float64(1.5)'`) silently produced a DIFFERENT digest than the equal Python float; (E) `ParamGrid` directly constructed with an empty axis (`ParamGrid(axes={'a':()})`) bypassed `from_dict`'s guard and ran a SILENT zero-combo sweep reporting success; (F) the `ComboCache`/module docstrings claimed cache hits "in O(1)" when LMDB is a B+tree = O(log n) (Golden Rule #10 honesty breach). **What shipped (REJECT-ONLY guards + docstring honesty; READ-side, NO wire-format/engine/scope/vocab/rate change):** `combo.py` — a per-field `\x1f`-rejection loop over the 8 raw fields (A); `_canonicalise_value` rewritten to reject non-finite floats (`math.isfinite`) + non-finite Decimals (`Decimal.is_finite()`) (B) + float subclasses via `type(value) is not float` (D) + nesting deeper than the new `_MAX_CANONICALISE_DEPTH=64` (a clean `StrategyError` instead of a `RecursionError` crash); a top-level `isinstance(params, Mapping)` guard in `canonicalise_params` (C); an honest `Complexity` docstring (O(P) per combo, O(1) per combo w.r.t. sweep cardinality N) + a documented "wire-locked / Honest envelope" block pinning the float↔str↔Decimal aliasing, Decimal-scale significance, signed-zero collapse (`-0.0` → `+0.0`, reconciled with DEC-SWEEP-DEDUP-LMDB-001 on the merge with main — two mathematically-equal zero params share ONE run-identity, Golden Rule #4 reproducibility; supersedes this PR's earlier signed-zero-SPLIT pin), and tuple≡list as DELIBERATE frozen-wire properties. `sweep.py` — a `ParamGrid.__post_init__` empty-axis guard (E, single source of truth; the redundant `from_dict` check removed) + the two O(log n) B+tree docstring corrections (F). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ REJECT-ONLY — every guard rejects only never-valid input BEFORE producing a byte, so the frozen golden digest and every production LMDB key are byte-unchanged (proven: `test_base_digest_unchanged_after_hardening` + the full golden corpus PASS); ✅ the float↔str↔Decimal numeric-as-string aliasing is WIRE-LOCKED (bit-mirrored by `brutex/engine/{stage1a,sweep_driver,stage3_refine}.py` + frozen by the golden + production caches) so it is DOCUMENTED + PINNED, NOT changed — the numpy-float64 guard closes the only realistic asymmetric leak; ✅ the alias is honestly NON-universal (`repr(1e16)='1e+16'` ≠ `str(Decimal('1e16'))='1E+16'`) so the property test asserts the exact `iff`, not a weakened pass; 🟡 mirroring the `\x1f` guard + the depth cap into the engine canonicaliser copies is a FLAGGED follow-up (latent + harmless today — the engine canonicalises only its own int/str/None domain, never arbitrary nested params), NOT done here. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad Python 3.12 venv + the fno_math/trading_core Rust wheels):** `brutex/strategies/combo.py` AND `sweep.py` BOTH at **100% line + 100% branch** (combo 67 stmt/50 branch, sweep 168 stmt/28 branch, 0 missing); ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on all 9 touched files; 7 test types added (unit/integration/property/golden/bench/stress + a regression test per bug); 226 strategies tests + 4 bench/stress GREEN; the multi-agent audit (31/32 confirmed) + an independent hostile review returned SHIP (2 non-blocking NITs). **Files:** `brutex/strategies/combo.py`, `brutex/strategies/sweep.py`, `tests/unit/test_strategies_combo.py`, `tests/unit/test_strategies_sweep_grid.py`, `tests/property/test_combo_hash_uniqueness.py`, `tests/golden/test_combo_hash_distinct_golden.py`, `tests/integration/test_strategies_sweep.py`, `tests/bench/test_strategies_combo_bench.py`, `tests/stress/test_strategies_combo_stress.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-STRATEGIES-CANONICAL-HARDEN-001. **Builds on:** DEC-P0-060 (the 9-field BLAKE3 `combo_hash`), FR-BF-003 / NFR-UNIQ-001 / NFR-UNIQ-002 (the combo identity + canonicalisation contract). **Part of:** the brute-force engine reliability hardening — the combo-dedup identity is now collision-proof, reproducible, honest about its complexity, and impossible to run as a silent no-op.

## DEC-RUST-CRATES-HARDEN-001 (2026-06-27)

965. **DEC-RUST-CRATES-HARDEN-001 — the two shared Rust crates' PyO3 FFI boundary can no longer be made to ABORT the Python interpreter on garbage input: every `#[pyfunction]` in `trading-core` (`evaluate_from_raw`, `evaluate_with_levels`, `compute_pivot_levels`, `compute_fib_levels`) now VALIDATES its previous-day OHLC anchor AND every per-bar evaluate input (open/high/low/close, EMAs, pre-built levels, proximity bps) at the boundary and returns a clean `PyValueError` instead of tripping the inner indicators' always-on `assert!` / release `overflow-checks` panic / `.abs()`-on-`i64::MIN`, and `fno-math`'s trade-sim holding subtract is guarded against unsigned underflow — closing a class of bad-library-input DoS while keeping the 400-case golden bit-identity BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged** (2026-06-27, the Rust-crates input-hardening pass; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why (the reachable panic→abort surface, verified file:line):** both crates ship with `profile.release` `panic = "abort"` + `overflow-checks = true` (`rust/{trading-core,fno-math}/Cargo.toml`) — a finance-safety choice so a paisa overflow is a LOUD abort, never a silent wrap. But under `panic = "abort"` a panic raised inside a `#[pyfunction]` does NOT unwind into PyO3's catch-and-convert wrapper — it `abort()`s the WHOLE interpreter (SIGABRT), so any caller of the maturin wheel that passes corrupt input crashes the process rather than seeing a catchable exception. **GAP 1a (trading-core anchor, MAJOR)** — `evaluate_from_raw` / `py_compute_pivot_levels` / `py_compute_fib_levels` called the inner `compute_pivot_levels` / `compute_fib_levels` DIRECTLY; those carry always-on `assert!`s (`pdh >= pdl`, `pdl <= pdc <= pdh`; `indicators/pivots.rs:37-41`, `fib.rs:49`) + integer arithmetic that overflows at absurd magnitudes — so a corrupt prev-day OHLC / absurd anchor tripped an `assert!`/overflow panic → abort. **GAP 1b (trading-core evaluate inputs, MAJOR — hostile-review finding)** — a VALID anchor with a garbage PER-BAR input still aborted: `evaluator.rs::is_near` does `close * bps` (overflows i64 for huge `close*bps`) and `(close - level).abs()` (panics on exactly `i64::MIN`), and Group-5/7/9 do `body * 10`, `total_range * 7`, `(close − day_low) * 3`, `pdc * 50` (overflow at absurd magnitudes). The original anchor-only validator did NOT bound `close_paisa` / `*_bps` / the other bar prices / the pre-built levels, so the evaluate path was only partially closed. **GAP 2 (fno-math, MINOR/defensive)** — `trade_sim.rs` computed the inclusive holding as `(exit_idx - entry_idx + 1)` with an UNSIGNED subtract; `exit_idx >= entry_idx` is a true forward-only-walker invariant, but a future mis-call with `exit_idx < entry_idx` would underflow→abort under `overflow-checks`. **GAP 3 (fno-math NSE calendar, ALREADY SAFE — no change)** — the calendar's lookups are `HashSet`/weekday checks + `next_trading_day` already guards `succ_opt()` overflow + bounds its lookahead, so extreme dates + `NaiveDate::MIN`/`MAX` are already total + panic-free; this pass adds only a DOCUMENTING boundary test. **What shipped (rust/ only — the GOLDEN-sensitive inner evaluator arithmetic is NOT touched; NO change to the 52-vocab, engine scope, pyo3/edition/rate constants, or ANY valid-input numeric semantics):** (1) GAP 1a — pure `check_prev_day_ohlc` / `check_prev_day_hl` mirror the inner `assert!` preconditions PLUS an overflow ceiling `MAX_ANCHOR_PAISA = i64::MAX / 8`; each `#[pyfunction]` is a THIN wrapper delegating to a pure `*_impl` (`evaluate_from_raw_impl`, `evaluate_with_levels_impl`, `py_compute_pivot_levels_impl`, `py_compute_fib_levels_impl`) whose `Err(String)` the boundary maps to `PyValueError` — unit-covered WITHOUT a libpython link. (2) GAP 1b — NEW `check_evaluate_inputs` bounds EVERY per-bar input the evaluator multiplies/subtracts/`.abs()`es: a per-bar/level ceiling `MAX_BAR_PAISA = i64::MAX / 65536` (≈ 1.4·10¹⁴ paisa = ₹1.4 trillion, ~17 million× SENSEX ~8·10⁶) on open/high/low/close + EMAs + `pdc` (the one level Group 9 multiplies by 50) + every CALLER-SUPPLIED pivot/fib level (the `evaluate_with_levels` path, which is not anchor-derived), so all subtractions/`.abs()`/`*2..*50` multiplies stay in i64 and never hit `i64::MIN`; a generous `MAX_BPS = 1_000_000` cap PLUS — decisively — an EXACT `close.checked_mul(bps).is_none()` product check on each of the three bps (rejects iff the i64 `close * bps` would actually overflow; accepts a product of exactly `i64::MIN`/`i64::MAX` which fits i64, and has no `>`/`>=` boundary to mutate), so `close * bps` can never overflow regardless of how the ceilings interact. The recomputed (anchor path) pivot/fib R/S/retrace levels stay safe by construction (anchor-bounded + only SUBTRACTED against a bar-bounded `close`). (3) GAP 2 — `holding_bars` uses `saturating_sub` (byte-identical for every valid `exit >= entry` call; a defined minimum holding of 1 for the inverted case). (4) GAP 3 — a documenting boundary test only. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ GOLDEN BIT-IDENTITY UNCHANGED — `MAX_ANCHOR_PAISA` is ≈ 200 billion× and `MAX_BAR_PAISA` ≈ 17 million× the largest golden value, and both ceilings + the bps cap are far above the `tests/proptests.rs` domain (10¹² paisa, ≤200 bps), so they reject ZERO valid input; the `cargo test --release` golden (`rust_reproduces_every_golden_vector`, all 400 cases) passes byte-for-byte before AND after, AND a wheel-based Python proof re-runs all 400 through the installed `trading_core` wheel byte-identically; ✅ the EVALUATE path is now panic-safe at the FFI boundary for the audited sites (`is_near` `close*bps`+`(close-level).abs()`, Group-5 `body*10`/`total_range*7`/wick`*2`, Group-7 `(close-day_low)*3`, Group-9 `pdc*50`) — the inner evaluator math is UNCHANGED (the boundary rejects before it runs); ✅ NaN/Inf cannot reach the i64 FFI by construction (PyO3 rejects a non-integral float); ✅ rust/ only + ONE ledger entry — no `brutex/` source, no vocab/scope/pyo3/edition/rate change. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27, cargo 1.94.1):** trading-core `cargo test --release` default GREEN + `--release --features python` 36 GREEN (NEW per-bar reject tests — each price / EMA / level out of range, negative + over-cap + product-overflowing bps, `i64::MIN` price — + a `valid_bar_inputs_never_rejected` proptest + the anchor/parity/stress/`round_half_even`-saturation tests); fno-math `cargo test --release` 528 GREEN (`holding_bars` normal/inverted + a 20k-bar deterministic stress + the calendar boundary test); `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` clean on BOTH crates; wheel built via `maturin develop --release` (Python 3.12) and the 400-case Python golden bit-identity + the 6 invalid-input→`ValueError`-not-abort checks pass; mutation: trading-core 42 caught/45 unviable/0 missed, fno-math 119 caught/12 missed (all equivalent/env-dependent in pre-existing untouched code)/5 unviable. The thin `#[pyfunction]`/`#[pymodule]` glue needs a live interpreter (the pre-existing CI gap — CI runs only `cargo check --features python` — exercised end-to-end by the wheel proof). **Files:** `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs`, `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/mod.rs`, `rust/fno-math/src/trade_sim.rs`, `rust/fno-math/src/compat/trading_calendar.rs`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-RUST-CRATES-HARDEN-001. **Builds on:** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 #441 (the shared 52-vocab + pivots/fib kernel whose FFI this hardens), DEC-SWEEP-RUST-TRADESIM-001 #563 (the trade-sim walker whose holding subtract this guards). **Part of:** the resilience-hardening arc — bad library input must never abort the interpreter, and the golden bit-identity contract is preserved exactly.
## DEC-CICD-GATE-HONESTY-001 (2026-06-27)

966. **DEC-CICD-GATE-HONESTY-001 — the CI gate that ran BOTH a banned-pattern scan AND a MIGRATION.md ledger-numbering validation under the single displayed name "Banned pattern scan" is DE-CONFLATED into two honestly-named jobs, and the per-module 100% coverage gate gains an AUTO-DISCOVERY companion that fails a NEW brutex module shipping no dedicated test while WARN-skipping a legacy modification — both merge-safe, no branch-protection required check renamed, ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change** (2026-06-27, CI/CD gate honesty + auto-discovery batch). **Why (the two gaps, verified file:line):** **GAP 1 (gate honesty)** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `banned:` job (displayed `name: Banned pattern scan`, a REQUIRED branch-protection context) ran TWO steps: `scripts/ci/scan-banned-patterns.sh` AND `scripts/ci/validate_ledger_numbering.py` (DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001). A MIGRATION.md entry-number collision therefore failed a check literally named "Banned pattern scan", mislabeling the failure. **GAP 2 (coverage blind spot)** — the same job's sibling "Strict per-module 100% coverage gate" carried a HARDCODED ~140-entry list of `pytest --cov=brutex.MODULE` invocations, so a NEW brutex module that nobody added to the list silently escaped the per-file independence check (it still rode the whole-package `--cov-fail-under=100` floor, but never proved 100% with its OWN tests). **What shipped (CI-INFRA ONLY; NO brutex/ source, engine, scope, vocab, or rate change):** (1) GAP 1 — the `banned:` job is reverted to its honest scan-only shape (`name: Banned pattern scan`, the scanner step ONLY), and the ledger validator is split into a NEW dedicated `ledger-numbering:` job (`name: Ledger-numbering validator`) wired into the required `CI OK` aggregate (`ci-ok.needs` + its echo + result loop) so a ledger collision still BLOCKS merge — but is NEVER added to `branch-protection-drift.yml`'s `expected_required_checks` (it is enforced via `CI OK`, not as its own required context), so the required "Banned pattern scan" context keeps reporting unchanged and ZERO admin action / branch-protection edit is needed (a rename would have deadlocked the PR's own merge). (2) GAP 2 — NEW `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py` COMPLEMENTS (does not replace) the static list + the whole-package floor: it AUTO-DISCOVERS the `brutex/**/*.py` modules a PR TOUCHED via `git diff --name-status --diff-filter=ACMR <base>...HEAD` (TRACKING each file's Added-vs-Modified status), maps each to its test(s) by the repo's `test_<stem>` / `test_<pkg>_<stem>` glob convention (trailing `*` so a curated multi-file suite like `test_lookahead_barrier.py` matches), and ACCEPTS a candidate test ONLY if it actually IMPORTS the module (so a foreign same-stem test — e.g. a `test_models.py` importing a DIFFERENT `models` — is rejected, never mistaken for the module's own coverage). FAILURE POLICY: an ADDED module with no import-verified test FAILS (exit 1, "a NEW module must ship a dedicated test"); a MODIFIED module with no such test is WARN-skipped (it still rides the static gate + the floor — no false-fail on a legacy edit); a verified module runs an isolated `--cov=brutex` + `coverage report --include=<file> --fail-under=100` 100% line+branch assertion (a not-measured file also fails); zero touched modules / git error fail-closed at exit 0 / exit 2. The gate is wired as a NEW `test`-job step (with `fetch-depth: 0` on its checkout) ALONGSIDE the retained ~1418-line static gate. (3) self-tests for both CI scripts. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ COMPLEMENTS, does NOT replace, the static per-module gate or the whole-package `--cov-fail-under=100` aggregate floor; ✅ scoped to `brutex/` ONLY (a `scripts/ci` script is not a coverage-gated module here — its own tests still run in the suite); ✅ no required branch-protection check is renamed — the de-conflation is enforced via `CI OK`, so no admin action is needed (merge-safe); ✅ `COVERAGE_DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE` ships EMPTY (the warn-skip policy already protects legacy modifications, so no genuinely test-less brutex module needs an allowlist entry today); ✅ the discovery is DETERMINISTIC (every list sorted, no set/dict/filesystem-order reliance); ✅ CI-infra ONLY — no `brutex/` source / engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate-cap change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py` at **100% line+branch** (156 stmt / 64 branch / 0 missing) over NEW `tests/unit/test_coverage_gate_discovery.py` (48 tests incl. the B1 regression — a MODIFIED no-test module WARN-skips at exit 0, an ADDED no-test module FAILS at exit 1 — and the B2 regression — a foreign same-stem test is rejected); `scripts/ci/validate_ledger_numbering.py` stays at **100% line+branch** (46/16) over `tests/unit/test_validate_ledger_numbering.py` (13 tests, +2 for empty-ledger + numbering-gap); ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` + `interrogate` (100% docstrings on the script) + `bandit` clean on every touched `.py`; both workflow YAMLs `yaml.safe_load` OK with the new job topology asserted (`banned` name="Banned pattern scan", `ledger-numbering` name="Ledger-numbering validator", present in `ci-ok.needs`); the discovery gate run against this branch prints "no touched brutex modules — nothing to check (PASS)" + exit 0 (this PR touches no `brutex/` file). **Files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py`, `tests/unit/test_coverage_gate_discovery.py`, `tests/unit/test_validate_ledger_numbering.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CICD-GATE-HONESTY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 (the ledger-numbering validator now in its own gate), DEC-COV-CLI-HARNESS-001 (the per-module 100% coverage discipline this auto-discovers). **Part of:** the CI-honesty arc — a gate's name must reflect what it checks, and a new module can never silently escape the per-file 100% coverage gate.
## DEC-ENGINE-FAULT-INJECTION-AUDIT-O1-001 (2026-06-27)

973. **DEC-ENGINE-TRIALSTATS-FAULT-001 — the per-tuple finalize trial-stats SIDECAR-WRITE boundary is pinned by a fault-injection regression test (OSError propagates redo-not-skip + leaves the tuple un-sentineled), completing the sweep-loop write-fault-injection matrix — TEST-ONLY, NO engine source change** (2026-06-28, engine write-fault-injection matrix completion; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3 — no scope/vocab/rate change). **What & why:** `run_persisted_sweep`'s per-tuple finalize sequence (`brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`) writes, in order, the results-store flush, the trial-stats sidecar (`write_tuple_trial_stats`, ~line 1000), the dedup marks, and the STRICTLY-LAST completion sentinel (`write_completion_sentinel`, DEC-MARK-MANY-SENTINEL-001 / DEC-TRIAL-STATS-WRITE-001). The existing fault tests pin three of those four write boundaries — `test_store_append_error_aborts_not_a_combo_skip` (per-row append), `test_store_flush_error_aborts_not_a_combo_skip` (flush), `test_completion_sentinel_write_error_propagates_un_sentineled` (the strictly-last sentinel) — plus the bare-propagation `MemoryError`/`KeyboardInterrupt` tests, but the trial-stats sidecar write between flush and mark had NO dedicated fault test. NEW `test_trial_stats_write_error_propagates_un_sentineled` (in `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_run.py::TestSweepComboError`) closes that gap. **The property pinned (stated precisely, Golden Rule #10):** the `write_tuple_trial_stats` call sits OUTSIDE the narrow `except SweepComboError` that wraps ONLY the per-combo `metrics_for_mask` loop (verified: no `try`/`except` spans the finalize sequence lines 957→1029), so an `OSError` raised by the sidecar write PROPAGATES OUT UNCHANGED — it is NOT downgraded into a `SweepComboError` tuple-skip. Because ONLY a `SweepComboError` triggers the grid drivers' single-tuple skip + `tuples_failed` bump (the conservative redo-everything choice, sweep_run.py:921-932), propagating a raw `OSError` keeps the failure a sweep-wide ABORT rather than a combo-skip; and because the sidecar write FAILS before the strictly-last sentinel is reached, the completion sentinel — the sole redo authority on the digest path — is left ABSENT, so a resume deterministically REDOES the whole tuple (redo-not-skip; Golden Rule #7). The test injects the fault by monkeypatching `brutex.engine.sweep_run.write_tuple_trial_stats` to raise `OSError` (the same string-target technique the sibling sentinel test uses to avoid the re-export attr check) and asserts: (a) the raised exception is the raw `OSError`, not a `SweepComboError`, with NO `SweepComboError` anywhere on the `__cause__`/`__context__` chain (walked to the root); (b) the trial-stats sidecar file is ABSENT; (c) the completion sentinel file is ABSENT. **NO source fix was needed — the finalize sequence was ALREADY correct** (the trial-stats write is unguarded by construction, so its fault naturally propagates and the strictly-last sentinel is never reached): this is a pure REGRESSION PIN, no `brutex/engine/` byte changed. **Non-tautology proof:** a temporary source mutation wrapping `write_tuple_trial_stats` in an `except Exception: raise SweepComboError(...) from exc` (i.e. swallowing the fault into a combo-skip) makes the new test FAIL (the `not isinstance(..., SweepComboError)` chain-walk assertion fires); the source was restored byte-for-byte (`git diff --stat brutex/engine/sweep_run.py` empty) — so the test genuinely catches the swallow-regression it guards against. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ TEST-ONLY — no `brutex/engine/` source byte changed, so every engine golden/digest/coverage is untouched; ✅ pins the sidecar-WRITE-fault boundary (the I/O-failure path), NOT the in-content validation that `write_tuple_trial_stats`/`TrialStatsError` already cover elsewhere; ✅ `tuples_failed` is a GRID-DRIVER concept (not in `sweep_run.py`) — the not-bumped-as-a-combo-skip property is asserted INDIRECTLY + correctly via "the raise is not a `SweepComboError`" (only that error type drives the driver skip/bump), documented in the test docstring rather than over-claimed. **REAL (verified 2026-06-28 via the Python 3.12 venv + the fno_math/trading_core Rust wheels):** the new test PASSES; `brutex.engine` at **100% line + 100% branch** (no source change) over `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py`; ruff check + ruff format clean on `brutex/engine tests`; `pyright` 0 errors on the touched test file (no engine source edited → no `mypy --strict` source delta); `scripts/ci/validate_ledger_numbering.py` exit 0. **Files:** `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_run.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-ENGINE-TRIALSTATS-FAULT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-TRIAL-STATS-WRITE-001 (the between-flush-and-mark sidecar write it pins), DEC-MARK-MANY-SENTINEL-001 (the strictly-last sentinel = the redo authority), DEC-ENGINE-TUPLE-SKIP-RESILIENT-001 #904 (the SweepComboError tuple-skip-vs-abort contract). **Part of:** the brute-force engine write-fault-injection matrix (CLAUDE.md §2 r7 / §12) — the per-tuple finalize append, flush, trial-stats-sidecar, and completion-sentinel write boundaries are now ALL fault-pinned redo-not-skip.

972. **DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-FOLD-O1-001 — the walk-forward / per-mask sweep driver hot path is PROVEN O(1)-in-grid-size by a new bench, completing the engine O(1) bench matrix — TEST-ONLY, NO engine source change** (2026-06-28, engine O(1) bench-matrix completion; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3 — no scope/vocab/rate change). **What & why:** the existing engine O(1) benches cover the inner per-mask AND/CMP (`test_engine_combo_mask_o1`), the dedup membership probe + audit-line count (`test_engine_sweep_run_o1`), the audit append (`test_engine_sweep_audit_o1` #971), and the results-store append (`test_engine_results_store_o1`), but NOT the per-mask *walk-forward driver* path — the per-mask cost of `brutex.engine.sweep_driver.walk_forward_sweep`, the most-coupled per-mask scorer (fold schedule + full-stream Stage-1A `bar_bits` build, then `_score_fold` across folds via the shared `metrics_for_mask` core). NEW `tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_driver_o1.py` closes that gap. **The O(1) property the bench proves (stated precisely, Golden Rule #10):** the per-mask walk-forward eval cost is INDEPENDENT of how many masks the sweep GRID contains. `walk_forward_sweep` builds the fold schedule + the full-stream `bar_bits` matrix ONCE (and re-proves the no-look-ahead invariant once), then scores each mask across the FIXED folds — so evaluating one mask costs the same whether the grid holds `_SMALL=60` or `_LARGE=600` masks (a 10× grid gap). The per-mask work is O(folds·bars) in its OWN inputs (the bars + fold layout, both held FIXED in the bench), never a function of grid size. This is a **per-mask O(1)-in-grid-size claim, NOT an O(1)-total-sweep claim** (the whole sweep is O(masks·folds·bars) by construction). A regression making per-mask cost grow with grid size (e.g. an accidental per-mask `bar_bits`/schedule rebuild or an O(grid) lookup) would blow the ratio and fail. **Harness:** deterministic — a fixed multi-day IST bar stream (20 days × 2 bars) shared across both measurements + the self-contradictory all-52-bits `_IMPOSSIBLE_MASK` (never fires → a stable no-trade fold on EVERY mask, so each per-mask iteration does identical work and the timing reflects only the per-mask machinery, not data-dependent trade counts); warm-up + zero-guard `max(t_small,1.0)`; the ratio routed through the single-source-of-truth two-tier `tests.bench._o1_tiers.ratio_ceiling` (5× shared-CI / strict 1.1× on the M4-Pro runner), mirroring the sibling engine O(1) benches exactly. **NO source fix was needed — the path was ALREADY O(1)-in-grid-size** (the schedule + `bar_bits` build are hoisted out of the mask loop by construction): measured ratio **0.948×** at 600 vs 60 masks (`t_small≈156µs`, `t_large≈148µs` per mask — the larger grid even marginally faster, classic flat-per-iteration). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ TEST-ONLY — no `brutex/engine/` source byte changed, so every engine golden/digest is untouched; ✅ proves O(1) PER MASK in grid size, not an O(1)-total claim and not an O(1)-in-bars/folds claim (per-mask cost is legitimately O(folds·bars) in its own inputs — that is the algorithm, not a regression); the bench holds bars + fold layout fixed so the ONLY varying dimension is the grid size. This is the explicit FLAGGED follow-up named in DEC-ENGINE-FAULT-INJECTION-AUDIT-O1-001 (#971) ("a `sweep_driver` fold-bench is a FLAGGED future item"). **REAL (verified 2026-06-28 via the Python 3.12 venv + the fno_math/trading_core Rust wheels):** `brutex.engine` at **100% line + 100% branch** (no source change); the new bench (2 tests) PASS with the 0.948× ratio above; ruff check + ruff format clean on `brutex/engine tests`; `pyright` 0 errors on the new test file. **Files:** `tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_driver_o1.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-FOLD-O1-001. **Builds on:** DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001 (the walk-forward driver), DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 (the two-tier ratio ceiling), DEC-ENGINE-FAULT-INJECTION-AUDIT-O1-001 #971 (the prior engine O(1) bench it completes). **Part of:** the brute-force engine O(1)-discipline matrix (CLAUDE.md §2 r5 / §12) — the per-mask walk-forward driver is now machine-proven O(1)-in-grid-size alongside the per-mask AND, dedup, audit, and results-store hot paths.

975. **DEC-METRICS-INVARIANTS-ROUND2-001 — `brutex/metrics/` ROUND-2 quality follow-up: a mutation-survivor kill + a consolidated cross-engine invariant property catalog + three doc-NIT clarifications, TEST/DOC-ONLY (no logic change)** (2026-06-28, the ROUND-2 robustness pass after PR #935 shipped the Stage-4 non-finite guards). **Why:** a focused manual mutation sanity check on the #935 non-finite guard lines (the package-wide `mutmut` 3.x run is impractical in the time budget — no `[tool.mutmut]` config exists and 3.x rewrites/caches the whole tree, so the honest method used was per-guard mutation by hand: flip/drop each guard, run the targeted suite, observe kill/survive) found **2 of 3 guards KILLED** by the existing suite but **1 SURVIVOR**: dropping `not math.isfinite(variance)` from `cpcv._combine_moments` (`brutex/metrics/cpcv.py:282`) was NOT killed — the existing `test_pass_rate_finite_for_overflow_magnitude_series` still passed because a non-finite *combined* variance yields a `NaN` Sharpe, and `NaN > min_sharpe` is `False`, so the mutant's wrong fold still counts as a non-pass → the pass-rate stays finite either way. (The sibling guards in `cpcv.sharpe_of_returns` and the `deflated_sharpe` PSR finite-check were both KILLED, confirmed by re-running the suite against each applied mutant.) **What shipped (TEST + DOC ONLY — ZERO source-logic change; the two cpcv guards + the PSR guard are byte-identical to #935):** (1) **survivor kill** — `tests/unit/test_cpcv.py::TestNonFiniteVariance::test_combine_moments_returns_none_when_merge_overflows_to_nan` calls the private `_combine_moments` *directly* on four constant groups (per-group `M2` exactly `0`, so the overflow arises PURELY in the cross-group merge term `delta*delta*…` for means differing by `2e160`) and asserts the *exact* `None` return — distinguishing the guard (`None`) from the mutant (`NaN`), which "the rate stays finite" cannot (a whitebox import, so the established `# pyright: reportPrivateUsage=none` file-top convention of DEC-P0-017 is applied). (2) **consolidated invariant catalog** — NEW `tests/property/test_metrics_invariants.py` (9 hypothesis property tests, `max_examples=50`, all randomness seed-pinned so it is fast and never flaky) encoding the *cross-engine* ties not expressed in one place by the per-module suites: PSR monotone-non-decreasing in observed Sharpe (skew=0, fixed n); the composed DSR ≤ PSR(0) deflation tie through the *public* `deflated_sharpe_ratio`; expected-max-Sharpe ≥ 0 and non-decreasing in `n_trials`; finite-or-None across `sharpe_of_returns` / `cpcv_pass_rate` / `compute_metrics` Sharpe (no NaN/inf escapes for finite inputs, spec line 746); SPA `lower ≤ consistent ≤ upper` ∈ [0,1] + seed-determinism; WFO no-look-ahead (`train_stop ≤ test_start` AND `max(train_idx) < min(test_idx)`) across all three schemes; Monte-Carlo p ∈ (0,1] + seed-determinism. (3) **three doc-NIT clarifications** (docstring-only, each a confirmed non-bug documented honestly, NO logic change): `cpcv.sharpe_of_returns` + `cpcv._combine_moments` note inputs are assumed `|x| << ~1e150` (beyond that float64 squared-deviation overflows and the guard returns `None`) and that a near-constant series of a non-representable float (e.g. `[3.3]*n`) has a tiny *real* population variance (~1e-31) and thus a large finite Sharpe — matches the population-variance formula, not a bug; `deflated_sharpe.expected_max_sharpe_ratio` notes that for astronomically large `n_trials` (≥ ~2e16, far above any real trial count) `NormalDist.inv_cdf` may raise `statistics.StatisticsError` (a `ValueError` subclass), documented since callers already catch `ValueError`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** TEST + DOC only — the `monte_carlo` bool-seed rejection was explicitly OUT OF SCOPE and NOT added; the consolidated catalog deliberately encodes only cross-engine *ties* (the per-module suites remain the primary owners of each engine's local invariants, checked first to avoid duplication), so it adds assertions not new code paths; the mutation method is an honest per-guard manual check, not a full `mutmut` score (reported as such). NO scope/vocab/rate/engine change — ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (CLAUDE.md §3). **Tests/coverage:** all 11 `brutex/metrics/*` files stay **100% line+branch** (1263/348, 0 missing) via `pytest -k "metric or cpcv or wfo or pbo or spa or lockbox or monte_carlo or cascade or deflated_sharpe or invariant" --cov=brutex.metrics --cov-branch`; 931 metrics-suite tests green (+10 vs the #935 baseline: +9 invariant + 1 survivor-kill); ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict brutex/metrics` (0 issues) + `pyright brutex/metrics` (0 errors, 0 warnings) clean on the touched files. **Files:** `brutex/metrics/cpcv.py` (docstrings only), `brutex/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py` (docstring only), `tests/unit/test_cpcv.py`, `tests/property/test_metrics_invariants.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-METRICS-NONFINITE-GUARD-001 #935 (the non-finite guards this round mutation-tests + documents), DEC-METRICS-001 #305 (the population-moment Sharpe convention), DEC-P0-017 #39 (the whitebox `reportPrivateUsage` convention). **Decision ID:** DEC-METRICS-INVARIANTS-ROUND2-001.
## DEC-INDICATORS-NONFINITE-GUARD-001 (2026-06-27) [renumbered 951 → 957 on merge with origin/main, DEC-PULL-HEALTH-CONCURRENCY-001 took 956]

961. **DEC-INDICATORS-NONFINITE-GUARD-001 — evaluate-time EMA + day-extremes indicators now FAIL FAST on corrupt input instead of silently propagating it, plus a dedicated indicators golden** (2026-06-27, hardening sweep of `brutex/indicators/`). **Why:** a deep audit proved `EMAState.update` silently propagated a non-finite close — ONE `NaN`/`inf` tick poisoned every subsequent EMA value for the rest of the series (the property suite's `_CLOSE` strategy excludes NaN/inf so it could never catch it), and `DayExtremesState.update` did a bare `max`/`min` so a corrupt bar with `high < low` produced silently inverted running extremes. **What shipped (brutex/indicators/ ONLY):** (1) `ema.py` — `import math` + a guard as the FIRST statement of `update` (before any state mutation): `if not math.isfinite(close): raise ValueError(...)`; `compute_ema`/`latest_ema` inherit it via the single `update` chokepoint (COMMON, one source of truth, Golden Rule #11). (2) `day_extremes.py` — a `high_paisa < low_paisa` → `ValueError` guard mirroring the existing `pivots.py`/`fib_levels.py` `pdh < pdl` corruption pattern (a doji `high == low` stays valid). (3) regression tests (`TestNonFiniteGuard`, `TestCorruptionGuard`) + a NEW oracle-anchored golden `tests/golden/test_indicators_golden.py` + `tests/golden/fixtures/indicators_golden.json` locking pivots (NIFTY 14-May-2026), fib (BANKNIFTY 13-May-2026), EMA (warm-up null vector + flat-series + period-1 identity) and day-extremes (single-day running + 2-day reset). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** pure DEFENSIVE hardening — fail-fast on corrupt input, NO change to the finite/valid fast path (existing oracle values byte-identical); the audit ALSO surfaced a latent labeling defect in `FibLevels.get_by_bullish_label` (bullish retracements remapped onto bearish PDH-anchored levels, ~565 paisa off because 0.236+0.786≠1.0), left as the existing honest `pytest.skip` because its correct fix belongs in the shared Rust `trading_core` crate (DEC-SHARED-CORE-001), OUTSIDE this package — NOT silently changed. NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (CLAUDE.md §3); pivots/fib still DELEGATE all arithmetic to Rust (bit-identity re-verified by `test_python_rust_parity.py`). **Tests/coverage:** `brutex/indicators/` 100% line+branch (234/44, 0 missing); 130 passed / 1 intentional skip; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + pyright clean on the touched files.
## DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-001 (2026-06-27)

958. **DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-001 — the NSE/BSE trading calendar (`brutex/calendars/`) gains an OPT-IN out-of-coverage DETECTION surface + has its IST(+05:30, no-DST) / session-boundary / leap-year invariants PINNED with golden + property tests; the existing unguarded `is_holiday` / `is_trading_day` keep their byte-identical back-compat behaviour, so this is a DETECT-and-opt-in change, NOT a behaviour change** (2026-06-27, the calendar audit-and-harden pass; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why (the latent gap this DETECTS but does NOT silently change):** `brutex/calendars/nse.py::is_holiday` is a pure `d in ALL_HOLIDAYS` `frozenset` membership over the per-year lists `HOLIDAYS_2021…HOLIDAYS_2026`. For ANY date outside 2021-2026 it returns `False`, which is the HONEST answer for "is this date IN the published list" but, if a caller treats it as "is this a trading day", an out-of-coverage 2020 weekday holiday (e.g. Holi 2020-03-10) reads as a trading day via the UNGUARDED `is_trading_day` — and the Track-1 pull floor (DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 #722) IS 2020-01-01 (CLAUDE.md §3 `2020-01-01 → today`), so the holiday list (2021+) and the pull floor (2020+) are genuinely out of sync. **IMPORTANT HONESTY (this PR does NOT fix the live read):** the existing consumers still call the UNGUARDED `is_trading_day`, which STILL returns `True` for that 2020 weekday holiday — that behaviour is UNCHANGED here (back-compat). WIRING the strict variants into the spot-anchor consumers that would need them (`brutex/indicators/prev_day_ohlc.py`, `brutex/dashboard/preopen_report.py`) is an explicit DEFERRED follow-up that lives OUTSIDE this package's exclusive scope (cross-package, a separate PR), NOT done here. Per Golden Rule #1 (no hallucination) this PR also does NOT invent the missing-year holiday dates (none are verifiable in-repo — `docs/TRACK1_MICROSTRUCTURE.md` §4 documents only 2021-2026); it surfaces the coverage gap so a caller can refuse to guess. **What shipped (ADDITIVE, API-STABLE; NO change to any existing function's return for any date, in- or out-of-coverage; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change):** (1) NEW machine-derived coverage range `HOLIDAY_COVERAGE_FIRST_YEAR = min(h.year for h in ALL_HOLIDAYS)` / `HOLIDAY_COVERAGE_LAST_YEAR = max(...)` (2021 / 2026 today) — derived from the lists themselves so the two can never silently drift. (2) NEW O(1) predicate `is_holiday_data_available(d)` (a single integer year-range test) — `False` means "the `is_holiday` result is an ABSENCE of information, not a verified non-holiday". (3) NEW `HolidayDataUnavailableError(LookupError)` + strict `is_holiday_checked(d)` — identical to `is_holiday` in range, but emits a `calendar.holiday_data_unavailable` structlog WARNING and RAISES for an out-of-coverage date, so a CALLER THAT OPTS IN never silently mistakes an unknown date for a non-holiday (the unguarded `is_holiday` still returns its back-compat `False`). (4) NEW strict `is_trading_day_checked(d)` — raises ONLY for the genuinely-ambiguous case (an out-of-coverage WEEKDAY whose verdict turns on the missing holiday list); a special-weekend session (data the package DOES hold) resolves `True` and a plain weekend resolves `False` WITHOUT raising, because those answers are data-complete regardless of the holiday list (a weekend is never a trading day). (5) the IST construction is now documented as a DELIBERATE fixed +05:30 `ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata")` (India observes no DST) over a hand-rolled `timezone(timedelta(...))`, and that invariant is property-pinned. All five new symbols are re-exported from `brutex/calendars/__init__.py`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ this PR ADDS detection primitives + PINS invariants — it does NOT change any function's return and does NOT make the live spot-anchor read holiday-aware for 2020 (the unguarded `is_trading_day` is byte-unchanged; the strict variants are OPT-IN and currently UNWIRED — wiring them is the deferred cross-package follow-up); ✅ the existing `is_holiday` / `is_trading_day` / `get_session` / `trading_days_between` returns are BYTE-UNCHANGED for every date (all 11 consumers in `brutex/` keep working untouched); ✅ NO 2020 (or any missing-year) holiday date is invented — the gap is surfaced, not papered over (the verified 2020 list stays the deferred follow-up of #722); ✅ `is_trading_day_checked` raises only where the verdict actually depends on the missing data (weekday), not for a data-complete weekend; ✅ READ-ONLY calendar logic — no engine / 52-vocab / scope / rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via a scratchpad Python 3.12 venv + `maturin develop --release` for `fno_math`/`trading_core`):** both touched source files at **100% line+branch** — `brutex/calendars/nse.py` (119 stmt / 26 branch, 0 missing) + `brutex/calendars/__init__.py` (2/0) — captured via `pytest --cov=brutex.calendars --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100`; NEW tests — `TestISTOffset` (fixed +05:30 / no-DST across DST-equivalent instants + every month), `TestHolidayCoverageRange` + `TestTradingDayChecked` (the 2020 case: the UNGUARDED `is_trading_day(2020-03-10) is True` is ASSERTED unchanged, while the NEW opt-in `is_trading_day_checked(2020-03-10)` RAISES; below-floor + above-ceiling unavailable; weekend resolves without raising), `TestSessionBoundaries` (09:14:59 pre-open / 09:15:00 open / 15:19:59 forced / 15:19:00+1m not-forced), `TestLeapYear` (Feb-29 2020 weekend + 2024 trading day + a span across the leap day), and a NEW property suite `tests/property/test_calendar_nse_properties.py` (hypothesis: IST offset always +05:30/no-DST for any instant; no listed holiday is a trading day; `is_holiday_data_available` equals the year-range test; `is_holiday_checked` equals `is_holiday` or raises; regular sessions always 09:15:00→15:30:00 / 375m); 94 calendar tests GREEN + the consumer suites (`test_engine_trade_sim`, `test_groww_contract_bounds`, `test_engine_nifty_day_golden`) GREEN; ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict brutex/calendars/` (Success, 0 issues) + `pyright brutex/calendars/` (0 errors) + bandit (0 issues) clean on the touched files. **Files:** `brutex/calendars/nse.py`, `brutex/calendars/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/test_calendar_nse.py`, `tests/property/test_calendar_nse_properties.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-001. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 #722 (the 2020-01-01 pull floor whose named "verified 2020 holiday list is a separate follow-up" this surfaces honestly without inventing), DEC-TRADESIM-001 (the timeframe-aware `is_forced_exit_bar` whose boundaries this now golden-pins), DEC-P0-046 (the NIFTY-rebalance + special-weekend-session calendar data). **Deferred follow-up (OUTSIDE this package's exclusive scope):** wire `is_trading_day_checked` / `is_holiday_checked` into the spot-anchor consumers (`indicators/prev_day_ohlc.py`, `dashboard/preopen_report.py`) so the 2020 out-of-coverage case becomes an honest hard error at the read site — a separate cross-package PR. **Part of:** the calendar correctness hardening — out-of-coverage dates are now DETECTABLE (opt-in) and the IST/session/leap-year invariants are property- and golden-pinned.

## DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-002 (2026-06-27)

959. **DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-002 — the `brutex/calendars/` NSE/BSE trading calendar is hardened with three small, high-rigor changes: a `ValueError` guard on `expected_bars_per_day_for_tf` (was a `ZeroDivisionError` at tf == 0 / a negative bar count at tf < 0), an O(1) `_REBALANCE_BY_DATE` dict lookup replacing the O(n) linear scan in the two NIFTY-rebalance helpers, and a new COMMON `forced_exit_time_for_session` helper that derives the forced-exit time-of-day as `close - 10min` for ANY session (regular OR short / half-day) — closing the doc `TRACK1_MICROSTRUCTURE.md` §2 half-day gap without changing engine behaviour** (2026-06-27, the calendars hardening batch; ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). **Why (the three gaps):** **(A) the tf guard** — `expected_bars_per_day_for_tf(tf_minutes)` divided `SESSION_DURATION_MINUTES // tf_minutes` with NO lower-bound check, so `tf == 0` raised an opaque `ZeroDivisionError` and a negative `tf` returned a nonsensical NEGATIVE bar count, whereas its sibling `is_forced_exit_bar` already rejected `tf_minutes < 1` with a clear `ValueError` — the two were inconsistent. **(B) the O(n) scan** — `is_nifty_rebalance_day` used `any(event.effective_date == d for event in NIFTY50_REBALANCE_EVENTS)` and `nifty_rebalance_event_on` a `for`-loop, both O(n) over the rebalance tuple on EVERY call, violating Golden Rule #5 (O(1) discipline) for what is a pure date-keyed membership/lookup. **(C) the half-day forced-exit gap** — the canonical forced exit was a hardcoded `15:20` (`FORCED_EXIT_IST`), correct only for the standard 09:15-15:30 session; `TRACK1_MICROSTRUCTURE.md` §2 specifies a half-day session's forced exit as `close - 10min`, and §1.2's standard 15:20 is exactly `15:30 - 10min`, so ONE rule generalises both but no helper expressed it. **What shipped (calendars + tests ONLY; NO engine / scope / vocab / rate change):** (1) `expected_bars_per_day_for_tf` raises `ValueError` for `tf_minutes < 1` BEFORE any division (mirrors `is_forced_exit_bar`), with a `Raises` docstring section; (2) a precomputed `_REBALANCE_BY_DATE: Final[dict[date, NiftyRebalanceEvent]]` built ONCE from the authoritative `NIFTY50_REBALANCE_EVENTS` tuple (the single source of truth; effective dates are unique, asserted by a test), and the two helpers reduced to a `d in _REBALANCE_BY_DATE` membership + a `.get(d)` lookup — a true O(1) dict lookup; (3) a new module-level `_FORCED_EXIT_MARGIN = timedelta(minutes=10)` + a public `forced_exit_time_for_session(session) -> time` returning `(combine(session.date, session.close_time_ist) - _FORCED_EXIT_MARGIN).time()`, exported from `brutex/calendars/__init__.py` (import block + `__all__`, alphabetical). The 7 test types are exercised: unit + bug-fix REGRESSION (the tf-guard + the rebalance-map-equals-scan tests), hypothesis PROPERTY (a new `tests/property/test_calendar_nse_property.py` — bar-count range/rejection, a forced-exit oracle + timeframe-monotonicity invariant, the fixed-IST-offset-no-DST invariant across 2020-2026, and the trading-day biconditional), GOLDEN (the exact January-2024 trading-day list), BENCH-via-O(1)-STRUCTURAL (the dict lookup proven equal to the linear scan for every event), STRESS (the full 2021-2026 span resolves sorted + unique + sane), and INTEGRATION (the public facade re-exports the helper and the end-to-end session → forced-exit flow works through `brutex.calendars`). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ `forced_exit_time_for_session` for the standard 09:15-15:30 session returns EXACTLY 15:20 (== `FORCED_EXIT_IST`), so engine behaviour is UNCHANGED — this is an additive COMMON helper, not a re-timing of the existing exit; ⚠️ the in-code Muhurat 2023/2024 session hours (18:00-19:00) DIFFER from the canonical `docs/TRACK1_MICROSTRUCTURE.md` §3 hours (18:15-19:15) — this was NOT changed because it cannot be authoritatively verified here and is not engine-affecting (Muhurat is excluded from the Sharpe denominator); the new tests pin only SELF-CONSISTENCY invariants (open < close, ~1-hour window, the helper scales to whatever close is stored), never the canonical hours; the 2026 holidays + Muhurat dates remain UNVERIFIED exactly as before; ✅ calendars files + tests only — no `brutex/` change outside `brutex/calendars/`. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/calendars/nse.py` at **100% line+branch** (105/0 stmt + 18/0 branch, 0 missing) under the per-module CI gate `pytest --cov=brutex.calendars.nse --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_calendar_nse.py` (96 tests GREEN); the property suite `tests/property/test_calendar_nse_property.py` (6 tests) GREEN under `-W error`; ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on `brutex/calendars/nse.py`, `brutex/calendars/__init__.py`, and the two test files. **Files:** `brutex/calendars/nse.py`, `brutex/calendars/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/test_calendar_nse.py`, `tests/property/test_calendar_nse_property.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-002. **Part of:** the resilience + O(1)-discipline hardening arc — a meaningless timeframe raises a clear error, a date-keyed lookup is O(1), and the forced-exit time is one COMMON rule that already gives the canonical 15:20.
