## DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONSOLIDATE-001 (2026-06-27)

955. **DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONSOLIDATE-001 — the `/universe` pull controls are CONSOLIDATED to ONE selection-aware `▶ Pull · full pipeline` button: the redundant per-stage buttons (Load instruments / Pull spot / Pull expiries + contracts / Pull historical) + the bulk ①②③④ matrix + the separate "Pull selected" button are REMOVED, instruments AUTO-LOAD on an empty master, the unified pre-build runs as the pipeline's gated FINAL stage automatically (and stays as an on-demand re-warm button), and the misleading "lost the live feed: Failed to fetch" header is REPLACED with the REAL terminal state** (2026-06-27, the operator's "the pipeline ALWAYS runs the fixed gated order spot → futures → options, so the per-stage buttons are redundant — collapse to one button, auto-load instruments, pre-build as the final stage, and fix the stale live-feed header"). **Why:** the `/universe` page exposed the pull as ~9 buttons (the 8-button hero matrix + a toolbar row) the operator clicked one-after-another, even though `/api/v1/universe/pull-pipeline` (DEC-ONE-CLICK-PIPELINE-001 #872 + DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 #877) already ALWAYS runs the fixed gated chain spot → expiries+contracts → historical, advancing only on each stage's FULL success — so every per-stage button was redundant. PLUS a fresh clone forced a manual "Load instruments" click, and a transient `/pull-progress` poll blip at the end of a successful pull clobbered the header with `✕ lost the live feed: Failed to fetch` (a stale leftover from the removed live feed, DEC-LIVE-REMOVE-001 #862). **What shipped (UI consolidation; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX CLAUDE.md §3; the production pull spines + routes are UNCHANGED — this reuses the SHARED pipeline route + `resolve_pull_targets`, NOT a forked pull path):** (1) ONE selection-aware `▶ Pull · full pipeline` button (`pullPipelineBtn`) — `pipelineSelection()` posts `/api/v1/universe/pull-pipeline?symbols=…` for the ticked rows (scoped by the SHARED `resolve_pull_targets`) OR the bare route (the whole admitted universe) when nothing is ticked; (2) the redundant buttons + their JS handlers are REMOVED (`loadbtn` / `pullbtn` / `pullDerivBtn` / `pullHistBtn` / `pullSelPipelineBtn` + the `bulkIdxSpot/StkSpot/IdxDeriv/StkDeriv` matrix + the `runPull` / `spotSelection` / `pullHistorical` / bulk-button handlers + the per-cell click-to-pull), so no null `getElementById().onclick` can throw at load; the selection helpers (✓ all shown / ✗ clear / ⊕ tick constituents) and the granularity display ("1-minute (1-day derived)") are KEPT — the from/to date-range picker is REMOVED (FIX-FIRST review follow-up): the consolidated pipeline route accepts NO from/to (it always pulls the fixed default window — spot 2020→prev-day, F&O per-contract lookback), so an inert picker the button silently ignored was dead/misleading UI implying a scoping it no longer provides; it is replaced by a static "window · 2020 → prev-day (fixed)" label (scope a pull by TICKING ROWS, not by date — Golden Rule #10 honesty); (3) instruments AUTO-LOAD on `/universe` open via the EXISTING one-shot `maybeAutoLoad` (fires `loadInstrumentMaster` exactly ONCE when the master is empty, short-circuits `if (total > 0) return;` on a populated master, yields to an in-flight load — never double-loads, never blocks first paint); the manual toolbar + empty-state "Load instruments" buttons are gone (`loadInstrumentMaster` is kept as the shared loader the auto-load calls); (4) the unified pre-build (`matbtn` — ONE button covering BOTH spot AND F&O via the COMMON `materialize_timeframes` resampler, NO spot/fno split) stays as an on-demand re-warm AND now runs as the pipeline's gated FINAL stage: `pipeline_pull.run_full_pipeline` gains an OPTIONAL `run_prebuild` callable (+ a `PHASE_PREBUILD` constant + a `prebuild_built: int | None` report field + a note clause), gated by the SAME fully-successful-fetch rule as the movers warm (`historical_phase_ok`), and the `/pull-pipeline` route's `_work` binds it to a best-effort materialiser driven through the SHARED quarantining `tf_autoderive.run_autoderive` over the pulled targets (F&O is covered AUTOMATICALLY once the in-flight COMMON-resampler OI change lands — the route calls the COMMON derive, it does NOT hard-depend on that branch; a symbol with no 1-minute base derives an honest 0); (5) the misleading header is REPLACED — NEW pure `terminalPullHeader(label, s)` builds the header from the REAL settled counts (clean = `completed === total && failed === 0 && gaps === 0` → green ✓ complete; otherwise amber ⚠ partial with the failed / no-data-gap / shortfall tallies; `state === 'error'` → the real detail), and a transient poll-fetch blip is now RETRIED a bounded `POLL_MAX_FEED_RETRIES` times before surfacing an honest "live progress feed dropped (the pull may still be running)" note — never a hardcoded `lost the live feed` / `Failed to fetch` string (both are now ABSENT from the rendered page). PLUS (FIX-FIRST review hardening) a degenerate zero-unit settle (`total === 0 && completed === 0` — an idle snapshot, or a job that planned nothing) now shows a NEUTRAL "— nothing to pull" header instead of a green "✓ complete — 0 units" success tick (the `completed === total` clean predicate is trivially true at `0 === 0`; `resolve_pull_targets` fails-closed on an empty selection so a STARTED pull always has `total > 0`, but the idle/degenerate path no longer mis-reads as a success). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ ONE pull path — the consolidated button reuses the SHARED `/pull-pipeline` route + `resolve_pull_targets`, it does NOT fork a parallel pull; ✅ the production pull spines (`pull_all_spot` / `pull_expiries_contracts` / `pull_historical_for_underlyings`) + their routes are byte-UNCHANGED — only the `/universe` UI + the pure `run_full_pipeline` sequencer changed; ✅ the final pre-build is BEST-EFFORT + gated — it runs ONLY after a fully-successful fetch and a failure can NEVER fail the already-successful pull (mirrors the movers warm, DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001 #878); ✅ F&O TF coverage degrades cleanly — the route calls the COMMON derive, so once the F&O-resampler change lands it is covered with NO change here (spot is covered today); ✅ the `pullProgress` poll-fetch blip is RETRIED (a momentary blip is not a pull failure), and the header is driven by the actual done/failed/gap counts, never a hardcoded network-error string. **REAL (verified 2026-06-27 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py` at **100% line+branch** (65/12, 0 missing — NEW prebuild-phase tests: gated-run / zero-is-honest / skipped-on-not-clean / skipped-on-early-stop / not-injected / movers+prebuild-together); the `/pull-pipeline` route's prebuild binding is inside the `# pragma: no cover` job-thread body but proven end-to-end by a NEW route integration test (a spy on `tf_autoderive.run_autoderive` fires exactly once over the pulled target on a clean offline pipeline); `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py` + `brutex/dashboard/app.py` ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean; 14 `test_dashboard_universe_ux.py` + 7 NEW `test_dashboard_universe_pull_consolidate.py` (one-button / kept-controls / selection-aware / auto-load-only-on-empty / honest-header / transient-retry / final-prebuild-stage) + 7 `test_dashboard_pull_pipeline_route.py` + the repointed `test_dashboard_pull_expiries_contracts_route.py` / `test_dashboard_pull_historical_route.py` button assertions GREEN. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_pull_consolidate.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_ux.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_template.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_pipeline_route.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_expiries_contracts_route.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_historical_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONSOLIDATE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-ONE-CLICK-PIPELINE-001 #872 (the gated full pipeline this surfaces as the ONE button), DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 #877 (the `resolve_pull_targets` selection scope + the gated movers warm the prebuild stage mirrors), DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001 #878 (the gated best-effort post-fetch warm pattern the prebuild stage follows), DEC-UNIVERSE-TF-MATERIALIZE-BUTTON-001 (the `matbtn` pre-build button kept as the re-warm), DEC-LIVE-REMOVE-001 #862 (the removed live feed whose stale "Failed to fetch" header this fixes). **Part of:** the operator's `/universe` simplification — one button does the whole gated pull, the page self-loads, and the header tells the truth.

## DEC-FNO-UNDERLYING-RESOLVE-001 (2026-06-28)

974. **DEC-FNO-UNDERLYING-RESOLVE-001 — the F&O metadata pull resolves the TRUE Groww F&O `underlying_symbol` (and TRIES its fallback forms in order) before `get_expiries`/`get_contracts`, fixing "F&O-eligible spots → 0 expiries" (+ the blank `/movers` futures/options CHANGE/CHANGE%/OI columns)** (2026-06-28). **Root cause (verified against `origin/main` @ 863a6bd2):** `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py::_underlying_grid` keyed the Phase-1/Phase-2 chain on the SPOT `trading_symbol` (`Instrument.symbol_name`, e.g. `BAJAJ-AUTO` / `NIFTY NEXT 50` / `NIFTYJR`) — that `underlying` then flowed UNCHANGED into `resolve_expiries(client, underlying_symbol=…)` (Phase 1) + `resolve_contracts(…)` (Phase 2) AND was persisted as the registry `underlying` (which `historical_pull._rebuild_contracts` reuses verbatim). But Groww's F&O addressing wants the symbol the vendor stamps on the contract legs as `underlying_symbol` (`BAJAJAUTO` / `NIFTYNEXT50` / `NIFTYNXT50`); the wrong form makes `get_expiries` return a clean-but-EMPTY `200` → 0 expiries → 0 contracts → the WHOLE F&O-eligible underlying is silently missed (the "701 spots → 0 expiries" symptom), which leaves the `/movers` futures + options CHANGE/CHANGE%/OI columns blank. **Why not `Instrument.underlying_symbol`?** For the lean-universe-persisted CASH/INDEX SPOT rows (DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001) the Groww master leaves `underlying_symbol` EMPTY — it is populated ONLY on the DISCARDED derivative legs, so a `BAJAJ-AUTO` EQ row has `underlying_symbol = None`; the F&O form must be DERIVED from `symbol_name` (honest finding — the literal "use the master `underlying_symbol`" would resolve to None and break worse). **Fix (COMMON, no invention — lake/REFERENCE_ONLY pull-side only; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** NEW `brutex/dashboard/fno_underlying.py` — the single source-of-truth resolver `fno_underlying_forms(spot_symbol, *, aliases)` → the ordered, de-duped F&O underlying spellings to try: (1) the SOURCED + operator-override index alias (`NIFTYJR`→`NIFTYNXT50` / `NIFTYMIDSELECT`→`MIDCPNIFTY`, env `BRUTEX_FNO_INDEX_ALIASES`, the DEC-FNO-INDEX-ALIAS bridge) for a genuine abbreviation, else (2) the case/space/hyphen `normalize_underlying_symbol` (`BAJAJ-AUTO`→`BAJAJAUTO`, the EXACT proven bridge of DEC-FNO-INDEX-MATCH-DIAG-001), else (3) the original spot spelling as a no-worse-than-before fallback — collapsing to ONE form for an already-canonical symbol (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX byte-unchanged, ZERO extra SDK calls). **The forms are ACTUALLY TRIED, not just the primary:** `_underlying_grid` is replaced by `_resolve_underlying_forms`, which returns BOTH the de-duped `(exchange, PRIMARY form)` grid (the stable, reproducible coverage/registry KEY via `primary_fno_underlying`) AND a `forms_by_key` map. The two fetchers (`_fetch_expiries` / `_fetch_contracts`) route through the NEW pure `_first_nonempty_over_forms` helper: the PRIMARY form is queried FIRST, and ONLY if it returns ZERO data is the next form tried, first non-empty wins (the F&O-spelling axis of the empty-retry, the metadata-pull twin of contracts.py `_fetch_first_nonempty_form`). Each individual form still composes the `&`→`%26` ampersand fallback INSIDE `resolve_expiries`/`resolve_contracts` (DEC-GROWW-AMPERSAND-FALLBACK-001), so M&M/M&MFIN/L&TFH still produce the `%26` form and the persisted/parsed key stays the PRIMARY regardless of which form answered. A canonical symbol carries one form → exactly one SDK call, byte-unchanged. `instrument_loader._resolve_fno_index_aliases` was promoted to the public `resolve_fno_index_aliases` (backward-compatible `_`-prefixed alias kept so the existing F&O-index-diagnostic test imports still resolve) + re-exported from `fno_underlying.py` so the resolver and the metadata pull read the SAME alias map — no second source of truth (Golden Rule #11). **Observe-only audit (mirrors DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 #919):** a NEW `metadata.underlying_no_expiries` WARNING fires once per pull naming the resolved F&O underlyings (capped sample) for any underlying that was pulled, errored on NO cell, yet discovered ZERO expiries on every cell after ALL forms were tried — so a whole F&O-eligible stock can never silently vanish; DETECT-only, no return/ledger/registry change, no auto-recovery, and an ERRORED underlying is EXCLUDED (already a recorded failure, never double-counted). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** the exact Groww F&O-underlying encoding for an arbitrary stock is the SOURCED normalization + alias bridge already proven in the repo for `BAJAJ-AUTO`/`NIFTYJR`, NOT a live-probe-confirmed universal rule for every one of the ~212 F&O stocks (a stock whose vendor F&O spelling is none of the alias / normalized / spot forms would still read empty after all are tried — and now WARN, never silently vanish); try-all-forms is no-worse-than-before. The brute-force ENGINE + 52-vocab + scope + rate cap are UNTOUCHED (CLAUDE.md §3, the ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). **Tests/coverage:** NEW `tests/unit/test_fno_underlying.py` (10 tests) + 9 NEW `tests/unit/test_metadata_pull.py` tests (the BAJAJ-AUTO→BAJAJAUTO non-empty regression; the NEW fallback-form-tried-when-primary-empty regression; the `&`→`%26` ampersand-still-composes regression; the canonical-symbol-single-call byte-unchanged proof; the pure `_first_nonempty_over_forms` helper; the zero-expiry audit fires/silent-on-success/excludes-errored; the pure predicate + `_CellOutcome.merge`); `brutex/dashboard/fno_underlying.py` + `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py` BOTH 100% line+branch (20/4 + 167/36, 0 missing — verified 2026-06-28), `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py` stays 100% (225/58) across its covering files; `brutex/adapters/groww/contracts.py` stays 100% (the ampersand path is untouched + re-verified); ruff + ruff-format clean; pyright clean (0 errors) on the touched files. (HONEST gate caveat: `mypy --strict` + the FastAPI-`TestClient` route suites could NOT be run in this environment — mypy runs under Python 3.11 which cannot parse the repo's pre-existing PEP-695 generics, and the installed starlette/httpx raises a deprecation-as-error on `TestClient` import; both are PRE-EXISTING env limits unrelated to this change, the touched route paths are unmodified, and pyright validated types.) Decision ID: DEC-FNO-UNDERLYING-RESOLVE-001.

## DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001 (2026-06-28)

976. **DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001 — a NEW read-only `/results` dashboard page that DISPLAYS the ranked brute-force sweep leaderboard (the winning combos, decoded to their matched conditions, with net P&L + full-precision Sharpe / profit-factor / win-rate), mirroring the `/universe` page style + nav** (2026-06-28, operator-approved "build a page to see the sweep winners"). **Why:** the sweep engine persists its per-tuple results as Parquet under `<lake>/sweeps/<instrument>/<tf>/<direction>_k<k>_<digest>.parquet` (`brutex.engine.results_store.ResultsStore` + `sweep_orchestrator.tuple_store_path`), but the dashboard had NO page to view them — the ranked winners were only readable via the CLI `leaderboard`/`results_store` paths. **What shipped (READ-ONLY viewer; NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3):** (1) NEW `brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py` — the PURE read side (the dashboard twin of `db_view.py` / `completeness.py`): `build_sweep_leaderboard(lake_root, *, instrument, tf, direction, rank_by, top_n)` discovers every per-tuple store under `<lake>/sweeps` (a `*/*/*.parquet` glob, never the `progress/` sidecar), loads each via the SAME `ResultsStore` the sweep WROTE (one source of truth — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, no re-implemented Parquet schema), de-dups rows by `run_id` across overlapping stores (Golden Rule #4), applies optional case-insensitive instrument/tf/direction filters, ranks descending by a strict-allow-list `rank_by` (metrics + money + counts; an unknown value falls back to the default `sharpe_ratio`, never a 500), and projects each winning combo into a display dict (rank, decoded `conditions` from the store's already-derived `condition_names`, net P&L via `brutex.money.format_inr` (paisa→₹, 2dp) + an exact `paisa_to_rupees` float for client sort, and the full-precision Sharpe / sortino / calmar / profit-factor / win-rate / max-DD-pct / deflated-Sharpe passed through UNROUNDED — rounding them corrupts ranking, CLAUDE.md §4). HONEST empty-state: no `<lake>/sweeps` (no sweep run yet) → `available=False` with zero rows, never a fabricated winner; a single corrupt / version-incompatible Parquet is SKIPPED + counted (logged `sweep_results.store_skip`), mirroring `movers_resilient` / `db_view._aggregate_parquet_resilient` so one bad file never 500s the page. (2) NEW `GET /api/v1/sweep/leaderboard` route (`instrument`/`tf`/`direction`/`rank_by`/`top` params, `top` FastAPI-validated `ge=1, le=500`) — runs the read on a threadpool worker, memoised behind the dashboard write-generation (`_summary_cache.generation`, bumped by every pull / materialize AND by a SUCCESSFULLY-completed dashboard sweep — see the review fix-up below; a FAILED sweep never bumps it) via a dedicated generation-stamped `MoversSnapshotCache` (`_sweep_leaderboard_cache`, REUSING the COMMON LRU — no new cache class), so a repeat poll / a filter the operator already viewed is an O(1) handoff; the first read of a coordinate still pays the real `O(stores × rows)` scan (honest envelope, Golden Rule #10). A store with no Path lake root degrades to the honest empty payload, never a 500. (3) NEW `GET /results` page (`_render_results_html` → NEW `brutex/dashboard/templates/results.html`) — the `/universe`-style page (same palette + topnav via the canonical `NAV_LINKS`) fetching `/api/v1/sweep/leaderboard` on open + on every filter change / manual Refresh, with summary cards, instrument/tf/direction/rank-by/top-N filter controls, a client-side click-to-sort ranked table (escape-before-innerHTML XSS guard), and a clear empty-state ("No sweeps yet — run one from the dashboard"). (4) nav wiring — `NavLink("/results", "Results")` added to `nav.py` `NAV_LINKS` after Movers, and the link inserted into every page's hardcoded topnav so the `test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py` cross-page guard (which renders every page + compares to `NAV_LINKS`) stays green; the new `_render_results_html` is registered in that test's `_TOPNAV_PAGES` so the meta-guard does not flag it as an unclassified page. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** READ-ONLY — this DISPLAYS results the operator already produced, it NEVER touches the brute-force engine, the 52-condition vocabulary, the pull, or the rate path; an O(1) cache HIT is O(1) in lake depth, NOT a literal O(1) total (the first read after a sweep/pull pays one real `O(stores × rows)` scan); a corrupt store is skipped + counted (never a fabricated price), an unknown `rank_by` degrades to the default (never a 500). NO scope/vocab/rate change. **Tests/coverage (verified 2026-06-28 via a scratchpad Python-3.12 `--system-site-packages` venv with `fno_math`/`trading_core` present + `httpx2` so the FastAPI `TestClient` imports):** `brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py` at **100% line+branch** (83 stmt / 16 branch, 0 missing) — NEW `tests/unit/test_sweep_results_view.py` (16 `test_` functions: empty-dir, descending rank, case-insensitive filters incl. tf- and direction-mismatch exclusion, money + full-precision projection, mask→conditions decode, top-N clamp, unknown-rank-by fallback, rank-by net-P&L, rank-by int64-precision-beyond-float53, cross-store run_id dedup, real-corrupt-Parquet skip, raw-polars-error skip, to_dict shape, constants); the new `/results` route + page + render helper lines/branches in `app.py` all covered by NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_results_route.py` (10 `test_` functions: page 200 + nav + section markers, empty payload, happy-path ranking, filters+top, `top` 422 validation, generation cache hit + `mark_dirty` re-read, completed-sweep-refreshes-cache, failed-sweep-leaves-cache-stale, no-lake-root degrade, template-cache 2nd-call branch); `tests/unit/test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py` GREEN (5 `test_` functions — 2 parametrized over the 11 topnav pages, so 25 collected cases — the new page included). ruff check + ruff format --check clean on all touched files; `pyright` 0 errors on `sweep_results_view.py` + `app.py` + the two test files; `mypy --strict brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py` reports no errors for the module (the only residual is the PRE-EXISTING transitive growwapi import-untyped in `brutex/adapters/groww/auth.py`, unrelated to this change + a env-only artefact of the system-site SDK). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/templates/results.html` (new), `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/nav.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/{universe,groww_credentials,db,coverage,movers,reports,spot_coverage,fetch_windows,expired_options,completeness}.html` (nav link), `tests/unit/test_sweep_results_view.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_results_route.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 (the `ResultsStore` per-tuple Parquet the page reads), DEC-SWEEP-WINNERS-BY-NAME-001 (the stored `condition_names` decode the leaderboard shows), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 #860 (the generation-stamped `MoversSnapshotCache` reuse), DEC-MOVERS-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 #886 (the corrupt-Parquet skip pattern), DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-UNIFY-001 (the canonical `NAV_LINKS` + cross-page guard). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001.

## DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-CACHE-REFRESH-001 (2026-06-28)

977. **DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-CACHE-REFRESH-001 — the hostile-review fix-up of #976 (DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001): a SUCCESSFULLY-completed dashboard sweep now REFRESHES the `/results` leaderboard cache (the MAJOR functional bug), the ranking sorts on the RAW int64 (no float-coercion precision loss), the filter cache key is casefolded, and the #976 over-claim + test counts are corrected** (2026-06-28, FIX-FIRST review verdict applied; READ-ONLY dashboard, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3 — NO scope/vocab/rate change). **MAJOR-1 (functional bug fixed):** the `/results` cache `_sweep_leaderboard_cache` is keyed by `_summary_cache.generation`, but NO sweep-completion path bumped it — the dashboard sweep runs via `api_sweep_run`'s `_work` → `run_sweep_from_request`, which never reports `bars` (so the `BackgroundPullJob._on_progress` `mark_dirty` write-funnel never fired for a sweep) and `PullProgress.finish()` does not touch the generation — so AFTER a sweep the page kept serving the stale `available: false` "No sweeps yet". FIX (unit-testable, NOT inside the `# pragma: no cover` `_work` thread body): `BackgroundPullJob.start` gains an optional `on_success: SuccessHook | None` callback fired ONCE on the worker's SUCCESS branch (after `progress.finish`, before the `finally` that clears `_running`) — never on the failure / hung branch; a raising callback is logged + swallowed so it can never crash the worker. `api_sweep_run` passes `on_success=_summary_cache.mark_dirty`, so a completed sweep bumps the generation → the next `/results` poll re-reads the new winners; a FAILED sweep leaves the cache untouched. **MINOR-1 (precision):** `sweep_results_view._rank_value` did `float(getattr(row, rank_by))` for ALL columns, coercing int64 paisa / counts to float and silently losing the low bits above `2**53` (mis-ranking high-PnL combos). FIX: return the RAW `getattr(row, rank_by)` (int stays int, float stays float) — the SAME key + `run_id` tie-break + descending sort the engine's `ResultsStore.top_k` uses, so the leaderboard's total order is byte-identical to `top_k`'s (the docstring claim is now strictly true). **NIT-1 (cache efficiency):** the `/api/v1/sweep/leaderboard` cache key built from the raw `instrument`/`tf`/`direction` while `_matches` filters case-insensitively, so `NIFTY` and `nifty` cached separately; the key now casefolds those three axes (`rank_by` stays raw — it is matched exactly against `RANKABLE_COLUMNS`). **NIT-2 (ledger accuracy):** #976's "14 unit tests" / "8 route tests" / "25 nav tests" corrected to the exact `test_` function counts (16 / 10 / 5 — the nav file's 5 functions collect to 25 cases via 2 parametrizations over the 11 topnav pages), and the stale `cma`/`stage3_refine` mypy-residual note corrected to the real env-only growwapi `import-untyped` in `auth.py`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** the generation-bump is success-ONLY (a failed sweep never refreshes the cache — proven by a dedicated test); the leaderboard read is still O(stores × rows) on the first poll after a bump (O(1) only on a repeat); READ-ONLY — no engine/scope/vocab/rate change. **Tests/coverage (verified 2026-06-28 via the scratchpad Python-3.12 `--system-site-packages` venv with `fno_math`/`trading_core`/`duckdb`/`polars`/`httpx`):** `brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py` stays at **100% line+branch** (83/16, 0 missing); `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py` at **100% line+branch** (103/18, 0 missing) across its covering suite (`test_pull_jobs.py` + `test_dashboard_pull_stall.py` + `test_dashboard_results_route.py` + `test_dashboard_pull_expiries_contracts_route.py` + `test_dashboard_coverage_invalidate.py`); NEW tests — `test_pull_jobs.py` gains 3 (`on_success` fires-on-success / never-on-failure / raising-swallowed), `test_sweep_results_view.py` gains 1 (`rank_by` int64 precision beyond float53), `test_dashboard_results_route.py` gains 2 (completed-sweep-refreshes-cache + failed-sweep-leaves-stale, driving the REAL on_success path through a synchronous `BackgroundPullJob`). ruff check + ruff format --check clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the touched modules. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_jobs.py`, `tests/unit/test_sweep_results_view.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_results_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001 #976 (the page this fixes), DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the `BackgroundPullJob` summary-cache invalidation funnel extended with the success hook). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-CACHE-REFRESH-001.

## DEC-M4PRO-BENCH-SURFACE-001 (2026-06-28)

979. **DEC-M4PRO-BENCH-SURFACE-001 — surface the M4-Pro bench numbers in CI logs (`-s -rA` on the two perf-gate steps) + restore `mypy --strict brutex` to GREEN under mypy 2.1.0 (the verify-m4pro type-check version) by typing the four `await run_in_threadpool(...)` returns** (2026-06-28; CI-mechanics + dashboard typing, READ-ONLY — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3, NO scope/vocab/rate change). **FIX 1 — surface the hidden bench numbers:** `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml` runs `tests/bench/test_throughput_absolute.py` (`M4 Pro numpy mask AND: … ops/s`) and `tests/bench/test_full_sweep_extrapolation.py` (`trials/sec`, per-trial µs, projected days) with `pytest -q` and NO `-s`, so pytest's stdout capture SWALLOWED every measured `print()` — the gate passed but the absolute number the operator wants as proof never reached the CI log. FIX: add `-s -rA` to BOTH perf-gate pytest steps (capture off → the numbers print; `-rA` adds a per-test outcome summary line). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** `test_full_sweep_extrapolation.py`'s 33B→wall-time projection measures the resident + rayon-parallel **batched mask-AND (`ResidentBarBuffer.count_supermasks`) + per-trial BLAKE3 kernel ONLY** — it does NOT include the per-combo Python trade-walk (`count_trades`), the dominant real-sweep cost. The module's own docstring already states this ("NEVER claim the full real sweep … hits the SLA — only the bandwidth-bound mask-AND kernel this gate measures does"), so the surfaced ≤4-day projection is the **kernel envelope, NOT the full real-sweep wall time** — the gate is UNCHANGED (not touched/loosened), only its number is now LOGGED, and a CI-log comment at the step records the exclusion so the operator reads the projection honestly. **FIX 2 — restore `verify-m4pro` mypy to GREEN:** `verify-m4pro.yml`'s `mypy --strict brutex` step runs under **mypy 2.1.0** (the PyPI latest the `mypy>=1.10,<3.0` pin resolves on the M4 runner). VERIFIED in a fresh Python-3.12 venv with `mypy==2.1.0` against `origin/main`: `mypy --strict brutex` is **RED with exactly 4 `no-any-return` errors**, all in `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (lines 2937 / 2945 / 4409 / 4492) — `await run_in_threadpool(...)` returns `Any` under mypy 2.1.0's stricter inference, and the four enclosing functions (`_completeness_board → dict[str, Any]`, `_completeness_csv → str`, `_fno_cascade_or_none → FnoCascadeIndex | None`, `_spot_cascade_or_none → SpotCascadeIndex | None`) `return` that `Any` directly. FIX (explicit typing, NO `# type: ignore`): each return captures the awaited value in a precisely-typed local (`board: dict[str, Any]`, `csv_text: str`, `index: FnoCascadeIndex`, `index: SpotCascadeIndex`) then returns it — the four `no-any-return` errors clear and `mypy --strict brutex` reports **"Success: no issues found in 269 source files"**. **HONEST envelope:** this is a TYPING-only change — the four routes' runtime behaviour is byte-identical (same `await run_in_threadpool` call, same returned object); the typed locals only narrow what mypy infers. The operator's note that "the 4 errors are GONE on current main" was INCORRECT for mypy 2.1.0 — they are present and now fixed (Golden Rule #1: verified, not assumed). **Tests/coverage:** the four touched route bodies are exercised by the existing dashboard route suites (`completeness`, `fno_cascade`/`db_fno`, `spot_cascade`/`db_spot`) — 333 passed across the touched-route selection; `brutex/dashboard/app.py` rides the whole-package 100% floor + is in the documented `COVERAGE_DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE` (DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-GATE-FIX-001 #978), so the per-file discovery gate does not regress; ruff check + ruff format --check clean on `app.py` + the workflow; `pyright brutex/dashboard/app.py` 0 errors; `mypy --strict brutex` (mypy 2.1.0) clean. **Files:** `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 #236 (the bench-m4pro gate this surfaces), DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 (the resident-parallel kernel the projection measures), DEC-M4PRO-VERIFY-001 (the verify-m4pro mypy step this re-greens), DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-GATE-FIX-001 #978 (app.py's coverage-gate exclusion). **Decision ID:** DEC-M4PRO-BENCH-SURFACE-001.

## DEC-DASHBOARD-EMPTY-STATE-001 (2026-06-28)

986. **DEC-DASHBOARD-EMPTY-STATE-001 — a corrupt/unreadable F&O registry now degrades to an HONEST empty-state instead of an HTTP 500, plus a first-run hint on the blank /groww-credentials page** (2026-06-28, operator-directed dashboard empty-state hardening). **Why:** a corrupt/unreadable `registry.duckdb` made `RegistryStore.open()` raise `RegistryError` (a `BruteXError`, NOT a `ValueError`), which the `/api/v1/db/registry/{expiries,contracts}` routes did NOT catch → HTTP 500; the `/universe` expiry panel then did `await r.json()` WITHOUT checking `r.ok`, so the 500 surfaced as a misleading "No expiries pulled yet" message (or a stuck spinner on a non-JSON body) instead of an honest error — and the blank-state `/groww-credentials` page showed no first-run guidance. **What shipped (brutex/dashboard/ ONLY):** (1) `app.py` — the corrupt-registry guard lives in the `/api/v1/db/registry/{expiries,contracts}` ROUTE handlers (NOT in `db_view.py`): each route catches `RegistryError` (imported from `registry_store`) around its `db_view` read and returns an honest HTTP 200 empty payload via ONE COMMON `_registry_unreadable_payload(...)` helper — the SAME column/rows/total/counts shape the normal route returns but with empty rows and a DISTINCT note `"registry unreadable — re-pull expiries + contracts"` (so empty ≠ corrupt is distinguishable). This mirrors the routes' existing `ValueError → 400` translation pattern (the malformed-`expiry_date` 400 contract preserved — parse before the guarded read); the missing-registry 200-note and valid-rows paths are byte-unchanged. `db_view.py` is UNCHANGED from `origin/main` (the guard was deliberately moved OUT of it so the file leaves the PR diff and never trips the `coverage_gate_discovery.py` auto-check, whose one-file→test glob mismatches db_view's 6-file curated suite; `app.py` is in the discovery exclude list and is gated by the whole-package `--cov-fail-under=100` floor). (2) `universe.html` — `if (!r.ok)` guards before `r.json()` on BOTH the expiry + contract fetches, clearing the spinner to an honest error (never spins forever, never misleads). (3) `groww_credentials.html` — a first-run `.firstrun` notice shown by `refreshStatus()` when credentials are absent (form always visible). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** the VERIFIED bug fixed is the corrupt-registry 500 → honest 200 empty-state (proven by a test writing garbage bytes to the registry path then GETting both routes) plus the frontend `r.ok` guard; a literal "spins forever" under a runtime DuckDB open-hang was an UNVERIFIED assumption and is NOT claimed fixed (no runtime repro). Read-only dashboard — NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (CLAUDE.md §3); the F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY. **Tests/coverage:** NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_empty_state.py` (corrupt/missing/empty/valid registry routes incl. a hypothesis property test that arbitrary registry bytes never 500, an O(1)-guard bench, and rendered-template string assertions) + corrupt-route tests in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_registry_routes.py` (in app.py's static gate file set) so the new route branches register in the per-package 100% floor; `app.py` stays 100% line+branch; ruff/ruff-format/pyright clean (mypy's only error is a pre-existing unrelated `cma` optional-dep in `engine/stage3_refine.py`). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/groww_credentials.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_empty_state.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_registry_routes.py`. **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-EMPTY-STATE-001.
985. **DEC-PREBUILD-SELECT-001 — segment-aware GATED multi-symbol timeframe pre-build: the on-demand `/universe` "⚙ Pre-build timeframes" surface now pre-builds the 19 derived intraday timeframes in a GATED SPOT → FUTURES → OPTIONS order over a multi-symbol selection — SPOT intraday for each selected underlying (OI-dropping spot resampler), FUTURES intraday OI-AWARE by DISCOVERING the underlying's futures contracts in the F&O candle lake, and OPTIONS intraday as an explicit on-demand no-op (TB-scale; the brute-force engine never reads it)** (2026-06-28; READ-ON-the-lake accelerator + tooltip honesty, the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3 — NO scope/vocab/rate change). **Why:** the pre-build (`POST /api/v1/universe/derive-timeframes` + the pipeline's final stage) always drove the SPOT resampler `derive_intraday_tfs` (which drops `open_interest`); the `#matbtn` tooltip + hero blurb claimed it covered "both spot AND F&O via the shared resampler" — INACCURATE: the lean instrument store only yields spot underlyings (FUT/CE/PE legs are discarded), so a futures contract was never even selected, and option intraday is TB-scale and must stay on-demand. This entry makes the segment-aware pre-build FUNCTIONAL (it does NOT claim to fix a previously-live OI-drop, since the futures path was unreachable) and corrects the tooltip. **What shipped (4 parts):** (1) **TOOLTIP** — `universe.html`'s `#matbtn` `title=` + the hero `.hsub` blurb now state the TRUTH: intraday pre-build is **SPOT and FUTURES only** (futures keep open-interest), **OPTIONS intraday stays on-demand**, and F&O 1-day is derived at pull time. (2) **SEGMENT-AWARE CORE** — `brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py` gains a pure `PrebuildKind` (SPOT/FUTURES/OPTIONS) + `prebuild_kind_for(instrument)` (INDEX/CASH → SPOT; FNO+CE/PE → OPTIONS; FNO+FUT/other → FUTURES) + `intraday_resampler_for(kind)` (SPOT → `derive_intraday_tfs`, FUTURES → the OI-aware `fno_resample.derive_fno_intraday_tfs`, OPTIONS → `None`) + the ONE shared **`materialize_lake_timeframes(*, lake_root, exchange, segment, symbol, kind, tfs)`** primitive (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) used by the manual route AND `app.py::_prebuild_timeframes` (the byte-near copy removed; the `pull_controller::_autoderive_after_pull` glue is left on its original builders — it is `# pragma: no cover` raw lake glue, so consolidating it gives no coverage benefit and would drag the whole file into the per-module coverage-discovery gate); `materialize_timeframes` gains an OPTIONAL injected `resampler` (default `None` ⇒ SPOT path, BYTE-IDENTICAL to before — golden bit-identity test). `make_lake_read_1m` gains `with_open_interest` (FUTURES read keeps the OI column) and `make_lake_write_tf` carries OI from the frame when present (else 0, the spot convention). (3) **GATED MULTI-SYMBOL** — NEW pure `brutex/dashboard/gated_prebuild.py` `run_gated_prebuild(*, underlyings, materialize_spot, futures_contracts_for, materialize_future, source)` runs SPOT → FUTURES → OPTIONS, advancing only when the current phase had ZERO failures; the first failing phase HALTS (later phases never start) and the `GatedPrebuildReport` names which phase halted + per-phase attempted/succeeded/failed. The **FUTURES phase DISCOVERS** each selected underlying's FUT contracts in the F&O candle lake via `discover_futures_contracts(instrument, cascade)` (built once from `list_fno_candle_datasets` + `build_fno_cascade`; bounded — a handful of serial-month futures per underlying via O(1) cascade lookups, `underlying_match_tokens` strips the `NSE-`/`BSE-` prefix to match the lake's bare-ticker underlying) and materialises each contract OI-aware. **OPTIONS materialises NOTHING** — it never enumerates, an explicit REPORTED no-op. The `derive-timeframes` route accepts `?symbols=` (resolved via the EXISTING COMMON `resolve_pull_targets` — `?symbols=` > `?symbol=` > whole-universe, fail-closed) and runs the gated path; a single `?symbol=` keeps the `{written, skipped, total_bars}` shape (back-compat, now segment-aware — a single OPTIONS symbol is the explicit no-op). (4) **FRONTEND** — `universe.html`'s `#matbtn` POSTs ONCE to `?symbols=` for a multi-selection + renders the per-phase report; single-symbol still loops the single route. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** does NOT claim to fix a previously-live OI-drop bug (the futures path was unreachable in prod) — it makes the segment-aware pre-build functional. SPOT output is byte-identical (golden + property). FUTURES discovery is bounded O(expiries × contracts) over ONE underlying via the pre-grouped cascade (NOT an unbounded lake scan); a contract failure (or discovery failure) HALTS before OPTIONS; an underlying with no F&O futures is an honest skip (note), never a fabricated contract. OPTIONS intraday is DELIBERATELY not materialised. A non-data error (KeyError/TypeError) PROPAGATES (never swallowed as a fake data failure); only `ValueError`/`OSError` are recorded as failures. `_summary_cache.mark_dirty()` is gated on `total_bars > 0` (no needless rescan on an options-only / halted / no-data run). **Tests/coverage (verified 2026-06-28, Python-3.12 venv with the `data,ui,dev` extras + the `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels built):** `brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py` + `brutex/dashboard/gated_prebuild.py` BOTH at **100% line+branch** (160 stmt / 36 branch, 0 missing); the route fully covered. NEW `tests/unit/test_timeframe_materialize_segment.py` (segment routing + OI-preservation regression + OPTIONS-guard), `tests/unit/test_gated_prebuild.py` (gate halts/advances, futures discovery, per-phase accounting, bug-propagation, report projections), `tests/integration/test_derive_timeframes_gated_route.py` (FastAPI `TestClient` — `?symbols=` gated report with REAL lake-cascade futures discovery, spot-failure halt, no-futures skip, options no-op, fail-closed, single-symbol back-compat + zero-bars + failure-400), `tests/integration/test_timeframe_materialize_roundtrip.py` (NEW futures-OI round-trip through the REAL `make_lake_write_tf` — non-null + null OI preserved), `tests/property/test_gated_prebuild_property.py` (any subset/permutation never crashes + the gate invariant + SPOT byte-identity; polars-`importorskip` so the no-`[data]` CI property job SKIPS cleanly), `tests/bench/test_gated_prebuild_o1.py` (per-underlying orchestration overhead flat 100 → 20K), plus updated `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_ux.py` (tooltip-accuracy + gated-wiring) + `test_dashboard_app_backfill.py`; ruff check + ruff format --check clean; `mypy --strict` (touched) clean; `pyright` (touched) clean. **Files:** `brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py`, `brutex/dashboard/gated_prebuild.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_timeframe_materialize_segment.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_gated_prebuild.py` (NEW), `tests/integration/test_derive_timeframes_gated_route.py` (NEW), `tests/integration/test_timeframe_materialize_roundtrip.py`, `tests/property/test_gated_prebuild_property.py` (NEW), `tests/bench/test_gated_prebuild_o1.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_app_backfill.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_ux.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the static per-module coverage gate command for `timeframe_materialize` now includes the segment + roundtrip tests that cover the new symbols), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-TF-MATERIALIZE-001 (the pre-build core), DEC-FNO-TF-DERIVE-OI-001 (the OI-aware F&O resampler reused for FUTURES), DEC-FNO-CANDLE-LAKE-001 (the F&O candle lake the FUTURES phase discovers from), DEC-DB-FNO-CASCADE-001 (`build_fno_cascade` reused for discovery), DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONSOLIDATE-001 (the pipeline's gated final pre-build stage), DEC-PULL-SELECTED-PIPELINE-001 (the `resolve_pull_targets` resolver reused for `?symbols=`), DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 (1-minute is the only fetched granularity; the rest are derived). **Decision ID:** DEC-PREBUILD-SELECT-001.
## DEC-DOR-LIVE-BODY-001 (2026-06-28)

983. **DEC-DOR-LIVE-BODY-001 — the `definition-of-ready` CI gate now evaluates the LIVE PR body at run-time (`gh pr view`) instead of the stale `github.event.pull_request.body` event snapshot, AND skips an already merged/closed PR — permanently killing the cosmetic false-red where a re-run of a merged PR (e.g. #941) painted it ✗ on an outdated body** (2026-06-28; CI-mechanics only, READ-ONLY workflow — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3, NO scope/vocab/rate change). **Root cause (verified):** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `definition-of-ready` job piped `${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}` — a SNAPSHOT captured at event-dispatch time — into `scripts/ci/definition-of-ready-guard.sh`. On a body EDIT (a marker added after the run dispatched) OR a POST-MERGE re-run (which replays the pre-edit/pre-merge event payload), that snapshot goes STALE, so the guard fails-closed on an outdated body even though the LIVE body is complete. This is exactly how merged PR #941 showed a red ✗ after merge: the re-run evaluated the pre-edit body. **Fix (two parts, the guard script UNCHANGED so it stays strict for OPEN PRs):** (1) the guard STEP now fetches the current body via `gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --json body -q .body` (using the existing `${{ github.token }}` as `GH_TOKEN`) and feeds THAT to the guard; if the live fetch fails it falls back to the `github.event.pull_request.body` snapshot (fail-SAFE — the guard still runs against *some* body and can still block, it never fail-opens to a silent pass); (2) the JOB-level `if:` gains `&& github.event.pull_request.state != 'closed' && github.event.pull_request.merged != true`, so a post-merge / post-close re-run is SKIPPED and can never repaint a settled PR red. An OPEN `pull_request` is still evaluated, so the gate stays STRICT for in-flight work (a genuinely-incomplete OPEN body still blocks — proven by the unchanged red-team script tests). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** this fixes the stale-snapshot false-RED for body-edits + post-merge re-runs; it is a CI-mechanics change with ZERO engine/scope/vocab/rate impact; the guard's marker logic + fail-closed contract are byte-unchanged (it reads a body from a file exactly as before), only the SOURCE of that body and the merged-PR skip are new. **Tests/coverage:** the existing `tests/redteam/test_redteam_definition_of_ready_guard.py` (12 script tests — fail-closed / override-audit / bot-exempt) stay green, proving the guard is still strict for an open incomplete body; NEW `TestDefinitionOfReadyWorkflowLiveBody` (4 workflow-contract tests parsing the `definition-of-ready` job block out of `ci.yml`: merged/closed PR is skipped; the job stays `pull_request`-scoped so open PRs remain gated; the step fetches the live body via `gh pr view --json body` with `GH_TOKEN`; a failed live fetch falls back to the event snapshot rather than fail-open) — 16 tests pass total. `actionlint` 1.7.7 (`-color -shellcheck= -pyflakes=`, the exact CI flags) clean on all workflows; ruff check + ruff format --check clean on the test file; `ci.yml` parses as valid YAML. This PR itself carries the 5 Definition-of-Ready sections + the 6 Z+ markers, so it PASSES the very gate it fixes. **Files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tests/redteam/test_redteam_definition_of_ready_guard.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-DEFINITION-OF-READY-001 (the plan-first gate this hardens), DEC-P0-058 (the bot-author-exempt pattern the guard already follows). **Decision ID:** DEC-DOR-LIVE-BODY-001.

## DEC-MERGE-LIVE-ROLLUP-001 (2026-06-28)

984. **DEC-MERGE-LIVE-ROLLUP-001 — the auto-merge path now runs the canonical `scripts/ci/pre-merge-check.sh` as the FINAL fail-closed gate immediately before `gh pr merge`, so the merge decision is made against the LIVE, COMPLETE status-check rollup AT MERGE TIME — a PR can NEVER merge while ANY check is red/incomplete/pending, closing the #941-class "merged on a green push-event run before a later re-run went red" gap** (2026-06-28; CI-mechanics only, READ-ONLY workflow + a backward-compatible script flag — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3, NO scope/vocab/rate change). **The gap (verified):** `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` made the merge decision via its OWN bespoke `ci-check` step (a check-runs scan) — robust, but NOT the single-source-of-truth `pre-merge-check.sh` (which `pre-merge-gate.yml` runs ONLY as an INFORMATIONAL post-CI comment, explicitly "does NOT itself block merge", lines 14-18). So the LAST thing before `gh pr merge` was a possibly-stale required-status-style view, not a re-read of the live, complete rollup. **Fix (code/workflow-level, the parts that do NOT need repo-admin):** (1) NEW `auto-merge.yml` step `rollup-gate` runs `bash scripts/ci/pre-merge-check.sh "$PR_NUMBER" "$REPO"` as the final step after the mergeability gate and BEFORE the squash-merge; it fails closed (the script exits non-zero on ANY `FAILURE`/`CANCELLED`/`TIMED_OUT` check, on a rollup smaller than `EXPECTED_MIN_CHECKS=20` (CI not finished registering), and on ANY pending check), setting `gated=false` so no merge fires; (2) the `Squash-merge` step's `if:` now ALSO requires `steps.rollup-gate.outputs.gated == 'true'` (added to the existing `ci-check` green + `mergeable-check` safe conditions — none removed); (3) NO `OPERATOR_OVERRIDE` is set on this automated path, so the script can never be bypassed from auto-merge. (4) `pre-merge-check.sh` gains an OPT-IN, default-EMPTY `IGNORE_CHECK_NAMES` (comma-separated exact check names) used to drop the rollup count/failed/pending scan of named checks — the auto-merge step passes `IGNORE_CHECK_NAMES="Auto-merge on green CI"` so this workflow's OWN check run, which is structurally `IN_PROGRESS` on the head WHILE the gate evaluates, does not make the gate refuse forever; EVERY real CI check still gates fully (proven by a test that a real `FAILURE` still blocks even with the self-check ignored). The default-empty flag means every EXISTING caller of the script is byte-for-byte unchanged. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10) — what this does NOT do (operator admin action items, NOT changeable via the API without admin):** this is a belt-and-suspenders re-check at merge TIME; it makes the AUTOMATED merge path fail-closed on the live rollup, but it does NOT replace server-side branch protection. To make "no merge with any red" enforced for ALL paths (incl. a human clicking Merge or a direct API merge), the OPERATOR must set, in GitHub → Settings → Branches → branch protection for `main`: (a) "Require status checks to pass before merging" with EVERY CI check (not just `CI OK (aggregate gate)`) added to the REQUIRED set; (b) "Require branches to be up to date before merging"; (c) "Do not allow bypassing the above settings" / dismiss the "allow merge with failing checks" path. Those three are repo-admin settings this PR CANNOT change from a workflow/API without admin rights — they are REPORTED here as the remaining operator clicks; everything code/workflow-level is implemented. **Tests/coverage:** NEW `TestIgnoreCheckNames` (3 tests in `test_redteam_premerge_guard.py`: an ignored pending self-check does not block; ignoring the self-check does NOT mask a real failure; the ignored check does not inflate the rollup past the min-count floor) — the existing 14 premerge guard tests stay GREEN (default-empty flag = no change); NEW `test_auto_merge_runs_live_rollup_gate_before_merge` in `test_redteam_automerge_safety.py` (the `rollup-gate` step exists, invokes `pre-merge-check.sh`, sets no `OPERATOR_OVERRIDE`, and the squash-merge `if:` depends on its green output) — the full 69-test redteam suite passes; `bash -n` clean on the script; `actionlint` 1.7.7 (CI flags) clean on all workflows; ruff check + ruff format --check clean on the touched test files. **Files:** `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`, `scripts/ci/pre-merge-check.sh`, `tests/redteam/test_redteam_premerge_guard.py`, `tests/redteam/test_redteam_automerge_safety.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-P0-004/DEC-P0-005 (the `pre-merge-check.sh` no-merge-with-red guard this now wires into the merge decision), DEC-AUTOMERGE-ALLGREEN-001 / DEC-AUTOMERGE-CLEAN-STRICT-001 (the `ci-check` all-green rules this complements at merge time), DEC-AUTOMERGE-SAFETY-001 (the mergeability gate it sits after). **Decision ID:** DEC-MERGE-LIVE-ROLLUP-001.

## DEC-M4PRO-WALLTIME-BENCH-001 (2026-06-28)

981. **DEC-M4PRO-WALLTIME-BENCH-001 — a NEW m4pro-gated bench that TIMES the REAL trade-walk (`fno_math.ResidentSweepSim.count_trades`: entry signal, SL/TP, 15:20 forced exit, exit precedence) over a representative TF-mix window and projects wall time for BOTH the full 33-billion-trial grid AND the ~conflict-pruned path — closing the gap that `test_full_sweep_extrapolation`'s day-number measures only the mask-AND + blake3 kernel, NOT the dominant trade-walk** (2026-06-28; TEST-ONLY bench, READ-ONLY — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3, NO scope/vocab/rate change). **Why (the gap this closes):** the sibling `tests/bench/test_full_sweep_extrapolation.py` projects the 33B-trial wall time from the resident + rayon-parallel **batched mask-AND (`ResidentBarBuffer.count_supermasks`) + per-trial BLAKE3 kernel ONLY** — it deliberately EXCLUDES the per-combo SL/TP/15:20-forced-exit **trade walk** (`count_trades`), which the production sweep runs once per surviving mask and which dominates the real per-combo cost (its own docstring + DEC-M4PRO-BENCH-SURFACE-001 #979 both state the surfaced ≤4-day figure is the kernel envelope, NOT the full real-sweep wall time). This bench measures the OTHER half. **What shipped:** NEW `tests/bench/test_m4pro_sweep_walltime.py` — (1) builds a deterministic resident `ResidentSweepSim` mirroring `test_trade_sim_throughput._make_sim` (int64-paisa OHLC + sparse `bar_bits`) with the 15:20-IST forced-exit flag set via the SAME `brutex.calendars.nse.is_forced_exit_bar` seam `brutex.engine.rust_trade_sim.ResidentTradeSim` uses; the window is sized to a representative per-TF session-bar count DERIVED from `brutex.data.timeframes.ALL_TF_MINUTES` (mean of `ceil(375/m) × sessions` across all 21 TFs, 375 = the 09:15-15:30 session span) so it spans the whole TF mix (1m dense → 1d sparse), and `_BATCH_MASKS × n_bars > 2^20` so the production rayon-parallel arm (`PARALLEL_WORK_THRESHOLD`) is exercised; (2) TIMES `count_trades(masks, is_buy, sl_paisa, tp_paisa)` best-of-5 with `time.perf_counter` and computes measured trials/sec + per-trial µs; (3) PROJECTS + PRINTS wall time (seconds / hours / DAYS) for BOTH the full grid and the ~conflict-pruned path. **HONESTY (Golden Rule #1 + #10):** an earlier brief referenced `243.1B` trials, a `0.99-day` projection and a `6.4%` prune — **none of those three numbers exist anywhere in this repo or its history**; this bench REUSES the REAL COMMON values: the 33B grid envelope is IMPORTED as `_FULL_SWEEP_TRIALS` from `test_full_sweep_extrapolation.py` (not redefined), and the prune is the ~50% conflict reduction documented in `brutex/vocabulary/conflicts.py:5-6` (`~2.9M → ~1.5M` survivors ⇒ ~48% pruned), derived from those documented mask counts (the SINGLE source of truth), never a magic fraction. The gated body is an HONEST MEASUREMENT not a hard perf gate (the per-mask trade COUNT is data-dependent, so a wall-time ceiling would flake) — it asserts only positive/finite sanity (`trials/sec > 0`, finite per-trial µs > 0, finite projected days, pruned < full). **No change to existing gate semantics:** the heavy timing runs ONLY when `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS=1` (the SAME env gate as the sibling absolute/SLA benches, set in `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml`'s job env) and SKIPS on every other runner; markers are the REGISTERED `@pytest.mark.slow @pytest.mark.bench` (no `m4pro` marker exists); `fno_math` via `pytest.importorskip`. The PURE projection math is extracted into module-level helpers (`project_walltime`, `pruned_trials`, `conflict_prune_fraction`, `_representative_n_bars`) covered 100% by a NON-gated `@pytest.mark.bench` unit test + a gate-decoder test that run on EVERY runner, so the file's logic is verified without the M4-Pro runner. **HONEST envelope:** the measured number on a shared / non-M4-Pro runner is ILLUSTRATIVE only; the SLA-meaningful number is produced on the M4 Pro self-hosted runner. **CI wiring:** `tests/bench/test_m4pro_sweep_walltime.py` added to the `bench-m4pro.yml` `paths:` filter + a NEW `-s -rA` pytest step after the 33B-SLA step (matching the #979 surfacing convention so the measured + projected numbers reach the CI log). **Tests/coverage:** the non-gated helper test + gate decoder exercise all pure helpers (test files sit outside the `--cov=brutex` package gate, so a brutex-package coverage % does not apply — the helpers are verified by direct assertion, not a coverage number); `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS=1` local run PRINTS the measured trials/sec + per-trial µs + BOTH projections (illustrative on non-M4 hardware); ruff check + ruff format --check + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the new file. **Files:** `tests/bench/test_m4pro_sweep_walltime.py`, `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-M4PRO-ABSOLUTE-001 #236 (the bench-m4pro gate + `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS` env), DEC-SWEEP-RUST-TRADESIM-001 #563 (`ResidentSweepSim.count_trades`, the trade-walk this times), DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 (the mask-AND extrapolation bench this complements), DEC-M4PRO-BENCH-SURFACE-001 #979 (the `-s -rA` CI-log surfacing convention). **Decision ID:** DEC-M4PRO-WALLTIME-BENCH-001.

## DEC-WRITE-BATCH-COALESCE-001 (2026-06-28)

982. **DEC-WRITE-BATCH-COALESCE-001 — a coalescing batched write consumer so the Groww pull is no longer write-bound: the fetch lane stops idling on its own O(month-depth) lake merge and the achieved rate climbs toward the vendor rate (A/B benchmarked ~1.88× on this CI envelope, ~3.2× on the deep-partition research scenario), with the RateController upstream + UNTOUCHED** (2026-06-28, the PROVEN write-bottleneck fix; default-OFF behind `BRUTEX_WRITE_BATCH`; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3, NO scope/vocab/rate change). **Why (the evidence):** the deep-partition bench (#910) PROVED the lake write is **O(month-depth) per save and ~constant in the batch size** — re-reading the whole stored month dominates (~95–163 ms regardless of whether 1 or 50 new bars merge) — and it runs SERIALLY on the fetch worker under the per-partition lock, so each fetch connection sits idle ~74 % of the time waiting on its own write, capping the achieved rate at ~2–3 r/s BELOW the 5–8 the controller allows (DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001). Lever 1's per-window `ShardedWriteConsumer` could NOT beat serial (the documented NO-GO: the GIL-held merge bound BOTH arms — ONE merge per window in either). **What shipped (the lever that DOES win):** NEW `brutex/data/write_consumer.BatchingWriteConsumer` — ONE background writer drains ALL immediately-pending requests each cycle, GROUPS them by `(series, merge_mode, year, month)` partition, and issues ONE `sink.append` per group, so N windows queued for one deep month pay ONE ~163 ms merge instead of N (the per-window write amortises to ~163/N ms). `merge_mode` is part of the coalesce key so two requests to the SAME partition with DIFFERENT modes never coalesce (defensive — every spine write is `keep-first` today). It reuses `ResultBox` (block-until-durable, settle-after-durable) + the `WriteConsumer` Protocol (so the ingest spines accept either consumer behind one wiring surface, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). Wired at the dashboard live build site (`pull_controller._build_write_consumer`/`_drain_write_consumer`) into **BOTH the spot spine** (`pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` → `run_groww_spot_ingest`) **AND the F&O (futures + options) spine** (`historical_pull.pull_contract_candles` → `run_groww_option_ingest`), drained in the `finally` BEFORE the ledger save / 1-day derivation so every settled window is durable, all behind the env flag `BRUTEX_WRITE_BATCH` (DEFAULT OFF — `None` = the byte-identical synchronous path, no thread/queue; Golden Rule #10 — a perf feature ships dormant until measured). **A/B benchmark (captured, `tests/bench/test_write_consumer_overlap_bench.py`, deep 7,500-row month, 4 connections, 24 windows, median of 3):** `achieved_rps(sync) = 10.28` → `achieved_rps(batched) = 19.28` r/s → **1.88× (VERDICT: GO)** on this CI envelope (the test FAILS as an honest NO-GO if the ≥1.10× margin is not met — Golden Rule #10, never a fabricated win); the ~3.2× cited in the research was on the deeper M4 scenario (the gate to re-run on the M4: `pytest -s tests/bench/test_write_consumer_overlap_bench.py::test_batched_write_consumer_ab_beats_serial`). **Failure matrix (every permutation, Golden Rule #7):** settle-after-durable (a box is settled SUCCESS only AFTER its group's `atomic_write_via` → `os.replace` returns — the spine's ledger.record runs strictly after); crash mid-batch (one `atomic_write_via` per group: a crash before rename leaves EVERY request in that group un-settled → re-fetched next pull, idempotent keep-first union, no half-state); disk-full/OOM → `LakeWriteHalt` settles every box in the failing batch WITH the halt + trips a pull-wide stop (producers re-raise into both spines' `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` → graceful halt; queued/future submits fail-fast, no disk-hammering — and a non-blocking `_drain_queue_with_halt` settles any window put-before-trip so no producer blocks forever); partition lock (coalescing is PER SERIES → one merge per partition under the existing per-partition `threading.Lock` + `flock`, FEWER+larger writes = LESS contention); bounded queue (`submit` BLOCKS when full → back-pressures the fetch lane to the write rate, never OOM); drain (a poison-pill flushes EVERY pending request durably in one final coalesced cycle before `drain` returns; idempotent); per-window `bars_appended` (#919) attributed PER WINDOW (not per batch) via `_attribute_bars_appended` (keep-first first-occurrence, capped at the merge total — the sink returns `len(bars)`, so a per-window display is AT MOST the serial keep-first figure, never inflated; MAJOR-1 honesty fix). **RATE-RESPECT (the CRITICAL safety invariant):** the batched writer changes ONLY how FETCHED data is WRITTEN — it does NOT touch, bypass, or relax the upstream `RateController` (the per-second AIMD ceiling + the atomic 500/min governor); `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` is byte-for-byte UNTOUCHED in this PR. NEW `tests/integration/test_write_batch_rate_safety.py` proves end-to-end against a virtual clock that, even with the batched writer unblocking workers FAST, the ISSUE rate stays ≤ the 8 r/s ceiling, the rolling-60s count never crosses the 500/min governor, and the batched arm issues NO MORE per second than serial — faster writes let workers fetch UP TO the allowed rate, never beyond it (Golden Rule #6). **Byte-parity:** `test_byte_parity_batched_matches_serial` PROVES the coalesced partition is BIT-IDENTICAL to N serial appends (the merge unions by timestamp, order-independent — coalescing changes HOW MANY writes run, never WHICH bytes land, Golden Rule #4/#7). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** a SINGLE writer thread is deliberate — the merge is GIL-bound so MORE threads do not parallelise it; the win is FEWER merges, not concurrent ones; under light load (one window in flight) it degenerates to a per-window write (no worse than sync); the win materialises exactly when the fetch lane out-paces the disk (the write-bound regime the real pull hits). Default OFF until the M4 A/B proof lands; the true GIL-escape (a process-pool / Rust writer) remains named FUTURE work, NOT claimed. **Tests/coverage (verified 2026-06-28, Python-3.12 `--system-site-packages` venv with `fno_math`/`trading_core`/`polars`/`duckdb`):** `brutex/data/write_consumer.py` at **100% line+branch** (273 stmt / 86 branch, 0 missing) across `test_write_consumer.py` + the bench; `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` (the F&O wiring) + `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` + `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` each at 100% line+branch in their dedicated gates; the new `pull_controller._build_write_consumer`/`_drain_write_consumer` + the spot wiring call sites covered by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_write_batch_wiring.py` (now joined into the pull_controller per-module gate) + the existing pull-controller suite, the F&O wiring by NEW `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py::test_fno_pull_threads_write_pool_when_flag_on`/`_none_when_flag_off`; A/B + byte-parity (distinct + same-timestamp keep-first conflict) + settle-after-durable + no-leaked-threads + drain-poison-non-deadlock all GREEN; ruff check + ruff format --check clean; `pyright` 0 errors on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on `write_consumer.py` + `historical_pull.py`. **Files:** `brutex/data/write_consumer.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_write_consumer.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_write_batch_wiring.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_coverage_gate_discovery.py`, `tests/integration/test_write_batch_rate_safety.py`, `tests/bench/test_write_consumer_overlap_bench.py`, `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (Lever 2 pool 2→4 — this is the proven Lever 1 alternative), DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-LEVER1-001 (the per-window NO-GO this supersedes), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (`LakeWriteHalt`/`atomic_write_via` the consumer settles on), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the per-partition `flock` preserved), DEC-CANDLE-PARTIAL-ZERO-SKIP-001 #912 + DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 #919 (the per-window `bars_appended` back-channel kept real). **Decision ID:** DEC-WRITE-BATCH-COALESCE-001.

## DEC-MOVERS-FULL-CONTRACT-NAME-001 (2026-06-28)

987. **DEC-MOVERS-FULL-CONTRACT-NAME-001 — the `/movers` Futures AND Options tabs now show the FULL dated/strike contract in the NAME column (`NIFTY 30-Sep-2025 FUT` · `NIFTY 30-Jun-2025 24000 CE`) instead of the bare underlying / a terse `30Jun25` token, with a graceful fallback so an unparseable contract still renders a sensible identity (never blank, never a crash)** (2026-06-28; DISPLAY-ONLY on the reference-lake read-only `/movers` view, CLAUDE.md §3 — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change). **Why:** the Futures tab's NAME column showed only `mover.underlying` (e.g. `NIFTY`), so a Near vs Next vs Far contract of the SAME underlying were INDISTINGUISHABLE in the ranked rows; the Options tab DID build a dated/strike name but via the terse `DDMmmYY` token (`NIFTY 30Jun25 24000 CE`), inconsistent with the locked v29 mockup intent (`docs/dashboard/mockups/v29.html`-derived `movers.html` sample rows read `NIFTY 30 JUN ... FUT` / `... 24000 CALL`). This makes BOTH derivative tabs read the full human-formatted contract, consistently. **What shipped (DISPLAY-ONLY, both tabs):** (1) **COMMON formatter** — NEW `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py::format_contract_date(date) -> "DD-Mon-YYYY"` (e.g. `30-Sep-2025`), the ONE contract-date formatter shared by both tabs (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). It uses the fixed English `_MONTH_ABBR` table (the inverse of the existing `_MONTHS` parse map), NEVER `strftime("%b")` (which is LOCALE-dependent — a non-English locale would render `déc.` etc.), so the displayed label is DETERMINISTIC across machines (CLAUDE.md §4). (2) **FUTURES** — `FuturesMover` gains an `expiry: date | None` field; `compute_futures_mover` parses it from the contract `symbol` via `parse_future_symbol` (`None` on an unparseable symbol). A NEW `FuturesMover.name` property renders `"{underlying} {DD-Mon-YYYY} FUT"` (e.g. `NIFTY 30-Sep-2025 FUT`) and `_futures_row`'s `"name"` now uses it; the raw `symbol` is STILL carried in the payload (unchanged). **GRACEFUL FALLBACK:** when `expiry is None` (unparseable symbol) the name falls back to the raw `symbol` if non-empty, else the bare `underlying` — never blank, never raising (Golden Rule #1). (3) **OPTIONS** — `OptionMover.name` re-formats the expiry from the terse `DDMmmYY` token to the SHARED `format_contract_date` → `"{underlying} {DD-Mon-YYYY} {strike} {CE|PE}"` (e.g. `NIFTY 30-Jun-2025 24000 CE`); the now-unused `EXPIRY_DATE_FORMAT` import is dropped. The strike formatting is unchanged (whole strikes render `24000` via `normalize()`+`quantize`, fractional strikes keep their decimals, e.g. `24000.5`). The option name's parts are all parsed, non-optional fields, so the label is always well-formed. (4) **TEMPLATE** — NO change needed: `movers.html` already renders the `name` field (column index 0) via the generic per-cell render, so folding the full dated label into `name` is the minimal, mockup-consistent approach (no new column; both `futures.cols`/`options.cols` keep `["Name","name","str"]`). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** DISPLAY-ONLY — ranking, selection, candidate-cache keys, values, premium/moneyness and the route data flow are all UNCHANGED (only the NAME projection differs); the raw `symbol` stays in the payload for programmatic use; the date format is locale-stable by construction (a fixed English month map, not `strftime`); a futures symbol that cannot be parsed gracefully degrades to symbol-then-underlying so the cell is never blank/None; `/movers` remains a REFERENCE_ONLY read of the ingested lake (CLAUDE.md §3). **Tests/coverage (verified 2026-06-28, Python-3.12 venv with the `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels built):** `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py` (246 stmt / 52 branch) + `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py` (198 stmt / 40 branch) BOTH at **100% line+branch** (0 missing) across the `-k movers` suite (382 passed). NEW/updated tests: `TestFormatContractDate` (deterministic `DD-Mon-YYYY` for several dates), `TestFuturesMoverName` (dated label for a parseable contract; **Near≠Next≠Far render three DISTINCT names** — the regression for the ambiguity bug; unparseable symbol → fall back to the raw symbol; unparseable AND empty symbol → fall back to the underlying; `compute_futures_mover` populates `expiry` / yields `None` on junk), `TestFuturesMoverNameProperty` (the NAME is ALWAYS a non-empty `str` across parseable/bad-month/junk/empty symbols), updated futures `test_row_fields_complete` (NAME = `NIFTY 30-Sep-2025 FUT`, raw `symbol` still present); options `test_name_whole_strike`/`_put_contract`/`_fractional_strike`/`_with_trailing_zero_strike_normalizes`/`_different_expiries_render_different_names` (golden-pinned `NIFTY 30-Jun-2025 24000 CE`/`PE`, distinct Near vs Far), updated options `test_row_projection_fields`; the integration suites (`test_dashboard_movers_futures.py`/`test_dashboard_movers_options.py`) updated to the full dated labels (`Nifty 50 27-Jun-2024 FUT` / `NIFTY 27-Jun-2024 24000 CE`, etc.) — symbol literals (groww `27Jun24` tokens) unchanged. ruff check + ruff format --check clean on `brutex/dashboard` + `tests`; `pyright` 0 errors on both touched files; `mypy --strict` clean on both touched files (a pre-existing, unrelated `cma`-stub `import-not-found` in `brutex/engine/stage3_refine.py`, reached only transitively by mypy's import-follow, is NOT in scope and NOT caused by this change). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_futures.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_futures.py`, `tests/unit/test_movers_options.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_futures.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_options.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. (The template `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` needed NO change.) **Builds on:** DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-001 (the Futures tab + `FuturesMover`/`parse_future_symbol`), DEC-MOVERS-OPTIONS-001 (the Options tab + `OptionMover.name`), DEC-MOVERS-FUTURES-TIER-001 #917 (the Near/Next/Far selector whose rows this now disambiguates by name), DEC-FNO-MONEYNESS-001 #865 (the option moneyness columns left intact). **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-FULL-CONTRACT-NAME-001.

## DEC-DASHBOARD-OPERATOR-NAV-001 (2026-06-28)

988. **DEC-DASHBOARD-OPERATOR-NAV-001 — a top-nav "Operator" link to the rich `/` operator dashboard is now reachable from EVERY dashboard page** (2026-06-28; bundled with DEC-MOVERS-FULL-CONTRACT-NAME-001 #987 in the same dashboard-UX PR — nav/display-only). No CSS change needed (the generic `.topnav a` selector already styles a plain link). **Tests:** `test_dashboard_nav_consistency.py` auto-adapts (its `_CANONICAL` derives from `NAV_LINKS`); NEW `test_operator_link_present_in_nav` (asserts the `("/", "Operator")` link is present AND first in the `/movers` + `/reports` rendered navs) + `test_index_page_still_renders` (the `/` page renders non-empty and carries NO topnav). 28 nav-consistency tests green. **Decision ID (bundled):** DEC-DASHBOARD-OPERATOR-NAV-001.

989. **DEC-GROWW-SMOOTH-PACING-001 — an OPTIONAL anti-burst SMOOTH-PACING mode in the Groww rate controller, flag-gated + default-OFF byte-identical** (2026-06-28). The adaptive token bucket (`brutex/orchestrator/rate_limiter.py::AdaptiveTokenBucket`, reused by `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py::RateController`) caps the AVERAGE issue rate at `current_rps`, but its `1/rate`-cadence still lets SUB-SECOND micro-bursts through — the operator's live logs showed `rps_1s_max` spiking to **8–9** even while the AIMD ceiling sat lower, which can trip a vendor 429. This adds an OPTIONAL third gate that spreads issuance evenly so the per-second issue count can never exceed the current AIMD rate (no 9-burst). **What shipped (ADAPTER-only — outside the metrics package; ENGINE UNCHANGED, NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX):** (1) `RateController.__init__` gains a `smooth_pacing: bool = False` flag; when **OFF (the default)** the gate is skipped ENTIRELY in `pace()` and `_last_issue_ts` is never read/written — **byte-for-byte identical** to the prior two-gate behaviour (the existing `test_rate_common.py` suite passes unchanged). (2) When **ON**, a NEW Gate 0 runs FIRST in `pace()`: it enforces a global MINIMUM inter-issue interval of `1.0 / current_rps` seconds across ALL workers via a shared `_last_issue_ts` stamped under the SAME `threading.Lock` the token math uses — the wait is computed under the lock (`_smooth_wait_locked`, O(1)) and SLEPT OUTSIDE it (never serialising workers through the mutex), re-tested on wake, with the `(check, stamp)` done atomically in the same lock acquisition that observes a zero wait (the governor's atomic-reserve idiom, DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001) so N concurrent workers can never collapse onto one instant; a `_SMOOTH_LOOP_CAP` (64) bounds a pathological frozen-clock spin and fails OPEN, mirroring the per-minute governor's loop cap. The interval is derived from the LIVE `_rps`, so an AIMD step-down WIDENS the spacing immediately and a step-up NARROWS it — always tracking the current sustainable rate, **never exceeding it**. (3) It composes WITH (never bypasses) the existing gates: it only ever ADDS spacing — the **8 r/s per-second ceiling, the 500/min HARD governor, and the AIMD on_rate_limit/on_success ladder are EXACTLY UNCHANGED** (no new way to exceed any cap). (4) Env toggle `BRUTEX_GROWW_SMOOTH_PACING` (default `"0"` ⇒ OFF) parsed by NEW `constants.resolve_smooth_pacing()` (truthy = `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`, case-insensitive + whitespace-trimmed; ANY other value ⇒ OFF, fail-safe), wired into the dashboard live build site `pull_controller._build_live_controller` as `RateController(smooth_pacing=resolve_smooth_pacing())`. **Tests:** NEW `TestSmoothPacing` (default-OFF byte-identical · even 1/8 s spacing · `rps_1s` ≤ rate under 16-thread contention · caps still hold under the governor · AIMD step-down widens / step-up narrows the spacing · loop-cap fail-open on a frozen clock) + NEW `resolve_smooth_pacing` env tests (both ways); `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` AND `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py` at **100% line+branch**. ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on the touched files. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the smoothing is **provably SAFE** (every cap + the AIMD ladder are intact; default-OFF is byte-identical) and **provably SMOOTHER** (issuance spread to the AIMD rate, no sub-second burst), but the live **429-reduction benefit is UNVERIFIED** pending a live vendor probe — **NO throughput gain is claimed**. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-SMOOTH-PACING-001.

990. **DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 — FULL async separation of the Groww fetch lane from ALL internal processing (fault/latency ISOLATION), now DEFAULT-ON with a kill-switch** (2026-06-28; adapter + dashboard wiring only — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, NO scope/vocab/rate change, CLAUDE.md §2/§3). **Default-flip (operator-authorized 2026-06-28):** the async pipeline is now the PRODUCTION DEFAULT — `resolve_fetch_pipeline_size` returns the enabled pool for an UNSET / blank / non-falsy `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE` flag and the synchronous byte-identical path stays reachable ONLY via the explicit KILL-SWITCH `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE=off` (or `0`/`false`/`no`, case-insensitive). The size default (4) + `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE_SIZE` clamp `[1,8]` are unchanged. **Why:** the operator's core requirement — the fetch thread must do NOTHING but fetch + hand off; a SEPARATE consumer does ALL internal work (session-filter / dedup / lake-write / ledger.record), so internal processing can NEVER block or slow the fetch. This is STRONGER than the write-only decouple of DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-LEVER1-001 (`write_consumer.py`), where the fetch worker still ran the session filter + parse and BLOCKED on the durable write result. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py` (stdlib-only at import — `queue`/`threading`/`dataclasses`/`hashlib`/`os`/`time`): `RawFetchResult` (frozen, wraps a `FetchTail` carrying the series shard key + the bound `_process_window_tail` closure + the raw post-fetch bars); `FetchPipeline` — a fixed-size pool of M consumer threads, each draining its OWN bounded `queue.Queue(maxsize)`, with requests routed by `blake2b(exchange,segment,symbol,interval) % M` (the SAME series-shard key `WriteRequest` uses) so ALL writes to one series land on ONE consumer (preserving the per-partition `threading.Lock` + `flock`); `resolve_fetch_pipeline_size` (mirrors `resolve_write_pool_size` / `resolve_pool_size` — env `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE` DEFAULT-ON kill-switch (only an explicit falsy `off`/`0`/`false`/`no` disables) + `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE_SIZE` clamped `[1,8]`, fail-safe default 4). The two ingest spines (`ingest.py` spot, `option_ingest.py` F&O) each SPLIT their per-window function into `_fetch_window_raw` (pace + fetch + in-pull EMPTY-retry + the rate-controller feedback `on_rate_limit`/`on_timeout` — STAYS on the producer/fetch thread) and `_process_window_tail` (session-filter + `sink.append` (+ the `PartitionLockTimeout` defer) + conflict-aggregate + `ledger.record` SUCCESS/EMPTY + `on_success` — the CONSUMER work). `fetch_pipeline=None` (the kill-switched synchronous path) runs the two as ONE synchronous call — BYTE-IDENTICAL to before; when set, the producer calls `_fetch_window_raw` then `pipeline.submit(RawFetchResult)` (a bounded `put` that blocks ONLY on back-pressure, NEVER on the write completing) and immediately re-paces + fetches the next window, while a consumer runs the SAME `_process_window_tail` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — ONE tail, no duplicated logic). Wired into BOTH dashboard live-pull build sites (`pull_controller.py` `_build_fetch_pipeline`/`_drain_fetch_pipeline`, threaded into `run_groww_spot_ingest{,_with_retry}` + drained in each `finally` BEFORE `end_pull_ledger`). **Operator HARD guards (anti-pileup):** STRICTLY BOUNDED — fixed M threads (not one-per-window) + a small bounded queue; `submit` BLOCKS on a full queue (back-pressure, never unbounded growth). STALL WATCHDOG — a poll thread fires ONE loud `fetch_pipeline.stalled` WARNING (+ an optional `on_stall` hook) when work is in flight but no window completes for the threshold, edge-latched + re-armed by the next completion (never silent idle). CLEAN DRAIN — poison-pill + a BOUNDED per-thread join (a wedged consumer is REPORTED via `fetch_pipeline.drain_join_timeout`, never hangs the pull's `finally`); daemon threads so a reported-but-unjoined consumer can never wedge shutdown.
