A consumer `LakeWriteHalt` (disk-full / OOM) trips a pool-wide stop, re-raised on the next `submit` AND at `drain` so it reaches the spines' `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` (graceful pull halt); any other tail failure is captured + re-raised at drain (never a fabricated success). **Settle-after-durable (Golden Rule #7):** the consumer's `ledger.record(SUCCESS/EMPTY)` runs strictly AFTER `sink.append` (→ `atomic_write_via` → `os.replace`); `drain()` runs before the final ledger flush, so every queued window is processed + recorded before the ledger persists; a never-drained window (hard kill) leaves its row UNSETTLED → re-fetched next pull (idempotent keep-first). **The rate controller (8/500 + AIMD) stays ENTIRELY on the producer side, UNCHANGED.** **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this delivers ISOLATION — the fetch lane's throughput is decoupled from internal processing (PROVEN by a stalled-consumer test: each tail sleeps 60 ms yet the producer issues all fetches in well under N×60 ms, vs ≥1.0× for the synchronous path) — it is NOT a throughput increase (the achieved rate is still vendor-bound; the controller still caps the issue rate). DEFAULT-ON (operator-authorized 2026-06-28) makes the isolation the production behaviour; the `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE=off` kill-switch instantly reverts to the byte-identical synchronous path if the operator ever needs it. The dashboard pull path is wired; the CLI `brutex fetch` path + the F&O `historical_pull.py` build site are explicit FOLLOW-UPS (the `fetch_pipeline` param exists on `run_groww_option_ingest`, only the dashboard binding ships). **Tests/coverage (Python-3.12 venv, `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels built):** `fetch_pipeline.py` (175 stmt / 46 branch), `ingest.py` (212/52), `option_ingest.py` (292/76), `run_ingest.py` (147/30) ALL at **100% line+branch** (0 missing); the new `_build_fetch_pipeline`/`_drain_fetch_pipeline` helpers covered by `tests/unit/test_dashboard_fetch_pipeline_wiring.py`. NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py` (resolve default-ON/kill-switch + construction guards, sharding, anti-pileup queue-cap+blocking-producer, stall-watchdog fires/edge-latch/no-inflight/hook-error, halt-trips-pool, generic-failure-reraise, post-halt-drop, no-leaked-threads, idempotent + bounded-join drain, no-deadlock racing producers) + `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py` (8 tests — byte-parity sync-vs-pipeline incl. same-partition keep-first conflict, settle-after-durable, never-drained→unsettled→re-fetch recovery, the ISOLATION PROOF, caps-intact pace-once-per-fetch, the F&O twin, a real `PoolRunParallel` run). The pre-existing env-sensitive bench `tests/bench/test_pull_at_scale_gate.py::test_pull_at_scale_gate_saturates_allowed_rate` is RED on origin/main too (CPU-saturation timing gate on a busy shared box — 75% pool-idle on pristine main vs 50% with this change, i.e. NOT a regression) and is NOT in this change's scope. ruff check + ruff format --check clean; `mypy --strict` clean on all touched files (the only mypy errors are pre-existing `growwapi`/`cma` missing-stub `import-untyped`/`import-not-found` in untouched `auth.py`/`reauth.py`/`stage3_refine.py`, reached transitively, NOT caused here); `pyright` 0 errors/0 warnings on all touched source + test files. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_fetch_pipeline_wiring.py` (new), `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-LEVER1-001 (the write-only decouple this generalises), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (the `LakeWriteHalt` global-stop), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the per-partition lock the sharding preserves), DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001 (the `PartitionLockTimeout` defer the tail keeps). **Hostile-review fixes (2026-06-28, folded before merge):** (BLOCKER) `drain()` no longer HANGS FOREVER when a consumer is wedged inside `sink.append` (a stalled external SSD / NFS hiccup) AND its bounded queue is FULL — the poison-pill was an UNBOUNDED blocking `q.put` that blocked permanently so the bounded join never ran (the pull's `finally` hung, the ledger never persisted, no signal). FIX: a `_draining` `threading.Event` the consumers ALSO check on a timed `queue.get` (guaranteed exit once a consumer's queue empties even without a poison) + a BOUNDED non-blocking poison `put` that FALLS THROUGH to the join on `queue.Full`; the stall watchdog is now stopped only AFTER the join (was stopped FIRST, blinding it exactly when a wedge mattered) so a wedge during drain is still surfaced as `fetch_pipeline.stalled`. Regression: a 1-consumer / queue_maxsize=2 / wedged-sink / 3-same-shard-submit test (the queue fills) proves `drain()` returns BOUNDED + REPORTS the wedged consumer (confirmed FAILS before the fix). (MAJOR) a tail-side `PartitionLockTimeout` transient in async mode is no longer silently DROPPED — `_run_tail` now folds it via `pipeline.fold_tail_transient(series_key)` so the deferred window is COUNTED, surfaced at drain, ledger-recorded FAILED, and re-pulled the next pull (across-pull retry). (MAJOR — the completion-count completion) the async producer returns a DEFERRED per-series `IngestReport` with `bars_appended==0` (the consumer does the durable write on a background thread), which made the controller falsely report `total_completed==0` / a `known_gap_only` verdict even though every bar was durably written; FIX: `FetchPipeline` accumulates per-`(symbol,interval)` `SeriesTotals` (`fold_totals(...,series_key=)`/`fold_tail_transient(series_key)` + `per_series_totals()`), and `pull_all_spot`/`pull_candles` call the NEW `_reconcile_pairs_with_pipeline` AFTER the drain to OVERRIDE each deferred report's `bars_appended`/`conflicts`/`still_failed_windows` with the consumer's real totals, so the async path's reported counts + verdict EQUAL the synchronous path's (14 controller tests restored to green). (MAJOR) `scan_underlying_all_empty` is SKIPPED when a `fetch_pipeline` is active (the synchronous bar counts aren't known pre-drain), avoiding a false `pull.underlying_all_empty` flood. (MAJOR) the `finally` now drains the fetch pipeline FIRST then the write consumer (a pipeline consumer's tail feeds the write consumer, so the reverse order could lose a late write). (MINOR) `_build_fetch_pipeline` wires the watchdog `on_stall` hook to the pull-health `pull.stalled` degraded alert (best-effort, swallows any error). HONEST: async tail-transients re-pull NEXT pull via the ledger FAILED row (they do NOT trigger the SAME-pull until-clean retry, which decides before drain — the across-pull retry is the stated minimum). **B1 liveness fix (2026-06-28, re-review on head 6141dccf — a decisive repro PROVED a real SUBMIT-path liveness gap a prior hostile re-review missed, distinct from the drain() poison-put BLOCKER above):** `submit()`'s back-pressure `put` was an UNBOUNDED `self._queues[shard].put(result)` with NO timeout + NO `_stopped` recheck — `_raise_if_stopped()` ran only BEFORE the put. So a producer back-pressured on a FULL shard queue whose OWN consumer was WEDGED FOREVER (a stalled SSD/NFS hiccup inside `sink.append`) was NEVER released when a PEER consumer tripped the pool-wide stop: the pull halted logically (`fetch_pipeline.halt` fired) yet the fetch thread stayed wedged in the put forever — the operator's #1 "looks alive but stuck/hang" failure. A decisive repro (workers=2 / queue_maxsize=1 / wedged-forever consumer on a deterministic shard split + a peer `LakeWriteHalt`) confirmed the producer stayed blocked the full 10 s window against the old code, and is RELEASED within a bound after the fix. FIX (`submit()` only): the put is now a BOUNDED, stop-aware loop — `put(result, timeout=_CONSUMER_GET_POLL_SECONDS)` retried on `queue.Full`, rechecking `_raise_if_stopped()` (a peer halt re-raises → releases the producer → reaches the spine's `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS`) AND `_draining` (a pull-end drain DROPS the un-enqueued window fail-fast → re-fetches next pull, idempotent keep-first) before retrying. Back-pressure for the HEALTHY-but-slow consumer is PRESERVED (the loop keeps blocking across retries — the window is NEVER dropped while the pull is live), so isolation + no-OOM are intact and settle-after-durable + byte-parity are untouched. Two permanent regression tests in `TestNoDeadlock` (`test_blocked_submit_released_when_peer_consumer_trips_stop` — FAILS against the old unbounded put (the producer stays blocked the full 10 s), PASSES after; `test_blocked_submit_dropped_when_draining` — the drain-branch drop); `fetch_pipeline.py` stays 100% line+branch (222 stmt / 54 branch, 0 missing); ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` (3.12) / `pyright` clean; 247 groww ingest + pipeline + drain + byte-parity tests green. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001.
992. **DEC-ACCOUNT-PULL-SINGLEFLIGHT-001 — a cross-process SINGLE-FLIGHT lock so only ONE pull runs at a time per Groww account / lake, closing the C4 gap that two concurrent pulls (a CLI `brutex fetch` AND a dashboard pull) each get their OWN per-process rate budget so the ACCOUNT sees the SUM (~16 r/s at the 8 r/s ceiling) → 429-storm / ban risk** (2026-06-28; the account-rate twin of the per-partition write-lock #887; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3, NO scope/vocab/rate change). **Why (the gap):** the Groww rate controller (`brutex/adapters/rate_common.py::RateController` — the AIMD per-second ceiling + the 500/min governor, CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6) is PER-PROCESS. Two pulls sharing one Groww account / one `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT` — e.g. a CLI `brutex fetch` while a dashboard pull runs — each get their own ceiling, so the ACCOUNT's request rate DOUBLES, defeating the very rate safety the controller exists to provide (Golden Rule #6). There was no guard preventing concurrent pulls from sharing one account. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_singleflight.py` — `pull_singleflight_lock(lake_root)` takes a NON-BLOCKING advisory `fcntl.flock` (`LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB`) on a stable single-flight lock file `<lake_root>/.locks/pull_singleflight.lock` (the dot-prefixed `.locks/` sibling of `bars/`+`options/`, never seen by a dataset glob / lake scanner; 0o600 owner-only). On contention — a peer process is mid-pull — the acquire RAISES `PullAlreadyRunningError` IMMEDIATELY (non-blocking, fail-fast: a pull runs for hours, so blocking would silently queue a second pull behind the first; instead the operator gets a clear "a pull is already running" naming the held lock path). The kernel releases the flock on fd-close / process death, so a crashed pull never leaves a stale lock (no PID-file recovery needed); O(1). **Wiring (`brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py`):** `BackgroundPullJob` gains an injectable `lake_root_resolver` (default the COMMON `brutex/config/paths.py::resolve_lake_root` — `$BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT` → `$HOME/.brutex/lake`, so the guard is ACTIVE by default, NOT dormant) + an injectable `singleflight_factory` (default the live lock). `start()` takes the cross-process lock AFTER the in-process `_running` flag (so a same-process double-click is filtered by the cheap flag first) but BEFORE any work is spawned: on `PullAlreadyRunningError` it rolls back `_running`, marks the progress FAILED with the actionable message, logs `pull_job.singleflight_refused`, and returns `False` — NEVER spawning a second pull that would double the account rate. The lock is held for the WHOLE pull lifetime and released in `_run`'s `finally` (and in `_on_hung` for a wedged run, under the same run-identity gate, so clearing `_running` actually admits a future pull). A `None`-returning resolver DISABLES the guard (a dry-run / test that never touches a real account). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** guards TWO concurrent pulls sharing one lake root on ONE machine/filesystem — it is NOT a distributed lock across hosts (an `flock` is local) and NOT a queue (the second pull is REFUSED, not deferred); `fcntl.flock` is POSIX (Linux + macOS — the Track-1 hardware envelope), Windows OUT OF SCOPE; it composes WITH (never relaxes) the per-process `RateController` and the per-partition write-lock #887. The `app.py` build site is byte-unchanged (it builds the job with defaults → guard active); the resolver/factory are injected, never globals (CLAUDE.md §4). **Tests/coverage:** `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_singleflight.py` at **100% line+branch** (held → second-acquire-refused via a SEPARATE fd, release-lets-reacquire, owner-only perms, distinct-roots-never-contend, error-released, contended-path-does-not-close-the-holder's-lock, pre-existing-lockfile-reused) + `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py` at **100% line+branch** (default-guard-active-and-held-for-the-run via the REAL flock, held-lock-refuses-and-rolls-back, refused-then-idle-can-start-again, released-on-worker-exception, None-resolver-disables, best-effort-release-swallows-errors, `_on_hung`-releases). NEW `tests/unit/test_pull_singleflight.py` (8) + `tests/unit/test_pull_jobs_singleflight.py` (8); the existing `tests/unit/test_pull_jobs.py` + `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_stall.py::TestBackgroundPullJobWatchdog` gain an autouse fixture pointing the default resolver at `None` (those tests probe progress/watchdog, not the guard, and several capture-but-never-run the worker, which would leak a process-wide flock); `tests/unit/test_dashboard_results_route.py` points its resolver at the tmp lake. ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_singleflight.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_singleflight.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_jobs_singleflight.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_jobs.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_stall.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_results_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the per-partition advisory `flock` this mirrors at the account/whole-pull granularity), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 #922 (the 8 r/s per-process ceiling this stops a second process from doubling), DEC-PULL-STALL-DETECTION-001 (the run-identity gate / `_on_hung` release path this hooks into). **Decision ID:** DEC-ACCOUNT-PULL-SINGLEFLIGHT-001.
993. **DEC-ENV-PERSIST-SLA-001 — `.env` persistence (GAP C6) + an honest pull-ETA estimate (GAP C5)** (2026-06-28). Two independent operator-facing gaps closed with two NEW small modules + two MINIMUM-line bootstrap edits + a runbook. **GAP C6 (env persistence):** `BRUTEX_*` env vars (credentials `BRUTEX_GROWW_API_KEY` / `BRUTEX_GROWW_TOTP_SECRET`, pool/pacing flags `BRUTEX_GROWW_SMOOTH_PACING` / `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT` …) previously vanished on every shell/reboot, so the operator re-exported them by hand before each overnight pull. NEW dependency-free `brutex/config/dotenv.py` loads a `.env` file (search order repo-root → cwd → `~/.brutex/.env`, de-duplicated) ONCE at process bootstrap, **NEVER overriding an already-set process env var** (a real exported value ALWAYS wins over the file — no surprise shadowing), a **no-op when no `.env` exists**, and **secret VALUES are NEVER logged** — only the (already-public) applied KEY NAMES. `python-dotenv` is intentionally NOT added as a dependency: a tiny safe `KEY=VALUE` parser (ignores comments/blanks, tolerates `export `, strips matching surrounding quotes, splits on the FIRST `=`). Pure + fully injectable (`bootstrap_env(env=, repo_root=, cwd=, home=)`) so the unit tests touch no real process env. Wired with the MINIMUM lines at BOTH startup entry points: `brutex/cli.py::main` (covers `brutex fetch`/`dashboard`/`run`) and the dashboard app factory `brutex/dashboard/app.py::build_app`. **GAP C5 (honest wall-clock ETA):** NEW pure `brutex/observability/pull_eta.py` `estimate_pull_eta(total_windows, achieved_rps)` → `seconds = total_windows / max(achieved_rps, EPSILON_RPS)` (a `1e-3` floor so a stalled 0-r/s pull yields a FINITE estimate, never `inf`/`ZeroDivisionError`; negative windows clamped to 0) returning an immutable `PullEta` (`.seconds`/`.hours`) + a `format_eta` helper (`Xh Ym` / `Xm Ys` / `Xs`). NEW runbook `docs/runbooks/PULL_ETA.md` — NIFTY end-to-end first (spot + its F&O), then scaling to the full universe (all symbols' spot+futures+options) — with worked numbers clearly labelled **MEASURED vs PROJECTED**: at the MEASURED ~3 r/s (`cf1afd97-brutex.log`, MIGRATION.md #921) ~67k spot windows ⇒ **~6h 12m**; PROJECTED ~3h 43m at 5 r/s and ~2h 19m at the configured 8 r/s ceiling (UNVERIFIED — the log showed the vendor 429ing at 5, MIGRATION.md #922). **Golden Rule #10 honesty:** `achieved_rps` is a MEASURED INPUT (read from `/metrics` `pull.achieved_rps` / the live snapshot), NOT a constant baked in; the estimate is deliberately optimistic (ignores 429 back-off, the 06:00 IST re-mint pause, lake-write contention) so the REAL pull is generally SLOWER — no fake O(1), no "minutes" claim; the full-universe figure is honestly MULTI-DAY (consistent with the §8 M4 Pro 2–4-day class), to be read live from the pull's own planned-window total. **Tests:** NEW `tests/unit/test_config_dotenv.py` (parse/quote/comment/export/empty-key edge cases; apply never-overrides; no-op when absent; defaults to `os.environ`; masked-keys-never-values log assertion) + `tests/unit/test_pull_eta.py` (windows/rps math; zero/negative-rps epsilon guard; zero/negative-windows clamp; `format_eta` tiers; frozen dataclass; the 67k@3rps headline). `brutex/config/dotenv.py` AND `brutex/observability/pull_eta.py` BOTH at **100% line+branch** (64/26 + 26/4, 0 missing); the two bootstrap call-lines covered by the existing CLI-`main` + dashboard `build_app` suites. ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file. SCOPE-LOCKED: NO change to `rate_common.py` / `constants.py` / `pull_controller.py` / `ingest.py` / `option_ingest.py` / `fetch_pipeline.py` / `pull_jobs.py`; ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change. **Decision ID:** DEC-ENV-PERSIST-SLA-001.

994. **DEC-RATE-CLOCK-SLEEPWAKE-001 — the Groww rate controller now detects a laptop sleep/wake monotonic clock gap and resets its rolling window + AIMD anchors, so a post-wake pull can never burst past the cap nor stall** (2026-06-28). `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py::RateController` paces off `time.monotonic()`. When the operator's MacBook SLEEPS overnight and WAKES, monotonic jumps forward by a large delta (and a rare platform/NTP glitch can step it slightly back). Two failure modes this closes: **(a)** stale timestamps in the rolling-60 s issue / 429 / timeout histories could let a post-wake burst overshoot the per-SECOND (8 r/s) OR per-MINUTE (500/min) cap — most acutely the per-minute governor's fail-OPEN path, which on a future-stamped deque (a backward glitch) spins to its loop cap then admits past the cap; and **(b)** the AIMD timing anchors (`_last_step`, `_last_snapshot_log`, smooth-pacing `_last_issue_ts`) would mis-time recovery/backoff by counting the entire sleep as elapsed pacing time (e.g. a single post-wake `on_success` interpreting hours-since-last-step as a clean recovery window). **What shipped (ADAPTER-only; ENGINE UNCHANGED, NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap change):** (1) a NEW `CLOCK_GAP_THRESHOLD_S = 5.0 * PER_MIN_WINDOW` (**300 s = 5 min**) — set comfortably ABOVE every normal operational gap (the longest of which is one AIMD recovery window, `STEP_UP_WINDOW = 60 s`; even at the 1 r/s deep floor a call lands every ~1 s) so genuine pacing NEVER false-trips, while a minutes-to-hours laptop sleep always does; (2) a NEW `_last_seen: float` anchor (seeded at construction) + a NEW O(1) `_handle_clock_gap_locked(now)` helper that, when `abs(now - _last_seen) > CLOCK_GAP_THRESHOLD_S`, CLEARS the rolling `_issues`/`_hits`/`_timeouts` deques, re-bases `_last_step` + `_last_snapshot_log` to `now`, resets the smooth-pacing `_last_issue_ts` to the `-inf` construction sentinel (so the first post-wake issue admits immediately, then the per-second spacing re-binds), logs a `rate.clock_gap` warning, and always advances `_last_seen` to `now` (so a steady stream of sub-threshold deltas never accumulates a false trip); it NEVER touches `_rps` — a wake neither steps up nor down, it only forgets stale TIMING. (3) The helper is called FIRST in every lock-held critical section that reads the clock — both `pace()` gates (smooth + governor), `on_rate_limit`, `on_timeout`, `on_success`, and `_maybe_log_snapshot` (so even a DEFAULT controller, whose `pace` reads the clock under lock only there, re-bases on wake). **Tests:** NEW `TestClockGapSleepWake` (7 tests) — governor no-burst-overshoot across an 8 h sleep · no-stall after a large backward glitch · smooth-pacing no-stale-baseline-block across sleep · AIMD anchors re-based (no instant multi-rung jump, recovery still one rung per genuine post-wake window) · default-controller re-base via the snapshot hook · sub-threshold delta does NOT trip the gap (the false branch — ladder still steps down) · threshold-above-every-operational-window invariant. `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` at **100% line+branch** (184/44); the full 67-test `test_rate_common.py` suite + the broader rate-keyword suite (574 passed, 4 unrelated skips) green; ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on the touched files. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** O(1) per critical section, no new threads, deterministic with an injected clock; this is a DETECT-and-reset robustness guard, not a wall-clock sync — it relies on a single inter-event monotonic delta, so it cannot distinguish a true sleep from a hypothetical 5-min+ idle with zero controller calls (a non-issue: an active pull calls the controller many times per second). **Decision ID:** DEC-RATE-CLOCK-SLEEPWAKE-001.

## DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001 (2026-06-28)

995. **DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001 — a LIVE pull-rate monitor on the dashboard: req/sec · req/min · req/hour + a STALL light, site-wide** (2026-06-28; #990–994 reserved by in-flight PRs). A self-injecting dashboard widget + a dedicated O(1) JSON endpoint surface the live Groww-pull rate from the REAL controller/meter snapshots, so the operator SEES whether a pull is flowing, throttled, or stalled at a glance — visible on `/universe` and the operator page, reachable site-wide. **REAL data source (cited, no fabrication):** the dashboard already mirrors every live pull's `RateController.snapshot()` (`brutex/adapters/rate_common.py:670` — `current_rps` = allowed, `recent_minute` = rolling-60s issue count, `recent_hits` = recent 429s) + the transport `CallMeter.snapshot()` (`brutex/adapters/call_meter.py:139` — `effective_rps` = measured achieved) into an in-memory `RateLimitPanel` on each `_observe_rate` tick (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py:921`) via `make_rate_observer` (`brutex/dashboard/app.py:704`); this PR reads that SAME panel — no new pull-side instrumentation, no change to `rate_common.py`/`constants.py`. **What shipped (READ-ONLY dashboard; ENGINE UNCHANGED, NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO scope/vocab/rate change):** (1) NEW pure `brutex/dashboard/pull_rate_view.py` `build_pull_rate_view(...)` → an immutable `PullRateView` carrying **req/sec** (achieved `effective_rps` vs allowed `current_rps`), **req/min** (the controller's MEASURED rolling-60s `recent_minute`), **req/hour** (an OBSERVED extrapolation `req/min × 60`, so named + labelled — there is no measured trailing-hour window, Golden Rule #10), and a **stall signal** — `seconds_since_update` + a `flow_state` ∈ {`idle`,`flowing`,`stalled`} where `idle` = no live tick within a 12 s staleness window (every live number ZEROED so an ended pull never shows a fake "live" figure — Golden Rule #1) and `stalled` = an ACTIVE pull whose achieved r/s is at/below the pull-health monitor's shared `STALLED_RPS_FLOOR` (0.5 r/s — COMMON with the `pull.stalled` Telegram alert) — plus the configured `ceiling_rps` (8, `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`) / `ceiling_per_min` (500, `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN`) LIMITS (CLAUDE.md §6 — the per-second cap is UNVERIFIED, shown as the injected ceiling not a vendor-documented limit). (2) `RateLimitPanel` extended with `recent_minute` / `ceiling_per_min` (fed from the controller snapshot) + a monotonic `last_update_monotonic` freshness baseline (`-inf` until the first tick) stamped by a SINGLE `_stamp_rate_update` from BOTH `update_rate_limit` + `update_throughput`; a shared `to_json_dict()` drops that non-JSON `-inf` baseline so `/api/v1/state` + `/api/v1/rate` stay byte-consistent (COMMON, §11). (3) NEW route `GET /api/v1/pull/rate` — a pure in-memory O(1) read (never touches the lake/store lock, never blocks the pull) returning the derived view; an `inf` age is JSON-rendered `null`. (4) NEW self-contained `/static/bx-rate-monitor.js` — a dependency-free, self-injecting fixed-position widget (a green/red/dark STALL light + the three rate numbers, req/hour tagged "obs"), polling every ~3 s, best-effort (a fetch error leaves the last render), loaded via a `<script defer>` on `universe.html` + `v29.html` so it never blocks first paint. **Scenarios covered:** no-pull idle (zeroed + dark) · flowing (real numbers, green) · stalled (near-zero achieved, red) · never-updated (`null` age) · stale-boundary inclusive · negative-age clamp · governor-disabled (`-1` cap → widget dash) · legacy `/api/v1/state`+`/api/v1/rate` still valid JSON. **Failure modes:** malformed/absent snapshot keys default safely (no KeyError); a fetch error in the widget is swallowed; `inf`/`-inf` never reach JSON. **Tests:** NEW `tests/unit/test_pull_rate_view.py` (10 cases, all branches) + `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py` (route idle/flowing/stalled, panel wiring, legacy-route JSON safety, widget served + referenced). `brutex/dashboard/pull_rate_view.py` at **100% line+branch** (41/6, 0 missing); all NEW `app.py` lines covered; 229 dashboard integration tests green. ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file. **Rollback plan:** revert the PR — additive only (one new module, one new route, one new static file, two `<script>` includes, additive panel fields); no existing behaviour changes when no pull runs. **Out of scope:** any change to the rate controller's pacing / the 8-r/s ceiling / the 500/min governor (READ-ONLY); the CLI pull path (no `_observe_rate` seam); a measured trailing-hour counter (req/hour stays an honest extrapolation). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** req/sec + req/min are MEASURED from the controller/meter; req/hour is an OBSERVED projection (× 60), labelled as such in the field name + the widget; the limits are the configured (UNVERIFIED per-second) ceilings; the stall verdict is an OBSERVATION, not auto-remediation; the live numbers can only be seen during an ACTUAL pull (this PR's tests drive the panel directly — no live-pull proof is claimed). **Decision ID:** DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001.

## DEC-PULL-HARDENING-FOLLOWUP-001 (2026-06-28)

996. **DEC-PULL-HARDENING-FOLLOWUP-001 — consolidated fast-follow for the Groww-pull-hardening gaps the 19-agent verification found: CLI single-flight wiring · honest stall accounting · disk-full lock mapping · EDQUOT halt · loud two-lake-root residual** (2026-06-28). The hardening batch (#951–#995) was adversarially re-verified across extreme failure permutations; the BLOCKER B1 (forever-wedged-consumer release) was already fixed+merged. This PR closes the REMAINING actionable gaps with small, scope-locked fixes (the architecturally-significant ones are flagged as follow-ups, NOT implemented). **(B2/M1 — CLI single-flight wiring, HIGH):** the cross-process pull lock `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_singleflight.py` was wired ONLY into the dashboard `BackgroundPullJob`; the CLI `brutex fetch` path took NO lock, so a CLI pull + a dashboard pull on the SAME lake could run at once and DOUBLE the Groww account request rate (~16 r/s at the 8 r/s ceiling — exactly the failure the module exists to prevent, CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #6). FIX: NEW `cli._enter_pull_singleflight(stack, lake_root)` `__enter__`-s `pull_singleflight_lock(lake_root)` into `cmd_fetch`'s `ExitStack` (held for the whole fetch, released on exit — exactly as `pull_jobs.start()` does); on contention it prints a clear actionable operator message and returns False so the CLI fails fast (exit 1) instead of double-running. Taken ONLY on the genuine persisting LIVE pull — `--dry-run`/`--inspect` (no real lake data, no real account requests) deliberately skip the gate. **(MINOR — honest stall accounting):** in `fetch_pipeline.submit()`, the `_stopped` re-raise path on a FULL queue counted the window in `_submitted` but never called `_mark_completed()` (unlike the sibling `_draining` drop branch), leaving `in_flight > 0` after a halt → one SPURIOUS `fetch_pipeline.stalled` WARNING during teardown. FIX: mark the window completed before re-raising so the stall indicator stays honest (`_stopped` is only ever set by `_trip`, which always records `_exc`, so the re-raise always fires — no double-count). **(M3 — disk-full lock mapping):** the single-flight `.locks` dir/lockfile creation ran the `mkdir`+`os.open(O_CREAT)` with NO guard, so a full disk raised a raw `OSError` that escaped the dashboard `start()` path uncaught — inconsistent with `partition_lock.py`. FIX: wrap them in `lake_write_guard()` so ENOSPC→`LakeWriteHalt("disk_full")`, identical to the partition lock. **(m5 — EDQUOT halt, COMMON):** `atomic_io.lake_write_guard` mapped ONLY `ENOSPC`→`disk_full`; an `EDQUOT` (filesystem disk-quota exhaustion — the SAME "out of space" operator condition on a quota'd mount) re-raised raw and, on the write path, crashed the whole pull mislabelled as an escaped code bug. FIX: a NEW `_DISK_FULL_ERRNOS = {ENOSPC, EDQUOT}` (EDQUOT admitted defensively via `getattr` for the few platforms lacking it) — ONE source of truth covering both lake writers + the merge-read path; `EROFS`/`EACCES` still propagate raw (never over-broad, Golden Rule #1). **(M2 — two-lake-root residual, DOCUMENTED loudly + runbook):** the lock is keyed by `lake_root`, NOT by the Groww account, so the SAME account pulled into TWO distinct `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT`s still doubles the rate. Keying on credentials/feed-token needs the live token threaded into both build sites + a system-wide cross-user lock dir — a larger change, flagged as a follow-up. The residual is now stated LOUDLY in the `pull_singleflight.py` module docstring AND a NEW `docs/runbooks/data-fetch-runday.md` §6a operator note ("never run two pulls on one account at once, even into different lake roots"). **Scope-locked:** ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX); no scope/vocab/rate-cap change; READ-no-new-pull-instrumentation. **Tests (gate-discovered files):** `test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py` (NEW blocked-producer-release-on-stop in-flight accounting test — deterministic full-queue + peer-trip), `test_pull_singleflight.py` (NEW lockfile-open-ENOSPC→`LakeWriteHalt` test), `test_atomic_io.py` (NEW EDQUOT→`disk_full` + EROFS-propagates tests), `test_cli_retry_storm.py` (NEW `_enter_pull_singleflight` acquire/contention + `cmd_fetch` refused-on-peer-lock + dry-run-skips-the-gate tests). `fetch_pipeline.py` (224/56), `pull_singleflight.py` (31/0), `atomic_io.py` (43/6) ALL at **100% line+branch**; every NEW `cli.py` line+branch (the helper + the gate) covered (cli.py is package-wide-gated; the pre-existing live `# pragma`-style gaps are unrelated). ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub mypy notes in `auth.py`/`reauth.py` are an environment artifact, not in any touched file). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the single-flight gate is per-LAKE not per-ACCOUNT (the two-lake-root hole is documented, not closed); EDQUOT only arises on a quota'd mount (a plain external SSD returns ENOSPC, already handled); the stall-accounting fix is cosmetic (no data effect — it only stops one spurious teardown WARNING); the true vendor 8 r/s ceiling stays UNVERIFIED (out of scope — a live probe, not code). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-HARDENING-FOLLOWUP-001.

## DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 (2026-06-29)

997. **DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 — a CLI `brutex fetch` pull's live rate (req/sec · req/min · req/hour) now shows up on the dashboard's PULL RATE widget, via a small cross-process file bridge** (2026-06-29). The live-rate WIDGET shipped in DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001 (#995 — `brutex/dashboard/pull_rate_view.py` `build_pull_rate_view` → `PullRateView`, route `GET /api/v1/pull/rate`, `static/bx-rate-monitor.js`) reads an IN-MEMORY `RateLimitPanel` populated only on a DASHBOARD pull's `_observe_rate` tick. A CLI `python -m brutex fetch` pull runs in a SEPARATE process, so it never touches that panel and the widget sat IDLE while a CLI pull was actively hammering Groww — the explicit "the CLI pull path (no `_observe_rate` seam)" out-of-scope note of #995. This PR adds that missing CLI seam as a thin cross-process VISIBILITY bridge, changing NO pacing decision. **What shipped:** **(1) NEW `brutex/data/rate_bridge.py`** — the shared file MODEL + publisher + reader: a frozen `RateBridgeSnapshot` (the SAME measured fields the in-memory panel mirrors — allowed `current_rps`, achieved `effective_rps`, `recent_minute` = req/min, `recent_429`, `ceiling_per_min` — plus a CROSS-PROCESS-comparable `wall_time` (`time.time()`) + a diagnostic `monotonic`); `rate_bridge_path(lake_root)` → `<lake_root>/.rate/pull_rate.json` (a dot-prefixed sidecar dir, sibling of `.locks`, never matched by a dataset glob); `publish_rate_snapshot(...)` / `publish_from_snapshots(controller_snap, meter_snap, ...)` (the SAME `.get(...)` mapping `make_rate_observer` uses — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) writing the file atomically via `atomic_io.atomic_write_simple` (tmp → `fsync` → `os.replace`, so a concurrent reader never sees a torn file) wrapped in `lake_write_guard()` so a full-disk ENOSPC maps to `LakeWriteHalt("disk_full")` like every other lake-write site (DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001); and a BEST-EFFORT `read_rate_snapshot(lake_root)` → `RateBridgeSnapshot | None` that returns `None` for EVERY non-happy case (absent / unreadable / corrupt-JSON / not-an-object / unrecognised `schema` / missing-or-wrong-typed field) so a damaged bridge file can NEVER break the dashboard (Golden Rule #1). **(2) Publisher wiring (CLI side, `cli.py`):** NEW `_make_cli_rate_bridge_on_window(inner, lake_root, controller, adapter)` wraps `cmd_fetch`'s existing per-window `on_window` checkpoint to ALSO publish the live `RateController.snapshot()` + transport `CallMeter.snapshot()` to the bridge file on each processed window; a `None` controller (`--dry-run` / `--inspect` — no real account pacing) returns the checkpoint UNWRAPPED (zero overhead, no bridge written). **(3) Reader (dashboard side, `pull_rate_view.py` + `app.py`):** NEW pure `build_pull_rate_view_merged(...)` projects the FRESHER of the in-memory panel (age `now_monotonic − last_update_monotonic`) and the bridge file (age `now_wall − wall_time`) — the smaller `seconds_since_update` wins — through the existing `build_pull_rate_view`, so the widget shows whichever pull (dashboard OR CLI) ticked most recently; the `/api/v1/pull/rate` route best-effort reads the bridge via a NEW `_rate_bridge_lake_root_or_none(instrument_store)` (returns `None` — never raises — when no store is wired, so the route never 500s). When NO bridge file is present the behaviour is BYTE-IDENTICAL to projecting the panel alone (the no-CLI-file fallback); when nothing is fresh → honest IDLE/zeros. The widget JS is UNCHANGED — the JSON shape is the same `PullRateView`. **Scenarios covered:** fresh CLI bridge + idle panel → CLI numbers shown · stale CLI bridge → idle · no bridge file → in-memory panel fallback · panel fresher than bridge → dashboard numbers · no store wired → panel fallback (no 500) · corrupt bridge → ignored (panel projected) · ENOSPC at publish → `LakeWriteHalt` · live CLI pull writes the bridge per window · dry-run writes none. **Failure modes:** every bridge read failure degrades to `None`; missing snapshot keys default safely (no KeyError); a meterless adapter publishes a 0 achieved-rps. **Tests (gate-discovered files):** NEW `tests/unit/test_rate_bridge.py` (16 cases — round-trip, atomic-overwrite, every read-failure branch, ENOSPC→halt), `tests/unit/test_pull_rate_view.py` (7 NEW merge cases — no-bridge byte-identity, bridge-fresher, panel-fresher, equal-age-prefers-panel, fresher-but-stale-idle, None-fields-default), `tests/unit/test_cli_retry_storm.py` (4 NEW — helper None-controller passthrough + real-snapshot publish, live-pull-publishes-per-window, dry-run-publishes-none), `tests/integration/test_dashboard_cli_rate_bridge.py` (6 NEW route-level — fresh CLI surfaced, stale ignored, no-file fallback, panel-fresher, no-store no-500, corrupt fallback). `brutex/data/rate_bridge.py` at **100% line+branch** (52/4, 0 missing) + `brutex/dashboard/pull_rate_view.py` at **100% line+branch** (46/8, 0 missing); the NEW `app.py` route branches + the `cli.py` helper are covered under the package-wide 100% gate. ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on the new modules (the env's local mypy runs on Python 3.11 and cannot parse the codebase's PEP-695 generics — an environment artifact, not a code error; CI runs mypy on 3.12). **Scope-locked:** ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX); no scope/vocab/rate-cap change; req/hour stays the honest "observed" extrapolation (req/min × 60, CLAUDE.md §6 — the per-second cap is UNVERIFIED, shown as the injected ceiling). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is a cross-process VISIBILITY bridge (file-based, best-effort), NOT shared rate ACCOUNTING — the per-process rate caps are unchanged and the single-flight pull lock (DEC-PULL-HARDENING-FOLLOWUP-001) already prevents two concurrent pulls on one lake, so at most one publisher is ever active; the widget reflects the ACTIVE pull's real measured rate and reads IDLE when none is fresh, never a fabricated number (Golden Rule #1); the cross-process clock is wall-time (`time.time()`), so a large host clock jump could mis-age the bridge by that delta (the staleness window is 12 s — a normal NTP step is negligible). **Decision ID:** DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001.

## DEC-FNO-ASYNC-PIPELINE-WIRE-001 (2026-06-29)

998. **DEC-FNO-ASYNC-PIPELINE-WIRE-001 — wire the EXISTING async fetch pipeline into the F&O / options historical pull so its writes overlap fetches (the bulk of the 67k-window backfill)** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why (the gap, confirmed file:line):** the spot spine already runs the full async fetch/process separation (DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 #951 — `_build_fetch_pipeline`/`_drain_fetch_pipeline` in `pull_controller.py`, threaded into `run_groww_spot_ingest`), but the F&O historical pull — `pull_contract_candles` (`brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`), which is the BULK of the backfill (every futures + options contract × strike × expiry) — built ONLY the Lever-1 `write_pool` and NEVER a `fetch_pipeline`; its ingest call passed no `fetch_pipeline` (defaulted `None`), so each contract's whole SUCCESS-path tail (session-filter + `sink.append` + conflict-aggregate + `ledger.record`) ran SYNCHRONOUSLY on the fetch worker. The code even admitted it (the `option_ingest.py` `pull.underlying_all_empty` suppression note: "the option path is not wired to the pipeline in production yet"). With the connection pool able to issue toward the 8 r/s ceiling (DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 pool 2→4) but the per-contract serial write tail dominating each cycle, the achieved rate stayed ~2.9 r/s with the pool ~75% idle while the rate ceiling allowed 6–8 (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 / §6 — the per-second cap stays UNVERIFIED, the ceiling is the operator-DIRECTED 8 r/s `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`, DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 #922). **What shipped (REUSE #951's machinery — NO new pipeline ARCHITECTURE; minimal, mirrors the spot wiring; the wiring lives in `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, plus a hostile-review MAJOR-1 correctness fix to the shared per-series accumulator in `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`):** (1) `pull_contract_candles` now builds `fetch_pipeline = _build_fetch_pipeline(dry_run=dry_run)` via the SAME COMMON helper the spot spine uses (lazy-imported from `pull_controller`, mirroring the existing `_build_write_consumer` lazy import — no copy, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON), threads it through `_run_phase` into EVERY `run_groww_option_ingest(..., fetch_pipeline=fetch_pipeline)` call, and DRAINS it FIRST in the `finally` (`_drain_fetch_pipeline(fetch_pipeline)` before `_drain_write_consumer`) — mirroring the #951 MAJOR-4 drain-order fix (the producer must flush its tail before the writer + before the ledger persist + the 1-day derivation reads the just-written lake). (2) **No double-write / lost-write — the pipeline SUBSUMES write_pool.** The fetch_pipeline owns the ENTIRE tail (incl. `sink.append`), so the Lever-1 batched `write_pool` is now built ONLY when the pipeline is OFF: `write_pool = None if fetch_pipeline is not None else _build_write_consumer(...)`. The two are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (only one is ever non-`None`), so there is no redundant double background hop even when `BRUTEX_WRITE_BATCH` is also set — the pipeline's consumer is the SINGLE writer (the documented "ONE or the other" contract, `run_ingest.py:347`). (3) **Async completion-count reconcile (the F&O twin of `pull_controller._reconcile_pairs_with_pipeline`).** In async mode the producer returns a DEFERRED per-pair `IngestReport` with `bars_appended == 0` (the durable write + ledger.record run on a BACKGROUND consumer) and a tail-side transient (`PartitionLockTimeout`) is folded onto the pipeline; without a reconcile the phase result would read 0 bars and a tail-transient-deferred contract would be FALSELY marked `candle_status=complete`. NEW pure `_reconcile_phase_with_pipeline(phase, pipeline, *, selected_symbols)` runs AFTER the drain (totals final): it OVERRIDES each merged pair's `bars_appended`/`conflicts`/`still_failed_windows` (= the consumer's per-series `transient`) with the real durable totals, then RE-DERIVES `bars`, `still_failed_windows`, the clean `complete` set (excluding any contract with a quarantine OR a tail-transient residual), and the `clean` barrier — so the async-mode reported counts + verdict equal the synchronous path's (Golden Rule #7 settle-after-durable preserved; per-series sharding intact — one `(exchange,segment,symbol,interval)` → one consumer → partition-lock order). `_PhaseResult` gains `merged_pairs` + `failure_symbols` (kept ONLY for this reconcile; the synchronous path never reads them — a `None` pipeline / empty-totals reconcile returns the phase byte-identically, same object). (3b) **MAJOR-1 fix (hostile-review, folded before merge) — the per-series transient flag is now LAST-WRITE-WINS, not cumulative** (`fetch_pipeline.py` `_accumulate_series` / `SeriesTotals.transient`). The shared pipeline's per-series `transient` counter was CUMULATIVE across until-clean rounds and never cleared, so a contract that hit a `PartitionLockTimeout` in round 1 but DURABLY SUCCEEDED in round 2 still carried `transient == 1` → the reconcile put it in `still_failing` and reported `clean=False` even though its bars were durably in the lake (a MISLEADING verdict + a needless re-pull; the synchronous path correctly marks it complete). FIX: a durable-success fold now CLEARS the flag (`transient=0`) and a tail-transient fold SETS it (`transient=1`), OVERWRITTEN not summed — and because all windows of one series route to ONE consumer thread (the per-partition-lock invariant) these folds are SERIALISED, so the stored value reflects the series' NEWEST outcome, matching the synchronous spine's `passes[-1]` last-round residual. The naive `still = transient if bars==0 else 0` shortcut was REJECTED (it would false-mark-complete a series whose FINAL round transient'd but had bars from an earlier round). The pool-level `tail_transients` observability count stays cumulative (unchanged). Spot's verdict is IMMUNE (it derives completeness from `bars_appended > 0` + the synchronous `final_still_failed`, never the per-series transient), so this is the COMMON fix at the shared accumulator, with the F&O reconcile the consumer that newly relies on it. (3c) **MAJOR-2 fix (CI-gate failure `test_second_run_skips_settled_windows`, folded before merge) — drain the pipeline BEFORE the per-phase ledger persists.** `_run_phase` opens its OWN per-phase WindowLedger and persists it in its `finally` (`end_pull_ledger`); the pipeline was drained only in the OUTER `pull_contract_candles` `finally`, AFTER `_run_phase` returned — so a still-queued consumer tail's `ledger.record` (the tail incl. `ledger.record` runs async) landed on an ALREADY-PERSISTED ledger and was LOST, so that window re-fetched needlessly on the next pull (the no-skip-of-settled invariant broke — caught by the full-suite `test_composite_pull.py::test_second_run_skips_settled_windows`, which the isolated touched-file coverage run did not exercise). FIX: NEW `_drain_fetch_pipeline_in_phase` (delegates to the COMMON `pull_controller._drain_fetch_pipeline`) drains the pipeline in `_run_phase`'s `finally` BEFORE `end_pull_ledger`, so every consumer tail ledger-records before the ledger is written to disk — settle-after-durable at phase granularity, mirroring the spot spine's drain-then-persist order. The outer caller drain stays as an idempotent safety net (drain is idempotent — a second call with no live threads is a no-op). The write_pool is NOT affected (its `WriteConsumerSink.append` blocks until durable, so its synchronous tail already records the ledger before persist). (4) **Kill-switch respected:** the SAME `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE=off` disables it for F&O too (default ON); a dry-run / construction failure → `None` → the byte-identical synchronous (or Lever-1 write_pool) path. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10 — NO #906 trap):** this does NOT raise the cap (stays 8/500) — it only lets the connection pool USE the allowed headroom instead of idling on its own serial write tail; the throughput gain is EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED (~2–3× toward the ceiling, from the #921 root-cause arithmetic + the proven spot speedup) but UNMEASURED on a real F&O run — to be MEASURED, NOT claimed. The `pull.underlying_all_empty` diagnostic is SUPPRESSED in pipeline mode (`option_ingest.py` — the per-pair counts are deferred to the consumer, so a synchronous scan would see every pair as 0-bars and flood a false flag); a post-drain scan is a KNOWN pre-existing flagged FOLLOW-UP (left as-is, noted), NOT addressed here. **Tests:** NEW in `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py` — `test_fno_pull_constructs_passes_and_drains_fetch_pipeline` (spies the COMMON `_build_fetch_pipeline`/`_drain_fetch_pipeline` + the ingest `fetch_pipeline` kwarg: ONE pipeline built default-ON, forwarded to every ingest call, drained exactly once), `test_fno_pull_write_pool_none_when_fetch_pipeline_on` (with `BRUTEX_WRITE_BATCH=1` AND the pipeline ON, EVERY ingest call gets `write_pool=None` + a non-`None` pipeline — the mutual-exclusion / no-double-write proof), plus four `_reconcile_phase_with_pipeline` unit tests (folds deferred totals + excludes a tail-transient contract from clean + breaks the barrier; synchronous `None` is a same-object no-op; empty-totals no-op; an unmatched series keeps its producer report); the two pre-existing write_pool tests gain the `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE=off` kill-switch so they exercise the Lever-1 fallback; PLUS the MAJOR-1 regression suite — at the pipeline level (`tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py`: round-1-transient→round-2-success clears the flag; success-then-transient stays failing) AND end-to-end at the F&O reconcile (`tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`: the same two directions through a real `FetchPipeline` + `_reconcile_phase_with_pipeline`). The MAJOR-2 drain-order fix is regression-pinned by the WHOLE-SUITE `tests/unit/test_composite_pull.py::test_second_run_skips_settled_windows` (a second pull over the same selection must re-fetch NOTHING — the exact symptom: the last contract re-fetched before the fix) plus the F&O caller test asserting the pipeline is DRAINED before return. The existing F&O async-separation integration tests (`tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py`) + the `run_groww_option_ingest` producer/consumer suite still pass unchanged; both touched source files stay at 100% line+branch and the affected unit + integration suites are green under the full-package CI gate command (`pytest --cov=brutex --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 --ignore=tests/bench tests/unit tests/integration tests/property`). `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` AND `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py` BOTH at **100% line+branch** (251/54 + 224/56, 0 missing). ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub mypy notes in `auth.py`/`reauth.py` + two pre-existing `func-returns-value` notes in `test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py` are environment/repo artifacts, not in any line authored here — same note as #996). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 #951 (the async pipeline machinery + the spot wiring this mirrors), DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 #921 (Lever 2 pool 2→4 — the connections that generate demand the pipeline now lets the pool USE; Lever 1 write_pool this subsumes), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 #922 (the 8 r/s ceiling this lets the pool reach, unchanged). **Decision ID:** DEC-FNO-ASYNC-PIPELINE-WIRE-001.

## DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 (2026-06-29)

999. **DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 — bound the durable lake write with a wall-clock DEADLINE so a hung write (a wedged `fsync`/`os.replace` that NEVER raises) can never permanently stall the fetch lane** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why (the HUNG-WRITE BLIND SPOT, confirmed file:line + a prior code audit):** the async fetch pipeline (`brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`) DECOUPLES the durable write from the producer onto a bounded `queue.Queue(maxsize=4)` consumer, so internal work never blocks the fetch — but the consumer's durable write itself (`sink.append` → `ParquetWriter.write` → `atomic_io.atomic_write_via` → `os.fsync` + atomic `os.replace`) carries NO inherent wall-clock bound, and the existing bounds do NOT cover it: `run_with_deadline` (`deadline.py`) bounds only the FETCH SDK call, and `partition_lock.py`'s 120 s `DEFAULT_PARTITION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` bounds only the cross-process `flock` ACQUIRE — a hung write happens AFTER the lock is held, inside the merge / render / fsync / replace. So a WEDGED durable write that NEVER raises (a hung `fsync`/`os.replace` on a stalled external SSD / NFS mount) blocked its consumer thread forever, filled that consumer's bounded queue, and eventually wedged the PRODUCER on `FetchPipeline.submit`'s `queue.put` back-pressure FOREVER — the whole fetch lane stalling at 0 r/s while the rate controller still "allowed" the 8 r/s ceiling. The back-pressure loop only breaks on `_stopped` / `_draining`, which a non-RAISING hang never sets. (PROVEN: the new regression test deadlocks for the full watchdog window against the unbounded `sink.append`.) **What shipped (REUSE the COMMON `run_with_deadline` freeze guard — NO copy, CLAUDE.md §11; minimal per-window graceful deferral, mirrors the existing `PartitionLockTimeout` defer):** (1) **NEW `brutex/data/errors.py::WriteDeadlineExceeded(DataLakeError)`** — a TRANSIENT / RETRYABLE signal carrying the exhausted `deadline_seconds`; it subclasses `DataLakeError`, NOT `LakeWriteHalt`, so it is NOT in either ingest spine's `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` (it DEFERS one window, it never halts the pull). (2) **NEW constant `GROWW_WRITE_DEADLINE_S = 90.0`** in `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py` (+ `__all__`) — GENEROUS: a merely-SLOW deep-month merge (hundreds of ms typical; pathological partitions a few seconds) always completes well within it, but a true hang trips it in bounded time far under the 600 s pull watchdog; NOT a vendor-documented limit; operator-tunable via env `BRUTEX_GROWW_WRITE_DEADLINE_S`. (3) **NEW COMMON module `brutex/adapters/groww/write_deadline.py`** — `append_with_deadline(sink, *, exchange, segment, symbol, interval, bars, deadline_seconds=None)` runs `sink.append` through `run_with_deadline(lambda: sink.append(...), deadline)` and, on the resulting `TimeoutError`, re-raises `WriteDeadlineExceeded(deadline)`; ANY error `sink.append` raises ITSELF (a `PartitionLockTimeout` lock-acquire, a `LakeWriteHalt` disk-full, a `WriterError`) propagates UNCHANGED (`run_with_deadline` re-raises the worker's exception) — ONLY a TIMEOUT is reclassified, so the bound is ADDITIVE, never reclassifying a real write error; plus `resolve_write_deadline_seconds(raw=None)` (env override; falls back to the audited default for unset / blank / non-numeric / NON-FINITE `nan`/`inf` / non-positive — a bad value can NEVER disable the bound, mirroring `resolve_partition_lock_timeout_seconds`'s validation shape, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). (4) **Both ingest spines wired** — `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py` (spot) + `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` (F&O) `_process_window_tail` now call `append_with_deadline(sink, ...)` and CATCH `(PartitionLockTimeout, WriteDeadlineExceeded)` in ONE defer block (a lock-acquire timeout is OUR partition contention; a write-deadline is OUR wedged-disk hang — both are OUR-pipeline stalls, not vendor pressure, so the rate stays unchanged): record the window FAILED in the ledger, return a transient outcome, DEFER it to the next pull (re-pull, idempotent keep-first sink). So the consumer RETURNS + keeps processing subsequent windows and the back-pressured producer is RELEASED. The two pre-existing `ingest.window.lock_deferred` / `option.ingest.window.lock_deferred` WARNINGs are unified to `ingest.window.write_deferred` / `option.ingest.window.write_deferred` (carrying `error_type` = the class name, which DISTINGUISHES `PartitionLockTimeout` from `WriteDeadlineExceeded`, + a `defer_seconds`). **PREFER per-window deferral over tripping the whole pipeline:** the affected window is deferred + the consumer/producer keep going; the pipeline is NOT tripped (a `WriteDeadlineExceeded` is a normal tail-transient — it folds onto the pipeline's `tail_transients` tally via the EXISTING `fold_tail_transient` path, exactly like a `PartitionLockTimeout`, so the across-pull retry round re-pulls it). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10 — the zombie-write tradeoff stated, not buried):** `run_with_deadline` runs `sink.append` in a DAEMON worker thread; a wedged C-level `fsync` thread CANNOT be killed — it dies with the process. The guarantee is "the FETCH LANE is never blocked" (the producer is released + the window is deferred + re-pulled), NOT "the zombie write thread is terminated". The abandoned daemon STILL holds that partition's in-process `threading.Lock` + cross-process `flock` until its wedged syscall finally returns or the process exits; because all windows of ONE series route to ONE consumer (the per-partition-lock shard invariant), a LATER window of the SAME partition could block on the still-held in-process lock — but that later append is ALSO wrapped here, so it too defers in bounded time rather than wedging. A persistently-wedged volume therefore defers the same window(s) every pull until the volume recovers (the operator's signal to act), NEVER silently losing data (idempotent keep-first sink + the durable window ledger). The number of abandoned daemons is bounded by the distinct wedged partitions, not by the window count. This bounds the WRITE; it is NOT a memory cap and not a true RSS ceiling (out of scope, as in DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001). O(1) per window — the deadline wrap is one `threading.Event.wait`, NOT per-bar. **Tests:** NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_write_deadline.py` (16 cases — every `resolve_write_deadline_seconds` branch incl. nan/inf/zero/negative fallback; the normal + slow-but-OK paths return the sink result and forward the exact kwargs; the default-deadline-when-None path; a HUNG sink that blocks on a never-set `Event` raises `WriteDeadlineExceeded` in BOUNDED time WITHOUT waiting for the wedged write — the fetch-lane-freed proof; `PartitionLockTimeout`/`LakeWriteHalt`/`WriterError` propagate UNCHANGED). NEW ADVERSARIAL integration tests in `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py::TestHungWriteDoesNotBlockFetchLane` — `test_producer_not_blocked_by_a_hung_write` (the centerpiece: 1 consumer, `queue_maxsize=1`, ~12 windows where the FIRST window's durable write HANGS forever, deadline patched to 0.2 s via the real env var; a watchdog thread asserts `ingest_spot` RETURNS within a 20 s wall-time budget — the forward-progress / no-deadlock proof — then asserts the hung window is recorded FAILED-deferred [never SUCCESS, never lost], the LATER windows wrote durable Parquet [SUCCESS — the consumer kept processing], `pipeline.tail_transients >= 1` [surfaced for re-pull], and `pipeline.drain()` returns cleanly [no hang on drain/join]; WITHOUT the fix this test DEADLOCKS for the full watchdog window — verified by temporarily reverting to the unbounded `sink.append`, which failed with exactly the `"ingest_spot did NOT return — the fetch lane was BLOCKED by the hung write"` assertion); `test_hung_write_then_normal_pull_recovers_the_deferred_window` (the deferred window RE-PULLS + lands durably on a fresh non-hung pull — recoverable, zero corruption). The two pre-existing lock-defer log-event tests in `test_groww_ingest.py` + `test_groww_option_ingest.py` updated to the unified `write_deferred` event + assert `error_type == "PartitionLockTimeout"` (the lock-acquire case still distinguished). `brutex/adapters/groww/write_deadline.py` AND `brutex/data/errors.py` BOTH at **100% line+branch** (27/4 + 21/0, 0 missing); `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py` + `option_ingest.py` + `constants.py` all stay at **100% line+branch** including the changed defer block (218/54 + 299/80 + 56/6, 0 missing). ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub mypy notes in `auth.py`/`reauth.py`/`stage3_refine.py` are environment/repo artifacts surfaced only because the local venv has the real `growwapi` installed — NOT in any line authored here, same note as #996/#998). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/write_deadline.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/data/errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_write_deadline.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry), `CLAUDE.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 #951 (the producer/consumer pipeline whose hung-write blind spot this closes), DEC-FNO-ASYNC-PIPELINE-WIRE-001 #998 (the F&O wiring + the `fold_tail_transient` defer path this reuses), DEC-GROWW-PULL-CALL-DEADLINE-001 (the `run_with_deadline` freeze guard reused here), DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001 (the `PartitionLockTimeout` per-window defer pattern this mirrors), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (the disk-full halt this leaves untouched — a `LakeWriteHalt` still propagates as a pull-wide stop, never demoted to a write-deadline defer). **Decision ID:** DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001.

    **Follow-up (hostile-review gate-closure, same branch):** the review found the F&O `WriteDeadlineExceeded` defer arm (`option_ingest.py:601-611`) was structurally "covered" but never driven by a REAL timeout — only the spot path was — the "covered-but-never-run" coverage-honesty trap (coverage.py does not split a conditional-expression's arms). Closed with: (1) **F&O real-timeout tests** — NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py::test_ingest_hung_write_real_timeout_defers_window` + `…_logs_write_deadline_exceeded` feed a HUNG (deadline-exceeding, `threading.Event`-blocked) write to `ingest_option_contract`, so a GENUINE `run_with_deadline` timeout → `WriteDeadlineExceeded` drives the F&O arm — asserting the window is FAILED/deferred (re-pulls), the lane keeps going, and the log carries `error_type=WriteDeadlineExceeded` + `defer_seconds=0.2` (the else-arm `exc.deadline_seconds`, NOT `timeout_seconds`). PROVEN via a coverage-JSON run that those two tests ALONE execute `option_ingest.py` lines 601/609/612/619-620 with ZERO missing branches in the defer region — the F&O arm is really exercised by a real timeout, not the lock-timeout test. (2) **`test_same_partition_zombie_lock_second_window_defers_in_bounded_time`** — two same-month-partition windows where the FIRST hangs; the SECOND (same consumer, same in-process partition lock held by the abandoned daemon) STILL defers in a bounded 20 s budget rather than wedging — proving the honest-envelope zombie-lock tradeoff is itself deadline-bounded. (3) **`test_one_wedged_shard_does_not_freeze_a_healthy_shard`** — `workers=2`, a HUNG symbol routed (via the REAL `_series_shard_key`/`_shard_index`) to a different shard than a HEALTHY symbol: the healthy shard's windows land durably + SUCCESS while the hung shard defers FAILED — one bad partition cannot freeze the pool. (4) **`test_write_completing_at_the_boundary_records_success_not_timeout`** — a write that finishes under the deadline records exactly one SUCCESS, no FAILED, no double-record, zero `tail_transients` (the slow-but-OK path is never SUCCESS-on-timeout). **Sentinel hardening (item #5, DONE — clean + non-breaking):** `run_with_deadline` now raises a NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/deadline.py::DeadlineExceeded(TimeoutError)` for its OWN deadline (was a bare `TimeoutError`); `append_with_deadline` matches THAT subclass instead of the broad `TimeoutError`, so a future writer raising its OWN `TimeoutError` / `socket.timeout` (e.g. a network-backed `sink.append`) propagates UNCHANGED instead of being silently deferred as a hung durable write. Backward-compatible: `DeadlineExceeded` IS a `TimeoutError`, so EVERY existing `except TimeoutError` caller — the reauth re-mint (`reauth.py:247`) + the candle-call `from_groww_exception` `"deadline exceeded"` message-hint classification — catches it byte-identically (the message is unchanged); reauth + client + live + errors suites (94+ tests) stay GREEN, proven. NEW `deadline.py` tests pin the subclass-is-a-TimeoutError back-compat + that an `fn`-raised `TimeoutError` is re-raised as the EXACT object (never re-typed). All 6 changed source modules at **100% line+branch** (`write_deadline.py` 27/4 · `deadline.py` 21/4 · `ingest.py` 218/54 · `option_ingest.py` 299/80 · `constants.py` 56/6 · `errors.py` 21/0, 0 missing); ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change.

## DEC-UNIVERSE-WINDOW-SEGMENTS-001 (2026-06-29)

1005. **DEC-UNIVERSE-WINDOW-SEGMENTS-001 — the `/universe` "fetch windows" inline summary renders ALL THREE segments (spot · futures · options) instead of freezing at the hardcoded SPOT total during the F&O pull phase** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; READ-ONLY / display-only — no server, engine, lake, or pacing change). **Why (confirmed file:line):** the `/universe` page's inline "fetch windows (spot, all recorded): N …" line (`brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`) read ONLY the SPOT bucket — `refreshWindowsLine()` was gated on a `windowsBucket` variable hardcoded to `'spot'` in `startAndPoll`, and read `counts[windowsBucket]` — so once the spot phase finished and the pull moved into the FUTURES then OPTIONS phases the line FROZE at the spot total, even though `GET /api/v1/coverage/windows` ALREADY returns `counts.spot` / `counts.futures` / `counts.options` (built server-side by `db_view._window_counts_total`'s `GROUP BY market, status`, folded into the three buckets via the shared `db_view._window_market_bucket`, which maps `groww-option` → options and `groww-future` → futures). The F&O windows are durably recorded in the SAME unified window ledger — this was purely a DISPLAY gap, no data loss. **What shipped (client-side JS in `universe.html` ONLY — the API already returns all three buckets; reuses the existing generation/mtime-cached payload, O(1) per poll):** (1) `refreshWindowsLine()` now iterates a `WINDOW_SEGMENTS = ['spot','futures','options']` list, computing the same `resolved / no-data / pending / failed / total` arithmetic per NON-EMPTY bucket via ONE shared helper `windowBucketTallies(c)` (COMMON, no copy-paste — CLAUDE.md §11 / Golden Rule #11), and renders a per-segment breakdown PLUS an honest COMBINED total, so the futures/options counts grow LIVE during the F&O phase. (2) the misleading `windowsBucket = 'spot'` hardcode + the `if (!windowsBucket) return;` early-return are removed; the line is now gated on a `pullStarted` boolean set true in `startAndPoll` (the existing pull-started signal). (3) the label no longer claims "all recorded" for a single segment — it reads "fetch windows (all segments): spot N · futures N · options N · … total". **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the bucket counts are bucket-GLOBAL (every recorded window in the ledger, not per-pull) — the SAME honest scope the line always had; an empty segment is skipped from the breakdown (rendered "none yet" when none has any window) so the line stays readable; READ-ONLY — no engine/scope/vocab/rate change, the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **Tests:** extended `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py::…::test_windows_ledger_fast_path_through_real_connection` to ALSO record a future (`groww-future`) + an option (`groww-option`) window and assert the payload's `counts.futures` / `counts.options` buckets are present + populated — pinning the contract the frontend now relies on (so a server-side regression that stopped splitting the namespaces would be caught). `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` + `brutex/dashboard/app.py` stay at 100% line+branch (no Python source changed — the route + `_window_counts_total` were already returning all three buckets); ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean. No JS test harness exists in the repo (no `package.json` / jest / vitest), so the per-segment JS rendering is verified via the pinned backend contract test + manual review, NOT an automated DOM test. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on:** DEC-COVERAGE-WINDOWS-O1-001 #893 (the `_window_counts_total` GROUP BY + the generation-cached three-bucket `counts` payload this line now renders in full), DEC-COVERAGE-FUTURES-TAB-001 #673 (which first surfaced the `futures` bucket in the payload), DEC-FNO-WINDOW-PLAN-001 #879 (which seeds the F&O PLANNED windows the futures/options buckets now count), DEC-PROGRESS-WINDOW-UNITS-001 / DEC-EMPTY-RESOLVED-REPORTING-001 (the original window-line + its resolved/no-data/pending/failed arithmetic this preserves per segment). **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-WINDOW-SEGMENTS-001.

## DEC-PULL-RATE-WIDGET-VISIBILITY-001 (2026-06-29)

1000. **DEC-PULL-RATE-WIDGET-VISIBILITY-001 — wire the live rate observer through the metadata + F&O phases AND load the PULL RATE widget on every dashboard page, so the widget never goes blank mid-pull** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; observe-only — never touches pacing). **Why (TWO confirmed gaps, both proven file:line):** the live PULL RATE widget (`brutex/dashboard/static/bx-rate-monitor.js`, DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001) polls `GET /api/v1/pull/rate`, which projects the in-memory `RateLimitPanel`. (1) **Frontend coverage gap:** the widget `<script>` was loaded ONLY by `templates/v29.html` + `templates/universe.html` — NOT by the pages a pull is actually WATCHED on (`coverage` / `spot_coverage` / `fetch_windows` / `completeness` / `db` / `movers` / `results` / `reports` / `expired_options`), so on those pages the widget was simply ABSENT. (2) **Backend staleness gap (the important one):** the panel is fed by `_observe_rate` ONLY on the SPOT phase's per-window `on_window` tick (`pull_controller.make_window_observer`, wired into `pull_all_spot`). The METADATA phase (`metadata_pull.pull_expiries_contracts`) and the long F&O / historical phase (`composite_pull.pull_historical_for_underlyings` → `option_ingest.run_groww_option_ingest`) have NO rate-observe seam, so after the ~42 s spot phase the panel's `last_update_monotonic` stopped moving and — once `pull_rate_view.STALE_AFTER_S` (12 s) elapsed — the route reported `idle` for the ENTIRE ~38-minute F&O phase even though the SHARED `RateController` was actively pacing real fetches. The widget went blank mid-pull. **What shipped (ONE COMMON observe-only mechanism — REUSE `make_rate_observer`, NO copy of the panel-mapping logic, CLAUDE.md §11; a periodic snapshot was chosen OVER threading an `on_window` seam through the 4-layer F&O spine because it ALSO covers the metadata phase — which has no per-window hook — and needs ONLY the shared `SessionRateController`, not the F&O adapter's call-meter that is built inside the candle factory + unreachable upstream):** (1) **NEW `brutex/dashboard/rate_sampler.py::RatePanelSampler`** — a context-managed background daemon that, every `DEFAULT_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_S` (2 s), reads the SHARED controller via the NEW `SessionRateController.peek()` (returns the controller IFF a real pull already built one, else `None` — NEVER builds, so a dry-run / pre-pull tick conjures no live controller and the panel stays honestly idle) and pushes its `RateController.snapshot()` to the panel through the EXISTING `make_rate_observer(state)` callback. The controller snapshot carries the ALLOWED rate + the MEASURED rolling-60 s issue count (`recent_minute`) but NOT the transport call-meter's inter-arrival `effective_rps` (which lives in the F&O client pool, unreachable here), so the sampler derives the achieved r/s from the controller's OWN measured `recent_minute / 60` — a REAL measured achieved rate (a per-minute average, openly so), so the widget's flowing / stalled verdict is honest instead of pinned to a fake 0 (which would falsely read "stalled" all through the F&O phase). The loop mirrors `pull_stall.PullStallWatchdog` (an injectable `spawn` seam — daemon thread by default, capturing fake in tests — + a `threading.Event` `_stop.wait(interval)` body), so it is fully deterministic + 100%-coverable with zero real threads. Each tick is O(1) (one `snapshot` + one panel write) + best-effort (a snapshot / observer error is swallowed + logged, so the sampler can never block / slow / crash the pull it merely watches). (2) **NEW `SessionRateController.peek()`** in `pull_controller.py` — the non-building twin of `.get()` (which lazily builds a LIVE controller needing creds on first call). (3) **`/api/v1/universe/pull-pipeline` wiring** — the route's `_work` wraps the WHOLE `run_full_pipeline(...)` call in `with RatePanelSampler(session_rate=_session_rate, observer=make_rate_observer(state)):`, so the SHARED controller is sampled through metadata + F&O (the spot per-window observe still runs underneath unchanged — both feed the same panel, last fresh write wins, no harm). (4) **Frontend — every dashboard template loads the widget** — the self-contained, idempotent (guard at `bx-rate-monitor.js:33`) `<script defer src="/static/bx-rate-monitor.js"></script>` is now injected just before `</head>` in EVERY `templates/*.html` that lacked it (the 9 pull-watching pages named above + `groww_credentials` + `welcome` for parity), so the widget is present site-wide. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1 + #10):** OBSERVE-ONLY — the sampler READS the controller's `snapshot` + WRITES the panel; it touches NO pacing decision (never calls `pace` / `on_success` / `on_rate_limit`), so the fetch rate is byte-for-byte UNCHANGED. It NEVER builds a controller (`peek()` → `None` on a dry-run / pre-pull, so no fabricated "live" reading). The achieved r/s shown during the metadata + F&O phases is the controller's MEASURED rolling-minute rate (`recent_minute / 60`), a per-minute average, NOT the spot phase's per-call inter-arrival figure — an honest, real measured rate, openly so (the `req/min` + `req/hour` gauges read the SAME `recent_minute` the spot path does). The `_work` body carries the existing `# pragma: no cover — runs on the job thread` (the sampler-wrapping line rides it, exactly like the sibling `make_rate_observer(state)` spot wiring), so app.py coverage is unaffected; the sampler PRIMITIVE itself is separately tested at 100%. **Tests:** NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_rate_sampler.py` (8 cases — every `sample_once` branch: a built controller pushes one observer call with `effective_rps = recent_minute / 60`; a `None`-controller session pushes nothing + returns False; a snapshot missing `recent_minute` → honest 0 achieved; a raising snapshot is best-effort swallowed → False; + the full lifecycle: `start` spawns the drive body, the drive loop ticks until stopped, the context manager starts-on-enter / stops-on-exit, and the production daemon-thread spawn ticks then exits cleanly). NEW `SessionRateController.peek()` tests in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` (`peek` returns `None` before any build — building NOTHING — and returns the SAME built controller after `get()`, without rebuilding). NEW `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py::TestFnoPhaseLiveness` — `test_route_goes_idle_after_spot_without_the_sampler` (the REGRESSION / pinned bug: a spot-phase tick aged past `STALE_AFTER_S` with no F&O feed → `/api/v1/pull/rate` honestly flips to `idle` + zeroed `req_per_min` — the blank widget the operator saw) + `test_sampler_keeps_route_live_during_fno_phase` (THE FIX: a SHARED controller paced by an F&O pull — 360 issues in the trailing minute = a real 6 r/s — driven through `RatePanelSampler.sample_once()` makes `/api/v1/pull/rate` return `flowing` / active=True / `req_per_sec_achieved`≈6.0 / `req_per_min`=360 / `req_per_hour_observed`=21600 DURING the F&O phase). NEW `test_widget_referenced_on_every_dashboard_template` asserts EVERY `templates/*.html` carries the widget + the 9 pull-watching pages are all present. `brutex/dashboard/rate_sampler.py` AND `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` BOTH at **100% line+branch** (48/4 + 501/118, 0 missing — pull_controller including the new `peek()` both arms); `brutex/dashboard/app.py` unaffected (import line covered, wiring inside the pragma-excluded `_work`). ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched `brutex/` file — the only `mypy --strict brutex` errors are the pre-existing `growwapi` / `cma` stub notes in `auth.py` / `reauth.py` / `stage3_refine.py` (files NOT touched here; surfaced only because the local venv has the real optional `groww` / `optimize` extras installed, NOT in CI's mypy job — same environment artifact noted in #996 / #998 / #999). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/rate_sampler.py` (new), `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/{completeness,coverage,db,expired_options,fetch_windows,groww_credentials,movers,reports,results,spot_coverage,welcome}.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_rate_sampler.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry), `CLAUDE.md`. **Builds on:** DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001 (the panel + `/api/v1/pull/rate` route + the widget this feeds through every phase), DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 #958 (the cross-process bridge the route merges with — untouched), DEC-PULL-STALL-DETECTION-001 (the `make_window_observer` spot per-window observe this complements for the non-spot phases), DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 (the `SessionRateController` whose shared controller this samples, now with `peek()`). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-RATE-WIDGET-VISIBILITY-001.

1002. **DEC-FETCH-NONBLOCKING-HANDOFF-001 — a bounded on-disk SPILL overflow so a SUSTAINED-SLOW (not hung) disk can never back-pressure the Groww fetch lane to the write rate, with bounded memory** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; pacing is OBSERVE-ONLY — the RateController is untouched). **Why (the SUSTAINED-SLOW BLIND SPOT, confirmed file:line):** the async fetch pipeline (`brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`) hands every fetched window to a bounded `queue.Queue(maxsize=4)` write consumer; PR #962 (DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 #999) covers a HUNG write (a 90 s deadline raises + defers the window) but NOT the SUSTAINED-SLOW case — a disk where each durable write COMPLETES (no hang, no deadline) but is slow (e.g. 0.5–2 s/window). There, `submit`'s "healthy-but-slow consumer: keep blocking (retry)" branch (`fetch_pipeline.py`, the `_back_pressure_put` loop) blocks the producer on `queue.put` once the queue fills, coupling the fetch rate to the write rate — exactly the coupling a fixed bounded queue can NEVER remove, because a slow-but-not-hung disk fills any fixed buffer. PROVEN: the new regression test `test_regression_without_spill_the_fetch_lane_throttles_to_write_rate` (NO spill) takes ≥ 0.3 × N × write_sleep, while the centerpiece WITH the spill finishes issuing all fetches in < 0.5 × N × write_sleep. **The DESIGN chosen (Option A — bounded spill-to-disk overflow — and WHY, honestly):** the producer→consumer handoff is a Python CLOSURE (`_run_tail`) that captures the live `sink`/`ledger`/`pipeline` + the window's `raw` bars; none of the live objects is picklable, so a literal "serialize the whole tail to disk" is intractable. BUT the BULK memory that grows with a backlog is the window's `list[CandleBar]` (frozen `slots` dataclasses — losslessly serialisable to JSON with exact `Decimal` round-trip via `str(Decimal)`); the live `sink`/`ledger`/`pipeline` are SHARED single instances that do NOT multiply with windows.
