So the spill reclaims memory by spilling ONLY the bulk bars and keeping the tiny closure resident. **What shipped:** (1) **NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_spill.py`** — `FetchSpillArea` (a per-pull bounded on-disk overflow under `<lake_root>/.fetch-spill`, a `.locks`-style sidecar outside `bars/`+`options/` so no scanner sees a spill file as data): `try_spill(bars)` serialises the bars to JSON (each `CandleBar` → `{ts(ISO), o/h/l/c(str(Decimal)), v(int), oi(int|null)}`, the inverse `_decode_bars` reconstructs + re-validates each bar via the dataclass `__post_init__`), two-phase RESERVES their size against a hard byte cap (`GROWW_FETCH_SPILL_MAX_BYTES`, default 256 MiB, env-tunable `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_SPILL_MAX_BYTES`) under a lock, and atomically writes them via the COMMON `atomic_io.atomic_write_via` (tmp → `fsync` → `os.replace`; a disk-full at the spill → the existing `LakeWriteHalt` graceful-pull-halt path, NOT a new failure mode); `load(handle)` reloads; `discard(handle)` deletes + releases the budget; `cleanup()` sweeps stragglers at drain. Returns `None` (no spill) when the cap is hit → the caller back-pressures (preferring a slowdown to an OOM). A `SpilledWindow` handle is a tiny `(path, size_bytes)`. (2) **`FetchPipeline` gains the spill seam** — `FetchTail` gains an optional `rehydrate(bars)` hook (the spine swaps the window's bars in place in the closure's captured `raw`); `RawFetchResult` gains an optional `spilled` handle; the pipeline gains a per-shard UNBOUNDED-IN-COUNT, BOUNDED-IN-MEMORY OVERFLOW `collections.deque` of spilled handles (the real bytes live on disk, gated by the byte cap). `submit` is now: NON-BLOCKING `put_nowait` (the common, byte-identical fast path) → on a FULL queue, `_spill_full_window` spills the bars + appends the tiny handle to the shard overflow + DROPS the in-memory bars (a CLEAN ownership handoff under `_overflow_lock`: the producer drops the bars AFTER appending the handle, the consumer cannot observe a half-handed-off list) + RETURNS IMMEDIATELY → on a spill MISS (no spill area / no `rehydrate` hook / cap hit) FALL BACK to the existing bounded `_back_pressure_put` with the bars INTACT (never a dropped-bars EMPTY window). The consumer (`_run_consumer`) drains its queue, then `_drain_overflow(shard)` (rehydrate each spilled window's bars from disk + `_process_one` + discard the spill); `_process_one` rehydrates a spilled window before `tail.process` and discards the spill file in a `finally` on EVERY exit (success / captured tail failure / stop-drop) so the bounded spill never leaks; `drain` sweeps any straggler via `cleanup()`. (3) **Both ingest spines wired** — `ingest.py` (spot) + `option_ingest.py` (F&O) build the `FetchTail` with a `rehydrate=lambda b: raw.raw_bars[:] = b` hook (the frozen `_RawWindow.raw_bars` is a mutable list whose CONTENTS are swapped in place — `_process_window_tail` is BYTE-UNCHANGED, the sync path BYTE-IDENTICAL). (4) **Live build site wired** — `pull_controller._build_fetch_pipeline(*, dry_run, lake_root)` builds `FetchSpillArea.under_lake_root(lake_root)` + threads it into `FetchPipeline(spill_area=…)`; both `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` + the F&O `historical_pull` pass `lake_root`. **PREFER a bounded spill over an unbounded queue:** an unbounded in-memory queue would risk OOM (rejected); the spill bounds memory to the byte cap on disk, and past the cap the bounded back-pressure resumes (a slowdown, never an OOM). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this guarantees "the fetch lane never blocks on a SLOW write while memory stays bounded" UP TO the spill cap — a disk that falls behind for the ENTIRE pull, past the 256 MiB cap, re-applies the bounded back-pressure (the correct choice). It is NOT a throughput increase (the achieved rate is still vendor-bound — Groww 429s above ~5 r/s — and the RateController still caps the issue rate; pacing is OBSERVE-ONLY here). It bounds the OVERFLOW; it is NOT an OS-level RSS ceiling (a true RSS cap needs `setrlimit`/cgroups — out of scope, as in DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001). It PRESERVES PR #962's hung-write deadline (a HUNG write still defers via `WriteDeadlineExceeded` — orthogonal), keep-first idempotency (a spilled window's bars are byte-identical on reload; a never-discarded spill re-pulls next pull via the unsettled ledger row), and the durable window-ledger settle-after-durable contract (the ledger.record still runs on the consumer strictly after `sink.append`; `drain` flushes the overflow before the ledger persists). The spill payload is serialised as **JSON** (NOT `pickle`) — deliberately chosen so the on-disk overflow buffer carries NO arbitrary-code-execution surface on load (the `bandit` B403/B301 + `ruff` S301/S403 pickle findings are eliminated at the ROOT, not suppressed) even though the spill is only an ephemeral same-process / same-run buffer (written + read + deleted by this process within one pull); the JSON format preserves the exact `Decimal` rupee values via `str(Decimal)` text and re-validates every reloaded bar through the dataclass `__post_init__`. **Tests:** NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_spill.py` (23 — every `resolve_fetch_spill_max_bytes` branch; spill→load→discard round-trip; the JSON exact-`Decimal` round-trip with `open_interest` BOTH `None` and an INTEGER + the empty-window case; the two-phase byte-budget reserve/release; the CAP rejection; the disk-full→`LakeWriteHalt` envelope with the budget RELEASED; idempotent discard; the `cleanup` straggler sweep incl. the unlink-failure-logged branch + the missing-dir branch; `under_lake_root`). NEW per-spine `_rehydrate`-hook unit tests in `test_groww_ingest.py` (`test_spine_wires_a_rehydrate_hook_that_swaps_bars_in_place`) + `test_groww_option_ingest.py` (`test_ingest_async_pipeline_spine_wires_rehydrate_hook`) — a capturing fake pipeline drives the wired hook by hand (spill drops the bulk, reload restores it) and asserts `_process_window_tail` reads the RESTORED bars + folds the durable totals, so each spine's spill-hook line is 100%-covered by its OWN named test (the per-module coverage gate). NEW `TestSpillOverflow` (6) in `test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py` — a full queue SPILLS to the overflow + the consumer rehydrates + processes + discards; the cap-hit / no-rehydrate-hook / no-spill-area fall back to bounded back-pressure with bars intact; a spilled overflow window dropped fail-fast on a hard-stop STILL discards its spill; drain sweeps a straggler. The CENTERPIECE adversarial `TestSustainedSlowDiskDoesNotBackPressure::test_slow_disk_does_not_throttle_the_fetch_lane` (a SLOW-but-COMPLETING 0.5 s/append sink + the PRODUCTION queue depth 4 + a spill area + 12 windows) asserts: (a) FORWARD PROGRESS — the producer issues ALL fetches in < 0.5 × (N × 0.5 s) [impossible if it blocked on the write rate]; (b) bounded spill (≤ 1 MiB); (c) EVERY window durable (all SUCCESS, none lost, keep-first); (d) clean drain (spill released + dir empty). Its mirror REGRESSION PIN `test_regression_without_spill_the_fetch_lane_throttles_to_write_rate` (the IDENTICAL slow sink + NO spill) asserts the pull takes ≥ 0.3 × (N × 0.5 s) — the coupling the spill removes — so the fix is provably real, not a no-op. NEW `TestOptionTwin::test_option_window_spills_and_rehydrates_durably` exercises the F&O spine's spill rehydration end to end (6 contracts through a slow option sink + spill → all durable). `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_spill.py` (90/10) AND `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py` (270/70) BOTH at **100% line+branch** (0 missing); `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py` (220/54), `option_ingest.py` (301/80), `dashboard/pull_controller.py` (500/118) + `historical_pull.py` (251/54) ALL stay at **100% line+branch** including the changed spill-build + `_rehydrate` lines. ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub mypy notes in `auth.py`/`reauth.py` + the `# type: ignore[override]` unused-ignore on the test sinks + the `drain()/set()` `func-returns-value` are environment/repo artifacts surfaced only because the local venv has the real `growwapi` installed + all pre-exist on the base, byte-for-byte — NOT in any line authored here, same note as #999). **Merge note (rebased onto #1001 DEC-CLI-FETCH-ISOLATION-001):** the five pipeline-lifecycle helpers this PR extended were RELOCATED by #1001 from `pull_controller.py` into the COMMON `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_pipeline.py`; the spill wiring was therefore folded INTO `pull_pipeline.build_fetch_pipeline(*, dry_run, lake_root=None)` (the single COMMON builder, `lake_root`-gated so the dashboard spot/F&O + CLI build sites all thread the spill area; a `None` lake_root keeps the pre-spill bounded back-pressure byte-identical), and the CLI `cmd_fetch` build site passes `lake_root=resolved` so the CLI pull gets the spill too. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_spill.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_pipeline.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_spill.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_fetch_pipeline_wiring.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 #951 (the producer/consumer pipeline whose slow-write back-pressure this decouples), DEC-FNO-ASYNC-PIPELINE-WIRE-001 #998 (the F&O wiring this reuses), DEC-CLI-FETCH-ISOLATION-001 #1001 (the COMMON `pull_pipeline` builders this extends with the spill), DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 #999 (the HUNG-write deadline this is orthogonal to + preserves), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885 (the `atomic_write_via` disk-full→`LakeWriteHalt` path the spill reuses), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 (the `.locks` sidecar pattern the `.fetch-spill` dir mirrors). **Decision ID:** DEC-FETCH-NONBLOCKING-HANDOFF-001.
## DEC-CLI-FETCH-ISOLATION-001 (2026-06-29)

1001. **DEC-CLI-FETCH-ISOLATION-001 — wire the async fetch pipeline into the CLI `brutex fetch` spot pull so it is fetch/write-ISOLATED like the dashboard** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why (the CLI lacked the dashboard's protection, confirmed file:line):** the dashboard pull paths (`pull_controller.py` spot `pull_all_spot` + F&O `historical_pull.py`) BUILD the async fetch/process separation pool (`FetchPipeline`, DEFAULT ON) + an optional coalescing batched write consumer, thread `write_pool=`/`fetch_pipeline=` into the ingest, and DRAIN both in a `finally` — so each window's tail (session-filter + the durable Parquet `sink.append` + `ledger.record`) runs on a SEPARATE consumer pool, never INLINE on the fetch worker. But `brutex/cli.py::cmd_fetch` called `run_groww_spot_ingest_with_retry` with NEITHER kwarg (both default `None`), so the spot CLI pull ran every window tail INLINE on the fetch worker between fetches — the dashboard had the isolation, the CLI did not (and PR #962's hung-write deadline assumes the pipeline consumer path). The `run_groww_spot_ingest{,_with_retry}` signatures already ACCEPTED `write_pool`/`fetch_pipeline` (since DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-LEVER1-001 / DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001) — the seam existed; this is the CLI BINDING. **What shipped (COMMON, NO copy-paste, CLAUDE.md §11):** (1) the FIVE pipeline-lifecycle helpers (`build_fetch_pipeline` / `drain_fetch_pipeline` / `build_write_consumer` / `drain_write_consumer` / `reconcile_pairs_with_pipeline` + the private `_pipeline_stall_alert` hook) were RELOCATED VERBATIM from `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` into a NEW COMMON module **`brutex/adapters/groww/pull_pipeline.py`** — the single source of truth now shared by the dashboard SPOT build site (re-imports them under the SAME private `_`-names → its call sites are byte-unchanged), the F&O `historical_pull.py` build site (repointed off the private `pull_controller._*` indirection straight to the public `pull_pipeline.*`, dropping its `reportPrivateUsage` ignores), AND the CLI. (2) `cmd_fetch` now builds `write_consumer = build_write_consumer(sink, dry_run=_no_persist)` + `fetch_pipeline = build_fetch_pipeline(dry_run=_no_persist)`, threads `write_pool=`/`fetch_pipeline=` into the `run_groww_spot_ingest_with_retry` call (forwarded verbatim to every retry round), and wraps the pass + `end_pull_ledger` in a `try/finally` that DRAINS the pipeline FIRST then the write consumer (the SAME ordering the dashboard uses — a pipeline consumer tail may FEED the write consumer, so the pipeline must flush before the write consumer stops) BEFORE the ledger persist (settle-after-durable). (3) AFTER the `with` block, when `fetch_pipeline is not None`, the deferred per-pair report is RECONCILED via `reconcile_pairs_with_pipeline` (the completion-count fix — async mode returns `bars_appended == 0` per series since the consumer did the durable write on a background thread; the drained pipeline's per-series totals are folded back so the printed `bars_appended` + the exit-code residual are HONEST, not a false 0). **Opt-out / dry-run preserved:** `_no_persist` (`--dry-run` / `--inspect`) builds NEITHER (both `None` → byte-identical synchronous path), the pipeline stays kill-switchable via `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE=off` (→ `fetch_pipeline=None`, the pre-this-PR fully-synchronous inline-tail path), and the batched write consumer stays gated on `BRUTEX_WRITE_BATCH`. The upstream `RateController` (per-second AIMD ceiling + the 500/min governor) is UNTOUCHED — it stays entirely producer-side (Golden Rule #6); fetch/rate behaviour is otherwise byte-unchanged. PR #962's write deadline + the keep-first sink idempotency + the durable window-ledger contract are all preserved (the pipeline consumer is the SAME tail the deadline already wraps). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this isolates the fetch lane from the write on the CLI (the dashboard's existing benefit), NOT a new throughput claim — a CLI pull's wall time can still be bound by the pipeline's per-series serial consumer (all windows of one symbol+interval route to ONE shard) + the rate controller's pacing; the GUARANTEE is "the fetch lane keeps PROGRESSING through a slow/hung write" (the producer issues fetches without waiting on the tail), proven by the fetch-span signal below. **Tests:** NEW `tests/integration/test_cli_fetch_isolation.py` (7 tests): `TestCmdFetchWiresAndDrainsThePipeline` — a clean live pull threads a LIVE `fetch_pipeline` (+ `write_pool` when `BRUTEX_WRITE_BATCH=1`) and drains BOTH (pipeline first) in the `finally`; the **exception path** (a mid-pull crash) STILL drains both in the `finally` then propagates; `--dry-run` + the `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE=off` kill-switch thread `fetch_pipeline=None`/`write_pool=None` (the **regression pin** of the old fully-synchronous inline-tail call shape). `TestCliFetchIsolationProof` — the **ANTI-FAKE** centerpiece: a REAL `cmd_fetch` spot pull over a REAL `ParquetBarSink` whose every `append` SLEEPS 0.4 s (above the per-window pacing) with the producer pinned to a serial window runner — with the pipeline ON the FETCH SPAN (first→last fetch instant) lands < 0.7× the n × 0.4 s serial write floor (the slow write never blocks the fetch lane, the data still durable after drain), and with the `=off` kill-switch the SAME pull's fetch span inflates to ≥ 0.9× (n-1) × 0.4 s (the inline tail blocks the next fetch — the exact slowdown this wiring removes, pinning the old behaviour). The existing `test_dashboard_fetch_pipeline_wiring.py` + `test_dashboard_write_batch_wiring.py` (the coverage source for the relocated helpers) + `test_pull_historical.py` (the F&O build-site spy) were repointed to `pull_pipeline`. `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_pipeline.py` at **100% line+branch** (71/20, 0 missing); `brutex/cli.py` stays **100% line+branch** under the full CLI suite (587/112, 0 missing); `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` + `historical_pull.py` stay **100% line+branch**. ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub `unused-ignore` notes in `auth.py`/`reauth.py` + the env-skew `# type: ignore[override]` on the integration test's `_SlowSink.append` — required in CI, flagged "unused" only by the local venv's older `growwapi` — are environment/repo artifacts, NOT in any production line authored here; same note as #999). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_pipeline.py` (new), `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/integration/test_cli_fetch_isolation.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_cli_retry_storm.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_fetch_pipeline_wiring.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_write_batch_wiring.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on:** DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 #951 (the spot async pipeline this CLI-binds), DEC-FNO-ASYNC-PIPELINE-WIRE-001 #998 (the F&O build site repointed to the COMMON home), DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-LEVER1-001 (the `write_pool` seam), DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 #999 (the per-window write deadline the CLI consumer path now also runs through), DEC-CLI-LEDGER-CHECKPOINT-001 #884 (the CLI mid-pull ledger flush this preserves). **Decision ID:** DEC-CLI-FETCH-ISOLATION-001.

## DEC-FUTURES-LOOKBACK-60D-001 (2026-06-29)

1003. **DEC-FUTURES-LOOKBACK-60D-001 — the FUTURES-only default historical-pull lookback is now 60 days before expiry (`expiry − 60 days → expiry`); OPTIONS stay UNCHANGED at 30 days** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; entry numbered **#1003** because main's ledger reaches **#1001** and **#1002 is reserved by the in-flight DEC-CLI-FETCH-ISOLATION-001's sibling branch**, so the next free ledger number is 1003). **Why (operator direction):** when the operator passes NO explicit from/to dates, the F&O 1-minute pull defaults each contract to the recent tail of its trading life. The pre-existing default (DEC-FNO-PULL-ORDER-LOOKBACK-001 #905) was a UNIFORM 30-day lookback for ALL F&O — `DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 30` applied to FUT and CE/PE alike. The operator now wants a FUTURE's default span widened to 60 days (a future carries a continuous liquid life over its whole serial month, so the fuller recent tail is wanted), while an OPTION keeps the tighter 30-day default (an option's liquid life is short and the chain is huge — every strike × CE/PE — so 30 days stays bounded). **CHECK confirmed before implementing:** futures was 30 days on base main (`contract_bounds.py:103 DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 30`, uniform), NOT already 60 — proceeded. **What shipped (pull-PLANNING window only — F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO lake-schema / stored-bar / rate / vocab / engine change):** (1) **`brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py`** — NEW `DEFAULT_FUTURES_LOOKBACK_DAYS: Final[int] = 60` (a fixed DAY-count, NOT calendar months; operator-directed) alongside the existing 30-day option constant, which is RENAMED to the OPTION-specific `DEFAULT_OPTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS: Final[int] = 30` with the legacy name kept as a back-compat alias (`DEFAULT_FNO_LOOKBACK_DAYS = DEFAULT_OPTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS`, still 30); all three exported. (2) `default_fno_minute_window` gains a REQUIRED keyword-only `is_option: bool` and branches the lookback START — `expiry − DEFAULT_OPTION_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (30) for an option vs `expiry − DEFAULT_FUTURES_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (60) for a future — keeping the EXISTING `max(full_start, …)` / `min(full_end, expiry + 1 day)` clamps, the empty-window guard, and the `None`-expiry guard BYTE-for-byte (only the day-count selection changed). (3) **`brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`** — `_resolve_minute_windows` passes `is_option=contract.contract_type in {"CE", "PE"}` (the types are exactly FUT/CE/PE/PERP; FUT → `is_option=False` → 60 days, CE/PE → `is_option=True` → 30 days). An explicit operator from/to range STILL overrides for BOTH (the `explicit_dates` branch is byte-unchanged). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this changes ONLY the DEFAULT planning window when no dates are given (an explicit from/to range is byte-for-byte unchanged); 60 / 30 are fixed day-counts, NOT calendar months; both bounds stay clamped into `[full_start, full_end)`; pull-side only — no lake schema / stored-bar / rate / vocab / engine change. The only OTHER caller of `default_fno_minute_window` is the test suite (verified by a repo-wide grep — `historical_pull._resolve_minute_windows` is the sole production caller); the required `is_option` keyword means every caller is explicit (the split is never guessed). **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_groww_contract_bounds.py` — the `default_fno_minute_window` block rewritten to the split: FUT (`is_option=False`) → `expiry − 60d` (golden 2024-01-25 → 2023-11-26..2024-01-26), CE/PE (`is_option=True`) → `expiry − 30d` (golden 2023-12-26..2024-01-26, proving options UNCHANGED), the start/end clamp edges for BOTH branches, the `None`-expiry guard for BOTH branches, the collapsed-span fallback for BOTH branches, plus the two-new-constant + legacy-alias assertions. `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py` — `test_minute_window_defaults_split_futures_60_options_30` (integration: FUT start 2023-11-26 / CE/PE start 2023-12-26 in `report.start_dates`) + `test_resolve_minute_windows_default_splits_futures_60_options_30` (proves the `is_option` routing through `_resolve_minute_windows`: FUT→60, CE/PE→30); the explicit-dates override test is byte-unchanged (covers BOTH). **Both changed source files at 100% line+branch** (`contract_bounds.py` 79/20 · `historical_pull.py` 251/54, 0 missing). ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub mypy notes in `auth.py`/`reauth.py` are environment/repo artifacts surfaced only because the local venv has the real `growwapi` installed — NOT in any line authored here, same note as #999). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_contract_bounds.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on / supersedes:** DEC-FNO-PULL-ORDER-LOOKBACK-001 #905 (the prior uniform 30-day default — this SPLITS it: futures to 60, options stay 30), DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 #894 (the earlier futures-3mo / options-30d split that #905 collapsed — this re-introduces a futures/options split with a 60-day futures window). **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LOOKBACK-60D-001.

1004. **DEC-RATE-MONITOR-EXPAND-001 — a BIGGER, trustworthy live rate monitor: add a req/10min metric + a click-to-expand large overlay + REAL trailing-window evidence counts, proving the displayed rates are measured tracking not fabrication** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; OBSERVE-ONLY — the `RateController` pacing is byte-for-byte untouched; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; entry numbered **#1004** because main's ledger head is **#1003** so the next free number is 1004). **Why (operator direction):** the operator asked for (a) a large, easy-to-read view of the live pull rate, (b) it must NOT disturb any existing page layout, (c) a **req/10min** metric alongside req/sec, req/min, req/hour, and (d) PROOF the numbers are real tracking, not fabricated. **Investigation (confirmed file:line):** the live rate widget (`brutex/dashboard/static/bx-rate-monitor.js`, DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001 / DEC-PULL-RATE-WIDGET-VISIBILITY-001 #1000) polls `/api/v1/pull/rate` (`brutex/dashboard/app.py`), which projects the in-memory `RateLimitPanel` fed by `make_rate_observer` from the controller's `RateController.snapshot()` (`brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`) plus the cross-process bridge (`brutex/data/rate_bridge.py`, DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 #997). TRACE OF EACH RATE: `recent_minute` = `len(self._issues)`, where `_issues` is a deque the per-minute governor PRUNES to `PER_MIN_WINDOW` (60 s) at `rate_common.py` — so req/min was a REAL trailing-60 s issue count, but req/hour was an `× 60` EXTRAPOLATION (`pull_rate_view.req_per_hour_observed`, openly "obs") and there was NO req/10min or longer measured window at all (the 60 s ring held nothing older). **What shipped (COMMON, runtime, O(1)-amortized + O(1)-MEMORY; pacing UNTOUCHED):** (1) **`brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`** — a NEW OBSERVE-ONLY trailing-hour per-second issue COUNTER ring: a FIXED-SIZE `_issue_buckets` (`TRAILING_LOG_BUCKETS` = 3600 ints, one per second of `TRAILING_LOG_WINDOW_S` = 3600 s) + a head index + `_issue_newest_sec`. EVERY admitted issue (governor-on OR governor-off) is counted into its integer-second bucket by `_record_issue_locked(now)` right after `bucket.acquire()` in `pace()` — the single true "a request is issued" point — advancing the ring head to that second (`_advance_issue_ring_locked`, zeroing the elapsed buckets, bounded to one full ring pass). This is the **SCALABLE** design chosen OVER a per-issue timestamp deque: a deque would grow O(rate × 3600) ≈ 18 000 floats at 5 r/s and TRIPPED the `DEC-MEMLEAK-GATE-001` 256 KiB sustained-memory stress ceiling (`tests/stress/test_memory_growth.py::test_rate_controller_memory_flat`, which the deque draft failed at 333 815 B); the fixed ring is **O(1) MEMORY** (3600 ints, flat regardless of rate), so the stress test passes. It is NEVER read by any pacing gate (the governor still reads its own 60 s `_issues` deque), so it changes NO pacing decision and the fetch rate is byte-identical. `_count_in_window_locked(now, window)` first rolls the ring forward to `now` (so idle seconds read as empty) then sums the buckets for seconds `ceil(now-window)..floor(now)` (O(window-seconds), documented honestly, NOT claimed O(1)); `snapshot()` now also returns the REAL counts `recent_1s` / `recent_60s` / `recent_600s` / `recent_3600s` (windows `LOG_WINDOW_1S` / `_60S` / `_600S` / `_3600S`). The clock-gap handler (DEC-RATE-CLOCK-SLEEPWAKE-001) zeroes the ring too, so a laptop sleep/wake never counts stale pre-sleep issues. `recent_60s` equals the governor's `recent_minute` when a governor is wired (two independent sources — a built-in cross-check). (2) **`pull_rate_view.py`** — `PullRateView` gains `req_per_sec_count` (trailing-1 s evidence), `req_per_10min` (the NEW metric = trailing-600 s real count), and `req_per_hour_measured` (trailing-3600 s real count, a TRUSTWORTHY companion to the retained `req_per_hour_observed`); `build_pull_rate_view` + `build_pull_rate_view_merged` thread the new counts (panel + bridge paths), idle ⇒ all zeroed (never a stale "live" count — Golden Rule #1). (3) **`app.py`** — `RateLimitPanel` + `update_rate_limit` + `make_rate_observer` carry the three counts (default 0 for an older snapshot, honest idle); the `/api/v1/pull/rate` route extracts the panel + bridge counts and passes them through. (4) **`rate_bridge.py`** — `RateBridgeSnapshot` carries the three counts (schema bumped 1 → 2; an old schema-1 CLI file is ignored as unrecognised → the dashboard projects the panel until the CLI re-publishes, never a crash); `publish_from_snapshots` maps them from the controller snapshot (so the CLI `brutex fetch` path auto-publishes them — `cli.py` is mapping-based, unchanged). (5) **`bx-rate-monitor.js`** — the COLLAPSED pill keeps its small footprint (zero layout impact) but gains a req/10min row + a MEASURED req/hour; clicking it opens a LARGE fixed-position dismissible overlay (idempotent guard, an ✕ + backdrop-click close) that ALSO shows the RAW EVIDENCE — the actual integer counts in the trailing 1 s / 60 s / 600 s / 3600 s windows — so the operator can see req/sec = the 1 s count, req/min = the 60 s count, req/10min = the 600 s count, req/hour = the 3600 s count add up. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** OBSERVE-ONLY — reads the controller, writes the panel; touches NO pacing decision (the fetch rate is byte-unchanged). req/sec·min·10min·hour are now REAL measured per-second issue counts, not a per-second figure multiplied up; the older `req_per_hour_observed` extrapolation is RETAINED (labelled "obs"). During the first hour of a pull the MEASURED req/hour is the honest partial-hour count SO FAR (it grows as the window fills, never inflated). The per-second backtesting cap stays officially UNVERIFIED (CLAUDE.md §6); the 8 r/s ceiling / 500/min governor shown are the configured INJECTED limits. `_count_in_window` is O(window-seconds) not O(1) (documented, not faked); the ring is O(1) MEMORY. **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py::TestTrailingWindowIssueLog` — the PROOF test feeds KNOWN issue timestamps and asserts each window count is EXACTLY the number of issues inside it, plus the fixed-size-ring / whole-ring-zero-on-long-jump / snapshot-rolls-forward cases, the governor cross-check (`recent_60s == recent_minute`), the governor-off path still records, the unseeded-advance no-op, and the clock-gap zeroes the ring; the `DEC-MEMLEAK-GATE-001` stress test `test_rate_controller_memory_flat` PASSES with the fixed ring (the deque draft failed it); `tests/unit/test_pull_rate_view.py` — the new measured fields project (active + idle + panel + bridge + None-default); `tests/unit/test_rate_bridge.py` — schema-2 round-trip + the new counts + defaults; `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py` — the route returns `req_per_10min` / `req_per_hour_measured` / `req_per_sec_count`, the observer maps them, the served widget contains req/10min + the overlay + the idempotent guard, and `TestMeasuredCountsAreRealEndToEnd` drives a REAL `RateController` through `pace()` → snapshot → observer → route and asserts the route's measured metrics EQUAL the controller's real windowed counts (the end-to-end "provably real" proof). **`brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` (228/58) · `brutex/dashboard/pull_rate_view.py` (48/8) · `brutex/data/rate_bridge.py` (55/4) ALL at 100% line+branch**; `app.py`'s new observer + route lines covered. ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing env-skew `unused-ignore` in `test_rate_common.py` + the `reportPrivateUsage` warnings in `test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py` BOTH pre-exist on main byte-for-byte — NOT introduced here, same note as #999). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_rate_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/data/rate_bridge.py`, `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-rate-monitor.js`, `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_rate_view.py`, `tests/unit/test_rate_bridge.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on:** DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001 #995 (the widget + view this expands), DEC-PULL-RATE-WIDGET-VISIBILITY-001 #1000 (the site-wide widget + F&O-phase observer wiring), DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 #997 (the cross-process bridge this extends to schema 2), DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001 (the governor `_issues` deque this log is decoupled from). **Decision ID:** DEC-RATE-MONITOR-EXPAND-001.
1009. **DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-ATTEMPTED-001 — the `/universe` mapping-integrity gate now distinguishes never-attempted from attempted-and-zero, scopes to TRADABLE F&O underlyings, and reads GREEN on a clean selective pull** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; READ-ONLY observability — never touches a pull/engine path; entry numbered **#1009** because main's ledger reaches **#1006** (DEC-NIFTY-DYNAMIC-STRATEGY-001 merged via #973) and the in-flight sibling branches reserve **#1007 (#972) + #1008 (#974)**, so the next free unique ledger number is 1009 (#1004 is a pre-existing gap in main's ledger; the validator is uniqueness-based so the gap is fine)). **Why (a benign-but-real observability defect, proven file:line from the verification of a SELECTIVE single-symbol pull — `composite_pull.started requested:["NIFTY"]`):** the dashboard banner `Mapping integrity: 750 spot(s) pulled ZERO expiries` fired FALSE RED. Three structural defects: (1) `brutex/data/mapping_integrity.py reconcile_mapping_integrity` could only test "has a covered-year row" — it had NO way to tell a NEVER-attempted underlying (never pulled, the common case on a selective pull) from an ATTEMPTED-and-empty one, so every un-pulled name was branded a gating `none` failure. (2) An attempted-and-EMPTY underlying (the M&M silent-vanish) was indistinguishable from never-pulled at the reconciler level, because `coverage_years_from_records` keeps only `expiries_pulled > 0` cells and DROPS the attempted-empty `pending expiries_pulled=0` row that Phase-1 expiry discovery (`brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py _on_expiry_cell`) actually writes. (3) `InstrumentStore.fno_eligible_underlyings` clause (b) (the EQ arm) had NO `reference_only = FALSE` filter, so the ~539 NIFTY-Total-Market REFERENCE_ONLY constituents (which have no option chain) inflated the eligible set ~2.5× and the gate could never go green even after a complete F&O pull. **What shipped (READ-ONLY; NO pull/engine/scope/vocab/rate change):** (1) NEW reason `REASON_NOT_ATTEMPTED = "not_attempted"` + NEW pure `attempted_pairs_from_records(records)` (collects `(exch_id, underlying_symbol)` for ANY coverage row, regardless of `expiries_pulled` — so an attempted-empty cell IS in the set, a never-pulled name is NOT). `reconcile_mapping_integrity` gains an optional `attempted` parameter: a zero-expiry eligible spot WITH a row → gating `none` (the real M&M); WITHOUT a row → neutral `not_attempted` (never gates); `attempted=None` preserves the pre-change behaviour (back-compat — treats all eligible as attempted). `MappingIntegrityReport` gains a `not_attempted` count; `gating_failures` / `is_green` STILL gate only on non-whitelisted `none`, so `not_attempted` + `partial` stay green. `report_to_dict` exposes `not_attempted`. (2) The dashboard builder `brutex/dashboard/app.py _build_mapping_integrity_report` reads `store.list_coverage()` ONCE and projects it both ways (covered-years + attempted set), passing `attempted=attempted_pairs_from_records(coverage)`. (3) `brutex/data/instrument_store.py fno_eligible_underlyings` clause (b) gains `AND i.reference_only = FALSE` (matching the sibling `has_placeholder_stock_economics` probe), so the eligible set is the ~212 tradable F&O underlyings, not the ~750 with NTM constituents. (4) The `brutex/dashboard/mapping_integrity_csv.py` SUMMARY adds a `Not attempted (no pull run yet)` line; the `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html` banner now reads `attempted but pulled ZERO expiries` for reds and shows a `not pulled yet` tally, so it honestly separates the two states. **Before/after:** before, a clean selective pull of only NIFTY branded the OTHER ~750 eligible spots "pulled ZERO expiries" RED (never-attempted indistinguishable from attempted-empty, and 539 reference-only names padding the count); after, the gate reads GREEN on that same pull (the un-pulled names are `not_attempted`, neutral), counts only the ~212 tradable F&O underlyings, AND still flags a genuine attempted-and-empty stock (M&M's `pending expiries_pulled=0` row → `none` → RED). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** READ-ONLY observability — DETECTS, never auto-remediates; the attempted-empty marker is the coverage row Phase-1 ALREADY writes (no pull-side change needed — defect 2 is a reconciler-read fix, pinned by `test_attempted_empty_cell_records_a_coverage_row`); `attempted=None` keeps every existing caller byte-equivalent. **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_mapping_integrity.py` — never-attempted-is-neutral, attempted-zero-is-gating, green-on-clean-selective-pull, mixed-attempted-and-not, back-compat `attempted=None`, `attempted_pairs_from_records` keeps any row, `report_to_dict` carries `not_attempted`. `tests/integration/test_instrument_store_edges.py::TestFilteredScans::test_fno_eligible_underlyings_excludes_reference_only_eq`. `tests/unit/test_metadata_pull.py::test_attempted_empty_cell_records_a_coverage_row`. `tests/integration/test_dashboard_mapping_integrity.py` (+ `.csv`) updated to seed the attempted-empty M&M marker + a never-attempted-green case. `tests/unit/test_mapping_integrity_csv.py` + the golden `tests/golden/test_mapping_integrity_csv_golden.py` (digest regenerated for the new `not_attempted` row + SUMMARY line). `brutex/data/mapping_integrity.py` + `brutex/dashboard/mapping_integrity_csv.py` both at 100% line+branch. PLUS the MINOR stale "5 r/s ceiling (lowered 8 → 5)" prose in `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` reconciled to the live `8 r/s` ceiling (`GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`, DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002, CLAUDE.md §6) — docstring/comment only, behaviour byte-unchanged (the code already injected the constant). **Files:** `brutex/data/mapping_integrity.py`, `brutex/data/instrument_store.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/mapping_integrity_csv.py`, `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_mapping_integrity.py`, `tests/unit/test_mapping_integrity_csv.py`, `tests/unit/test_metadata_pull.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_mapping_integrity.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_mapping_integrity_csv.py`, `tests/integration/test_instrument_store_edges.py`, `tests/golden/test_mapping_integrity_csv_golden.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on:** DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-RECONCILE-001 #870 (the reconciler this extends), DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-EXPORT-001 #873 (the CSV companion), DEC-NIFTY-TOTAL-MARKET-REFTAG-001 (the `reference_only` column the EQ filter uses), DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 #922 (the live 8 r/s ceiling the prose reconciles to). **Decision ID:** DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-ATTEMPTED-001.

1007. **DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-DATERANGE-001 — re-add a from/to spot DATE PICKER to the `/universe` "Pull · full pipeline" section and properly WIRE it through the `/pull-pipeline` route into the SPOT history + metadata-year phases** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; entry numbered **#1007** because main's ledger reaches **#1003** and **#1004–#1006 are reserved by sibling in-flight branches**, so the next free ledger number for this branch is 1007). **Why (re-wire the picker DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONSOLIDATE-001 removed, resolving its honesty concern):** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONSOLIDATE-001 (#920) REMOVED the from/to date picker from the `/universe` pull bar BECAUSE the consolidated `/pull-pipeline` route ignored from/to and always pulled the fixed default window — an inert picker was dead/misleading UI (Golden Rule #10), so it was replaced with a static "window · 2020 → prev-day (fixed)" label. The BACKEND in fact already supported explicit dates everywhere ELSE: `resolve_candle_range` (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, floor `GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR=date(2020,1,1)`, prev-day cap, `from>to`→`ValueError`) + `pull_all_spot(from_date, to_date, year, …)` + `default_date_range` for the UI pre-fill + the `/universe` renderer already fills the `__BRUTEX_DATE_FROM__`/`__BRUTEX_DATE_TO__`/`__BRUTEX_DATE_MAX__` tokens; precedent pickers exist on `/db` + `/reports`. The ONLY gap was the `/pull-pipeline` route hard-coding `from_date=None, to_date=None` (spot) + `_resolve_metadata_years(None, None)`. This PR re-adds the picker AND wires it, so the control is honest again. **What shipped (READ-ONLY / pull-PLANNING only — NO lake-schema / stored-bar / rate / vocab / engine change):** (1) **Frontend `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`** — the static fixed-window `.ctl-field` chip is replaced by a `.daterange` group with two native inputs `id="pipeFrom"` / `id="pipeTo"` (`type="date" min="2020-01-01"`, `max=__BRUTEX_DATE_MAX__` = today IST, `value=__BRUTEX_DATE_FROM__` / `__BRUTEX_DATE_TO__` filled per render by the SHARED `_fill_default_dates` → `default_date_range`), styled to match the `/db` picker (the `.daterange` CSS rule is restored). A new `pipelineDateQuery()` helper appends `&from_date=` / `&to_date=` to the pull URL ONLY when the input is non-blank (blank ⇒ no param, mirroring `db.html`); the `pullPipelineBtn` onclick folds it into BOTH the scoped (`?symbols=…`) and the bare whole-universe URL. A pull-bar lead note states the range applies to SPOT history (F&O uses its per-contract default lookback). DOM is unchanged via `textContent`/static template only — NO `innerHTML` (CodeQL XSS guard). (2) **Backend `/api/v1/universe/pull-pipeline` route (`brutex/dashboard/app.py`)** — NEW `from_date: str | None = Query(None)` / `to_date: str | None = Query(None)` params (mirroring `pull-expiries-contracts`); validated EAGERLY via `resolve_candle_range(from_date, to_date, year=None, now=datetime.now(UTC))` in a `try/except ValueError → HTTPException(400)` (a reversed / non-ISO range is a clean 400 before the background job is queued; a below-2020 `from_date` is CLAMPED up by `resolve_candle_range`, not an error). the validation re-uses the SAME `resolve_candle_range` the spot phase re-runs (one source of truth); no JS test harness exists in the repo, so the JS wiring is pinned via the template-render + route integration tests below. **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_pipeline_route.py` — 5 NEW route tests (a capturing-spine fixture records the kwargs each phase received): blank dates ⇒ `pull_all_spot` gets `from_date=None`/`to_date=None` + the full 2020-origin metadata grid (default-preservation); ## DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-DETECT-001 (2026-06-29)

1008. **DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-DETECT-001 — an OBSERVE-ONLY diagnostic that flags a fetch window the pull marks SUCCESS but is actually TRUNCATED (its bars stop materially before the window end) so it can never silently stay incomplete** (2026-06-29; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; DETECT-only — NO status/skip/ledger/engine change, NO auto-re-pull; entry numbered **#1008** because #1004–#1007 are RESERVED by the in-flight sibling PRs — #1004=DEC-RATE-MONITOR-EXPAND-001 (#969), #1005=#970 (merged to main), #1006=#971 mapping-integrity, #1007=#972 date-picker — so the next free ledger number is 1008; the DEC-ID validator is uniqueness-based, so the numeric gap is fine). **Why (the SUCCESS-without-completeness BLIND SPOT, confirmed file:line):** `classify_window_status` (`brutex/data/window_status.py:88-92`) returns `SUCCESS` the moment the vendor returns ANY bar (`raw_bars > 0`) with NO completeness check, and the unified ledger then treats `SUCCESS` as terminal/skippable (`brutex/data/window_ledger.py:86` `_SKIPPABLE`, `:293` `is_skippable`). So a window that SHOULD hold ~30 days but returned only the first 2 days is stamped `SUCCESS`, becomes `is_skippable`, and is NEVER re-pulled to complete — a real data-completeness gap. **The design (false-positive-safe — flags TRUNCATION, never SPARSITY):** a naive "expected bar count vs actual bar count" check would false-flag a genuinely-sparse illiquid option (a far-OTM strike legitimately returns few-but-real bars) and imply a giant wasteful re-pull. This does NOT do that. The signal is TEMPORAL COVERAGE, not bar density: the NEW pure `brutex/data/partial_window_detect.py::classify_partial_window` compares the date of the window's LAST stored bar against where the last bar SHOULD be — the window's end boundary clamped to (a) the contract's expiry/delisting and (b) the last completed NSE trading session before now (reusing the COMMON `brutex/calendars/nse.py::is_trading_day`, never a re-implemented weekday rule, CLAUDE.md §11). A contract whose bars run up to its expiry/window-end is COMPLETE even if sparse (density is never consulted). The flag fires `SUSPECTED_PARTIAL` ONLY when the last bar lags the expected end by STRICTLY MORE than a conservative, env-tunable tolerance of trading sessions (`PARTIAL_WINDOW_TOLERANCE_SESSIONS`, env `BRUTEX_PARTIAL_WINDOW_TOLERANCE_SESSIONS`, default 5), and EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES (each `NOT_TRUNCATED`): an EMPTY window (no bars — the EMPTY status owns it), a LIVE-EDGE window (its end is within `PARTIAL_WINDOW_LIVE_EDGE_SESSIONS`, env-tunable, default 3, of today — the vendor may not have published the most recent sessions yet), and an AT-EXPIRY window (the last bar reaches the expiry session — a dead contract has no later bar). Pure + clock-injected, O(1) per window, no I/O. **Surfaced PULL-side** (the lowest-risk surface — the pull's window tail is the only place the last-bar timestamp + window end + contract expiry are all in hand): `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py::_observe_partial_window` runs the classifier in the SUCCESS-path consumer tail (`_process_option_window_tail`, after the ledger record) and emits ONE `window.suspected_partial` WARNING per truncated window (symbol via `repr()`, with `last_bar_date` / `expected_end_date` / `missing_sessions` / `expiry`), mirroring the existing observe-only `pull.underlying_all_empty` flag (DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 #919) and the read-side `completeness.symbol_reconcile_mismatch` (#907). It is FULLY wrapped in a try/except that swallows + logs (`window.suspected_partial_error`) any diagnostic failure, so it can NEVER block / slow / crash the pull. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this DETECTS and WARNs; it does NOT auto-remediate (no status flip, no skip change, no re-pull trigger) — the operator decides whether to re-pull a flagged window. It is heuristic + false-positive-guarded (the conservative session tolerance + the empty/live-edge/at-expiry exclusions keep a sparse illiquid contract, a holiday cluster, a one-day publish-lag, and a live-edge tail from tripping it); a residual false-positive is possible at the boundary but is a benign WARNING, never a data change. Wired on the F&O `option_ingest` SUCCESS tail (the path with the per-window raw bars in hand); the classifier itself is vendor-neutral and reusable for a future spot-side surface (NOT wired there here — flagged FUTURE, not claimed). **Tests:** NEW `tests/unit/test_partial_window_detect.py` (23 tests — the dedicated import-verified test the coverage-discovery gate requires for a new module): a clearly-truncated window IS flagged; a sparse-but-complete illiquid window is NOT; a live-edge window is NOT; an at-expiry window is NOT; an empty window is NOT; the expiry/today clamps; the env-tunable tolerance + live-edge knobs + their non-positive/malformed/missing fallbacks; the session helpers. NEW `TestPartialWindowFlag` in `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py` (5 tests): a truncated window fires exactly one `window.suspected_partial` WARNING (unit + end-to-end through `_process_option_window_tail`), a sparse-complete window is silent, an empty window is silent, and the diagnostic raising NEVER breaks the pull (logs `window.suspected_partial_error`). `brutex/data/partial_window_detect.py` at **100% line+branch** (70/26, 0 missing); `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` stays **100% line+branch** (313/82, 0 missing). ruff / ruff-format / `pyright` clean on every touched file; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file (the pre-existing `growwapi`-stub mypy notes in `auth.py`/`reauth.py` + the `cma`-stub note in `stage3_refine.py` are environment/repo artifacts surfaced only by the local venv's extras, NOT in any line authored here — same note as #999/#1003). **Files:** `brutex/data/partial_window_detect.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_partial_window_detect.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Builds on:** DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 #919 (the observe-only pull-side flag pattern this mirrors), DEC-COMPLETENESS-RECONCILE-DIAG-001 #907 (the observe-only read-side diagnostic pattern), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the SUCCESS/skip authority this observes but never changes), DEC-DERIV-MINUTE-BOUNDS-001 #711 (the expiry-as-trading-life-bound rationale reused for the end clamp). **Decision ID:** DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-DETECT-001.
## DEC-NIFTY-DYNAMIC-STRATEGY-001 (2026-06-29)

1006. **DEC-NIFTY-DYNAMIC-STRATEGY-001 — design lock (ADR-0012) for a NIFTY-only dynamic futures brute-force strategy system: 3 strategies distinguished ONLY by Fibonacci anchor (prev-day OHLC / rolling-weekly / weekly-static), both directions, all sharing VWAP + EMA20/200 + standard pivots P/R1-R5/S1-S5 + prev-day H/L + close/body/wick level checks + BOS/CHoCH + curated candles; frictionless signal-only on NIFTY futures (VWAP feasible because futures carry volume, unlike spot per DEC-VENDOR-VOLUME-NORMALIZE-001), options translation carries costs/slippage/lots; intraday only with 15:20 IST forced exit, Mode A (SL/TP grid) + Mode B (no SL/TP); output is a dynamic time-of-day × combo expectancy map + adaptive runtime selector, NOT a static strategy** (2026-06-29, operator: "as of now we are going to do a thorough drill down deep brute force check only for nifty spot indices futures and options alone"; "three unique strategies where every fibonacci level is unique"; "i need only dashboard operator webpage"). **Why:** focus the engine on one high-conviction underlying; futures (not spot) unlock a session-anchored VWAP because spot indices carry no volume; the 3-anchor split makes the strategies directly comparable on identical machinery. **What shipped (DOCS-ONLY design lock):** `docs/adr/0012-nifty-dynamic-futures-strategy.md` capturing D1-D10 + rationale + the 9-PR build sequence; no engine code. The Fib anchor is a swept STRATEGY parameter (not bits) to keep the vocab lean; the vocab grows from 52 toward ~58-66 conditions (VWAP + R5/S5 + BOS/CHoCH) which adopts a u128 mask for DYNAMIC headroom — ADR-gated by DEC-PLUGIN-001 (this ADR is the gate), O(1) per-bar preserved (u128 AND = two u64 ANDs). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ scope-locked to NIFTY, verified against current code (pivots stop at R4/S4 today `pivots.py:50`; Fib prev-day-only today `fib_levels.py:1`; expiry from instrument-master `expiry_date` `instruments.py:206` — R5/S5, the 2 new Fib anchors, and the roll are ADDITIONS the build PRs make, not assumptions); ✅ O(1) per-bar preserved; 🟡 runtime speed UNPROVEN here (design only; M4-Pro SLA is a model not a measurement — real benchmark is PR-8); 🟡 exact trial count is a FORMULA (~4e12 raw across 3 strategies) not a frozen number until vocab+grid lock in PR-1/PR-2; ✅ out-of-box edge cases (futures-roll series construction, expiry-day trade lifecycle, VWAP session reset, data gaps/halts, weekly-anchor cold-start + Muhurat/short-week, effective-N floor, look-ahead on new indicators) each named with a policy + owning PR in ADR §4.5 after the 4-agent hostile review; 🚫 no engine code, no scope expansion beyond NIFTY, no `/results` deletion yet (PR-8 wire-first-then-delete). **Files:** `docs/adr/0012-nifty-dynamic-futures-strategy.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-NIFTY-DYNAMIC-STRATEGY-001. **Builds on** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441), DEC-VENDOR-VOLUME-NORMALIZE-001, DEC-PLUGIN-001, DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001, DEC-FUTURES-LOOKBACK-60D-001. (Ledger: #1006 = max-existing(1005)+1; #1004 is a pre-existing gap in main's ledger, not reserved by this branch. This entry AMENDS CLAUDE.md §3 Rule #3 engine-scope — operator-authorized NIFTY-futures brute-force engine surface — with the companion CLAUDE.md §3 clause owned by PR-1, recorded here so the scope change is not by omission.)

## DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 (2026-06-29)

1010. **DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 — PR-1 of ADR-0012 (D4/D7): a manifest→codegen layer for the shared condition vocabulary + the u64→u128 mask widening + a NEW (LAYOUT-ONLY) condition-bit layout for VWAP-position / pivot R5-S5 proximity / BOS / CHoCH (bits 52-59, `implemented=false` until PR-2 supplies their indicator math)** (2026-06-29; ENGINE scope per ADR-0012 — NIFTY futures + the 3 spot indices; data-independent, synthetic fixtures only). **Why:** the prior "add one condition = hand-edit ~7-8 sites" workflow is error-prone and the u64 mask had no headroom; ADR-0012 D7 mandates "a single manifest edit + codegen" and D4 the u128 widening for genuine DYNAMIC headroom (Golden Rule #11). The vocab is the SHARED `trading-core` crate consumed bit-identically by BruteX (PyO3) + TickVault (native), so bit-identity is the contract. **What shipped:** (1) NEW `rust/trading-core/conditions.toml` — the SINGLE source-of-truth manifest: the existing 52 conditions at bits 0-51 (exact names/groups, never renumbered — DEC-PLUGIN-001 grow-only) + 8 NEW bits appended at 52-59, each with `bit`/`name`/`group`/`description`/`reserved`/`applies_to_1day`/`implemented`. The new bit map is: 52 `close_above_vwap` (VWAP Position, `applies_to_1day=false` per ADR D12), 53 `close_below_vwap` (VWAP Position, `applies_to_1day=false`), 54 `near_pivot_r5` (Pivot Proximity Extended), 55 `near_pivot_s5` (Pivot Proximity Extended), 56 `bos_bullish` / 57 `bos_bearish` / 58 `choch_bullish` / 59 `choch_bearish` (Market Structure) — ALL `implemented=false` (LAYOUT ONLY). (2) NEW `scripts/codegen_vocab.py` — ONE generator (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) that emits BOTH `rust/trading-core/src/bits.rs` AND `brutex/vocabulary/bits.py` (the `BIT_*` constants, `NAME_TO_BIT`/`BIT_TO_NAME`, `GROUP_RANGES`, `TOTAL_CONDITIONS`, `MASK_WIDTH`, `IMPLEMENTED_MASK`, `APPLIES_TO_1DAY_MASK`) from the manifest, with a `--check` mode (regenerate-to-memory + byte-diff, exit 1 on drift) for CI; `brutex/vocabulary/describe.py` now imports `GROUP_RANGES` from the generated `bits.py` (no hand-maintained copy). The evaluator's boolean branches stay HAND-WRITTEN — codegen owns the bit LAYOUT only, and the new `implemented=false` bits have NO branch so the evaluator emits 0 for them. (3) u128 widening: `rust/trading-core/src/{bits.rs,evaluator.rs,python.rs,lib.rs}` (`evaluate_atoms` → `u128`, `bit()` shifts `1u128`, PyO3 returns `u128` ↔ Python `int`), `brutex/vocabulary/` (Python `int` is already arbitrary-precision), `brutex/engine/combo_mask.py` (`MAX_VOCAB_BITS` 64→128 + the "ADR required for u128" guards now cite ADR-0012/DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 as the SATISFIED gate; the numpy oracle/fallback uses TWO u64 limbs `(lo,hi)` because numpy has no uint128, and `count_supermasks` routes a >64-bit mask/bar to that two-limb reference so the u64 Rust kernel never silently truncates), `brutex/engine/results_store.py` (the mask is persisted as TWO `Int64` limb columns `mask_bits_lo`/`mask_bits_hi` via an unsigned↔signed offset — a u128 does not fit one signed Int64 — and `MASK_BITS_MAX` widened to `(1<<TOTAL_CONDITIONS)-1`), `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py` (`mask:%016x` → `%032x`). (4) Regenerated `tests/golden/fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json` (version 1→2, `total_conditions` 52→60, `expected_u64` int → `expected_mask` 32-nibble hex STRING so a bit ≥53 keeps full precision; the both-ways bit-identity gate is partitioned over the IMPLEMENTED bits only, with a separate test proving the LAYOUT-ONLY bits are ALWAYS clear). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the new bits are LAYOUT-ONLY (`implemented=false`) — the evaluator emits 0 for them; NO bit was set `implemented=true` without real indicator math (that is PR-2). ✅ u128 for headroom, ADR-gated (not a silent transition). 🟡 numpy has NO uint128 — the real solution is Python `int` scalars + two u64 limbs for the numpy oracle/fallback + native `u128` in Rust; the production `fno_math` kernel stays u64-native (today's bits 0-59 all fit u64) with a two-limb fallback guarding any future ≥64-bit mask, NOT a u128 rewrite of that kernel (explicit follow-up if/when bits ≥64 land). ✅ O(1) per-bar preserved (u128 AND = two u64 ANDs); the existing O(1) ratio + mask-AND benches stay green. **Files:** `rust/trading-core/conditions.toml` (new), `scripts/codegen_vocab.py` (new), `rust/trading-core/src/{bits.rs,evaluator.rs,python.rs,lib.rs}`, `rust/trading-core/tests/{golden_vectors.rs,proptests.rs}`, `brutex/vocabulary/{bits.py,describe.py}`, `brutex/engine/{combo_mask.py,results_store.py,sweep_run.py}`, `scripts/{gen_vocab_golden_vectors.py,gen_condition_truth_table.py,check_vocab_rust_parity.py}`, `tests/golden/fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json`, the touched tests under `tests/{unit,property,golden,integration}/`, `CLAUDE.md` §3, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001. **Builds on** DEC-NIFTY-DYNAMIC-STRATEGY-001 (#1006 — ADR-0012, the mask-width gate), DEC-PLUGIN-001 (grow-only + ADR-gated mask-width transition), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441 — the shared trading-core crate). (Ledger: #1010 = max-existing(1009)+1; #1007/#1008/#1009 are RESERVED/used by the in-flight sibling PRs (#1009 = DEC-MAPPING-INTEGRITY-ATTEMPTED-001, merged to main), so this PR-1 entry takes the next free number 1010 after a fresh merge onto main — the DEC-ID validator is uniqueness-based, the numeric gap is fine.)

## DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 (2026-06-29)

1011. **DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 — PR-2 of ADR-0012: the evaluate-time INDICATOR math for the new condition bits — session-anchored futures VWAP (bits 52/53), pivot R5/S5 (bits 54/55), and two new Fibonacci anchors (rolling-weekly + weekly-static, NO new bits). BOS/CHoCH (bits 56-59) are HONESTLY DEFERRED — left `implemented=false`** (2026-06-29; ENGINE scope per ADR-0012 — NIFTY futures + the 3 spot indices; data-independent, synthetic fixtures only; NO scope/rate-cap change). **Why:** PR-1 (DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 #1010) declared bits 52-59 as LAYOUT-ONLY (`implemented=false`); PR-2 supplies the real indicator math and flips a bit to `implemented=true` ONLY when that math is real, tested, AND look-ahead-clean (CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #10 honesty mandate). **What shipped — bits flipped `implemented=true` (4):** (a) **VWAP position 52/53** (`close_above_vwap`/`close_below_vwap`) — a NEW session-anchored futures VWAP STATE object in BOTH the shared Rust `trading-core` (`rust/trading-core/src/indicators/vwap.rs::VwapState`) AND its bit-for-bit Python twin (`brutex/indicators/vwap.py::VwapState`): running `cum(typical·vol)/cum(vol)`, **reset at 09:15 IST** (new IST day or backwards time-of-day step), **excludes the 09:00-09:15 pre-open auction volume** (caller passes `is_pre_open`; CLAUDE.md §7), **resets on contract roll** (engine-injected `session_key` change; ADR D11), **`None` during warm-up AND on the 1day timeframe** (`applies_to_1day=false` in the manifest — a session VWAP is degenerate with one bar/session, ADR D12) so the bit simply does not fire. The resolved `vwap_paisa` is fed into the snapshot exactly like EMA; the evaluator branch is `if let Some(vwap)` (`evaluator.rs`) / mirrored in the Python marshalling shim. **OVERFLOW (PR-2 risk #2): the Rust accumulators are `i128`** (price·volume over a session exceeds i64) snapped to i64 at read with truncating division == Python `//` on the unbounded-int twin (bit-identical). (b) **Pivot R5/S5 54/55** (`near_pivot_r5`/`near_pivot_s5`) — `PivotLevels` extended (both langs) with `r5 = PDH + 4·(P−PDL)`, `s5 = PDL − 4·(PDH−P)` (the same linear floor-trader ladder one rung past R4/S4; pure integer, deterministic; `PIVOT_LEVELS_LEN` 10→12, the levels APPENDED `[…,pdc,r5,s5]` never renumbered, `compute_pivot_levels` returns 9→11 entries `[r5,r4,r3,r2,r1,p,s1,s2,s3,s4,s5]`). The evaluator adds two `is_near` checks reusing the Group-2 pivot tolerance. **Fibonacci 3-anchor (NO new bits, the existing bits 19-29 work with any anchor — the anchor is a swept STRATEGY parameter per ADR D2/D4):** two new look-ahead-clean producers of the SAME 15-level `FibLevels` (`brutex/indicators/weekly_anchors.py`): `rolling_weekly_anchor` (trailing 5 completed sessions, max-High/min-Low) + `weekly_static_anchor` (last COMPLETED ISO week's High/Low, frozen for the current week). Cold-start (no prior 5 sessions / no completed prior week) → `None` → combo INELIGIBLE (ADR §4.5 #6, PR-4/5 enforce the gate). The Muhurat evening session is excluded AUTOMATICALLY — `is_trading_day(muhurat) is False`, so `find_prev_trading_day` never visits it (ADR §4.5 #7). **LOOK-AHEAD (ADR §4.5 #13, Property P-06):** both anchors read ONLY data strictly before today (same proof as `prev_day_ohlc`); `weekly_static_anchor` walks BACKWARDS so it never even enumerates a future-dated key. A dedicated index-based `LookAheadBarrier` property test (`tests/unit/test_weekly_anchors.py`) advances the cursor to today's ordinal and asserts `max_touched < today_index` for BOTH anchors, plus a sanity test proving the barrier instrumentation actually CATCHES a deliberate future read (not a vacuous proof). **What was HONESTLY DEFERRED — bits LEFT `implemented=false` (4):** **BOS/CHoCH 56-59** (`bos_bullish`/`bos_bearish`/`choch_bullish`/`choch_bearish`) — these require stateful fractal swing detection where a swing is only CONFIRMED k bars LATER, the single highest look-ahead-risk item in PR-2 (an index peek the timestamp guard would NOT catch). Rather than ship unproven look-ahead-clean math, they remain LAYOUT-ONLY (the evaluator emits 0, the golden `layout_only_bits_are_always_clear` test proves they are inert) and become a focused follow-up PR with a dedicated `LookAheadBarrier` fuzzing test PROVING no peek. This is an honest deferral, NOT a failure (CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #10). **Golden bit-identity (the TickVault contract):** the ABI grew — `evaluate_with_levels` + `evaluate_from_raw` both take `vwap_paisa: Option<i64>` (after `ema200_paisa`) + a 12-entry pivot list; the golden generator + the Rust golden reader (`golden_vectors.rs`) + the Python bit-identity test all thread it, and `tests/golden/fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json` + `tests/golden/condition_truth_table.csv` were regenerated so the both-ways coverage audit holds for all 56 implemented bits (52-55 now fire both ways; the generator snaps `close` onto R5/S5 + varies VWAP above/below close). **O(1) per-bar:** VWAP = two i128 adds + one divide (proven independent of session depth by a new `test_vwap_update_is_o1_in_session_bars` ratio bench); R5/S5 = two integer adds; weekly anchors recompute once/day (bounded). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ 4 bits (52-55) flipped `implemented=true` with real, tested, look-ahead-clean math; ✅ BOS/CHoCH (56-59) HONESTLY left `implemented=false` (deferred, not faked);
