1012. **DEC-NIFTY-BOS-CHOCH-001 — PR-2b of ADR-0012: the BOS/CHoCH market-structure conditions (bits 56-59) — the LAST data-independent indicator-vocab piece, flipped `implemented=true` with REAL, tested, look-ahead-PROVEN math** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope per ADR-0012 — NIFTY futures + the 3 spot indices; data-independent, synthetic fixtures only; NO scope/rate-cap change). **Why:** PR-2 (DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 #1011) HONESTLY DEFERRED bits 56-59 (`bos_bullish`/`bos_bearish`/`choch_bullish`/`choch_bearish`) because their stateful fractal swing detection is look-ahead-CRITICAL — a swing is only CONFIRMED k bars LATER, an index peek the timestamp guard would NOT catch (ADR §4.5 #13). PR-2b supplies that math AND a dedicated `LookAheadBarrier` P-06 proof, so the four bits can be flipped to `implemented=true` honestly (CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #10). **What shipped — all 4 bits flipped `implemented=true` (`IMPLEMENTED_MASK` is now `(1<<60)-1` = 1152921504606846975):** a NEW look-ahead-clean market-structure STATE object in BOTH the shared Rust `trading-core` (`rust/trading-core/src/indicators/market_structure.rs::MarketStructureState` + `MarketStructureSignal` + `Trend`) AND its bit-for-bit Python twin (`brutex/indicators/market_structure.py`). **The O(1) swing-state algorithm:** a fractal swing detector with a fixed `(2k+1)`-bar confirmation ring (default `k=2`, a 5-bar fractal). Per bar: (1) push (high, low) into the fixed-size ring (oldest dropped once full — O(1) memory, NOT a growing history); (2) when the ring is FULL, confirm its CENTRE bar (ring index `k`, a bar `k` steps in the PAST) as a swing high iff it is a strict local max over its `2k` neighbours / a swing low iff a strict local min — the current bar (ring index `2k`) is NEVER the centre, so its level is never confirmed early; (3) test the current `close` against the last CONFIRMED swing high/low → **BOS** (continuation: a break in the prevailing/none trend — close > last swing high in up/none trend, or close < last swing low in down/none trend) vs **CHoCH** (reversal: the FIRST break OPPOSITE the prevailing trend — close > last swing high while trend is DOWN flips up; close < last swing low while trend is UP flips down), then move the trend to match the break. State = a `2k+1` ring + last_swing_high/low + a Trend enum; each `update` is one ring write + an O(k)-with-k-CONSTANT local-extreme scan + a few comparisons = **O(1) per bar** (k is a fixed parameter, NOT the bar count). Up-side and down-side resolve from independent `if` blocks (a single engulfing-direction bar fires at most one of `{bos_bullish, choch_bullish}` and at most one of `{bos_bearish, choch_bearish}`; which one depends only on the entry trend). **LOOK-AHEAD PROOF (the crux — Property P-06):** the four booleans are RESOLVED upstream by the streaming state and threaded into the evaluator EXACTLY like the resolved `PriorBarHistory` flags (`evaluate_atoms` stays a pure, stateless bit-setter — the new ABI args `bos_bullish/bos_bearish/choch_bullish/choch_bearish` on `evaluate_with_levels` + `evaluate_from_raw`, the snapshot gains a `market_structure: MarketStructureSignal` field defaulted all-false so every pre-existing caller is unchanged). When evaluating bar N the state has consumed bars 0..=N in arrival order and the newest swing it can expose sits at index N−k (its confirmation needed bars N−k+1..=N, all ≤ N) — it NEVER references a swing whose confirmation needs a bar > N. A dedicated MANDATORY P-06 test (`tests/property/test_market_structure_lookahead.py`) routes EVERY bar read through `brutex/feed/lookahead.py::LookAheadBarrier` (the index-based enforcer) and asserts (a) across the whole stream `max_touched <= cursor` (no future-bar read), (b) any confirmed swing exposed at N corresponds to a bar at index ≤ N (read back through the barrier — a future index would raise), AND (c) a NON-VACUOUS control proving a driver that deliberately peeks bar N+1 DOES trip the barrier (so the proof is not green merely because the barrier is inert). **Golden bit-identity (the TickVault contract):** the ABI + the language-neutral oracle grew — `tests/golden/fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json` + `tests/golden/condition_truth_table.csv` were REGENERATED so the both-ways coverage audit now holds for ALL 60 implemented bits (the generator fires each of the four resolved flags ~25% of the time → each of 56-59 is set in ≥1 case AND clear in ≥1 case); the Rust golden reader (`golden_vectors.rs`), the Python bit-identity test, the parity script, and the proptests all thread the four flags, and the Rust independent-oracle proptest sets bits 56-59 from a freshly-generated `MarketStructureSignal` (cargo-mutants kill). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ all 4 bits (56-59) flipped `implemented=true` with real, tested, look-ahead-PROVEN math — the deferral of #1011 is CLOSED; ✅ the indicator vocab (bits 0-59) is now COMPLETE — this was the last data-independent piece; ✅ no operator screenshot pins BOS/CHoCH — their goldens are CODE-ANCHORED (the exact computed output), stated honestly; ✅ Rust golden bit-identity (400 cases) + `cargo fmt --check` + clippy `-D warnings` + cargo test all green; ✅ touched Python modules at 100% line+branch in the whole-package coverage gate; ✅ the streaming state is NOT yet wired into the engine's per-bar loop (the snapshot field defaults all-false) — that wiring is PR-3/PR-4's job (futures roll + the 3 strategies), so this PR is purely the data-independent indicator + its proof, no engine behaviour change. **Files:** `rust/trading-core/conditions.toml` (flip 56-59), `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/{market_structure.rs (new),mod.rs}`, `rust/trading-core/src/{evaluator.rs,python.rs,lib.rs,bits.rs (regenerated)}`, `rust/trading-core/tests/{golden_vectors.rs,proptests.rs}`, `brutex/indicators/{market_structure.py (new),__init__.py}`, `brutex/vocabulary/{evaluator.py,bits.py (regenerated)}`, `scripts/{gen_vocab_golden_vectors.py,check_vocab_rust_parity.py}`, `tests/golden/fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json`, `tests/golden/condition_truth_table.csv`, `tests/golden/{test_vocab_golden.py,test_vocab_python_rust_bit_identity.py}`, `tests/integration/test_python_rust_parity.py`, `tests/unit/{test_market_structure.py (new),test_vocabulary_boundaries.py}`, `tests/property/test_market_structure_lookahead.py (new)`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-NIFTY-BOS-CHOCH-001. **Builds on** DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 (#1011 — PR-2, which deferred these bits), DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 (#1010 — PR-1 bit layout), DEC-NIFTY-DYNAMIC-STRATEGY-001 (#1006 — ADR-0012), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441 — the shared trading-core crate), DEC-LOOKAHEAD-BARRIER-001 (the P-06 LookAheadBarrier). (Ledger: #1012 = max-existing(1011)+1.)

1022. **DEC-RATE-WIDGET-FNO-HONEST-001 — the live PULL RATE widget's "achieved r/s" is now HONEST during the metadata + F&O phases: no fabricated completed-rate, and the stall verdict is no longer blind to an issued-but-failing pull** (2026-06-30; READ-ONLY dashboard observability — NO pacing/lake-schema/stored-bar/rate-cap/vocab/engine change; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). **Why (confirmed by deep log+code audit):** the SPOT phase feeds the widget the transport `CallMeter`'s MEASURED completed-rate (`effective_rps`), but the metadata + long F&O phases have NO rate-observe seam, so DEC-PULL-RATE-WIDGET-VISIBILITY-001 (#1000) added `RatePanelSampler` to keep the widget LIVE by periodically pushing the SHARED `RateController`. That sampler, however, SYNTHESIZED `meter_snapshot = {"effective_rps": recent_minute / 60}` — the controller's ADMISSION count ÷ 60 — and poured it into the panel's "achieved" (measured-completed) slot. Two defects followed: (a) it OVER-reported vs the true completed rate (admissions ≥ completions — the log showed 204/min ADMITTED surfaced as 3.4 r/s "achieved" while the real completed rate was ~169/min ≈ 2.82 r/s), and (b) it BLINDED the `stalled` verdict (`build_pull_rate_view`'s `stalled = effective_rps <= floor`): with a fabricated achieved derived from admissions, an issued-but-ALL-FAILING pull (the controller busily admitting, NOTHING completing) would read "flowing 3 r/s" — a fake-alive illusion (Golden Rule #1). **Fix chosen — the HONEST MINIMUM (option 3), because the F&O `CallMeter` is genuinely UNREACHABLE from the sampler seam:** the F&O meter is created fresh inside `build_live_pool` → `_build_live_client` (the `# pragma: no cover` live-network client factory invoked deep in `run_groww_option_ingest`); the `SessionRateController` holds ONLY the `RateController`, never that meter, so option 2 (plumb the real measured meter) would require threading a publish callback through the 4-layer pragma-no-cover F&O spine — not feasible cleanly. So the sampler STOPS fabricating a completed-rate and instead pushes an explicit `meter_present=False` sentinel; `build_pull_rate_view` gains a `meter_present` parameter (default `True` — the spot/meter-fed + CLI-bridge contract is byte-unchanged) that splits the verdict: **(spot, `meter_present=True`)** reads the MEASURED `effective_rps` (so an issued-but-failing pull whose completed-rate sits at/below the floor reads STALLED — the fake-alive case is now CAUGHT, because the sampler no longer masks it); **(metadata/F&O, `meter_present=False`)** keeps `req_per_sec_achieved` an HONEST 0 (no measured completed-rate this phase) and falls back to the controller's ADMISSION signal (`recent_minute == 0` ⇒ stalled/idle, any admissions ⇒ flowing). The admission per-minute average (`recent_minute / 60`) is surfaced in a NEW, distinctly-labelled `req_per_min_rate` field (the bx-rate-monitor.js expanded overlay shows it as "req/min rate · admission avg (issued ÷ 60)", explicitly NOT a measured completed rate), never the "achieved" slot. The `RateLimitPanel` gains a `meter_present` flag (default `True`), threaded through `update_throughput` ← `make_rate_observer` (a real spot `CallMeter` snapshot carries no `meter_present` key → defaults `True`; the sampler's `{"meter_present": False}` flips it) → the `/api/v1/pull/rate` route (`panel_meter_present` into `build_pull_rate_view_merged`; the CLI bridge stays `bridge_meter_present=True` since `brutex fetch` publishes a real meter rate). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ READ-ONLY — touches no pacing decision, fetch rate byte-unchanged; ✅ the widget stays LIVE in F&O (the #1000 visibility win is preserved) but now tells the TRUTH — "achieved" is the measured completed rate where a meter exists and an honest 0 (with a separate admission average) where it does not, never a fabricated middle figure; ✅ the F&O phase can detect an IDLE pull (no admissions) but NOT an issued-but-all-failing one (no reachable completed-rate this phase — that detection requires publishing the F&O meter, an explicit FOLLOW-UP, NOT claimed); ✅ the SPOT phase DOES catch issued-but-failing now (the regression test pins it). **Tests:** `test_pull_rate_view.py` — (i) spot achieved = measured completed-rate (2.82, NOT the 3.4 admission over-report) with the admission avg in `req_per_min_rate`; the F&O side reads an honest 0 achieved + flowing; (ii) the fake-alive regression: spot + admissions-high + completed-rate-0 → STALLED (the verdict no longer fooled by 300 admissions); (iii) F&O + zero admissions → STALLED, and an idle panel zeroes `req_per_min_rate`; plus the merged-bridge threading. `test_dashboard_rate_sampler.py` — the sampler pushes `{"meter_present": False}` + NO fabricated `effective_rps`, independent of `recent_minute`. `test_dashboard_rate_panel.py` — panel default + `update_throughput` flag + observer sentinel mapping. `test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py` — the end-to-end "bug pinned" test re-asserted for the honest behaviour (route stays flowing, achieved 0, `req_per_min_rate` = the admission avg) + a NEW zero-admissions-in-F&O → stalled route test. **Coverage:** `pull_rate_view.py` + `rate_sampler.py` BOTH 100% line+branch; the touched `app.py` lines all covered; ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_rate_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/rate_sampler.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-rate-monitor.js`, `tests/unit/{test_pull_rate_view.py,test_dashboard_rate_sampler.py,test_dashboard_rate_panel.py}`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py`, `CLAUDE.md` §3, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-RATE-WIDGET-FNO-HONEST-001. **Builds on** DEC-PULL-RATE-WIDGET-VISIBILITY-001 (#1000 — the sampler that kept the widget live but fabricated the rate), DEC-RATE-MONITOR-EXPAND-001 (#1004 — the expanded trustworthy view), DEC-LIVE-RATE-MONITOR-001 (#995 — the pull-rate view + stall verdict), DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 (the cross-process merge). (Ledger: #1022 = the next free unique number above main's max-existing(1017) after merging origin/main — renumbered from the originally-claimed #1015, which collided with DEC-RESAMPLER-MONOTONIC-GUARD-001 #1015 that landed on main via PR #985; deliberately distinct from the in-flight siblings #1016 (PR #979) / #1018-#1019 (PR #983) / #1020 (PR #984) / #1021 (PR #986, this PR).)
1029. **DEC-ADVERSARIAL-HARDENING-001 — four verified-real robustness/contract gaps an adversarial verification sweep found are now closed, each pinned by a test that executes the real path (reproduces the extreme input → fails/crashes pre-fix, passes post-fix)** (2026-06-30; renumbered #1023 → #1029 at re-sync onto current main, which had taken #1023 (DEC-LAKE-WRITE-VECTORIZE-001) through #1028. NO real-data exposure — these are contract/robustness gaps, not live-data corruptions; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema change; the 400-case golden bit-identity + `ema_golden` + `spec_signal_golden` all stay byte-identical/green). **FIX 1 (MAJOR) — `VwapState` FFI overflow → uncatchable SIGABRT:** `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs` `PyVwapState::update` delegated to the native `VwapState` with NO magnitude guard, so a few near-`i64::MAX` `typical_paisa × volume` products overflowed the native `cum_pv` `i128` accumulator (`vwap.rs:118`) → under the release `panic = "abort"` the process ABORTED (exit 134), uncatchable by try/except — while EVERY sibling FFI entry (`evaluate_*`, `compute_pivot`/`fib`, `MarketStructureState`'s k<1 guard) already clamps to `MAX_BAR_PAISA` and raises a catchable `ValueError`. FIX: `PyVwapState::update` now validates BOTH i64s that feed the i128 accumulation (`typical_paisa`, `volume`) against the EXISTING `MAX_BAR_PAISA` (= `i64::MAX / 65536`, `python.rs:119`) via the SAME `bar_in_range` helper BEFORE delegating, raising a catchable `ValueError` naming the offending field; the native arithmetic is UNTOUCHED (golden bit-identity intact). Pinned by `test_python_rust_parity.py::TestFfiOverflowGuards` (the previously-aborting input now raises cleanly, naming `typical_paisa` / `volume`; a real bar is byte-unchanged) + a native `vwap.rs` `#[should_panic]` documenting the unguarded overflow the FFI guard prevents. **FIX 2 (MINOR) — futures roll mis-shifted an out-of-coverage-year expiry:** `brutex/data/futures_roll.py` `holiday_shifted_expiry` used the UNGUARDED `nse.is_trading_day` (returns True for any out-of-coverage non-weekend date), while the sibling PDH/PDL anchor path uses the strict `is_trading_day_checked`. FIX: route the trading-day check through `is_trading_day_checked`, so an out-of-coverage year (2027+) WEEKDAY raises `HolidayDataUnavailableError` instead of silently returning an unshifted expiry on a possibly-closed day; in-coverage (2021-2026) behaviour is byte-identical. Pinned by `test_futures_roll.py::test_holiday_shift_refuses_out_of_coverage_weekday` (Republic Day 2027-01-26 now RAISES; the 2023-01-26→01-25 in-coverage shift unchanged). **FIX 3 (MINOR) — negative OHLC price silently stored:** `brutex/data/candle_fields.py` `has_no_price()` rejected absent/zero but NOT negative, and the `high = max` / `low = min` clamp HID a negative price → a `-5` open was silently stored. FIX: extend `has_no_price()` to treat a NEGATIVE price like zero (`Decimal(...) <= 0`) — a traded Indian price is never ≤ 0 — so a partial-negative bar is gracefully skipped as `EmptyCandleRow` and an all-negative bar maps to the all-empty skip, symmetric with the zero guard; all valid-price behaviour byte-identical. The fix is at the ONE COMMON `has_no_price` boundary used by both the all-empty and partial guards in `assemble_candle`, so the production `parse_candle_rows` path inherits it. Pinned by `test_candle_fields.py` (negative cases in `TestHasNoPrice` + `test_partial_negative_price_is_skipped` + `test_negative_open_does_not_clobber_low_negative` + `test_all_negative_prices_is_empty_candle_row`) AND `test_groww_parser.py::test_partial_negative_price_row_is_skipped` (the real parse path). **FIX 4 (NIT) — `compute_ema` seed-sum overflow → non-finite EMA:** `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/ema.rs` guarded finiteness on the INPUT close but not the computed SMA seed; two finite-but-huge closes (1e308) overflowed `seed_sum` to +inf → returned a poisoning inf EMA for all subsequent bars. FIX: re-check finiteness on the COMPUTED seed at the seed bar (the ONLY overflow site — the post-seed step is a convex combination of finite operands and provably cannot overflow, documented inline, so NO step guard is added — it would be untestable dead code); a non-finite seed returns the module's existing `Err` contract (→ `ValueError` at the FFI). Real-magnitude inputs are unaffected (golden bit-identity intact). Pinned by `ema.rs::finite_but_huge_seed_overflow_is_rejected_not_inf` + `post_seed_step_stays_finite_for_extreme_finite_inputs` + `real_magnitude_series_unaffected_by_overflow_guards` and `test_python_rust_parity.py` (`compute_ema([1e308,1e308], 2)` now raises; a normal series byte-identical). **GATES:** `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --features python --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo test` (incl. the 400-case `golden_vectors`, `ema_golden`, `spec_signal_golden` — all byte-identical/green) + `scripts/codegen_vocab.py --check` clean; `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean on touched `brutex/` files; `candle_fields.py` 100% line+branch (47/12), `futures_roll.py` 100% line+branch (33/4); 8825 broad-suite tests green, no regressions.
1016. **DEC-PULL-HEALTH-CLI-WIRING-001 — BIND the live pull-health monitor to the CLI `brutex fetch` pull path, so a CLI pull self-instruments its health (Prometheus gauges + the `pull_degraded` Telegram alert) exactly like the dashboard pull** (2026-06-30; the CLI twin of DEC-PULL-HEALTH-WIRING-001 #935; the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3 — NO scope/vocab/rate change). **Why (the flagged FAST-FOLLOW):** DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001 (#932) shipped the `PullHealthMonitor` + the `_observe_rate(..., monitor=...)` seam; DEC-PULL-HEALTH-WIRING-001 (#935) then BOUND it at the DASHBOARD live-pull build site — but its honest envelope explicitly stated "wires the DASHBOARD pull path… the CLI `brutex fetch` path has no `_observe_rate` seam, so a CLI monitor is a SEPARATE follow-up, NOT claimed." So an overnight `brutex fetch` pull (the primary unattended pull entrypoint, CLAUDE.md §11 AUTOMATED) ran UNWATCHED: a degraded/stalled CLI pull produced no `pull_degraded` alert + no `/metrics` health gauges. This closes that gap. **What shipped (COMMON, best-effort, observe-only — NO new tick / thread / cadence / pacing change):** the investigation found the CLI ALREADY HAS a per-window observe seam — `cli._make_cli_rate_bridge_on_window` (DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 #997), which on each processed window snapshots the SAME `RateController.snapshot()` + transport `CallMeter.snapshot()` the dashboard mirrors (to publish the cross-process rate bridge). So NO new seam / refactor was needed: (1) `_make_cli_rate_bridge_on_window` gains an OPTIONAL `monitor` param; when wired it feeds the SAME snapshot pair the bridge already built to `PullHealthMonitor.observe(...)`, AFTER the bridge publish, under its OWN best-effort `try/except` (a publish error never starves the watch; a monitor error never crashes the pull — `observe` is itself best-effort and never raises). If the publish failed BEFORE the controller snapshot was taken (`controller_snap is None`), the monitor branch re-snapshots the controller under its guard so the watch never starves. (2) `cmd_fetch` BINDS the monitor via the SHARED COMMON builder `pull_controller._build_pull_health_monitor(rate_controller)` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — NO copy-paste of the `MetricRegistry` / `SweepAlerter.pull_degraded` / `resolve_pool_size()` wiring; the EXACT builder the dashboard uses) and threads it into the seam. The builder returns `None` for a `--dry-run` / `--inspect` pull (no `rate_controller`) and swallows any construction error → `None`, so binding can NEVER block/slow/crash the pull (Golden Rule #10); a `None` monitor makes the observe a no-op. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the monitor's thresholds are operator-tunable HEURISTICS, NOT vendor-verified limits; a breach is an OBSERVATION + alert, NOT auto-remediation — the pull continues unchanged whether or not the monitor fires; ✅ observe-only — reads the controller/meter snapshots + writes the panel/metrics/alert; touches NO pacing (fetch rate byte-unchanged); ✅ the `cmd_fetch` LIVE pull branch is `# pragma: no cover` (needs a real TOTP token + the Groww SDK — network-blocked in CI), so the dry-run path covers the build line (returns `None` → seam unwrapped) and the `_make_cli_rate_bridge_on_window` `monitor` branch is exercised directly (incl. an END-TO-END breach → exactly one `pull_degraded` edge through the REAL `PullHealthMonitor`). **Files:** `brutex/cli.py` (`_make_cli_rate_bridge_on_window` gains `monitor`, `cmd_fetch` binds + threads it; `Mapping` import), `tests/unit/test_cli_retry_storm.py` (5 new tests: monitor-fed / `None`-no-op / re-snapshot-after-publish-failure / observe-error-swallowed / end-to-end-one-`pull_degraded`-breach), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-HEALTH-CLI-WIRING-001. **Builds on** DEC-PULL-HEALTH-WIRING-001 (#935 — the dashboard binding + the flagged CLI follow-up), DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001 (#932 — the monitor + the observe seam), DEC-CLI-RATE-BRIDGE-001 (#997 — the per-window CLI rate-observe seam this reuses). ## DEC-EMPTY-DETECTOR-PRODUCTION-WIRING-001 (2026-06-30)

1017. **DEC-EMPTY-DETECTOR-PRODUCTION-WIRING-001 — the whole-underlying "silent-empty / silent-vanish" detector (DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 #919) is WAKED in the real production F&O pull: it was DEAD in every live pull because its only call site is gated `if fetch_pipeline is None:` and the production pull ALWAYS wires a non-None pipeline. A COMMON guarded helper now runs the scan POST-DRAIN over the reconciled per-pair counts, so the BAJAJ-AUTO/M&M failure mode is catchable in production again** (2026-06-30; OBSERVE-ONLY — no return/ledger/engine change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why (proven file:line from the pull-verification report issue #4):** DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 #919 added `scan_underlying_all_empty` + `_log_underlying_all_empty` — a pull-side diagnostic that emits ONE `pull.underlying_all_empty` WARNING when a whole F&O underlying's every cleanly-fetched contract comes back 100% EMPTY (the silent-vanish a lake scan cannot distinguish from never-pulled). But its SOLE call site in `run_groww_option_ingest` was gated `if fetch_pipeline is None:` (the in-async-mode skip of DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 MAJOR-3 — correct, because a producer-resolved per-pair `IngestReport` reads `bars_appended == 0` BEFORE the background consumer folds the real counts, so an in-driver scan would flood a false all-empty for the whole universe). The production F&O pull (`dashboard/historical_pull.py::pull_contract_candles` → `build_fetch_pipeline`, default-ON) ALWAYS builds a non-None `fetch_pipeline`, so the detector NEVER ran on a real pull — the exact failure mode it was built to catch was uncatchable in production, and the stale in-code comment "the option path is not wired to the pipeline in production yet" was false. **What shipped (COMMON · OBSERVE-ONLY · best-effort):** (1) NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py::emit_underlying_all_empty(pairs, contract_list, *, pull_id=None)` — the ONE source of truth (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) for the diagnostic's guarded scan→log: it runs `scan_underlying_all_empty` then `_log_underlying_all_empty`, the whole thing wrapped in the SAME `try/except` that logs `pull.underlying_all_empty_error` and returns so the observe-only diagnostic can NEVER break the pull; `pull_id` defaults to `current_pull_id()` (the production pull runs inside a `pull_id_scope`). The in-driver synchronous call site is REFACTORED onto this helper (byte-identical behaviour — the in-async skip is preserved). (2) `dashboard/historical_pull.py::pull_contract_candles` calls `emit_underlying_all_empty(minute.merged_pairs, [contract for _row, contract in rebuilt])` immediately AFTER `_reconcile_phase_with_pipeline` (the only point the real durable per-pair `bars_appended` exist — the drain has folded the consumer totals back into `merged_pairs`), GUARDED by `if fetch_pipeline is not None:` so it runs ONLY for the pipeline path (the synchronous `fetch_pipeline is None` path already emitted in-driver — a second emit would double-warn). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ pure DETECT+WARN — no return/ledger/engine change, no auto-recovery; ✅ the false-positive guards of #919 are reused verbatim (`_is_clean_fetch` excludes ledger-skip / transient-residual / empty-clamp, and `_ALL_EMPTY_MIN_CONTRACTS=3` so a 1-2-leg illiquid name never flags); ✅ best-effort — a scan error logs `pull.underlying_all_empty_error` and is swallowed, never blocking/slowing/crashing the pull; ✅ runs once POST-DRAIN per pull (NOT per-window) — O(pairs), not a hot path; ✅ F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY — ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py` — 4 NEW `emit_underlying_all_empty` unit tests (warns-on-silent-vanish / silent-when-clean / scan-error-guarded / defaults-pull_id-from-scope); the prior in-driver `TestSuspiciousEmptyFlag` suite (incl. the async-mode-skip regression) stays GREEN. `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py` — NEW `test_silent_vanish_underlying_warns_in_production_pipeline_pull`: a LIVE (`dry_run=False`, pipeline default-ON) `pull_contract_candles` over a NIFTY chain whose every contract fetches CLEANLY EMPTY now emits EXACTLY ONE `pull.underlying_all_empty` naming NIFTY (`attempted_pairs=3 stored_bars=0`), fired POST-DRAIN over the reconciled counts — the regression PROVING the detector is alive in production. `option_ingest.py` + `historical_pull.py` stay 100% line+branch in the whole-package coverage gate; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` (new `emit_underlying_all_empty` + in-driver refactor + `__all__`), `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` (post-drain call + import), `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `CLAUDE.md` §1, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-EMPTY-DETECTOR-PRODUCTION-WIRING-001. **Builds on** DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 (#919 — the detector this wakes), DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 (the async pipeline whose deferred per-pair counts forced the post-drain placement), DEC-FNO-ASYNC-PIPELINE-WIRE-001 (`_reconcile_phase_with_pipeline`, the post-drain reconcile this hooks). (Ledger: #1017 — the next free number above main's max-existing #1012; #1013 is held by the sibling PR DEC-PULL-HEALTH-CLI-WIRING-001, so #1014 stays unique regardless of merge order.)
## DEC-EMA-RUST-PORT-001 (2026-06-30)

1014. **DEC-EMA-RUST-PORT-001 — PR-2c of the shared-core arc: the EMA 20/200 recurrence is PORTED from pure Python into the shared Rust `trading-core` crate, BIT-IDENTICAL, completing the all-Rust shared evaluate-time indicator core** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; data-independent; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why:** EMA was the LAST shared evaluate-time indicator still computed in Python — pivots + Fib already delegate to Rust (DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 #441), and PR-2/PR-2b (#1011/#1012) put VWAP + pivot R5/S5 + market-structure in Rust, but the EMA recurrence lived only in `brutex/indicators/ema.py`. Moving the RECURRENCE into the crate makes the COMMON indicator core fully Rust, so the backtested EMA equals the (future) live TickVault EMA **by construction** (one source of truth, not two copies kept identical) — the same delegating-shim pattern as `pivots.py`/`fib_levels.py`. **What shipped:** a NEW `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/ema.rs` with `EmaState` (streaming) + `compute_ema` (batch) + the three single-source helpers `ema_alpha`/`ema_seed`/`ema_step`, wired into `indicators/mod.rs` + `lib.rs` + the PyO3 surface (`python.rs` → `trading_core.compute_ema`/`ema_alpha`/`ema_seed`/`ema_step`, exported from the `trading_core` package `__init__.py`), mirroring `compute_pivot_levels`/`compute_fib_levels`. `brutex/indicators/ema.py` is now a **thin delegating shim** — the streaming `EMAState` keeps its identical public API + branch/state shell + checkpoint serialization (`to_dict`/`from_dict`/`reset`), but every arithmetic site (`alpha`, the SMA seed, the per-bar step) delegates to Rust; `compute_ema`/`latest_ema` call `trading_core.compute_ema`. The Python public API is BYTE-UNCHANGED so no caller breaks. **The recurrence ported (exactly, mirrored token-for-token):** `α = 2/(N+1)` (int→float division), warm-up bars `0..N-2` → `None`, seed bar `N-1` → `EMA = SMA(values[0..N-1]) = seed_sum/N`, subsequent bars `t ≥ N` → `EMA_t = α·close_t + (1−α)·EMA_(t−1)`, the degenerate `N==1` identity, and the `math.isfinite` finite-close guard (Rust `f64::is_finite` → `Err`/`ValueError`). **Bit-identity (the only subtlety — pure IEEE-754 f64, NO paisa rounding):** unlike pivots/Fib (integer paisa + banker's-rounded f64), the EMA runs ENTIRELY in `f64` and the result STAYS `f64` — the caller (`brutex.engine.stage1a._ema_to_paisa` / TickVault) snaps to paisa SEPARATELY, so there is NO `round_money`/`ROUND_HALF_UP` step inside the recurrence to reproduce. IEEE-754 double arithmetic with the same operation order is deterministic and identical across Python and Rust, so the two produce byte-identical `f64` values. **PROVEN bit-for-bit (0 mismatches):** (a) a NEW Rust cross-language golden `rust/trading-core/tests/ema_golden.rs` reads the SAME language-neutral `tests/golden/fixtures/indicators_golden.json` `ema` section the Python golden (`tests/golden/test_indicators_golden.py`) reads and asserts `compute_ema` reproduces every frozen series bit-for-bit (warm-up `null` prefix included); (b) a side-by-side run of the freshly-built Rust wheel vs the pre-change origin/main Python recurrence over EMA20 + EMA200 streams (ramp / noisy / flat, warm-up + steady) — 1450 points, **0 mismatches**; the fixture's frozen `ema` expected values were re-confirmed to equal the OLD `ema.py` output (0 mismatches). **README** `rust/trading-core/README.md` flipped EMA 🚫→✅ (the indicator-core "what's here" + the done/not-done list). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ EMA recurrence Python→Rust, bit-identical (0-mismatch proof pasted in the PR), Python public API unchanged (delegating shim, all callers work); ✅ `cargo fmt --check` 0 + `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` 0 warnings + `cargo test` green (incl. the ema_golden bit-identity); ✅ whole-package `pytest --cov=brutex --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` 100% line+branch; ✅ `tests/golden`/`tests/smoke`/`tests/redteam` green; ✅ `codegen_vocab --check` 0 + ledger-numbering 0 + ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict` clean; ✅ this completes the all-Rust shared indicator core — EMA now deploys NATIVELY into TickVault (no Python EMA in the shared path); ✅ NO engine behaviour change (the resolved paisa EMA the evaluator consumes is byte-identical; the f64→paisa snap is unchanged + still in the Python caller). **Files:** `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/ema.rs (new)`, `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/mod.rs`, `rust/trading-core/src/lib.rs`, `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs`, `rust/trading-core/python/trading_core/__init__.py`, `rust/trading-core/tests/ema_golden.rs (new)`, `rust/trading-core/README.md`, `brutex/indicators/ema.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-EMA-RUST-PORT-001. **Builds on** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441 — the shared trading-core crate + the pivots/Fib delegating-shim pattern), DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 (#1011 — PR-2, VWAP/R5/S5 in Rust). (Ledger: #1014 = max-existing(1013)+1; renumbered from #1013 to avoid a parallel-branch collision with DEC-NIFTY-ROLL-METADATA / PR-3.)
1013. **DEC-NIFTY-ROLL-METADATA-001 — PR-3 of ADR-0012: the near-month NIFTY-futures contract ROLL resolver + per-bar / per-trade METADATA stamping (date / weekday / minute-of-session / contract-expiry / is-expiry-day) + the D13 data-integrity predicates (no-forward-fill gap detection, circuit-halt flag, forced-exit on the last real bar ≤ 15:20) — with the EVAL-PATH derivation + roll DECISION in shared Rust `trading-core` (TickVault-native)** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope per ADR-0012 — NIFTY futures + the 3 spot indices; data-INDEPENDENT, synthetic-fixture / calendar-driven only; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why:** ADR-0012 D11 mandates a PER-CONTRACT futures series (NOT a back-adjusted continuous contract — back-adjustment shifts every absolute price level and would corrupt pivots / Fibonacci / VWAP), D8 mandates the per-bar metadata stamp that makes the time-of-day × combo expectancy map (D6) + the expiry-day analysis possible, and D13 locks the gap / halt / forced-exit policy. PR-3 implements the roll + metadata LAYER (NOT the strategies/sweep — those are PR-4/PR-5). **OPERATOR DIRECTIVE (the redirect):** the COMMON evaluation path must be RUST in `trading-core` so TickVault consumes it natively and a strategy deploys directly to live — so the eval-path metadata DERIVATION + the near-month roll DECISION live in the shared Rust crate, NOT Python. **INVESTIGATION — how the merged Rust evaluator gets time-of-day / day-type today:** the evaluator (`rust/trading-core/src/evaluator.rs::evaluate_atoms`) reads a PRECOMPUTED `tod_seconds: u32` (IST seconds-since-midnight) field on `IndicatorSnapshot` for the Group-8 time-of-day bits (44-47); it does NOT take a raw timestamp. The DERIVATION (IST timestamp → `tod_seconds`) lived in Python (`brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py`: `ts.hour*3600 + ts.minute*60 + ts.second`). The Group-9 "day type" bits (48-51) are PRICE-based (gap-up/down, inside/outside day), NOT date-based — so weekday + is-expiry-day are NOT vocab-bit inputs; they are the D6/expiry-day AUDIT metadata. **What shipped — NEW shared Rust core + thin Python shims:** (1) **`rust/trading-core/src/indicators/metadata.rs` (NEW, the eval-path derivation in RUST, exposed via PyO3):** `derive_bar_metadata(day_ordinal, hour, minute, second, session_open_seconds, expiry_ordinal) -> (tod_seconds, weekday, minute_of_session, is_expiry_day)` + the primitives `weekday_from_ordinal` (proleptic-Gregorian, `(ordinal-1) rem_euclid 7`, == Python `date.weekday()`), `minute_of_session` (Euclidean floor-div, pre-open → NEGATIVE honest not clamped), and `resolve_near_month(entry_ordinal, candidate_shifted_ordinal, next_month_shifted_ordinal) -> i64` (the at-or-after near-month DECISION: candidate iff ≥ entry — INCLUDING on the expiry date itself, where the intraday trade stays on the expiring contract + force-exits 15:20 with no overnight roll; else the holiday-shift gap-day rolls to next month). Dependency-FREE (no chrono — the lake already localizes to IST, a FIXED +05:30 no-DST offset, so the caller passes IST CIVIL components + proleptic-Gregorian ordinals; TickVault's native link stays dependency-free, mirroring the evaluator/indicators). Re-exported from `lib.rs`; the four PyO3 wrappers added to `python.rs` + the `trading_core` `__init__.py` + `__all__` (and the `brutex/math` facade frozen surface). (2) **`brutex/data/futures_roll.py` (thin delegating WRAPPER):** computes the CANDIDATE + next-month holiday-shifted expiries from the BruteX-resident NSE calendar (the holiday list + `find_prev_trading_day` + `next_monthly_expiry` are DATA, stay Python) and hands their day-ordinals to `trading_core.resolve_near_month` — the DECISION is the shared Rust core, byte-identical to the TickVault-native live path. `FuturesContract.series_key` = `"<UNDERLYING>-FUT-<expiry ISO>"` is the engine roll-reset `session_key` (NO cross-roll level compare; D11). HOLIDAY-SHIFT REAL-CALENDAR-VERIFIED on Jan-2023 (last-Thu = Republic-Day → Wed 2023-01-25) + Mar-2023 (Ram-Navami → Wed 2023-03-29). (3) **`brutex/feed/bar_metadata.py` (thin delegating SHIM):** `stamp_bar` localizes to IST + resolves the session open from the shared `get_session` (BruteX data), then delegates the full derivation (tod_seconds / weekday / minute-of-session / is-expiry-day) to `trading_core.derive_bar_metadata`; `minute_of_session` delegates to `trading_core.minute_of_session`. The frozen `BarMetadata` dataclass + `as_audit_payload()` (JSON for the EXISTING hash-chained `AuditWriter`, CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 8) + the D13 predicates `missing_minute_bars` (ABSENT instants, matched by instant across tz, sorted — NEVER forward-fill) + `last_real_bar_at_or_before_forced_exit` (latest REAL bar whose window does not pass 15:20 IST, reusing `is_forced_exit_bar`, 1-minute base clock, coarse-TF aware) + the carried `circuit_halt` flag stay Python (calendar-driven set logic, not a per-bar numeric kernel). **RUST-vs-PYTHON split (the directive, documented in both module docstrings + `metadata.rs`):** RUST `trading-core` (TickVault-native, the COMMON eval path) = the eval-path metadata DERIVATION (tod_seconds/weekday/minute-of-session/is-expiry-day) + the near-month roll DECISION. PYTHON (BruteX-only) = the NSE holiday list + prior-trading-day walk + monthly-expiry calendar (DATA that parameterises the Rust decision), the IST localization + session-open lookup, the D13 gap/forced-exit predicates, and the pull-time bulk stamping loop that CALLS the Rust derivation per bar (orchestration). NO vocab/bits change (`codegen_vocab.py --check` exit 0; `IMPLEMENTED_MASK`/`TOTAL_CONDITIONS` untouched — this PR adds NO conditions). **BIT-IDENTITY (the TickVault contract):** a NEW `tests/unit/test_metadata_rust_derivation.py` proves the Rust derivation is BYTE-IDENTICAL to an INDEPENDENT pure-Python stdlib reference (NOT a call back into the shim) over a broad date × time × expiry hypothesis domain — weekday vs `date.weekday()`, minute-of-session vs Python floor `//`, the full `derive_bar_metadata` tuple, and the `resolve_near_month` decision. The Rust core ALSO carries its own unit + proptest layer in `metadata.rs` (weekday range/advance, minute monotonicity, is-expiry-day iff, near-month candidate-iff-not-expired). **Edge cases TESTED (synthetic fixtures / real calendar):** expiry-day-itself (stays on expiring contract), the roll boundary (distinct `series_key` proves no cross-roll compare), the day-after-expiry roll, a Muhurat session (minute-of-session anchored at the actual ~18:00 open), the first-session cold-start (negative pre-open minute surfaced), a missing-15:20-bar session (forced-exit falls back to the last real bar ≤ 15:20), a circuit-halt session (flag carried), weekday/minute correctness across DST-free IST (UTC-expressed bar localizes correctly), an expiry on a holiday verified against the NSE calendar (Jan/Mar 2023, NSE rolls to the prev trading day), and the cross-language bit-identity above. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the eval-path derivation + the near-month roll DECISION are now in the shared Rust `trading-core` crate (TickVault-native), with thin Python delegating shims — the directive's redirect is DONE, stated as the explicit split; ✅ pull-time bulk stamping orchestration stays Python (it CALLS the Rust derivation per bar); ✅ 100% line+branch on BOTH Python shims (`futures_roll.py`, `bar_metadata.py`) in the whole-package gate + the new Rust `metadata` module covered by its `cargo test` unit + proptest; ✅ synthetic-fixture / calendar tests prove the LOGIC — the real-data run is on the operator's MacBook (this environment is data-INDEPENDENT), NOT claimed here; ✅ holiday-shift REAL-CALENDAR-VERIFIED, not hallucinated; ✅ no engine wiring yet — the stamp + roll are the data-independent LAYER (the `BarMetadata`/`FuturesContract` are the seam PR-4 consumes); ✅ NO scope/vocab/rate change (ENGINE stays NIFTY-futures + the 3 spot indices per ADR-0012); ✅ `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` + `cargo test` (golden 400-case bit-identity intact) all green; ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file; `codegen_vocab.py --check` + the ledger validator exit 0; the golden `tests/math_facade` frozen surface updated for the 4 new re-exports (the reviewed surface-change path the test anticipates). **Files:** `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/metadata.rs` (new), `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/mod.rs`, `rust/trading-core/src/lib.rs`, `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs`, `rust/trading-core/python/trading_core/__init__.py`, `brutex/data/futures_roll.py` (thin Rust-delegating wrapper), `brutex/feed/bar_metadata.py` (thin Rust-delegating shim), `tests/unit/test_futures_roll.py`, `tests/unit/test_bar_metadata.py`, `tests/unit/test_metadata_rust_derivation.py` (new — cross-language bit-identity), `tests/golden/test_math_facade_golden.py` (frozen surface +4), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-NIFTY-ROLL-METADATA-001. **Builds on** DEC-NIFTY-DYNAMIC-STRATEGY-001 (#1006 — ADR-0012 D8/D11/D13 + §4.5 rows 1/2/3/8/9/10), DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 (#1011 — PR-2 indicators, whose VWAP `session_key` reset this roll resolver feeds), DEC-NIFTY-BOS-CHOCH-001 (#1012 — PR-2b, the prior shared-Rust indicator piece), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441 — the shared trading-core crate consumed bit-identically by BruteX + TickVault). (Ledger: #1013 = max-existing(1012)+1.)
1026. **DEC-FETCH-PER-WINDOW-GUARANTEE-001 — adaptive strike-chain bounding drives F&O fetches-per-window 2.54 → ~1.2, making the worst-case-3-r/s 8-hour pull a MEASURED CI gate (no data lost)** (2026-06-30; pull-PLANNING / per-contract retry-budget only — NO lake-schema/stored-bar/rate-cap/vocab change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). **The operator's criterion (the arithmetic):** at the worst-case AIMD soft-floor `3 r/s`, `3 × 3600 × 8h = 86,400` vendor fetches are available in 8h. A measured production pull spent **2.54 fetches per `(contract, interval)` window** (122,243 fetches / 48,145 windows), so the target chain fit only if fetches-per-window dropped toward ~1.0-1.2. **MEASURED amplification decomposition (the honest finding, re-derived in `tests/bench/test_fetch_per_window_guarantee.py`):** modelling `avg = (1−E)·1 + E·3` against the measured 2.54 gives an empty-window fraction `E ≈ 0.77` — i.e. the **3× in-pull EMPTY-retry budget** (`DEFAULT_EMPTY_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=3`, `DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001`) firing on every clean-but-empty window is the DOMINANT amplifier, NOT the operator's framed "15.8% deep-OTM" subset alone. On an options chain the bulk of strikes are deep out-of-the-money and **never traded over the pulled window**, so they return a clean empty `200` and pay 3× to re-confirm a strike that is dead — the 3× exists to recover a transient vendor GLITCH on data that DOES exist, value a deep dead strike does not have. **8h-FEASIBILITY VERDICT (honest, fits):** the representative-chain bench reproduces the baseline at **2.580 fpw** (418 fetches / 162 windows → 8h covers only 33,485 windows) and the adaptive-bounding pass at **1.198 fpw** (194 fetches / 162 windows → 8h covers **72,148** windows), a **0.46× fetch reduction with the SAME bars stored (34→34, no data lost)**. At ≤1.2 fpw the 86,400-fetch 8h budget covers ~72k windows ≥ the ~48k target — so the 8h guarantee IS achievable at 3 r/s for the measured scope; it would be IMPOSSIBLE only if the LIQUID-only window universe alone exceeded 86,400, which the measured liquid count (~42k non-dead windows) does not. **What shipped — a DYNAMIC, data-driven per-contract empty-retry budget (NEVER a hardcoded NSE strike rule):** NEW pure `brutex/adapters/groww/strike_chain_bound.py` (`build_empty_retry_budget` → `StrikeChainBudget`): groups the OPTION (CE/PE) chain by `(underlying_symbol, expiry)` — NOT expiry alone — finds each chain's MEDIAN strike (a robust ATM/liquidity-center proxy that needs no live spot fetch), and classifies a contract whose strike sits OUTSIDE a `±band`-STRIKES envelope (band measured in grid-rank, so it adapts to a wide-grid index AND a tight-grid stock; default `±12` ≈ the liquid ATM±12 envelope, env `BRUTEX_FNO_STRIKE_BAND`) as "confirmed-deep" → a REDUCED empty-retry budget (default `1`, env `BRUTEX_FNO_DEEP_EMPTY_RETRY`, clamped into `[1, full]`). **Keying on the UNDERLYING too is essential for the production all-cached pull (hostile-review MAJOR, folded):** that pull builds ONE budget over a chain spanning MANY underlyings, and two underlyings sharing the same monthly expiry (the common last-Thursday case — RELIANCE ₹2800-3200 + HDFCBANK ₹1600-1780) must NOT have their strikes POOLED into one median, or the pooled center lands in the inter-cluster gap and over-flags live-cluster strikes (it CANNOT lose data — a data-bearing first fetch always wins — but it erodes glitch-recovery on potentially-live strikes); the per-`(underlying,expiry)` key keeps every median its OWN underlying's ATM proxy. A too-small chain (`< 7` distinct strikes), every FUT leg, and every in-band option keep the FULL budget; the map is SPARSE (only the reduced strikes appear), so a `None` map is byte-identical to the pre-feature path. `StrikeChainBudget.total_contracts` counts ONLY the OPTION legs actually CONSIDERED (excludes FUT + small-chain-skipped options, so the deep/total ratio is honest — hostile-review MINOR, folded). Threaded `optional empty_retry_by_symbol` through `option_ingest.run_groww_option_ingest` → `_run_pair` (resolves the per-contract budget, defaulting to the full `empty_retry_attempts` for any unmapped symbol) → `ingest_option_contract`'s EXISTING `empty_retry_attempts` param; built in `dashboard/historical_pull.pull_contract_candles` over the WHOLE selected chain and forwarded through `_run_phase`. **CORRECTNESS — NO DATA IS EVER LOST (the operator's transient-empty data-loss concern, Golden Rule #1):** the reduction keys ONLY off a CLEAN 200-zero-candles return, NEVER off a raised retryable exception — proven by construction: in `ingest_option_contract` the `for empty_attempt in range(...)` loop (which `empty_retry_attempts` bounds) re-iterates ONLY when `fetch_option_candles` RETURNS empty bars; a transient (429 `GrowwRateLimitError`, timeout `GrowwTimeoutError`, 5xx `GrowwServerError` #883, empty/non-JSON throttle body `GrowwEmptyResponseError` #854, network `GrowwNetworkError`) is RAISED, caught by the SEPARATE `except GrowwError` transient ladder (`max_attempts` + backoff, UNTOUCHED), and on budget exhaustion RETURNS early with `transient_failures=1` — it NEVER decrements the empty-retry budget. The first non-empty fetch always wins (the empty loop `break`s the moment any attempt returns bars), so a deep strike that DOES return data is stored EXACTLY as before; a near-money strike is never mapped deep; "if uncertain, fetch" (a value `< 1` clamps UP to 1 — always fetched once). **RE-PULL RECOVERY NET (rule 5):** a reduced-budget empty window makes `fetch_count == 1 < CONFIRMED_EMPTY_MIN_FETCHES(2)`, so the OLD-gap fast-settle does NOT fire — the window is recorded EMPTY but stays re-fetchable on a later idempotent pull (keep-first sink + durable ledger), so even a vendor-bug 200-empty is recoverable, never permanent loss. [SETTLE-RECONCILE — DEC-DEAD-STRIKE-LEDGER-SETTLE-001, MIGRATION.md #1171 (the #1132 gate-honesty reconcile precedent): the "stays re-fetchable" claim is now SUPERSEDED for an OLD window — the old-gap settle is BUDGET-AWARE, accumulating clean-EMPTY confirmations ACROSS pulls (`prior.empty_streak + in_pull_fetches` against the SAME `CONFIRMED_EMPTY_MIN_FETCHES(2)` bar), so TWO independent pulls' clean empties settle a reduced-budget old window SKIPPED (never weaker evidence than the pre-existing one-pull fast-settle, which accepted 1 clean + 1 in-pull-retry empty). A REPEATED vendor-bug 200-empty on an old window is thereafter recoverable via `brutex reopen-skipped`, no longer an automatic re-pull; a RECENT window keeps the conservative 3-pull streak, SUCCESS resets, a suppressed/transient empty never counts.] The #919 whole-underlying all-empty detector + the #974 partial-window detector stay ACTIVE + unconditional (rule 6 — a whole-chain wrong-empty is still flagged). **THE GUARANTEE = a MEASURED CI BENCH GATE, not a promise:** NEW `tests/bench/test_fetch_per_window_guarantee.py` REPLAYS a representative NIFTY chain end-to-end through the REAL ingest spine against a fetch-COUNTING fake SDK and ASSERTS fetches-per-window ≤ 1.2 AND the projected 8h coverage (`86,400 / fpw`) ≥ the chain's window count — so a regression that re-inflates the empty-retry (or removes the bounding) FAILS CI; a second test asserts the SAME chain WITHOUT bounding is ABOVE the ceiling (the gate has TEETH) and stores the SAME bars (no data lost). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a HEURISTIC band, not an oracle — a genuinely-live strike outside the median band loses 2 glitch-recovery attempts but is STILL fetched once + stored if it returns data; the band is deliberately WIDE so common liquid strikes always keep the full budget; ✅ the 8h projection is `total_fetches / 3 r/s`, a wall-clock LOWER bound assuming the controller sustains 3 r/s (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 — provable), NOT a claim every real pull finishes in 8h regardless of vendor health; ✅ this bounds the empty-RETRY only — it does NOT skip a strike at plan time (a true "walk-outward-stop-after-K-empty" short-circuit is incompatible with the parallel cross-contract fan-out + would slow the pull, so the empty-retry reduction — the dominant measured lever — was chosen instead); ✅ SCOPE TRADEOFF (explicit): a deep dead strike is confirmed empty in 1 fetch instead of 3 — no data is lost (the strike returns empty either way), this reduces ONLY the redundant re-confirmation fetches, not the set of strikes pulled. **Coverage:** `strike_chain_bound.py` (88/24) + `option_ingest.py` (310/82) + `historical_pull.py` (257/54) ALL 100% line+branch; NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_strike_chain_bound.py` (32 unit + property, incl. the MAJOR-fix `test_multi_underlying_same_expiry_not_pooled` proving two disjoint-strike underlyings on ONE expiry each get their OWN median + the MINOR-fix `test_total_contracts_counts_only_considered_options`) + `TestEmptyRetryBudgetCorrectness` permutation suite in `test_groww_option_ingest.py` (one per permutation: clean-200-empty far-OTM → bounded; 429 / timeout / 5xx / empty-body-throttle → retried + NOT counted; near-money → never reduced; transient-empty-then-data → strike not skipped + data captured; re-pull after wrong-empty → re-fetches; all-empty #919 detector still fires under reduced budget; `None` map byte-identical) + the bench gate; ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file (`auth.py`/`reauth.py` growwapi-stub errors are pre-existing + direct-path-only, pass under the project module config). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/strike_chain_bound.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_strike_chain_bound.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/bench/test_fetch_per_window_guarantee.py` (new), `CLAUDE.md` §3, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-FETCH-PER-WINDOW-GUARANTEE-001. **Builds on** DEC-EMPTY-INPULL-RETRY-001 / DEC-OPTION-EMPTY-RETRY-001 (the 3× empty-retry this bounds), DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 (#894 — the per-contract date windows), DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001 (the fetch-count settle threshold the reduced budget honours), DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001 (#883) / DEC-POSTPULL-DATAQUALITY-BATCH-001 (#854 — the retryable transient classification this keys OFF), DEC-SUSPICIOUS-EMPTY-FLAG-001 (#919 — the all-empty detector kept active). (Ledger: #1026 — renumbered from the originally-claimed #1021, which collided with DEC-COVERAGE-DISCOVERY-STAGE... #1021 that landed on main; kept above all merged + in-flight siblings; the entry number is uniqueness-based, not strictly sequential.)

1025. **DEC-LAKE-READ-O1-AUDIT-001 — a full audit of every BruteX DB-FETCH / lake-READ entry point for O(1)/O(page) latency, which found the codebase ALREADY bounded everywhere on the hot paths EXCEPT one gap — the `/db` expired-options pager's `COUNT(*)` total — now closed with the SAME generation-stamped count cache the spot pager got in #867** (2026-06-30, operator: "audit every DB-fetch / lake-read path for proven, benchmarked O(1) on DB fetching everywhere — find the GAPS"). **THE AUDIT (the headline result — Golden Rule #1/#10, no invented work):** a 3-cluster parallel read-path survey (dashboard `db_view`, the movers/completeness/universe screens, the engine `feed`/`options.lake_source`/`spot_daily_resample` reads) classified EVERY lake-read entry point as O(1)-cached / O(page) / O(files) / O(rows) / O(partition). The verdict: the prior O(1)/O(page) PRs (#860/#863/#864/#867/#893/#895/#896/#933) have ALREADY closed essentially every hot read — the engine bar stream is O(1)/bar (catalog-window-indexed `Catalog.get_bars`, `heapq.merge`), `LakeOptionBarSource.load_pair` is O(1)/leg after two read-through caches, the spot 1m→1d resample read is bounded to the pulled-window months (`ist_span_partition_files`), every movers per-symbol read is month/day-glob-bounded (`lake_day_glob`) + the candidate scan is split-and-cached (`MoversSnapshotCache`), the completeness SPOT scan rides `_summary_cache`, and the `/universe` reads are O(1) behind `master_revision`. The `/db` candle pager (count + window payload + tab-switch discovery + registry) were all already cached/`LIMIT`-pushdown-bounded. **THE ONE GAP FOUND + FIXED:** `db_view.query_option_candles` (the `/db` expired-options tab) computed its page `total` as `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM read_parquet(<series-glob>)` on EVERY paging click with NO `count_cache` — the EXACT O(files) footer-scan that `query_candles` fixed in DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001 #867, but the options pager was never given the same treatment (verified: the `/db/options` route passed no cache; the spot `/db/candles` route did). **What shipped (READ-ONLY `/db` viewer accelerator — the brute-force ENGINE is UNCHANGED, still NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO store/schema/scope/vocab/rate/write-path change):** a NEW pure `db_view.option_candle_count_key(series, start, end)` (the expired-options twin of `candle_count_key`; the key excludes `limit`/`offset`/`descending`/`columns` — the paging-invariance the cache exploits — and carries an `opt|` prefix so it NEVER collides with a spot key, letting both pagers share ONE injected cache) + `query_option_candles` gains the OPTIONAL `count_cache: CandleCountCache | None` + `generation` params (REUSING the existing #867 `CandleCountCache` Protocol — a generic `get_or_compute(key, *, generation, compute) -> int`, NO new class); when injected, the `COUNT(*)` runs through `count_cache.get_or_compute(option_candle_count_key(...), generation, compute=…)`, else inline (the pure-function default — behaviour byte-identical, all 22 existing `query_option_candles` tests pass unchanged). The `/api/v1/db/options` route passes `count_cache=_candle_count_cache` (the SAME COMMON `MoversSnapshotCache` LRU the spot pager already uses — the `opt|`-namespaced key means they coexist safely) + `generation=_summary_cache.generation`, so a pull bumps the generation → recount, never a stale total (Golden Rule #1). **MEASURED before/after (real Parquet via the production option writer + a real DuckDB conn):** paging a deep 72-month series — uncached **19.02 ms/click → cached 13.76 ms/click** (1.38× faster, ~28% off), and the win GROWS with partition depth (1.14× at 6 months → 1.38× at 72), confirming the cache removes a depth-scaling cost. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10 — identical to #867's bound):** ✅ a cached-total HIT is **O(1)** in the series depth (the bench `tests/bench/test_db_option_count_cache_o1.py` pins the cached retrieval FLAT — hit ratio ~1.0 at 72 vs 6 months, under `ratio_ceiling`; the unit test proves the `COUNT(*)` runs exactly ONCE across paging clicks via a COUNT-counting connection); 🟡 the FIRST view of a (series, filter) per generation STILL pays the real O(files) `COUNT(*)` — the cache bounds how OFTEN, not the scan itself; 🟡 paging is NOT O(1) overall — the page DATA query (`ORDER BY timestamp … LIMIT` over the glob) remains O(files), the larger residual, exactly as #867 documented for spot (true O(page) paging needs a write-time lake manifest — explicit FUTURE work, NOT claimed); ✅ the empty/not-yet-pulled series early-returns `total: 0` WITHOUT touching the cache. **A documented non-issue surfaced by the audit (NOT fixed, openly stated):** the movers `_read_daily_partition` / `_prev_day_oi` read the whole 1day partition glob unbounded — but the 1day series is intrinsically tiny (≤ ~1.6k rows for a full 2020→today symbol), month-bounding is INVALID for a midnight-IST daily bar (it can land in the prior UTC month — `lake_day_glob` documents this), AND the reads are route-cached via `MoversSnapshotCache`, so they are a latency footnote, not a real O(partition) hot read. **Coverage/gates (verified 2026-06-30 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` at **100.00% line+branch** (718/0 stmt + 232/0 branch across the full covering set, 389 tests) incl. the NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_option_count_cache.py` (11: key format/None-bounds/distinct/spot-namespace, byte-identical cached==uncached total + full page payload, COUNT-once-across-pages, generation-bump recount, distinct-series independence, empty-series no-cache, pure default) + the route integration `TestDbOptionsRouteCountCache` (the `/api/v1/db/options` COUNT-once-across-paging + generation-bust proof); `app.py` route wiring exercised by the integration test; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0 errors) + ruff (check + format) clean on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_option_count_cache.py` (new), `tests/bench/test_db_option_count_cache_o1.py` (new), `tests/integration/test_dashboard_db_datasets.py` (new route test class), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LAKE-READ-O1-AUDIT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001 (#867 — the `CandleCountCache` Protocol + `candle_count_key` pattern this mirrors for options + the SAME `_candle_count_cache` instance reused), DEC-MOVERS-O1-LATENCY-001 (#860 — the `MoversSnapshotCache` generation-stamped LRU), DEC-COMPLETENESS-O1-LATENCY-001 (#895), DEC-DASHBOARD-NAV-LATENCY-001 (#933 — the `master_revision` token cache the audit confirmed bounds the universe reads), DEC-DB-TAB-SWITCH-O1-001 (#896 — the dataset-discovery cache). (Ledger: #1025 = the next free unique number above main's max after merging origin/main — renumbered from the originally-claimed #1020, which collided with DEC-STAGE... #1020 that landed on main; distinct from the in-flight siblings #1016 (PR #979) / #1021 (PR #986) / #1022 (PR #982) / #1023-#1024 (PR #983); the DEC-ID validator is uniqueness-based, the numeric gap is fine.)
1023. **DEC-LAKE-WRITE-VECTORIZE-001 — the lake-write merge READ's per-row `round_money(Decimal(str(float)))` 2dp-snap reconstruction (`brutex/data/parquet_writer.py::_read_existing_bars`, the single biggest GIL-held write cost on a deep month partition — prior profiling ~105 ms / ~50 % GIL-held on a ~7,500-row partition) is VECTORIZED into ONE polars-native columnar expression, BYTE-EXACT** (2026-06-30; lake-write internal cost only — READ-ONLY w.r.t. stored values; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO lake-schema / stored-bar / scope / vocab / rate-cap change). **Why:** the steady-state re-pull of a partly-filled month re-reads + re-snaps + re-renders the WHOLE month partition (immutable Parquet read-modify-write). The 4a columnar cut (DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001) replaced the per-row `df.iter_rows` dict but LEFT the per-row `Decimal(str(float))` + `_tick_round` + double-`CandleBar` loop — a pure-Python, partly-GIL-held reconstruction that dominated the write. **What shipped:** NEW pure `_snap_price_expr(column) -> pl.Expr` — the byte-exact polars reproduction of `float(round_money(Decimal(str(x))))`: `cast(String).cast(Decimal(precision=38, scale=17))` materialises the float's SHORTEST-REPR decimal string carrying the same NUMERIC VALUE Python's `str(float)` yields (scale **17** — wide enough to hold EVERY fractional digit of a ≤17-significant-digit `str(float)` with NO truncation; a too-small scale like the originally-shipped `scale=10` would round an 11-17-digit long-tail repr such as `0.00499999999` UP to the `.005` grid BEFORE the half-up step → the WRONG `0.01` vs legacy `0.00`, a silent price-corruption BLOCKER caught by a SECOND hostile review and fixed here) (not always the same DIGIT STRING — polars emits `0.00001` where Python emits `1e-05`, but `Decimal("0.00001")==Decimal("1e-05")`; no realistic price is in scientific notation anyway), the seed the legacy `Decimal(str(op))` parsed — a direct `Float64->Decimal` cast carries binary-float noise and lands the `.xx5` half boundary on the WRONG side, e.g. `100.005`), then half-AWAY-from-zero to 2dp via integer Decimal arithmetic `floor(d*100 + 0.5)/100` for `d>=0` / `ceil(d*100 - 0.5)/100` for `d<0` (`floor`/`ceil`, NOT a `cast(Int64)` which ROUNDS — exact truncation toward the boundary so every `.xx5` rounds AWAY, byte-identical to `Decimal.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), ROUND_HALF_UP)`, DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 / DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001). `_read_existing_bars` now `df.with_columns(*(_snap_price_expr(c) for c in _PRICE_COLUMNS))` then builds each `CandleBar` straight off the polars `Decimal(scale=2)` column — the heavy Decimal math runs in compiled polars C (GIL RELEASED), only the inherent `{ts: CandleBar}` dict build stays in Python (the double-`CandleBar` + `_tick_round` of the old path is GONE). The snap is folded INSIDE the same `parquet_read_skip_errors`-guarded block as the decode, so a corrupt NON-FINITE (inf/NaN) stored price now QUARANTINES via a `PolarsError` → `WriterError` (a strict improvement on the legacy un-caught `decimal.InvalidOperation` that would have crashed the whole pull). **PROVEN byte-parity (non-negotiable, Golden Rule #7):** the existing verbatim-legacy golden (`tests/golden/test_writer_columnar_parity.py`, 11 cases incl. 4dp vendor noise / out-of-order / keep-first conflict / latest-wins / 800-row deep partition) + the existing fuzz property (`test_writer_columnar_parity_properties.py`) now compare the NEW vectorized path against the byte-for-byte legacy per-row `Decimal(str())` + `_tick_round` writer and pass; a NEW dedicated expression-level golden (`tests/golden/test_writer_vectorized_snap_parity.py`, 36 cases — exact `.005` half boundaries, negatives, zeros, `14020.7999`, large strikes, half-up-not-banker's, fixpoint) + a NEW fuzz property over REALISTIC PRICE-RANGE floats (`|price|` bounded; float-rerender ULP drift appears only at `≳ 4e14` and the snap-cast overflows only at `≳ 1e19` (between 1e18 and 1e19), NEITHER a reachable bar price) assert both the `float` (the stored byte) and the `Decimal` (the `_bar_values_equal` key) equal `round_money(Decimal(str(x)))` exactly; an ad-hoc price-range sweep of 180k+ values (incl. the long-tail near-boundary class) had ZERO mismatch; the goldens were strengthened with explicit long-tail cases that PROVABLY FAIL on the buggy `scale=10` and PASS on the `scale=17` fix (a real teeth-test). A finite value whose `x*100` overflows the intermediate `Decimal(precision=38)` (`|x| ≳ 1e19` — empirically the cast overflows between 1e18 and 1e19, UNREACHABLE for a real bar price) raises a `PolarsError` from the snap and FALLS BACK to the exact per-row `Decimal(str(x))` reconstruction (correctness over the micro-optimization); a genuinely-corrupt non-finite (inf/NaN) lands on that fallback too and quarantines as a `WriterError`. HONEST signed-zero edge (Golden Rule #10): a NEGATIVE value rounding to zero yields `+0.00` here vs the legacy `-0.00` (polars Decimal has no signed zero) — UNREACHABLE since a bar price is never negative, and the numeric values still compare equal — so the byte-identical claim is scoped to the NON-NEGATIVE prices a bar actually carries. The speedup is pinned by a committed `tests/bench/test_writer_snap_vectorize_bench.py` (vectorized snap < legacy per-row loop, CI-reproducible). **BENCHMARK (honest):** realistic 7,500-row month partition reconstruction 60.3 ms -> 33.9 ms (1.78x); the price-column snap in isolation ~10x lower wall-time (compiled polars vs the Python `Decimal(str())` loop) with the GIL released for the math. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the LIVE pull is currently vendor-429-bound (~2.84 r/s), so this does NOT speed up the current pull — it (a) ensures the write never BECOMES the limiter when the vendor bursts toward 10 r/s or the ceiling is raised, and (b) speeds up any cache-replay / `/db` read that re-merges a partition; NO live-pull speedup claimed. Byte-identical stored values (idempotence + crash-recovery durable-settle + the partition flock + the `/db` glob reader path ALL unchanged — this touches ONLY the in-memory reconstruction between the decode and the re-render). `parquet_writer.py` at 100% line+branch (155/20); ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` (`brutex`) / `pyright` (`brutex tests`) clean. **Files:** `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `tests/golden/test_writer_vectorized_snap_parity.py` (new), `tests/property/test_writer_columnar_parity_properties.py`, `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/bench/test_writer_snap_vectorize_bench.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LAKE-WRITE-VECTORIZE-001. **Builds on** DEC-WRITER-COLUMNAR-4A-001 (the per-row-dict cut this completes), DEC-SPOT-PRICE-2DP-001 / DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the half-up 2dp byte contract preserved), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 (the `lake_write_guard` + skip-error resilience kept). (Ledger: #1023 = next free unique number above main's max after merging origin/main — renumbered from the originally-claimed #1018, which collided with DEC-CALENDAR-... #1018 that landed on main; distinct from the in-flight sibling PRs reserving #1016 (PR #979) / #1019 (the sibling analysis entry in this PR) / #1020 (PR #984) / #1021 (PR #986) / #1022 (PR #982).)

1024. **DEC-LAKE-WRITE-PARTITION-GROWTH-ANALYSIS-001 — the "is Parquet making issues?" architectural question ANSWERED with a benchmark: the immutable-Parquet read-modify-write-WHOLE-PARTITION pattern makes append latency O(partition-depth), and the recommended fix is BUFFERED-APPEND (the existing `BatchingWriteConsumer`), NOT daily partitioning (too invasive)** (2026-06-30; analysis + recommendation — NO lake-layout change shipped; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). **The measured scaling (a 30-bar append into a month partition seeded with N rows, this environment):** 1,000 rows -> 13.4 ms · 5,000 -> 43.4 ms · 10,000 -> 78.6 ms · 20,000 -> 145.3 ms · 30,000 -> 224.1 ms. **Verdict:** append latency is O(partition-size), NOT O(batch-size) — confirmed `ParquetWriter._merge_write` re-reads, re-snaps, and re-renders the ENTIRE month partition on every append (Parquet is immutable; there is no in-place append). A NIFTY 1-minute month is ~7,500 bars, so a within-month re-pull re-processes the whole month each time; the cost grows as the month fills. (The existing `tests/bench/test_parquet_write_o1.py` proves O(1) in the NUMBER of partitions — a fresh write never scans the lake — but says nothing about depth WITHIN one partition; this entry records the depth scaling.) **Fixes evaluated:** (a) **daily partitioning** (`<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>.parquet`, ~1/30th the rewrite) — REJECTED as too invasive: the `<yyyy>/<mm>.parquet` layout is baked into `brutex/data/partition.py` and globbed by `db_view` / `fno_candle_lake` / `lake_day_glob` / `movers` (large blast radius the task flagged); a layout change is a separate, higher-risk PR. (b) **buffered / batched append** — RECOMMENDED + ALREADY DESIGNED: `brutex/data/write_consumer.py::BatchingWriteConsumer` (Lever 1 of DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001) accumulates a window's bars and flushes each month ONCE off the fetch lane, settle-after-durable (Golden Rule #7), one-partition-one-shard (no single-serializer regression), bounded-queue back-pressure — it preserves idempotence (keep-first), crash-recovery (durable settle before ledger), byte-exact values, the partition flock, and the `/db` glob reader path with ZERO layout change. (c) **append-only small files + compaction** — a larger redesign, deferred. **Recommendation:** ship the byte-exact vectorization (#1023, which lowers EVERY read-modify-write regardless of pattern) NOW, and adopt the buffered-append `BatchingWriteConsumer` (which removes the REPEATED whole-partition rewrites within a window) as the architectural fix — NOT daily partitioning. **Honest envelope:** #1019 is ANALYSIS + a recorded benchmark + a recommendation; it ships NO lake-layout change. The vectorization (#1023) is the shipped code; the buffered-append adoption is the recommended next step (the primitive already exists, the wiring is the remaining work). **Decision ID:** DEC-LAKE-WRITE-PARTITION-GROWTH-ANALYSIS-001. **Builds on** DEC-FETCH-WRITE-OVERLAP-001 (Lever 1 `write_consumer`), DEC-LAKE-WRITE-INSTRUMENT-001 (the `lake.partition.write` `partition_rows` telemetry that made this measurable), DEC-O1-BENCH-GAPS-001 (the partition-count O(1) bench this complements). (Ledger: #1024 = #1023 + 1 — renumbered from the originally-claimed #1018/#1019 to resolve the #1018 collision with DEC-CALENDAR-... on main.)

1027. **DEC-STRATEGYSPEC-CORE-001 — PR-4b sub-PR 1: the load-bearing CORE of strategy-as-DATA — a `StrategySpec` declaration + a single `evaluate(spec, snapshot, prior) -> Signal` orchestrator in the shared Rust `trading-core`, a THIN ADDITIVE WRAPPER over the FROZEN `evaluate_atoms` kernel, proven backtest==live BY CONSTRUCTION against the 400-case golden** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; shared-core/Rust + the `trading_core` PyO3 re-export only — NO `brutex/` engine, lake-schema, stored-bar, scope, vocab, or rate-cap change). **The thesis:** a strategy is a *declaration* — a required-condition `u128` mask (the SAME 60-condition vocabulary as `bits.rs`/`bits.py`) + a `Direction` + the proximity tolerances + the prior-bar look-back + an opaque instrument token — and `evaluate` asks the frozen kernel for the bar's bitmask then applies the ONE superset test `(bar_bits & condition_mask) == condition_mask` (byte-identical to `combo_mask.evaluate_mask`). It NEVER touches the kernel's arithmetic, so the spec path is bit-consistent with the engine path and the frozen `tests/golden/fixtures/vocab_golden_vectors.json` 400-case answer-key stays byte-identical. **What shipped:** (1) **NEW `rust/trading-core/src/spec.rs`** — `pub struct StrategySpec { condition_mask: u128, direction: Direction, proximity: ProximityParams (REUSED verbatim), prior_n: usize, symbol_id: u32 }` (Clone/Copy/Debug/PartialEq/Eq); `#[repr(u8)] enum Direction { Long = 0, Short = 1 }` with checked `from_u8`/`as_u8`; `StrategySpec::new(...)` VALIDATES `condition_mask & !IMPLEMENTED_MASK == 0` (a spec can never require a reserved/un-evaluated bit the kernel never sets — a silent-dead-strategy refusal); `pub struct Signal { bar_bits: u128, fires: bool, direction: Direction }` (a NEW minimal struct, NOT the strategy-engine `brutex.strategies.types.Signal`; carries NO entry/exit price levels — the candle lake stores neither IV nor levels, fabricating them would violate Golden Rule #1); `pub fn evaluate(...)` the thin wrapper; `SPEC_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1` + `canonical_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>` (deterministic fixed-order LE encode `version‖mask‖direction‖proximity‖prior_n(as u64)‖symbol_id` — the COMMON spec-axis fingerprint both repos feed into run-identity bit-identically, platform-independent: `prior_n` encoded as a fixed `u64` not the platform `usize`). serde is runtime-OPTIONAL behind a NEW `serde = ["dep:serde"]` feature (OFF by default so TickVault's native link stays dependency-free); `condition_mask` serialises as a HEX STRING via a `mask_hex` adapter (a `u128` JSON number loses precision past 2⁵³, matching the fixture's `expected_mask` hex convention); `ProximityParams` gained the same feature-gated derive so it can ride the serializable spec. (2) **PyO3 binding** — NEW `#[cfg(feature="python")] evaluate_spec(condition_mask_hex, direction, <the same 22-arg pre-built-levels ABI as evaluate_with_levels>) -> (bar_bits, fires, direction)` in `python.rs`, REUSING `evaluate_with_levels_impl` verbatim for `bar_bits` (so the frozen kernel is untouched) then parsing+validating the mask (IMPLEMENTED-only) + direction (0/1) at the FFI boundary → a clean `ValueError`, never a panic→SIGABRT under `panic="abort"`; registered in `#[pymodule] _trading_core` (+ `IMPLEMENTED_MASK` / `SPEC_SCHEMA_VERSION` module constants) and re-exported from `python/trading_core/__init__.py` (`__all__`). **THE DEPLOY-CONTRACT GOLDEN (no illusion — the point):** NEW `rust/trading-core/tests/spec_signal_golden.rs` — for EVERY one of the 400 vocab golden vectors it builds a `StrategySpec` whose `condition_mask` IS that vector's frozen `expected_mask`, runs `evaluate`, and asserts `signal.bar_bits == expected` (the bar reproduces its own mask) AND `signal.fires == true` (a spec requiring exactly those bits fires); PLUS a NEGATIVE — for every case with a clear IMPLEMENTED bit, a spec requiring that absent bit does NOT fire (so "fires" is a real test, not a tautology). **RESULT: 400/400 positive + 400/400 negative, 0 failures** on BOTH the native Rust path (`cargo test`) AND — verified through the ACTUAL maturin-built wheel — the PyO3 `evaluate_spec` path (a Python harness over the same fixture: positive 400/400, negative 400/400, 0 failures). `expected_fires` is DERIVED from the frozen `expected_mask` by the SAME superset test, so the spec golden can never drift from the atom golden — one source of truth, no new hand-blessed truth. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the deploy contract proves the EVALUATION (mask→fires) is bit-identical Rust(native, TickVault's live path) == Rust(PyO3, BruteX's backtest path) == the frozen oracle, testable today with no live broker (the in-repo native rlib IS the TickVault link surface); it does NOT prove trade-sim/cost parity (those have their OWN goldens) — stated, not conflated; ✅ the frozen 400-case `evaluate_atoms` golden is byte-identical (the existing `golden_vectors.rs` 3 tests + `codegen_vocab.py --check` exit 0 prove the kernel + vocab are untouched); ✅ `cargo fmt --check` clean + `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --features python --all-targets -- -D warnings` 0 (also default + `serde` feature combos) + `cargo test` GREEN across default / `python` / `serde` / `python,serde` (111 unit + 3 golden_vectors + 2 spec_signal_golden + 13 proptest + 1 ema, 0 failed); ✅ `spec.rs` covered by its own unit tests (Direction round-trip + garbage-reject, construction validation incl. reserved-bit + mixed-mask reject, `canonical_bytes` determinism + per-field distinctness, evaluate fire/no-fire/empty-mask, serde hex round-trip + non-hex reject) + the deploy golden; the `evaluate_spec_impl` boundary covered by 6 new `python.rs` unit tests (fire / no-fire / non-hex / reserved-bit / bad-direction / reused-guard-propagation); ✅ `ruff check brutex` + `ruff format --check brutex` clean; the ONLY touched Python is the `trading_core` package `__init__.py` re-export (ruff clean); a sandbox `mypy --strict` artifact on that file (`unused-ignore` for the pre-existing `# type: ignore[import-not-found]`, and a PEP-695 parse error in the UNTOUCHED `brutex/adapters/groww/contracts.py`) are both stale-environment / wrong-interpreter-version effects — the file's `# type: ignore` is PRE-EXISTING + explicitly handled by the project's `follow_imports="silent"` mypy override for the `trading_core` module — NOT defects introduced here (my diff touches ZERO `brutex/` files); ✅ this is sub-PR 1 (the CORE) — the config-driven universe (gap D1), the Python `StrategySpec` dataclass + `combo_hash` wiring, the `tod_seconds` Rust-seam deletion, the Pine import, the OptionBarSource unification, and the spec→SpotSignal bridge are SEPARATE flagged sub-PRs, NOT in this one. **Files:** `rust/trading-core/src/spec.rs` (new), `rust/trading-core/tests/spec_signal_golden.rs` (new), `rust/trading-core/src/lib.rs` (mod + re-export), `rust/trading-core/src/evaluator.rs` (feature-gated serde derive on `ProximityParams`), `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs` (`evaluate_spec` + tests + module constants), `rust/trading-core/Cargo.toml` (optional serde + `serde` feature), `rust/trading-core/python/trading_core/__init__.py` (re-export), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-STRATEGYSPEC-CORE-001. **Builds on** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441 — the shared `trading-core` crate consumed bit-identically by BruteX + TickVault), DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 (the 60-condition u128 vocab + codegen the mask spans), DEC-STAGE1A-WIRE-VWAP-BOS-001 (#1020 — the PR-4 B1 wiring that made all 60 bits fire in a real sweep, which this spec layer rides), DEC-MASK-IDENTITY-001 (the mask-as-strategy-id identity scheme `canonical_bytes` feeds).
