## DEC-STAGE1A-WIRE-VWAP-BOS-001 (2026-06-30)

1020. **DEC-STAGE1A-WIRE-VWAP-BOS-001 — PR-4 B1: WIRE the session-anchored VWAP + the BOS/CHoCH market-structure state into the production sweep builder (`Stage1AMatrixBuilder.push`) so the previously-DEAD bits 52/53 (close above/below VWAP) + 56-59 (BOS/CHoCH up/down) actually FIRE — with the per-bar COMPUTE running in the shared Rust `trading-core` (new PyO3 state bindings), NOT re-implemented in Python** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; data-independent / synthetic-fixture only; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **The dead-engine-path bug (B1, confirmed file:line on origin/main):** PR-2/PR-2b (#1011/#1012) put the VWAP + R5/S5 + BOS/CHoCH logic into the shared Rust crate and the evaluator ABI (`evaluate_with_levels` already accepts `vwap_paisa` + the four market-structure flags; the Rust gates `evaluator.rs:373` `if let Some(vwap)` + `:401-411` `if ms.bos_*/choch_*` exist), and `IndicatorSnapshot` carries `vwap_paisa: int|None = None` (`evaluator.py:76`) + `market_structure = MarketStructureSignal()` all-false (`:83`). BUT the production sweep matrix builder `Stage1AMatrixBuilder.push` (`stage1a.py`) built the snapshot WITHOUT populating either field — no `VwapState`/`MarketStructureState` existed anywhere in `brutex/engine` — so the evaluator always received `vwap_paisa=None` + an all-false signal, and bits 52/53/56-59 could NEVER be set in a real sweep despite green unit goldens (R5/S5 — 54/55 — already fired; they read pivots the builder DOES build, so they are untouched). **OPERATOR DIRECTIVE honored (the per-bar compute MUST run in Rust):** rather than driving the Python twins `brutex/indicators/{vwap,market_structure}.py` (which would put the running-sum / fractal-swing arithmetic in Python), this PR ADDS minimal PyO3 `#[pyclass]` bindings — `trading_core.VwapState` + `trading_core.MarketStructureState` — over the EXISTING native Rust `indicators::vwap::VwapState` / `indicators::market_structure::MarketStructureState`, and `stage1a` drives THOSE. The only arithmetic in the Python diff is the HLC3 typical price `(high+low+close)/3` snapped via the SAME `_price_to_paisa` (`round_money` ROUND_HALF_UP) seam OHLC/EMA already use (one snap definition, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON, equal to the dashboard turnover proxy); the VWAP `cum(price·vol)/cum(vol)` accumulation (i128, 09:15 reset, auction exclusion) and the look-ahead-clean fractal-swing BOS/CHoCH resolution physically execute in Rust — the bit-identical BruteX==TickVault guarantee, the same delegating pattern as the EMA recurrence (#1014). **What shipped:** (1) **`rust/trading-core/src/python.rs` — two NEW `#[pyclass]` wrappers** (`PyVwapState` name="VwapState" + `PyMarketStructureState` name="MarketStructureState", behind the existing `python` feature): each holds the native core struct and delegates `update(...)` verbatim; the market-structure constructor validates `k >= 1` and raises a clean `ValueError` (never trips the native `assert!` → `abort` under `panic="abort"`); registered via `add_class::<>()` in the `#[pymodule]` + re-exported from the `trading_core` package `__init__.py` (+ `__all__`). VWAP `update` returns `Option<i64>` (the resolved paisa level, `None` during warm-up); market-structure `update` returns the `(bos_bull, bos_bear, choch_bull, choch_bear)` tuple. (2) **`brutex/engine/stage1a.py` — the B1 wiring:** `Stage1AMatrixBuilder.__init__` holds a `trading_core.VwapState()` + `trading_core.MarketStructureState()`; `push` computes the HLC3 typical paisa, feeds the bar to the Rust VWAP (`session_day = bar_day.toordinal()`, `is_pre_open` from the shared NSE helper, `tod_seconds` from the IST wall-clock; reset on the IST-date change) + to the Rust market structure (high/low/close paisa), and threads the resolved `vwap_paisa` + a `MarketStructureSignal` built from the four returned booleans into the snapshot. Also the n1 nit: `push`'s "u64 / bits 0-51" return docstring corrected to "u128 / bits 0-59 incl. the resurrected groups". O(1) per bar preserved (one Rust VWAP multiply-add + one O(k)-with-k-constant swing scan; the Rust state is O(1) memory — a bounded 2k+1 ring + scalar accumulators). **n2 confirmed:** the new bits 52/53/56-59 are NOT in `ANCHOR_DEPENDENT_MASK` (which only clears the pivot/PDH-PDL/Fib/day-type bits 6-29 + 48-51 on the first prior-day-less day), so the first-day `mask &= _NON_ANCHOR_MASK` correctly PRESERVES them (VWAP + market structure need no prior day). **DECISION (honest, stated explicitly):** the Python twin modules `brutex/indicators/{vwap,market_structure}.py` are LEFT UNTOUCHED — they remain the documented bit-for-bit reference with their own unit/property/bench tests + checkpoint serialization (whose internal-attribute introspection a pure Rust-delegating shim would break, beyond this PR's B1 scope). The PRODUCTION sweep path (stage1a) now drives RUST, which is the path the operator's "compute in Rust" directive targets + the bit-identical engine surface; the twins are proven bit-equal to Rust by the frozen golden vectors. Folding the twins onto the Rust pyclass is a flagged COMMON follow-up, NOT claimed done here. **THE LOAD-BEARING PROOF (anti-illusion gate):** a NEW `tests/integration/test_stage1a_vwap_bos_bits_fire.py` drives the ACTUAL `Stage1AMatrixBuilder.push` production path (never a mock) over a crafted 1-minute bar script engineered (k=2 fractal) to cross VWAP both ways AND print every BOS/CHoCH direction, and asserts EACH of bits 52/53/56-59 is SET on >=1 produced bar mask + the directions land at the engineered swing-lag-correct bars. **PROVEN it fails on origin/main + passes with the wiring:** with origin/main's `stage1a.py` swapped in (the Rust wheel + test held constant), 6 of the 15 tests FAIL (the headline all-six, the direction-at-bars, the VWAP-below proof, the first-bar seed, the degenerate-bar, the BOS-then-CHoCH) with `min() arg is empty` / bit-never-fired — exactly the dead path; restoring the wiring → all 15 pass (raw output in the PR). **Operator-mandated worst-case edge battery (each a real assertion through the production path):** first bar of session seeds VWAP from itself; a zero-volume bar yields no VWAP (no div-by-zero / NaN / crash) and a mid-session zero-volume spike never biases the VWAP; the 09:15 IST session reset wipes the prior day (a high day-1 VWAP cannot leak into a low day-2 → the day-2 bits equal a standalone day-2 run); a degenerate `high==low==close` bar has a well-defined typical price; a flat stream fires NONE of the six (not-always-on) + a monotonically-falling stream never sets close_above_vwap; a choppy stream prints a BOS strictly before a CHoCH; NO look-ahead (a prefix's masks are byte-identical with/without the tail — no future bar leaks into a past output); idempotent bit-for-bit on re-run; and an O(1)-SPACE assertion (the Rust market-structure ring + VWAP accumulators do not grow with bar count — 2000 bars vs 50 leave the same footprint). PLUS a hypothesis PROPERTY test (200 examples): for any random single-session stream the masks are deterministic on re-run AND close_above_vwap / close_below_vwap are never BOTH set on one bar (the VWAP-is-a-bracketed-mean invariant). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ bits 52/53/56-59 now FIRE in the real sweep, proven by a test that FAILS on main + PASSES here; ✅ the per-bar VWAP + BOS/CHoCH compute runs IN RUST (new PyO3 bindings) — the Python diff contains NO VWAP/BOS/CHoCH arithmetic, only the shared HLC3 snap + calls into the Rust state objects + reading their outputs; ✅ O(1) time + O(1) Rust-side space per bar; ✅ look-ahead-clean (non-repainting, verified by the prefix-equality oracle) + idempotent; ✅ `cargo fmt --check` 0 + `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --features python --all-targets -- -D warnings` 0 + `cargo test` 73 green (golden 400-case bit-identity intact); ✅ `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` + `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py` at 100% line+branch (with the existing engine suites) + the new integration test module itself 100% line+branch; ✅ `codegen_vocab.py --check` exit 0 (conditions.toml untouched — NO vocab change); ✅ ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` clean on every touched file; ✅ B2 (roll-aware `session_key` reset on a futures roll, vs the current IST-date reset) + M1 + D1 are SEPARATE PR-4 follow-ups, NOT in this PR (the VWAP is fed a constant `_DEFAULT_SESSION_KEY` so it resets only on the date change — byte-identical for the continuous spot-index series the engine sweeps today). **Files:** `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs`, `rust/trading-core/python/trading_core/__init__.py`, `brutex/engine/stage1a.py`, `tests/integration/test_stage1a_vwap_bos_bits_fire.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-STAGE1A-WIRE-VWAP-BOS-001. **Builds on** DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 (#1011 — PR-2, the native Rust VwapState + the `vwap_paisa` ABI field this populates), DEC-NIFTY-BOS-CHOCH-001 (#1012 — PR-2b, the native Rust MarketStructureState + the four market-structure ABI flags this populates), DEC-EMA-RUST-PORT-001 (#1014 — the Rust-delegating-state pattern this mirrors), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441 — the shared trading-core crate consumed bit-identically by BruteX + TickVault). (Ledger: #1020 — renumbered at merge from the PROVISIONAL #1015 after main absorbed #1015 DEC-RESAMPLER-MONOTONIC-GUARD-001 (#985) + #1017 DEC-EMPTY-DETECTOR-PRODUCTION-WIRING-001 (#980), with #1018/#1019 claimed by sibling PR-4 branches #987/#988; #1020 is the next free unique number.)

1021. **DEC-COVERAGE-DISCOVERY-STAGE1A-001 — add `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` to `COVERAGE_DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE` in `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py` so a stage1a-touching PR is not blocked by the auto-discovery per-module gate's single-stem mismatch** (2026-06-30; PROVISIONAL — parallel siblings; CI/test-tooling only, NO engine/scope/vocab/rate change, ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). **Why (confirmed root cause, file:line):** PR-4 B1 (#1020, DEC-STAGE1A-WIRE-VWAP-BOS-001) is the first PR to touch `stage1a.py` since the auto-discovery gate (DEC-CICD-GATE-HONESTY-001) landed, surfacing a LATENT stem-mismatch. The discovery gate maps a module ONLY to its stem-matching tests (`test_engine_stage1a*`), but stage1a.py's coverage is a multi-file-suite property: `test_engine_stage1a.py` covers the matrix builder + the resurrected VWAP/BOS bits (≤line 475), while the PRE-EXISTING walk-forward helpers (lines 652-659, 740, 751-753, 779-796, 846-882 — `trading_day_starts`, `WalkForwardSchedule.n_folds`, `_day_to_bar`, `_walk_forward_schedule_hash`, `build_walk_forward_schedule`) are covered by the differently-stemmed `test_engine_walk_forward.py`. So the discovery gate runs only `test_engine_stage1a.py` standalone → **82.41%** (175 stmts / 25 missed = the 25 walk-forward lines), failing the per-module 100% assertion even though the code is genuinely fully covered. **What shipped (one-line change + justification comment):** added `"brutex/engine/stage1a.py"` to `COVERAGE_DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE` with a comment EXACTLY mirroring the existing `app.py` / `pull_controller.py` / `db_view.py` entries (each excluded for the identical "100% is a curated multi-file-suite property, not a single-file one; duplicating the other files' coverage into the stem file would violate Golden Rule #11 COMMON" reason). **HONEST — this is NOT a coverage dodge (verified locally with the project `.venv`, raw lines in the PR):** stage1a.py stays FULLY gated at 100% by TWO independent backstops after the exclude: (1) the STATIC per-module engine gate in `ci.yml` (~line 379) runs the WHOLE `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` suite together at `--cov=brutex.engine --cov-fail-under=100` — measured `brutex/engine/stage1a.py 175 0 24 0 100.00%` (covers BOTH the walk-forward helpers AND the new VWAP/BOS lines, since `test_engine_walk_forward.py` is part of that glob); (2) the whole-package `--cov=brutex --cov-fail-under=100` floor runs the full suite (unit+integration+golden+property). Combined-suite reproduction (`test_engine_stage1a.py` + `test_engine_walk_forward.py` + `test_stage1a_vwap_bos_bits_fire.py`) measured `175 0 24 0 100.00%` — proving the code is genuinely 100%, the discovery-gate quirk is purely the stem-matcher. The new VWAP/BOS lines do NOT become ungated (the static unit-only engine gate alone reaches 100% on them). The exclude only removes the structurally-impossible single-stem 100% assertion for this multi-file-suite module — the COMPLEMENT honesty the gate's own docstring + Golden Rule #10 demand. **Files:** `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-COVERAGE-DISCOVERY-STAGE1A-001. **Builds on** DEC-CICD-GATE-HONESTY-001 (the discovery gate + the precedent `app.py`/`pull_controller.py`/`db_view.py` exclude entries this mirrors), DEC-STAGE1A-WIRE-VWAP-BOS-001 (#1020 — the PR that surfaced the latent mismatch). (Ledger: #1021 — renumbered at merge from the PROVISIONAL #1016, the unique number immediately after its sibling entry #1020 in this same PR.)
1019. **DEC-SESSION-FORCED-EXIT-001 — PR-4 (M1): the Stage-2 trade-simulation forced exit is now SESSION-AWARE — the boundary is the bar session's own close − 10min (15:20 IST on a regular day, the early close − 10min on a half-day / Muhurat session) instead of a hardcoded 15:20** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; signal-only Stage-2 sim; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why (the bug, verified on main):** `TradeSimWalker.push` (`brutex/engine/trade_sim.py`) called `is_forced_exit_bar(t, tf)` whose boundary constant `_FORCED_EXIT_SECONDS` is fixed to 15:20 IST. A session-aware `forced_exit_time_for_session` helper existed (`brutex/calendars/nse.py`) but was NOT wired into the sim. Consequence: an EVENING Diwali Muhurat session (e.g. 2021-11-04, 18:15-19:15 IST) force-exits on EVERY managed bar (every evening bar is "≥ 15:20") — so a Muhurat entry never even opens (its next bar reads as a forced-exit bar); an AFTERNOON Muhurat (2025-10-21, 13:45-14:45) and any future early-close half-day exit at the WRONG instant. backtest ≠ live on every non-regular session. **What shipped (single source of truth — call the existing helper, do NOT duplicate the time logic):** (1) NEW COMMON `nse.forced_exit_seconds_for_session(session) -> int` — the seconds-since-midnight IST twin of `forced_exit_time_for_session` (which it CALLS), in the same unit `is_forced_exit_bar` compares against, so the boundary is resolved once and fed straight in with no time→seconds re-derivation at the call site; exported from `brutex/calendars/__init__.py`. (2) `is_forced_exit_bar(t, tf_minutes, forced_exit_seconds=None)` gains an OPTIONAL boundary arg defaulting to `_FORCED_EXIT_SECONDS` (15:20) — so every pre-existing caller (`bar_metadata.py`) is BYTE-IDENTICAL; only a session-aware caller passes a non-default boundary. (3) `TradeSimWalker` resolves the bar's session boundary via a new `_forced_exit_seconds(bar_day_ist)` that calls `get_session(d)` → `forced_exit_seconds_for_session`, memoising the LAST IST date only (a 1-slot cache: a chronological feed re-resolves once per new day → **O(1) per bar, O(1) space**); `push` passes the resolved boundary into `is_forced_exit_bar`. A date with NO trading session (`get_session` → `None`) deterministically falls back to the 15:20 default (no crash — a real contiguous feed never hits this, a crafted feed must not raise). (4) **`ResidentTradeSim` (`brutex/engine/rust_trade_sim.py`) — the Rust-kernel seam — is made session-aware THE SAME WAY (hostile-review MAJOR-1, option (a)):** its construction-time `forced`-flag precompute (handed verbatim to the Rust `fno_math.ResidentSweepSim`) previously derived flags against the hardcoded 15:20, but its pure-Python fallback IS `simulate_trades` (now session-aware), so on a Muhurat/half-day the Rust path and the fallback would have SILENTLY DIVERGED — breaking the module's own "fallback is bit-identical" + "single source of truth for forced-exit flags" contracts. The precompute loop now resolves each bar's session boundary via the identical COMMON `get_session` → `forced_exit_seconds_for_session` → `is_forced_exit_bar`, with the SAME 1-slot last-IST-date cache (O(1) per bar), so the kernel flags MATCH `simulate_trades` on every session. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ regular-day behaviour is byte-for-byte 15:20 (regression-pinned); ✅ the session boundary is the EXISTING `forced_exit_time_for_session` logic (close − 10min), reused not duplicated; ✅ BOTH the Stage-2 `TradeSimWalker` (the live production sweep path) AND the `ResidentTradeSim` Rust-kernel seam are session-consistent — `rust_trade_sim` no longer diverges on a non-regular session (the MAJOR-1 inconsistency is CLOSED, not deferred); ✅ no real HALF_DAY date exists in 2021-2026 (NSE retired pre-festival half-days; `SessionType.HALF_DAY` is forward-compat), so the half-day case is proven via a genuine HALF_DAY `TradingSession` driven through the production `get_session` seam (a monkeypatch), AND the afternoon-Muhurat case proves the early-close path on real in-scope calendar data; ## DEC-CALENDAR-2020-HONEST-001 (2026-06-30)

1018. **DEC-CALENDAR-2020-HONEST-001 — PR-4/M3: honest 2020 trading-day handling for the prev-day + weekly Fibonacci anchors (loud-guard, NO fabricated holiday dates)** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; calendar-decision only; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; data-independent). **Why (real bug on `origin/main`, file:line):** the Track-1 data-pull floor is `2020-01-01` (`GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR`, CLAUDE.md §3, MIGRATION.md #722) but the hardcoded NSE/BSE holiday + Muhurat lists in `brutex/calendars/nse.py` only span `[HOLIDAY_COVERAGE_FIRST_YEAR, HOLIDAY_COVERAGE_LAST_YEAR]` = 2021-2026. The spot-anchor consumers used the UNGUARDED `is_trading_day` — `brutex/indicators/prev_day_ohlc.py` (`find_prev_trading_day` walk `:93`, `lookup_prev_day_ohlc` guard `:120`) + `brutex/indicators/weekly_anchors.py` (`rolling_weekly_anchor` `:111`, `weekly_static_anchor` `:172`). Proven on main: `is_trading_day(date(2020,3,10))` returns `True` and `find_prev_trading_day(date(2020,3,11))` SILENTLY returns `2020-03-10` (the calendar weekday NSE observed as the 2020 Holi trading holiday) as the "prior trading day" — a silent WRONG verdict, and the "automatic Muhurat exclusion" claim does not hold pre-2021. **Honesty decision — OPTION (b) the LOUD GUARD, NOT fabricated dates (Golden Rule #1):** I did NOT add a 2020 NSE holiday/Muhurat list. I could not verify a full 2020 NSE holiday circular from an in-repo source or cite one here, and `nse.py` already documents the project policy "we do NOT hallucinate the missing-year holiday dates; we surface the gap honestly" (DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-001). So the four trading-day decision points + the shared backward walk are wired to the EXISTING strict `is_trading_day_checked` (which `nse.py` already provided for exactly this case), which raises `HolidayDataUnavailableError` for an out-of-coverage WEEKDAY rather than guess. A weekend / leap-day-Saturday / special-weekend-session resolves WITHOUT raising (the answer is data-complete independent of the holiday list); only the genuinely-ambiguous out-of-coverage weekday is loud. **What shipped:** `prev_day_ohlc.py` + `weekly_anchors.py` import/use `is_trading_day_checked` in place of `is_trading_day` (4 call sites + the shared `find_prev_trading_day` walk); docstrings updated; `nse.py` module docstring updated to record these consumers are now WIRED (other unguarded `is_trading_day` callers, e.g. the dashboard pre-open report, remain a deferred opt-in follow-up). **Single source of truth + O(1):** the coverage span is still DERIVED from the per-year frozensets (`HOLIDAY_COVERAGE_{FIRST,LAST}_YEAR = min/max(h.year for h in ALL_HOLIDAYS)`), so the guard can never drift from the data; `is_trading_day_checked` is O(1) (one integer-range test + one `frozenset` membership) and O(1) space — no new state. **Proof (anti-illusion, both directions verified):** NEW `tests/unit/test_calendar_2020_honest.py` drives the REAL production functions (`is_trading_day_checked` / `find_prev_trading_day` / `lookup_prev_day_ohlc` / `rolling_weekly_anchor` / `weekly_static_anchor`) over every requested extreme edge case — a 2020 weekend (honest `False`, no raise), the 2020-02-29 leap-day Saturday (honest `False`), the 2019-12-31 / 2020-01-01 year boundary (loud), a 2020 weekday (loud), an uncovered FUTURE year 2030 (loud), prev-day + both weekly anchors across a 2020 holiday (loud, never a silent holiday-as-prev-day), and 2021-2026 unchanged regressions (incl. `find_prev_trading_day(2021-01-04) == 2021-01-01` does NOT walk into 2020). Verified the 7 new 2020-honest assertions FAIL on `origin/main` (stash the `brutex/` fix → "DID NOT RAISE" / silent True) and PASS with the fix; the 14 regression/edge assertions pass both ways. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ option (b) loud-guard chosen — NO 2020 holiday date fabricated; ✅ in-coverage 2021-2026 behaviour byte-identical (the unguarded `is_trading_day` itself is UNCHANGED — only these anchor consumers route through the strict variant); ✅ touched-module 100% line + 100% branch (`brutex.indicators.prev_day_ohlc` 44/14, `brutex.indicators.weekly_anchors` 66/28, `brutex.calendars.nse` 123/24, all 0 missing); ✅ ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` clean on the touched files; ✅ existing prev_day/weekly/calendar/futures-roll suites (196) + calendar property suites (13) green — no regression; ✅ this fixes ONLY the 2020 anchor path, the dashboard pre-open report + any other unguarded caller are a flagged follow-up, NOT claimed done. **Files:** `brutex/indicators/prev_day_ohlc.py`, `brutex/indicators/weekly_anchors.py`, `brutex/calendars/nse.py` (docstring), `tests/unit/test_calendar_2020_honest.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-CALENDAR-2020-HONEST-001. **Builds on** DEC-CALENDAR-HARDEN-001 (the strict `is_trading_day_checked` + `HolidayDataUnavailableError` + the derived coverage span this PR wires), DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001 (#722 — the 2020 pull floor that created the gap). 1015. **DEC-RESAMPLER-MONOTONIC-GUARD-001 — PR-4 M2: the v1 OHLCV resampler now REJECTS a non-increasing 1-minute bar (out-of-order OR exact duplicate) with an O(1)-per-bar feed-integrity guard, instead of silently mis-bucketing it** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; data-INDEPENDENT, synthetic-`CandleBar` tests only; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change). **Why (real bug on main):** `brutex/feed/resampler.py::resample_bars` trusts that its input is sorted strictly-ascending and re-sorts NOTHING (`resampler.py:39`), but it added NO ordering guard — the bucketing loop checked only tz-awareness then opened a new bucket whenever `bucket_start` changed. So a DUPLICATE timestamp summed the offending bar's volume twice into the SAME bucket (e.g. two 10-volume bars at one instant → a corrupt 20), and an OUT-OF-ORDER bar that fell back into an already-emitted bucket window opened a SPURIOUS SECOND output bar with wrong OHLC. This is the SYMMETRIC hazard to the missing-bar policy and to the already-guarded execution path. **Policy (justified from the codebase, NOT invented):** RAISE `ResampleError`. Evidence: (a) `resample_bars` already raises `ResampleError` for EVERY other input-contract violation (unknown interval, up-sampling, non-integer-multiple, naive tz), so the ordering violation joins the SAME error style — no new error style introduced; (b) the sibling feed-integrity guard `brutex/execution/driver.py::BacktestDriver.run` (`driver.py:155-160`) already rejects `this_ts <= prev_ts` (out-of-order OR duplicate) by RAISING `NonMonotonicBarError` — so "raise on non-monotonic" is the ESTABLISHED feed convention, not a silent dedup; (c) a silent dedup-keep-first here would itself be an illusion (it would HIDE corrupt vendor data the aggregate exists to faithfully reflect). **What shipped:** in the bucketing loop, an O(1) guard tracks ONLY the previous bar's raw timestamp (`prev_ts`, never a growing set → O(1) time + O(1) extra space per bar) and raises `ResampleError("...strictly-increasing...")` the moment `bar.timestamp <= prev_ts`, BEFORE the offending bar is bucketed (so no partial corrupt result is ever returned). Module + `resample_bars` docstrings updated to state the strictly-ascending contract + the new raise. **Normal input byte-identical:** the guard never fires on a clean strictly-increasing stream — the existing `tests/unit/test_feed_resampler.py` (+ the cross-instrument golden) stay GREEN unchanged, and a 600-bar regression asserts field-by-field equality to an independent epoch-floor reference fold. **PROOF (no illusion — verified both directions):** NEW `tests/unit/test_feed_resampler_monotonic_guard.py` (13 tests) drives the REAL `resample_bars` over every extreme edge case — empty / single bar (no crash, guard never fires) · exact duplicate (volume NOT double-counted: a sanity floor proves the suppressed 20 really WAS the double-count) · duplicate-then-valid (equal-then-greater) · strictly-decreasing (fully reversed) · one out-of-order bar mid-stream · out-of-order back into a closed bucket · no-partial-output-before-raise · large 600-bar regression (byte-identical) · sub-second-distinct-but-unique (NOT a duplicate, passes) · a hypothesis property test (ANY non-strictly-increasing offset list raises; ANY clean stream succeeds + conserves total volume). The 8 bad-input assertions FAIL on origin/main ("DID NOT RAISE ResampleError" — the falsifying example `offsets=[0, 0]` is the silent double-count) and PASS with the guard (stash→fail, restore→pass, raw output captured). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ O(1) per bar + O(1) extra space (only `prev_ts` tracked, no re-sort); ✅ raise policy justified from two in-repo precedents, not guessed; ✅ clean-input output byte-identical (existing suites + golden unchanged-green); ✅ `brutex/feed/resampler.py` 100% line + 100% branch locally (53 stmts / 22 branch, 0 missing); ✅ ruff check + ruff format --check clean (whole `brutex`), `mypy --strict` clean on the touched module + the new test; data-INDEPENDENT — no real-lake run claimed; this is the `feed.resampler` guard ONLY (the session-anchored `data.tf_resampler` is a separate path, NOT touched). **Files:** `brutex/feed/resampler.py`, `tests/unit/test_feed_resampler_monotonic_guard.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-RESAMPLER-MONOTONIC-GUARD-001. **Builds on** the feed-integrity convention of the execution driver's `NonMonotonicBarError` guard. 1031. **DEC-INTERIOR-GAP-DETECT-001 / DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-REPULL-001 / DEC-SINK-DEDUP-COUNT-001 — PR-A (fetch-completeness honesty): a SUCCESS spot window with a CONFIRMED interior multi-session hole OR a trailing truncation is DEMOTED to a re-pullable ledger status (bounded), and the sink reports the DEDUPED bars-added count, not the input batch size** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; one of two sibling PRs from the triaged fetch-path edge-case sweep — entry numbered **#1031** because main's ledger now reaches **#1030** (after sibling PR #991 DEC-COMBO-DECODER-001 took #1028) so the next free unique numbers are 1031/1032/1033; the DEC-ID validator is uniqueness-based so the numeric gap is fine). **Honest severity (read first):** these are MED/LOW data-completeness-honesty fixes — **NONE is a crash or a HIGH bug.** The adversarial triage DISPROVED the alleged HIGH (a non-`Mapping` candle payload → raw `TypeError` → whole-pull crash) against the actually-installed `growwapi` SDK (its `get_historical_candles` returns `dict(...)` on success or RAISES; it can never hand back `None`/a scalar), and it disproved the whole error-classification cluster. The only real surface is data-completeness honesty + a handful of low-probability vendor-corruption guards (PR-B). **The three fixes (each a confirmed gap, file:line):** **(1) interior-gap (#1, MED) — `data/window_status.py:88-92` + `ingest.py` `ledger.record` on `raw_bars>0`:** a window bookended by real bars with a multi-SESSION interior hole settled `SUCCESS` (skippable) and was never re-pulled. NEW pure `brutex/data/interior_gap_detect.py` (`classify_interior_gap` + the observe-only `observe_interior_gap`) detects the LONGEST contiguous run of bar-LESS NSE trading sessions strictly INTERIOR to `[first_bar, last_bar]`, flagging ONLY a run `> INTERIOR_GAP_TOLERANCE_SESSIONS` (env-tunable, default 5) — so a legitimately low-liquidity-but-continuous window is NEVER flagged (the signal is a long contiguous hole, NOT bar density); out-of-NSE-calendar-coverage years honestly ABSTAIN (Golden Rule #1). **(2) partial-window promote (#3, MED) — `data/partial_window_detect.py` (was observe-only, DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-DETECT-001 #1008):** `observe_partial_window` now RETURNS its verdict (back-compat — every prior caller ignored the return), so the spot tail can DEMOTE a confirmed trailing-truncation, preserving the existing covered-year/liquidity/live-edge/at-expiry guards so it never false-flags. **(3) dup-bars accounting (#6, LOW) — `data/sink.py`:** the honest DEDUPED bar count is now surfaced as a NEW `SinkAppendResult.bars_net_new` (summed from a NEW per-partition `WriteResult.bars_added` — fresh write adds all, a merge adds only new timestamps, a keep-first conflict adds 0), while `bars_appended` STAYS the INPUT count (`len(bars)`). **Hostile-review MAJOR-1 folded:** an earlier draft made `bars_appended` itself the deduped count, which SILENTLY flipped three downstream `> 0` control-flow gates that read it as "did this call carry data?" — `spot_daily_resample`'s derived/no-minute split (a latest-wins daily self-heal sets `rewrite=True` but `added=0` → false `no_minute`), and `pull_controller`'s completed/no-data split (an idempotent re-pull → `bars_appended=0` → a real-data symbol mis-flips `completed → no_data`). Keeping `bars_appended` as the input count leaves every gate byte-identical; the deduped figure lives in the separate `bars_net_new` for an honest ledger/report column. **NO data change — the on-disk merge was always idempotent; this only ADDS an honest count field, changing NO control flow.** **The DEMOTE mechanism (bounded, data-safe):** a NEW `degraded` flag threaded `classify_window_status(raw_bars, error_type, degraded=)` → `WindowLedger.record(degraded=, degraded_reason=)`: a clean bars-returning `SUCCESS` flagged incomplete is recorded `FAILED` (re-pullable, NOT in `_SKIPPABLE`) with the completeness reason (`INTERIOR_GAP` / `SUSPECTED_PARTIAL`) as `last_error`, AND the `empty_streak` is BUMPED so it settles `SKIPPED` after `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` consecutive degraded pulls — exactly REUSING the existing genuine-EMPTY bounded machinery, so the re-pull can NEVER loop forever (the universe pull still converges) and the stored bars are KEPT the whole time (the demotion only re-opens the window for completion). A re-pull that comes back COMPLETE records a clean `SUCCESS` (streak reset). **Hostile-review MAJOR-2 folded:** the DEMOTION is gated to a DENSE INDEX (`instrument.is_index` — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX) on the FETCHED `1minute` interval ONLY. The spot pull ALSO fans out over the ~750 REFERENCE_ONLY underlyings (illiquid NTM small/mid/micro-caps + delisted/suspended names), where a multi-session no-print stretch is legitimately sparse-but-complete — demoting those would be a re-pull storm (the exact false-positive class the options exclusion already guards against), so the false-positive-safety rationale only holds for the dense indices. For a non-index spot symbol the WARNING still fires (observe-only visibility) but the window is NEVER demoted/re-pulled. The derived `1day` (resampled from 1-minute, never vendor-fetched, DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001) is also exempt. **Hostile-review MAJOR-3 folded (the dry-run regression):** the demotion is OPT-IN behind a `detect_completeness_gaps: bool = False` flag threaded `ingest_spot` -> `run_groww_spot_ingest` -> `run_groww_spot_ingest_with_retry`, set `True` ONLY at the two REAL-VENDOR production sites (the dashboard `pull_controller` live pull + the CLI live pull `detect_completeness_gaps=not dry_run`). Without this gate a `brutex fetch --dry-run` would FALSE-RED: its `_DryRunGrowwSpotAdapter` -> `synthetic_spot_bars` returns a few bars on each window's FIRST day regardless of span, so every wide 1-minute window would classify as truncated -> FAILED -- exactly the dry-run whose purpose is to prove the pipe runs GREEN. Defaulting OFF keeps dry-run / synthetic / unit-test pulls byte-identical (the observe-only WARNING still fires regardless -- visibility is never gated, only the re-pull action). **PROOF (no illusion):** NEW `tests/unit/test_interior_gap_detect.py` (17 tests; the module at 100% line+branch) drives the REAL classifier over continuous / sparse-but-continuous / small-interior-blip / large-interior-hole / leading-trailing-density / out-of-calendar-coverage / env-tunable cases; NEW `TestDegradedDemotion` (window_ledger) pins the demote→FAILED→bounded-SKIPPED-at-threshold + the complete-repull-resets-to-SUCCESS + EMPTY-ignored paths; NEW `TestBarsAddedDedup` + `TestParquetBarSinkDedupCount` prove a full re-pull reports `bars_net_new==0` while `bars_appended` STAYS the input count; NEW `TestIngestSpotCompletenessRepull` drives the END-TO-END spine — a gappy `1minute` INDEX window demotes to `INTERIOR_GAP`, a truncated one to `SUSPECTED_PARTIAL`, a complete one settles `SUCCESS` with no warning, a `1day` window is never demoted, AND a non-index equity is WARNed-but-NOT-demoted (MAJOR-2 regression); the `observe_partial_window` return-value path is pinned. A hostile-reviewer pass on the diff returned FIX-FIRST with two MAJORs (the dedup-gate flip + the illiquid-universe demotion) — BOTH folded as above before this entry. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ MED/LOW completeness-honesty only — no crash/HIGH bug fixed (the alleged HIGH was DISPROVEN against the real SDK); ✅ bounded re-pull (settles after the threshold — no infinite loop), data-safe (bars kept), `1day` exempt; ✅ no scope/vocab/rate/engine change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, the F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY (this PR touches ONLY the SPOT spine; the F&O `option_ingest` partial-window observe stays observe-only, an explicit non-goal here); ✅ every touched `brutex/` file at 100% line + 100% branch (`interior_gap_detect` 66/18, `partial_window_detect` 83/30, `window_status` 58/6, `window_ledger` 161/44, `sink` 47/8, `parquet_writer` 148/20, `adapters/groww/ingest` 228/54, all 0 missing); ## DEC-COMBO-DECODER-001 (2026-06-30)

1028. **DEC-COMBO-DECODER-001 — PR-4b/2: a dual-layer (Simple + Pro) human-readable decoder that turns any winning combo (a raw u128 condition mask) into TWO plain-English readings of the SAME rule — a beginner Simple sentence + a trader-precise Pro sentence — plus a derived market-regime label** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; READ-SIDE ONLY — no engine/vocab/lake/pull/rate change; data-INDEPENDENT, synthetic-mask tests only). **What shipped (NEW `brutex/dashboard/combo_decoder.py`):** a pure, O(1)-per-condition decoder `decode_combo(condition_mask: int, direction: str, timeframe: str) -> ComboExplanation`. The `ComboExplanation` dataclass carries (a) `conditions` — one `ConditionLabel{bit, technical_name, pro_label, simple_label}` per SET bit, in ascending bit order; (b) `simple_sentence` — the beginner everyday-words reading; (c) `pro_sentence` — the trader-precise reading (`close>VWAP`, `near R1`, `Fib 50%`, `CHoCH↑`, …); (d) `regime_label` (uptrend / downtrend / reversal / breakout / sideways / volatile / mixed) DERIVED from the set bits by read-side combination rules (NO new bits); (e) `direction_label` ("Buy" / "Sell"). It works on a RAW condition mask — it does NOT depend on PR \#990's StrategySpec. **The dual-label dictionary (operator-approved):** every one of the 60 vocabulary conditions (the canonical `NAME_TO_BIT` names from `brutex/vocabulary/bits.py` — the codegen'd manifest, the ONE source of truth) maps to BOTH a Pro term and a Simple phrase (e.g. `ema20_above_ema200` → "EMA20>EMA200" / "trend is up"; `near_pivot_s1` → "near S1" / "at a floor (support)"; `near_fib_50` → "Fib 50%" / "at the halfway bounce zone"; `close_above_vwap` → "close>VWAP" / "price beats the day's average price"; `choch_bullish` → "CHoCH↑" / "trend just flipped up"). **CRITICAL sync guarantee (no silent gaps):** a coverage test asserts the dual-label dict keys are EXACTLY `set(NAME_TO_BIT.keys())` (all 60) AND the four sentence-composition groups (trend → level → candle/structure → time) partition all 60 names exactly once — so a future condition appended to `conditions.toml`/`bits.py` WITHOUT a label (or left out of every group) FAILS the build. **Regime derivation (read-side rules, honest precedence):** reversal = a CHoCH bit NOT confirming the EMA trend (a CHoCH ↑ concordant with `ema20_above_ema200` is a CONTINUATION → uptrend, NOT reversal — this honest precedence is what makes the operator's example combo read `uptrend` as approved); breakout = any BOS bit; volatile = large body OR outside day; sideways = inside_day AND a small-body/doji/alternating bar; uptrend/downtrend = the EMA-trend bit (a both-set conflict → mixed); else mixed. **The operator's example combo decodes (verified on the real path):** mask = {close_above_vwap, ema20_above_ema200, near_pivot_r1, near_fib_50, choch_bullish, early_morning}, direction long, 15m → regime `uptrend`, direction `Buy`; Simple = "Buy on 15m when trend is up, price beats the day's average price, at a ceiling (resistance), at the halfway bounce zone, trend just flipped up and first hour (uptrend)."; Pro = "Buy 15m [uptrend]: EMA20>EMA200, close>VWAP, near R1, Fib 50%, CHoCH↑ and early morning." (both FROZEN as a golden). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule \#10):** ✅ O(1) per condition — a bounded scan of the at-most-60 bits, independent of bar count (bits ≥ TOTAL_CONDITIONS / forward-compat headroom are IGNORED, proven by a high-bit test); ✅ READ-SIDE ONLY — no engine/vocab/lake mutation, `git diff --name-only` is the new module + its test + this ledger entry only; ✅ the empty mask (0) is an HONEST direction-only sentence ("Buy on 15m (no conditions)."), never a fabricated rule; 🟡 the Simple phrasing is operator-approved wording, NOT a vendor-defined taxonomy — awkward edges (e.g. `near_fib_618`/`near_fib_786` both read "deep retrace zone"; `near_fib_127/161/200/261` all read "extension target") are deliberate beginner simplifications, not bugs; 🟡 the regime is a HEURISTIC label for explainability, not a tradable signal. **Coverage/gates (verified 2026-06-30 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv + the maturin-built `trading_core` wheel):** `brutex/dashboard/combo_decoder.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (66 stmt / 16 branch, 0 missing), 84 tests pass — `tests/unit/test_dashboard_combo_decoder.py` (the 60-name + group-partition sync tests, the frozen operator-example golden, one crafted mask per regime rule incl. the concordant-CHoCH continuation case, edge cases [empty/full mask, both directions, single-condition no-`and`-join, high-bit-ignored, group ordering], and a parametrized per-name decode of all 60); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean on both files (isolated `--follow-imports=silent`; the only package-wide mypy errors are pre-existing `growwapi`-stub issues in unrelated `adapters/groww/auth.py`/`reauth.py`, present on origin/main, environment-specific); `pyright` 0 errors 0 warnings (whitebox test uses the repo's `# pyright: reportPrivateUsage=none` convention to read the internal label/group tables). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/combo_decoder.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_combo_decoder.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-COMBO-DECODER-001. **Builds on** `brutex/vocabulary/bits.py` (DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 — the 60-name `NAME_TO_BIT` manifest this keys off) and `brutex/vocabulary/describe.py` (the existing family-grouped mask decoder this complements with human labels). (Ledger: \#1028 — renumbered from \#1027 to avoid a same-cycle collision with sibling PR \#990 DEC-STRATEGYSPEC-CORE-001, which was simultaneously re-synced to \#1027 (next free above main's max #1026); giving this entry \#1028 keeps both PRs mergeable in either order. Earlier history: originally \#1026, bumped when DEC-FETCH-PER-WINDOW-GUARANTEE-001 \#1026 merged to main first. Per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 the entry takes a free unique number re-checked immediately before push; the DEC-ID is uniqueness-based, not strictly sequential.)
1038. **DEC-FETCH-PARSER-HARDENING-001 — PR-B (fetch-path resilience): three CONFIRMED non-crash fetch-path resilience gaps closed — drop a vendor bar dated past the requested window-end, halt gracefully on a lake-OOM during the MERGE write, and ISOLATE a corrupt-partition error to one symbol in the async pipeline instead of tripping the whole pool** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; sibling of PR-A DEC-INTERIOR-GAP-DETECT-001). **Honest severity (read first):** these are LOW-probability vendor-corruption / resilience guards — **NONE is a crash or a HIGH bug.** The adversarial triage DISPROVED the alleged HIGH (a non-`Mapping` candle payload → whole-pull crash) against the actually-installed `growwapi` SDK. **SCOPE NOTE (Golden Rule #2 — single source of truth):** this PR's ORIGINAL plan also included a #5 negative-price reject + a #8 nan/inf loud-reject in `candle_fields.py`/`models.py`, but main merged DEC-ADVERSARIAL-HARDENING-001 (#1029, PR #993) FIRST, which ALREADY shipped overlapping handling under the AUTHORITATIVE OPPOSITE philosophy — a negative price is treated like zero/empty (`has_no_price` → graceful SKIP, NOT loud-reject) and `to_price` already rejects non-finite. So #5/#8 are SUPERSEDED and were DROPPED from this PR (the `candle_fields.py`/`models.py`/`parser.py` files reset to main verbatim) rather than re-implemented or fought; this PR keeps ONLY the three genuinely non-overlapping fixes below. **The three fixes (each a confirmed gap, file:line):** **(1) future-timestamp drop (#9) — `adapters/ingest_common.py`:** NEW pure `drop_bars_after(bars, window_end)` drops every bar whose IST date is STRICTLY AFTER the window's end (a bar exactly ON the end-boundary date is KEPT), so a vendor bar dated past the requested window-end is never stored; wired into BOTH the spot tail (`adapters/groww/ingest.py`) AND the F&O/option tail (`adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`) at the same point each tail assembles its window's bars. The comparison is on the IST calendar date (the lake partitions by IST month), so the UTC→IST boundary is handled by the shared `to_ist`/date helpers. **(2) lake-OOM on the MERGE write (#4) — `data/parquet_writer.py`:** `_merge_write`'s read-modify-write body (the existing-partition read + the 2dp-snap merge + the sort) is now wrapped in the COMMON `lake_write_guard()` (DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 #885), so an ENOSPC/`MemoryError` during the MERGE — not just the FRESH render #885 already guarded — maps to a `LakeWriteHalt` graceful pull halt; a non-`ENOSPC` `OSError` is NOT mis-escalated (the guard re-raises it as-is). **(3) corrupt-partition async isolation (#10) — `adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`:** NEW pure `_is_pool_isolatable(exc)` + the async consumer's `_process_one` now CATCHES a per-symbol-quarantinable `BruteXError` (e.g. a `WriterError` from ONE corrupt existing Parquet partition's merge READ) → logs `fetch_pipeline.window_quarantined` + advances the window (leaving its ledger row UNSETTLED → re-pulled next pull) WITHOUT setting the pool-wide `_stopped` latch, so one bad file can never freeze the whole fan-out — mirroring the SYNCHRONOUS spine's per-symbol quarantine. A pull-wide STOP (`LakeWriteHalt`/`DailyQuotaExceeded`/`QuotaInvariantError`, the `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` set) AND any non-`BruteXError` genuine code bug (`ValueError`/`KeyError`/…) STILL trip the pool, exactly as before — a real bug is NEVER silently swallowed. The heavy `quota_tracker` import is lazy (the async-pipeline import-cost contract) and a unit test pins the isolatable predicate against `run_ingest._GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` so the two lists can never drift. **PROOF (no illusion):** NEW `TestDropBarsAfter` (on-boundary-keep / strictly-after-drop / IST-date-boundary / empty) + future-bar-drop tests in BOTH spine suites; NEW `test_merge_loop_oom_halts` (an ENOSPC injected into the merge body raises `LakeWriteHalt`, a plain OSError is NOT escalated); NEW `TestIsPoolIsolatable` (WriterError/generic-BruteXError isolatable → True; LakeWriteHalt/quota/ValueError/KeyError → False; matches `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS`) + an end-to-end `test_isolatable_writer_error_quarantines_window_and_does_not_trip` that drives `_process_one` with a `WriterError`-raising tail and asserts the window is quarantined (one `fetch_pipeline.window_quarantined` WARNING) + the pool is NOT tripped (drain returns cleanly, the next healthy window still processes) + a `test_corrupt_partition_isolates_one_symbol_not_the_pool` integration test through the REAL spine. Also de-flaked the pre-existing main hung-write test `test_one_wedged_shard_does_not_freeze_a_healthy_shard` (it fails deterministically on a contended runner at the 0.2 s write-deadline because the HEALTHY shard's write exceeds it — widened the deadline 0.2→0.5 s + drain-join 1.0→4.0 s, same ordering invariant, same fix as PR-A). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ LOW-probability resilience guards only — no crash/HIGH bug fixed (the alleged HIGH was DISPROVEN against the real SDK); ✅ `drop_bars_after` keeps the on-boundary bar + drops only strictly-after, never a real in-window bar (proven both directions); ✅ the async isolation NEVER swallows a genuine code bug (it still trips the pool) and never loses data (a quarantined window's ledger row stays unsettled → re-pulled, keep-first idempotent sink); ✅ no scope/vocab/rate/engine change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, the F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; ✅ every touched `brutex/` file at 100% line + 100% branch (`ingest_common` 288/66, `parquet_writer` 180/24, `fetch_pipeline` 280/76, `adapters/groww/ingest` 223/54, `adapters/groww/option_ingest` 314/82, all 0 missing); ✅ ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / `pyright` (0 errors) clean on every touched file; ✅ #5/#8 DROPPED as superseded by main's #1029 (NOT re-implemented — the candle_fields/models/parser files are byte-identical to main). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`, `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `tests/unit/test_ingest_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py`, `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer.py`, `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry), `CLAUDE.md` (decision block). **Decision ID:** DEC-FETCH-PARSER-HARDENING-001. **Builds on** DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 (#885 — the `lake_write_guard`/`LakeWriteHalt` this extends to the merge write), DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 (#999 — the async fetch pipeline + per-window deferral this isolation pattern joins), DEC-ADVERSARIAL-HARDENING-001 (#1029 — the merged negative-price/nan-finite handling that SUPERSEDED this PR's dropped #5/#8). (Ledger: #1038 = the next free unique number above main's current max #1037 after PR-A's #1031 and the #994 movers PR's #1034–#1037 all merged, so this PR-B entry carries no number collision, per the no-strict-contiguity uniqueness rule of DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001. Renumbered from a provisional #1034 when #994 landed that slot on main.)
## DEC-MOVERS-CALENDAR-TIERS-001 (2026-06-30)

1034. **DEC-MOVERS-CALENDAR-TIERS-001 — the `/movers` Options Near/Next/Far + Weekly/Monthly tiers are now driven by the AUTHORITATIVE vendor expiry calendar (`registry.duckdb`), not the sparse lake-partition set, PLUS three folded hardening fixes: a metric-pill sort reset, an opt-in Top-Volume floor, and a broadened post-pull warmer grid** (2026-06-30; READ-ONLY dashboard + pull-PLANNING warm only — NO lake-schema/stored-bar/rate-cap/vocab change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3). Four consolidated `/movers` fixes, each with its own decision sub-ID:

   **FIX 1 — DEC-MOVERS-CALENDAR-TIERS-001 (PRIMARY, correctness):** the Options tier classification (`brutex/dashboard/movers_options.py` `_tier_expiry_by_underlying` / `_monthly_expiries`) derived the Near/Next/Far + Weekly/Monthly tiers from the STORED lake candle partitions, so a sparsely-pulled lake MISLABELS a tier — the operator REPORTED a wrong "Far" expiry (a late August date) on a lake that was missing intermediate July weeklies. **Root cause (file:line):** `compute_options_candidates` discovered the per-underlying expiry universe ONLY from `_discover_options` (the on-disk `bars/<exch>/FNO/…` set); when an intermediate expiry has no pulled candles the lake-only serial ordering collapses — the Weekly/Monthly track classification reads the WRONG set, so a tier can land on a wrong serial expiry OR skip past a real one. **Fix:** the FULL vendor calendar already exists at read time in `registry.duckdb` (`brutex/data/registry_store.py` `RegistryStore.list_expiries`, populated from the vendor `get_expiries` list by `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py::pull_expiries_contracts` in the production `/pull-pipeline` metadata phase). NEW `load_registry_expiries(registry_path, *, exchange=None)` reads the full per-underlying calendar (path resolved via `db_view.registry_path_for(store.path)` → `<lake_root>/registry.duckdb`); `_tier_expiry_by_underlying` gains an optional `calendar_expiries` map + a NEW pure `_tier_universe` that uses the calendar's `>= on_date` set as the AUTHORITATIVE expiry universe for tier+track classification when present, else falls back to the lake-partition set. `_monthly_expiries` (max-per-calendar-month) is CORRECT once fed the full calendar (full July {07,14,21,28-Jul} → 28-Jul=monthly, 07/14/21-Jul=weekly) — kept verbatim. **GRACEFUL FALLBACK (Golden Rule #1):** an ABSENT / EMPTY / UNREADABLE registry (a CLI-only-pulled lake, or a `RegistryError` from a stale cache) yields `None` → the current lake-partition derivation, so those lakes are never broken. **HONEST NO-DATA:** a calendar expiry positioned as a tier but with ZERO pulled contract candles is surfaced honestly — `OptionsCandidates.calendar_only_expiry` flags it and `build_options_payload` emits a "the {tier} expiry is on the vendor calendar … but NO option contract candles have been pulled for it yet" note, instead of silently skipping to a wrong serial expiry. The route (`app.py::api_movers`) memoises the calendar per write-generation in a NEW `_options_calendar_cache` (REUSES the COMMON `MoversSnapshotCache` — a metadata pull bumps the generation → re-read), keyed per exchange, and threads it into both the live `compute_options_candidates` and the post-pull warmer. **WHAT THE TESTS PROVE (honest — Golden Rule #1; the tests do NOT reconstruct the operator's exact real lake, which we do not have):** `TestCalendarDrivenTiers::test_operator_case_weekly_near_next_far_07_14_21` proves the FIX — fed a representative full registry calendar {07,14,21,28-Jul,+Aug} as-of 2025-06-25, the calendar-driven path yields Weekly Near/Next/Far = 07/14/21-Jul with 28-Jul classified monthly (the CORRECT full-calendar tiers); `test_without_calendar_the_sparse_lake_mislabels_far` DEMONSTRATES THE BUG CLASS on a simplified sparse lake {07-Jul, 04-Aug} (track='all'/'weekly') where the lake-only derivation skips/mislabels the Far weekly, and the calendar path corrects it. Supporting: `TestTierUniverse` (calendar-wins / underlying-absent / empty-set / `>= on_date` filter fallbacks) + `TestLoadRegistryExpiries` (missing→None, empty→None, populated, exchange-filter, `RegistryError`→None) + integration `TestCalendarDrivenTiersEndToEnd` (sparse July lake + a real RegistryStore round-trip → Far weekly = calendar 21-Jul honest-empty; registry-less fallback) + a route test (`/api/v1/movers` with a real registry → "vendor calendar" note).

   **FIX 2 — DEC-MOVERS-SORT-RESET-001 (frontend):** `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html` — the metric-pill onclick set `state.category` but never reset the client-side column sort, so a manual VOLUME sort persisted across metric-tab switches (the asset-tab handler already reset it). FIX: the pill onclick now sets `state.sort = {idx:null,dir:1}` and calls `renderHead()`, so the sort + the stale ▼ arrow reset to the new tab's server ranking.

   **FIX 3 — DEC-MOVERS-MIN-VOLUME-001 (opt-in Top-Volume floor):** a NEW optional `?min_volume=` floor (route default `0` = byte-identical) filters the "Top Volume" ranking to `volume >= min_volume` (on top of the long-standing zero-volume exclusion).
