1030. **DEC-FIB-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-001 — PR-4b sub-PR 3: the 3 Fibonacci strategies as ONE-LINE DATA declarations (strategy = DATA) — a symbol-agnostic `StrategyDefinition` registry where adding a strategy is ONE `register(...)` line, ONE strategy per Fib ANCHOR, with DIRECTION (Long/Short) a SWEPT DIMENSION inside each (NOT a separate strategy), runnable against the REAL anchor primitives and rendered through the FROZEN decoder** (2026-06-30; PROVISIONAL — main moves, renumber at push if #1030 is taken; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; declaration/registry/read-side ONLY — NO `brutex/` engine, lake-schema, stored-bar, scope, vocab, or rate-cap change; NO Rust touched — the frozen `trading_core` 400-case golden is byte-untouched). **The operator decree (strategy-as-DATA + the #1030 CORRECTION):** there are exactly **3 unique strategies** — the 3 Fib ANCHORS (prev_day, rolling_weekly, weekly_static) — and **DIRECTION (Long/Short) is a SWEPT DIMENSION inside each strategy, NOT a separate strategy**: the brute-force sweep tries BOTH directions on each anchor, exactly as it sweeps the condition mask + timeframe (this supersedes the first draft's 6 `_long`/`_short` definitions). Adding a strategy is ONE entry, no rewrite; symbol-agnostic; readable; no illusion — every field is USED. **WRAP, not extend (the load-bearing design decision):** the shared Rust `trading_core.StrategySpec` (DEC-STRATEGYSPEC-CORE-001 #1027) is FROZEN and carries only `(condition_mask, direction, proximity, prior_n, symbol_id)` — `fib_anchor`/`timeframe`/`exit` were DEFERRED from `spec.rs` because they are NOT bits and do not change the per-bar `evaluate_atoms` arithmetic. The Rust spec keeps ONE `direction` field PER CONCRETE spec; only the Python DEFINITION carries the SWEPT `directions` SET. Rather than touch the frozen crate (which would risk the byte-identical 400-case golden), the NEW pure-Python `brutex/strategies/fib_definitions.py` WRAPS it: a `StrategyDefinition` adds anchor + the swept directions + timeframes + exit + symbol context, and `StrategyDefinition.spec_args(condition_mask, direction)` projects one concrete `(mask, direction)` back onto the Rust spec's `(condition_mask_hex, direction_u8)` ABI — so the SAME frozen evaluator/decoder consume it unchanged. **What shipped (NEW `brutex/strategies/fib_definitions.py`):** (1) the data model — `FibAnchorKind{PREV_DAY, ROLLING_WEEKLY, WEEKLY_STATIC}` (the anchor is a SWEPT STRATEGY PARAMETER per ADR-0012 D4, never a vocab bit — tripling the 11-bit Fib group for zero analytical gain is the D4/D66 anti-pattern), `Direction{LONG, SHORT}` (`.as_u8()` → 0/1 matching `spec.rs`; `.value` → the decoder's "long"/"short" token), `ExitConfig` (the declared exit POLICY — 15:20 IST forced exit per ADR-0012 D5 + optional `stop_loss_bps`/`take_profit_bps` for Mode A vs the forced-exit-only Mode B; `has_sl_tp` discriminates), and the frozen `StrategyDefinition{name, anchor, symbols, directions, timeframes, exit, condition_scope}` where **`directions` is the swept direction set (BOTH Long+Short by default, order-preserving de-duplicated, never empty)** — direction is NOT pinned on a strategy — plus `candidate_mask` (the OR of the scope's bits, or the full `IMPLEMENTED_MASK` for an empty scope — always ⊆ `IMPLEMENTED_MASK`), `spec_args(mask, direction)` (validates the mask is within scope AND the direction is one the strategy sweeps), and `expand(mask) -> tuple[ConcreteSpec, ...]` (the direction-sweep: one concrete `ConcreteSpec{strategy_name, direction, condition_mask_hex, direction_u8}` PER swept direction — Long AND Short by default; the actual sweep additionally crosses `{masks} × {timeframes}`). (2) `FibStrategyRegistry` + module `fib_registry` + a one-line `register(...)`, mirroring `brutex.strategies.registry.StrategyRegistry` (dup-name rejection, `get`/`names`/`all`/`clear`). (3) **the 3 Fib definitions declared** (one per anchor: `fib_prev_day`, `fib_rolling_weekly`, `fib_weekly_static`) — everything but the anchor identical so the three are directly comparable (ADR-0012 D2); each sweeps BOTH directions by default. (4) **runnable, not a stub** — `resolve_fib_levels(definition, today, daily_candles)` dispatches on the anchor to the REAL primitive (`prev_day_ohlc.lookup_prev_day_ohlc` / `weekly_anchors.rolling_weekly_anchor` / `weekly_anchors.weekly_static_anchor`) then feeds the resolved `(high, low)` into the SAME `fib_levels.compute_fib_levels` (the shared-Rust Fib math); resolution takes only the definition (anchor) — the LEVELS are direction-agnostic (direction is a swept dimension, so a strategy's Long and Short sweeps share one set of levels per day); a cold-start returns `None` (combo INELIGIBLE per ADR-0012 §4.5 #6, never a crash or a fabricated level — Golden Rule #1). (5) **symbol-agnostic** — `symbols` is a free tuple (config, not a hardcoded index); `for_symbols(definition, symbols)` returns a re-symboled copy (name-suffixed), proving the SAME declaration runs for any symbols with no rewrite. (6) **decoder bridge** — `render_definition(definition, condition_mask, direction, timeframe=)` projects via `spec_args` (direction is a PARAMETER — the chosen swept direction) then feeds `(direction, timeframe)` into the FROZEN `combo_decoder.decode_combo`, so a Fib strategy reads exactly like any other winning combo (no bespoke decoder). **PROOF (no illusion — every claim on the real path):** `tests/unit/test_strategies_fib_definitions.py` (54 tests) — the **3-registered** assertion (`fib_registry.names()` is exactly the 3 anchor strategies, `len == 3`); the **one-line-add** test (registers a 4th ANCHOR-strategy with ONE `register(...)` line, asserts it appears + is valid + sweeps BOTH directions + RESOLVES to real `FibLevels`); the **expand-produces-both-directions** test (`PREV_DAY.expand(mask)` yields 2 specs, directions `[LONG, SHORT]`, `direction_u8` `[0, 1]`, SAME mask hex, SAME strategy name) + a single-direction-restricted variant + scope-error propagation; the **symbol-agnostic** test (a `for_symbols` copy resolves byte-identically — levels track the daily candles, not the symbol string); each of the 3 (correct anchor + BOTH swept directions + 15:20 exit); the 3 anchors resolving to REAL fib levels on a crafted 2024-01 daily series (prev-day uses the prior trading day's H/L, rolling-weekly the trailing-5-session extremes, weekly-static the last-completed-ISO-week extremes); each cold-start path returning honest `None` (prev-day no prior candle, rolling-weekly <5 sessions, weekly-static no completed prior week); scope rejection (unknown vocab name at construction, out-of-scope bit at `spec_args`/`expand`/`render_definition`) + **direction-not-swept rejection** (a Long-only strategy refuses a Short `spec_args`/`render`); the directions de-dup (order-preserving, the duplicate dropped) + the already-canonical no-rewrite branch. PLUS a frozen golden `tests/golden/test_strategies_fib_definition_golden.py` pinning `fib_prev_day`'s FULL declaration (name/anchor/the swept `directions` set/symbols/timeframes/forced-exit/SL/TP/candidate-mask-hex + the Long-slice rendered-direction + spec-mask-hex) AND its Long-direction Simple + Pro sentences byte-for-byte — Simple: \"Buy on 15m when trend is up, price beats the day's average price, at the halfway bounce zone and first hour (uptrend).\"; Pro: \"Buy 15m [uptrend]: EMA20>EMA200, close>VWAP, Fib 50% and early morning.\" **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ this is the DECLARATION + anchor-resolution + decoder-bridge layer — the brute-force mask + direction + timeframe SWEEP, the frictionless trade-sim, and the SL/TP grid are PR-5 (sweep) / PR-4 (sim); `expand` is the per-mask DIRECTION slice of that grid (the full grid also crosses masks × timeframes — stated, not claimed shipped); the `ExitConfig` is the declared exit POLICY consumed by that later sim, NOT executed here, and `resolve_fib_levels` produces the per-day Fib LEVELS the sweep evaluates against — it does NOT itself fire trades (stated, not conflated); ✅ DIRECTION is a swept dimension — the registry holds 3 STRATEGIES (one per anchor), and Long/Short live in each strategy's swept `directions` set, NOT as 6 separate registrations; ✅ symbol-agnostic — admits NO symbol to the engine (ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX); the reference `NSE-NIFTY` is plain config (ADR-0012 D1) re-symbolable via `for_symbols`; ✅ WRAP not extend — `git diff --name-only` is the new module + its 2 tests + this ledger entry only, ZERO Rust / ZERO frozen-spec change (the `codegen_vocab.py --check` exit 0 + no `rust/` diff prove the 400-case golden + vocab are untouched); ✅ an unknown-anchor is structurally impossible (the field is the exhaustive 3-member `FibAnchorKind` enum — the resolution dispatch is total), and an unknown vocab CONDITION + an unswept DIRECTION are both rejected (the testable analogues). **Coverage/gates (verified 2026-06-30 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv + the maturin-built `trading_core`+`fno_math` wheels):** `brutex/strategies/fib_definitions.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (140 stmt / 38 branch, 0 missing), 54 tests pass; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 3 touched files; `mypy --strict --follow-imports=silent` clean on all 3 (the only package-wide mypy errors are pre-existing `growwapi`-stub issues in unrelated `adapters/groww/auth.py`/`reauth.py`, present on origin/main, environment-specific — my diff touches ZERO of those files); `pyright` 0 errors 0 warnings; `scripts/codegen_vocab.py --check` exit 0 (vocab/golden untouched). **Files:** `brutex/strategies/fib_definitions.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_strategies_fib_definitions.py` (new), `tests/golden/test_strategies_fib_definition_golden.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-FIB-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-001. **Builds on** DEC-STRATEGYSPEC-CORE-001 (#1027 — the frozen Rust `StrategySpec` this WRAPS), DEC-COMBO-DECODER-001 (#1028 — the `decode_combo` the render bridge feeds), ADR-0012 D2/D4/D5 (the 3-anchor Fib strategy design with direction as a swept parameter, anchor-as-parameter, 15:20 forced-exit/Mode-A-B), and the PR-2 anchor primitives `prev_day_ohlc`/`weekly_anchors`/`fib_levels`. (Ledger: #1030 = next free unique number above main's current max (#1029); PROVISIONAL — re-checked immediately before push, the DEC-ID is uniqueness-based not strictly sequential per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001.)


1042. **DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-001 — the audit-log auto-resume now RECOVERS from a torn final JSONL line left by a crash / SIGKILL mid-append, instead of dying with `AuditError` — restoring the §11 AUTOMATED unattended auto-resume guarantee** (2026-06-30; PR-H1; orchestrator/engine audit-log reader only — NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/engine change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **The defect (confirmed by adversarial verification):** the hash-chained audit-log readers `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py::_read_entries` (reached via `AuditWriter.open(resume=True)`) and the sweep-side twin `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py::_read_entries` raised `AuditError` / `SweepAuditError` on a malformed FINAL line. Both writers `flush()` + `os.fsync` per append, so a `SIGKILL` between the `write(line + "\n")` and the next durable append can only ever leave a TORN TAIL — an interrupted, partial / newline-LESS final line. The old readers treated that torn tail as fatal corruption, so an unattended restart died on resume — defeating the auto-resume guarantee the §11 AUTOMATED / Golden-Rule-#7 idempotence contract depends on. The integration test `tests/integration/test_replay_audit_log.py::test_resume_from_kill_roundtrip` was `pytest.skip`-stubbed for exactly this missing kill-recovery harness. **The fix (hash-chain-safe — Golden Rule #8 preserved):** the writer always appends `line + "\n"` in ONE `write()`, so a COMMITTED record is DEFINED as a line terminated by `"\n"`; a crash can therefore only damage the FINAL line and only by stripping its trailing newline. The new `_read_entries_with_torn_tail` (in BOTH modules) skips ONLY a newline-LESS final line (the torn tail — partial JSON OR complete-but-unterminated, including the only-line and blank-remnant cases) and returns a `torn_tail` flag; everything newline-terminated is parsed strictly. A malformed line that DOES carry a trailing newline (so it is NOT the file's final line, OR is a fully-flushed garbage final record) is REAL corruption and STILL raises — mid-file integrity is NOT weakened. The resume path (`open(resume=True)`) calls `_truncate_torn_tail` (atomic `os.replace` of a sibling temp keeping the longest `"\n"`-terminated prefix, `fsync`-before-rename) so the next append continues a pristine chain. `verify_chain` (via `_read_entries`) tolerates the torn tail but a MID-FILE hash-chain break among committed entries STILL raises `AuditChainCorruption` / `SweepAuditChainCorruption` — a torn tail can never mask genuine corruption of committed entries. **COMMON note (Golden Rule #11):** the two audit chains are deliberately STANDALONE — `orchestrator/audit.py` is SHA256, `engine/sweep_audit.py` is BLAKE3, and `sweep_audit.py`'s module docstring states it does NOT import/wrap the orchestrator log — so the recovery logic is duplicated in both (each `_read_entries_with_torn_tail` / `_truncate_torn_tail` is the documented STANDALONE twin of the other), NOT extracted to a shared helper that would couple the two chains. **PROOF (no illusion):** UN-SKIPPED `test_resume_from_kill_roundtrip` (a real clean-chain → partial newline-less append → resume → continue → `verify_chain == 3`); NEW `tests/unit/test_audit_torn_tail.py` (39 tests, every case parametrized over BOTH chains) covering torn-tail partial JSON, torn-tail complete-JSON-no-newline, torn-tail-only-line → empty valid state, blank unterminated remnant, a NON-final malformed line (MUST raise), a committed (newline-terminated) garbage final line (MUST raise), a mid-file hash-chain break (MUST raise from verify), break-plus-torn (break wins), clean-file-unchanged, empty/blank-terminated/missing-file edges, `_truncate_torn_tail` keep-prefix / only-torn-line-empties / IO-error-wraps, and the replay-after-recovery continuation; the pre-existing `test_orchestrator_audit.py::TestKillRecovery` test that encoded the OLD raise-on-torn-tail contract was updated to the new recover-on-torn-tail contract + a NEW companion proving a committed garbage final line still raises. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ ONLY an unterminated FINAL line is forgiven — every committed (newline-terminated) line is parsed strictly + the committed-prefix hash chain is fully verified, so real corruption is never masked; ✅ the torn tail is uncommitted (its content is never chained in), so this does not "accept torn content as valid" — it drops it; ✅ truncation is atomic (`os.replace`) so an interruption DURING the repair cannot itself corrupt the committed prefix; ✅ both touched source modules at 100% line + 100% branch (`orchestrator/audit.py` 185/36, `engine/sweep_audit.py` 176/32, 0 missing) + the new test module 100%; ✅ ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict brutex` (290 files, clean) / `pyright brutex tests` (0 errors in touched files — the 23 package-wide pyright errors are pre-existing hypothesis-decorator false-positives in unrelated property/doctor test files, present on origin/main); ✅ NO Rust diff, no scope/vocab/rate change — the brute-force ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py`, `tests/integration/test_replay_audit_log.py`, `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_audit.py`, `tests/unit/test_audit_torn_tail.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-001. **Builds on** DEC-AUDIT-FSYNC-DURABILITY-001 (the per-append flush+fsync that guarantees a crash leaves at most a torn tail) + the hash-chain design of the ingest/sweep audit logs (Golden Rule #8). (Ledger: re-synced with origin/main + renumbered #1041 → #1042 to clear a fresh collision after main advanced — the merged DEC-VIX-TRADE-STAMP-001 took #1040 and DEC-GROWW-AUTH-ERROR-DETAIL-001 took #1041, so #1042 is the next free unique number above main's current max #1041, per the uniqueness rule of DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001; re-checked at push. Earlier this entry was renumbered #1039 → #1041 to clear the prior collision with the merged DEC-CALENDAR-2020-DATA-001 (#1039).)
1040. **DEC-VIX-TRADE-STAMP-001 — India VIX is now STAMPED on every trade (`vix_at_entry` / `vix_at_exit`) via a generic reference-series provider; REFERENCE-ONLY, never a signal** (2026-06-30; ENGINE scope UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; the VIX stamp is captured + carried for downstream filter analysis but is NEVER part of the brute-force pattern combinations or the 60-condition vocabulary — the hard scope guard is unchanged). **The gap closed:** `vix_at_entry` / `vix_at_exit` were SPEC'd in a docstring (`brutex/universe.py:68` `UnderlyingSpec.reference_only`) and the golden corpus (`tests/golden/test_india_vix_reference_golden.py`) but implemented NOWHERE — no dataclass field carried them, no code assigned them, and the trade simulator never received the VIX series. The engine produced trades with no VIX context at all. **What shipped:** (1) `brutex/metrics/types.py` — `ClosedTrade` gains `vix_at_entry: Decimal | None = None` + `vix_at_exit: Decimal | None = None`. VIX is a volatility INDEX LEVEL, **not money** — it keeps full `Decimal` precision and is NEVER routed through the `brutex.money` paisa rounding (rounding a metric breaks ranking, CLAUDE.md §4). `__post_init__` rejects a non-finite (NaN/inf) Decimal but otherwise leaves the field untouched; both default `None` for callers that do not stamp. (2) NEW `brutex/engine/reference_series.py` — the generic, COMMON·DYNAMIC·SCALABLE stamp mechanism (VIX is the FIRST of N reference stamps, NOT a hard-wired one-off): `ReferenceSeries` is an O(1) `timestamp → close` dict lookup over one series' bars (a gap / ATR / breadth series is a future instance built identically, no re-architecting), and `TradeReferenceStamper` owns a named series and resolves a trade's entry+exit instants to `(vix_at_entry, vix_at_exit)`. (3) `brutex/engine/trade_sim.py` — `TradeSimWalker` + `simulate_trades` take an optional `reference_stamper`; the single trade-construction site (`_close`, which `finish` also routes through) stamps each emitted `ClosedTrade`. With no stamper the engine output is byte-identical (both VIX fields `None`). **No hallucination (Golden Rule #1):** a VIX bar missing at a trade's entry / exit timestamp stamps `None` — NEVER a fabricated, interpolated, or carried-forward number — and emits one `reference_series.vix_miss` structlog WARNING per miss so the gap is visible, never silent. VIX shares the index's trading calendar + timeframes, so an aligned feed hits on every bar; the `None` path guards a crafted / partial feed. **O(1) per trade (Golden Rule #5):** `level_at` is one dict probe; stamping a trade is two probes — no scan over the series per trade. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ per-trade `vix_at_entry`/`vix_at_exit` is the PRIMARY deliverable and is fully wired at the trade simulator's construction site (the COMMON injection seam every trade flows through); 🟡 propagating the VIX series end-to-end through the sweep driver / walk-forward / K-of-N loops (so a production sweep auto-builds the stamper from the lake's `NSE-INDIAVIX` series) is a FOLLOW-UP — the sweep callers do not yet receive the VIX series and threading it through `evaluate_combo`/`metrics_for_mask`/`_simulate_window`/the WF scorer is a wider plumbing change deliberately deferred to keep this PR scoped; 🟡 aggregate VIX context on the per-combo `ResultRow` (mean/min/max VIX across a combo's trades) is a noted FOLLOW-UP, NOT claimed (`ClosedTrade` is not itself persisted to Parquet — `ResultRow` is the persisted aggregate; the stamp's serialization contract here is the frozen-dataclass round-trip). **Tests (100% line + branch on every touched file):** NEW `tests/unit/test_engine_reference_series.py` (10 — O(1) lookup present/absent, duplicate-timestamp last-wins, stamp present/missing-entry/missing-exit/missing-both → `None` + the logged warning, the `from_vix_bars` constructor); `tests/unit/test_engine_trade_sim.py` `TestVixStamp` (no-stamper → `None`, present at entry+exit, missing at entry/exit/both, the streaming `finish` path); `tests/unit/test_metrics_compute.py` (the VIX default/accept/non-finite-reject/dataclass-serialization-round-trip cases); and the golden `tests/golden/test_india_vix_reference_golden.py` now ACTUALLY asserts a stamped value on a constructed trade run through the real stamper over the VIX week (entry 15.25 / exit 15.35), plus the `None`-on-missing-bar case. Verified 2026-06-30 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv + the maturin-built `trading_core` + `fno_math` wheels: `brutex/engine/reference_series.py` 100% (33 stmt / 4 branch), `brutex/engine/trade_sim.py` 100% (183 stmt / 56 branch), `brutex/metrics/types.py` 100% (55 stmt / 24 branch); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on `brutex tests`; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (291 files); `pyright` 0 errors 0 warnings on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/metrics/types.py`, `brutex/engine/reference_series.py` (new), `brutex/engine/trade_sim.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_reference_series.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_engine_trade_sim.py`, `tests/unit/test_metrics_compute.py`, `tests/golden/test_india_vix_reference_golden.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-VIX-TRADE-STAMP-001. (Ledger: #1040 = next free unique number above the file's current max (#1039, taken by DEC-CALENDAR-2020-DATA-001 when it merged to main first); the DEC-ID is uniqueness-based, re-checked immediately before push per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 — this entry renumbered #1038 → #1039 → #1040 across successive re-syncs as sibling branches took #1038 then #1039.)

1041. **DEC-GROWW-AUTH-ERROR-DETAIL-001 — a failed Groww access-token mint now surfaces the SANITIZED vendor reason (so the operator sees WHY auth failed) instead of a bare redacted "issuance failed", with the api_key / TOTP secret / minted 6-digit code provably scrubbed** (2026-06-30; adapter auth layer only — READ/observe surface, ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change). **Problem (operator-reported):** when the dashboard "Test credentials" probe (or any live pull's initial mint / 06:00-IST re-mint) failed, `brutex.adapters.groww.auth.get_access_token` wrapped EVERY `token_factory` failure as `GrowwAuthError(safe_message="Groww access-token issuance failed")` — a CATEGORICAL message with the real cause THROWN AWAY. The dashboard `/api/v1/groww/credentials/test` route surfaces `str(exc)` (= the redacting `safe_message`), so the operator saw only "Groww access-token issuance failed" and could not tell a wrong TOTP secret from an expired key, an un-whitelisted IP, or a vendor 5xx — Groww's HTTP-400 `displayMessage` (typically `Groww API Error 400: <reason>`) never reached the log or the UI. **FIX (secret-safe reason surfacing):** the `except` block now (1) SANITIZES the SDK exception's text via a NEW pure `_sanitize_reason(text, *secrets)` that scrubs every api_key / TOTP-secret / minted-code occurrence to `***` — blank secrets skipped (a `str.replace("", …)` would corrupt the whole string), longest-secret-first so an overlapping pair is fully masked; (2) makes the SANITIZED reason the `safe_message` itself (`"Groww access-token issuance failed: <reason>"`) so the dashboard's `str(exc)` finally shows WHY, AND attaches it as a NEW `GrowwAuthError.detail` attribute (typed `str | None`, defaulting `None`) reachable by callers without re-parsing `str`; (3) emits a NEW `groww.token.issuance_failed` structlog event (`reason` = sanitized, `status` = the SDK exception's NUMERIC `code` via `_vendor_status` — a `bool` rejected (it is an `int` subclass), and ONLY an int or a DIGIT-ONLY string (coerced to int, mirroring `errors._classify_generic`) survives so an arbitrary free-text `code` can NEVER reach the `status` field unscrubbed (hostile-review MINOR folded — the `reason` is the only sanitized free-text channel); `error_type` = the exception class name) so it lands in `brutex.log`; NO `print`. The exception TYPE contract is preserved — `GrowwAuthError` (a `BruteXError`) still raised, so every `except GrowwAuthError` caller + `is_auth_failure` + the re-auth latch are byte-unchanged; only the redacted TEXT widened from categorical to "categorical + sanitized reason". **SECRET HYGIENE (proven, Golden Rule #10 + L-14 `safe_message` discipline):** the api_key, the TOTP shared secret, and the minted 6-digit code are ALL scrubbed BEFORE the reason touches the `safe_message`, the `.detail`, OR the structlog event — a parametrized regression raises a vendor message embedding all three (verbatim + URL-substring forms) and asserts NONE appears in `str(exc)` / `.detail` / the captured event `repr`, while `***` confirms the reason was carried (not dropped wholesale). **Coverage/gates (verified 2026-06-30 via the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `brutex/adapters/groww/auth.py` + `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` BOTH at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (59/10 + 56/20, 0 missing) across the groww auth/errors/reauth/live/client + dashboard-credentials-route suites (147 tests pass); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 5 touched files; `pyright` 0 errors 0 warnings on the touched source + test; `mypy --strict` reports ONLY the 2 PRE-EXISTING `growwapi`-stub artifacts on the untouched `_real_token_factory` import line (byte-identical on pristine `main`, environment-specific) — ZERO new errors from this diff. **Hostile-review verdict: SHIP** (no BLOCKER/MAJOR); two MINORs folded — the `_vendor_status` digit-only `status` hardening above, and the live/reauth secret-absence assertions strengthened to embed `fake_secret` verbatim so the scrub is genuinely exercised end-to-end (not a near-tautology). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/auth.py` (the `_sanitize_reason`/`_vendor_status` helpers + the reason-surfacing except + the structlog event), `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` (`GrowwAuthError.detail`), `tests/unit/test_groww_auth.py` (the sanitize/surface/no-leak/structlog/status-none/numeric-only/helper regressions), `tests/unit/test_groww_live.py` + `tests/unit/test_groww_reauth.py` (the exact-string assertions updated to the reason-bearing form + a secret embedded so the scrub is non-trivially proven), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-AUTH-ERROR-DETAIL-001. (Ledger: #1041 = next free unique number after rebasing onto origin/main — main merged through #1040 `DEC-VIX-TRADE-STAMP-001` since this branched, so the provisional number was renumbered to #1041 to avoid the collision; the DEC-ID is the stable handle per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001.)

1044. **DEC-DSR-KURTOSIS-FIX-001 — the Stage-4 cascade kill-gate was fed EXCESS kurtosis where the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) needs NON-excess (Pearson) kurtosis, OVER-stating the DSR and biasing the gate toward PASS; the wire boundary now adds back `GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` (+3) to match the correct sibling** (2026-06-30; statistical "truth-filter" correctness fix — metrics/engine only, ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change). **The defect (wave-2 verification, traced end-to-end):** the DSR/PSR formula of Bailey & López de Prado (2012/2014) is defined on the **non-excess** (Pearson) kurtosis `g4` where a Gaussian == 3.0 (`brutex/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py:27-28,78-82,151-154`; `GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS = 3.0` at `:82`). `compute_metrics` stores **EXCESS** kurtosis (Gaussian == 0.0, `_excess_kurtosis` at `brutex/metrics/compute.py:409-415,615`), and the CORRECT sibling `with_stage4_statistics` converts it back with `kurtosis=metrics.kurtosis + GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` (`compute.py:729`). The cascade `CandidateInput.kurtosis` field is EXPLICITLY documented as non-excess (`brutex/metrics/cascade.py:192` `# Distribution moments for the Deflated Sharpe PSR (non-excess kurtosis)`) and is fed straight into `deflated_sharpe_ratio(...)` by the kill-gate (`cascade.py:545`, filter #2). But the production wire `build_candidate_input` filled that field with the RAW excess value — `kurtosis=_finite(metrics.kurtosis)` (`brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py:678`), NO `+3` — VIOLATING the field's own contract. So the DSR kill-gate received kurtosis 3.0 too LOW; in the estimator-variance radicand `1 − g3·SR + (g4−1)/4·SR²` a smaller `g4` shrinks the radicand, inflating the PSR Z-score, OVER-stating the DSR for a combo whose observed Sharpe beats the deflation benchmark `SR_0` — exactly the surviving combos — so a luckier-than-real strategy passed the gate when it should have been killed. **FIX (minimal, at the wire boundary):** `cascade_wire.py:678` now reads `kurtosis=_finite(metrics.kurtosis) + GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` (importing the existing `GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` constant from `brutex.metrics.deflated_sharpe`, NOT a hardcoded 3.0), bit-for-bit matching the sibling `with_stage4_statistics`. An undefined-shape (`None`) kurtosis maps via `_finite` to `0.0 + 3.0 = 3.0` — the honest Gaussian non-excess default (the old `0.0` was a non-excess kurtosis of zero, itself wrong). **Math verification (no guessing — Golden Rule #1):** confirmed end-to-end via the scratchpad 3.12 venv that for the reconstructed fat-tailed candidate (16 trades; non-excess kurtosis ≈ 3.14, i.e. excess ≈ 0.14) in the gate-relevant PASS regime (`SR_hat > SR_0`, N=5 V=0.03) the corrected non-excess DSR is LOWER than the old excess DSR (≈ 0.775 → ≈ 0.766), and that `CandidateInput.kurtosis == compute_metrics(...).kurtosis + GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the PSR's monotonicity in kurtosis flips sign with `SR_hat − SR_0`; for a would-FAIL combo already below `SR_0` the corrected DSR can be marginally HIGHER, but it stays below the gate — so the de-biasing acts exactly where it matters (the surviving / PASS combos). **Tests (regression, 100% line+branch on the touched file):** `tests/unit/test_engine_cascade_wire.py::TestBuildCandidateInput` gains `test_kurtosis_is_nonexcess_matching_compute_sibling` (the candidate's kurtosis == the independently-recomputed `compute_metrics(...).kurtosis + GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` over the SAME reconstructed trades, and `!= metrics.kurtosis` so the +3 actually moved the value — the smoking gun the OLD code would fail), `test_kurtosis_none_defaults_to_gaussian_nonexcess` (constant-PnL → undefined kurtosis → candidate carries 3.0, not 0.0), and `test_nonexcess_kurtosis_lowers_overstated_dsr_for_passing_combo` (feeding the corrected kurtosis through `deflated_sharpe_ratio` exactly as the kill-gate does yields a LOWER DSR than the buggy excess value for a PASS-regime combo). Verified 2026-06-30: `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (404 stmt / 114 branch, 0 missing) over `tests/unit/test_engine_cascade_wire.py` (113 tests pass); the metrics/cascade/compute/deflated-sharpe + golden + property suites (183 tests) green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on `brutex tests`; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (291 files); `pyright` introduces ZERO new errors (the 23 pre-existing baseline errors live in untouched `hypothesis`-`@given` property + `test_doctor` files, byte-identical on pristine origin/main); `git status --short rust/` empty (no Rust diff). **Files:** `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py` (the `GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` import + the `+3` at the wire boundary + the field-convention docstring/comment), `tests/unit/test_engine_cascade_wire.py` (the 3 regression tests + a deterministic fat-tailed fixture), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DSR-KURTOSIS-FIX-001. (Ledger: #1044 = next free unique number above the file's current max #1043 `DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-DISK-CACHE-001`, which merged to main first while this PR was open; renumbered #1042 → #1043 → #1044 across successive main advances to avoid the collision; the DEC-ID is the stable handle per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 — re-checked immediately before push.)

1043. **DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-DISK-CACHE-001 — the daily Groww access token is now CACHED to disk (0600, session-anchored) and reused across cold starts, so a pull mints AT MOST once per session per machine instead of 3+ times — killing the self-inflicted token-issuance rate-limit storm** (2026-06-30; adapter layer only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; no lake-schema/stored-bar/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **Problem (operator-reported, fresh-clone dashboard pull):** the credentials were CORRECT (key 976 chars, secret 32 chars, TOTP minted fine) but `GrowwAPI.get_access_token` raised `GrowwAPIRateLimitException` ("rate limit … exceeded"). ROOT CAUSE (6-agent deep audit, traced to file:line): BruteX re-mints a brand-new token on EVERY live-client/pool construction, and a single "Pull · full pipeline" run builds THREE independent `SdkRefresher`s — spot via `pull_controller`→`build_live_pool`, metadata via `metadata_pull`→`build_live_client`, F&O via `historical_pull`→`build_live_pool` (each a distinct mint) — plus one per `/api/v1/groww/credentials/test` click, one per CLI `brutex fetch`, and a fresh mint on every process/container restart (the token lived ONLY in `SdkRefresher._sdks`, in-memory, never persisted). ≥3 uncoordinated mints in seconds tripped the vendor's token-ISSUANCE path. **HONEST (Golden Rule #1):** whether Groww DOCUMENTS a token-issuance rate limit is UNVERIFIED — the SDK rate table (`docs/groww/api-reference/01-introduction.md:128-134`) covers only Orders / Live Data / Non-Trading and labels the TOTP flow "No Expiry"; the observed `GrowwAPIRateLimitException` raised BY the issuance call is the runtime evidence a limit exists on that path. The fix is correct regardless: mint less, cache, reuse. **WHAT SHIPPED:** (1) NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/token_cache.py` (stdlib-only, NO SDK import, no import cycle): `groww_token_cache_path()` (env `BRUTEX_GROWW_TOKEN_CACHE_PATH`, default `~/.brutex/cache/groww_access_token.json`); `load_cached_token(creds, *, now_utc)` validates exists / mode-0600 / JSON / `schema==1` / api_key blake3-FINGERPRINT match (never the key) / session match, returning `None` on ANY miss (logs the reason, NEVER raises); `store_token(creds, token, *, now_utc)` writes atomically at 0600 via the COMMON `atomic_io.atomic_write_simple(chmod=0o600)` (best-effort, logs on failure); `current_session(now_utc)` is the 06:00-IST-anchored session date, REUSING the existing `ingest_common.now_ist` IST zone (hostile-review m1 — no second IST notion). (2) `errors.py` — NEW `GrowwTokenIssuanceThrottled(GrowwAuthError)` with `is_retryable=True` (the ONE retryable auth-family error; `is_rate_limit` stays `False` so it never steps the data-fetch rate ladder). (3) `auth.py` — `get_access_token`'s except classifies a rate-limit issuance failure (via the SINGLE-SOURCE `from_groww_exception` → `GrowwRateLimitError`, covering the SDK class name / a 429 `code` / the live "rate limit …" message) → raises the throttle subclass, ORDERED BEFORE the generic terminal `GrowwAuthError` (hostile-review M2); the #999 secret-sanitization (`_sanitize_reason` / `.detail` / structlog) is preserved on BOTH arms. (4) `reauth.py` — `SdkRefresher.__init__` is CACHE-FIRST (`_cold_start_sdks`): a valid same-session token builds the SDKs with NO network mint, so the 2nd/3rd pipeline phase + a restart + a concurrent process all reuse the token the first phase wrote (collapsing the 3-mint storm to ONE); a cold-start issuance THROTTLE re-checks the cache then rides a bounded exponential back-off (`GROWW_TOKEN_ISSUANCE_RETRY_*`, default 3 attempts) before re-raising the RETRYABLE throttle (quarantine → across-pull re-pull, never a crash) — the back-off runs OUTSIDE any pool lock (hostile-review M2, never inside `reauth`'s locked block or past `run_with_deadline`). **B1 (BLOCKER, folded):** the in-pull `reauth()` FORCES a real network mint and NEVER reads the cache — it is called ONLY because the current token was REJECTED, so re-reading the same-session cache would loop the dead token against `max_reauths=1`; it force-mints (still freeze-guarded) and OVERWRITES the cache, so the 06:00-IST revoked-token case self-corrects AND the fresh token is shared. (5) `client.py` — a throttle raised by `reauth` propagates OUT of `_call` as retryable WITHOUT re-entering the reauth branch (no infinite recursion; regression-pinned). (6) `constants.py` — `GROWW_TOKEN_RESET_HOUR_IST=6` + cache-path + back-off knobs (all env-overridable). (7) `.gitignore` — added `**/groww_access_token*` so a redirected cache can never be committed (hostile-review M3). **M1 (folded):** NO dashboard "redaction" rewrite — that bug does NOT exist (#999 already surfaces the real reason via `safe_message`); touching it was dropped. **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** this eliminates the self-inflicted 3×/run storm ONCE the first mint succeeds; a throttle on the genuinely-FIRST mint of a fresh clone is RIDEABLE (bounded back-off → quarantine → across-pull retry), NOT eliminated. The cache is PER-MACHINE, so a Groww ACCOUNT-WIDE issuance limit shared across many hosts is OUT OF SCOPE (needs a networked token broker — not claimed). The token is plaintext at 0600 (as sensitive as the already-on-disk TOTP secret — not encrypted at rest; OS-keyring is a flagged follow-up); a leak is bounded to ≤1 trading day (the 06:00 reset). The 06:00-IST reset is UNVERIFIED from vendor docs (asserted in CLAUDE.md §6 / ADR-0009 / production logs — the token died at exactly 06:00 IST); a wrong boundary is SELF-CORRECTING on the token's first real use (the rejected token drives the forced reauth mint that overwrites the cache) at the cost of at most one extra mint that day, and the hour is a config constant for a future probe. **NO DATA LOST (Golden Rule #1):** a cached token is reused ONLY when same-session + matching-fingerprint + parse-valid; a stale-session / wrong-credential / corrupt cache is a MISS → fresh mint; nothing is ever fabricated. **POST-MERGE-VERIFICATION MUST-FIX (8-agent adversarial pass, folded before push):** the cache-corruption lens found ONE surviving MAJOR — `load_cached_token` raised `UnicodeDecodeError` on a NON-UTF-8 cache file: `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (`token_cache.py:185`) was wrapped only in `except OSError`, but `UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError` subclass (NOT an `OSError`), so a corrupt-bytes cache file ESCAPED the guard and crashed `SdkRefresher.__init__` (and the whole cold-start pull build) — strictly WORSE than the re-mint storm the cache prevents, and a breach of the module's documented "returns None on ANY failure, NEVER raises" contract. FIX: the read-step except is broadened to `except (OSError, ValueError)` (`reason="undecodable"`), so a non-UTF-8 file is now a cache-MISS that re-mints. Two NIT-level worst-case hardenings folded alongside: (a) `current_session` now REJECTS a naive (tz-unaware) datetime with a `ValueError` rather than silently mis-bucketing the session via `astimezone`'s local-time interpretation (every production caller passes aware UTC — fail-loud-on-misuse); (b) a NEW defensive `SdkRefresher._safe_cache_load` wraps the injected `_token_cache_load` so ANY future cache-load regression degrades to a real mint (logged `groww.token.cache_load_failed`) instead of crashing `__init__` — "a cache problem must never break the build". The remaining verification NITs were NOT folded: the abandoned-deadline-daemon out-of-lock write is benign (last-writer-wins of a valid token); and the throttled-mint `auth_failure=True` quarantine label was DELIBERATELY left — contrary to the synthesize note it is NOT zero-control-flow-risk (`is_auth_failure` matches the `GrowwAuthError`-subclass throttle and the derived `auth_aborted` flag halts the auto-retry wrapper, so excluding the throttle would change re-pull behaviour), so it stays unchanged pending a separate decision. **Tests (100% line + branch on every touched file — verified 2026-06-30 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `token_cache.py` 110/26, `reauth.py` 80/6, `auth.py` 67/12, `errors.py` 57/20, `client.py` 89/10, `constants.py` 64/6 — ALL 100.00% (0 missing), 60 token-cache+reauth tests pass (217 across the groww suite). The non-UTF-8 regression (`test_non_utf8_bytes_returns_none`) FAILS before the except broadening; the defensive-guard regression (`test_raising_cache_load_degrades_to_mint_never_crashes_init`) FAILS before `_safe_cache_load`; the naive-datetime guard (`test_naive_datetime_rejected`) pins the new branch. NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_token_cache.py` (38 — every miss reason + 06:00 boundary + env overrides + secret-hygiene no-leak + write-failure best-effort) + `test_groww_reauth.py` `TestColdStartCache`/`TestColdStartThrottle`/`TestReauthForcedMint` (incl. the B1 REGRESSION that a revoked-but-valid-session cache does NOT loop the dead token — forced mint overwrites it — and the 3-phase one-mint-via-cache proof) + `test_groww_auth.py` `TestIssuanceThrottle` (429-code / rate-limit-message / SDK-class-name → throttle; 400-Invalid-TOTP stays terminal; the throttle never leaks the api_key/secret/code) + `test_groww_errors.py` + `test_groww_client.py` (throttle-from-reauth propagates retryable, no recursion) + `test_groww_constants.py`; a suite-wide autouse conftest fixture isolates the on-disk cache so no test touches `~/.brutex`. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files; `pyright` 0 errors on the new/changed source (2 PRE-EXISTING `_real_token_factory`/`_real_totp` reportPrivateUsage warnings, byte-identical on pristine main); `mypy --strict` reports ONLY the 2 PRE-EXISTING `growwapi`-stub artifacts on the untouched SDK-import lines — ZERO new errors from this diff. **Hostile-review verdict: SHIP** — BLOCKER B1 (cache-first reauth loop) + MAJORs M1 (nonexistent redaction bug — dropped) / M2 (throttle-subclass lock-freeze + arm ordering) / M3 (`.gitignore` glob) / M4 (honest storm scope) + MINOR m1 (reuse `now_ist`) ALL folded before push. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/token_cache.py` (new), `brutex/adapters/groww/{errors,auth,reauth,client,constants}.py`, `.gitignore`, `tests/unit/test_groww_token_cache.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_groww_{reauth,auth,errors,client,constants,live}.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-DISK-CACHE-001. 1046. **DEC-ADAPTER-ROBUSTNESS-001 — two batched MINOR adapter / rate-controller hardening fixes (H8 + H10), both confirmed by wave-2 verification on main** (2026-06-30; adapter + rate-controller layer only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). Batched into ONE PR to save merge-thrash cycles on the busy main. **DEFECT 1 (H8) — `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`:** the `_RATE_LIMIT_HINTS` tuple carried a bare `"429"` substring, so the message sniffer in `_classify_generic` false-matched ANY generic-exception message merely CONTAINING `429` — a delisted-strike error code (`STK-429-DELISTED`), an order id, a timestamp (`...T09:15:00` over a date like `2024-04-29`) — wrongly mapping a TERMINAL error to a retryable `GrowwRateLimitError` → re-pulled forever, needlessly stepping the AIMD rate ladder DOWN + escaping per-symbol quarantine. **FIX:** dropped the bare `"429"` substring; `_RATE_LIMIT_HINTS` is now phrase-only (`"rate limit"`, `"too many request"`). This loses ZERO genuine rate-limit detection because a real status-429 is already caught STRUCTURALLY by `_CODE_TO_ERROR` (`code == 429`, int OR digit-string, consumed FIRST in `_classify_generic` before the message hints) and the live Groww-SDK message shape `"Rate limit has breached for your request."` still matches the `"rate limit"` phrase — VERIFIED end-to-end against the real `from_groww_exception` → `is_retryable` pipeline (a `code=429`/`code="429"`/phrase exception still maps retryable; the unrelated-`429`-substring message now maps to the terminal base `GrowwError`, not retryable, not a ladder-stepping rate-limit). **DEFECT 2 (H10) — `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`:** the OBSERVE-ONLY trailing-window counter `_count_in_window_locked` binned the oldest integer second with `math.ceil(now - window)`, dropping the bucket that HOLDS `now - window` when `now` is fractional — so the documented `recent_60s == recent_minute` operator cross-check (the issue-ring count vs the governor deque's float-instant count) read falsely UNEQUAL near a fractional-second window boundary. **FIX:** use `math.floor(now - window)` (matching the intended `(now - window, now]` window — the boundary bucket's sub-range `(now - window, floor(now - window) + 1)` IS inside the window), and SOFTENED the "equals" wording in the `LOG_WINDOW_60S` constant docstring + the `snapshot()` comment + the method docstring to "approximates / agrees to within one boundary second" (the integer-second ring and the float-instant deque are NOT bit-identical by construction). This is **OBSERVABILITY ONLY — ZERO rate-safety impact**: the issue ring is observe-only (NEVER read by a pacing gate — the §2 Rule 6 token bucket + 500/min governor are untouched); no pacing / governor / ceiling logic changed. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** both are LOW-severity robustness fixes (H8 a terminal-error mis-classification self-inflicting re-pulls; H10 a cosmetic cross-check off-by-one) — neither is a crash, a rate-safety regression, or a data-loss bug; the per-second + per-minute rate caps + the AIMD ladder are byte-unchanged. STEP-0 re-confirmed BOTH defects still present on `origin/main` (`be0ef48a`) before implementing. **Tests (REAL, regression, 100% line+branch on both touched modules):** `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py` gains `test_bare_429_substring_is_not_a_rate_limit` (4 unrelated-`429` messages → terminal, not retryable, not rate-limit — FAILS under the old bare substring) + `test_genuine_rate_limit_still_retryable_without_bare_substring` (code=429 int/str + the two phrase shapes → still retryable `GrowwRateLimitError`); `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py::TestTrailingWindowIssueLog` gains `test_recent_60s_cross_checks_recent_minute_at_fractional_boundary` (a boundary-second issue at a fractional `now` → `recent_60s == recent_minute == 1`; FAILS under the old `ceil`) + `test_count_in_window_keeps_the_boundary_second_bucket` (probes the primitive directly). Verified 2026-06-30 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv: `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (57/20, 0 missing, 78 tests) and `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (228/58, 0 missing, 81 tests) over the CI per-module gate test files; 263 rate/errors/rate-safety/CLI-bridge/dashboard-panel/ingest tests green; `ruff check brutex tests` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean on both touched modules (the 1 package-wide `cma`-stub error + the 23 pyright `hypothesis`-decorator errors are PRE-EXISTING, byte-identical on pristine `origin/main`, NONE in any touched file); `git status --short rust/` empty. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-ADAPTER-ROBUSTNESS-001. 1047. **DEC-PULL-QUARANTINE-ROBUST-001 — three batched per-symbol pull-quarantine robustness fixes (PR-H11): a single bad vendor row now quarantines ONE symbol instead of crashing the WHOLE multi-symbol pull** (2026-06-30; parser / candle-field / option-dedup layer only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE CLASS OF BUG (Wave-3 verification on main, all re-confirmed STILL-REAL before implementing):** the ingest quarantine (`run_ingest.py:475` `if not isinstance(exc, BruteXError): raise exc`) isolates ONE symbol only for a `BruteXError` subclass — but two fetch-path bugs raised RAW `OverflowError`/`TypeError` that ESCAPED the quarantine and crashed the entire pull, plus one defensive collision gap. **DEFECT 1 (CONFIRMED-MAJOR, escaped crash) — `brutex/adapters/groww/parser.py`:** `parse_timestamp_ist`'s STRING branch ran `naive.replace(tzinfo=_IST).astimezone(UTC)` with NO guard; a parseable-but-pathological year-0001 string (`"0001-01-01T00:00:00"`) raised a raw `OverflowError("date value out of range")` on the IST→UTC shift (which can push a year-0001 datetime below `datetime.min`). The epoch branch already caught `OverflowError → CandleParseError`; the string branch did not. **FIX:** wrap the string-branch shift in `try/except (OverflowError, OSError, ValueError)` raising `CandleParseError("out-of-range candle timestamp: …")` — mirroring the epoch branch verbatim. **DEFECT 2 (CONFIRMED-MAJOR, escaped crash) — `brutex/data/candle_fields.py`:** `to_int` (volume / open-interest) had NO upper bound; a vendor-glitch oversized count (e.g. `2**70`) passed parsing, then crashed the Parquet write — `parquet_writer` builds a `pl.Int64` Series from it and polars raises a raw `TypeError("found value of type Int128")`, which (raised inside `lake_write_guard()`, which only maps ENOSPC/OOM) ESCAPED the per-symbol quarantine. **FIX:** add an inclusive int64-ceiling check (`> 2**63 - 1`) in `to_int` raising `CandleParseError` at PARSE time — mirroring the negative-count clamp in `assemble_candle` (an impossible count must never crash a multi-year pull). The exact int64 max stays storable (boundary inclusive). **DEFECT 3 (RE-CONFIRMED still-real, honesty/consistency) — `brutex/data/candle_fields.py` `has_no_price`:** a present `-inf` was SILENTLY swallowed as a "no-price" partial-bar skip — `Decimal(str(-inf)) = -Infinity <= 0` → `True` — while `+inf` and `nan` correctly raised the LOUD non-finite `CandleParseError` (they compare `False`/`False`). That asymmetry HID genuinely-malformed `-inf` data instead of surfacing it (Golden Rule #1 — a non-finite price is a data mismatch, never a no-trade bar). **FIX:** `has_no_price` returns `False` for ANY non-finite value (`not decimal_value.is_finite()`) so `-inf` falls through to `to_price`'s loud non-finite guard, symmetric with `+inf`/`nan`. **DEFECT 4 (RE-CONFIRMED still-real, defensive collision) — `brutex/data/option_dedup.py` `option_bar_key`:** the 5-field blake3 content key joined `underlying ‖ expiry ‖ strike ‖ side ‖ epoch` with the ASCII unit separator (`\x1f`) and the docstring CLAIMED the separator is "never present in a value", but NOTHING enforced it — a separator-bearing field value would let two DISTINCT tuples hash to the SAME key, a SILENT false-dedup that DROPS a real bar (§2 Rule 7 idempotence: dedup must never lose data). **FIX:** raise `CandleParseError` if any field value contains the separator (a vendor symbol/expiry/strike is plain ASCII, so this never fires in practice — it converts an impossible-but-catastrophic collision into a loud, quarantinable error). **EVERY escaped-exception fix now resolves to `CandleParseError` (a `BruteXError` subclass), so `run_ingest` quarantines the ONE bad symbol and the pull CONTINUES for the rest.** **SKIPPED (honest, re-probed still-real but DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE for this quarantine PR):** the `tf_resampler.py` `_validate_input` "no monotonic/duplicate-timestamp guard" item — re-probed and confirmed the derived-TF resampler does NOT crash on dup/non-monotonic input (it silently aggregates and self-`.sort()`s at the end); it is NEITHER a crash NOR a quarantine bug, the docstring EXPLICITLY delegates sorting to the caller, duplicates are already removed upstream at the lake-write boundary (keep-first sink), and a hard raise in `_validate_input` would be a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE across ~7 lake-fed callers (`spot_resample`/`fno_resample`/`fno_daily_resample`/`spot_daily_resample`/`tf_autoderive`/`movers_snapshot`) with regression risk and NO existing dup-guard pattern to mirror — better as a separate focused PR (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 2 / §9: don't expand scope, don't change code you don't fully own). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** Defects 1+2 are MAJOR escaped-crash fixes (a single malformed vendor row took down the whole pull); Defect 3 is a LOW-severity honesty/consistency fix (a silently-skipped `-inf` becomes loud); Defect 4 is a LOW-probability defensive guard (a plain-ASCII vendor value never carries `\x1f`). None changes the happy path — a normal candle / option key is byte-unchanged. STEP-0 re-confirmed all four defects STILL-REAL on `origin/main` (`3c8f299e`) via direct repros before implementing (year-0001 → raw OverflowError; `2**70` → `pl.Int64` build TypeError; `has_no_price(-inf)=True` vs `has_no_price(+inf)=False`; two distinct tuples → equal key). **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after, 100% line+branch on EVERY touched file):** `tests/unit/test_groww_parser.py::test_out_of_range_string_year_rejected` (year-0001 string → `CandleParseError`, not raw OverflowError); `tests/unit/test_candle_fields.py` gains `TestToInt::test_int64_overflow_rejected` (volume + open_interest `2**70` → CandleParseError) + `test_int64_ceiling_kept` (the `2**63-1` boundary stays storable) + `TestHasNoPrice::test_non_finite_is_not_no_price` (`-inf`/`+inf`/`nan`/`Decimal(-Infinity)` → False) + `TestAssembleCandle::test_partial_negative_infinity_is_loud_not_skipped` (an `-inf` price among real prices raises the non-finite CandleParseError, never an EmptyCandleRow skip); `tests/unit/test_option_dedup.py::TestKey::test_separator_in_value_rejected` (each of the 4 string fields with `\x1f` → CandleParseError) + `test_separator_collision_is_prevented`; and an INTEGRATION-style `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py::test_year0001_vendor_row_quarantines_pair_not_crashes_pull` proving a bulk pull where the BADTS symbol's REAL `parse_candle_rows` hits the year-0001 row quarantines ONLY that symbol (`failed_pairs == 1`, `ingest.quarantine` names it) and the good NIFTY symbol still lands (`bars_appended == 5`) — extending the existing CandleParseError/OutOfScope quarantine-continues suite. Verified 2026-06-30 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv: `brutex/adapters/groww/parser.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (53/18, 0 missing), `brutex/data/candle_fields.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (54/16, 0 missing), `brutex/data/option_dedup.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (50/6, 0 missing) over the CI per-module gate test files; touched-module + parquet-writer + option-ingest-pipeline regression suites green; `ruff check brutex tests` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (292 files); `pyright` 0 errors on all touched files (the 23 pyright `hypothesis`-decorator errors + 1 `cma`-stub error are PRE-EXISTING, byte-identical on pristine `origin/main`, NONE in any touched file — as recorded in the #1046 ledger entry); `git status --short rust/` empty. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/parser.py`, `brutex/data/candle_fields.py`, `brutex/data/option_dedup.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_parser.py`, `tests/unit/test_candle_fields.py`, `tests/unit/test_option_dedup.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-QUARANTINE-ROBUST-001. 1045. **DEC-INSTRUMENTSTORE-O1-001 — `InstrumentStore.get` is now genuinely O(1) via an in-memory `symbol_name` index + a CI bench gate, replacing the per-call O(n) DuckDB `SEQ_SCAN` that the "O(1) lookup" docstring falsely claimed** (2026-06-30; PR H9 of the hardening sweep — data-store read path only, ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; no lake-schema/stored-bar/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **Problem (Wave-2 verification, re-confirmed on current main):** `brutex/data/instrument_store.py::get(symbol_name, *, as_of=None)` ran a DuckDB `SELECT * FROM instruments WHERE symbol_name = ? ORDER BY snapshot_date DESC LIMIT 1` on EVERY call, yet the module docstring (`:48-49`) advertised "**O(1) lookup** — primary key + 5 secondary indexes … one B+tree descent" and the method docstring claimed "O(log n)". NO index covers `symbol_name` (the secondary indexes are `idx_instr_segment/underlying/type/expiry/in_scope`), so DuckDB's planner used a full **`SEQ_SCAN`** — proven by `EXPLAIN` (`Type: Sequential Scan`, `~N rows`) — making `get` genuinely **O(rows) per call**. The path was ALSO ungated by any bench (Wave-2 measured p99 1.30/1.69×), so it could regress freely. This violates the operator's HARD O(1) rule (CLAUDE.md §2 Golden Rule #5) AND the no-hallucination honesty rule (Golden Rule #1 — a docstring claiming O(1) over an O(n) scan). The dominant production caller is the dashboard `store.get(symbol)` (four call sites in `app.py`, all `as_of=None`). **WHAT SHIPPED (one method rewrite + lazy index, no API/contract change):** (1) a NEW lazy in-memory index `self._symbol_index: dict[str, list[tuple[date, Instrument]]] | None` mapping each `symbol_name` → its snapshots NEWEST-first, built ONCE on the first `get` via `_build_symbol_index()` (a single `SELECT * … ORDER BY symbol_name, snapshot_date DESC` scan — byte-identical rows to what the per-call SQL read, only amortised). (2) `get` now serves from it: `as_of=None` (the hot path) is a single dict lookup + first-element read = **O(1)**; an `as_of` query walks that symbol's snapshot list newest-first to the first snapshot ≤ `as_of` = O(snapshots-per-symbol), bounded by the small number of distinct pull days (1-2 after `prune_to_latest_snapshot`), NOT O(rows). The EXACT contract is preserved — same return type / `None`-handling / case-sensitivity / temporal `as_of` semantics, verified by a parity test against a direct DuckDB query. (3) **No-stale-cache invalidation (the correctness risk on mutable data, solved):** the index is set back to `None` by EVERY method that mutates the `instruments` table — `upsert_many` (on COMMIT and defensively on ROLLBACK) and `prune_to_latest_snapshot` — so the next `get` rebuilds from the committed rows; the `_StoreMeta` write-RLock already serialises every public method, so there is no read/invalidate interleaving (the `connection` property is read-only by contract, so mutation never bypasses the typed methods). (4) a module-level `_SNAPSHOT_DATE_COL_INDEX = _INSTR_COLUMNS.index("snapshot_date")` so the temporal key is read off a `SELECT *` row at a position derived from the column list (can't drift on a column re-order; mirrors `_row_to_instrument`'s existing positional unpack). **COMMON note (Golden Rule #2):** this mirrors the existing true-O(1) `InstrumentSnapshot.get` (`self._by_symbol.get(...)`, `:573-575`) — the temporal store now has the same dict-backed point lookup, adapted for the multi-snapshot `as_of` dimension the frozen snapshot view does not carry. **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** the per-call lookup is O(1) (`as_of=None`) / O(snapshots-per-symbol) (`as_of`); the FIRST `get` after construction or any write pays one real O(rows) index build (amortised, not per-call). Space is O(rows) — bounded by the lean ~750-underlying pruned universe (the ~89k FUT/CE/PE legs are discarded per DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001), so the index is a small, O(1)-bounded footprint, NOT an unbounded cache. **MEASURED:** before, `get` latency scaled ~linearly with master size (the SEQ_SCAN); after, the 4000/40-underlying hit-latency ratio is **1.007×** (flat — ~704 ns vs ~709 ns/call), passing even the strict 1.1× M4-Pro tier. **CI-ENFORCED so it can't regress:** NEW `tests/bench/test_instrument_store_get_o1.py` mirrors the repo's `_o1_tiers` two-tier pattern (`ratio_ceiling(5.0)` shared-CI, strict 1.1× on M4-Pro) — a regression to a per-call scan would scale with master size and FAIL the gate. **Tests (100% line + branch on the touched module):** NEW `TestGetO1Index` in `tests/integration/test_instrument_store.py` (13 — old-query parity for present+absent symbols, empty store, single row, `as_of` walk-to-first-on-or-before, `as_of`-before-all → None, index invalidation on upsert, on prune (the stale-`as_of` regression that FAILS without invalidation), on a forced upsert ROLLBACK, latest-among-multiple-snapshots) + the O(1) bench. **STRENGTHENED post-hostile-review (MINOR-1 honesty fix):** the timing bench alone did NOT actually catch the O(n) regression it advertised — at the 40/4000 sizes the OLD per-call `SEQ_SCAN` `get` measures only ~1.14× (DuckDB's ~3 µs fixed query-dispatch overhead swamps the tiny linear scan), so it stayed UNDER the shared-CI 5.0× ceiling. The fix adds a DIRECT, timing-independent **zero-query structural guard** (`test_primed_get_issues_zero_duckdb_queries` / `…_as_of…` / `test_first_get_builds_index_with_exactly_one_scan`): a proxy spies the writer connection's `execute` and asserts a PRIMED `get` issues ZERO DuckDB queries (and the first `get` pays exactly ONE full-table build scan, never a per-symbol `WHERE symbol_name` scan), so ANY regression to a per-call scan FAILS structurally regardless of timing noise — teeth-verified (the three tests all FAIL under an injected per-call-scan regression, pass after restore). The bench module + `test_get_ratio_below_ceiling` docstrings were CORRECTED (Golden Rule #1/#10) to describe what the timing tier really enforces — a flat-latency smoke check (~1.01× across the 100× jump), NOT the O(n) gate — pointing to the zero-query test as the real guard; the positive flat-latency assertion is unchanged. **NIT-1 (deterministic tiebreak):** `_build_symbol_index`'s `ORDER BY` gains a trailing `, security_id` so two DISTINCT instruments sharing one `(symbol_name, snapshot_date)` (symbol_name is NOT in the PK) resolve the newest-first head identically on every build, pinned by `test_same_snapshot_date_collision_is_deterministic` (parity across an invalidate+rebuild). Verified 2026-06-30 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv: `brutex/data/instrument_store.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (482 stmt / 76 branch, 0 missing) across the three CI gate suites (`test_instrument_store.py` + `_edges.py` + `_read_write_split.py`, 107 pass / 2 Track-2 skips); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on `brutex tests`; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (292 files); `pyright` 0 errors on the touched source + test (the only pyright errors are PRE-EXISTING `@composite`-strategy `draw` false-positives + a `test_doctor.py` artifact, byte-identical on pristine main — ZERO from this diff); `git status --short rust/` empty (no Rust touched). **Files:** `brutex/data/instrument_store.py` (the `_symbol_index` field + `_build_symbol_index` + the rewritten `get` + the two invalidation sites + `_SNAPSHOT_DATE_COL_INDEX`), `tests/integration/test_instrument_store.py` (`TestGetO1Index`), `tests/bench/test_instrument_store_get_o1.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-INSTRUMENTSTORE-O1-001. The DEC-ID is the stable handle.)

1048. **DEC-CALENDAR-CHECKED-TWINS-001 — add `get_session_checked` + `trading_days_between_checked` strict twins so an out-of-coverage weekday holiday is REFUSED instead of silently fabricated as a REGULAR session (PR-H12)** (2026-07-01; `brutex/calendars/nse.py` + `brutex/calendars/__init__.py` re-export only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE GAP (Wave-3 verification on `origin/main` `a1effa11`, re-confirmed STILL-REAL before implementing):** `get_session` (`nse.py:435`) and `trading_days_between` (`:473`) route through the UNGUARDED `is_trading_day`, which returns `True` for an out-of-coverage weekday (`is_holiday` silently returns `False` for a year outside `[HOLIDAY_COVERAGE_FIRST_YEAR, HOLIDAY_COVERAGE_LAST_YEAR]`, currently 2020-2026). So `get_session(date(2030, 6, 24))` (a Monday BEYOND coverage) FABRICATES a full 09:15-15:30 `REGULAR` session and `trading_days_between` INCLUDES it — while their strict siblings `is_holiday_checked` (`:345`) / `is_trading_day_checked` (`:396`) correctly RAISE `HolidayDataUnavailableError` for the same date. The two date-reasoning helpers had NO `_checked` twin, so a caller that wants the honest refuse-to-guess contract could not get it. **WHAT SHIPPED (mirrors the existing `_checked`-twin pattern verbatim — same error type, same docstring shape, same weekend/special-session data-complete carve-outs):** (1) `get_session_checked(d)` — muhurat + special-weekend sessions resolve to their held session WITHOUT raising (data-complete), a plain weekend resolves to `None` WITHOUT raising (a weekend is never a trading day, holiday list or not), and a plain weekday routes through `is_trading_day_checked` so an out-of-coverage weekday RAISES `HolidayDataUnavailableError` instead of fabricating a REGULAR session; in-coverage behaviour is byte-identical to `get_session`. (2) `trading_days_between_checked(start, end)` — routes each day through `is_trading_day_checked`, so a range containing an out-of-coverage weekday RAISES rather than silently including an unknown holiday as a trading day; a pure-weekend out-of-coverage span resolves without raising; in-coverage output equals `trading_days_between`. Both re-exported from `brutex/calendars/__init__.py` (`__all__`). **CALLERS — audit result (Golden Rule #9/#10, honest):** ALL FOUR `get_session` production callers are LEGITIMATELY LENIENT and were LEFT UNCHANGED — `engine/trade_sim.py:363` + `engine/rust_trade_sim.py:151` use `get_session` for the per-bar forced-exit time-of-day with a DOCUMENTED 15:20 fallback when `None` (DEC-SESSION-FORCED-EXIT-001; a crafted/malformed feed must not raise), `feed/bar_metadata.py:244` stamps a per-bar session-open on a REAL fed bar (falls back to `SESSION_OPEN_IST`), and `adapters/synthetic/generator.py:141` is the synthetic test-bar generator (deliberately fabricates sessions across arbitrary ranges — that IS its purpose). `trading_days_between` has ZERO production callers (only the definition + the `__init__` re-export). So NO caller does out-of-coverage date-reasoning that SHOULD be strict today — the twins are a DETECT-and-opt-in surface for future callers, exactly like `is_trading_day_checked` was when introduced. The lenient `get_session` / `trading_days_between` keep their byte-identical back-compat behaviour. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this closes a MAJOR correctness-honesty gap (a fabricated session for an unknown date) by ADDING an opt-in strict path, NOT by changing any existing behaviour; no caller was switched (none needed it — verified, not assumed); a switch to strict for any lenient caller would be a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE with regression risk and was deliberately NOT done (CLAUDE.md §9 — don't expand scope). **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after, 100% line+branch on `nse.py`):** `tests/unit/test_calendar_nse.py` gains `TestGetSessionChecked` (regular-weekday-in-range matches unchecked · in-range holiday → `None` · in-range weekend → `None` · muhurat session · out-of-coverage weekday 2030-06-24 RAISES while the unguarded FABRICATES a REGULAR session · out-of-coverage weekend/Sunday resolve `None` without raising · special-weekend override) + `TestTradingDaysBetweenChecked` (in-range matches unchecked · excludes in-range holiday · empty range · out-of-coverage weekday in span RAISES while unguarded INCLUDES it · pure-weekend out-of-coverage span resolves without raising). 1049. **DEC-AUDIT-RESUME-TAILREAD-001 — `AuditWriter.open(resume=True)` / `SweepAuditWriter.open(resume=True)` now recover the tail with an O(1) reverse read instead of loading the WHOLE hash-chained log into memory (PR-H13)** (2026-07-01; `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` (SHA256 ingest chain) + `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py` (BLAKE3 sweep chain) only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE DEFECT (Wave-3 verification on `origin/main` `1d13cdb3`, re-confirmed STILL-REAL before implementing):** both resume paths called `_read_entries_with_torn_tail(path)` — which parses EVERY line of the log into an `AuditEntry`/`SweepAuditEntry` list — only to read `entries[-1]` (its `seq + 1` and `entry_hash`) for the resumed chain seed. Under §11 AUTOMATED the watchdog auto-resume re-pays this full O(n) parse on EVERY restart. MEASURED cost of the discarded work: n=1000 → ~31 ms / ~654 KiB; n=50000 → ~1596 ms / ~32.8 MiB — a ~50× time+memory blow-up that scales with the whole log, for a value that lives on ONE line. **CRITICAL PRE-CHECK (answered honestly, the pivot of the whole fix — Golden Rule #10):** `open(resume=True)` was NOT doing whole-chain hash-VERIFICATION — it only PARSED the lines and used `entries[-1]`; it never cross-checked `seq`/`prev_hash`/recomputed `entry_hash` across the chain. Full-chain integrity verification is the SEPARATE `verify_chain(path)` contract (called by `brutex audit verify`), which is UNTOUCHED. Because resume never verified the chain, replacing the full parse with a tail-read loses NO integrity guarantee — it drops only redundant work. (Had resume been verifying, the full read would have been KEPT and only the tail-seq/hash read optimised — it was not, so the tail-read is safe.) **WHAT SHIPPED (one new function per chain — deliberately STANDALONE, SHA256 vs BLAKE3, no cross-import, mirroring the existing duplicated `_read_entries_with_torn_tail`/`_truncate_torn_tail` twins):** a NEW `_read_tail_entry(path) -> (last_committed_entry_or_None, torn_tail)` that opens the file binary, seeks to the END, and reads BACKWARDS in `_TAIL_CHUNK_BYTES` (8 KiB) chunks to isolate the FINAL committed (newline-terminated, non-blank) line — parsing ONLY that one line — plus a pure `_last_nonblank_committed_line(chunk)` helper that scans a byte chunk from the end for the last non-blank `\n`-terminated line. **TORN-TAIL PRESERVED byte-for-byte (DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-001 intact):** `torn_tail` is computed identically — the file's final line is a torn tail iff the file is non-empty AND does not end in `\n` (an interrupted append) — read via a single 1-byte seek to `size-1`; the resume path still calls `_truncate_torn_tail(path)` (unchanged: atomic `os.replace` of a sibling temp + best-effort `fsync`) BEFORE re-opening for append, so a torn remnant is dropped and the chain resumes on pristine bytes. **HASH-CHAIN INTEGRITY PRESERVED (Golden Rule #8):** the recovered tail entry's `seq + 1` + `entry_hash` seed the next append exactly as before; a garbage FINAL committed (newline-terminated) line is still parsed strictly and RAISES (real corruption, not a torn tail); mid-file integrity remains the `verify_chain` contract. `open(resume=True)` in both writers now calls `_read_tail_entry` and branches on `last is not None` (identical seed to the old `entries[-1]`); `_read_entries_with_torn_tail`/`_read_entries`/`read_entries` are KEPT for the non-resume callers (`verify_chain`, the dashboard tail view) that genuinely need every entry. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the reverse read is O(1) in the number of ENTRIES PARSED (exactly ONE — the final committed line) and O(tail-bytes) in I/O (one 1-byte seek + one or a few 8-KiB chunk reads, NOT the whole file), NOT a literal O(1)-total in every degenerate case (a single committed line LONGER than the chunk size loops back through it — bounded by that one line's length, still never the whole multi-entry log); the parse count is the load-bearing win and is CI-pinned. Correctness is byte-identical to the old full read for the tail seed + torn flag (parity-proven). **PARITY + TEETH TESTS (REAL, fails-before/passes-after, 100% line+branch on both touched files):** `tests/unit/test_audit_torn_tail.py` (the cross-chain SHA256+BLAKE3 dual-backend matrix) gains a full `_read_tail_entry` section — empty file, missing file (raise), single entry, many entries, a torn partial final line (recovers the last complete entry + parity), a file ending exactly on a newline vs mid-line, only-a-torn-line → `(None, True)`, trailing blank committed lines skipped, only-blank-lines → `(None, False)`, a corrupt committed final line RAISES, a multi-chunk reverse walk (monkeypatched 4-byte `_TAIL_CHUNK_BYTES`), a single line exceeding the chunk (the for/else exhaustion arm), resume-continues-a-valid-chain + resume-after-torn-truncates, a size-parametrised parity sweep, and the **O(1)-parse TEETH test** — a spy on `AuditEntry.from_json_line` / `SweepAuditEntry.from_json_line` proving a 500-entry log's tail-read invokes it EXACTLY ONCE while the old full read invokes it 500×, with both agreeing on the recovered tail entry (the load-bearing proof the fix is genuinely O(1)-parse, not merely faster). `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_audit.py` gains the sweep-side (BLAKE3) `_read_tail_entry` tests so `brutex.engine.sweep_audit` reaches 100% under the engine-only CI gate (`--cov=brutex.engine`, which runs ONLY `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py`); the `brutex.orchestrator.audit` strict gate already composes `test_audit_torn_tail.py` (DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-001 #1042). Verified 2026-07-01 on the scratchpad 3.13 venv (repo `python_requires` ≥ 3.12; PEP-695 generics): `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (226 stmt / 54 branch, 0 missing) over the composed audit gate (`test_orchestrator_audit.py` + `test_audit_torn_tail.py`, 170 passed) AND `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (217 stmt / 50 branch, 0 missing) under the full `--cov=brutex.engine` gate (all `test_engine_*.py`, 1264 passed at aggregate 100.00%); the audit chaos/property/stress/integration + sweep-resume-chaos suites green (271 + 7 passed); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all four files; `mypy --strict brutex/orchestrator/audit.py brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py` clean; `pyright` 0 errors on all four files (the `reportPrivateUsage` warnings on the whitebox test imports are PRE-EXISTING and `reportPrivateUsage = "warning"` per `[tool.pyright]`, byte-identical class on pristine `origin/main` — never errors); `git status --short rust/` empty. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py`, `tests/unit/test_audit_torn_tail.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_audit.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-AUDIT-RESUME-TAILREAD-001.
