1050. **DEC-LOOKAHEAD-HONESTY-001 — the look-ahead barrier docs no longer over-claim "belt-and-suspenders" strategy-look-ahead coverage they don't enforce, AND a rejected future index is recorded only AFTER the bounds check so a FAIL can't poison the touched-index trail (PR-H14)** (2026-07-01; `brutex/feed/lookahead.py` (one 3-line correctness reorder + honest docstrings) + `brutex/cli.py` (docstring/help/comment honesty only, the `cmd_verify_lookahead` BODY is `# pragma: no cover`) + `CLAUDE.md` §4 (the ONE over-claiming look-ahead bullet) only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE THREE FINDINGS (Wave-3 verification on `origin/main` `deb3398a`, all three re-confirmed STILL-REAL before implementing):** **(a)** the P-06 index barrier is INERT as a strategy-look-ahead guard in the runner/driver event loop — `strategies/runner.py:150,157` and `execution/driver.py:148,168` each `advance_to(step)` then `guard(step, event.bar)` at the SAME `step`, so `access(step)` always has `index == current_index` (never `> current_index`); a future-peeking STRATEGY reads off `state`, which the barrier never sees, so it cannot trip `LookAheadError` there — YET `CLAUDE.md` §4 + `feed/lookahead.py` overclaimed "belt-and-suspenders — the timestamp guard catches a future *signal*; the index barrier catches a future *bar read*". **(b)** `brutex verify-lookahead`'s `_replay_slice` (`cli.py:3542-3548`) is a tautology — it only does `advance_to(index); access(index)` per bar, `index == index`, so it PASSES for ANY non-empty slice and can NEVER fail, yet its docstring/help claimed it replays "exactly as the engine consumes them" and "a wiring regression that peeked ahead would [trip]". **(c)** `LookAheadBarrier.access` appended the touched index BEFORE the `index > current_index` bounds check (`feed/lookahead.py:179-185`), so a rejected future index POISONED `touched_indices` / `max_touched` (and a `LookAheadReport.max_index_touched`) on a FAIL. **FIX CHOSEN — (c) real correctness; (a)+(b) DOC-HONESTY (Golden Rule #10):** for (a) wiring the barrier into every strategy bar read would require routing all arbitrary strategy state reads through the barrier — an invasive/risky rewrite of the strategy read path with no clean seam — and the REAL strategy-look-ahead guard already exists and is integration-tested (`ReplayFeed.ensure_no_lookahead`, the *timestamp* check wired at `runner.py:207`), so per the operator's explicit "prefer the doc-honesty fix if wiring the barrier into every strategy read is invasive/risky" the docs were CORRECTED to state that the runner/driver barrier asserts only the advance/access CURSOR invariant (a feed/barrier desync or a wiring regression) and that `ensure_no_lookahead` is the real strategy-look-ahead guard; the barrier's index-`> N` teeth are genuinely exercised by the property tests + the manual recheck (an `access` at a future index), so the two guards are COMPLEMENTARY, not literally-redundant coverage of the same failure at the same site. For (b) making the CLI exercise real engine consumption would need standing up a StrategyRunner/BacktestDriver (a strategy + execution config the lake-slice shim has none of) — invasive — so the docstring/help/inline comment were CORRECTED to honestly say it re-confirms forward feed ORDERING + the advance/access cursor invariant over a lake slice (a lightweight ordering/cursor smoke check), NOT strategy consumption, and that a well-formed slice always PASSES by construction. **(c) THE CORRECTNESS FIX (clean, minimal):** `access` now runs the `index > current_index` guard FIRST and appends `index` to `_touched` ONLY after it passes, so a rejected look-ahead index never enters the trail; `touched_indices` / `max_touched` docstrings tightened to "*permitted* index". **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** (a)+(b) change ONLY documentation/help text — no runtime behaviour, no new teeth were faked; the genuine strategy-look-ahead defence (`ensure_no_lookahead`) is unchanged and was always the real guard; (c) is a small behaviour change (a FAIL's trail no longer contains the forbidden index) that makes the recorded audit trail HONEST (only permitted reads), with ZERO effect on the pass/fail verdict (`verify_with_barrier` still catches the `LookAheadError` and reports `passed=False`). **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after, 100% line+branch on the touched CODE module):** `tests/unit/test_lookahead_barrier.py` — the prior `test_violating_index_is_recorded_before_raising` (which PINNED the poisoning behaviour, asserting `touched_indices == (9,)`) is REPLACED by `test_rejected_index_is_not_recorded_and_does_not_poison_trail` (a permitted `access(1)` IS recorded, the rejected `access(9)` is NOT: `touched_indices == (1,)`, `max_touched == 1` not 9); `test_verify_detects_lookahead_run` flipped from `indices_checked == 2` / `max_index_touched == 3` to `indices_checked == 1` / `max_index_touched == 0` (the violating index no longer counted). `tests/property/test_lookahead_properties.py` gains `test_p06_rejected_index_never_enters_trail` (a hypothesis sweep proving after a permitted read + a forbidden `access(> N)` the trail holds only the permitted index and `max_touched <= current_index`). (a)+(b) are doc-only so need no test; the existing CLI dispatch test `test_main_dispatch_verify_lookahead_threads_slice` (which mocks `cmd_verify_lookahead`) is unaffected and still passes. Verified 2026-07-01 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv: `brutex/feed/lookahead.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (64 stmt / 12 branch, 0 missing) over `test_lookahead_barrier.py` + `test_lookahead_properties.py` (24 passed) AND `brutex/cli.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (600 stmt / 116 branch, 0 missing) over the composed CLI gate (`test_cli_*` unit+integration + `test_main_entrypoint` + `test_engine_stage3_wire` + `test_universe_phases` + `test_gated_prebuild_property` + `test_raw_integrity_wiring`, 223 passed) — the `cmd_verify_lookahead` docstring/comment edits ride the function's existing `# pragma: no cover`; the runner/driver/lookahead integration suites green (75 passed, 1 skip); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (292 files); `pyright` 0 errors on all touched files (the 23 pre-existing `hypothesis`-`@given`/`@composite` `draw` false-positives + 1 `test_doctor` artifact live in UNTOUCHED files, byte-identical on pristine `origin/main`, NONE introduced by this diff); the doc validators (`validate_no_hallucination` / `validate_dec_ids` / `no-dhan-guard` / `scan-banned-patterns`) exit 0; `git status --short rust/` empty. **Files:** `brutex/feed/lookahead.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `CLAUDE.md`, `tests/unit/test_lookahead_barrier.py`, `tests/property/test_lookahead_properties.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LOOKAHEAD-HONESTY-001. 1051. **DEC-EMA-PARITY-001 — the Python STREAMING EMA update now RAISES a `ValueError` on a seed that overflows to a non-finite value, matching the Rust core AND the Python batch path (was returning a poisoning `+inf`) (PR-H15)** (2026-07-01; `brutex/indicators/ema.py` (one finiteness re-check added to the streaming seed branch) + `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `# 18a` gate count comment refreshed) only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE DEFECT (Wave-3 verification on `origin/main` `11531bd1`, re-confirmed STILL-REAL before implementing):** `EMAState.update` (`ema.py:156-161`, the streaming path) computes its SMA seed at the seed bar (`bars_seen == period`) via the bare `trading_core.ema_seed(self.seed_sum, self.period)` FFI, which is a pure division that only guards `period < 1` — it does NOT re-check the RESULT's finiteness. So a run of finite-but-huge closes (e.g. two `1e308` closes) overflows `seed_sum` to `+inf`, and the streaming `update` RETURNED `inf` — poisoning every subsequent bar (`_ema_to_paisa(inf)` → a corrupt paisa) on the LIVE hot path `engine/stage1a.py:412-413` (`self._ema_fast.update(close_float)`). This DIVERGED from BOTH (i) the Rust core `EmaState::update` (`rust/trading-core/src/indicators/ema.rs:187-205`), which re-checks `is_finite(seed)` after the SMA and returns `Err` → mapped to a `ValueError` at the FFI; AND (ii) the Python BATCH path `compute_ema` (`ema.py:219` → `trading_core.compute_ema`), which delegates to that SAME Rust `update` and therefore already RAISED `ValueError("EMA seed overflowed to a non-finite value (inf); the warm-up close sum is too large")`. STEP-0 re-confirmed the split at runtime on the scratchpad venv: streaming `update` returned `inf`, while batch `compute_ema` and `trading_core.compute_ema` both raised the byte-identical `ValueError`. **THE FIX (mirror the Rust seed guard exactly — the streaming twin):** after the seed is computed, add `if not math.isfinite(seed): raise ValueError(...)` with the BYTE-IDENTICAL message the Rust guard emits (`"EMA seed overflowed to a non-finite value ({seed}); the warm-up close sum is too large"`), so the streaming `update`, the batch `compute_ema`, and the Rust core now behave IDENTICALLY: streaming == batch == Rust, all raising a catchable `ValueError` on an overflowed seed instead of one path poisoning downstream state with `inf`. The bare `trading_core.ema_seed` FFI is deliberately UNCHANGED (it is a pure division primitive used only here; the finiteness re-check lives at the STREAMING call site — the Python twin of the Rust `update` guard — not in the shared division). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** a MINOR correctness/parity fix — the divergence only manifests on an extreme finite-but-huge input sequence that overflows the f64 warm-up sum (real-magnitude NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX closes sum far below `f64::MAX`, so the golden seed is byte-unchanged and the happy path is untouched — the finite-series streaming output is bit-identical to before AND to the batch path); the per-`close` `math.isfinite(close)` guard already rejected a directly-non-finite close, so this closes the remaining seed-OVERFLOW gap where each close is individually finite but their sum is not. NO Rust change is required or made — the Rust core ALREADY guards; this is a PYTHON-side fix bringing the Python streaming path up to the Rust contract. **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after, 100% line+branch on `ema.py`):** `tests/unit/test_ema.py` gains `TestStreamingSeedOverflowGuard` (the streaming `update` RAISES not returns inf on two `1e308` seed-bar closes · the seed bar never emits a non-finite value · streaming == batch == Rust raise the byte-identical message · the guard leaves `value` `None` on a caught overflow · the normal finite series streams unchanged and == batch bit-for-bit) and `tests/integration/test_python_rust_parity.py` gains `TestEmaStreamingSeedParity` (the streaming path raises like the batch AND the Rust FFI on the SAME overflow input, and a real-magnitude series streams == batch == Rust bit-for-bit) — the existing `TestFfiOverflowGuards::test_compute_ema_finite_but_huge_seed_raises_not_inf` only exercised the Rust FFI/batch path, NOT the Python streaming `EMAState.update` where the divergence lived. Fails-before PROVEN: the 5 new raising tests all FAIL against the unfixed `ema.py` (stashed) and PASS after (the finite-series test passes either way). Verified 2026-07-01 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv: `brutex/indicators/ema.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (59 stmt / 16 branch, 0 missing) over the CI per-module gate (`--cov=brutex.indicators.ema … tests/unit/test_ema.py`, 37 passed); `tests/integration/test_python_rust_parity.py` (12 passed); the vocab-parity validator `scripts/check_vocab_rust_parity.py` exits 0 (400 golden vectors, 0 mismatches); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (292 files); `pyright` 0 errors on all touched files (the 23 pre-existing `hypothesis`-`@given`/`@composite` `draw` false-positives + 1 `test_doctor` artifact live in UNTOUCHED files, byte-identical on pristine `origin/main`, NONE introduced by this diff); `git status --short rust/` empty. **Files:** `brutex/indicators/ema.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tests/unit/test_ema.py`, `tests/integration/test_python_rust_parity.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-EMA-PARITY-001. (Ledger: #1051 = next free unique number above the file's current max #1050 `DEC-LOOKAHEAD-HONESTY-001`; the DEC-ID is the stable handle — re-checked immediately before push.)


1052. **DEC-UNIVERSE-PER-PHASE-PROGRESS-001 — the `/universe` pull section now shows, for EVERY window phase (spot / futures / options), a LIVE windows count + progress bar + status breakdown — CONSISTENTLY, so each phase reads identically as the pull runs** (2026-07-01; `brutex/dashboard/pull_progress.py` + `pull_jobs.py` + `db_view.py` + `app.py` (route + `_work` phase tags) + `templates/universe.html` + tests only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; READ-ONLY dashboard + a pull-PLANNING phase LABEL only — no pacing/fetch change; NO Rust touched). **THE GAP:** the live `/api/v1/universe/pull-progress` payload was a SINGLE, phase-UNAWARE aggregate — all three phases (spot → metadata → historical=futures+options) share ONE `BackgroundPullJob`/`PullProgress`, so as each phase runs it OVERWRITES the shared counters and only the CURRENTLY-running phase's numbers are visible; futures vs options were never separated at all. The per-segment window counts DID already exist, cached: `db_view._window_counts_total(conn, ledger_glob)` returns `{spot|futures|options: {STATUS: n}}`, memoised in the generation-stamped `_window_counts_cache` (`MoversSnapshotCache`) keyed `(generation, ledger-mtime)` — the SAME source the `/coverage/windows` page reads. **THE FIX (additive, REUSE-not-rescan):** (1) NEW pure `db_view.phase_window_progress(counts_for_bucket)` folds ONE bucket's status counts into `{done=SUCCESS+SKIPPED, total=all-5-summed, success, empty, failed, pending=PLANNED}` (O(1), the SUCCESS+SKIPPED settled authority = `SETTLED_STATUSES`, re-declared inline as string literals so the pure display projection needs no `window_ledger` import); (2) NEW pure `fno_current_phase_from_counts` refines the coarse `historical` label to futures-vs-options from the counts (futures is current while it has PLANNED work or no windows yet, else options) — the mapping-doc's lower-touch path, so NO segment tag is threaded through the F&O spine; (3) NEW pure `build_phase_progress(counts, *, current_phase)` assembles ONE row per `WINDOW_PHASES` (spot/futures/options, pull order) + the current-phase flag (spot label → spot; historical/futures/options label → the counts-refined sub-phase; metadata/idle/unknown → NO window row current, since metadata writes no windows); (4) NEW `phase_progress_payload(conn, lake_root, *, current_phase, count_cache, generation)` reads the per-segment counts THROUGH the SAME `(generation, ledger-mtime)` cache key `_build_window_payload_duckdb` uses (two routes now share ONE warm entry — a WIN, NO new O(files) scan; O(1) on a repeat poll), None-safe (no ledger Parquet → `[]`); (5) `PullProgress`/`BackgroundPullJob` gain an O(1) `phase` slot + `set_phase()` (a LABEL only — no counter is keyed by it, so a stale/empty phase can never fabricate progress) surfaced in `ProgressSnapshot.phase`/`to_dict`, set by the one-click pipeline's `_work` at each transition (`spot` → `metadata` → `historical`, the F&O sub-phase derived from counts); (6) the `/api/v1/universe/pull-progress` route ADDS a `phases` array ALONGSIDE every existing flat snapshot key (never removed), read on the threadpool (store RLock stays on one thread, DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001); (7) FRONTEND `universe.html` — a NEW `#phaseProgress` block rendered by `renderPhases()` inside the EXISTING `pollProgress` poll (ZERO extra button/poll), three identical rows (name · done/total windows · progress bar · status breakdown) with the current phase highlighted, built with `createElement`/`textContent` (NEVER `innerHTML` — the CodeQL XSS guard; 1055. **DEC-GROWW-HTTP-SOCKET-TIMEOUT-001 — every underlying Groww SDK HTTP request now carries a connect + read SOCKET timeout, so a half-open / dead socket fails in SECONDS instead of burning the 45 s wall-clock guard × ~6 retries (~4.5 min/window) on a flaky network** (2026-07-01; NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/http_timeout.py` + `brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py` (the one factory seam) + `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` (a robust class-name timeout classifier) + `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py` (two new tunables) only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty. **NO pacing change** — the AIMD ladder, per-second ceiling (Rule 6), 500/min governor, and ledger logic are all byte-untouched). **THE GAP (network-resilience sweep GAP-1, re-confirmed against the ACTUALLY-INSTALLED `growwapi` SDK before implementing):** the SDK issues EVERY REST call through **module-level `requests`** — `GrowwAPI._request_get` / `_request_post` / `_request_put` (`growwapi/groww/client.py:1380-1483`) each call `requests.get(url, ..., timeout=timeout, **kwargs)` where the per-call `timeout` **DEFAULTS TO `None` (INFINITE)**, and `get_historical_candles` / `get_expiries` / `get_contracts` (`client.py:875-994`) all funnel through `_request_get` WITHOUT forwarding one; BruteX's `GrowwClient` never passes a timeout either. So the ONLY bound on a half-open / dead socket was the 45 s wall-clock FREEZE GUARD (`GROWW_PULL_CALL_TIMEOUT_S`, run via `run_with_deadline` in `client.py:198-204`), which on a flaky network burns 45 s × the bounded retry ladder (~6 attempts) ≈ 4.5 min PER window before the transient is even classified. **THE SEAM (investigated the REAL SDK first — no assumption):** the installed SDK exposes NO `requests.Session` object to mount an `HTTPAdapter` on (verified: `hasattr(GrowwAPI, 'session')` is False; it uses module-level `requests.get`/`post`/`put`), but the three `_request_*` bound methods DO honour an explicit `timeout` kwarg — they simply default it to `None`. So the cleanest, most-robust reach to the socket layer is to **WRAP each of the three bound methods at construction time** so a call that passes `timeout=None` (every call BruteX makes) is transparently rewritten to `timeout=(connect, read)` (a `requests` connect-and-read tuple), while an EXPLICIT non-`None` timeout is left untouched (the SDK's own timed `get_access_token` static path's hardcoded 15 s keeps its value). This mutates the constructed instance's `__dict__` (an instance attribute SHADOWING the class method), NOT the `GrowwAPI` class, so it is per-connection and can never leak into another SDK object. **THE FIX (applied at the SINGLE COMMON factory seam so BOTH live build sites inherit it, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** NEW `http_timeout.py` `apply_default_timeout(sdk, *, timeout=None)` (dependency-free — patches ANY object with the three `_request_*` callables, so it is unit-tested against a fake with no `growwapi` / `requests` / network) + `resolve_http_timeout()` (env-tunable `(connect, read)`, mirroring `write_deadline.resolve_write_deadline_seconds`'s validation shape — a blank / non-numeric / non-finite / non-positive env value fails SAFE to the audited default, so a bad value can NEVER disable the bound, Golden Rule #1); `reauth._real_sdk_factory` (the `# pragma: no cover` default `sdk_factory` BOTH `live.build_live_client` + `live.build_live_pool` default to) now returns `apply_default_timeout(GrowwAPI(token))`. NEW constants `GROWW_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S=10.0` + `GROWW_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT_S=30.0` (env `BRUTEX_GROWW_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S` / `BRUTEX_GROWW_HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT_S`), BOTH comfortably BELOW the 45 s wall-clock cap so the socket timeout fires FIRST — the 45 s guard stays as belt-and-suspenders for a hang OUTSIDE the socket (a wedged non-network syscall the socket timeout cannot see). **CLASSIFICATION (already-retryable, made ROBUST):** a resulting `requests.ConnectTimeout` / `requests.ReadTimeout` / base `requests.Timeout` / stdlib `socket.timeout` is now mapped to a RETRYABLE `GrowwTimeoutError` by a NEW `_TIMEOUT_ERROR_NAMES` frozenset (`{"ReadTimeout","ConnectTimeout","Timeout","timeout"}`) matched by CLASS NAME — INDEPENDENT of the `requests` message text (which varies by version / pool wrapper) and needing neither `requests` nor `urllib3` importable (the optional-extra resilience, mirroring `_NETWORK_ERROR_NAMES`). Checked in `from_groww_exception` AFTER the typed Groww SDK map (a vendor-typed error always wins) but BEFORE `_NETWORK_ERROR_NAMES`, so a `ConnectTimeout` (which is ALSO a `requests.ConnectionError` by inheritance, but whose OWN class name is `"ConnectTimeout"`, not in the network set) reads as a TIMEOUT (the gentle timeout ladder), never a plain network blip. A socket timeout is NOT a quota signal, so it rides `GrowwTimeoutError` (already in `is_retryable`, NOT `is_rate_limit`) — it flows into the existing retry → defer → re-pull machinery and never steps the per-second rate ceiling down. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the wall-clock guard runs the SDK call in a daemon thread and abandons it on timeout — it FREES the fetch lane but the zombie `requests` call keeps its socket open until the OS finally gives up (which on an infinite timeout may be minutes); the socket timeout makes the SDK ITSELF raise in seconds, so both bounds now coexist (socket timeout fires first for a network stall; 45 s wall-clock remains for a non-socket hang). A missing `_request_*` helper (an SDK-shape change) DEGRADES that method to no-patch + a `groww.http_timeout.missing_method` structlog warning rather than crashing the pull (the 45 s guard still bounds an un-patched call). Best-effort per construction (three attribute wraps, O(1) — NOT a per-request cost). **PROVEN AGAINST THE REAL SDK (scratchpad 3.12 venv with `growwapi` + `requests` 2.34.2 installed):** a real `GrowwAPI('faketoken')` after `apply_default_timeout` issues `_request_get` with `timeout=(10.0, 30.0)` injected on an omitted call and preserves an explicit `5`; a REAL local socket that accepts then STALLS raises `requests.ReadTimeout` in **1.00 s** (the 1 s read timeout), NOT 45 s — the fail-fast regression teeth. **Tests (REAL, 100% line+branch on every touched source file):** NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_http_timeout.py` (24 — every env-resolution branch incl. `nan`/`inf`/`-1`/blank fails-safe · injection on omitted + `timeout=None` · explicit-timeout preserved · all three helpers patched · returns-same-object · env-override resolution · a missing AND a non-callable helper skipped+warned · positional-arg + return-value pass-through through GET/POST/PUT · both defaults below the 45 s cap · **hostile-review NIT-1: a `timeout` passed POSITIONALLY on a bindable-signature helper is honoured, never double-injected — no `TypeError: multiple values`** · **hostile-review MAJOR: a `pytest.importorskip("growwapi")` contract test pins the REAL `growwapi.GrowwAPI._request_get`/`_request_post`/`_request_put` are still callable, so a future private-API rename that would SILENTLY no-op the patch FAILS CI loudly**) + NEW `tests/unit/test_groww_socket_timeout_failfast.py` (the fail-fast teeth: a stalled real socket raises `ReadTimeout` within the read timeout ≪ 45 s AND classifies retryable) + `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py` gains `test_socket_timeout_classified_retryable` (parametrised `ReadTimeout`/`ConnectTimeout`/`Timeout` → retryable `GrowwTimeoutError`, not rate-limit) + `test_connect_timeout_reads_as_timeout_not_network` (the name-split priority) + `test_typed_groww_class_wins_over_timeout_name_collision` + `tests/unit/test_groww_constants.py` gains `test_http_socket_timeouts_are_below_the_wall_clock_cap`. Verified 2026-07-01 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv: `brutex/adapters/groww/http_timeout.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (40 stmt / 10 branch, 0 missing), `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py` **100.00%** (60/22, 0 missing), `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py` **100.00%** (66/6, 0 missing), `brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py` stays **100.00%** (80/6, 0 missing — the factory body rides the pre-existing `# pragma: no cover`); 924 groww unit tests + 56 groww/ingest/live/pull integration tests green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 8 touched files; `mypy --strict` clean on `http_timeout.py`/`errors.py`/`constants.py` + the new test files (the `reauth.py` `growwapi` `import-untyped`/`unused-ignore` is a PRE-EXISTING env artifact — byte-identical on pristine `origin/main` where `growwapi` is likewise installed, and the CI type-check job runs WITHOUT the optional extra so `import-not-found` is correct there); `pyright` 0 errors on all 8 touched files (the 2 `reportPrivateUsage` warnings on the `reauth.py` `_real_token_factory`/`_real_totp` imports are PRE-EXISTING, byte-identical on `origin/main`; the whitebox test files silence `reportPrivateUsage` at the file top per the DEC-P0-017 convention); `git status --short rust/` empty. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/http_timeout.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_http_timeout.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_socket_timeout_failfast.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_constants.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-HTTP-SOCKET-TIMEOUT-001. 1056. **DEC-RATE-WIDGET-FNO-MEASURED-001 — the live PULL RATE widget's "achieved r/s" now shows the REAL MEASURED completed rate during the metadata + F&O phases too (not an honest 0), by REGISTERING the client pool's shared transport `CallMeter` into the session controller so the observe-only sampler can reach it — the follow-up that closes the reachability gap DEC-RATE-WIDGET-FNO-HONEST-001 (#1022) could not** (2026-07-01; `brutex/dashboard/` READ-ONLY observe-only wiring only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO pacing/rate-cap change (fetch rate byte-unchanged), NO scope/52→60-vocab/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **ROOT (the #1022 gap):** the SPOT phase feeds the widget the transport `CallMeter`'s MEASURED completed-rate via the per-window observe, but the METADATA + long F&O phases have NO rate-observe seam, so #1022 — correctly refusing to fabricate `effective_rps = recent_minute/60` (which OVER-reported admissions ≥ completions AND blinded the stall verdict) — pushed a bare `meter_present=False` sentinel, leaving "achieved" an HONEST 0 for the ENTIRE ~38-min F&O phase. #1022 judged the F&O meter genuinely UNREACHABLE from the sampler seam (it is built fresh inside `build_live_pool`→`_build_live_client`, deep in the pull spine, and the `SessionRateController` held only the `RateController`). **THE INSIGHT (this PR):** the meter is unreachable from the SAMPLER, but the pull BUILD SITES both build the client pool AND receive the session controller — so they can PUBLISH the pool's shared meter into the controller, from where the sampler reads it. **WHAT SHIPPED (all in `brutex/dashboard/`):** (1) `SessionRateController` gains a thread-safe `register_meter(meter)` / `peek_meter()` pair (the meter twin of `get`/`peek`) storing a READ handle to the pool's shared `CallMeter`; `register_meter(None)` is silently ignored so a transient no-`.meter` factory oddity never blanks a live meter, a second pull's pool meter overwrites (the pool holds ONE aggregate). (2) NEW COMMON `register_pull_meter(session_rate, source)` seam (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — no copy of the extraction) mirrors `_observe_rate`'s `getattr` probe: it reads `.meter` on *source* (a `ClientPool`/`GrowwClient`) and, failing that, on `source.client.meter` (a `MarketAdapter`); a `None` session OR a source with no meter is a NO-OP. (3) the THREE pull build sites call it right after building their pool/client — `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` (`register_pull_meter(session_rate, adapter)`), F&O `pull_contract_candles` (`register_pull_meter(session_rate, client)`, lazy import to avoid a module-load cycle), metadata `pull_expiries_contracts` (same) — so the shared meter reaches the observe-only `RatePanelSampler`. (4) `rate_sampler.sample_once` now reads `peek_meter()`: when a meter is registered it pushes the meter's REAL `snapshot()` (the MEASURED `effective_rps`; a genuine `CallMeter` snapshot carries no `meter_present` key so the observer defaults it `True` — the measured-completed slot), else it falls back to the honest `{"meter_present": False}` sentinel of #1022 (NEVER the old admission fabrication). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** READ-ONLY + observe-only — `register_pull_meter` stores a handle and changes NO pacing decision, can never block/crash the pull (a dry-run / injected-factory pull with no live `session_rate`, or a client with no `.meter`, is a silent no-op leaving the honest-0 fallback); the widget stays LIVE in F&O (the #1000 visibility win preserved) but now tells the TRUTH — "achieved" is the MEASURED completed rate where a meter is registered, an honest 0 (with the admission average still in its OWN `req_per_min_rate` field) before the pool is built; the F&O phase now ALSO catches an issued-but-ALL-FAILING pull (`meter_present=True` → the stall verdict reads the MEASURED `effective_rps`, so a completed-rate at/below the floor reads STALLED — the fake-alive case #1022 could not catch in F&O), end to end through the real `/api/v1/pull/rate` route. **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after):** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` — `TestSessionRateControllerMeter` (peek-before-register is None / register-then-peek returns the SAME instance / register-None-ignored keeps the prior meter / second-meter overwrites) + `TestRegisterPullMeter` (None-session no-op / registers from a pool's `.meter` directly / registers from an adapter's `.client.meter` / a source with no meter anywhere is a no-op). `tests/unit/test_dashboard_rate_sampler.py` — `test_registered_meter_pushes_measured_snapshot` (a REGISTERED meter → the sampler forwards the MEASURED snapshot verbatim, `effective_rps` 2.82 NOT the admission avg 3.4, no `meter_present` sentinel) alongside the preserved meter-absent fallback tests. `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py::TestFnoPhaseLiveness` — `test_sampler_reports_measured_rate_when_meter_registered` (a real `CallMeter` measuring 28 completions/10 s → the F&O route's `req_per_sec_achieved` reads the MEASURED 2.8, NOT the honest-0 fallback and NOT the admission avg 6.0, admission avg still separate in `req_per_min_rate`) + `test_measured_meter_below_floor_reads_stalled_in_fno` (a busily-admitting controller + a fresh 0-completion meter → the F&O route reads STALLED, the issued-but-failing case now caught). Verified 2026-07-01 on the scratchpad 3.12 venv: all FOUR touched source modules at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** — `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` (460 stmt / 104 branch, 0 missing), `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` (261 stmt / 56 branch, 0 missing), `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py` (169 stmt / 36 branch, 0 missing), `brutex/dashboard/rate_sampler.py` (52 stmt / 8 branch, 0 missing) — each over its full covering test set (`scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py` OK for the two it maps; the two large modules measured explicitly over their pipeline/route suites); 143 rate-sampler+controller+monitor tests green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files; `mypy --strict` clean on the four touched source files (`--follow-imports=silent`; the 4 pre-existing `growwapi`-stub errors in UNTOUCHED `auth.py`/`reauth.py` are byte-identical on pristine `origin/main`, NONE introduced by this diff); `pyright` 0 errors on all touched files (the `reportPrivateUsage` WARNINGs on `_issues`/`_clock`/`_drive`/`_stop`/`_running` in the test files are non-fatal and predate this diff on `origin/main`). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/metadata_pull.py`, `brutex/dashboard/rate_sampler.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_rate_sampler.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-RATE-WIDGET-FNO-MEASURED-001. 1057. **DEC-SUPERVISOR-AUTORESTART-001 — a process supervisor that closes the ONE real §11 AUTOMATED gap: the sweep watchdogs only DETECT a crash — nothing AUTO-RELAUNCHED the process after a hard crash / reboot (the operator had to re-run the command). Now `brutex supervisor` auto-relaunches the sweep daemon with exponential backoff + a max-restart cap, and launchd/systemd templates survive a reboot** (2026-07-01; orchestrator + CLI + docs only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE GAP (verified on current main):** `brutex/observability/watchdog.py` + `brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py` are pure DETECTORS — they detect a hung worker / a retry storm and fire callbacks, but NOTHING relaunches the process after a hard crash / reboot; the `sweep_watchdog.py` docstring even flagged "it does not kill the worker — termination / restart is the supervisor's policy decision, wired in a Wave-2 follow-up". The sweep's checkpoint auto-resume (DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001) already makes a RELAUNCH bit-identical (chaos-tested), so all that was missing was something to DO the relaunch. **TWO complementary pieces shipped (both close the gap):** **(1) `brutex/orchestrator/supervisor.py` `ProcessSupervisor`** — a PURE, dependency-injected supervise loop (mirrors the two watchdogs' design): inject the child-launch callable, the `BackoffPolicy` (base/factor/cap/reset-after-uptime/max-restarts), the audit sink, a monotonic clock, and a sleeper, so it is deterministic + 100%-tested with a FAKE child + injected clock/sleeper (no real subprocess/sleep). It handles: child exits 0 → STOP (no relaunch); child exits non-zero OR dies by signal (negative POSIX returncode) → RELAUNCH after `min(base·factor^n, cap)` backoff; an operator SIGTERM/SIGINT that arrives WHILE the child is alive → the supervisor ACTUALLY TERMINATES the child (graceful `shutdown_child`: SIGTERM → bounded grace wait → SIGKILL) and does NOT relaunch — the child is never orphaned; `max_restarts` consecutive crashes → GIVE UP loudly (audit row + `EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR`); a child up longer than `reset_after_uptime_seconds` before dying RESETS the backoff (a long-lived crash is not a crash loop). **The operator-stop wait is INTERRUPTIBLE (the headline fix):** the loop polls `child.wait_for(poll_interval_seconds)` in short slices and re-checks the stop predicate BETWEEN slices — a bare blocking `os.waitpid` is NOT interrupted by a delivered signal (PEP 475 auto-retries it), so a single `child.wait()` would have blocked until the child died on its own and the operator stop would never be acted on (an orphaned-child / double-spawn bug); the sliced backoff sleep is likewise interruptible so a stop DURING a long backoff is prompt. The CLI `cmd_supervisor` wires `install_signal_stop()` into `stop_requested`, so a real SIGTERM/SIGINT trips the flag the loop now acts on. Every restart / clean-exit / operator-stop / give-up appends ONE hash-chained audit row (`SUPERVISOR_RESTART`/`SUPERVISOR_CLEAN_EXIT`/`SUPERVISOR_OPERATOR_STOP`/`SUPERVISOR_GIVE_UP`; the operator-stop row's `phase` is `pre_launch`/`shutdown`/`post_exit`/`during_backoff`) to `<lake>/sweeps/audit/supervisor.jsonl` (Golden Rule #8, observable). O(1) state per restart (a counter + last-exit record), bounded memory (a 500-crash run adds NO state — proven). The production adapters (`PopenChildProcess` over a real `subprocess.Popen` started `start_new_session=True` in its own process group, `build_subprocess_launcher`, `install_signal_stop`) are `# pragma: no cover` — the SAME live-side-effect boundary the CLI daemon loop is excluded at — with ONE deterministic real-subprocess integration test proving the wrapper wiring (crash-once-then-succeed via a marker file → exactly one relaunch); the pure `_SignalStop` latch is un-pragma'd + unit-tested. **Wired to a `brutex supervisor` CLI subcommand** (`cmd_supervisor`, `# pragma: no cover` live-loop shim) that spawns `<python> -m brutex sweep-daemon <forwarded args after -->` as the child. **(2) OS-service templates** (the real hard-reboot solution, config the operator installs once — no code test): `docs/runbooks/supervisor-templates/com.brutex.supervisor.plist` (launchd `KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit=false}` → macOS relaunches on a NON-ZERO exit / reboot, NOT on a clean exit 0 so a completed sweep does not spin-loop) + `docs/runbooks/supervisor-templates/brutex-supervisor.service` (systemd `Restart=on-failure`, same clean-exit-does-not-relaunch semantics) + a full install runbook `docs/runbooks/supervisor-autorestart.md` (documenting both are for the always-on `--schedule` mode; `--once` must NOT run under an unconditional keep-alive). The two layers are COMPLEMENTARY: the OS service keeps the SUPERVISOR alive across reboots; the supervisor keeps the SWEEP DAEMON alive across in-session crashes. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the in-process supervisor survives a CHILD crash while the supervisor itself is alive — surviving a machine REBOOT/logout is the OS service manager's job (the shipped templates); a wedged/unkillable child (uninterruptible-sleep kernel hang) cannot be force-killed by any userspace supervisor (`shutdown_child` escalates SIGTERM → SIGKILL and reports honestly if it still will not die); this bounds WHEN a relaunch happens, not the sweep's O(Σ work) — a resumed sweep still costs the §8 wall-time envelope, no "millions in minutes" claim. **Hostile-review FIX-FIRST folded (this revision):** the initial cut of `run()` only checked `stop_requested()` AFTER `child.wait()` RETURNED and never called `shutdown_child`, so a `launchctl stop` / bare `kill` orphaned the child (it kept running while the supervisor spun a fresh one) — the MAJOR correctness bug. FIXED as above (interruptible poll + terminate-while-alive + own process group). Also folded: the launchd/systemd templates flipped from the unconditional `KeepAlive=true` / `Restart=always` (which spin-loop a clean `--once` completion) to `{SuccessfulExit=false}` / `on-failure`; the sliced-sleep interruptibility; the `_SignalStop` latch un-pragma'd + tested; and the CI gates cleared — **bandit** (B404/B603 on the justified list-form `subprocess.Popen(argv)` with no `shell=` given a minimal per-line `# nosec B404`/`# nosec B603` + inline safety comment), **No-dhan guard** (the `Chil`+`dHan`+`dle` false-positive in `ChildHandle`/`PopenChildHandle` renamed to `ChildProcess`/`PopenChildProcess`), the **DEC-ID validator** (the bogus `DEC-SWEEP-CHECKPOINT-001` citation → the real `DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001` ledger entry, in code + runbook + this ledger + the PR body), the **6× CodeQL "Statement has no effect"** (the bare `...` bodies of the `ChildProcess`/`AuditSink` Protocol stubs — new-file alerts, since the identical docstring-`+...` pattern is baseline-suppressed on pre-existing Protocols — replaced with docstring-only bodies), and the **CodeQL "variable defined multiple times"** (the redundant `launcher =` reassignment at `test_orchestrator_supervisor.py`). **Verified 2026-07-01 (fresh isolated 3.12 venv):** `brutex/orchestrator/supervisor.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** over the NEW CI per-module gate (`--cov=brutex.orchestrator.supervisor … tests/unit/test_orchestrator_supervisor.py`); the real-subprocess integration test (`tests/integration/test_supervisor_real_subprocess.py`, 1 passed) — INCLUDING the NEW run()-level test that flips the stop flag WHILE the fake child is alive and asserts the child was TERMINATED + outcome OPERATOR_STOP + NO relaunch, the SIGTERM→SIGKILL-on-ignored-terminate escalation on that path, the sliced-sleep promptness, and the `_SignalStop` latch; 1062. **DEC-NIFTY-FIB-AXIS-001 — the three Fibonacci-anchor strategy families (prev-day / rolling-weekly / weekly-static) are now a SWEPT AXIS of the brute-force grid, so a sweep actually tests all three strategies (before this PR the Stage-1A builder HARDCODED the anchor to prev-day, so 2 of the 3 declared families NEVER appeared in any result)** (2026-07-01; `brutex/engine/` + `brutex/strategies/` + `brutex/cli.py` only — ENGINE scope UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; the anchor is a swept STRATEGY parameter per ADR-0012 D4, NOT a new vocabulary bit — the 60-condition vocab is UNTOUCHED; NO rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `trading_core.compute_fib_levels(high, low)` is anchor-AGNOSTIC, so the anchor CHOICE is pure Python, `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE GAP (readiness-audit #1 architectural blocker, confirmed against real code):** `brutex/strategies/fib_definitions.py` declares the 3 anchor families + a runnable `resolve_fib_levels` dispatcher, but the SWEEP engine imported NONE of it — `stage1a.py::_compute_anchors` fed `prev_ohlc.high/low` into `compute_fib_levels` UNCONDITIONALLY, and the grid enumerated `instrument × tf × direction × k × sl × tp × proximity` with NO anchor axis, so every sweep result used ONE anchor (prev-day). **WHAT SHIPPED — the axis threaded end-to-end (COMMON, CLAUDE.md §11):** (1) `FibAnchorKind` RELOCATED to the pure-leaf `brutex/strategies/types.py` (already imported by `brutex.engine.*`) so the engine threads it as a grid axis WITHOUT pulling `fib_definitions`' `dashboard.combo_decoder` import into the engine graph; `fib_definitions` re-exports it (one enum). (2) NEW pure `resolve_fib_anchor_levels(anchor, today, daily)` in `fib_definitions.py` — the ONE anchor→(high,low)→Fib dispatcher (takes the enum directly), consumed by BOTH `resolve_fib_levels` AND the engine; `stage1a` reuses it, never re-implements the 3-way branch. (3) `stage1a.Stage1AMatrixBuilder` / `build_bar_bits` gain `fib_anchor=FibAnchorKind.PREV_DAY` (DEFAULT-PRESERVING — the goldens still pin the same matrix) + a BOUNDED rolling daily-candle history (`_DAILY_HISTORY_MAX = 15` completed days, O(1)/bar — R-4) that the multi-day rolling-weekly / weekly-static anchors read; `_compute_anchors` dispatches Fib on the anchor while pivots STAY prev-day (R-2). (4) `SweepGridConfig` gains a `fib_anchors` axis (default `(PREV_DAY,)`, deduped + non-empty-guarded), threaded through `SweepTuple.fib_anchor` → `count_sweep_tuples`/`iter_sweep_tuples`/`bloom_capacity_hint` (all ×`|fib_anchors|`) → `_tuple_digest` (the store address) → `to_run_config` → `SweepRunConfig.fib_anchor` → `build_bar_bits`. (5) **RUN-IDENTITY (Golden Rule #4, the settled decision):** the anchor enters `canonical_trade_params` UNCONDITIONALLY as `"fib_anchor": fib_anchor.value` (`brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`, the ONE params-layout source) — so each strategy gets a distinct, reproducible `combo_hash`; NOT omitted for the prev-day default (no production sweep tree exists yet, so this is a zero-cost identity choice; no `indicator_version` bump needed since the anchor IS in the params). (6) **R-1 (resident kernel):** `ResidentSweepKernel`/`ResidentKernelCache` carry + KEY ON the anchor (the `bar_bits` matrix is anchor-specific), and `run_persisted_sweep` FAILS-FAST when a kernel's anchor ≠ the tuple's (like the existing `n_bars` guard). (7) **R-2 (Fib-only cold-start clear):** `_NON_FIB_MASK` clears ONLY the Group-4 Fib bits (19-29) on a Fib-cold-but-pivot-warm day (a cold rolling-weekly week keeps its warm prev-day pivots) — `FIB_DEPENDENT_MASK` + `PIVOT_DEPENDENT_MASK` are DISJOINT and their union is the unchanged `ANCHOR_DEPENDENT_MASK` (first-day clear byte-identical, no Fib level fabricated on a cold week — Golden Rule #1). (8) the CLI `sweep-all`/`sweep-daemon`/`sweep-verify` gain a `--fib-anchors` CSV arg (default `prev_day`, byte-identical). **SCOPE-BIGGER-THAN-THE-DESIGN-DOC (folded for Golden Rule #4 consistency, honest):** the design checklist listed the store digest + run-identity but MISSED three consistency surfaces the identity change required — `sweep_supervisor._grid_descriptor` (checkpoint identity) + `_tuple_cache_params` (cache-skip key, else a false-skip of the 2nd anchor), and `stage3_wire.recover_survivor_cell` + the `Stage3CellRecord` manifest (Stage-3 default-OFF re-derives run_ids over the `sl×tp×proximity×fib_anchor` product; the manifest cell gained an ADDITIVE `fib_anchor` field defaulting to prev-day, the `rel_path` precedent), + `sweep_verify` reproduction. These are the SAME mechanical additive threading, NOT riskier — every path defaults to prev-day = byte-identical. **STAGE-4 CASCADE ANCHOR THREADING — BOTH cascade-input paths (hostile-review MAJOR + a re-review BLOCKER, both folded before merge — `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py` + `brutex/engine/stage3_wire.py` + `brutex/cli.py`):** the Stage-3→Stage-4 handoff dropped the swept anchor, so the CPCV/robustness re-simulation re-scored a non-prev-day survivor against the WRONG (prev-day) Fib levels. TWO distinct spec-assembly sites feed the Stage-4 cascade — the Stage-3 refined-cell path (`cascade_specs_for_refined_cells`, `stage3_wire.py`) AND the Stage-2 grid-winner path (`cmd_sweep_all`, `cli.py`) — and BOTH now thread the anchor: (a) `CascadeTupleSpec` gains `fib_anchor: FibAnchorKind = FibAnchorKind.PREV_DAY`; `spec_from_store_rows` gains a `fib_anchor` kwarg carried onto the spec; `candidates_for_spec` threads `fib_anchor=spec.fib_anchor` into `build_bar_bits`; the manifest `_spec_to_dict`/`_spec_from_dict` round-trip the anchor (additive parse — a pre-axis manifest defaults prev-day, the SAME precedent). (b) the Stage-3 refined-cell site passes `tuple_.fib_anchor` into `spec_from_store_rows` (`stage3_wire.py:848`). (c) **the re-review BLOCKER — the Stage-2 grid-winner cascade in `cmd_sweep_all` also feeds these specs, and it was MISSED in the first pass** (it built specs via `spec_from_store_rows(...)` with NO `fib_anchor=`, so a non-prev-day grid winner was STILL re-scored against prev-day Fib in Stage-4). FIX: the inline Stage-2 assembly loop was FACTORED OUT of the pragma'd `cmd_sweep_all` shim into a new pragma-free, unit-tested helper `cascade_wire.build_stage2_cascade_specs(results_root, grid, *, top_k)` that threads `fib_anchor=sweep_tuple.fib_anchor` onto each grid-winner spec; `cmd_sweep_all` now calls it. So EVERY Stage-4-reachable `spec_from_store_rows`/`CascadeTupleSpec` site (grid winners + refined cells + manifest replay) carries the swept anchor — no path defaults prev-day for a swept non-prev-day tuple. DEFAULT-PRESERVING everywhere (an unset `fib_anchor` is byte-identical to the prev-day cascade). Proven by fails-before/passes-after tests: (i) a ROLLING_WEEKLY refined cell over a multi-day history whose prev-day and rolling-weekly Fib windows differ (2021-01-19) produces a cascade candidate whose Group-4 Fib bit fires under rolling-weekly (30 test-day entries) but NOT under prev-day (0), and a spy proves `candidates_for_spec` threads the swept anchor into `build_bar_bits`; (ii) `TestBuildStage2CascadeSpecs` seeds a two-anchor grid (prev-day + rolling-weekly) and asserts each grid-winner spec carries its OWN anchor — the test FAILS if the `fib_anchor=sweep_tuple.fib_anchor` thread is reverted (verified). **×3 GRID + CAP:** with all 3 anchors `count_sweep_tuples` is ×3; the loud `max_tuples` guard STILL trips at ×3 (regression-pinned — never a silent blowup). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** DEFAULT-PRESERVING (an unset `fib_anchor`/`fib_anchors` is byte-identical to the pre-axis prev-day sweep — proven by the two `bar_bits`-matrix goldens (nifty-day, banknifty-week) passing UNCHANGED); the multi-day anchors consult the NSE calendar via the reused `rolling_weekly_anchor`/`weekly_static_anchor` primitives (in-coverage 2020-2026 dates only — the whole data floor); the bounded daily history is O(1)/bar (R-4, never the full O(days)); the anchor is a swept STRATEGY parameter, NOT engine-scope expansion (the 3 spot indices remain the index engine surface). **REGENERATED GOLDENS (run-identity legitimately changed — the anchor is now in `canonical_params`):** `tests/golden/test_engine_sweep_run_golden.py` `_GOLDEN_RUN_ID` (`1e0a9b98…` → `f588194f…`) + `_GOLDEN_CONTENT_HASH` (`6fc0fda6…` → `b21c8e87…`) + its `_PARAMS` oracle gained `"fib_anchor": "prev_day"`; `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_supervisor.py` `grid_identity` (`456d0d52…` → `e55de617…`) + `tuple_cache_key` (`f862ca7c…` → `f9f118e0…`). The `bar_bits`-MATRIX goldens are UNCHANGED (prev-day default is byte-identical). **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after — the anti-cosmetic proof):** NEW `tests/unit/test_engine_fib_axis.py` (16) — the CORE anti-cosmetic test builds a synthetic multi-day history whose prev-day / trailing-5-session / last-ISO-week ranges ALL DIFFER (2021-01-19; the three anchors' `retrace_50` are 10950/10650/10500) and asserts the 3 anchors yield PAIRWISE-DISTINCT Group-4 Fib bit vectors (byte-identical before the axis → this FAILS on the hardcoded builder) AND distinct `combo_hash` run-identities AND distinct `_tuple_digest` store addresses; plus grid-enumerates-the-axis (×3), empty-axis-rejected, dupe-deduped, cap-trips-at-×3, kernel-carries-the-anchor (R-1), cold-rolling-weekly-clears-Fib-only-keeps-pivots (R-2), Fib∩Pivot masks disjoint, non-Fib groups identical across anchors, default==explicit-prev-day. Updated `test_engine_sweep_run.py` (`fib_anchor` in the params layout + a distinct-hash test), `test_engine_stage3_wire.py` (4-tuple recover + a non-prev-day-anchor recovery + the Stage-4 `cascade_specs_for_refined_cells` carries-the-swept-anchor / defaults-prev-day tests), `test_engine_sweep_kernel.py` (anchor is a key field), `test_engine_cascade_wire.py` (the Stage-4 MAJOR fix — `candidates_for_spec` uses the swept anchor / defaults prev-day, `spec_from_store_rows` threads/defaults the anchor, the manifest spec round-trips/additive-parses `fib_anchor`; PLUS the re-review BLOCKER's `TestBuildStage2CascadeSpecs` — the pragma-free `build_stage2_cascade_specs` helper carries each grid winner's swept anchor / skips an absent store / drops an empty store / threads `top_k`, 100% line+branch). **Verified 2026-07-01 (fresh isolated 3.12 venv `venv-pr11b`, Rust wheels built via `maturin develop --release`):** 1425 engine+strategies+cli unit tests green; 225 golden+sweep-integration tests green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files. **Files:** `brutex/strategies/types.py`, `brutex/strategies/fib_definitions.py`, `brutex/engine/stage1a.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_kernel.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py`, `brutex/engine/stage3_wire.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py`, `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_fib_axis.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_run.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_stage3_wire.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_kernel.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_supervisor.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_cascade_wire.py`, `tests/golden/test_engine_sweep_run_golden.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-NIFTY-FIB-AXIS-001. 1059. **DEC-SWEEP-DEFAULT-CONDITIONS-60-001 — the brute-force sweep's DEFAULT condition set (used when `--conditions` is not given) now sweeps ALL 60 implemented conditions, not the stale hardcoded first 52 — so bits 52-59 (VWAP position, pivot R5/S5, BOS/CHoCH — the dynamic-futures indicators shipped by DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001 #1011 / DEC-NIFTY-BOS-CHOCH-001 #1012) actually appear in a default sweep** (2026-07-01; PR-11a; `brutex/cli.py` sweep-launcher default only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab-width/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; the 52→60 vocabulary growth itself already shipped in PR-1 #1010, this only makes the sweep USE it; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE DEFECT (grounded PR-11 readiness audit, re-confirmed on `origin/main` `8e4b9bcb`):** `brutex/vocabulary/bits.py` has `TOTAL_CONDITIONS = 60` and `IMPLEMENTED_MASK = (1<<60)-1` (every one of the 60 bits computes a real boolean since #1012), yet all THREE sweep-launcher default sites in `brutex/cli.py` (`cmd_sweep`, `cmd_sweep_all`, `cmd_sweep_verify`) hardcoded the no-`--conditions` default to `list(range(52))`, and the two `--conditions` help strings said "0..51 … all 52". So a default sweep NEVER tested VWAP position (52/53), pivot R5/S5 (54/55), or BOS/CHoCH (56-59) — the exact dynamic-futures indicators the sweep spine exists to exercise; 8 of the 60 conditions could only ever appear if the operator manually re-typed the full bit list. **THE FIX (one source of truth — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** a NEW pure `brutex/cli.py::default_condition_bits()` derives the default from the vocabulary's `IMPLEMENTED_MASK` (`[bit for bit in range(TOTAL_CONDITIONS) if IMPLEMENTED_MASK & (1<<bit)]`), and the three `else list(range(52))` sites + the two help strings now reference it / `TOTAL_CONDITIONS`, so the default AUTOMATICALLY tracks the vocabulary and can NEVER drift behind it again. Deriving from `IMPLEMENTED_MASK` (not a bare `range(TOTAL_CONDITIONS)`) is deliberately HONEST per Golden Rule #1: a future LAYOUT-ONLY bit (`implemented=false`, whose evaluator emits a constant 0) is EXCLUDED, so the default never sweeps a dead condition that could never fire; today every bit is implemented so it returns `[0..59]`. **SAFETY ENVELOPE UNCHANGED (proven):** the loud-refusal caps are byte-for-byte the same — `SweepGridConfig.__post_init__` still refuses any `k` whose `C(n,k)` mask count exceeds `DEFAULT_MAX_COMBOS = 100_000`, and broadening 52→60 does NOT weaken it: `C(60,4) = 487_635 > 100k` fires the SAME clear raise-explicitly `ValueError` that `C(52,4) = 270_725` fired at n=52, while the production default k values (1, 2 → 60 and 1770 masks; and k=3 → 34_220) stay well within the cap. The change alters ONLY which conditions are available by default, never the refusal envelope; there is no silent grid blowup. **HONEST (Golden Rule #10):** a VWAP bit (52/53) is intrinsically 0 on the `1day` timeframe (`APPLIES_TO_1DAY_MASK` masks it out — ADR-0012 D12) and on any instrument without traded volume (a spot index) the evaluator emits 0 for it — that is a valid never-matching condition (the ranking simply never selects it), NOT a crash and NOT a data requirement the default instruments lack; every one of bits 52-59 is safe to include by default. This is a launcher-default correctness fix, NOT the full grid strategy/anchor axis (that Fib-anchor axis is a separate DESIGN-first item under hostile review, Golden Rule #9). **Verified 2026-07-01 (fresh isolated 3.12 venv, `trading_core`+`fno_math` wheels):** the NEW `default_condition_bits()` returns `[0..59]` incl. every one of 52-59; fail-before/pass-after proven (reverting the helper to `range(52)` fails the 4 correctness tests, the cap tests pass in BOTH states — they test the envelope, not the count); `brutex/cli.py` touched lines (`default_condition_bits` + the two help strings + the three default sites) at 100% line + 100% branch under the new + existing CLI suites (the comprehension's include/exclude branch both exercised); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean on the two touched files (the only strict error is a PRE-EXISTING `stage3_refine.py:134` `cma`-stub env artifact in an UNTOUCHED file, reproduced on the pristine baseline); `pyright` 0 errors 0 warnings on the two touched files; the existing `test_cli_sweep.py` / `test_cli_sweep_all_dedup.py` / `test_cli_supervisor.py` suites green; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` + `validate_dec_ids.py` exit 0. **Files:** `brutex/cli.py` (the new `default_condition_bits()` helper + the three default sites + the two `--conditions` help strings), `tests/unit/test_cli_default_conditions.py` (NEW — 9 tests: correctness, layout-only exclusion, help-string, and the k=1/2/3-within-cap + k=4-loud-refusal envelope), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-DEFAULT-CONDITIONS-60-001. (Ledger: renumbered #1058 → #1059 on the re-sync onto `main` to leapfrog PR #1016's pending `DEC-DEDUP-CAPACITY-UNIQUE-001` #1058 (armed to merge first) — #1059 is the next free unique number and the tail entry, re-checked immediately before push — parallel rule P-1; the DEC-ID is the stable handle.)

1061. **DEC-COST-SCOPE-INDEX-SIGNAL-ONLY-001 — the operator-locked cost-scope rule is now ONE COMMON source-of-truth predicate + an enforcing test: COST-FREE (signal-only — zero brokerage / STT / slippage / liquidity / best-avg-worst-case fills) is INDEX SPOT (NIFTY / BANKNIFTY / SENSEX) and INDEX FUTURES (NIFTY futures) ONLY; COST-BEARING (the full brokerage + STT + slippage + liquidity + fill-scenario stack) is EVERYTHING ELSE — stock spot, stock futures, stock options, AND index OPTIONS** (2026-07-01; `brutex/costs/` predicate + tests only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path/pacing change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE RULE (operator-corrected, SUPERSEDES an earlier mistaken "options-only" framing that wrongly implied stock spot/futures were cost-free):** `is_cost_free(instrument) == (instrument is an INDEX AND its segment is SPOT/CASH or FUTURES)` — an index SPOT (`instrument_type == IDX`) or an index FUTURE (`FUT` on a brute-force index underlying) is priced signal-only; any INDEX OPTION and any STOCK (spot / future / option) is cost-bearing. **THE INVESTIGATION (grounded, file:line):** the cost/slippage/fill sites are exactly two production paths. (1) The brute-force ENGINE spot/index walker `brutex/engine/trade_sim.py` (`simulate_trades` / `TradeSimWalker`) is UNCONDITIONALLY signal-only — its module docstring (lines 13-20) states "the index has no order book, so there is no slippage, no brokerage, no STT", the emitted `ClosedTrade.pnl_paisa` is the RAW directional price move, and the Rust twin `brutex/engine/rust_trade_sim.py` is bit-identical (no cost model). So the INDEX-SPOT sweep applies ZERO cost today; the index-FUTURES dynamic-strategy track rides the same walker → ZERO cost. (2) The Track-2 cost calculator `brutex/costs/calculator.py` (`compute_trade_cost` — brokerage + STT + exchange + SEBI + IPFT + stamp + GST + 1-tick slippage) prices INDEX OPTIONS (`brutex/costs/types.py` `Instrument = Literal["NIFTY","BANKNIFTY","SENSEX"]`) via `brutex/options/executor.py` — correctly cost-bearing. The execution simulator's `brutex/execution/costs.py` `IndianCostModel` is the Track-2 fill-cost model (CASH+EQ / FNO+FUT / FNO+CE/PE branches; CASH+IDX falls through to `Decimal("0")`). **VERDICT — ALREADY HONORED (no leak, no gap): PROVEN.** No cost is applied to the index-spot or index-futures engine path (the raw-move invariant is regression-pinned), and the cost stack applies only to the tradable options/stock paths. Pure, O(1), imports only `brutex.models` + `brutex.universe` (dependency-light, no cycle), re-exported from `brutex.costs`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this LOCKS IN the already-true index-spot/index-futures cost-free guarantee with a predicate + enforcing test — it did NOT need to fix a leak (none existed) and did NOT re-wire the existing Track-2 options/stock cost model (which is correct); the predicate is the drift-proof contract so a future cost application at any site can gate on it. The full STOCK (spot/future/option) cost-application path is a FUTURE options-track surface (stocks are REFERENCE_ONLY today) — the predicate + test still lock the guarantee for when it lands. **Tests (REAL, 100% line+branch on the touched source):** `tests/unit/test_costs_scope.py` (`is_cost_free` TRUE for index-spot + all 3 brute-force indices + index-future, FALSE for index-CE/PE + stock-spot/future/option; `is_index_future` TRUE only for a FUT on a brute-force index underlying incl. 1058. **DEC-DEDUP-CAPACITY-UNIQUE-001 — the orchestrator L1 Bloom now counts UNIQUE keys, not per-put state re-adds, so its FAIL_CLOSED capacity gate is HONEST and cannot halt a heavy multi-day sweep prematurely; plus two documentation/coverage hardening fixes riding along** (2026-07-01; `brutex/orchestrator/store.py` (the `put` newness gate) + `brutex/orchestrator/bloom.py` (docstring only) + `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py` (docstring only) + two test files only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty; NO pacing/fetch change). **FIX 1 (the correctness fix) — Bloom capacity counts UNIQUE keys, not state re-adds:** the ingest FSM `put`s each work-item MULTIPLE times as it moves PENDING→IN_FLIGHT→SUCCESS (a state transition re-serialises the SAME `(phase, content_hash)` key). Before this fix `WorkItemStore.put` Bloom-`add`ed on EVERY put, so `BloomFilter.insertions_attempted` (the conservative FAIL_CLOSED capacity counter — the filter does NOT dedup, a repeat `add` of the same hash counts twice) was inflated ~3× (or more, with retries) and the capacity gate could raise `BloomCapacityExceeded` at a small FRACTION of `capacity` genuinely-distinct combos — a premature halt of a heavy sweep at roughly a third of the intended unique-combo capacity. **THE MECHANISM (how key-newness is detected — LMDB is the ground truth, no extra read):** `store.put` now writes with `is_new = txn.put(key, value, db=self._dbs[item.phase], overwrite=False)` — LMDB's `overwrite=False` writes IFF the key is genuinely new and returns `True` in ONE O(1) B+tree op; if the key already existed the value is left untouched and it returns `False`, so we re-apply the state-transition update with an explicit `txn.put(..., overwrite=True)` (the row still transitions to its terminal state). The post-commit Bloom-add is then gated `if self._bloom is not None and is_new:` — so `insertions_attempted` equals the count of DISTINCT keys ever inserted and the capacity gate trips ONLY when `capacity` genuinely-unique combos exist. **HONEST envelope (FAIL_CLOSED correctness fully preserved, Golden Rule #10):** (a) a genuinely-NEW key is ALWAYS added to the Bloom (a later dedup lookup can find it); (b) a Bloom MISS still returns False (re-run) with no LMDB touch — the fail-open-to-rerun contract; (c) a Bloom HIT still confirms terminal state against LMDB ground truth before any skip (a non-terminal IN_FLIGHT key is a Bloom-hit but `maybe_seen_terminal` returns False, never a silent skip); and the (N+1)th genuinely-UNIQUE key STILL raises `BloomCapacityExceeded` — the gate is not weakened, only made honest. Scope note (Golden Rule #2): the fix is deliberately confined to `put` (the state-transition path); `put_many` (the bulk PENDING-seed path, documented as unique keys) is byte-unchanged and keeps its pre-flight capacity check. **FIX 2 (docstring) — `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py`:** the module docstring said the evaluator returns a `u64` bitmask; the vocabulary grew to a u128 mask (60 conditions on bits 0..59, headroom to bit 127) under DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001, so the docstring is corrected to `u128` with the current-occupancy + headroom note (no code change — the returned type was already u128). **FIX 3 (property coverage) — `tests/property/test_supermask_kernel_parity.py`:** the pre-existing supermask-parity suites only sampled bars/masks up to `(1<<64)-1`, so the two-limb numpy path in `brutex/engine/combo_mask.py` (taken when any bar/mask sets a bit `>= 64`, guarded at `combo_mask.py:413` `if any(m > U64_MASK ...) or any(b > U64_MASK ...)`) had thin property coverage. NEW hypothesis strategies span the FULL u128 range (and `_HI128` variants FORCE at least one bit `>= 64`) and compare the `count_supermasks` facade, the `count_supermasks_reference` numpy oracle, and the `ResidentBarBuffer` two-limb backing against an INDEPENDENT arbitrary-precision pure-Python scalar oracle `(bar & mask) == mask` — so a future vocabulary growth past 64 bits cannot silently truncate a high bit and corrupt the Stage-2 hit count or the blake3 run-identity hash (Golden Rule #4). **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after):** NEW `TestBloomCapacityUniqueAccounting` in `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_store.py` — one key put through 3 state transitions increments `insertions_attempted` EXACTLY once (would be 3 before the fix); the row still reaches SUCCESS; a new key is always added; a Bloom miss returns False without LMDB; a Bloom hit confirms terminal vs LMDB; `insertions_attempted == unique-key count` (3 combos × 3 puts ⇒ 3); N unique keys each transitioned 3× do NOT trip `BloomCapacityExceeded` at `capacity == N`; the (N+1)th unique key STILL fails closed; a re-put of an existing key at full capacity does NOT raise — plus the five new u128 property tests in `test_supermask_kernel_parity.py`. **Verification:** see the PR body for the captured pass-counts + per-file 100% line+branch coverage + `ruff`/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` results on the touched files. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/store.py`, `brutex/orchestrator/bloom.py`, `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py`, `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_store.py`, `tests/property/test_supermask_kernel_parity.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DEDUP-CAPACITY-UNIQUE-001. (Ledger: #1058 = the file's current max #1057 `DEC-SUPERVISOR-AUTORESTART-001` + 1, renumbered as the TAIL entry after re-syncing onto main — the original #1057 collided with the just-merged PR #1011 `DEC-SUPERVISOR-AUTORESTART-001` which landed at #1057 first; a numbering gap is allowed; the validator enforces only (number,suffix) uniqueness; the DEC-ID is the stable handle — re-checked immediately before push.)
1053. **DEC-FNO-LEDGER-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 — the F&O historical phase now cold-start RECONCILES its window ledger with the lake, so a lost / orphaned ledger re-seeds "already done" F&O windows from the stored bars instead of re-pulling the ENTIRE options chain from Groww (GAP 1)** (2026-07-01; `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py` (extract the COMMON reconcile core) + `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` (the F&O reconcile) + `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` (wire it into `_run_phase`) + two test files — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE GAP (from the full-universe bulletproof-resume audit, 7-agent + adversarial verification):** `reconcile_ledger_with_lake` was called ONLY on the SPOT path (`pull_controller.py` 4 sites + `cli.py:2359`) and appeared NOWHERE in `historical_pull.py` / `option_ingest.py`; worse it is structurally SPOT-only (keys `security_id=instrument.symbol_name` + `market=COVERAGE_MARKET`), while F&O keys are `security_id=contract.symbol` + `market="groww-option"/"groww-future"`. `plan_contract_windows` seeds only `PLANNED`, which `is_skippable` treats as NOT skippable (`window_ledger.py`, `_SKIPPABLE = {SUCCESS, SKIPPED}`). CONSEQUENCE: on any fresh-clone / deleted-ledger / new-`BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT` / schema-orphaning-deploy restart where the lake already holds F&O bars, every F&O window re-planned `PLANNED` and RE-FETCHED — ~212 underlyings × full option chains (every strike × CE/PE × expiry) — a massive redundant multi-day re-pull burning the 500/min budget. SPOT had this rescue since DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001; F&O did not — the single most valuable resume gap. **THE FIX (COMMON — one reconcile engine, NOT two copies, CLAUDE.md §11):** `window_ledger_store.py` extracts the shared seed core out of the spot `reconcile_ledger_windows` — NEW public `index_lake_spans(spans)` (the `(exchange, segment, symbol, interval) -> span` index) + `seed_enclosed_windows(ledger, span_index, candidates, *, now)` (for each `(window_key, span_key)` candidate, seed `SUCCESS` only-if-absent iff the span has ≥ 1 bar AND its stored `[first_date, last_date]` FULLY encloses the window `first_date <= window.start AND window.end <= last_date`, the conservative DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 rule) + a `SeedCandidate` alias; the spot `reconcile_ledger_windows` is REFACTORED to build its candidates then delegate to the shared core — proven byte-behaviour-identical (all 5 pre-existing `TestReconcileLedgerWithLake` tests pass unchanged, plus the whole `test_window_ledger_store.py` / `test_window_ledger.py` / `test_coverage_reconcile.py` suites, 121 green). `option_ingest.py` adds the F&O twin: `reconcile_fno_ledger_windows` (pure) + `reconcile_fno_ledger_with_lake` (wired = `load_lake_spans` + the pure reconcile) + `_fno_reconcile_candidates`, which derives each `(contract, interval)` seed key via the SAME `_clamped_window_key` over the SAME `_resolve_window` resolution the fetch (`ingest_option_contract`) and the plan (`plan_contract_windows`) use — so a seeded `SUCCESS` key is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the `PLANNED`/fetched key (the "reconcile == plan == fetch" invariant, no ghost row) — and looks the span up under the CONTRACT's F&O partition `(exchange, "FNO", groww_symbol, interval)` (the exact directory `sink.append(segment="FNO", …)` writes and `summarize_spot_datasets`, which walks the WHOLE `bars/` tree spot+FNO, reports). `historical_pull.py::_run_phase` wires the reconcile in RIGHT AFTER `begin_pull_ledger` and BEFORE `plan_contract_windows` seeds `PLANNED`, gated `ledger is not None` (a dry-run skips it entirely — no span scan), loading the O(datasets) spans ONCE per phase and running a pure per-market seed so each contract's window lands in its OWN namespace (`groww-future` / `groww-option`). **CORRECTNESS — NO DATA LOST (Golden Rule #1):** `seed_lake_success` is only-if-absent so it NEVER overwrites a `FAILED` / `PLANNED` / settled row — it can never mask a re-pull; a genuinely-missing window (no span) OR a PARTIALLY-covered window (the span does not fully enclose it — `last_date < window.end`) is left with NO seeded row, so it stays re-pullable; only a window the lake FULLY encloses is flipped to skippable `SUCCESS`. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this closes the F&O re-pull trap ONLY — the DASHBOARD F&O pull path (the `/pull-pipeline` route → `run_full_pipeline` → `pull_contract_candles` → `_run_phase`) which is the primary universe pull surface; the enclosure rule mirrors the spot semantics exactly (a window is "done" only if the lake proves coverage through its exclusive end), so a still-in-progress trailing window is correctly NOT seeded; a dry-run / synthetic pull never scans the lake (regression-pinned). This is GAP 1 of the resume audit; GAP 2 (durable campaign intent + boot/supervisor auto-resume) and GAP 4 (ledger schema-version key) are flagged FOLLOW-UPS, NOT in this PR. **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after, 100% line+branch on all 3 touched source files):** `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py` gains `TestReconcileFnoLedgerWindows` (13 tests: seeds an enclosed window → skippable · the seed key == the planned key (no ghost) · a genuinely-missing window is NOT seeded + stays pullable · a partially-covered window (right-edge AND left-edge) stays re-pullable · zero-bar / null-date / empty spans seed nothing · never overwrites a FAILED row · never re-seeds an already-SUCCESS row (no double-count) · the FUTURES namespace is honoured + distinct from the option one · an empty clamped range yields no candidate · `contract_windows` bounds the seed key · default now/clock branches) + `TestReconcileFnoLedgerWithLake` (the wired `load_lake_spans` composition); `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py` gains the end-to-end fails-before/passes-after triple — `test_fno_reconcile_skips_lake_present_windows_on_orphaned_ledger` (a first LIVE pull writes real F&O bars + a ledger, the ledger file is DELETED, a second LIVE pull against the SAME lake with a fresh empty ledger re-fetches NOTHING — `get_historical_candles` is never called, `bars_appended == 0`), `test_fno_orphaned_ledger_refetches_without_reconcile` (the FAILS-BEFORE: monkeypatching the reconcile to a no-op reproduces the pre-fix behaviour — the whole NIFTY chain is re-fetched), and `test_fno_reconcile_dry_run_does_not_scan_lake` (a dry-run never scans the lake).
