1060. **DEC-TOKEN-MINTER-CENTRAL-001 — a CENTRALIZED single-writer Groww daily-access-token minter (ONE AWS Lambda is the SOLE writer; both TickVault and BruteX read the token READ-ONLY from Parameter Store), delivered as the Lambda handler + Terraform IaC + docs, so the multi-app 06:00-IST "minting storm" is eliminated by construction** (2026-07-01; operator-directed option C adapted to the EXISTING AWS infra — region `ap-south-1`, creds already in SSM Parameter Store as KMS-encrypted SecureStrings; NEW `deploy/aws_token_minter/` package (handler + Terraform + `build_lambda_package.sh` + `deploy.sh`) + `docs/adr/0014-centralized-token-minter.md` + `docs/runbooks/aws-token-minter.md` + one `pyproject.toml` ruff per-file-ignore addition + this entry only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, the project scope rule §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched; NO `brutex/` package code touched — the read-side wiring is a SEPARATE PR). **HONESTY (Golden Rule #10 + #1) — NOT DEPLOYED:** this session has NO AWS access; the deliverable is CODE + IaC only, the operator runs `./deploy.sh` / `terraform apply`. No claim is made that the Lambda runs, mints, or that any alarm has fired in a real account. **THE PROBLEM:** BruteX (backtest) and TickVault (live) both mint their OWN Groww access token on an auth-expiry mid-run (the in-process auto-re-mint, DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001 #909); run concurrently against the same Groww account they BOTH mint around the 06:00-IST daily reset (the project rules §6 "Token lifetime", VERIFIED from production logs 2026-06-23) — a competing-mint "storm" that has made the reset flaky (one mint invalidating the other's fresh token). **THE DESIGN (operator's exact option C, built to spec — no alternatives invented):** ONE AWS Lambda is the SOLE minter, serialized `reserved_concurrent_executions = 1`. On an EventBridge schedule (default `cron(35 0 * * ? *)` = 00:35 UTC = **06:05 IST**, shortly after the reset) AND on an on-demand manual invoke it (1) reads `/tickvault/prod/groww/api-key` + `/tickvault/prod/groww/totp-secret` via SSM `GetParameter(WithDecryption=True)` (SSM KMS-decrypts the SecureStrings), (2) computes the TOTP, (3) mints via `GrowwAPI.get_access_token(api_key, totp)`, (4) writes the token to `/tickvault/prod/groww/access-token` via `PutParameter(Overwrite=True, Type='SecureString', KeyId=<kms key>)` (retried on a transient SSM WRITE throttle). Both apps then read that ONE token READ-ONLY, so no app ever mints — the storm is gone by construction. **NO DynamoDB / no CAS:** a distributed lock coordinates MULTIPLE writers; here there is exactly ONE writer that is SERIALIZED (`reserved_concurrent_executions = 1`), so an overlapping scheduled + manual invoke cannot race the write — the two mints run strictly in order and the last `PutParameter` writes the newest token (Groww's single-active-token session model is UNVERIFIED per Golden Rule #1, and the serialized single writer makes it moot). DynamoDB would add cost + a moving part with ZERO correctness benefit, deliberately omitted. **DELIVERABLE 1 — `deploy/aws_token_minter/handler.py` (self-contained Lambda):** the bundle does NOT import the `brutex` package (deployed independently); the TOTP + mint logic mirrors `brutex/adapters/groww/auth.py` CONCEPTUALLY, re-implemented here. Every real AWS/Groww side effect is an INJECTED callable with a real default shim marked `# pragma: no cover` (`boto3` is on the Lambda runtime; `growwapi`/`pyotp` are BUNDLED into the deploy zip by the build step — only runnable in AWS against the live vendor); the PURE decision logic — `resolve_config` (env parse + validate), `mint_token` (read creds → TOTP → mint → write, TOTP computed INSIDE the guarded try + sanitized, an in-handler exponential backoff on a transient issuance 429 via `_is_rate_limit`, terminal on a wrong-TOTP/expired-key/empty-token failure with a SANITIZED reason raised `from None` so no raw vendor exception is chained into a CloudWatch traceback), `_put_token_with_retry` (bounded SSM-throttle retry), `_emit_metric` (best-effort `TokenMintSuccess` CloudWatch datum), `run` (orchestrates + emits success/failure metric on ANY error) — is driven to **100.00% line + branch** by a fake SSM + fake CloudWatch + fake TOTP/mint in `tests/deploy/test_aws_token_minter_handler.py` (51 tests). **DELIVERABLE 2 — Terraform IaC (`main.tf`/`variables.tf`/`outputs.tf`/`versions.tf`):** provisions ONLY the token param, the minter Lambda (`reserved_concurrent_executions = 1`) + a `null_resource` build step that pip-installs `growwapi`+`pyotp` into the zip + its EventBridge schedule + a stale-token CloudWatch alarm (metric-math `FILL(m1, 0)` over a 24h SUM with `TreatMissingData=notBreaching` — a daily-job missing-data treatment that DOESN'T flap on a healthy day, yet a real absence of a success still pages) + a Lambda-Errors alarm + an SNS topic, and THREE least-privilege IAM roles — (a) minter = `ssm:GetParameter` on the two cred params + `ssm:PutParameter` on the token param + `kms:Decrypt`/`Encrypt`/`GenerateDataKey` on the ONE existing key + namespace-scoped `cloudwatch:PutMetricData` + own log group; (b) reader-tickvault = `ssm:GetParameter` on the token param + `kms:Decrypt` ONLY; (c) reader-brutex = same as (b). The EXISTING KMS key + the two cred params are REFERENCED via `data` sources, never created/managed. Region / path-prefix / schedule cron / SNS alert endpoint / pinned dep versions are all Terraform variables (defaults per the operator's infra). Every IAM policy is resource-scoped to specific ARNs (never `*` except `PutMetricData`, which the AWS API forbids resource-scoping — constrained instead by a `cloudwatch:namespace` `StringEquals` condition). **DELIVERABLE 3/4 — `docs/adr/0014-centralized-token-minter.md`** (the serialized single-writer design, the no-DynamoDB rationale, the failure-mode table + the secret-hygiene `from None` + daily-job alarm sub-sections, the least-privilege IAM matrix, every AWS behavioural claim CITED to an AWS docs URL per Golden Rule #1) + **`docs/runbooks/aws-token-minter.md`** (exact paths/region/schedule + the one-command `./deploy.sh` deploy — build + `terraform init` + a plan that requires a `yes` confirm, never auto-approved — + the on-demand `aws lambda invoke` + the reader-role wiring + rollback). A minter-scoped runbook was created (NOT the in-flight #1015 broker's `aws-token-broker.md` / `TOKEN_BROKER_CONTRACT.md`, which are absent on `origin/main`) so there is NO cross-PR file conflict. **ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION FIXES (17-permutation review — 4 MAJOR + 6 MINOR + CI folded before merge):** MAJOR-1 SECRET LEAK — the terminal `TokenMintError` is raised `from None` (was `from exc`) so the raw vendor exception (which may echo the api-key) is NOT chained into the Lambda-runtime CloudWatch traceback; MAJOR-2 ALARM FALSE-FIRES — the stale-token alarm switched to `FILL(m1, 0)` metric-math so it no longer flaps daily on a healthy pipeline; MAJOR-3 DEAD-TOKEN OVERWRITE — `reserved_concurrent_executions = 1` serializes overlapping invocations (the ADR's uncited "both write the SAME value / the loser's token is also valid" claims were REMOVED, the Groww session model stated UNVERIFIED); MAJOR-4 — the PR-body external claims gained inline citations; CODEQL — the 3 Protocol-stub `...` no-effect statements became `raise NotImplementedError`; MINOR-1 a NON-domain SSM/KMS error now ALSO emits `success=0`; MINOR-2 the token `PutParameter` retries a transient SSM throttle; MINOR-3 the TOTP construction moved INSIDE the guarded try + sanitized; MINOR-4 `growwapi`+`pyotp` are now REALLY bundled into the deploy zip (a `null_resource`/`build_lambda_package.sh` pip-install step). **INDEPENDENT-REVIEW MAJOR (2nd pass) — CROSS-PLATFORM LAMBDA WHEEL BUNDLING:** `build_lambda_package.sh` pip-installed with NO platform flags, so a bundle built on the operator's macOS/ARM64 machine (§8 Apple M4 Pro) vendored macOS/ARM wheels — and `growwapi` drags in native-extension transitive deps (pynacl, pydantic-core, pandas, aiohttp, protobuf) whose macOS/ARM binaries would `ImportError` on the FIRST real mint in the x86_64 Linux Lambda runtime (`terraform apply` SUCCEEDS but the mint silently fails). `build_lambda_package.sh` + `deploy.sh` stay `shellcheck`-clean. **VERIFICATION (honest envelope, Golden Rule #10):** `handler.py` at **100.00% line + branch** (157 stmt / 26 branch, 0 missing) over the fake-driven 51-test suite (each MAJOR/MINOR fails-before / passes-after pinned); 1068. **DEC-CALENDAR-2020-BUDGET-SATURDAY-001 — the real 2020-02-01 (Saturday) Union Budget special NSE + BSE trading session, which sits INSIDE the 2020-01-01 data-pull floor (`GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR`), is now registered as a special-weekend session so `is_trading_day(2020-02-01)` returns True and that genuine full trading day is no longer scored as non-trading** (2026-07-01; `brutex/calendars/nse.py` special-weekend-sessions map + tests only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F\&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE BUG (adversarial-sweep MAJOR M1, confirmed against real code + external sources):** `SPECIAL_WEEKEND_TRADING_SESSIONS` (`brutex/calendars/nse.py`) registered the Union Budget Saturday/Sunday sessions for 2025-02-01 and 2026-02-01 but OMITTED 2020-02-01 — and the map's OWN preceding comment even asserted “Special weekend trading sessions for Budget Day on Feb-1-Saturday occurred 2020-02-01 + 2025-02-01” while deliberately not adding the 2020 one (per DEC-CALENDAR-2020-DATA-001, which scoped in only the 2020 holiday list + the 2020 Diwali Muhurat session). Because 2020-02-01 is a Saturday, `is_trading_day` → `not is_weekend(d) and not is_holiday(d)` returned FALSE for it, so a GENUINE full trading session inside the 2020-01-01 pull floor was scored non-trading — corrupting the PDH/PDL anchors + per-session stats on/around that day for all 3 indices (e.g. `find_prev_trading_day(2020-02-03)` walked past the Sat session to Fri 2020-01-31, so Mon 03-Feb’s prior-day anchor came from the WRONG session). **FACT CORROBORATION (Golden Rule #1, no hallucination):** India’s FY2020-21 Union Budget was presented on Saturday 1 Feb 2020 and NSE + BSE held a live full-day special trading session that day — a well-known real event, corroborated by (a) the map’s OWN pre-existing comment in `brutex/calendars/nse.py` (“Special weekend trading sessions for Budget Day on Feb-1-Saturday occurred 2020-02-01 + 2025-02-01”), (b) the IDENTICAL 2025-02-01 Budget-Saturday entry already registered in `SPECIAL_WEEKEND_TRADING_SESSIONS` (same regular-hours session shape), and (c) the public record of the FY2020-21 Union Budget Saturday session (the NSE special-trading-session circular cited in the map’s `# Source:` line + Business Standard / Good Returns / DD News coverage of the 1-Feb-2020 Budget-Day Saturday session). No CLAUDE.md §7 Budget-Day statement is relied on — §7 (market-microstructure facts) does not assert Budget-Day opening hours, so it is NOT cited here (Golden Rule #1: cite only real sources). **THE FIX (one map entry, mirrors the existing 2025/2026 format exactly):** add `date(2020, 2, 1): (SESSION_OPEN_IST, SESSION_CLOSE_IST)` to `SPECIAL_WEEKEND_TRADING_SESSIONS` (regular 09:15–15:30 REGULAR hours, 15:20 forced-exit — identical to the other special Saturday sessions). `is_trading_day`/`is_trading_day_checked`/`get_session`/`find_prev_trading_day` all consult `is_special_weekend_session` (which reads the map), so the single map add flips every downstream verdict with NO other code change. **COMPLETENESS (in-scope Budget-Saturdays checked — no other date is missing):** across the 2020-01-01→today floor Feb-1 fell on a weekend ONLY in 2020 (Sat), 2025 (Sat) and 2026 (Sun) — 2021-2024 Feb-1 were weekdays — so with 2020-02-01 added the three entries are the COMPLETE set of Budget weekend sessions in scope; no other real special-weekend session was invented. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** a pure calendar-data correctness fix — it flips exactly ONE date from non-trading to trading (a real session); the happy path (every other date) is byte-unchanged; no other special session was added (only corroborated ones). **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after, 100% line+branch on `brutex/calendars/nse.py`):** `tests/unit/test_calendar_nse.py::TestSpecialWeekendSessions` gains `test_budget_day_2020_is_special_weekend_session`, `test_budget_day_2020_promotes_saturday_to_trading_day` (`is_trading_day(2020-02-01)` True — fail-before False), `test_budget_day_2020_prev_trading_day_anchor` (`find_prev_trading_day(2020-02-03)` == 2020-02-01 — fail-before 2020-01-31), `test_budget_day_2020_get_session_regular_hours_forced_exit` (REGULAR 09:15–15:30, 375 min, 15:20 forced-exit), and `test_budget_day_2020_not_in_holiday_list`. Fails-before/passes-after PROVEN by temporarily deleting the map key: `is_trading_day(2020-02-01)` reads False → True and `find_prev_trading_day(2020-02-03)` reads 2020-01-31 → 2020-02-01. 1063. **DEC-SWEEP-CACHE-RESUME-DEDUP-001 — the sweep dedup cache now REPOPULATES its L1 Bloom from the persisted L2 LMDB on `open()`, so a RESUME actually skips the combos the prior run already evaluated (before this fix a restart re-ran the ENTIRE prior sweep — days of work — because the fresh in-RAM Bloom was empty and a Bloom-negative was treated as conclusive without consulting LMDB), plus the probe-then-act in `record_digest`/`seen_digest` is now fully atomic under one lock** (2026-07-01; `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py` + `brutex/data/lmdb_membership.py` + two test files only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty; NO pacing/fetch change). **THE DEFECTS (adversarial verification sweep + completeness critic; both CONFIRMED against the real code):** (1) RESUME-DEDUP BREAK (CRITICAL, Golden Rules #4 & #7) — `SweepCache.open()` built a FRESH EMPTY `BloomFilter` and never repopulated it from the persisted L2 LMDB exact store, and `seen_digest` treated a Bloom-negative (`might_contain == False`) as CONCLUSIVE (`return False`) WITHOUT consulting LMDB. So on a resume every digest the previous run recorded to LMDB reported Bloom-negative → `seen_digest` returned False → the combo was RE-RUN. A restart re-did the entire prior sweep (days of work on the §8 envelope) and could double-write results — a direct violation of idempotence (Rule #7) and reproducibility (Rule #4). The pre-existing `test_reopen_reloads_persisted_membership` test had to MANUALLY seed the Bloom (`cache2._bloom.add(d)`) to make the reopen work — the smoking gun that the production `open()` path never repopulated it. (2) NON-ATOMIC CHECK-THEN-ACT (concurrency) — `record_digest`'s `if digest in self._exact: return False` probe ran OUTSIDE `self._lock`, and the `self._exact.add()` was also outside; `seen_digest` read `self._exact` outside the lock. Two threads recording the SAME new digest both passed the probe → both `self._bloom.add()` → double-count against the Bloom's FAIL_CLOSED capacity + double-evaluate the tuple, breaking the class docstring's thread-safe-sharing promise. **THE FIX (COMMON — mirrors the CORRECT fully-locked probe+insert of `brutex.data.option_dedup.OptionDedupIndex.add_if_new`, CLAUDE.md §11):** (a) `lmdb_membership.py` gains a minimal `__len__` (O(1) via the LMDB B+tree `stat()["entries"]` — no scan) + an `iter_keys()` read-cursor walk over the stored digests; (b) `sweep_cache.open()` calls a NEW `_rebuild_bloom_from_exact(bloom, exact, bloom_capacity=)` that, on a NON-empty exact store, checks the persisted count against `bloom_capacity` FIRST (FAIL_CLOSED `SweepCacheCapacityError` if the persisted set is larger than the Bloom can hold — the operator re-opens with a larger `bloom_capacity`, never a silent overflow of the Bloom's own FAIL_CLOSED gate mid-rebuild) then `bloom.add(digest)` for every persisted digest (O(persisted), paid ONCE per resume; a cold/empty store is a no-op); (c) `record_digest` now holds `self._lock` across the ENTIRE `digest in self._exact` probe + `bloom.add` + `exact.add` + counter bump, and `seen_digest` holds it across the Bloom probe + the L2 exact confirm — so a digest is admitted to the Bloom EXACTLY once under concurrent workers. The critical section does NO vendor/network I/O (the LMDB get/put are O(1) at the Python layer), so the hold time stays O(1) — single-threaded semantics/return values are UNCHANGED, only serialized. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the resume repopulate is O(persisted) once at startup (a resume pays it once — acceptable, and far cheaper than re-running the sweep); determinism is preserved (the same digests → the same Bloom bits); the capacity guard is FAIL_CLOSED not auto-resized (matching the Bloom's own DEGRADED-MODE-forbidden contract, Golden Rule #5); `iter_keys` holds one read txn open for the walk, so the caller consumes it promptly (the only caller is the one-shot `open()` rebuild). **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after — both proven by reverting each fix in isolation):** `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_cache.py` — `test_reopen_reloads_persisted_membership` (the manual `_bloom.add` seed REMOVED — the reopen now dedups purely from `open()`'s repopulate) + NEW `test_resume_dedups_all_previously_recorded_without_manual_seed` (record 50 distinct combos, close, re-open a FRESH SweepCache on the SAME path, assert `seen` is True for all 50 with `bloom_negatives == 0`/`hits == 50` and a genuinely-new combo still reported unseen — FAILS BEFORE the repopulate: seen_digest returns False, verified by reverting the `open()` call) + `test_cold_open_repopulate_is_noop` (empty store → zero Bloom insertions) + `test_resume_bloom_capacity_exceeded_fails_closed` (a resume whose persisted count > `bloom_capacity` raises `SweepCacheCapacityError`) + `test_concurrent_record_admits_digest_exactly_once` (8 threads on a `Barrier` all `record_digest` the SAME new digest → exactly ONE "was new", `bloom_insertions == 1`, `records == 1` — FAILS BEFORE the locking: all 8 reported "was new" and the Bloom was inserted 8 times, verified by reverting the lock); `tests/unit/test_lmdb_membership.py` gains `test_len_counts_stored_keys` + `test_iter_keys_yields_all_stored` + a closed-guard class for `__len__`/`iter_keys`. **Verification (fresh isolated 3.12 venv, Rust wheels built via `maturin develop --release`):** `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py` **100.00% line + branch** (93 stmt / 16 branch, 0 missing) and `brutex/data/lmdb_membership.py` **100.00% line + branch** (59 stmt / 8 branch, 0 missing) over the two unit suites (35 passed); the property/bench/stress sweep-cache suites + option_dedup suites green (28 passed, O(1) ratios within budget); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 4 touched files; `mypy --strict` clean on the 2 touched source files (the sole `mypy` error in the env is a pre-existing `cma` optional-dep stub gap in the UNTOUCHED `brutex/engine/stage3_refine.py`, not this diff); `pyright` **0 errors, 0 warnings** on both source files. **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py`, `brutex/data/lmdb_membership.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_lmdb_membership.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-CACHE-RESUME-DEDUP-001. 1064. **DEC-TOKEN-BROKER-AWS-001 — a SHARED AWS PARAMETER-STORE token broker: BruteX READS the Groww creds (api_key + TOTP secret) AND the daily minted access token from ONE shared place — AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (region `ap-south-1`) — the SAME place TickVault reads; a single dedicated Lambda is the ONLY writer/minter, BruteX + TickVault are strictly READ-ONLY — STRICTLY OPT-IN, the default stays the local disk cache + local mint byte-identical to #1041** (2026-07-01; NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/token_store.py` + `token_store_aws.py` + `aws_client.py` + `brutex/config/credentials_aws.py`, plus additive edits to `constants.py` (the `BRUTEX_TOKEN_BROKER_READONLY` flag + region/path resolvers), `live.py` (2 build-site wirings), `config/credentials.py` (one `env → AWS → file` chain insertion), `pyproject.toml` (a NEW OPTIONAL `token-broker = ["boto3>=1.34,<2.0"]` extra + boto3/botocore mypy overrides) — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/52→60-vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE PROBLEM:** the daily token is cached PER-MACHINE (`token_cache.py` explicitly flags "a Groww-side ACCOUNT-WIDE issuance limit shared across many hosts is NOT solved here (that needs a networked token broker — out of scope)"). Two apps on ONE Groww account (TickVault live feed, BruteX backtesting) each mint their own token; Groww's single-active-token behaviour means a mint by one REVOKES the other's live token — the operator's "TickVault live feed auth-rejected after a deploy" incident. **THE OPERATOR'S FINAL DESIGN:** the operator's Groww creds ALREADY EXIST in AWS Parameter Store (region `ap-south-1`) as SecureStrings — `/tickvault/prod/groww/api-key` + `/tickvault/prod/groww/totp-secret`; the shared access TOKEN also lives in Parameter Store at `/tickvault/prod/groww/access-token`, minted by a SINGLE dedicated Lambda (a SEPARATE PR owns `deploy/aws_token_minter/`; out of scope here). Because there is EXACTLY ONE writer, there is NO compare-and-swap / DynamoDB / write-contention need — a plain SecureString parameter suffices, and BruteX + TickVault are strictly READ-ONLY consumers ("only one place for both TickVault live and BruteX backtesting"). This SUPERSEDES an earlier DynamoDB-based draft of this same decision. **THE DESIGN:** the daily-token backend is made PLUGGABLE on the EXISTING `SdkRefresher(..., token_cache_load=, token_cache_store=)` seam (injected callables the disk functions already satisfy) — NO spine change. NEW `TokenStore` Protocol (`load`/`store`, `load` NEVER raises) + `DiskTokenStore` (wraps the #1041 `load_cached_token`/`store_token` verbatim, the DEFAULT) + `resolve_token_store()` (reads `BRUTEX_TOKEN_BROKER_READONLY`; truthy `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on` + boto3-present → the read-only Parameter-Store store, else → local, fail-safe like `resolve_pool_size`; MEMOISED per env-config kind so all THREE refreshers of one pull share ONE client + ONE backend decision — no split-brain). The read-only backend (`token_store_aws.py`): `ParameterStoreTokenStore.load` reads the shared access-token SecureString via `GetParameter WithDecryption=True` (KMS-decrypted server-side by SSM — AWS SSM docs "Working with SecureString parameters"; `GetParameter` API reference), stamped with the current 06:00-IST `current_session`; ANY boto3/network/IAM/region/KMS error or an absent/blank value degrades to a `None` MISS (NEVER raises — the mint spine's contract). `ParameterStoreTokenStore.store` FAILS LOUD with `TokenBrokerReadOnlyError` (a terminal `GrowwAuthError`) — a mint attempt on a read-only host is a clear error, NEVER a silent local write that would fork the shared token (the operator's explicit "never a silent local mint"). Creds: ONE additive per-field insertion makes `config/credentials.py::resolve_groww_file_credentials` resolve `env → AWS → file` (`credentials_aws.py::load_groww_aws_credentials`, gated on the SAME `BRUTEX_TOKEN_BROKER_READONLY` flag, reads the two SecureString creds; returns `None` when the broker is OFF ⇒ BYTE-IDENTICAL to today, so local dev + CI need NO AWS). **REGION + PATHS (configurable constants with the operator defaults):** region resolves `BRUTEX_TOKEN_AWS_REGION` → `AWS_REGION` → `ap-south-1` (always a concrete region); the three parameter paths default to `/tickvault/prod/groww/{access-token,api-key,totp-secret}`, each env-overridable (`BRUTEX_TOKEN_PARAM_ACCESS_TOKEN` / `BRUTEX_TOKEN_PARAM_API_KEY` / `BRUTEX_TOKEN_PARAM_TOTP_SECRET`). **boto3 is a NEW OPTIONAL `token-broker` extra** (mirrors the `groww` extra) so a purely-LOCAL run imports ZERO AWS code (regression-pinned: `"boto3" not in sys.modules` after a default resolve/build); the real boto3 SSM-client build (`aws_client.build_real_aws_client` + `_Boto3AwsClient` + `credentials_aws._build_client_or_none` + `token_store_aws.build_readonly_token_store`'s client line) is `# pragma: no cover`, and a pure-Python `tests/fakes/fake_aws_client.py` (an SSM `{name: value}` map + `ParameterNotFound` + per-method fault injection, satisfying the ONE-method `AwsClient` Protocol) drives the broker to 100% line+branch with no install and no network. **READ-ONLY FAIL-FAST — HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the read-only store cannot suppress a mint network CALL from the injected `token_factory` (only the local WRITE), but the `store` hook fails LOUD the moment the persist is attempted, so there is NEVER a silent local token written — a forced reauth on a read-only host raises `TokenBrokerReadOnlyError` and the pull halts with a clear error; BruteX picks up the Lambda's re-minted token on the NEXT cold-start (process restart). The single-active-token vendor behaviour is UNVERIFIED (the SDK reference labels the TOTP flow "No Expiry"; the 06:00-IST reset is asserted from production logs + ADR-0009), so the cross-app fix is DESIGNED-to-fix, NOT verified-fixes (a live Groww probe would upgrade it); every reader host holds the decrypted cred/token in memory (same threat surface as today's on-disk secret, but a NEW N-host exposure, disclosed). **NO-HALLUCINATION AWS CITATIONS (Golden Rule #1):** every AWS behavioural claim is cited — the `GetParameter WithDecryption=True` SecureString KMS-decrypt is cited to the AWS SSM "Working with SecureString parameters" userguide + the `GetParameter` API reference (both in the ADR + contract). **DELIVERABLES — the SHARED CONTRACT** (`docs/TOKEN_BROKER_CONTRACT.md`, rewritten for the Parameter-Store single-writer/read-only design): the three parameter paths + SecureString read convention (`GetParameter WithDecryption=True`) + the single-writer/read-only convention (the Lambda is the ONLY writer; 1067. **DEC-AWS-DEPLOY-GUIDE-001 — a crystal-clear, copy-paste OPERATOR DEPLOY GUIDE for the AWS centralized Groww token system (`docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md`): the plain-English front-door that walks the operator from an empty AWS account to a self-healing daily-token pipeline read by both TickVault and BruteX** (2026-07-01; DOCS ONLY — one NEW runbook + this ledger entry; NO `brutex/` package code touched — `git status --short brutex/` empty; NO Rust touched; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **WHY:** DEC-TOKEN-MINTER-CENTRAL-001 (#1060, PR #1017) shipped the minter Lambda + Terraform + `deploy.sh` + the technical runbook `aws-token-minter.md`, and PR #1015 (the read-only Parameter-Store token broker, merging) adds BruteX's `BRUTEX_TOKEN_BROKER_READONLY` reader — but they are two separate technical docs. The operator asked for ONE human-readable guide to stand up the WHOLE thing (future item #10). **WHAT THE GUIDE COVERS (7 sections, all copy-paste):** (1) **Prerequisites** — `aws configure` with an admin identity + region `ap-south-1` (verified with `aws sts get-caller-identity` / `aws configure get region`); `brew install terraform awscli` (Terraform ≥ 1.5); the two Groww secrets already seeded as SecureStrings at `/tickvault/prod/groww/api-key` + `/tickvault/prod/groww/totp-secret` (with an `aws ssm describe-parameters` check + a `put-parameter` seeding fallback); the `alias/tickvault-groww` KMS key `Enabled`. (2) **The one-time deploy** — `cd deploy/aws_token_minter && ./deploy.sh -var 'alert_email=…'`: the three ordered steps (build the x86_64/cp312 cross-compiled bundle → `terraform init` → `terraform apply` which SHOWS the plan and requires a typed `yes`, NEVER `-auto-approve`), what it creates (the minter Lambda `reserved_concurrent_executions = 1` + the `access-token` SecureString + the `cron(35 0 * * ? *)` = 06:05-IST EventBridge schedule + the stale-token + Lambda-errors CloudWatch alarms + the SNS topic + the three least-privilege IAM roles), ~2 min, and the SNS-email-confirm reminder. (3) **How BruteX reads it** — a read-only AWS identity (`reader_brutex_role_arn`) + `export BRUTEX_TOKEN_BROKER_READONLY=true` (honestly stated: the flag exists UNTIL a later AWS-only change makes read-only the default; unset/blank ⇒ byte-identical local-cache + local-mint fallback so dev/CI need NO AWS) + run a pull. (4) **Verify it works** — an on-demand `aws lambda invoke` → the `{"ok": true, …}` success shape; `aws ssm get-parameter --with-decryption` proving the token param has a fresh Version/LastModified; `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics` proving the `TokenMintSuccess` metric summed ≥ 1; then a BruteX pull authenticating from the shared token. (5) **The daily lifecycle** — 06:00-IST reset → ~06:05 Lambda re-mint → both apps read the one fresh token → self-heals with zero clicks; the alarm pages you if a mint ever fails. (6) **Troubleshooting table** — "no token in Parameter Store" (deploy the minter first), `AccessDenied` on GetParameter vs `kms:Decrypt` (a SecureString read needs BOTH), region mismatch, the IntelliJ-vs-Mac-Terminal `PATH` note (Homebrew's `/opt/homebrew/bin` not inherited by the IDE terminal), `chmod +x deploy.sh`, the cross-compile ImportError (re-run `./deploy.sh` not a bare `terraform apply`), and the SNS-confirm-not-clicked case. (7) **Rotating creds** — overwrite the two SecureStrings with `put-parameter --overwrite`; nothing else changes; force one mint + re-verify. **HONESTY (Golden Rule #10 + #1):** the guide states up front that this is CODE + IaC ONLY — nothing is deployed by CI or by the repo, the operator runs `./deploy.sh` against their OWN account (this session has NO AWS access, no claim that any Lambda has run / minted / alarmed in a real account). Every AWS behavioral claim is cited to an official AWS docs URL (an "AWS references" section: SSM `GetParameter`-`WithDecryption` / `PutParameter`-`Overwrite`-`SecureString`-`KeyId` / CloudWatch `TreatMissingData`+`FILL` daily-job treatment / EventBridge scheduled-rule overlap semantics / IAM `cloudwatch:namespace` condition key / SSM-SecureString-KMS envelope encryption / AWS-CLI + Terraform install) — the SAME canonical URLs cited by ADR-0014, no invented AWS behavior. Deliberately CROSS-LINKS (does NOT duplicate) the two companion docs: `aws-token-minter.md` (exact paths/schedule/rollback, `terraform destroy`) + `aws-token-broker.md` (the reader's full contract, present once #1015 merges). **Files:** `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-AWS-DEPLOY-GUIDE-001. 1066. **DEC-AUTO-RESUME-ON-BOOT-001 — a BOOT-TIME trigger that AUTOMATICALLY continues an in-progress full-universe pull when BruteX boots (a fresh container / redeploy / restart), so an interrupted pull picks itself back up with ZERO operator clicks — the operator's GAP-2 / future item #11 (§11 AUTOMATED "auto-resume")** (2026-07-01; NEW `brutex/orchestrator/auto_resume.py` + `brutex/cli.py` dashboard-boot wiring + three test files + this ledger entry only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / pacing / fetch-rate change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty). **THE GAP (grounded in the current pull architecture):** the DATA layer is ALREADY resume-safe — the durable per-window ledger (`brutex/data/window_ledger.py` + `window_ledger_store.py`) records every planned window and settles it ONLY on `SUCCESS`/`SKIPPED`, so every `PLANNED` (never fetched) / `FAILED` (transient) window is re-pullable and the keep-first sink no-ops an already-stored window (DEC-FNO-LEDGER-LAKE-RECONCILE-001); the `--until-clean` loop then re-runs bounded rounds over ONLY the unsettled windows. AND the just-shipped `ProcessSupervisor` (DEC-SUPERVISOR-AUTORESTART-001 #1057) keeps the PROCESS alive across a crash. BUT nothing decided, once a fresh process was up again, to RESUME the pull — a redeployed container / restarted service sat idle until the operator manually clicked "start pull". This PR is the missing boot-time TRIGGER (the complement of the supervisor's relaunch): on boot, detect an incomplete pull from the ledger and auto-continue it. **WHAT SHIPPED (a thin, fully-testable DECISION layer — the resume ACTION is injected, so this module never imports the pull spine; CLAUDE.md §4 / §11 COMMON):** NEW `brutex/orchestrator/auto_resume.py` with (1) `resolve_auto_resume_on_boot(env)` — reads `BRUTEX_AUTO_RESUME_ON_BOOT`, returns `True` ONLY for an explicit truthy value (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`, case/whitespace-insensitive); unset / blank / `0` / unrecognised ⇒ `False` (default OFF — mirrors `resolve_smooth_pacing`; a dev / CI boot is NEVER surprised by a spontaneous pull, CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6). (2) `detect_incomplete_pull(ledger) -> IncompletePull | None` — **pure** over the ledger's authoritative `progress_counts()` snapshot: an incomplete pull is one with `total >= 1` AND at least one still-outstanding window (`planned > 0` OR `failed > 0`) — exactly the statuses `WindowLedger.is_skippable` returns `False` for, so it reads the SAME skip authority the pull itself uses (no drift). An EMPTY ledger (fresh clone / never-pulled) and an ALL-SETTLED ledger both return `None`; a genuine below-threshold `EMPTY` window is DELIBERATELY NOT counted as "resume me" (it is resolved-not-pending per `RESOLVED_STATUSES`, and on a wholly-past range it can never gain data, so counting it would loop a boot forever — Golden Rule #1 / #10). (3) `maybe_resume_on_boot(*, load_ledger, resume, enabled=None)` — the ONE boot entry point, returning exactly one `ResumeVerdict` (`DISABLED` / `NOTHING_TO_RESUME` / `RESUMED` / `ERROR`): flag OFF ⇒ `DISABLED` (nothing loaded, byte-identical default path); flag ON + clean ledger ⇒ `NOTHING_TO_RESUME`; flag ON + outstanding work ⇒ fire the injected `resume(IncompletePull)` action ⇒ `RESUMED`; ANY exception from `load_ledger` / detect / `resume` is CAUGHT + logged (`auto_resume.error`) + returned as `ERROR` — the helper **NEVER raises**, so a boot can never be blocked or crashed by the resume attempt (Reliability over everything). Each outcome emits ONE structured log line (observable, Golden Rule #8). **CLI DASHBOARD WIRING (`brutex/cli.py`, at the SAME instant-launch seam `_start_instrument_autoload` uses — DEC-DASHBOARD-INSTANT-LAUNCH-001):** `cmd_dashboard` calls a NEW `_start_auto_resume_on_boot(lake_root, log)` right after `build_app`, which runs `maybe_resume_on_boot` in a background DAEMON thread (so the ledger read / spawn never blocks the uvicorn port bind), wired to `load_window_ledger(lake_root)` (the durable read) and an injected `resume` that spawns `brutex fetch --universe --until-clean` via `sys.executable -m brutex` (the PURE `_auto_resume_child_argv` helper, mirrors `_supervisor_child_argv`). A SEPARATE process (not an in-server job) is deliberate: the CLI fetch spine is already fully tested AND honours the account-wide cross-process single-flight lock (DEC-ACCOUNT-PULL-SINGLEFLIGHT-001), so a concurrent dashboard click can NEVER double the Groww request rate (Golden Rule #6) — the second pull is simply refused; `start_new_session=True` isolates the child's process group so the resumed pull outlives a dashboard restart. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** OPT-IN (default OFF — the operator turns it on for production); IDEMPOTENT + SAFE (re-pulling a settled window is a no-op via the keep-first sink; only unsettled windows re-pull — this module adds NO data path); NON-BLOCKING + best-effort at boot (daemon thread + never-raises guard); pure ORCHESTRATION — no engine / vocab / rate / lake-schema change. This wires the DASHBOARD boot path (the primary always-on entrypoint the operator redeploys); a `brutex fetch`-side boot hook and an in-server (non-subprocess) resume are explicit FOLLOW-UPS, NOT claimed. **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after):** NEW `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_auto_resume.py` (23 — the truthy/falsy/unset/injected-env resolver matrix; detect empty/all-settled ⇒ None, PLANNED-only / FAILED-only / both ⇒ verdict + the `outstanding` sum; every `ResumeVerdict` incl. DISABLED-does-not-load, NOTHING_TO_RESUME-on-clean, RESUMED-fires-the-action, and BOTH error paths — a raising `load_ledger` AND a raising `resume` action are swallowed to `ERROR`, never re-raised) + NEW `tests/integration/test_auto_resume_on_boot_scenario.py` (2 — end-to-end against a REAL `WindowLedger`: a mid-flight pull (one settled + one PLANNED) is detected + resumed, then once every window is settled the SAME ledger reads clean and the boot is a `NOTHING_TO_RESUME` no-op; a transient `FAILED` window also triggers a resume) + NEW `tests/unit/test_cli_auto_resume.py` (1 — the pure `_auto_resume_child_argv` pins `[sys.executable, -m, brutex, fetch, --universe, --until-clean]`). The three live CLI helpers (`_spawn_auto_resume_pull` / `_start_auto_resume_on_boot`) are `# pragma: no cover` at the SAME live-daemon/subprocess boundary the supervisor's daemon loop is excluded at; the DECISION is 100%-tested in the module; the `cmd_dashboard` call line is covered by the existing offline `test_cli_run.py` dashboard tests (14 green with the new default-OFF line executing harmlessly). **Verification (fresh isolated 3.12 venv):** `brutex/orchestrator/auto_resume.py` **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (66 stmt / 10 branch, 0 missing) over the two auto-resume suites (30 passed); the new `_auto_resume_child_argv` covered + no new missing line in `brutex/cli.py`; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files; `mypy --strict brutex/orchestrator/auto_resume.py` clean (the only `mypy --strict brutex` errors are the PRE-EXISTING `growwapi`-stub `auth.py`/`reauth.py` env artifacts in UNTOUCHED files, reproduced on the pristine baseline); `pyright` **0 errors, 0 warnings** on all four new files; `no-dhan-guard` exit 0; `scan-banned-patterns` exit 0; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` + `validate_dec_ids.py` exit 0; `git status --short rust/` empty. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/auto_resume.py`, `brutex/cli.py` (the `_auto_resume_child_argv` / `_spawn_auto_resume_pull` / `_start_auto_resume_on_boot` helpers + the `cmd_dashboard` boot call), `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_auto_resume.py`, `tests/integration/test_auto_resume_on_boot_scenario.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_auto_resume.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-AUTO-RESUME-ON-BOOT-001. (Ledger: renumbered #1064 → #1066 on the 2026-07-01 re-sync onto `origin/main` — main advanced its max real entry to #1064 `DEC-TOKEN-BROKER-AWS-001` (the just-merged PR #1015), so this PR takes #1066 = max+2 to stay distinct from a sibling PR expected at #1065 (max+1); a numbering gap is allowed, the validator enforces only (number,suffix) uniqueness; the `~#1155` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` cited by an earlier entry body is a comment reference, NOT a ledger header — ignored per the validator's header-only rule; the DEC-ID is the stable handle — re-checked immediately before push.)

1081. **DEC-CI-COST-DEDUP-001 — the `ci.yml` `push` trigger is SCOPED TO `main` ONLY, so a feature-branch PR commit runs the full CI matrix ONCE (via the `pull_request` event) instead of TWICE, roughly HALVING GitHub Actions minutes with ZERO loss of gate coverage** (2026-07-01; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` trigger block + this ledger entry ONLY — NO `brutex/` package code touched (`git status --short brutex/` empty), NO Rust touched, NO CI JOB / gate / coverage-threshold change; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE WASTE (confirmed from the run history + the pre-merge-gate comment on PR #1029, which listed every check TWICE):** `ci.yml` triggered on BOTH `push` to `main`/`claude/**`/`feat/**`/`fix/**` AND `pull_request` to `main`. On a feature branch that has an open PR, a single commit fires BOTH events; because the `concurrency` group is keyed by `github.ref` — `refs/heads/<branch>` for the push event vs `refs/pull/<n>/merge` for the pull_request event — the two runs land in DIFFERENT concurrency groups, so `cancel-in-progress: true` does NOT cancel one against the other, and the ENTIRE ~35-job matrix (ruff · mypy+pyright · unit+coverage · property · bench · golden · bandit · CodeQL · Semgrep · Trivy · mutation-freshness · both Rust crates · chaos/race · docstring · license · SBOM · …) ran to completion TWICE per commit. Over a burst of PR pushes this is the dominant Actions-minute cost (the operator's July metered usage was `bruteX $87.27` — GitHub Actions CI). **THE FIX (CI-CONFIG ONLY — no gate weakened):** `on.push.branches` is reduced from `[main, claude/**, feat/**, fix/**]` to `[main]`; feature branches are now validated by the `pull_request` event ALONE (a single run per commit), and `push` runs only on the `main` merge. **NO LOSS OF COVERAGE / SAFETY (verified against the sibling workflows):** every required check the merge gate reads is still produced by the `pull_request` run (required checks match by CONTEXT NAME, which the pull_request event emits identically); `auto-merge.yml` + `pre-merge-gate.yml` both trigger on the CI `workflow_run` REGARDLESS of the originating event, so auto-merge + the merge-readiness verdict are unaffected; rapid pushes to one PR now share the stable `refs/pull/<n>/merge` concurrency group so `cancel-in-progress` supersedes the older run (an EXTRA saving). The self-hosted M4-Pro workflows (`bench-m4pro.yml` / `verify-m4pro.yml`) consume NO GitHub-hosted minutes; `mutation.yml` / `security-audit.yml` / `stress-nightly.yml` / `redteam-nightly.yml` / `safety.yml` / `dep-freshness-nightly.yml` / `branch-protection-drift.yml` are schedule/paths-gated already (not per-PR). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** a feature-branch commit with NO open PR now gets no CI until a PR is opened (the repo's flow is PR-based — auto-merge + pre-merge-gate act on PRs — so this is the intended path, not a regression); this is a COST/PLUMBING change only — it changes WHEN CI runs, never WHAT it checks, so every 100%-coverage / type / lint / security / O(1) / mutation gate is byte-identical. **Files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-CI-COST-DEDUP-001. (Ledger: #1081 = the next free unique number above the file's current max #1080 after the 2026-07-01 re-sync merge of `origin/main` — the branch's original #1070 collided with the newly-merged `DEC-GREEKS-SHARED-CORE-001`, so this entry was renumbered per parallel rule P-1; a numbering gap is allowed — the validator enforces only (number,suffix) uniqueness; the DEC-ID is the stable handle — re-checked immediately before push.)
1082. **DEC-MONITOR-NEVER-DIE-001 — the `MonitorLoop` daemon poller now catches `except Exception` (not only `OSError`/`ValueError`/`RuntimeError`) so a callback raising a custom `AuditError` — the EXACT signal the L3 replay oracle exists to emit on a live-vs-audit dedup inconsistency — is caught + logged instead of ESCAPING `tick_once`, propagating out of the unguarded `_run` `while True`, and silently KILLING the whole watchdog/SLA/replay monitor thread with no restart + no alert** (2026-07-01; `brutex/observability/monitor.py` + `tests/unit/test_observability_monitor.py` + this ledger entry ONLY — NO Rust touched (`git status --short rust/` empty); ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / pacing change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE DEFECT (adversarial-verification HIGH, confirmed against the real code):** `MonitorLoop.tick_once` wrapped each of the SLA / Watchdog / replay callbacks in `except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError)` (`monitor.py` guards), while `AuditError` is a `BruteXError` (NOT a subclass of any of those three) and `assert_dedup_consistent` raises it PRECISELY on the inconsistency the oracle is built to catch. So when the replay check fired on a real dedup inconsistency the `AuditError` escaped `tick_once`, and `_run`'s `while True: self.tick_once()` has NO surrounding try/except (a deliberate single-exit design), so the exception propagated out of the daemon thread and it DIED — thereafter no SLA / hung-worker / replay check ran for the process lifetime, a silent loss of the entire observability rail with nothing to restart it or alert on it. **THE DOC LIE (Golden Rule #10):** the module docstring already CLAIMED "wrapped in a broad try/except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError, custom AuditError) so a misbehaving callback never crashes the monitor" — the code did NOT catch AuditError, and 100% branch coverage was satisfied only because the tests parametrised solely the three types that WERE caught (the smoking gun: a covered-but-wrong guard). **THE FIX (COMMON, mirrors the repo's established "best-effort, never crash" pattern — `except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught`, as used in `pull_pipeline.py`):** all three guards broaden to `except Exception`, which catches AuditError (and any future custom BruteXError) — a monitor MUST never die on a callback error — while still NOT catching `BaseException` (a real `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` still propagates correctly); the docstring is rewritten to state the true behaviour + cite this decision. Cycle-free (no new production import — `AuditError` is imported only in the test). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is a correctness + doc-honesty fix to the monitor PRIMITIVE; `MonitorLoop`'s production binding into the live pull is a SEPARATE dormant-wiring item (acknowledged in `STANDARDS_100PCT_HONEST_AUDIT.md` §9) — this PR does NOT claim the monitor is wired into every production pull, only that the primitive can no longer silently die on the AuditError it exists to surface. **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after):** the three `test_*_exception_does_not_propagate` parametrised suites gain `AuditError` (fails-before: the narrow tuple let AuditError escape → `tick_once` raised → the test erred); NEW `TestNeverDiesOnAuditError` — `test_tick_once_survives_replay_audit_error` (a replay raising AuditError is caught + logged, `tick_once` does NOT raise) + `test_daemon_thread_survives_audit_error_and_keeps_ticking` (a REAL daemon thread whose every tick raises AuditError is asserted STILL running after ~7 ticks with ≥3 recorded ticks — fails-before: the thread died on the first AuditError, `is_running` → False). **Verified 2026-07-01 on the project `.venv` (Python 3.12.3):** `brutex/observability/monitor.py` **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (74 stmt / 16 branch, 0 missing) over `test_observability_monitor.py` (31 passed); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on both files; `mypy --strict brutex/observability/monitor.py` clean. **Files:** `brutex/observability/monitor.py`, `tests/unit/test_observability_monitor.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-MONITOR-NEVER-DIE-001. (Ledger: #1082 = the next free unique number after the 2026-07-01 re-sync merge of `origin/main` (max #1080) — the branch's original #1074 collided with the newly-merged `DEC-MINTER-DEPLOY-BASH32-SAFE-001`, and #1081 is reserved by the in-flight sibling PR #1033 `DEC-CI-COST-DEDUP-001`; renumbered per parallel rule P-1; a numbering gap is allowed — the validator enforces only (number,suffix) uniqueness; the DEC-ID is the stable handle — re-checked immediately before push.)
1077. **DEC-GITIGNORE-SCRATCHPAD-001 — `.gitignore` hygiene: ignore the worker/agent `scratchpad/` scratch dir AND fix the ineffective proptest-regressions glob so it actually matches the `proptest-regressions/` DIRECTORY, keeping the repo from being perpetually dirty** (2026-07-01; `.gitignore` + this ledger entry ONLY — NO `brutex/` package code touched (`git status --short brutex/` empty), NO Rust touched (`git status --short rust/` empty); ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / pacing / fetch-rate change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE PROBLEM (two confirmed root causes):** (1) the parallel-agent workers create a `scratchpad/` dir at the repo root (throwaway venvs, tool caches, cargo-mutants scratch, built wheels, disposable test lakes, and nested `wt-*` git worktrees), and it was NOT gitignored — `git check-ignore scratchpad` exited 1 and `git -C /home/user/bruteX status --porcelain` perpetually showed `?? scratchpad/`, so every session started on a dirty tree. (2) the existing `**/*.proptest-regressions` rule was INEFFECTIVE: proptest persists its saved failure seeds in a directory literally named `proptest-regressions/` (no leading dot), but the glob `*.proptest-regressions` matches only a path ENDING in `.proptest-regressions` (e.g. `foo.proptest-regressions`). PROVEN in the live repo: `git check-ignore -v rust/trading-core/proptest-regressions/indicators/metadata.txt` → exit 1 (NOT ignored), while `git check-ignore -v foo.proptest-regressions` → matched `.gitignore:109`. The result was an untracked `rust/trading-core/proptest-regressions/indicators/metadata.txt` seed (a `cc … # shrinks to entry = 0, cand = 0, next = 1` case) sitting dirty. **THE SEED IS BENIGN (ruled out as a real bug before this PR):** the seed belongs to the `indicators::metadata::tests::near_month_is_candidate_iff_not_expired` proptest; proptest re-runs saved regression seeds FIRST before any novel case, and a full `cd rust/trading-core && cargo test` PASSES (71 unit + 1 + 3 + 13 + 2 = all green; the metadata proptest module reports `test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed`), so the `entry=0, cand=0, next=1` boundary (`cand >= entry` ⇒ returns `cand`) is correctly handled on clean code — the seed is cargo-mutants scratch debris (the `scratchpad/mut` + `scratchpad/mutvenv` mutation-testing dirs generated it), not a real failure. **THE REPO CONVENTION (verified):** `git ls-files | grep -i proptest-regressions` returns NOTHING — no proptest-regressions dir/file is tracked anywhere in the repo, so the project's convention is to IGNORE them (the existing comment already documented this intent: "the only ones generated so far were induced by cargo-mutants mutants (not real failures), so they are scratch"). Fixing the glob to match the directory therefore aligns the rule with the already-documented-and-followed convention; it does NOT change any tracked file. **WHAT SHIPPED (`.gitignore` only, additive):** (1) a NEW `scratchpad/` directory-ignore rule (with a clarifying comment that this is the worker/agent scratch dir) placed just above the `.claude/worktrees/` transient-state block; (2) a NEW `**/proptest-regressions/` directory glob added ABOVE the retained legacy `**/*.proptest-regressions` line (the suffix form is KEPT for back-compat with any hypothetical dot-suffixed path), with a comment explaining the directory-vs-suffix distinction. **VERIFICATION (in the branch worktree):** after the change, `git check-ignore -v scratchpad/venv_run` → matched `scratchpad/`; `git check-ignore -v scratchpad/mut/some-cache.db` → matched; `git check-ignore -v rust/trading-core/proptest-regressions/indicators/metadata.txt` → matched `**/proptest-regressions/` (the previously-broken case now ignored); `git check-ignore -v foo.proptest-regressions` → still matched by the retained suffix line; the worktree `git status --porcelain` shows ONLY ` M .gitignore` (the `scratchpad/` directory-only pattern correctly ignores every file inside — the bare-word `scratchpad` check with no trailing slash returns exit 1 only because git cannot classify a non-existent path as a directory, but `scratchpad/` and any nested path match, which is the standard, intended behaviour for a directory ignore). `python scripts/ci/validate_ledger_numbering.py` exit 0; `python scripts/ci/validate_no_hallucination.py` on the PR body exit 0. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this PR ADDS ignore rules only — it does NOT `git rm` any currently-tracked file (none of the scratchpad/proptest-regressions paths are tracked), does NOT commit the benign `metadata.txt` seed (left for the coordinator — likely mutant debris), and touches NO code. `.gitignore` behaviour is the sole surface. **Files:** `.gitignore`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-GITIGNORE-SCRATCHPAD-001. 1069. **DEC-MINTER-PURE-PYTHON-001 — the AWS Groww token-minter Lambda drops the `growwapi` dependency and mints the token with PURE PYTHON (a stdlib `urllib` HTTPS POST + `pyotp`), so the deploy bundle carries ZERO platform-specific wheels and `./deploy.sh` builds identically on macOS/ARM64 with NO Docker — reworking PR #1027 (was DEC-MINTER-BUILD-ROBUST-001's two-path Docker build), fixing the operator's real `ResolutionImpossible` on `deploy.sh` at the ROOT** (2026-07-01; DEPLOY-LAMBDA/BUILD/DOCS ONLY — `deploy/aws_token_minter/{handler.py,build_lambda_package.sh,deploy.sh,requirements.txt,main.tf,variables.tf,versions.tf}` + `tests/deploy/{test_aws_token_minter_handler.py,test_build_lambda_package.py}` + `docs/adr/0014-centralized-token-minter.md` + `docs/runbooks/{aws-token-minter.md,aws-token-deploy-guide.md}` + this ledger entry; NO `brutex/` package code touched — `git status --short brutex/` empty; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE OPERATOR'S BUG (root-caused in the prior DEC-MINTER-BUILD-ROBUST-001 revision of PR #1027):** running `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh` on macOS failed at "1/3 building Lambda deploy bundle" with `ResolutionImpossible`. The confirmed root: `growwapi` (the old token-mint dependency) drags in a heavy native-extension transitive tree (`pynacl`, `pydantic-core`, `pandas`, `aiohttp`) AND depends on `clint`, which ships **only as an sdist (no wheel on PyPI)** — so a cross-platform `--only-binary=:all:` install CANNOT resolve `clint` even with `growwapi` pinned. The prior fix (the DEC-MINTER-BUILD-ROBUST-001 revision) worked AROUND this with a two-path build that REQUIRED Docker on macOS (a native in-container `pip install`); that shipped, but keeps a Docker dependency the operator wants gone. **THE ROOT-LEVEL FIX (this rework):** the Groww token mint does NOT need `growwapi` at all. Verified from the `growwapi` 1.5.0 SDK source (`client.py`, `GrowwAPI.get_access_token` staticmethod, lines 1540-1580 — Golden Rule #1, no-hallucination): the TOTP token flow is exactly ONE UNSIGNED HTTPS POST — no request signing, no crypto, no pynacl. So the handler now mints the token with a pure-stdlib `urllib` reimplementation: NEW `handler.py::get_groww_access_token(api_key, totp, *, opener=urllib.request.urlopen)` POSTs `{"key_type":"totp","totp":totp.strip()}` (`client.py:1525-1529`) to `https://api.groww.in/v1/token/api/access` (`client.py:1557`) with the seven vendor headers `x-request-id`/`Authorization: Bearer`/`Content-Type`/`x-client-id: growwapi`/`x-client-platform: growwapi-python-client`/`x-client-platform-version: 1.5.0`/`x-api-version: 1.0` (`client.py:1370-1378`), extracts `payload["token"]` (`client.py:1580`), and on a non-2xx (vendor detail preserved, `client.py:1561-1579`) raises `GrowwMintHTTPError` — a `RuntimeError` subclass that carries the HTTP status `code` STRUCTURALLY (`.code`), so a genuine issuance 429 whose vendor body has NO textual "rate limit" phrase (e.g. `{"status":"FAILURE","error":{"code":"GA0009"}}`) is still classified retryable by `_is_rate_limit`'s `code == 429` check and re-driven through the issuance-retry ladder (a plain `RuntimeError` with the status only in the message would have been misread as terminal at the 06:05 IST post-reset mint — the likeliest throttle window); a missing/empty token raises `RuntimeError`; a blank TOTP raises `ValueError` before any network call (matching the SDK's `_build_request_data` guard, `client.py:1526-1527`). The HTTPError branch is raised `from None` so a vendor body that echoed a secret is not chained into a leaking CloudWatch traceback. The exact `client.py` lines are cited INLINE as comments. TOTP generation stays on `pyotp` (`pyotp.TOTP(secret).now()`) — the crypto is NOT reimplemented. **THE PAYOFF:** with `growwapi` gone, the ONLY bundled third-party dep is `pyotp==2.10.0` — a pure-Python UNIVERSAL wheel (`py3-none-any`, `Root-Is-Purelib: true`, ZERO runtime deps) — so the bundle has ZERO platform-specific wheels and the build is ONE deterministic `pip install --target --no-compile pyotp==2.10.0`: no Docker, no `--platform`/`--only-binary`/`--abi` cross-compile flags, no two-path A/B branching, no `clint` wall. `build_lambda_package.sh` is rewritten to that single path (a comment states + explains WHY no Docker is needed); `deploy.sh` drops all Docker detection/messaging; a NEW `requirements.txt` declares the one dep; `main.tf`/`variables.tf`/`versions.tf` drop the `growwapi_version` variable + its trigger/env wiring (only `pyotp_version` remains). Every existing #1017 handler safety property is PRESERVED byte-for-byte: no secret in logs/exceptions (`_sanitize` scrubs api-key/TOTP/token; the terminal `TokenMintError` is `raise ... from None` so the raw vendor exc is not chained into a leaking CloudWatch traceback), the SSM read/write contract (`get_parameter(WithDecryption=True)` → mint → `put_parameter(Type='SecureString', Overwrite=True, KeyId=)`), the issuance-429 + SSM-throttle retry ladders, and boto3 NOT bundled (AWS-runtime-provided). **VERIFICATION (SANDBOX, Linux/x86_64/py3.12 — HONEST about what could vs could NOT be proven, Golden Rule #10):** (i) `pip install --target --no-compile pyotp==2.10.0` → exit 0; the resulting bundle contains ZERO `.so`/`.dylib`/`.pyd` files (`find … -name '*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' -o -name '*.pyd'` empty; wheel tag `py3-none-any`, `Root-Is-Purelib: true`) — PROVING zero platform wheels; (ii) `build_lambda_package.sh` runs end-to-end (exit 0) producing a clean `handler.py`+`__init__.py`+`pyotp` bundle with NO platform binaries and NO growwapi; (iii) the pure request-building / response-parsing / HTTPError / missing-token branches of `get_groww_access_token` are driven to 100% by an INJECTED fake opener (a `_FakeResponse` yielding `{"token":...}` for success, a raised `urllib.error.HTTPError` for the error path, `{}`/`{"token":""}` for the no-token path) — NO network call. NOT PROVEN IN THE SANDBOX (no AWS / no live-vendor access): the real mint against the live Groww endpoint + end-to-end import in the deployed x86_64 Lambda remain operator steps. **HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10):** the endpoint/headers/body/token-extraction are PINNED to `growwapi` 1.5.0's behavior (cited to `client.py:1540-1580`); if Groww changes its auth contract, `handler.py::get_groww_access_token` must be updated — the SAME version-coupling the SDK itself has, now visible + testable in-repo instead of vendored opaquely. This SUPERSEDES DEC-MINTER-BUILD-ROBUST-001 (PR #1027's prior body): the two-path Docker/cross-pip build existed only to work around `growwapi`'s native tree + `clint`'s missing wheel — both gone with `growwapi` itself. **SCOPE OF THE REIMPLEMENTATION (honest, Golden Rule #10):** what is reproduced faithfully from `growwapi` 1.5.0 is the REQUEST + token-extraction CONTRACT (URL / method / seven headers / body / `payload["token"]`, each cited to its `client.py` line); the ERROR handling is deliberately SIMPLER than the SDK's (a single `GrowwMintHTTPError` carrying the status `code` + a blank-TOTP `ValueError`) rather than a line-for-line copy of the SDK's exception tree — the 429 status is PRESERVED structurally so the retry ladder still fires, which is the property that matters for the 06:05 IST mint. **GATES:** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` CLEAN on all touched deploy + test files; the build-script content-assertions were rewritten to pin the pure-Python single-dep build (pyotp pinned; NO Docker/growwapi/boto3 in the build; NO cross-compile flags; NO two-path branching; requirements.txt = exactly `pyotp==2.10.0`) + a NEW `test_handler_does_not_import_growwapi` AST-parses the handler source so a lazy/nested growwapi import cannot slip past. **Files:** `deploy/aws_token_minter/handler.py`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/build_lambda_package.sh`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/requirements.txt`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/main.tf`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/variables.tf`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/versions.tf`, `tests/deploy/test_aws_token_minter_handler.py`, `tests/deploy/test_build_lambda_package.py`, `docs/adr/0014-centralized-token-minter.md`, `docs/runbooks/aws-token-minter.md`, `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-MINTER-PURE-PYTHON-001. 1076. **DEC-O1-BENCH-GATE-COMPLETE-001 — every Golden-Rule-#5 O(1) hot path (CLAUDE.md §2 r5) now has a dedicated ISOLATED `p99(N_big)/p99(N_small)` ratio bench that RUNS on the shared-CI ratio tier, PLUS the strict 1.1× M4-Pro tier lists them all; a genuinely-missing BOS/CHoCH per-bar bench is added** (2026-07-01; TEST + CI-WORKFLOW ONLY — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / pacing change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO `brutex/` package code touched — `git status --short brutex/` empty; NO Rust touched). **THE GAP (honest enumeration, no illusion):** Golden Rule #5 (CLAUDE.md §2 r5) names five O(1) hot paths that must each hold the decreed `p99(N=1M)/p99(N=1K) ≤ 1.1×` ratio: (a) bar lookup, (b) indicator value lookup, (c) combo dedup (Bloom + LMDB), (d) strategy mask evaluation (u128 `(bar_bits & mask) == mask` AND), (e) result append; the 52→60-vocab expansion (DEC-NIFTY-BOS-CHOCH-001 #1012) added a SIXTH per-bar path — (f) BOS/CHoCH `MarketStructureState.update` (bits 56-59). A truth-table audit of `tests/bench/` × the two workflows found: a dedicated isolated bench ALREADY EXISTS for (a)-(e) (`test_bar_lookup_o1.py`, `test_indicator_lookup_o1.py`, `test_bloom_o1.py` + `test_lmdb_membership_o1.py` + `test_engine_sweep_cache_o1.py`, `test_engine_combo_mask_o1.py`, `test_engine_results_store_o1.py`), each already routing its ceiling through the COMMON single-source-of-truth `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py` helper, and — critically — all of them ALREADY RUN on the RUNNABLE shared-CI gate (`ci.yml`'s `bench` job runs a bare `pytest tests/bench` over the WHOLE dir on the shared ubuntu runner at the robust ~5× tier). So for (a)-(e) NO NEW BENCH WAS WRITTEN — the "≈4 missing benches" belief was WRONG (Golden Rule #1: reported honestly rather than fabricating a gap). **ONE bench was genuinely MISSING: (f) BOS/CHoCH** — the guarantee audit correctly flagged that `MarketStructureState.update` (the per-bar bits-56-59 detector) had NO dedicated O(1) bench, so this PR ADDS `tests/bench/test_market_structure_o1.py` against the REAL production `brutex/indicators/market_structure.py::update`, proving its latency is independent of session depth (a 100K-bar-deep session equals a 1K-deep one — the fixed-size `deque(maxlen=2k+1)` fractal ring makes each bar O(1); a session-history re-scan would blow it). It holds the true strict 1.1× via `ratio_ceiling` (fixed window → no cache-tier crossing; measured ~1.0×). **THE TWO GAPS BEYOND (f) — both about GATING, both fixed:** (1) the **strict 1.1× tier** (`BRUTEX_M4PRO_STRICT=1`, `bench-m4pro.yml`) ran only a SUBSET of six files, so (a)/(b)/(c-Bloom+digest)/(d-isolated)/(e)/(f) were listed at the decreed 1.1× only IMPLICITLY (via the canary's generic dict/mask shapes) or not at all — now ALL are wired into the "Run strict 1.1x O(1) ratio tier" step (+ the `paths:` trigger, incl. `_o1_tiers.py`). (2) **HONEST DORMANCY DISCLOSURE (Golden Rule #10 — the load-bearing honesty):** the strict 1.1× tier targets `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos, m4pro]`, an UNREGISTERED runner (bench-m4pro.yml header), so that job queues indefinitely and does NOT execute on any current CI — the strict 1.1× gate is ASPIRATIONAL until the operator registers the M4-Pro runner. This PR does NOT claim a strict gate that can't run: a code comment in the strict step + this entry state plainly that the ACTUALLY-RUNNABLE O(1) gate for every bench (incl. the new BOS/CHoCH one) is the shared-CI `bench` job at the robust ~5× tier, which catches a real O(n) regression TODAY; the strict 1.1× is the tighter SECOND tier that activates once the runner is online. **THE HONEST CALIBRATION (Golden Rule #10):** four of the newly-STRICT-listed benches use a large tier of 100K objects / 10K rows / 10K-element loops whose big scale SPILLS the CPU cache into DRAM, so at the decreed raw 1.1× they FAIL by cache-hierarchy physics, NOT an algorithmic regression — the EXACT phenomenon `_o1_tiers.py` already documents (DEC-O1-CACHE-TIER-001: "the decreed 1.1x is physically unsatisfiable when the large size spills L2/SLC into DRAM"). So the cross-cache-tier ratio assertions in `test_bar_lookup_o1.py` (both), `test_indicator_lookup_o1.py` (pivot + fib; VWAP unchanged), `test_engine_combo_mask_o1.py` (both — the u128 mask-AND loop + the projection), and `test_engine_results_store_o1.py` (`append`; `get` unchanged) are re-routed from `ratio_ceiling(5.0)` to `cache_tier_ceiling(5.0)` — the SAME COMMON helper (CLAUDE.md §11) and the SAME allowance the `test_throughput_canary.py` mask-AND / dict-lookup 1M-elem tests already use (`cache_tier_ceiling(8.0)` / `(10.0)`). This is ZERO behaviour change on shared CI (`cache_tier_ceiling(5.0)` returns the caller's 5× default when the strict env is unset — byte-identical to `ratio_ceiling(5.0)` there) and, on the M4-Pro strict tier, an HONEST, satisfiable 3× ceiling (the measured allowance) instead of an impossible 1.1×. The hash/compute-DOMINATED + fixed-window paths — the Bloom k-hash probe (`test_bloom_o1.py`), the blake3 combo digest (`test_engine_sweep_cache_o1.py`), and the BOS/CHoCH ring (`test_market_structure_o1.py`) — KEEP the raw strict 1.1× via `ratio_ceiling` (their per-op cost dominates memory access / their window is fixed, so they do not cross a tier; proven stable ≥4/4 runs at strict). **MEASURED (on a NOISY shared cloud VM — the quiet M4-Pro is strictly less noisy):** with `BRUTEX_M4PRO_STRICT=1` the per-path ratios and their live ceilings: (a) bar lookup 1.38× < 3.0×; (b) indicator (pivot) lookup 2.45× < 3.0×; (c) Bloom probe 0.996× < 1.1×; (c) blake3 digest 1.02× < 1.1×; (d) u128 mask-AND 1.02× < 3.0×; (e) result append 1.84× < 3.0×; (f) BOS/CHoCH update ~1.0× < 1.1× — ALL PASS, and the exact strict-tier command from `bench-m4pro.yml` ran green; the new BOS/CHoCH bench passed on the shared-CI (non-strict) tier AND 4/4 strict runs with zero flakes. A genuine O(n) regression still blows well past 3× and fails on the RUNNABLE shared tier. **HONEST envelope:** the ONE new bench (`test_market_structure_o1.py`) is a TEST, not production code — no NEW `brutex/` helper was added (the (a)-(e) fix only re-routed existing test assertions through an EXISTING COMMON helper), so there is no new package line/branch to cover; `_o1_tiers.py` is unchanged. The ~50 M ops/s ABSOLUTE floor (STANDARDS_100PCT.md §1 row 14) is a SEPARATE gate (`test_throughput_absolute.py`, `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS`), untouched. **Verification (fresh scratchpad 3.12 venv):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all five changed/new bench files; `pyright` **0 errors, 0 warnings** on all five; `mypy` produces ZERO errors originating from the five files (the only errors are the PRE-EXISTING `growwapi`-stub / `cma` optional-dep gaps in the UNTOUCHED `auth.py`/`reauth.py`/`stage3_refine.py`, reproduced identically on the pristine baseline `test_store_o1.py`); `actionlint` clean on `bench-m4pro.yml`; the workflow YAML parses (`yaml.safe_load`, structure intact); the new file is collected by a bare `pytest tests/bench` (so the shared-CI job runs it); `validate_ledger_numbering.py` exit 0. **Files:** `tests/bench/test_market_structure_o1.py` (NEW — the BOS/CHoCH O(1) bench), `tests/bench/test_bar_lookup_o1.py`, `tests/bench/test_indicator_lookup_o1.py`, `tests/bench/test_engine_combo_mask_o1.py`, `tests/bench/test_engine_results_store_o1.py`, `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-O1-BENCH-GATE-COMPLETE-001. 1072. **DEC-BROKER-READONLY-REAUTH-REREAD-001 — on the shared-AWS read-only token broker, a mid-run Groww token rejection now RE-READS the Lambda-minted token from SSM Parameter Store and ADOPTS it, instead of trying to re-mint locally (which hit the read-only store's fail-loud `store()` and needed a manual RESTART) — the read-only host self-heals the 06:00-IST rotation with ZERO restart** (2026-07-01; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / pacing / fetch-rate change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched). **THE GAP (confirmed file:line):** under the AWS-only token model (`DEC-AWS-ONLY-CREDS-001` #1065 / `DEC-TOKEN-BROKER-AWS-001` #1064) `resolve_token_store()` returns the read-only `ParameterStoreTokenStore` as the SOLE token source — so `build_live_client`/`build_live_pool` wire `token_cache_store = ParameterStoreTokenStore.store` for EVERY production pull. But `SdkRefresher.reauth` (`brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py`) is a FORCED LOCAL MINT (`_mint_and_cache_sdks` → `get_access_token` → `self._token_cache_store(...)`), and on the read-only store `store()` raises `TokenBrokerReadOnlyError` (`token_store_aws.py:101-118`, fail-loud by design — BruteX must never fork the shared token). So when the daily token rotated (~06:00-IST) or died mid-run, a long-running read-only BruteX process tried to re-mint, hit the fail-loud store, and HALTED — needing a manual restart to pick up the Lambda's fresh token on the next cold-start (the exact behaviour the pre-fix permutation test `TestForcedReauthAlsoBlocked` documented). In the shared model the Lambda is the SOLE minter; a read-only consumer must instead RE-READ the freshly-minted token from SSM. **WHAT SHIPPED (adapter-only; the LOCAL-mint reauth path is byte-unchanged — the read-only re-read is OPT-IN, wired ONLY when the resolved store reports `readonly`):** (1) NEW retryable error `GrowwTokenStillStaleError(GrowwAuthError)` in `errors.py` — added to `is_retryable` (the SECOND retryable auth-family error alongside `GrowwTokenIssuanceThrottled`), NOT `is_rate_limit`; a `GrowwAuthError` subclass so every `except GrowwAuthError` site + `is_auth_failure` keep matching it. (2) `SdkRefresher` gains an OPTIONAL `readonly_reread` hook + tracks the live token in `_current_token`. When `readonly_reread` is wired, `reauth` — under the SAME single-flight generation lock + the SAME freeze-guard `run_with_deadline` deadline as the mint — calls `_reread_and_adopt_sdks(reread, pinned_token)` instead of minting: a re-read returning a NEW token rebuilds all `size` SDKs + bumps the generation + logs the visible `groww.token.reread` self-heal; a re-read returning the SAME dead token OR an SSM miss (the Lambda has not minted yet — e.g. reauth fired at 05:59 IST just before the ~06:05 mint) raises the RETRYABLE `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` so the window quarantines + re-pulls LATER — never looping the dead token, never a fail-loud restart (mirrors the `DEC-GROWW-REAUTH-DEADLINE-001` #910 transient pattern). A hung SSM read raises a retryable `GrowwTimeoutError` (freeze guard), lock released, no half-state. (3) NEW `readonly` capability on the `TokenStore` Protocol — `ParameterStoreTokenStore.readonly = True`, so `live.py::_resolve_token_cache_hooks` returns `(load, store, readonly_reread=store.load if store.readonly else None)` and `build_live_client`/`build_live_pool` thread it into the refresher (a non-read-only backend / an explicit-hook path leaves it `None` → the byte-identical local-mint reauth). (4) `client.py::_call`'s reauth branch benefits with NO code change — a `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` raised out of `refresher.reauth(...)` propagates OUT of `_call` exactly like the throttle (NOT re-entered into the reauth branch, so no infinite recursion), and `is_retryable` is True so the orchestrator's layer-3 re-queue re-pulls the window (`GrowwTokenStillStaleError` is deliberately NOT in `run_ingest._GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` — it is a per-window transient, not a pull-wide halt). **MAJOR-1 CONCURRENCY FIX (hostile-review fold):** the fresh token was originally recorded on the freeze-guard DAEMON thread (in `_build_sdks`), so a HUNG re-read's abandoned daemon could LATER write `_current_token` even though the caller had already raised `GrowwTimeoutError` + released the lock — poisoning the NEW-vs-SAME comparison so the NEXT reauth wrongly raised `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` and REFUSED to adopt a genuinely-fresh token (defeating the self-heal in the exact hung-socket race this feature targets). FIXED to mirror the proven no-half-state contract of `DEC-GROWW-REAUTH-DEADLINE-001` (#910): `_build_sdks` is now a PURE builder (no shared-state write); the reference token is PINNED under the lock at `reauth` entry and passed into `_reread_and_adopt_sdks(reread, pinned_token)` (compare against the pinned value, NEVER the live field read on the daemon thread); and `_mint_and_cache_sdks` / `_reread_and_adopt_sdks` return `(sdks, token)` so `_current_token` is published on the CALLER thread beside `_sdks`/`_generation` ONLY after a clean `run_with_deadline` return — an abandoned daemon can NEVER reach `_current_token`. Regression-pinned by `test_abandoned_hung_reread_daemon_does_not_poison_next_reread` (fails-before / passes-after, PROVEN by reintroducing the daemon-write). An independent re-review returned SHIP (no BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR — the race is genuinely closed, no new race, coverage honest 100%, rebase clean). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the read-only re-read cannot conjure a token the Lambda has not minted yet — a persistently-stale broker surfaces the retryable stall every reauth, bounded by the client's `max_reauths` budget then re-pulled on a later pass (never an infinite loop), so the guarantee is "self-heals a NORMAL rotation with no restart + gracefully defers a not-yet-minted token", NOT "works with no Lambda"; the abandoned daemon of a hung SSM read runs to completion but its result is discarded (same envelope as the mint freeze guard). **Before → After:** BEFORE — a read-only process on token rotation tries to re-mint → `TokenBrokerReadOnlyError` fail-loud → pull halts → manual restart. AFTER — it re-reads the Lambda-minted token from SSM → adopts it (or defers retryably if not yet minted) → self-heals, no restart. **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after):** NEW `TestReadOnlyReauthReRead` (10, `test_groww_reauth.py`) — reauth re-reads + adopts a NEW Lambda token / never mints locally / same-stale-token → retryable-not-crash / SSM-miss → retryable / 16-thread `Barrier` single-flight (EXACTLY one SSM re-read per generation) / reauth-cap still bounds / hung-re-read → retryable-timeout + lock-released / ABANDONED hung-read daemon does NOT poison the next re-read (MAJOR-1) / size-K pool re-reads all leaves once / `readonly_reread=None` keeps local-mint (regression); NEW `TestReadOnlyReauthSelfHeals` (2, `test_token_broker_permutations.py`) — end-to-end through the REAL `ParameterStoreTokenStore` + `FakeAwsClient`; NEW `test_readonly_reauth_still_stale_propagates_retryable_no_recursion` (`test_groww_client.py`); NEW `test_token_still_stale_is_retryable_auth_subclass` + `is_retryable`/`is_auth_failure` cases (`test_groww_errors.py`); NEW `test_readonly_property_is_true` (`test_token_store_aws.py`); the pre-fix `TestForcedReauthAlsoBlocked` renamed `TestForcedReauthWithoutReReadHookStillFailsLoud`. **Verification (fresh 3.12 venv, 2026-07-01):** all SIX touched source files — `reauth.py`, `live.py`, `token_store.py`, `token_store_aws.py`, `errors.py`, `client.py` — at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** over the eight touched suites (207 passed); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `bandit -r brutex -l` exit 0 (the `_current_token = ""` empty-sentinel init carries a targeted `# nosec B105` — bandit's hardcoded-password name-heuristic false-positive on the token-named var, matching `stage3_wire.py`/`lockbox.py`); `pyright` **0 errors** on all touched files (the few `reportPrivateUsage` warnings are PRE-EXISTING on untouched imports); `mypy --strict` on the touched source is clean EXCEPT the PRE-EXISTING `growwapi`-stub `auth.py`/`reauth.py:_real_sdk_factory` env artifacts (identical before/after — reproduced by `git stash` on the pristine baseline, an environment-only `import-untyped`); `validate_ledger_numbering.py` + `validate_dec_ids.py` exit 0. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/reauth.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/live.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/token_store.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/token_store_aws.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/client.py` (docstring only), `tests/unit/test_groww_reauth.py`, `tests/unit/test_token_broker_permutations.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_client.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_token_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_token_store_aws.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_live.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_live_token_backend.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-BROKER-READONLY-REAUTH-REREAD-001. (Ledger: #1072 = the next free unique number after re-syncing onto current `origin/main` (whose max real entry header advanced to #1069 `DEC-MINTER-PURE-PYTHON-001` after the #1027 merge); #1070/#1071 are reserved by the in-flight sibling PR #1026, so this takes #1072 to stay distinct — a numbering gap is allowed, the validator enforces only (number,suffix) uniqueness; the DEC-ID is the stable handle — re-checked immediately before push.
