## DEC-MULTICORE-SWEEP-PHASE1-001 (2026-07-01)

1080. **DEC-MULTICORE-SWEEP-PHASE1-001 — the FIRST safe, tested slice of MULTI-CORE brute-force grid-sweep parallelism, behind a DEFAULT-OFF worker-count flag (`BRUTEX_SWEEP_WORKERS`, default 1 = the EXISTING sequential path byte-for-byte): a `ProcessPoolExecutor` of `workers-1` EVAL workers running the UNCHANGED per-tuple body, drained by a SINGLE serializing writer-actor that applies both hash-chained audit chains, the contiguous-clean-prefix checkpoint, and the coarse `SweepCache` in canonical enumeration order via a reorder min-heap** (2026-07-01; ENGINE SCOPE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Rust touched). **WHY (the audit's #1 lever):** a full production sweep is ~33 billion trials at a pure-Python per-bar `build_bar_bits` + `simulate_trades` floor; the sequential `run_supervised_grid` uses ONE core, so a compute-heavy grid leaves the M4 Pro's other cores idle. **THE GIL (honest — Golden Rule #10):** the dominant per-tuple cost is CPU-bound pure Python, so a `ThreadPoolExecutor` would serialise on the GIL (~1× on compute) — **processes are MANDATORY, threads are useless here** (stated in a code comment + this entry). **THE DESIGN (Design 3, mirrors `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`):** NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py` — a `ProcessPoolExecutor` of `workers-1` EVAL workers each running `run_one_tuple` (the UNCHANGED per-tuple body: `build_bar_bits` → `simulate_trades` → `rank_combos` → per-tuple Parquet + trial-stats sidecar + completion sentinel) with a `BufferedAuditCollector` (a worker CANNOT compute a chain-correct `entry_hash` — it has no global `seq`/`prev_hash` — so it BUFFERS the `SWEEP_*` audit lines as plain data) and a `_NoDedup` (which RAISES if consulted — the digest path structurally never consults dedup). The parent (THIS thread) is the single WRITER-ACTOR: it enumerates `iter_sweep_tuples(grid)` in canonical order, gates resume/cache in the PARENT (never a worker), dispatches `(index, tuple, bars)` (bars are already in parent memory — no un-picklable `bars_for`/`store_for` closure crosses the boundary; workers rebuild `store_for` from `(root, grid)` via `make_store_for`), drains results through a reorder MIN-HEAP keyed on the enumeration `index`, and applies ALL ordered state (both audit chains, the checkpoint, `SweepCache.record`, progress) in canonical enumeration order — so the per-tuple Parquet tree is BYTE-IDENTICAL to a sequential run, both audit chains are CONTENT-IDENTICAL MODULO TIMESTAMPS (the supervisor `SUPERVISOR_START` payload additionally carries a `workers` key; `ts_utc` participates in each entry's chain hash, so the chains are NOT literally byte-for-byte across two runs) AND independently verify, and the checkpoint state is identical — regardless of worker interleaving (the golden test is named `..._modulo_ts` to match this honest claim). **SCOPE (Golden Rule #3) — DIGEST PATH ONLY:** the parallel path is sound only on the PRODUCTION digest path where `run_persisted_sweep` bypasses dedup (`bypass_dedup = trial_stats_digest is not None`, `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py:909` — VERIFIED; the completion sentinel `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py:1048-1062` is the sole redo authority, so which worker runs which tuple is irrelevant to the file set). `run_one_tuple` ALWAYS supplies a digest (`brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py:838` — VERIFIED), so the production `run_supervised_grid`/`run_parallel_grid` path IS always the digest path; `workers>1` on the LEGACY no-digest path (`run_sweep_grid`, where a worker without the shared dedup would rank an unfiltered survivor set → bit-divergent Parquet) is HARD-REFUSED via `refuse_parallel_on_legacy_path`. **CORRECTNESS INVARIANTS:** (1) DETERMINISM PINS — every worker forces `OMP_NUM_THREADS`/`RAYON_NUM_THREADS`/`POLARS_MAX_THREADS` to `1` (a nested-BLAS/rayon thread count would BOTH oversubscribe AND risk an order-DEPENDENT float reduction → non-determinism); proven by the sequential-vs-parallel golden. (2) CONTIGUOUS-CLEAN-PREFIX CHECKPOINT — the parent advances `checkpoint.record(i)` only over the applied `0..i-1` prefix and FREEZES at the first failure (the `had_failure` latch re-implemented under out-of-order completion), so a failed tuple is NEVER permanently skipped (the sweep_heal C5 lesson); post-failure successes still `SweepCache.record` so a resume short-circuits them via the cache tier, not the frozen checkpoint. (3) SPAWN, not FORK — the pool uses `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` because the parent holds the watchdog daemon thread + durable-writer/logging locks, and a fork-after-threads inherits those locks in an arbitrary state → a classic child deadlock (this was OBSERVED and fixed; the golden test deadlocks under fork). (4) NO DEADLOCK + BOUNDED MEMORY UNDER HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCKING — dispatch is gated on BOTH a bounded in-flight FUTURES window (`~2×pool_size`) AND a reorder-heap cap (`~2×pool_size`, `_HEAP_CAP_MULTIPLIER`): when a legitimately-slow HEAD tuple blocks the apply prefix while its siblings complete, their `_Outcome` objects (each a `SweepRunSummary` + buffered audit) would otherwise pile into the heap — O(T − next_apply), unbounded on a multi-million-tuple sweep. Coupling DISPATCH to APPLY-progress (no new tuple dispatched while the heap is at cap) keeps the heap GENUINELY O(pool_size) (the honest tradeoff: a blocked head throttles throughput — bounded memory > max throughput; the heap can transiently overshoot the cap by the futures already in flight, so the ceiling is `pool_size·(_HEAP_CAP_MULTIPLIER + _INFLIGHT_MULTIPLIER)`, still O(pool_size)); `next_apply` is always already in the heap or `pending` (dispatch is strictly in enumeration order and never skips), so pausing on a full heap can NEVER deadlock. A stall watchdog RAISES `SweepStallError` (unlike `fetch_pipeline`, which only WARNs) if NO future COMPLETES within `stall_seconds` while work is in flight — the clock measures time-since-last-COMPLETION (reset on any future resolving, not only on an APPLY), so a slow-but-progressing head with completing siblings never SPURIOUSLY aborts; only a genuine no-completion hang does — a wedged worker's future never resolves, so this is the guarantee the sweep can never hang forever. (5) WORKER-OOM / crash → the broken future propagates → the pool tears down cleanly + a `SUPERVISOR_ABORT` line is written + the error re-raises (a GLOBAL stop, not a per-tuple skip). **THE SEAMS (widenings only — the sequential path is byte-unchanged):** `AuditSink` Protocol + `BufferedAuditCollector`/`BufferedAuditRecord` in `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` (`AuditWriter`/`SweepAuditWriter` satisfy it structurally); `DedupSink` Protocol + public `direction_label` in `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`; public `tuple_label`/`tuple_cache_params`/`SUPERVISOR_ACTION_*` re-exports in `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py` (ONE source of truth, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — the parallel driver emits the byte-identical supervisor chain without re-defining the labels); `run_persisted_sweep`/`run_one_tuple`/`run_sweep_grid` `audit`/`dedup` annotations WIDENED to the Protocols (a pure widening, `ComboDedup`/`AuditWriter` still satisfy them). **CLI wiring:** `cmd_sweep_all` resolves `resolve_sweep_workers()` and dispatches `run_parallel_grid` ONLY when `workers>1`, else `run_supervised_grid` UNCHANGED (the DEFAULT-OFF path; `cmd_sweep_all` is `# pragma: no cover` — the driver itself is 100% tested). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** on the CLAUDE.md §8 reference hardware — Apple M4 Pro, 14-core (10P+4E), 48 GB RAM, 10 usable cores — the realistic ceiling on a compute-heavy grid is **~6–8×, NOT 10×** (the single writer-actor's per-tuple `fsync`, the reorder overhead, and inter-process result marshalling eat ~20–40%); a grid with fewer tuples than cores, or one dominated by a single huge-`N_bars` instrument, sees far less — **no number of cores speeds up ONE tuple's latency** (its `simulate_trades` is a pure-Python per-bar walk); parallelism is strictly ACROSS independent tuples. The `~6–8×` is a PROJECTION pending a `pytest-benchmark` core-scaling run (the actual Amdahl parallelizable share is UNVERIFIED), NOT a guarantee; **no "millions in minutes."** **DEFERRED to follow-up PRs (explicitly NOT shipped here):** block-partition kernel locality (each worker rebuilds its resident kernel per distinct `(instrument, tf, proximity, prior_n, fib_anchor)` — contiguous block dispatch to preserve the DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 reuse win is future work); a persistent/resident cross-pool worker kernel; sharding the single audit-actor past ~64 cores (its `fsync` throughput is the far-machine Amdahl ceiling); a `pytest-benchmark` core-scaling + RSS-vs-48GB memory bench; and RAISING the default worker count above 1 (an operator decision behind an ADR — this slice ships default 1, byte-identical). **TESTS (the headline is the whole point):** NEW `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_parallel.py` (46 tests) — the HEADLINE golden `TestSequentialEqualsParallelGolden` runs a fixed grid BOTH sequential (`workers=1` via `run_supervised_grid`) AND parallel (`workers=4` via `run_parallel_grid`) and asserts every per-tuple Parquet + sidecar + sentinel is BYTE-IDENTICAL (SHA-256 tree equal), the ingest audit chain is identical modulo timestamps AND verifies, and the checkpoint state is identical (+ stable across repeated parallel runs at `workers=3` and `workers=4`); plus crash-mid-parallel resume (delete a tuple's outputs → a resume RE-runs it byte-identically — redo-not-skip, Golden Rule #7), failed-tuple contiguous-prefix checkpoint freeze (+ the post-failure cache-record-not-checkpoint branches), `workers>1`-on-legacy-path hard-refuse, the `workers<2` guard, the stall watchdog raising `SweepStallError`, worker-crash → global stop, bounded in-flight back-pressure, the `BufferedAuditCollector` seam, `_worker_init`'s determinism pins, `_run_tuple_in_worker` (success/no-bars/`SweepComboError`→failed marker), and the DEFAULT-OFF proof (`resolve_sweep_workers({}) == 1`). TWO NEW head-of-line-blocking regression tests (from the hostile review): `TestHeadOfLineHeapBound` proves the reorder heap stays `≤ heap_cap + max_inflight` (a small constant multiple of pool_size, FAR below a 40-tuple grid) while index 0 is blocked and many siblings complete — it FAILS on the un-capped code (heap grows to 39 = O(T)); `TestHeadOfLineStallClock` proves a slow-but-progressing head with completing siblings does NOT raise `SweepStallError` (it FAILS on the reset-only-on-apply code with a spurious stall) AND that a genuine full hang (nothing ever completes) STILL aborts within the deadline (the liveness guarantee preserved). The `BufferedAuditCollector`/`BufferedAuditRecord`/`AuditSink` seam is ALSO tested directly in `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_audit.py` (`TestBufferedAuditCollector`, 7 tests) so the strict per-module `--cov=brutex.orchestrator.audit` gate measures the collector at 100% (its lines live in `audit.py`, which that gate scopes) — closing the CI coverage gap that failed on the pre-review head (audit.py 664/681-687/692 uncovered because those tests only lived in `test_engine_sweep_parallel.py`). **VERIFICATION (fresh 3.12 venv, verified 2026-07-01 post-hostile-review):** `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py` at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (255 stmts / 48 branch, 0 missing — grown from 247 by the head-of-line heap-cap gate + completion-based stall reset); the WHOLE `brutex.engine` package at **100.00% line + branch** the way CI runs it (`pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` → TOTAL 4605/0 stmts, 1224/0 branch, 1348 passed) AND the WHOLE `brutex.orchestrator.audit` gate at **100.00%** (`--cov=brutex.orchestrator.audit … test_orchestrator_audit.py test_audit_torn_tail.py` → 245/0, 54/0, 177 passed — the CI-flagged gap CLOSED); the other touched modules 100% over their suites — `sweep_run.py` (260/74), `sweep_supervisor.py` (184/26), `sweep_orchestrator.py` (223/68); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all touched files; `mypy --strict` clean on all touched files (the only remaining package-wide errors are the PRE-EXISTING `growwapi`/`cma`-stub artifacts in the untouched `auth.py`/`reauth.py`/`stage3_refine.py`, identical before/after); `pyright` **0 errors, NO NEW warnings** on all touched files (2 PRE-EXISTING `reportPrivateUsage` warnings remain on `sweep_supervisor.py:107` `_direction_label` + `:837` `_atomic_write`, both untouched by this PR). CodeQL/docstring housekeeping folded: the redundant `...` Ellipsis bodies of the two `-> object` Protocol stubs (`AuditSink.append`, `AuditWriterLike.append`) were DELETED (docstring-only, pyright-clean); the two typed-return `DedupSink` stubs keep `docstring + ...` (pyright MANDATES a stub body for a non-`object` return — matching the codebase's established `AuditAppend` pattern); `_Outcome` gained `@functools.total_ordering` (complete ordering, heap semantics unchanged — the heap only consults `__lt__`); the SUPERVISOR_ACTION_* + `tuple_label`/`tuple_cache_params` re-exports were added to `sweep_supervisor.__all__`; the dead `os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS","1")` was removed; and `_NoDedup.seen`/`mark_many` gained docstrings + shed their dishonest `# pragma: no cover` (they ARE reached by the legacy-path guard test — closing the interrogate 100% docstring gate). The existing sweep/audit suites stay green (no regression from the Protocol widenings). **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py` (NEW), `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_parallel.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_audit.py` (the `BufferedAuditCollector` per-module-gate tests), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-MULTICORE-SWEEP-PHASE1-001. **Builds on** DEC-SWEEP-WIRE-GA-001 (the sequential `run_supervised_grid` this mirrors), DEC-MARK-MANY-SENTINEL-001 (the completion sentinel = the sole redo authority the digest-path scope rests on), DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 (#951/#998 — the `fetch_pipeline` producer/consumer + stall-watchdog template), and DEC-SWEEP-RESIDENT-KERNEL-001 (the kernel-locality win block-partition dispatch will preserve in a follow-up). 1074. **DEC-MINTER-DEPLOY-BASH32-SAFE-001 — `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh` expands the `EXTRA_ARGS` array with the empty-safe `"${EXTRA_ARGS[@]+\"${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}\"}"` idiom at BOTH sites (the `ALERT_EMAIL` scan loop + the final `terraform apply`), so a no-extra-args deploy no longer aborts under `set -euo pipefail` on macOS system bash 3.2 (the reference host, CLAUDE.md §8)** (2026-07-01; DEPLOY-SCRIPT ONLY — `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh` + `tests/deploy/test_build_lambda_package.py`; NO `brutex/` package code touched; NO Rust touched; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE BUG (hostile-review MINOR of DEC-MINTER-PURE-PYTHON-001 #1069):** under `set -u` (deploy.sh line 31), bash 3.2 — the macOS system `/bin/bash` — treats a bare `"${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}"` on an EMPTY array as an unbound-variable error and aborts `./deploy.sh` when the operator passes no extra `-var` args (bash 4.4+ silently tolerates it, which is why it slipped through). **THE FIX:** the alternate-value idiom expands to NOTHING on an empty array and to the quoted elements otherwise, on bash 3.2 AND 4.4+ — verified in-sandbox (empty→0 iterations, no error; non-empty→iterates). **VERIFICATION:** a NEW `test_deploy_expands_extra_args_safely_under_set_u` content-assertion (both sites use the safe idiom; the bare unsafe forms are gone) — fails-before / passes-after; ruff + ruff-format clean; the shellcheck gate runs in CI. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the bash-3.2-specific abort cannot be reproduced on this Linux bash 5.x host — the idiom is the documented-correct portable fix, proven valid here and pinned by the static test; CI shellcheck covers the shell lint. **Decision ID:** DEC-MINTER-DEPLOY-BASH32-SAFE-001.
1075. **DEC-DEPLOY-EMPTY-ARGS-FIX-001 — `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh` no longer DIES on macOS's default bash 3.2 when run with no extra args (every empty-array expansion under `set -euo pipefail` is guarded with the portable `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` idiom, so `terraform apply` is actually reached); PLUS the DOWNSTREAM one-time-setup failures the operator then hit are closed so the flow is `git pull → terraform apply → invoke` with NO file edits: `reserved_concurrent_executions` becomes a VARIABLE defaulting to `-1` (unreserved — applies on a default-quota-10 account), the minter is granted SSM-scoped `kms:Decrypt` on the default `alias/aws/ssm` key (var `allow_ssm_default_key_decrypt=true`) so existing creds need NO re-put, and the required custom KMS key is pre-flighted in `deploy.sh` + documented for fresh deploys (the key stays a `data` source, never a terraform resource)** (2026-07-01; DEPLOY-SCRIPT + TERRAFORM-VAR + DOCS + TEST — `deploy/aws_token_minter/{deploy.sh,main.tf,variables.tf}` + `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md` + `tests/deploy/test_deploy_empty_args_regression.py` (the STANDARDS §1 row 10 bug-fix regression test) + this ledger entry; NO `brutex/` package code touched — `git status --short brutex/` empty; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty; the KMS key stays a `data` source per ADR-0014 §5, see the DESIGN CALL; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **FIX 1 — THE EMPTY-ARGS BUG (operator-reported, verbatim `./deploy.sh: line 77: EXTRA_ARGS[@]: unbound variable`):** `deploy.sh` sets `set -euo pipefail` (nounset); on macOS's default bash 3.2, expanding an EMPTY array as `"${arr[@]}"` is treated as an UNBOUND VARIABLE and aborts (a documented bash 3.2 behavior fixed in bash 4.4), so with no extra args the script died right before `terraform apply`. The old script expanded `EXTRA_ARGS` bare at TWO sites (the `for arg in "${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}"` scan ~line 55 AND `terraform apply "${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}"` ~line 77). CI never caught it because CI (and this sandbox) runs bash 5.x where an empty-array `"${arr[@]}"` is harmless. FIX (portable, bash-3.2 AND 4+): every expansion now uses the alternate-value guard `${EXTRA_ARGS[@]+"${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}"}` — `${var+word}` yields `word` only when the array is SET and NOTHING when unset/empty, so the nested `"${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}"` is expanded only when the array has elements (never tripping nounset), and when it does the quoted `[@]` preserves each element verbatim (incl. a value with spaces like the `cron(35 0 * * ? *)` `-var`); `EXTRA_ARGS` is initialised `EXTRA_ARGS=()` and filled only when `"$#" -gt 0` (`"$@"`/`"$#"` are POSIX-special-cased safe with zero args under nounset — only ARRAY `[@]` is the trap). `build_lambda_package.sh` was CHECKED and is CLEAN (no array expansion — unchanged). VERIFIED (sandbox, stubbed terraform/aws/build): no-args now reaches `terraform apply` with `arg-count=0`; with-args preserves all incl. the space-containing `-var`; `ALERT_EMAIL` env folds + de-dups; `shellcheck` + `bash -n` CLEAN on both scripts. **FIX 2 — RESERVED CONCURRENCY (operator's 3rd apply error: `InvalidParameterValueException: Specified ReservedConcurrentExecutions … decreases account's UnreservedConcurrentExecution below its minimum value of [10]`):** the default AWS account has a total Lambda concurrency of 10, so `reserved_concurrent_executions = 1` (hard-coded in `main.tf`) is REJECTED because reserving any leaves < 10 unreserved. FIX: a NEW `variable "lambda_reserved_concurrency"` (`variables.tf`) defaulting to `-1` (AWS's sentinel for UNRESERVED — the provider omits the setting), wired into `aws_lambda_function.minter` (`reserved_concurrent_executions = var.lambda_reserved_concurrency`), so a fresh default-quota account applies cleanly with NO reservation. HONEST SAFETY: `-1` drops the #1017 single-writer HARDENING (`reserved_concurrent_executions = 1`), but the minter is ALREADY the SOLE token writer, fires as a DAILY single-shot cron (~06:05 IST) + rare on-demand invoke, and its SSM write is idempotent last-writer-wins (`PutParameter Overwrite=True`) — a concurrent double-invoke is vanishingly unlikely and, if it happened, both mints write a valid fresh token — so `-1` is safe for the token-minter's access pattern. An operator WITH concurrency headroom (a raised account limit) can set `-var 'lambda_reserved_concurrency=1'` to restore the strict single-writer serialization; documented in the runbook + the variable description. **FIX 3 — KMS KEY MUST PRE-EXIST (operator's 2nd apply error `Error: reading KMS Key (alias/tickvault-groww): couldn't find resource` at `main.tf:27`):** the custom KMS key `alias/tickvault-groww` is a Terraform `data` source (referenced, never created), and the stack ENCRYPTS the `access-token` param it creates under it (`key_id = data.aws_kms_key.groww.arn`, `main.tf:73`), so the key must pre-exist regardless of where the two creds live. FIX (docs + pre-flight only — the key STAYS a `data` source, see the DESIGN CALL): `deploy.sh` gains a best-effort PRE-FLIGHT that probes `aws kms describe-key` (only when the `aws` CLI is present; honors `-var 'kms_key_alias=…'`/`-var 'region=…'`; skips silently otherwise so terraform stays authoritative) and, on a missing key, prints the EXACT `aws kms create-key`+`create-alias` commands then exits 1 BEFORE build/apply so the operator never hits the opaque mid-plan error; runbook §1d documents the same create step. **FIX 4 — CRED DECRYPT WITHOUT A RE-PUT (the operator's plan output CONFIRMED the decrypt-scope concern):** the minter Lambda IAM policy's `DecryptEncryptWithGrowwKey` statement (`main.tf`) scopes `kms:Decrypt`/`Encrypt`/`GenerateDataKey` to `[local.kms_key_arn]` = `data.aws_kms_key.groww.arn` = ONLY the custom key (the operator's plan showed `arn:aws:kms:…:key/1c8ec712-…`); the two reader roles Decrypt the SAME single key; `access_token` is encrypted under it too. CONSEQUENCE: if api-key/totp-secret were seeded earlier under the DEFAULT `alias/aws/ssm` key (very likely — the custom key did not exist yet), the least-privilege minter role could NOT decrypt them → the mint would fail with `KMSAccessDeniedException`. To AVOID forcing the operator to re-put the two creds (the "zero manual file edits / fewest steps" goal), the stack now ALSO grants the minter `kms:Decrypt` on the AWS-managed `alias/aws/ssm` key — TIGHTLY scoped with a `Condition StringEquals { kms:ViaService = ssm.<region>.amazonaws.com }` so the key is usable ONLY through Systems Manager, never via a direct KMS call. Mechanism: a NEW bool var `allow_ssm_default_key_decrypt` (default `true`) gates a `data "aws_kms_alias" "ssm"` (resolves `alias/aws/ssm` via `.target_key_arn` — attribute confirmed against the hashicorp/aws provider docs, Golden Rule #1) + a `dynamic "statement"` (`DecryptCredsViaSsmDefaultKey`) added to the minter policy; the UNCONDITIONAL custom-key statement stays for the token write. **LEAST-PRIVILEGE JUSTIFICATION (sourced, not from memory):** the `aws/ssm` key's own AWS-managed key policy ALREADY delegates decrypt to any in-account IAM principal *through SSM* via the `kms:CallerAccount` + `kms:ViaService` pattern ([AWS default key policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policy-default.html); [SSM SecureString KMS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/secure-string-parameter-kms-encryption.html)), so this IAM statement grants the minter NOTHING beyond what the account can already do through SSM — it merely scopes the minter to that exact path (Decrypt-only, SSM-only). Set `-var 'allow_ssm_default_key_decrypt=false'` to limit the minter to the one custom key (then a re-put IS required — documented). **DESIGN CALL — keep the KMS key a `data` source (do NOT make it a terraform resource):** ADR-0014 records an EXPLICIT operator directive (`docs/adr/0014-centralized-token-minter.md:16-19` — "Groww creds ALREADY EXIST … KMS-encrypted — do NOT create them") and ADR §5 (`:239-240`) states the key + the two creds are "never created or managed by this stack." Making terraform own the key (`aws_kms_key`+`aws_kms_alias`) would (a) contradict a locked operator directive + need a NEW ADR (CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #2); (b) put the key that encrypts the operator's REAL Groww creds into this stack's lifecycle, so `terraform destroy` (documented in `aws-token-minter.md` §8) would DELETE it — a data-loss footgun the ADR deliberately avoided; AND (c) the operator ALREADY created `alias/tickvault-groww` manually, so an `aws_kms_alias` RESOURCE would COLLIDE with the existing alias and force a `terraform import` = MORE manual work — the opposite of the goal. So the key stays a `data` source; the fresh-deploy create step is documented + pre-flighted. **FINAL ONE-TIME-SETUP SEQUENCE (fewest operator steps; region ap-south-1, stack defaults):** (1) create the custom key IF absent — `aws kms create-key --region ap-south-1 --description 'Groww token-minter SecureString key (tickvault)' --query KeyMetadata.KeyId --output text` then `aws kms create-alias --region ap-south-1 --alias-name alias/tickvault-groww --target-key-id <KeyId>` (the operator already did this; `deploy.sh` pre-flights it for fresh deploys); (2) ensure the two creds exist as SecureStrings under ANY key — the default `alias/aws/ssm` is FINE (NO re-put needed, thanks to FIX 4): `aws ssm put-parameter --region ap-south-1 --type SecureString --name /tickvault/prod/groww/api-key --value '<API_KEY>'` (+ totp-secret) — omit `--key-id` to use the default key, or the operator's existing creds already satisfy this; (3) `git pull && cd deploy/aws_token_minter && ./deploy.sh` (→ build → init → `terraform apply`; NO `-var` needed for creds/concurrency — creds resolve via the SSM-path `data` sources at the tfvars defaults, `lambda_reserved_concurrency=-1` and `allow_ssm_default_key_decrypt=true` are the defaults; the only optional `-var` is `alert_email`); (4) `aws lambda invoke --region ap-south-1 --function-name "$(terraform output -raw minter_lambda_name)" /dev/stdout` for the first mint. For the operator's ALREADY-set-up account, steps (1)+(2) are DONE, so after this PR merges the sequence is exactly `git pull → terraform apply (via ./deploy.sh) → aws lambda invoke` with NO file edits and NO cred re-put. **HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10):** the pre-flight is BEST-EFFORT (runs only when the `aws` CLI is on PATH; probes describe-key, not the creds' actual key-id); `allow_ssm_default_key_decrypt=true` grants Decrypt on the default SSM key SSM-scoped — an operator wanting the minter limited to the one custom key opts OUT (`=false`) + re-puts; `-1` reserved concurrency is the safe universal default (NOT the strict single-writer hardening — opt into `=1` with headroom); the ViaService-scoped grant relies on the documented `aws/ssm` key-policy delegation (sourced above), verified against AWS docs but NOT live-applied in this sandbox (no AWS access — `terraform fmt -check` CLEAN, full `terraform validate`/apply are operator steps, the registry provider download is proxy-blocked here); the deploy stays operator-run — nothing is applied by CI or this repo. **GATES:** `shellcheck deploy.sh` + `shellcheck build_lambda_package.sh` + `bash -n deploy.sh` CLEAN; `terraform fmt -check -diff` CLEAN on the module (no formatting drift); the `aws_kms_alias` `.target_key_arn` attribute + the `aws/ssm` key-policy delegation are cited to authoritative AWS/hashicorp docs (Golden Rule #1). **Files:** `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/main.tf`, `deploy/aws_token_minter/variables.tf`, `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md`, `tests/deploy/test_deploy_empty_args_regression.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DEPLOY-EMPTY-ARGS-FIX-001. 1078. **DEC-DEPLOY-REMOTE-STATE-001 — a REMOTE Terraform STATE BACKEND (S3 + DynamoDB state-lock) for the AWS Groww token-minter deploy, so `terraform apply` is FRESH-CLONE-REPEATABLE + IDEMPOTENT: run it from ANY fresh clone on ANY machine, any number of times, with NO "already exists" conflicts** (2026-07-01; DEPLOY/DOCS ONLY — `deploy/aws_token_minter/{backend.tf (NEW),deploy.sh}` + `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md` + this ledger entry; NO `brutex/` package code touched — `git status --short brutex/` empty; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE BUG (deploy-repeatability gap):** the token-minter Terraform (DEC-TOKEN-MINTER-CENTRAL-001 #1060, DEC-MINTER-PURE-PYTHON-001 #1069) used LOCAL state — a `terraform.tfstate` file on the operator's disk (gitignored via the `*.tfstate` rule in `deploy/aws_token_minter/.gitignore`). Local state is NOT portable: a FRESH CLONE on another machine has no state, so `terraform apply` there thinks NOTHING exists and tries to RE-CREATE the already-deployed Lambda / SSM `access-token` param / EventBridge rule / IAM roles → `EntityAlreadyExists` (IAM) / `ResourceInUse` (Lambda/SSM) conflicts. The deploy was therefore NOT fresh-clone-repeatable and NOT safely re-runnable from a second machine. **THE FIX (state lives in AWS, not on disk):** (1) NEW `deploy/aws_token_minter/backend.tf` — a `terraform { backend "s3" {} }` block that bakes ONLY the fixed `key = "tickvault/groww-token-minter/terraform.tfstate"` + `region = "ap-south-1"` + `encrypt = true`; the account-derived `bucket` + `dynamodb_table` names are supplied at init time via `-backend-config` (so the `.tf` never hardcodes an account id). (2) `deploy.sh` gains an IDEMPOTENT bootstrap BEFORE `terraform init` (the chicken-and-egg: the bucket + lock table must EXIST before Terraform can use them as a backend) — it resolves the account id via `aws sts get-caller-identity`, derives the globally-unique bucket name `tickvault-tfstate-<ACCOUNT_ID>`, then CHECK-THEN-CREATEs: an **S3 state bucket** guarded by `aws s3api head-bucket` (created only if absent; then hardened UNCONDITIONALLY with `put-bucket-versioning` Status=Enabled + `put-bucket-encryption` AES256 default SSE + `put-public-access-block` all-four-true — the put-* calls are idempotent so a re-run just re-asserts them; the `create-bucket` call handles the us-east-1-rejects-LocationConstraint special case even though the default region is ap-south-1) and a **DynamoDB lock table** `tickvault-tfstate-lock` (key `LockID` string, `PAY_PER_REQUEST`) guarded by `aws dynamodb describe-table` + a `wait table-exists` after a create; then `terraform init -input=false -reconfigure -backend-config=bucket/dynamodb_table/region` points Terraform at that remote backend, and `terraform apply` runs unchanged (still SHOWS the plan + requires a typed `yes`, NEVER `-auto-approve`). Re-runs are no-ops (both guards short-circuit). The `deploy.sh` step banners renumber 1/3→1/4 accordingly and it now also fail-fasts if the `aws` CLI is absent. **ONE-TIME MIGRATION (the operator already deployed with LOCAL state):** documented in the runbook — run ONCE, by hand, `terraform init -migrate-state -backend-config="bucket=tickvault-tfstate-<ACCOUNT_ID>" -backend-config="dynamodb_table=tickvault-tfstate-lock" -backend-config="region=ap-south-1"` and answer `yes` when Terraform offers to COPY the existing local `terraform.tfstate` up to S3. `deploy.sh` itself always runs a PLAIN `terraform init` (never `-migrate-state`), so it never silently moves state — the migration is a deliberate, confirm-`yes`, one-time operator step. After migration every fresh clone reads the remote state. **DOCS:** `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md` gains a NEW "§2b. Fresh clones + repeat deploys (remote state)" section — the fresh-clone flow (`git clone`/`git pull` → `cd deploy/aws_token_minter` → `./deploy.sh` bootstraps the bucket/table if missing → `terraform init` reads the SHARED remote state → `terraform apply` is a `0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy` no-op on an already-deployed stack), the one-time `-migrate-state` step, and an explicit Before/After (Before: local state → fresh clone loses it → re-create conflicts; After: S3 + DynamoDB lock → any clone/machine reads the same state → idempotent, no conflicts); the §2 numbered deploy list is updated 3-step → 4-step (build → bootstrap remote state → init → apply). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10 + #1):** DEPLOY-INFRASTRUCTURE + DOCS ONLY — nothing is deployed by CI or by this repo; the operator runs `./deploy.sh` against their OWN AWS account (this session has NO AWS access, no claim any bucket/table/state was actually created in a real account). The bootstrap is best-effort idempotent per the check-then-create guards; a genuinely broken AWS identity / permissions failure surfaces as the underlying `aws` CLI error (not silently swallowed). POSIX-shell (bash-3.2-safe: the `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` empty-array idiom under `set -u`); the `us-east-1` LocationConstraint branch is defensive (the default region is ap-south-1). **GATES:** `shellcheck deploy.sh` CLEAN; `backend.tf` written in canonical `terraform fmt` style (2-space indent, `=`-aligned block) — `terraform fmt -check` / `terraform validate` could NOT be RUN in this environment because `registry.terraform.io` is proxy-denied here (no provider download / no `terraform` binary available), stated honestly, NOT claimed green; `scan-banned-patterns` + no-hallucination clean on this body; `validate_ledger_numbering.py` (number,suffix) unique. **Files:** `deploy/aws_token_minter/backend.tf` (NEW), `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh`, `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DEPLOY-REMOTE-STATE-001. 1079. **DEC-DEFLAKE-HUNG-WRITE-TEST-001 — the shared hung-write isolation integration test `test_one_wedged_shard_does_not_freeze_a_healthy_shard` is DE-FLAKED at the ROOT: the healthy shard's success no longer RACES a tight wall-clock write-deadline under CI load, it is driven off an EXPLICIT completion Event, so the "Unit tests + coverage (100% gate)" job stops intermittently reddening every PR** (2026-07-01; TEST-ONLY — `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py` + this ledger entry; NO `brutex/` package code touched — `git status --short brutex/` empty; NO Rust touched — `git status --short rust/` empty; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / pacing / fetch-rate change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE FLAKE (root-caused against the real code):** the test (part of `TestHungWriteDoesNotBlockFetchLane`, the DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 #999 adversarial suite) runs two symbols on two consumer shards — the HUNG shard (`AAA`) blocks its write on `gate.wait(timeout=30.0)` so its write-deadline must fire + defer it; the HEALTHY shard (`BBB`) must write DURABLY. Both shared ONE env var `BRUTEX_GROWW_WRITE_DEADLINE_S` (prior widened 0.2 s → 0.5 s in #1038/#1031), which forced the healthy write into a TIGHT window `healthy_write_time < deadline < 30 s`. The healthy write runs INSIDE `append_with_deadline` → `run_with_deadline` (a daemon worker + `done.wait(deadline)`); under a contended runner (the wedged-write daemon thread + the full parallel suite — the operator's 13m26s CI run) the OS occasionally did NOT schedule the healthy write's worker within 0.5 s, so `done.wait(0.5)` timed out on a write that was merely SLOW-TO-SCHEDULE (not hung) → `WriteDeadlineExceeded` → the healthy partition was DEFERRED → `assert _spot_part(...).exists()` + `healthy_statuses == {"SUCCESS"}` FAILED. This was a TIMER race, never a real isolation failure. **THE FIX (deterministic — Option 1, remove the wall-clock race from the assertion; intent preserved, NO illusion):** (1) the healthy write signals a NEW `healthy_written = threading.Event()` the INSTANT its durable `append` RETURNS, and the test WAITS on that Event (`healthy_written.wait(timeout=15.0)`) BEFORE asserting the healthy shard — so the healthy-path success is observed by EXPLICIT synchronization, not by beating a timer against the assertion; (2) the deadline is raised to a GENEROUS 5.0 s — a fast in-memory Parquet write (~tens of ms) cannot miss a 5 s bound unless the machine cannot schedule ANY thread for 5 full seconds (a genuinely wedged box, not a merely busy runner), while 5.0 s ≪ 30 s keeps the HUNG shard's deadline firing + deferring deterministically; the deadline MECHANISM is STILL exercised (the hung shard trips `WriteDeadlineExceeded` → FAILED-deferred → `tail_transients >= 1`); (3) the drain-join is raised 4.0 s → 12.0 s (> 2 × the 5.0 s deadline) because the hung shard's TWO windows route to ONE consumer + deadline-fire SEQUENTIALLY (~5 s each = ~10 s), so BOTH hung windows are deterministically recorded FAILED before drain returns — no race — while staying ≪ the 30 s hung wait + the 20 s producer watchdog. **TEETH PRESERVED (proven, NOT weakened):** the test STILL FAILS if the isolation property is genuinely broken — a mutation that freezes the HEALTHY shard's write (simulating the pool failing to isolate it) makes `healthy_written.wait(15.0)` time out and the test fail with the exact assertion `"the healthy shard's write never completed — it was frozen by the wedged shard"` within 15 s (deterministic, never a hang), verified by an injected-fake regression harness. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this removes the healthy-shard FALSE-NEGATIVE only — it does NOT weaken what the test proves (a wedged shard is isolated + deferred + counted; the hung shard's assertions `hung_statuses == {"FAILED"}` + `tail_transients >= 1` are unchanged and now deterministic); the generous 5.0 s deadline is not a magic number chosen to "just pass" but a bound a completing in-memory write cannot miss short of a wedged kernel scheduler; `@pytest.mark.flaky` / `pytest-rerunfailures` were explicitly NOT used (they HIDE flakiness rather than remove it). **VERIFICATION (SANDBOX, Linux/x86_64/py3.12):** the target test PASSES 10/10 back-to-back (each ~11.1 s) AND 6/6 under a saturating CPU-stressor load (`nproc + 2` busy-loops — the exact scheduler-contention condition that caused the original flake), all stable; the whole file (19 tests) green in 30.5 s; the broken-isolation mutation FAILS the test at the healthy-write assertion (teeth intact). **COVERAGE (100% gate satisfied):** TEST-ONLY diff → `brutex/` package coverage is structurally unchanged (`[tool.coverage.run] source = ["brutex"]`, `fail_under = 100` — test files are not part of the gate); `brutex/adapters/groww/write_deadline.py` re-verified 100.00% line + branch (27/4, 0 missing) with the touched test + `test_groww_write_deadline.py`; the touched test file's only uncovered lines are the PRE-EXISTING defensive `except Exception` producer-crash safety nets (identical on `origin/main`, unchanged by this diff). **GATES:** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` CLEAN on the touched test file; `pyright` 0 errors (2 PRE-EXISTING `reportPrivateUsage` warnings on the deliberate `_shard_index`/`_series_shard_key` COMMON imports, unchanged); `mypy --strict brutex` (CI's scope) unaffected — the touched file is under `tests/`, which CI's `mypy --strict brutex` does not type-check, and the file's `type: ignore[override]` count is byte-identical to `origin/main` (13 = 13, none added/removed). **Before → After:** BEFORE — the healthy write races a 0.5 s deadline → flakes intermittently under CI load (`WriteDeadlineExceeded` on a slow-to-schedule but non-hung write → healthy partition deferred → `healthy_statuses == {"SUCCESS"}` fails). AFTER — deterministic: the healthy write signals an explicit completion Event the test waits on, under a 5.0 s deadline a completing write cannot miss; no wall-clock race, the hung shard's defer stays deterministic, the isolation teeth are intact. **Files:** `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DEFLAKE-HUNG-WRITE-TEST-001. 1091. **DEC-FETCH-SPILL-ISOLATION-001 — the async fetch pipeline's SPILL-file load is GUARDED (a load failure defers ONE window — never a silent consumer-thread death) + the on-disk spill directory is NAMESPACED PER PULL (`<lake>/.fetch-spill/pull-<pid>-<uuid>/`) so two concurrent pulls sharing one lake root can never delete each other's live spill files** (2026-07-02; fixes audit finding C-3 (MAJOR, confirmed by executed repro) of the Groww-pull guarantee audit). **ROOT CAUSE (file:line at the pre-fix HEAD `0a982935`):** (a) `fetch_pipeline.py:835` — the consumer's spill rehydration `tail.rehydrate(self._spill_area.load(spilled))` sat INSIDE the outer `try/finally` (no `except`) and BEFORE the inner `try/except Exception` that guards only `tail.process(tail)`, so a `FileNotFoundError` from `FetchSpillArea.load` (`fetch_spill.py:303` `handle.path.read_bytes()`) propagated out of `_process_one` through `_run_consumer`/`_drain_overflow` and KILLED the consumer thread SILENTLY — `_trip` never fired, `_mark_completed` never fired, `submit`'s back-pressure loop (exits only on `_stopped`/`_draining`) could wedge the PRODUCER forever on the dead shard's full queue, and `drain()` returned CLEAN (`_exc is None`); (b) `fetch_spill.py:103/246` — the spill dir was the FIXED, SHARED `<lake_root>/.fetch-spill` and `cleanup()` unlinked EVERY file in it, so a concurrent pull's drain (CLI `brutex fetch` + a dashboard pull share `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT`) deleted THIS pull's LIVE spill files — the exact trigger for (a). **FIX (two complementary halves, pipeline/spill only — NO engine/lake-schema/stored-bar/scope/vocab/rate change):** (1) GUARDED REHYDRATION — `_process_one` wraps the spill load in its own `try/except Exception` (KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit still propagate): a load failure logs a LOUD `fetch_pipeline.spill_load_failed` (error_type + shard_key), folds `fold_tail_transient()` (so `drain()`'s `fetch_pipeline.drained` totals surface the deferral count HONESTLY), `_mark_completed()`s (the watchdog progress clock advances), and RETURNS — the window's ledger row was never recorded so it stays UNSETTLED → re-fetched next pull (idempotent keep-first sink); the outer `finally` still discards the spill handle (byte budget released, discard is missing-file-idempotent); the consumer KEEPS RUNNING. (2) PER-PULL NAMESPACE — `FetchSpillArea.under_lake_root` builds a UNIQUE `pull-<pid>-<uuid12>` subdir per pull; `cleanup()` removes ONLY its own namespace dir (files, then `rmdir`), PLUS a conservative stale-straggler sweep of sibling entries older than `_STALE_SPILL_SECONDS` (24 h — a hard-killed pull's leftover dir, bounded by the 256 MiB spill cap, would otherwise accrete forever now that no other pull sweeps it), gated to run ONLY when the parent dir is literally `.fetch-spill` (a directly-constructed area never sweeps an arbitrary parent). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the deferral relies on the ledger-row-stays-unsettled re-pull (the SAME mechanism the #1038 corrupt-partition quarantine uses) — the deferred window is NOT re-attempted within the same pull; the per-series reconcile does not attribute the pipeline-level transient to a `(symbol, interval)` (the pipeline holds only the string shard key — pull-level totals + the drain log carry the honest count); the 24 h stale threshold is a heuristic far beyond every bounded pipeline deadline (fetch 45 s · write 90 s · drain join 60 s), and even a wrongly-swept LIVE file is now NON-FATAL by fix (1) — that one window defers + re-pulls, never lost data. **REGRESSION TESTS (fail-before/pass-after, VERIFIED by reverting the guard):** NEW `TestSpillLoadIsolation` (`tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_pipeline.py`, parametrized deleted+corrupt spill file) reproduces the EXACT audit scenario — a spilled window's file removed mid-pipeline — and proves: the pipeline COMPLETES, a post-failure window is still processed (consumer alive; against the unguarded code this times out — 2 failed + 2 errors observed on the revert run), `tail_transients == 1`, the `fetch_pipeline.spill_load_failed` WARNING fires, `drain()`'s `fetch_pipeline.drained` log carries `tail_transients=1` (the drain path surfaces the failure count honestly), the sabotaged window is never processed off fabricated bars, and the byte budget is released. NEW `TestPerPullIsolation` (`tests/unit/test_groww_fetch_spill.py`, 8 tests): two areas under one lake root never collide; one pull's `cleanup()` leaves the sibling's LIVE spill intact + loadable (the pre-fix flat dir deleted it); the stale sweep removes a 25 h-old straggler dir/empty dir/legacy flat file while keeping a fresh sibling; sweep failures are logged + swallowed; an unstatable (dangling-symlink) entry is skipped; no sweep outside a `.fetch-spill` parent; cleanup survives a missing parent; the own dir is never swept even if stale. Two integration assertions updated to the new layout (`spill_dir` removed at drain). **GATES:** `fetch_pipeline.py` 100.00% line+branch (287/76, 0 missing) + `fetch_spill.py` 100.00% line+branch (134/22, 0 missing); 140 spill/pipeline/wiring/async-separation tests GREEN; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` CLEAN on every touched file. 1083. **DEC-PULL-STALLED-REFIRE-001 — the `pull.stalled` CRITICAL alert now RE-FIRES on every stall episode instead of paging the operator AT MOST ONCE per process: `DwellProvider.__call__` surfaces the REAL value on recovery (predicate-False WITH a present value) so the SLA detector's BREACH→OK edge fires, instead of returning `None` which the detector skips — leaving the rule stuck in BREACH forever** (2026-07-01; `brutex/observability/pull_health.py` + `tests/unit/test_observability_pull_health.py` + this ledger entry ONLY — NO Rust touched (`git status --short rust/` empty); ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / pacing change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE DEFECT (adversarial-verification MAJOR, re-confirmed against current code by a dedicated agent):** the `pull.stalled` rule wraps its achieved-rps provider in a `DwellProvider` whose `predicate` (`rps < stalled_floor`) is IDENTICAL to the `SLARule`'s own breach predicate (`LESS_THAN stalled_floor`), so the only non-`None` value the provider could EVER return was a breaching one. On recovery (`rps >= floor`) the provider hit `if value is None or not self.predicate(value): return None`, and `SLADetector.check_once` does `if value is None: continue` WITHOUT touching rule state — so once `pull.stalled` transitioned OK→BREACH it could NEVER return to OK: `_on_recovery` never fired (recovery unlogged), and a later genuine stall gave `new_state == BREACH == prev_state` → no edge → `_on_breach` never fired again. Net: the CRITICAL `pull_degraded` Telegram page reached the operator AT MOST ONCE per process across ALL stall→recover→stall episodes — precisely the multi-episode overnight-pull pattern (429-storm / write-stall) where the operator most needs to be paged each time. 100% branch coverage did NOT catch it: the only fire→recover test (`test_achieved_below_allowed_fires_and_clears`) covers a NON-dwell rule (plain bidirectional provider), and no test exercised stall→recover→stall. **THE FIX (COMMON, minimal, Option A — ZERO change to `SLADetector`, honoring the module's stated "layered on top of the detector WITHOUT modifying it" design):** `DwellProvider.__call__` now distinguishes the two `None`-worthy cases — `value is None` (underlying value genuinely unavailable) STILL returns `None` (the detector's None-skip contract for every OTHER rule is preserved verbatim), but `not self.predicate(value)` with a PRESENT value now `return value` (resets the streak AND surfaces the real recovered reading) so the detector sees a non-breaching value and fires the BREACH→OK edge. The dwell asymmetry is deliberate + correct: a breach still requires K consecutive stalled samples (no premature CRITICAL on a transient dip), while recovery fires on the FIRST healthy sample (paging fast on recovery is harmless; paging NEVER on a re-stall is not). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** Option A was chosen over "reset detector state on `None` after a breach" (Option B) BECAUSE Option B would BREAK the None-skip contract — every other rule returns `None` to mean "no data this tick", and flipping them OK on a `None` would fabricate spurious recoveries; Option A touches only the one stateful provider. This fixes the alert-re-arming; it does NOT change WHAT counts as a stall (the floor + dwell are unchanged) nor add any new production wiring. **Tests (REAL, fails-before/passes-after):** `test_predicate_false_resets_streak` updated (a predicate-False real value now surfaces, streak-reset still proven by the following non-fire); NEW `test_recovery_surfaces_real_value_not_none` (stall→recover→stall at the provider level surfaces `0.0 → 5.0 → 0.0`, was `0.0 → None → …` before) + `test_none_still_returned_when_value_unavailable` (the None-skip contract preserved) + `test_stalled_refires_after_recovery` (END-TO-END through `PullHealthMonitor.observe`: stall→recover→stall pages `pull.stalled` EXACTLY TWICE — fails-before: once, because the state stuck at BREACH). **Verified 2026-07-01 on the project `.venv` (Python 3.12.3):** `brutex/observability/pull_health.py` **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (136 stmt / 30 branch, 0 missing) over `test_observability_pull_health.py` (25 passed); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on both files; `mypy --strict brutex/observability/pull_health.py` clean. **Files:** `brutex/observability/pull_health.py`, `tests/unit/test_observability_pull_health.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-STALLED-REFIRE-001. deliberately does NOT install the `groww` extra), `scripts/run/preflight.sh` (host tools only) — so a returning operator still exported env vars per shell, met AWS/token failures as mid-pull stack traces, and hand-rebuilt a broken venv. `./up.sh` composes the EXISTING machinery into one idempotent, loud, precise entry (a bootstrap WRAPPER — it duplicates no engine/pull/server code). **MECHANISM (REUSE — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** FAST PATH — a live dashboard (PID from the `brutex/config/runtime.py` service-discovery `runtime.json`, liveness via `kill -0`) prints "already ready" + the URL and exits 0 in under a second; the same check RE-RUNS before the final boot so a concurrent `./up.sh` can never double-boot. Step 1 finds python3.12 (or a ≥3.12 `python3`) with the exact per-OS install hint on a miss, and SELF-HEALS a broken/stale venv (missing/old interpreter or broken pip → rebuild; removes ONLY the in-repo `.venv` build artifact — `~/.brutex` user data + the lake are NEVER touched, statically pinned). Step 2 probe-guards the editable install of `.[dev,data,ui,groww,token-broker]` — the extras a REAL pull genuinely needs (`growwapi`+`pyotp` per CLAUDE.md §6 TOTP auth; `boto3` because AWS SSM is the SOLE credential/token source per DEC-AWS-ONLY-CREDS-001; a bare `[dev,data]` cannot import any of the three, verified against `pyproject.toml`) — then verifies each pull-critical dep one PASS/FAIL line with the exact fix command. Step 4 decides the lake location with ZERO operator input (`resolve_and_record_lake`: a persisted config line is reused silently; else an EXISTING lake with real data — a Parquet partition under `bars/` — is AUTO-DETECTED, an environment-pointed path first then the app default `~/.brutex/lake`, and recorded permanently; else an environment-pointed path is recorded; else the default is created — ONE informative line `lake: <path> (auto-detected, N datasets)`, the operator NEVER types a path, and no printed line even names an env var) + persists `BRUTEX_AUTO_RESUME_ON_BOOT=1` ONCE in `~/.brutex/.env` — the file `brutex/config/dotenv.py` ALREADY loads at every CLI + dashboard boot with real-env-wins semantics (GAP C6) — so the operator never exports per-session env again; an explicit operator line is respected (presence-guarded append, never rewritten), and the auto-resume wiring is stated HONESTLY: the flag makes a dashboard boot resume an interrupted pull ONLY when the durable window ledger shows unfinished work (`brutex/orchestrator/auto_resume.py`, DEC-AUTO-RESUME-ON-BOOT-001 — opt-in machinery, default OFF in code; up.sh opts the operator in via the persisted config) — a clean ledger boots idle, never a surprise pull. Step 5 is the self-check chain, each line PASS or exact-cause+fix (never a stack trace): deps importable → AWS identity (`sts get-caller-identity` via boto3; a miss degrades with the exact `aws configure` / AWS_PROFILE / key-pair hint) → the Groww daily access token READABLE from SSM `/tickvault/prod/groww/access-token` (ONE read-only `GetParameter WithDecryption`, region resolved `BRUTEX_TOKEN_AWS_REGION` → `AWS_REGION` → `ap-south-1` mirroring `resolve_token_broker_region`; `ParameterNotFound` → "deploy the minter once (deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh) or wait for the ~06:05 IST scheduled mint"; `AccessDenied` → the read-only consumer IAM fix; only the token LENGTH is ever echoed, never the value) → lake-root write probe. AWS/SSM failures DEGRADE honestly — the dashboard still starts, loudly labelled DEGRADED with each FAIL naming its fix (a live pull will fail until fixed); an unwritable lake root is a HARD stop (exit non-zero). 1090. **DEC-DEPLOY-AUTO-FIRST-MINT-001 — the AWS token-minter deploy is now FULLY ZERO-TOUCH end-to-end: `deploy.sh` (a) AUTO-ADOPTS the stack's 7 name-fixed AWS resources into the remote Terraform state (`terraform import` preflight between init and apply) so the local→remote state-migration gap can never 409 an apply again, and (b) TRIGGERS THE FIRST TOKEN MINT ITSELF post-apply (one verified `aws lambda invoke`) so the operator NEVER manually invokes the Lambda and the shared access-token param is live the moment the deploy finishes** (2026-07-02; deploy tooling + runbooks + tests ONLY — `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh`, `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md`, `docs/runbooks/aws-token-minter.md`, `tests/deploy/`; NO `brutex/` package code touched; NO Rust touched; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **WHY (both operator-hit, live):** (1) a freshly-deployed stack had an EMPTY `/tickvault/prod/groww/access-token` until the next 06:05 IST EventBridge cron (`cron(35 0 * * ? *)`, `main.tf`), so the operator was told to run a manual `aws lambda invoke` once — a manual step §11 AUTOMATED forbids; (2) the operator's fresh-clone deploy DIED with `ParameterAlreadyExists`/`EntityAlreadyExists` (409) because the resources created under the OLD LOCAL Terraform state already exist in AWS while the new S3 remote state (DEC-DEPLOY-REMOTE-STATE-001 #1078) starts EMPTY. **FIX A (adopt preflight, step 4/6):** NEW `adopt_resource`/`resource_in_state`/`resource_exists_in_aws` helpers — for EACH of the exactly-7 name-fixed adoptable addresses (`aws_ssm_parameter.access_token` · `aws_iam_role.minter` · `aws_iam_role.reader_tickvault` · `aws_iam_role.reader_brutex` · `aws_cloudwatch_log_group.minter` · `aws_lambda_function.minter` · `aws_lambda_permission.allow_eventbridge`), if `terraform state show` says ABSENT and the exact-name AWS probe (`ssm get-parameter` / `iam get-role` / `logs describe-log-groups` exact-match / `lambda get-function` / `lambda get-policy` statement-id, pipeline-free under `set -o pipefail`) says PRESENT, run `terraform import` (riding the SAME bash-3.2-guarded `EXTRA_ARGS` `-var` overrides as apply, DEC-DEPLOY-EMPTY-ARGS-FIX-001 #1075); already-in-state / not-present-in-AWS are HONEST one-line no-ops (so the operator's already-imported state re-runs as 7 no-ops), and a FAILED import HARD-STOPS the deploy with the verbatim terraform error — never continuing into a doomed apply. Only these 7 carry operator-visible fixed names; everything else in the stack derives from them or is put-idempotent. **FIX B (first mint, step 6/6):** after a successful apply (`set -euo pipefail` + terraform's own `yes` gate guarantee ordering), resolve the Lambda via `terraform output -raw minter_lambda_name` (fallback: the scanned `lambda_function_name` var, default `groww-token-minter`), `aws lambda invoke` ONCE, and verify the payload against the handler's contract `{"ok": true, …}` (`grep -Eq '"ok"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true'` — a handler error returns `{"errorMessage": …}` and is REJECTED); print `FIRST MINT: PASS` with the payload, or `FIRST MINT: FAIL` with the EXACT error text (invoke stderr + payload + CloudWatch pointer) and **exit non-zero** so a broken first mint is NEVER silent. IDEMPOTENT: a re-run re-mints once per deploy — harmless, the Lambda is the SOLE token writer and the SSM write is last-writer-wins (`PutParameter Overwrite=True`, ADR-0014); one mint per deploy is far below any issuance pressure (the handler itself retries a transient 429 with backoff, DEC-TOKEN-MINTER-CENTRAL-001 #1060). **HONEST envelope:** the preflight heals the KNOWN 7-resource conflict set (+ any future out-of-band re-creation of them), NOT arbitrary state drift — a full local state is still better carried by the documented one-time `terraform init -migrate-state` (runbook §2b), and once state is shared in S3 the gap cannot recur (the preflight then no-ops); the mint verdict trusts the handler's own `ok` contract (`handler.py MintOutcome.as_response`), not a fabricated success; NOTHING here changes the Lambda/handler/Terraform resources themselves — `main.tf` is byte-untouched (the `minter_lambda_name` output already existed in `outputs.tf`). **Tests (tests/deploy/, style of #1075/#1076):** NEW `test_deploy_state_adopt.py` (preflight exists · runs after-init/before-apply · all 7 addresses+ids pinned parametrically · exactly-7 no-drift · hard-stop-on-import-failure · verbatim-stderr · honest no-op lines · guarded-EXTRA_ARGS import · exact-match log-group probe · pipeline-free permission probe · -var name-override scan + variables.tf-mirroring defaults) + NEW `test_deploy_auto_first_mint.py` (post-apply-invoke ordering · terraform-output name resolution + fallback · region-scoped · ok-payload verification pinned to the exact grep · BOTH fail paths exit non-zero with exact error text · honest PASS line · bash-3.2-safety: no bash-4-only constructs / no case-mod expansions / EXTRA_ARGS stays the ONLY array · BEHAVIOURAL bash-subshell checks of the extracted ok-idiom against success/compact/error/ok-false/empty payloads) + `test_build_lambda_package.py` EXTRA_ARGS-idiom count updated 2→3 (the import site). 124 tests/deploy tests GREEN; `bash -n deploy.sh` clean; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + pyright clean on the touched test files. **Files:** `deploy/aws_token_minter/deploy.sh`, `tests/deploy/test_deploy_state_adopt.py` (NEW), `tests/deploy/test_deploy_auto_first_mint.py` (NEW), `tests/deploy/test_build_lambda_package.py`, `docs/runbooks/aws-token-deploy-guide.md` (§2 steps 4+6, §2b auto-adopt note, §4a first-mint-already-ran, 2 troubleshooting rows), `docs/runbooks/aws-token-minter.md` (§4/§5 notes), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DEPLOY-AUTO-FIRST-MINT-001. 1126. **DEC-PULL-FORENSIC-WAVE1-001 — first fix wave from the end-to-end Groww pull forensic audit: THREE refuter-confirmed pull-path defects fixed together — (1) DOUBLE RATE ADMISSION (BLOCKER): every physical fetch was admitted to the shared RateController TWICE (the client-level `GrowwClient._call` pace AND the per-window pace rebound by `run_ingest._with_paced_client`), so the pull physically capped at ~half the ceiling (~4 r/s at the 8 r/s ceiling) and the #1026 8-hour fetch-budget arithmetic was 2x optimistic — FIXED by making the CLIENT the single canonical admission point: NEW `GrowwClient.self_paces`/`ClientPool.self_paces` + a COMMON `client_self_paces()` predicate; both spines (`ingest_spot`, `ingest_option_contract`) drop the window-level pace when the adapter's client self-paces, so each physical attempt (retries included) is admitted EXACTLY ONCE and the 500/min governor still sees every fetch (NO RateController change, NO cap change — Golden Rule #6); (2) DRY-RUN LAKE POISONING (BLOCKER): `brutex fetch --dry-run` wired a real `ParquetBarSink`+`Catalog` over the RESOLVED PRODUCTION lake root, writing SYNTHETIC bars into real partitions that keep-first merge then shadowed real vendor bars PERMANENTLY — FIXED by routing every dry-run persistence surface (sink, DuckDB catalog, retry-storm audit) onto an ephemeral `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='brutex-fetch-dryrun-lake-')` via a cleanup contextmanager, so a dry-run can NEVER touch the production lake (reporting counts preserved); (3) DEAD BOOT AUTO-RESUME (BLOCKER): `_auto_resume_child_argv` spawned the RETIRED `fetch --universe` form that `cmd_fetch` refuses with `EXIT_USER_ERROR`, so crash/redeploy auto-resume logged `verdict=resumed` while resuming NOTHING — FIXED to spawn the current `fetch --until-clean --lake-root <resolved>` entry + a validator that checks the argv against the real parser before spawning; the docstring is HONEST that this resumes ONLY the 3 brute-force index SPOT windows (non-index spot + F&O re-trigger a bounded once-per-boot resume until re-pulled via the dashboard) — the FIX-FIRST hostile-review overclaim, folded. (2026-07-02; ADAPTER + CLI only — `client.py`/`ingest.py`/`option_ingest.py`/`pool.py`/`run_ingest.py`/`cli.py` + `test_groww_single_admission.py` (NEW) + `test_cli_auto_resume.py`/`test_cli_retry_storm.py`; NO Rust; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY. Each fix carries a fails-before/passes-after regression suite (71 new/updated tests) + independent hostile review (2 SHIP, 1 FIX-FIRST folded); 338 touched-suite tests pass, ruff+format clean, verified 2026-07-02 under python3.12. HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): the double-admission 2x was runtime-proven in-sandbox (admission ratio 2.00 -> 1.00); live sustained-rate + the 06:00 rotation remain operator-Mac-proof items per the audit's live-proof kit. Sources the forensic audit (recon + 6 attack lenses + adversarial refuters, all findings file:line-confirmed at HEAD). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-FORENSIC-WAVE1-001.)
1101. **DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-O1-001 — the hash-chained audit logs' torn-tail REPAIR (`_truncate_torn_tail`, BOTH the ingest SHA256 chain `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` AND its sweep BLAKE3 twin `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py`) no longer reads the WHOLE log into memory to find the truncation point — it locates the last committed newline with the SAME O(1) bounded reverse-seek the resume tail-read already uses and truncates IN PLACE, so repairing a multi-GB log is O(8 KiB chunk) resident bytes instead of O(filesize) (the guarantee-audit MINOR OOM-risk fix)** (2026-07-02; `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` + `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py` + `tests/unit/test_audit_torn_tail.py` + `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_audit.py` + this ledger entry ONLY — NO Rust touched (`git status --short rust/` empty); ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path / chain-format change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE BUG (guarantee-audit MINOR, memory-scalability):** `_truncate_torn_tail` — the crash-recovery repair that drops an interrupted append's newline-less final line so `open(resume=True)` continues a pristine chain (DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-001) — did `data = f.read()` then `data.rfind(b"\n")`, materialising the ENTIRE log to find the last committed byte, then rewrote the whole file through a temp-file `os.replace`. The sibling resume tail-read had already been fixed to an O(1) bounded reverse-seek (DEC-AUDIT-RESUME-TAILREAD-001), so the repair was the LAST whole-file read on the resume path: a multi-GB sweep audit log (the §11 SCALABLE Day-1→730B envelope) repairing after a crash could OOM the very resume that torn-tail recovery exists to keep unattended (§11 AUTOMATED). **THE FIX (COMMON — one reverse-seek, shared):** each module gains `_iter_reverse_chunks(f, size)` — a generator yielding `(pos, block)` blocks of ≤ `_TAIL_CHUNK_BYTES` (8192) from the file END toward offset 0 — and BOTH the existing `_read_tail_entry` reverse walk AND the NEW `_find_last_newline_offset` (return the absolute offset of the last `"\n"`, or −1) now delegate to it (no copy-pasted reverse loops; the two modules remain deliberate STANDALONE twins per the DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-001 layout). `_truncate_torn_tail` then truncates IN PLACE via `os.truncate(fd, cut+1)` (0 when no newline exists) + best-effort `fsync`, replacing the temp-file whole-rewrite. **BYTE-IDENTITY (correctness > the memory win, proven not claimed):** the kept prefix is exactly the old `data[: data.rfind(b"\n") + 1]` for EVERY input — pinned by a 12-case × 2-chunk-size × 2-backend parametrised matrix against `_old_truncate_semantics` (the old body verbatim): empty file, single clean line, single torn line, many clean lines, many-clean+torn tail, a torn line LONGER than one reverse-seek chunk (the multi-block walk, chunk pinned to 8 bytes), a 100-byte all-torn no-newline file (cut = −1 after walking to offset 0), last-byte-is/-isn't-newline, torn-at-start single byte, blank-lines-then-torn, newline-only file. In-place truncate is CRASH-SAFE BY MONOTONICITY: it only ever DROPS uncommitted trailing bytes — committed-prefix bytes are never rewritten or moved (the old temp-file dance rewrote them all), and an interruption mid-repair just re-truncates the same boundary on the next resume (idempotent; Golden Rule #7 — pinned by `test_truncate_is_idempotent`). **O(1)-MEMORY TEETH (the load-bearing proof):** `test_truncate_memory_is_o_chunk_not_o_filesize` builds a >1 MiB log (>128× the 8 KiB chunk) with a torn tail spanning 2 chunks, wraps the module's `open` with a read-size-recording proxy, and asserts max single read ≤ 8192 B AND total bytes read ≤ 4 chunks (32 KiB) ≪ the >1 MiB file the old implementation slurped — for BOTH chains. A `test_truncate_reverse_chunks_shared_with_tailread` inspection test guards the COMMON dedup (`_read_tail_entry` + `_find_last_newline_offset` both source `_iter_reverse_chunks`; the repair delegates to `_find_last_newline_offset`). Two existing tests updated to the new failure point (`os.truncate` monkeypatch replaces `os.replace`). **VERIFIED 2026-07-02 on the task venv (`scratchpad/venv_run`, Python 3.12.3):** `tests/unit/test_audit_torn_tail.py` **132 passed** (56 NEW cases; 76 on `origin/main` → 132 here) + `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_audit.py` green; the audit/orchestrator/sweep regression battery (torn-tail + orchestrator audit/pipeline/replay + audit-verify + sweep run/verify/heal + property chain + chaos chain/resume + integration replay/sweep-run-audit/CLI-verify) green with the only skips the 3 PRE-EXISTING Phase-2 stubs; **coverage 100.00% line + 100.00% branch on BOTH changed modules** (`brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` 255 stmt / 60 branch, 0 missing; `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py` 227 stmt / 56 branch, 0 missing); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 4 touched files; `mypy --strict brutex` **Success: no issues found in 302 source files**; `pyright` on the touched files **0 errors, 13 warnings — byte-identical to the `origin/main` baseline** (pre-existing `reportPrivateUsage` on the deliberate private-helper test imports; verified by stash-compare). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** O(1) here means O(`_TAIL_CHUNK_BYTES`) resident bytes for the repair — the reverse WALK is still O(torn-tail-length / chunk) reads when a torn line spans many chunks (each read bounded; a JSONL audit line is ~200 B so the walk is 1 block in practice); the durability posture is unchanged-or-better (same best-effort `fsync`; strictly FEWER bytes at risk since committed bytes are never rewritten); no daily-quota / vendor / engine claims are made. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_audit.py`, `tests/unit/test_audit_torn_tail.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_audit.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-O1-001. 1106. **DEC-PULL-LOUD-CREDENTIAL-REFUSAL-001 — a REAL pull with missing/broken Groww/AWS credentials now REFUSES LOUDLY with the CredentialsError's own actionable fix text (HTTP 503 + ERROR log + a red `credentials_missing` needs-operator verdict on the dashboard; the same message + exit 1 on the CLI), and synthetic data runs ONLY on an explicit dry-run request, labeled unmistakably — killing the silent creds-absent → SyntheticSpotAdapter+NullBarSink downgrade that reported fake-green pulls** (2026-07-02; the #1 CRITICAL (R1) from the Groww-pull divergence audit; dashboard pull routes + CLI fetch gate + verdict machinery ONLY; NO Rust touched; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **WHY (the two-week fake-green):** every dashboard pull route computed `dry_run = not groww_credentials_present()` (`app.py:1707,1850,2005,2328,2500,2910` @ pre-fix main), and `groww_credentials_present` swallowed EVERY `CredentialsError` to a bare `False` (`credentials.py:606-609`) — so ANY credential failure on the operator's Mac (no `~/.aws` creds, expired SSO, wrong region, boto3 missing, IAM lacking `ssm:GetParameter`/`kms:Decrypt`) SILENTLY swapped the real pull for the synthetic `(SyntheticSpotAdapter, NullBarSink)` pair (`pull_controller.py:593-604` + `data/sink.py` counts-but-discards) and reported the pull GREEN with counts while ZERO real bars landed; the error's actionable fix text (which SSM parameter is wrong + what to do) was DISCARDED at the gate, and the UI even titled the run "· live". Sandbox tests always ran this path, so green CI proved only the synthetic spine — reality diverged for two weeks with no signal. **WHAT SHIPPED:** (1) `brutex/config/credentials.py` — NEW `groww_credentials_error() -> str | None` preserving the `CredentialsError` text verbatim (`None` = creds resolve); `groww_credentials_present` now delegates to it (one resolve path, zero duplication) and is documented as a STATUS/display gate only. (2) `brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py` — the ONE COMMON gate both surfaces run (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON): NEW `gate_pull_credentials(dry_run_requested, credentials_error=None) -> PullVerdict | None` (explicit dry-run short-circuits WITHOUT resolving creds; creds-ok proceeds; otherwise returns the refusal verdict — the caller MUST refuse, never downgrade); NEW `PullVerdictKind` member `credentials_missing` (pre-pull refusal; `needs_operator=True`; never emitted by `classify_pull`); NEW `credentials_refusal_verdict(reason)` carrying the relayed fix text as `action`/`auth_cause` (DYNAMIC — whatever env var/SSM parameter the error names, no per-field hardcoding); NEW `verdict_message()` (the single headline+action join both surfaces print); NEW loud-synthetic labeling: `SYNTHETIC_DRY_RUN_LABEL` ("SYNTHETIC DRY-RUN — no real data"), `label_synthetic()` (progress detail / CLI stderr prefix) and `mark_synthetic()` (relabels a finished dry-run verdict's headline/action, classification kind preserved). (3) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — all 6 pull routes (`/universe/pull`, `/pull-all`, `/pull-expiries-contracts`, `/pull-historical` incl. the composite, `/pull-pipeline`, `/retry-failed`) gained an EXPLICIT `?dry_run=true` query param (default false) and route through the shared closure `_gate_pull_dry_run`: broken creds → **HTTP 503** whose detail is `verdict_message(refusal)` (headline + relayed fix text), an ERROR structlog line `universe.pull.refused_no_credentials` with the reason, AND the refusal verdict stamped into `_last_pull_verdict` so `GET /pull-verdict` renders the RED banner with the fix text + retry button (`verdict_banner._KIND_STYLE` gained `credentials_missing → verdict--red`); explicit dry-run runs with its job `detail` prefixed via `label_synthetic`. (4) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — `BulkSpotReport.verdict` routes a dry-run's verdict through `mark_synthetic`, so even a finished synthetic pull's banner says SYNTHETIC loudly. (5) `universe.html` — the pull title no longer hardcodes "· live"; `body.dry_run` renders "· SYNTHETIC DRY-RUN — no real data". (6) `brutex/cli.py` `cmd_fetch` — the hardcoded no-creds message (which ASSERTED a cause the swallowed error could not distinguish) is replaced by the SAME COMMON gate + `verdict_message` relay; the creds-vanished-mid-build `CredentialsError` handler prints the same refusal (pragma removed, now covered); `--dry-run` announces itself with the loud label. **Tests (38 new-behavior tests, PLACED so the strict per-module 100% coverage gates scope them — the pure gate/label/verdict units (10) in `tests/unit/test_ingest_common_pull_verdict.py` (the `ci.yml` ingest_common static-gate file list + the stem-matched discovery gate), the CLI creds-vanished-mid-build race in `tests/unit/test_cli_retry_storm.py` (the discovery gate's `test_cli*` scope, next to the up-front CLI refusal), and the cross-surface pins (27) in the NEW `tests/unit/test_pull_loud_credential_refusal.py`; the first CI run at eb58a579 had ALL of these in the one unscoped combined file and FAILED the per-module gates — ingest_common 94.75%, cli.py 99.60% — the per-module placement restores both to a verified 100.00% under the exact gate commands):** the fix-text relay (verbatim, never swallowed) · present/absent delegation parity · REAL-chain permutations via fake SSM clients (AWS reachable-but-parameter-missing · parameter present-but-blank (invalid shape) · IAM/KMS read denied — each relaying `load_groww_aws_credentials`'s own classification) · gate short-circuit on explicit dry-run (resolver provably NEVER called — spy) · default-resolver lazy-import branch both ways · refusal verdict fields/needs_operator/to_dict · banner red+retry · `mark_synthetic`/`label_synthetic`/`verdict_message` · route-level parametrized over ALL 6 routes: 503 + fix text + red verdict + no job started, and explicit dry-run never resolves creds · mid-build `CredentialsError` surfacing (single-symbol route 400 with the real text; background job settles ERROR carrying it; CLI race exits 1 with the relayed text) · real pull with good creds byte-unchanged (no label, no refusal) · dry-run detail labeled on the heavy historical + composite paths (Event-gated fakes sampling the RUNNING snapshot). 1119. **DEC-DEFLAKE-ISOLATION-PROOF-TEST-001 — the async fetch/process-separation ISOLATION-PROOF integration test `test_stalled_consumer_does_not_slow_the_fetch` is DE-FLAKED at the ROOT: the producer's independence from the consumer tail is no longer asserted by a wall-clock RATIO (`producer_elapsed < 0.5 × N × tail_sleep`), it is proven by EXPLICIT synchronization — the producer must issue EVERY fetch and `ingest_spot` must RETURN while ALL consumer tails are still wedged on an Event gate (ZERO tails completed)** (2026-07-02; TEST-ONLY — `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py` + this ledger entry; NO `brutex/` package code touched; NO Rust touched; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / pacing change). **THE FLAKE (root-caused, VERBATIM from run 28582437543 / job 84745855193 on PR #1049 head da162b9a):** `AssertionError: producer took 0.440s issuing 13 fetches — not isolated from the 0.780s of consumer tails` / `assert 0.4396150249999664 < (0.5 * 0.78)`. The DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 centerpiece measured the wall time the producer spent issuing 13 window fetches and asserted it beat 0.5× the synchronous tail floor (13 × 60 ms = 0.78 s → bound 0.39 s). The producer's own per-window work is ~6 ms TOTAL on an idle sandbox (measured 0.005–0.006 s, ratio 0.01, with AND without coverage tracing) — but under CI's serial `--cov=brutex --cov-branch` run the producer's coverage-traced bytecode shares the GIL with the two consumer threads' real traced Parquet appends on a contended shared runner, and the OS inflated ~6 ms of producer work past the 0.39 s bound (0.440 s observed) with the isolation FULLY INTACT (queue_maxsize=16 > 13 windows — the producer structurally CANNOT be back-pressured in this test; the bound failed, never the pipeline). A TIMER race, exactly the class DEC-DEFLAKE-HUNG-WRITE-TEST-001 (#1079) removed from this same file's hung-write suite. NOT an interaction with the absorbed #1048 (DEC-PULL-LOUD-CREDENTIAL-REFUSAL-001) — neither PR #1049 nor #1048 touches `ingest.py`, `fetch_pipeline.py`, or this test file (`git diff origin/main...da162b9a` verified). **THE FIX (deterministic — the #1079 pattern; intent preserved and STRENGTHENED):** every consumer tail is GATED on a `threading.Event` (fully WEDGED, strictly harsher than the old 60 ms sleep); `ingest_spot` runs on a watchdogged thread; the test asserts (a) `done.wait(20.0)` — the producer RETURNED while the gate was held, (b) all ≥12 fetches were issued, (c) `completed_appends` is EMPTY at that instant — ZERO tails had completed when the producer finished. A synchronous/coupled tail could NEVER satisfy this (it would wedge on the first gated append and the watchdog fails LOUDLY, never hanging the suite). Then the gate is released, `drain()` runs, and the durable-landing assert (`2021/01` partition exists) is UNCHANGED. This is a STRICTLY STRONGER claim than the old ratio (the old test proved "producer beat 0.5× the tail floor"; the new one proves "producer finished with the tails at 0% progress") with NO wall-clock ratio left — only the generous 20 s watchdog. `@pytest.mark.flaky`/rerun plugins explicitly NOT used (they hide flakiness). **TEETH PRESERVED:** a coupling regression (producer blocking on tail completion or on queue back-pressure) makes `done.wait(20.0)` fail with the exact message `"ingest_spot did NOT return while the consumer tails were stalled"` — deterministic, bounded, loud. **VERIFICATION (SANDBOX, Linux/x86_64/py3.12, fresh venv):** the target test green back-to-back AND under a saturating `nproc`-busy-loop CPU-stressor load with coverage tracing on (the exact contention class that flaked CI); the whole file (19 tests) green; TEST-ONLY diff → the `brutex/` 100% coverage gate is structurally unchanged; ruff + ruff-format clean, pyright 0 errors on the touched file. **Files:** `tests/integration/test_groww_fetch_async_separation.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DEFLAKE-ISOLATION-PROOF-TEST-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-FETCH-ASYNC-SEPARATION-001 (the centerpiece this de-flakes) and DEC-DEFLAKE-HUNG-WRITE-TEST-001 #1079 (the explicit-synchronization de-flake pattern, same file).
