plain spot bars never carry always-None Greek fields) + the ONE canonical `GREEKS_OVERLAY_FIELDS` order — ten NULLABLE physical columns appended after `open_interest`: `iv/delta/gamma/theta/vega/rho` (Float64 FULL precision — DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 forbids rounding statistical values), `spot_at_bar` (the ONE 2dp-snapped price — the enrich join MATERIALIZED), `t_years_used`, `rate_used`, `greeks_provenance_id` (Int32 bit-pack: formula_version + rate_source_id + rate_version + q_bias + tte_convention + style_flag + per-bar STATUS — the staleness key; `pack/unpack_greeks_provenance` pure + property-tested lossless). `parquet_writer.py`: `_render_bytes` branches on bar type (a plain batch renders the byte-identical 7-column blob — legacy partitions untouched, NO migration); `_read_existing_bars` + `_reconstruct_bars_per_row` are SCHEMA-TOLERANT (the plan's "single biggest correctness trap" — a legacy 7-column partition reads the overlay as NULL, never `KeyError`, and round-trips byte-identically; a NaN-Greek partition quarantines as a `WriterError`, never a raw crash); `_tick_round` is type-preserving (snaps OHLC + `spot_at_bar`, Greeks pass at full precision); the merge loop gains ONE overlay branch — `_bar_values_equal` STAYS OHLCV+OI-only, a Greek difference NEVER trips keep-first (a vendor re-pull's plain bar can never strip a stored Greek — regression-pinned), `latest-wins` overwrites a differing overlay (the enrich-heal contract). `fno_candle_lake.py`: `FNO_CANDLE_LAKE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 2→3 + the ten `source="bar"` nullable rows advertised (the CHEAP moneyness family STAYS `derived` — the ADR D10 cost-class hybrid preserved). **WHAT (the enrichment — plan §15.4):** NEW `brutex/data/greeks_enrich.py` — `enrich_greeks_for_targets` (per-target QUARANTINED driver mirroring `derive_daily_for_targets`), the pure `enrich_option_bars` core (per bar: reuse-if-stamp-current → rate/T/spot/no-arb pre-screens → ONE `compute_greeks(price=close, sigma=None, forward=S·e^{rT}, …)` kernel call), the window-bounded schema-tolerant `read_option_rows` (`ist_span_partition_files` — O(pulled-window) month files, never O(lake-depth)) and the `write_option_greeks` `latest-wins` write through the SAME `ParquetBarSink`→partition-flock spine (DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001). NEW COMMON `brutex/data/spot_join.py` (`spot_close_by_ts_window` + `utc_instant` — the plan's "lift `_underlying_spot_close_by_ts` to `brutex/data/`"; `db_view._utc_instant` now DELEGATES to it; the probe segments were already COMMON in `partition.SPOT_PROBE_SEGMENTS`; db_view's DuckDB page-BETWEEN variant stays for the /db read path until Phase 3a — stated, not hidden). EXERCISE STYLE is derived from WHICH probe segment supplies the spot (INDEX → `european_exact`; CASH → the ADR §3 #1 default `american_style_approx` — computed but FLAGGED in the stamp, never silently exact; no spot → UNKNOWN). **EVERY unsolvable bar stores an HONEST stamped NULL (plan §15.8), never a fabricated value:** `no_spot` (exact-minute join miss — NEVER a carried-forward spot), `at_expiry` (T at/under the 600 s floor, incl. T ≤ 0 — the theta/gamma blow-up zone, distinguishable from solver failure), `no_rate` (a curve with no row on/before the bar date), `below_intrinsic` (premium under the DISCOUNTED no-arb floor `S − K·e^{−rT}` CE / `K·e^{−rT} − S` PE — the property suite CAUGHT that a naive spot-intrinsic screen false-flags legitimate deep-ITM PUT premiums; fixed to the discounted parity), `no_solution` (kernel honest-None: above the upper bound / IV clamp / non-convergence), `bad_input` (e.g. a zero-price stored bar — per-bar quarantined). **FUT legs are NEVER enriched** ("never a bogus Greek for a future") — the FUT partition stays raw 7-column at ZERO write cost and its overlay columns READ as NULL via the schema-tolerant read-back, semantically identical to a stamped-NA row (an explicit, stated economy vs the plan table's stamped-NA wording). **WIRING (fully automatic, zero human input):** `historical_pull.py::_enrich_greeks_from_minute` — the F&O Greeks twin of `_derive_daily_from_minute`, at the SAME post-drain seam in `pull_contract_candles` (`if not dry_run:` after the pipeline drain + reconcile — the fetch lane is NEVER blocked), whole body guarded → any failure logs ONE `fno.greeks_enrich.error` and the pull SUCCEEDS untouched (proven by a live-pipeline wiring test). **MIXED-SCHEMA HARDENING (the schema change's blast radius, measured then closed):** polars ≥1.4 REFUSES multi-file reads over mixed 7/17-column trees (empirically confirmed) — the three whole-tree option readers (`spot_daily_resample.make_lake_read_1m_window`, `timeframe_materialize.make_lake_read_1m`, `options/lake_source._contract_bars`) now scan with `missing_columns="insert", extra_columns="ignore"` (byte-identical for a uniform tree — the existing bounded-read spy + byte-identity tests still pass), and every DuckDB `/db` read already used `union_by_name=true`. **IDEMPOTENCE / RESUMABILITY (Golden Rule #7, tested):** a bar whose stored stamp matches the current INPUT bits with status OK is REUSED (O(1) compare, no re-solve); an identical restate is detected PRE-write (`EnrichStats.changed == 0` → no partition I/O at all — re-enrich twice is byte-identical, hash-pinned); a NULL-status bar is RE-ATTEMPTED each pass (a later spot arrival HEALS `no_spot` bars — tested); each partition write is the atomic flock-guarded tmp→fsync→`os.replace`, so a crash mid-pass leaves every partition fully-old-or-fully-new (a simulated mid-pass write crash corrupts nothing and the next pass heals incrementally — tested). **HONEST COMPLEXITY (plan §15.7):** the pass is O(bars-in-pulled-window), ONCE per pull, post-drain, month-file-bounded — NOT a literal O(1)-total; the per-bar IV solve is the kernel's bounded O(1)-per-call (#1100's pinned envelope); reads of stored Greeks afterwards are plain O(1)-per-bar column projections; a formula/convention bump re-materializes at an honest O(all-stored-option-bars), stamp-driven + resumable. **NOT in this PR (explicit):** the Phase-3 read surfaces — `/db` stored-column read with the derived fallback (3a), `/movers` delta/iv cells (3b), executor delta-target (3c), and the §15.10 derived-TF close-snapshot propagation (locked semantics, lands with the resample-consuming surfaces); the F&O `1day` derived partitions carry NO Greeks yet. **VERIFICATION (fresh runs, 2026-07-02, repo venv Python 3.12.3 + the #1100 trading_core wheel):** `brutex/data/greeks_enrich.py` (259 stmts/52 branches) + `brutex/data/spot_join.py` (25/4) BOTH **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** via the NEW CI gate 12e; `brutex/data/models.py` (106/40) + `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py` (227/50) + `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` (285/64) ALL re-measured 100.00% line+branch over their covering suites; NEW tests — `tests/unit/test_greeks_enrich.py` (45: every §15.8 status family incl. expiry-minute T→0, deep ITM/OTM, penny, below-parity, zero-volume, zero-price, no-rate, style stamps, reuse/heal/restate bookkeeping) + `tests/unit/test_data_spot_join.py` (8) + `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer_greeks.py` (28: 17-column render, legacy byte-identity, keep-first-never-strips-Greeks, latest-wins heal, NaN quarantine, partial-overlay tolerance, per-row fallback) + `tests/integration/test_greeks_enrich_lake_roundtrip.py` (14: end-to-end solve-and-store, FUT untouched, re-enrich byte-identical, vendor re-pull preservation, incremental new-bar enrich, no-spot heal, crash-mid-pass durability+resume, zero-option pull, window bounding, mixed-schema daily-derive/TF/executor readers) + `tests/property/test_greeks_enrich_properties.py` (6: lossless stamp round-trip; stored-value no-arb — IV round-trip recovers sigma, CE/PE delta monotone in strike, gamma/vega ≥ 0, CE≡PE gamma) + frozen `tests/golden/fixtures/greeks_enrich_golden.json` + `tests/golden/test_greeks_enrich_golden.py` (deterministic generator, byte-identical re-runs proven) + `TestGreeksEnrichWiring` (4: a LIVE pipeline-wired pull stores non-NULL `iv` for CE while FUT stays 7-column; dry-run never enriches; an enrich failure never fails the pull; target-building skips); suite-wide: 74 new-module + 61 pull-historical + 28 writer-greeks + 140 writer/sink/lake + 497 db/option + 106 resample + 9 roundtrip tests green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched file; `pyright` 0 errors. **Files:** `brutex/data/greeks_enrich.py` (NEW), `brutex/data/spot_join.py` (NEW), `brutex/data/models.py`, `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py`, `brutex/data/fno_candle_lake.py`, `brutex/data/spot_daily_resample.py`, `brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py`, `brutex/options/lake_source.py`, `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (gate 12e), `docs/GREEKS_ENGINE_PLAN.md` (§15 status + §15.6 gate status), `docs/adr/0015-shared-greeks-engine.md` (§2b status + §5 rows 1/2/2b), 7 test files (5 NEW) + the frozen golden fixture + generator, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR2B-001. **Builds on** DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR2-001 (#1100) + DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR1-001 (#1094) + DEC-GREEKS-GENERATION-TIME-001 (#1071) + DEC-GREEKS-SHARED-CORE-001 (#1070) + DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 (#887). (Ledger: #1111 = live main max #1106 `DEC-PULL-LOUD-CREDENTIAL-REFUSAL-001` + 5, over-provisioned for collision-proofing against the in-flight sibling queue (originally #1105 above the then-max #1100, renumbered when siblings #1104/#1106 landed first); `validate_ledger_numbering.py` enforces (number,suffix) uniqueness — re-checked immediately before push; the DEC-ID is the stable handle.)
1122. **DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR3-001 — Greeks engine PR-3 (plan §15.10): derived-timeframe Greeks propagation by CLOSE-SNAPSHOT — the ONE canonical resampler (`tf_resampler.resample_1m_to_tf`) now carries every stored Greeks-overlay column by LAST-VALUE whenever the input frame has it, so every resample-consuming surface (the on-demand TB-scale option TF read `fno_resample.resample_session_to_tf`, `derive_fno_intraday_tfs`, the movers/display path) inherits the LOCKED semantics automatically — PLUS the Phase-3a `/db` DISPLAY of the stored overlay: the F&O candle browser's COLUMNS picker now offers the 10 stored Greeks overlay columns end-to-end (backend projection + validation + typed-NULL legacy-tree tolerance + frontend picker/rendering) — ENGINE UNCHANGED, spot/futures byte-identical** (2026-07-02; the FOURTH implementation increment of the MERGED Greeks plan — implements the §15.10 semantics LOCKED by DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR1-001 #1094 over the stored overlay of DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR2B-001 #1111 (merged PR #1053, squash a09fded5); under DEC-GREEKS-SHARED-CORE-001 #1070 + DEC-GREEKS-GENERATION-TIME-001 #1071. ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / vocab / rate-cap / lake-write-path change; F&O stays REFERENCE_ONLY.) **WHAT (one seam, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** in `brutex/data/tf_resampler.py::resample_1m_to_tf`, after the carry-last OI branch, each of the ten `GREEKS_OVERLAY_FIELDS` columns (`iv/delta/gamma/theta/vega/rho/spot_at_bar/t_years_used/rate_used/greeks_provenance_id`) PRESENT in the input frame is aggregated `pl.col(name).last()` per bucket — a derived N-minute bar's Greeks (+ input stamps + provenance) are EXACTLY its LAST constituent 1-minute bar's stored values. **Greeks are STATE, not FLOW** (the rule `close` and carry-last OI already obey): never summed, never averaged, never OHLC-aggregated — mathematically identical to re-running the kernel at the derived bar's close instant (same option close, same same-minute spot, same T), so it is zero-recompute, O(1) per derived bar, and bit-identical across every TF (§15.10). **NA propagates honestly:** a bucket whose LAST constituent minute carries a §15.8 stamped NULL (`no_spot` / `iv_solve_failed` / …) yields the SAME NULL — NEVER backfilled from an earlier constituent minute (a stale-spot fabrication); a mid-bucket NULL never poisons a solved last minute (plain `.last()`, deliberately NOT last-non-null). **Additive-only:** a spot / futures / legacy 7-column frame carries none of the overlay columns, so its output is byte-identical (regression-pinned); IV OHLC aggregation is explicitly NOT provided (§15.10 — no consumer, invites averaging misuse). The 1m identity passthrough (`clone`) keeps the overlay unchanged; the DAILY (375) bucket snapshots the session's last minute. **WHAT (/db stored-overlay DISPLAY — the operator's "Greeks entirely done: code, frontend, backend, tables, db columns" addendum; plan Phase 3a, which post-#1111 means DISPLAYING the STORED columns — superseding §15.10's pre-store read-time-derived `_fno_derived_rows` sketch for /db):** VERIFIED FIRST that merged #1053 did NOT expose the stored columns (`CANDLE_COLUMNS` was 7-only, `_select_list` rejected `iv` as unknown, `db.html` `CANDLE_COLS` was 7-only). NOW: `db_view.py` gains `FNO_GREEKS_COLUMNS` (a verbatim re-export of `models.GREEKS_OVERLAY_FIELDS` — ONE source of truth, drift-pinned by test; §11 COMMON) + `FNO_GREEKS_COLUMN_TYPES` (per-column DuckDB SQL type); `query_candles` widens its valid-column set by the overlay for `segment="FNO"` ONLY (a spot page still rejects `iv` as unknown — the overlay exists only under FNO). SCHEMA TOLERANCE: a MIXED legacy/enriched tree already unions (`union_by_name=true` inserts NULLs for files lacking a column), and a PURE-legacy tree (NO file carries it — otherwise a DuckDB binder-error 500) is handled by NEW `_greeks_tolerant_select` + `_physical_union_columns` (ONE `DESCRIBE` Parquet-footer probe, paid ONLY when an overlay column is actually requested — a plain OHLCV page never pays it) substituting `CAST(NULL AS <type>) AS <col>` — honest NULL cells, never a fabricated Greek (Golden Rule #1). `db.html` gains `FNO_GREEKS_COLS` + `curCols()` branching `fno → CANDLE_COLS + FNO_GREEKS_COLS` (spot stays 7-col; the expired-options lake keeps OPTION_COLS) + the numeric type-chips for the new columns. SELECT-* (columns=None) already carried the stored overlay on an enriched tree since #1111 — now the PICKER can name the columns explicitly too. **VERIFICATION (fresh runs, 2026-07-02, repo venv Python 3.12.3 + the #1100 trading_core wheel):** NEW `tests/property/test_tf_resampler_greeks_close_snapshot.py` — 9 tests incl. the §15.10 TEST OBLIGATION hypothesis property (random 1-minute windows × TFs {2,3,5,10,15,30,60} × random NULL minutes → EVERY derived bar's overlay equals its arithmetically-recomputed last constituent's, NA propagating), never-aggregated pin (last ≠ sum/mean/first), daily-bucket snapshot, NULL-last-never-backfilled, mid-bucket-NULL isolation, no-overlay byte-identity, 1m passthrough, and the on-demand session path (`resample_session_to_tf`) inheriting the snapshot INCLUDING the forming-bucket cutoff guard; `brutex/data/tf_resampler.py` re-measured **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (40 stmts/18 branches) via BOTH tf_resampler gates: the static 21c gate (extended to include the new suite) AND the auto-DISCOVERY gate (`coverage_gate_discovery.py` stem-matches `test_tf_resampler*` for touched modules — the first CI run at ee991e93 FAILED it at 93.10% because the suite was stemmed `test_tf_greeks_...`; renamed to `test_tf_resampler_greeks_close_snapshot.py` so the discovery set carries the overlay AND the carry-last OI branch — the same per-module-gate-scoping lesson as Phase-2b's models gate, now learned for BOTH gate layers); resampler regression suites (`test_tf_resampler`, `test_tf_resampler_session_bounds`, `test_fno_resample`, `test_spot_resample`) all green; `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` re-measured **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (772 stmts/252 branches) under the EXACT unchanged ci-gate file list — NEW `TestFnoGreeksProjection` (7: writer-schema drift pin · enriched values returned · pure-legacy typed-NULLs · mixed-tree union · spot-rejects-overlay · select-* carries overlay · empty-partition stable columns) in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py` + the frontend picker pin `test_fno_greeks_columns_offered_in_picker` in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_ux.py`; 326 db_view-gate + 116 db-integration tests green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the touched files (the only local mypy noise is the pre-existing growwapi-installed-stub baseline artifact, proven identical with the diff stashed). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** this ships the PROPAGATION RULE at the canonical seam PLUS the Phase-3a /db stored-column DISPLAY — the `/movers` delta/iv cells are DELIBERATELY NOT folded in (the plan scopes them as the separate Phase 3b with its own `movers_options` gate — stated per the addendum's no-silent-expansion honesty requirement), and the executor delta-target (3c), and enriching the derived F&O `1day` PARTITION writer chain remain the NEXT gated PRs (the daily *bucketing* through `resample_1m_to_tf` snapshots correctly; the `fno_daily_resample` CandleBar writer does not yet persist the overlay); consumers only see propagated Greeks when their READER selects the overlay columns (the enrich reader does; the movers day-glob reader gains them in 3b). O(1) per derived bar per column, O(bars) per resample — no new I/O. **Files:** `brutex/data/tf_resampler.py`, `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/db.html`, `tests/property/test_tf_resampler_greeks_close_snapshot.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_ux.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (tf_resampler gate file list), `docs/GREEKS_ENGINE_PLAN.md` (§15.10 status), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR3-001. **Builds on** DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR2B-001 (#1111) + DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR2-001 (#1100) + DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR1-001 (#1094) + DEC-RESAMPLE-ANCHOR-002 + DEC-FNO-TF-DERIVE-OI-001. 1121. **DEC-DOCTOR-LIVE-AUTORUN-001 — ZERO-COMMAND auto-run of the Mac live-proof kit: the operator NEVER runs `brutex doctor --live` — he starts BruteX as always (IDE ▶ / `./up.sh` / `brutex dashboard`, all funnelling into `cmd_dashboard`) and the health proof runs ITSELF: the CHEAP kit stages auto-run on dashboard boot in a background daemon thread, the one-time EXPENSIVE probes auto-run ONCE around the first REAL pull, and the verdict lives on a persistent dashboard status element (a site-wide pill + red diagnostics banner)** (2026-07-02; operator law — he refused to run any command; `brutex/doctor_autorun.py` NEW + `cli.cmd_dashboard` wiring + `dashboard/app.py` route/gate wiring + `static/bx-liveproof.js` NEW + the 12 templates; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / pull-path change; `brutex/doctor_live.py` itself UNTOUCHED — `doctor --live` stays available for manual debugging). **WHY:** #1120 built the kit but left it a MANUAL command — for THIS operator that is a dead tool (the two-week silent-failure episode happened precisely because nothing ran the checks unprompted). The proof must ride the surfaces he already touches, with the verdict where he already looks (the dashboard). **WHAT (three bounded auto-runs, one holder):** NEW `brutex/doctor_autorun.py` `LiveProofAutorun` — app-owned (injected via `build_app(liveproof=…)`, no module-global state, CLAUDE.md §4), a single lock around tiny state, never held across a kit run or I/O. (1) **Startup preflight** — `cmd_dashboard` builds the holder for the RESOLVED lake root and kicks `start_preflight()` (O(1): spawns a daemon worker; the uvicorn bind is NEVER blocked — the DEC-DASHBOARD-INSTANT-LAUNCH-001 seam pattern, both steps guarded so a failure only logs and the dashboard still boots). The worker runs kit stages {0-4} (env-identity incl. lake-root/SSD-mount [G1] + growwapi version [G2], creds presence [R1], TOTP/clock [M3/N1], token READ — never a mint — + ONE authenticated smoke call [R7/M1], instrument-master reachability [M17/R8]) with `keep_going=True`: ≤ 2 network fetches total (1 authenticated vendor call + 1 keyless master CSV), inside the kit's own 40-call budget, transcripts/quarantine under `_liveproof/<run_id>/` exactly like a manual run. (2) **First-real-pull probes** — the loud-refusal gate's SUCCESS path (`_gate_pull_dry_run`, every dashboard pull route) calls `on_real_pull()`: single-flight, and ONLY when no settled cached verdict exists, it runs kit stages {1,3,5,6,7,8} (2020 1-minute depth [R6], the VIX ADR-0009 §3.2 hard gate [R5], 1-day derivation + NSE bhavcopy cross-check [G7], riding creds/token/spot-1m prerequisites; ≤ ~10 vendor calls) with an injected **1 r/s probe controller ceiling under a dedicated 16/min hard slice** (`AUTORUN_PROBE_CEILING_RPS` + `AUTORUN_PROBE_CEILING_PER_MIN` — the probe controller is a SEPARATE `RateController` instance from the pull job's, rolling per-minute governors share NO state across instances, so the operator-confirmed account-level 500/min cap holds by BUDGET SPLIT, not by a shared governor: pull ≤ 8 r/s → 480/min worst-case + probes ≤ 16/min = 496 ≤ `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN` (4/min headroom absorbing rolling-window boundary fencepost counting); both probe bounds only ever LOWER the issue rate, Rule 6 safe direction — this CORRECTS the hostile review's MAJOR-3 finding that the entry's original "the 500/min governor rides on top" wording was false) so an in-flight pull's pacing is never meaningfully stacked on; the probes share ZERO state with the pull job. Verdicts PERSIST as schema-versioned JSON under `<lake>/_liveproof/autorun/{preflight,probes}.json` — later startups/pulls READ the cache instead of re-probing; a failed/error/corrupt/schema-drifted cache re-probes on the next pull (bounded: one attempt per pull trigger, single-flight; `pass`/`warn` are settled). (3) **UI** — NEW `GET /api/v1/liveproof` (O(1) lock-guarded snapshot; `{"present": false}` when unwired; READ-ONLY — polling never starts a run) + NEW site-wide `bx-liveproof.js` (the bx-rate-monitor pattern: self-injecting, dependency-free, loaded by ALL 12 templates): a bottom-left pill (green pass / amber warn / red fail-error / grey not-applicable / "checking…" while running) + a RED top banner on fail/error listing the kit's diagnostic lines VERBATIM (textContent-only — zero HTML-injection sink) + a click-to-expand detail card with per-stage statuses. **HONESTY (Golden Rules #1/#10 — R1's silent degrade is NOT reintroduced):** `pass` REQUIRES the run's vendor-proof stages to have genuinely PASSed (`token` for preflight; `depth`/`vix`/`bhavcopy` for probes — a required-stage SKIP can never read green); with NO credentials the verdict is `not_applicable` — headline **"live-proof: not applicable (no credentials)"** carrying the CredentialsError fix text VERBATIM from the SAME seam the pull refusal uses (`groww_credentials_error`), and NO kit stage runs, NO vendor/network call is made (spy-tested); the loud-refusal gate ADDITIONALLY mirrors its exact `verdict_message(refusal)` text onto the banner via `note_credentials_refusal` so the 503 and the banner agree even when creds break AFTER boot; every diagnostic line shown is the #1120 golden catalog line VERBATIM (proven by BYTE-EQUALITY of the autorun's lines against a direct `run_live_doctor` run over identical fakes); the widget renders NOTHING when unwired/disabled (no invented state). **Zero new operator surface:** default ON; `BRUTEX_AUTORUN_LIVEPROOF=0` is a code-level escape hatch (only an explicit falsy value disables — unset/blank/garbage stay ON), documented, never required. **Tests (all offline, riding the kit suite's ONE fake `KitDeps` composition — COMMON):** `tests/unit/test_doctor_autorun.py` (75 — toggle matrix; verdict payload round-trip + 14 fail-closed corrupt shapes; cache write/read/missing/corrupt/schema-drift/unreadable; kind policy incl. required-SKIP→fail and required-WARN→warn (bhavcopy-unreachable); no-creds spy (zero kit calls); creds-seam + kit crashes → honest `error` verdict; unwritable-cache volume keeps the in-memory verdict; single-flight both runs; first-pull probes → cache → no re-probe (incl. a REBUILT holder across sessions); failed cache re-probes bounded; refusal-note semantics incl. mid-run; end-to-end green preflight+probes through the REAL `run_live_doctor` over benign fakes; per-failing-stage byte-exact catalog lines for env/creds/totp/token/master + VIX-absent + bhavcopy-mismatch; secret-hygiene: the TOTP secret value appears in NO verdict/cache), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_liveproof_route.py` (10 — present:false unwired; status served; route read-only; real pull triggers probes ONCE then cached; explicit dry-run NEVER triggers; refusal 503 detail == banner line; async non-blocking startup — the app serves /api/v1/state + shows `running` while a REAL daemon-thread preflight is blocked mid-run; probes-vs-pull no-interaction — a blocked probe run leaves /pull-progress + a second real pull fully 1127. **DEC-FNO-FAR-EXPIRY-WINDOW-001 — the F&O DEFAULT 1-minute pull window is now the operator-decreed STRICT LAW `[expiry − lookback → expiry] ∩ [full_start → full_end)` for EVERY contract (near / current / far — never a substitute window): a far-future contract whose window has NOT OPENED yet (`expiry − lookback` ON/AFTER the envelope end) is fetched NOT AT ALL — an honest SKIP with ZERO vendor calls and ZERO ledger rows, logged `fno.window_not_open` per contract with its `opens_on` date — instead of the pre-fix silent degrade to the FULL 2020→today range (~2,373 days ≈ 80 × 30-day chunks of dead history per contract; a verified forensic audit of a real production pull log measured 4 such contracts × 80 chunks = 320 vendor calls = 22.5% of the entire ADANIENT pull wasted)** (2026-07-02; `brutex/adapters/groww/contract_bounds.py` + `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` + tests + this ledger entry + the CLAUDE.md §1/§6 wording — pull-PLANNING default-window fix, NO lake-schema / stored-bar / rate-cap / 52→60-vocab / scope change; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063). **THE BUG (real-log-verified):** `default_fno_minute_window` (DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 #853 / DEC-FUTURES-LOOKBACK-60D-001 #1003) clamped `expiry − lookback` into the resolved envelope; for a far-expiry contract (e.g. a Sep-2026 monthly pulled on 2026-07-02: expiry−30d = 2026-08-30 > full_end 2026-07-01) the span collapsed to `start >= end` and the "conservative never-skip" fallback returned the FULL `(full_start, full_end)` — the guard designed for a genuinely-dead span silently amplified a far-month contract into a 6.5-year history pull (chunk tier per CLAUDE.md §6). **THE LAW (operator decree, supersedes the interim recent-lookback approach reviewed in this PR's first iteration):** ONE window rule for every contract — strictly `[expiry − lookback, expiry] ∩ envelope`. NOT OPEN YET ⇒ fetch NOTHING: `default_fno_minute_window` returns `None` (ONLY when `expiry` is present AND `lookback_start >= full_end` on a VALID envelope); NEW pure `fno_window_opens_on(expiry, is_option)` = the ONE `expiry − lookback` anchor (COMMON); `historical_pull._resolve_minute_windows` OMITS a `None`-window contract from the map + logs one honest `fno.window_not_open` (contract, expiry, opens_on); `pull_contract_candles` resolves windows FIRST and builds the pull workload (`by_market`, `selected_symbols`, the #1026 empty-retry budget) from ONLY the in-window contracts — a map-absent symbol must never reach the ingest (it would fall back to the FULL range inside `_resolve_window`), so the skipped contract gets NO plan row, NO fetch, ZERO ledger rows; the report gains `contracts_not_yet_in_window` (+ `to_dict`). Once the calendar reaches `opens_on` the window OPENS with its FIXED start (`expiry − lookback`, never moving across daily pulls; only the end advances with the prev-day envelope). The `None`-expiry guard, the expired-before-envelope full-range fallback, and the degenerate/inverted envelope (`full_start >= full_end` — full-range, never `None`) are byte-identical to pre-fix; explicit operator dates OVERRIDE and can still pull ANY range (they never reach the helper — `explicit_dates=True` short-circuits verbatim, regression-pinned). **THE HOSTILE-REVIEW MAJOR, DISSOLVED BY THE LAW (moving-start ↔ ledger-GC interplay):** the interim recent-lookback approach anchored the far-expiry start to `full_end − lookback`, which ADVANCES every daily pull, while `WindowLedger.prune_superseded`'s trailing-END rule (DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001) assumes STABLE starts (`tiles.get(window_start)`) — so each daily pull would have stranded ONE un-collectable orphan row per (far-expiry contract, interval): unbounded ledger growth, empirically 5 pulls → 5 rows. The strict law ELIMINATES the moving anchor entirely — a not-yet-open contract writes NO row, an open contract's start is FIXED at `expiry − lookback` — so the EXISTING trailing-END rule collects the daily rows with NO new GC mechanism (5-simulated-daily-pulls through the REAL `plan_contract_windows` + prune path converge to ONE row, pinned). LEGACY pre-fix full-range orphans keep the STABLE `2020-01-01` anchor: INERT under the new stable-start default plan (off-tiling → kept — a BOUNDED one-time orphan per far-expiry contract×interval pulled during the buggy era, never re-fetched wholesale, a settled SUCCESS row never wrongly pruned) and STILL collected by the EXISTING shorter-end rule on any explicit full-range re-plan — both pinned. **VERIFIED 2026-07-02 (task venv, Python 3.12.3 + locally-built `fno_math`/`trading_core` wheels):** fails-before PROVEN behaviourally on BOTH prior baselines (origin/main → the far option resolves `(2020-01-01, 2026-07-01)`; the interim commit → `(2026-06-01, 2026-07-01)`; the law requires `None`); NEW tests — `test_default_far_expiry_option_not_open_returns_none` + `..._future_not_open_returns_none` + `..._boundary_lookback_start_equals_full_end` (opens NEXT day ⇒ None) + `test_default_near_expiry_just_inside_full_end_unchanged` (1-day window, stable start) + `test_default_window_start_is_stable_across_daily_pulls_once_open` + `test_fno_window_opens_on_option_and_future` + degenerate/inverted-envelope fallbacks (hostile-review NIT folded) + `test_resolve_minute_windows_far_expiry_not_open_skipped_and_logged` (CE opens_on 2026-08-30 / FUT 2026-07-31) + `..._open_contract_start_is_stable_across_days` + END-TO-END `test_pull_skips_not_yet_open_contracts_no_fetch_no_ledger` (LIVE-shaped mixed pull: vendor sees ZERO calls for the far pair, persisted ledger holds ZERO far rows, report counts 2, near chain byte-normal) + `test_pull_all_contracts_not_yet_open_is_a_clean_noop` + `test_resolve_minute_windows_explicit_overrides_far_expiry` + `test_plan_contract_windows_open_far_contract_stable_start_converges` (5 pulls → 1 row) + `test_legacy_far_expiry_full_range_row_inert_under_stable_start_plan` + `..._prunable_by_full_range_replan`; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict brutex` Success (309 files); `pyright` 0 errors on all touched files. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the VISIBLE consequence of the law — a far-month contract has NO candles in the lake until it enters its final 30d (options) / 60d (futures) window, so the `/movers` Far tier will honestly show "on the vendor calendar … but NO option contract candles pulled" (the DEC-MOVERS-CALENDAR-TIERS-001 #1034 `calendar_only_expiry` path) for stock monthlies until they open — that is the LAW working, not a data gap; an operator wanting a far contract earlier passes explicit dates (which override byte-identically); the skip is pull-PLANNING only — the keep-first idempotent sink + durable ledger mean nothing already stored changes (Golden Rule #7); 1129. **DEC-EMPTY-WINDOW-CIRCUIT-BREAKER-001 — mass-empty circuit breaker + un-cementable SKIPPED settles: clean-but-empty HTTP 200 bursts (the vendor soft-throttle shape [R2] / mis-addressed requests [R3]) can no longer PERMANENTLY settle >60-day-old windows as `SKIPPED` in ONE pull under a green "✅ Pull complete / No action needed" verdict — REVISED after a FIX-FIRST hostile review (2 MAJOR + 6 minors + 3 NITs) whose MAJOR-1 found the first cut FALSE-HALTING the operator's own 2020→today backfill** (2026-07-02; fixes the next CRITICAL from the committed pull-divergence register `docs/groww/pull-divergence-register.md` §1 rows R2/R3 per DEC-DOCTOR-LIVE-PROOF-KIT-001 #1120; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope / vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / pacing change — the 8 r/s + 500/min governor is untouched). **WHY (the register's finding):** the repo itself documents empty/HTML bodies as the observed live-throttle shape (`errors.py:174-190`), and the proven M&M-`&` case (DEC-GROWW-AMPERSAND-FALLBACK-001 #870) showed a mis-addressed request gets a clean-but-EMPTY 200 too — yet the old-gap fast-settle (DEC-OLD-GAP-FAST-SETTLE-001) treated an empty confirmed across an in-pull retry (two fetches landing SECONDS apart, inside the same throttle episode) on a >60-day-old window as "genuine no-data" and settled it terminal `SKIPPED` in one pull; on a 2020→today backfill essentially EVERY window is that old, so one throttle episode could convert real history into permanent gaps, silently. **WHAT (five arms):** **(1) Circuit breaker (COMMON — one implementation, both spines; REDESIGNED per hostile-review MAJOR-1):** `brutex/adapters/empty_circuit_breaker.py` `EmptySettleBreaker` — a per-pull-pass, thread-safe, O(1)-per-observation counter the spot spine (`ingest.py` `_fetch_window_raw`) AND the F&O spine (`option_ingest.py` `ingest_option_contract`) feed every fetched window's final shape into. Two trip rules, each keyed to a DIFFERENT throttle signature (the review's fix — the first cut's pull-wide consecutive counter + CUMULATIVE min-series gate false-tripped on ≥3 clustered late-listing prefixes: the worklist tail of late-listed NTM names on the real backfill, empty-dominated resumes, and small targeted pulls of recent F&O listings — all three now regression-pinned fail-before/pass-after at PRODUCTION defaults in `test_empty_circuit_breaker.py::TestFalseTripScenarios` + spine-level twins): **(rule 1, CONSECUTIVE — the mid-pull throttle)** trips only when the CURRENT consecutive counted-empty run (reset by any data window) (a) reaches `EMPTY_BREAKER_CONSECUTIVE_LIMIT=40`, (b) spans ≥ `EMPTY_BREAKER_MIN_SERIES=3` DISTINCT series **within the run itself** (run composition, NOT cumulative), and (c) contains ≥1 **post-data empty** — an empty from a series that already landed data THIS pull (a producing series going quiet is the throttle shape; a never-yet-producing series' leading empties are exactly a late-listing prefix and can NEVER satisfy (c)); **(rule 2, FRACTION — the throttle-from-pull-start, where no series ever lands data and rule 1 is structurally silent)** trips once counted empties ≥ `EMPTY_BREAKER_FRACTION_LIMIT=0.8` of ≥ `EMPTY_BREAKER_MIN_OBSERVATIONS=50` observed AND span ≥ `EMPTY_BREAKER_FRACTION_MIN_SERIES=10` distinct counted series (NEW floor + env `BRUTEX_EMPTY_BREAKER_FRACTION_MIN_SERIES`) — a targeted pull of ≤4 symbols (≤8 series at both intervals) stays under it, the ~750-underlying bulk universe crosses it within ~5 symbols even fully sequentially. All knobs env-overridable with fail-safe parsing + the `BRUTEX_EMPTY_BREAKER=off` kill switch. A trip raises `MassEmptySettleHalt` (naming empty/observed/consecutive counts + the three candidate causes — Golden Rule #1), a `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` member on BOTH runners (+ `pull_jobs._is_pull_halt`, + the CLI fetch `_pull_halt_errors` Telegram set). **CALIBRATION CORRECTED (hostile-review MAJOR-2 — the first cut's arithmetic was wrong):** spot 1-minute tiles at **30-day** windows (`groww/chunks.py`), so a 2020→today (~2,370 days) single-symbol backfill is **~80 windows at 1m** (+~14 at 1day) — NOT the "~27 at 90-day tiles" the first cut derived its defaults from; under the redesign the 40-limit no longer needs to out-size any prefix (prefixes are structurally ineligible) and is purely the halt-latency knob (40 confirmed-empty windows ≈ ≥80 vendor calls ≈ 10-15 s at the 8 r/s ceiling), and `MIN_OBSERVATIONS=50` is honestly re-labelled a sample-size floor, NOT a single-symbol guard (one symbol's ~80 1m windows CROSS 50 — the small-pull guard is the series floor). **(2) Expected-empty knowledge (register rule 4):** three exclusions — (a) the injectable `expected_empty(symbol, window_end)` predicate (the F&O runner wires the confirmed-deep far-OTM strike budget via `_deep_strike_expected_empty`); (b) NEW per-call `expected` hint: both spines pass `WindowLedger.is_expected_empty_recheck(key)` — a window whose OWN ledger row is already `EMPTY` (a prior pull saw it empty: the empty-dominated RESUME re-confirmation) or is `REOPENED`-marked (a deliberate `brutex reopen-skipped` re-check — breaker-exempt by design, so reopen + re-pull can never re-trip endlessly; minor M-1) is observed but never counted; (c) leading-empty RETRO-CLEARING (a pre-listing prefix un-counts the moment its series lands data). **(3) Un-cementable settles:** `WindowLedger.reopen_skipped(market=, security_id=, limit=)` demotes `SKIPPED` → retryable `FAILED` (`empty_streak` reset, `last_error=REOPENED_MARKER`), surfaced as `brutex reopen-skipped` (`--symbol`/`--market`/`--limit`); the selection pass is honestly O(rows log rows) (the deterministic `sorted` that buys the bounded `--limit` sample — NIT fix; each re-open O(1)); **minor M-2:** the CLI command now runs its load→mutate→save INSIDE the account-wide pull single-flight lock (`pull_singleflight_lock`) and REFUSES loudly (`EXIT_USER_ERROR`) while a pull holds it — a mid-pull re-open would be silently overwritten by the pull's next whole-file ledger persist (doc note in the command help + docstring). **(4) Honest verdicts:** `WindowLedger.newly_settled_skipped` per-pull tally; `classify_pull` gains `settled_skipped` + `mass_empty_cause`; the `mass_empty_halt` `PullVerdictKind` (needs_operator=True, ranked under `auth_expired`); EVERY settling verdict names the count + the re-verify path, and (minor M-1) both the halt action and the settle note now explain the BOUNDED re-verify (`brutex reopen-skipped --limit N`), that REOPENED re-checks are breaker-exempt (no endless re-trip), and the `BRUTEX_EMPTY_BREAKER_*` tuning envs + kill switch; **minor M-4:** `settled_skipped > SETTLED_SKIPPED_OPERATOR_THRESHOLD=50` (named config constant; the verdict layer stays pure — no env read) flips `needs_operator=True` on ANY kind incl. `clean`/`known_gap_only` — a mass write-off is confirmed by a human once (the first full backfill legitimately trips this once, by design); **minor M-3:** the dashboard SPOT halt handler in `pull_controller.pull_all_spot` now fires the CRITICAL Telegram `emit_pull_halt_alert` from the catch site (the caught halt never reaches the job layer's escaping-exception alert path — parity with CLI/F&O restored), + an honest comment that `final_still_failed` UNDERCOUNTS after a mid-pass halt (the aborted pass never appended — NIT); **minor M-5:** the F&O bulk route (`historical_pull._run_phase`) now CATCHES the halt (drain + ledger persist still run in the `finally`), folds `mass_empty_cause`/`settled_skipped` onto `_PhaseResult` → `HistoricalPullReport` and exposes the SAME polished verdict via `HistoricalPullReport.verdict` (classify_pull — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON with `BulkSpotReport.verdict`) + `to_dict()["verdict"]` + a halt note + the M-3 alert at ITS catch site. **(5) Doctor accuracy:** `doctor --live` stage-5 [R2/R3] wording says settles are breaker-guarded + reversible (golden fixture regenerated in-PR). **CodeQL fix:** `MassEmptySettleHalt.__init__` restructured to a SINGLE `super().__init__` call site (choose the message, then one base-init — the multiple-`__init__` alert shape is structurally gone), and a zero-arg construction renders "(unspecified rule)" instead of the degenerate "( rule)" hole (NIT). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the rules are HEURISTICS; documented blind spots (module docstring): (a) a throttle-from-start against a pull SMALLER than the 10-series fraction floor (e.g. the very first 3-index backfill, 6 series) does NOT halt — the settled-count note + the M-4 needs_operator threshold + `doctor --live` stage 5 are the nets; (b) a throttle starting exactly at a symbol boundary of a strictly SEQUENTIAL pull (only never-yet-producing series empty) is shape-identical to a late-listing tail — rule 1 silent, rule 2 diluted; same nets (pinned as an explicit honest-envelope test); (c) empties re-confirming prior-EMPTY rows are uncounted, so a throttle spanning two consecutive pulls is under-counted on the second — those settles ride the across-pull ≥3-sightings streak standard. 1132. **DEC-FETCH-PER-WINDOW-GATE-HONESTY-001 — the fetch-per-window CI bench gate now measures the PRODUCTION quantity (real default windows → real 30-day chunk tiling), pins a ceiling DERIVED from the replayed chain (≈ 2.404, measured 2.399 fpw) instead of the flattering single-chunk 1.2, and ASSERTS the honest 8h verdict: at the worst-case 3 r/s the audited 48,145-window production scope does NOT fit 8 hours (true wall-clock ≈ 10.7 h)** (2026-07-02; bench-test + docs ONLY — ZERO `brutex/` source change, the pull's fetch behaviour is BYTE-IDENTICAL; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, CLAUDE.md §3; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **THE DEFECT (gate honesty):** a verified forensic audit of a real production pull measured **2.59 vendor fetches per `(contract, interval)` window**, while the DEC-FETCH-PER-WINDOW-GUARANTEE-001 (MIGRATION.md #1026) gate (`tests/bench/test_fetch_per_window_guarantee.py`) read `1.198` and PASSED. Root cause: the gate's replay range (`2025-01-01 → 2025-01-31`, 30 days) tiled into ONE 30-day vendor chunk (the 1-minute tier of `docs/groww/api-reference/03-backtesting.md` "Backtesting Data Limits", `brutex/adapters/groww/chunks.py`), whereas the PRODUCTION default windows do NOT fit one chunk: an option's default span is `expiry − 30d → expiry + 1d` = **31 days → 2 chunks** (DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 #894, now the strict window law of DEC-FNO-FAR-EXPIRY-WINDOW-001 #1127) and a future's is `expiry − 60d → expiry + 1d` = **61 days → 3 chunks** (DEC-FUTURES-LOOKBACK-60D-001). The gate measured ONLY the window-level EMPTY-retry amplification (#1026's actual lever) and was structurally blind to the chunk tiling every production window pays, so its "8h fits" arithmetic did not hold in production — a lab quantity presented as a production guarantee (the Golden Rule #10 failure this entry fixes). **Re-derived on CURRENT main FIRST (the world changed since the audit):** PR #1052 (DEC-PULL-FORENSIC-WAVE1-001 #1126 — the single-admission-per-fetch law: 1 rate admission per physical fetch) changes admission ACCOUNTING, not fetch counts; PR #1057 (DEC-FNO-FAR-EXPIRY-WINDOW-001 #1127) SKIPS not-yet-open far contracts entirely (zero fetches AND zero windows), shrinking a pull's SCOPE but not the per-open-window cost. So the honest per-window cost on current main = structural chunks × bounded empty-retry passes ≈ 2.4 — consistent with the audited 2.59, whose residual carries live transient retries + a different liquid/dead mix (neither replayed; stated, not hidden). **What shipped — the gate rewrite (`tests/bench/test_fetch_per_window_guarantee.py`):** (1) **the PRODUCTION-shaped gate** `test_production_shaped_fetch_per_window_gate` — the replay derives every contract's window from the REAL window law (`contract_bounds.default_fno_minute_window`, exactly as `historical_pull._resolve_minute_windows` does — nothing inlined) and every structural chunk count from the REAL planner (`chunks.plan_candle_windows`), then runs the 162-option + 1-future chain through the REAL `run_groww_option_ingest` spine with the #1026 adaptive empty-retry budget against a fetch-COUNTING SDK. **MEASURED: 391 fetches / 163 windows = 2.399 fpw** (option chunks {2}, future chunks {3}; 71 bars stored = one distinct bar per liquid chunk — no data lost). The ceiling is DERIVED from the replayed chain, never hand-picked: per option window `structural chunks (2) × the pinned single-chunk pass allowance (1.2)`, per liquid future window its structural chunks once → `(162·2·1.2 + 3)/163 ≈ 2.404`; a structural FLOOR (`Σ chunks / windows ≈ 2.006`) plus an option-chunks-`≥ 2` pin guarantee the gate can never silently degrade back to the single-chunk lab shape that flattered production. (2) **the ORIGINAL single-chunk quantity stays independently pinned** — `test_empty_retry_bounding_single_chunk_pin` (bounded `194 / 162 = 1.198 ≤ 1.2`) + the unchanged teeth test `test_baseline_without_bounding_exceeds_ceiling` (baseline `418 / 162 = 2.580 > 1.2`, same 34 bars stored with and without the budget) — so #1026's real lever (the adaptive empty-retry bounding, `strike_chain_bound.py`) keeps its own regression gate, now explicitly labelled a LAB quantity. (3) **the honest 8h arithmetic (Golden Rule #10 — never fake feasibility):** at the worst-case sustained `3 r/s` (the AIMD soft floor, CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6), `3 × 3600 × 8h = 86,400` fetches cover `86,400 / 2.399 ≈ 36,018` windows — BELOW the 48,145-window production scope the #1026 forensic audit measured (122,243 fetches / 48,145 windows), so **8h @ 3 r/s does NOT fit the audited scope; the TRUE achievable wall-clock is `48,145 × 2.399 / 3 r/s ≈ 10.7 h`**. The gate ASSERTS the infeasibility (`86,400 / fpw < 48,145`) so the claim can never go stale in EITHER direction: a genuine structural improvement (a wider vendor chunk tier, a write-time manifest, a shorter default span) flips the pin and FAILS LOUDLY, forcing the ceiling + this ledger claim to be consciously re-derived — the forcing function the stale "1.2 / FITS" claim lacked. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the replay is a CONTROLLED deterministic chain (bulk deep-OTM + empty, a narrow liquid band, one liquid future) — it measures OUR pipeline's structural + empty-retry fetch cost, NOT live vendor 429 storms (those ride the separate transient ladder, untouched — DEC-GROWW-SERVER-ERROR-RETRY-001 #883); ✅ the 48,145 reference is the PRE-#1127 audited scope — the far-contract skip has since shrunk the per-pull scope by an UNMEASURED amount, so the infeasibility verdict is stated against the audited reference and a fresh production audit would be needed to claim a current number (NOT claimed); ✅ at the production per-second ceiling `8 r/s` (`GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`, DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 — vendor-SUSTAINED 8 is UNVERIFIED per CLAUDE.md §6) the same audited scope would take ≈ 4.0 h, but the gate deliberately pins the worst-case 3 r/s; 1135. **DEC-PULL-FORENSIC-WAVE3-001 — forensic-audit Wave 3: SIX re-verified pull-path defects fixed in one wave — the Phase-2 lost-contracts BLOCKER (a settled cell whose contract fetch failed is now REBUILT from the registry's persisted expiries), the dead cold-start ledger seed (reconcile now runs BEFORE plan), the premature daily resample (now AFTER the async-pipeline drains), the fresh-write duplicate-timestamp leak (keep-first within-batch de-dup), the dead CLI timeout AIMD ladder (on_timeout wired), and the stale CLI ceiling comments.** (2026-07-02; Wave 3 of the forensic-audit series — DEC-PULL-FORENSIC-WAVE1-001 #1126 → DEC-PULL-FORENSIC-WAVE2-001 #1128. A read-only recon agent re-verified ALL TEN remaining audit findings at HEAD 97204033 with file:line evidence — every one CONFIRMED (unlike Wave 2's 3-of-4 phantoms); the six code-only/zero-risk fixes ship here, built by FOUR PARALLEL isolated-worktree implementers each independently hostile-reviewed to a SHIP verdict before assembly.) **FIX #4 (BLOCKER · DEC-PHASE2-REGISTRY-REBUILD-001):** `universe_phases.run_two_phase` built Phase-2 contract jobs ONLY from this run's in-memory Phase-1 discoveries; Phase 1's settled skip includes `expiries_only`, so a cell that settled in run 1 with FAILED contract jobs was dropped from run 2's Phase 1 → absent from `expiries_by_cell` → NO contract job ever rebuilt → the year's contracts lost forever. FIXED at the ONE common seam: `contract_jobs_from` gains keyword-only `persisted: Iterable[ContractJob]` (set-de-duped, sorted union; empty default byte-identical) + `run_two_phase(persisted_jobs=…)`; `metadata_pull.pull_expiries_contracts` builds `persisted_jobs` from `registry.list_expiries()` grid-restricted to this run's (exchange, underlying) pairs (injected read, no global state; a selective pull never resurrects other underlyings), threaded into BOTH the run and the Phase-2 progress denominator (an all-cells-skipped pull's bar reads n/n, never n/0); the existing settled-contract skip still filters the union so a healthy re-run issues ZERO extra calls (run-3 convergence pinned). HONEST caveats (hostile-review folded): a recovered cell's coverage ROW stays `expiries_only`/`contracts_pulled=0` (display under-count only — attribution exists only at discovery time; explicit non-goal); an expired expiry that GENUINELY returns zero contracts is re-pulled once per pull (recovery-over-data-loss direction, governor-bounded — the recon's #12 confirmation-count fix is the Wave-4 companion that closes this properly). **FIX #7 (MAJOR):** `pull_controller` called `plan_windows` BEFORE `reconcile_ledger_with_lake` at both call sites while the reconcile seed is ABSENT-only (`seed_lake_success` never overwrites a PLANNED row) — so the cold-start seed was a permanent no-op and a lost/corrupt ledger + populated lake re-fetched the ENTIRE history. FIXED: reconcile now runs BEFORE plan at both sites (+ the misleading comment corrected); seed semantics untouched. **FIX #15 (MAJOR):** `_resample_daily_after_pull` ran BEFORE the `finally`'s `_drain_fetch_pipeline`/`_drain_write_consumer` while the async pipeline is default-ON — the daily PDH/PDL anchor was derived from an INCOMPLETE 1-minute lake. FIXED: the resample runs AFTER both drains via a `fetch_phases_ok` latch (drains still run on every failure path — byte-identical failure behavior, existing suites police it). **FIX #11 (MAJOR · DEC-FRESH-WRITE-BATCH-DEDUP-001):** `parquet_writer` sorted but never de-duplicated the incoming batch, so a corrupt vendor payload with duplicate timestamps stored BOTH rows on a fresh-partition write (and a settled month is never rewritten — the dupes persisted). FIXED: keep-first within-batch de-dup by timestamp before the fresh render — the SAME rule `_merge_write` already applies against the existing partition; a VALUE-conflicting within-batch dupe records the existing BarConflict surface; the sibling `option_parquet_writer` was audited and is already safe (its fresh branch de-dups via `.unique(keep="first")`). **FIX #16 (MINOR):** the CLI live pull bound only `pace`/`on_success`/`on_rate_limit` — `on_timeout` was never wired, so the AIMD step-down ladder was DEAD for 5xx/timeout storms on `brutex fetch` (the dashboard wires it; `run_ingest` accepts it). FIXED: `on_timeout` bound + threaded, mirroring the dashboard; a ceiling-consistency guard test pins the wired ceiling to `GROWW_RATE_LIMIT_RPS_CEILING`. **FIX #17 (MINOR):** stale `cli.py` comments claiming the ceiling is "5 r/s (lowered 8 → 5)" corrected to the live 8.0 / DEC-GROWW-RATE-CEILING-8-002 (comment-only; the constant + every rate value UNTOUCHED — Golden Rule #6). 1134. **DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-RESCUE-001 — the lost-ledger lake rescue ACTUALLY rescues (the enclosure off-by-one made it DEAD CODE), a failed ledger reload is LOUD, concurrent pulls can no longer clobber each other's ledger rows (flock + read-merge-write save), and the settled-window skip is finally VISIBLE ("skipped N already-pulled windows (no vendor hit)")** (2026-07-02; pull-side ledger/report/observability only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change). **ROOT (verified investigation, file:line on main):** the dashboard pull's settled-window skip works when the durable ledger survives (a two-run repro shows run 2 = 0 vendor calls), but on the operator's machine the ledger was evidently EMPTY at run-2 start and the safety net that should have rescued it could NEVER fire: `seed_enclosed_windows`'s enclosure test (`window_ledger_store.py:590` pre-fix) required `window.end <= last_date`, comparing the fetch-EXCLUSIVE window end against the bar-INCLUSIVE lake `last_date` — for a default-window F&O contract the ledger key ends at `expiry + 1 day` (`contract_bounds.py` `default_fno_minute_window` via `option_ingest.py` `_fno_reconcile_candidates`) while the last stored bar is ON expiry, so the test was `expiry + 1 <= expiry`: ALWAYS false — `reconcile_fno_ledger_windows` deterministically seeded 0 windows even over a maximally dense lake, and a lost ledger re-downloaded the whole chain (~1,100 wasted calls). Additionally (a) `load_window_ledger` silently degraded to an empty ledger on a read error (WARNING only — the pull never SAID it was re-verifying everything); (b) `save_window_ledger` whole-file-replaced `ledger.parquet` with NO cross-process lock, so two concurrent pulls on one lake last-writer-wins clobbered each other's rows (the exact silent-loss class DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 closed for bar partitions — but not for the ledger); (c) window skips logged only at DEBUG (`option_ingest.py` / `ingest.py`), so an operator could never SEE the skip engaging. **FOUR FIXES:** (1) **enclosure off-by-one** — the COMMON seed core `seed_enclosed_windows` (shared by the spot `reconcile_ledger_windows` AND the F&O `reconcile_fno_ledger_windows`, so both benefit consistently) now tests `first_date <= start AND (end − 1 day) <= last_date` (boundary pinned exactly: `end − 1 == last_date` seeds; `end − 1 == last_date + 1` does not), PLUS a **live-edge guard**: a window whose coverage INCLUDES the current IST day (`end − 1 >= today_ist`) is NEVER seeded — a mid-session partial store puts a bar on today without the session being complete and a span-level check cannot tell partial from complete, so the trailing live-edge window is conservatively left to the fetch (data completeness preserved; the F&O reconcile injects its clamp clock's date so reconcile == plan == fetch stays deterministic). (2) **LOUD load failure** — a ledger file that EXISTED but could not be read marks the degraded empty ledger `WindowLedger.load_failed=True`; both pull drivers surface it (`BulkSpotReport.ledger_load_failed` + `HistoricalPullReport.ledger_load_failed` + to_dict) and the notes announce "window ledger reload FAILED — running full re-verify pull (no skip)" (historical note prefix + the /universe pipeline note prefix + `universe.pull_all.ledger_reload_failed` / `historical.pull.ledger_reload_failed` WARNINGs; the store-level `window_ledger.load_failed` WARNING stays). Never crashes the pull; a MISSING file stays an honest fresh start, not a failure. (3) **flock + merge the save** — `save_window_ledger` now holds the COMMON `partition_write_lock` (DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 mechanics) keyed on the ledger path across a READ-MERGE-WRITE: the on-disk rows are merged with the in-memory rows per key via the NEW pure `merge_ledger_rows` — disk-only rows (a concurrent writer's work) are KEPT, memory-only rows are written, and a same-key semantic conflict is resolved by the documented total order: the MORE-SETTLED status wins (SUCCESS/SKIPPED > EMPTY > FAILED > PLANNED), then the newer `last_attempt_at`, then the higher `attempts`, then a deterministic full-row tie-break (writer-order-independent). Rows this ledger deliberately pruned (`prune_superseded`) are TOMBSTONED (`WindowLedger.pruned_keys()`) so the merge never resurrects them (DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001 stays won). A bounded lock-acquire expiry (`PartitionLockTimeout`) SKIPS that save with a loud `window_ledger.save_lock_timeout` WARNING (the next flush / pull-end save retries) — never a mid-flush crash; disk-full still maps to the pull-wide `LakeWriteHalt` (DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-WRITE-HALT-001 unchanged). (4) **VISIBLE skips** — ONE aggregate INFO per spine driver pass (`ingest.windows_skipped_settled` in `run_ingest.py` + `option.ingest.windows_skipped_settled` in `option_ingest.py`, per-window skips stay DEBUG) + `windows_skipped` folded into `BulkSpotReport` / `HistoricalPullReport` (each phase's FIRST pass — later until-clean rounds re-skip the same settled windows by design, so summing passes would double-count) + the notes render "skipped N already-pulled window(s) (no vendor hit)" (historical note + the /universe pipeline note, spot + F&O summed). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** stated plainly — the rescue was largely DEAD pre-fix (the F&O reconcile seeded 0 windows EVER; on a DEFAULT floor→today spot pull the daily whole-range window and the trailing sub-daily window were equally dead — their exclusive end sits at today while the storable `last_date` is at most yesterday; only interior sub-daily tiles and historical sub-range pulls ever seeded), so this fix GROWS the span-masking surface from ~zero to LIVE: the enclosure is a SPAN test, not a DENSITY test — a window inside the lake's `[first_date, last_date]` seeds SUCCESS even if it has an INTERIOR HOLE, and on a lost ledger that window is then auto-skipped; the compensating, operator-visible signal is the /completeness scoreboard (density-based — it reads the LAKE, not the ledger), NOT the fetch-time interior-gap detector (DEC-INTERIOR-GAP-DETECT-001 #1031), which never sees a seeded window (skipped before any fetch). The load-bearing safety stands prominent: `seed_lake_success` seeds strictly ONLY-IF-ABSENT so a FAILED/EMPTY/PLANNED row is never masked; the merge conflict rule prefers settledness over recency by DESIGN (an absent row is never skippable, so the failure mode of a wrong merge pick is a redundant idempotent re-fetch, never a masked window); the merge-save adds one O(N) on-disk read per save (the adaptive flush throttle self-paces on the measured save duration, so it never dominates); EMPTY-below-threshold behaviour is UNCHANGED and PINNED (still re-fetches, settles SKIPPED at exactly 3). **Regression tests (fails-before verified by stashing the source fix and re-running):** (a) `TestFnoDefaultWindowRescue::test_dense_lake_seeds_all_expired_default_window_contracts` — was `assert 0 == 3` on main (the dead rescue); (b) `test_lost_ledger_second_pull_makes_zero_vendor_calls` — two in-process `pull_contract_candles` runs over a fake SDK + REAL Parquet lake with `ledger.parquet` deleted between them: run 2 makes ZERO F&O vendor calls (on main: `assert ['NSE-NIFTY-2…', …] == []` — the wholesale re-fetch); (c) `TestSaveMergeCrossProcess` — the two-writer sequence + 8-thread interleaved savers lose NO row and the same-key conflict keeps the settled row (on main: last-writer-wins clobber); (d) `test_corrupt_ledger_reload_failure_is_announced` + `test_ledger_reload_failure_is_loud` — the note/report/WARNING surface; (e) `test_second_pull_reports_skipped_settled_windows` + the two spine INFO tests — skip counts in report + INFO log; (f) `test_empty_below_threshold_still_refetches_and_settles_at_three` — the no-over-skip pin; plus the live-edge over-skip pin `test_live_edge_window_with_partial_today_bar_not_seeded` (on main: `assert 1 == 0` — the old rule would have seeded a window covering a possibly-partial today). **Coverage/gates (verified 2026-07-02 on the repo 3.12 venv):** every touched source file at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** — `window_ledger.py` (167/44), `window_ledger_store.py` (221/64), `option_ingest.py` (339/90), `run_ingest.py` (149/30), `historical_pull.py` (308/68), `pipeline_pull.py` (87/22), `pull_controller.py` (473/108 via its curated 5-file suite); 625 tests across the eight touched suites + 302 broader ledger-touching integration/CLI/doctor tests + 82 report-consumer route/stress tests all green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on `brutex tests`; `mypy --strict brutex` — ZERO new errors (the only package error is the PRE-EXISTING missing-`cma`-stub artifact in untouched `engine/stage3_refine.py`, byte-identical on pristine origin/main in this environment); `pyright` on all 14 touched files — 0 errors, warnings byte-identical to main (16 pre-existing). **Files:** `brutex/data/window_ledger.py` (`load_failed` + prune tombstones + `pruned_keys`), `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py` (enclosure fix + live-edge guard + `merge_ledger_rows`/`LedgerRow` + flock read-merge-write save + loud load flag), `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py` (today_ist wiring + docstring + driver INFO), `brutex/adapters/groww/run_ingest.py` (driver INFO), `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` (`BulkSpotReport.windows_skipped`/`ledger_load_failed` + WARNING + done-INFO fold), `brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py` (pass/phase/report skip + reload-failure threading + note clauses), `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_pull.py` (the /universe note fold), `tests/unit/test_window_ledger.py`, `tests/unit/test_window_ledger_store.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_option_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_run_ingest.py`, `tests/unit/test_pull_historical.py`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline_pull.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-RESCUE-001. **Builds on** DEC-FNO-LEDGER-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (the rescue this wakes), DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-001 (the unified skip authority), DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 (#887 — the flock mechanics reused), DEC-WINDOW-TRAILING-GC-001 (the GC the tombstones preserve). (Ledger: #1134 — renumbered from the provisional #1133 after PR #1061 (DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR3B-001) took #1133 on main first; = max-existing + 1, re-checked immediately before push per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001; the DEC-ID is the stable handle.)

(2) **NEW PyO3 `trading_core.seconds_of_day`** (`python.rs` `py_seconds_of_day` + a pure `seconds_of_day_impl` twin, no-libpython unit-covered) with the RANGE guard AT the FFI boundary [hostile-review C3]: `hour <= 23`, `minute <= 59`, `second <= 59` → a clean `ValueError` naming the offending component — never an inner `overflow-checks` panic → SIGABRT under `panic="abort"` (a garbage `hour = 2_000_000` would overflow `hour * 3600` unguarded; unit-tested on BOTH the impl and the wheel). Re-exported from the wheel `__init__.py`; the facade surface golden updated DELIBERATELY (+`seconds_of_day`) [C8]. (3) **The three call-site swaps:** `vocabulary/evaluator.py` Group-8 tod + `engine/stage1a.py` VWAP tod now call the binding; `feed/bar_metadata.py::_seconds_of_day` DELEGATES to it (its callers/tests byte-unchanged), and the regular 09:15 session-open seconds is HOISTED to a module constant via a new `_session_open_seconds` (the Muhurat/half-day dynamic open keeps the per-call derivation — both branches unit-tested) [C16]. A SOURCE-SCAN guard test asserts no `* 3600` tod arithmetic remains in the three eval-path modules — NARROWLY scoped: `calendars/nse.py` keeps its calendar-construction copies DELIBERATELY (out of the eval path, the named exclusion) [C13]. (4) **The constant-cost-sensitive perf gate [C5]:** NEW `tests/bench/test_tod_seam_bench.py` — a same-process comparative micro-bench asserting the binding's per-call cost ≤ `max(5 µs, 60 × inline)`; the design review PROVED a cross-tier ratio bench is mathematically BLIND to a uniform per-bar constant (both tiers move equally), so the comparative bound with an absolute floor is the real gate. **MEASURED (stated, not promised):** binding `57 ns/call` vs inline `81 ns/call` — the Rust binding is FASTER than the Python arithmetic it replaced; Stage-1A end-to-end `15,159 → 14,869 ns/bar` (−1.9%, within noise — NO regression; the design's Option-B fallback trigger [>5% per-bar regression] is nowhere near, so the civil-components ABI fallback is NOT needed). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ bit-identity proven the strong way — the 400-case vocab golden + the Python↔Rust bit-identity golden + the stage1a/VWAP suites all re-run GREEN THROUGH the seam (same inputs → same masks, byte-for-byte); ✅ the Stage-1A path still derives the same value twice per bar (its own VWAP site + the evaluator's site — now both via the seam): the redundant double-derivation is KNOWN DEFERRED DEBT [C12], threading one value through is a larger refactor, out of scope; ✅ the seam is a per-bar CONSTANT-cost swap (measured net-negative here), NOT an O() change; ✅ the tod ORACLE stays independent — the test-side inline expressions are marked do-NOT-clean-up (their independence from the seam under test is the point) [C16]. **Coverage/gates (verified 2026-07-02 via the repo 3.12 venv + the maturin-rebuilt wheel):** `brutex/feed/bar_metadata.py` 100.00% line+branch standalone from its stem suite; `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py` 100.00% via the EXACT ci.yml 19a static-gate invocation (`tests/unit/test_vocabulary.py` alone); `brutex/engine` 100.00% via the EXACT whole-engine static gate (`tests/unit/test_engine_*.py`, 1354 tests) — every touched module verified against its REAL gate invocation (the #1064 static-gate lesson applied); NO new evaluator/bar_metadata test STEMS created — the existing `test_vocabulary.py` / `test_bar_metadata.py` files are EXTENDED [C6]; cargo fmt + clippy `-D warnings` + test GREEN across default / `python` / `serde` / `python,serde`; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on every touched file; `codegen_vocab.py --check` exit 0. **Files:** `rust/trading-core/src/indicators/metadata.rs` (factored fn + tests), `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs` (guarded binding + impl + tests), `rust/trading-core/src/lib.rs` (re-export), `rust/trading-core/python/trading_core/__init__.py` (re-export), `tests/golden/test_math_facade_golden.py` (surface +1), `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py` + `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` + `brutex/feed/bar_metadata.py` (call-site swaps + hoist), `tests/unit/test_vocabulary.py` + `tests/unit/test_bar_metadata.py` (extended), `tests/bench/test_tod_seam_bench.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-TOD-SECONDS-RUST-SEAM-001. **Builds on** DEC-SPEC-IDENTITY-WIRING-001 (#1138 — PR-4b sub-PR 4, whose hostile-reviewed design v2 specifies this sub-PR), DEC-NIFTY-ROLL-METADATA-001 (the shared metadata derivation this factors from), DEC-STRATEGYSPEC-CORE-001 (#1027). 1139. **DEC-LAKE-WRITE-UNIQUE-001 — dup-train PR-1: the write-side duplicate-bar invariant is COMPLETED and its blast radius bounded — the vendor-duplicate collapse is now COUNTED + WARNED on every write path (never silent), an ALREADY-poisoned month file SELF-HEALS on the next merge touch (even the added==0 no-op path — before this the poisoned bytes were returned forever), the read-side collapse becomes keep-FIRST + logged (was silent last-wins), a P9 strictly-increasing tripwire guards every render, and ONE poisoned symbol degrades to a counted skip / quarantine verdict instead of "whole /movers page 500s / whole pre-build stage aborts / derive-timeframes route 500s"** (2026-07-03; write-invariant + read-resilience only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-SCHEMA change — partition layout + columns byte-identical, only stored-row uniqueness + observability + resilience). **ROOT (forensically measured, deterministically reproduced across two pulls):** the vendor payload can physically carry duplicate 1-minute rows — 135 duplicates measured in one ADANIENT January window. While this PR was in flight, main merged DEC-FRESH-WRITE-BATCH-DEDUP-001 (#1137, PR #1062 Wave-3 finding #11) closing the FRESH-render storage hole itself (`_dedup_batch`, per-merge_mode, fresh branch only) — this PR **ADOPTS that helper VERBATIM (never re-implemented, never fought — the #1038 reconcile discipline)** and completes the remaining, non-overlapping gaps the forensic triage named: (b) `_merge_write`'s no-op path returned an already-poisoned closed-month file's bytes forever (`added==0` → no rewrite, so a pre-#1137 poisoned lake NEVER self-healed); (c) `_read_existing_bars` collapsed stored duplicates silently LAST-wins (violating the DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 keep-first law, logging nothing); (d) NEITHER branch reported the collapse COUNT (silent normalisation); (e) blast radius — a poisoned symbol's `ResampleInputError` (the #1125 DEC-RESAMPLER-INPUT-GUARD-001 tripwire) was NOT in `movers_read_skip_errors` (one poisoned symbol 500'd the whole /movers page), escaped `run_gated_prebuild`'s `(ValueError, OSError)` per-symbol catch (one poisoned symbol aborted the whole pre-build stage), and 500'd `POST /api/v1/universe/derive-timeframes`. **FIVE FIXES:** (1) **collapse observability** — `write()` counts the batch's duplicate timestamps (one O(batch) set) and emits ONE aggregated `lake.vendor_duplicate_rows` WARNING per write (symbol/interval/window/count) covering BOTH branches (fresh collapses via the adopted #1137 `_dedup_batch`, merge via its timestamp-keyed dict — both previously silent); a differing pair still records a `BarConflict` through the EXISTING machinery (`ingest.conflict.summary` picks it up with zero new plumbing; the options writer `option_parquet_writer.py` was already safe on both branches — the reference pattern); (2) **merge self-heal** — `_merge_write` compares the stored file's PHYSICAL row count (NEW `_stored_physical_rows`, an O(footer) pyarrow `num_rows` read — no column decode, so the steady-state no-op re-pull pays only a metadata read) against the unique-timestamp count and FORCES a deduped rewrite even when `added == 0`, logging `lake.partition.dedup_healed` (kept/dropped); the rewrite rides the normal atomic write under the partition locks `write()` ALREADY holds on this path (verified — never re-acquired); (3) **keep-FIRST read collapse** — `_read_existing_bars` (BOTH decode paths: columnar + the per-row overflow fallback) keeps the FIRST physical row per timestamp — honouring keep-first — and logs `lake.partition.duplicate_collapsed` via ONE shared `_log_duplicate_collapse` (never silent); (4) **blast-radius hardening** — `ResampleInputError` added to the COMMON `movers_read_skip_errors` set (a poisoned symbol is SKIPPED + counted on /movers, /db, sweep-results — never a 500) and to `gated_prebuild`'s per-symbol quarantine (NEW `_PER_SYMBOL_DATA_ERRORS = (ValueError, OSError, ResampleInputError)` — deliberately the NARROW subclass, NOT `DataLakeError` broadly, so `LakeWriteHalt` STILL propagates as a pull-wide global stop, regression-pinned in BOTH phases), which makes the derive-timeframes `?symbols=` route return the honest per-symbol gated verdict (200, poisoned symbol named in `failed`, healthy symbols built) instead of a 500; (5) **P9 writer tripwire** — NEW `_assert_strictly_increasing` runs after dedup before EVERY render (fresh + merge); a violation raises a loud `WriterError` NAMING the partition (impossible post-dedup — a genuine invariant assert, covered by direct unit tests of the assertion path). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the self-heal fires on the next WRITE touch of a poisoned partition, NOT proactively — a poisoned closed month nobody re-pulls stays poisoned until touched (the read-side chokepoint + the full lake auto-heal sweep are PR-2/PR-3, explicitly OUT OF SCOPE); the footer-probe failure edge (pyarrow cannot read a footer polars just parsed — essentially unreachable) SKIPS the heal for that write with a logged `lake.partition.rowcount_probe_failed` rather than guessing (never mis-heals; pinned); the fresh-dedup semantics are #1137's per-merge_mode rule VERBATIM (latest-wins takes the later in-batch occurrence — the merge-mirror convergence rule), not re-litigated here; the self-heal READ collapse (`_read_existing_bars` + its per-row twin) is deliberately MODE-INDEPENDENT keep-FIRST — for a poisoned stored file healed under `latest-wins` it keeps the FIRST physical occurrence where the fresh latest-wins in-batch rule would keep the LATER one (an ACCEPTED, documented divergence, pinned by `test_latest_wins_heal_still_keeps_first_physical_row`: only the derived-1day path uses latest-wins, a PHYSICAL duplicate daily timestamp is implausible there, and the production keep-first spine is unaffected); the dedup count is one O(batch) set + the tripwire O(n) + the probe O(footer) — each strictly cheaper than the Parquet render it guards, NOT zero. **Fails-before (verbatim, re-measured against LIVE origin/main 563605d8 — post-#1137 — by checking the three source files out to main and re-running):** `22 failed, 40 passed in 6.64s` — still failing on live main: the WARNING tests (`test_identical_dups_store_unique_timestamps_and_warn` — #1137 stores unique but stays SILENT), ALL heal tests (`test_noop_merge_on_poisoned_closed_month_still_heals` — the poisoned bytes returned verbatim), the keep-first/collapse-log tests, the tripwire + probe suites, `test_spot_ingest_dup_vendor_batch_stores_unique_warns_and_conflicts` + the F&O-sink twin (no WARNING through the REAL spine), the movers 500 pair, the three prebuild quarantine tests, and the derive-route 500 (`status_code=500` captured on main); the LakeWriteHalt-propagation pins + the storage-uniqueness property test pass on BOTH (regression guards + #1137's win, as designed). **Verification (fresh runs 2026-07-03, repo venv Python 3.12.3, post-merge of main 563605d8):** every touched source file at **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** under its stem-matched suites — `parquet_writer.py` (284 stmts/76 branches, incl. the chaos suite), `gated_prebuild.py` (108/20), `movers_resilient.py` (9/0); `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py` → "3 touched module(s) at 100%"; 29 NEW tests (16 writer unit + 1 hypothesis property + 2 real-ingest/F&O-sink integration + 4 movers-poison integration + 5 prebuild quarantine/global-stop unit + 1 derive-route verdict integration); regression families green — writer/sink/option-writer/parity 186+, ingest spines 240, movers 320, prebuild+derive-route+app 104, db_view+resamplers 195; `ruff check brutex tests` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict brutex` — ZERO new errors (only the PRE-EXISTING missing-`cma`-stub artifact in untouched `engine/stage3_refine.py`, byte-identical on pristine origin/main in this environment); `pyright` on all 9 touched files — 0 errors, 0 warnings. **Files:** `brutex/data/parquet_writer.py` (WARNING + heal + tripwire + probe + keep-first read; #1137's `_dedup_batch` adopted verbatim), `brutex/dashboard/movers_resilient.py` (skip-set widening), `brutex/dashboard/gated_prebuild.py` (`_PER_SYMBOL_DATA_ERRORS`), `tests/unit/test_parquet_writer_dedup.py`, `tests/property/test_parquet_writer_dedup_property.py`, `tests/integration/test_ingest_vendor_dup_rows.py`, `tests/integration/test_movers_resilient_poison_skip.py`, `tests/unit/test_gated_prebuild.py`, `tests/integration/test_derive_timeframes_gated_route.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-LAKE-WRITE-UNIQUE-001. **Builds on** DEC-FRESH-WRITE-BATCH-DEDUP-001 (#1137 — the fresh-dedup storage fix adopted verbatim), DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 (the keep-first law now enforced on the read collapse), DEC-RESAMPLER-INPUT-GUARD-001 (#1125 — the tripwire whose blast radius this bounds), DEC-SINK-DEDUP-COUNT-001 (#1031), DEC-MOVERS-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 (#886 — the per-symbol skip pattern extended), DEC-PREBUILD-SELECT-001 (the gated quarantine widened). (Ledger: #1139 — renumbered from the provisional #1135 after PRs #1062/#1056/#1064 took #1135-#1138 on main first; = live-main max #1138 + 1, re-checked immediately before push per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001; the DEC-ID is the stable handle.)
