1152. **DEC-GROWW-AMPERSAND-CANDLE-FALLBACK-001 — the `%26` ampersand try-both-forms fallback is extended from the RESOLUTION calls to the CANDLE fetch itself, at the ONE chokepoint BOTH candle paths share (`candles.fetch_candle_windows`), so M&M / M&MFIN / L&TFH / GVT&D / J&KBANK spot + contracts whose chain RESOLVES fine no longer silently return clean-empty candles forever** (2026-07-03; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3; NO lake-schema / stored-bar / scope / vocab / rate-cap change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **ROOT (the audit's #1 finding):** DEC-GROWW-AMPERSAND-FALLBACK-001 (#898) fixed ONLY `get_expiries` / `get_contracts` — the candle fetch still sent the raw `&` (the HTTP query-string separator) verbatim: `option_ingest.fetch_option_candles` passed `contract.symbol` and the spot `adapter.fetch_ohlcv` passed `groww_symbol_by_pair` straight to `fetch_candle_windows`, so an `&` underlying's whole candle series read as an honest-looking empty. **FIX (COMMON — one seam, no copy):** `fetch_candle_windows` now derives the form order from the SAME shared `contracts.underlying_symbol_forms` (plain FIRST — byte-identical for a no-`&` symbol, regression-pinned) and, ONLY when the WHOLE tiled fetch of the plain form returns a clean 200-EMPTY AND the symbol contains `&`, retries ONCE with the `%26`-encoded form inside the SAME logical fetch; first non-empty wins. A RAISED transient (429/timeout/5xx/empty-body) propagates out BEFORE the emptiness check — the fallback keys ONLY off a clean empty, the retry ladders are untouched (pinned). Both paths inherit it for free (spot + option regression tests prove the two-call order `plain → %26`). **ACCOUNTING (documented + tested):** the fallback lives INSIDE one logical fetch — the option spine's `fetch_count` / ledger `in_pull_fetches` semantics are UNCHANGED (an all-empty `&` contract with `empty_retry_attempts=2` records `in_pull_fetches=2` over 4 physical SDK calls); every physical call still rides `client.pace` + the call meter, so rate admission + metering see every real call. Observability: `groww.candles.symbol_form_fallback` (attempt, DEBUG) + `groww.candles.symbol_form_fallback_result` (INFO when the encoded form RECOVERED bars, DEBUG when both forms empty). **HONEST (Golden Rule #1/#10):** the exact SDK encoding remains vendor-UNVERIFIED (the #898 hypothesis — a live Groww probe is still owed); try-both is no-worse-than-before by construction — a working plain form never reaches the fallback, and an all-empty pair records the same empty as today, never a fabricated bar. `candles.py` at 100% line+branch (8 new fallback tests + spot/option path integration + the accounting pin); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **AMENDED (same entry, 2026-07-03 — the 4-agent hostile-review hardening round):** (1) *verify-path correction (Fix 1, MAJOR)* — the raw-integrity capture hook was bound to the PLAIN key symbol, so a `%26` fallback recovery landed TWO records under the SAME `(plain symbol, interval, window)` key and latest-wins made the ENCODED payload's hash authoritative under coordinates that did not produce it; `integrity_verify.verify_one` then re-issued the PLAIN form (no fallback) → EVERY recovered `&`-window was a GUARANTEED false `raw_integrity.verify_mismatch`. FIXED by recording the ISSUED symbol form: `RawIntegrityRecord` gains an optional `issued_symbol` (+ a `fetch_symbol` property; absent/None ⇒ the key symbol, so ALL legacy records verify exactly as before — back-compat regression-pinned, and a plain-form record's sidecar JSON line stays BYTE-identical via `build_record`'s identical-form→None normalisation), the `RawPayloadHook` carries the per-physical-call issued form (`fetch_candle_windows` passes each form), `make_capture_hook` threads it, and `verify_one` re-issues `record.fetch_symbol` (e2e test: the SDK sees `NSE-M%26M` on verify, hash matches; latest-wins semantics unchanged — the field is NEVER part of the 6-tuple key). (2) *terminal-error containment (Fix 2, MINOR)* — a TERMINAL `GrowwError` raised by the SPECULATIVE `%26` attempt previously propagated into the per-contract quarantine, converting a pre-fallback honest-empty into a perpetual FAILED window (contradicting the no-worse-than-before claim); now ONLY the encoded attempt is wrapped — a terminal error logs `groww.candles.symbol_form_fallback_error` (WARNING, `error_type`) and returns the plain form's clean-empty result, while a RETRYABLE error keeps propagating (rides the existing ladders, pinned both ways). (3) *accounting honesty (Fix 3)* — `in_pull_fetches` counts LOGICAL fetches; for `&`-symbols the PHYSICAL vendor-call count can be up to 2× per logical fetch (all-empty windows), so the DEC-FETCH-PER-WINDOW-GATE-HONESTY-001 (#1132) production-fpw envelope WIDENS up to 2× for all-empty `&`-windows — the CI bench gates are UNAFFECTED (the replay chain contains no `&` symbol; every physical call still rides `client.pace` + the call meter, so the rate caps are never overshot — CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6).

1153. **DEC-GROWW-AUTH-HALT-001 — a TERMINAL Groww auth failure (dead credential / re-mint budget exhausted) now HALTS the pull LOUDLY as a pull-wide global stop with the CRITICAL Telegram pull-halt alert, instead of quarantining EVERY symbol one by one into a silent all-failed "completion" (the silent-for-days shape)** (2026-07-03; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate change). **ROOT (audit finding #2):** `GrowwAuthError` (`is_retryable=False`) was NOT in the global-stop sets, so a dead credential fell to the per-symbol/per-contract quarantine — the pull "completed" all-failed with no alert. **FIX:** `GrowwAuthError` joins `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` in BOTH ingest spines (`run_ingest.py` + `option_ingest.py`), `fetch_pipeline._is_pool_isolatable` (terminal auth → trips the pool), `pull_jobs._is_pull_halt` (dashboard alert path), and the CLI `cmd_fetch` `_pull_halt_errors` wrap — all consulting ONE new predicate `errors.is_terminal_auth_failure(exc)` (`isinstance GrowwAuthError AND NOT is_retryable`) so the decision has a single source of truth. **THE CRITICAL CARVE-OUT (regression-pinned):** the two RETRYABLE `GrowwAuthError` SUBCLASSES — `GrowwTokenIssuanceThrottled` (throttled mint) + `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` (read-only broker re-read racing the Lambda mint) — are carved BACK OUT at every check site: they stay per-symbol quarantinable / re-raise with NO alert, never a halt. The mid-pull auto-re-mint self-heal (DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001) is UNTOUCHED BY CONSTRUCTION — a healed 06:00 IST token reset never raises out of `client._call` at all, proven by an END-TO-END regression (a `BackgroundPullJob` pull whose first vendor call auth-expires, the `SdkRefresher` re-mints, the pull finishes DONE with ZERO alerts). `emit_pull_halt_alert` needs no type mapping (reason = class name `GrowwAuthError`, reason-scoped dedupe). The spines' drift-pinning test now ALSO asserts the two tuples are in lockstep + pins terminal-auth-trips / retryable-isolatable on `_is_pool_isolatable`. Regression tests: spot + option spines halt-on-terminal / quarantine-on-retryable (the two prior quarantine-documenting tests INVERTED deliberately), dashboard alert-fires-once + retryable-never-alerts, CLI alert-then-reraise + retryable-reraise-no-alert, `is_terminal_auth_failure` truth table. **HONEST:** the derived `auth_aborted` report flag + `retry_failed_windows` auth handling are preserved for the retryable-quarantine shape; the halt path reuses the EXISTING alert machinery (DEC-TELEGRAM-PULL-HALT-001/-DASHBOARD-001) — no new notifier surface. All touched files 100% line+branch; ruff/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. **AMENDED (same entry, 2026-07-03 — the 4-agent hostile-review hardening round):** (a) *FP-1 hardening (06:00 IST rotation false-halt)* — with `max_reauths=1` (the `GrowwClient` default) + a ZERO-pause post-refresh retry, a worker whose re-read adopts the Lambda's FRESH token at the 06:00–06:05 rotation could 401 once more (fleet-propagation lag — vendor-UNVERIFIED, treated as possible per Golden Rule #1), exhausting the budget → terminal `GrowwAuthError` → the NEW halt killed the whole ~750-symbol overnight pull where pre-PR one pair quarantined. FIXED with BOTH cheap levers: NEW `constants.GROWW_MAX_REAUTHS = 2` injected at BOTH production builders (`build_live_client` + every `build_live_pool` leaf — covers the CLI, dashboard pull-controller, historical-pull and metadata-pull sites; the `GrowwClient` default stays 1 for offline/tests) + NEW `client.REAUTH_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS = 1.5` slept via the injectable `self.sleep` before each post-refresh retry (tests stay instant; deliberately NOT the 429 ladder). Regression-pinned: rotation-lag double-401 → two re-mints → the pull completes DONE with ZERO halt alerts (client-level + end-to-end `BackgroundPullJob`), and a truly-dead credential still exhausts the bounded budget → halts with EXACTLY one CRITICAL alert. (b) *graceful pull-spine catch* — the dashboard pull entrypoints now CATCH the spine's terminal-auth raise and map it to their EXISTING loud abort verdicts instead of letting it escape as a generic job error: `pull_controller.pull_all_spot` (the `auth_expired` verdict + synthesized per-pair quarantine rows + the minute-phase global-stop skip), `pull_controller.pull_candles` (FAILED 1day cell + honestly-SKIPPED minute cell), and `historical_pull` (`auth_aborted` + the "auth token expired" note + remaining market buckets stopped) — each fires the CRITICAL Telegram `emit_pull_halt_alert` AT the catch site (parity with the mass-empty handlers, DEC-TELEGRAM-PULL-HALT-001) and re-raises any RETRYABLE auth-family shape unchanged. **HONEST — a KNOWN false-NEGATIVE stays open (explicit flagged FOLLOW-UP, NOT claimed fixed):** on the production READ-ONLY broker (DEC-AWS-ONLY-CREDS-001 / DEC-BROKER-READONLY-REAUTH-REREAD-001), a TRULY dead credential whose Lambda never rotates surfaces per-window as the RETRYABLE `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` → transient defer forever → this halt NEVER fires for that shape (it can stay silent for days; only the heuristic `pull.stalled` net of DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001 catches it) — the fix is a streak-based StillStale escalation, deferred. Also noted: latent FP-2 (`auth.py:191` wraps a transient local-mint failure into the terminal `GrowwAuthError` — production-UNREACHABLE under DEC-AWS-ONLY-CREDS-001's read-only store, so accepted) and FP-3 (whether a per-instrument/entitlement 401 shares the terminal auth exception class is vendor-UNVERIFIED — if it does, one restricted instrument could halt a healthy pull; needs a live probe).

1146. **DEC-FNO-EXPIRY-SCOPE-001 — expiry-LEVEL date scoping for the F&O historical pull (operator req #30): an expiry is IN SCOPE iff it falls within the requested `[from → to]` window (BOTH endpoints inclusive); an IN-scope expiry keeps the UNTOUCHED per-contract window law (options `expiry − 30d` / futures `expiry − 60d` ∩ envelope); an OUT-of-scope expiry costs ZERO vendor calls + ZERO ledger rows + ONE honest `fno.expiry_out_of_scope` log per (underlying, expiry) — and NEVER deletes stored data** (2026-07-03, same PR as #1145 on `claude/pipeline-pack-04nyec`; pull-PLANNING selection only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO vocab/rate-cap/window-law/lake change; the DEFAULT no-dates pull is byte-identical, pinned). **WHY:** the `/pull-pipeline` explicit from/to dates reshaped SPOT windows only — the F&O phase deliberately ignored them (the over-pull-safety scoping of DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-DATERANGE-001 #1007: a wide verbatim range over the whole options chain would pull far too much), so an operator could not date-bound the F&O side AT ALL. The decree: the dates should bound WHICH EXPIRIES are pulled — never reshape the per-contract windows. **DESIGN — scope SELECTS expiries, never reshapes windows:** NEW pure `brutex/adapters/groww/expiry_scope.py` — `expiry_in_scope(expiry, *, scope_start, scope_end)` (both bounds inclusive; `None` = unbounded; both-`None` = everything in), `partition_contracts_by_scope` → order-preserving `ScopePartition` (`in_scope` + `out_by_expiry` + `contracts_out_of_scope`/`expiries_out_of_scope`), `log_out_of_scope_expiries` (ONE sorted log line per `(underlying, expiry)` group with `{underlying, expiry, scope_start, scope_end, contracts_skipped}`; silent when clean). `pull_contract_candles` gains `scope_start`/`scope_end` — NEW params DISTINCT from its existing window-reshaping `from_date`/`to_date` (the two can coexist; composite tests exercise both) — with the partition + log at the ONE chokepoint STRICTLY BEFORE `_rebuild_contracts`, so an out-of-scope expiry never reaches `_resolve_minute_windows`/`by_market`/`plan_contract_windows` (zero vendor calls, zero ledger rows, stored bars untouched); threaded route → `composite_pull.pull_historical_for_underlyings(scope_start=, scope_end=)` → `pull_contract_candles` (the `/pull-pipeline` route parses the already-`resolve_candle_range`-validated from/to ONCE via the shared `_parse_iso_date_arg` inside the same try→400 guard and passes ONLY scope to the F&O phase — `from_date`/`to_date` still NOT passed; SPOT keeps its verbatim dates; the phase-(a) metadata pull is deliberately NOT scoped — the registry caches the FULL calendar). `HistoricalPullReport` gains `expiries_out_of_scope`/`contracts_out_of_scope` (+ `to_dict` keys); **`contracts_selected` now counts IN-SCOPE legs only** (documented — the completed/selected ratio stays the real pull ratio; the excluded legs ride the two new fields); notes: a partial skip appends `", N expiries out of scope skipped"` (historical + composite + pipeline `_complete_note`), an ALL-out selection gets its OWN honest base note `"all N selected contract(s) across M expiry(ies) fall outside the requested expiry scope — nothing pulled (already-stored bars untouched)"` — never the misleading "no contracts selected — pull expiries + contracts first". **THE 10 PINNED PERMUTATIONS (a–j):** (a) `expiry == to` → IN, with the UNTOUCHED 30d/60d window law (`start_dates` pins `expiry − 30d` CE / `expiry − 60d` FUT); (b) `expiry == to + 1 day` → OUT: zero vendor calls, zero ledger rows (live-shaped, `load_window_ledger`), EXACTLY one log; (c) a weekly+monthly mix → exactly the in-range subset pulled; (d) 52 weeklies × NIFTY+SENSEX under a 2-week scope → 4 in / 100 groups out (counts pinned); (e) a year-boundary scope; (f) `from == to == expiry` single-day; (g) scope AFTER all expiries → clean no-op, zero calls/rows, the all-out note, NO failure signal; (h) DEFAULT (no dates) → planned windows BYTE-IDENTICAL to the `_resolve_minute_windows` law (ingest-spy); (i) route end-to-end — explicit dates reach SPOT as the raw strings verbatim AND the historical phase as parsed scope dates with NO `from_date`/`to_date` kwargs; (j) an out-of-scope expiry's REAL `ParquetBarSink`-stored bars are sha256-IDENTICAL after the scoped pull. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** scoping is pull-PLANNING selection only — it never deletes, rewrites, or re-windows anything already stored (the strict window law of DEC-FNO-FAR-EXPIRY-WINDOW-001 #1127 — incl. the far-future `fno.window_not_open` skip — and the 30d/60d defaults of DEC-FNO-LOOKBACK-SPLIT-001 #894 / DEC-FUTURES-LOOKBACK-60D-001 #1003 apply UNCHANGED to every in-scope expiry); the readers project `SELECT *` (`_select_list(None)` + `union_by_name=true`, so a legacy pre-Greeks F&O tree renders its 7 columns without a binder-error 500 — strictly safer than the old explicit Greeks projection per DEC-GREEKS-ENGINE-PR3-001) and no dangling `curCols`/`cstate.cols`/`.qcol` reference survives (grep-pinned). **(2) date filters AUTO-APPLY + the honest applied-range chip** — root cause: `bx-datepicker.js`'s "Go to" dispatched a `change` event nothing consumed and `db.html` only re-queried on the Apply button (the two-stage trap); the candle view now wires `change` → auto-apply on `cstart`/`cend`/`cdir` (grid-only `#dbgrid` swap, no control teardown), an EMPTY date input renders "—" never today's date (the inert-filter illusion closed), and a NEW pure `resolve_applied_range` reports the TRUE default per dataset — SPOT `[2020-01-01 (GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR, DEC-PULL-FLOOR-2020-001) → today-IST]`, an F&O contract / expired-option series its FULL STORED LIFE (a resilient `MIN`/`MAX` over the IST-date span; `(None, None)` = an honest "no stored data" for an empty partition) — with explicit bounds winning per side independently; the chip is REPORTING metadata (the `WHERE` uses the raw bounds, row set + total byte-unchanged; every returned row lies inside the selected range — test-pinned ascending AND descending) and renders via `textContent` (XSS-safe). **(3) the derived-1day off-by-one FIXED** — a 1day bar is stamped midnight-IST = the PREVIOUS calendar day 18:30 UTC (`spot_daily_resample.py`, DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001), but `_date_bounds` compared the UTC date while the grid renders IST, so filtering `2026-02-03` returned the 02-04 row and DROPPED the 02-03 row; `_date_bounds` is now interval-keyed — `1day` compares the IST calendar date (`_IST_DATE_EXPR` = `+ INTERVAL '330 minutes'` before `::DATE`), every intraday interval keeps the UTC date BYTE-IDENTICAL — empirically verified fails-before/passes-after and session-`TimeZone`-independent (UTC / Asia/Kolkata / America/New_York pinned). **(4) broker-style Greeks display, DISPLAY-ONLY** — `db.html::fmtCell` renders `iv` as PERCENT 2dp (×100 is correct: the stored Greeks-overlay `iv` is an annualized DECIMAL FRACTION per `brutex/options/greeks.py`) and `delta` 3dp / `gamma` 5dp / `theta` 2dp / `vega` 3dp / `rho` 2dp; a `null` Greek renders a blank cell BEFORE `fmtCell` (never a fabricated "0.000"); the payload + stored values stay FULL precision — statistical metrics are never rounded (CLAUDE.md §4, DEC-MONEY-2DP-001). **(5) the `/universe` hero text HONESTY fix (Golden Rule #1)** — the claim "Options fan ATM±10 (indices) / ATM±3 (stocks)" was FALSE: the real pull resolves `get_expiries` → `get_contracts` and ingests ALL vendor-listed strikes, never a relative-to-spot fan (verified against `adapters/groww/contracts.py` + the CLAUDE.md §6 options-contract-resolution row; `strike_chain_bound` only lowers the EMPTY-RETRY budget for far strikes, it never skips one — DEC-FETCH-PER-WINDOW-GUARANTEE-001); the hero now states the all-listed-strikes rule and a test asserts the false claim is GONE. **(6) per-expiry "listed N · with data M" chip** — NEW `fno_cascade.build_expiry_counts` + `app.py::_fno_listed_by_expiry` join the vendor registry calendar (`RegistryStore.count_contracts`, populated by the metadata phase) against the lake-backed cascade contracts, so a young live chain reads e.g. "listed 120 · with data 14" self-explanatorily; GRACEFUL degrade to `listed=None` (chip shows "with data M" only) on an absent registry / unknown underlying (`count_expiries==0`) / `RegistryError` — never a 500, never a misleading whole-underlying "listed 0". **HOSTILE-REVIEW MAJOR FOLDED (4-agent review, verdicts SHIP·SHIP·SHIP·FIX-FIRST):** the applied-range chip's stored-life `MIN`/`MAX` scan re-ran on EVERY default-bounded paging click — the exact O(files)-per-click read DEC-LAKE-READ-O1-AUDIT-001 / DEC-DB-CANDLE-COUNT-CACHE-001 exist to prevent; the span is paging-invariant, so it is now MEMOISED behind the SAME injected generation-stamped cache as the COUNT under the collision-free keys `candle_span_key` ("span|coords") / `option_candle_span_key` ("optspan|series") — a prev/next click is an O(1) hit, a pull bumps the generation → re-scan (never stale), the no-cache pure default keeps the inline scan (`CandleCountCache` made generic over the memoised value; scan-once-across-paging + sort-flip + generation-bump + explicit-bounds-no-scan all regression-pinned). **PERMUTATIONS test-pinned:** empty lake, single bar, dup-poisoned partition must-NOT-500 (rides the DEC-DB-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 / DEC-LAKE-WRITE-UNIQUE-001 resilient reads — good rows render, span degrades, page 200s), timezone/midnight-IST boundaries, page boundaries ascending AND descending. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the SPOT chip shows the FILTER WINDOW `[2020-01-01 → today]`, not the stored span (a documented asymmetry — a late-listed spot symbol's chip can pre-date its data); the expired-OPTIONS page read remains non-resilient to a corrupt file (PRE-EXISTING, unchanged line — the span reader is reached only after the page read scanned the same glob, so NO NEW failure path; flagged scope gap); `fmtCell` keys the iv×100 on the column NAME — correct for the Greeks overlay, while the expired-options lake's per-bar `iv` stamp fraction-ness is fixture-pinned but not independently verified (today's Groww F&O reader sets `iv=None`; flagged); a per-expiry "listed 0 · with data M>0" is possible under registry↔lake drift (reviewer MINOR, flagged fast-follow); the per-underlying-pick registry read is O(expiries) uncached (bounded, off the paging hot path; flagged); frontend behaviour is string-presence-tested (repo convention — no JS harness). **Verification (fresh runs 2026-07-03, repo venv 3.12.3):** `db_view.py` **100.00% line + 100.00% branch** (824 stmts/274 branches, 0 missing) + `fno_cascade.py` **100.00%** (81/12) across the combined db suites (486 passed); 1154. **DEC-SURFACE-TRIAL-001 — the `/results` + `/reports` execution-grade SURFACE TRIAL (every displayed number independently recomputed against the real routes — VERDICT: no divergence found anywhere; the 13-test trial suite ships as the permanent regression net) + the #1069-review leftover folds (MINOR-1 probe-stat-outside-the-lock FIXED, MINOR-2 disproven-and-documented, three comment/doc NITs)** (2026-07-03; READ-side + tests + docs only — ENGINE UNCHANGED, NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; the ONLY `brutex/` source change is the `summary_cache.py` lock-scope hoist — behaviour-preserving on every existing test). **PART A — THE TRIAL (the deliverable):** fixtures are written with the REAL repo writers — `/results` via the engine's own `ResultsStore` (two per-tuple stores under `<lake>/sweeps/<instrument>/<tf>/` incl. a run_id DUPLICATED across both stores + a third deliberately CORRUPT `.parquet`; rows carrying `net_pnl_paisa ∈ {−1, 123456789, 2**60, 2**60+1}`, a sharpe TIE, a `deflated_sharpe=None`, the no-condition `mask_bits=0`), `/reports` via the lake's `ParquetWriter` (five 1-day symbols over the Mar-2024 calendar spanning a weekend + the Mar-8 holiday, incl. a MISSING Mar-6 daily bar, prices engineered so `%CHNG` lands EXACTLY on `+0.005`/`−0.005`/`0`/`±5%`/`−6%`/`+0.004`; a minute-basis symbol whose Mar-4 1-minute window is a HOLE while its daily bar exists). The REAL routes are driven through the established `build_app`+`TestClient` pattern, and EVERY displayed number is recomputed INDEPENDENTLY test-side — pure-integer hand-rolled western-grouped ₹-formatting (no `format_inr`, no `Decimal`), `fractions.Fraction` CHNG/%CHNG + an away-from-zero half-up 2dp rounder (no `decimal`), a single-pass negated-key ranking sort (vs production's two-pass stable sort), brute-force per-day top-mover picks — then asserted equal cell-for-cell against the wire JSON / parsed sheet XML (values AND fill-style indices). Families trialed: DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 boundaries (`₹-0.01` · odd-paisa lakh grouping · `2**60` paisa = `₹11,529,215,046,068,469.76`); EXACT-int-not-float ranking with genuine teeth (`float(2**60)==float(2**60+1)`, run_ids arranged so a float coercion PROVABLY inverts the pair — the test asserts the exact and float-coerced orders differ AND production matches exact); run_id-ASC tie-break; cross-store dedup `total_rows`; `store_count`/`skipped` with the corrupt store; top-slice bounds `rows == min(top, total)` with `total_rows` invariant; unknown-`rank_by` → sharpe fallback echo; bit-exact (`==`, no approx) metric passthrough; the pre-open row law (weekend calendar step, contiguity SKIP over the missing daily bar — Mar-7 absent, never a stale anchor — first-session absence); ±0.005 half-up display cells (away from zero on the negative); top-mover abs-max (−6% beats +5%), INCLUSIVE `min_pct` (`>=` pinned at exactly 5), alphabetical tie, no-qualifier day absent, `mode=all` ignoring `min_pct`; `.xlsx` `(day,symbol)` vs `.zip`-all `(day,−pct,symbol)` ordering; one member/year + one sheet/non-empty-month; green/red/neutral fills from the FULL-precision sign incl. the deliberately-PINNED "0 < pct < 0.005 displays 0.00 but fills GREEN" edge (flagged to the operator as a display-consistency question, not a defect); minute basis (IEP = 09:15 1-minute open; PREV. CLOSE = the prior session's LAST 1-minute close proven against a 2-bar ANCHOR day — REVIEW ROUND-1 FIX (Golden Rule #10): as first shipped, the only asserted row's anchor day (Mar-5) carried ONE bar, so last-vs-first was indistinguishable and an arg_max→arg_min mutation of `db_view._intraday_last_close_by_date` SURVIVED the trial (the fixture's 2-bar day was the unanchored Mar-1 — this entry's original "proven against a 2-bar day" sentence was a verification overclaim); the fixture now gives Mar-5 TWO bars with DISTINCT closes (310.50 then 311.00), the asserted 311.00 anchor genuinely distinguishes last from first, and the arg_min mutation is verified KILLED; and the minute-window HOLE skip — the Mar-5 row absent rather than stale-anchored on Mar-1). **HONEST VERDICT (Golden Rule #10): the trial found ZERO divergence — no production bug to fix; the suite itself is the deliverable** (`tests/unit/test_surface_trial_results.py` 6 tests + `tests/unit/test_surface_trial_reports.py` 7 tests). Two candidate findings from the research were resolved: the `format_inr` western-vs-en-IN grouping inconsistency (the page's `num()` uses en-IN while ₹-strings group western) is a DISPLAY-CONSISTENCY question deferred to the operator, arithmetic exact either way; the fills-vs-cell sub-boundary edge is pinned as current behaviour. `/operator` re-confirmed a nav ALIAS of `/` (nav.py maps "Operator" → `/`), not a route. **PART B — #1069 leftovers, per the verified research verdicts:** **MINOR-1 (REAL, fixed):** the revision-probe `os.stat` ran UNDER `SummaryCache._lock` (both `generation` and `get_or_refresh`), so a probe wedged on a stalled external-SSD volume (the production mode DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 #999 guards the write path against) would hold the lock indefinitely and block the pull's `mark_dirty` write funnel + every generation-keyed read — inverting the module's own "no I/O under the lock" design intent. FIX: NEW `_probe_token()` runs the probe with NO lock held; NEW `_reconcile_revision_locked(token)` applies it under the lock (baseline-no-bump / bump-once semantics byte-identical); both call sites hoist. Thread-safety envelope (documented in the `revision_probe` param notes): out-of-order tokens can only OVER-invalidate (a spurious extra bump — each keyed cache recomputes lazily at most once per distinct generation read), NEVER miss a change (the next probe of the final on-disk state differs from any stale baseline), and `_generation` stays monotonic. Regressions: `test_stalled_probe_never_blocks_mark_dirty` (a probe blocked on an Event; `mark_dirty` must complete while it is stalled — DEADLOCKS before the fix) + `test_out_of_order_probe_tokens_over_invalidate_never_miss` (the B→A-stale→B replay: bumps fire, monotonic holds); all 6 pre-existing probe tests pass unchanged. **MINOR-2 (NOT-REAL for the reviewed sequence, documented):** an OSError probe outage returns `None` → the early-return never touches `_last_revision`, so recovery compares the post-CLI-write token against the PRE-outage baseline and bumps — nothing is swallowed. The narrower REAL variant (app COLD-STARTS during a probe outage, a CLI write lands, the probe recovers → first token is a no-bump baseline, outage-era caches survive until the next signal) is recorded as honest-envelope note (c) on the `revision_probe` param — deliberately NOT mechanised (a first-token bump would spuriously invalidate every healthy warm start, contradicting the by-design baseline-no-bump; the outage window is loudly logged per probe call). [COLD-OUTAGE RECONCILE — DEC-SUMMARY-CACHE-COLD-OUTAGE-BUMP-001, MIGRATION.md #1280a: the "deliberately NOT mechanised" clause is SUPERSEDED — the variant is now mechanised WITHOUT breaking the healthy-warm-start contract by keying the recovery bump on (probe WIRED ∧ a pre-baseline None actually observed ∧ entries populated), so a healthy first token still records a no-bump baseline and the spurious cost is bounded to at most ONE bump per process.] **NIT-1:** `movers_snapshot.filter_to_ist_minute` + `_read_session_bars` docstrings overclaimed "never include data after 13:45" — the kept, inclusive 13:45 bucket-OPEN bar aggregates trades through 13:45:59; reworded to the MINUTE-granular guarantee ("never any bar STARTING after the as-of minute"), comment-only. **NIT-2:** the `test_intraday_resample_and_cutoff_slice` comment still explained the pre-#1069 resampled-bucket-label cutoff; rewritten to the unified raw-1m mechanism (the outcome was coincidentally identical). **NIT-3:** CLAUDE.md's #1149 blurb said "All five touched `brutex/` modules 100% line+branch", conflating the five coverage-VERIFIED modules (which include the UNtouched `movers_options.py`) with the six-member TOUCHED set (incl. `app.py` + `nse.py`); corrected in place. **Verification (fresh runs 2026-07-03, repo venv):** the 13 trial tests + the 35-test `test_summary_cache.py` suite green; `summary_cache.py` at 100.00% line + 100.00% branch (the hoist relocates, never removes, branches); `movers_snapshot.py` byte-identical behaviour (comment-only) — movers suites green; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + pyright clean on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/summary_cache.py` (MINOR-1 hoist + MINOR-2/thread-safety honest notes), `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py` (NIT-1 docstrings), `tests/unit/test_surface_trial_results.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_surface_trial_reports.py` (new), `tests/unit/test_summary_cache.py` (2 regressions), `tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers.py` (NIT-2 comment), `CLAUDE.md` (active branch + blurb + NIT-3), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-SURFACE-TRIAL-001. **Builds on** DEC-HARDENING-LEFTOVERS-001 (#1149 — the probe seam + the review that flagged the leftovers), DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001 (the /results surface), DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001/DEC-REPORTS-EXCEL-CATEGORIES-001/DEC-PREOPEN-MINUTE-BASIS-001 (the /reports surface), DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the boundaries trialed), DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 (#999 — the stalled-volume mode motivating MINOR-1). 1175. **DEC-LAKE-HEAL-001 — dup-train PR-2: the lake gains ONE bounded invariant scanner + a fully automatic keep-FIRST healer, closing the #1139 gap that a poisoned SETTLED month (or a cross-file/foreign-month row, or a legacy-key drifted dir) stayed poisoned forever unless a write happened to touch it** (2026-07-03; data-lake integrity + operator surfaces only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063, NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-SCHEMA change — partition layout + columns byte-identical; only stored-row uniqueness, placement, and observability). **SCANNER** (NEW `brutex/data/lake_invariants.py`): ONE bounded scan — per-file physical-rows vs unique-timestamp count (options tree keyed `(side,timestamp)`), per-file UTC-month membership (subsumes cross-file overlap: one file per UTC month per series, so any same-ts pair across files is a foreign row in one of them; the 1day midnight-IST straddle + GIFTNIFTY early-IST bars are UTC-consistent, never false-flagged — test-pinned), and per-dir legacy-key drift via the #911 ladder MOVED to the COMMON pure `brutex/data/lake_keys.py` (`completeness._resolve_spot_category` is now a thin delegating wrapper — byte-equivalence matrix-pinned, existing completeness suites untouched; drift scope gated to `SPOT_PROBE_SEGMENTS` so FNO groww_symbol dirs are never mangled). THREE detection layers over the ONE scanner core (`classify_bar_keys`, shared verbatim): **L1** free piggyback on `reconcile_catalog_from_lake(check_invariants=True)` (classification rides the timestamp column reconcile already reads — ZERO extra read calls, spy-pinned; findings on the new defaulted `ReconcileResult.findings`; healed via ONE `heal_after_reconcile` call at the `cascade_wire.load_bars_for_manifest` reconcile chokepoint — the CLI replay/sweep-mirror loader — while the verify-style `cmd_catalog_reconcile`, the sweep-all inline reconcile, and the mid-pull `contract_bounds` reconcile stay detect-only by design); **L2** post-pull scoped to the pulled symbols × `ist_span_partition_months` (dashboard spot `pull_all_spot` + single-symbol `pull_candles` glue `_heal_after_pull`, and the F&O `pull_contract_candles` glue `_heal_lake_after_pull` over the rebuilt contracts × the UNION of their resolved windows — each wired at the post-drain seam BEFORE the downstream 1-minute readers — the Greeks enrichment + the pipeline's final prebuild derivations (the mid-pull daily derive was removed by DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 #1145, reconciled on the merge-with-main) — so they read clean 1-minute; `LakeWriteHalt` RE-RAISES into the existing pull-halt handling, every other heal error is swallowed + logged `lake_heal.post_pull_error` so a heal bug never fails a pull; the CLI `brutex fetch` path has no such seam — covered by L1/L3/census, stated not hidden); **L3** a ONE-TIME dashboard-startup sweep stamped by a lake CONTENT token (sha256 over `relpath|size|mtime_ns` of every parquet; sentinel `.lake_heal/last_sweep.json`; throttled `BRUTEX_LAKE_HEAL_THROTTLE_S` daemon thread, `RatePanelSampler`-shaped, synchronous 100%-tested `run_sync`, never crashes boot; `cmd_dashboard` now constructs the `SummaryCache` explicitly and hands the SAME instance to `build_app` AND the sweeper's `on_healed=mark_dirty`). **HEALER** (NEW `brutex/data/lake_heal.py`, default AUTO-ON, escape hatch `BRUTEX_LAKE_HEAL=observe` — observe touches NOTHING, recursive-byte-pinned): per finding — BOTH partition locks in the writers' order → quarantine-COPY the original to `<lake>/.quarantine/<ts>/<relpath>` (a `.locks/`-style sibling, invisible to every walker; never auto-deleted; restore = copy back) → mode-independent keep-FIRST dedup → atomic rewrite THROUGH the normal write privates via the NEW public `ParquetWriter.heal_partition` + `read_partition_bars` (reuses `_read_existing_bars`/P9/`_render_bytes`/`_atomic_write` in-module — zero duplication, Greeks overlay round-trips, probe-failure never guesses; `write()`/`_merge_write`/`_dedup_batch` bodies UNTOUCHED so the #1067 pin suite runs unmodified) → catalog upsert (raw_hash ROTATES — a healed partition is never mistaken for untouched, Golden Rule #4; NEW `Catalog.delete_partition` for quarantine-MOVED/merged-away files) → one hash-chained audit JSONL line per partition (`<lake>/audit/lake-heal.jsonl`, `LAKE_HEAL_*` actions, opened/closed via the ONE COMMON `lake_heal_audit` context manager every seam shares) → ONE Telegram alert per batch (`SweepAlerter.lake_heal_report`, `QUARANTINE_NEW` kind reused, dedupe `lake-heal:<scope>`, best-effort `emit_lake_heal_alert`). Cross-file/foreign rows are REASSIGNED whole (copy-forward keep-first into the canonical month file, then row-removed from the source — crash-convergent, never value-edited); a drifted dir is MERGED keep-first into its canonical dir (1minute + 1day merged; derived TF dirs quarantine-moved, rebuilt from the merged 1minute); a `files≥20 ∧ >50%`-poisoned batch is REFUSED (mass-heal guard, the sweep-heal C7 twin); `LakeWriteHalt` propagates (disk-full during heal = graceful pull/CLI halt). STRICTLY ROW-REMOVING/ROW-REASSIGNING — never value-editing. **DERIVED RECALL** (mandatory, test-pinned): after a symbol's 1minute heals, its 1day is RE-DERIVED over the affected months (`derive_daily_for_targets`, latest-wins overwrites the poisoned daily bar; FNO passes include_oi + the OI-carry resampler) and its materialised intraday-TF months are DELETE-and-REBUILT via `materialize_lake_timeframes` — an in-place re-derive would silently KEEP a poisoned keep-first bucket; the rebuild is O(symbol-history) (no month-bounded TF rebuild exists — honest, not built), a rebuild failure leaves the months deleted + loudly logged. **CENSUS + SURFACES:** READ-ONLY `brutex lake audit-unique [--json]` (per-segment INDEX/CASH/FNO/OPTIONS clean/dup/foreign/overlap/drift counts + the ENGINE-index NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX verdict; exit 0 clean / 1 poisoned / 2 error; tree-sha READ-ONLY pin); a bounded `doctor` check (`check_lake_uniqueness` — engine-index series only + last-sweep sentinel, whole-lake stays the CLI's job); a `/universe` "Lake uniqueness" chip via `GET /api/v1/universe/lake-uniqueness` behind the COMMON generation-stamped cache (`MoversSnapshotCache` + `_nav_latency_key` — O(1) repeat poll, first compute per generation honestly O(files)). 1156. **DEC-RESULTS-SURFACE-HONESTY-001 — the surface-trial-2 fixes: four verified `/results` + `/reports` surface defects closed — (1) the leaderboard gains SNAPSHOT-ERA honesty (payload `snapshot_hashes` + `mixed_snapshot_eras` + a per-row `snapshot_era` marker + a loud mixed-era banner — honest MARKER, deliberately NOT a row exclusion), (2) the cross-process freshness token gains a SWEEPS-TREE component so an out-of-band CLI `sweep-all` write bumps the dashboard generation on the next poll, (3) a duplicate `run_id` with DIFFERENT metrics is counted + logged (`run_id_conflicts`) instead of silently first-wins-masked, and (4) the `/reports` symbol-chip `innerHTML` string-concat DOM-XSS sink is closed (createElement/textContent)** (2026-07-03 on `claude/stoic-maxwell-km8gfe`; READ-side dashboard + templates + tests only — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO lake-schema/stored-bar/scope/vocab/rate-cap/write-path change; on a single-era, conflict-free tree every pre-existing payload field is byte-identical — pinned). **THE FOUR DEFECTS (from the executed surface trial, re-verified on live main):** **(1) MED — mixed-era co-ranking with zero marker:** `build_sweep_leaderboard` (`brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py`) co-ranked rows from stores swept under DIFFERENT `data_snapshot_hash` eras (pre-heal poisoned-era results next to post-heal ones) in ONE table with no payload hint. FIX (honest-marker approach): a NEW `_snapshot_eras` scan reads the tree's OWN audit chain (`<sweeps>/audit/sweep-all.jsonl` `SWEEP_START` payloads — the SAME self-description `results_report._recorded_snapshot_hash` reads; the relpath is a test-PINNED copy, not an import, so the dashboard surface stays free of drift) into a `(instrument, tf, direction, mode, k)` → era-set map (`k` = the row's `mask_bits` popcount — the sweep enumerates exactly-k-of-bits masks); the payload gains `snapshot_hashes` (sorted distinct eras behind the DISCOVERED rows) + `mixed_snapshot_eras` (`len > 1`) and every row a `snapshot_era` marker — the hash when its coordinates saw ONE era, `ambiguous` when re-swept under several (per-FILE recorded hashes do not exist; the filename digest folds the hash one-way — the per-file authority is dup-train PR-3's census, NOT claimed), `unknown` when the chain carries no signal (absent/corrupt chain → logged `sweep_results.era_scan_failed`, empty hashes — no fabricated single-era verdict, Golden Rule #1). `results.html` renders a loud `#eraBanner` ("results span N data eras … census/heal pending (dup-train PR-3)") via `textContent` ONLY. WHY NOT exclusion/quarantine: exclusion without PR-3's at-rest census could hide legitimate multi-era research (an operator comparing eras deliberately) and the read side cannot even pick WHICH era is "current"; the marker kills the one-clean-table ILLUSION — quarantine stays PR-3 (`results_report`'s #1150 seam is the engine-side arm). **(2) MED — CLI-sweep staleness:** the #1069 `lake_revision` probe statted ONLY `window_ledger/ledger.parquet`, so an out-of-band `ResultsStore` write (CLI `sweep-all` in another process) never bumped the generation — the `/results` leaderboard served pre-write data on its cached keys until a restart, and INCONSISTENTLY (a never-polled filter key computed fresh while a polled key served stale). FIX: `lake_revision` becomes a composite `"<ledger>|<sweeps>"` token; the NEW `sweeps_revision` component is a bounded directory-mtime sha256 digest over `<lake>/sweeps` (root + first-level + second-level `<instrument>/<tf>/` dirs). HONEST COST (Golden Rule #10): **O(directories), NOT O(files)** — one `scandir` of the root plus one per instrument dir, bounded by instruments × timeframes (dozens), never the store count; a root-only stat would MISS a store landing in an existing `<tf>/` dir (dir mtimes move only for direct children — the exact staleness bug), and every repo writer lands via tempfile+`os.replace` (a rename, which moves the parent dir mtime); an exotic in-place rewrite that never renames is NOT detected (no repo writer does this); component semantics mirror the ledger's — stable `absent` sentinel, `None` = no-signal on any other OSError (either component `None` ⇒ composite `None`, never a half-signal). **(3) LOW-MED — silent divergent-duplicate masking:** `_load_rows_resilient`'s `by_run_id.setdefault` silently kept first-path-wins when the SAME `run_id` appeared with DIFFERENT metrics (the engine's `ResultsStore.append` RAISES on this — Golden Rule #4). FIX: keep the deterministic first-wins (sorted store paths — discovery-order-independent) but COUNT (`run_id_conflicts` payload field) + LOG one `sweep_results.run_id_conflict` WARNING per dropped divergent row + surface in the page status note ("N run-id conflict(s) — duplicate run_ids with different metrics (first-wins, logged)"); an IDENTICAL duplicate stays a silent conflict-free dedup. Deliberately NOT a raise — the read-only dashboard must render; the engine's strictness stays engine-side. **(4) LOW — `/reports` DOM-XSS sink:** `reports.html`'s `renderChips` built each chip via `chip.innerHTML = '<span>' + s.symbol + …` — server-derived `s.symbol`/`s.exchange` string-concatenated into `innerHTML` (a hostile lake directory name surfacing through `/api/v1/reports/preopen/symbols` would execute). FIX: the chip is built via `document.createElement` + `textContent` (the repo law: textContent-never-innerHTML for server strings — the `movers.html`/`db.html` convention), badge + exchange included. **Fails-before (verbatim, `brutex/` checked back to pre-fix via `git stash`):** the new suites → `16 failed, 1 deselected in 3.35s` (every TestSnapshotEraHonesty + TestRunIdConflicts pin, the `TestCliSweepFreshness::test_out_of_band_sweep_store_refreshes_leaderboard_same_cache_key` staleness regression — `total_rows` stayed 1 after the out-of-band store write — and all 6 template pins incl. `assert "chip.innerHTML" not in html`), plus `tests/unit/test_lake_revision.py` failing collection with `ImportError: cannot import name 'sweeps_revision'`. **Verification (fresh runs 2026-07-03, repo venv):** `lake_revision.py` (51 stmts/8 branches) + `sweep_results_view.py` (133/32) BOTH **100.00% line + branch** under their covering suites; 52 covering tests + `test_dashboard_results_route.py` + `test_surface_trial_results.py` + `test_summary_cache.py` (53) green; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` → Success (2 source files); `pyright` → 0 errors on every touched file. **Test types:** unit (era/conflict/probe suites) + integration (the out-of-band CLI-sweep freshness regression through the real route/cache/probe spine) + regression (each fails-before pin) + golden-style static template pins; property/bench/stress/mutation ride the standing CI lanes. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/sweep_results_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/lake_revision.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/results.html`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/reports.html`, `tests/unit/test_sweep_results_view.py`, `tests/unit/test_lake_revision.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_lake_revision.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_reports_template_xss.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_dashboard_results_template_era.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-RESULTS-SURFACE-HONESTY-001. **Builds on** DEC-SURFACE-TRIAL-001 (#1154 — the executed trial that surfaced the four defects), DEC-LAKE-READ-UNIQUE-001 (#1150 — the engine-side quarantine seam this marker complements; PR-3 census/heal remains the follow-up authority), DEC-HARDENING-LEFTOVERS-001 (#1149 — the revision-probe seam extended), DEC-DASHBOARD-RESULTS-PAGE-001 (the /results surface), DEC-DASHBOARD-XSS-HARDENING-001 (the textContent law applied to /reports). 1159. **DEC-DOCTOR-KIT-HONESTY-001 — the doctor live-proof kit HONESTY fixes: four defects from the operator's red-banner report (log 23c543ba) closed — (1) ZERO-COMMAND auto-bisect: a FAILing stage-6 depth probe now AUTO-BISECTS the true 1-minute floor itself and reports it as an advisory WARN naming the floor ("1-minute depth floor for BSE-SENSEX: <date>"), never a FAIL instructing the operator to run `--depth-bisect`; (2) the stage-8 bhavcopy cross-check gets its OWN NSE-allowlisted getter — the Groww shim's SSRF allowlist was blocking archives.nseindia.com and the kit mislabelled OUR wiring bug "external dependency"; (3) the live-proof pill's headline is ONE flow-scoped worst-of line so a mixed run can never read as a contradictory PASS-then-FAIL toast; (4) the 122-vs-123 prebuild daily gap is DIAGNOSED as the DELIBERATE forming-session guard (documented + pinned, NO behaviour change)** (2026-07-03; the follow-up PR to DEC-UNIVERSE-UI-POLISH-002 #1158 — `brutex/doctor_live.py` + `brutex/doctor_autorun.py` + `brutex/data/bhavcopy.py` + `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-liveproof.js` + a docstring note in `brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py`; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **FIX 1 (zero-command law — the operator NEVER runs commands):** `doctor_autorun.run_kit_stages` built `KitOptions` without `depth_bisect` (doctor_autorun.py:641) and `KitOptions.depth_bisect` defaults False (doctor_live.py:741), so a Groww clean-empty at the 2020-01-01 boundary (the operator's BSE-SENSEX case) rendered a red banner INSTRUCTING `--depth-bisect`. NEW `KitOptions.auto_bisect` (default False — the manual CLI is byte-unchanged): `stage_depth` runs `probe_depth(bisect=True)` under it — the bisect spends calls ONLY on a failing symbol (a boundary hit returns after exactly 1 call, regression-pinned: passing symbols cost 1 call each, never a bisect) — and a FOUND floor renders the NEW catalog line `depth.autobisect_floor` as `_worst(status, WARN)` (an advisory "PASS with warnings" pill via PROBES_REQUIRED's PASS/WARN acceptance), while no-data-anywhere renders `depth.autobisect_absent` (a FAIL that prescribes NO command). BUDGET HONESTY: `compute_call_budget` grants the SAME `DEPTH_BISECT_BUDGET`=60 extension to `auto_bisect` (never double-granted with `--depth-bisect`; a full bisect is ~14 calls/symbol, hard-capped `DEPTH_PROBE_MAX_CALLS`=20), `run_kit_stages` sets `auto_bisect` ONLY when the depth stage is in the run (`DEPTH_STAGE_ID`=6 — the preflight keeps the plain 40), and the run.start transcript + per-symbol depth events log `auto_bisect`. **FIX 2 (mislabelled "external dependency"):** `stage_bhavcopy` called `fetch_index_bhavcopy(deps.http_get, …)` where `KitDeps.http_get` is the GROWW `urllib_http_get` whose `_check_url` admits ONLY growwapi-assets.groww.in (instrument_loader.py:35-52) → archives.nseindia.com was refused by OUR OWN allowlist (`GrowwInstrumentFetchError`) and the generic except mislabelled it "external dependency". NEW `brutex/data/bhavcopy.py::urllib_http_get_nse` (REUSES the module's own `_check_url`/`BHAVCOPY_ALLOWED_HOSTS` NSE allowlist — no copy, §11 COMMON; browser-ish User-Agent since the NSE archive refuses default library agents) + NEW `KitDeps.nse_http_get` wired in `build_real_deps` and used at the stage-8 call site; the except arms are SPLIT — a `GrowwInstrumentFetchError` (or an allowlist-shaped `BhavcopyError`) renders the NEW `bhavcopy.wiring` FAIL ("kit wiring: URL blocked by local allowlist" — an internal kit bug), and ONLY a genuine network/HTTP/parse failure against NSE keeps the honest `bhavcopy.unreachable` WARN. With the fix the cross-check actually RUNS on the Mac (a `deps.http_get`-must-not-be-called regression pins the routing). **FIX 3 (contradictory toast):** `bx-liveproof.js` set the pill headline from the PREFLIGHT summary alone, so a preflight-PASS + probes-FAIL run toasted PASS then FAIL. NEW `unifiedHeadline(data)` renders ONE flow-scoped worst-of line — "live-proof — preflight: PASS · probes: FAIL — depth[R6]" (`KIND_LABEL` short labels + `failingStageLabels` pointers derived from the verdicts' own "FAIL <stage>[<register>]:" catalog prefixes — pointers only, the diagnosis wording stays the golden catalog's verbatim); the pill DOT's existing `worstClass` worst-of is NOT re-implemented; textContent-only rendering preserved (CodeQL XSS gate) and PR #1076's 8 s never-occlude auto-collapse (`AUTO_MIN_MS`/`bxlp-min`) preserved alongside (both test-pinned). **FIX 4 (VERDICT: documented-deliberate, NOT a bug — no behaviour change):** the 122-vs-123 ADANIENT gap traced to the EXACT span arithmetic: `materialize_lake_timeframes(include_daily=True)` derives the daily with `before = run-day IST` and `resample_1m_to_daily` DROPS any session whose IST date is `>= before` (the no-look-ahead forming-session guard), while the intraday materialisation (`resample_1m_to_tf`) has no such guard — so when the stored 1-minute contains the run day's own session, the 20 intraday TFs carry ALL 123 sessions and the `1day` carries 122: EXACTLY ONE session, the live edge, diverges. The refuter's partition observations are the midnight-IST stamping (an IST date-D daily bar stamps (D−1) 18:30 UTC → the 2026-01-01 session's bar lives in the 2025/12 UTC partition; the 2026/07 daily partition holds only Jul-2's bar because Jul-1's lives in June and Jul-3's — the run day — is guard-excluded): shifted/excluded by design, never lost. HONEST envelope: the guard is whole-day-granular — even a post-close run excludes the run day (the code cannot cheaply prove the session closed) — and SELF-HEALS on the next pipeline run via the latest-wins derived `1day`; documented in `materialize_lake_timeframes`'s docstring + pinned by NEW `TestPrebuildLiveEdgeDivergencePinned` (3 tests: the exactly-one-session divergence, the prior-UTC-month placement, the post-close-exclusion + next-day self-heal). TESTS (each fix FAILS before / PASSES after): `TestStageDepth` gains 4 auto-bisect tests (WARN-naming-the-floor / passing-symbols-never-bisected + budget arithmetic 40+60 / absent-without-a-command / manual `--depth-bisect` byte-unchanged) + `test_e2e_probes_auto_bisect_failing_depth_is_warn_naming_the_floor` + `test_run_kit_stages_grants_auto_bisect_only_to_depth_runs`; `TestStageBhavcopy` gains 3 (nse-getter-routing / Groww-allowlist-refusal→wiring-FAIL / bhavcopy-own-allowlist-refusal→wiring-FAIL); `test_pill_headline_is_flow_scoped_worst_of_never_preflight_only`; the golden diagnostics fixture regenerated (+3 catalog lines: `depth.autobisect_floor` [R6] · `depth.autobisect_absent` [R6] · `bhavcopy.wiring`, added to the register-crossref exemption as a kit-internal wiring row). `doctor_live.py` + `doctor_autorun.py` + `bhavcopy.py` at 100% line+branch from their stem-mapped suites; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on every touched file. **AMENDED IN PLACE (2026-07-03, same PR, pre-merge — operator decree, verbatim "See don't even need to run these fucking bhavcopy and this issue dude okay?"): the AUTORUN no longer runs the depth [R6] or bhavcopy [G7] stages AT ALL — `doctor_autorun.PROBE_STAGES` drops stages 6+8 (now `{1, 3, 5, 7}`: creds → token → spot-1m → VIX) and `PROBES_REQUIRED` collapses to `{"vix"}` — SUPERSEDING fix 1's "auto-bisect quiets the banner" framing for the startup/first-pull path: the autorun makes ZERO depth-probe vendor calls and ZERO NSE bhavcopy fetches, so neither the SENSEX red banner nor a bhavcopy warning can appear at startup by construction. 1311. **DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-FLAKE-002 — de-flake the responsive-under-write timing gate AGAIN (read budget 0.5 s → 1.0 s + writer hold 2 s → 4 s; the 0.5 s ceiling of DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-FLAKE-001 spuriously failed on a loaded GHA runner now that the suite runs ~12.5k tests / ~17 min)** (2026-07-04, autonomous CI-red fix on PR #1093: `test_cache_served_coverage_spot_responsive_under_write` failed run 28689390506 with `assert 0.5562308909999274 < 0.5` — "cache-served /api/v1/coverage/spot took 556.2ms while the writer held the lock"). **Root cause (verified NOT a merge regression):** the PR's diff does not touch the coverage/spot path, the SummaryCache, or the store-lock plumbing (the branch's `app.py` delta is the Greeks-health import + two `observe` call sites + a docstring date); coverage passed at 100.00% and locally the timed read completes in single-digit ms across repeated runs. The failure signature itself exonerates the code: a genuine regression to the blocking path waits out the FULL `_WRITER_HOLD_S` (then 2.0 s = 4x OVER budget), while CI measured 556 ms — an 11% overshoot that is scheduling/GC jitter on a loaded shared runner, the EXACT flake class #539 already de-flaked once (0.2 s → 0.5 s after a 204.76 ms spike). The suite has since grown to 12,512 tests (~17 min wall), raising runner-load jitter. **Fix (1 test file, threshold-only — NO product/runtime change):** `_WRITER_HOLD_S` 2.0 → **4.0 s**, `_READ_BUDGET_S` 0.5 → **1.0 s** (still = hold / 4). The pass/fail separation stays unambiguous (a true blocking regression now waits ~4.0 s = 4x OVER the 1.0 s budget) with ~2x the jitter headroom (the observed 556 ms spike passes with 44% margin; a healthy read keeps ~250x headroom). Widening the hold remains FREE on the passing path — `_HeldLock.__exit__` releases the lock the instant the fast read returns, so the full hold elapses ONLY on the regression path. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #1/#10):** ✅ the 3-test file re-run green locally post-change; ruff + ruff-format clean; the change strictly RELAXES the healthy-pass condition + WIDENS regression separation, so it cannot newly-fail a healthy run — only remove the flake. 🟡 a timing gate on a shared runner can never be provably flake-proof — if 1.0 s ever flakes, the next step is the `BRUTEX_M4PRO_ABS` env-gate precedent of DEC-HARDENING-LEFTOVERS-001 (#1149), not another blind widening. Scope: ONLY this one timing gate (Golden Rule #3). **Builds on:** DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-FLAKE-001 (#539, the first widening) · DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 (the oracle this hardens) · CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #10.

1263. **DEC-INDEX-SURROGATE-COLLISION-DETECT-001 — the Groww instrument-master index build now DETECTS a 32-bit surrogate `security_id` collision between two DISTINCT indices at build time — keep-first + ONE loud `instrument_master.index_security_id_collision` WARNING naming BOTH colliding groww_symbols — instead of the store's silent, order-dependent last-wins overwrite** (2026-07-03; fix (d) of the data-safety batch — hermetic, `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py` + its unit suite only. PROBLEM (confirmed): a non-numeric index `exchange_token` (indices carry STRING tokens) becomes the model's int `security_id` via `_security_id` → `int.from_bytes(blake2b(gsym, digest_size=4))` — a deterministic 32-bit surrogate derived from the `groww_symbol`, computed per-row with NO cross-row awareness; `build_index` first-wins-dedups on the gsym KEY only, so two distinct-gsym indices whose surrogates blake2b-collide into the same 32-bit value BOTH enter `universe`/`by_groww_symbol`, and the silent drop happens DOWNSTREAM at the store: PK `(security_id, exch_id, segment)` + the `identity_deduped` LAST-wins overwrite silently drops one `Segment.INDEX` row, order-dependently, with ZERO warning (~1e-7 birthday odds — but silent + non-deterministic). FIX (build-time detection at the single COMMON `build_index` chokepoint every consumer imports, UPSTREAM of the store's silent dedup): one O(1) reverse map `index_identity_owner: dict[(Exchange, security_id) → gsym]`, probed AFTER the first-wins gsym dedup and scoped `segment is Segment.INDEX` (only index rows ever carry a hashed surrogate — numeric vendor tokens are used directly; the key mirrors the store's INDEX PK partition) — a second distinct-gsym index claiming an owned identity is KEPT-FIRST-dropped with the WARN naming `kept`/`dropped`/`security_id`/`exchange`, so the in-memory index and the persisted table now AGREE (both retain the first) instead of silently diverging. WARN-not-raise (data-safety-first): a raise would abort the whole ~750-underlying master load on a ~1e-7 event — a one-index blip must never become a 100% pull outage; keep-first mirrors the module's own first-wins gsym dedup + the lake's keep-first ledger semantics. HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): a real collision still leaves one REFERENCE_ONLY index unresolvable — availability IDENTICAL to today's silent store drop, only now LOUD + deterministic (first-wins vs store-order last-wins); the surrogate scheme itself (digest_size=4) is NOT widened — values byte-identical, no PK shift — a wider digest / explicit index-id map is a conscious operator follow-up if the warning ever fires; detector deliberately scoped to `Segment.INDEX` (broadening to the full store key is a trivial additive follow-up, kept minimal to match the reported failure). `_security_id` surrogate bytes + `InstrumentIndex` fields + the `build_index` signature ALL UNCHANGED. TESTS (fail-before/pass-after): `test_index_surrogate_collision_keeps_first_and_warns_regression` (two forged-collision INDEX rows → `universe` of 1, first kept, second absent, exactly ONE warning naming both — before the fix: universe of 2, no warning, the store then dropped one silently) + `test_non_index_identical_security_ids_both_kept_no_warning` (the `segment is INDEX` False path — CASH equities out of the detector's scope) + `test_distinct_index_surrogates_no_false_positive` (real NIFTY+VIX rows both load, no warn) + `test_engine_index_surrogates_are_mutually_distinct` (NSE-NIFTY/NSE-BANKNIFTY/BSE-SENSEX pin three mutually-distinct surrogates today — no latent collision in the locked engine universe). `instruments.py` at 100% line+branch (130 stmts/38 branches, 0 missing); ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the touched files. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate-cap/stored-bar/schema change.)
1264. **DEC-FETCH-SPILL-COUNT-CAP-001 — the fetch-pipeline on-disk overflow spill is now bounded in live WINDOW (handle) COUNT as well as on-disk BYTES — a tiny/empty-window flood past the count cap falls back to the SAME bounded, stop/drain-aware back-pressure instead of parking an unbounded number of resident overflow handles in memory** (2026-07-03; fix (e) of the data-safety batch — hermetic, `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_spill.py` + a comment-only `fetch_pipeline.py` reconcile + the two unit suites. PROBLEM (confirmed): the per-shard overflow deque (`FetchPipeline._overflow`) was bounded ONLY in on-disk BYTES — on a full queue, `submit → _spill_full_window` spills the bars to disk and appends a TINY `RawFetchResult(tail=…, spilled=handle)` HANDLE to the shard deque, and `FetchSpillArea.try_spill` gated ONLY on `self._reserved + size > self._max_bytes`. Each handle is a resident object graph (frozen `FetchTail` + `process`/`rehydrate` closures + `shard_key` + `SpilledWindow`), so deque MEMORY is O(handle count) — and `_encode_bars([]) == b"[]"` is 2 bytes, so a slow consumer fed an empty/tiny-window flood (the deep-OTM options chain is mostly empty) could park ~134M empty-window handles under the 256 MiB byte cap before it ever tripped → OOM; the `fetch_pipeline.py` comment claiming the deque is "unbounded in COUNT but bounded in MEMORY" was FALSE. FIX (COMMON — reuses the existing byte-budget machinery verbatim, same single `_lock`, same reserve-in-`try_spill` / release-in-`discard` / reset-in-`cleanup` lifecycle, zero new sync primitive): NEW `_DEFAULT_FETCH_SPILL_MAX_WINDOWS = 8192` (generous — at ~KB per handle graph it bounds the overflow to low tens of MiB; a NORMAL 30-day 1-minute window is ~0.6-0.8 MB so the byte cap trips FIRST at a few hundred windows — the count cap binds ONLY on the tiny/empty pathology) + env `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_SPILL_MAX_WINDOWS` via NEW `resolve_fetch_spill_max_windows` (the byte-for-byte structural twin of `resolve_fetch_spill_max_bytes` — unset/blank/non-int/non-positive fail-safe to the audited default, a bad value can never DISABLE the bound); `FetchSpillArea.__init__` gains keyword `max_windows` (defaulted — every existing construction site compiles + behaves identically; `< 1` → ValueError) + `_reserved_windows`; `under_lake_root` resolves both caps (live site `pull_pipeline.py` unchanged); `try_spill` gates `bytes-over OR count-over → None` and reserves BOTH under the ONE lock (one atomic two-phase reserve — two concurrent spills can never jointly overshoot either cap); the write-failure path releases BOTH; `discard` frees one slot (floored ≥ 0, same double-release guard as bytes); `cleanup` resets both; NEW thread-safe `reserved_windows` property mirrors `reserved_bytes`. PIPELINE UNCHANGED (comment-only): a count-cap `None` is byte-identical, from `submit`'s view, to a byte-cap `None` — `_spill_full_window` returns False WITHOUT `rehydrate(())` (bars intact, never lost) and the producer rides the EXISTING bounded `_back_pressure_put` (each timeout rechecks `_stopped` → re-raise + release, `_draining` → drop + re-fetch-next-pull) — NO deadlock, NO drop: a producer blocked on the cap still observes stop/drain (regression-pinned); the false `_overflow` comment is reconciled to "bounded in BOTH count AND memory". HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): bounds the OVERFLOW (bytes + handle count), NOT an OS-level RSS ceiling (setrlimit/cgroups out of scope, as DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001); when BOTH caps are hit the pull honestly SLOWS to the write rate (the pre-spill back-pressure — preferring a slowdown to an OOM, a permanently wedged volume stays PR #962's deadline's job); the count budget is GLOBAL while the deques are per-shard, so a shard with an empty overflow can be back-pressured because OTHER shards filled the global budget — a fairness nuance (memory is legitimately global), not a correctness/deadlock bug. TESTS (fail-before/pass-after, both proven failing against the reverted byte-only gate): `test_count_cap_rejects_spill_despite_byte_headroom` (max_windows=1 + 256 MiB headroom: the second EMPTY 2-byte spill returns None — pre-fix it returned a handle; discard frees the slot) + pipeline end-to-end `TestSpillWindowCountCap::test_count_cap_bounds_overflow_then_back_pressures_no_data_loss` (stalled consumer + max_windows=3: the deque never exceeds 3, the past-cap submit back-pressures bounded, releasing the consumer completes it, ALL four distinct-close windows processed with real bars, both budgets drain to 0) + `test_producer_blocked_on_count_cap_observes_drain` (a count-cap-blocked producer is released by `_draining` via the existing `fetch_pipeline.submit_dropped_draining` drop — re-fetched next pull, never a wedged fetch lane) + resolver suite `TestResolveFetchSpillMaxWindows` (every branch) + symmetric reserve/release pins (byte-cap rejection reserves no slot; disk-full LakeWriteHalt releases BOTH; cleanup resets BOTH; idempotent discard floors at 0; byte cap still binds independently under a huge window cap; `under_lake_root` default/explicit/env threading). The two test-file copies of the spillable-tail fixture were hoisted to ONE module-level `_spillable_result` (§11 COMMON). `fetch_spill.py` (160 stmts/28 branches) + `fetch_pipeline.py` (288/76) BOTH 100% line+branch; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the touched files (the repo-wide runs carry only the pre-existing env-stub findings, verified identical at clean HEAD). ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate-cap/stored-bar/schema change.)
1265. **DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-DEGRADED-TOMBSTONE-001 — a `record(degraded=True)` interior-gap/truncation SUCCESS→FAILED demotion is now TOMBSTONED in the window ledger exactly as `reopen_skipped`'s demotions are, so a CONCURRENT pull's on-disk clean `SUCCESS` can no longer silently override the demotion at the merge-on-save** (2026-07-03; fix (b) of the data-safety batch — `brutex/data/window_ledger.py` + `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py` + their two unit suites; landed BEFORE fix (a) so (a)'s cold-start degraded demotions are merge-protected. PROBLEM (confirmed): `WindowLedger.record()` demotes a clean bars-returning fetch to a re-pullable `FAILED` when `degraded=True` (DEC-INTERIOR-GAP-DETECT-001 / DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-REPULL-001), but the durable save's per-key merge (`merge_ledger_rows`) resolves a same-key conflict by `_row_preference`, whose FIRST key is the settledness rank (`SUCCESS`/`SKIPPED` 3 > `EMPTY` 2 > `FAILED` 1 > `PLANNED` 0) — so when a concurrent pull sharing the lake had already written a disk `SUCCESS` for the same window, the demoting pull's OWN save preferred the disk `SUCCESS` over its in-memory `FAILED` and the demotion was silently undone: the window read settled/skippable forever WITH the confirmed interior gap. The `reopen_skipped()` SKIPPED→FAILED demotion was already protected by the `_reopened` tombstone; `record()`'s demotion had no such protection. FIX (the THIRD instance of the deliberately-parallel per-set tombstone shape `_pruned`/`_reopened` — reuses the existing tombstone plumbing verbatim, zero new merge path): NEW `WindowLedger._degraded` set (`repr=False`/`compare=False`, never serialised — per-instance lifetime between load and save) populated in `record()` under the held lock by the EXACT guard `if degraded_success and status == FAILED:` (`degraded_success` selects the clean-SUCCESS-forced-to-FAILED case; `status == FAILED` excludes the accept-gap `SKIPPED` settle at the threshold, which is legitimately terminal rank-3 and must never be pinned against a concurrent SUCCESS) + NEW `degraded_keys()` snapshot accessor (the twin of `reopened_keys()`/`pruned_keys()`); `merge_ledger_rows` gains keyword `degraded_keys: frozenset[_RowKey] = frozenset()` (default byte-identical) and the reopened conflict short-circuit FOLDS to ONE branch `if key in reopened_keys or key in degraded_keys: continue` (in-memory demoted row wins outright — the disk copy never reaches the rank compare, O(1) set membership); `save_window_ledger`'s merge call threads `degraded_keys=ledger.degraded_keys()` alongside the pruned/reopened feeds. IDEMPOTENT + DURABLE: the tombstone is not in `to_rows` — Parquet schema unchanged, load→save→load stays a row fixed point, and re-running the demoting writer's save is bit-identical; a genuine later FILL surfaces correctly (the filling pull records `SUCCESS` with an EMPTY tombstone set, so ITS save keeps the SUCCESS). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10, same class the `_pruned`/`_reopened` docs state): this closes the DEMOTING writer's own-save resurrection (the reported bug); it does NOT force the demotion onto a SECOND writer's later flush — a concurrent writer that does not itself run the gap detector (a CLI `brutex fetch`, or `detect_completeness_gaps=False`) records plain SUCCESS and can re-mask under the more-settled rule on ITS save, a pre-existing property of the merge rule, not a regression; a re-masked `SUCCESS` is SKIPPABLE, so it does NOT self-heal on a steady-state pull — an INTERIOR gap re-demotes on the next lost-ledger COLD-START (the #1266 seed density cross-check leaves it un-seeded → re-planned → re-fetched) or an explicit operator re-plan; a re-masked TRAILING truncation needs the re-plan (the cold-start check is interior-only) — hostile-review wording fix, the docstring says the same. Not distributed consensus. TESTS (fail-before/pass-after, teeth proven by reverting the conflict line): ledger side `TestDegradedTombstone` (`test_degraded_demotion_tombstones_key` — the demoted key lands in `degraded_keys()`; `test_degraded_accept_gap_not_tombstoned` — threshold settle SKIPPED adds NO tombstone; `test_plain_records_not_tombstoned` — SUCCESS/EMPTY/transient-FAILED never tombstone; `test_degraded_keys_empty_by_default`; `test_from_rows_has_no_degraded_tombstone` — round-trip carries no tombstone) + store side `test_merge_keeps_degraded_over_disk_success` (memory FAILED "INTERIOR_GAP" vs disk SUCCESS: without the tombstone the disk SUCCESS wins — the bug, asserted in-test as teeth; with it the demotion survives) / `test_merge_reopened_still_wins` (the `or`'s first-operand short-circuit) / `test_merge_no_tombstone_uses_preference` (both sets empty → ordinary preference) / `test_merge_default_degraded_keys_omitted` (omitted kwarg byte-identical) / end-to-end `test_save_preserves_degraded_demotion` (disk SUCCESS → load → `record(degraded=True)` → save → reload reads FAILED "INTERIOR_GAP", not skippable — fails-before with the reverted line, verified). REVIEW-FOLD (post-batch hostile review): (1) the tombstone set is no longer add-only — a later SETTLED re-record of the SAME key (a genuine complete `SUCCESS` re-pull / the accept-gap `SKIPPED` settle) DISCARDS its earlier same-process tombstone, so the "a SKIPPED settle is never tombstoned" contract holds UNCONDITIONALLY (a re-pullable FAILED/EMPTY re-record deliberately KEEPS it — no completeness evidence, and discarding there would let a concurrent disk SUCCESS re-mask the gap on our own save); pinned by `test_success_repull_discards_stale_tombstone` + `test_accept_gap_settle_discards_prior_demotion_tombstone` + `test_repullable_rerecord_keeps_tombstone`. (2) the LOAD-BEARING save snapshot ORDER (`to_rows()` BEFORE `degraded_keys()` — the reason a demoted FAILED observed in the row snapshot is always still tombstoned) is now EXPLICIT in `save_window_ledger` with a comment, no longer an implicit argument-evaluation-order accident. `window_ledger.py` + `window_ledger_store.py` BOTH 100% line+branch (re-proven post-fold); ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on the touched files (the repo-wide runs carry only the pre-existing env-stub findings, verified identical at clean HEAD). ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate-cap/stored-bar/schema change.
1266. **DEC-COLDSTART-SEED-INTERIOR-GAP-001 — the lost-ledger COLD-START seed no longer span-stamps `SUCCESS` over a fetched `1minute` INDEX window whose lake span contains an interior multi-session hole — a density cross-check REUSING the COMMON `interior_gap_detect` core leaves the gappy window un-seeded (→ `PLANNED` → fetched → the fetch-time detector bounds it), and `/completeness` reads the symbol honestly NOT-`full`** (2026-07-03; fix (a) of the data-safety batch — `brutex/data/interior_gap_detect.py` + `brutex/data/window_ledger_store.py` + `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` + `brutex/dashboard/coverage_reconcile.py` + their suites; lands AFTER fix (b) #1265 so the degraded demotions the un-seeded window later produces are merge-protected. PROBLEM (confirmed): on a lost/corrupt-ledger cold-start, `seed_enclosed_windows` seeded a window `SUCCESS` purely from a SPAN test (lake `[first_date, last_date]` enclosing the window) with NO density/continuity check; `SUCCESS` is skippable, so a window with real bars at both ends but a multi-session interior hole was stamped settled and NEVER re-pulled — and the old docstring's compensation claim ("/completeness is density-based") was FALSE: the spot completeness verdict is LEDGER-backed (`_spot_dimension_verdict_with_floor` reads `full` on ledger-settled), so the hole read `full`; the fetch-time detector (DEC-INTERIOR-GAP-DETECT-001 #1031) could not compensate because a seeded window is skipped before any fetch. FIX (COMMON, zero logic copy — CLAUDE.md §11): (1) `interior_gap_detect.classify_interior_gap_dates(*, covered_dates, tolerance_sessions=None)` EXTRACTED as the date-set core (tolerance resolve + de-dup/sort + too-few + out-of-calendar abstain + `_largest_interior_session_gap`); `classify_interior_gap` becomes a thin timestamp→IST-date delegator (every existing caller byte-identical, GOLDEN-pinned equal). (2) `db_view.summarize_spot_datasets` gains keyword `session_date_segments: frozenset[str] | None = None` — default `None` BYTE-IDENTICAL (the hot /coverage + /completeness pollers untouched); when a dataset's `segment ∈ set` AND `interval == TRACK1_SPOT_INTERVAL` (`1minute`), the SAME single resilient aggregate appends `array_agg(DISTINCT <_IST_DATE_EXPR>)` (ONE pass, the SQL twin of `_ist_date` — IST parity GOLDEN-pinned incl. a 20:30-UTC midnight-rollover bar) and the row carries `session_dates: frozenset[date]` (empty on a zero-row/all-unreadable partition — the seed then honestly ABSTAINS). (3) `coverage_reconcile.load_lake_spans` forwards the kwarg; the SPOT wrapper `reconcile_ledger_with_lake` passes `_SESSION_DATE_SEGMENTS = {"INDEX"}` (the literal matches the on-disk partition dir + `Segment.INDEX.value` — REVISION 2), so ONLY the ~3 dense index `1minute` datasets pay the O(sessions) DISTINCT scan, once at pull start. (4) `seed_enclosed_windows` (NO signature change): after the enclosure + live-edge checks, and ONLY when `window_key.interval == TRACK1_SPOT_INTERVAL` AND the span carries `session_dates` (BELT-AND-BRACES — REVISION 1: the daily-phase reconcile runs `intervals=("1day",)`, and a DERIVED `1day` window is never fetched, so un-seeding it could never self-heal and would sit `PLANNED` forever; the read-side gate additionally never attaches `session_dates` to a `1day` row), the window's in-range covered dates are classified by the COMMON core — a confirmed interior gap SKIPS the seed with ONE `window_ledger.seed_interior_gap_skip` WARNING (span_key + window bounds + `largest_gap_sessions`); FAIL-CLOSED: any error inside the check logs `window_ledger.seed_interior_gap_error` and skips the seed (a re-pull is always data-safe — idempotent keep-first sink). 1267. **DEC-DAILY-OPEN-SUBSTITUTION-HONESTY-001 — the completeness surface now REPORTS, per symbol, how many stored 1-minute sessions have their FIRST present minute strictly after the 09:15 IST canonical open — i.e. the sessions whose DERIVED 1-day open is a silently SUBSTITUTED first-present-minute price (`tf_resampler` aggregates a bucket's open with `.first()`) — computed read-side in the SAME single per-session scan the coverage summary already runs, surfaced on every completeness projection, INFORMATIONAL only (the verdict stays `full`)** (2026-07-03; fix (c) of the data-safety batch — `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` + `brutex/dashboard/completeness.py` + the `completeness.html`/`universe.html` templates + their suites; lands LAST, rebased onto fix (a) #1266's `summarize_spot_datasets` enrichment so both share ONE per-session CTE.
