1166. **DEC-RUST-HARDENING-R2-001 — Rust FFI hardening round 2: four hardening tasks over the two PyO3 kernel crates — (1) fno-math FFI-boundary overflow guards (a garbage/hostile input now raises a clean Python `ValueError` instead of tripping `overflow-checks = true` + `panic = "abort"` → SIGABRT killing the WHOLE host interpreter), (2) twin-parity GOLDENS for the stateful indicator twins (`VwapState` / `MarketStructureState`, Rust production vs Python mirror) — which surfaced + closed ONE latent twin domain hole, (3) the trading-core `MAX_ANCHOR_PAISA` safety comment RE-DERIVED for the coefficient-4 pivot ladder (r5/s5) it had silently drifted from, (4) a `brutex doctor` wheel-source freshness stage + an import-time compiled-symbol handshake in the `trading_core` shim** (2026-07-03 on `claude/vigilant-mayer-9y1hni`; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (+ the authorized NIFTY-futures dynamic track) per CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change; both crates keep `panic = "abort"` + `overflow-checks = true` — the guards move the failure to the FFI edge, they NEVER weaken the finance-safety profile). **TASK 1 (R2-RC-F1 — fno-math overflow guards):** `add_u64` rewrote onto a pure `add_u64_checked` (`checked_add` → `Result<_, String>`, the `#[pyfunction]` maps to `ValueError`; the EXACT old-abort repro `add_u64(2**63, 2**63)` — previously SIGABRT exit 134, uncatchable from Python — now a clean `ValueError`, pinned from Python AND in `cargo test`); the `ResidentSweepSim` trade-sim kernel gains ONE boundary envelope `MAX_PRICE_PAISA = i64::MAX / 8` (mirrors the sibling trading-core `MAX_ANCHOR_PAISA` idiom): `check_price_column` validates all four OHLC paisa columns ONCE at `build` (O(N_bars), NOT on the hot loop) and `check_level_distance` validates the SL/TP distances (`[0, C]`; `None` = leg disabled always valid) at the `simulate_masks`/`count_trades` batch entry via new pure `*_impl` cores — so the hot-loop walker arithmetic stays DELIBERATELY UNGUARDED with the guarantee carried entirely by the boundary proof (`|entry ± d| ≤ 2C`, `|pnl| ≤ 3C < i64::MAX`; each unguarded site carries the derivation doc). The trading-core metadata FFI edges got the SAME treatment (the same SIGABRT class): `weekday_from_ordinal` / `minute_of_session` / `derive_bar_metadata` are now range-guarded pure `*_impl` fns (`day_ordinal ∈ [1, 3_652_059]` — the exact Python `date.toordinal()` domain; civil seconds `∈ [0, 86_399]`; h/m/s reuses the existing `seconds_of_day_impl` guard), each exact abort repro (`weekday_from_ordinal(i64::MIN)` overflowing `ordinal − 1`; `minute_of_session(i64::MAX, −1)` overflowing `tod − open`; `hour = 2_000_000` overflowing `hour·3600`) pinned Err-not-abort in `cargo test` + `ValueError` from Python; valid-domain delegation pinned byte-identical to the pure core. NO valid input is ever rejected (the ceiling ≈ ₹1.15·10¹⁶ paisa; SENSEX ≈ 8·10⁶) — every existing golden byte-unchanged. **TASK 2 (R2-RC-F2 — twin-parity goldens):** the "bit-for-bit twin" claim for the STATEFUL indicators (`trading_core.VwapState`/`MarketStructureState` — the production side Stage-1A drives — vs the Python mirrors in `brutex/indicators/`) previously rested on manual mirroring (the frozen 400-case answer-key pins the EVALUATOR bits, not the per-bar `.update()` derivation; no test imported both twins). NEW language-neutral golden streams `tests/golden/fixtures/twin_state_golden_vectors.json` (fixed seed 20260703; expected values frozen FROM THE RUST PRODUCTION TWIN by `tests/golden/generate_twin_state_golden.py`; 4 VWAP + 10 market-structure streams covering IST session/day-ordinal resets, the pre-open exclusion, zero/negative-volume skip bars, `MAX_BAR_PAISA`-ceiling bars whose `cum_pv` exceeds i64 (the i128/unbounded-int truncating-division seam), k ∈ {1,2,3} fractal confirmation delays incl. break-on-the-confirming-bar + tied-extreme no-confirm windows, and i64-extreme levels) replayed through BOTH twins by `tests/unit/test_twin_state_golden_parity.py` (sha256 fixture manifest + non-vacuity pins: all four BOS/CHoCH signals actually fire). **TWIN-DIVERGENCE VERDICT: NO divergence on the valid domain — every per-bar output of both twins is bit-identical to the frozen expectation across all 14 streams. ONE LATENT domain hole found + closed:** for a NEGATIVE `typical_paisa` the twins would silently diverge by one paisa once `cum_pv` went negative (Rust i128 `/` truncates toward zero; Python `//` floors) — a negative typical is not a real price (HLC3 of positive prices), so BOTH twins now reject it with an identical guard-first `ValueError` at the boundary (`vwap_update_guard` in `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs` + the mirrored guard in `brutex/indicators/vwap.py::VwapState.update`), closing the hole at the domain edge instead of leaving a silent one-paisa disagreement; the non-negative envelope is what makes the documented floor==trunc identity in `VwapState.value` unconditionally true. **TASK 3 (comment-only, ZERO behavior change):** the `MAX_ANCHOR_PAISA` safety comment in `rust/trading-core/src/python.rs` still derived its bound against the COEFFICIENT-3 ladder (`r4 = pdh + 3·(p − pdl)`, "≤ 7·(i64::MAX/8)"), stale since PR-2 (DEC-NIFTY-INDICATORS-001) added the coefficient-4 rungs `r5 = pdh + 4·(p − pdl)` / `s5 = pdl − 4·(pdh − p)`: the loose `p ≤ pdh` bound NO LONGER suffices at coefficient 4 (it shows only `9M > i64::MAX`), but the always-on `pdl ≤ pdc ≤ pdh` asserts give `p − pdl ≤ ⅔·(pdh − pdl) + 1`, hence `|r5| ≤ 19M/3 + 4 ≈ 6.34·M < 8M ≤ i64::MAX` — STILL provably overflow-free at the SAME ceiling; the constant did NOT need lowering and no golden moved. The comment now carries the full coefficient-4 derivation so the proof matches the shipped ladder. **TASK 4 (R2-CC-G1 — wheel-source freshness):** run identity records `code_commit_sha` + `trading_core.__version__`, but nothing bound the installed `.so` to the source tree — a run could record commit X while executing commit-W Rust kernels, silently (the exact failure three audit agents hit: a stale wheel missing `seconds_of_day`). NOW: (a) the `trading_core` shim asserts at import — UNCONDITIONAL, no env escape (one could not help: the re-export from-import would fail regardless) — that the compiled module exposes EVERY re-exported symbol (`_EXPECTED_COMPILED_SYMBOLS`), raising an actionable `ImportError` naming the missing symbol(s) + the `maturin develop --release` remedy; (b) NEW `__build_crate_version__` (derived from the `.so`-baked `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, never hardcoded; deliberately NOT in `__all__` so the frozen `brutex.math` facade golden is untouched) + the in-repo fingerprint `rust/trading-core/python/trading_core/EXPECTED_BUILD.json` (pinned test-equal to `_EXPECTED_COMPILED_SYMBOLS` so the two cannot drift) feed (c) NEW `brutex/doctor.py::check_wheel_freshness` — a non-fatal advisory **WARN** stage (NEW `WARN` status on `CheckResult`/`DoctorReport`; never blocks the doctor) comparing installed surface + crate version against the fingerprint, `BRUTEX_SKIP_WHEEL_FRESHNESS=1` skips THIS STAGE ONLY. HONEST reachability envelope (Golden Rule #10) documented in-code: through the `brutex` CLI the stage's "not importable" WARN arm can never execute — `brutex.cli` transitively imports `trading_core`, so a symbol-stale wheel hard-fails with the shim's own actionable ImportError first; the stage's WARN teeth via the CLI are the drift classes that still import (crate-version mismatch, unexpected extra symbols, stale/malformed fingerprint). **HONEST RESIDUAL GAP (Golden Rule #10, the named follow-up):** the version + symbol-set handshake catches a stale wheel that dropped/added a symbol or changed crate version; it does NOT catch same-version, symbol-compatible BEHAVIORAL drift (Rust source changed while the version + symbol surface stayed identical — that wheel imports clean and passes this stage). Closing that class needs a `build.rs` source-content digest baked into the wheel and compared by the doctor — deliberately OUT of this change's scope, stated at every surface (shim docstring, fingerprint `_comment`, doctor docstring, this entry). **Verification (fresh runs 2026-07-03, repo venv 3.12.3, rebuilt wheels installed):** `cargo test --release` — fno-math **537 passed** (536 unit + 1 doctest), trading-core **133 passed**, 0 failed; `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --release --all-targets` clean on both crates; pytest — NEW `test_fno_math_overflow_guard.py` (17) + `test_trading_core_ffi_guards.py` (14) + `test_twin_state_golden_parity.py` (6) + `test_doctor_wheel_freshness.py` (25) + `test_doctor.py` (38) = 100 passed; the golden + Rust-parity sweep (`tests/golden` + `test_python_rust_parity.py`) 312 passed; the vwap-related sweep 44 passed; the live ValueError-not-SIGABRT proof from Python: `fno_math.add_u64(2**63, 2**63)` → `ValueError: add_u64: … overflows u64 …`, interpreter alive (exit 0). 1164. **DEC-PIPELINE-STALL-HEARTBEAT-001 — the pipeline pull's stall watchdog now HEARS the post-fetch stages (Greeks enrichment · timeframe prebuild · movers warm) via the COMMON `emit_progress_beat` seam, and a HUNG declaration is an honest STALLED-SUSPECT marker that HOLDS the single-flight while the worker thread is alive — closing the forensically-proven false-positive kill + double-run race; PLUS the frozen job-progress counters ("45/45 units, 0 BARS" through a 14.48M-bar historical fill) are fixed** (2026-07-03 on `claude/stoic-maxwell-km8gfe`; dashboard job/progress layer + four one-line loop beats + tests ONLY; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO lake-schema/stored-bar/scope/vocab/rate-cap change — the fetch behaviour is byte-identical). **FORENSICALLY PROVEN BUG (operator run 2026-07-02, six logs):** the `PullWatchdog` (`pull_stall.py`, `DEFAULT_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600`, poll = timeout/3) received heartbeats ONLY on the per-pair fetch advance + ledger sync (`pull_jobs._on_progress` / `sync_from_ledger`); the post-fetch GREEKS enrichment (6.5 min small-run, 1-3 h projected full-history), PREBUILD (10.2 min small-run, 1-5 h projected) and MOVERS WARM (6.4 min) never beat. Last fetch beat 13:58:21 → the timer fired `_on_hung` at ~14:11:10 (`pull stalled — no progress for 769s (timeout 600s)`), FAILED the progress AND cleared `_running` + released the account single-flight — while the worker thread kept running and SUCCEEDED (prebuild done 14:15:08, 47.9M bars; movers warm + gate release clean). Two harms: (a) a false FAILED headline on a succeeding run; (b) the released single-flight admitting a SECOND pull concurrent with the still-running zombie worker — a double-run race on the same lake. **FIX 1 (heartbeat seams — REUSE, no new plumbing, §11 COMMON):** the process-global `brutex/observability/progress_beat.py` seam (DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001) is ALREADY registered by `BackgroundPullJob._run` for the whole run, so the three silent stages now beat it per unit of work — `greeks_enrich.enrich_greeks_for_targets` beats per CONTRACT (loop top), `gated_prebuild._run_spot_phase` beats per UNDERLYING + `_run_contract_phase` per CONTRACT, `timeframe_materialize.materialize_timeframes` beats per derived TIMEFRAME (within-symbol granularity for a deep-history partition), `movers_warm.warm_movers_snapshots` beats per warm JOB — each a one-line `emit_progress_beat()` (no-op when nothing is registered, so CLI/standalone callers are byte-unchanged; best-effort; O(1)). **FIX 2 (honest HUNG semantics — the design chosen over both alternatives):** `_on_hung` no longer fails the run or releases anything: it fires the CRITICAL pull-halt alert ("stalled-suspect … worker still running — NOT killed", naming the silent PHASE) + marks the progress via NEW `PullProgress.mark_stalled` (a `stalled`/`stall_detail` DEGRADED marker on the snapshot/JSON — state stays `running`; a no-op unless RUNNING so a late edge can never stamp a settled run) and DELIBERATELY keeps `_running` + the account flock HELD — the worker thread still owns the lake, so releasing IS the double-run race; the release happens ONLY in `_run`'s `finally` when the thread actually exits (a never-exiting wedge keeps the flag held, LOUDLY — alert + marker + `pull_stall.stalled_suspect` log; a process restart releases the flock on fd close). The timer is NOT stopped at the edge, so a later heartbeat fires the HUNG→HEALTHY recovery: NEW `PullWatchdog.on_recovery` post-construction hook (factory signature unchanged) → `_on_recovered` clears the marker; both edges identity-gated (a stale edge never touches a newer run); `finish`/`fail` also clear the marker. Detection is PRESERVED: a genuine hang (seams silent) still alerts within one poll — the seams make silence a TRUE signal; the timeout was NOT raised and the watchdog NOT removed. **FIX 3 (frozen counters, the sibling display bug):** the pipeline job runs `ledger_synced=True`, so the historical phase's per-pair hook only refreshed the LABEL and `_metadata_progress_sync` hard-coded `bars=0` — the UI froze at the metadata phase's "45/45 units, 0 BARS, 0 failed" (45 = 2 expiry cells + 43 contract jobs) while 14.48M bars streamed. Now: `PullProgress.sync`/`sync_from_ledger` accept `bars=None` = PRESERVE the cumulative tally (the metadata sync passes it — never wipes the spot phase's bars); `BackgroundPullJob.set_phase` gains `pair_progress=` (default False, everything else byte-identical) and the pipeline enters the historical phase with `set_phase("historical", pair_progress=True)`, flipping the per-pair hook to `PullProgress.advance(grow_total=True)` — an OPEN-ENDED O(1) advance (total grows with completed, since the pair total is unknown at the job layer) so units + cumulative bars + failed all MOVE; HONEST envelope: percent reads 100 during that phase (the displayed total is "units processed so far", not a known denominator — no worse than the frozen 45/45 it replaces, stated in the docstring); the route also stamps honest `set_phase("prebuild")` / `set_phase("movers")` labels so a stall marker names the true silent stage. **TESTS (fail-before/pass-after):** NEW `tests/unit/test_pipeline_stall_heartbeat.py` (11) — (a) a fake pipeline whose greeks+prebuild+movers stages span 3×1200 s of fake clock WITH the seams beating → the real `PullWatchdog` never fires and the job finishes `done`; (b) the same shape with the seams SILENT → the alert fires ONCE + `stalled=true` + state stays `running` + a second `start` is REFUSED mid-wedge (single-flight held), then the worker's exit releases + finishes `done`; (c) the metadata `bars=None` preserve + the historical pair-progress advance past the 45/45 freeze (units 45→48, bars 0→14.48M, failed 1) + the label-only spot contract + the `set_phase` reset; (d) the NAMED forensic regression — the REAL `enrich_greeks_for_targets` loop under a 769 s-equivalent fake-clock silence with per-contract polls → zero alerts (reverting the greeks beat fails it); plus per-seam beat-count pins for all four loops (greeks 3/contracts, prebuild 4/spot+futures+options, timeframes 3/TF incl. a skip, movers 3/job). REWRITTEN pins: `test_dashboard_pull_stall.py` (hung edge → alert + stalled-suspect + flight HELD; worker-success-after-hung finishes `done`; recovery clears; raising mark/clear swallowed; late hung/recovery edges identity-gated; the white-box `_run`-finally false-arm) — the prior release-on-hung + stale-finally interleavings (which DEPENDED on the removed release) are superseded; `test_pull_jobs.py::TestOnHung` + `test_pull_jobs_singleflight.py::test_on_hung_holds_the_guard_until_worker_exit` (spy guard: `exited==0` at the edge, `==1` only at worker exit); `test_pull_progress.py` to_dict + `test_dashboard_pull_expiries_contracts_route.py` metadata-sync pins flipped to the new honest values. **Verification (fresh runs 2026-07-03, repo venv):** 263 touched-module suite tests + the 11 new green; per-module coverage gate (`scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py --base origin/main`) 100% line+branch on every touched `brutex/` module; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` clean on every touched file; structlog-only (`pull_stall.stalled_suspect` / `pull_stall.stalled_recovered` events). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/{pull_jobs,pull_stall,pull_progress,gated_prebuild,movers_warm,app}.py`, `brutex/data/{greeks_enrich,timeframe_materialize}.py`, `tests/unit/test_pipeline_stall_heartbeat.py` (NEW) + 5 updated test files, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Supersedes** the release-on-hung arm of DEC-PULL-STALL-DETECTION-001 (#945 — the detector + timer + per-run identity gate are KEPT; only the edge's kill/release action is replaced) and extends DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001 (the seam this reuses) + DEC-SPOT-WINDOW-PROGRESS-001 / DEC-METADATA-LIVE-PROGRESS-001 (the ledger-synced progress contract, now phase-aware). 1162. **DEC-CI-GATE-INTEGRITY-R2-001 — the CI/CD gate-integrity hardening pass (R2-CI-1..6): six confirmed workflow-integrity gaps closed across the six GitHub Actions workflows, EVERY change ADD-only (a gate is added, made louder, or narrowed to the right event — NO gate is removed, skipped, or loosened; the task's HARD no-weakening rule + CLAUDE.md §12 100%-standards + §13 merge-readiness charter honoured)** (2026-07-03 on `claude/focused-tesla-6smqxr`; `.github/workflows/{ci,mutation,branch-protection-drift,stress-nightly,bench-m4pro,verify-m4pro}.yml` + this ledger entry ONLY — ZERO `brutex/` source touched, so the ENGINE stays NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063, and NO route/lake-schema/stored-bar/scope/vocab/rate-cap change; actionlint was the intended review tool but is unavailable in this sandbox, so a PyYAML structural parse of all six files (all OK) + the 4-agent hostile review stood in — the review found NO blockers, all SHIP, zero MAJORs). **R2-CI-1 (DEC-CI-OK-NODHAN-GATE-001 · ci.yml):** the zero-dhan enforcement guard `no-dhan-guard` (no event `if:`, so it never legitimately skips) is now a member of the required `ci-ok` aggregate's `needs:` list (+ its echo line + its entry in the status-collection array), so a RED no-dhan-guard is a HARD fail of the one branch-protection-required `CI OK` context — it is enforced VIA the aggregate, deliberately NOT registered as a direct required context, so the branch-protection-drift expected snapshot is untouched (ci-ok `needs:` count is now exactly 32). **R2-CI-2 (DEC-DRIFT-MISSING-RULE-FAIL-001 · branch-protection-drift.yml):** the WORST-case drift — the `main` protection rule missing ENTIRELY (the `gh api .../branches/main/protection` fetch 404s) — used to `::warning::` + `exit 0` and alert nobody, silently GREEN, directly contradicting the workflow's own claim to catch a removed rule; it now writes a CRITICAL `drift-summary.txt`, sets `RULE_MISSING=true`, the issue-open step fires on `always() && (RULE_MISSING || (failure() && drift failure))` so it files/refreshes the drift-alert issue on the missing-rule path too, and a NEW final step (`if: RULE_MISSING == 'true'`) `exit 1`s the job AFTER the alert — so a deleted/absent rule can never report success; the present-rule compare path stays byte-identical (still fails via the compare step's `sys.exit(1)`). **R2-CI-3 (mutation.yml + ci.yml):** (a) the three `Open GitHub issue on failure` steps (python state.py + rust fno-math + rust trading-core) were `if: failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule'` — a push-to-main mutation FAILURE alerted nobody; widened to bare `if: failure()` (this workflow has NO pull_request trigger, so there is no PR-noise path to suppress). (b) concurrency `cancel-in-progress` is now `${{ github.event_name != 'push' }}`: a push run is no longer silently CANCELLED mid-flight by a newer push (a cancelled run is not a failure and emits NO signal, so a surviving-mutant failure would vanish) — push runs now always run to completion (and can alert); schedule + workflow_dispatch keep `cancel-in-progress=true` (event-keyed group, so the weekly pass + manual dispatches still supersede their own kind). (c) the ci.yml `mutation-py` header comment is reworded `per-push` → `per-PR on critical modules` + a HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10) documenting that this per-run gate covers EXACTLY TWO modules (`brutex/orchestrator/state.py` ≥98% / 300 s + `brutex/money.py` ≥99% / 240 s) kept small to fit `timeout-minutes` — the BROAD per-module mutation pass (Python state.py + Rust fno-math + Rust trading-core, ≥85% each) lives in mutation.yml on schedule/dispatch/push-to-main; comment-only, no `if:`/name/timeout/floor change, so the `Python mutation (mutmut on critical modules)` required context is byte-preserved. **R2-CI-4 (DEC-CI-OK-PR-ONLY-NAME-001 · ci.yml):** the `ci-ok` job `name:` is now event-conditional — the exact branch-protection-required string `CI OK (aggregate gate)` is minted ONLY on `pull_request`; a non-PR run reports `CI OK (non-PR aggregate)`, deliberately NOT a required context. This closes a shadow where a green non-PR `CI OK (aggregate gate)` run (several sub-gates — conv-commits/zplus-pr-guard/definition-of-ready/dec-id-validator/bugfix-regression-scan/no-hallucination-scan — SKIP on non-PR events and skipped==pass) could SHADOW a red pull_request run on the manual-merge path; on `pull_request` the name is byte-identical to the drift expected snapshot (line 133) so no existing green requirement breaks. HONEST (Golden Rule #10): the manual-merge shadow's real-world EXPLOITABILITY is UNVERIFIED (it depends on the server-side branch-protection matcher's multi-run semantics, not reproducible from this sandbox), but the mechanism is now CLOSED by construction — a non-PR run can no longer mint the required name (a SECOND guard on the #571 hole DEC-AUTOMERGE-CLEAN-STRICT-001 already closed); NARROWS the producing event (adds enforcement), removes no gate. **R2-CI-5 (stress-nightly.yml + bench-m4pro.yml + verify-m4pro.yml):** each self-hosted/nightly workflow gains a `permissions: issues: write` + an `Open issue on failure` step mirroring safety.yml's proven COMMON (§11) dedup-by-title-per-sha alert (labelled bug + the job kind + critical), gated `if: failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule'` — so a failing NIGHTLY run (the primary silent path) now alerts. HONEST (Golden Rule #10): schedule-only by design (matches the finding's own plannedFix + the safety.yml pattern) — a failure on a push/workflow_dispatch trigger of these three still alerts nobody; that residual is observability-completeness ONLY (none of the three is a `ci-ok` need or a branch-protection required context, so no merge gate is affected), a deliberate asymmetry vs R2-CI-3(a)'s bare `failure()` (which is a quality gate on push-to-main). **R2-CI-6 (DEC-DRIFT-EXPECTED-SUBSET-DOC-001 · branch-protection-drift.yml):** the FALSE `Required: every gate in ci.yml's ci-ok needs:` comment (the `expected_required_checks` set is really a curated SUBSET — 22 direct required contexts, not all 32 needs) is rewritten into a POLICY comment explaining the 11 ci-ok needs (actionlint, rust-trading-core, ledger-numbering, no-dhan-guard, zplus-pr-guard, definition-of-ready, dec-id-validator, bugfix-regression-scan, no-hallucination-scan, conv-commits, chaos-race) that are enforced TRANSITIVELY through the one required `CI OK (aggregate gate)` context and must NOT be added to the expected set (adding them would make each independently required, regressing the manual-merge path); doc-accuracy, no behaviour change, but it makes the drift detector's own contract HONEST. **Folded doc-accuracy NITs (the only quick-safe items the 4-agent review surfaced; both verified before editing, both in assigned files, neither weakens a gate):** branch-protection-drift.yml's R2-CI-6 comment `~31 needs` → `32 needs` (+ `~11` → `11`, the enumerated list is exactly 11 including no-dhan-guard from R2-CI-1) and ci.yml's R2-CI-4 cross-reference `line 93` → `line 133` (R2-CI-6's added comment block pushed the `CI OK (aggregate gate)` snapshot literal down). **4-agent hostile review verdicts (embedded in the PR body):** addresses-finding — SHIP (each edit closes its finding); no-weakening (ADD-only) — SHIP; yaml-expr-correctness — SHIP; required-context-coherence — SHIP (R2-CI-4 STRENGTHENS auto-merge; one MINOR stale-prose coherence note in the OUT-OF-SCOPE auto-merge.yml filed as a follow-up, not a fix here since auto-merge.yml is outside the assigned file set). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** VERIFIED — all six files parse as valid YAML, each fix reviewed against the real file lines, no gate removed/skipped/loosened; UNVERIFIED — actionlint could not run in this sandbox (structural parse + review substituted), the live Groww vendor cannot be exercised from the sandbox (no rate-limit / §2 Rule 6 constant is touched by this CI-only PR), and the R2-CI-4 manual-merge shadow's exploitability is UNVERIFIED-but-mechanism-closed. **Test types:** static (YAML structural parse of all six workflows) + review (4-agent hostile) + doc-accuracy verification (ci-ok needs count = 32, snapshot literal at line 133, both grepped from the live files). **Files:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/mutation.yml`, `.github/workflows/branch-protection-drift.yml`, `.github/workflows/stress-nightly.yml`, `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml`, `.github/workflows/verify-m4pro.yml`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-CI-GATE-INTEGRITY-R2-001. **Builds on** DEC-CICD-GATE-HONESTY-001 (the ledger-numbering de-conflation this extends), DEC-AUTOMERGE-CLEAN-STRICT-001 (#571 — the manual-merge shadow R2-CI-4 adds a second guard on), CLAUDE.md §2 Golden Rules #10/#11 + §12/§13. 1161. **DEC-MAPPING-COLLISION-HONESTY-001 — instrument-mapping collisions are made LOUD + DETERMINISTIC end-to-end (the mapping-collision honesty pack + its 3 hostile-review folds): (a) the `(exchange, trading_symbol)` pair maps (`by_exchange_symbol` / `groww_symbol_by_pair`) now genuinely FIRST-WIN on a pair collision — consistent with `by_groww_symbol`, as the docstring already claimed — and WARN (`instrument_master.pair_key_collision`) naming BOTH the kept and the dropped groww_symbol; (b) a write-boundary DISTINCT-name identity collision in `InstrumentStore.upsert_many` — two rows sharing one `(security_id, exch_id, segment)` identity under DIFFERENT `symbol_name`s, the OBSERVED live "13, NSE, CASH" case — keeps the graceful last-wins dedup (the bulk INSERT stays PK-crash-proof) but WARNs (`instrument_store.security_id_collision`) naming BOTH symbols and is COUNTED on the NEW `UpsertResult.security_id_collisions`, and — the review's task-spec-gap fold — the count is now THREADED into the actual `/universe` LOAD REPORT end-to-end (`load_instrument_master` captures the previously-DISCARDED UpsertResult → a `"security_id_collisions"` report key the `load-instruments` route serialises verbatim + the `universe.load.groww` counts log line; fail-before: the field was WRITE-ONLY — no caller read it); (c) `universe_constituents.py` — an NTM ISIN/ticker duplicate keeps the DETERMINISTIC lowest-security_id choice but WARNs naming both candidate rows, and `held_members`' `name_by_id` is PARTITIONED to NSE cash equities so a cross-segment security_id collision can no longer return the WRONG company name; (d) a BLANK — and per the review fold now also WHITESPACE-only (`" "`/`"\t"`) — `trading_symbol` row is EXCLUDED from the pair maps (it would collapse rows onto the `(exchange, "")` / `(exchange, " ")` key; it stays pullable by its own groww_symbol + in the universe) and counted in ONE aggregate `instrument_master.blank_symbol_pair_skipped` WARNING** (2026-07-03; `brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py` + `brutex/data/instrument_store.py` + `brutex/universe_constituents.py` + `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`; 1170. **DEC-MONEYNESS-REGISTRY-STEP-001 — the display ATM±N strike-grid step now derives from the AUTHORITATIVE vendor strike chain in `registry.duckdb` when available, and the lake-observed fallback is honestly labelled LOW-CONFIDENCE on both `/db` and `/movers` — a sparsely-pulled expiry can no longer silently overestimate the step** (2026-07-03; READ-ONLY display fix — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY, NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change). **THE GAP:** both moneyness surfaces derived the grid step from the SPARSE lake-observed strike set (`db_view._fno_strike_step` sibling-partition glob; `movers_options.compute_options_candidates` screened-ladder `strikes_by_key`) — on a sparsely-pulled expiry (only alternate strikes have candles: the 30d option window + quarantines make this real) the min OBSERVED gap is an integer multiple of the true base step, so the ATM±N depth was DIVIDED ("ITM -10" read "ITM -5") and the `step/2` ATM band WIDENED (true ±1 strikes read "ATM"). **THE FIX (mirrors DEC-MOVERS-CALENDAR-TIERS-001's registry-with-graceful-fallback pattern):** (1) `brutex/data/moneyness.py` gains the ONE confidence-aware resolver `resolve_strike_step(observed, *, authoritative_strikes=None) -> StrikeStepResult(step, confidence)` + `StepConfidence` StrEnum (`registry`/`observed`); `derive_strike_step` keeps the single gap-math source of truth + a back-compat `authoritative_strikes=` facade kwarg. (2) NEW COMMON `brutex/dashboard/registry_strikes.py::load_registry_strike_chains(registry_path, *, exchange/underlying/expiry)` reads the FULL vendor CE/PE ladders per `(underlying, expiry)` from `RegistryStore.list_contracts` (float→`Decimal(str(...))` — the engine's Decimal-only guard), with the exact `load_registry_expiries` graceful triad: absent/empty/`RegistryError` → `None` (a CLI-only lake is never broken), imported by BOTH db_view and movers_options' wiring (no dashboard cross-import). (3) `/db`: `query_candles` gains `registry_path=` (the route passes `registry_path_for(store.path)`); the one chain is memoised behind the SAME injected `count_cache` + write-generation under the new `fno_strike_chain_key` (`strikechain|` namespace, collision-free), and the page payload carries `strike_step_confidence` (`"registry"`/`"observed"`/`null`); `db.html` renders a small muted `.stepnote` honesty line on an `observed` page. (4) `/movers`: `compute_options_candidates`/`run_options_snapshot` gain `registry_strike_chains=`; `build_app` loads the per-exchange chain set via a dedicated generation-stamped `_options_strikes_cache` (`MoversSnapshotCache`, mirrors `_options_calendar_cache`; the post-pull warm mirrors it) and `OptionMover`/`_option_row` carry `strike_step_confidence` (qualifying a PRESENT step only — no step ⇒ `null`, never a dangling flag); `movers.html` appends a trailing `" ~"` marker to an `observed` moneyness chip (suffix — the `startsWith` tint is untouched). **HONEST (Golden Rule #1/#10):** "authoritative" = the vendor-listed chain AS OF the last metadata pull — live vendor chain completeness is UNVERIFIED from this sandbox (Groww unreachable); a registry↔lake underlying-token mismatch degrades gracefully to the observed ladder + the low-confidence label (regression-pinned); the no-registry behaviour is byte-identical in the STEP (only the honesty label is new). Regression-pinned fails-before/passes-after on BOTH paths (sparse 24000/24100 lake reads "OTM +1"/"+4" observed → "OTM +2"/"+8" registry); generation-memoisation pinned on both caches (one registry read per generation, re-read on bump). `moneyness.py` + `registry_strikes.py` + `db_view.py` + `movers_options.py` 100% line+branch; touched `app.py` lines ride the route/warm suites; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on every touched file.

1190. **DEC-TOKEN-STALE-PAUSE-001 — a dead daily token PAUSES the fetch lane instead of burning window attempts: the read-only broker's `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` reauth outcome now enters a bounded, single-flight-aware, watchdog-beating WAIT (`SdkRefresher.await_token_recovery`, default 420 s, env `BRUTEX_GROWW_TOKEN_STALE_WAIT_S`) inside `GrowwClient._call`, so the recurring 06:00-IST reset → external-Lambda mint lag never reaches the window ladder — the forensic 111-ledger-FAILED-window / 339-wasted-call shape is eliminated; a genuinely dead broker still fails LOUDLY after ONE shared per-generation deadline (fail-fast re-entries; the FAILED-defer + until-clean + DEC-VENDOR-DOWN-BREAKER-001 dead-credential escalation paths are byte-preserved)** (2026-07-04 on `claude/stoic-maxwell-km8gfe`; Groww adapter reauth/client layer + tests ONLY — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO lake-schema/stored-bar/scope/vocab/rate-cap change — a fetch against a LIVE token is byte-identical). **FORENSICALLY PROVEN BUG (operator's real overnight run, 2026-07-04, log timestamps 00:30:00.946Z→00:35:30.251Z = 06:00:00→06:05:30 IST):** at the 06:00-IST Groww token reset the read-only AWS SSM token broker (DEC-AWS-ONLY-CREDS-001 — the Lambda is the SOLE minter, operator-confirmed the ONLY deployment mode) held no fresh token until the Lambda's 06:05:31 mint. During those 5.5 minutes every fetch raised the RETRYABLE `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` (DEC-BROKER-READONLY-REAUTH-REREAD-001 — deliberately NOT terminal-auth), and the F&O window ladder (`option_ingest` transient path, `_DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2` → 3 attempts) burned ALL 3 attempts INSIDE the outage for 111 windows (339 failed calls across 115 windows, attempt distribution 115/113/111), settling them ledger-FAILED — rescued only by the outer until-clean rounds (wasteful + operator-scary), and every failure fed `on_timeout` → 339 `rate.timeout` events drove the AIMD ladder toward the deep 1 r/s floor. This recurs on EVERY 06:00-IST crossing (CLAUDE.md §6 token-lifetime row). **FIX (the operator decree "a dead token should pause the fetch lane, not burn window attempts") — the ONE COMMON chokepoint is the client `_call` reauth branch (the single-flight `SdkRefresher` machinery of DEC-GROWW-TOKEN-REAUTH-001 #909/#910):** (1) *the gate* — `_call` wraps `refresher.reauth(...)` in `except GrowwTokenStillStaleError:` → NEW `SdkRefresher.await_token_recovery(seen_generation, wait_seconds, poll_seconds, sleep, clock, method)`: the worker WAITS, polling every `GROWW_TOKEN_STALE_POLL_S` (5 s), until EITHER the generation moves past `seen_generation` (a fresh token was adopted — the call retries via the existing `attempt -= 1` reauth buy-back, so NO window attempt is spent and NO ladder feed happens) OR the wall-clock deadline expires (a fresh `GrowwTokenStillStaleError` propagates EXACTLY as before — window defers FAILED, re-pullable). ONLY that error class engages the gate: `is_terminal_auth_failure` stays terminal (a revoked key never loops), `GrowwTokenIssuanceThrottled` propagates as before, and the LOCAL-mint mode (`readonly_reread=None`) re-mints synchronously inside `reauth` and never raises StillStale — the gate cannot double-wait there by construction. (2) *single-flight-aware waiting (no SSM stampede)* — per poll tick at most ONE waiter (a non-blocking `_stale_leader_lock` holder) re-reads the broker, REUSING the existing `reauth` lock+generation single-flight verbatim (§11 COMMON); every other pool thread only polls the in-process generation (pinned: 8 real threads → EXACTLY 6 re-reads, 5 stale + 1 adopting). (3) *shared per-generation deadline (dead-broker bound)* — the deadline anchor is stamped at the FIRST stale observation per generation and SHARED across all waiters + ladder re-entries, so a never-minting broker costs ONE bounded pause then every re-entry fails FAST (pinned: total fake wall-clock == one bound; the ladder then feeds `on_timeout` 3× and records FAILED exactly as today, keeping the until-clean loop bounded and the DEC-VENDOR-DOWN-BREAKER-001 StillStale-streak escalation timely). (4) *observability + liveness* — ONE bounded-cadence `groww.token.stale_wait` structlog WARNING per pool (`GROWW_TOKEN_STALE_LOG_EVERY_S=30`, elapsed + deadline + method) and an `emit_progress_beat()` per tick (the DEC-PIPELINE-STALL-HEARTBEAT-001 seam) so the 600 s pull stall watchdog can never false-fire during the pause. (5) *rate-controller honesty* — during the pause ZERO vendor calls issue (the wait lives inside the already-admitted call; the controller is NOT redesigned) and the 429/timeout ladder is no longer fed by the outage (pinned: `on_timeout`/`on_rate_limit` receive ZERO calls in the outage replay). **CALIBRATION (Golden Rule #10):** 420 s default covers the measured 331 s worst case with margin, stays under the 600 s watchdog, and is env-tunable; `0` is the explicit revert lever (byte-identical pre-gate propagation, resolver-pinned); non-finite/negative/garbage env values fail SAFE to the default (an `inf` pause would re-introduce the unbounded hang the deadline forbids). **TESTS (fail-before = the operator-log forensics above; 1180. **DEC-CI-FORK-PR-HARDEN-001 — fork-PR attack surface CLOSED on the PUBLIC repo: (1) auto-merge trust no longer keys on the SPOOFABLE `claude/*` head-branch NAME — trust = the explicit author allowlist (SJParthi, dependabot[bot], renovate[bot]) OR a LIVE-API `author_association` ∈ {OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR}; (2) `pre-merge-gate.yml` no longer executes PR-controlled code — its checkout is PINNED to the base repo's `main` and the trusted copy of `scripts/ci/pre-merge-check.sh` runs with the PR number passed as DATA only; (3) `auto-merge.yml` gains the same base-pinned checkout for its rollup-gate script (also fixing a latent defect: the workflow had NO checkout at all, so the DEC-MERGE-LIVE-ROLLUP-001 rollup gate could only ever fail closed on a missing script file — auto-merge was inert since #944)** (2026-07-04; a prior security audit, each claim re-verified against the live files before editing. THE TWO HOLES: (a) `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` `trust-check` classified a PR trusted if `HEAD_REF == claude/*` — a branch NAME is attacker-chosen on a public repo, so a stranger's fork named `claude/anything` would have been auto-squash-merged to main once CI went green; the rule is REMOVED and the general rule is now `gh api repos/<repo>/pulls/<n> --jq .author_association` ∈ {OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR} — a fork PR from a random user reads FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR/CONTRIBUTOR/NONE → NOT trusted; the REAL automation (owner-authored `claude/*` PRs, author SJParthi = OWNER) is covered by BOTH the allowlist and the association, no regression; the trust decision is logged explicitly ("trust decision: TRUSTED/NOT TRUSTED — …"). Every other auto-merge gate (draft skip, CI-OK all-green, all-runs-complete, mergeability denylist, live rollup, merge-race handling) is byte-for-byte UNCHANGED. (b) `.github/workflows/pre-merge-gate.yml` — a `workflow_run` job holding `pull-requests: write` — checked out `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` and ran `scripts/ci/pre-merge-check.sh` FROM THE PR TREE, so a fork PR could rewrite that script and run arbitrary code with the job token; VERIFIED the script needs ONLY the PR number + `gh`/`python3` (it queries `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup`, never reads the working tree), so the checkout is pinned `ref: main` + `persist-credentials: false` and the posted-comment behaviour + permissions are unchanged. ANTI-PATTERN SWEEP: all 13 workflows scanned — pre-merge-gate.yml was the ONLY `workflow_run`/`pull_request_target` job checking out a PR-controlled ref; a directory-wide redteam pin (`test_no_workflow_run_job_checks_out_pr_head`) keeps it that way. TESTS: NEW `tests/redteam/test_redteam_fork_pr_harden.py` (10) — meta-pins (no branch-name trust condition, association-gated, base-pinned checkouts, directory sweep) + FUNCTIONAL classifier tests that EXECUTE the real `trust-check` script with a stubbed `gh`: a `claude/*`-named fork from a FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR/CONTRIBUTOR/NONE → `trusted=false`, SJParthi-allowlist + OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR associations → `trusted=true`, draft → `trusted=false`; full redteam suite 79 passed. GATES: actionlint v1.7.7 (the CI-pinned version, same `-shellcheck= -pyflakes=` flags) exit 0; yamllint (relaxed) warnings-only/exit 0 (not a repo gate); `validate_ledger_numbering.py` exit 0. HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10): these are WORKFLOW-side mitigations — the remaining structural defence is SERVER-SIDE and only the repo OWNER can flip it; **FOLLOW-UP (owner click-path, NOT done — a GitHub settings task, impossible from code): GitHub → SJParthi/bruteX → Settings → Branches → "Add branch ruleset" (or classic "Add branch protection rule") for `main`: enable "Require a pull request before merging", "Require status checks to pass" with the check `CI OK (aggregate gate)`, "Require branches to be up to date before merging", and restrict who can push/merge (bypass list = owner only); AND Settings → Actions → General → Fork pull request workflows: set "Require approval for all outside collaborators".** Also honest: `pre-merge-gate.yml` remains INFORMATIONAL (comment-only) per its own header; the auto-merge checkout fix makes the rollup gate functional again — before it, every auto-merge attempt since the rollup gate landed refused with `gated=false` (fail-closed, safe, but inert). CI-workflow + redteam-test + docs ONLY — ZERO `brutex/` code touched; ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change. **Files:** `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`, `.github/workflows/pre-merge-gate.yml`, `tests/redteam/test_redteam_fork_pr_harden.py` (new), `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (§1/§3 active branch). **Decision ID:** DEC-CI-FORK-PR-HARDEN-001. ClosedTrade materialisation) at 257× vs its own Python arm on a sparse 6k-bar fixture (density-dependent; the blueprint spike read ~40× at ~81 trades/mask) — pinned as a NEW ratio bench (`tests/bench/test_trade_sim_throughput.py::test_resident_trade_sim_wired_vs_fallback_speedup`, floor 15× — raised from the round-1 5× by review fold (g) below — wired arm ASSERTS `rust_active`). **MECHANISM:** (1) CONSTRUCTION — one `ResidentTradeSim(bars, bar_bits, tf_minutes)` per tuple, built inside `run_persisted_sweep` AFTER the kernel n_bars/fib_anchor guards and ONLY when survivors exist (`_build_trade_sim`; the per-tuple build makes the tf_minutes/fib_anchor/n_bars identity trivially consistent — the co-located-in-`ResidentKernelCache` option was REJECTED for its tf_minutes cache-key hazard AND because the golden/kernel=None arm would never exercise the Rust path); a ctor failure maps to the #904 tuple-skip contract — `SweepComboError` naming the tuple + "trade-sim construction" (grid: TUPLE_FAILED + non-zero verdict, NEVER a grid-wide abort), `MemoryError` re-raised BARE first (DEC-LAKE-WRITE-HALT-001 global stop). (2) CHUNKING — `_trade_sim_chunk_masks(n_bars) = max(1, min(256, (4·2²⁰)//n_bars))`: the 256-mask cap for small windows, a cells budget for production multi-year 1-minute windows (~500k bars → 8 masks/chunk) bounding peak `Vec<Vec<TradeRecord>>` marshal + ClosedTrade materialisation ≤ ~cells/2 trades per chunk (the review's deliberately-conservative memory bound); chunk size NEVER changes results — pinned by chunk-invariance tests ({1, 2, 3, 5(=len), 7(>len)} → byte-identical stores) + a per-mask alignment oracle test (crafted fixture with PAIRWISE-DISTINCT per-mask metrics, asserted as the fixture's teeth; every persisted row joined back via the u128 limbs and compared field-by-field to a direct `metrics_for_mask` call). (c) the per-call `rust_trade_sim.call_fallback` WARNING is memoised ONCE per (instance, reason) — the sweep chunks a tuple into up to thousands of `simulate_masks` calls, so a u128-era vocabulary would otherwise WARN per chunk (millions of lines on a production-scale sweep); the fallback itself stays per-call + bit-exact (log-once repeat + new-reason-rewarns tests). (d) the envelope guards check BOTH bounds (`not 0 <= x <= U64_MASK`) — a NEGATIVE mask/bar_bits (API misuse only; `build_bar_bits`/`iter_masks_k_of_bits` emit non-negative ints) now routes to the bit-exact oracle instead of a wheel-dependent PyO3 `OverflowError` asymmetry (construction + per-call tests, oracle parity). (e) PER-COLUMN MUTATION TEETH: the construction price-guard's 4-column scan is pinned at the guard-function seam one column at a time, both signs, plus the exact-ceiling in-envelope boundary (`TestEnvelopeGuardSeamPerColumn`) — needed because CandleBar's OHLC invariant (`low <= open, close <= high`) makes a bar corrupt in ONLY the open/close column unrepresentable through the public ctor (a huge open drags high with it), so a column-drop mutant survived any CandleBar-built fixture; the two REPRESENTABLE single-column cases (high=+big, low=−big) are ALSO pinned end-to-end through the real ctor. All 7 hand-run guard mutants (4 column drops, 2 negative-bound drops, ≤→< boundary) verified KILLED. (f) the u128 sweep-equality test is no longer vacuously satisfiable: `condition_bits=[0, 64, 65]` puts a genuinely FIRING mask in the guarded batch — the ranking gate drops the two zero-trade u128 masks and EXACTLY one real trade-bearing row persists (pinned `persisted == 1` on both arms + independent-oracle `total_trades > 0`), so the wired-vs-fallback byte-equality compares real rows, never two degenerate zero-trade stores. (g) the wired-speedup bench floor RAISED 5× → 15× (measured 265× sandbox / ~40× spike — the 5× floor would have passed an order-of-magnitude wiring regression) and the bench's fallback arm switched from poking `_rust` to a `_ForcedFallbackTradeSim` subclass (the unit/golden `_ForcedFallbackSim` pattern; clears the diff's sole new pyright reportPrivateUsage diagnostic). (h) `sweep_parallel.py` docstring's dangling `_worker_env` → `_worker_init`. 1181. **DEC-SWEEP-LOOKAHEAD-GUARD-001 — the brute-force SWEEP path gains its own no-look-ahead defence-in-depth: permanent suffix-independence property gates over the whole sweep spine + an OPT-IN runtime index barrier (`BRUTEX_SWEEP_LOOKAHEAD_GUARD=1`, default OFF, zero-cost OFF contract) reusing the COMMON `feed/lookahead.py` `LookAheadBarrier`** (2026-07-04; PR-3. HONEST FRAMING (Golden Rule #10): two audit agents verified the sweep spine is structurally CAUSAL today — `stage1a` updates prior-bar history only AFTER each bar's evaluation, `trade_sim` enters at the NEXT bar's open — so this is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH against FUTURE regressions, not a bug fix; both pre-existing runtime guards (`ReplayFeed.ensure_no_lookahead` + the runner/driver-wired `LookAheadBarrier` cursor invariant, DEC-LOOKAHEAD-BARRIER-001/DEC-LOOKAHEAD-HONESTY-001) protect only the library-strategy path, which `feed/lookahead.py` itself admitted. THREE deliverables. (1) **THE REAL TEETH — permanent suffix-independence property gates** (`tests/property/test_sweep_suffix_independence.py`, 7 tests, hypothesis-driven suffix mutation with extreme-weighted prices ₹1/₹1,000,000): Stage-1A `build_bar_bits` prefix-projection under an ABSENT suffix (`build_bar_bits(bars)[:k+1] == build_bar_bits(bars[:k+1])` — the streaming-state form) + the resident-kernel arm (`ResidentSweepKernel.bar_bits`) under extreme suffix MUTATION; the resample path into the engine on BOTH resamplers (the epoch-anchored `feed/resampler.resample_bars` and the canonical session-anchored `data/tf_resampler.resample_1m_to_tf` that materialises the derived-TF partitions the sweep reads): a mutated suffix DAY never changes an earlier derived bucket + every fully-CLOSED prefix bucket is unchanged when later bars arrive; the FULL-SPINE trade invariance extending the walker-local property cited at `trade_sim.py` §"No look-ahead" (bars → `build_bar_bits` → `mask_to_entry_signals` → `simulate_trades` end-to-end: a trade closed at bar K is bit-identical under ANY mutation of bars strictly after K — the mutation flows through the RECOMPUTED bar bits + entry signals, so the whole derived-state chain is covered, not just the walker); and engine STATELESSNESS (`metrics_for_mask` + a full `run_persisted_sweep` over a PREFIX window are bit-identical — store bytes + `store_content_hash` — before/after a full-series sweep in the same process: no global mutable state can smuggle future information into a prefix evaluation). These run in the normal CI property suite forever — a future look-ahead bug anywhere in the spine fails them. (2) **OPT-IN RUNTIME BARRIER** — NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_lookahead.py`: `sweep_lookahead_guard_enabled()` (truthy literals 1/true/yes/on; anything else fail-safe OFF) + `GuardedBarWindow` (an index-guarded read-only `Sequence` view REUSING the COMMON `LookAheadBarrier` at `record=False` O(1) memory — NO copy, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) + `maybe_guard_bars`, wired at ONE seam: `run_persisted_sweep` resolves the flag ONCE at setup (never inside any per-bar loop). ON: sequential iteration advances a forward-only CONSUMPTION FRONT; any indexed/sliced/reversed bar read AHEAD of the front raises `LookAheadError` (e.g. a future `bars[i+1]` peek fires the moment it executes on the FIRST sequential pass over the window - the Stage-1A build when kernel=None, the first trade-sim walk on the kernel path; after that pass every in-window index is consumed data, so a later-phase peek is inside the front and is the property gates' layer, not the barrier's); the ON-mode sweep output is pinned BIT-IDENTICAL to OFF (the barrier observes, never alters). HONEST ENVELOPE of what ON catches: the front is monotone across the WHOLE sweep run (phases legitimately re-walk the same window: Stage-1A first, then one trade-sim walk per surviving mask, then the finalist re-simulation), so the barrier is strongest during the FIRST sequential pass and does NOT re-arm per phase; it does NOT interpose on DERIVED per-bar state (`bar_bits`, walker-internal state, indicator streams) — a future-information flow through derived state is caught by the property gates of (1), not by the barrier; the two layers are complementary, mirroring the feed-path pairing. **ZERO-COST OFF (the hard constraint, MEASURED + STRUCTURAL):** OFF returns the caller's bars object ITSELF (`maybe_guard_bars(bars) is bars` — identity-pinned), so no wrapper and no per-bar flag check exist anywhere in the hot path; NEW bench gate `tests/bench/test_sweep_lookahead_off_cost.py` pins (a) the identity contract, (b) the OFF seam cost O(1)-in-bar-count (1k vs 100k bars, via the COMMON `ratio_ceiling` two-tier), (c) an A/B assert that the whole OFF seam costs LESS than one bare no-op walk over a 100k-bar window (a hidden per-bar cost cannot pass); the pre-existing sweep O(1) gates (`tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_run_o1.py`) stay green unmodified. (3) **DOCS** — `feed/lookahead.py`'s honesty docstring + CLAUDE.md §4's no-look-ahead bullet now state the sweep path's three layers (structural causality + permanent property gates + the opt-in barrier with this envelope). 1200. **DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-HONESTY-001 — honest LIVE pull progress (Session-A operator forensics 2026-07-04, all three items in ONE decision): (1) a linear ETA (`started_at` / `units_per_sec` / `eta_seconds`, the engine `sweep_progress` pattern ported with a PHASE-scoped rate baseline) on the pull snapshot + both frontends, with the MANDATORY refuter amendment that `eta_seconds` is `None` while the run is open-ended (a linear ETA over a growing denominator is an illusion); (2) a LIVE bars counter for the async F&O phase — `FetchPipeline` gains an `on_bars` fold-seam hook and `PullProgress` an O(1) `add_bars(delta)`, so the headline bars tally advances by exactly the background-folded deltas instead of freezing at the spot phase's count; (3) the grow-total percent-pin illusion is KILLED — the pipeline's F&O historical phase drops `pair_progress=True` and instead drives ABSOLUTE, market/interval-FILTERED ledger counts through the throttled COMMON `make_live_sync`, plus a STICKY `open_ended` snapshot flag rendered as "N units · total unknown"** (2026-07-04; number taken from the Session-A reserved block #1200–#1209, operator reservation 2026-07-04. THE THREE FORENSIC BUGS (verified on origin/main `23dbf08` — scratchpad SA-verify-PR1): (a) `ProgressSnapshot` had NO started_at/rate/eta anywhere, so the operator watched a multi-hour pull with no time-to-done signal; (b) in async mode every per-pair `IngestReport` is producer-resolved with `bars_appended == 0` (the REAL counts are folded by the background consumer via `FetchPipeline.fold_totals` under `_totals_lock`) so the headline bars counter FROZE for the whole F&O phase; (c) `advance(grow_total=True)` pins `total = completed` → `percent` reads a fabricated 100 while thousands of windows are still pending (`pull_progress.py:210-215` pre-change). THE FIX, per surface: `pull_progress.py` — snapshot gains `started_at`/`phase_started_at`/`phase_base_completed`/`open_ended` + derived `elapsed_seconds`/`units_per_sec`/`eta_seconds` (linear; `None` when idle/settled, when no rate is measured yet, when total is unknown, and ALWAYS when `open_ended`); the rate baseline is stamped by the FIRST counter mutation after `start()`/`set_phase()` so a ledger sync opening on cross-run absolute counts (thousands of previously settled windows) can never fabricate a burst rate; `advance(grow_total=True)` now marks `open_ended=True`; `set_phase(open_ended=True)` sets the STICKY marker — a later `set_phase("prebuild")`/`set_phase("movers")` does NOT clear it (regression-pinned), only `start()` does; NEW O(1) `add_bars(delta)` (running-only, non-negative, bars-not-units so the ETA baseline is untouched); `to_dict` adds ONLY additive keys (`started_at`/`units_per_sec`/`eta_seconds`/`open_ended` — the `_FLAT_KEYS` integration pin holds). `fetch_pipeline.py` — `FetchPipeline(on_bars=...)` invoked once per `fold_totals` with that window's `bars_appended` delta, under the totals lock, GUARDED (`fetch_pipeline.on_bars_error` structlog, never trips the pipeline); `fold_tail_transient` never fires it. `pull_pipeline.build_fetch_pipeline(on_bars=...)` threads it; the spot/CLI build sites pass nothing (spot path byte-unchanged). `historical_pull.py` — `pull_contract_candles(on_bars=, on_ledger_sync=)`: on_bars rides BOTH modes exactly-once (async: the pipeline fold carries the real delta while the per-pair report honestly adds 0; sync: the per-pair report carries the real bars and no fold exists — the no-double-count invariant, regression-pinned in both modes); on_ledger_sync is fed from the pull's OWN ledger via the COMMON `make_live_sync` (lazy import, the register_pull_meter precedent) FILTERED to `frozenset(by_market) × (interval,)` — the ledger is CROSS-RUN and CROSS-MARKET, so an unfiltered fold would pollute the F&O denominator with every spot window (fails-before-pinned) — plus ONE unthrottled final push post-drain (the spot spine's `pull_all_spot` parity). `window_ledger.progress_counts(markets=, intervals=)` — optional per-record membership filters, one bounded O(N) sweep, `None` defaults byte-identical; `pull_controller.make_live_sync(markets=, intervals=)` forwards them. `composite_pull.pull_historical_for_underlyings` threads both hooks verbatim. `app.py` `/pull-pipeline` `_run_historical` — `set_phase("historical", open_ended=True)` (pair_progress DROPPED at this site; the grow-total mechanism itself stays for consumers with genuinely no ledger), `on_bars=_pull_job.add_bars`, `on_ledger_sync` → `sync_from_ledger(bars=None)` (cross-run ledger bars must never clobber the live tally). `pull_jobs.py` — `set_phase(..., open_ended=)` passthrough + `add_bars(delta)` (progress + mark_dirty + watchdog beat — bars landing IS real progress, so a long single-pair stream never false-trips the stall detector). FRONTENDS (textContent-only, CodeQL XSS guard): `universe.html` shows `ETA ~Xh Ym` (hidden when null) on the running headline, and when `open_ended` renders "N units · total unknown" + counter "N / ?" + an honest '?' in the "of total" stat instead of a pinned 100%; `bx-rate-monitor.js` gains a hidden-by-default ETA pill row fed by a best-effort second poll of `/api/v1/universe/pull-progress` (null → hidden; the backend owns the open-ended verdict). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): the ETA is a LINEAR extrapolation of the CURRENT phase rate, not a guarantee; the F&O ledger denominator still GROWS mid-phase (per-market planning) and the filtered counts are CROSS-PULL for the same scope — hence `open_ended` stays TRUE for that phase and no ETA/percent is claimed over it; the live bars tally counts bars PROCESSED (the report `bars_appended` input-count semantics it replaces), not net-new lake rows (DEC-SINK-DEDUP-COUNT-001 #1031 keeps those separate); a sync-mode F&O pull ticks bars per PAIR (coarser than async's per window). Engine + vendor surfaces untouched: the Groww fetch spines' rate pacing (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6, DEC-GROWW-RATE-PERMIN-001) and the NSE/Groww pull scope are byte-unchanged — this is READ-side progress observability only; ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). Fails-before regressions: percent-pinned-at-100-while-pending → honest filtered counts + open_ended; frozen-bars → advances by exactly the folded deltas (async) / per-pair bars (sync), never double; ETA absent under grow_total; open_ended persists across `set_phase("prebuild")`/`set_phase("movers")`. Decision ID: DEC-PULL-PROGRESS-HONESTY-001.)
1222. **DEC-PREBUILD-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 — a corrupt/truncated Parquet month file now QUARANTINES that ONE symbol in the pipeline timeframe prebuild instead of aborting the ENTIRE prebuild on EVERY run: `gated_prebuild`'s per-symbol data-error set gains polars' `PolarsError` via a lazy, wheel-free `_per_symbol_data_errors()` resolver** (2026-07-04; C2 of the Session-C resilience pack (PR-2, sibling of DEC-VOLUME-KEEPALIVE-001 #1223). CONFIRMED MECHANISM on main: the prebuild's 1-minute base read (`timeframe_materialize.make_lake_read_1m` → `pl.scan_parquet(...).collect()`) raises `polars.exceptions.ComputeError` (a `PolarsError`) on a corrupt month file — matched by NONE of the prior `_PER_SYMBOL_DATA_ERRORS = (ValueError, OSError, ResampleInputError)`, so the exception unwound `run_gated_prebuild` entirely, `run_pipeline_prebuild_guarded` collapsed the run to `PrebuildOutcome(symbols_built=0, ok=False, crashed="ComputeError")`, the movers warm stayed gated (#1145), and — the corrupt file persisting on disk — EVERY subsequent pipeline run aborted identically until manual cleanup. FIX (ONE source file, `brutex/dashboard/gated_prebuild.py`): the module constant is REPLACED by module-private `def _per_symbol_data_errors() -> tuple[type[BaseException], ...]` returning `(ValueError, ResampleInputError, *parquet_read_skip_errors())` — the prior set PLUS `PolarsError`, reusing the ONE data-layer skip-set source of truth (`data/errors.py:parquet_read_skip_errors`, the #886/#1038 discipline — the prebuild was the last unguarded consumer); the three except sites (spot materialise / contract discovery / contract materialise) evaluate the tuple at EXCEPTION time (zero hot-path cost, O(1) after first import). 1223. **DEC-VOLUME-KEEPALIVE-001 — SSD-spindown / wedged-lake-volume protection in THREE layers: (1) a best-effort volume-keepalive write-probe daemon (NEW `brutex/data/volume_keepalive.py`), (2) a wedged-pause gate at the TOP of `FetchPipeline.submit` so the producer never enters the unbounded spill fsync while the volume is wedged, (3) a `> 900 s` wedge raising `LakeWriteHalt('volume_wedged')` FROM THE PRODUCER THREAD — wired at the ONE COMMON build site `build_fetch_pipeline` (CLI + dashboard both route through it)** (2026-07-04; C3 of the Session-C resilience pack (PR-2, sibling of DEC-PREBUILD-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 #1222). CONFIRMED GAP on main: the CONSUMER-side durable write was already 90 s-bounded (`append_with_deadline`, DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 #999 — each wedged append defers its window, a throughput collapse but NOT a permanent hang), while the PRODUCER-side spill (`FetchSpillArea.try_spill` → `atomic_write_via` mkstemp/write/fsync/replace on the SAME lake volume, fetch_spill.py) ran on the FETCH thread with NO deadline — a spun-down/wedged external SSD hung the fetch lane UNBOUNDEDLY at the first full-queue spill. THIS closes that producer hang + adds the wedge gate; the 90 s consumer bound is PRE-EXISTING, not claimed here. MECHANISM: `VolumeKeepalive(probe_path, *, interval_s, probe_deadline_s, halt_after_s, monotonic, probe)` — ONE daemon thread probes every `interval_s` (default 30 s, `BRUTEX_VOLUME_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_S`) with a 1-byte write+fsync to `<lake_root>/.volume-keepalive` (a sidecar, never `*.parquet`, mirrors `.locks`) under the COMMON `run_with_deadline` freeze guard (default 15 s, `BRUTEX_VOLUME_KEEPALIVE_PROBE_DEADLINE_S`); a `DeadlineExceeded`/`OSError` sets the `wedged` Event + edge-logs `volume_keepalive.wedged`, a success clears it + edge-logs `volume_keepalive.recovered`; the daemon ONLY observes — it never raises into the pull. `FetchPipeline.submit` gains `_pause_if_wedged()` AFTER `_raise_if_stopped()` and BEFORE the in-flight accounting/spill: while wedged it polls `_stopped.wait(0.5)` re-checking stop (a peer trip re-raises) and `_draining` (drain NEVER deadlocks behind the pause), edge-logs `fetch_pipeline.paused_wedged` once per episode, and once `wedged_seconds() >= halt_after_s` (default 900 s, `BRUTEX_VOLUME_WEDGE_HALT_S`) `_trip()`s the pool + raises `LakeWriteHalt('volume_wedged')` ON THE PRODUCER — propagating through BOTH spines' `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` to the CLI halt handler / `pull_jobs.is_pull_halt` → `emit_pull_halt_alert` → the CRITICAL Telegram alert with ZERO new alert plumbing (test-pinned end-to-end). `build_fetch_pipeline` builds+starts it via `_build_volume_keepalive(lake_root)` (own guard → `pull.volume_keepalive.build_failed` → `None`, the pipeline still builds; `lake_root=None` / dry-run / `BRUTEX_GROWW_FETCH_PIPELINE=off` / the `BRUTEX_VOLUME_KEEPALIVE=off` kill-switch → no daemon; a pipeline build failure stops an already-started keepalive — no leak); `drain()` stops it on ALL exit paths (early idle return, normal join, captured-halt re-raise). HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10): layer 1's keepalive-PREVENTS-spindown is HOST-DEPENDENT (drive firmware / OS power policy may ignore periodic 1-byte fsyncs) — layers 2 (pause) + 3 (halt + CRITICAL alert) are the actual guarantee; each expired probe abandons one unkillable daemon thread (bounded ≈ wedge_duration/interval); a paused producer is a deliberate throughput sacrifice and windows already in flight at wedge onset still burn one 90 s consumer deferral each (the pause BOUNDS the waste, it does not eliminate it — no data lost: idempotent keep-first sink + durable ledger re-pull); the sync kill-switch path has NO spill and its inline tail is already 90 s-bounded, so no unbounded hang exists there (not claimed covered); the gate is PROCESS-LOCAL; POSIX envelope, same as the existing locks; the pause only DELAYS issue — no rate ceiling is raised (Golden Rule #6 untouched). NEW tests (88): `test_volume_keepalive.py` (63 — resolvers/lifecycle/hanging-probe/OSError/recovery-edge/fake-monotonic/stop-unlink), `test_fetch_pipeline_wedge_gate.py` (14 — pause/recover on the producer thread, one edge log across two paused producers, 900 s → `LakeWriteHalt('volume_wedged')` + pool tripped + drain re-raise, peer-trip release, drain-releases-pause, THE VERIFIED-GAP REGRESSION: a wedged spillable submit makes ZERO `try_spill` calls while paused and spills exactly once after recovery, alert-chain pins against BOTH spines' `_GLOBAL_STOP_ERRORS` + `is_pull_halt` + a `SweepAlerter.pull_halted` spy), `test_pull_pipeline_keepalive.py` (11 — wiring/kill-switch/dry-run/build-failure/thread-leak oracle). Gates: `volume_keepalive.py` 100.00% (124/22), `fetch_pipeline.py` 100.00% (324/90), `pull_pipeline.py` 100.00% (90/26) line+branch; `data/errors.py` change docstring-only (the `LakeWriteHalt` reason-token list gains `volume_wedged`), 100.00% on its suites; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` (whole package, 328 files) + `pyright` 0 errors on every touched file. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change. **Files:** `brutex/data/volume_keepalive.py` (NEW), `brutex/adapters/groww/fetch_pipeline.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/pull_pipeline.py`, `brutex/data/errors.py` (docstring), `tests/unit/test_volume_keepalive.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_fetch_pipeline_wedge_gate.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_pull_pipeline_keepalive.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-VOLUME-KEEPALIVE-001. 1186. **DEC-SWEEP-RUST-METRICS-001 — Phase B of the Rust-migration blueprint: the measured-hot part of the sweep's per-mask trades→metrics TAIL (the `build_equity_curve` running-sum equity fold + `_drawdown_stats`' O(N_bars) drawdown scan) is ported into the SAME fno-math kernel as one fused function (`fno_math.sweep_drawdown_stats(n_bars, start_equity_paisa, [(exit_idx, pnl)]) → (max_dd_paisa, max_dd_pct, max_dd_duration_bars, ulcer_index)`), FLAG-GATED default OFF (`BRUTEX_SWEEP_RUST_METRICS`; the flip to ON-by-default is a SEPARATE later ADR, explicitly NOT here), bit-identical to the Python oracle inside a PROVEN f64-exactness envelope — the frozen `_GOLDEN_CONTENT_HASH`/`_GOLDEN_RUN_ID` literals are UNCHANGED and the ON arm REPRODUCES them byte-for-byte** (2026-07-04, branch `claude/sweep-rust-metrics-9y1hni`; ENGINE SCOPE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/audit-schema change). **THE EXACTNESS PROOF (Golden Rule #4 — the load-bearing design):** the Python oracle folds equity in ARBITRARY-PRECISION ints and computes `dd_pct = drop / peak` via CPython's `long_true_divide` (correctly rounded on the exact rational); a naive `(drop as f64)/(peak as f64)` double-rounds whenever either operand exceeds 2⁵³ — and the Phase-A price envelope (`MAX_PRICE_PAISA = i64::MAX/8 ≈ 1.15e18`) is ~128× LARGER than 2⁵³, so "inputs already validated" does NOT imply exactness (hostile-review MAJOR, folded). The kernel therefore only ever receives inputs inside `MAX_EXACT_EQUITY_PAISA = 2⁵²`: the Python wrapper PRE-GUARDS `start_equity_paisa + Σ|pnl| ≤ 2⁵²` in EXACT int arithmetic (O(trades)/mask), under which every equity value `|e| ≤ 2⁵²`, `peak ≤ 2⁵²`, `drop = peak − e ≤ 2⁵³` — BOTH convert to f64 EXACTLY, so the IEEE division of exact operands IS the correctly rounded quotient = CPython's result bit-for-bit; the same bound makes every kernel i64 add provably overflow-free (2⁵³ ≪ i64::MAX), so an out-of-envelope mask NEVER reaches the kernel — it routes to the Python oracle with ONE warn-once WARNING, never a raise the pure-Python arm would not have produced (the Phase-A fallback law; an i64-overflow-adjacent input is an ENVELOPE EXIT, not an error — folded MAJOR). Float discipline pinned: `sum_sq_pct` is a strictly SEQUENTIAL left-to-right f64 fold (NO Kahan, NO rayon, NO `mul_add` — source-level pins `use rayon`/`rayon::`/`.mul_add(` absent), running max via `>` (matches Python `max()` on the +0.0-only domain), `sqrt` IEEE-correctly-rounded both sides, `× 100.0` single-rounding both sides. **MUST-STAY-PYTHON classification (recorded per review):** skewness's `math.pow(m2_n, 1.5)` and CAGR's `growth ** (1.0/span)` (+ its OverflowError→inf clamp) are libm `pow` — NO correct-rounding guarantee → NOT PORTED; the Welford/Pébay moments, percentiles/tail-ratio, sortino and every O(trades) aggregate stay Python (not the measured bottleneck); `math.fsum` is ABSENT from this entire path (verified — only trial_stats/cascade_wire use it, out of scope). **ZERO-TRADE SHORTCUT (66%-of-fixture finding, folded MAJOR):** a zero-trade mask's curve is CONSTANT = start > 0, so `_drawdown_stats` is analytically exactly `(0, +0.0, 0, +0.0)` including the SIGN of zero (proof on the constant + a bit-level pin vs the real scan); the ON arm serves it as a pure-Python O(1) shortcut with ZERO FFI — no speculative Rust. **MECHANISM:** (1) `rust/fno-math/src/metrics.rs` — pure `drawdown_stats_checked` (`Result<_,String>`, checked_* boundary validation: n_bars ≥ 1, start ∈ (0, 2⁵²], idx < n_bars, `checked_abs`/`checked_add` envelope sum — i64::MIN pnl and Σ-overflow are clean Errs, NEVER a panic under the preserved `panic=abort`+`overflow-checks` profile) + the `#[pyfunction]` wrapper mapping to `ValueError`; stateless per-call `vec![0i64; n_bars]` scatter (a resident per-tuple buffer is impossible at this seam — the fenced `sweep_run` hands bars+trades per mask; the alloc is ~8 B/bar and an alloc failure aborts, the SAME envelope as Phase-A construction, stated not solved). (2) `brutex/engine/rust_metrics.py` — the seam module: per-call env read (`_TRUTHY` IMPORTED from `sweep_lookahead`, §11 COMMON; per-call chosen over a process memo so `sweep_parallel` workers read their OWN inherited env and no global FLAG state exists — the ~0.1 µs probe vs a multi-ms tail is bench-pinned), `exceeds_exact_equity_envelope` (exact ints), `drawdown_stats_via_kernel` (lazy import; `wheel_missing`/`wheel_stale`/`kernel_error` warn-once fallbacks; `MemoryError` re-raised BARE — OOM stays a GLOBAL stop; domain validation `_valid_drawdown` REFUSES a poisoned kernel result LOUDLY — ERROR `sweep_rust_metrics.kernel_result_refused`, never silently adopted, the mask served by Python — while an in-domain wrong answer is honestly the golden/property layer's to catch), the engaged-once INFO `sweep_rust_metrics.engaged` (the anti-vacuous-gate signal), and `reset_observability_memo_for_tests` (the memos are LOG-VOLUME-only state, results never depend on them). (3) `brutex/engine/sweep_driver.py` — `metrics_from_trades` gains the ON arm `_metrics_from_trades_via_kernel`: mirrors `build_equity_curve`'s last-wins `ts_to_index` + span expression IN THE SAME FILE, maps exit_ts→idx, zero-trade shortcut, kernel call, then the NEW curve-less `compute_metrics_from_scalars`; EVERY contract input (empty bars, start ≤ 0, tf ≤ 0 span, non-bar exit_ts) FALLS THROUGH to the verbatim Python tail so the exact error messages/types (the `_combo_error` fingerprint feed) fire from ONE source on BOTH arms — never duplicated. (4) `brutex/metrics/compute.py` (read-only oracle — behaviour-preserving seam ONLY, justified in-docstring): `compute_metrics` gains keyword-only `drawdown: tuple | None = None` (None ⇒ `_drawdown_stats(equity)` exactly as before — the default path is byte-identical, golden-pinned) delegating to the extracted `_compute_metrics_impl` (the verbatim body with `equity.start_equity_paisa`/`equity.span_years` parameterised — compute_metrics reads NOTHING else from the curve); NEW public `compute_metrics_from_scalars(trades, total_bars, benchmark, *, start_equity_paisa, span_years, drawdown)` RE-ASSERTS the bypassed EquityCurve invariants (start > 0, span finite > 0) as belts; `_empty_metrics` now takes the drawdown 4-tuple (the zero-trade branch rides the same seam). **SEAM PLACEMENT (deviation from one reviewer, majority + fence ruling):** the conflict fence forbids `sweep_run.py`/`ranking`/`cli`/`trade_sim`, so the "sweep_run-local tail + once-per-run flag resolution" shape is UNIMPLEMENTABLE; the seam lives in the COMMON `metrics_from_trades` — the flag arms EVERY consumer together (sweep, walk-forward `_score_fold`, validation, Stage-3, and `metrics_for_mask` the re-attribution oracle) — SAFE precisely because the arms are bit-identical, pinned by a walk-forward dual-arm test (equal run_hash + every per-fold metric, raw `==` floats) and the sweep golden; a per-CHUNK batched metrics call (and therefore a metrics chunk-invariance test) is N/A at this per-mask seam. **MEASURED (sandbox RATIOS ONLY — NOT the §8 M4 Pro; live Groww unreachable, no vendor claims):** per-mask tail on a 20k-bar window: zero-trade 14.10 ms → 0.01 ms (~1683×, the O(1) shortcut), traded-200 14.27 ms → 1.96 ms (~7.3×, the fused kernel + curve-less metrics); the ON arm RETAINS a per-mask O(N_bars) Python `ts_to_index` dict build (ClosedTrade carries timestamps, not indices — the kernel-side idx fast path needs the fenced `sweep_run` chunk loop and Phase-A record indices, an explicit FUTURE follow-up);
