1260. **DEC-SUPERVISOR-CRASHLOOP-ALERT-001 — the sweep supervisor's abnormal-exit relaunch now fires a best-effort, DEDUPED operator alert with rolling-window crash-loop escalation, closing the "a child can OOM-SIGKILL-loop all night with ZERO operator signal" gap** (2026-07-04 on `claude/trusting-newton-krdxvc`, PR-C of the engine-scale pack part (a); orchestrator + notifications + CLI-wiring ONLY — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3 + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake change; the relaunch behaviour and every exit state are byte-unchanged when no alerter is wired — the default). THE GAP: `ProcessSupervisor.run`'s relaunch branch (DEC-SUPERVISOR-AUTORESTART-001 #1052) audit-stamped + structlog'd each relaunch but pushed NOTHING to the operator, so a crash-looping child (e.g. an OOM SIGKILL every few minutes, backoff-paced, streak reset by a >60 s uptime) could relaunch indefinitely in silence. FIX (mirrors the pull_halted/rate_breach alert pattern): (1) NEW `SweepAlerter.child_relaunched(*, child, exit_code, signal, relaunch_count, detail)` in `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py` — WARN for an isolated relaunch, ESCALATES to CRITICAL at `CRASH_LOOP_RELAUNCH_THRESHOLD = 3` in-window relaunches (the ONE source of truth for the bar); the two tiers carry DISTINCT dedupe keys (`child-relaunch:<child>` / `child-crash-loop:<child>`) so the WARN-tier coalescing can never swallow the CRITICAL escalation; a POSIX signal death (negative returncode) is surfaced as "signal N". (2) NEW `TelegramEventKind.CHILD_RELAUNCHED` (`"child.relaunched"`) with a REAL 300 s dedupe window in `telegram.py`, so an all-night loop coalesces to one push per 5 min per key. (3) `ProcessSupervisor` gains an injectable structural `RelaunchAlerter` Protocol seam (`alerter=None` default — the supervisor never imports notifications) + `alert_window_seconds` (default `DEFAULT_ALERT_WINDOW_SECONDS = 600.0`, validated > 0) + a relaunch-timestamp list PRUNED to the rolling window on every relaunch, stamped on the EXISTING injectable `clock` (default `time.monotonic`) so escalation tests are fully deterministic; the supervisor passes the in-window COUNT — the severity decision lives in the alerter. BEST-EFFORT by construction: `_alert_relaunch` wraps the sink call in a swallow-and-log `except Exception` (a raising alerter never crashes/blocks/slows the loop — regression-pinned), fires AFTER the audit stamp + BEFORE the backoff sleep, in the relaunch branch AND — hostile-review MINOR-3 fold — at the terminal GIVE-UP verdict: NEW `SweepAlerter.supervisor_gave_up(*, child, exit_code, signal, restarts, max_restarts)` (ALWAYS CRITICAL — the sweep is DOWN and nothing relaunches it — on NEW `TelegramEventKind.SUPERVISOR_GAVE_UP` `"supervisor.gave_up"` with a ZERO dedupe window [terminal, fires once per run] + dedupe key `supervisor-gave-up:<child>`), fired best-effort by `ProcessSupervisor._alert_gave_up` right after the give-up audit stamp, so the give-up reaches the operator even when `max_restarts` is BELOW the crash-loop bar or crashes are spaced wider than the rolling window (the two silent-give-up shapes the review named); the relaunch body's "keeps relaunching until the max-restart cap" clause now names the terminal CRITICAL so it can no longer go stale at exactly that moment; clean exit / operator stop still never alert. PRODUCTION BINDING: `cli.cmd_supervisor` wires `alerter=SweepAlerter()` (silent no-op when Telegram is disabled — the default) — PINNED by a dedicated wiring test (`test_cli_supervisor.py::test_cmd_supervisor_binds_sweep_alerter`, hostile-review MAJOR-2: `cmd_supervisor` is pragma-no-cover, so without this pin deleting the `alerter=` argument would silently revert the feature to dormant — the exact ledger-documented failure mode of #935/#1014). HONEST envelope: state stays O(1) in run length (the window list is bounded by the backoff-paced relaunch rate within ONE window, never total restarts); the alert is an OBSERVATION, not auto-remediation — the max-restart give-up law is untouched. **Files:** `brutex/orchestrator/supervisor.py`, `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py`, `brutex/notifications/telegram.py`, `brutex/cli.py` (cmd_supervisor binding), `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_supervisor.py` (NEW `TestRelaunchAlert`, 12 tests incl. window-prune + raising-alerter + signal-mapping + the give-up terminal alert / raising-give-up-alerter / no-alerter-noop trio), `tests/unit/test_notifications_sweep_alerts.py` (NEW `TestChildRelaunched`, 9 tests + `TestSupervisorGaveUp`, 5 tests), `tests/unit/test_cli_supervisor.py` (the MAJOR-2 binding pin + a GAVE_UP-exits-nonzero pin). Gates: `supervisor.py` 100.00% line+branch (197/48), `sweep_alerts.py` 100.00% (177/16), `telegram.py` 100.00% (236/46); ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` carries ONLY the pre-existing sandbox `cma`-extra import gap (byte-identical on the pristine tree); `pyright` 0 errors on every touched file. **Decision ID:** DEC-SUPERVISOR-CRASHLOOP-ALERT-001.
1261. **DEC-AUDIT-VERIFY-STREAM-001 — the orchestrator audit chain's `verify_chain` now STREAMS (flat O(1) RAM) instead of materialising the FULL entry list, porting the proven `engine/sweep_audit` generator pattern; corruption discrimination byte-identical** (2026-07-04 on `claude/trusting-newton-krdxvc`, PR-C part (b); `brutex/orchestrator/audit.py` READ-side ONLY — the writer/append path + every hash byte UNCHANGED; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). THE GAP: `verify_chain` opened with `entries = _read_entries(path)` — the whole log as a Python list — so verifying a multi-GB long-run audit chain cost O(N) resident entries (the SHA-256 twin of the BLAKE3 gap DEC-SWEEP-SCALE-OPERABILITY-001 already closed in `engine/sweep_audit.py`). FIX (the direct port of that decision's pattern — deliberately a STANDALONE twin, the two chains do not import one another): NEW public `iter_entries(path)` streaming primitive (`_iter_committed_entries` generator: one raw line + one parsed entry at a time; missing file raises AT CALL time; the DEC-AUDIT-TORN-TAIL-001 discriminator applied line-by-line — unterminated final line skipped, blank committed filler skipped, a malformed COMMITTED line still raises `AuditError` naming `path:line_no`) + NEW O(1) `_has_torn_tail` predicate (one seek + one byte; empty file never torn); `_read_entries_with_torn_tail` is RE-EXPRESSED as `list(iter_entries(path)) + _has_torn_tail(path)` so the discriminator lives in ONE place (§11 COMMON — its list contract + return values byte-preserved for the resume/read callers); `verify_chain` now enumerates `iter_entries` carrying ONLY `prev_hash` + a running count, with the three per-entry checks UNCHANGED in content AND order (seq ordering → prev_hash linkage → recomputed entry_hash, including the tampered-non-finite-payload `AuditPayloadError` → `AuditChainCorruption` mapping). CORRUPTION DISCRIMINATION IDENTICAL: every pre-existing byte-exact pin (`TestVerifyChainTamper` + `TestAuditChainCorruptionPins` + the torn-tail/kill-recovery + NaN-tamper suites) passes UNMODIFIED against the streamed implementation, plus NEW deep-mid-file re-confirmations (payload tamper at seq 40 / prev_hash break / seq gap / NaN tamper — same type + seq + reason). FLAT RAM PROVEN: a tracemalloc comparative oracle pins 100k-entry peak ≤ 1.5× the 10k-entry peak + 64 KiB slack (10× the entries, ~flat peak — an O(N) list would read ~10×), a stream-vs-list oracle pins `verify_chain` peak < `read_entries` peak / 5, and a monkeypatch-poison test proves the list readers are never routed through. HONEST envelope: `read_entries` deliberately KEEPS its O(N) list contract (dashboard/replay callers); on a file carrying BOTH an early chain break AND a later malformed line the streamed walk now surfaces the EARLIER (chain) verdict first — for any single corruption the verdict is identical, and no repo caller/test depended on the old whole-file-read-first ordering. 1262. **DEC-SLA-LAUNCH-GUARD-001 — `brutex sweep-all` gains an SLA-HONESTY launch guard: the projected wall-clock (tuple_count × an openly-UNBENCHMARKED per-tuple estimate) is checked against the CLAUDE.md §8 2-4-day envelope BEFORE launch — over-envelope grids are REFUSED unless `--acknowledge-sla-overrun` is passed (then a LOUD warning proceeds)** (2026-07-04 on `claude/trusting-newton-krdxvc`, PR-C part (c); NEW pure engine module + CLI wiring ONLY — the sweep hot path is untouched, the guard is one multiply + one compare; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). THE GAP: nothing stopped an operator from launching a grid whose honest projection was weeks — the §8 "2-4 days" envelope existed only as prose. FIX: NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_sla_guard.py` — `SLA_ENVELOPE_DAYS = 4.0` (the §8 ceiling; the boundary is INCLUSIVE), `check_sweep_sla(tuple_count, *, acknowledge, ...)` → frozen `SlaProjection` with `SlaDecision` ∈ {allowed, refused, acknowledged}, honest `refusal_message()` / `acknowledged_warning()` operator texts, and ONE loud `sweep.sla_projection` structlog event per launch (INFO allowed / WARNING otherwise) carrying `tuple_count` + `per_tuple_seconds` + `projected_wall_clock_seconds` + `envelope_seconds` + `decision` + the explicit honesty flags `per_tuple_estimate_benchmarked=False` and `projection_model="serial"`. THE HONEST-ESTIMATE CAVEAT (Golden Rule #10, the load-bearing clause): `SWEEP_PER_TUPLE_SECONDS = 30.0` is an **UNBENCHMARKED, conservative PLACEHOLDER** — no end-to-end per-tuple measurement on the §8 reference envelope (Apple M4 Pro) was possible in this environment, and a toy-fixture micro-measurement on foreign sandbox hardware would have been a MISLEADING number, so the constant is openly labelled an estimate that MUST be re-measured on the real envelope, and is operator-overridable via `BRUTEX_SWEEP_PER_TUPLE_SECONDS` (`resolve_per_tuple_seconds`, injectable env mapping; a malformed / non-positive / non-FINITE override is a clean user-config error — hostile-review MINOR-1 fold: `nan` bypassed the original bare `> 0` check and would have projected "≈ nan days", so validation is now the ONE `math.isfinite`-checked helper `_require_positive_finite`, shared by the env resolver, the explicit `per_tuple_seconds` param, and `envelope_seconds`). The guard's messages state verbatim that it "projects from an estimate; it does NOT certify the §8 SLA either way" — the §8 "~33B trials in 2-4 days" claim itself stays UNMEASURED and is NEVER claimed met. WIRING: `cmd_sweep_all` runs the guard right after `SweepGridConfig` construction + the stage-3 fail-fast (projection input = `count_sweep_tuples(grid)`), refusal → `EXIT_USER_ERROR` with the honest message, acknowledgement → the loud WARNING then proceed; NEW `--acknowledge-sla-overrun` flag on the `sweep-all` parser ONLY — the unattended `sweep-daemon` deliberately has NO acknowledge flag (mirrors the `--allow-out-of-scope` daemon-refusal precedent: an unattended run never overrides the guard; the env-var estimate calibration remains its honest knob), pinned by a parser test. PROJECTION-GRAIN honesty: the unit is one grid TUPLE (a tuple's true cost varies with bar count + mask population — linear-in-tuples is the first-order model, not an oracle), stated in the module docstring, and the public knob names SAY "TUPLE" (`SWEEP_PER_TUPLE_SECONDS` / `BRUTEX_SWEEP_PER_TUPLE_SECONDS` / `SlaProjection.per_tuple_seconds` — hostile-review MINOR-5 fold: the original `..._PER_TRIAL_...` names conflated a grid tuple with a §8 "trial" [one mask evaluation, ~6 orders finer], renamed BEFORE the contract shipped). PROJECTION-MODEL honesty (hostile-review MINOR-4 fold): the projection is SERIAL — it does not model the parallel driver's multi-worker speedup, so it can over-refuse a parallel launch (fails in the SAFE direction); the refusal message states this verbatim and names `BRUTEX_SWEEP_WORKERS` as a lever alongside `--max-tuples`. 1288. **DEC-ENGINE-MISC-PACK-001 — engine/misc polish pack, part 1 of 2: (a) a CROSS-PROCESS derive-phase flock at the FIXED sidecar `<lake_root>/.locks/derive.lock` (NEW `brutex/data/derive_lock.py`, the #887 partition-lock pattern + the pull_singleflight fixed-path precedent) — writer = `materialize_lake_timeframes` holds a BOUNDED exclusive flock per symbol; reader = the `/movers` spot stored-first branch takes a NON-BLOCKING shared probe (`derive_in_progress`) and, while a separate-process derive is mid-rewrite, honestly falls back to the on-the-fly 1-minute resample; (b) SweepCache Bloom auto-grow STEP 1 — a resume whose persisted L2 exact-store exceeds the configured `bloom_capacity` now REBUILDS at `max(persisted, ceil(capacity × 1.25))` IFF the grown bit array fits the 16 GiB `MAX_BLOOM_BYTES` wall; above the wall the FAIL_CLOSED refusal STAYS, naming the sharded / mmap'd Bloom follow-up** (2026-07-04; PR-4 of the P2 polish train). **(a) DERIVE FLOCK:** confirmed gap — every individual month-file write is atomic + per-partition-flocked (#887), but NOTHING signalled across processes that a whole-TF-SET rewrite was in flight: the in-process `PrebuildGate` is explicitly PROCESS-LOCAL, so a dashboard `/movers` stored-first read (`movers_stored_read.read_stored_day_frame`) concurrent with a CLI-process pipeline prebuild could observe a HALF-REFRESHED TF set (some timeframes rewritten, some stale). The reader probe is O(1), never blocks, and NEVER writes (an absent lock file reads `False` without being created — a read-only lake stays read-only); `movers_snapshot._read_intraday_bars` probes it BEFORE the stored read and the fallback rides the PINNED byte-equality reference path (the 1-minute resample), counted under the existing honest `resampled_reads` provenance — no new payload field. POSIX (Linux + macOS), Windows out of scope, kernel-released on process death (no stale-lock recovery) — all exactly the #887 envelope. NAMED FOLLOW-UPS (scoped OUT, honestly): probing in the other stored-TF readers (the `/db` viewer, the doctor freshness compare); teaching the process-local `PrebuildGate` to honor the cross-process lock (a `gated:true` payload for a CLI-process pipeline); the FUTURES/OPTIONS movers session readers need nothing (locked 1-minute-native, DEC-FNO-TF-DERIVE-OI-001). **(b) BLOOM AUTO-GROW STEP 1:** confirmed anchor — the resume refusal lives in `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py` (`_rebuild_bloom_from_exact`, NOT `orchestrator/bloom.py`, whose 16 GiB `MAX_BLOOM_BYTES` wall + `BloomTooLargeError` are UNTOUCHED and stay the hard invariant) and was UNCONDITIONAL: `persisted > bloom_capacity` refused every organic overflow, forcing a manual knob turn. FIX (all in `sweep_cache.py`): NEW pure `_auto_grow_capacity(configured, persisted, fpr)` — identity when `persisted <= configured` (byte-identical, no log); else `grown = max(persisted, ceil(configured × 1.25))` (the `max` is the correctness clamp — a bare ratio can still under-size and overflow the FAIL_CLOSED Bloom gate mid-rebuild) IFF `_compute_m_bytes(grown, fpr) <= MAX_BLOOM_BYTES` (the pure sizing helper bloom.py exposes for exactly this audit), with ONE loud `sweep_cache.bloom_auto_grow` structlog event (persisted / configured_capacity / grown_capacity / m_bytes — Golden Rules #1/#8: the operator knob was exceeded, say so); above the wall the refusal STAYS FAIL_CLOSED with an HONEST message — a `--sweep-cache-bloom-capacity` / `BRUTEX_SWEEP_CACHE_BLOOM_CAPACITY` raise CANNOT help above the wall; the remedies are a looser `bloom_fpr` or the sharded / mmap'd Bloom follow-up (NAMED, not shipped — STEP 1 stops at the bounded grow). `SweepCache.open` restructured to open the LMDB exact store FIRST and pre-size the Bloom from `len(exact)`; ANY construction/rebuild fault (wall refusal, a `BloomConfigError`) closes the just-opened env before re-raising (no leak — regression-pinned by an immediate re-open); the `_rebuild_bloom_from_exact` >capacity guard is KEPT as defence-in-depth (now unreachable from `open`, directly unit-tested). entries sorted ascending by the UTF-8 BYTES of the `/`-separated relative path (UTF-8 byte order == code-point order, so Rust's byte sort == Python's `encode("utf-8")` key sort); per-file frame = `path-bytes ‖ 0x00 ‖ u64-le(len) ‖ raw bytes` (unambiguous — no cross-file boundary shift can collide, test-pinned); PLUS a Rust self-consistency test per crate (`SOURCE_DIGEST` == fresh recompute over the real checkout) and a Python independent hand-rolled framing oracle + bounded hypothesis property (twin == manual-frame blake3 for arbitrary small trees). **DOCTOR SEMANTICS (mirrors wheel_freshness — WARN, non-fatal, `BRUTEX_SKIP_WHEEL_FRESHNESS=1` stays the ONE escape hatch for all four wheel stages):** skip-env → SKIP; wheel not importable → WARN + rebuild hint (same programmatic-only reachability envelope as freshness); installed module lacking a usable `__source_digest__` (a wheel predating this handshake) → WARN "rebuild", never a crash; no `rust/<crate>` tree next to the installed `brutex` package (wheel-only install) → honest SKIP "not checkable"; twin recompute failure → WARN; mismatch → WARN naming BOTH hex digests; match → PASS; `run_doctor`/`main` gain optional `wheel_source_crate_root`/`fno_math_wheel_source_crate_root` (default = the repo checkout resolved from the `brutex` package location); the `test_doctor.py` aggregate pin updated 7 → 9 stages. **HASH-PRIMITIVE DECISION:** the Python twin hashes with the `blake3` PyPI package — ALREADY a BruteX BASE dependency (`pyproject.toml` per DEC-SWEEP-REALTIME-GUARANTEE-001 #549), so NO new dependency and NO reliance on `fno_math.blake3_hash` (the prompt's fallback caveat is moot: the digest input AND the hash primitive are both wheel-independent, so a stale wheel cannot influence its own expected value). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** LOCAL-machine scope ONLY — verified today: there is NO committed wheel anywhere and CI builds every wheel from source via maturin per job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:78,181,283`), so CI can never observe a stale wheel and NO "CI teeth" are claimed (the goldens gate FRAMING PARITY in CI, not wheel staleness); mismatch is a WARN not a FAIL (an operator observation, consistent with wheel_freshness); the digest covers `Cargo.toml` + `src/**/*.rs` only — a change confined to `build.rs` itself or the crate's `tests/`/`fuzz/` does NOT move the digest (deliberate: those do not alter the shipped kernel's behaviour), and ONE NAMED residual remains: the excluded `python/` shim IS shipped wheel behaviour (maturin's mixed layout packages `rust/<crate>/python/<pkg>/__init__.py` INTO the wheel), so a local wheel stale ONLY in the shim escapes ALL FOUR wheel stages (the freshness stages fingerprint the compiled module's version+symbols, not shim content; this digest covers the compiled kernel's source only) — folding the shim files into a future FRAMING v2 is the named follow-up, NOT claimed here; the stage detects source-tree drift, NOT toolchain drift (same source rebuilt by a different rustc yields the same digest — the CI golden/parity suites remain the behavioural correctness proof); dangling symlinks are outside the set on both sides (is-file predicates follow links). **LIVE END-TO-END PROOF:** both wheels rebuilt locally with `maturin develop --release` (Python 3.12 venv) — baked `__source_digest__` values `ce641a07…` (trading-core) / `e03c7179…` (fno-math) matched the Python twin's recompute byte-for-byte and `check_wheel_source_digest`/`check_fno_math_wheel_source_digest` returned live PASS through `run_doctor` (pinned in `tests/unit/test_doctor_wheel_source_digest.py::TestLiveWheels`). Gates: `brutex/wheel_digest.py` + `brutex/doctor.py` 100% line+branch across their mapped suites; `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --release` green on BOTH crates (+ trading-core `cargo check --features python`); trading-core's committed `Cargo.lock` updated for the new `[build-dependencies] blake3`; fno-math's lock UNCHANGED — blake3 was ALREADY locked as its runtime dependency, so the new build-dep edge resolved with zero lock change (`cargo test` left the lock byte-unmodified; the empty fno-math lock diff is CORRECT) (build-script-only either way — the shipped rlib dependency tree is unchanged, TickVault's native link stays dependency-free); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on every touched Python file. Sibling doc reconciliations: both wheel shims' (`rust/*/python/*/__init__.py`) "named follow-up" paragraphs now state the follow-up is CLOSED by this decision (import-time handshake deliberately does NOT gate on the digest — an older wheel must keep importing so the doctor can warn). **HOSTILE-REVIEW FOLDS (FIX-FIRST round, all MINOR/NIT — no BLOCKER/MAJOR):** (1) the lock-file sentence above CORRECTED — only trading-core's `Cargo.lock` moved (the prior "both locks updated" wording contradicted the diff; the review verified the empty fno-math lock diff is correct); (2) the `python/`-shim residual NAMED in the honest envelope here + in the `_check_one_wheel_source_digest` docstring; (3) §8-reference-machine (Apple M4 Pro / APFS) test portability — the two non-UTF-8-filename tests now PROBE the filesystem and `pytest.skip` when it refuses such names (APFS EILSEQ) instead of erroring, and the twin-vs-oracle hypothesis property dedups drawn names on their casefolded-NFD form so a case-/normalization-insensitive volume can never collapse two drawn files into one while the oracle frames both (Linux CI keeps the full teeth — nothing skips there); (4) the doctor's twin-recompute catch WIDENED to include `RecursionError` so an adversarial symlink CYCLE under `src/` WARNs instead of crashing `run_doctor` (Rust's build-time recompute still aborts loudly on such input — purely-local adversarial input, both sides still agree on every well-formed tree, no parity drift; a visited-set / symlink-dir rejection is FRAMING-v2 material, not claimed); (5) the live-PASS assertions (`TestLiveWheels` + the two sibling live-PASS tests) now SKIP on a LOCAL machine whose installed wheel is genuinely STALE — the skip message names the exact `maturin develop --release` rebuild command per stale crate (the self-explanatory local failure mode the review asked for) — while under CI (`CI` env set, as GitHub Actions always does) they still HARD-ASSERT PASS, because there the wheels are built from the job checkout by construction and a mismatch is a real regression. **Decision ID:** DEC-RUST-SOURCE-DIGEST-TWIN-001. ## DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-FLUSH-001 (2026-07-04)

1275. **DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-FLUSH-001 — the throttled mid-pull window-ledger flush becomes an O(dirty) incremental DELTA APPEND (first step of the incremental ledger format): a dirty-key set on `WindowLedger` + NEW `window_ledger_store.append_ledger_delta` writing ONLY the rows dirtied since the last flush to `<lake>/window_ledger/deltas/<time_ns>-<pid>.parquet` under the EXISTING ledger `partition_write_lock`; `make_live_ledger_flush` switches to the delta append; `load_window_ledger` folds `base + deltas`; the pull-end `save_window_ledger` subsumes + deletes the folded deltas** (2026-07-04; PR-2 of the P2 polish train). **WHY:** every throttled mid-pull flush was `save_window_ledger` — an O(N) whole-file READ-MERGE-WRITE measured at ~4 s/save on a ~841k-row pre-planned universe ledger — re-paid on every eligible fire for rows that had not changed. **MECHANISM:** every row-writing mutator (`plan` insert, `seed_lake_success`, `record`, `settle_known_gap`, the `reopen_skipped` demotion) stamps its key into `WindowLedger._dirty` (O(1)); `dirty_rows()`/`dirty_keys()`/`clear_dirty()` expose the batch; `append_ledger_delta` writes the batch with the SAME fixed 13-column schema via the COMMON `atomic_write_via` (ENOSPC/OOM → `LakeWriteHalt`, DEC-WINDOW-LEDGER-WRITE-HALT-001 preserved), clears the keys ONLY on success, and a `PartitionLockTimeout` skips loudly (`window_ledger.delta_lock_timeout`) with the keys kept dirty. **FOLD SEMANTICS (deliberate deviation, regression-pinned):** the load fold is **newer-file-wins per window key** (filename order == append order — appends serialise under the flock), NOT the sketch-named `merge_ledger_rows`: the delta stream is a WAL replay of ONE lake's serialised write chronology, and the merge rule's more-settled preference would RESURRECT a deliberate demotion (a `reopen_skipped` SKIPPED→FAILED / a degraded SUCCESS→FAILED, DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-REPULL-001) from an older, more-settled copy — pinned by `test_delta_fold_never_resurrects_a_deliberate_demotion`. `merge_ledger_rows` STAYS the cross-process arbiter inside `save_window_ledger` (unchanged). **CONSUMER FRESHNESS (in scope, the correctness shims):** (a) `lake_revision._ledger_revision` folds the deltas-DIR stat into the cross-process token (a delta append no longer touches the base file, so the #1149 token would have FROZEN for the whole pull); (b) `db_view`'s ledger readers are delta-aware — `_ledger_records_cached` + `spot_window_rollup` key their caches on `(base mtime, delta name set)` and tolerate a base-less delta-only lake, `build_window_payload`'s DuckDB fast path + `phase_progress_payload` DEFER to the fold-aware Python read while deltas are pending (mid-pull O(N) processing, bounded to the pull — the pre-#893 cost; the SQL-side delta fold restoring O(page) mid-pull is a NAMED follow-up), and a base-less deltas-only lake reads as source=`ledger`, never the frozen `status_log` sidecar; `load_or_migrate_window_ledger` likewise treats deltas-only as a LIVE ledger. **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** deltas cannot express a DELETION — `prune_superseded` does not stamp (the pull-end full save with its `pruned_keys` tombstones is the prune authority); a crash before the pull-end save leaves orphaned deltas which the NEXT pull's first full save folds + subsumes — a scheduled standalone BASE COMPACTION is the NAMED follow-up, deliberately NOT built; a row re-dirtied between a flush's snapshot and its clear rides until its next mutation / the pull-end save (the same bounded-staleness window the throttle already accepts); a failed delta unlink after a save is loudly logged (`window_ledger.delta_prune_failed`) since a stale delta would newer-wins-override the fresher base until the next successful save. Repointed pins in the SAME commit: `TestLiveFlush` (delta artifact), the CLI mid-pull checkpoint spy (`append_ledger_delta`), the lake_revision composite-token formats. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change. **Decision ID:** DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-FLUSH-001.

## DEC-WRITTEN-SETTLED-CENSUS-001 (2026-07-04)

1276. **DEC-WRITTEN-SETTLED-CENSUS-001 — an OBSERVE-ONLY written-vs-settled census: the pull now cross-checks the window ledger's settled `SUCCESS` series against the lake spans it ALREADY loaded for its cold-start reconcile, surfacing a ledger↔lake disagreement as ONE `pull.written_settled_mismatch` WARNING (samples capped 20) — DETECT + WARN only, NO auto-remediation** (2026-07-04; PR-2 of the P2 polish train). NEW pure `brutex/dashboard/pull_census.py`: frozen `WrittenSettledCensus` + `build_written_vs_settled_census(ledger_rows, spans, *, intervals, symbols)` — a **series-level** `(symbol, interval)` fold: a series with ≥ 1 ledger `SUCCESS` row but NO bar-holding lake span reads **settled-but-unwritten** (the loud lost-partition shape); a bar-holding span with NO `SUCCESS` row reads **written-but-unsettled** (safe — those windows re-fetch idempotently — but now VISIBLE); the `intervals` scope is LOAD-BEARING (the span list also carries the DERIVED `1day` + 19 intraday-TF partitions, which legitimately have no ledger rows — DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001) and `symbols` scopes to the pull's own universe. One guarded `emit_written_settled_census` (WARNING iff mismatched, DEBUG otherwise, any internal error → `pull.written_settled_census_error` — the #1014 observe-only wiring contract, can NEVER break a pull). WIRED at BOTH spines' post-drain seams over a **pre-pull-CONSISTENT snapshot**: the F&O `_run_phase` + the spot `pull_all_spot` each capture the census pair AT the cold-start-reconcile point — the SAME already-loaded spans (the spot site hoists `load_lake_spans` out of `reconcile_ledger_with_lake` onto the byte-identical `reconcile_ledger_windows` core, zero extra I/O) plus a pre-plan `ledger.to_rows()` snapshot — and EMIT once post-drain, so THIS pull's own fresh writes/settles can never false-flag against the pre-pull span read. HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10): series-level, NOT per-window (a per-window enclosure test needs trading-calendar-aware tail handling or every trailing weekend-bounded window false-flags — the per-window refinement is a NAMED follow-up); pre-pull spans mean the CURRENT pull's writes are out of the census envelope (re-loading fresh post-drain spans is a NAMED follow-up); a dry-run emits over empty inputs (a silent clean census). `pull_census.py` 100% line+branch (12 unit tests: both mismatch classes, both scope guards, cap-across-classes, clean-silence, guard-swallows) + one integration pin per spine (F&O: exactly one WARNING naming the contract; spot: exactly one WARNING naming the symbol + an agreeing-pull-stays-silent regression). ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no ledger/status writes, no vendor calls, no scope/vocab/rate change. **Decision ID:** DEC-WRITTEN-SETTLED-CENSUS-001.

## DEC-SKIPPED-AUDIT-ROUNDROBIN-001 (2026-07-04)

1277. **DEC-SKIPPED-AUDIT-ROUNDROBIN-001 — `reopen-skipped` MECHANIZED: every pull automatically re-audits ≤ 25 terminally-`SKIPPED` windows, ROUND-ROBIN across pulls via a persisted `last_audit_pull_id` + cursor sidecar — so the whole SKIPPED population is eventually re-verified without an operator ever running the CLI** (2026-07-04; PR-2 of the P2 polish train). WHY: re-opening was MANUAL-ONLY (`brutex reopen-skipped`, cli.py) and `WindowLedger.reopen_skipped(limit=)` always selected the SAME head-of-sort rows, so round-robin coverage was structurally impossible — a vendor-bug 200-empty settled SKIPPED stayed cemented until a human intervened. MECHANISM: (1) `window_ledger.py` — NEW `SKIPPED_AUDIT_PER_PULL = 25` + `WindowLedger.audit_reopen_skipped(*, start_after, cap) -> (count, new_cursor)`: walks the deterministic (market, symbol, interval, start, end) sort STRICTLY AFTER the cursor, WRAPPING to the head when the tail runs short; each selected row is demoted through the SAME extracted `_demote_skipped_locked` body the operator re-open uses (status→`FAILED`, `empty_streak` reset — the FULL fresh confirmation budget — `REOPENED` marker stamped so the re-check is breaker-EXEMPT via `is_expected_empty_recheck`, `_reopened` merge tombstone + `_dirty` stamp recorded; `reopen_skipped` itself refactored onto the helper, byte-identical). (2) `window_ledger_store.py` — a tiny JSON SIDECAR `<lake>/window_ledger/skipped_audit_cursor.json` (NOT a 14th ledger Parquet column — the fixed `_COLUMNS` schema + `_row_preference` merge rank stay byte-untouched), written via the guard-FREE `atomic_write_simple` (a cursor write failure — even ENOSPC — logs `skipped_audit_cursor_save_failed` and NEVER `LakeWriteHalt`s a pull; a corrupt/missing sidecar tolerantly restarts the rotation from the head, which is DATA-SAFE); `run_skipped_audit(ledger, lake_root, *, pull_id, cap)` short-circuits on a matching `last_audit_pull_id` (at most once per pull — Golden Rule #7), runs the rotation on the pull's OWN in-memory ledger (so the `reopened_keys` tombstones flow into the pull-end merge-save and the demotions PERSIST), saves the advanced cursor (an empty selection PRESERVES the prior position) and logs ONE `pull.skipped_audit`; `run_skipped_audit_guarded` is the best-effort seam wrapper (`None` ledger / any error → 0, `pull.skipped_audit_error`). (3) ONE seam: `pull_controller.pull_all_spot`'s minute phase, after the cold-start reconcile + census snapshot and BEFORE `plan_windows` — the reopened FAILED rows are simply re-fetched by the normal spine (a reopened OPTION-market row persists via the pull-end save and re-fetches on the NEXT F&O phase, which loads the shared ledger). **HONEST BUDGET (Golden Rule #10, stated on the constant's docstring):** 25 windows ≈ `25/86,400 ≈ 0.03%` of the worst-case 8h @ 3 r/s call budget — and since each re-opened window regains the FULL fresh confirmation budget (~2-3 fetches under the empty-retry law) the true per-pull ceiling is ~50-75 fetches ≈ 0.06-0.09%, still negligible. NAMED FOLLOW-UPS (not this PR): the CLI `brutex fetch` seam (no equivalent pre-plan hook today — the #935/#1175 CLI-seam precedent), a `/universe` audit chip, per-symbol audit scoping. Tests: 6 unit (head/rotation/wrap/no-op/cap-0/breaker-exempt) + 9 store (cursor round-trip / missing-silent / 3×corrupt+wrong-shape loud / once-per-pull / rotation-across-pulls / prior-cursor-preserved / guarded no-op+swallow / ENOSPC-save-loud) + 2 integration (a live `pull_all_spot` demotes a seeded SKIPPED option row + persists cursor + merge does NOT resurrect; a second pull converges to 0). ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), stored bars untouched (re-open is DATA-SAFE), no scope/vocab/rate change. **Decision ID:** DEC-SKIPPED-AUDIT-ROUNDROBIN-001.

## DEC-SUMMARY-CACHE-COLD-OUTAGE-BUMP-001 (2026-07-04)

1280a. **DEC-SUMMARY-CACHE-COLD-OUTAGE-BUMP-001 — the `SummaryCache` cold-start-during-outage envelope (the DEC-SURFACE-TRIAL-001 #1154 MINOR-2 "deliberately not mechanised" note (c)) is MECHANISED: a probe-outage cold start now invalidates its outage-populated caches ONCE on the first probe recovery — at most ONE spurious bump per process, and the healthy-warm-start baseline-no-bump contract is byte-preserved** (2026-07-04; PR-2 of the P2 polish train). **THE GAP:** if the app STARTS while the revision probe errors (`lake_revision` maps every non-FileNotFoundError `OSError` to `None` — a stalled external volume) and a CLI write lands BEFORE the probe recovers, the first recovered token was recorded as a plain no-bump baseline, so caches populated over the now-stale lake survived until the next `mark_dirty`/ledger move — documented as the deliberate cost of baseline-no-bump (a naive first-token bump would spuriously invalidate EVERY healthy warm start). **MECHANISM (the discriminating key that makes it safe):** ONE new private flag `SummaryCache._cold_probe_outage`, armed in `_reconcile_revision_locked` iff `revision_probe is not None ∧ token is None ∧ _last_revision is None` — a WIRED probe erroring pre-baseline; the wired-ness check is LOAD-BEARING because an UNwired cache also reconciles `None` on every read (`_probe_token`'s no-probe path) and must never arm it. The baseline branch then bumps the generation iff `flag ∧ self._entries` (caches were actually populated during the outage — an observed-only outage records a plain baseline) and clears the flag unconditionally. **AT-MOST-ONCE, STRUCTURALLY:** `_last_revision` transitions `None → non-None` exactly once per process, so a later post-baseline outage + recovery can never re-arm or re-bump (regression-pinned); a healthy warm start (first probe call already non-`None`) never sets the flag — even with an entry populated before any generation read — so the #1149 baseline-no-bump contract is untouched (the pre-existing `test_probe_baseline_recorded_without_bump` + `test_probe_none_is_noop_then_baseline` pass UNMODIFIED). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** the bump is a heuristic over-invalidation (the outage-populated caches MAY have been perfectly fresh — one extra lazy recompute per keyed cache, never a missed change; the same over-invalidate-never-miss envelope as the out-of-order-token note (b)); `self._entries` non-emptiness is an EXACT proxy at cold start (pre-baseline, any entry was necessarily populated while the probe was erroring or before any probe observation); per-kind outage tracking + an outage-vs-unwired sentinel at the `_probe_token` layer + any `lake_revision.py` change are explicit NON-goals (named follow-ups). The #1154 MINOR-2 "deliberately not mechanised" wording is reconciled in place (bracketed COLD-OUTAGE RECONCILE note); CLAUDE.md's copy of the #1154 blurb is coordinator-owned — flagged as a follow-up, NOT edited here. NEW pins: `test_cold_start_outage_recovery_bumps_once_and_recomputes` · `..._without_entries_is_plain_baseline` · `..._at_most_once_per_process` (incl. the post-recovery None→same-token no-op + a real change still bumping) · `test_healthy_warm_start_with_entries_never_bumps` · `test_unwired_probe_never_arms_the_outage_flag`; `summary_cache.py` 100% line+branch (112/24, 0 missing); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. READ-side dashboard cache only — ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change. **Decision ID:** DEC-SUMMARY-CACHE-COLD-OUTAGE-BUMP-001.
## DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-LOCKED-TS-001 (2026-07-04)

1280b. **DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-LOCKED-TS-001 — hostile-review MAJOR P2-1 of the PR-2 fix-round FIXED: the ledger-delta filename timestamp is now minted INSIDE the cross-process `partition_write_lock` (it was sampled `time.time_ns()` BEFORE the acquire) AND bumped strictly past every delta already on disk, so filename order == append order BY CONSTRUCTION — the load-bearing invariant the newer-file-wins fold of DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-FLUSH-001 (#1275) relies on** (2026-07-04; PR-2 fix-round). **THE HAZARD (review-confirmed, file:line):** `append_ledger_delta` computed `directory / f"{time.time_ns():020d}-{os.getpid()}.parquet"` before `with partition_write_lock(...)`; under cross-process contention (the exact CLI+dashboard shared-lake scenario DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887 exists for — `flock` has no FIFO fairness) the later-locking writer could carry the EARLIER filename, inverting the fold order vs the real serialised append order, so a same-key row from the inverted pair could wrongly win/lose the fold (including cross-process re-surfacing of a deliberate `reopen_skipped` demotion) until the next full save re-arbitrated via `merge_ledger_rows` — bounded impact (the pull-end full save is the authority), but a direct break of the "creation order is real, not a clock guess" basis `list_ledger_deltas` pins. **FIX:** NEW private `_next_delta_path(directory)` — called ONLY under the flock — samples `time.time_ns()` and bumps it strictly past the numeric prefix of every existing `deltas/*.parquet` (`ts = max(ts, on_disk_max + 1)`), so the ordering holds even against a wall-clock STEP-BACK (the on-disk maximum is the floor, not the clock — strictly stronger than the sketch's per-process `-<seq>` suffix, which cannot order across processes); a foreign non-numeric `*.parquet` prefix is ignored (never blocks an append); the `delta_lock_timeout` log now names the deltas directory (no filename exists when the acquire expires). O(deltas) per append, bounded by the pull-end save's delta subsumption. **REGRESSIONS (the review-demanded same-key contention pin):** NEW `TestDeltaLockedTimestamp` — `test_same_key_later_append_wins_even_on_clock_step_back` (writer 1 demotes SKIPPED→FAILED + appends; writer 2 re-settles the SAME key strictly later under a clock monkeypatched to `1` ns — the later append must carry the LATER filename and the fold must keep the re-settle; FAILS on the pre-fix code) · `test_delta_filename_is_minted_under_the_flock` (a separate-fd non-blocking `flock` probe inside the mint proves the lock is HELD — the #887 held-lock test pattern) · `test_foreign_delta_filename_never_blocks_the_mint`. FOLDED IN THE SAME COMMIT (review MINOR P2-3, docs-only): `run_skipped_audit`'s docstring now STATES the crash-window honesty envelope — the advanced cursor persists BEFORE the pull-end save persists the demotions, so a pull crashing between the two advances the rotation while its ≤ cap demotions are lost (they wait one rotation cycle; DATA-SAFE, deliberately best-effort). `window_ledger_store.py` 100% line+branch (344/90, 0 missing) via its own suite; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change. **Decision ID:** DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-LOCKED-TS-001.

1293. **DEC-PREBUILD-INCREMENTAL-001 — the pipeline prebuild is now INCREMENTAL at per-SYMBOL granularity: a symbol whose 1-minute source files are byte-for-byte unchanged since its last stamped derive is SKIPPED without reading a single bar, so a nothing-changed re-run's prebuild becomes O(changed symbols) instead of re-reading + re-resampling EVERY contract's full 1-minute base across 20 timeframes (~2 h measured on the operator's 2026-07-04 run)** (2026-07-04; round-4 findings pack item 4, ledger block #1290–#1299 — the BOUNDED per-symbol first step as instructed; a per-TF stamp is explicitly NAMED future work, NOT claimed). MECHANISM: NEW `brutex/data/derive_stamp.py` — `source_1m_token` (sha256 over the symbol's sorted `1minute/**/*.parquet` `relpath·size·mtime_ns` triples — the house content/mtime-token pattern of `lake_revision.py` #1149, per-symbol), a JSON sidecar `DeriveStamp` at `<lake>/.derive_stamps/<exch>/<seg>/<symbol>.json` (outside `bars/`, never `*.parquet` — the `.locks` sidecar convention #887), the pure `should_skip_derive` rule, `incremental_prebuild_enabled` (env `BRUTEX_PREBUILD_INCREMENTAL`, default ON; `0`/`off`/`false`/`no` disables) and `remove_derive_stamp`. `materialize_lake_timeframes` gains `incremental: bool | None = None` (None → env): token BEFORE the read (a racing write over-derives next run, never a stale skip) → skip iff token+tf-set+include_daily match AND the daily-cutoff rule holds AND every requested derived interval dir exists (`_derived_dirs_present` — an out-of-band deletion / failed heal rebuild falls through to a full derive); a successful FULL derive writes a fresh stamp (best-effort — a failed save logs `derive_stamp.save_failed` and costs one future re-derive, never a raise); a skip returns `MaterializeResult(unchanged=True)` + logs `prebuild.derive.unchanged_skip`. CORRECT UNDER HEAL/LATEST-WINS BY CONSTRUCTION: every 1-minute-mutating path (pull append, DEC-LAKE-HEAL-001 quarantine-move + rewrite, re-pull) atomically replaces month files → the token MOVES; the healer's derived recall (`lake_heal._run_recall`) ADDITIONALLY removes the symbol's stamp outright and its TF rebuild passes `incremental=False` (heal must always rebuild what it just quarantined, and its subset-tf/no-daily shape never writes a stamp) — regression-pinned (`test_recall_removes_the_derive_stamp`). NO STALE `1day`: the stamp records the cutoff used + the data's last IST session; a later-day re-run skips ONLY when the stamped cutoff already lay strictly AFTER the data's last session (every session final) — a run whose cutoff EXCLUDED the forming session re-derives on the next day and finalises that daily bar (pinned end-to-end). BYTE-EQUALITY GOLDEN: two clone lakes — one taking the stamped skip, one forced full — end in recursively identical `bars/` bytes (`test_golden_stamped_skip_lake_equals_full_rederive_lake`). VISIBILITY: `PrebuildOutcome.unchanged_skips` (counted at the `run_pipeline_prebuild` materialise seam; a skipped symbol still counts `symbols_built` — its derived data is present + current), the `pipeline.prebuild.done` log carries it, and the pipeline note appends `", N unchanged symbol(s) skipped (incremental)"`. MEASURED (synthetic, 20 F&O symbols × 5 sessions × 375 bars, all 19 TFs + 1day, tmpfs): full re-run `3.571 s` → stamped re-run `0.012 s` (~300× on the re-run; per symbol ~180 ms full vs ~0.6 ms skip). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): the production ~2 h figure was measured on the operator's lake — the skip removes the read+resample per unchanged symbol but the re-run still pays one O(files) stat walk per symbol (NOT O(1)-total; the exact production wall-clock is NOT re-measured here — a fresh run report will state it); the token is size+mtime_ns-based (an out-of-band write preserving both is undetected — no production writer does that; same envelope as #1149); per-SYMBOL granularity only (one changed month re-derives that symbol's whole history — the per-TF/month refinement is the named follow-up). `derive_stamp.py` + `timeframe_materialize.py` + `pipeline_prebuild.py` + `pipeline_pull.py` ALL 100% line+branch; `lake_heal.py` rides its 78-test suite; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change.

1294. **DEC-INGEST-BOUNDARY-INTEGRITY-001 — the ingest data-integrity pack (audit 2026-07-03): four boundary gaps closed as ONE change set — (a) the ingest-boundary session filter is now CALENDAR-AWARE (each bar judged against its OWN IST date's real NSE session via `calendars/nse.get_session` — muhurat/special-weekend/regular/no-session), (b) the parser's DEFENSIVE epoch-timestamp branch is LOUD once per pull, (c) an ALL-FILTERED window (vendor bars > 0, session-filter survivors == 0) is demoted to a re-pullable FAILED via the existing #1031 degraded machinery, and (d) the sink's keep-first-DEDUPED `bars_net_new` (#1031 computed it, never persisted it) is threaded into the durable window ledger** (2026-07-03 on `claude/sharp-hypatia-5hhycf`; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; DATA-SAFETY LAW held throughout — no legitimate bar lost, re-pull idempotence preserved [keep-first dedup; a SUCCESS whose bars all dedup to zero net-new STAYS SUCCESS, regression-pinned on BOTH spines], vendor junk never crashes). **GAP (a) — calendar-aware session filter (`brutex/data/session.py` NEW `filter_to_trading_session` + `SessionFilterResult`), wired at BOTH ingest tails (`adapters/groww/ingest.py::_process_window_tail` + `option_ingest.py::_process_option_window_tail`, replacing the date-blind fixed-09:15-15:30 `filter_intraday_session` there):** two real defects closed — a bar on a NON-TRADING date (weekend/holiday leak whose wall clock looked in-session) previously entered the lake, and an evening Diwali-MUHURAT bar (18:15-19:15) was WRONGLY DROPPED. Now: per-bar IST via `astimezone`, ONE `get_session` lookup per unique IST date (dict cache — O(bars + unique_dates), O(1) amortized per bar, never claimed more); keep iff time-of-day ∈ [open, close) of that date's session; a no-session date drops the bar COUNTED (`dropped_non_trading_date`), an off-session wall clock drops it COUNTED (`dropped_off_session`); EXACTLY ONE aggregated structlog WARN per window when count > 0 (`ingest.session_filter.dropped` / `option.ingest.session_filter.dropped` — window identity + per-cause counts, never per-bar spam, never a crash). GOLDEN parity pinned: on a regular trading day the kept-set is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the legacy filter (full-day minute sweep). SANCTIONED BEHAVIOR CHANGES (regression-pinned): a muhurat evening bar is now KEPT (both spines), a special-weekend (Budget Saturday) bar KEPT, a regular-hours bar ON a muhurat date now DROPPED (the exchange is closed then), a holiday/weekend in-window-looking bar now DROPPED+counted, a 09:00 pre-open bar dropped+counted (unchanged). OUT-OF-COVERAGE ABSTENTION (Golden Rule #1): a date outside the published holiday-list span (`is_holiday_data_available`, 2020-2026) falls back to the legacy fixed window — byte-identical to the old filter there, never dropping MORE (an unknown post-2026 muhurat evening would still drop — the honest limit until the calendar is extended). The GIFTNIFTY `is_session_exempt` bypass is preserved; `filter_intraday_session` is KEPT as the date-blind legacy helper (the golden oracle + the doctor live-proof probe's deliberate consumer — every caller grepped and dispositioned); the DAILY (`1day`) path stays deliberately UNFILTERED on both spines (a daily bar has no intraday time — documented); the RESAMPLERS are untouched BY DESIGN — they derive every TF from the stored (already boundary-filtered) 1-minute, so this single choke point covers all 21 TFs. **GAP (b) — epoch-branch loud WARN (`adapters/groww/parser.py::parse_timestamp_ist`):** parsing behavior UNCHANGED; taking the numeric branch now emits ONE `groww.parse.epoch_timestamp` WARNING per pull (module-level thread-safe guard keyed on `current_pull_id()` — the sanctioned tiny process-global, precedent MetricRegistry — with the explicit reset seam `reset_epoch_timestamp_warnings()`; an UNBOUND pull scope dedups under the `""` key, still warned once per process — decided + tested; O(pulls) memory of 12-char ids). HONEST: the vendor's epoch semantics are UNVERIFIED (no live probe from this sandbox) — the branch assumes Unix-UTC seconds; if Groww ever sent IST-naive epochs every bar would silently shift +05:30, which is exactly why the branch firing is now LOUD (docstring + this entry carry the risk). Tests: many epoch rows one pull → exactly ONE warn; two pull ids → two; no-pull-id → one under `""`; string path → zero; 8-thread barrier → one; non-finite epoch still flagged; whole epoch payload through `parse_candle_rows` → one. **GAP (c) — all-filtered SUCCESS made distinguishable + re-examinable:** `classify_window_status` judges on RAW vendor count, so a window whose bars ALL got session-filtered recorded SUCCESS with 0 stored bars and was never re-pulled. Discriminator `raw_bars > 0 AND post-session-filter survivors == 0` (ORTHOGONAL to sink dedup — a full-dedup re-pull passes bars THROUGH the filter and stays SUCCESS, pinned on both spines) rides the EXISTING #1031 degraded demotion (FAILED + NEW reason constant `session.ALL_FILTERED` stamped as `last_error`, `empty_streak` bumped, BOUNDED settle SKIPPED after `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` — data-safe, stored bars kept). An OLD on-disk ledger loads with `bars_net_new=None` — the honest UNKNOWN, NEVER a fabricated 0 (unlike the other two optional columns there is NO safe derivable floor); a lake cold-start seed likewise records None; the deferred/failed-write records carry a KNOWN 0 (nothing landed); `bars` stays the INPUT batch size (every `>0` gate untouched). Both spines thread the REAL `SinkAppendResult.bars_net_new` at their ledger-record sites (proven with a sink whose net-new deliberately differs from bars_appended); the `/db` window-ledger grid gains the `bars_net_new` column (`dashboard/app.py`, last column). HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10): daily path unfiltered by design; vendor epoch semantics UNVERIFIED; the muhurat-keep (and the muhurat-date regular-hours-drop) is a deliberate operator-facing behavior change; resamplers untouched by design; old ledgers read `bars_net_new=None`; out-of-coverage dates keep legacy fixed-window semantics; already-stored out-of-session/holiday bars from PRE-fix pulls are NOT retroactively cleaned (read-side unchanged — a re-pull re-filters at the boundary). 1295. **DEC-SWEEP-STREAMING-RANK-002 — the Stage-3 leaderboard selection (`stage3_select.group_survivors`) is rewritten from accumulate-ALL-then-two-pass-sort (O(candidates) RAM per LeaderboardKey) to a BOUNDED per-key top-K min-heap (O(top_k) RAM per key), BYTE-IDENTICAL output — part 2 (the leaderboard-RAM fix) of the DEC-SWEEP-STREAMING-RANK-001 series (#1184 lazy run-id / #1187 its test hardening)** (2026-07-04, branch `claude/trusting-newton-prb`; ENGINE semantics UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track; no scope/vocab/rate/lake change). THE PROBLEM: `group_survivors` appended EVERY candidate row into a per-`LeaderboardKey` list and only then ran the stable two-pass sort (run_id asc, then Sharpe desc) + `[:top_k]` trim — O(N) retained rows for N streamed candidates even though only `top_k` (spec default 10,000) survive. THE FIX: rows now stream ONCE (the `rows` iterable is consumed lazily — a generator suffices, pinned) through a per-key `heapq` min-heap of NEW frozen `_HeapEntry(sharpe, run_id, seq, row)` wrappers whose `__lt__` means "ranks strictly WORSE than" — smaller Sharpe, then LARGER `run_id` (run_id is a hex STRING and cannot be negated into a tuple key, hence the wrapper with the inverted comparison), then LARGER insertion index `seq` — so the heap ROOT is always the worst kept entry and, among equal-lowest-Sharpe entries, the LARGEST run_id is evicted FIRST (run_id-asc preferred), with `seq` (unique per input row) making the order a STRICT total order so eviction is deterministic even for duplicate `(sharpe, run_id)` rows. BYTE-IDENTITY PROOF SHAPE: the old two-pass stable sort orders exactly by (Sharpe desc, run_id asc, insertion order asc) — the same strict total order the heap retains the K-best of — and the final emit re-runs the ORIGINAL discipline restricted to the kept set (sort by `(run_id, seq)` asc, then stable Sharpe-desc pass), so key iteration order, per-board row order, and every row byte match the old path. FULL-precision Sharpe throughout (never rounded — the DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 money-only boundary); NaN needs no handling BECAUSE it is out of the domain — `ResultRow` rejects non-finite metrics at construction (pinned in the suite, so the old sort's NaN behaviour is moot, not silently changed). PINNED BY: (1) a GOLDEN-EQUALITY suite (`TestGoldenEqualityVsReference`) against `_group_survivors_reference` — a VERBATIM test-side copy of the pre-#1295 implementation — asserting `repr()` STRING equality (dict key order + row order + every field; strictly stronger than `==`) over adversarial fixtures: an equal-Sharpe tie cluster larger than K, duplicate run_ids (full ties with distinguishable payloads — insertion order decides, exactly as the old stable sort did — AND differing-Sharpe repeats), fewer-than-K / exactly-K / K+1 boundaries, interleaved multiple leaderboards, extreme-FINITE Sharpe (±1e308, ±5e-324, signed zero — `-0.0` canonicalised by ResultRow, comparator falls through to run_id exactly like `sorted`), and 5 seeded random permutations of a 90-row 3-board duplicate-heavy soak; (2) direct `_HeapEntry` comparator tests incl. the tie-eviction law (equal Sharpe → larger run_id ranks worse → evicted first); (3) a tracemalloc BENCH (`tests/bench/test_stage3_select_bounded_memory.py`): streamed 10k vs 100k candidates at fixed K=64 — traced peak MEASURED flat at ratio 1.001 (62,566 → 62,622 B) vs the old implementation's 9.992 (7.9 MB → 79.4 MB) against a 2.0 ceiling with EXECUTABLE teeth — a second bench test runs the pre-#1295 accumulate-all reference shape through the SAME harness and asserts it EXCEEDS the ceiling, so the gate can never silently go vacuous (hostile-review NIT-1 folded; the #1026 executable-teeth precedent) (honest framing: a Python-allocator peak bound over generator-fed input, NOT an RSS claim); (4) the existing stage3/wire/results/golden/surface-trial suites pass UNMODIFIED (203 + 315 golden + 13 surface-trial). HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10 — what is NOT claimed): this bounds ONLY `group_survivors`' internal retention; TWO upstream O(all-rows) accumulation sites remain and are NAMED follow-ups, not shipped — (a) `stage3_wire.run_stage3_pass` still `extend`s every per-tuple store's rows into one `grid_rows` list BEFORE calling `group_survivors` (each store is finalist-trimmed, but the concatenation is unbounded in tuple count), and (b) `select_stage3_survivors` → `load_results_tree` still materialises the WHOLE persisted tree in one in-memory `ResultsStore` before `.rows()` — streaming those callers is the next slice of this decision series; time stays O(rows · log top_k) (was O(rows log rows)) — still a one-shot between-stage selection, NOT a Rule-#5 O(1) hot path, and no O(1) claim is made. Cross-store duplicate-run_id semantics are UNTOUCHED upstream (`ResultsStore.append` conflict-refuse + `load_results_tree`'s collision guard — the surface-trial-pinned tie-breaks ride those, byte-unchanged). 1296. **DEC-INSTRUMENT-HEADER-ADDITIVE-001 — the Groww instrument-master header check now TOLERATES purely-ADDITIVE vendor drift: extra TRAILING columns after the verified 21 parse cleanly with ONE loud `groww.instruments.header_extra_columns` WARNING naming the extras, instead of an `InstrumentFormatError` that killed the ENTIRE universe load (empty universe → zero-symbol pull)** (2026-07-04 on `claude/dreamy-tesla-js5kz6`; adapter parse guard + doc-honesty companions ONLY — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, NO scope/vocab/rate/lake change). THE GAP: `parse_instrument_csv` (`brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py`) required EXACT tuple equality of the CSV header against `INSTRUMENT_CSV_COLUMNS`, so a benign 22nd trailing column — the single most likely REAL vendor evolution — aborted the whole ~162k-row master exactly like a destructive schema break. FIX: the guard now requires the FIRST 21 columns to match `INSTRUMENT_CSV_COLUMNS` exactly (order + names — a missing, reordered, or renamed column among the 21 STILL raises `InstrumentFormatError` byte-identically); extras beyond 21 are accepted (parsing keys on the known 21 names, so trailing extras are inert) and surfaced as ONE WARNING carrying `extra_columns` + `count`. SAFETY CARVE-OUT (Golden Rule #1): an extra trailing column that DUPLICATES a known column name is REFUSED with a named `InstrumentFormatError` — `csv.DictReader` keeps the LAST occurrence per key, so a trailing duplicate would silently OVERWRITE the real cell values (corrupted lot/tick/symbol worse than a refusal). Tests (7 new in `tests/unit/test_groww_instruments.py`): extra-trailing parses + exactly one warning naming the extra; two extras both named + count=2; exact-21 emits NO warning (byte-identical baseline); missing / reordered / renamed each still raise; duplicate-known-name extra raises. `instruments.py` at 100% line+branch (141/44, 0 missing; 43 tests green). DOC-HONESTY COMPANIONS folded into this entry (comments/docstrings only, ZERO logic change — the 52→60 vocabulary grew in DEC-VOCAB-U128-CODEGEN-001 #1010 but three engine doc surfaces still showed 52-era combinatorics): (a) `engine/combo_mask.py::count_combos` doctests updated to the true default-vocab values C(60,1)=60 / C(60,2)=1770 / C(60,3)=34220 (computed, not guessed; doctest run verified green — no `--doctest-modules` in the pytest config, fixed for honesty); (b) `engine/sweep_cache.py` `DEFAULT_BLOOM_CAPACITY` comment C(52,4)=270,725 → C(60,4)=487,635 (the 5M capacity headroom claim still holds); (c) `engine/sweep_driver.py` `DEFAULT_MAX_COMBOS` comment updated to C(60,3)/C(60,4)/C(60,5) AND its stale "admits a full-vocab K≤4 sweep" claim corrected to the TRUTH the suites already pin — the 100,000 cap admits K≤3 and loudly REFUSES C(60,4)=487,635 (`test_default_bits_k4_hits_loud_refusal_cap`). Immutable records (MIGRATION history, ADRs, spec docs) deliberately untouched. 1350. **DEC-LAKE-UNIQUENESS-OFFLOAD-001 — the `/api/v1/universe/lake-uniqueness` census route is VERIFIED already-offloaded and PINNED with the regression the round-5 finding wanted; a class-sweep confirms NO remaining `async def` route in `app.py` inlines a heavy lake scan/walk on the event loop** (2026-07-05 on `lake-uniqueness-offload-local`; test + docs ONLY — ZERO `brutex/` source change; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX per CLAUDE.md §3, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY per DEC-P0-063; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake change). **THE FINDING (operator's real run, 2026-07-05):** `GET /api/v1/universe/lake-uniqueness` (the DEC-LAKE-HEAL-001 #1175 duplicate-census verdict, the `/universe` chip's data source) measured 30–46 s (max 46,615 ms) as the lake grew to ~40k+ contracts, flagged as "the one remaining route with >5 s latency … the same CLASS of defect: a heavy synchronous lake walk on the event loop" and the target of the DEC-DASHBOARD-EVENTLOOP-OFFLOAD-001 #1143 class sweep. **VERIFIED-ALREADY-FIXED (Golden Rule #1 / #10 — the honest finding):** the route does NOT run on the event loop — it was CREATED already-offloaded at its birth in #1074 (DEC-LAKE-HEAL-001): `api_universe_lake_uniqueness` does only the cheap `_require_store()` on the loop, then `payload = await run_in_threadpool(_build_lake_census_payload_cached)`, so `scan_lake_invariants` + `build_lake_census` + `census_to_dict` all run on a threadpool worker (the exact house pattern DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 / #1143's preopen fix use). EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED: with `scan_lake_invariants` monkeypatched to a blocking stub, a concurrent `/api/v1/state` answered in ~2.7 ms while the scan held a worker — the loop is free; the route's 30–46 s is the scan's OWN O(files) latency (matching the finding's own "did NOT cause a full blackout this run" note — a loop-blocking route would have blacked out every request as #1143's preopen route did for 6 minutes). So there was NO source fix to make; fabricating one would violate Golden Rule #1. **CLASS-SWEEP (the #1143 discipline, applied to origin/main):** every `async def` route in `brutex/dashboard/app.py` that touches a heavy lake read — the census (4321), `/coverage/windows` build_window_payload (4369), the `/api/v1/movers` compute_*_candidates (4617/4759), preopen symbols + `.xlsx`/`.zip`/log-tail (4847/4874/4919/4999/5313), `/completeness` scoreboard+CSV+per-symbol summarize_spot_datasets (3982/3993/4048), the `/db` datasets discovery + F&O/spot cascades + candle/option query + registry (5504/5527/5659/5715/5850/5911/5962) — was audited and EACH already wraps its blocking work in `run_in_threadpool`; the only non-offloaded heavy call site (`materialize_lake_timeframes` / `build_fno_cascade` at 3331/3345) is inside the `/pull-pipeline` BACKGROUND job body, not a loop-blocking read route; the HTML page renderers (`_render_universe_html` etc.) return static templates (no lake work). Verdict: NO remaining un-offloaded route — the #1143 sweep was already complete for this class. **THE FIX (the pin):** the census route was the ONE offloaded lake route WITHOUT a dedicated event-loop regression (only preopen + `.xlsx` had one from #1143), so this adds `test_lake_uniqueness_scan_runs_off_the_event_loop` to `tests/unit/test_dashboard_eventloop_offload.py` — REUSING that suite's `_BlockingStub` + `_assert_loop_free_while_blocked` harness: it monkeypatches `scan_lake_invariants` to block a worker, asserts `/api/v1/state` still completes within the 2 s budget (a free loop; wedged loop = the whole 5 s hold, unambiguous), then asserts the released request returns the REAL census payload (`present:True`, `findings_total:0`, `files_scanned:0` — the genuine `build_lake_census`+`census_to_dict` ran on the worker over a valid empty `LakeScanReport` the stub returns). A future refactor that inlined the scan onto the `async def` body FAILS this test — exactly the #1143 preopen regression class, now permanently guarded. HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10): this does NOT reduce the route's own 30–46 s scan latency (an O(files) whole-lake walk over the census — a true reduction needs a write-time lake manifest / incremental census, the SAME named future work as #867/#1025, NOT claimed here); it PINS the offload so the loop stays free while the scan runs, keeping every OTHER dashboard request responsive during the census. Gates (fresh runs 2026-07-05, repo venv): `tests/unit/test_dashboard_eventloop_offload.py` 4 passed (3 pre-existing + the new pin); `scripts/ci/coverage_gate_discovery.py --base origin/main` green (NO touched `brutex/**` module — test + docs only); ruff check + ruff-format clean on the touched test; `mypy --strict` introduces 0 NEW diagnostics (the 2 residual errors at the `_assert_loop_free_while_blocked` return are PRE-EXISTING on pristine main, byte-identical — the #1294 "pre-change baseline / 0 new diagnostics" standard); `pyright` 0 errors on the touched file. **Files:** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_eventloop_offload.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. 1302. **DEC-TF-REMAT-LATEST-WINS-001 — the derived intraday-TF re-materialisation writes LATEST-WINS, so a stale partial-day bucket can never FREEZE: a 15m/5m bucket materialised mid-day from only its first few 1-minute bars is REPLACED by the next prebuild's correct full-bucket recompute instead of being keep-first-discarded forever** (2026-07-05 on `claude/dreamy-tesla-js5kz6`; fix-pack #2 item A of the 2026-07-05 audit follow-ups — audit risk #3; ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change). THE GAP: `make_lake_write_tf` (`brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py`) appended via the sink's DEFAULT `keep-first` merge, while the sibling derived `1day` writer (`spot_daily_resample.make_lake_write_1day`) was already `latest-wins` — so a partial-day intraday bucket written mid-pull froze (the re-materialise recomputed the correct bucket but the keep-first conflict kept the stale stored one, silently). FIX (ONE argument + docs — REUSES the existing `merge_mode="latest-wins"` plumbing end-to-end `ParquetBarSink.append` → `ParquetWriter.write` → `_merge_write`/`_dedup_batch`, DEC-1MINUTE-ONLY-DERIVE-1DAY-001 / FIX-2; NO new write path, the write stays atomic tmp→fsync→`os.replace` via the shared `atomic_write_via`): the derived-TF writer's `sink.append` now passes `merge_mode="latest-wins"`, mirroring the derived-daily mechanism — the principle DEC-LAKE-HEAL-001 already established for derived intraday data ("keep-first would keep poison"; its healer delete-and-rebuilds). SCOPE LAW: ONLY DERIVED data is recomputable and may be replaced — the VENDOR 1-minute base is written elsewhere, never routes through this writer, and STAYS keep-first (`DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001` reproducibility preserved, regression-pinned by `test_vendor_1minute_base_stays_keep_first`). IDEMPOTENT: re-materialising unchanged data rewrites identical values byte-identically (the existing rerun byte-equality pin `test_futures_include_daily_and_second_run_adds_zero_net_new` passes UNMODIFIED under latest-wins, plus the new third-run byte-pin). 1303. **DEC-WRITE-DEADLINE-LOCK-ORDER-001 — the partition-lock acquire default is lowered 120 s → 75 s so the ordering invariant `lock-acquire timeout < durable-write deadline (90 s)` holds with real margin: the lock bound was UNREACHABLE (the 90 s write deadline abandoned the write thread while it still blocked in the `flock` poll loop — leaking the thread + lock fd per contended window — so the clean `PartitionLockTimeout` defer path could never fire)** (2026-07-05 on `claude/dreamy-tesla-js5kz6`; fix-pack #2 item B of the 2026-07-05 audit follow-ups — audit risk #4; constants/docs/observe-only WARN seam ONLY — NO pacing/rate/lake-schema change, ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX). THE INVERSION (audit-verified): `GROWW_WRITE_DEADLINE_S = 90.0` (`brutex/adapters/groww/constants.py`, DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001) wraps the WHOLE `sink.append` INCLUDING the cross-process `flock` ACQUIRE, whose own bound (`brutex/data/partition_lock.py` `DEFAULT_PARTITION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001) sat at 120 s — strictly ABOVE the outer deadline, so a contended acquire always hit the outer deadline first: window deferred (data-safe, re-pulled) but via the WRONG path — an abandoned daemon thread + open lock fd per occurrence instead of the bounded-acquire's own clean transient. FIX (minimal honest): `DEFAULT_PARTITION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` 120.0 → 75.0 (15 s margin for the merge/render/fsync/replace that follows a slow acquire; still generous for a normal multi-second peer write and still well under the 600 s pull watchdog); honest-envelope comments updated in BOTH modules. SINGLE-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH decision: the two constants deliberately STAY in their own modules — `brutex.data` must never import `brutex.adapters` (layering), so the ordering is pinned by the cross-module regression test `tests/unit/test_write_deadline_lock_order.py::TestOrderingInvariant` (imports BOTH constants, asserts strict ordering + a ≥10 s margin + the audited 75/90 pair) — a future re-inversion fails CI by name. ENV-OVERRIDE HONESTY: `BRUTEX_PARTITION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S` / `BRUTEX_GROWW_WRITE_DEADLINE_S` CAN re-invert the ordering at runtime — the cheap use-time seam WARNs: `append_with_deadline` (`brutex/adapters/groww/write_deadline.py`) on its DEFAULT-deadline path compares the effective `resolve_partition_lock_timeout_seconds()` against the effective write deadline and emits ONE `groww.write_deadline.lock_timeout_inversion` structlog WARNING per process (thread-safe warn-once sentinel + explicit `reset_lock_timeout_inversion_warning()` test seam — the `groww.parse.epoch_timestamp` warn-once precedent, DEC-INGEST-BOUNDARY-INTEGRITY-001; observe-only, never raises, never changes pacing; `lock == deadline` counts as inverted — strictly-below is the law). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): the WARN covers the default-deadline path only — an explicit per-call `deadline_seconds` (the tests' tiny-timeout driver) deliberately skips the configuration check; the check runs where BOTH effective values are cheaply reachable (the adapters side) — the writers' own lock sites do not know the write deadline and carry no warn (documented, not forced); a write ALREADY holding the lock that wedges mid-fsync still resolves via the 90 s `WriteDeadlineExceeded` abandon with its documented zombie-thread envelope (DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 — unchanged; this fix re-orders only the CONTENDED-ACQUIRE case onto the clean `PartitionLockTimeout` defer). Tests: `TestInversionWarnSeam` (default config never warns · env-inverted warns ONCE across two windows with both values · equal-boundary warns · reset seam re-arms · explicit-deadline skips · write-deadline-side inversion warns); existing `test_partition_lock.py` (36) + `test_partition_lock_property.py` + `test_groww_write_deadline.py` (16) + `test_groww_constants.py` all green unmodified. 1313. **DEC-PREBUILD-GIL-VECTORIZE-001 — the pipeline prebuild's two GIL-held per-row frame→`CandleBar` conversion loops are VECTORIZED into ONE COMMON batched converter, byte-identical lake output, so the in-process prebuild stops starving the dashboard event loop's `GET /`** (2026-07-04; perf(data); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO lake-schema / stored-bar / scope / vocab / rate-cap change; the sink write path is byte-unchanged). **NAMING HONESTY UP FRONT (hostile-review MAJOR folded, Golden Rule #1/#10):** this decision was drafted as `DEC-PREBUILD-STARVATION-CAP-001` with TWO arms — (A) a `POLARS_MAX_THREADS` prebuild thread cap at the CLI dashboard/pull entrypoints and (B) this vectorization. Arm (A) is **NOT implemented anywhere in the tree** — `brutex/cli.py` is fenced by open PRs (#1112 `fix(cli)` verified live via the GitHub API, plus #1131/#1130/#1086/#1085), and the only `POLARS_MAX_THREADS` write in the tree is the PRE-EXISTING per-worker `=1` pin on the ENGINE sweep path (`brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py:356`, deliberately untouched). The cap stays a REPORTED FOLLOW-UP with its exact recipe (an `os.environ.setdefault("POLARS_MAX_THREADS", str(max(2, cpu_count - 2)))` — setdefault so an operator env override always wins — placed BEFORE the first polars import at the dashboard/pull entrypoints ONLY, never the engine/sweep path, which owns its own per-worker pin); it gets its OWN decision ID when it ships after the cli.py fence clears — no ID is reserved now, so no code can cite an unlanded claim again. **WHY:** the one-click pipeline's timeframe prebuild runs INSIDE the dashboard server process (DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 #1145);
