1401. **DEC-HARDWARE-ENVELOPE-001 — a COMMON runtime hardware-envelope module (`brutex/config/hardware_envelope.py`) + the pipeline timeframe-prebuild PARALLELISED across the host's CPU cores via a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, byte-identical lake output; the Groww fetch pool / rate ceiling / per-minute governor DELIBERATELY untouched (a real vendor limit)** (2026-07-05; perf(dashboard); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change; the sink write path is byte-unchanged). **WHY:** the one-click pipeline's derived-timeframe prebuild (DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 #1145) resamples the stored 1-minute lake into the 19 intraday TFs + the derived `1day` for EVERY pulled symbol (spot underlyings + FUT/CE/PE contracts) strictly SINGLE-THREADED, so a full-universe prebuild used ONE core while the other 13 on the operator's M4 Pro (CLAUDE.md §8, 10P+4E, 48 GB) sat idle — the biggest single-threaded win in the pull. **DELIVERABLE (a) — the COMMON config leaf** `brutex/config/hardware_envelope.py` (imports nothing from `dashboard`/`engine`; **stdlib-only**, `psutil` is NOT a dependency): a frozen CPU-only `HardwareEnvelope(logical_cores, physical_cores, performance_cores, efficiency_cores, source)`; `detect_envelope()` (cached via `cached_envelope()`/`reset_envelope_cache()`) with the macOS→Linux→fallback cascade — macOS `sysctl hw.perflevel0/1.logicalcpu` (P/E split) + `hw.logicalcpu`/`hw.physicalcpu`; Linux `len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))` (cgroup/CI-aware); fallback `os.cpu_count()`, `None`→1; `envelope_from(overrides)` test seam; sizing helpers `cpu_pool_workers(env, *, reserve=2, cap=None, prefer_performance=True, envelope=None)` (→ **8** on the M4 Pro: 10 P-cores − 2 reserved) + `library_thread_budget(env, workers)`, env-overridable (`BRUTEX_CPU_WORKERS`) for deterministic CI. **IN-BRANCH REFACTOR (pre-merge, this entry):** the module's original draft ALSO carried RAM detection (`hw.memsize`/`/proc/meminfo` fields on the dataclass) + its own `memory_budget_bytes(env, *, fraction, floor, workers=1)` (available-RAM-preferring, floor-CLAMPED, silent-ignore `BRUTEX_MEM_FRACTION` override) — semantics CONTRADICTING the authoritative `brutex/hardware_envelope.py` `memory_budget_bytes` that DEC-RAM-BUDGETS-001 (#1360) merged to main first (total-RAM, floor-only-on-undetected, fail-LOUD env override); the duplicate half was STRIPPED before merge — this config leaf is CPU-ONLY, RAM detection + every RAM-scaled budget DELEGATE to `brutex.hardware_envelope` (one source of truth per axis, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON; `tests/unit/test_config_hardware_envelope.py::TestRamDelegationPin` fails if the duplicate surface reappears). **MERGE-FOLD (main's DEC-ENGINE-MISC-PACK-001 derive flock × this thread pool):** main's cross-process `derive_write_lock` (ONE fixed-path exclusive flock held per symbol inside `materialize_lake_timeframes`) would SERIALISE the whole thread-pool fan-out (flock contends per open file description — the branch's own `test_threaded_prebuild_not_slower` bench gate caught the regression: parallel 2.15 s vs sequential 1.60 s on the sandbox); fixed by (a) a process-local REENTRANCY registry in `brutex/data/derive_lock.py` (`_HELD_DEPTHS` — only the FIRST in-process holder takes/releases the real flock, nested holders ride it; cross-PROCESS semantics byte-unchanged, wedged-peer timeout tests untouched) and (b) the parallel orchestrator holding the derive lock ONCE around the whole pool run (readers' `derive_in_progress` honestly reads "in flight" for the run — the conservative signal; the sequential path keeps its per-symbol hold); ALSO folded on the same merge: main's `disk_guard` preflight (DEC-LAKE-FOOTPRINT-MEASURED-001) hoisted to ONE COMMON `_disk_guard_outcome` applied on BOTH the sequential AND the parallel path, so `workers > 1` can never bypass the disk-space gate (`TestParallelDiskGuard` + the derive-lock reentrancy suite pin all of it; `derive_lock.py` 100% line+branch 57/6, `pipeline_prebuild.py` 100% 194/54). `engine/sweep_parallel.py::auto_sweep_workers` now DELEGATES to `cpu_pool_workers({}, reserve=2, cap=8, prefer_performance=False, envelope=envelope_from(...))` — the ONE sizing formula (CLAUDE.md §11) — with a proven byte-unchanged result (`min(max(1,n-2),8)==max(1,min(n-2,8))` for cap≥1; verified over cpu∈{None,0,1,2,3,10,14,16,20}). **DELIVERABLE (b) — parallel prebuild** `brutex/dashboard/prebuild_parallel.py` (`PrebuildWorkItem`/`PrebuildWorkResult`/`materialize_work_item`/`resolve_prebuild_workers`/`run_work_items`) + `pipeline_prebuild.run_pipeline_prebuild_parallel` (the threaded twin of `run_pipeline_prebuild`, wired through `run_pipeline_prebuild_guarded(workers=)` and the `/pull-pipeline` route via `resolve_prebuild_workers(target_count=len(targets))`). **Why THREADS not processes** (20-agent design audit, GO-WITH-MITIGATIONS): the heavy per-symbol work is off-GIL (polars resample + the Parquet writer both release the GIL), so a `ThreadPoolExecutor` genuinely scales AND avoids every process hazard — no pickling of the materialise closure / raised exceptions, and `emit_progress_beat` (a process-global singleton) keeps feeding the 600 s pull stall-watchdog for free (a ProcessPool child's beat is a no-op → false HUNG kill). Kill switch `BRUTEX_PREBUILD_WORKERS=1` (+ a `<=1`-target tiny fallback) forces the sequential in-process path. **FIVE merge-blocking mitigations folded (11+20-agent review):** **M1** — the daily forming-session cutoff is resolved ONCE per run in the orchestrator and threaded as `daily_before=` into EVERY worker (`materialize_lake_timeframes` resolves `None`→now-IST PER CALL, so a run straddling midnight IST wrote an extra trailing `1day` bar for late symbols → order-dependent bytes); **M2** — `PartitionLockTimeout` / `WriteDeadlineExceeded` FAILED to unpickle (`f"{x:g}"` fed the formatted message string → `ValueError: Unknown format code 'g'`) and `LakeWriteHalt` double-prefixed its `reason` — all three fixed with a `__reduce__` reconstructing from the raw field (standalone hardening: threads don't pickle, but any process pool / mp-queue / cross-process audit would hit it; live-reproduced + regression-pinned); **M3** — a `LakeWriteHalt` (or a genuine bug) from any worker re-raises on the parent via `future.result()` (the `worker_pool_broken` reason token added for the process-pool era, now moot under threads but documented); **M4** — work items are DEDUPED by `(exchange, segment, symbol)` before sharding (the loose token-set contract discovery can match a #911 drift pair like `NSE-M&M` vs `M&M` to the SAME partition under two underlyings → a double-write/derive-stamp race); **M5** — dissolved by the thread pivot (beats inherited). Per-symbol quarantine (`gated_prebuild.per_symbol_data_errors`, now a public alias) runs inside each worker; the tallies (`unchanged_skips`/`opens_substituted`) fold PARENT-SIDE from the returned results (single-threaded fold, no shared-counter race). **CORRECTNESS — BYTE-IDENTITY (Golden Rule #7):** different symbols write different partitions under the per-partition `flock` (DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 #887), and the fixed `daily_before` removes the only clock-dependent input, so the threaded lake is byte-for-byte identical to a sequential run — proven by `tests/integration/test_prebuild_parallel_byte_identical.py` (3 seeded symbols, `workers=3` real pool AND `workers=1` kill switch, every derived Parquet compared byte-for-byte). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** MEASURED on the 2-usable-core sandbox — seq 1.766 s vs threaded 1.270 s = **1.39×** over 12 symbols (`tests/bench/test_prebuild_parallel_bench.py`); a bigger box scales further but NO "2 h → 20 min" claim is made without a live M4-Pro measurement; the win is a COLD contract build (an incremental unchanged-skip re-run is near-zero work either way, DEC-PREBUILD-INCREMENTAL-001) and is floor-bounded by the external-SSD write bandwidth; the shared-process polars thread pool is deliberately left at its default (a thread pool shares ONE rayon pool — pinning per-worker would serialise it; `library_thread_budget` is exposed for the process-pool/entrypoint case, not applied here); Linux `physical_cores==logical_cores` (no reliable stdlib HT split — an honest over-report). **GATES:** `config/hardware_envelope.py` 100% line+branch (109/20), `prebuild_parallel.py` 100% (75/14), `pipeline_prebuild.py` 100% (152/38), `gated_prebuild.py` 100% (125/22); `data/errors.py` `__reduce__`s covered; `auto_sweep_workers` delegation covered by the engine worker-count suite; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean on every touched file. **Files:** `brutex/config/hardware_envelope.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/prebuild_parallel.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/pipeline_prebuild.py`, `brutex/dashboard/gated_prebuild.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/data/errors.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py`, `tests/unit/test_config_hardware_envelope.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_prebuild_parallel.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_pipeline_prebuild_parallel.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_data_errors_pickle.py` (NEW), `tests/integration/test_prebuild_parallel_byte_identical.py` (NEW), `tests/bench/test_prebuild_parallel_bench.py` (NEW), `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry), `CLAUDE.md` (§8 note). **Decision ID:** DEC-HARDWARE-ENVELOPE-001. 1360. **DEC-RAM-BUDGETS-001 — RAM-scaled memory budgets (PR-5 of the hardware-envelope portability train): the two hand-picked, CLAUDE.md-§8-keyed byte budgets — the 8 GiB sweep rank-region default (`brutex/engine/sweep_mem_budget.py` `DEFAULT_MEM_BUDGET_BYTES`, #1352) and the 16 GiB Bloom bit-array wall (`brutex/orchestrator/bloom.py` `MAX_BLOOM_BYTES`, DEC-P0-047) — are now DERIVED from the machine's detected total physical RAM through ONE new stdlib-only module, `brutex/hardware_envelope.py`** (2026-07-05; branch `claude/hw-pr5-ram-budgets`; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the operator-authorized NIFTY-futures track; NO scope/vocab/rate/lake-schema/stored-bar change; nothing hashed into run identity touched — §2 Rule 4). **THE MECHANISM:** `detect_total_ram_bytes()` (POSIX `os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE') × sysconf('SC_PHYS_PAGES')` primary; macOS `sysctl -n hw.memsize` subprocess fallback at a fixed absolute path, 5 s bounded; ANY failure → the honest sentinel `0` = "unknown", NEVER "no RAM") is cached ONCE per process (thread-safe, `reset_hardware_envelope_cache()` test seam) so a derived budget can never flap mid-run; `memory_budget_bytes(fraction, floor_bytes, workers=1, env, env_var)` is the ONE COMMON derivation — explicit env override WINS (validated fail-LOUD on garbage/non-positive, mirroring the `resolve_mem_budget_bytes`/`resolve_positive_int_env` house patterns, Golden Rule #1); undetected RAM → `floor_bytes` (the old constant) EXACTLY, bit-for-bit pre-PR behavior; detected RAM → `int(total × fraction / workers)`, deliberately NOT clamped to the floor (a smaller machine derives a smaller budget — the portability point), with ONE `hardware_envelope.budget_derived` INFO line per process per budget when the figure differs from its floor. **THE SEMANTICS LAW (regression-pinned in `tests/unit/test_hardware_envelope.py::TestFortyEightGibRegressionPin`, enumerating BOTH derive call sites):** at a simulated 48 GiB §8 box every derived budget is ≥ its old constant — both shipped fractions give EXACT parity by construction (`48 GiB × 1/6 = 8 GiB`; `48 GiB × 1/3 = 16 GiB`); an 8 GiB box shrinks both; the undetected sentinel floors both. **DERIVED (2 constants):** (1) `DEFAULT_MEM_BUDGET_BYTES` — now the FLOOR of a `fraction=1/6` derivation; `resolve_mem_budget_bytes` delegates to the common helper with `env_var=BRUTEX_SWEEP_MEM_BUDGET_BYTES`, so the #1352 explicit-override contract is byte-unchanged (existing error messages preserved verbatim, test-pinned) and the production per-tuple re-resolution in `sweep_run.py:1341` is stable via the process-cached detection (once-per-process law satisfied without new plumbing); (2) `MAX_BLOOM_BYTES` — now `Final[int]` DERIVED ONCE AT IMPORT via new public `resolve_max_bloom_bytes()` (`fraction=1/3`, floor `MAX_BLOOM_BYTES_FLOOR=16 GiB`, NEW env `BRUTEX_MAX_BLOOM_BYTES` validated fail-loud), so every consumer — the `__post_init__` `BloomTooLargeError` guard (refusal still BEFORE any allocation), `sweep_launch.launch_bloom_identity_ceiling`'s lazy import + the legacy no-digest `SweepLaunchCapacityError` arm, and the inverse-sizing tests — auto-tracks the derived wall with ZERO consumer code change; scout-verified results-safe (the Bloom is an L1 prefilter over the LMDB exact ground truth, rebuild-on-resume, NOT in run identity — sizing moves only performance and WHEN a construction/launch refuses, never result bytes; the historical ≈4.097e9-identity figure is re-pinned deterministically AT the 16 GiB floor in `test_engine_sweep_launch.py`). **KEPT FIXED (deliberate, the conservative bar — full classification table in the PR body/scratchpad):** `BATCH_RANK_BYTES_PER_KEPT` (a bytes-per-object retention MODEL, not a budget), Bloom `DEFAULT_CAPACITY` + `SweepCache` `DEFAULT_BLOOM_CAPACITY` (FAIL_CLOSED correctness-guard trip-points — RAM-deriving would move a correctness boundary per machine), every LMDB `map_size` default (`sweep_cache` 2 GiB / `lmdb_membership` + `store` 10 GiB / `strategies.sweep` 1 GiB — VIRTUAL address space faulted on demand, not resident RAM), `_TRADE_SIM_CHUNK_MASKS`/`_TRADE_SIM_CHUNK_CELLS` (determinism-adjacent FFI batch boundaries, the latter coupled to the Rust 2^20 rayon threshold), `write_consumer`/`fetch_pipeline` queue depths + `sweep_parallel` heap/inflight multipliers (deliberate back-pressure/bounded-memory design points with unmeasured per-entry cost), `movers_cache` 256 (39-key warm-grid functional floor), `kernel_cache` 8 (grid-derived working set at both production callers), `greeks_enrich` `_SPOT_MEMO_CAPACITY=2` (documented locality design), `stage1a` `_DAILY_HISTORY_MAX` (correctness floor in the determinism zone), `DEFAULT_MAX_COMBOS`/`DEFAULT_MAX_TUPLES` (honesty guardrails — conscious-opt-in policy, not memory), `ROW_GROUP_SIZE` (byte-reproducibility determinism pin), plus telegram/partition-lock/dashboard-deque (too small to matter) and the Groww-lane spill/queue/quota constants (hard-excluded vendor lane / disk-not-RAM). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** a PORTABILITY + headroom change, NOT a measured speedup — no perf claim anywhere; detection reads TOTAL physical RAM, not available/free (each fraction is a heuristic share of the whole box, exactly as the old constants were); the macOS `sysctl` path is UNVERIFIED on real macOS in this Linux sandbox (mocked-subprocess unit seam only; on macOS builds whose `sysconf` exposes `SC_PHYS_PAGES` the primary path serves); ADR-0016's "48 GB safety ASSERTED, NOT MEASURED" caveat stays OPEN — this entry does NOT close it; `psutil` deliberately NOT added (stdlib-only detection). `hardware_envelope.py` (83/28) + `sweep_mem_budget.py` (73/24) + `bloom.py` (115/18) + `sweep_launch.py` ALL 100% line+branch; 1354. **DEC-PARTITION-LOCK-REALPATH-001 — the cross-process partition lock now keys its sidecar on the CANONICALISED partition path (`sha256(os.path.realpath(dest))`), closing the path-alias hole where two processes reaching ONE physical partition via different path spellings (a symlinked lake root, a relative `lake_root`, a `..` component) computed DIFFERENT lock files and did NOT mutually exclude — silently re-opening the lost-update race DEC-LAKE-PARTITION-FLOCK-001 exists to close** (2026-07-05 on `claude/dreamy-tesla-js5kz6`; fix-pack #3 FALLBACK fix of the 2026-07-05 audit follow-ups — taken because primary FIX D (`combo_digest` structural reproducibility hashes) is blocking-overlapped by open PR #1086's live hunk inside `sweep_cache.combo_digest`; ONE-line mechanism change in `brutex/data/partition_lock.py::partition_lock_path` + docs — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, no scope/vocab/rate/lake-schema change). THE GAP (audit limitation, partition_lock.py:305-330): `partition_lock_path` hashed `str(dest)` RAW, so `flock` mutual exclusion held only for byte-identical path spellings — e.g. a CLI `brutex fetch` launched with a relative `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT` and a dashboard pull on the absolute path, or a lake mounted through a symlink, each locked a DIFFERENT `.locks/<digest>.lock` sidecar while read-modify-writing the SAME physical Parquet partition. FIX: `os.path.realpath(dest)` before hashing — resolves symlinks + `..` + relative prefixes; the IDENTITY on an already-canonical absolute path, so every existing on-disk lock-file name for a canonical path is UNCHANGED (no cross-version split-lock window on the normal deploy — a mid-upgrade mixed fleet on canonical paths keys identically before and after). A not-yet-created dest is handled (POSIX non-strict `realpath` resolves the existing prefix + keeps the non-existent tail — first-write-of-a-month case, pinned). The documented POSIX-only (Linux + macOS) envelope is unchanged; the per-partition granularity (different partitions → different lock files) and O(1)-per-write cost hold (one realpath walk per lock-path computation — O(path components), dwarfed by the Parquet read-modify-write it guards). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): canonicalisation makes path ALIASES converge; it does NOT make two DIFFERENT lake roots pointing at distinct physical trees share locks (nor should it), and hard links to one file via genuinely different canonical paths remain out of scope (no repo writer creates them). TESTS (fails-before/passes-after verified by stash-revert — 4 of 7 fail pre-fix): `tests/unit/test_partition_lock.py::TestLockPathRealpathCanonicalisation` — symlinked-lake-root alias maps to the SAME lock file · `..`-component alias same · relative-vs-absolute dest same (monkeypatched cwd) · END-TO-END cross-alias mutual exclusion (a holder via the real path blocks a prober via the symlink spelling, through the REAL `partition_write_lock`/`flock`) · the canonical-absolute digest is BYTE-UNCHANGED vs the pre-fix scheme (pinned `sha256(str(dest))` equality) · a non-existent dest tail keys consistently before/after creation · different partitions still differ. COVERAGE: `partition_lock.py` 100.00% line+branch (100/12) under `test_partition_lock.py` (35) + `test_partition_lock_property.py`; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` 0 new diagnostics; `pyright` 0 errors on the touched files. THE INCIDENT (live, recurring 2 days; forensic probe + the full-run forensic workflow, logs 2026-07-04/05, pull_id `22fc7739f719`): after the pipeline's final prebuild completed, the movers-warm phase held the `PrebuildGate` for HOURS — Jul 4 the warm ran ≥ 3 h 39 m with NO `pipeline.movers_warm.done` ever logged; the forensics measured **170-256 s PER warm key over the 39-key grid ≈ 1.7-2.6 h of movers gating** (one BSE key with ZERO candidates cost 169.4 s of pure walk; pre-materialization the SAME whole-grid warm took 28 s). ROOT CAUSES (file:line at branch time): (a) each of the 39 warm jobs called `compute_spot/futures/options_candidates` WITHOUT the `datasets=` memo param (`app.py:3168-3174, 3213-3220, 3280-3290`) → `resolve_candle_datasets(lake_root, None)` → a fresh full-lake `list_candle_datasets` dir-walk PER JOB (`movers_snapshot.py:945-962`) — the options prebuild (DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 #1145) had exploded the tree to ~10⁵-10⁶ partition dirs, so each walk ran ~3 min on the external SSD (§8 hardware envelope); (b) `warm_movers_snapshots` called `job()` bare — exceptions best-effort-swallowed but SLOWNESS unbounded (`movers_warm.py:287-299`); (c) the gate released only in the route's `finally` AFTER the warm (`app.py:3461`; `prebuild_gate.py:83`) — though the half-filled-lake hazard the gate exists for ends at prebuild completion; (d) the 600 s PullWatchdog is observe-only and fed a beat per coordinate, so sub-600 s coordinates never alerted; (e) the gated payload's "movers warm 6/9" was the per-SEGMENT `i/N`, read by the operator as 7-of-9-total. FIXES: (1) **memo** — NEW `_work`-scoped `_warm_datasets(gen)` reuses the EXACT generation-stamped route memo (`_db_datasets_cache` key `"movers_candle_datasets"`, DEC-MOVERS-DISCOVERY-MEMO-001) and every warm compute receives `datasets=` — ONE walk per write generation shared warm↔route (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); byte-identity pinned (`TestWarmMemoByteIdentity` — memoised == self-scan for spot/futures/options on real lakes; plus the route-level single-walk pin `test_pull_pipeline_warm_shares_one_dataset_walk`, 39 jobs → 1 walk). (2) **deadline** — `warm_movers_snapshots` gains `job_deadline_s` (None → `resolve_warm_job_deadline_s()`: env `BRUTEX_MOVERS_WARM_JOB_DEADLINE_S`, default `DEFAULT_WARM_JOB_DEADLINE_S=300.0`, fail-safe validation mirroring `resolve_write_deadline_seconds` — blank/non-numeric/non-positive/non-finite → default, a bad value can NEVER disable the bound); each job runs under the COMMON `run_with_deadline` (`adapters/groww/deadline.py` — the #910/#999 freeze guard REUSED, stdlib-only, no copy; the dashboard already imports `adapters.groww.*`); a `DeadlineExceeded` is counted `failed` + ONE `movers.warm.job_timeout` WARN + CONTINUE; a job's OWN `TimeoutError` stays the generic `job_failed` path (never re-typed — distinguishable, pinned). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10, the #999 pattern): the abandoned worker is a daemon thread that CANNOT be killed — it dies with the process; a late completion caches the CORRECT generation-keyed value, never a wrong snapshot. (3) **gate release at prebuild** — `_prebuild_timeframes` calls `_prebuild_gate.release(outcome.ok)` the moment the guarded prebuild returns (ok OR failed); the `finally` release STAYS as the idempotent backstop (early stop / raised phase / `LakeWriteHalt` global stop — all still release, pinned by the existing gate suites); `prebuild_gate.py` docstrings + the gated note re-state the REAL release condition ("movers stay gated until the final prebuild finishes (the movers warm then continues un-gated in the background)…") and `movers.html`'s fallback string matches. REGRESSION (the decree test): `test_pull_pipeline_blocked_warm_never_holds_the_movers_gate` — a warm job blocking on a `threading.Event` while `/api/v1/movers` serves the normal NON-gated payload (gate `blocking=False`, `last_ok=True`) mid-warm; plus `test_pull_pipeline_wedged_warm_times_out_and_job_completes` (env deadline 0.05 s, all 3 spot coordinates time out, the job still settles `done`, gate released). (4) **observability + honesty** — `movers.warm.job_start` INFO per coordinate (bounded ≤ 39; start+done lines bound each job's elapsed from the log alone; `emit_progress_beat` per coordinate unchanged — the #1082 watchdog stays fed); `PrebuildGate.set_progress` gains keyword-only `segment` → `GateSnapshot.progress_segment` → payload `warm_segment` → `movers.html` renders "movers warm futures 6/9" (unlabelled reporters read `None` — back-compat; release/set_phase/idle all clear it, pinned). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): the warm's TOTAL wall-clock is bounded per-job (worst-case ≈ 39 × deadline in the background), NOT eliminated — the first open per never-warmed coordinate still pays one real scan; the gate release means `/movers` may serve while the warm is still populating the cache (a cold coordinate computes on demand — the pre-#1145 normal); the memo prevents re-WALKS, not the per-coordinate candidate computation itself. TESTS: `test_movers_warm.py` +4 (deadline resolver fail-safe matrix · timeout counted/warned/continues · own-TimeoutError stays generic · job_start with resolved env deadline), `test_prebuild_gate.py` +1 and 6 updated (segment plumbing incl. reset/idle/release + the new note), `test_dashboard_pull_pipeline_route.py` +3 (blocked-warm gate regression · one-walk pin · wedged-warm timeout end-to-end), `test_movers_discovery_memo.py` +3 (byte-identity), `test_dashboard_movers_gate.py` / `test_dashboard_js_perf_frontend.py` note-text pins updated. COVERAGE: `movers_warm.py` + `prebuild_gate.py` 100.00% line+branch; the `app.py` warm closures ride the `# pragma: no cover` job-thread convention and are EXERCISED by the route regressions above; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` clean (335 files); `pyright brutex tests` 0 errors on touched files (37 = pre-existing baseline, 0 new). Builds on DEC-PULL-MOVERS-WARM-001 #878, DEC-MOVERS-WARM-GRID-001 #1034, DEC-MOVERS-DISCOVERY-MEMO-001, DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 #1145, DEC-PREBUILD-GATE-HONEST-NOTE-001 #1292, DEC-GROWW-REAUTH-DEADLINE-001 #910 + DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 #999 (the reused freeze guard). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/movers_warm.py`, `brutex/dashboard/prebuild_gate.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, tests as named. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-WARM-UNBLOCK-001. (Ledger: numbered by deliberate high-jump above live max #1354 — uniqueness is the gate, per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 practice for parallel in-flight branches.)

1431. **DEC-PREBUILD-LOG-FLOOD-001 — the prebuild's per-partition `lake.partition.write` telemetry no longer WIPES the fetch-phase audit trail: the DERIVED-timeframe writers emit it at DEBUG (same event name + fields), and the surviving INFO record is ONE per-symbol `lake.derived.write_summary` aggregate (timeframe count + total derived bars) — a prebuild of N partitions now costs O(symbols) INFO lines, never O(partitions)** (2026-07-05 on `claude/movers-warm-unblock`, same incident pack as #1430; fix(data); logging-level + one aggregate event ONLY — ZERO write-path/stored-byte change, ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, no scope/vocab/rate change). THE DEFECT (MED, confirmed + adversarially verified by the full-run forensic workflow, logs 2026-07-04/05, pull_id `22fc7739f719`): the prebuild emits one INFO `lake.partition.write` per derived partition — **205,609 of the 206,606 retained log lines (~132 lines/s)** — and the 10 MiB × 5 rotating-file setup (`brutex/observability/logging.py:61-62`, `_DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`/`_DEFAULT_BACKUP_COUNT`) turned over in **~26 minutes**, WIPING the entire 15.7 h fetch-phase audit trail (rate/429/window-settle telemetry). An UNDOCUMENTED interaction of DEC-LAKE-WRITE-INSTRUMENT-001 (#937 — the per-partition write instrument, designed when a pull wrote O(vendor-windows) partitions) × DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 (#1145 — which then materialised ~66,722 contracts × up-to-20 TFs of tiny derived partitions through the same writer). Proof the telemetry EXISTED and was rotated away (not never-emitted): sibling snapshot `af8fd60c` showed full rate telemetry mid-fetch. FIX (demote-at-the-writer + aggregate-at-the-symbol; the telemetry is DEMOTED, never dropped — Golden Rule #1): (a) `ParquetWriter.__init__` gains `partition_log_level: str = "info"` (validated — unknown value raises `WriterError` fail-closed); the `lake.partition.write` emission uses the per-writer level with IDENTICAL event name + fields (`append_ms`/`lock_wait_ms`/`rows`/`partition_rows`/`partition` — per-partition forensics remain available at DEBUG for a deliberately-verbose session); (b) the DERIVED-path writer builders construct at `"debug"` — `timeframe_materialize.make_lake_write_tf` + `spot_daily_resample.make_lake_write_1day` (the ONLY writers on the prebuild's derived fan-out; the LIVE-PULL vendor writers keep the INFO default — rare + valuable, exactly the #937 intent); (c) `materialize_lake_timeframes` emits ONE `lake.derived.write_summary` INFO per SYMBOL on BOTH completion paths (intraday-only + include_daily) carrying `exchange/segment/symbol/timeframes_written/total_bars/skipped/include_daily` — the aggregate form of the per-partition fields (the unchanged-skip path keeps its existing `prebuild.derive.unchanged_skip` INFO; no double-count). ARITHMETIC (honest): the worst measured run's ~205,609 INFO lines collapse to ~67k-symbol × 1 ≈ 67k? NO — the summary is per MATERIALISED SYMBOL (underlyings + contracts actually derived that run, ≤ ~66,722 on a full-lake first materialisation, and the incremental stamp (DEC-PREBUILD-INCREMENTAL-001) makes the steady-state far smaller) vs ~20× that in per-partition lines — a ≥ ~20× volume cut on the flood path with the full per-partition detail one `--log-level debug` away; rotation size/count untouched (a config seam exists per-call via `configure_logging` — deliberately NOT bumped: the log-volume fix is the real one, a bigger buffer only delays the wipe). PINNED: `test_prebuild_log_volume_is_o_symbols_not_o_partitions` (integration, REAL builders over a tmp lake: ≥ 4 derived partitions written → EVERY `lake.partition.write` captured at `log_level="debug"`, exactly ONE `lake.derived.write_summary` INFO with `total_bars == result.total_bars`) + `test_intraday_only_materialize_also_emits_one_summary` (the non-daily path) + `TestPartitionLogLevel` (unit: default writer INFO with full fields · debug writer same-event-same-fields · unknown level → `WriterError`). COVERAGE: `parquet_writer.py` + `timeframe_materialize.py` + `spot_daily_resample.py` at their pre-change 100% line+branch under their stem suites (the new builder lines ride the existing `# pragma: no cover` raw-I/O convention and are exercised by the roundtrip integration pins); ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/`pyright` clean (0 new diagnostics). 1510. **DEC-STORED-DATA-VALIDATION-001 — stored-data validation pack: the READ boundary + the derived-TF prebuild + the lake census now REFUSE / SURFACE price-corrupt stored bars instead of silently consuming them, the vendor OHLC clamp is counted + WARNed, and the movers//db 2dp display cells follow the pinned ROUND_HALF_UP law via ONE shared JS formatter** (2026-07-05 on `claude/stored-data-validation`; the round-2 adversarial audit's confirmed stored-data defects L1-a/L1-b/L1-gap/L1-gap-2/L3-a, every one live-reproduced before fixing; ENGINE semantics unchanged for clean data — the goldens pass byte-identical; a previously-silently-accepted CORRUPT bar now failing loudly is the ONE sanctioned behavior change; Groww constants untouched, no scope/vocab/rate change, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY). **L1-a (MED, read boundary):** zero/negative but internally-ORDERED prices (open=-5, high=-1, low=-10, close=-2) passed silently into Stage-1A + run identity (reproduced: a day_low of -1000 from a raw-planted partition; the only ≤0 screen was ingest-parse-time #912 `has_no_price`, bypassed when READING pre-#912 legacy bars). FIX: price positivity is enforced at the ENGINE READ BOUNDARY `feed/replay.py::arrow_table_to_bars` (the `ReplayFeed._load_bars` → `Catalog.get_bars` → Stage-1A seam) — it gains an optional `source=` and, per row, checks every OHLC price `> 0` BEFORE construction (naming the real defect) then wraps the constructor's ordering guard, so a corrupt stored bar raises a LOUD `ValueError` naming the partition coordinates (ReplayFeed passes `exchange/segment/symbol/interval`) + the bar ts — the graceful per-symbol error surface the ingest/prebuild quarantines already handle. DELIBERATELY NOT at the shared `models._validate_price_bar` constructor: `CandleBar`/`FnoGreeksBar`/`OptionBar` is the general in-memory bar container, and legitimate consumers build a non-positive-price bar ON PURPOSE to feed their own corrupt-input classifier — the Greeks engine's BAD_INPUT/BELOW_INTRINSIC stamping (DEC-GREEKS-CORRECTNESS-AUDIT-001), the executor's `require_tradeable_price` guard, the Rust trade-sim out-of-envelope fallback, the columnar-writer round-trip — so a constructor-level reject would turn every one of those into dead code (proven: the first CI run put positivity in the constructor and broke 19 legitimate downstream tests; the fix relocated it to the read boundary). 1480. **DEC-LAKE-MANIFEST-O1-001 — the lake gains a durable WRITE-TIME dataset manifest (`<lake_root>/.manifest/datasets.jsonl` + `datasets.meta.json`, NEW `brutex/data/lake_manifest.py`), and `db_view.list_candle_datasets` serves discovery MANIFEST-FIRST in O(manifest-rows) — killing the post-restart O(files) `bars/` walk (measured 2026-07-05: 2,355,002 files, `latency_ms: 1784347` ≈ 29.7 MINUTES to the first `/movers` row)** (2026-07-05 on `claude/lake-manifest-o1`; feat(data/dashboard); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY, no lake-SCHEMA/stored-bar/scope/vocab/rate change, Groww constants untouched). THE INCIDENT (operator-hit, live): a dashboard restart loses the in-process generation-keyed discovery memos (`_db_datasets_cache` / `MoversSnapshotCache`), so the FIRST discovery re-walked the whole post-prebuild `bars/` tree (~10⁵-10⁶ per-contract partition dirs, DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 #1145) — the O(files) walk #867/#1025 explicitly named as "true O(page) needs a write-time lake manifest, NOT claimed". THIS ENTRY CLAIMS IT. MECHANISM: (1) WRITE-TIME maintenance — `ParquetWriter.write`'s FRESH branch probes `not any(interval_dir.rglob("*.parquet"))` BEFORE the file lands (the dataset-creation signal; the hot existing-partition merge path costs ZERO manifest work) and, after the partition locks release, calls the best-effort O(1) `record_dataset` (flock via the COMMON `partition_write_lock` on the manifest's own sidecar — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON; ONE fsynced JSONL append + an atomic `datasets.meta.json` rewrite `{version, ledger_token, rows}`; appends only layer onto a walk-built base — a missing manifest is NEVER accreted partially). (2) READ-TIME validation (Golden Rule #1 — never a stale illusion): the manifest serves ONLY when the CURRENT window-ledger `os.stat` token (`"mtime_ns:size"`, the #1149 `lake_revision` approach; every production pull checkpoints the ledger, DEC-CLI-LEDGER-CHECKPOINT-001 #884) equals the stamped token AND the physical line count equals `meta.rows` AND every line parses — ANY failure (absent/stale/corrupt/truncated/torn) falls back GRACEFULLY to the legacy walk (byte-identical results, golden-pinned incl. a #911-style drift-key dir + invalid-coordinate dirs) and an UNFILTERED walk REBUILDS the manifest stamped with the token captured BEFORE the walk began (a mid-walk vendor write stales the rebuild on the very next read — never a silently-partial claim; the rebuild UNIONS keep-first with parseable on-disk rows so a concurrent prebuild writer's record is never dropped). (3) REMOVALS invalidate: the heal's ONE file-removal chokepoint (`lake_heal._quarantine_move` — whole-file quarantine AND the intraday-TF delete-and-rebuild route through it) + `ParquetWriter.heal_partition`'s quarantine-MOVE branch call `invalidate_manifest` (meta-FIRST unlink so any torn removal fails closed). (4) Every writer-side helper is BEST-EFFORT: a manifest failure logs + invalidates and NEVER raises into the pull (the manifest is an accelerator; the `bars/` tree stays the source of truth). CONVERGENCE PROPERTY: the prebuild creates its ~10⁵ derived-TF datasets WITHOUT moving the ledger, and each `record_dataset` re-stamps the CURRENT token, so a post-pull lake converges to served-hot with NO walk; a vendor pull into EXISTING datasets moves the ledger → the FIRST discovery after it pays one walk + rebuild (exactly what that read already paid pre-manifest via the generation bump — no regression). MEASURED (synthetic lake, walk vs manifest-served, best-of-N): 150 datasets × 30 months (4,500 files) 10.6 ms → 0.86 ms (12.4×); 2,000 × 30 (60,000 files) 154 ms → 8.6 ms (18.0×); 5,000 × 12 (60,000 files) 371 ms → 22.7 ms (16.4×) — on warm tmpfs; the production win is the ELIMINATION of the cold-external-SSD per-dir I/O (the measured 29.7 min), not the warm-cache ratio. HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10): manifest-first is **O(manifest-rows) ≈ O(datasets)**, NOT a literal O(1)-total (bench-pinned FLAT in FILE count — 30× the month files, same latency); the FIRST discovery ever (and the first after each vendor pull / heal invalidation) still pays one real walk; a HAND-COPIED partition (the documented #1149 out-of-band bypass) updates neither manifest nor ledger and is invisible until the next walk — the SAME envelope `lake_revision` documents; a crash BETWEEN a dataset's dir-creation and its first durable write can leave an empty interval dir whose later re-pull write sees `dataset_created=False` — the window's re-pull + the next walk-rebuild recover it (narrow, stated, not claimed away). TWO further BOUNDED honesty windows (hostile-review MINORs, folded): (a) COLD-WALK ∩ ACTIVE-PREBUILD under-listing — while NO manifest base exists, `record_dataset` no-ops, so a non-ledger writer (the prebuild) creating a dataset AFTER the rebuilding walk passed its directory is in neither the walk nor the on-disk union; the rebuild is stamped with a still-current token and under-lists it until the next ledger move / heal invalidation — the SAME window the pre-manifest generation-keyed memo had (a walk racing a prebuild missed the same dirs), so no regression, but the prior absolute 'never a stale illusion' wording overclaimed and is softened in the module docstring; (b) FAILED-INVALIDATION ghost row — a heal removing a dataset's LAST file invalidates best-effort, and if BOTH manifest unlinks fail with a real OSError (a `.manifest`-dir permissions fault; a meta-only failure still fails closed — the meta-first order) one GHOST row (an empty page, never wrong data) is served until the next ledger move. LEAF-IMPORT DESIGN (CodeQL cycle break, folded pre-merge): `lake_manifest` deliberately imports NOTHING from the ledger/calendar graph — the window-ledger path is a TEST-PINNED twin (`ledger_file_path`, constants pinned equal to `window_ledger_store.ledger_path` by test, the `lake_revision._SWEEPS_DIRNAME` precedent of DEC-HARDENING-LEFTOVERS-001) because even a function-local `window_ledger_store` import placed the module inside the `window_ledger` → `interior_gap_detect` → `observed_sessions` import cycle CodeQL flagged (`py/cyclic-import` ×3 on PR #1177: the `parquet_writer`/`db_view` → `lake_manifest` edges closed the loop); the manifest's whole transitive import set is stdlib + `atomic_io` + `errors` + `partition_lock` + `observability.progress_beat` (import-order-proven: importing `lake_manifest` alone loads NO `window_ledger*`/dashboard module), so the writer AND the dashboard import it cycle-free; a DI alternative (callers inject the token) was REJECTED because it would force `parquet_writer` → `window_ledger_store`, re-entering the same cluster. The property suite is additionally LEAN-JOB-SAFE: the one db_view-dependent property guards behind a module-level try-import + `skipif` (the heavy `duckdb` import broke the `.[dev]`-only property job's collection), while the three manifest-only properties still RUN there — proven under a duckdb+polars import-block simulation. HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10): single-flight bounds the CONCURRENCY of a cold scan (N pollers → 1 scan), NOT its cost — the one scan is still O(files) (the manifest sibling attacks the cost); the wait is UNBOUNDED by design (pre-fix, every cold poller duplicated the wedged scan and hung anyway — now at most ONE scan is in flight to wedge, and a raised scan hands over deterministically). MECHANISM: (1) SHARD — one self-contained, atomically-replaced 0o600 JSON per dataset (v1: kind/key-echoed-VERBATIM-from-the-on-disk-dir [a #911 drift dir is its own shard] / `identity_key` / `row_count` / dataset+per-file `min_ts`/`max_ts` / per-file `rows`+`mtime_ns`+`size`+`raw_hash` / observability-only `updated_utc`), where `rows` is the per-file DISTINCT-identity-key count — `(timestamp,)` bars, `(side,timestamp)` options, test-PINNED against `lake_invariants.UNIQUE_KEY_*` — NEVER physical rows; `files` sorted by rel (the keep-FIRST QUALIFY order); `.manifest/` is a dot-dir sibling of `bars/`+`options/` holding no `*.parquet`, provably invisible to every lake scanner; the golden-pinned #1480 `datasets.jsonl`/`meta` is byte-untouched. (2) ANTI-ILLUSION LAW (Golden Rule #1) — `load_valid_dataset_stats` serves ONLY after per-request revalidation: parse+version+key-echo+sorted+sum invariant · FILE-SET EQUALITY (an any-depth walk of the dataset dir — a STAGE-3 CORRECTION: the legacy `**/*.parquet` DuckDB glob reads depth-stray files, so a fixed-depth scan could have validated a shard whose counts EXCLUDE a stray the legacy scan counts; a stray-carrying dataset now always falls back, pinned manifest==legacy) · PER-FILE `mtime_ns:size` stat-token equality (token captured by the WRITER post-`os.replace` while the partition flock is STILL held) · MONTH-BOUNDS SANITY (each file's stamped bounds inside its rel-path UTC month — the prefix-sum exactness / anti-G-RACE-1 guard: foreign-month poison self-disables the manifest until lake_heal rewrites); ANY failure ⇒ the byte-identical legacy live scan + ONE `lake.stats_manifest.fallback` naming the clause + best-effort read-side reseed. (3) WRITE HOOKS — five sites, ALL inside the already-held partition locks, each BEST-EFFORT (log + unlink shard + return; never raises into the pull; the caught set is `(OSError, OverflowError, PartitionLockTimeout, ValueError)` — `OverflowError` joined in review round 3 as defence-in-depth for the arbitrary-shard-bytes class; a `LakeWriteHalt` from `.locks/` creation on a genuinely full disk deliberately PROPAGATES) and INCREMENTAL (one row upsert, never a rescan): `ParquetWriter.write` BOTH branches keyed on the NEW explicit `WriteResult.file_rewritten` — bytes RENDERED, never `bars_added` (the Greeks latest-wins `added==0` restate IS recorded; the merge NO-OP touches nothing) · `_heal_partition_locked` rewrite re-stamp (rotated `raw_hash`) + quarantine-MOVE row removal · `OptionParquetWriter._merge_partition` (`added>0`) + option `heal_partition` · `lake_heal._quarantine_move` whole-shard unlink beside `invalidate_manifest`; sinks/consumer delegate — no extra hook; shard writes via the guard-FREE `atomic_write_simple` under the COMMON `partition_write_lock` on the shard path (NEW fail-loud `STATS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S=5.0`, env `BRUTEX_STATS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S`; lock order strictly partition→shard; readers take NO lock; deadline-ordering pinned 5+75 < 90 s `GROWW_WRITE_DEADLINE_S`). LAZY ACCRETION (the anti-storm law): an ABSENT shard costs the writer ONE cheap O(1) probe — a shard-path key digest + one failed `os.stat`, probed FIRST via the public `partition_stats_tracked` so an unviewed dataset's write never even runs the hook's `os.stat(dest)` / the option twin's O(frame) bounds fold (review round 2: the prior "exactly ONE failed os.stat" claim was literally false — it omitted the digest, and the pre-fix hooks statted dest / folded bounds BEFORE probing) — and the shard is NEVER created write-side, so the prebuild's ~10⁵-10⁶ derived-TF partition writes cost one such probe each (no shard-IO/inode storm; bench-pinned zero shards across a write storm) and seeding is READ-side only. 1520. **DEC-MANIFEST-LOG-FLOOD-001 — the manifest recorder's per-dataset `lake_manifest.dataset_recorded` telemetry no longer WIPES the prebuild-completion audit trail: `record_dataset` emits it at DEBUG (same event name + fields), and the surviving INFO record is the aggregate `lake_manifest.record_summary` (dataset count + elapsed + exchange/segment/interval histograms + distinct-symbol count), flushed at most once per `RECORD_SUMMARY_INTERVAL_S` (60 s) of recording activity plus once at each natural manifest boundary (`load_manifest_datasets` / `rebuild_manifest` / `invalidate_manifest`) — recording N datasets now costs a BOUNDED number of INFO lines, never O(datasets)** (2026-07-06 on `claude/manifest-log-flood`; fix(data); logging-level + one aggregate event ONLY — ZERO manifest/on-disk/write-path change, ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change). THE DEFECT (endgame forensics on the operator's real run, adversarially confirmable): DEC-LAKE-MANIFEST-O1-001 (#1480, PR #1177)'s `record_dataset` logged `lake_manifest.dataset_recorded` at INFO once per dataset+interval — during the prebuild it emitted **94,190 lines at ~190 lines/s, consuming ~95% of two 10 MiB rotation files in ~8 minutes**, rotating away the prebuild-completion audit trail (the `gate_released` / `pipeline.prebuild.done` evidence) — the EXACT flood class DEC-PREBUILD-LOG-FLOOD-001 (#1431) fixed for `lake.partition.write` (the demote-per-event + aggregate-INFO pattern named in `timeframe_materialize.py`'s `make_lake_write_tf` comment), re-introduced one PR later by the manifest recorder. FIX (demote + aggregate, mirroring #1431 — the telemetry is DEMOTED, never dropped, Golden Rule #1): (a) the per-dataset success event rides DEBUG with IDENTICAL name + fields (`exchange`/`segment`/`symbol`/`interval` — full per-dataset detail one `--log-level debug` away); (b) NEW module-local aggregation seam in `lake_manifest.py`: a per-lake `_RecordSummaryWindow` (count + first→last monotonic recording span + exchange/segment/interval count HISTOGRAMS + a distinct-symbol set; O(distinct coordinates per window) memory, cleared on every emit) guarded by a tiny module lock, folded by `_note_dataset_recorded` on every successful record (O(1); the log call runs OUTSIDE the lock); the aggregate `lake_manifest.record_summary` INFO (`lake_root`/`datasets_recorded`/`elapsed_s`/`exchanges`/`segments`/`intervals`/`distinct_symbols` — every per-dataset field preserved in aggregate form) is emitted INLINE when a window's recording span reaches NEW public `RECORD_SUMMARY_INTERVAL_S = 60.0` (read at call time, test-patchable) and by NEW public `flush_record_summary(lake_root)` (returns the flushed recording count; 0-and-silent when nothing is pending), which the three natural manifest boundaries call at entry — `load_manifest_datasets` (the FIRST post-prebuild read surfaces the trailing burst), `rebuild_manifest`, `invalidate_manifest`. ARITHMETIC (honest): the measured 94,190 INFO lines over ~8 minutes collapse to `≤ ceil(elapsed/60 s) + boundary-flushes` per lake per process — ≤ ~9 interval aggregates + one boundary flush for that run, a ~10⁴× volume cut on the flood path, bounded by RUN DURATION not dataset count; rotation size/count untouched (the same deliberate stance as #1431 — the log-volume fix is the real one, a bigger buffer only delays the wipe). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): the pending window is per-PROCESS best-effort telemetry state, NEVER part of the on-disk manifest contract — a crash before a flush loses the trailing (≤ 60 s of activity) window's aggregate line (the per-dataset DEBUG lines exist only in a deliberately-verbose session); the manifest's correctness surface (record/load/rebuild/invalidate semantics, freshness tokens, fail-closed validation) is byte-unchanged, regression-pinned by the untouched 41-test base suite. PINNED: NEW `TestRecordLogVolume` (`tests/unit/test_lake_manifest.py`, 6 tests) — the decree pin `test_n_records_emit_bounded_info_and_n_debug` (N=40 recordings → EXACTLY 40 DEBUG `dataset_recorded` lines + ≤ 1 INFO line total, the ONE `record_summary` carrying the full aggregate: count 40, `{"NSE": 40}` exchange / `{"FNO": 40}` segment / 20-20 interval histograms, 20 distinct symbols) + silent-empty-flush + inline interval-elapsed emit (patched interval 0) + all three boundary flushes (load / rebuild / invalidate, each surfacing the pending window exactly once, the second read silent). COVERAGE: `lake_manifest.py` 100.00% line+branch (230 stmts / 40 branches, 0 missing) under its six manifest suites (71 tests: unit + db_view + parquet_writer + lake_heal + property + golden, plus the o1 bench pair); ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict --no-incremental` clean (347 files); `pyright` 0 errors on the touched files. 1432. **DEC-COMBO-DIGEST-REPRO-HASHES-001 — the three Golden-Rule-#4 reproducibility hashes (`data_snapshot_hash` / `indicator_version` / `code_commit_sha`) are now STRUCTURAL, required keyword-only parameters of `combo_digest` (and of the `SweepCache.seen` / `.record` convenience wrappers) — a caller omitting them is a `TypeError` + a type-check failure, never a silent dedup alias; for identical logical inputs the digest is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-change convention, so existing Bloom/LMDB dedup stores and run identities are NOT invalidated** (2026-07-06 on `claude/dreamy-tesla-js5kz6`; fix(engine); ENGINE surface = dedup-key construction only — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track UNCHANGED, no scope/vocab/rate/lake change, zero stored bytes touched). THE AUDIT RISK (confirmed on live main at `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py::combo_digest`): the digest hashed `mask/instrument/tf/direction/canonical_params` but NOT the three reproducibility hashes CLAUDE.md §2 Golden Rule #4's run-identity formula requires — correctness rested on CONVENTION alone (`sweep_supervisor._tuple_cache_params` injected them into `params` before calling). Any caller that forgot would silently ALIAS dedup entries across different data snapshots — a combo evaluated on OLD data would be SKIPPED on NEW data (a stale-skip correctness bug in the Bloom+LMDB membership tier, the exact bug class P0-1 of the §9 hostile review exists to prevent; the cache-skip path has no preload-and-reflush safety net). THE FIX (smallest structural diff — required keyword-only params chosen over a frozen dataclass because every production call site already holds the three values as `grid.data_snapshot_hash` / `.indicator_version` / `.code_commit_sha` flat fields): `combo_digest(mask, instrument, tf, direction, params=None, *, data_snapshot_hash, indicator_version, code_commit_sha)` injects the three INTERNALLY into the canonical params payload under the SAME legacy keys (`code_commit_sha` keeps its grid-field name — it IS Golden Rule #4's `code_commit_hash` leg, documented in the docstring), so the canonical JSON — and therefore the BLAKE3 digest — is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-change convention; a caller-supplied `params` carrying any RESERVED key raises `SweepCacheError` loudly (ONE channel — two channels could silently disagree; `_RESERVED_REPRO_KEYS`); `SweepCache.seen`/`.record` gain the same required kwargs and thread through. CALLERS MIGRATED (every one found by repo-wide grep, tests included): `sweep_supervisor.tuple_cache_key` + its `cache.seen`/`cache.record` sites and `sweep_parallel`'s two sites now pass the grid hashes explicitly; `_tuple_cache_params` no longer carries the three keys (docstring states why; the public `tuple_cache_params` re-export contract updated + pinned); NO caller uses a sentinel — every production path has real hashes, and no display-only caller of `combo_digest` exists (verified by the grep). BYTE-IDENTITY PROOF (the hard constraint): golden hex constants CAPTURED BY RUNNING THE PRE-CHANGE (main) CODE with the hashes inside `canonical_params` — 4 vectors in `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_cache.py` (`_GOLDEN`/`_GOLDEN_EMPTY`/`_GOLDEN_PRODUCTION_SHAPE` — the last a full production-shaped `_tuple_cache_params` payload) + 2 re-frozen in `tests/golden/test_engine_combo_digest_golden.py` + an END-TO-END pin `test_tuple_cache_key_byte_identical_to_pre_structural_convention` (the REAL `tuple_cache_key` over the `_grid()` fixture equals the hex captured from pre-change main via a stash A/B — `a840ae68…baac92`); the structural API reproduces every one exactly, so a resume against an existing dedup store still skips exactly the work it already did. NEW TEETH: omission → `TypeError` pinned at runtime (`cast`-bypassed) for `combo_digest` + `seen` + `record` (the static contract is the required-kwarg signature itself under `mypy --strict`/`pyright`); changed `data_snapshot_hash` / `indicator_version` / `code_commit_sha` each move the digest (unit + a 200-example hypothesis property `test_digest_always_depends_on_each_reproducibility_hash` — the stale-skip kill-switch); reserved-key-in-params raise parametrized over all three keys; the param-key hypothesis strategy is structurally collision-free (max 12-char keys < the 15-char shortest reserved key, documented). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): this closes the FORGOTTEN-caller aliasing class structurally; it does NOT verify the hash VALUES a caller passes (a caller passing a wrong-but-present hash still keys wrongly — Golden Rule #4's value integrity remains the run-identity layer's job); `grid_identity` (the checkpoint key) already carried the three hashes and is UNTOUCHED. COVERAGE: `sweep_cache.py` (130/22) + `sweep_supervisor.py` (189/32) + `sweep_parallel.py` (298/62) ALL 100.00% line+branch under their stem suites (`coverage_gate_discovery --base origin/main`: 3 touched modules at 100%); 1,304 sweep unit tests + 60 integration green; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict --no-incremental` clean on all 10 touched files; `pyright` 0 errors (5 pre-existing private-usage warnings, 0 new). **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_cache.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_supervisor.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_parallel.py`, `tests/golden/test_engine_combo_digest_golden.py`, `tests/property/test_engine_sweep_cache_properties.py`, `tests/bench/test_engine_sweep_cache_o1.py`, `tests/stress/test_engine_sweep_cache_bounded_memory_stress.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-COMBO-DIGEST-REPRO-HASHES-001. 1491. **DEC-THREAD-BUDGET-BOUNDS-001 — the polars global thread pool is pinned ONCE per process at the ONE entrypoint (`brutex.cli` dispatch, right AFTER the byte-exact-stdout-pinned polars-free `version` fast path and BEFORE every subcommand that can import polars) to FULL PHYSICAL WIDTH by default, and every concurrent-reader DuckDB connection is bounded at creation (`SET threads TO <budget>`, `physical_cores // 2`) — the per-connection DuckDB caps ARE the contention fix; budgets derived from the consolidated hardware envelope with fail-safe kill switches (`BRUTEX_POLARS_THREADS` / `BRUTEX_DUCKDB_THREADS`)** (2026-07-06 on `claude/hw-thread-bounds`, the #1490 sibling; perf(config/data/dashboard/cli); parallelism-only — query results + stored bytes BYTE-IDENTICAL; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap change; the Groww fetch pool / per-second ceiling / 500-per-min governor are a REAL vendor limit per CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 and are untouched; `engine/sweep_parallel.py`'s per-worker `OMP/RAYON/POLARS=1` determinism pins + `greeks_enrich._worker_init`'s spawn-worker pins + `data/catalog.py` verified ZERO-diff). **WHY:** polars sizes its process-global pool to ALL logical cores at first import, and DuckDB defaults EVERY connection to all cores — so one dashboard process (the #1401 parallel prebuild + movers + request handlers + the instrument-master/registry/ad-hoc reader connections) stacks several full-width library pools and thrashes. **HONEST PREMISE CORRECTION (Golden Rule #1):** the "N workers each spawn a full-width polars pool" framing is TRUE for DuckDB (per-CONNECTION pools) but FALSE for polars (ONE process-global pool shared by all worker THREADS) — and dividing the polars budget by the prebuild WORKER count would SERIALISE the shared resample pool (the exact hazard the #1401 ledger documents). The DUCKDB per-connection divisor is therefore the number of concurrently-competing library POOLS (`DEFAULT_EXPECTED_LIBRARY_POOLS = 2` — polars' one global pool + the live DuckDB pools), giving `physical_cores // 2` per connection (M4 Pro: 14 → 7). The POLARS default is deliberately DIVISOR 1 = FULL physical width (hostile-review MAJOR, folded): the #1401 parallel prebuild's worker threads SHARE the one global pool and #1401 deliberately ran it at full width — a static `// 2` would have IRREVERSIBLY halved the box in the exact phase the operator cares most about (polars reads the env exactly once per process), while during a prebuild the heavy movers/DuckDB reader load is GATED away (`PrebuildGate`, DEC-PIPELINE-AUTOPREBUILD-001 #1145), so there is no real cross-library contention then; the entrypoint bound still caps polars at PHYSICAL cores (its own default is ALL LOGICAL cpus — an SMT over-report where they differ) and gives the operator ONE lever (`BRUTEX_POLARS_THREADS`, or `expected_workers=` for a genuinely-concurrent multi-pool setup). **MECHANISM (all in the consolidated `brutex/config/hardware_envelope.py` — config leaf, never imports polars/duckdb):** `polars_thread_budget` / `apply_polars_thread_bound` (writes `POLARS_MAX_THREADS`; an operator-preset value is RESPECTED never overwritten; polars ALREADY imported ⇒ the var would be silently ignored, so nothing is written and ONE `hardware.polars_bound.too_late` WARN fires per process — never a pretend-bound; every outcome logs ONCE per process via the shared log-once registry, because the `version` command's byte-exact stdout contract is test-pinned and a test session drives the entrypoint hundreds of times) wired in `brutex.cli._dispatch` after the `version` early-return and before the `status` dispatch (verified: importing `brutex.cli` pulls in neither polars nor duckdb, and BOTH production processes — CLI fetch AND the in-process uvicorn dashboard — enter through `main`→`_dispatch`); 1537. **DEC-PULL-BEAT-PERRUN-001 — progress beats become PER-RUN (pull-id-keyed channels): the ~600 s pull stall watchdog reads ONLY its own run's beat channel, so an unrelated in-process thread's `emit_progress_beat()` can NEVER refresh the current run's heartbeat and mask a real pull stall** (2026-07-06 on `claude/serene-planck-5h1vtg`; observability/dashboard + adapter thread-binding only; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope/vocab/rate change; all 10 production emit sites byte-untouched). **THE ANTI-MASKING GUARANTEE + MECHANISM:** the single process-global `_BEAT` slot of DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001 accepted a beat from ANY thread, so a foreign in-process emitter (a leaked/abandoned worker, a stale superseded run's thread, a future unrelated seam) could keep a genuinely-wedged pull's watchdog "alive" past the 600 s alarm. `brutex/observability/progress_beat.py` is now a KEYED registry — channels keyed by the EXISTING 12-hex `pull_id` (`brutex/observability/correlation.py`, no second run token): a run registers its beat KEYED on its own run id, `emit_progress_beat` routes by the emitting thread's ambient `current_pull_id()` (or an explicit arg), a keyed MISS falls back OUTWARD-ONLY to the `LEGACY_CHANNEL` ("" — the unkeyed back-compat slot, zero-arg semantics byte-preserved) and NEVER into a keyed channel it was not addressed to; an unroutable beat with a non-empty registry is DROPPED + WARNed once per register-epoch (`progress_beat.foreign_beat_dropped`, naming `repr(channel)` + the channel count); an EMPTY registry stays the silent CLI/unit-test no-op. The registered callback is the identity-gated closure `BackgroundPullJob._beat_for(watchdog)` (`if self._watchdog is not watchdog: return`) — even a somehow-leaked channel can only beat its OWN, already-stopped watchdog, never a newer run's. **RUN WIRING:** `BackgroundPullJob.start` gains keyword-only `pull_id` (None AND "" both MINT via `new_pull_id` so a run can never key the legacy channel; explicit id honored), publishes `self._pull_id` under the job lock beside the run-identity watchdog, stamps `watchdog.run_id` post-construction (the on_recovery pattern — the injected `watchdog_factory` signature stays `(on_hung)`), and `_run` opens `pull_id_scope(run_pull_id)` as the OUTERMOST worker-body context — closing the documented pipeline scope gap (metadata/F&O/prebuild/movers/greeks phases now share ONE run id on the worker thread, and the durable journal heartbeat records the run id — the `_maybe_journal_heartbeat` no-bound-`pull_id` skip no longer fires there). NEW `inherited_pull_id_scope` in `correlation.py` (explicit wins incl. explicit "" — the documented binds-empty trap; None + non-empty ambient → INHERIT; None + no ambient → mint, byte-identical standalone) swapped in at BOTH `pull_controller` entrypoints (`pull_all_spot` / `pull_candles`) — LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic: without it the entrypoints shadow-mint a fresh id under the job's run scope, every spot-phase fan-out worker's capture-then-rebind (`run_ingest._run_pair`) carries the minted id ≠ the registered channel key, ALL pace/flock seam beats drop, and under heavy 429 throttling (zero completed windows → zero direct `_on_progress` beats) the run would FALSE-STALL. Consumer/pool thread binding: `FetchPipeline` captures `current_pull_id()` at construction (driver thread, inside the run scope; strictly per-run object) and each consumer thread's `_run_consumer` loop binds it once; `prebuild_parallel.run_work_items` captures the driver's id and re-binds it PER TASK (never per thread — pool threads are reused; `bound_contextvars` restores on exit so no id leaks into a later run's task). **FIXED LATENT RACES:** the blanket-unregister clobber (a stale worker's `unregister` could starve a NEWER run's beat — a keyed unregister now pops ONLY its own channel) and the stale-channel-to-wrong-watchdog route (the `_beat_for` identity gate). **EVENT NAMES BYTE-PRESERVED, `pull_id` additive:** `pull_stall.stalled_suspect` / `pull_stall.stalled_recovered` / `pull_stall.wedged` (pull_jobs) + `pull_stall.watchdog_alive` (pull_stall, via the new `PullWatchdog.run_id`); the stdlib printf CRITICAL/INFO lines, `PULL_WORKER_NAME`, the 600 s default, the timeout/3 cadence and the wedge interlocks are byte-unchanged; `observability/watchdog.py` untouched. **DELIBERATE journal-grouping change:** under a dashboard pipeline the per-phase journal/summary records now group under ONE run `pull_id` (inherited scopes) — `test_pull_jobs.py`'s unbound-beat journal pin re-pinned to the new contract (an in-run beat journals under the RUN id; the unbound skip still covered via the stale-between-runs shape), and `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` pins inherit/explicit-wins/standalone-mint by name. **HONEST ENVELOPES (Golden Rule #10):** Greeks spawn-mode ProcessPool children still cannot beat (unchanged documented envelope — not fixed, not claimed); the CLI `brutex fetch` path has no scope/registrant — beats stay a silent no-op there (no CLI stall coverage claimed); the PRIMARY heartbeats (the direct `_on_progress` / `sync_from_ledger` / `add_bars` beats) are channel-independent — originally shipped UNgated, a residual stale-run masking side-door CLOSED by the same-branch FIX ROUND below; the failure direction of any FUTURE emit site that misses the capture-then-rebind binding is a LOUD false stalled-SUSPECT WARN (single-flight held, nothing killed), NEVER a silently masked true stall — the standing discipline is stated in the module docstring. **FIX ROUND (same branch, adversarial-review fold — 5 confirmed MAJORs + the MINOR/NIT set):** (1) **direct-hook anti-masking gate** — `BackgroundPullJob._beat()` (the funnel behind `_on_progress`/`sync_from_ledger`/`add_bars`) now reads the emitting thread's ambient `current_pull_id()` and, under the job lock, drops a NON-EMPTY id that does not match the CURRENT run's (`pull_job.foreign_beat_dropped`, WARNed once per run) — closing the reviewed zombie path (a `drain`-abandoned fetch-pipeline consumer un-wedging after run A ended and folding its backlog via `app.py`'s `on_bars=_pull_job.add_bars` could beat run B's watchdog; the consumer carries A's re-bound id, so the discriminator exists exactly for the threads that can go stale); an EMPTY ambient id (legacy callers/tests/unrebound hooks) keeps the pre-gate behaviour, and the watchdog is beaten OUTSIDE the job lock (the timer thread's watchdog-lock → job-lock edge forbids the inverse order). The residual stale-`add_bars` PROGRESS-tally pollution (bars count only, never the watchdog) is a named non-goal here. (2) **metadata-phase pool workers rebound (COMMON)** — `orchestrator/parallel.py::PoolRunParallel` now submits every task via `contextvars.copy_context().run(fn, item)` (one fresh copy per task), so EVERY pool user — the metadata `pull_expiries_contracts` fan-out (`_fetch_expiries`/`_fetch_contracts`, whose paced `rate_common.pace`/reauth-wait beats previously resolved to "" and DROPPED on every production pipeline pull, re-opening the DEC-PULL-CONTENTION-ANTISTALL-001 false-stall class + a guaranteed known-benign `foreign_beat_dropped` WARN) and every spine fan-out — inherits the driver's ambient run id automatically; the existing explicit capture-then-rebind sites are now redundant-but-harmless defence in depth, and per-task copies mean no bind can leak across a reused pool thread. (3) **write consumers rebound** — `ShardedWriteConsumer._run_shard` + `BatchingWriteConsumer._run` (the opt-in `BRUTEX_WRITE_BATCH` writer whose partition-flock lock-wait beat is the EXACT GAP-#15 forensic scenario) bind the construction-captured run id (both are built inside the scoped controller body; CLI "" → legacy, byte-identical). (4) **stall-edge id race closed** — `_on_hung`/`_on_recovered`/`_on_wedged` stamp the race-free `watchdog.run_id` instead of reading `self._pull_id` OUTSIDE the identity-gated lock (a stale edge could stamp a NEWER run's id); a singleflight-REFUSED `start()` now rolls back `_pull_id`/`_watchdog` too (no phantom id). (5) **channel-collision honesty** — `register_progress_beat` WARNs loudly on overwriting a DIFFERENT live callback (`progress_beat.channel_collision` — two live runs sharing one id is a caller bug; while both live the older run's beats route to the NEWER registrant, a residual the key-is-the-identity design cannot discriminate, now stated not hidden); `unregister_progress_beat` gains an optional `beat` identity guard (pop only when the channel still holds the caller's closure — a finished run can never starve a duplicate-id survivor; `_run`'s finally passes it). (6) **drop-magnitude observability** — a lock-guarded per-epoch drop counter rides the once-per-epoch WARN (running count) and debug-flushes as `progress_beat.drop_summary` when the epoch closes. (7) **O-honesty + hot-path fast-exit** — `emit_progress_beat` gains an UNLOCKED empty-registry fast path (`pull_id is None and not _BEATS` — the CLI no-op no longer pays the contextvars copy+scan; benign race documented), its "one contextvars read" comment corrected to the real full-context copy + scan, its docstring O(1) scoped to "in registered channels", `reset_progress_beats` relabelled O(registered channels); the delivered-beat path passes the already-known run id into `_maybe_journal_heartbeat(pull_id=...)` (one context scan per beat, never two); the flatness pin's absolute slack tightened 0.05 → 0.005 s so a real O(channels) scan now FAILS the bound (empirically the linear-scan arm passed under the old slack). (8) **journal-shape honesty** — the deliberate one-run-id grouping leaves `record_pull_start`/`record_pull_finish` bracketing ONLY the spot phase, so a pipeline run's journal reads finished-then-heartbeats (post-spot phases keep heartbeating under the SAME id; `JournalRun.records()` orders them after `finished`, non-chronological) and `sleep_gaps` tolerates the one reversed pair — the shape is now PINNED (`test_pull_journal.py`) and stated here; relocating start/finish to the run level is a named follow-up, NOT done. 1492. **DEC-SUSPICION-SWEEP-FIXES-001 — the 19-agent suspicion-sweep fix + hardening pack: (D1, MED) the SPOT pull's AIMD ladder is no longer BLIND to client-absorbed 429s — the FULL controller hook triple (`pace` + `on_rate_limit` + `on_success`) is now bound into the Groww client at the ONE COMMON spine seam every production spot pull flows through, and the spine's own per-window feedback hooks stand DOWN when the client self-reports; (D2, LOW) the F&O spine no longer DOUBLE-COUNTS a propagated exhausted 429 (7 ladder hits per exhausted window → 6); (D3, MED) the `/db` window-ledger route no longer re-PARSES the whole ledger Parquet (~841k rows measured) on EVERY paging click — an mtime-keyed cached row projection, one parse per ledger flush; plus four MED-priority gap closures: (G1) a sweep-launch derived-TF FRESHNESS refusal gate at the sweep_preflight seam, (G2) a future-Muhurat `clamp_window_end` partial-settle enumeration pin, (G3) a no-production-import AST pin on the epoch-anchored legacy `feed.resample_bars`, (G4) the `rate_common` 5→8 production-ceiling docstring reconcile** (2026-07-05 on `claude/suspicion-sweep-fixes`; post-fix → **2**). The F&O/metadata path was always correct (`historical_pull.py:388-389` bakes the triple into the client — the template). **D1 FIX (the COMMON choice, CLAUDE.md §11):** rather than duplicating hook plumbing at two build sites (and breaking ~25 builder-monkeypatching test fakes), the binding lives at the ONE seam BOTH sites already feed — `_with_paced_client` gains `on_rate_limit`/`on_success` params and rebinds via NEW `GrowwClient.with_rate_hooks(*, pace, on_rate_limit, on_success)` + `ClientPool.with_rate_hooks` (re-fanned into EVERY leaf, shared meter preserved; a `None` hook keeps the current binding so pace-only callers are byte-identical); `run_groww_spot_ingest` passes its hook args through, covering the dashboard bulk (`pull_all_spot`), dashboard single (`pull_candles`) and CLI (`cmd_fetch` → `run_groww_spot_ingest_with_retry`) paths — current AND future spot callers — in one place; both build-site docstrings now point at the seam. PEP-695 generic) + `compute_pcr` (both variants via two calls to the one fold) + the typed `RatioStatus` **zero-denominator sentinel ON THE WIRE** (`oi_status`/`vol_status` — a zero call-side denominator is `null` + `"zero_denominator"`, NEVER `Infinity`, raw sums preserved so "puts alive, calls dead" stays visible) + fail-loud law (unknown side / identical sides / `PcrCoverage` wiring mismatch → `ValueError`; 1535. **DEC-MOVERS-ASOF-LATEST-DEFAULT-001 — the `/movers` Spot screen's default as-of TIME now resolves to the SAME latest available minute across EVERY timeframe, so switching 1m ↔ 2m ↔ 3m ↔ 3hour ↔ 1day on a finalized day always shows the IDENTICAL latest close (the Groww/Dhan-consistent behaviour), instead of the per-TF last-bucket-START pin (3min → 15:27 partial-bucket close, 3hour → 15:15) that made a TF switch show DIFFERENT closes** (2026-07-07 on `claude/movers-asof-default-latest-minute`; fix(dashboard); READ-ONLY dashboard — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, NO lake/schema/scope/vocab/rate change). **ROOT (operator-found, verified on origin/main):** at a fixed as-of cutoff `C` the LTP is `round_money(bars[-1].close)` — the close of the last RAW 1-minute bar with `minute_of_day ≤ C` — because `filter_to_ist_minute` cuts the raw 1m frame BEFORE `resample_1m_to_tf` (`movers_snapshot._read_session_bars`), and the resampler takes `close = .last()`; the close is therefore TF-INDEPENDENT at a fixed cutoff (proven: at 09:15 both 2m + 3m read +0.27%/24337.30). The defect was purely the DEFAULT cutoff: the frontend `fillTimes()` rebuilt a per-TF 09:15-step grid and pinned `state.time` to the first grid slot, and a coarse TF's grid never reaches 15:29, so a finalized-day 3m default froze at 15:27 (its last slot) while 1m reached 15:29 → different closes on a TF switch (operator proof: Dixon 1D/5m/3m/2m/1m all C=13237.00 on the broker). **WHY DESIGN 2 (cut-at-`None`, verified):** `_stored_serves_cutoff(minutes, cutoff_min)` opens `if cutoff_min is None: return True` and `_read_session_bars` applies `filter_to_ist_minute` only when `cutoff_min is not None`, so the whole-day path (`time=None` → `cutoff_min=None`) ALREADY (a) keeps the last raw 1m bar = the latest traded minute, identical across every TF by construction (resampler `close=.last()` on a TF-independent cut), and (b) stays on the FAST stored path for every TF with zero parity risk. The correct default already existed in the backend; the fix is essentially frontend — stop pinning a per-TF grid slot, default to blank (`""` → `None` → whole-day → latest). Designs 1 & 3 (resolve a concrete minute and pass it AS the cutoff) were rejected: both route non-divisor TFs (2m/10m) to the slower resample fallback, a self-inflicted perf/parity cost. **DELIVERABLES:** (1) `movers_snapshot.minute_to_hhmm(minute_of_day)` — the pure O(1) inverse of `_cutoff_minute` (`929 → "15:29"`, matches the `session_bar_times` grid string EXACTLY so an injected minute is always a selectable `#time` option; round-trips `_cutoff_minute(minute_to_hhmm(m)) == m`); the readers (`_cutoff_minute`/`filter_to_ist_minute`/`_read_session_bars`/`_stored_serves_cutoff`) are UNCHANGED — the default rides the already-tested `cutoff_min=None` whole-day path. (2) `movers_warm.latest_movers_minute(lake_root, day)` — a data-fact resolver (sibling of `latest_movers_date`): ONE bounded DuckDB `MAX(minute-of-day)` over the spot INDEX+CASH `1minute` partitions day-bounded to the month glob, converted to IST `HH:MM`, guarded EXACTLY like `latest_movers_date` (`apply_duckdb_thread_bound`; `(duckdb.Error, OSError) → None` — it backs the DEFAULT poll so it must NEVER 500; `None` → the frontend shows a plain "latest" label and still cuts whole-day). (3) `app.py` ADDITIVE display echo ONLY (cutoff threading byte-unchanged): a new `_latest_movers_minute_cache` (`MoversSnapshotCache`) memoises the resolver per `(generation, date)`; when `time is None` and the interval is intraday the resolved minute is stamped as a NEW `latest_time` key on the spot/futures/options payloads (`None` for an explicit `time`, a daily interval, or an empty lake) — `time` continues to echo `None` for the default intraday poll (whole-day), which the frontend renders as `latest (HH:MM)`. `echo == cut` holds in VALUE (both are the MAX minute of existing bars), so the DEC-HARDENING-LEFTOVERS-001 minute-honesty semantic is preserved. (4) frontend `movers.html` `fillTimes()` prepends a `Latest` (`value=""`) option, drops the `state.time = sel.value` first-slot pin, and PRESERVES a retained explicit pick across TF switches iff it is still a valid slot for the new TF (else falls back to Latest); the load-success handler replaces the wrong intraday-`(daily)` label with `latest (HH:MM)` from `latest_time` and ADOPTS an explicit echoed `j.time` back into the picker (injecting an off-grid minute as a `document.createElement('option')` so an explicit as-of survives TF switches) — every server string on the `.value`/`.textContent` path, `#time` grid `innerHTML` is code-generated numeric strings + one static literal (XSS-safe, DEC-DASHBOARD-XSS-HARDENING-001). (5) NEW `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-movers-time.js` — the §11-COMMON extraction of the default/persist/adopt logic (`defaultTimeOptions`, `resolveTime`) + a node-executed golden (mirroring `test_dashboard_halfup_format.py`). **INVARIANTS PRESERVED:** as-of minute honesty (explicit picks stay honestly partial — the cut is still on the raw 1m frame before resample); stored↔resample parity (default is `cutoff_min=None` → stored-fast for every TF, byte-equal); money 2dp; cache/warm (`time` unchanged in `candidate_key`; the intraday default now aligns to the already-warmed `time=None` snapshot family — better cache alignment, not a bypass). **THE core regression pin (the test that would have caught the bug):** at the default as-of (`time=None`) `compute_spot_candidates` yields the IDENTICAL `ltp` across `{1minute,2minute,3minute,3hour,1day}` on a finalized-day fixture with distinct closes at 15:27/15:28/15:29; teeth — the OLD per-TF default (`time="15:27"` vs `"09:15"`) produces DIFFERING closes. **GATES:** touched modules 100% line+branch; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` + pyright at baseline. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/{movers_snapshot,movers_warm,app}.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/movers.html`, `brutex/dashboard/static/bx-movers-time.js`, `brutex/dashboard/discovery_warm.py` (the `latest_movers_minute` memo key), tests, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-ASOF-LATEST-DEFAULT-001.
