1529. **DEC-PULL-UI-STALENESS-001 + DEC-PULL-HEADER-SUBUNIT-001 — the pull-watching UI can no longer freeze silently on stale data: BOTH poll surfaces (the site-wide `bx-rate-monitor.js` widget + the `/universe` pull-progress header) gain a CLIENT-clock "updated Xs ago" staleness readout (amber → LOUD RED explicit-"STALE" past justified thresholds) + a self-recovering exponential-backoff poll that NEVER gives up, and the `/universe` header gains per-expiry sub-unit progress derived ENTIRELY client-side** (2026-07-06 on `claude/laughing-dirac-ytxj3k`; fix(dashboard); FRONTEND-ONLY — ZERO Python source change (tests + docs excepted); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, no scope/vocab/rate change). **ROOT (operator incident 2026-07-06 — a browser tab showed 38-minute-old pull data with zero indication; all three causes re-verified in source):** (a) the widget's `poll()` (`bx-rate-monitor.js`) mapped a non-ok response to `null` (render silently skipped) and its `.catch` was a silent no-op ("leave the last render in place"), while `setInterval(poll, POLL_MS)` never adapted — on ANY failure the last DOM values persisted forever with no staleness marker; (b) `universe.html`'s `pollProgress` had NO `r.ok` check — a 500-with-JSON body yielded `s.state === undefined` → fell through to the settled branch → `terminalPullHeader` painted "— nothing to pull" and `finishLive()` killed the watch (ONE transient non-ok detached the page from a live pull); and its catch gave up after 5 quick retries (~3 s budget), painted "live progress feed dropped" and STOPPED polling forever — the 38-minute freeze, recoverable only by manual refresh; (c) a giant unit (a whole index option chain) held `completed/total` still for minutes while `s.current` ticked per processed pair (F&O label `"<contract.symbol> <interval>"`, `option_ingest.py`; the ledger-synced NON-pair_progress (set_current-only) mode moves only `set_current` — `pull_jobs._on_progress`'s `if self._ledger_synced and not self._pair_progress:` branch; the grow-total elif DOES advance `completed`, refuter-confirmed relabel — the client fix is mode-agnostic either way, anchored on ANY completed/total movement) — the header showed NO movement and no per-expiry field exists anywhere in the payload. **MECHANISM (DEC-PULL-UI-STALENESS-001):** both surfaces render "updated Xs ago" from the CLIENT clock — monotonic `performance.now()` primary (`Date.now()` fallback; immune to NTP/wall-clock jumps) PLUS a `Date.now()` wall-clock twin stamped on every success, the reported age = `max(monotonicAge, wallAge)` (round-4 refuter-confirmed suspend guard: on some browser/OS combinations `performance.now()` may NOT advance across a system suspend — implementation variance, stated as such per Golden Rule #1 — so a post-sleep tab could under-report staleness for up to a warn threshold; a wall jump can only OVER-report age, the safe direction for a staleness indicator) — measuring time since the last SUCCESSFUL poll, on a ~1 s ticker — mandatory client-side because the snapshot's `updated_at`/`started_at` are server `time.monotonic()` floats (useless as wall-clock; `pull_progress._monotonic`); the widget's server-side `seconds_since_update` is shown ADDITIONALLY in the expanded overlay ("server: Ns since last tick" / "server: never ticked"), never replacing the client measurement. The WORDING is success-honest (refuter-confirmed fix, round 3): the universe chip claims "updated Xs ago" ONLY after a validated snapshot actually arrived THIS watch (`hadProgressSuccess`, flipped after the shape guard, reset at watch start + settle); before that the watch-start baseline reads "no update yet (Xs)" — mirroring the widget's "no data yet (Xs)" split — so a watch whose progress endpoint fails from the very FIRST poll still escalates amber → red without ever telling the operator fresh data arrived. Thresholds: widget warn 10 s (≈3 missed 3 s polls + 1 s margin — a sub-7 s successful response never flaps amber; a 7–10 s in-flight response CAN graze amber with a TRUE age readout — round-5 refuter reconcile of the earlier blanket "one slow response never flaps amber" claim — whose failure-GATED action tail then reads "awaiting response", never a false "retrying") / red 30 s (10× the poll cadence == the backoff cap, so "retrying" — rendered only when a failure was actually COUNTED, round 5 — reads literally true); universe warn 5 s (past the RETAINED 5×600 ms quick-retry envelope ≈3 s — a literal 3× of the 600 ms cadence would be 1.8 s and flap on GC pauses/tab throttling) / red 15 s (the cadence miss + the first two failed backoff waits 3+6 s — an unambiguous outage on a page the operator actively watches). Failure = fetch rejection ∪ non-ok status ∪ JSON-parse throw ∪ malformed-shape throw ∪ a 10 s `AbortController` bound on a hung fetch on BOTH surfaces (`FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` / `FEED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS`) — the abort timer stays ARMED through the BODY read, cleared only after `r.json()` settles, so a headers-then-stalled-body response aborts too (refuter-confirmed fixes, two rounds: the first cut cleared the WIDGET's timer at headers, leaving the body read unbounded; and the UNIVERSE fetch initially carried NO bound at all while its visibilitychange recovery was gated on `pollTimer` — which is null exactly while a poll is IN FLIGHT — so a stalled-body/half-open-connection universe poll had NO abort, NO scheduled retry and NO tab-return re-poll: a permanent wedge with the chip falsely claiming "retrying". The universe fetch now passes `opts.signal` with the killer cleared only in the `finally`, the one-fetch-site pin in `test_dashboard_universe_stall_chip.py` counts the call PREFIX so the ONE site may carry the options argument, and the visibility re-poll gates on a `watchActive` flag set in `startAndPoll`/cleared in `finishLive` — the `pollGen` token makes a re-poll during an in-flight fetch safe, the hung straggler drops on its gen check); EVERY failure feeds the staleness clock and schedules the next poll on capped exponential backoff (base 3 s doubling to a 30 s max, exponent clamped BEFORE `Math.pow`; universe keeps `POLL_MAX_FEED_RETRIES`/`pollFeedRetries` with GENUINE semantics as the quick-retry budget in FRONT of the backoff, and the pinned "live progress feed dropped" wording survives inside the never-give-up stale chip); ANY success resets the failure count, stamps the client clock, clears the stale marking instantly and resumes the normal cadence — NO terminal give-up state anywhere (the widget loop never stops; the universe loop settles ONLY on a VALIDATED `state ∈ done/error/idle` body, and a non-ok/malformed poll can NEVER paint the terminal header). Re-entrancy tokens (`pollSeq`/`pollGen`, bumped in `finishLive`) make a superseded in-flight response render nothing + schedule nothing; a `visibilitychange` listener re-polls a foregrounded tab immediately instead of waiting out a backoff (the widget invokes `poll()` DIRECTLY — round-6 refuter-confirmed fix: the earlier `schedulePoll(0)` 0 ms TIMER left a few-ms window in which an in-flight poll's failure callback, landing between the visibilitychange task and the timer task, passed its `seq !== pollSeq` guard and REPLACED the instant re-poll with a backoff wait of up to 30 s; `poll()` bumps `pollSeq` synchronously, mirroring the universe twin's direct `pollProgress()` call, pending timer cleared first); widget CSS `.bxrm-stale`/`.bxrm-stale-warn` + root border (the expanded-overlay value rules carry the `.bxrm-grid .gv.bxrm-stale`/`-warn` compound selector, specificity 1-3-0, so they beat the base `#…Overlay .bxrm-grid .gv` colour rule at 1-2-0 — refuter-confirmed fix: the first cut's 1-1-0 overlay rules LOST that contest and were dead CSS, the overlay "updated" value never turned red/amber), universe `.chip.stale`/`.on`/`.red` (`#feedage`), all writes `textContent`/`className`/`classList` — never `innerHTML` in any new code. **MECHANISM (DEC-PULL-HEADER-SUBUNIT-001):** the running header + a new `#subunit` span show `"expiry <DDMmmYY> · sub-unit N this unit"` derived ENTIRELY client-side: `trackSubUnit` counts DISTINCT `s.current` labels observed since `completed/total` last moved (the unit-boundary anchor `completed+'/'+total` — covers frozen-total AND grow-total phases; a restart's decrease resets like an increase; `Set` capped at 4096 then honest transition-counting); `expiryFromCurrent` parses the expiry token RIGHT-ANCHORED off the label's first space-token, mirroring `data/fno_symbol.py`'s `EXCH-UNDERLYING-DDMmmYY[-STRIKE]-TYPE` grammar (`docs/groww/api-reference/03-backtesting.md:33-35`; option ≥5 tokens → `len-3`, future ≥4 → `len-2`, regex-whitelisted `DDMmmYY` — a hyphenated underlying like `BAJAJ-AUTO` never confuses the parse); spot / empty / junk labels ⇒ the chunk is OMITTED (never garbage) and a count < 2 hides the counter (phases that advance `completed` per pair see ≤1 distinct label per anchor — no noise; ≥2 distinct labels under a frozen anchor is precisely the giant-unit signature), so the degraded header is byte-identical to today; the two test-pinned running-header template literals keep their shape with the note string-appended after them (round 6: both now interpolate `${s.current || '…'}` RAW — the `esc()` double-escape fix below — so "preserved verbatim" no longer holds and the open-ended pin is repointed accordingly, the third sanctioned repoint). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the frontend suites (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_progress_frontend.py` +34 — a round-5/6 refuter reconcile: the pre-round-4 "+29" had gone stale against the diff (main 8 → 39 at round 4 = +31, → 41 with the two round-5 regression tests = +33, → 42 with round 6's M&M double-escape regression test = +34) — incl. the regression-named `test_regression_rate_widget_silent_catch_hid_staleness` / `test_regression_universe_poll_gave_up_and_froze_38_minutes` / `test_regression_universe_non_ok_poll_never_settles_the_header` / `test_regression_giant_unit_progress_was_invisible` / `test_regression_universe_hung_fetch_could_wedge_poll_forever` / `test_regression_universe_hung_start_post_shows_stale` and the round-3 `test_regression_rate_widget_eta_row_starved_by_shared_pollseq` / `test_regression_universe_amber_chip_claimed_update_that_never_arrived` / `test_regression_universe_stale_chip_claimed_retrying_during_hung_start_post`; `tests/integration/test_dashboard_pull_rate_monitor.py` +1 on the SERVED bodies) are SUBSTRING asserts pinning the PRESENCE of the new constants/branches/elements/classes in the shipped JS — NOT its execution (this repo has no headless JS runner; 1523. **DEC-STORE-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 — wall-clock deadline + wedge fail-fast + per-underlying deferral for the registry/coverage DuckDB writes** (2026-07-06 on `claude/compassionate-cori-tcye57`; the metadata/historical twin of DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 (MIGRATION.md #999); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change). **ROOT:** the registry (`brutex/data/registry_store.py`, plain `threading.RLock` held across every unbounded `conn.execute`) + coverage (`InstrumentStore.upsert_coverage`, the SHARED dashboard writer RLock via the `_StoreMeta` metaclass) DuckDB writes carried NO wall-clock bound — a WEDGED external-SSD write that never raises would hold the store lock FOREVER, freezing every Phase-2 metadata worker (8 `PoolRunParallel` threads piling up behind one wedged `upsert_contract`), the `run_two_phase` draining thread (`_on_expiry_cell`'s writes), and — on the coverage side — every dashboard route touching a typed store method, with no guard firing (the 600 s pull watchdog only OBSERVES). **FIX (COMMON — reuse, never copy):** (1) the #999 primitive (`DeadlineExceeded` + `run_with_deadline`) MOVED VERBATIM to its ONE COMMON home `brutex/config/deadline.py` (the layer BOTH adapters and data already import — the `hardware_envelope` precedent; the #910 relocation precedent), gaining `what`/`thread_name` labels whose DEFAULTS reproduce the Groww message + thread name byte-for-byte (the `"deadline exceeded"` substring stays load-bearing for `from_groww_exception`); `brutex/adapters/groww/deadline.py` becomes a byte-compatible re-export shim (same class object, zero caller churn); NEW `resolve_env_seconds` is the ONE env-seconds validation shape — `resolve_write_deadline_seconds` + `resolve_partition_lock_timeout_seconds` now DELEGATE to it byte-identically (their existing branch tests pass UNMODIFIED — the proof). (2) NEW transient error `brutex/data/errors.py::StoreWriteDeadlineExceeded(DataLakeError)` — deliberately NOT `LakeWriteHalt` (never a pull-wide stop) and NOT `RegistryError`/`CatalogError` (terminal); carries `deadline_seconds`/`store`/`op`/`latched` (all-positional, `__reduce__` pickle fix — the `:g`-re-format discipline); retryability is a CATCH-SITE contract exactly like #999 (never an `is_retryable()` membership — that predicate is the Groww family). (3) NEW `brutex/data/store_write_deadline.py::StoreWriteDeadlineGuard` — one instance PER STORE; `run(fn, op=, deadline_seconds=None)` executes ONLY raw `conn.execute` closures under `run_with_deadline` while every Python store lock stays CALLER-held (RLock ownership is per-thread, so a breach unwinds + releases the lock on the OWNING thread — never orphaned); env-tunable default `STORE_WRITE_DEADLINE_S=90.0` via `BRUTEX_REGISTRY_WRITE_DEADLINE_S` (fail-safe resolver; 90 s mirrors the audited `GROWW_WRITE_DEADLINE_S`, NOT freshly benchmarked for DuckDB — honest); plus the WEDGE LATCH: after a breach the zombie still holds the DuckDB connection's INTERNAL mutex, so every later guarded write fails fast in O(1) (`latched=True`, no thread, no wait, no guard log — the caller-layer events carry context), token-identity-matched and SELF-CLEARING when the zombie's idempotent keyed write finally completes (one `store.write_recovered` INFO). (4) `RegistryStore` — NEW batch methods `upsert_expiries`/`upsert_contracts`/`mark_candle_statuses` (ONE guarded batch per Phase-1 cell / Phase-2 job / whole completion-stamp loop — O(1) guard cost per BATCH, never per row; module-level SQL constants shared with the byte-identical per-row delegates `upsert_expiry`/`upsert_contract`; `set_candle_status` keeps its same-thread UPDATE+count pair in one guarded batch; `upsert_contracts` validates every leg UPFRONT so an invalid mid-list leg persists NOTHING instead of a prefix — sanctioned error-path micro-difference, either way the job fails + re-pulls idempotently); reads gain a wedge fail-fast (`RegistryError("…write wedged…; read refused…")` — the read-side callers already catch + degrade); `close()` SKIPS the raw `conn.close()` under a zombie (one `store.close_skipped_wedged` WARN, still marks closed — the `with` exit can never freeze); `open()` (the parent-dir `mkdir` — itself a metadata WRITE syscall that blocks on a wedged volume exactly like the #999 fsync (moved inside the closure in fix round 2) — + connect + real DDL + `schema_meta` INSERT on EVERY open, including request-thread read opens) runs WHOLE under `run_with_deadline` so a fresh open on a still-wedged volume fails LOUDLY with the terminal `RegistryError` after one deadline. (5) `InstrumentStore` — `upsert_coverage`'s DELETE+INSERT pair runs as ONE guarded batch (a breach between them leaves the row ABSENT → the cell reads never-pulled → re-attempted: the fail-safe direction, honestly documented — there was never a transaction here); the wedge fail-fast is STORE-WIDE (fix round 2 — one check in the `_synchronized` metaclass wrapper, after the RLock acquire, plus the explicitly-locked `schema_version` property): EVERY typed method touching `self._conn` (`list_coverage`/`get_coverage`/`list_incomplete_coverage`, but equally `get_meta`/`fno_eligible_underlyings`/`upsert_many`/`set_meta` — the per-request dashboard-route calls) refuses with `CatalogError` while the conn is wedged (the NEXT pull's Phase-1 seed read fails a job headline instead of freezing on the conn mutex while holding the shared writer RLock; a route thread can no longer park on the wedged conn holding the RLock and transitively re-freeze the guarded pull lane — pre-fix the next `upsert_coverage` queued on the RLock BEFORE the guard's latch could raise); allowlisted out: `upsert_coverage` (its latch already raises the TRANSIENT defer error) + `close()`, and a CLOSED store still reads "closed" first; `close()` skips BOTH raw closes under a zombie. (6) `metadata_pull` — the PER-UNDERLYING deferral: Phase-1 expiry persistence MOVES INTO the fetcher (`_fetch_expiries` → `upsert_expiries`, the exact Phase-2 shape) so a breach is captured PER CELL by the engine's record-and-resume (`PoolRunParallel`/`run_two_phase`), the cell records `failed` (NEVER settled — the settle-correctness rule: a deferred cell settling would skip it next pull while the registry lacks its expiries) and derives NO Phase-2 jobs (zero vendor calls against unpersisted expiries); Phase-2's `_fetch_contracts` batches the whole leg list (a breach = the job's `contract_failures` defer, rebuilt + re-pulled next run per DEC-PHASE2-REGISTRY-REBUILD-001); the callback-side coverage writes catch-and-count (a Phase-1 rollup defer is a SAFE swallow — the cell's persisted status is already non-settled; the post-Phase-2 `_rewrite_contract_counts` BREAKS on the first defer naming the remaining cells — the rest would only fail fast on the latch; fail-safe: a previously-`complete` cell keeps a stale display count until the next successful pull); everything counted in NEW `MetadataPullReport.store_write_deferrals` (default 0, `to_dict` key) with FIVE loud WARN events (`metadata.expiry_cell.write_deferred` / `metadata.coverage_cell.write_deferred` / `metadata.contract_job.write_deferred` / `metadata.contract_counts.write_deferred` / `store.write_deadline_exceeded`, fields `run_id`/`exchange`/`underlying`/`year|expiry`/`error_type`/`defer_seconds`/`latched` — the ingest.py `write_deferred` convention). (7) `pipeline_pull.metadata_phase_ok` gains `store_write_deferrals == 0` — a wedged-volume metadata phase stops the chain GRACEFULLY after metadata via the existing `stopped_after=PHASE_METADATA` verdict (a stop, never a crash, never a halt). (8) `historical_pull._mark_complete` stamps completions as ONE `mark_candle_statuses` batch; a breach WARNs `historical.mark_complete.write_deferred` + returns an honest 0 and NEVER raises past the seam (the candles already landed durably; unmarked contracts keep `none` and re-mark idempotently next pull — the window LEDGER, not this stamp, drives window re-pull, so no candle data is ever lost). **HEALTHY-PATH BYTE-IDENTITY:** same SQL constants/parameters/statement order/connections/lock serialization (the caller holds the lock for the batch exactly as before; the statements merely run on one short-lived daemon per batch while the caller blocks on `Event.wait`); registry + coverage DuckDB contents bit-identical (batch-vs-per-row A/B pinned); the 90 s deadline vs ms-scale keyed upserts fires only on a genuine hang; zero new log events on success; the ONLY visible deltas are the report's new `store_write_deferrals: 0` key and the Phase-1 write relocating fetch-side (PK-idempotent keyed rows — DB content identical; ORACLE: the pre-existing registry/metadata/pipeline/historical suites pass UNMODIFIED except the report-shape extension). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** the zombie daemon write CANNOT be killed — the guarantee is "no pull driver/worker lane is ever blocked longer than one deadline ONCE the wedge latch is set; every Python store lock is caller-held + deterministically released on breach; the affected underlying's cell/job is deferred, loudly WARNed, counted, and re-attempted next pull; while the volume stays wedged, registry writes/reads/open/close + EVERY non-exempt InstrumentStore typed method fail fast + loud; on recovery the zombie's idempotent keyed write completes harmlessly and the store self-heals" — NOT "the zombie thread is terminated". NAMED RESIDUAL (fix round 2 re-scope): the latch is set only AT the first breach, so a caller whose statement reached the wedged conn BEFORE that breach (latch not yet set) still blocks the lane unboundedly on the conn's internal mutex — it dies with the process, like the zombie; only callers arriving AFTER the breach are protected. NAMED FOLLOW-UPS: `InstrumentStore` typed WRITERS outside the coverage family (`set_meta` — vendor_floor/lake_footprint/instrument_loader writers — `upsert_many`/`prune_to_latest_snapshot`) still carry no deadline of their OWN (they now wedge-fail-fast once a coverage breach latched, but an initial hang inside one of them is unbounded — the deadline covers the coverage write; the `/db` whitebox reads wedge-fail-fast too since fix round 4 — split-read-cursor survival under an ENGINE-level wedge is UNVERIFIED, see that round); `InstrumentStore.open` + `Catalog.upsert` (already under #999's `append_with_deadline` on the ingest spines) stay unwrapped; the composite re-read is gated upstream). **FIX ROUND 2 (same branch — 2 confirmed review MAJORs folded):** (1) MAJOR open-deadline mkdir gap — `RegistryStore.open`'s `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` ran on the CALLER thread BEFORE `run_with_deadline` wrapped `_connect`, while the docstring + this entry claimed the WHOLE open sequence was deadline-bounded; on the exact targeted failure mode (wedged external SSD / hard NFS mount) mkdir is a metadata write syscall that blocks in uninterruptible sleep exactly like the #999 fsync, so a fresh open (and every dashboard read-side open via `load_registry_expiries`/`registry_strikes`, which open per request) froze AT the mkdir with no guard — violating the change's own stated guarantee in its own failure class; FIX: the mkdir is the FIRST line of the `_connect` closure (mkdir + connect + DDL + `schema_meta` stamp all inside the deadline), pinned by a hung-mkdir regression (`test_hung_mkdir_fails_loudly_within_bound`, a gate-blocked `Path.mkdir` monkeypatch that raises after release so no conn leaks) alongside the untouched `test_hung_open_fails_loudly_within_bound`. (2) MAJOR coverage-store guarantee hole — typed methods OUTSIDE the coverage family (`get_meta`/`fno_eligible_underlyings`/`list_index_equity_instruments`/`upsert_many`/`set_meta`) were `_StoreMeta`-wrapped but NOT wedge-checked: a route thread (e.g. `/universe/mapping-integrity` runs `fno_eligible_underlyings` before the wedge-checked `list_coverage`, recomputing exactly when a pull moves the generation) could acquire the shared writer RLock post-breach and block UNBOUNDEDLY on the zombie-held conn mutex, so the pull's next guarded `upsert_coverage` queued on the RLock BEFORE the guard's latch check could run — the guarded pull lane transitively re-froze exactly like the pre-change failure, contradicting the guarantee headline while the ledger's own follow-up ("exposure unchanged from today") missed the transitive re-freeze; FIX: the O(1) wedge fail-fast moved INTO the `_synchronized` wrapper (post-RLock-acquire `self._ensure_not_wedged()` for every public method except the `_WEDGE_EXEMPT` allowlist {`close`, `upsert_coverage`} — close handles the wedge itself, upsert_coverage's latch already raises the TRANSIENT `StoreWriteDeadlineExceeded` the defer sites catch; a CLOSED store skips the check so `_ensure_open`'s "closed" error stays first, pinned by the existing wedged-close test), the explicitly-locked `schema_version` property wedge-checks too, the three now-redundant in-method coverage-read checks removed (ONE check, §11 COMMON), and the guarantee wording in `store_write_deadline.py` + this entry re-scoped to NAME the residual (a reader that reached the wedged conn BEFORE the first breach still blocks unboundedly); regression asserts `get_meta`/`set_meta`/`fno_eligible_underlyings`/`list_index_equity_instruments`/`upsert_many`/`schema_version` all refuse "wedged" while `upsert_coverage` still raises the transient latched error, and heal-recovery re-verifies every family. **FIX ROUND 3 (same branch — 1 confirmed review MAJOR folded):** MAJOR durable-prefix settle hole — `upsert_contracts`' `_write` executed one AUTO-COMMITTING `conn.execute` per leg with NO transaction, so a mid-batch deadline breach (wedge onset at leg k+1) left legs 1..k DURABLY committed by the abandoned zombie; if the process then died before the volume recovered (the realistic operator response to a wedged external SSD), the next pull's `settled_contract_jobs(registry.list_contract_jobs())` saw the surviving `(exch, underlying, expiry)` triple (ANY row settles the job) and `contract_jobs_to_pull` SKIPPED the job whenever `expiry < today` — the remaining legs of that expired expiry were never fetched again, silently (a permanent partial chain), directly falsifying this entry's own "persisted no contracts … re-pulled on the NEXT pull" claim; expired expiries dominate the 2020→today metadata backfill grid, so the hole sat in the MAINLINE scope of the exact failure class (wedged volume + restart) this change exists to handle (empirically reproduced: a 3-leg batch hung on leg 2 → breach → the contracts table durably held exactly 1 leg → the settled set contained the triple → jobs-to-pull for the expired expiry == []). The change already guarded the analogous prefix hazard on the VALIDATION path (upfront leg validation persists NOTHING on an invalid mid-list leg) but not on the breach path — only `upsert_contracts` × the any-row settle inference was fail-UNSAFE (Phase-1 `upsert_expiries` + `mark_candle_statuses` prefixes are fail-safe: a failed cell status / `candle_status='none'` both re-attempt; `upsert_coverage`'s DELETE+INSERT gap is honestly documented fail-safe). FIX: the contract batch is now ATOMIC — `_write` brackets the per-leg INSERTs in ONE explicit `BEGIN TRANSACTION`/`COMMIT` with a `ROLLBACK`-then-re-raise arm for a REAL mid-batch statement error (propagated UNCHANGED — the same nothing-or-all contract as the upfront validation); the wedge latch already serializes the conn, so no other statement can interleave with the open transaction; a zombie that dies with the process commits NOTHING (DuckDB discards the uncommitted transaction — verified cross-connection: uncommitted rows are invisible to a second connection, exactly what a restart sees), making the "persisted no contracts" WARN true and the settled-job inference sound, while a zombie that later completes IN-process commits the FULL batch atomically (the honest recovery case); O(1) per BATCH (`BEGIN`/`COMMIT` bracket the loop, never per row); healthy-path DuckDB contents byte-identical (same INSERTs, same order, same values — the batch-vs-per-row A/B oracle passes unmodified). Fails-before regressions (both verified failing on the pre-fix tree): `test_mid_batch_breach_commits_nothing_and_expired_job_still_pulled` (hang on leg 2 of 3 for an EXPIRED expiry → breach → a SECOND duckdb connection — the durability oracle — reads ZERO contract rows and `contract_jobs_to_pull` still returns the job; after in-process recovery the FULL 3-leg batch is committed and only THEN does the settle inference skip it) + `test_upsert_contracts_mid_batch_statement_error_rolls_back_whole_batch` (a real error at leg 2 → the error propagates unchanged + zero rows persisted) + `test_upsert_contracts_empty_batch_is_a_no_op` (the empty transaction is a durable no-op); the `_GateConn` test proxy gains `hang_on_match` (hang on the Nth matching statement). **FIX ROUND 4 (same branch — 1 confirmed review MAJOR folded):** MAJOR unverified load-bearing envelope claim — the `_ensure_not_wedged` docstring (and this entry's NAMED FOLLOW-UPS) asserted as FACT that "the `/db` whitebox reads survive on the SPLIT read cursor (`_LockedReadConn`), untouched here", and that claim was the stated justification for exempting the `connection` property (a `property` — never metaclass-wrapped, never wedge-checked) from the store-wide wedge fail-fast. The claim is UNVERIFIED and structurally UNVERIFIABLE by this suite: every wedge test hangs a Python-level proxy (`_GateConn` / `_CoverageGateConn`) BEFORE the statement reaches the real DuckDB engine, so no test ever holds a genuine DuckDB engine-level lock while probing the read cursor (the wedged-close test's `read_conn.execute("SELECT 1")` probe ran against an engine that was never actually wedged). The read cursor is `conn.cursor()` on the SAME in-process database instance; a zombie wedged inside a REAL auto-commit `execute` (WAL write / fsync on the wedged volume — the exact targeted failure) plausibly holds engine-level transaction-manager/commit locks that block a NEW read transaction — the pre-existing "empirically verified on 1.5.3" note covers MVCC reads during an OPEN write transaction, NOT a wedged commit. If the claim is false, one blocked `store.connection` read holds the shared `_read_lock` forever, every later dashboard read (completeness / coverage / `/db` / option series — all ride `store.connection`) queues behind it, threadpool workers leak per poll, and the whole dashboard freezes — the exact freeze class this change exists to close, hidden behind an unstamped assertion (Golden Rule #1). FIX (option b — close the hole regardless of DuckDB internals, PLUS restamp the claim): `_LockedReadConn` gains a required `ensure_ready` hook — the store's own bound `_ensure_not_wedged`, threaded by the `connection` property (ONE source of truth, §11 COMMON, never a copy) — invoked at the top of every `execute` AFTER the prior-hold `_release()` (a raise can never leak a held read lock) and BEFORE the `read_lock.acquire()` (a post-breach reader never even queues behind a pre-breach reader possibly blocked inside the engine); a wedged store refuses the `/db` whitebox read in O(1) with the same terminal `CatalogError`, self-healing the moment the zombie completes; the `_ensure_not_wedged` + `connection` docstrings restamp read-cursor survival under an engine-level wedge as UNVERIFIED and name the proxy-recipe limitation. Healthy path byte-identical (one bound-method call + one boolean per `execute` — O(1) per read, same rows, same locking). Regressions (folded into the coverage wedge test): a wedged `s.connection.execute` raises "wedged" in < 0.1 s; the refusal leaks no read-lock hold (a timed `_read_lock.acquire` succeeds post-raise); a view HOLDING the read lock from a prior healthy execute drops it BEFORE the wedge raise (release-then-check order); the post-heal `s.connection` read round-trips. **Decision ID:** DEC-STORE-WRITE-DEADLINE-001. 1521. **DEC-RATE-LOG-OUTSIDE-LOCK-001 — every structlog emission in `RateController` moved OUTSIDE `_lock`: rate.* events are CAPTURED under the lock (level + event + every field VALUE resolved at the original emission program point) and EMITTED strictly AFTER the lock is released via ONE module-level choke point `_flush_rate_logs`, so a wedged/blocking/slow log sink can no longer freeze `pace()` (and the dashboard rate sampler's `snapshot()` read path) for every worker — pacing DECISIONS byte-identical** (2026-07-06 on `claude/eager-hawking-1xd2gm`; fix(adapter/rate); ONE source file touched — `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py` — plus tests + this ledger; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY, NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/pacing-decision change: the AIMD ladder, 429/timeout stepdowns, recovery, governor atomic-reserve (DEC-GROWW-GOVERNOR-ATOMIC-001), smooth-pacing latch, and clock-gap reset all keep their exact statement positions and ordering; CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 rate envelope untouched). **ROOT:** the `rate.429`/`rate.stepdown`/`rate.timeout`/`rate.stepup`/`rate.clock_gap`/`rate.smooth_pacing_latched` emissions ran WHILE HOLDING `RateController._lock`; structlog routes through stdlib handlers (stderr StreamHandler + rotating JSON file handler) — real blocking `write()` I/O behind handler locks — so one wedged sink parked a thread ON the pacing lock and every other worker's `pace()`/`on_*`/`snapshot()`/`current_rps` blocked behind it, stalling the ENTIRE pull's pacing (the class docstring promised the lock is "NEVER held across network I/O or a sleep" but emissions were the unclosed third category). **MECHANISM (COMMON, no new locks/threads/queues, zero shared mutable state):** module-level `_PendingLog = tuple[str, str, dict[str, object]]` + `_flush_rate_logs(*events: _PendingLog | None)` (None slots skipped; plain-string level dispatch so NO structlog machinery is touched under the lock; same-thread emission so contextvars like `pull_id` merge at emit time — an async hand-off thread was deliberately rejected: drop risk + contextvars loss). Per site: `_handle_clock_gap_locked` + `_maybe_latch_smooth_locked` now RETURN their captured event instead of emitting; `pace()` gate 0/gate 1 loops, `_maybe_log_snapshot`, `on_rate_limit` (gap→429→latch→stepdown slots), `on_timeout` (gap→timeout→stepdown), `on_success` (gap→stepup) each wrap their critical section in `try:`/`finally: _flush_rate_logs(...)` with slots pre-initialized to None — positional flush order == the pre-change in-lock emission order, and an in-lock exception still emits whatever was captured before the raise, after release. Fields are captured at the pre-change program point (a stepdown 429 still reads `current_rps=5.0, recent_hits=3` even though the call returns with 4.0 and cleared hits; `gap_s` captured before the `_last_seen` overwrite; the latch's `current_rps` stays the PRE-stepdown rate). O(1): same number + placement of lock acquisitions (critical sections strictly SHORTER); the hot no-event path binds None locals and skips the flush via a None-guard (gate loops) — the stress gate `test_rate_controller_memory_flat` (≥100K events, tracemalloc-net-flat) passes UNMODIFIED. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** (a) the EMITTING thread itself still blocks on a wedged sink AFTER releasing the lock — the guarantee is "no potentially-blocking I/O under `_lock`; all other workers proceed", NOT "logging can never block any thread"; (b) cross-thread interleaving of log lines relative to state transitions is no longer lock-serialized (per-thread order fully preserved; no test pinned cross-thread order — verified); (c) ONE sanctioned behavioral delta: a RAISING sink can no longer abort rate decisions (pre-change a raise from the in-lock `rate.429` emit aborted the latch+stepdown; now decisions commit under the lock and telemetry raises afterward, later slots in the same finally lost after the first raise — decisions-before-telemetry is strictly safer, pinned by test). **TESTS (`tests/unit/test_rate_common.py::TestLogEmissionOutsideLock`, 8 tests):** the REQUIRED blocking-sink regression (a wedged `_LOG` with bounded Events: thread A wedges emitting rate.429, probe thread B completes `pace()`+properties+`snapshot()`+`on_success()` in ms with the 429 decision already committed and `_lock` unheld — FAILS pre-fix by 5 s deadlock-timeout, verified by revert); the scripted-scenario GOLDEN (429-burst 5→4 → pace → timeout storm 4→3 → clean-60 s recovery 3→4 → 400 s clock gap: EXACT sleep list + `_rps` trajectory + ordered (event, fields) list hard-coded — passes on the PRE-change source too, verified by revert = the byte-identity oracle); the all-sites lock-free audit pin (a probe sink asserting `_lock.acquire(blocking=False)` succeeds at EVERY emission across all 6 clock-gap call sites + 429/latch/timeout/stepup/snapshot — the permanent AUTOMATED "no emission under _lock anywhere in this module" gate, fails pre-fix); capture-at-point field pins (kill the lazy re-read-at-flush mutant); the raising-sink decisions-commit pin; the same-call 429→latched→stepdown order pin. ALL 94 pre-existing tests in the file pass UNMODIFIED (incl. the 16-thread governor Barrier, exact-sleep sequences, TestThrottleLogging field values, TestClockGapSleepWake, TestSmoothPacingAutoLatch); `rate_common.py` at 100% line+branch (307/86, 0 missing); property rate-limiter suite + 173 controller-consumer dashboard/adapter tests green; ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` clean. **Files:** `brutex/adapters/rate_common.py`, `tests/unit/test_rate_common.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-RATE-LOG-OUTSIDE-LOCK-001.

1701. **DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 — the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures sweep LAUNCH capstone: a NEW vendor-truth series RESOLVER (`brutex/data/futures_series.py`) + ONE alias-aware sweep-slice LOADER (`brutex/feed/series_load.py`) + the launch wiring through every sweep-family mouth, with the failure-mode law (interior holes refuse loudly naming months; head/tail unowned spans clamp+WARN; calendar observe-only) and `roll_schedule` entering `canonical_trade_params` under a hard instrument⟺schedule invariant** (2026-07-06 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; PR-5 of the ADR-0012 build sequence). **THE RESOLVER (`resolve_futures_series(lake_root, start=, end=)`):** ONE `os.scandir` over `bars/NSE/FNO` keeps `-FUT`-suffixed dirs, parses each with the canonical `parse_fno_symbol` (the #882 scan-and-parse pattern — NEVER `strftime` reconstruction; unparseable `-FUT` names → the `unparsed_dirs` evidence field + one `futures_series.unparsed_dir` WARN each; a hand-made literal `bars/NSE/FNO/NSE-NIFTY-FUT/` poison dir parses to `None` → ignored — the alias never reaches a path-building API), and derives VENDOR-TRUTH ownership windows `(E_{k-1}, E_k]` — the expiry day is owned by the EXPIRING contract, the `resolve_near_month` `>=` law. Duplicate parsed expiries refuse (ambiguous lake). FAILURE-MODE LAW: an INTERIOR hole (consecutive selected expiries > `MAX_MONTHLY_EXPIRY_GAP_DAYS=40` apart) is a LOUD `FuturesSeriesError` naming the missing expiry month(s) by walking the calendar inside the gap (naming abstains to the day-gap number on calendar-coverage errors — the gate itself never depends on calendar coverage), NOT maskable by `--allow-missing-slices`; HEAD/TAIL unowned spans are GRACEFUL — vendor-predecessor → calendar-fallback (previous month's holiday-shifted expiry) → coverage-abstain clamp + `head_clamped`/`tail_unowned_days` evidence + one `futures_series.head_unowned`/`tail_unowned` WARN (spot-mirroring: a partially-backfilled lake loads what exists; operator-flagged default) [RECONCILED by DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001 #1703: the head span now stays UNOWNED (the pre-fix backward ownership extension served the first contract's far-month bars as series bars), the tail WARN fires on ANY positive overhang (the pre-fix >40-day gate silently truncated up to 40 days), the head-clamped calendar cross-check runs at the NATURAL own_start (no more false `expiry_drift`), and a window STARTING inside an interior hole now REFUSES via a first-selected-segment predecessor gap gate (pre-fix the successor silently served the missing month's dates)] [RE-RECONCILED by DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-002 #1704: the coverage-ABSTAIN head fallback is BOUNDED at `expiry − MAX_MONTHLY_EXPIRY_GAP_DAYS`, never the arbitrary window start — the abstain also fires on the 2027+ holiday-table horizon, where adopting the window start silently owned months of missing-predecessor dates with zero WARN; byte-identical at the 2020 floor]. The calendar (`futures_roll.resolve_active_future_expiry`) is an OBSERVE-ONLY cross-check: drift → one `futures_series.expiry_drift` WARN naming BOTH the computed expiry AND the nearest parsed lake expiries + a returned `CalendarCrossCheck(status="drift")` row; the 2027+ coverage horizon abstains (`status="abstain"`) — the UNVERIFIED calendar==vendor equality is never load-bearing (Golden Rule #1) and the Dec-2026 eager-next-month coverage cliff is off the critical path. The registry (`registry.duckdb`) is never read (vendor dir names are the truth — the droppable-cache law #1034). `futures_roll`/`OptionsUnderlying` are imported LAZILY inside the cross-check/naming helpers (importing the module stays trading_core-wheel-light). **THE LOADER (`load_sweep_slice`):** every sweep-family bar mouth previously inlined the same reconcile+`ReplayFeed` block; it is now ONE function (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) — the spot/verbatim-dir path is the moved block byte-identically (optional reconcile + one `ReplayFeed` read; an `on_reconcile` hook seam carries the cascade's L1 heal); the alias path stitches per-contract reads with the EXACT authoritative IST-DATE ownership cut (`bar.timestamp.astimezone(IST).date()` — the SAME conversion `stage1a.push` keys on, so loader cut and engine cursor derive from the ONE `roll_schedule` and can never disagree). The IST-date cut (never a 09:15 clamp) keeps muhurat-evening/special-weekend bars owned by their own date, and the derived FNO `1day` bar (midnight-IST-stamped, living in the UTC month D−1 file) cuts identically. Per-(contract, interval) ZERO-BAR owned window → loud refusal distinct from a missing contract ("stored partition EMPTY over its owned window — re-pull / run the pipeline prebuild"; the `reconcile=False` variant additionally names the reconcile remedy) [RECONCILED by DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001 #1703: the refusal is now SESSION-GATED — a boundary sliver whose in-window owned span holds NO expectable NSE session instant (a day-only `--end` the morning after an expiry, a post-close `--start`, a holiday/weekend run after a roll, a degenerate intersection) SKIPS with one `series_load.boundary_segment_no_session` WARN instead of a false "re-pull" whole-sweep refusal; an out-of-coverage 2027+ date abstains back to the loud refusal]; boundary monotonicity break → loud raise (duplicates across boundaries are structurally impossible under disjoint IST-date ownership; within-contract keep-first dedup stands, DEC-LAKE-READ-UNIQUE-001). **MOUTHS REPOINTED:** `cmd_sweep_all` (resolve ONCE up front; loader per pair with `resolution=` passed down; `FuturesSeriesError` → EXIT_USER_ERROR; the G1 derived-TF freshness gate probes the resolved CONTRACT dirs — probing the alias dir would silently abstain, a gate bypass; the gate stays OI-blind + 1day-abstaining, the pre-existing #1492 envelope); `cmd_sweep` (loader with `reconcile=False` — its no-reconcile law preserved; threads `resolution.roll_schedule` + `apply_1day_mask_for` through `sweep_report` → `rank_sweep_over_bits`/`validate_out_of_sample`); `sweep-verify` (Tier 2 re-derives futures row identities from the tree's OWN audit-recorded schedules — NEW `recorded_roll_schedules_from_audit`; an underivable tuple is an honest `row_identity_underivable` WARN finding, never a crash; Tier-3 `--recount` loads through the SAME loader+resolver and COMPARES the recorded `params["roll_schedule"]` against the re-derived schedule — a mismatch is named on BOTH sides and rides the context-mismatch refusal ladder, so a lake that gained/lost a contract is surfaced with evidence, not a bare hash diff); `cmd_verify_lookahead` (loader, `reconcile=False`); `cascade_wire.load_bars_for_manifest` (loader; keeps its L1 heal via the `on_reconcile` seam + the belt-and-braces `dedup_bars` pass); the options-sim replay (`_replay_spot_signals_for_row` — loader for the bar read; a futures winner row still raises `OptionsUnderlying(...)` `ValueError` BEFORE any read and is caught+skipped by the AUTOMATIC winners hook's per-row net — futures→options translation is PR-6) [RECONCILED by DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001 #1703: the MANUAL `brutex options-sim` path had NO such net (a raw traceback); it now refuses a futures-series run_id up front with the DEC-CLI-USER-ERROR-HYGIENE-001 one-liner naming PR-6]. The dashboard Run Sweep needed NOTHING (`resolve_sweep_request` stays the docstring-pinned PURE function; it delegates to `cmd_sweep_all` and inherits everything). **RUN IDENTITY (Golden Rule #4, operator-flagged default):** `SweepRunConfig` gains `roll_schedule: tuple[int, ...] | None = None` with the `__post_init__` HARD INVARIANT `(instrument == NSE-NIFTY-FUT) ⟺ (roll_schedule is not None)` — both directions, so no instrument can ever mint both a with-key and a without-key identity (the #1062 conditional-params bug class contained); `canonical_trade_params` emits `params["roll_schedule"]` (a JSON-canonical int list) IFF present — `bar_bits` are a function of `(bars, schedule)`, the schedule derives from LAKE state (dir names) which `code_commit_hash` cannot capture, and the recorded key makes each futures run SELF-DESCRIBING for the recount's evidence check; `canonical_spec_params` deliberately does NOT carry it (the spec axis has no futures sweep tree — its params vocabulary stays dormant). Spot run_ids BYTE-IDENTICAL (no schedule ⇒ no key — the unmodified `test_engine_sweep_run_golden.py` literals are the CI proof). THREADING is argument-plumbed, never a grid field (identity-safe like `unsafe_allow_out_of_scope_instruments` — enters NONE of `_tuple_digest`/`_grid_descriptor`/`_tuple_cache_params`): `run_one_tuple`/`run_sweep_grid`/`run_supervised_grid`/`run_parallel_grid` (+ the picklable worker context) gain `roll_schedule_by_instrument`; `SweepTuple.to_run_config(grid, roll_schedule=)`; `ResidentSweepKernel`/`ResidentKernelCache` carry + key the schedule (the kernel roll-schedule mismatch guard mirrors the R-1 fib-anchor guard); `stage3_wire` folds the schedule into its bits memo key + `recover_survivor_cell` + the refined-row identity re-derivation. **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** resolution is O(FNO-dir count) ONCE per launch, NOT O(1) (per-entry cost = one suffix compare + a parse for `-FUT` names; O(C log C) sort over C ≈ 78 contracts); slice loading is O(files overlapping the window) per contract; ONLY per-bar access + the per-bar key cursor are O(1) — no O(1)-total claim. Contract lake depth is the 60-day pull tail — indicator warm-up beyond a contract's stored life cannot be conjured; the per-contract hard reset (#1702) makes that an honest cold-start, never a fabricated level. No trade spans a roll — every boundary is a session-date boundary and `trade_sim` DROPS a pending entry whose fill bar lands on a later session date (**R2-OC-2, `brutex/engine/trade_sim.py` — the source-verified docstring contract**), with the session-aware forced exit (#1019) closing every open position on the EXPIRING contract [STRUCTURALLY ENFORCED by DEC-TRADESIM-OPEN-SESSION-GUARD-001, MIGRATION.md #1743: an open position now closes at the expiring session's last stored bar on any session-date change — the clause no longer depends on the expiry-day tail being complete]. F12: a lake change between two launches HONESTLY re-keys (the full-content bxsnap2 digest covers every stitched bar). **NAMED FOLLOW-UPS (not claimed):** D6 time-of-day × combo expectancy map (PR-5b); D14's DSR effective-N threshold (PR-7 — only `MIN_TRADES=30` guards the futures ranking mouth at launch); consuming the #1013 BarMetadata/FuturesContract seam + D8 stamping in the sweep path; futures→options translation (PR-6); the spot 1day mask audit (#1702); warm-up-from-own-contract-tail refinement; a registry cross-check doctor rule; cascade/stage-4 manifest carriage of a futures winner's schedule (`candidates_for_spec` has the default-None seam; the manifest does not yet carry it) [CLOSED by DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001 #1703 — the automatic cascade threads `roll_schedule_by_instrument`, the manifest carries `roll_schedules`, the manual replay re-uses them, and a schedule-less futures pool SKIPS loudly]. ENGINE UNCHANGED for spot — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX byte-identical (the whole unmodified golden suite green, 393 tests); no vocab/rate/lake-schema change; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY outside the one authorized alias. **Files:** `brutex/data/futures_series.py` (NEW), `brutex/feed/series_load.py` (NEW), `brutex/engine/{sweep_run,sweep_orchestrator,sweep_supervisor,sweep_parallel,sweep_kernel,stage3_wire,sweep_verify,sweep_preflight,sweep_driver,sweep_report,validation,cascade_wire,sweep_scope}.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/universe.py` + `brutex/strategies/spec.py` (#1700), `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` (#1702), docs as named. **Decision ID:** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001. **Builds on** ADR-0012/#1006, #1010–#1012, DEC-NIFTY-ROLL-METADATA-001, DEC-ENGINE-SCOPE-GUARD-001 (#1178), DEC-SWEEP-PREFLIGHT-001, DEC-SUSPICION-SWEEP-FIXES-001 (#1492 G1). (Ledger: #1701 — renumbered from #1569 at the 2026-07-10 fold (main's tail passed #1655; #1645–#1699 wave-reserved; coordinator-assigned band #1700–#1710).)

1702. **DEC-STAGE1A-ROLL-RESET-001 — Stage-1A B2 CLOSED: the roll-aware per-contract `session_key` replaces the constant `_DEFAULT_SESSION_KEY` for the futures track, and a key change triggers a TOTAL hard reset of EVERY stateful builder member (never only the VWAP key), making the stitched build bit-identical to per-segment fresh builders; plus the D12 `apply_1day_mask` builder flag** (2026-07-06 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; closes the `stage1a.py` B2 follow-up comment — "the roll-aware, per-contract session_key (B2 — reset on a futures roll, not only a date change) is a SEPARATE follow-up" — by name). **WHY A TOTAL RESET:** `futures_roll.py`'s locked D11 policy promises "every session/level indicator recomputes per-contract", but a stitched multi-contract stream through ONE builder that reset ONLY the VWAP key would keep pivots (prev-day OHLC), the weekly-Fib `_daily_history`, EMA20/200, `PriorBarHistory`, `DayExtremesState` and `MarketStructureState` continuous across a 20-60-pt basis gap — a swing confirmed on the old contract would manufacture phantom BOS/CHoCH (bits 56-59), precisely D11's "no level-cross condition ever compares prices across a roll boundary". **WHAT SHIPPED:** `Stage1AMatrixBuilder.__init__` gains kw-only, default-preserving `roll_schedule: tuple[int, ...] | None = None` (validated non-empty + strictly increasing non-negative day ordinals) + `apply_1day_mask: bool = False`, and stores `self._prior_n` for the reset re-construction; `build_bar_bits` forwards both as NEW kw-only args appended after the existing signature. In `push`, IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the existing day-rollover block: `roll_schedule is None` ⇒ the constant `_DEFAULT_SESSION_KEY` (spot byte-identical); else an O(1)-amortized MONOTONE CURSOR over the sorted schedule finds the first entry `>=` the bar's IST day ordinal — `session_key = the owning expiry's `toordinal()`` (the exact `resolve_near_month` `>=` law expressed over the vendor schedule; deterministic, stable, 2020+ ordinals ≈ 737,000+ fit the FFI u64 and can never collide with the Rust cold-sentinel key 0); a bar BEYOND the last entry raises `ValueError` (loader/schedule desync — a genuine bug, never a silent constant-key fallback; plain `ValueError` per stage1a's own input-contract convention — `Stage1AInputError` does not exist); a key CHANGE calls NEW `_roll_to_new_contract()` — fresh `trading_core.VwapState()` (recreated even though its own key-change branch would reset it, so "post-roll state == fresh-builder state" is EXACT rather than argued) + fresh `MarketStructureState()` (no FFI `reset()` exists — fresh construction is the only correct mechanism) + `EMAState.new(20/200)` + `PriorBarHistory(prior_n=self._prior_n)` + `DayExtremesState()` + `_current_day/_today_ohlc/_prev_day_ohlc/_anchors = None` + `_daily_history.clear()` — so the EXISTING day-rollover branch seeds a pristine day-1 state and the EXISTING first-day `_NON_ANCHOR_MASK`/`_NON_FIB_MASK` clears fire on the new contract's first day (the honest ADR-0012 §4.5 #6 cold-start semantics, REUSING the machinery). The VWAP feed passes `session_key` into the EXISTING `VwapState.update` ABI slot — the key-change reset branch is ALREADY implemented + byte-frozen in the twin-state golden (`twin_state_golden_vectors.json` contains mid-day key-roll streams); ZERO Rust change, zero new `trading_core` exports (`test_math_facade_golden.py::_EXPECTED_SURFACE` untouched). A boundary can only fall on an IST-day change (ownership is date-granular), so the contract reset composes cleanly with `_roll_to_new_day` (contract check first, then the day roll). **D12 (`apply_1day_mask`, operator-flagged default: MASK not refuse):** futures `1day` partitions carry REAL volume, so the previously unenforced `APPLIES_TO_1DAY_MASK` becomes a LIVE D12 violation (each 1day bar is its own VWAP session firing bits 52/53 against its own HLC3); the flag ANDs the FINAL mask with the vocabulary's own `APPLIES_TO_1DAY_MASK` (clears exactly ToD 44-47 + VWAP 52-53 — the existing `test_applies_to_1day_mask_clears_exactly_tod_and_vwap_bits` bit-set pin is the source of truth, REUSED not re-invented); the launcher derives it from the ONE predicate NEW `stage1a.apply_1day_mask_for(instrument, tf_label)` — a pure function of two run-identity fields, so NO params key (no double-carry). Spot is deliberately NOT flipped (its VWAP bits are structurally 0 at volume=0 but its 1day ToD-bit behaviour is UNAUDITED — masking could silently change spot 1day results; the spot-side unification is a NAMED follow-up). **PROOF RUN (this branch, real wheels):** the roll-segmentation equivalence oracle — `build_bar_bits(stitched, roll_schedule=S) == concat(build_bar_bits(seg) for seg)` bit-for-bit over a 2-contract ~40-pt-basis stream through the REAL resolver+loader; spot identity `build_bar_bits(bars) == build_bar_bits(bars, roll_schedule=None)`; the constant-key invariance `build_bar_bits(seg) == build_bar_bits(seg, roll_schedule=(last_ordinal,))` on a single-contract stream; the cursor-exhaustion raise; the 1day-mask exact bit clear — all verified end-to-end (the permanent property/golden pins land with the test phase of this PR series). SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY PROVEN, not argued: the FULL unmodified golden suite (stage1a literal ints · nifty-day/banknifty-week/sensex-forced-exit shas · sweep-run run-id + store_content_hash literals · twin-state vectors · vocab goldens · math-facade surface) passes with ZERO edits. ENGINE UNCHANGED for spot; no vocab/rate/lake change. **Files:** `brutex/engine/stage1a.py`, consumers per #1701. **Decision ID:** DEC-STAGE1A-ROLL-RESET-001. **Closes** the B2 follow-up of DEC-STAGE1A-WIRE-VWAP-BOS-001 (#1020). (Ledger: #1702 — renumbered from #1570 at the 2026-07-10 fold (main's tail passed #1655; #1645–#1699 wave-reserved; coordinator-assigned band #1700–#1710).)

1703. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001 — the round-1 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (#1700–#1702): the Stage-4 cascade is no longer schedule-blind for futures winners (manifest `roll_schedules` carriage + a loud skip for a schedule-less futures pool), the resolver refuses a window STARTING inside an interior hole, the head span stays UNOWNED (no far-month-bar substitution) with an honest cross-check, ANY tail overhang WARNs, the loader's zero-bar refusal is session-gated (no more false "re-pull" refusals at roll boundaries), plus the file-entry scan guard, repr-named WARNs, the kernel D12-flag guard, the manual options-sim futures refusal, and the recount absent-schedule evidence note** (2026-07-07 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; 23 confirmed findings from the 3-refuter adversarial verification round, every MAJOR fixed with a fails-before/passes-after regression). **(1) Cascade schedule carriage (findings 3/6/11/13/17/21, MAJOR):** `cmd_sweep_all`'s AUTOMATIC Stage-4 cascade rebuilt every futures winner's `bar_bits` via `candidates_for_spec(..., roll_schedule=None)` over the roll-STITCHED alias bars — EMA20/200, prior-history, PDH/PDL/pivot/Fib anchors and BOS/CHoCH crossed every roll basis gap (the exact D11 violation the sweep's #1702 hard resets prevent), so `cascade-report.json` verdicts for futures winners were computed on a DIFFERENT signal series than the sweep's, silently. FIX: `run_and_write_from_specs` gains `roll_schedule_by_instrument` (threaded from the launch's resolved map at the `cli.py` call site), `run_cascade_over_specs` gains `roll_schedules` and passes each pool's OWN schedule into `candidates_for_spec`; the manifest gains the additive `roll_schedules` field (`(instrument, (expiry_ordinal, ...))` pairs; absent key parses `None` — byte-compatible for every spot manifest) and `run_and_write_from_manifest` replays the FROZEN schedules; belt-and-braces: a pool whose instrument is the futures alias with NO schedule available (a pre-carriage manifest) SKIPS with one `cascade_wire.futures_pool_skipped_no_roll_schedule` WARN naming the remedy — honest degradation, never a schedule-blind re-score (Golden Rule #1) [EXTENDED by DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-002 #1704: the MANUAL replay additionally cross-checks the FROZEN schedules against a ONE-shot re-resolution of the CURRENT lake (`check_replay_roll_schedule`) and REFUSES on drift naming both schedules — a drifted lake can no longer silently rewrite the report nor die on a misattributed desync raise]. **(2) Interior-hole start-side gate (findings 1/10, MAJOR):** selection dropped any contract with `expiry < start`, so the pairwise continuity gate never saw a hole the window STARTED inside — the successor's back-month bars silently served the missing month (reproduced: May+Jul lake, June missing, start Jun-2 → one July segment owning Jun-2→Jul-31, no refusal). FIX: the FIRST selected segment is gap-checked against its predecessor in the FULL ordered dir set (a predecessor is excluded only when its expiry precedes the window start, given a later dir was selected) — an over-bound gap raises the SAME month-naming interior-hole refusal via the shared `_interior_hole_error` builder; boundary-pinned at exactly 40 vs 41 days. Deliberately CONSERVATIVE: a window starting in the last-month tail of the post-hole contract also refuses (consistent with the pairwise law — the lake has a hole adjacent to the window start and the remediation is identical; avoiding the false arm would make the observe-only calendar load-bearing). **(3) Loader session-gated EMPTY refusal (findings 2/16/22, MAJOR):** the resolver selects by IST DATE, the loader cuts by DATETIME, so a fresh post-roll segment intersected entirely OUTSIDE market hours (day-only `--end` = midnight UTC = 05:30 IST the day after an expiry; a post-close `--start`; Good-Friday-after-March-expiry) read zero bars and hard-refused the WHOLE sweep with a WRONG "re-pull the contract" remediation. FIX: NEW `series_load._expected_bar_time_in_window` walks the intersection's IST dates against the REAL NSE calendar (`get_session_checked` — muhurat/special-weekend aware; intraday labels live in `[open, close)`, the derived FNO `1day` bar at midnight IST) — a span with NO expectable bar instant SKIPS with one `series_load.boundary_segment_no_session` WARN; a span the calendar says SHOULD hold bars keeps the loud refusal; an out-of-coverage (2027+) date ABSTAINS back to the refusal (never a silent skip the calendar cannot vouch for). **(4) Head law (findings 14/18/19, MINOR):** the head clamp REPLACED segment[0].own_start with the window start — a backward ownership EXTENSION that loaded up to ~30 days of the first contract's pre-front-month (far-month basis) life as "near-month series" bars, and made the post-clamp calendar cross-check emit a FALSE `expiry_drift` on every head-clamped launch. FIX: the head span stays UNOWNED (own_start keeps its natural vendor/calendar value; the span loads NOTHING — true spot-mirroring), the WARN gains `unowned_days`, and the cross-check now evaluates at the segment's REAL first owned date (head-clamped fixture reads `ok`). **(5) Tail law (findings 4/12/20, MINOR):** the tail WARN fired only past `MAX_MONTHLY_EXPIRY_GAP_DAYS` (40), silently truncating up to 40 days (`--end today` over a weeks-stale lake) against the module's own "never silent" claim and the #1700 clamp+WARN law. FIX: ANY `tail_unowned_days > 0` WARNs (an `exceeds_monthly_gap` field carries the escalation); the pinned silent-small-overhang test flipped. **(6) Scan hygiene (findings 7/8, MINOR):** `_scan_future_dirs` gains `entry.is_dir()` (a stray regular FILE named like a contract no longer poisons ownership/roll_schedule then dead-ends the loader — skipped + `futures_series.non_dir_entry` WARN) and the unparsed-dir WARN is `repr()`-named (the #907/#919 hostile-input convention). **(7) Kernel D12 guard (finding 5, NIT):** `ResidentSweepKernel` records `apply_1day_mask` and `run_persisted_sweep` fail-fasts on a mismatch (the D12 twin of the anchor/schedule guards; unreachable via the production cache whose key holds the flag's only inputs). **(8) Manual options-sim (finding 9, MINOR):** `cmd_options_sim` refuses a futures-series run_id up front with the one-liner naming PR-6 (the automatic hook's per-row net never covered the manual path — a raw `ValueError` traceback). **(9) Recount evidence (finding 23, MINOR):** the F16 schedule-evidence loop now prints an explicit informational note when the RECORDED schedule is absent (audit missing/rotated) — "recount identities derive from the CURRENT lake's schedule" — instead of leaving only a bare hash diff (the refusal ladder is unchanged: sha/indicator/snapshot gates still own it). **ACCEPTED (finding 15, NIT):** the #1700 wording "the unmodified golden suite is the proof" is precise for RUN_IDs only — the spot session-key WIRING identity is proven by the dedicated unit spy tests (`test_spot_path_feeds_exactly_the_default_session_key` + `test_constant_key_single_contract_is_output_invariant`), not by the goldens (whose stage1a fixture is volume-0 and whose sweeps never touch bits 52/53); recorded here rather than re-attributed, a volume-bearing spot-shaped golden stays open as a cheap hardening follow-up. **SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY:** every behavior change is futures-alias- or evidence-side-scoped; the spot loader path, spot manifests (absent `roll_schedules` key semantics: the key serialises `null` exactly like the `stage3`/`leaderboard_trials` precedent), and all spot run_ids are untouched — the full unmodified golden suite stays green. **Files:** `brutex/data/futures_series.py`, `brutex/feed/series_load.py`, `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_kernel.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, covering suites `tests/unit/{test_futures_series,test_feed_series_load,test_engine_cascade_wire,test_engine_sweep_kernel,test_engine_sweep_run}.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (#1701 bracketed reconciles), `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001. **Amends** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 (#1701) / DEC-STAGE1A-ROLL-RESET-001 (#1702). 1704. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-002 — the round-2 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (amends #1701/#1703): the MANUAL cascade replay cross-checks the manifest's FROZEN roll_schedules against a ONE-shot re-resolution of the CURRENT lake and REFUSES on drift; the resolver's calendar-coverage head ABSTAIN is bounded (never the window start); a schedule-only lake drift (snapshot-identical) refuses the sweep-all resume UP FRONT; the sibling evaluators gain the roll pass-throughs; plus the round-1 CLI fixes' first executing regression tests and the real-loader bench gate** (2026-07-07 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; 12 confirmed findings from the round-2 3-refuter adversarial verification, every MAJOR fixed with a fails-before/passes-after regression). **(1) Replay schedule cross-check (findings 1/4/9, MAJOR):** `load_bars_for_manifest` re-resolved the futures alias from the CURRENT lake (per `(instrument, tf)` — up to ~21 repeated O(FNO-dirs) scans) while `run_and_write_from_manifest` re-scored under the manifest's FROZEN `roll_schedules`, and NOTHING compared the two — a head-backfilled lake silently rewrote `cascade-report.json` with D11-violating bar_bits (reproduced: Stage-1A keyed every backfilled-contract bar to the frozen FIRST expiry, so no hard reset fired at the real roll), and a tail-grown lake crashed with a misattributed "genuine bug" desync raise. FIX: NEW pure `cascade_wire.check_replay_roll_schedule` refuses loudly naming BOTH schedules + the `brutex sweep-all` remediation; the replay resolves ONCE over the manifest window and passes the VALIDATED resolution into every `load_sweep_slice` (the loader's cut and the frozen resets provably share one schedule); a pre-carriage manifest keeps the #1703 loud pool skip; the #1701 "re-keys the snapshot hash rather than silently re-resolving" docstring claim — which was UNENFORCED on this path — is reconciled to the enforced cross-check. **(2) Head-abstain bound (finding 8, MAJOR):** `_head_own_start`'s abstain fires on the 2027+ holiday-table horizon too (not just the pre-2020 edge), and the abstain adopted the arbitrary WINDOW START — a 2027 lake (reproduced live) silently owned months of dates belonging to MISSING predecessor contracts with `head_clamped=False` and ZERO WARN, serving far-month bars across un-reset roll gaps. FIX: the abstain is bounded at `expiry − MAX_MONTHLY_EXPIRY_GAP_DAYS`; any earlier span stays UNOWNED + WARNs via the standard head law; BYTE-IDENTICAL at the 2020 floor (regression-pinned). **(3) Resume-honesty gate (finding 11, MINOR):** `roll_schedule` enters the run identity but NOT `_tuple_digest`, and the schedule can grow while the snapshot stays byte-identical (a successor contract whose in-window owned span is SESSIONLESS — expiry Thursday + holiday Friday + weekend joins the schedule with zero bars); a same-root re-launch then resumed recorded-schedule rows at the sentinels while Stage-3/cascade recovery re-derived under the fresh schedule → an uncaught `Stage3WireError` blaming a grid mismatch. FIX: NEW 100%-tested `sweep_verify.stale_roll_schedule_refusal` (recorded-vs-fresh compare, refusing ONLY on a proven snapshot-identical mismatch; moved-snapshot / absent / unreadable audits abstain — the grown-lake monthly re-launch and the crash-resume are never blocked) wired at the `cmd_sweep_all` mouth; integration-reproduced end-to-end on the REAL 2026 Good-Friday adjacency. **(4) cmd_cascade user-error net (findings 10/12, MINOR):** the try/except covered only `load_manifest`; it now wraps the bar load + replay for `(CascadeWireError, FuturesSeriesError)` (an interior hole that appeared since launch is a one-line user error); a raw `ValueError` deliberately stays loud — with (1) in place a Stage-1A desync raise is a genuine bug again. **(5) Evaluator pass-throughs (finding 2, MINOR):** `evaluate_combo` / `evaluate_combo_walk_forward` / `walk_forward_sweep` / `combo_returns` / `validate_candidate` gain `roll_schedule`/`apply_1day_mask` (validate_candidate threads BOTH composed builds — OOS + the CPCV producer); the walk-forward run-hash folds them in CONDITIONALLY (the `canonical_trade_params` precedent — spot hashes byte-identical, pinned); regression proves each schedule genuinely reaches the Stage-1A build. **(6) Round-1 test debt (finding 6, MAJOR):** commit da461a99's three CLI fixes lived under pre-existing `# pragma: no cover` with ZERO executing tests and the launch-cascade carriage was exercised but UNASSERTED (dropping the argument silently degraded every futures launch cascade to the pool skip with the whole suite green). NEW pins at the REAL mouths: the launch's `cascade/manifest.json` carries `roll_schedules` == the resolved schedule AND `cascade-report.json` scores >0 futures pools; the manual replay round-trips byte-identically then REFUSES a drifted lake; `cmd_options_sim` on a futures row exits `EXIT_USER_ERROR` naming PR-6; the recount absent-schedule note executes against an audit-rotated tree. **(7) Bench honesty (finding 5, MINOR):** the "stitched-slice per-bar access is O(1)" gate timed a locally built plain list (vacuous for ANY loader regression); it now times the REAL `load_sweep_slice` return over a two-contract Parquet mini-lake + pins the materialised-`list` contract. **(8) Case hint (finding 3, NIT):** `classify_engine_sweep_target`'s lower-case did-you-mean branch now covers the futures alias (`nse-nifty-fut` → "did you mean 'NSE-NIFTY-FUT'?"; hint-never-admit). **(9) Evidence freshness (finding 7, MINOR):** the round-1 whole-package Layer-A run predated the fix commits; a FULL-suite Layer-A coverage run was LAUNCHED at this round's final HEAD [RECONCILED by DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-003 #1705, round-3 finding 6: that relaunch DIED at ~16% with NO verdict (no `LAYERA2_EXIT` sentinel ever appended), so no completed whole-package 100% run exists for that HEAD — the completed local evidence is the pre-fix-tree run (15,972 passed / TOTAL 100.00%) plus the per-module discovery gate (19 touched modules at 100% line+branch, exit 0) at the final HEAD; whole-package 100% AT HEAD is owned by the CI coverage gate on push, per Rule 13(a) — never claimed from an incomplete local run]. SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY: every behavior change is futures-alias-, evidence- or refusal-side-scoped; spot run_ids/manifests/hashes untouched (unmodified goldens green). **Files:** `brutex/data/futures_series.py`, `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py`, `brutex/engine/{sweep_verify,sweep_driver,robustness,candidate}.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/universe.py`, covering suites + `tests/integration/test_sweep_all_futures_launch.py`, `tests/unit/test_cli_options_sim_refusal.py` (NEW), `tests/bench/test_futures_series_o1.py`. **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-002. **Amends** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 (#1701) / DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001 (#1703).
