1705. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-003 — the round-3 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (amends #1701/#1703/#1704): the D11 roll-reset regression net gains the `_daily_history` killers (rolling-weekly/weekly-static roll-equivalence cases + a dedicated mutant-teeth pin); the cascade's presence ⟺ alias roll-schedule invariant is enforced in BOTH directions (manifest parse validation + the shared-core refusal for a spot pool carrying a schedule); the resume gate refuses a sentinel-bearing futures tree whose audit is absent/unreadable AND derives both recorded readings from ONE audit parse; the loader's boundary-sliver gate is TF-BUCKET-GRID-aware (no more false whole-sweep EMPTY refusals on a sub-bucket coarse-TF fragment); the contract scan stops following contract-named SYMLINKs; and the #1704 item-(9) Layer-A evidence claim is reconciled to what actually completed** (2026-07-07 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; 8 confirmed findings from the round-3 3-refuter adversarial verification — no MAJOR this round; every fixed finding carries a fails-before/passes-after regression, proven by stashing each fixed source file). **(1) `_daily_history` mutation blindness (finding 1, MINOR):** the P1 roll-equivalence oracle claimed ANY partial-reset mutant — explicitly including "daily history" — breaks the stitched==fresh equivalence, but `_daily_history` is only POPULATED under a non-PREV_DAY fib anchor (`stage1a.py` gates the record on `_fib_anchor is not FibAnchorKind.PREV_DAY`) and every roll test built with the default PREV_DAY anchor — an omitted `self._daily_history.clear()` in `_roll_to_new_contract` was PROVABLY invisible in-tree (executed: the mutated build stayed byte-identical under every existing stream) while a production ROLLING_WEEKLY futures tuple would have evaluated Group-4 fib levels from PRE-roll daily candles across the roll basis gap with zero test signal. FIX: `tests/property/test_stage1a_roll_equivalence.py` gains two deterministic warm-anchor cases (two 8-trading-day June-2025 segments, post-roll prices INSIDE the pre-roll band; ROLLING_WEEKLY + WEEKLY_STATIC) + a `_DailyHistoryLeakMutant` teeth test proving the SAME stream diverges under the omitted clear (mutant re-verified KILLED: commenting the clear fails exactly the two new cases); the oracle docstring now states the member's anchor-gated population honestly. **(2) Cascade invariant, positive direction (finding 2, MINOR):** `run_cascade_over_specs` guarded only futures-alias-WITHOUT-schedule; a `roll_schedules` entry for a SPOT instrument (the manifest has no integrity digest — a hand-edited/corrupt file was trusted verbatim) was APPLIED silently, rebuilding the spot pool's bar_bits WITH per-contract hard resets (breaking `cmd_cascade`'s byte-identity contract) and, for a short schedule, dying on Stage-1A's raw beyond-schedule ValueError misattributed as a code bug. FIX: `_roll_schedules_from_payload` validates at the parse boundary (instrument must satisfy `is_futures_series_symbol`; schedule shape = non-empty, strictly increasing, non-negative — the `SweepRunConfig.__post_init__` law mirrored) and the shared core raises `CascadeWireError` for a non-alias pool holding a schedule (both caught by cmd_cascade's existing user-error net). **(3) Sentinel-blind resume abstain (finding 8, MINOR):** `stale_roll_schedule_refusal` abstained on an absent/rotated/corrupt audit — the exact sentinel-vs-fresh-schedule crash it exists to prevent recurred with a misattributed Stage-3 message. FIX: NEW `results_root` param (wired at the `cmd_sweep_all` mouth): on an absent/unreadable audit, ONE cheap glob bounded to the scheduled futures instruments' own subtrees (`<root>/<instrument>/<tf>/*.complete.json`) refuses the resume naming the sentinel + the fresh-root remediation; no sentinels (a fresh/spot tree) or no root passed → the prior abstain stands (the best-effort envelope is preserved — the gate still never blocks on a diagnostic failure alone). **(4) Doubled audit parse (finding 4, NIT):** the same gate invoked `recorded_context_from_audit` + `recorded_roll_schedules_from_audit`, each independently `list(read_entries(...))`-ing + re-chain-verifying the whole `audit/sweep-all.jsonl` — a doubled O(entries) once-per-launch cost (the #1492 D3 pattern). FIX: shared `_entries_from_audit` + pure `_context_from_entries`/`_schedules_from_entries`; the gate parses ONCE (spy-pinned: exactly one `read_entries` call); both public readers byte-identical. **(5) Coarse-TF sliver over-claim (finding 7, MINOR):** `_expected_bar_time_in_window` tested bare session OVERLAP — exact for `1minute` labels but an over-approximation for coarse TFs (a `4hour` day carries ONLY the 09:15 + 13:15 labels), so a sub-bucket window fragment (an expiry-day `--start 13:30`, or a sub-minute `--start 15:29:30`) EMPTY-refused the whole sweep with a wrong "re-pull" remediation for COMPLETE data. FIX: the intraday branch finds the FIRST resampler-grid label (`open + k·tf`, DEC-RESAMPLE-ANCHOR-002 — exact timedelta ceil-division, no float) at/after the fragment start and requires it inside both the fragment and `[open, close)`; an unknown (non-lake-TF) interval label ABSTAINS to the loud refusal, as does the 2027+ calendar horizon (unchanged); fail-closed controls pinned (a fragment holding a grid label still refuses a missing partition). **(6) Symlink scan guard (finding 3, NIT):** `_scan_future_dirs` guarded a contract-named stray FILE but `entry.is_dir()` FOLLOWS symlinks — a contract-named symlink at a foreign dir was accepted as an owning segment, serving the TARGET's bars as NIFTY series bars under that expiry's window (defense-in-depth: same local-FS trust boundary as the file case). FIX: `entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)` — a symlink now rides the same skip + `futures_series.non_dir_entry` WARN. **(7) Ledger evidence honesty (finding 6, MINOR):** #1704 item (9) claimed a Layer-A re-run at that round's final HEAD; the relaunch actually DIED at ~16% with no verdict — the sentence is reconciled in place (bracketed, per the stale-text convention) and this round's whole-package claim is likewise owned by CI on push, never a local claim without a completed run. **(8) Findings ACCEPTED as evidence records (finding 5):** the O()-claims verification lens confirmed every launch-capstone complexity claim (per-bar O(1)-amortized roll cursor, honest O(FNO dirs) once-per-launch resolution, real-loader bench) — no defect, recorded as evidence. SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY: every behavior change is futures-alias-, manifest-validation-, evidence- or refusal-side-scoped; spot pools with no schedule entry take byte-identical paths; the unmodified golden suite stays green. **Files:** `brutex/data/futures_series.py`, `brutex/feed/series_load.py`, `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, covering suites `tests/unit/{test_futures_series,test_feed_series_load,test_engine_cascade_wire,test_engine_sweep_verify}.py`, `tests/property/test_stage1a_roll_equivalence.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (#1704 bracketed reconcile). **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-003. **Amends** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 (#1701) / DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001 (#1703) / DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-002 (#1704). (Ledger: #1705 — renumbered from #1573 at the 2026-07-10 fold (main's tail passed #1655; #1645–#1699 wave-reserved; coordinator-assigned band #1700–#1710).)

1706. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-004 — the round-4 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (amends #1701/#1703/#1704/#1705): the resume gate is LAUNCH-GENERATION-SCOPED so a legitimate multi-launch futures root (the sanctioned monthly grown-lake cadence AND the crash-resume it exists to protect) is never again refused as "UNREADABLE/inconsistent"; a readable-but-SWEEP_START-less audit over sentinels now REFUSES; the recount treats an ABSENT recorded roll_schedule as a context MISMATCH (divergence degrades to INCONCLUSIVE, never verdict-grade CORRUPT); `cmd_sweep_verify` parses the audit ONCE; the manifest schedule parse is strictly int-not-bool; hostile operator-typed symbols are repr-quoted at every scope-refusal/log surface; and the shared audit-parse helper's false "chain-verify" claim is reconciled** (2026-07-07 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; 12 findings from the round-4 3-refuter adversarial verification — 3 MAJOR + 5 MINOR fixed, 2 NIT fixed, 2 evidence records accepted; every fixed MAJOR/MINOR carries a fails-before/passes-after regression, proven by stashing each fixed source file). **(1) Multi-launch refusal (findings 1+8+11, MAJOR/MAJOR/MINOR):** `stale_roll_schedule_refusal` derived context+schedules from the WHOLE audit via `_context_from_entries`/`_schedules_from_entries`, which raise on ANY cross-launch inconsistency — yet the gate itself ADMITS a moved-snapshot re-launch into the same root, and `cmd_sweep_all` appends that second launch's SWEEP_START (different `data_snapshot_hash`, grown schedule) to the SAME `resume=True` audit. Every third launch — including a crash-resume of launch 2 with IDENTICAL snapshot AND schedule — then raised into `_futures_sentinel_refusal` and was REFUSED with the misattributed "audit log is UNREADABLE/inconsistent" for a healthy chain-valid audit (reproduced end-to-end with the real `AuditWriter`; the `cmd_sweep_daemon` one-root-per-cycle shape wedged the §11 unattended cadence permanently from cycle 3). FIX: NEW `_matching_snapshot_entries` scopes BOTH derivations to the SWEEP_START entries recorded under the launch's OWN `fresh_snapshot` — the only generation whose sentinel tuple digests can pair with this grid (the digest folds the snapshot; a foreign-snapshot sentinel can never short-circuit) — so a moved snapshot abstains over ANY number of prior generations, a matching-generation crash-resume passes, and a schedule drift WITHIN the matching generation still refuses with both schedules named; whole-file consistency stays `sweep-verify`'s separate diagnosis contract (`recorded_context_from_audit` unchanged). Regressions: two-launch moved-snapshot cycle-3 abstain, crash-resume-of-launch-2 pass, matching-generation drift refusal (all fail pre-fix). **(2) SWEEP_START-less abstain hole (finding 10, MINOR):** a chain-VALID audit with ZERO SWEEP_START entries (copytruncate rotation / truncation-to-empty) yielded `recorded_ctx=None` → blind abstain past the sentinel probe — the round-3 finding-8 crash class recurring through the exists-but-empty shape. FIX: an existing audit recording no SWEEP_START now routes to `_futures_sentinel_refusal` with the honest reason "the audit log records no SWEEP_START context" (no sentinels → abstain as before). **(3) Recount false CORRUPT verdict (finding 9, MAJOR):** with the audit rotated and explicit context overrides supplied, a missing recorded roll_schedule for a recounted futures symbol was only PRINTED as informational — `context_match` stayed True, so a schedule-only lake drift (the gate's own SESSIONLESS-successor class: schedule grows, snapshot byte-identical) made the shadow re-sweep byte-diverge and `compare_recount` condemn a HEALTHY tree verdict-grade CORRUPT, heal plan included — violating the command's own "verdict-grade ONLY under a fully matched recorded context" contract (the schedule IS recorded context: it enters `canonical_trade_params`). FIX: the absent recorded schedule APPENDS a context mismatch (evidence text preserved: names the derived schedule + the absence) → recount REFUSES (or compare-with-caveat INCONCLUSIVE under `--allow-context-mismatch`), `cell_evidence` false, heal plan suppressed — the Tier-3 twin of Tier-2's `row_identity_underivable` WARN; the integration pin now asserts `recount REFUSED` + `EXIT_VERIFY_INCONCLUSIVE` (fails pre-fix). **(4) Doubled audit parse in `cmd_sweep_verify` (finding 5, MINOR):** this branch re-introduced at the verify mouth the exact double whole-audit parse round-3 removed at the launch mouth (`recorded_context_from_audit` + `recorded_roll_schedules_from_audit`, each O(audit-lines) over one-SWEEP_START-per-tuple production audits). FIX: NEW public `recorded_audit_facts` (ONE `_entries_from_audit` pass → both facts; absent → `(None, {})`; spy-pinned exactly one `read_entries` call), `cmd_sweep_verify` refactored onto it. **(5) Hostile-symbol line forging (finding 3, MINOR):** `classify_engine_sweep_target`'s generic + coordinate-mismatch refusal reasons, `ScopeReport.refusal_message`/`override_warning`, and the `sweep.scope_override` structlog events interpolated the operator-typed symbol BARE — an embedded `\n`/ESC forged `[brutex]` stderr lines / injected ANSI, contradicting the branch's own #907/#919 repr-naming convention. FIX: `{symbol!r}` / `repr(verdict.symbol)` at every named surface (dashboard 400-JSON path already safe via textContent); regression pins `repr(hostile) in message` + no raw `\x1b`/newline. **(6) False "chain-verify" claim (finding 4, MINOR):** `_entries_from_audit`'s docstring + the gate comment claimed "read + chain-verify" while `read_entries`' own contract is explicitly WITHOUT chain verification — a Golden-Rule #1/#10 false claim in a code contract. FIX: both claims reconciled to the honest parse-only envelope (chain integrity owned by `verify_chain` under Tier-1 `sweep-verify`); behavior unchanged by design — the gate is a best-effort drift detector, never the integrity authority. **(7) Manifest ordinal coercion (finding 2, NIT):** `_roll_schedules_from_payload` documented itself as THE hand-edited-manifest validation boundary yet `int(ordinal)` silently accepted `true`→1, truncated `739000.9`, and parsed int-strings. FIX: strict int-not-bool `_strict_ordinal` (the `_schedules_from_entries` mirror), 3-way parametrized refusal regression. **(8) Bench sensitivity over-claim (finding 6, NIT):** the roll-schedule O(1) bench docstring claimed "a cursor that rescans the schedule per bar … blows the ratio", but a ~14-entry big-tier schedule makes that exact regression a ~1.05× shift — UNDER both ceilings. FIX: docstring reconciled to the honest envelope (the gate owns HISTORY-scaling regressions; the cursor's O(1) amortisation is owned by code review + the unit reset suite). **ACCEPTED as evidence records:** finding 7 (Layer-A status: the one completed whole-package run is GREEN but pre-fix; at-HEAD 100% is owned by the CI coverage gate on push — unchanged stance) and finding 12 (identity/reproducibility chain verified defect-free). SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY: every change is futures-alias-, refusal-, evidence- or message-side; spot run paths unchanged; goldens green. **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_scope.py`, `brutex/universe.py`, covering suites `tests/unit/{test_engine_sweep_verify,test_engine_cascade_wire,test_engine_sweep_scope,test_universe,test_dashboard_sweep_runner,test_dashboard_sweep_run_route}.py`, `tests/integration/{test_sweep_all_futures_launch,test_cli_sweep_scope,test_cli_sweep_scope_guard}.py`, `tests/bench/test_engine_stage1a_o1.py` (docstring). **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-004. **Amends** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 (#1701) / DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001..003 (#1703–#1705). (Ledger: #1706 — renumbered from #1574 at the 2026-07-10 fold (main's tail passed #1655; #1645–#1699 wave-reserved; coordinator-assigned band #1700–#1710).)
1707. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-005 — the round-5 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (amends #1701/#1703–#1706): `sweep-verify` is USABLE on the sanctioned multi-generation daemon root (facts scope to ONE generation — the `--data-snapshot-hash` one when given, else the LATEST recorded — with an honest note naming the other generations, never a pre-flag usage refusal); the resume gate closes the mid-file-lossy-audit hole with a DIGEST-AWARE fresh-sentinel probe (zero false positives — a foreign-generation sentinel still resumes); the futures series resolver REFUSES a same-month duplicate expiry dir (vendor-impossible for strictly-monthly NIFTY futures — previously an observe-only WARN that abstained entirely on 2027+ windows); and the audit schedule reader enforces the SAME shape law as its manifest twin** (2026-07-07 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; 12 findings from the round-5 3-refuter adversarial verification — 3 MINOR fixed, 1 NIT fixed, 1 NIT accepted with reason, 7 evidence records accepted; every fix carries a fails-before/passes-after regression, proven by stashing the fixed sources: 14 new unit tests + the 2 fix-integration tests FAIL at the pre-fix tree). **(1) Doctor locked out of the daemon root (finding 6, MINOR):** the sweep daemon reuses ONE results root across cycles, so its audit accretes a NEW context + a GROWN futures `roll_schedule` every moved-snapshot cycle — and `cmd_sweep_verify` derived facts from the WHOLE audit BEFORE the explicit context flags were even read (`recorded_audit_facts` at cli.py rode `_context_from_entries`/`_schedules_from_entries`, which raise on ANY cross-generation disagreement), so from the second cycle onward EVERY tier — including the Tier-3 recount, the only metric-corruption oracle — exited EXIT_USER_ERROR ('inconsistent recorded context') on the flagship production tree, and the flags could not rescue it. FIX: `recorded_audit_facts(audit_path, *, snapshot=None)` scopes BOTH facts to ONE generation via the NEW shared `_sweep_start_snapshots` pass (explicit snapshot wins; default = the LAST SWEEP_START's generation — the audit is append-only, so the last entry belongs to the newest launch) and returns the OTHER generations' snapshots for `cmd_sweep_verify`'s honest warn-grade note (repr-quoted, capped 5 + count; the note names `--data-snapshot-hash` as the way to scope another generation); an explicit UNRECORDED snapshot honestly returns no facts (the flags-only path); WITHIN-generation inconsistency still raises (one launch records ONE context — a disagreement there is real corruption); the single-fact readers (`recorded_context_from_audit` — `results_report`'s consumer — and `recorded_roll_schedules_from_audit`) are UNCHANGED. Regressions: daemon-audit latest-generation scoping, explicit-snapshot scoping, unrecorded-snapshot no-facts, within-generation raise, SWEEP_START-less empties (unit) + the end-to-end two-cycle daemon root now verifying with the note (integration, EXIT_USER_ERROR pre-fix). **(2) Mid-file-lossy audit resume hole (finding 11, MINOR):** after round-4's scoping, a lossy audit that RETAINED a matching-generation SPOT SWEEP_START while LOSING the futures ones took `matching` non-empty, then `recorded.get(instrument)` returned None and the per-instrument loop fell through to the abstain — even though the tree held sentinels minted under THIS generation, whose rows' schedule is exactly as unverifiable as with the audit absent (round-3's refusal rationale verbatim; proven by execution in the round-5 review). The naive generation-BLIND glob refusal would false-refuse the legitimate crash-resume of a spot-only-completed launch over foreign-generation futures sentinels — so the FIX is digest-aware: `stale_roll_schedule_refusal` gains `fresh_sentinel_paths` (per-instrument EXPECTED sentinel paths of THIS launch), and `cmd_sweep_all` derives them from the fresh grid (`iter_sweep_tuples` → `tuple_store_path` → `completion_sentinel_path`; the tuple digest folds the fresh `data_snapshot_hash`, so ONLY a sentinel at one of these exact paths can short-circuit this grid's tuples; O(grid) path derivations once per futures launch, existence probed lazily on the missing-recorded-schedule arm only). A fresh-digest sentinel with NO matching-generation recorded schedule now REFUSES naming the sentinel + the remediation; a foreign-generation sentinel abstains (zero false positives). Regressions: unit refusal/abstain matrix (mapping absent/empty/not-on-disk/recorded-present) + TWO integration pins at the real CLI mouth — the lossy-audit refusal (EXIT_OK pre-fix) and the foreign-generation-sentinel resume (EXIT_OK both sides — the pin against the naive over-refusing fix). **(3) Same-month poison contract dir (finding 10, MINOR):** two dirs with DIFFERENT parsed expiries in the SAME calendar month — vendor-impossible for strictly-monthly NIFTY futures, hence always lake corruption — passed both the duplicate-expiry gate (identical expiry only) and the continuity gates (gap > 40 days only), silently minting a bogus mid-month `roll_schedule` entry (an extra Stage-1A D11 hard reset + a re-keyed run identity) with only the OBSERVE-only `expiry_drift` WARN, which abstains entirely on a 2027+ calendar-horizon window. FIX: the pairwise continuity loop refuses two SELECTED segments sharing `(expiry.year, expiry.month)` — 'ambiguous lake … NIFTY futures are strictly monthly … quarantine the foreign dir'; structurally vendor-impossible, so it can never false-refuse a legitimate lake (a same-month dir OUTSIDE the selection cannot poison the schedule — ownership clamps to the window and the schedule folds SELECTED expiries only). CONSEQUENCE: the resume-gate integration fixture's `02Apr26/30Apr26` pair — a vendor-IMPOSSIBLE same-month duplicate this gate now refuses (the repo calendar's real expiries are `2026-03-30` and `2026-04-28`) — is repointed to the calendar-real holiday adjacency (expiry Mon `2026-03-30`, Tue `2026-03-31` a trading holiday — the SAME sessionless-overhang shape, now drift-WARN-free). Regressions: the poison refusal naming both dirs + the month, and the calendar-abstaining (2027) variant (both fail pre-fix). **(4) Audit schedule reader shape law (finding 1, NIT):** `_schedules_from_entries` validated only int-not-bool while its manifest twin `_roll_schedules_from_payload` additionally enforces non-empty + strictly-increasing + non-negative — a hand-edited type-valid-but-shape-invalid line (e.g. `[739200, 739100]`) passed the audit reader and degraded downstream (loudly, but inconsistently across the two boundaries). FIX: the SAME shape law at the audit parse boundary, seq-numbered refusal; 4 new parametrized regressions (empty / descending / duplicate / negative — all pass the reader pre-fix). **ACCEPTED (finding 2, NIT — fail-closed by design):** the resume gate refuses on a context-key-less SWEEP_START even in a FOREIGN generation whose sentinels are provably unpairable; skipping malformed entries whose snapshot "parses and differs" would partially TRUST a malformed line's own claim about its generation — the strictly-broader fail-closed refusal is kept (reachable only via tampering/version drift; degradation loud + remediation-naming, never wrong results). **ACCEPTED as evidence records (no defect):** findings 3 (lake-dir parsing injection/traversal-safe), 4 (no scope-law bypass --symbols→bars), 5 (no REFERENCE_ONLY leakage / log forging / secrets), 7 (O-complexity honesty holds at head), 8 (Layer-A run green but pre-fix — at-HEAD 100% owned by the CI coverage gate on push, the #1706 stance re-affirmed), 9 (coverage-honesty sweep: no gaming), 12 (identity/reproducibility mainline defect-free). SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY: every change is futures-alias-, doctor-, refusal- or evidence-side; spot paths unchanged (unmodified spot goldens green). **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/data/futures_series.py`, covering suites `tests/unit/{test_engine_sweep_verify,test_futures_series}.py`, `tests/integration/test_sweep_all_futures_launch.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-005. **Amends** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 (#1701) / DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001..004 (#1703–#1706). (Ledger: #1707 — renumbered from #1575 at the 2026-07-10 fold (main's tail passed #1655; #1645–#1699 wave-reserved; coordinator-assigned band #1700–#1710).)
1708. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-006 — the round-6 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (amends #1701/#1703–#1707): the loader's 1day boundary-sliver gate is SESSION-CLOSE-aware, so a bare-date `--end` the morning after an expiry no longer false-EMPTY-refuses the ENTIRE multi-interval futures launch with an impossible remediation; and the resume gate's digest-aware fresh-sentinel probe also guards the ZERO-matching-entries arm (an audit that lost its whole fresh-generation tail)** (2026-07-07 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; 4 confirmed findings from the round-6 3-refuter adversarial verification — 1 MAJOR fixed, 1 MINOR fixed, 1 NIT fixed, 1 NIT accepted as an evidence record; both behavior fixes carry fails-before/passes-after regressions, proven by stashing each fixed source file). **(1) Futures 1day live-edge false whole-launch refusal (finding 3, MAJOR):** `_expected_bar_time_in_window` (`brutex/feed/series_load.py`) treated the midnight-IST derived-1day stamp inside ANY window as an expectable instant — but the 1day bar SUMMARISES its whole session and is written by the POST-session pipeline prebuild, so on the successor contract's FIRST owned day (the day after expiry) a bare-date `--end` puts that day into a pre-open sliver `[00:00 → 05:30 IST]` where the bar STRUCTURALLY cannot exist yet; the loud `'1day' is EMPTY … re-pull / run the pipeline prebuild` refusal fired with a remediation impossible until ~15:30 IST + prebuild, and because `cmd_sweep_all` preloads every slice under one refusal net, the single 1day slice aborted the WHOLE futures launch — recurring every morning after every monthly expiry, on exactly the D12 futures-1day surface this PR launches (the intraday variant of the identical scenario was fixed in round 1; this was its unfixed 1day residual). FIX: the 1day stamp counts as expectable only when the window ALSO reaches that day's session CLOSE (`seg_end >= close` — `stamp < close`, so the stamp-in-window check is subsumed): a pre-close fragment now SKIPS with the ONE `series_load.boundary_segment_no_session` WARN like every other boundary sliver, while a window covering the close (any completed past session — including `seg_end ==` the close exactly, boundary-pinned) keeps the loud genuine-prebuild-gap refusal. WINDOW-relative and deterministic — never a wall-clock read; muhurat/special-session closes ride the same `get_session_checked` session the gate already consults. Regressions (`tests/unit/test_feed_series_load.py`): the live-edge morning-after-expiry skip (names the successor contract + interval; FAILS pre-fix) + the close-minus-one-minute skip (FAILS pre-fix) + the close-covering and exactly-at-close refusal pins (unchanged behavior, both sides green). **(2) Resume-gate probe bypass on a fully-lost fresh generation (finding 4, MINOR):** `stale_roll_schedule_refusal` returned `None` on `if not matching:` BEFORE consulting `fresh_sentinel_paths` — the round-5 finding-11 digest-aware probe ran only on the per-instrument recorded-schedule-`None` arm INSIDE a non-empty matching generation. An audit that lost ALL fresh-generation `SWEEP_START`s at a line boundary (or a pre-launch backup restore — exactly what the gate's own remediation text invites) while keeping an OLDER generation's entries therefore abstained, and a schedule-only lake drift resumed at this launch's own fresh-digest sentinels with rows minted under the LOST recorded schedule — the misattributed grid-mismatch crash class this thrice-hardened gate exists to refuse (executably reproduced pre-fix). FIX: the zero-matching-entries arm now probes THIS launch's expected sentinel paths through the NEW shared `_existing_fresh_sentinel` helper (the recorded-`None` arm refactored onto it byte-equivalently): a fresh-digest sentinel's `SWEEP_START` is always appended BEFORE its tuple runs, so its existence with ZERO matching-generation entries is PROOF of audit loss — refuse naming the sentinel + the tail-lossy/restored diagnosis + the fresh-root remediation; a legitimate moved snapshot / crash-resume leaves no sentinel at those exact paths (foreign-generation digests re-address), so the abstain is preserved with zero false positives (`cmd_sweep_all` already threads `fresh_sentinel_paths` — no mouth change). Regressions (`tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_verify.py`): the generation-lost refusal (FAILS pre-fix — returned `None`) + the moved-snapshot abstain matrix on the new arm (empty mapping / empty path list / expected-path-not-on-disk — all still resume). **(3) Pragma rationale names its futures exercisers (finding 2, NIT):** `load_bars_for_manifest`'s function-level `# pragma: no cover` predates the launch, and this PR added the launch-critical futures replay wiring (the once-per-replay `resolve_futures_series` + `check_replay_roll_schedule` cross-check + the per-slice `resolution=` threading) INSIDE that exclusion — genuinely executed with negative assertions by `tests/integration/test_sweep_all_futures_launch.py`'s three cascade tests, but the docstring's no-cover rationale still cited only the pure-core/heal suites, so a future edit could regress with no named guard. FIX: the rationale now names the three futures-branch exercisers explicitly (docstring-only; the alternative pure-prologue hoist is a possible future refactor, deliberately not done in a review-fix round). **(4) ACCEPTED as an evidence record (finding 1, NIT):** the whole-package Layer-A coverage run is FINISHED and GREEN (verbatim `TOTAL 38729 0 9384 0 100.00%` · `15972 passed, 30 skipped`), measured on a pre-round-4 tree; the finding itself independently re-measured every touched module at 100% line+branch at HEAD — no defect, recorded as evidence (at-HEAD 100% remains owned by the CI coverage gate on push, the #1706/#1707 stance re-affirmed). SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY: both fixes are futures-alias-/refusal-side only — the spot/verbatim loader path and every spot gate path are untouched (unmodified spot goldens green). **Files:** `brutex/feed/series_load.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py`, `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py` (docstring), covering suites `tests/unit/{test_feed_series_load,test_engine_sweep_verify}.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-006. **Amends** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 (#1701) / DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001..005 (#1703–#1707). (Ledger: #1708 — renumbered from #1576 at the 2026-07-10 fold (main's tail passed #1655; #1645–#1699 wave-reserved; coordinator-assigned band #1700–#1710).)
1709. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-007 — the round-7 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (amends #1701/#1703–#1708): the resume gate's "context precedes the sentinel" premise is made TRUE on the PARALLEL driver (the production default) by ONE fsynced pre-dispatch `SWEEP_LAUNCH` context line per futures instrument, so a parent crash inside the launch window is never again condemned as a tampered/lossy audit; `sweep-verify` generations are keyed by the FULL context TRIPLE (a same-snapshot code-upgrade re-launch no longer locks every tier); the same-month poison-dir gate runs over the WHOLE scanned dir set (the selection-evasion holes closed); the manifest schedule parse refuses duplicate-instrument entries; the alias loader refuses a foreign launch coordinate up front; and a case-drifted NIFTY dir is WARNed as scan evidence** (2026-07-08 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; 8 findings from the round-7 3-refuter adversarial verification — 2 MAJOR fixed, 3 MINOR fixed, 2 NIT fixed, 1 NIT accepted as an evidence record; every fixed finding carries a fails-before/passes-after regression, proven by stashing each fixed source file: 12 new unit tests + the 1 fix-integration test FAIL at the pre-fix tree). **(1) Crashed PARALLEL launch condemned as audit loss (finding 1, MAJOR):** the round-6 fresh-sentinel probe's core premise — "a fresh-digest sentinel's SWEEP_START is always appended BEFORE its tuple runs, so its existence with ZERO matching-generation entries is proof of audit loss" — is INVERTED on the parallel driver (`run_parallel_grid`, the auto-default at workers>1): the EVAL worker itself durably writes the per-tuple store + completion sentinel (`_run_tuple_in_worker` → `run_persisted_sweep`), while the tuple's SWEEP_START reaches the durable `audit/sweep-all.jsonl` only when the parent's strictly in-order apply cursor replays the buffered records (`_apply_ready_prefix`). A fresh futures launch whose parent crashed (OOM/power-loss) after any out-of-order tuple completed left fresh-digest sentinels with ZERO fresh-generation audit entries — and every re-launch into the same root then refused deterministically and PERMANENTLY (the gate runs before the AuditWriter opens, so the audit could never gain the fresh SWEEP_START), misdiagnosing the sanctioned crash-resume as "a tail-lossy/restored audit" with a work-discarding fresh-root remediation; the round-6 "zero false positives" claim had been verified only on the fsync-per-append SEQUENTIAL driver. FIX (the finding's own recommendation): `cmd_sweep_all` appends ONE fsynced `SWEEP_LAUNCH` line per futures instrument (NEW `sweep_verify.SWEEP_LAUNCH_ACTION`) to the ingest chain AFTER the resume gate passes and BEFORE grid dispatch, carrying the SAME context triple + `params.roll_schedule` shape a SWEEP_START records; every generation-scoped audit reader (`_context_from_entries` / `_schedules_from_entries` / the NEW shared `_launch_context_pairs`, which `_matching_snapshot_entries` and `recorded_audit_facts` now ride) accepts BOTH actions (`_CONTEXT_ACTIONS`) — so any crash after dispatch leaves the fresh generation's schedule durably recorded and the re-launch compares recorded == fresh instead of refusing, while the launch line is a RECORDED schedule, not a bypass (a post-crash schedule-only lake drift still refuses with both schedules named). Spot launches append NOTHING — their audit stays byte-identical. Regressions: the crashed-parallel unit pair (launch-line resume + launch-line drift refusal; both FAIL pre-fix), the SWEEP_LAUNCH facts-reader unit, and the end-to-end integration `test_crashed_parallel_launch_prefix_audit_still_resumes` (a REAL launch's audit truncated to the strict pre-dispatch prefix — exactly the durable crash state — re-launches EXIT_OK, and the SWEEP_LAUNCH-before-any-SWEEP_START ordering is pinned; FAILS pre-fix). **(2) Same-snapshot code-upgrade lockout (finding 7, MAJOR):** `recorded_audit_facts` scoped its "generation" by `data_snapshot_hash` ALONE — but one SNAPSHOT does not imply one LAUNCH: a code-upgrade re-launch into the same root (any git commit lands while the lake does not move; the launch resume gate ACCEPTS it, silently ignoring the sweep_id-mismatched checkpoint) records a SECOND `code_commit_sha` under the SAME snapshot, and `sweep-verify` then raised 'inconsistent recorded context' from `_context_from_entries` and exited EXIT_USER_ERROR BEFORE the explicit `--data-snapshot-hash`/`--indicator-version`/`--code-commit-sha` flags were consulted — a healthy, launch-path-sanctioned root condemned with NO override, every tier (incl. the Tier-3 recount, the only metric-corruption oracle) locked out; the prior pin `test_within_generation_inconsistency_still_raises` had encoded exactly the inverted premise. FIX: generations are keyed by the FULL context triple; the target = the LAST entry matching every EXPLICIT flag given (all three flags threaded from `cmd_sweep_verify`; the audit is append-only, so the last candidate is the newest matching launch); other generations stay the honest warn-grade note (a same-snapshot other generation is counted — its snapshot string may equal the scoped one); a per-instrument schedule disagreement WITHIN one triple still raises (the launch gate refuses schedule-only drift up front, so no sanctioned cadence produces that shape — the replaced pin now asserts THIS raise). Regressions: code-upgrade scoping to the last triple + others-named, `--code-commit-sha` narrowing within a shared snapshot, `--indicator-version` narrowing/no-facts, within-triple schedule raise (all but the raise FAIL pre-fix). **(3) Same-month poison gate selection evasion (findings 2+6, MINOR):** the round-5 same-month refusal compared PAIRWISE-SELECTED segments only — a window ending BEFORE the legitimate same-month contract's ownership begins (finding 2: Jun/15Jul-poison/Jul/Aug dirs, window Jul-10→14 selects ONLY the poison) or falling WHOLLY inside the poison's stolen span (finding 6: May/10Jun-poison/Jun, window Jun-2→9 — a single selected segment, `pairwise` empty) resolved WITHOUT refusal, serving the planted dir's bars as series bars under a bogus roll_schedule with only the OBSERVE-only `expiry_drift` WARN (fully silent on a calendar-abstaining 2027+ window) — contradicting the round-5 comment "a same-month dir OUTSIDE the selection cannot poison the schedule". FIX: the (year, month) duplicate check runs ONCE over adjacent pairs of the FULL `ordered` dir set right after the duplicate-expiry pass (two same-month expiries are always adjacent in expiry order, so one pairwise pass subsumes the selected-pairs check); by the gate's own strictly-monthly argument a whole-lake check can never false-refuse a legitimate lake — and it deliberately refuses even when today's window would not touch the poisoned month (a later window silently would; the quarantine is forced now). Regressions: both executed repros + the outside-the-window whole-lake refusal (all three FAIL pre-fix). **(4) Manifest duplicate-instrument last-wins (finding 8, MINOR):** `_roll_schedules_from_payload` validated each entry's alias + shape but never UNIQUENESS — `[["NSE-NIFTY-FUT",[…,738030]],["NSE-NIFTY-FUT",[…,738031]]]` parsed cleanly and BOTH `dict(manifest.roll_schedules)` consumers (`run_and_write_from_manifest` + `load_bars_for_manifest`) silently adopted the LAST entry, while the audit twin `_schedules_from_entries` refuses the same per-instrument disagreement. FIX: duplicate-instrument refusal at the parse boundary the docstring claims owns the enforcement (regression FAILS pre-fix). **(5) Alias under foreign coordinates mis-remediates (finding 3, NIT):** via the loud CLI-only `--allow-out-of-scope` research override, the alias under e.g. NSE/INDEX resolved against the pinned `bars/NSE/FNO` tree while `load_sweep_slice` read every contract under the FOREIGN coordinates verbatim → zero bars → the misleading "EMPTY … re-pull the contract / run the pipeline prebuild" refusal (the real problem is the COORDINATE, not the data). FIX: `futures_series.SERIES_EXCHANGE`/`SERIES_SEGMENT` promoted PUBLIC and the loader refuses up front when `(exchange, segment) != (NSE, FNO)`, naming both the pinned and the wrong coordinate + the re-launch remediation, before any resolution or lake I/O (regression pins the message carries no EMPTY/re-pull; FAILS pre-fix). **(6) Case-drifted dir silently excluded (finding 4, NIT):** a `-FUT` name that PARSES but misses the series only by letter case (`NSE-nifty-30Sep25-FUT`) fell in neither scan bucket — dropped with zero WARN, unlike the repr-WARNed unparsed dirs (if it held a month's only copy the interior-hole gate still refused, but its remediation never named the drifted dir sitting right there). FIX: a parsed dir whose case-FOLDED triple matches the series but whose exact-case triple does not now emits ONE repr-named `futures_series.case_drift_dir` WARN (the #911 key-drift diagnostic convention); genuinely foreign dirs (BANKNIFTY / BSE-embedded) stay silent (regression pair: drift WARNed + foreign silent; the WARN test FAILS pre-fix). **(7) ACCEPTED as an evidence record (finding 5, NIT):** the whole-package Layer-A green run remains pre-round-4-tree evidence (its refresh attempt died mid-run); compensating per-module measurement at HEAD is green and at-HEAD 100% stays owned by the CI coverage gate on push — the #1706/#1707/#1708 stance re-affirmed, no defect. SPOT BYTE-IDENTITY: every change is futures-alias-, audit-, doctor-, refusal- or evidence-side; a spot launch appends no SWEEP_LAUNCH line and takes byte-identical paths (unmodified spot goldens green). **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `brutex/data/futures_series.py`, `brutex/feed/series_load.py`, `brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py`, covering suites `tests/unit/{test_engine_sweep_verify,test_futures_series,test_feed_series_load,test_engine_cascade_wire}.py`, `tests/integration/test_sweep_all_futures_launch.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-007. **Amends** DEC-NIFTY-FUTURES-SWEEP-LAUNCH-001 (#1701) / DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-001..006 (#1703–#1708). (Ledger: #1709 — renumbered from #1577 at the 2026-07-10 fold (main's tail passed #1655; #1645–#1699 wave-reserved; coordinator-assigned band #1700–#1710).)
1710. **DEC-FUTURES-LAUNCH-REVIEW-FIXES-008 — the round-8 hostile-review fix pack for the ADR-0012 futures launch (amends #1701/#1703–#1709): the sweep-verify/resume-gate VERDICT-grade audit reads are hash-chain-VERIFIED before parse, a launch GENERATION is the FULL context triple, the presence ⟺ alias roll-schedule law is enforced at the audit parse boundary, the futures dir scan admits ONLY canonical strftime-round-trip names, the 1day loader distinguishes deep history from the true live edge, and the structurally trade-less 1day grid is loudly LABELLED at launch** (2026-07-08 on `claude/magical-cray-g6agaw`; ENGINE SCOPE UNCHANGED — 3 spot indices + NSE/FNO/NSE-NIFTY-FUT; no scope/vocab/rate/lake-schema change; spot goldens untouched). **(f12, chain-verified verdict reads):** every recorded fact that gates a verdict-grade outcome — the Tier-2 context, the F16 recorded roll schedules, the Tier-3 `context_match` gate, and the launch resume gate's recorded-vs-fresh schedule comparison — was parsed from an integrity-UNVERIFIED file while the docstrings pointed at a `verify_chain` call nobody made (ONE well-formed hand-edited line could steer those verdicts); NEW `sweep_verify._verified_entries_from_audit` runs the streaming O(1)-memory `verify_chain` BEFORE the parse (tampered/truncated/rotated chain → `SweepVerifyError`; the resume gate lands it in the sentinel-gated unreadable arm), and `recorded_audit_facts` + `stale_roll_schedule_refusal` both ride it; the DISPLAY-surface `recorded_context_from_audit` (the /results report header) deliberately stays parse-only — an O(entries) SHA-256 sweep per dashboard poll would violate the read-side latency law, which is exactly why its facts never gate a verdict (honest envelope rewritten). **(f10, full-triple generation):** the resume gate's launch-generation scoping (round-4 findings 1/8/11) matched on `data_snapshot_hash` ALONE — a sessionless schedule drift under a byte-identical snapshot then a sanctioned code-upgrade (or indicator-bump) re-launch picked up the PRIOR commit's entries and permanently refused, though the stated hazard was impossible (the C1 sentinels re-address under C2 tuple digests and can never pair); `stale_roll_schedule_refusal` gains `fresh_indicator_version`/`fresh_code_commit_sha` and `_matching_generation_entries` compares the FULL `(data_snapshot_hash, indicator_version, code_commit_sha)` triple — mirroring `recorded_audit_facts`'s round-7 keying — so the code-upgrade re-launch abstains by design (parametrized fails-before regressions). **(f11, presence ⟺ alias at the parse boundary):** a well-formed hand-edited audit line stamping a `roll_schedule` on a SPOT instrument was ACCEPTED by `_schedules_from_entries` and only detonated downstream in `_verify_store_rows`, where the SweepRunConfig invariant's ValueError demoted the store to the warn-grade `row_identity_underivable` EARLY-RETURN — skipping the row_run_id/label/top_k corruption checks entirely, so ONE forged line laundered a genuinely corrupt spot store into a CLEAN Tier-2 verdict; the parse boundary now refuses a non-alias instrument carrying a schedule exactly like its manifest twin `_roll_schedules_from_payload`. **(f3+f5, canonical-name scan admit):** `strptime`'s `%b` is case-insensitive and `%d` accepts an unpadded day, so `NSE-NIFTY-30sep25-FUT`/`…-3Sep25-…` PARSED into the load-bearing admit set though the vendor writer never mints those names — `_scan_future_dirs` now admits ONLY a dir whose expiry token strftime-round-trips byte-exact, WARNs the drift as `case_drift_dir` evidence, and still feeds a drifted twin into the duplicate-expiry refusal (two dirs claiming one contract stays the loud ambiguous-lake refusal; a non-colliding drift stays WARN-only); the suffix prefilter goes case-INSENSITIVE so a case-only `…-fut` dir — previously silently invisible to BOTH evidence channels, the exact silent-exclusion class the round-7 WARN claims to close — is surfaced (never admitted: lake keys are case-exact). **(f8, 1day deep-history vs live edge):** the round-6 boundary rule skipped ANY 1day fragment ending before its session close — including a DEEP-HISTORY fragment whose midnight stamp the read window serves, so a genuinely missing historical 1day bar silently skipped and shifted `data_snapshot_hash` vs a healthy lake; `series_load._expected_bar_time_in_window` gains the `_now_utc` wall-clock seam (never part of run identity — it only decides skip-vs-refuse for EMPTY reads) and refuses when the close has already passed (`close <= now` — the prebuild owes the bar), while only the TRUE live edge (close still in the future — the morning-after-expiry pre-open sliver) keeps the round-6 skip. **(f9, hoisted coordinate pin):** the round-7 foreign-coordinate refusal lived only inside `load_sweep_slice`, AFTER `resolve_futures_series` — under `--allow-out-of-scope` with a foreign `--exchange/--segment` on a box with NO pinned tree the resolver won the race and named the WRONG problem ("no NSE/FNO lake tree — run the pipeline pull"); 1522. **DEC-PULL-RATE-BRIDGE-NONBLOCK-CACHE-001 — the `GET /api/v1/pull/rate` CLI-bridge file read is moved OFF the uvicorn event loop behind a TTL + content-token memo with a deadline-guarded, NON-BLOCKING single-flight refresh, threadpool-offloaded; two ADDITIVE honest-freshness payload keys (`bridge_source` / `bridge_probe_age_s`)** (2026-07-06 on `claude/vibrant-knuth-itozu6`; fix(dashboard); READ-side dashboard only — ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change; the pull's pacing + the bridge WRITE side are byte-untouched). **WHY:** the route (an `async def`) called `brutex.data.rate_bridge.read_rate_snapshot` — a synchronous `Path.read_bytes()` of `<lake_root>/.rate/pull_rate.json` — INSIDE its body on EVERY poll (the site-wide widget polls every ~3 s from every dashboard page; `v29` adds its own 5 s poller), i.e. ON the event loop. The lake is an external volume (CLAUDE.md §8): a merely-SLOW disk serialized its per-read latency in front of every request, and a WEDGED read syscall (a stalled external SSD / NFS mount that never raises — the #999 hang mode, read-side) froze the WHOLE dashboard indefinitely; the docstring's "never touches the lake" claim was false for the bridge half (now rewritten honestly). Design selected by a 3-designer + 3-judge panel (unanimous winner), grafting the deadline-bounded owner + once-per-outage loudness + the late-binding reader seam onto the content-token memo. **MECHANISM (composing EXISTING primitives — §11 COMMON, no copy):** (1) `brutex/dashboard/lake_revision.py` — the shared `_stat_token` core gains `include_ino: bool = False` (default False keeps every pre-existing ledger/sweeps token byte-unchanged — regression-pinned) + NEW public `rate_bridge_revision(lake_root)` = one `os.stat` of the COMMON `rate_bridge_path` folded to `mtime_ns:size:st_ino` (the inode because the publisher is an atomic tmp→fsync→`os.replace` — every publish swaps the inode, so an equal-size coarse-mtime rewrite still moves the token; missing file → the stable `ABSENT_TOKEN`; other OSError → WARN + `None` "no signal", inherited verbatim; docstring HONESTY NOTE: the token is live-vs-cached provenance + skip-decode, NOT wedge protection — `os.stat` wedges exactly like `read_bytes`, hence the probe runs INSIDE the guard). (2) NEW `brutex/dashboard/rate_bridge_cache.py` — `RateBridgeCache` (every dep injected: clock/probe/reader/guard; `reader=None` LATE-BINDS `brutex.data.rate_bridge.read_rate_snapshot` via module attribute at call time so the existing monkeypatch seam keeps working, test-pinned): `get(lake_root)` has three arms — [a] TTL HIT (`RATE_BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL_S=2.0 s`, env `BRUTEX_RATE_BRIDGE_TTL_S`, fail-loud parse, `0` = always revalidate; pinned `< pull_rate_view.STALE_AFTER_S=12`) → the zero-syscall O(1) memo, source `cached`; [b] IN-FLIGHT → return last-known IMMEDIATELY, source `unverified` (never a timeout-less wait — the load-bearing difference from `MoversSnapshotCache`'s Event wait / `SummaryCache`'s on-caller probe, which is why those were not reused for THIS read); [c] OWNER → the whole stat+decide+read refresh runs under the repo's ONE freeze guard `run_with_deadline` (`RATE_BRIDGE_READ_DEADLINE_S=0.5 s`, env `BRUTEX_RATE_BRIDGE_READ_DEADLINE_S`) — an unchanged non-None token REVALIDATES without re-reading; changed/first/`None` ("if uncertain, fetch") re-reads; a `None` token is stored as `None` (unknown never trusted — the next post-TTL owner re-reads); a raising INJECTED probe/reader (production ones never raise by contract) → one `rate_bridge_cache.refresh_failed` WARN, memo kept, `_probed_at` still advanced (TTL-cadence retry, never per-poll). `_inflight` is cleared ONLY by the refresh daemon's own `finally`, so a `DeadlineExceeded` leaves it SET — abandoned daemons bounded to EXACTLY ONE per outage, and the wedged read's eventual LATE return self-heals the memo (last-write-wins adoption, proven by test); once-per-outage `read_degraded` WARN + `read_recovered` INFO (the epoch-timestamp loudness pattern). `stamp_bridge_freshness` is the ONE place the two payload keys are written (the `summary_cache.stamp_freshness` §11 doctrine; 3-dp rounded age, `None` passthrough). (3) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `build_app` gains the `rate_bridge_cache` injection seam (the summary/movers/universe-cache precedent; `None` → a fresh production cache, owned per app instance); the route arm becomes `bridge_result = await run_in_threadpool(_rate_bridge_cache.get, bridge_lake_root)` (the app.py fast-read offload doctrine — even the O(1) hit's lock never runs on the loop) or an honest `BridgeReadResult(None, "unwired", None)` with ZERO cache work when no store is wired; the snapshot unpack + `build_pull_rate_view_merged` call are byte-identical; the return stamps the two keys onto `view.to_dict()`. `pull_rate_view.py` deliberately UNTOUCHED. **NO STALE ILLUSION, by construction (Golden Rule #1):** the cache stores the decoded `RateBridgeSnapshot`, never a view — `bridge_age`/`seconds_since_update` recompute per request from the snapshot's OWN `wall_time`, so a memoised snapshot AGES honestly and the 12 s `STALE_AFTER_S` machinery flips the verdict exactly as a re-read would (a frozen "flowing" is impossible; end-to-end pinned); a `cached` serve lags a publish by ≤ 2 s (< the 12 s verdict window — never a verdict-category flip from caching alone; invariant test-pinned); an `unverified` serve may lag arbitrarily but is LABELLED, with a growing `bridge_probe_age_s`; reported staleness only ever reads HIGHER than truth. **BYTE-COMPAT:** the payload key set == the frozen pre-change 17-key set ∪ exactly the two additive keys (pinned across no-store/fresh/stale/corrupt/absent), every pre-existing key equals a DIRECT un-cached `build_pull_rate_view_merged` computation field-for-field (fresh-bridge scenario), every degrade path (unwired/absent/corrupt/probe-error/wedged-with-empty-memo) yields `snapshot=None` → the panel-only projection byte-identical to today, and the ~10 pre-existing bridge tests + the 44-test monitor suite pass UNMODIFIED; `bx-rate-monitor.js` reads keys by name (additive keys ignored — verified). **MEASURED TEETH (verified by a temporary revert during development):** the same Event-wedged `read_rate_snapshot` scenario blocked the PRE-change route for the full 8 s wedge (`route took 8.02s` — the event-loop freeze), and returns in < 2 s (deadline 0.1 s + overhead) on the fixed route; the committed integration pin (`TestSlowReadLatencyBound`) asserts the owner AND followers bounded, `bridge_source="unverified"`, single-flight (reader-call counter 1), an unrelated route answering inside the bound, and live recovery after release. **O-COMPLEXITY (honest, per path):** steady-state hot path O(1) pure in-memory + one threadpool hop, ZERO syscalls; post-TTL revalidate O(1) + ONE `os.stat` on the guard's daemon (≤ 1 per 2 s per process while polled); content-change miss one stat + one ~300-byte read + JSON decode — constant in lake depth but a REAL disk read, not claimed free; wedged disk — EVERY response bounded (first-of-outage ≤ ~0.5 s, followers immediate) GIVEN an available AnyIO worker token — the route's offload rides `run_in_threadpool`'s DEFAULT 40-token limiter, shared by every offloaded dashboard read, and the SIBLING lake offloads (summary/movers/db_view) carry NO deadline guard, so a pool-wide wedge (every token stuck on an undeadlined sibling read of the same stalled volume) would queue this route's offload behind them; the per-path bounds are guarantees OF THE CACHE (the event loop stays free either way), pool-wide wedge protection is a NAMED follow-up — exactly ONE abandoned unkillable daemon per outage (the #999 stance: the guarantee is a free event loop + bounded latency + at-most-one zombie, never zombie reaping), self-healing on volume recovery. NOT claimed: any throughput win (a liveness/latency fix), or that the cold read got faster. **NAMED NON-GOALS:** the symmetric CLI WRITE-side hang (`publish_rate_snapshot`'s undeadlined fsync inside the pull's per-window `on_window` tick) is a separate follow-up, NOT fixed here; the panel copy under `state._lock` + the two O(1) probes stay on the loop (in-memory field ops, out of scope). **HOSTILE-REVIEW FOLD (MAJOR — guard-spawn failure):** a non-DeadlineExceeded raise from the guard — the production `run_with_deadline`'s ONE such path is `threading.Thread(...).start()` raising `RuntimeError("can't start new thread")`/`MemoryError` under thread/memory exhaustion, exactly the degraded-host regime this cache exists for (`_refresh` itself swallows every Exception, so a raise past the spawn means NO daemon owns `_inflight`) — previously RAISED out of `get()` (a 500 on the poll route through `run_in_threadpool`, violating its own "never raising" contract) AND permanently latched `_inflight` (the never-started daemon was the only clearer — every later poll served `unverified` with ZERO further refreshes until process restart). FIXED: the owner arm now catches `Exception`, releases the single-flight flag under the lock (idempotent for an injected guard whose daemon DID run — at worst an early release causing one duplicate last-write-wins refresh, never a wedge), WARNs ONCE per outage (`rate_bridge_cache.refresh_spawn_failed`, the `_degraded` latch shared with the deadline arm; `read_recovered` INFO on the flip out), and serves the last-known memo `unverified` with the honest growing `probe_age_s` — the NEXT poll retries (self-heal at poll cadence); `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` still PROPAGATE (never swallowed) but release the flag first. Regression-pinned BOTH levels, each failing on the pre-fix code (verified by a temporary revert): unit `TestGuardSpawnFailure` (never-raises + WARN-once + honest aging + next-poll-respawns-and-recovers + KI-releases-flag) + route integration `TestGuardSpawnFailureNever500s` (200 + `unverified` on the failing poll, `live` on the next). **GATES:** `rate_bridge_cache.py` 100.00% line+branch standalone (137/22 via its 51-test unit suite incl. real-guard wedge/adoption/leak + guard-spawn-failure pins); `lake_revision.py` 100.00% line+branch (63/14, 22 tests); every new/changed `app.py` line covered by the bridge+monitor suites (verified via coverage-JSON diff intersection — app.py rides its documented whole-package floor, `COVERAGE_DISCOVERY_EXCLUDE`); 218 touched-surface tests + the 65-test CLI retry-storm suite green; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict brutex` at the pre-change baseline (the one pre-existing `stage3_refine.py` cma-stub note, untouched file); `pyright` 0 errors, 0 warnings in touched files. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/rate_bridge_cache.py` (NEW), `brutex/dashboard/lake_revision.py`, `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_rate_bridge_cache.py` (NEW), `tests/unit/test_lake_revision.py`, `tests/integration/test_dashboard_cli_rate_bridge.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-RATE-BRIDGE-NONBLOCK-CACHE-001. (Ledger: renumbered #1492 → #1521 → #1522 across the PR #1206 merges with main — main's DEC-SUSPICION-SWEEP-FIXES-001 took #1492, then DEC-RATE-LOG-OUTSIDE-LOCK-001 took #1521; next free above live-main max #1521.)

1525. **DEC-DOCTOR-DAILY-CRON-001 — the daily 07:30 IST `brutex doctor` cron is WIRED (`.github/workflows/doctor-daily.yml`), closing the STANDARDS §11 P2 row** (2026-07-06 on `claude/relaxed-thompson-x1zqdm`; a daily health contract is inherently time-anchored ("runs every workday" cannot be satisfied event-only). **Triggers:** cron `"0 2 * * *"` (02:00 UTC = 07:30 IST EXACTLY — IST is fixed +05:30, no DST) + `workflow_dispatch` + a paths-filtered `push` smoke on `main` (only `.github/workflows/doctor-daily.yml` + `brutex/doctor.py` — the nightly-sibling convention: mutation/stress/redteam/security-audit each smoke their own paths); **NEVER `pull_request`** and never joins ci-ok (the DEC-M4PRO-PR-TRIGGER-001 class of reasoning: a scheduled observability contract must never gate PRs). **What it runs:** the PLAIN `brutex doctor` on a hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner with hermetic paths (`$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-doctor/{audit,runtime.json,lake}` — empty audit dir, absent runtime file, nonexistent `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT`), `pip install -e ".[data,ui]"` (the ci.yml run-smoke minimum CLI-boot set) + BOTH PyO3 wheels (retry-looped, verbatim ci.yml — `brutex.cli` transitively imports both); `brutex doctor --live` (the sandbox-blind Mac kit, `brutex/doctor_live.py`) NEVER runs in CI; `BRUTEX_SKIP_WHEEL_FRESHNESS` is never set — the two wheel-freshness handshakes (installed `.so` vs in-repo `EXPECTED_BUILD.json`) are the cron's SUBSTANTIVE teeth. **Envelope honesty ASSERTED, not assumed (Golden Rule #1 + #10):** a dedicated contract step awk-parses the doctor report and pins the exact 7-row verdict table — `audit_chain`/`runtime_file`/`audit_replay`/`derived_freshness`/`lake_uniqueness` = SKIP-with-reason (a PASS on an operator-envelope check against the hermetic empty envelope is a FABRICATED verdict → red, never fake-green) and `wheel_freshness`/`wheel_freshness_fno_math` = PASS (a WARN/SKIP means the run proved nothing — in CI the wheel was built from THIS commit, so drift = stale fingerprint = repo defect → red, never quietly hollow); a MISSING check name OR a changed check-row COUNT (the exact-7 count pin makes the check-set contract TWO-sided — an ADDED future check that fabricates PASS or quietly SKIPs against the hermetic envelope reds too, never sails through unclassified) → red, forcing a conscious reclassification; the awk line shape ($2 = check name, $3 = status, check rows framed by the two `====` rules) is pinned repo-side by `tests/unit/test_doctor.py::test_format_line_shape_pins_the_awk_field_contract`, so a `DoctorReport.format()` reshape reds its own PR instead of post-merge via the paths-filtered push smoke. The run summary states the envelope in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and embeds the report table. **Alerting:** on red, (a) ONE stable-titled (`doctor-daily: brutex doctor is RED` — deliberately SHA-FREE, STRONGER dedupe than mutation.yml's per-SHA title: a daily red on a moving main would otherwise mint one issue per day) tracking issue via `actions/github-script@v9` (labels bug/doctor/critical), whose body EMBEDS the doctor report table; repeat red days fold into it via `createComment`; a GREEN run AUTO-CLOSES it with a recovery comment (Golden Rule #1: a recovered doctor must not leave a stale open `critical` alarm — one issue per red EPISODE); a denied `issues: write` degrades to a warning via try/catch; BOTH issue-lifecycle steps (filer + closer) are REF-GATED to `refs/heads/main` — the tracking issue is repo-global state while the concurrency group serializes only per-ref, so an ungated branch `workflow_dispatch` could falsely close the live main alarm on a green branch run or race the find-then-create into two same-titled `critical` issues; the gate puts every issue-touching run in the ONE main concurrency group. Checkout runs `persist-credentials: false` (DEC-CI-FORK-PR-HARDEN-001 convention — the job's `issues: write` token never lands in `.git/config` under the third-party pip/cargo build surface); THREE of the workflow's script bodies are FUNCTIONALLY executed by the redteam suite, never just grep-pinned: the envelope-honesty assert step's bash against fixture reports (hollowing mutations like `exit 1`→`exit 0` fail loudly), BOTH `actions/github-script` issue-lifecycle bodies node-executed against a stubbed `github`/`context`/`core` (killing the empirically-verified surviving branch inversions — filer `if (open)` and closer `if (!open) return;` — which hollowed the issue lifecycle while every textual pin stayed green), and the Telegram bash with a call-recording stub `curl` on PATH (killing the verified deleted-send silent no-op). A timeout-kill/cancel mid-doctor leaves `doctor-report.txt` EXISTING but EMPTY (`tee` creates it at pipeline start; the doctor prints its whole report once at process end), so BOTH the issue filer AND the step summary treat an empty/whitespace-only report as unavailable (`raw.trim()` guard / `[ -s ]` non-empty test), embedding the honest 'doctor output unavailable' note instead of an empty code fence. The doctor JOB and the doctor/assert STEPS are UNCONDITIONAL and the whole step-`if:` surface is equality-pinned as an exact map (summary/upload `always()`, Telegram/filer the red guard, closer `success() && main`) — an empirically-verified surviving job-level never-true `if:` SKIPS the job while the run reports SUCCESS (the cron hollows with no red anywhere, functionally identical to deleting `schedule:` yet invisible to the trigger pins), and the doctor+assert paired variant is worse (the job completes green and the closer would close a genuine open alarm daily); the listForRepo dedupe query's `state: 'open'` arm is pinned textually AND functionally (a verified-surviving `state: 'all'` would match the CLOSED prior-episode issue via the deliberately-stable title — 'Still red' comments landing on a closed issue, the one-open-issue-per-red-EPISODE channel muted). (b) a best-effort Telegram step gated `failure() || cancelled()` + `continue-on-error: true`, secrets `BRUTEX_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`/`BRUTEX_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` env-mapped (`secrets.*` unusable in a step `if:`; names mirror the app env vars, gitleaks-allowlisted; runbook `docs/runbooks/telegram-setup.md` gains the provisioning section) — unset secrets → notice + exit 0, a failed send → warning, NEVER a job failure (no Telegram secret is provisioned in this repo's Actions today; the GitHub issue is the PRIMARY channel — itself best-effort, its filer try/catch degrades an API/permission failure to a warning retried on the next red run, so the only unconditional signal is the red run in the Actions tab). BOTH alert steps fire on `cancelled()` too (DEC-MUTATION-ALERT-CANCELLED-001 #1511: a job killed by its own `timeout-minutes` reports CANCELLED, live-probed run 28748795864) and BOTH are STEP-SCOPED to the doctor/assert step outcomes (`steps.doctor.outcome != 'success' || steps.assert.outcome != 'success'` — bare `failure()` is JOB-scoped, so a transient post-doctor infra flake (summary write / artifact upload) on a GREEN doctor day would have filed/extended the 'brutex doctor is RED' critical issue over an all-green embedded table and, on a recovery day, posted 'Still red' while skipping the `success()` closer; `!= 'success'` still fires on a setup/bootstrap failure — the doctor step is then SKIPPED — and a green-doctor/red-upload day now leaves the issue untouched until the next fully-green run closes it); `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: false` (nightly convention) means a CANCELLED conclusion can only be a timeout-kill or a manual cancel — both alert-worthy; job `timeout-minutes: 30` (~2× the cold ~12-15 min two-cargo-build run) + a step-level `timeout-minutes: 5` on the doctor step (step timeout = step FAILURE, also alertable) + `set -o pipefail` so `tee` can't mask the doctor's exit 1. **Pinned:** NEW `tests/redteam/test_redteam_doctor_daily.py` (32 tests: 19 meta-pins + 13 FUNCTIONAL executions across THREE harnesses — 5 subprocess runs of the real assert-step bash against fixture reports (green-on-expected / red-on-fabricated-envelope-PASS / red-on-WARN-wheel / red-on-missing-name / red-on-ADDED-unclassified-check), 5 node-executed runs of the real `actions/github-script` filer/closer bodies against a stubbed issues API (first-red creates the pinned title/labels issue · repeat-red folds via createComment, never a duplicate · green closes with a recovery comment · green-with-no-open-issue no-ops · an EMPTY/missing report reads 'doctor output unavailable', never an empty fence — each also asserting every recorded listForRepo query carries `state: 'open'` + `labels: 'bug,doctor'`), and 3 subprocess runs of the real Telegram bash with a call-recording stub curl (secrets-set sends EXACTLY once · unset-secrets notice + exit 0 with curl never invoked · failed-send warning, still exit 0); the established workflow-pin home — runs in ci.yml's smoke/redteam job on every PR AND redteam-nightly; imports no `brutex` module, zero coverage-gate impact): exists+parses · cron+dispatch+IST comment · no-pull_request + scoped push · minimal permissions · checkout `persist-credentials: false` · cancel-in-progress false + the EXACT concurrency-group value `doctor-daily-${{ github.ref }}` (a per-run group would keep a substring pin green with ZERO serialization) · job timeout ∈ [15,60] · the doctor JOB unconditional + the step-`if:` set equality-pinned as an exact map (a never-true job-level or doctor+assert-paired `if:` would skip-green the whole cron) · doctor-step own timeout/bash/pipefail · hermetic + never `--live` + wheel-skip never set · both wheels installed · all 7 `assert_status` contract lines + the exact-7 count pin · every alert `if` contains `cancelled()` · alert guards step-scoped to the doctor/assert outcomes · SHA-free stable title + createComment + doctor label + close-on-green wiring + the dedupe query's `state: 'open'` arm (textual count==2) · both issue-lifecycle steps main-ref-gated · Telegram env-mapped secrets + exit-0 guard + non-fatal send + no `secrets.` in any `if` · `continue-on-error` Telegram-only · the summary step embeds the report only when NON-empty (`-s`, never `-f`); PLUS a format-contract pin in `tests/unit/test_doctor.py` (`test_format_line_shape_pins_the_awk_field_contract`) freezing the `$2 = name / $3 = status` check-line shape both the workflow's awk and the redteam fixture renderer parse/render; the workflow YAML itself rides ci.yml's existing actionlint job. **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10) — what a green run PROVES:** the doctor CLI boots on a clean runner (full import chain incl. both wheels), both wheel handshakes PASS against the in-repo fingerprints, and the skip machinery abstained honestly. **What it does NOT prove:** production lake / audit-chain / vendor / AWS health — the production-envelope doctor remains `verify-m4pro.yml` (DEC-M4PRO-VERIFY-001 #773, daily 12:00 UTC = 17:30 IST on the operator's M4 Pro with the real lake); this workflow is its always-on hosted-runner MORNING complement and never double-claims production health. **NAMED NON-GOALS:** "alert if missed" (detecting a cron GitHub silently skipped — the TRACK2 §8 SLA's dead-man's-switch half) stays OPEN, a named follow-up; the docs-only C1–C12 check enumeration (internally inconsistent across TRACK2_OBSERVABILITY §7 vs TRACK1_RUNTIME_ARCHITECTURE §7B) is honestly NOT claimed implemented — the shipped doctor is the 7-check minimum-viable set and the contract asserts THOSE names; Telegram secret provisioning is an operator task (absence degrades gracefully). **Docs reconciled:** STANDARDS_100PCT.md §11 P2 row → ✅ DONE, §8 SLA row → 🟢, §2 prose → CRON LIVE, §4 AUTOMATED gap tail, §5 audit-chain row, §10 ROADMAP bullet, §12 amendment row; TRACK2_OBSERVABILITY.md §8 SLA mechanism cell (systemd-timer claim replaced with the real two-surface mechanism, "alert if missed" kept open); `docs/runbooks/telegram-setup.md` CI-secrets section. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate change. **Decision ID:** DEC-DOCTOR-DAILY-CRON-001. 1596. **DEC-BACKUP-OFFBOX-001 (renumbered from #1560 at the 2026-07-08 wave-resync) — automated incremental OFF-BOX backup of the lake + ledger + DuckDB masters + sweeps + hash-chained audit logs (restic → S3 Object-Lock / B2 immutable), with an O(1) injectable-clock DEAD-MAN freshness check (CRITICAL Telegram via the existing SweepAlerter, durable cross-run re-alert throttle), a TESTED byte-verified RESTORE DRILL (1 MiB known-bytes canary + stratified per-category sample + the audit-JSONL byte-PREFIX law; corruption negative proven by a real executable fake-restic stub), and ADR-0017's manual-acceptance register** (2026-07-06 on `claude/serene-euler-y5ra0z`; feat(backup/cli/notifications-docs); ops tooling ONLY — ENGINE UNCHANGED, NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (+ the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track); F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change; blueprint `docs/REMOTE_CONTROL_AND_ZERO_TOUCH_COMPARISON.md:304` rows 28/30 + the dead-man keystone `:27-31,:287`; automates + supersedes the manual tar §2 of `docs/runbooks/lake-backup-restore.md`, whose restore-ORDER law + consistency argument stand verbatim). DESIGN LAW: built OUTWARD from a 23-row failure-mode matrix — every failure maps to a deterministic triple (exit code + `backup.*` structlog event + alert-or-explicit-no-alert): phantom-`/Volumes` refusal via the COMMON `lake_root_identity` BEFORE any restic verb (pin: the mount gate precedes `forget --prune`, the one path by which a backup system can destroy data) · empty-set refusal (`--allow-empty` escape) · rc-3 partial = stamped SUCCESS + `consecutive_partials` streak (WARN ≤2, CRITICAL ≥3) · verify failure (nightly `restic check` + the rotating `--read-data-subset=k/56` state-cursor tier, `BRUTEX_BACKUP_VERIFY_SUBSET` auto|none|passthrough) → NO success stamp + CRITICAL `backup_repo_corrupt` · maintenance (`forget` + Sunday `--prune`) failure NEVER retracts the data-success stamp (`maintenance_ok=false`, WARN, exit 7 — the dead-man must not fire when the data IS off-box) · single-flight flock (the `_flock_singleflight` shape) with NO alert on benign overlap — held by the nightly run AND (round 5) the monthly restore drill, so the drill's canary backup/restore can never collide with the nightly `check`/`forget --prune` EXCLUSIVE restic repo locks and read as a false `drill_restic` failure or a false corruption page (round 6: the drill's default fire time moved Day-1 04:30 → 13:00 IST — OUTSIDE the nightly window, whose default `auto` subset read holds the lock to ~07:00+ by the runbook §5 math, so the busy skip is the exception, not the deterministic monthly norm launchd's no-retry one-shot made it — and a busy-skipped drill emits ONE WARN `backup_degraded(aspect="drill_skipped")` with its own honest body instead of vanishing into drill.err.log: a skipped drill is LOST verification, not the benign run-vs-run redundancy; run-vs-run contention stays exit 5, no alert) · a 48 h subprocess timeout BELTED by `running_since`+`BRUTEX_BACKUP_MAX_RUNTIME_HOURS` HUNG braces (a multi-day 8 TB seed reads RUNNING, never a false page) · secrets by construction (password only as FILE/COMMAND env to the CHILD, inherited RESTIC_PASSWORD STRIPPED, argv secret-free — a planted-password hygiene test pins absence from every argv + log event; no credential path is ever in the backup set, DEC-AWS-ONLY-CREDS-001). DEAD-MAN: O(1) by construction (one ≤1 KiB JSON read + pure `evaluate_deadman` + ≤1 publish + 1 ping — NEVER a lake walk); verdicts FRESH/RUNNING/HUNG/OVERDUE/NEVER_SUCCEEDED/STATE_CORRUPT/CLOCK_SKEW; a FUTURE `last_success_at` beyond 300 s tolerance ALARMS (the state-poisoning/silencing vector); a corrupt state file alarms and is NEVER overwritten (forensics); the DAILY deep tier cross-verifies the stamp against the REMOTE trust root (`restic snapshots --no-lock --json --latest 1 --tag brutex` — `--no-lock` load-bearing, round 6: the deep-due tick naturally lands in/near the nightly step-10 `forget`/Sunday `--prune` (and drill canary forget) EXCLUSIVE repo-lock windows, and a locking read there rc=1'd into a false CRITICAL page + `/fail` pings every tick until the prune ended (a failed call never advances the deep gate; since round 9 a FAILED metadata call pages the distinct cause-honest `deep_check_unavailable` via `backup.deadman.deep_failed` — `state_remote_divergence` is reserved for a COMPLETED comparison that disagrees), while its own shared lock could conversely fail the nightly's `forget`; verified on restic 0.16.4 that `--no-lock` succeeds under a held exclusive lock — safe, the call is read-only metadata; THREE tiers, rounds 3-5 of the hostile review: a `max_runtime_hours` stamp-PLAUSIBILITY bound screened FIRST — a `last_success_at` landing more than one bounded run-duration after the REMOTE latest snapshot's own time is divergence; the anchor is the remote time ALONE, the one stamp no on-box `state.json` write can move (round 5 dropped the forgeable `last_attempt_at` arm of the round-4 anchor, which let a TWO-field success+attempt bump read AGREE forever), so a stamp forgery that keeps the real id — bump-only or success+attempt — is caught WHEN it moves `last_success_at` more than `max_runtime_hours` past the remote snapshot's own time (round-6 honesty: a SUB-bound inflation ≤ 48 h-default is inherently indistinguishable from a slow legit run and stays bounded only by the shallow 30 h threshold on top of the inflated stamp; and the deep tier is FRESH-gated, so a forged/persistently-re-bumped `running_since` bypasses it — one-time poison caught only by the HUNG bound at `max_runtime_hours`, the persistent re-bump an acknowledged on-box-writer residual, runbook §6 item 8) — then id-first agreement (remote latest id vs the stamped `last_snapshot_id`, run-duration-tolerant), then the nearer-of-attempt/success time-gap fallback within `deadman_hours` for an id-less state; durable `last_deep_check_at` gate — a DIVERGED comparison advances it ONLY when its CRITICAL was actually DELIVERED (round 5: an undelivered divergence — Telegram outage/OFF — retries the bounded 120 s metadata call every hourly tick, exit 1 + /fail ping each tick, instead of going quiet for 24 h; the only-stamp-on-success law, one field over); a seed-window `max_runtime_hours` raise — set in `~/.brutex/.env` so the SEPARATE hourly launchd checker resolves the SAME bound, a shell-only export never reaches it (round 5) — stays in place until the next nightly success restamps — runbook step 6) — closing supra-bound plausible-stamp forgery at the next daily deep tick (worst-case detection latency ≈ `max_runtime_hours` + 24 h under defaults, i.e. a persistent re-bump is detected 48–72 h after the last real snapshot — round-6 honesty reconcile); the shallow check needs NO repo config (pinned); the checker pings `BRUTEX_BACKUP_HEALTHCHECK_URL` (`/fail` on breach) EVERY tick — the one external lane that catches checker/launchd/box/Telegram death (provisioning = ADR-0017 M6). ALERTS: ZERO `telegram.py` changes — 4 `SweepAlerter` methods (`backup_failed` / `backup_degraded` [WARN] / `backup_overdue` / `backup_repo_corrupt` — the latter's escalation promise split per source arm, round 5: the DRILL-mismatch arm honestly says nightly successes may keep stamping so the dead-man stays QUIET and that page is the only automated signal, while the nightly-verify arm keeps the keeps-escalating body) all ride PHASE_BLOCKED (0.0 s window — correct: the TelegramBucket dedupe cache is per-process in-memory and every launchd fire is a fresh process, so in-process TTL dedupe is structurally inert; the REAL cross-run bound is the checker-owned durable `deadman.json` stamp + `BRUTEX_BACKUP_REALERT_HOURS` = ≤4 CRITICAL/day while broken, only-stamp-on-successful-send) + module-level `emit_backup_failed_alert` mirroring `emit_pull_halt_alert`. STATE: TWO files, single-writer-per-file (runner owns `state.json`, checker owns `deadman.json` — no read-modify-write race), `atomic_write_simple(chmod=0o600)` (NOT `atomic_write_via` — a state ENOSPC must never mis-escalate to LakeWriteHalt, #890 split; alarm-over-silence: an unstamped success can only cause a FALSE alarm, never silence). SCOPE: fail-safe WHOLE-ROOT includes (`<lake_root>` + `~/.brutex/audit`; `.quarantine/` INCLUDED — post-heal it is the ONLY copy of removed poison rows, #1175), fixed excludes only for the provably transient (`.locks`,`.rate`,`*.tmp`,`.brutex-write-*`) + `--exclude-caches` + operator `BRUTEX_BACKUP_EXTRA_EXCLUDES` (default `logs:dedup-cache`). SCHEDULING: 3 launchd templates (nightly 03:35 run · hourly check · monthly Day-1 13:00 drill) GENERATED by `schedule_render.py` + golden-pinned byte-equal (docs can never drift); prune folded into the nightly run behind an IST-weekday gate — no 4th job; cron fallback documented. HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): a dead box is silent on-box (the external ping lane is the keystone, shipped as a hook, the ACCOUNT is manual M6); RPO = the schedule interval and sweeps/audit are the non-re-pullable loss window; per-FILE crash-consistency only (atomic writers; DuckDB masters may snapshot torn → rebuildable; set-level skew healed by the ledger-reconcile design per the prior runbook); subset verification is sampling (full pack read once per 56 successful nights ≈ 8 weeks; drill = 16 files + canary, not 8 TB; quarterly FULL restore stays manual M7); restic facts (exit-3 / n-of-t subset / stale-only unlock) cited to restic docs AND probed against the installed binary at install (runbook step 2). NEW `brutex/backup/` (errors/state/restic_runner/plan/run/deadman/restore_drill/schedule_render) + `brutex/config/backup_env.py` + `brutex backup {run,check,restore-drill,status}` CLI (nested-subparser idiom, dispatch after the `wipe` branch); zero new `pragma: no cover` — the default subprocess/clock/ping seams are executed for real (executable stub through the REAL runner; http.server ping fixture); every new + touched module 100% line+branch; 7-type discipline incl. hypothesis deadman totality property + golden argv/plist pins; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/pyright at the pre-change baseline. **Files:** `brutex/backup/*` (NEW ×9), `brutex/config/backup_env.py` (NEW), `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `docs/runbooks/backup-offbox.md` (NEW), `docs/runbooks/backup-templates/*.plist` (NEW ×3, generated), `docs/runbooks/lake-backup-restore.md` (banner), `docs/adr/0017-offbox-backup-restic.md` (NEW), tests as named in the spec, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (header blurb). **Decision ID:** DEC-BACKUP-OFFBOX-001.
