1583. **DEC-DAILY-CUTOFF-GROUNDED-001 — the prebuild's session-close daily cutoff is REPAIRED (the DEC-HARDWARE-ENVELOPE-001 #1401 M1 regression had left DEC-PREBUILD-SESSION-CLOSE-CUTOFF-001 production-DEAD) and gains the data-grounded DEFER-only variant (the #1279 named follow-up)** (2026-07-07 on `claude/blissful-curie-gp94rk`; item 2/10 of the polish pack; one commit with #1582). **Move 1 (the repair):** the `/pull-pipeline` route, the parallel prebuild orchestrator's None-resolution, and the lake-heal daily recall all pinned a plain today-IST DATE, bypassing `daily_derive_cutoff` entirely — all three now ride ONE law: the route + orchestrator pin ONE run INSTANT (NEW `calendars/nse.now_ist`, threaded as `daily_cutoff_now` — M1's one-value-per-run byte-identity is KEPT, the VALUE is now session-close-aware) and the heal recall delegates to `daily_derive_cutoff` (clock arm only). **Move 2 (the grounded variant):** NEW `nse.session_last_bar_complete` (last stored 1m bar + 1 minute ≥ the per-date session close — the half-open ingest filter's own law) + `nse.daily_derive_cutoff_grounded` (result ∈ {clock verdict, run day}; result ≤ the clock verdict ALWAYS; abstains to clock on EVERY unknown — out-of-coverage date, no bars, no calendar); `materialize_lake_timeframes` re-grounds the cutoff POST-READ for DENSE symbols only (the #1031 `is_index` gate — illiquid REFERENCE_ONLY names never defer on their own sparseness); env kill switch `BRUTEX_DAILY_CUTOFF_GROUNDED` (off-values shared via the NEW public `derive_stamp.DISABLED_ENV_VALUES`); an explicit `daily_before` stays LAW; the derive stamp records the EFFECTIVE cutoff (`should_skip_derive` unchanged — a deferred day is RE-derived on the next run, never skip-stranded); `_last_ist_datetime` is the one last-bar extraction (`_last_ist_date` delegates). **Move 3** is #1582's boundary pin. SANCTIONED behavior: a post-close pipeline run derives the run day's 1day bar SAME-RUN (previously deferred a day by the regression's date-pin); a provably-incomplete dense run-day session DEFERS instead of finalizing a partial daily bar; the heal recall is session-close-aware. Complete sessions are byte-identical grounded-vs-clock (property-pinned, `tests/property/test_daily_cutoff_grounded_parity.py`); the parallel==sequential prebuild golden is extended (`tests/integration/test_prebuild_parallel_byte_identical.py`). **ROUND-4 REVIEW FOLD (MAJOR — the route arm gains its own regression pin):** Move 1's ROUTE arm (`prebuild_cutoff_now = now_ist()` threaded as `daily_cutoff_now=` into BOTH the sequential `_materialize` closure and `run_pipeline_prebuild_guarded`) lives inside the `/pull-pipeline` job body's pre-existing `# pragma: no cover — runs on the job thread` shield — the EXACT mechanism that let the #1401 M1 regression ship undetected — and no executing test asserted the route's cutoff wiring, so re-introducing `daily_before=<date>` at the route would have passed the whole suite again. CLOSED with the #1492-G3 AST-pin idiom (NEW `tests/unit/test_app_prebuild_cutoff_pin.py`): an AST walk over `app.py` locates the ONE `_work` closure calling `run_pipeline_prebuild_guarded` and pins the route contract mechanically — exactly ONE `now_ist()` instant, bound to a name, BOTH downstream arms passing THAT SAME name as `daily_cutoff_now=` (no inline clock, no `**kwargs` smuggling), `include_daily=True`, and NO `daily_before=` keyword on those calls NOR anywhere in `app.py` (the #1401 regression shape) — teeth verified fails-on-regression by re-applying the exact #1401 edit (both pins fail, line-named). Honest envelope: an AST pin asserts the wiring SHAPE, not job-thread execution — the executing coverage of the law itself stays at the orchestrator/materialize layers, whose defense-in-depth below the route bounds the worst silent drift to a wrong 1day set for a day, self-healing. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX); touched modules 100% line+branch; ruff/`mypy --strict`/pyright at baseline. **Files:** brutex/calendars/nse.py, brutex/data/timeframe_materialize.py, brutex/data/derive_stamp.py, brutex/data/lake_heal.py, brutex/dashboard/{app,pipeline_prebuild,prebuild_parallel}.py, brutex/adapters/ingest_common.py, tests/integration/test_timeframe_materialize_grounded_cutoff.py, tests/property/test_daily_cutoff_grounded_parity.py, tests/unit/{test_app_prebuild_cutoff_pin,test_calendar_nse,test_derive_stamp,test_ingest_common,test_lake_heal,test_pipeline_prebuild_parallel,test_timeframe_materialize}.py. **Decision ID:** DEC-DAILY-CUTOFF-GROUNDED-001.

1585. **DEC-RETRY-COUNTER-SPLIT-001 — the conflated `in_pull_fetches` window-ledger counter is SPLIT into two persisted fields, `empty_retries` vs `transient_retries`, so the ledger records HOW a window's in-pull fetch total divided between clean 0-bar responses and retryable 429/timeout re-attempts** (2026-07-07 on `claude/blissful-curie-gp94rk`; item 4/10 of the polish pack). **SUPERSEDE NOTE:** this split was DECLINED TWICE — #924 (DEC-FETCHES-COL-HONESTY-001) refused it under the task's "do NOT add heavy new tracking just for display" and shipped a relabel instead, and #1355 (DEC-FETCHES-COL-RENAME-001) re-declined it for the same reason ("NAMED FOLLOW-UP … splitting the counter into separate `empty_retries` vs `transient_retries` ledger fields needs window-ledger schema tracking") after documenting that the counter genuinely conflates BOTH classes (the F&O spine's inner retry loop bumps it on every GrowwError retry). It is ACCEPTED now because the blocker was the SCHEMA tracking, not the counting: the ledger's proven optional-column back-compat template (the `empty_streak` / `bars_net_new` precedent — this is its THIRD use) carries the two nullable int64 columns appended LAST at zero migration cost, and the two classes are counted WHERE THEY ALREADY OCCUR in both spines (no new retry machinery, fetch behaviour byte-identical) — a data-honesty fix, no longer "heavy tracking just for display". MECHANISM: `WindowLedgerRecord` + `record()` gain `empty_retries` / `transient_retries`, default `None` = honest unknown (the `bars_net_new` law — an OLD ledger row loads `None`, NEVER a fabricated 0); `plan()` stamps a KNOWN 0/0; seed/known-gap stamp `None`; the reopen/audit demotion preserves the prior split; NEW public `LedgerRowTuple` is the ONE 16-field row-shape spelling (the store's `LedgerRow` aliases it); the store loads any pre-split Parquet arity with both columns as `None` and every other column byte-intact (ONE `_derive_retry_count` helper for both); BOTH spines thread the two counts into every `ledger.record` site, with the spine invariant test-pinned: `empty + transient + (1 if bars) == in_pull_fetches`; spot's tail transient half is structurally 0 (documented); the F&O spine's inline transient retries mean a clean tail can carry BOTH halves — exactly the conflation #1355 documented; `spot_daily_resample` stamps a KNOWN 0/0 (zero vendor fetches); the `/db` window-ledger grid gains the two columns via the generic renderer. HONEST: the in-CALL 6× ladder is STILL not persisted (the #924 caveat stands verbatim); the `/coverage/windows` display split over the new fields is the named follow-up. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX); touched modules 100% line+branch; ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` + pyright 0 new. **Files:** brutex/data/{window_ledger,window_ledger_store,spot_daily_resample}.py, brutex/adapters/groww/{ingest,option_ingest}.py, brutex/dashboard/app.py, tests/unit/{test_window_ledger,test_window_ledger_store,test_groww_ingest,test_groww_option_ingest,test_spot_daily_resample}.py, tests/integration/test_dashboard_coverage.py. **Decision ID:** DEC-RETRY-COUNTER-SPLIT-001. **Supersedes** the declined-follow-up stance of #924 + #1355 (the display entries themselves stand unedited).

1586. **DEC-GROWW-EPOCH-VERDICT-001 — the defensive epoch-timestamp branch gains a deterministic session-plausibility INTERPRETATION VERDICT + a live-probe runbook, discharging the DEC-INGEST-BOUNDARY-INTEGRITY-001 (b) follow-up (#1294) as far as this environment honestly can: parsing behaviour is byte-unchanged and the Unix-UTC assumption stays UNVERIFIED** (2026-07-07 on `claude/blissful-curie-gp94rk`; item 5/10 of the polish pack; a live vendor probe is impossible here, so the deterministic cross-check + runbook variant ships instead of a fabricated verification). NEW `brutex/adapters/groww/epoch_verdict.py`: classifies each numeric candle timestamp under BOTH interpretations (unix-utc vs ist-naive, exactly +05:30 apart) against the REAL NSE session calendar (`get_session_checked`; out-of-coverage dates ABSTAIN — **ROUND-1 REVIEW FOLD (log storm):** SILENTLY, via the non-warning `is_holiday_data_available` pre-check — the original routing through the strict calendar fired one undeduplicated `calendar.holiday_data_unavailable` WARN per check, i.e. up to 2×1024 per out-of-coverage epoch payload PER WINDOW (a 2027 pull after a vendor epoch flip — the exact scenario this module diagnoses — would have stormed the log across tens of thousands of windows); the ONE aggregate `epoch_timestamp_verdict` WARN stays the loud surface, and the pre-check deliberately abstains on out-of-coverage WEEKENDS too (an out-of-coverage date can never read in-session, so no directional evidence is lost — at most an `out_of_session` tally becomes `abstained`); zero-calendar-WARN regression pinned (fails-before verified); invalid timestamps are counted, never raised) and aggregates an `EpochVerdict` ∈ {unix_utc_consistent, ist_naive_consistent, contradictory, no_evidence} over a deterministic first-1024 sample. `parser.parse_candle_rows` collects row-level numeric timestamps and emits ONE `groww.parse.epoch_timestamp_verdict` WARNING per epoch-carrying payload (the `ohlc_clamped` #1510 precedent); string-timestamp payloads emit NOTHING (pinned); parsed bars are byte-identical (pinned); the #1294 once-per-pull `groww.parse.epoch_timestamp` WARN is unchanged. NEW `docs/runbooks/groww-epoch-timestamp-probe.md`: the verdict→action table + the live-probe procedure that ALONE can VERIFY the vendor's epoch semantics (Golden Rule #1 — the verdict is evidence-weighing, not verification). 1587. **DEC-CLI-DEPTH-FLOORS-001 — the CLI `brutex fetch` path gains the vendor-depth-floor learner + the learned-floor planning clamp, closing DEC-VENDOR-FLOOR-LAZY-PROBE-001's named follow-up so the CLI mirrors the dashboard build sites** (2026-07-07 on `claude/blissful-curie-gp94rk`; item 6/10 of the polish pack). The per-pull learner is built over the PACED replica of the pull's adapter (`with_paced_client(adapter, pace)` — the DEC-RATE-SINGLE-ADMISSION-001 seam, so learner probes ride the SAME rate admission as the pull) with the SAME instrument-master `schema_meta` sidecar the dashboard uses — a floor learned by EITHER entrypoint clamps BOTH; a persisted learned floor clamps 1-minute planning + fetching to `max(GROWW_HISTORY_FLOOR, learned floor)` via the EXISTING per-symbol `symbol_windows` seam (the daily path stays exempt). `--dry-run`/`--inspect` open no store, build no learner, thread `None` — planning byte-identical. **ROUND-1 REVIEW FOLD (MAJOR — the whole-pull DuckDB hold):** the original wiring opened ONE read-write `InstrumentStore` and held it on the fetch's ExitStack for the ENTIRE multi-hour pull; a DuckDB rw connection takes an EXCLUSIVE cross-process file lock, so (a) `brutex serve` booted during a CLI fetch failed at its own `InstrumentStore.open` (`CatalogError: Could not set lock on file` — a regression vs the pre-branch transient open in `_resolve_brute_force_instruments`, PROVEN by subprocess experiment), and (b) with a dashboard already running the CLI's open ALWAYS failed → the depth-floor feature silently never worked concurrently, so the "either entrypoint clamps BOTH" claim held only SERIALLY. FIXED: NEW `_TransientCliFloorStore` — every `get_meta`/`set_meta` is an open→op→close (milliseconds; O(symbols) reads once at pull start + at most one write per learned floor per pull), the DuckDB file is NEVER held across the fetch (regression-pinned: after construction AND use, a SECOND process opens `instruments.duckdb` rw successfully — the pre-fix shape verifiably fails this; a spy pins zero handles surviving any op, incl. a raising op). Per-op failures ride the EXISTING best-effort callers (`load_vendor_floors` → `{}` + ONE WARN; `VendorFloorLearner._persist` → WARN) — the fetch is never blocked. HONEST residual: while a dashboard PROCESS holds the file rw, each transient op still fails (DuckDB rw excludes all peers) — the degrade is now PER-OP and self-heals when the dashboard releases, instead of one boot-time failure disabling floors for the whole pull; true concurrent sharing (routing floors through the dashboard) stays a named non-goal. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no scope/vocab/rate-cap change; `brutex/cli.py` 100.00% line+branch; ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` + pyright at the pre-change baseline (0 new). **Files:** brutex/cli.py, tests/unit/test_cli_depth_floors.py. **Decision ID:** DEC-CLI-DEPTH-FLOORS-001.

1588. **DEC-ACCOUNT-LEASE-CROSSHOST-001 — the account pull single-flight gains its CROSS-HOST arm: an advisory heartbeat LEASE on shared lake storage (`<lake_root>/.locks/pull_lease.json`) refuses a pull start when a FRESH lease from a DIFFERENT host is present — best-effort DETECTION, honestly NOT mutual exclusion** (2026-07-07 on `claude/blissful-curie-gp94rk`; item 7/10 of the polish pack; the flock-based single-flight only ever covered ONE host, while the Groww account is one TOTP token across every machine sharing the lake). MECHANISM: atomic 0o600 lease writes, a 30 s daemon heartbeat refresh, token-conditional removal at exit (a stranger's lease is never deleted), released LIFO; the lease is entered STRICTLY AFTER both flocks at BOTH production sites (dashboard `BackgroundPullJob` via a `lease_factory` seam + CLI `_enter_pull_singleflight` via the same seam); same-host leases are soundly IGNORED (the flock already governs same-host); a crashed pull's lease self-heals within 180 s (staleness window); a damaged/unreadable lease reads as an honest `None`, NEVER a false block; kill switch `BRUTEX_PULL_LEASE=off` is a pinned pure no-op. HONEST envelope (stated in code + runbook, Golden Rule #10): DETECTION over shared storage + wall clocks — TOCTOU races, clock skew, hostname collisions, non-shared lake roots and non-BruteX consumers of the token are ALL outside the guarantee; the runbook (`docs/runbooks/data-fetch-runday.md`) documents the operator reading. **ROUND-1 REVIEW FOLD (MAJOR — bounded lease I/O):** the guard's synchronous lake-file ops (the enter read + first refresh, and the exit `clear()`) ran UNBOUNDED while BOTH single-flight flocks were held, and both release orders put the exit `clear()` AHEAD of the flock releases (pull_jobs LIFO + the CLI ExitStack) — a WEDGED (non-raising) lake volume (the exact scenario the sibling bounded 5 s daemon join exists for; under #999 a wedged volume lets the pull COMPLETE, so this finally IS reached) hung `clear()` forever, never released the account-keyed + lake-root flocks, and every future pull (dashboard or CLI) was refused `PullAlreadyRunningError` until process restart. FIXED: all three ops now run under the COMMON `run_with_deadline` freeze guard (the rate_bridge_cache #1522 precedent; NEW `PULL_LEASE_IO_DEADLINE_S`=5 s, env `BRUTEX_PULL_LEASE_IO_DEADLINE_S` via the COMMON `resolve_env_seconds` fail-safe parse) — a wedged op is ABANDONED with ONE `pull_lease.io_wedged` WARN (enter: cross-host detection degraded for this pull; exit: the leftover lease self-heals by going stale within the 180 s TTL) and the flocks always release promptly; a guard-thread spawn failure under thread exhaustion degrades identically. Teeth: the wedged-clear regression HUNG the pre-fix guard exit 21.19 s (measured, fails-before) and exits < 5 s fixed; wedged enter-read and wedged first-refresh pinned too. HONEST (#999 stance): the abandoned daemon worker cannot be killed — at most one zombie per wedged op; the two flock OPENS themselves (`os.open` on the sidecars) remain unbounded pre-existing behaviour, named not fixed. **ROUND-4 REVIEW FOLD (MINOR — the guard catch narrowed to the guard's OWN failure modes):** `_bounded_lease_io`'s `except (DeadlineExceeded, RuntimeError)` was broader than its documented intent ("only the guard's own failure modes … a genuine code bug still propagates" — FALSE: `run_with_deadline` re-raises ANY fn-raised error on the caller thread, so an fn-raised `RuntimeError` was silently reclassified as a `pull_lease.io_wedged` wedged-volume event, masking the real cause; concrete path: a degenerately deep-nested `pull_lease.json` makes `json.loads` raise `RecursionError` — a `RuntimeError` subclass `_read_lease_file` did not catch). FIXED at the root, two arms: (a) the COMMON freeze guard gains the typed `config.deadline.DeadlineSpawnError` (a `RuntimeError` SUBCLASS raised iff the guard's own `Thread.start()` fails, original error on `__cause__` — pre-existing broad catchers like the rate_bridge_cache #1522 spawn owner are byte-compatible) and `_bounded_lease_io` now catches EXACTLY `(DeadlineExceeded, DeadlineSpawnError)` — an fn-raised `RuntimeError` propagates as the genuine code bug it is (fails-before pinned: previously swallowed + mislabelled), while a real spawn failure still degrades to the fallback with the ONE `io_wedged` WARN (`error_type=DeadlineSpawnError`, pinned); (b) the hostile-input scenario is closed WHERE IT BELONGS — `_read_lease_file` adds `RecursionError` to its decode catch (corrupt-file territory: the honest-unknown `None`, per the "a damaged lease can never break or falsely block a pull start" pledge; fails-before pinned at both the reader and the full `pull_lease_guard`, which now enters cleanly over a 100k-deep hostile lease with ZERO `io_wedged` WARNs); the `io_wedged` WARN detail reworded to name both sanctioned modes (abandoned wedged op / never-spawned). `config/deadline.py` (39/8) stays 100% line+branch with the new spawn-error + not-retyped pins. **Companion route fold (MINOR):** the `/pull-pipeline` route additionally OFFLOADS its whole launch body via `run_in_threadpool` (the app.py offload doctrine / #1522 event-loop-freeze class) — the launch's synchronous guard acquisition (two flock opens + the lease read + the fsync'd lease write, all lake-volume I/O) previously executed ON the uvicorn event loop, so a wedged volume froze the WHOLE dashboard at launch-click time; regression-pinned (`get_running_loop()` inside `BackgroundPullJob.start` must raise — fails-before verified). Honest residual: the OTHER launch routes (spot bulk / metadata / composite / contract fetch / sweep) still call `start()` inline — their lease I/O is now deadline-bounded by this fold, their flock opens remain the named pre-existing exposure. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), no rate-cap change; `pull_singleflight.py` (183/22) + `pull_jobs.py` 100% line+branch; ruff/`mypy --strict`/pyright clean on touched files. **Files:** brutex/adapters/groww/pull_singleflight.py, brutex/config/deadline.py (round-4 fold), brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py, brutex/cli.py, docs/runbooks/data-fetch-runday.md, tests/unit/{test_pull_singleflight,test_pull_jobs_singleflight,test_cli_retry_storm,test_config_deadline}.py. **Decision ID:** DEC-ACCOUNT-LEASE-CROSSHOST-001.

1589. **DEC-DERIVE-LOCK-VISIBILITY-001 — the movers `PrebuildGate` honors the CROSS-PROCESS derive lock: a SEPARATE-process derive (a CLI-launched pipeline or lake heal holding `<lake_root>/.locks/derive.lock`) now yields the honest `gated:true` `/api/v1/movers` payload with `source="cross_process"`, closing the named PrebuildGate follow-up of DEC-ENGINE-MISC-PACK-001 (#1288)** (2026-07-07 on `claude/blissful-curie-gp94rk`; item 8/10 of the polish pack; previously the gate was PROCESS-LOCAL by documented design, so a CLI derive could serve half-built partitions to `/movers` with no gate). The gate gains an optional injectable `cross_probe` (default `None` = byte-identical to today; consulted ONLY while locally idle, and OUTSIDE the gate lock so a slow lake volume never wedges local gating); a probe `OSError` fails OPEN with ONE `movers.gate.cross_probe_failed` WARN per outage; a non-`OSError` propagates (a genuine code bug is never swallowed). `gated_movers_payload` gains the ADDITIVE `source` key + a stable cross-process note (the pipeline note is byte-unchanged, pinned VERBATIM; legacy no-source snapshots keep the pipeline wording). `build_app` wires `derive_in_progress` over the store's lake root into the DEFAULT gate only, and the movers route snapshots the gate via `run_in_threadpool` (lake-volume I/O never on the event loop — the app.py offload doctrine). FIXED at the root: NEW pure `derive_lock.derive_lock_held_by_this_process` (an O(1) ZERO-I/O read of the existing reentrancy registry) is wired as the gate's `local_derive_probe` and consulted FIRST — a same-process holder now gates with the honest `source="local_derive"` + a note naming "this dashboard process (its own lake-heal recall)", and `source="cross_process"` is emitted only when NO thread of this process holds the lock (up to the one-poll probe-ordering race, self-corrected on the next poll); a gate wired with `cross_probe` ALONE still attributes cross_process (documented — `build_app` wires BOTH). Regression-pinned: the real `derive_write_lock` held in-process reads `local_derive` end-to-end (pre-fix: `cross_process`), and a raw registry-less flock (what a foreign process looks like) still reads `cross_process`. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX); `prebuild_gate.py` 100% line+branch (130/16); `derive_lock.py` stays 100% (61/6); ruff clean; zero new mypy/pyright errors. **Files:** brutex/dashboard/{prebuild_gate,app}.py, brutex/data/derive_lock.py, tests/unit/test_prebuild_gate.py, tests/integration/test_dashboard_movers_gate.py. **Decision ID:** DEC-DERIVE-LOCK-VISIBILITY-001.

actually aligning is a named follow-up decision") into `test_predicate_alignment_pin_vs_honesty_counter_1267` (the EXACT old fixture, both surfaces now read 1); NEW EQUIVALENCE PROOF `test_sql_cte_equivalent_to_classifier_over_one_lake` — one REAL lake exercising EVERY case class (exact-09:15 · late 09:16 · pre-09:15 09:14 · afternoon Muhurat · evening Muhurat), per-session SQL verdicts recomputed with the PRODUCTION fragments (`_IST_DATE_EXPR`/`_IST_TS_EXPR`/`_SESSION_OPEN_MINUTES`/`_MUHURAT_EXCLUSION_SQL`, imported never re-derived) asserted equal to `classify_daily_open` per session, plus production-totals parity (census == detector == 2/5); RAM; the `BRUTEX_*` worker env overrides provably CANNOT move the key — test-pinned; `BRUTEX_BENCH_BASELINE_KEY` valid-slug override wins, invalid raises fail-loud) + NEW env-gated measurement suite `tests/bench/test_absolute_baseline.py` over the registry `tests/bench/_abs_baseline_registry.py` (6 hot-path entries: bar_lookup · mask_eval_scalar · mask_and_vector_1m [the 50 M-floor canary op] · dedup_bloom_probe · dedup_lmdb_contains · result_append; house best-of-N-MIN `perf_counter_ns` idiom per DEC-CANARY-MINTIME-001, all round samples recorded — deliberately NOT the pytest-benchmark fixture, whose JSON layout would couple the gate to a third-party format the repo's gates never consumed) + committed per-hardware baselines at `tests/bench/baselines/<hardware_key>.json` (ns_per_op single unit; per-ENTRY decision_id + live-verifiable provenance + workload_hash; `tolerance_pct` STRUCTURALLY capped `[0, 100)` AND its failure multiplier `1 + tolerance/100` required FLOAT-EXACTLY below 2.0 (round-2 review fix: `math.nextafter(100, 0)` passed the raw range check while its multiplier ROUNDS to exactly 2.0 in IEEE double, letting an exact-2x slowdown return OK — the schema now rejects that one top-ULP value) so a 2x slowdown can NEVER pass any governed config — property-tested over the whole `[0, 100)` cap range incl. that float boundary (a rejected tolerance is asserted rejected, a legal one asserted to fail 2x); boundary law FAIL iff `measured > blessed x (1 + tolerance/100)`, strict `>`, equality passes — boundary-pinned; a MORE-than-4x suspicious speedup FAILS (strict `<` — an exactly-4.0x speedup passes with the staleness WARN only), a more-than-2x-up-to-4x speedup WARNs "baseline stale") + `scripts/ci/bench_baseline_gate.py` (validate/compare/capture/govern/key; exit contract 0 ok-or-LOUD-abstain / 1 numeric [the ONE bounded re-measure] / 2 structural-never-retried / 3 usage). bench-m4pro gains measure→compare (ONE bounded fresh-process re-measure before failing a NUMERIC regression; both reports archived in the 90-day `abs-bench` artifact)→capture→artifact steps + a GitHub-hosted `bless-baseline` job (the ONLY contents/PR-write holder — the self-hosted runner never holds a contents/PR-write token: its inherited workflow-level token is issues:write only, for its own alert steps; the candidate travels runner→artifact→verbatim API commit with no edit surface; main-ref + schedule/dispatch pinned; its job-level permissions carry `issues: write` alongside contents/PR write — a job-level permissions block ZEROES every unspecified scope, so without it the bless-failure alert's own `issues.create` was a guaranteed 403 silencing the exact escalation it exists for [round-2 review fix, wiring-pinned incl. an every-issues-writing-job-holds-issues-write sweep over both workflows]) + the failure-issue step now fires on `cancelled()` too (the DEC-MUTATION-ALERT-CANCELLED-001 #1511 idiom); ci.yml's REQUIRED `bench` job (a `ci-ok` member) gains two <10 s stdlib steps — schema `validate` on every run + the `govern` entry-cell diff gate on PRs, incl. LIVE `gh api` verification that a cited provenance run exists ON THIS REPOSITORY (the `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY` repo pin, threaded `cmd_govern` → `govern(repo_slug=)` → `_verify_cell_run` and belt-doubled in `make_gh_run_verifier` — a completed run on a fork/foreign repo is a BREACH and its slug is never even queried; a missing/malformed slug fails CLOSED exit 2; the round-1 hostile review's BLOCKER: without the pin any public fork keeping `bench-m4pro.yml` at the required path with a chosen head_sha satisfied the verification), is bench-m4pro.yml, completed, CONCLUDED `success` (a failed/cancelled run is not provenance), and `head_sha` == the embedded commit (a fabricated-but-ledgered bump is machine-refuted; API outage = fail-CLOSED with named remediation after 3x5 s retries). GOVERNANCE LAW (mechanical): a diff touching `tests/bench/baselines/` with a MODIFIED cell requires ALL of — a NEW decision id (≠ base cell's, ≠ bootstrap), that id in the SAME PR's MIGRATION.md ADDED lines TOGETHER WITH the literal entry key and the literal new value token exactly as serialized (e.g. `55.0`), a FRESH live-verified run URL — while ADDED cells ride the standing bootstrap authorization (THIS entry), REMOVED cells and top-level fingerprint/context changes need a ledgered note, and a DELETED file needs its filename in the added lines; no override env exists. BOOTSTRAP (Golden Rules #1/#10): this PR ships ZERO measured numbers — `tests/bench/baselines/` holds only README.md (the two goldens are EXPLICITLY-SYNTHETIC format fixtures, labelled in-file); the first baseline is measured by the REAL M4 Pro (3 process-fresh runs; capture REFUSES a noisy triple, cross-run spread > tolerance/2). Because the measurement suite ALWAYS emits the full registry, capture CARRIES an already-blessed cell field-for-field UNCHANGED when it is not in `replace_entries` (byte-identical — no silent-bump surface; its fresh measurement, noise included, is ignored), so the additive bless on a partial baseline and the runbook's single-entry re-bless fold full-registry runs without refusing (round-1 review MAJOR — the pre-fix `OverwriteRefusal` red-looped the scheduled job on any partial baseline); the candidate's top-level context/fingerprint are refreshed from the FRESH measurement on a first capture or a FULL re-bless (`replace_entries` ⊇ every blessed cell), so a fold that runs can never re-emit the stale interpreter (the round-1 review's second MAJOR); a PARTIAL re-bless keeps the existing context (carried cells were measured under it — the honest red stands). HONEST REACHABILITY (round-3 review): a STANDING `context.python` STRUCTURAL red cannot be healed by a dispatch re-bless — the compare step exits 2 BEFORE capture, and the capture step's `if:` carries GitHub's implicit `success()` (deliberate: a red run never mints a candidate), so the dispatch dies at compare; the documented recovery is REMOVAL-FIRST (the retiring-a-machine recipe: delete `tests/bench/baselines/<key>.json` in a PR whose ledger entry names the filename — governance-enforced — then the next scheduled run ABSTAINS green-but-loud and the FIRST-capture path refreshes context under the bootstrap id), while the FULL-replace context refresh serves the PROACTIVE still-green-compare re-bless — runbook context-re-bless section reconciled + the removal-first↔success-gated-capture coupling wiring-test-pinned (`test_runbook_context_drift_recovery_is_removal_first`). Auto-blessed via a `github-actions[bot]` PR the operator merges after ONE nudge (GITHUB_TOKEN-created PRs do not trigger CI — close/reopen or an empty commit makes the required `CI OK (aggregate gate)` report; stated in the bless PR body itself; NO PAT — a PAT on operator hardware would reopen the credential surface DEC-CI-FORK-PR-HARDEN-001 closed). Until then compare ABSTAINS green-but-LOUD (`::warning` + `needs_capture`/`baseline_missing`/`abstain_entries` job outputs + a distinct per-key `bench`-labelled tracking issue on scheduled runs + the candidate/bless PR as the visible artifact — never a fake pass, never a false red); every COMPARED green run prints the positive attestation `BENCH-ABS GATE RAN: compared N/6 …` (golden-pinned); the compare additionally runs a daily BELT re-asserting every blessed decision id is a token in docs/MIGRATION.md (a direct-push smuggle reds the next scheduled run). SKIP-HONESTY: the measured fragment set must EQUAL the registry exactly — a pytest skip/rename is a named STRUCTURAL fail, and the registry↔`REQUIRED_ENTRY_KEYS`↔`ENTRY_WORKLOADS` pins + a workload-hash literal golden fail shared CI before a hot path can silently vanish (S11: a workload-param change PR must remove the affected baseline cells with a ledgered note, or the next m4pro compare STRUCTURAL-fails loudly). Deviation from the operator's literal `--benchmark-compare` is ledgered here: native compare warns-and-passes with no matching saved run, keys on drift-prone machine_info, cannot express per-entry floors/abstain/governance — and the repo's own precedent (entry #158 DEC-P0-020, the Agent-2 finding inside that entry) already matched the inline-threshold idiom over `--benchmark-compare`; the operator's INTENT (committed absolute baseline; CI fails loudly on absolute regression) is satisfied strictly better. HONEST envelope: bench-m4pro stays a NON-required, non-PR check (DEC-M4PRO-PR-TRIGGER-001) — a regression is caught post-merge on push/daily-cron as a red run + issue, NOT as a merge blocker (closable only by the operator adding it to branch protection); the gate is dormant until the runner is online AND the first bless merges; sub-tolerance (<50% default) drift passes (the 1.1x ratio tiers + 50 M/s floor stay as complements, UNTOUCHED); micro-benchmarks of 6 keyed ops, not end-to-end sweep wall time; the artifact path inside `download-artifact` (candidate.json at job CWD) is contract-test-pinned but UNVERIFIED on a real dispatch until the runner runs it; the hardware key is a coarse fingerprint (two identical boxes share a baseline — accepted). `github-actions[bot]` joins `PR_AUTHOR_EXEMPT_PATTERN` in the zplus/DoR guards (bot bless PRs carry no human plan-first body; both directions redteam-pinned); auto-merge trust deliberately NOT extended — the human merge click IS the bless sign-off. 1531. **DEC-SWEEP-EXIT-INDEX-FASTPATH-001 — the exit_idx-native fast path through the sweep chunk loop (the #1186 honest-envelope residual, "an explicit FUTURE follow-up", now DONE): both trade simulators return each mask's trades WITH their exit-bar indices, the metrics tail consumes a certified index stream O(trades) instead of building the per-mask O(N_bars) `exit_ts`→index dict, the three inline ts-index dict copies in `sweep_driver.py` consolidate onto ONE COMMON `build_ts_index`, and the kernel arm gains a per-process BURN-IN SELF-CHECK with an autorevert latch — the safety net the ADR-0017 default-ON flip (#1532) rides on** (2026-07-06 on `claude/amazing-darwin-hb4caw`; ENGINE SCOPE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track; NO scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/audit-schema change; results byte-identical on BOTH flag arms — the frozen `_GOLDEN_CONTENT_HASH`/`_GOLDEN_RUN_ID` literals are UNCHANGED and reproduced). **MECHANISM:** (1) NEW stdlib-only, cycle-free `brutex/engine/exit_index.py` — `build_ts_index` (THE `{bar.timestamp: index}` builder, last-wins on a malformed duplicate exactly like the three historical inline comprehensions it consolidates at `sweep_driver.py` `build_equity_curve`/`_exit_pairs`/`_assert_trades_confined` — §11 COMMON), `bars_strictly_increasing` (the PRODUCER-side certificate: strictly increasing timestamps ⇒ index↔timestamp bijection ⇒ a trade's TRUE exit index provably equals the last-wins dict lookup, so the fast path can never diverge from the dict arm — the #1186 "on a malformed duplicate both arms use the identical dict" invariant is PRESERVED by construction: an uncertified window simply withholds indices and stays on the dict), and `exit_indices_consistent` (the O(trades) CONSUMER-side belt: positional length + range + per-trade `bars[idx].timestamp == exit_ts`; a negative index is refused BEFORE Python's silent wraparound could alias it). (2) `trade_sim.py` — `TradeSimWalker.run_with_exit_indices` records each closed trade's exit bar index at the ONE `_close` seam (`run()` is now its thin delegate — one batch walk, trades byte-identical); module-level `simulate_trades_with_exit_indices` certifies the window once (an honest extra O(N_bars) timestamp scan on an already-O(N_bars) walk) and returns `(trades, exit_indices | None)`. (3) `rust_trade_sim.py` — `_to_trade_and_exit` (the kernel record ALWAYS carried the exit index; the pre-#1186 mapping discarded it), `simulate_masks_with_exit_indices` (per-mask `(trades, exit_indices | None)` pairs under a DOUBLE certificate: window `bars_strictly_increasing` checked ONCE at construction + per-mask `_monotonic` kernel-record certification — a non-monotonic stream on a certified window is a kernel ordering regression, indices refused with one `rust_trade_sim.exit_indices_uncertified` WARN per instance, the mask served through the dict path), `simulate_masks` now the thin delegate; the Python-fallback arm rides the SAME walker index walk. (4) `sweep_driver.py` — `metrics_from_trades(..., exit_indices=None)`: consumed ONLY by the kernel arm via `_exit_pairs` (consistent stream → O(trades) pairs, NO dict; inconsistent stream → warn-once `exit_indices_demoted` + DEMOTE-TO-DICT-NOT-ORACLE — the dict computes identical pairs, so a demotion can never change results, only cost); the OFF arm ignores the hint entirely (pinned: a poisoned stream is inert). `_simulate_window` returns the pair; `metrics_for_mask` + `_score_fold` thread it; `sweep_run._iter_mask_metrics` rides the pair-shaped batch and threads each mask's indices into the tail (`_reattribute_chunk_failure` deliberately STAYS on the `metrics_for_mask` oracle — re-attribution wants the engine-agnostic per-mask chain, not the hint). **BURN-IN SELF-CHECK + AUTOREVERT (the default-ON safety net):** NEW `rust_metrics` primitives (`SELF_CHECK_SAMPLES=16`, `self_check_pending`/`consume_self_check_sample`, `disable_kernel`/`kernel_disabled` latch, `drawdown_compare_key` — ints exact, floats by `struct.pack('<d')` bit pattern so a signed-zero divergence cannot hide behind float equality; total on poisoned huge ints because ints are compared never packed; `reset_self_check_for_tests`) orchestrated in `sweep_driver._self_checked_drawdown`: for the first 16 kernel-served masks per process the Python `_drawdown_stats` oracle (friend-imported — ONE oracle source of truth) ALSO runs over the same exits and the 4-tuples are bit-compared; a MISMATCH ships the ORACLE value (a wrong kernel number is never persisted, not even the one exposing the bug), latches the kernel OFF for the process (`sweep_rust_metrics.kernel_autoreverted` ERROR, once) and `drawdown_stats_via_kernel` short-circuits thereafter (warn-once `kernel_disabled`); a passed compare consumes one sample. The counter/latch are the same documented no-global-mutable-state exception as the observability memo — a mismatch never changes RESULTS, only which engine computes them. `sweep_rust_metrics_enabled` is rewritten over the NEW ONE constant `SWEEP_RUST_METRICS_DEFAULT` (`_TRUTHY`→ON; `_FALSY`→OFF, the explicit kill switch — `_FALSY` defined on `sweep_lookahead` beside `_TRUTHY`, imported not copied; unset/whitespace-empty→the default constant; any OTHER unrecognised value→FAIL-SAFE OFF with one warn-once `flag_unrecognised` event — a typo'd kill switch still kills) — `False` in this entry, flipped by #1532. **MEASURED (sandbox ratio ONLY — NOT the §8 M4 Pro):** on a 20k-bar window with 200 trades the certified fast arm serves the ON tail in 0.319 ms vs the dict arm's 1.944 ms (**6.1×** on the tail; 1696. **DEC-DB-OPAGE-HONESTY-001 — the `/db` candle pager's implied O(page) claim reconciled to the HONEST O(total matched rows), + two production-scale (≥500k-row) benches that DOCUMENT the real complexity curve** (2026-07-08 on `claude/db-opage-honesty`; fix(dashboard); READ-ONLY viewer — ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope/vocab/rate/lake-schema/stored-bar/write-path change; docstring/comment + additive-bench ONLY, ZERO executable source change). Closes the MAJOR-11 finding: `dashboard/db_view.py::query_candles` / `query_option_candles` documented O(page)-in-partition-depth paging ("a click never materialises more than `limit` rows … regardless of how many years are stored"), but the page DATA query runs `… QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY timestamp …)=1 ORDER BY "timestamp" LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` — the QUALIFY dedup window hash-partitions the WHOLE matched row set and the ORDER BY sorts it BEFORE the LIMIT/OFFSET slice, so the DuckDB engine cost is O(total matched partition rows) (plus one Parquet footer open per file; min/max row-group stats prune only the WHERE date range, never the window/sort); LIMIT bounds ONLY the Python materialisation (the FIRST page is not cheaper than the whole scan) and a deep OFFSET is O(row-groups-up-to-offset) on top; the page total is a COUNT(DISTINCT timestamp), O(rows) first-per-write-generation and O(1) cached. FIX (Golden Rule #10 — make the CLAIM true, NOT the code faster): both reader docstrings + the inline page-query comment rewritten to the honest complexity (mirroring the already-honest `lake_read.dedup_qualify_latest_sql` envelope stated only there before), and the keep-FIRST `lake_read.dedup_qualify_sql` docstring gains the same O(total rows) / NOT-O(page) note. QUALIFY-SKIP OPTIMISATION DEFERRED (documented, not risked): a clean partition's keep-FIRST dedup is a logical no-op, but there is NO reliable O(1)/footer-only "clean" signal (the only detector is `COUNT(*) == COUNT(DISTINCT ts)`, itself an O(rows) scan) AND skipping the window would be a constant-factor win, not a complexity change — so the read-side dedup correctness guard (DEC-LAKE-READ-UNIQUE-001) stays ON; a named follow-up, never a correctness risk traded for a perf win. PRODUCTION-SCALE BENCHES (G8 + G9, additive `tests/` only): NEW `tests/bench/test_db_candle_query_production_scale_o1.py` builds a synthetic ≥500k-row spot 1minute partition and MEASURES `query_candles` page latency — the first page (offset 0) SCALES with stored rows (measured 2026-07-08 sandbox: 20.0 ms @ 20k vs 140.2 ms @ 520k → 6.99× for 26× rows, the anti-O(page) teeth: a true O(page) reader would be flat) and a deep OFFSET is not cheaper than the first page (140.2 ms vs 195.7 ms → 1.40×, both pay the full scan), both under a generous 8 s ABSOLUTE scan ceiling; PLUS a B-8 arm on `tests/bench/test_ledger_delta_o_page_o1.py` measuring the fresh window-ledger fold GROUP BY at ≥500k base rows (11.8 ms @ 10k vs 230.1 ms @ 500k → 19.52× for 50× rows, < 8 s), two orders above the prior 1k-10k pins and approaching the disclosed ~841k full-universe worst case (DEC-SUSPICION-SWEEP-FIXES-001 #1492). Every threshold carries generous measured slack (shared-CI robust tier, NOT strict M4-Pro); NONE asserts a false O(page)/O(1) flatness. A write-time page manifest (true O(page) reads) stays the named future work (#867 / #1025). GATES: `db_view.py` + `lake_read.py` are docstring/comment-only (100% line+branch unchanged — no executable diff); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` at the pre-change baseline; the two new/extended bench files pass (10 passed, 1 pre-existing skip) and the ledger module's ceiling-mechanism doc-pin stays green. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/data/lake_read.py`, `tests/bench/test_db_candle_query_production_scale_o1.py` (NEW), `tests/bench/test_ledger_delta_o_page_o1.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DB-OPAGE-HONESTY-001. 1617. **DEC-SWEEP-RESULTS-DEPTH-001 — Phase-3 "results depth" lands as ONE run-end post-hoc pass: per-finalist trade capture (oracle re-sim + parity tooth) with 1-minute-path MAE/MFE + intraday-path equity, VIX-stamped trades, per-combo aggregates (regime/VIX-band/event/entry-hour lenses), deterministic per-tuple sidecar trio + stamp, buy-&-hold baselines, behavioral twin families, the R30 min-drawdown-first preset law, the R33 60-entry dual-language phrase table, the R47 refusal-only SPAN-margin ROI mechanism, and the global cross-bucket top-100 artifact at the binding P3→P4 contract path — wired into `cmd_sweep_all` by ONE fenced, default-ON, kill-switchable run-end CLI adapter** (2026-07-07 on `claude/elegant-johnson-cgufi7`; feat(engine/ranking/cli); ENGINE HOT PATH UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, zero diffs to `_iter_mask_metrics`/`run_persisted_sweep`/the Rust kernel/`rank_combos`/`ranked_combo_to_result_row`/`ResultsStore._render_bytes`; the frozen `_GOLDEN_CONTENT_HASH`/`_GOLDEN_RUN_ID` pins pass UNMODIFIED — the pass writes ONLY new files in dedicated subtrees, never the store bytes). 1543. **DEC-FUTURES-EXEC-TRANSLATION-001 — the futures translation executor (Phase 5 of the one-click sweep law, R13/R14/R15): an INDEX winner's trades re-priced on the FRONT-MONTH-AT-TRADE-TIME futures contract — the options executor's futures twin, NEW BUILD** (2026-07-07 on `claude/wonderful-wright-17gyqj`; NEW `brutex/futures/` package + `brutex/costs/futures_costs.py` — ENGINE UNCHANGED NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, options path untouched (R12), no scope/vocab/rate change, ZERO existing dashboard/orchestrator file edited). THE LAW (sweep-oneclick-requirements-living R13/R14/R15 + the execution-translation mapping): after ranking on the PURE spot signal, an INDEX winner is auto-re-priced on the nearest UNEXPIRED monthly futures contract as of each trade's ENTRY timestamp, resolved from the REAL F&O registry expiry calendar — NEVER a computed last-Thursday formula; a STOCK winner routes to SPOT and is gracefully DEFERRED today (an explicit annotation NAMING the future stock scope decree — R11/CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 3 — never a crash, never silent); the futures leg is a DISPLAY ANNOTATION on the SAME result row that can never re-rank/filter/mutate the pure signal. **(a) Executor** (`brutex/futures/executor.py`): `FuturesSignal`/`FuturesLeg`/`FuturesBarWindow`/`MaterializedFuturesTrade` (the R24 every-field record: entry/exit ts+price, direction/side, lot_size×n_lots, exit_reason, gross/charges/net, R22 MAE/MFE from the contract's OWN 1-minute path, R31 VIX stamps — missing = honest None counted)/`RejectedFuturesTrade`/`FuturesRuleResult` (count-dict tally projected 1:1 onto `n_rejected_*` — no catch-all, no unreachable else); PINNED reject order **lot_size → cost_regime → no_contract → no_data → stale_bar** with the two pure DATE gates proven (never-called-seam tests) to fire BEFORE any registry/lake I/O; `route_execution` lives ABOVE the executor (INDEX_FUTURES / STOCK_SPOT_DEFERRED / UNSUPPORTED — the automatic instrument-kind rule, no UI knob) so the core stays instrument-agnostic; HONEST reachability (Golden Rule #10): the cost-regime branch is exercised today ONLY via the SYNTHETIC cited-regime fixture (a stock-future signal with a monkeypatched lot fed straight to `materialize_futures_trade`) — NO natural input reaches it (index futures are cost-free per the verified table and skip the gate; `signals_from_spot_trades` lifts real `ClosedTrade`s (VIX passthrough; `exit_reason` passthrough when the trade carries one, else the honest generic `"signal"`); `execute_futures_sim` appends ONE run_id-stamped hash-chained audit row (R28/R41/R43), emits ONE aggregate `futures.sim.unverified_cost_window` WARN (spans DERIVED from regime-table data), and runs the R45 differential over a run_id-seeded deterministic sample — a mismatch logs `futures.sim.differential_mismatch` ERROR + stamps `suspect` on the audit payload. R15 FILL LAW: OPTIMISTIC = PRECISE only — entry/exit at the minute bar's OPEN ± one tick ADVERSE per side (long buy=open+tick/sell=open−tick; short sell=open−tick/cover=open+tick — computed adverse-both-sides DIRECTLY, deliberately NOT inheriting `calculator._apply_slippage`'s documented `# CHECK SIGN` short-branch favorable ambiguity; the LONG arm is golden-pinned BYTE-EQUAL to `_apply_slippage(...,"long")`), floored at one tick; NEVER the favorable bar extreme; gap-open beyond SL/TP fills at the REAL open (the sweep fixed the exit ts — levels are never re-evaluated); 15:20/Muhurat forced exits fill at the inherited minute's open; zero-range bars degenerate cleanly; a volume-0 PRINTED futures bar is REAL + TRADABLE (STALE_BAR is OPT-IN `reject_stale_bars=True`, default OFF — expiry-afternoon volume collapse counted as-is); the pessimistic/worst leg is DEFERRED — structurally absent, not faked. ROLL PINS (each a named test): registry-beats-last-Thursday (a Wednesday-shifted registry expiry wins over the naive Thursday), expiry-day front = the EXPIRING contract (`>=` inclusive; 15:20 < 15:30 ⇒ no trade straddles expiry, plus the FuturesTradeInput same-IST-date R18 invariant makes an overnight/straddling trade unrepresentable), post-expiry tail → M+1 (never the dead M), M/M+1 co-trading = earliest-expiry-≥-entry-date (deterministic, ties on symbol, never liquidity-picked), single trade never blends two contracts (ONE `load_window` call spy-pinned; no PDH/PDL/prev-close/prior-contract read exists on the seam), holiday-shifted expiry VERBATIM through the `DDMmmYY` token, suffix-independence (hypothesis property: fills+MAE/MFE bit-identical with the post-exit suffix present/absent/extreme — the DEC-SWEEP-LOOKAHEAD-GUARD-001 discipline). **(b) Contract resolver** (`contract_resolver.py`): `RegistryFrontMonthResolver(lake_root)` reads `db_view.registry_path_for(lake_root/"instruments.duckdb")` → `RegistryStore.list_contracts(side=="FUT")` (each row = the REAL vendor-listed holiday-shifted `expiry_date` + the `contract_symbol` lake key), cached ONCE per underlying, selection delegated to the SHARED `movers_futures.select_near_month` (§11 COMMON — the ONE front-month source); HONEST: a corruption CHECKSUM, NOT tamper-evidence — no secret key, whoever can rewrite the payload can restamp it; re-run byte-identical, upstream spot artifacts untouched). O(1) STORY (R29, honest — reworded by the review round's O1-WORDING fix): per-trade resolution is one `select_near_month` sort-based pick over the underlying's FULL ONCE-cached FUT calendar — **O(M log M) where M is the whole accumulated calendar INCLUDING expired months** (the SHARED picker SORTS the live set — the ONE front-month source per §11 COMMON, deliberately not forked into a second min-scan picker; the registry deliberately retains expired months, `registry_store.py`'s incremental-skip reason for being, and no live filter is possible at cache-build time since `on_date` varies per historical trade: ~13 contracts/listed-year, ~78 for NIFTY 2020→2026, growing ~13/yr), NOT merely the ≤ ~3 currently-live serial months; M is bounded (dozens) + independent of trade count so per-trade stays effectively O(1) (O(contracts) first load, stated); per-trade fills are two O(1) dict probes after a ONCE-cached O(bars-in-contract) read (≤ ~3 month files, stated); MAE/MFE is O(bars-in-trade) (≤ ~375 min, stated); `tests/bench/test_futures_exec_o1.py` pins per-trade latency FLAT vs signal count (200→2,000) AND contract count (3→30 all-live AND the real registry shape: 3 live vs 60-expired+3-live) at the `_o1_tiers` two-tier ceiling — never an O(1)-total claim. Repro: snapshot Mon 2025-09-29 over a lake holding Wed 2025-09-24 (close 24000) + Thu 2025-09-25 (close 24100) with Fri 2025-09-26 (the true immediately-preceding session) a HOLE → the baseline silently read 24100 from TWO sessions back; for LTP 24650 the screen printed **2.2822%** where the correct Friday-based figure is **0.2033%** — an unmarked, silently-wrong day-over-day %change. **FIX:** (a) NEW COMMON `calendars/nse.previous_trading_session(d, *, exchange=None)` — back-walk via the STRICT `is_trading_day_checked` (weekends + listed holidays stepped over; special-weekend Budget sessions honoured; termination guaranteed by the checked variant's coverage raise); past the coverage floor it ABSTAINS (`None`) with ONE `calendar.previous_session_coverage_exhausted` warning — never a guessed session; NSE/BSE/None parity + eager ValueError on a bad exchange. (b) the baseline readers become ENRICHED resolvers with byte-identical VALUE seams: `movers_snapshot.resolve_prev_close` → `PrevDayBaseline(value, found_date)` and `movers_futures.resolve_prev_oi` → `PrevOiBaseline(value, found_date)` (the OI 1-day scan physically STAYS in movers_futures — the DEC-LAKE-READ-UNIQUE-001 bypass-gate allowlist keeps its wired dedup entry for the module); `_prev_day_close`/`_prev_day_oi` are now thin `.value` wrappers (every historical pin green unmodified); `_prior_session_last_from_minute` APPENDS its found date (3-tuple — index-append, [0]/[1] stable). (c) ONE pure COMMON `prev_baseline_provenance(found_date, snapshot_day, *, exchange)` → `(found_iso|None, contiguous|None)` — no baseline → (None, None); calendar abstain → (iso, None) with the value STILL SERVED; else (iso, found == expected). (d) the three candidate loops stamp the defaulted additive fields on MoverSnapshot/FuturesMover/OptionMover, judging futures/options close + OI INDEPENDENTLY (the null-OI-1day edge: a prior 1-day bar with a real close but NULL OI sends the OI baseline to the minute fallback on a DIFFERENT day — regression-pinned prev_close_contiguous=True while oi_baseline_contiguous=False with exactly one kind=oi WARN), and emit `movers.prev_baseline_noncontiguous` ONLY on a strictly-False verdict — deduped per (symbol, kind), hard-capped 20/build with ONE `movers.prev_baseline_noncontiguous_suppressed` summary (function-local `_NoncontiguousWarnState` + reset seam; never module-global state). (e) row projectors EMIT-ON-FALSE: the additive keys appear ONLY on a False verdict, so contiguous AND abstained payloads are byte-for-byte the pre-fix wire — GOLDEN-PINNED both arms on all three tabs (FULL-row dict equality across a weekend AND across Holi 2024 + a FROZEN additive-key-NAME set pin); the NON-CONTIGUOUS repro golden pins the SERVED close still 24100 + `prev_close_session="2025-09-25"`/`prev_close_contiguous=false` + exactly one WARN naming found + expected; the ABSTAIN golden (pre-2020 snapshot) pins value-served/keys-omitted/no-WARN. (f) FRONTEND `movers.html`: the change/%chg (and oi_chg/oi_chg_pct) cells append a trailing " *" gated STRICTLY `=== false` (the " ~" moneyness-marker precedent, appended pre-esc so the marker rides the same escape), and the note gains " · * baseline is not the immediately-preceding NSE session (nearest-prior shown)" when any rendered row is flagged — textContent-only, substring-presence pinned (honest envelope: presence, not execution — no headless JS runner). **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this makes the wrong %change HONEST — stamped + warned + marked — it does NOT fix the number (the correct remediation is filling the hole: re-pull the missing session; the screen never fabricates a bar); a Diwali Muhurat day is a NON-session to the primitive (a Muhurat-bar baseline reads non-contiguous — accepted + documented); the `exchange` argument is inert parity today (NSE ≡ BSE holiday sets 2020-2026) and a nonstandard lake exchange dir abstains via `_calendar_exchange` (never a route 500); The catching unit test carried an unconditional `pytest.skip` documenting exactly this, and the module docstring FALSELY claimed the bullish 78% was screenshot-verified. **THE FIX (math single source of truth = `rust/trading-core`, DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 #441 — Python grows NO math copy):** `fib.rs::FibLevels` gains four i64 fields `retrace_bull_{23,38,62,78}_paisa = round_half_even(pdl + ratio * range)` (token-mirrored to the bearish lines: ratio-multiply BEFORE add, the one `f64` range cast, the crate's banker's rounding); deliberately NO `bull_50` — the bullish midpoint IS the shared `retrace_50_paisa` (exact integer-sum midpoint), 0%/100% anchors are pdl/pdh, extensions above PDH stay the existing (already-correct) `ext_up_*`. `python.rs`: NEW `FIB_COMPUTE_LIST_LEN = 19` for the `compute_fib_levels` FFI projection (original 15 order UNTOUCHED, bull tail APPENDED last, `debug_assert_eq!`); `FIB_LEVELS_LEN` stays **15** — the FROZEN `evaluate_with_levels` evaluator ABI (the two surfaces were an accidental 15-tuple PUN, now two documented distinct constants; `with_levels_rejects_wrong_fib_len` unchanged at 15); the evaluator's `FibLevels` rebuild zeroes the 4 unread bull fields; the `MAX_ANCHOR_PAISA` overflow proof notes the bull max `pdl + 0.786r < pdh + 3.236r` (bound unchanged). Python `fib_levels.py`: dataclass + 15→19 tuple-unpack + `get_by_bullish_label` remapped to the `retrace_bull_*` fields ("0"/"50"/"100" → the shared pdl/midpoint/pdh fields, extensions unchanged). **NAMING:** `retrace_bull_` not `retrace_up_` — avoids overloading the `ext_up_` axis vocabulary (extensions point up from PDH; the bull retracements sit INSIDE the band). **REJECTED ALTERNATIVES:** a direction-parameterised kernel (crate doctrine is token-explicit greppable ratio lines — one literal per level, mirrored Python↔Rust); 1580. **DEC-SOAK-REAL-TIER-001 — a REAL self-hosted multi-hour soak tier + a pure importable drift detector (RSS-ceiling / fd-growth / p99-latency-drift), with the false "24h soak REACHABLE" #208 claim honestly corrected and the un-completable 10M escape hatch fenced so it can no longer self-kill** (2026-07-06 on `claude/serene-maxwell-0irkzn`; feat(observability)+ci+test+docs; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX, F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; NO Groww vendor/rate/scope/vocab change; scope-locked to CI + observability + tests + docs). **THE PROBLEM (verified against the live repo):** `stress-nightly.yml` pinned `timeout-minutes: 60` on `ubuntu-24.04`, its `STRESS_EVENTS=10_000_000` "24h soak" dispatch was threaded into ONE sequential `pytest tests/stress -m stress`, and the alert gate was `if: failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule'` (a dispatched soak's self-kill was eyeball-only). `tests/stress/__init__.py` advertised `STRESS_DURATION_S=86400` which NO test read (dead knob). MIGRATION.md #208 (lines 2910/2925) claimed the 10M soak was "REACHABLE" — FALSE per Golden Rule #10: a 10M run of `test_audit_chain_sustained` alone linearly extrapolates to ~16.7 h (5000 events ≈ 30 s → 2000×) and the 60-min job timeout hard-kills it at ~1/17th complete. **WHAT SHIPPED:** (1) NEW pure `brutex/observability/process_probe.py` — the ONE COMMON cross-platform RSS+fd source of truth (Linux `/proc/self/status` VmRSS primary; `resource.getrusage` `ru_maxrss` fallback for the macOS self-hosted tier, bytes→KiB normalised, documented PEAK-not-current so the RSS rule is an absolute CEILING backstop not a growth slope — reviving the class the removed PR-#99 ru_maxrss gate abandoned; `/dev/fd` fd fallback; `None` = honest abstain, never a fabricated 0). `tests/stress/test_memory_growth.py::_read_rss_kib` now delegates to it (one RSS source, Golden Rule #11). (2) NEW pure `brutex/observability/soak_drift.py` — `SoakDriftMonitor` modelled on the in-repo `pull_health.py` precedent: it wraps the hysteresis-aware `SLADetector` with THREE CRITICAL GREATER_THAN rules (`soak.rss_ceiling` = latest RSS > ceiling · `soak.fd_growth` = latest.fd − baseline.fd > tolerance · `soak.p99_drift` = p99(latest)/p99(baseline) > ratio), mirrors each into a `MetricRegistry` gauge, and routes a breach/recovery edge to blanket-GUARDED callbacks (a raising alert sink — a Telegram outage — can never mask a breach nor crash the hours-long run, graft G4). Every provider abstains (`None`, the SLADetector skip contract) when its inputs are unavailable (probe abstained / baseline unset / empty-latency window / zero-latency baseline). The p99 uses the ONE COMMON `brutex.metrics.compute.percentile` (graft G3 — `_percentile` promoted to public `percentile`, linear-interp over a SORTED copy, for BOTH windows so the ratio is never a nearest-rank-vs-linear mismatch; `_percentile = percentile` back-compat alias). (3) NEW `SweepAlerter.soak_drift(rule, observed, threshold, detail)` — CRITICAL, `PHASE_BLOCKED` kind (the 0.0-coalescing precedent `pull_halted`/`vendor_down` use), deduped per rule, silent no-op when Telegram is disabled. (4) NEW `tests/stress/test_soak_sustained.py` — the ONE wall-clock driver behind the pure detector (ingest AuditWriter append + sweep `combo_digest` binned into time windows, per-op perf_counter latencies, per-window RSS/fd sampled and fed to the monitor; the HARD gate asserts NO DETERMINISTIC (RSS-ceiling / fd-growth) drift breach + chain integrity + ≥1 window — `soak.p99_drift` is OBSERVE-ONLY (neither the HARD gate NOR the real-time push), filtered out of the assertion; see the post-review correction below). TWO entry points, ONE code path (SCALABLE): `test_soak_short` (`@stress`, FIXED short budget, parametrised over tiny durations — the honest nightly regression that runs the REAL driver so no long-only path is dishonestly pragma'd) and `test_soak_sustained` (`@soak`, honours the full `STRESS_DURATION_S` — the live wiring of the previously-dead knob). Neither is coverage-measured (`[tool.coverage.run] source=["brutex"]` excludes `tests/`), so the 100% claim rides only on the pure modules. (5) NEW `.github/workflows/soak-selfhosted.yml` — the REAL tier: weekly cron + `workflow_dispatch(soak_minutes)`, `runs-on: [self-hosted, macos, m4pro]` (verify-m4pro/bench-m4pro precedent), **`timeout-minutes` = `soak_minutes + 30`** applied at BOTH the job level AND as a per-step bound (graft G2 belt-and-suspenders — the SELF-KILL FIX: a duration-DERIVED timeout can never re-open the fixed-60 trap) [MECHANISM CORRECTED by review-fix (vi): the originally-shipped `${{ fromJSON(inputs.soak_minutes || '360') + 30 }}` expression was INVALID — GHA expressions have no arithmetic operators — so the derivation now runs as shell arithmetic in a `plan` job feeding `fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.timeout_minutes)`], `STRESS_DURATION_S = soak_minutes × 60` (same plan-job derivation), `pytest tests/stress -m 'stress or soak'`, artifact upload always, and an "open issue on failure" that fires on BOTH schedule AND dispatch. The soak driver WIRES the `SoakDriftMonitor`'s `on_breach` to `SweepAlerter.soak_drift`, so the INSTANT a MONOTONE (`soak.rss_ceiling` / `soak.fd_growth`) rule edges the CRITICAL Telegram alert fires in real time — a trigger-independent AUTOMATIC signal (CLAUDE.md §11), a silent no-op when Telegram is disabled (the noisy `soak.p99_drift` rule is OBSERVE-ONLY, excluded from the push — see the post-review correction below — the original entry described this as active while the ONLY driver's `on_breach` was still a local list, the exact "shipped DORMANT" trap of DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001). (6) `stress-nightly.yml` honestly reclassified as a ~5-min ubuntu regression gate + a GUARD step (graft G5) that REFUSES `STRESS_EVENTS > 200000` (pointing at soak-selfhosted.yml, so the un-completable 10M path can never launch on the tier that physically cannot finish it) + the dispatch alert gate broadened so a manual mini-run failure is not eyeball-only. (7) #208's two "REACHABLE" lines struck-through + corrected in place; `tests/stress/__init__.py` two-budget docstring rewritten to the honest three-tier model. **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** this does NOT claim a 24h run happens in PR CI — the PR/unit tier verifies the drift LOGIC (100% line+branch on synthetic series) + a few-second real driver run; the ubuntu nightly is a ~5-min regression gate; ONLY the scheduled self-hosted job runs the multi-hour wall-clock, and only for the dispatched `soak_minutes` (default weekly = 6 h). `ru_maxrss` on macOS is a PEAK so the RSS rule is a ceiling backstop, not a slope. NAMED FOLLOW-UPS (recorded in ADR-0018, NOT built): a queue-age watchdog for an unregistered self-hosted runner; a Linux self-hosted soak variant. **TESTS:** NEW `tests/unit/test_observability_process_probe.py` (13) + `test_observability_soak_drift.py` (15) — both modules 100% line+branch on synthetic rising/flat/spiky/leak series; `test_notifications_sweep_alerts.py` +2 (soak_drift content + disabled-sink silent-no-op pin, sweep_alerts stays 100%); `test_metrics_compute.py` +1 (public `percentile` is the promoted alias); the short soak driver runs in the normal suite. **COVERAGE:** `process_probe.py` (35/10) + `soak_drift.py` (93/20) + `sweep_alerts.py` (209/18) ALL 100.00% line+branch; ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` clean on every touched module. **Files:** `brutex/observability/process_probe.py`, `brutex/observability/soak_drift.py`, `brutex/metrics/compute.py`, `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py`, `.github/workflows/soak-selfhosted.yml`, `.github/workflows/stress-nightly.yml`, `tests/stress/test_soak_sustained.py`, `tests/stress/test_memory_growth.py`, `tests/stress/__init__.py`, `tests/unit/test_observability_process_probe.py`, `tests/unit/test_observability_soak_drift.py`, `tests/unit/test_notifications_sweep_alerts.py`, `tests/unit/test_metrics_compute.py`, `pyproject.toml` (soak marker), `docs/adr/0018-real-soak-tier.md`, `docs/STANDARDS_100PCT.md` (row 11 + §closed-findings + §gate matrix + §task list reconciled — added by review-fix (v)), `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SOAK-REAL-TIER-001. (Ledger: high-jump numbering above the live max per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001 practice — uniqueness is the gate; re-verified before push.) **POST-REVIEW CORRECTIONS (same PR, adversarial-review fixes — Golden Rule #10):** (i) **`soak.p99_drift` demoted to OBSERVE-ONLY, removed from BOTH the HARD CI gate AND the real-time push.** The review reproduced a ~15% false-fail rate on an IDLE box (later/baseline p99 ratios spiking to 8–9× vs the threshold 2.0): a sub-second window's few ops are fsync-per-append-bound (`audit.append` fsyncs every record), so a window's p99 is dominated by transient fsync/GC/scheduler spikes — comparing every later window's p99 to a single warm first-window baseline fires on NOISE, not drift. On the shared ubuntu nightly (worse IO jitter) the flake rate is higher; a gate that cries-wolf ~15% of runs would auto-open false CRITICAL `bug,stress`/`bug,soak` issues and train the operator to ignore soak alerts (the opposite of §11). FIX: `_assert_healthy` now hard-gates ONLY the DETERMINISTIC oracles (RSS ceiling + fd growth + audit-chain integrity); `soak.p99_drift` breaches are filtered out of the assertion (`rule != RULE_P99_DRIFT`). The final fix (9f538e38) then ALSO excluded p99 from the real-time push — the driver's `_on_breach` early-returns for p99 via the shared `_fires_realtime_push` predicate BEFORE calling `alerter.soak_drift(...)` (pinned by `test_p99_drift_is_observe_only_not_a_realtime_push`) — because the sub-second-window p99 oscillates, so the detector fires a fresh OK→BREACH edge per up-crossing and pushing each would storm the operator on non-regression noise. So p99 fires NEITHER the HARD gate NOR the real-time push: it stays visible ONLY via the monitor's structlog breach warning + the `brutex_soak_p99_ratio` gauge (the sweep_alerts.py `soak_drift` docstring + the driver docstrings state this). HONEST GAP (Golden Rule #10): a genuine multi-hour p99 climb is therefore NOT auto-alerted — a smoothed/sustained-p99 push rule is a named follow-up, not claimed done. (ii) **The real-time drift alert (RSS/fd only) is now genuinely WIRED (was dormant).** The original ship claimed the running soak "fires the CRITICAL Telegram alert the instant a rule edges", but the ONLY driver's `on_breach` appended to a local list and `SweepAlerter.soak_drift` had ZERO callers repo-wide (the exact "shipped DORMANT" trap CLAUDE.md records for DEC-PULL-HEALTH-MONITOR-001). FIX: `test_soak_sustained._drive` now builds a `SweepAlerter()` and its `on_breach` calls `alerter.soak_drift(...)` adapting the `SLAEvent` (DEC-PULL-HEALTH-WIRING-001 precedent) — a best-effort push, silent no-op when Telegram is disabled (CI/dev), genuinely firing only on a Telegram-configured self-hosted soak. (iii) **The 10M escape-hatch fence no longer bypasses on the underscore form.** `stress-nightly.yml`'s guard used `[ "$STRESS_EVENTS" -gt "$max" ] 2>/dev/null`, which cannot parse the DOCUMENTED canonical value `10_000_000` (bash `[ -gt ]` chokes on underscores; `2>/dev/null` swallowed the error and the `if` fell through to "passed"), so the un-completable 10M run could still launch on the 60-min ubuntu tier and self-kill — defeating the fence's entire purpose. FIX: strip underscores (`ev=${STRESS_EVENTS//_/}`), then STRICTLY refuse any non-numeric input via `case "$ev" in ''|*[!0-9]*)` before the `-gt` comparison — so `10_000_000` is now correctly refused for exceeding the ceiling and a garbage string is refused outright, never error-suppressed into a pass. (iv) **`soak-selfhosted.yml` script-injection closed (SEC-1).** The "Show runner identity" step interpolated the `workflow_dispatch` input RAW into a `run:` shell (`echo "Soak minutes: ${{ github.event.inputs.soak_minutes || '360' }}"`), so a dispatch value with shell metacharacters would execute arbitrary code on the operator's persistent self-hosted M4-Pro (the job holds an `issues: write` token). FIX: pass the value via step `env: SOAK_MINUTES` and reference `$SOAK_MINUTES` in the script — DATA not code, the same env-indirection `stress-nightly.yml` already uses for `stress_events` (the three `fromJSON()`-guarded uses were already injection-safe; this raw echo was the one exception). (vi) **Round-6 BLOCKER: the duration-derived timeout was expression arithmetic — syntactically IMPOSSIBLE in GHA (SOAK-R6-1/OH6-1).** GitHub Actions expressions support ONLY `( ) [ ] . ! < <= > >= == != && ||` — no `+`/`*` — so the shipped `${{ fromJSON(soak_minutes || '360') + 30 }}` (job + step timeout) and `${{ ... * 60 }}` (`STRESS_DURATION_S`) were invalid workflow-file expressions: every trigger (weekly cron AND dispatch) would fail startup validation, NO job would run — including the `failure() || cancelled()` issue watchdog — reproducing the exact silent-death pathology this decision exists to close (and no PR gate could catch it: the file is YAML-valid, the workflow has no `pull_request` trigger). FIX: a tiny GitHub-hosted `plan` job derives `timeout_minutes=$((m + 30))` / `duration_s=$((m * 60))` in SHELL arithmetic (input digits-validated with the SAME underscore-strip + `case` fence as (iii) — never error-suppressed into `$(( ))`), and the soak job consumes `${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.timeout_minutes) }}` (a bare `fromJSON` of a precomputed needs-output IS valid) at BOTH the job and step level + `STRESS_DURATION_S` from `needs.plan.outputs.duration_s` — the "duration-DERIVED timeout" claim now ships WORKING; only the computation site moved. Verified: YAML parse + a raw-text scan asserting NO arithmetic remains in any `${{ }}` and every `needs.*.outputs.*` reference resolves (actionlint unavailable in the fix container — GitHub binary downloads blocked). ADR-0018 §2 item 3 wording reconciled; a garbage dispatch input now fails the operator-watched `plan` job (the soak job is skipped; the watchdog covers the SOAK job, the unattended-cron risk). (vii) **Soak drift artifact was pointed at the wrong temp root on the ONLY tier it runs on (SOAK-R6-2/SEC6-1).** The upload glob `/tmp/pytest-*` was copied from the ephemeral-ubuntu stress-nightly, but on the persistent macOS runner pytest's basetemp lives under `TMPDIR` (`/var/folders/.../T/`) so the glob matched NOTHING (`if-no-files-found: ignore` → a silently-empty artifact after a multi-hour failure) — and under an unset-TMPDIR daemon config it would instead match OTHER local pytest runs' temp trees (`pytest-of-<user>` retains the last 3 basetemps of ANY run) and upload them to a PUBLIC-repo artifact. FIX: the pytest step pins `--basetemp "$RUNNER_TEMP/soak-tmp"` (job-scoped, cleaned between runs) and the artifact uploads `${{ runner.temp }}/soak-tmp/**` — both failure modes closed. (viii) **`test_memory_growth`'s RSS backstop no longer computes a growth DELTA from the macOS `ru_maxrss` PEAK (OH6-3).** The (1) delegation of `_read_rss_kib` to the COMMON `read_rss_kib` silently changed behaviour on the macOS stress tier: off-Linux the reader fell back to the process-lifetime PEAK, and `_measure_growth`'s `rss_after − rss_before` then gated a PEAK-delta — violating `process_probe.py`'s own "NEVER as a growth slope" contract, contradicting the module docstring's "off-Linux the backstop is skipped", and partially re-importing the PR-#99 objection class (a legitimate large TRANSIENT allocation raises the peak where Linux current-VmRSS-after-gc would not). FIX: NEW slope-safe `process_probe.read_rss_kib_current()` (the `/proc` CURRENT-value path ONLY; `None` elsewhere — the peak fallback is never consulted, pinned by a must-not-call test); `test_memory_growth._read_rss_kib` delegates to IT, restoring the documented Linux-only backstop skip — the macOS resource-ceiling signal class stays where it belongs, the soak tier's `SoakDriftMonitor` RSS-CEILING rule; `process_probe.py` stays 100% line+branch (+2 unit tests). (ix) **`test_audit_chain_sustained.py`'s docstrings still advertised the retracted 10M/24h dispatch route (OH6-2)** — "Local 24h soak: `STRESS_EVENTS=10_000_000` via `workflow_dispatch`" / "the manual soak provides the real 24h soak target" / "for local 24h soak runs" were verbatim survivors of the exact claim (7) retracts (the fence now REFUSES that dispatch); rewritten to the three-tier model (nightly count ≤ 200000; the real soak is the DURATION-bounded `test_soak_sustained` on soak-selfhosted.yml). FIX: slack scales — `timeout_minutes = m + 30 + m/6` (360 → 450) — AND the raw tree is no longer uploaded: a bounded summarize step captures the tree listing + the last 64 KiB of each log/JSONL into `soak-drift-summary/` (the chain was already verified in-run by the pytest oracle; also caps the weekly public-artifact storage burn). **(OH7-1)** the soak tier's advertised real-time Telegram push was dormant-BY-CONFIGURATION and the auto-opened issue body asserted unhedged that it "fired": the workflow wires ZERO `BRUTEX_TELEGRAM_*` env / secrets, and `SweepAlerter` is a silent no-op without them. 1554. **DEC-GPU-GATE-RECONCILE-001 — ADR-0004 GPU-gate reconcile: Status PROPOSED → ACCEPTED (CPU-first arm EXECUTED + MEASURED), the never-run §6 tri-platform micro-benchmark RETIRED as scheduled work + RETAINED as a dormant FAIL-CLOSED PRECONDITION, mechanically pinned by a new drift-pin test** (2026-07-06 on `claude/stoic-davinci-7c7xp0`; docs + ONE new test, ZERO `brutex/`/`rust/` source change). GROUND TRUTH (verified 2026-07-06): ADR-0004 (DEC-GPU-ACCELERATION-ADR-001 #410, 2026-06-02) still read "Status: PROPOSED" and its §6 hard gate promised a tri-platform micro-benchmark (Rust-CPU baseline vs MLX-on-M4-Pro vs CuPy-on-cloud-NVIDIA) + a "comparison table the operator requires" filled with measured Current/Proposed/Δ numbers — that benchmark NEVER RAN (no MLX/CuPy code anywhere in `brutex/` or `rust/` — grep + AST re-verified this session; no CI job — `verify-m4pro.yml:77-80` reports the GPU device informationally only; `BRUTEX_GPU_OFFLOAD` exists in docs only), while the gate's FIRST leg's KERNEL was built + measured — at MICROBENCH scale (94,000-bar/~752 KB cache-resident bitset, single-core, dev/CI runner; NOT the leg's own ~770 MB multi-threaded envelope — round-2 review precision over this entry's original "satisfied" wording) — the SAME DAY the ADR landed (#411 measured 964 → 1,575 M ops·s⁻¹ bit-exact; #413 resident bars; #417 Rayon multi-core, measured on a 4-core dev/CI container; the 33B SLA is now a REAL M4-Pro hard gate, `tests/bench/test_full_sweep_extrapolation.py`) yet §4/§5.2 still called the kernel "(still-to-be-built)"/"roadmap" — the D-7 staleness `VERIFICATION_2026-06-03_INSTITUTIONAL_ARCH.md:106` flagged and nobody reconciled for a month (proof prose preconditions rot). DISPOSITION (`docs/adr/0004-gpu-acceleration.md` amended in place — the ADR is its own decision record, the sanctioned vehicle): (a) Status → ACCEPTED with an honest dated note (CPU-first arm EXECUTED + MEASURED #411/#413/#417; GPU arms DORMANT; the "no GPU code lands without the §6 gate" clause carried forward verbatim); (b) §6 RETIRED as scheduled work + RETAINED as a dormant FAIL-CLOSED PRECONDITION any future GPU-offload PR must satisfy FIRST — per-leg status now honest (baseline: kernel BUILT + measured at MICROBENCH scale — 94K-bar/~752 KB cache-resident bitset, single-core, dev/CI runner #411 + 4-core dev/CI-container Rayon scaling #417, `tests/bench/test_supermask_kernel_bench.py`; the §6-scale ~770 MB MULTI-THREADED baseline measurement stays OWED by the future benchmark itself — a round-2 hostile-review RELABEL over this entry's original "SATISFIED with measured figures" wording, which conflated the cache-resident single-core microbench with the leg's DRAM-streaming envelope; the same context tag added to the GUARANTEE_CHARTER §4 rows quoting 964→1,575; MLX + CuPy "NEVER RUN — DORMANT" with the reason each is unexecutable today), the dangling operator-table promise replaced by a CONDITIONAL deliverable (the Current/Proposed/Δ table was NEVER produced; it is produced if-and-only-if a GPU port is proposed — nothing the operator asked for is deleted; disposition surfaced for operator ack in the PR body's "Operator action required" section as a SEVERABLE item); (c) the stale "(still-to-be-built)"/"roadmap … NEON popcount" wording struck via dated brackets (the shipped kernel is scalar-autovec + Rayon, NOT hand-NEON — the D-7 class-2 overstatement not repeated); (d) "the real ~770 MB bitset" relabeled a spec SIZING ESTIMATE (`TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md:182` — the benchmark must first measure the actual artifact); every §4/§6 speedup figure verified ALREADY labeled "(estimate)" — NO numeric claim changed anywhere. MECHANICAL PIN (the #1492 G3 pattern): NEW `tests/unit/test_gpu_gate_drift_pin.py` walks `brutex/**/*.py` (AST-level — no `import mlx`/`cupy` in any form, no non-docstring `BRUTEX_GPU_OFFLOAD` string constant, and no non-docstring LITERAL GPU-rooted module-path string constant, so the dynamic-import shapes `importlib.import_module("cupy")` / `__import__("mlx.core")` are caught via their string argument — round-2 hostile-review fix; all four spellings now detected + teeth-pinned, numba-CPU usage pinned sanctioned, with the rebound-root alias `import numba as nb; nb.cuda` disclosed alongside the computed-string residual); docstring removal-notes sanctioned per the repo's removed-flag convention; 355 py / 39 rs on the FINAL post-merge tree (re-measured 2026-07-07 after the origin/main absorbs — main-side modules such as `brutex/observability/bench_baseline.py` + `brutex/data/greeks_enrich_pass.py` joined the scan, all outside this change set;
