THE LIMBO: DEC-CLAUDE-AUTOMATION-001 (#831, 2026-06-19) shipped `docs/runbooks/claude_automation.md` §3 — an opt-in `.github/workflows/claude-autofix.yml` snippet (`anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`; triggers `pull_request` + `issue_comment: created`; `permissions: {contents: write, pull-requests: write, issues: write}`; `secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; sole gate `vars.CLAUDE_AUTOFIX_ENABLED == 'true'`) "job-gated … so it stays dormant until enabled". ZERO WIRING (grep re-verified 2026-07-07 against the reconstructed tree — the original "13" file count was stale transcript-replay data from the destroyed pre-reconstruction base, corrected by the reconstruction round-1 review; the zero-references substance was and is true): `.github/workflows/` holds 18 files, none referencing autofix (`grep -rniE 'autofix|auto-fix|claude-autofix' .github/workflows/` exits 1); a repo-wide grep for `claude-autofix|CLAUDE_AUTOFIX|claude-code-action|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` hit ONLY the runbook §3 + ledger #831 — no secret, no variable, no test, no code. THE FOUR DISQUALIFIERS: (1) never wired + redundant — dormant since 2026-06-19 with zero uptake while the runbook's own §1 zero-click merge loop (auto-merge on green) already works without it; (2) security-regression vector — an `issue_comment`-triggered job runs in BASE-repo context on attacker-authored input on this PUBLIC repo, and the snippet carried secrets + contents:write with NO author-trust gate, re-opening exactly the privileged-trigger class DEC-CI-FORK-PR-HARDEN-001 (#1180) closed; author-trust gating alone would NOT bound the prompt-injection envelope of an agentic write-capable job whose prompt surface is comment/PR text; (3) sweep blind spot — the #1180 directory sweep (`test_no_workflow_run_job_checks_out_pr_head`) filters ONLY `workflow_run`/`pull_request_target`, so a verbatim ship would have bypassed the guard suite that hardened the repo; (4) limbo arithmetic — enablement is owner-manual (a session cannot add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or flip the repo variable, runbook §4), so SHIP merely converts doc-limbo into disabled-workflow-limbo, and the snippet's action inputs were self-declared UNVERIFIED (Golden Rule #1 forbids encoding them). WHAT SHIPPED: (a) runbook §3 replaced by a dated RETIRED banner (REQUIREMENTS.md-stub style) recording the decision, the zero-wiring evidence, the four disqualifiers, and a five-point REVIVAL-PRECONDITION checklist — any revival needs a fresh DEC + a Golden Rule #9 4-agent hostile review AND: live verification of claude-code-action's CURRENT release inputs (Golden Rule #1); the #1180 author-trust check (auto-merge.yml `trust-check` — allowlist SJParthi/dependabot[bot]/renovate[bot] OR live `author_association` ∈ OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR) EXTRACTED to ONE COMMON `scripts/ci/` script consumed by BOTH auto-merge.yml and the new workflow (Golden Rule #11 — the extraction is deliberately DEFERRED to revival time: after DELETE there is no second consumer, so extracting now would be a speculative refactor of a live security-critical workflow); trust-gate BEFORE any checkout of a PR-controlled ref (the #1180 H2 law); the new comment-trigger redteam sweep passing against it; the #1180 owner-side server settings (branch ruleset for `main` + Actions → "Require approval for all outside collaborators" — exact click-path in #1180's own honest-limits follow-up) confirmed DONE by the operator. (b) the HARDENING DIVIDEND, shipped regardless of the verdict because the gap exists independently of this design: `tests/redteam/test_redteam_fork_pr_harden.py` gains `test_no_issue_comment_privileged_workflows` — a directory-wide fail-closed pin that NO workflow whose `on:` includes a comment-family trigger (`issue_comment` / `pull_request_review_comment` / `discussion_comment`; the `on:` value NORMALIZED across GitHub Actions' three equivalent spellings — mapping / flow-list / scalar — via ONE common `_workflow_triggers` helper, also adopted by the sibling #1180 `workflow_run`/`pull_request_target` sweep: the round-1 hostile review demonstrated the un-normalized membership test failing OPEN for `on: issue_comment` / `on: [issue_comment]`, now closed + teeth-pinned by `test_issue_comment_sweep_flags_scalar_and_list_on_spellings`; explicit read-level declaration pinned clean; fully-gated default-token job pinned exempt; half-gated pinned flagged); the reconstruction round-4 review then closed a FIFTH fail-open: `_SECRET_REF_RE` matched only DOT-notation secret access (`secrets.NAME`) while GitHub Actions expression syntax equally accepts index/bracket notation (`secrets['NAME']` / `secrets["NAME"]`) — a comment-triggered job declaring read-only `permissions:` (dodging the write-scope AND undeclared-permissions checks) but exfiltrating a foreign secret via the bracket respelling produced ZERO violations (the secret-access twin of the `on:`-spelling / `.yaml`-extension / `write-all` bypasses, undisclosed) — the regex now matches BOTH spellings (whitespace-tolerant, quote class `+` so `yaml.safe_dump`'s doubled single quotes inside single-quoted scalars cannot re-open the hole; 1601. **DEC-MOVERS-EXPLICIT-BUCKET-ASOF-001 — an explicit `/movers` bucket-anchor TIME pick resolves to the COMPLETED bucket (broker-matching close) instead of a PARTIAL forming bucket** (2026-07-08 on `claude/movers-bucket-asof-fix`; fix(movers); READ-ONLY dashboard — ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX); F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no lake/schema/scope/vocab/rate change). **The defect (operator-reported thrice, 2026-07-07, NIFTYIT):** the ``/movers`` TIME dropdown on a coarse timeframe offers only the 09:15-anchored bucket-ANCHOR grid (`session_bar_times` — on 3-minute the last slot is 15:27), but the backend treated the picked anchor as an as-of INSTANT, so picking the last 3-minute slot cut the raw 1-minute frame at 15:27 inclusive and the "bucket" held ONLY the 15:27 minute bar (LTP ₹27,932.80) — while the broker's chart shows the COMPLETED candle labelled 15:27 (15:27 + 15:28 + 15:29 → close ₹27,940.85 = 2-minute @ 15:29 = 1-minute @ latest). The PREBUILT derived-TF lake partitions were always CORRECT (the stored 3-minute 15:27 bucket already aggregates the FULL bucket); the defect was ONLY the read-time as-of resolution. **Root cause (file:line):** the three tabs each computed `cutoff_min = None if daily else _cutoff_minute(time)` verbatim — `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py::compute_spot_candidates` (was :1451), `movers_futures.py::compute_futures_candidates` (was :1130), `movers_options.py::compute_options_candidates` (was :1160) — so an anchor pick cut at the bucket's OPEN minute and `filter_to_ist_minute` kept only the forming partial. **The fix (ONE COMMON as-of seam, CLAUDE.md §11):** NEW `brutex/dashboard/movers_snapshot.py::resolve_asof_cutoff(interval, time)` replaces the three copy-pasted lines — an EXPLICIT pick landing on a bucket ANCHOR of the selected TF's 09:15-grid resolves the effective cut FORWARD to the bucket's FINAL minute `min(anchor + minutes − 1, _SESSION_CLOSE_MIN − 1)` (clamped to the session's last minute 15:29); the downstream `<= cutoff` `filter_to_ist_minute` then caps at the day's actual latest available minute (no bar past the completed bucket is ever included — NO look-ahead, Golden Rule #1). All three `compute_*_candidates` now call the one seam. **Laws (each test-pinned):** TF=1minute is identity (anchor == end, byte-unchanged); blank / "Latest" cut stays whole-day (`None`) byte-identical (DEC-MOVERS-ASOF-LATEST-DEFAULT-001 preserved); a NON-anchor explicit time (the dropdown never emits one) keeps the pre-fix as-of-instant semantics; daily / unknown interval → `None`; the prev-close %CHNG baseline is untouched; a malformed time still raises `ValueError` → 400. **Honest provenance:** NEW `asof_through_label(interval, time)` yields the resolved bucket-END "HH:MM" ONLY when an anchor pick was extended; the route (`app.py::api_movers._resolve`) threads it as the ADDITIVE `resolved_through=` into `build_snapshot_payload` / `build_futures_payload` / `build_options_payload`, which echo an additive `asof_through` field + append " `HH:MM` bucket · through `HH:MM`" to the success note (default `None` → payload + note byte-identical). **Sanctioned semantic narrowing:** an anchor pick now has a TF-DEPENDENT effective as-of, so value TF-invariance (DEC-MOVERS-SPOT-VALUE-TF-INVARIANT-001) holds PER shared *resolved* as-of, not per picked-time string — `tests/unit/test_movers_spot_value_tf_invariant.py::test_value_constant_across_tfs_at_shared_cutoff` updated to assert value == the raw-1m HLC3 sum through each TF's resolved cutoff; the three pre-existing `test_intraday_cutoff_path` / teeth tests updated to the completed-bucket values (futures ₹20,050→₹20,100, options ₹150/OI1050→₹164/OI1100, spot explicit 15:27 → ₹22,000 with the old partial ₹21,800 now shown on 1minute@15:27). **Before/after PROVEN:** `tests/integration/test_movers_bucket_asof.py` (27 tests) — the read layer at cutoff 927 yields bar-1 ₹27,932.80 (pre-fix) vs cutoff 929 yields bar-3 ₹27,940.85 (post-fix); end-to-end `compute_spot_candidates(interval="3minute", time="15:27")` → ₹27,940.85; mid-day 10:00/5m → 10:04 close with 10:05 EXCLUDED (no look-ahead); 1hour@15:15 clamps to 15:29; day-ending-mid-bucket clamps to latest available; futures + options parity at the same TF+time; payload provenance echo. **Coverage / gates:** `movers_snapshot.py` / `movers_futures.py` / `movers_options.py` ALL 100.00% line+branch (the added `app.py` route lines covered by the movers route integration suites); ruff / ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` clean on all four touched modules; pyright at the pre-change baseline. **Numbering law:** live-max was #1581 (DEC-FORM-WINNER-PERSIST-001); this entry takes #1601 to stay clear of the in-flight #1582–1600 cluster (`scripts/ci/validate_ledger_numbering.py` requires only per-(number,suffix) uniqueness, not contiguity; re-verify immediately before push per P-1 and renumber if a merge-race collides). **Decision ID:** DEC-MOVERS-EXPLICIT-BUCKET-ASOF-001.

1630. **DEC-SWEEP-LOG-VOLUME-GUARD-001 — the sweep CLI's structlog output is BOUNDED at INFO by default (fail-loud `$BRUTEX_LOG_LEVEL` override): a bare `brutex sweep`/`sweep-all`/`sweep-daemon` process left structlog UNCONFIGURED (the default wrapper class filters at NOTSET), so the engine's per-trade DEBUG events (`trade_sim.entry`/`trade_sim.exit` — two per simulated trade) streamed unfiltered to stderr — a MEASURED 870 MB of log output on a ~200-session composite-e2e fixture, which on the §8 production 2-4 day full-grid run is a disk-fill risk (disk-full mid-sweep → `LakeWriteHalt` = a run-killer) plus severe I/O overhead** (2026-07-08 on `claude/sweep-log-level-guard`; fix(cli)). THE FIX (minimal + §11 COMMON): ONE dispatch-level guard in `cli._dispatch` — `args.command ∈ {sweep, sweep-all, sweep-daemon}` → the NEW `cli._configure_sweep_logging()` — routing through the EXISTING ONE COMMON `brutex.observability.logging.configure_logging` seam (the same seam `cmd_dashboard` configures at startup; ADR-0005) at INFO/console-renderer, at the `main()` dispatch BEFORE any engine module is even imported, so every engine logger's first use binds the filtering wrapper (structlog caches on first use); `sweep-daemon` inherits doubly (guard at its own dispatch + it reuses `cmd_sweep_all`). Env resolution is the NEW `observability/logging.resolve_env_log_level` (the env wrapper that module's own design contract prescribes — the core function stays env-free): unset/blank → default INFO; `DEBUG`/`INFO`/`WARNING`/`ERROR` accepted case-insensitively; ANYTHING else — including `CRITICAL`, since silencing ERROR would hide halts — raises → `CliUserError` → one `[brutex] invalid BRUTEX_LOG_LEVEL=…` line + exit 1 with the sweep handler NEVER invoked (junk is never a silent fallback). DEFER RULE: when `structlog.is_configured()` the guard validates the env var then no-ops — the dashboard's in-process sweep job (`run_sweep_from_request` → `cmd_sweep_all`) keeps `cmd_dashboard`'s INFO + rotating-file-sink configuration (reconfiguring would DROP that file sink, and structlog's first-use logger cache would ignore a mid-process swap anyway); that path was ALREADY bounded at INFO — the bare CLI process was the unbounded one. HONEST (Golden Rule #10): bounds LOG VOLUME ONLY — a sink-level threshold; NO event's level is changed and nothing at WARNING/ERROR is dropped (test-pinned); the hash-chained audit JSONL (Golden Rule #8 — `engine.sweep_audit.SweepAuditWriter` + `orchestrator.audit.AuditWriter`) is written by direct file appends, NOT structlog events, so audit records are byte-untouched at every level (pinned: neither module imports structlog); the 870 MB figure is the composite-run FIXTURE measurement — no production-run log size is claimed; `BRUTEX_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` deliberately restores the full per-trade stream (the operator's diagnosis lever, disk cost re-accepted explicitly). TESTS (each captures ACTUAL stderr bytes via capsys, never a sink mock): default suppresses a per-trade-shaped DEBUG event / INFO+WARNING+ERROR still emit at default / `DEBUG` env restores / junk fails loud pre-handler (fresh AND already-configured process) / all three sweep entries pass the ONE guard / a non-sweep command (`version`) stays logging-untouched / an existing configuration is deferred to / the audit-writers-are-structlog-free honesty pin — NEW `tests/unit/test_cli_sweep_log_level.py` (13) + `TestResolveEnvLogLevel` (13) in `tests/unit/test_observability_logging.py`; the six existing test files that drive `main([… "sweep*" …])` for OTHER behavior opt into ONE shared conftest fixture (`_inert_sweep_logging_guard`, module-level `usefixtures` mark — Golden Rule #11, no six-copy fixture) so no process-global logging config leaks between tests. R4 REVIEW FOLD (refuter-confirmed, same branch pre-merge): the dispatch guard alone covered ONLY the PARENT process — the production sweep is PARALLEL (`run_parallel_grid` builds a `ProcessPoolExecutor(mp_context=spawn, initializer=_worker_init)`), a SPAWN worker starts from a CLEAN interpreter (the parent's structlog config is NOT inherited), and the per-trade DEBUG events fire INSIDE the workers onto the inherited stderr fds — so the disk-fill stream was UNFILTERED on exactly the parallel path. FIX: `_worker_init` now applies the SAME bound worker-side via the NEW `observability/logging.configure_process_logging_best_effort` (`$BRUTEX_LOG_LEVEL` propagates to spawn children via the environment; junk falls back to INFO instead of raising — the parent entries already failed loud PRE-pool; defer-if-configured; ANY config failure swallowed — a worker must NEVER die over logging, best-effort by contract). REAL spawn regression net (`TestWorkerLogVolumeGuardSpawn`, capfd fd-level capture of actual child output through a REAL 2-worker `run_parallel_grid`): `trade_sim.*` ABSENT at default / `trade_sim.entry`+`exit` PRESENT with `BRUTEX_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` (the DEBUG twin proves the absence assertion non-vacuous) + in-process `_worker_init` binding/never-breaks pins + 5 direct helper-branch tests. The dashboard-launched sweep inherits the worker fix automatically (`run_sweep_from_request` → `cmd_sweep_all` → the same `run_parallel_grid` → `_worker_init`). MERGE-TO-MAIN FIX (folded when rebasing onto current main via a merge commit, same branch pre-merge): merging `origin/main` surfaced a TEST-ISOLATION leak the in-process worker/CLI logging config introduces — an in-process `_worker_init` / `_configure_sweep_logging` call configures structlog with `cache_logger_on_first_use=True`, freezing a shared module logger (e.g. `engine.sweep_run._LOG`) against the CURRENT processors list; the parallel suite's autouse `reset_configuration()` then swapped that list via `structlog.reset_defaults()`, ORPHANING the frozen proxy, so a LATER test's `structlog.testing.capture_logs` (which captures by mutating the current config's processors list IN PLACE, "to not break references held by bound loggers") could no longer observe that proxy — its INFO events silently bypassed the sink. That failed 9 `test_engine_sweep_run*.py` path-observability tests (`sweep_run.trade_sim_path` / `trade_sim_chunk_failed` / `bounded_rank_engaged` — ALL INFO events that DO emit under the bound, NOT DEBUG-suppression) with `len(events)==0` / `IndexError` when the `test_engine_*.py` coverage gate ran the files together (each passed alone). FIX (test-support only — the production log-volume bound is byte-untouched): `observability/logging.reset_configuration` now also clears structlog's first-use logger cache (NEW `_clear_structlog_first_use_cache` — resolves the proxy class via `type(structlog.get_logger())`, drops ONLY the overridden `bind` INSTANCE attribute on live `BoundLoggerLazyProxy` objects, never `_logger`, so each proxy re-assembles against the CURRENT config on next use), making the COMMON test-only reset a TRUE reset. Regression-pinned by `test_reset_unfreezes_capture_logs_for_module_loggers` (freeze → reset → `capture_logs` observes the event; 0 without the clear) and proven against the exact CI `tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` glob (was 1956 passed + 9 failed → 1965 passed). NO production path calls `reset_configuration`; the sweep INFO-default bound + the `_worker_init` worker bound are unchanged. OPERATOR NOTE (documented in the guard docstring): `BRUTEX_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR` also silences the WARNING-level operational events (stall-watchdog / quarantine warnings) an unattended launch-night sweep relies on — INFO (default) or WARNING recommended; ERROR is an opt-in hazard. `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py` stays 100.00% line+branch (its own 87-test suite). **Numbering:** takes #1630 — the next free number at/above the allocated floor (live-main max #1597 after merging origin/main; #1610–#1628 reserved/taken by in-flight PRs; the gap is legal — uniqueness is the law, DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001), re-verified against the merged file before push. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change; `brutex/cli.py` (1173 stmts/264 branches) + `brutex/observability/logging.py` (114/24, incl. the merge-fix cache clear) BOTH 100.00% line+branch via the discovery gate; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` clean on both touched source files. **Files:** brutex/cli.py, brutex/observability/logging.py, brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py, tests/conftest.py, tests/unit/{test_cli_sweep_log_level,test_observability_logging,test_engine_sweep_parallel,test_cli_user_error_hygiene,test_cli_sweep_launch_wiring,test_cli_backfill}.py, tests/integration/{test_cli_sweep,test_cli_sweep_scope,test_cli_sweep_scope_guard}.py, docs/MIGRATION.md, CLAUDE.md. **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-LOG-VOLUME-GUARD-001.

All inside the P2 engine/observability zone.** **(1, BLOCKER — `sweep-all --detach` argparse-abbreviation fork bomb)** the detach re-exec passed `[a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != "--detach"]` to `spawn_detached_sweep`; argparse's default `allow_abbrev=True` accepts `--det`/`--deta`/`--detac` → `detach=True`, and the exact-string filter leaves the abbreviated flag in the child argv, so the child re-entered `cmd_sweep_all` with `detach=True`, spawned ANOTHER detached session-leader child, and repeated forever (unbounded process spawn; the requested sweep never ran; the append-mode detach log + pidfile churned). FIX (spelling-immune, env-sentinel not sys.argv-string): `spawn_detached_sweep` now stamps `BRUTEX_SWEEP_DETACHED=1` into the child's environment (new `env=` param, sentinel always merged on top) and `cmd_sweep_all` honours `--detach` only when the new `running_as_detached_child()` predicate reads the sentinel ABSENT — so any surviving abbreviation is ignored in the child and the real sweep runs. Pinned by a child-env-carries-sentinel spawn test + a `running_as_detached_child` truth matrix + an integration test proving a `detach=True` child with `--det` in argv NEVER re-spawns (`spawn_detached_sweep` asserted uncalled). `sweep_detach.py` 100% line+branch (74/8, 25 unit). **(2, NIT+MINOR, same root — `mark_suspect`'s mid-run RUNNING exit-status write reset `wall_started_utc`)** `write_exit_status(state=RUNNING)` unconditionally set `started = now`, and `mark_suspect`'s never-launder belt writes `state=RUNNING, suspect=True` MID-run, so a SUSPECT run's `exit-status.json` reported its wall duration from the suspect-latch instant, not from launch (the finalize preserves the reset value) — a wrong forensic number on precisely the run an operator inspects. FIX: `write_exit_status` now PRESERVES a prior readable artifact's `wall_started_utc` for RUNNING too (only the very first enter, with no prior, stamps `now`); `ended` alone distinguishes RUNNING (None) from terminal (now). Observability-only, never identity; results byte-unchanged. `sweep_exit_status.py` 100% line+branch; pinned by a mid-run-RUNNING-preserves-launch regression. **(3, REJECTED — RUNCORE-DASHBOARD-COVERAGE, stale)** the finding claimed the dashboard one-click button runs `run_sweep_from_request` → `run_sweep_grid` directly, bypassing keep_awake/single-flight/G12/forensics. No code change; the round-2 "(d)" note is corrected above. **(4, Row-4 hazard pin STRENGTHENED)** the `.parquet`-glob hazard pin now ALSO exercises the FAILURE/diag-bundle finalize path (`test_runcore_writes_no_parquet_under_runs_dir_on_failure` — a raising body drives the failed exit-status + diagnostic-bundle write, then asserts still-no-`.parquet` under `runs/<run_id>/`), so the invariant holds on the forensic path an operator actually reads, not just the clean `pass` path; the physical `runs/`→`sweep_runs/` relocation stays the documented merge-integration P2/P3 follow-up. **STILL-OPEN named cross-phase / design follow-ups (round 3, honest — NOT claimed done):** Row 21 (per-run `run_id`-named whole-run LOG FILE on the internal disk, R40/R37 input) is NEW-named **DEC-SWEEP-RUNLOG-FILE-001** — a naive stdlib `FileHandler` on the root logger would capture an EMPTY forensic log because structlog is configured with a `PrintLoggerFactory` writing straight to stderr (its events do not traverse the stdlib root handlers), so shipping one would be a fake-empty artifact (Golden Rule #1); the correct fix is a careful per-run structlog reconfigure (or a dedicated structlog processor sink), deferred with this owner rather than shipped empty; the flight-recorder JSONL + diagnostic bundle already give a durable per-run structured event record on the internal disk in the interim. 1608. **DEC-SWEEP-STALL-OOM-GUARDS-001 — the parallel grid-sweep gains a HEAVY-GRID-AWARE stall watchdog + a distinct BrokenProcessPool QUARANTINE, closing two round-3 meta-refuter run-killers: (1) a legitimately-slow k=5 1-minute tuple no longer false-aborts a multi-hour grid near completion, and (2) a worker OOM no longer becomes a silent identical-resume livelock** (2026-07-08 on `claude/sweep-stall-oom-guards`; fix(engine); additive resilience — a CLEAN run is byte-identical, frozen sweep goldens + P-06/suffix-independence UNMODIFIED). **THE TWO DEFECTS (from the round-3 meta-refuter audit of `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py`):** (1, HIGH) the stall watchdog fired a flat `DEFAULT_STALL_SECONDS = 300.0` — but ONE k=5 1-minute NIFTY tuple (`C(60,5) = 5.46M` masks × hundreds of thousands of bars) runs as a single worker future FAR longer than 5 min with NO sub-tuple progress reported to the parent, so at the grid tail — when only slow heads remain in-flight and none COMPLETES within 300 s — `_await_next_result` raised `SweepStallError` → whole-run ABORT, killing a multi-hour grid near completion. (2, MED-HIGH) there was NO `concurrent.futures.process.BrokenProcessPool` handler: a k=5 worker OOM-killed while building `bar_bits`/finalists was caught by the generic `except Exception` → ABORT + re-raise, and because the checkpoint freezes at the last clean-prefix boundary an identically-configured resume re-dispatched the SAME deterministically-OOMing tuple → abort again = a silent no-progress loop across resumes. **THE FIXES (ONE change set, `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py` only — the SOLE source edit):** **(1) heavy-grid-aware stall bound** — each dispatched tuple's `mask·bar` work (`C(n_unique, k) × N_bars`, the exact per-tuple trade-sim work; `_tuple_work`) is stored per in-flight future in a new `_Dispatched` record; `_await_next_result` sizes the wait budget as `_effective_stall_seconds(max_inflight_work) = max(base_stall, work / STALL_MIN_MASK_BARS_PER_SEC)` so a tuple that legitimately needs N minutes gets a PROPORTIONAL bound while a light grid keeps the base floor byte-identically. The bound is FINITE, so a genuine no-progress hang is STILL caught (a wedged worker makes ZERO progress → its work-scaled deadline eventually elapses) — the guard is scaled, NOT disabled. `STALL_MIN_MASK_BARS_PER_SEC = 2.5e8` is a CONSERVATIVE hang-detection floor (Golden Rule #10: the resident Rust trade-walk is order-of-magnitude ~1e9 `mask·bar`/s, so 2.5e8 gives ~4× headroom against false-abort; it sets ONLY the false-abort-margin ↔ wedge-detection-latency trade-off, never results). Env knobs: `BRUTEX_SWEEP_STALL_SECONDS` (base floor) + `BRUTEX_SWEEP_STALL_MASK_BARS_PER_SEC` (throughput floor), both positive-float, unset→default, invalid→default+LOUD WARNING (`resolve_stall_seconds`/`resolve_stall_min_mask_bars_per_sec` over the shared `_resolve_positive_float_env`); the constructor's `stall_seconds`/`stall_min_mask_bars_per_sec` default to `None` → env-resolved, so `run_parallel_grid` (and the CLI) pick it up with no call-site change. **(2) OOM quarantine — durable, REVERSIBLE, visible** — `_drive` catches `BrokenProcessPool` DISTINCTLY (from `pool.submit` OR `future.result()` — `result()` runs BEFORE `pending.pop` so the broken future stays in `pending`), and `_await_next_result` catches a worker's surviving Python-level `MemoryError` (the cgroup/rlimit OOM shape — the pool does NOT break) as the single-tuple twin (`_quarantine_memory_error`). `_quarantine_broken_pool` first DRAINS already-FINISHED sibling futures (their REAL results apply — compute never discarded), then records every genuinely-broken in-flight tuple in the DURABLE quarantine sidecar `<root>/.sweep_quarantine.json` (fsync + atomic replace BEFORE anything else moves; `quarantine_sidecar_path`/`load_quarantined_tuple_labels`/`append_quarantine_entries` exported) and applies them as `"pool_broken"` outcomes — which deliberately do NOT `SweepCache.record` (that would permanently + invisibly drop the tuples from every identical resume — the adversarial-review MAJOR this round corrected) and do NOT advance the checkpoint (`had_failure` latch, the sequential failed-tuple semantics) — then raises the NEW distinct `SweepWorkerPoolBrokenError` naming the tuple(s), the SIDECAR, and the honest remediation (relieve pressure: reduce `BRUTEX_SWEEP_WORKERS` / the grid's k / raise `BRUTEX_SWEEP_MEM_BUDGET_BYTES`; then DELETE the sidecar entries and resume — the tuples are then genuinely RECOMPUTED, the ONE reversible lever). A resume gates the sidecar FIRST in `_gate_or_dispatch`: quarantined tuples are skipped VISIBLY as the DISTINCT `tuples_quarantined_prior` counter — surfaced on `SupervisedGridSummary` (new defaulted field, sequential path always 0), the COMPLETE audit payload, and the progress detail — NEVER folded into `skipped_cache`, so the completeness hole can never blend into a "successful" run. So a resume NEVER re-dispatches the poison tuple (no livelock), makes progress on the rest, and the loss is LOUD (distinct `SUPERVISOR_TUPLE_POOL_BROKEN` + `SUPERVISOR_TUPLE_QUARANTINED_PRIOR` audit actions + ERROR/WARNING logs + counters) and RECOVERABLE (delete the sidecar entry → recompute — regression-pinned). **FAIL-LOUD chosen over blind pool-rebuild-and-continue ON THE MERITS + the PR #1285 memory-budget-division interaction:** a broken pool from OOM means the machine is under memory pressure, and the per-tuple rank budget DIVIDES across workers (`brutex/config/hardware_envelope.py::memory_budget_bytes` sizes `total × fraction / workers` — the DEC-SWEEP-STREAMING-RANK-001 rank-region interaction) [CORRECTED by DEC-SWEEP-MEM-BUDGET-WORKERS-WIRE-001 (#1671): as originally wired the divisor was never passed (`workers` defaulted 1) — the claim was false until #1671 wired it; see that entry], so rebuilding and re-running the next heavy tuple would just re-OOM; the honest fix tells the operator to reduce the pressure (fewer workers RAISES each worker's per-tuple budget AND cuts total pressure) while durably quarantining the poison tuple so the eventual resume skips it. **REGRESSION PINS (proven fail-before/pass-after):** a slow-but-progressing heavy tuple whose work-scaled wait budget is handed to `_futures_wait` is FAR above 300 s and does NOT abort (the run completes); a genuinely-wedged heavy pool STILL aborts (finite bound, a clock jumping past the scaled deadline); a worker that deterministically breaks the pool → the in-flight tuples land in the durable sidecar (`tuples_pool_broken`; checkpoint FROZEN, cache NOT recorded) + `SweepWorkerPoolBrokenError` naming tuple + sidecar + remediation, AND a resume does NOT re-dispatch them (a recording fake pool proves indices 0/1 never re-submitted) while counting them DISTINCTLY (`tuples_quarantined_prior`, `skipped_cache` stays 0) and a REAL `run_parallel_grid` resume surfaces the counter on the returned summary; THE RECOVERY PIN — deleting the sidecar re-dispatches + recomputes the tuples (no permanent loss, Golden Rule #1); a worker `MemoryError` (pool NOT broken) quarantines ONLY the poison tuple + its innocent siblings recompute on resume; the drain pin — an already-finished sibling future's real result is applied, never quarantined; plus the `_apply` `pool_broken`/`quarantined_prior` branches (freeze + no-cache + distinct audit), the submit-raises-before-any-task empty-pending path, the sidecar helpers (missing/corrupt→LOUD-empty, merge, foreign-sweep filter), the constructor's positive-finite stall-knob refusal (a direct `0` would divide-by-zero), and `run()`'s ABORT-wrap of the distinct error. **ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW FIX ROUND folded (same branch, pre-merge):** the round-1 quarantine (`SweepCache.record` + checkpoint advance) was REJECTED as a permanent invisible data hole — a resumed run folded the poison tuples into `skipped_cache` forever and the remediation could not bring them back; replaced by the sidecar design above (reversible + `tuples_quarantined_prior` visible). The worker-survives `MemoryError` shape (which would have livelocked exactly as before) is now quarantined too. HONEST residual (named, NOT claimed): a deterministically-WEDGED non-OOM tuple (infinite loop, no allocation failure) still aborts via `SweepStallError` with a frozen checkpoint, so an identical resume re-dispatches IT — the stall path has no quarantine (pre-existing; a stall-quarantine is a possible future follow-up, deliberately not invented here); and the work-scaled hang-detection latency SCALES with `C(n_unique,k) × N_bars` — a wedged VERY heavy tuple is caught in ~4× its legitimate runtime (hours, not 300 s) — the deliberate correctness > fast-detection trade. **GATES:** `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py` 100.00% line + branch (442 stmts / 88 branch, 0 missing) under `pytest tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_parallel.py --cov=brutex.engine.sweep_parallel --cov-branch` (128 tests); `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py` (the additive defaulted `SupervisedGridSummary.tuples_quarantined_prior` field) 100.00% line + branch (190/32) under its module suite; the frozen sweep goldens (`tests/golden/test_engine_sweep_run_golden.py`) + `tests/property/test_sweep_suffix_independence.py` pass UNMODIFIED (21 tests); ruff + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean; `pyright` 0 errors on both touched files. ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX + the ADR-0012 NIFTY-futures track); F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope/vocab/rate/lake/audit-schema change (the new `SUPERVISOR_TUPLE_POOL_BROKEN` action appears only on a broken-pool run, never on a clean run — the clean-run audit vocabulary is byte-unchanged). **Files:** `brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py`, `brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_parallel.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-STALL-OOM-GUARDS-001. (Ledger: #1608 — the #1601 band is contested / a P2 #1605-area allocation, so this lands at #1608, above the live-grepped max #1593; the DEC-ID is the stable handle per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001.)

1616. **DEC-SWEEP-DATA-EDGE-GUARDS-001 — two surgical engine data-edge guards for sweep-result correctness: (1) a Muhurat-safe prev-day anchor at the Stage-1A roll seam, and (2) a bounded bad-tick (spike / fat-finger / vendor-scaling) screen at the engine read boundary** (2026-07-08 on `claude/data-edge-guards`; fix(engine); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change). Closes lens-D of the 2026-07-08 one-click-sweep gap register (`sweep-gap-register-jul8` — D-MAJ-1 + D-MAJ-2): the first "institutional" sweep would have silently ingested TWO classes of corrupt anchor with zero warnings. **(1) D-MAJ-1 — Muhurat-safe prev-day anchor.** `brutex/engine/stage1a.py::_roll_to_new_day` rolled `_prev_day_ohlc = self._today_ohlc` on EVERY IST-date change with NO calendar guard, so a Diwali *Muhurat* evening session's distorted ~1-hour OHLC became the NEXT regular day's pivot / PDH-PDL / Fib / day-type anchor (bits 6-29 + 48-51), poisoning 6 days across 2020-2025 (2020-11-14, 2021-11-04, 2022-10-24, 2023-11-12, 2024-11-01, 2025-10-21) — while the Muhurat-safe `indicators/prev_day_ohlc.py::lookup_prev_day_ohlc` (which walks calendar sessions and skips Muhurat) was NOT used by Stage-1A. FIX: at the roll seam, when the just-completed day is a Muhurat-session date (`calendars/nse.has_muhurat_session` / `MUHURAT_SESSIONS`), BOTH `_prev_day_ohlc` (pivots / prev-day Fib) AND `_daily_history` (the multi-day rolling-weekly / weekly-static Fib anchor) are LEFT UNTOUCHED — the prior REGULAR session's anchor carries through, mirroring exactly what `lookup_prev_day_ohlc` + the weekly anchors already do on their calendar-session walk. Look-ahead-clean (the decision keys ONLY on the just-completed day's own IST date); exactly ONE structlog WARN (`stage1a.muhurat_prev_day_anchor_skip`) per skipped session naming the date. PARITY PIN: across all 6 real Muhurat boundaries, Stage-1A's carried-through `_prev_day_ohlc` equals `lookup_prev_day_ohlc`'s answer (both skip the Muhurat session). Measured on the regression fixture (prior regular PDH 110 / PDL 90 / PDC 105): the FIXED next-day pivot P = 10167 paisa (from the prior regular session) vs the BUGGY P = 10407 paisa (poisoned by the Muhurat 1-hour bar 104.50/103.50/104.20) — a 240-paisa shift, with all 11 pivot rungs + PDH/PDL/Fib/day-type similarly poisoned on all 6 dates. The P-06 look-ahead + suffix-independence property suites pass UNMODIFIED; all engine goldens byte-identical. **(2) D-MAJ-2 — bounded bad-tick screen.** There was NO spike/fat-finger filter: a self-consistent SCALED bar (e.g. 27940→2794, every OHLC ÷~10, internally ordered + positive) passed `price_sanity.py`'s positivity + ordering checks and silently flipped every price-relative bit, corrupted the running EMA / VWAP / swing-ring, and — via `TodayOHLC.absorb`'s running max/min — poisoned the NEXT day's PDH/PDL/pivots too. FIX (mirroring the DEC-STORED-DATA-VALIDATION-001 precedent boundary): NEW `brutex/data/bad_tick.py` (`is_bad_tick` pure predicate + `BadTickScreen` stateful single-pass screen + `bad_tick_screen_enabled` kill-switch reader) wired into `brutex/feed/replay.py::arrow_table_to_bars` — the ONE choke point the sweep feed uses (`ReplayFeed._load_bars` → `Catalog.get_bars` → `arrow_table_to_bars`; ONE production caller). A bar whose close is `>= 4x` OR `<= 1/4x` the previous IN-SESSION KEPT close is SKIPPED-and-COUNTED (never value-edited, never fabricated); the FIRST bar of each session is exempt (no reopen-gap false trip); a skipped spike does NOT advance the baseline (a lone spike cannot cascade-flag its healthy successor); exactly ONE WARN per session (`feed.bad_tick_skipped`, flushed at the session boundary / stream end with the session's total skipped count + first offender); default-ON env kill switch `BRUTEX_BAD_TICK_SCREEN` (`0`/`false`/`no`/`off` disables); O(1)/bar. **THRESHOLD JUSTIFICATION (Golden Rule #10 — grounded in real Indian-market physics, not a magic number):** NSE applies index-wide circuit breakers at 10% / 15% / 20% daily moves *from the prior close*, halting the WHOLE market — so within a single continuous session the index physically cannot travel more than one 20% band, and a single-MINUTE move is a small fraction of that; the largest single-DAY NIFTY moves on record (COVID, March 2020) were ≈ −13% / +9% for the whole day, with single-MINUTE moves far smaller (well under a couple of percent). A fat-finger / decimal-shift / vendor-scaling corruption is characteristically an order of magnitude (×10 or ÷10 → close ratio 10.0 or 0.1). `BAD_TICK_MAX_RATIO = 4.0` therefore sits ~2 orders of magnitude ABOVE the largest plausible real single-minute return yet comfortably BELOW the ×10 scaling class (10 > 4 and 0.1 < 0.25) — it catches the scaled-bar family while being impossible to trip on real index / stock minute data; regular-day bars move `<< 0.25x` per minute, so every existing golden is byte-identical. (No real 1-minute lake fixture ships in-repo to cite an observed worst move — the bound is derived from the circuit-breaker envelope, deliberately conservative.) **SCOPE / HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10):** (a) the Muhurat guard fixes the prev-day ANCHOR roll; a ROLLING_WEEKLY / WEEKLY_STATIC sweep still hits the weekly-anchor resolver's PRE-EXISTING non-trading-`today` refusal when a Muhurat day is the current bar's day (a separate concern, outside this fix — PREV_DAY is the sweep default and is fully fixed); (b) the bad-tick screen is a HEURISTIC bounded-ratio guard, not an oracle — a sub-4× scaling error (e.g. ×2) is deliberately NOT caught (the dominant fat-finger class is order-of-magnitude); it screens each close against the previous IN-SESSION close only, so a corrupt FIRST bar of a session is not caught by this guard (positivity/ordering still apply). **GATES:** `brutex/engine/stage1a.py` + `brutex/data/bad_tick.py` + `brutex/feed/replay.py` ALL 100.00% line + branch; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` clean; `pyright` 0 errors/0 warnings. NEW tests: `tests/unit/test_engine_stage1a.py` (Muhurat: all-6-boundaries parity-parametrized + one-warn + regular-rollover-unchanged + daily-history-exclusion), `tests/unit/test_data_bad_tick.py` (predicate / kill-switch / stateful-screen — 21), `tests/integration/test_feed_replay_bad_tick_screen.py` (end-to-end wiring through `arrow_table_to_bars` — scaled-bar skip / reopen-gap exempt / clean byte-identical / kill-switch / source-None — 5). **Files:** `brutex/engine/stage1a.py`, `brutex/data/bad_tick.py`, `brutex/feed/replay.py`, `tests/unit/test_engine_stage1a.py`, `tests/unit/test_data_bad_tick.py`, `tests/integration/test_feed_replay_bad_tick_screen.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-DATA-EDGE-GUARDS-001. (Ledger: #1616 — renumbered from the original #1601, which collided with three sibling branches; the movers PR #1286 keeps #1601 and this entry takes the reserved #1616; the DEC-ID is the stable handle.)

`compute.py` + its test file verified byte-identical between the probe tree `a36248f` and this base, so the measurement stands; `compute.py` itself untouched). **(2) rate_common gated (the 10th pass-2 pair, runs LAST so a survivor never masks the 9 proven modules):** the loop pair format grows an OPTIONAL 3rd colon-field per-pair hard timeout — empty = the exact historical runner for the 9 proven pairs (minimal diff), `30` for rate_common (FIXER ROUND: raised from the original 20) plus `--test-time-base 45` on the rate_common `mutmut run` — because the module carries bounded fail-open spin loops (`_GOVERNOR_LOOP_CAP`/`_SMOOTH_LOOP_CAP`) whose loop-counter mutants spin forever: mutmut's internal timeout kills only the `sh` wrapper and the ORPHANED pytest grandchild holds the stdout pipe, wedging mutmut until the 120-min job kill (measured 6× on the probe tree: mutants 194/195/199/209/210/213); the wrap kills the pytest subtree INSIDE the sh so mutmut reads the `|| exit 1` as a kill — an infinite-loop mutant IS a caught defect. HONEST classifier arithmetic (FIXER ROUND 2026-07-07 — this entry's original "the spin mutant scores KILLED via `|| exit 1` … records KILLED, never TIMEOUT (locally verified)" claim and its "pre-decided fallback: wrap 20 s → 10 s" were BOTH FALSE/ineffective as written and are SUPERSEDED by this clause): mutmut 2.5.1 RECLASSIFIES a killed mutant slower than `test_time_base (default 0) + baseline × test_time_multiplier (default 2.0)` as OK_SUSPICIOUS (`mutmut/__init__.py:803-806`; exit bit 8, id listed by `mutmut results`), so a ~20-25 s wrap-kill against the workflow's own 5-7 s CI baseline was DETERMINISTICALLY suspicious — the rate_common pass would have gone red on EVERY schedule/push run even at zero genuine survivors (measured: the T8 cache recorded the spin mutants `ok_suspicious`; a fast-box run records them BAD_TIMEOUT instead because the 10×baseline hard timer beats the wrap when baseline < ~3.5 s). 1654. **DEC-LAUNCH-DISK-GATE-HERMETIC-001 — the `/launch` route test suite is made HERMETIC against the real runner disk: the `run_preconditions` disk probe moves from a DEF-TIME-bound `shutil.disk_usage` default argument to the house `disk_usage=None` module-seam pattern (`launch_button._default_disk_usage` — resolved at CALL time), so tests pin the probe deterministically; the PRODUCTION disk gate is byte-identical** (2026-07-09 on `claude/fix-launch-button-disk-flake`; fix(dashboard,test); entry number #1654 GRANTED by the coordinator slot map (the earlier max+3 reservation #1635 sat inside PR #1323's reserved #1633-#1636 block; #1637-#1653 are reserved by the landing map + PR #1338 @1652 + PR #1368 @1653) — renumber-on-merge if the map shifts again, the validator allows gaps). THE FLAKE (reproduced): the launch POST gate re-checks `disk_free` via `shutil.disk_usage(lake_root).free >= DEFAULT_MIN_DISK_FREE_BYTES` (20 GiB — `brutex/dashboard/launch_button.py`, the `_POST_GATE_CHECKS` 412 arm). On a CI runner with < 20 GiB free, 7 tests in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_launch_button.py` fail with 412s (reproduced on this branch's base with an `fallocate` ballast forcing free < 20 GiB — the exact class of main's disk-floor pins) and the unreached post-gate route lines drag `launch_button.py` to 98.29% → the whole-package 100% gate fails. The probe could NOT be monkeypatched because `disk_usage` was bound as a def-time DEFAULT ARGUMENT (the default captured the original `shutil.disk_usage` function object at import). THE FIX (test-hermeticity + injection seam ONLY — no behavior change to the real disk gate): (a) `run_preconditions(disk_usage: Callable[[str], Any] | None = None)` — `None` resolves the NEW module seam `_default_disk_usage(path) -> shutil.disk_usage(path)` at call time (the exact `spawner=None` → `_default_spawner` pattern already in the module; explicit `disk_usage=` injections byte-unchanged); (b) `tests/unit/test_dashboard_launch_button.py` gains an AUTOUSE `hermetic_disk` fixture pinning `_default_disk_usage` plenty-free (4× the floor) so every route test is deterministic, + the NEW `test_low_disk_412_nothing_spawned` (the disk-REFUSAL arm exercised hermetically via an injected under-floor probe — 412 naming `disk_free`, nothing spawned: the gate is proven NOT weakened) + a deterministic `disk_free is True` assertion on the state payload; (c) `tests/unit/test_launch_button.py` gains `TestDiskUsageSeam` pinning the production parity — `run_preconditions.__kwdefaults__["disk_usage"] is None`, `_default_disk_usage` delegates to `shutil.disk_usage` at CALL time (spy-proven), and the None arm resolves the monkeypatchable module seam both directions (green AND red). PROOF (fails-before / passes-after, captured in the PR): with an fallocate ballast forcing real free < 20 GiB, the base suite fails exactly the 7 route tests with 412s (measured: `7 failed, 10 passed`, real free 18.5 GiB); on this branch the SAME ballasted run passes 18/18 route tests and both designated suites together pass 127/127. NO assertion deleted or weakened; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate change; `launch_button.py` 100.00% line+branch (406/66) over its two designated suites; ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` clean on `launch_button.py` (the two test files stay at their pre-existing 8-error baseline — unchanged count); pyright 0 errors on all three touched files.
1637. **DEC-WINDOWS-MIDPULL-FLOOR-001 — the mid-pull `/coverage/windows` degradation pack (audit M5 + the M27-class row-page gap): the windows counts cache gains the #920 pull-time adaptive floor (its keying restructured stamp-token-IN-key → STABLE-key + stamp-DIGEST generation so the floor can structurally engage), the row-PAGE result is stamp-cached per (filters, page, symbol-map content) on the SAME injected cache, the stale "O(page)-on-repeat" builder headline is corrected to the true accumulation envelope, and the per-poll delta-listing probe drops its pathlib `Path.__lt__` sort hog** (2026-07-09 on `claude/pack-l1-windows-midpull`; perf(dashboard) — READ-side only, ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema/stored-bar change; fetch pacing byte-identical; ZERO writer behavior change — `window_ledger_store.py` gains ONE comment naming the mid-pull delta-compaction follow-up at the accrual site). THE REGIME (measured 2026-07-09, sandbox shared-CI class, 2k-row base): mid-pull ledger deltas accrue ~1 file/`LIVE_FLUSH_MIN_INTERVAL_S` (2 s) and are pruned only by the pull-end save's subsumption, so a multi-hour pull reaches hundreds→thousands of pending files; the `/coverage/windows` row-page query re-ran the WHOLE O(total rows + per-delta Parquet footer) QUALIFY fold on EVERY 4 s poll even within one stamp (only the counts were cached — DEC-LEDGER-DELTA-O-PAGE-001 #1533 cached counts only), measured 33 ms/warm-poll @ 50 pending deltas → 158 ms @ 400 (the 4 s+ poll class at thousands); AND the counts cache itself was constructed WITHOUT the adaptive floor its four sibling discovery memos carry, so every fresh stamp (≥1 per 2 s mid-pull) recomputed back-to-back. THREE FIXES, smallest-risk shapes: **(1) floor wiring that can actually fire** — `app.py`'s window caches are built by the ONE db_view factory `make_window_payload_caches` riding the `_LEDGER_READ_CACHE` probe/floor shape — the constant-True `_ledger_stamp_moved` probe + the tighter 120 s `_LEDGER_READ_FLOOR_CAP_S` cap (round-2 hostile-review MINOR fold, option (a) — supersedes round 1's `_pull_live` in-process probe, whose floor was blind to CROSS-PROCESS CLI churn; safe because these caches' generation IS the stamp digest, so steady state never reaches the floor branch — the `_ledger_stamp_moved` rationale verbatim), AND — the load-bearing half — `db_view`'s two count-cache call sites (`phase_progress_payload._counts` + `_build_window_payload_duckdb`) move the composite stamp token OUT of the cache key INTO the generation (`revision_generation(source.stamp_token)` on the stable `window-counts|<path>` / `window-counts-since|<path>|<since>` keys — the `_LEDGER_READ_CACHE` #1533 pattern): the #920 floor fires only on a generation MISMATCH of one stable key, which the prior stamp-in-key/`generation=0` layout structurally never produced (every stamp move was a MISS on a brand-new key — the floor flags alone would have been INERT, proven by the fails-before regression `test_midpull_floor_throttles_recomputes_bounded_and_logged`). SANCTIONED behavior change, honestly scoped: a stamp move — an in-process pull's delta flush AND a cross-process CLI pull's — within `min(max(2 s, the family's own compute duration), 120 s)` serves the PRIOR stamp's counts/page STALE — bounded (#920 ≤50%-duty law), ALWAYS logged `movers_cache.stale_served`, and the families floor independently so one bounded-stale poll may mix counts and rows from adjacent stamps (≤ one floor window apart, self-heals — stated in the builder docstring); steady state (immobile stamp) never reaches the floor branch, so idle reads are byte-unchanged. **(2) the row-page cache** — the page query + `_window_row` projection move into ONE `_page_rows()` closure memoised on its OWN SMALL DEDICATED `MoversSnapshotCache` instance threaded through the existing seam as `page_cache=` (round-2 hostile-review MEDIUM fold — a page entry holds up to `min(limit, WINDOW_ROWS_CAP)`=20k projected row-dicts and the route's DEFAULT limit IS the 20k cap, so sharing the 256-cap counts instance risked a worst-case ~256 × 20k-row retained set (GB-scale) AND page-key churn LRU-evicting the tiny counts entries; the dedicated `WINDOW_PAGE_CACHE_CAPACITY=8` instance bounds retained pages to ≤ 8 × min(limit, 20k) = 160k row-dicts worst case — stated, not hidden; the SAME class, no new cache class — §11 COMMON; the Protocol's `get_or_compute` widens to a method-level TypeVar, name kept for injector back-compat) under the stable key `window-page|<path>|repr((market, status, limit, offset, symbol-map token))` at the SAME stamp-digest generation — a repeat poll within one stamp is an O(1) handoff for counts AND page (pre-fix only counts), a fresh stamp recomputes ONCE per page coordinate, the LRU bounds retained pages, the tuple-`repr` key segment makes client-supplied `market`/`status` strings collision-proof (never a bare `|` join), and the NEW pure `_window_symbol_map_token` (order-free SHA-256 over the id→symbol items, `"0"` for None/empty, O(map) ≈ tens of µs vs the O(instruments) store read that builds the map each request) re-keys the page when an instrument-master reload changes the decoded display names — a cached page can never serve stale symbols (Golden Rule #1); PLUS the round-2 status ALLOW-LIST hardening — every NOT-known `?status=` value collapses onto the ONE `_UNKNOWN_WINDOW_STATUS` sentinel BEFORE key minting (its SQL arm is the literal `1 = 0`, never a `status = <sentinel>` bind), so N distinct bogus values cost ONE key + ONE fold instead of N (legacy empty-result parity pinned); the `page_cache=None` arm computes directly, byte-identical (pinned across 7 filter/page permutations × the both/counts-only/page-only injection arms by `test_page_cache_fresh_compute_byte_identical`). **(3) honesty + teeth** — the builder's FALSE "O(page)-on-repeat" first-line docstring is rewritten to the true envelope (counts+page stamp-cached; every FRESH stamp pays ONE O(total rows + delta footers) columnar fold PER family; deltas grow until the pull-end prune; NOT literal O(page)); NEW bench pin B-8 (`tests/bench/test_ledger_delta_o_page_o1.py::test_accumulation_regime_warm_poll_bounded`) covers the ACCUMULATION regime with three teeth — (i) deterministic zero-recompute at 400 pending deltas (the family-aware frozen sentinel), (ii) the DISCRIMINATING absolute bound `warm poll @ 400 deltas < 100 ms` (measured 4.2 ms post-fix ~×24 slack vs 158 ms pre-fix, the B-4/B-6 "deliberately not tier-routed" measured-slack discipline — a RATIO cannot discriminate here because the pre-fix cost was also roughly linear in deltas), (iii) the `cache_tier_ceiling(8.0)`-routed probe-growth ratio warm(400)/warm(50) (measured 3.0× — the residual per-poll term is the honest O(pending-delta) stamp-probe directory listing, how a flush is detected at all; the file is not in bench-m4pro.yml's strict list); B-1/B-2/B-4 reconciled to the page-cache truth (the `_SentinelCountCache` counts recomputes PER FAMILY). MEASURED before → after (same box, same seeding): warm poll 33 ms → 1.4 ms @ 50 pending deltas, 158 ms → 4.2 ms @ 400 (~21-38×; the pre-fix growth line extrapolated to the multi-hour thousands-of-deltas regime is the reported 4 s+ poll). Plus the probe-term micro-fix: `_ledger_delta_files` sorts by the NAME string instead of whole `Path` objects — order-identical for same-directory entries on this POSIX-only lake (one shared parent, zero-padded `time_ns-pid` names carry no case) while skipping `Path.__lt__`'s per-comparison part-normalisation, the measured hot term of the warm poll at hundreds of deltas. HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10): the within-stamp poll still pays TWO O(pending-delta) directory-listing probes (`build_window_payload`'s gate listing + `_ledger_scan_source`'s — merging them is a possible micro follow-up, NOT done) so warm polls are NOT flat vs delta count (1.4 → 4.2 ms across 50→400 — bounded-linear syscall work, stated in B-8); worst-case retained page memory is the stated 8 × min(limit, 20k)-row ceiling (an operator paging 8 distinct full-20k coordinates); mid-pull delta COMPACTION (bounding the file count itself) is DEFERRED by the coordinator — ONE comment now names it at the accrual site in `append_ledger_delta`. THE DEFECT (repo's own arithmetic, `db_view.py` WINDOW_ROWS_CAP note: ~841k-row ledger → 247 MB uncapped, ⇒ ~294 B/row ⇒ the 20k-row default response ≈ 5.9 MB): coverage.html's windows KPI card renders ONE integer (`b.count`) and universe.html's all-segments line reads ONLY `.counts`, yet each polled the BARE route (4 s / 5 s cadence) — ~70–88 MB/min/tab of dead payload mid-pull — while fetch_windows.html both downloaded the full 20k-row default AND rebuilt the whole `#panel` table via `innerHTML` on every changed payload (~20k rows × 10 cols re-parsed per 4 s poll mid-pull). FIX (additive; the server DEFAULT stays 20_000 — the fetch-windows page genuinely renders rows): (a) BACKEND — the route's `limit` validation widens `ge=1` → `ge=0`; `build_window_payload` treats EXACTLY `limit == 0` as counts-only (a negative direct-caller limit still clamps UP to 1, pinned) and the DuckDB fast path guards the row-page `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` query behind `limit > 0` — `matched` is already derived from the stamp-cached GROUP-BY counts, so counts-only costs ZERO row-page work (spy-pinned: no row-page SQL text is ever issued; the legacy pyarrow / `window_status.json` paths serve `selected[:0]` naturally); `capped` stays the honest `matched > limit`. Existing-caller parity pinned at BOTH layers: unit (counts-only payload == the default call's payload with `windows=[]`/`returned=0`/`capped=True` folded, all counts/meta byte-equal) + route (the default response stays rowful + shape-identical, `?limit=-1` → 422 never a 500). (b) FRONTEND counts-only consumers — coverage.html `pollWindows` + universe.html `refreshWindowsLine` append `?limit=0` (one-line URL edits; the dead ~5.9 MB row list stops shipping). (c) FRONTEND fetch_windows.html — a static-DOM Prev/Next pager + page-size select (200 default / 500 / 1000; the db.html `.pager` idiom, patched via textContent/disabled ONLY) drives `qs.set("limit"/"offset", …)`; the payload-skip memo key folds `winLimit()|winOffset` so a page flip can never be skip-rendered; a filter flip resets to page 1 (the pinned manual-flip force-render line kept verbatim); a stranded offset past a shrunken matched set snaps back to page 1 exactly once (bounded — the re-poll runs at offset 0); `renderWindows` splits the row builder into `windowsRowsHtml` and patches ONLY the tbody when the table shell stands (`tbody.innerHTML = windowsRowsHtml(rows)` — the SAME already-esc()'d builder strings the full rebuild writes, against a NARROWER target, the sanctioned db.html `patchGridRows` precedent; empty states + first paint keep the full rebuild) — the table shell / sticky header / scroll position survive a poll; the always-on "CAPPED" status suffix rewords to "paged (severity-first — FAILED/EMPTY on page 1)". XSS discipline unchanged: every payload value still flows through `esc()`, the pager through `textContent`; the `test_no_new_innerhtml_sink_vs_baseline` gate gains fetch_windows.html's ONE sanctioned narrower-target sink (mirroring db.html's). (d) M15 ADDENDUM — `bx-liveproof.js` previously issued a BARE `fetch(ENDPOINT)` with no timeout and no in-flight guard, so a hung/stalled server accumulated unbounded pending requests onto the browser's ~6-per-origin connection pool (queueing every other poller on the page); it now routes through its own bounded `fetchJson` mirroring `bx-rate-monitor.js` (10 s AbortController deadline armed THROUGH the body read — a headers-then-stalled-body response aborts too; cleared on both settle paths), at most ONE request in flight, and a monotonic `pollSeq` token discards a stale straggler (defensive — the in-flight guard already serialises); the hidden-tab guard stays the first statement of `poll()` + the visibilitychange catch-up + `setInterval(poll, POLL_MS)` cadence + the best-effort leave-last-render catch are byte-preserved (the `test_dashboard_widget_visibility_pause.py` suite re-pinned — its fetch-discipline test now holds BOTH widgets to the fetchJson shape). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): the JS is SOURCE-PINNED, not browser-executed (no JS harness exists in this repo — stated in every new test docstring); counts-only changes NOTHING for callers that pass `limit>=1` (byte-parity pinned); the fetch-windows page pays one extra request ONLY on the snap-back edge; on an ancient browser without AbortController the liveproof deadline arm is inert (same envelope as the sibling widget). DEDUPE: stacks BEHIND the in-flight PR #1315 (templates-only hidden-tab poll guards + a completeness payload memo) — this change deliberately adds NO hidden guards and touches different lines in the same templates; a trivial rebase is expected. Touched modules covered by the extended suites (`test_dashboard_db_view.py` counts-only class arm, `test_dashboard_coverage.py` route parity, `test_dashboard_js_perf_frontend.py` §(f), `test_dashboard_liveproof_widget.py` M15 pins); ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` clean; pyright at the pre-change baseline. 1639. **DEC-LATENCY-HONESTY-BATCH-001 — the zero-risk latency-honesty batch (audit findings M1-doc / M14-doc / M34-doc / M12-note / M18 / M13): four FALSE or self-contradicting O(1)/boundedness claims corrected to their honest envelopes, the /universe all-segments windows poller disarmed on settle, and the production `/movers` candidate cache wired onto the SAME pull-time adaptive floor its five floored siblings already carry** (2026-07-09 on `claude/pack-l3-honesty-batch`; docs + frontend + ONE cache-wiring change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema change; READ-side dashboard only). **DOCS-ONLY honesty corrections (Golden Rule #10 — words moved to match the measured truth, ZERO behavior change):** (M1) the `GET /api/v1/sweep-progress` route docstring claimed "a pure O(1) read that never touches the lake or the store lock" — FALSE: `DashboardState.sweep_progress_view` performs a synchronous `path.exists()` + `read_progress` of the lake-volume `<lake>/sweeps/progress/sweep-progress.json` file bridge ON the event loop; rewritten to the honest envelope (a stalled lake volume can block the loop for that stat+read — the class `RateBridgeCache` bounds for `/api/v1/pull/rate`); the offload is a NAMED follow-up owned by a separate in-flight change, deliberately NOT implemented here (isolated docs-only commit so that change rebases trivially). (M14) `db_view.query_candles`'s "DuckDB additionally skips row-groups via min/max stats" claim is DEFEATED by this query's own shape — the DEC-LAKE-READ-UNIQUE-001 dedup `QUALIFY` window must rank every partition row before `LIMIT`, and the date bounds compare a derived `(timestamp AT TIME ZONE …)::DATE` expression DuckDB does not prune through against the raw `timestamp` column's zone-map stats — so each paging click is honestly an O(partition rows) engine-side columnar scan with O(page) Python materialisation, flat enough for the shared-CI < 8× depth gate (`tests/bench/test_db_candle_query_o1.py`); genuine row-group pruning (stats-compatible raw-column predicates) is named future work, and the pre-existing "UTC calendar date" wording gains the honest 1day-IST parenthetical (`_date_bounds`). (M34) `db_view._build_window_payload_duckdb`'s unqualified "O(page)-on-repeat" FIRST LINE contradicted its own mid-pull honest envelope five paragraphs down — the headline now reads "O(page) on repeat only BETWEEN ledger stamps" with an explicit first-line honesty paragraph (a FRESH stamp pays one O(total physical rows incl. delta footers) fold; Python-side stays O(page)); minimal truthful first-line fix — the in-flight PACK-L1 branch touches the same docstring, a trivial merge conflict is accepted. (M12) `movers_cache.py`'s "Memory is bounded: an LRU keeps at most capacity snapshots resident" was count-true, byte-FALSE — reworded to bounded in ENTRY COUNT not bytes (total resident = `capacity × payload-size`; ≈256 × 4 MiB ≈ 1 GiB — the latency audit's probe figure, arithmetically derived, not re-measured on this branch; a byte-watermark / size-aware eviction is a NAMED follow-up, not claimed). **(M18, frontend fix):** `universe.html`'s `pullStarted` flag was set `true` in `startAndPoll` BEFORE the start POST and NEVER cleared, so ONE pull click — even a REFUSED start — armed the 5 s full-payload `/coverage/windows` interval poller FOREVER (until a page reload); `finishLive` now paints ONE final settled windows line (`refreshWindowsLine()` reads the guard synchronously at entry) then clears the flag, and because a refused/failed start lands in `finishLive` via the `catch`, the refused path disarms too — the pre-POST arm is KEPT (the watch-start paint stays); pinned by the NEW source-string suite `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_windows_poller.py` (presence + refreshWindowsLine-BEFORE-clear ordering + exactly-one-clear-site + the catch→finishLive path; HONEST envelope: substring pins on the shipped JS, not execution — no headless JS runner; fails-before verified by reverting the template). **(M13, SANCTIONED behavior change — the batch's one wiring delta):** `build_app`'s production `_movers_cache` was the LONE bare `MoversSnapshotCache()` beside five floored siblings, so during a pull every window-tick generation bump forced a full O(instruments × bars-read) candidate re-scan on EVERY `/movers` poll back-to-back (the exact #920 scan-storm class); the construction moves below `_pull_live` (first use is far later — order-safe) and opts in (`pull_active_probe=_pull_live, adaptive_floor=True`), SUPERSEDING the movers-rows carve-out of DEC-DB-DISCOVERY-ADAPTIVE-FLOOR-001 (#1250) — that carve-out was a design rationale recorded in `movers_cache.py`'s module docstring, NOT an operator decree (ledger-searched; no refusal entry exists), and the docstring is rewritten to record the sanctioned change. NEW envelope, stated not hidden: while a pull is genuinely running IN THIS PROCESS a `/movers` poll may serve a candidate set up to `min(max(2 s, its own scan duration), 600 s)` stale (every stale serve LOGGED `movers_cache.stale_served` — never silent), NEVER pre-pull data beyond that floor window; the moment the pull ends the probe reads `False` → fresh recompute, and the post-pull movers warm re-seeds at the end generation (REVIEW FOLD, same DEC: the three movers-warm call sites — spot/futures/options `_make_*_job` — now pass `force_fresh=True`, mirroring the discovery warm's documented pattern, so the still-`running` job's own newly-added pull-active floor can never serve a stale pre-pull entry back into the warm re-seed; regression-pinned in `test_movers_pull_floor.py`); an INJECTED cache (tests/legacy callers) is used VERBATIM — no floor smuggled (regression-pinned); the no-pull path is byte-identical (pinned). Regression suite `tests/integration/test_movers_pull_floor.py` (floored-under-pull / pull-scoped-recompute / injected-verbatim), fails-before verified by reverting the wiring (the floored discovery memo alone did NOT absorb the candidate re-scan — compute count 2 pre-fix, 1 post-fix). HONEST limits: a CLI pull in a separate process raises no in-process signal, so the floor never applies there (the #1250 envelope, unchanged); the M1/M34 offload + delta-compaction follow-ups stay owned by their own branches (PACK-L4 / named future work); no throughput number is claimed for M13 (a duty-cycle fix, not a measured speedup). **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/app.py`, `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`, `brutex/dashboard/movers_cache.py`, `brutex/dashboard/templates/universe.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_universe_windows_poller.py` (NEW), `tests/integration/test_movers_pull_floor.py` (NEW). **Decision ID:** DEC-LATENCY-HONESTY-BATCH-001. 1640. **DEC-SWEEP-PROGRESS-NONBLOCK-CACHE-001 — the `/api/v1/sweep-progress` file-bridge read is moved OFF the uvicorn event loop AND deadline-bounded (audit M1, the first of the three #1622 event-loop stragglers): the route's synchronous `path.exists()` + `read_progress()` of `<lake>/sweeps/progress/sweep-progress.json` — polled every ~2 s by v29.html — ran ON the loop, so a measured 1.5 s stalled read froze a concurrent `/api/v1/state` poll 9.1 ms → 1305.4 ms; the route's own docstring claimed "a pure O(1) read that never touches the lake", which was FALSE** (2026-07-09 on `claude/pack-l4-offload-stragglers`; fix(dashboard) — READ-side dashboard only, ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema change). THE FIX, the #1522 rate-bridge doctrine applied to its sweep-progress twin: NEW `brutex/dashboard/sweep_progress_cache.py` `SweepProgressCache` — a 1 s-TTL memo (under the 2 s poll cadence; deliberately NO stat/content token — a RUNNING sweep rewrites the ~300-byte file about once a second, so a token would almost never save the decode, and `os.stat` wedges exactly like the read) whose post-TTL refresh (`exists()` + `read_progress`, BOTH inside the guard) runs under the COMMON `run_with_deadline` freeze guard (0.5 s, env `BRUTEX_SWEEP_PROGRESS_READ_DEADLINE_S`; TTL env `BRUTEX_SWEEP_PROGRESS_TTL_S`, both fail-loud, `0` TTL = always revalidate) with a NON-BLOCKING single-flight (followers serve last-known immediately; a wedged disk leaves EXACTLY ONE abandoned daemon per outage whose late return self-heals the memo; a guard SPAWN failure is caught by the OWNER with the flag released — the #1522 hostile-review MAJOR fold, mirrored; KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit propagate with the flag released). `DashboardState.sweep_progress_view` gains the kw-only `file_read` seam (default `None` = the direct legacy read, byte-identical — every pre-existing view consumer/test unchanged): the cache's `read()` returns the file payload to serve or `None` to fall through to the in-process-push / idle arms EXACTLY like the direct `exists()` check (missing file → `None`; present-but-corrupt → `read_progress`'s own idle fallback — pre-cache behaviour preserved byte-for-byte); the route injects it AND offloads the whole view via `run_in_threadpool` (the app.py doctrine), staying on the DEFAULT AnyIO pool like `/api/v1/pull/rate` (a deadline-guarded LIVENESS poll — worker hold capped per outage; the lake limiter is #1642's concern). NO STALE ILLUSION (Golden Rule #1): every FILE-served payload is stamped at serve time (onto a per-request COPY, never the memo) with the ADDITIVE `progress_source` ∈ {live, cached, unverified} + `progress_probe_age_s` keys — a memoised serve lags a publish by ≤ the 1 s TTL, an `unverified` serve may lag arbitrarily but is LABELLED with a growing age; the in-process + idle arms are pure in-memory (zero staleness) and stay unstamped, byte-identical. The route docstring is rewritten to the honest envelope (the false "never touches the lake" claim corrected in the SAME change; a sibling docstring-only correction was observed committed-then-reset in the shared session tree — if PACK-L3 lands its own wording first the merge keeps whichever survives, the semantics agree). SANCTIONED behaviour deltas, honestly scoped: the file arm now lags a brand-new publish/appearance/disappearance by ≤ the 1 s TTL (below the 2 s poll cadence — no verdict-category impact), and a COLD-start wedge serves the honest idle fall-through (bounded ~0.5 s) instead of blocking the poll for the outage's duration. REGRESSION (fails-before verified by inlining the route body back: `/api/v1/sweep-progress` read 5041 ms): `tests/integration/test_dashboard_eventloop_realserver.py::test_sweep_progress_stalled_read_keeps_loop_free_and_is_bounded` — a REAL uvicorn server (the #1622 harness), `read_progress` stalled ~5 s, asserts (a) a concurrent `/api/v1/state` stays < 2 s AND (b) the sweep-progress response ITSELF is bounded < 2 s serving the honest fall-through, then (c) the late-returning daemon self-heals and the next poll serves the real file payload provenance-stamped. HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10): a wedged read syscall cannot be killed — the guarantee is a free loop + a bounded response + at most ONE abandoned daemon per outage (the DEC-FETCH-HUNG-WRITE-DEADLINE-001 stance); a cold-start wedge has no memo, so it honestly reads idle until the volume recovers; this is a latency/liveness fix, NO throughput claim. Files: NEW `brutex/dashboard/sweep_progress_cache.py` (100% line+branch, 37-test suite `tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_progress_cache.py`) + `brutex/dashboard/app.py` (the view seam, the route, the `build_app(sweep_progress_cache=)` injection) + the view-seam pins appended to `tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_progress.py` + the realserver guard. ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` on the touched modules introduces 0 new diagnostics (the one pre-existing `stage3_refine` import-note is on pristine main, byte-identical); pyright 0 errors on the new module. **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-PROGRESS-NONBLOCK-CACHE-001. (Ledger: #1640 — renumbered #1630→#1634→#1635→#1640 (slot-sync; absolute block assigned by the merge coordinator over #1323's #1633-#1636 reservation) across the pack-train fold + the #1352 main collision (main's #1631 = DEC-ONECLICK-TOP100-OBJECT-ROOT-001): main landed DEC-SWEEP-LOG-VOLUME-GUARD-001 at #1630 first, and the original high-jump clear of the concurrent PACK-L1/L2/L3 siblings (which raced the then-#1623+ band, now #1637-#1639) collided exactly as the renumber-on-merge clause anticipated. The DEC-ID is the stable handle.)

1641. **DEC-DASHBOARD-EVENTLOOP-OFFLOAD-003 — the SIX click-driven POST pull-LAUNCH routes' resolver/store reads are moved OFF the uvicorn event loop (audit M16 — the #1622 ledger's own named-but-unbuilt follow-up, closed): `POST /universe/pull` (`store.get`) · `/pull-all` (`resolve_pull_symbols`'s per-token `store.get`s + `_select_bulk_targets`' two whole-store reads) · `/pull-expiries-contracts` (selection + the `reference_only_security_ids` scan) · `/pull-historical` — the WORST offender: `RegistryStore.open` + `_resolve_historical_contracts` (a full `list_contracts` over the whole cached chain) + `_underlying_kind_map` over BOTH `_select_bulk_targets` reads, ALL on the loop — plus its multi-select COMPOSITE arm (`_start_composite_historical_pull` made async, its selection + REF-set reads offloaded) · `/retry-failed` (`resolve_pull_targets`); `/pull-pipeline` was ALREADY whole-body-offloaded (its own #1588-era fold) and is untouched** (2026-07-09 on `claude/pack-l4-offload-stragglers`; fix(dashboard) — READ/launch-side dashboard only, ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap change; the background pull WORK was already off-loop — this closes the PRE-job resolution gap). THE CLASS: a slow/stalled lake volume froze EVERY concurrent dashboard request the moment the operator clicked a Pull button, because the `async def` launch bodies resolved their selection synchronously (DuckDB store reads + the registry open/scan) before starting the background job. ONE consistent pass, the #1622 `api_universe_instruments` idiom on every route: the resolver/store reads move into a named threadpool closure (`_resolve_selection` / `_resolve_composite_selection` / `_resolve_direct_selection` / `_resolve_targets`) awaited via `run_in_threadpool`; `HTTPException`s raised inside propagate out of the offload unchanged, and every `ValueError` → 400 catch stays OUTSIDE the offload — VALIDATION SEMANTICS BYTE-PRESERVED (each arm's 400 detail text untouched; the empty/no-match `/pull-historical` selection still 400s BEFORE the job starts — never a fabricated contract; the six-step `underlying_kinds` map is still built only for a NON-empty selection, the pre-offload order). The parity oracle is the EXISTING route suites passing UNMODIFIED (the pull-historical grammar/400 suite, the expiries-contracts unknown-symbol/bad-kind/no-selection 400s, groww_primary's pull-all forms, the credential-refusal 503s — 125 tests re-run green). REGRESSION (fails-before verified by inlining `/pull-all`'s closure back onto the loop: a concurrent `/api/v1/state` measured 5005 ms vs the < 2 s budget): FIVE real-uvicorn guards in `tests/integration/test_dashboard_eventloop_realserver.py` (`_assert_launch_resolution_off_loop` — stalls `InstrumentStore.get` / `_resolve_historical_contracts` ~5 s per route, asserts the concurrent poll stays fast AND the released launch answers its EXACT pre-offload validation status/detail). HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10): the launch REQUEST itself still waits for its own resolution (no deadline claimed — a wedged volume delays the click's answer; only the LOOP is protected); and on the four non-pipeline job routes `BackgroundPullJob.start`'s cross-process flock/lease acquire still runs AFTER the awaited resolution back ON the loop (only `/pull-pipeline`'s whole-body offload runs it on a worker) — offloading/bounding `start` on those four routes is a NAMED follow-up, deliberately outside this coordinator-scoped resolver pass. HOSTILE-REVIEW FOLD (round 1, MEDIUM — reproduced): offloading the `/pull-historical` direct-arm resolution WIDENED the concurrency window on `RegistryStore.open` — open is WRITE-on-open (schema DDL + an `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO schema_meta` stamp), and the pre-offload on-loop execution had serialized it, so two simultaneous launch clicks could newly race a DuckDB Transaction/Constraint exception → `RegistryError` (a BruteXError, NOT a ValueError) escaping the offload uncaught → HTTP 500 (the reviewer reproduced 10/12 concurrent opens raising). The route now maps `RegistryError` from the resolution to an honest, retryable **503 "registry busy — retry"** (the registry read routes' RegistryError-degrade precedent; nothing launched, nothing corrupted), regression-pinned fails-before (guard removed → 500) by `test_concurrent_registry_open_race_is_503_not_500`; the OTHER `RegistryStore.open` sites were audited — every one runs on the single-flight JOB thread (`_work` bodies) or already sits behind a RegistryError degrade, so the direct arm was the only route-path exposure. Files: `brutex/dashboard/app.py` only (+ the realserver test file). ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` 0 new; pyright 0 errors on both touched files. **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-EVENTLOOP-OFFLOAD-003 (the exact id #1622 reserved for this class). 1642. **DEC-DASHBOARD-LAKE-IO-LIMITER-001 — the dedicated bounded LAKE-I/O capacity limiter (audit M4 — #1522's + #1622's own named follow-up, closed): every LAKE-touching dashboard offload (58 sites in `app.py`) moves off AnyIO's DEFAULT shared 40-token thread limiter onto the app's OWN 32-token `LakeOffload` limiter, so a WEDGED lake volume pins at most 32 lake workers and can no longer starve the liveness / in-memory / CPU offloads out of the default pool** (2026-07-09 on `claude/pack-l4-offload-stragglers`; fix(dashboard) — READ-side dashboard threading only, ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap change; payloads byte-identical — the dispatch limiter moved, nothing else). THE MEASURED REGIME (M4): 59+ `run_in_threadpool` sites shared the default 40-token limiter; ONLY the rate-bridge read was deadline-guarded, so each wedged lake read pinned a token FOREVER — the 41st offload queued 2701 ms behind 40 wedged workers, and the deadline-guarded `/api/v1/pull/rate` could not even START (its route-level bound holds only GIVEN a free token — #1522's honest envelope stated this exact gap; the `SummaryCache`/`MoversSnapshotCache` cold waiters block unbounded on their single-flight events, each wedged waiter holding a token too). THE FIX: NEW `brutex/dashboard/lake_offload.py` — `LakeOffload`, a tiny COMMON `run_in_threadpool` twin (`anyio.to_thread.run_sync(functools.partial(...), limiter=<own CapacityLimiter>)`; identical call/exception contract — `HTTPException` 400s propagate unchanged) sized `DEFAULT_LAKE_OFFLOAD_TOKENS=32` (deliberately BELOW the default pool's 40 so even a future chained offload cannot deadlock the whole pool; env `BRUTEX_LAKE_OFFLOAD_TOKENS`, fail-loud int ≥ 1 — a `0` would wedge every lake route shut, so it is REFUSED), constructed once per app in `build_app` (`lake_offload=` injection seam; imported LAZILY beside fastapi — anyio ships with the `[ui]` extra only, the app.py wheel-free-import doctrine) as `_run_lake`. CONVERTED (58 sites — every offload that touches the lake volume / a DuckDB store / the sweeps+sweep_runs trees): the instruments/expiries/contracts stats+rows · universe summary/instruments/index-constituents/load-instruments · the single-symbol `pull_candles` + ALL SIX launch-route resolution closures (#1641) + the `/pull-pipeline` whole-body launch · pull-progress `_phases` · coverage/coverage-spot/completeness(+CSV+per-symbol) · mapping/master/economics-integrity(+CSVs) · parse-skips · the lake-uniqueness census · coverage/windows + /options · the movers gate snapshot + resolve · preopen symbols + the two report `_build_rows` · the sweep `/run` launcher + `/sweep/leaderboard` · the six oneclick artifact readers · the `/db` tables/table/columns/query/datasets/cascades/candles/window-ledger/options/registry pages. KEPT ON THE DEFAULT POOL, deliberately (each named in-code): the deadline-guarded LIVENESS memos (`/api/v1/pull/rate` rate-bridge #1522 + `/api/v1/sweep-progress` #1640 — worker hold capped per outage by their own 0.5 s deadline guards, and they MUST stay startable during a lake outage — the whole point) · the `.xlsx`/`.zip` CPU renders (no lake I/O at render time) · the `/api/v1/logs` rotating-file tail (local disk, not the lake volume). PLUS one honest comment each at the `SummaryCache.get_or_refresh` cold-waiter `decision.wait()` + `MoversSnapshotCache.get_or_compute` `wait_event.wait()`: those waiters now hold LAKE-limiter tokens (bounded by the same 32) — the waiter SEMANTICS are deliberately unchanged (redesigning them is out of scope, stated).
