1643. **DEC-DB-CANDLES-TORN-READ-RETRY-001 — the `/db` candle pagers (`query_candles` + `query_option_candles`) gain the torn-read RETRY-ONCE guard — the candle twin of DEC-WINDOW-TORN-READ-RETRY-001 (#1227): a live pull's atomic `os.replace` landing between/inside one request's MULTIPLE independent `read_parquet` opens no longer 500s the page** (2026-07-09 on `claude/pack-l5-addenda`; fix(dashboard); READ-side viewer only — ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no lake/schema/scope/vocab/rate change; NUMBERING: renumbered provisional #1633→#1637→#1638→#1643 (slot-sync; absolute block assigned by the merge coordinator over #1323's #1633-#1636 reservation) across the pack-train fold + the #1352 main collision (sequential above live main-max #1630, shifted +1 when main's #1631 DEC-ONECLICK-TOP100-OBJECT-ROOT-001 landed; the DEC-ID is the stable handle)). ROOT CAUSE (scout-verified + deterministically reproduced): one pager request runs the deduped-total COUNT (`_execute_parquet_resilient`) and the page SELECT (`_execute_candle_page_resilient`) as TWO separate `conn.execute` calls over `read_parquet(glob)` — a concurrent writer's `os.replace` between/during them yields (i) a raced transient `duckdb.Error` → a route 500 on that paging click, and (ii) a total/rows disagreement; the corrupt-skip ladder (DEC-DB-CORRUPT-SKIP-001) never guarded the exact tear windows — `_execute_candle_page_resilient`'s `cursor.fetchall()` streaming read sits OUTSIDE its `try`, its degraded re-run is itself unguarded, and the #1228 manifest pruned-page path's own `fetchall` likewise sits outside its fail-closed ladder. REJECTED alternatives (recorded): a DuckDB transaction — DuckDB transactions DO NOT snapshot external parquet (scout-measured 10→25 rows INSIDE one BEGIN/COMMIT), and `COUNT(*) OVER ()` — it breaks the #867 count-cache design + its bench pins. FIX (the house idiom mirrored VERBATIM): NEW COMMON `db_view._retry_candle_read_once(operation, *, source, retry_sleep)` — retry ONCE on `duckdb.Error` after the SHARED `_DUCKDB_RETRY_DELAY_S` (0.1 s; `retry_sleep` injectable, `None` = the ALIASED `from time import sleep`; one `db.candle_read_retry` WARN with error_type + source) — wired in BOTH pagers at (a) the COUNT execute+fetch INSIDE `_legacy_count_total` (so the manifest whole-request-degrade RECOUNT rides the guard for free), (b) the #1228 manifest pruned page (covering its unguarded `fetchall`), and (c) the legacy page execute+fetch (covering `fetchall` + the corrupt-skip degrade re-run); every wrapped operation re-plans/re-globs FRESH from the partition directory per attempt, so the retry reads the freshly-replaced files; a retried success is cached NORMALLY by the injected count cache (connection-level proof: exactly ONE COUNT reaches DuckDB across two clicks). PLUS the honest observed-lower-bound clamp: when the page returned ROWS, the returned `total` is raised to at least `offset + len(rows)` on both pagers — an OBSERVED lower bound; an EMPTY page never adjusts the total (it proves nothing — `offset + 0` bounds only for k > 0 rows) — the CACHED-total vs live-page skew is INHERENT to the #867 generation-keyed design (a concurrent writer within one generation leaves the cached total stale) and stays, documented in both docstrings. HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): retry-once NARROWS the race, it does NOT eliminate it — a SECOND replace landing inside the 0.1 s retry window still raises (the route 500s; a genuine SQL bug likewise still propagates after one bounded pause — never silently swallowed, the #1227 contract); NAMED un-retried residuals (smaller windows, same class): the F&O/option stored-life SPAN reads, the derived prev-close BASELINE reads, and the `_greeks_tolerant_select` probe. Fails-before CAPTURED: with the fix reverted to merge-base a one-shot `duckdb.InvalidInputException` on the page read propagates raw (`RAISED ... calls=1`); fixed, the same injection recovers (`rows=3 total=3 calls=2`). TESTS: NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_candles_torn_read_retry.py` (17 — guard-primitive unit incl. the duckdb.Error-subclass hypothesis property + shape-errors-never-retried + both sleeper arms; count/page transient-recovers + persistent-still-raises + zero-sleep no-error parity + cached-not-poisoned + the clamp, on BOTH pagers) JOINS the ci.yml db_view per-module gate; `db_view.py` 100.00% line+branch over the full 16-file gate suite. ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW FIX ROUND folded (same branch, pre-merge): the clamp is GATED on a non-empty page (`if raw_rows:`) at BOTH sites — the unconditional `max(total, offset + len(rows))` FABRICATED `total == offset` on any empty page past the end (route-reachable via the unbounded `offset` query param; reproduced: a 3-row lake at offset=999999 read total=999999 where merge-base correctly read 3) — with empty-page-past-the-end + stale-cache-shrink regressions on BOTH pagers; the headlined #1228 manifest PRUNED-page retry window gains real teeth (a seeded manifest-served `query_candles` with a one-shot `duckdb.Error` inside the pruned page's FIRST attempt recovers via `_retry_candle_read_once` with exactly one 0.1 s sleep, `page_source` still `manifest`); `_retry_candle_read_once`'s docstring honesty-corrected (the pruned path RE-PLANS from the captured stats-context snapshot's FIXED rel-path list, NOT a fresh glob — correct because the replaced content is re-read and `_stats_tokens_intact` degrades to legacy on any token move) and the clamp wording reconciled here + in both pager docstrings; suite 17 → 21 tests, `db_view.py` stays 100.00% line+branch.**

1644. **DEC-OPENAPI-ANNOTATIONS-RESOLVE-001 — `/openapi.json` (and with it the `/docs` + `/redoc` UIs) renders again: the route closures' stringified `-> JSONResponse`/`Response`/`HTMLResponse` return annotations are made resolvable by hoisting the response classes into MODULE globals in BOTH `dashboard/app.py` and `dashboard/launch_button.py` — the module's OWN `_make_ws_handler` WebSocket-hoist idiom** (2026-07-09 on `claude/pack-l5-addenda`; fix(dashboard); docs-surface only — ZERO route behavior change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NUMBERING: renumbered provisional #1634→#1638→#1639→#1644 (slot-sync; absolute block assigned by the merge coordinator over #1323's #1633-#1636 reservation) across the pack-train fold + the #1352 main collision (sequential above live main-max #1630, shifted +1 when main's #1631 DEC-ONECLICK-TOP100-OBJECT-ROOT-001 landed; the DEC-ID is the stable handle)). ROOT CAUSE (scout-verified + reproduced on the pinned merge-base): `from __future__ import annotations` stringifies every annotation, and `build_app` (+ `register_launch_routes`) imports the FastAPI response classes FUNCTION-LOCALLY (the deliberate lazy-import doctrine), so the 71 route closures' return annotations are ForwardRefs unresolvable against `endpoint.__globals__` (the defining MODULE's dict — a function-local import is invisible to it); FastAPI's lenient `try_eval_type` KEEPS them at registration time and the failure surfaces lazily — `app.openapi()` raises `PydanticUserError` ("TypeAdapter[... ForwardRef('JSONResponse') ...] is not fully defined") → `/openapi.json` 500s and the `/docs`/`/redoc` UIs die on their schema fetch (their static HTML shells still served 200 — stated honestly). FIX: after the guarded function-local import SUCCEEDS, hoist ONLY the annotation-referenced classes into `globals()` strictly BEFORE any route registration — `app.py` hoists `HTMLResponse`/`JSONResponse`/`Response` (`PlainTextResponse` is a runtime value only, deliberately NOT hoisted), `launch_button.py` hoists `JSONResponse` — the EXACT mechanism `_make_ws_handler` has always used for `WebSocket`, chosen over a guarded module-level `from fastapi.responses import ...` because the closures' annotations statically resolve to the LOCAL import (ruff F401 flags the module-level one unused) and an `except ImportError: pass` arm trips the un-blanket-ignored S110 — the in-module precedent wins (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). TWO-MODULE COMPLETENESS pinned: fixing app.py ALONE still 500s the WHOLE schema on launch_button's two `-> JSONResponse` closures (verified both arms — full revert AND launch_button-only revert each fail the new suite with the same `PydanticUserError`-driven 500). The lazy-import CONTRACT is PRESERVED: both modules still import with fastapi absent (NEW subprocess meta-path-blocker pin; `build_app`'s friendly no-fastapi RuntimeError arm byte-untouched + still pinned by `test_build_app_raises_helpful_error_without_fastapi`). MEASURED post-fix: `/openapi.json` 200 with 86 paths, `/docs` 200, `/redoc` 200 (real `build_app` + `TestClient`). TESTS: NEW `tests/unit/test_dashboard_openapi_annotations.py` (5 — schema 200 + non-empty paths + direct `app.openapi()` + docs/redoc shells [companion pin, honest scope note] + the launch-route presence completeness pin + the no-fastapi subprocess import contract).**

1666. **DEC-CACHE-SERVE-LAST-KNOWN-001 — the probe-None "compute fresh, cache NOTHING" doctrine at the poll routes is replaced by SERVE-LAST-KNOWN-labelled: a revision-probe OUTAGE (a stalled lake volume) now serves the most-recent cached payload for the route's STABLE key prefix — labelled by the additive `revision_probe` degrade field, WARNed ONCE per outage (latched), recovered with one INFO — instead of re-paying the full O(stores × rows)/O(artifact) build on EVERY poll exactly while the volume is least able to serve it (the probe-outage compute-storm keystone; closes C-r2-3 for `/results`)** (2026-07-09 on `w1-keystone-floors`; fix(dashboard); NUMBERING: PROVISIONAL — claimed as live-main-max #1644 + 1 at authoring time, renumber at the merge slot per the batch coordinator's stitch; FINAL: coordinator-assigned block #1666–#1672 over 14 in-flight claims). **THE MECHANISM (movers_cache.py):** `MoversSnapshotCache` gains `serve_last_known(prefix, compute=)` → `(value, served_last_known)` + the `mru_prefix=` bookkeeping kwarg on `get_or_compute` (every successful resolution — clean hit / floor stale-serve / single-flight store — records `prefix → key` in a capacity-LRU-bounded pointer dict, with a direct `key == prefix` fallback for stable-key callers) + the NEW exported `OUTAGE_GENERATION = -1` sentinel: an outage poll with NO last-known entry computes ONCE and SEEDS the slot at the sentinel (a persistent outage pays the build once, not per poll; `revision_generation()` is non-negative and every caller passes ≥ 0, so the first post-recovery read ALWAYS recomputes — a lingering seed can never read as clean). The once-per-outage WARN (`movers_cache.revision_probe_outage`, `served=last_known|fresh_seeded`) + the recovery INFO (`movers_cache.revision_probe_recovered`) ride a capacity-bounded per-prefix latch — the `rate_bridge_cache` `_degraded` posture, never a per-poll log storm. **THE ABSENT-vs-OUTAGE SPLIT (oneclick_artifacts.py):** NEW frozen `ArtifactProbe(token, outage)` + `artifact_probe()` / `runs_probe()` — `FileNotFoundError`/`NotADirectoryError` = ABSENT (`outage=False`; the volume answered), any other `OSError` = OUTAGE (`outage=True`) — with `artifact_revision`/`runs_revision` now thin byte-compatible `.token` views; the previously SILENT OSError→None mapping gains the once-per-outage `oneclick.artifact_probe_outage` WARN + `oneclick.artifact_probe_recovered` INFO via the module `_ProbeOutageLatch` (bounded 64 paths, `reset()` test seam — the groww epoch-warn module-latch precedent). ABSENT artifacts keep the pre-change cheap fresh-uncached computes (awaiting payloads) — a DELETED artifact is never served from a stale entry (Golden Rule #1). **SITES REWIRED (app.py, 5 of the 7 census bypass sites):** `/api/v1/sweep/leaderboard` (the C-r2-3 storm — `sweep_results_revision` None is strictly an outage, the absent tree is the stable `absent|absent` composite; the stable filter key `lb_key` is the prefix; `_probe_outage_payload` stamps the marker on a SHALLOW COPY so the cached dict stays unmutated) + oneclick `/runs`/`/manifest`/`/top100`/`/events` (probe-split branches; stable prefixes exclude the revision; `mru_prefix` threaded on the cached path). a foreign path's memo is never served); absent stays fresh-uncached. **HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10):** the outage serve is BOUNDED only by the outage's duration (stated in the marker — the operator sees `revision_probe` on every affected payload); concurrent fresh-seed misses of one prefix may compute in parallel (the single-flight machinery is not engaged on the seed arm — bounded to the first poll wave, stated in the docstring); the marker is ADDITIVE (clean payloads byte-identical, pinned). **TESTS (fails-before captured):** the old T-c6 pin (`test_probe_outage_computes_fresh_uncached`) is REWRITTEN to the new contract (pre-fix: `KeyError: 'revision_probe'` + a 3-scans-for-3-polls storm, captured by stash-revert); 1667. **DEC-NAV-CACHES-FLOOR-REKEY-001 — the FLOORLESS cache family (the R8 nav-latency trio `/api/v1/coverage` + `/api/v1/universe/completeness` + `/api/v1/universe/mapping-integrity`, and the R9 `/results` `_sweep_leaderboard_cache`) is re-keyed L1-style — freshness token OUT of the KEY, INTO the generation via the ONE `revision_generation` digest bridge — and opted into the pull-time adaptive floor, so a mid-pull `mark_dirty` storm / a running dashboard sweep's per-flush revision moves are BOUNDED, LOGGED floored serves instead of a full O(datasets)+ledger / O(stores × rows) rebuild per poll (the #920 storm class these four were structurally blind to)** (2026-07-09 on `w1-keystone-floors`; companion of #1666 DEC-CACHE-SERVE-LAST-KNOWN-001 — the two compose at `/results`). **THE DEFECT:** all four instances were constructed with NO `pull_active_probe`/`adaptive_floor` AND folded their freshness token into the KEY at `generation=0` (`_nav_latency_key` / the `rev=` fold), so the floor was DOUBLY unreachable: mid-pull `_summary_cache.generation` bumps on EVERY window tick → every 4 s/15 s poll minted a COLD key → a full rebuild back-to-back exactly while a pull was running; the L2 key doubles as #1666's serve-last-known prefix); all four constructions gain `pull_active_probe=_pull_live, adaptive_floor=True`. 1672. **DEC-WRITE-DEADLINE-ZOMBIE-SLIM-001 — the abandoned zombie durable-write daemon no longer pins a GUARD-layer duplicate of the window's bars payload: `append_with_deadline` hands the payload through a ONE-SHOT single-slot holder the worker POPS inline in the call expression, and the guard frame `del`s its own `bars` parameter — so once the wrapped `sink.append` starts, the ONLY reference is the executing frame's own (the irreducible residue, now honestly documented as a BYTES envelope)** (2026-07-09 on `w3-engine-budget-zombie`; fix(adapter/groww); NUMBERING: provisional — assigned sequentially above the live main-max #1644 (+ this batch's #1671), subject to the batch coordinator's merge renumber; FINAL: coordinator-assigned block #1666–#1672 over 14 in-flight claims; the DEC-ID is the stable handle). FIX (guard-layer only, `config/deadline.py` byte-UNTOUCHED — no generic seam needed, every other `run_with_deadline` caller byte-identical): the payload rides `payload: list = [bars]`; the named worker fn calls `sink.append(..., bars=payload.pop())` INLINE (CPython transfers argument ownership into the callee frame — empirically verified on the venv 3.12: a callee that `del`s its arg frees the object while the guard thread is still wedged), and the guard frame `del bars` immediately after the handoff so the exception traceback carries an EMPTY holder, never the payload; `_append_popped` runs exactly once (the `run_with_deadline` worker contract), so the pop can never see an empty slot. THE DESIGN mirrors DEC-MOVERS-MIN-VOLUME-001 (#1034) EXACTLY: ONE COMMON pure module `brutex/dashboard/movers_underlying_class.py` (`normalize_underlying_class` — the twin of `normalize_futures_tier`/`normalize_min_volume`, blank/unknown → `all`; `candidate_passes_class` predicate; `filter_by_underlying_class` rank-time filter returning `(kept, n_unclassified_excluded)`; `class_note_suffix`/`class_echo` EMIT-ON-non-default helpers) applied at RANK time in `build_snapshot_payload`/`build_futures_payload`/`build_options_payload` over the SAME cached candidate set — NEVER a re-scan, never a new lake read. CLASSIFICATION is viewer-reads-storage-only (Golden Rule #1): SPOT resolves the kind from the lake segment (`spot_kind_from_segment` — `INDEX`→index, `CASH`→stock; the stored reflection of the master's `is_index`, CLAUDE.md §6); FUTURES/OPTIONS look the parsed underlying token up in a `{underlying → kind}` map built by `build_underlying_kind_map`, which REUSES the SAME `primary_fno_underlying` + `is_index` classification the six-step pull order uses (`historical_pull`/`composite_pull._underlying_kind_map`, DEC-PULL-SIX-STEP-ORDER-001 #1527 — never re-minted; the map key space is the `primary_fno_underlying` FORM space, `NIFTYJR`→`NIFTYNXT50`/`BAJAJ-AUTO`→`BAJAJAUTO` — the original "matches the contract underlying forms exactly by construction" claim here was FALSE, the PARSED contract token being hyphen-PRESERVING; CORRECTED by the fix round below, which normalises the token into the map's key space at the lookup). Each candidate dataclass (`MoverSnapshot`/`FuturesMover`/`OptionMover`) gains a DEFAULTED additive `underlying_kind: str = "unknown"` field set once at candidate-compute time (in the existing `replace(...)` alongside the contiguity stamps), never emitted in a row — so goldens + existing payloads are byte-identical. FRONTEND: a `<select id="uclass">All|Indices|Stocks` in the same control row (`movers.html`), textContent-only DOM, sending `&underlying_class=` ONLY when non-`All` (default byte-identical), wired into the onchange handlers. **DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the task's literal "thread the class into candidate_key" instruction** (recorded honestly): the class is a RANK-time filter over the SHARED cached candidate set — unlike the Near/Next/Far tier (#917, which changes WHICH contract each underlying contributes and so MUST be in the key), the class does NOT change which candidates are computed (every candidate carries its `underlying_kind`), so it is deliberately NOT in `candidate_key` (exactly the min_volume template) — threading it would triple-cache an identical set and violate "SAME cached candidate set". Cache-independence is proven instead by a route test: Indices then Stocks over the SAME coordinate return DIFFERENT row sets while `movers_cache.size() == 1`. HONEST: DISPLAY-zone read-only filter — the default `All` payload is byte-identical (pinned on all three tabs: no `underlying_class`/`excluded_unclassified` keys, no `Class:` note suffix); ENGINE UNCHANGED (NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX), F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY, no scope/vocab/rate change. `movers_underlying_class.py` (NEW) + `movers_snapshot.py` + `movers_futures.py` + `movers_options.py` ALL 100.00% line+branch; ruff + ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict` clean on all touched source incl. `app.py`; pyright 0 errors on the touched modules + `app.py`. **ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW FIX ROUND folded (same branch, pre-merge; 4-lens panel — security SHIP · visual SHIP · correctness FIX-FIRST · O-complexity FIX-FIRST):** (1) the MAJOR hyphenated/aliased-underlying MISCLASSIFICATION — the kind map keys the `primary_fno_underlying` FORM (`BAJAJAUTO`) but the candidate lookup passed the RAW parsed token, which is hyphen-PRESERVING (`parse_fno_symbol` yields `BAJAJ-AUTO`), so EVERY hyphenated F&O stock silently dropped out of BOTH Indices and Stocks and inflated `excluded_unclassified`; `fno_kind_from_underlying` now normalises the token INTO the map's key space AT the lookup (required kw-only `aliases=` — the SAME `primary_fno_underlying` + sourced alias map the builder uses, ONE normalisation law, no copy-paste between the futures/options call sites; `resolve_fno_index_aliases()` hoisted ONCE per compute call in both candidate loops so the per-candidate cost stays O(1)), and the falsified "exactly by construction" claims (module docstring, `build_underlying_kind_map`, both stamp comments, this entry) are honesty-corrected to the normalise-at-lookup mechanism; pinned by unit (hyphenated + `NIFTYJR`-aliased map/lookup round trips) AND route tests (a `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO-…-CE` option + a hyphenated futures contract each land in `Stocks` with `excluded_unclassified == 0`). (2) the futures-parse TRUNCATION twin — `parse_future_symbol` read `parts[1]`, so `NSE-BAJAJ-AUTO-30Sep25-FUT` parsed underlying `"BAJAJ"`; now right-ANCHORED (`"-".join(parts[1:-2])`, mirroring the canonical `parse_fno_symbol` — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON) with every consumer audited (all in `movers_futures.py`: the `_discover_futures` grouping key, the dated display name, the underlying-spot probe — each previously mis-keyed by the truncation): SANCTIONED corrections — a hyphenated future's display name now carries the FULL underlying and its spot/premium probe queries the full spelling instead of the truncated token; the stale "a stock name never hyphenates" comment corrected; parse pin added. (3) the memo-key STALENESS class (the O-complexity FIX-FIRST) — the `{underlying→kind}` map cache was keyed on the write generation alone, missing a keyless `load-instruments` (which moves the master WITHOUT bumping the generation — the documented `master_revision` trap the sibling nav-latency caches close); the key law now lives in ONE helper (`app._underlying_kinds_cached` — the map keyed on the `master_revision` CONTENT token at FIXED generation=0, the `_nav_latency_key` token-in-key precedent, which ALSO avoids pointless rebuilds on mid-pull write-generation ticks, the #920 lesson; the two copy-pasted `get_or_compute` sites collapsed onto it), and — because the cached F&O CANDIDATE sets carry the map's verdict STAMPED per row, so a fresh map beside stale stamps would still misclassify — the SAME master token is folded into the F&O candidate cache keys at ALL FOUR composition sites (route futures/options + the post-pull warmer's futures/options jobs), closing the staleness class END-to-END; the warmer additionally now THREADS `underlying_kinds` into its `compute_*_candidates` calls (previously it computed with the default `None`, stamping every warmed row `unknown` — an Indices/Stocks click on a freshly-warmed default coordinate returned EMPTY rows until the next generation bump — the same staleness class surfaced during the fold, fixed with route/warm key parity kept so warmed entries are still HIT; the pre-existing warm-parity pin `test_dashboard_movers_options.py::test_warm_grid_coordinate_poll_is_a_cache_hit_carrying_pcr` — design test #28, which primes the cache exactly as the warm job does — is re-keyed onto the NEW composite key + threaded kinds, staying the pure-cache-hit oracle under the new key law). Route-proven: a master-revision move (a new instrument row upserted with NO generation bump) reclassifies on the very next poll, and a call-count spy pins ONE map build per (generation, master-revision) across repeated futures+options polls. (4) the default byte-identity pin STRENGTHENED (finding 3) — full frozen-payload equality (kwarg-omitted ≡ `underlying_class=None` ≡ `"All"`, `json.dumps` sorted-keys equality, all THREE tabs; the kwarg-omitted call is byte-for-byte the pre-change caller shape). 1681. **DEC-NIFTY-PRICE-SOURCE-AXIS-001 — a NEW `PriceSource` cell-coordinate sweep axis for the price source of VWAP + EMA20/EMA200 over {open, high, low, close, hlc3}, mirroring the `fib_anchor` axis** (2026-07-10 on `claude/vwap-ema-price-source-axis`; feat(engine)). BEFORE: VWAP's typical price was hardcoded to HLC3 and the EMA20/EMA200 source was hardcoded to close — there was no way to brute-force the indicator price source. AFTER: an operator can sweep the VWAP and/or EMA price source via the CLI `--price-source-cells` flag (a one-factor-at-a-time lattice of `<vwap>:<ema>` cells over {open, high, low, close, hlc3}). By DEFAULT the axis is a single baseline cell `(hlc3, close)` — DORMANT, byte-identical to today, existing run_ids unchanged. OPERATOR-ORDERED: pivots + Fibonacci stay STATIC (standard formulas); VWAP + EMA are the genuinely run-time-dynamic indicators and get real drill-down over their price source. MECHANISM: the price source is a pre-FFI Python scalar reduction in `stage1a.py` (`_reduce_vwap_source_paisa` → typical_paisa i64; `_reduce_ema_source_float` → rupees f64; the HLC3/CLOSE arms are verbatim the pre-axis code; an exhaustive `assert_never` guards the enum), so a source variant is a per-cell choice of which OHLC reduction feeds the indicator scalar — carried in the run-identity `params` EXACTLY like the existing `fib_anchor` axis. NO vocabulary bits, NO `indicator_version`/crate bump, NO Rust change (Stage-1A stays Python). Params are DEFAULT-OMITTED — the source keys are emitted only when non-default — via the ONE `price_source_params_fragment` helper (`PriceSource` enum + the helper live in `strategies/types.py`), so existing run_ids stay BYTE-IDENTICAL (golden- and SHA-pinned: the default-cell run_id `b264fd0b…` matches main, and the default Stage-3 tree is SHA-identical to main). Threaded through the orchestrator, the kernel cache (with a source-mismatch guard), parallel, supervisor, verify, results-depth, cascade, and Stage-3 refinement. Nightly automation EXCLUDES the axis (stays baseline). SCOPE + BUDGET (honest — Golden Rule #10): VWAP-source cells are meaningful ONLY on the NIFTY-futures dynamic track (spot indices carry no real volume → bits 52/53 are junk; a NON-BLOCKING warn fires on spot); EMA-source cells apply everywhere; the 3-index production engine stays cardinality-1, untouched. The full 5-cell COMBINED single run does NOT fit ≤2 days (≈2.3-7.4 M4-days). The operator's bar is "max 2 days PER real sweep run" — each non-default cell staged as a SEPARATE cardinality-1 invocation is ≈ baseline (≈0.45-1.48 M4-days pre-Apriori, derived from the launch_button k≤6 = 4.2-13.9 M4-days × the ~10.7% k=1..5 fraction) ≤ 2 days, so the STAGED design satisfies the bar. Apriori is NOT in this checkout; no combined-with-Apriori headroom is claimed. OPERATOR DECISION ITEMS (surfaced, not silently decided): `hl2`/`ohlc4` EXCLUDED — HLC3-clones on liquid bars, and /2 and /4 introduce a half-paisa rounding tie the /3 path never hits; `high`/`low` DEFERRED — a systematically-biased line against the fixed-`close` comparison is a correctness hazard, both kept in the enum for a cheap round-2 if wanted. VERIFICATION: 100% line+branch on all touched modules incl. `stage3_wire.py`; whole-package aggregate 100.00% (21066 passed, 0 fail); the default-cell run_id byte-identical to main (golden) + the default Stage-3 tree SHA-identical to main; 5 hostile reviewers + 5 refuters (2 clean rounds), mutant-kill teeth verified RED→GREEN; ruff / ruff-format / `mypy --strict` / pyright (0 new) / doctest / citation-accuracy clean; P-06 suffix-independence unchanged; Rust crates untouched + green; the Rust interface contract (EMA = rupees f64, VWAP = paisa i64) documented for the sibling's future Stage-1A→Rust port. ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX (+ the operator-authorized NIFTY-futures dynamic track); no vocab (60-bit) / rate / scope change. **Numbering:** takes #1681 — the coordinator's slot-wave ASSIGNMENT above the reserved bands (the in-tree ledger max at fold time was #1651; the gap is legal, the PR #1236 high-jump precedent; uniqueness is the law, DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001). **Files:** brutex/engine/stage1a.py, brutex/engine/sweep_orchestrator.py, brutex/engine/sweep_kernel.py, brutex/engine/sweep_parallel.py, brutex/engine/sweep_run.py, brutex/engine/sweep_supervisor.py, brutex/engine/sweep_verify.py, brutex/engine/cascade_wire.py, brutex/engine/stage3_wire.py, brutex/engine/results_depth_pass.py, brutex/strategies/types.py, brutex/strategies/spec.py, brutex/universe.py, brutex/cli.py, docs/MIGRATION.md, CLAUDE.md. **Decision ID:** DEC-NIFTY-PRICE-SOURCE-AXIS-001.
1694. **DEC-SWEEP-RECONCILE-STATCACHE-001 — the sweep-launch catalog reconcile gains a durable, opt-in, VALUE-SAFE per-partition STAT CACHE, so a WARM (byte-unchanged) `brutex sweep-all` launch skips the redundant full-bytes `sha256` + timestamp re-read of every partition** (2026-07-08 on `claude/latency-sweep-reconcile-statcache`; feat(engine); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / write-path change; run identity BYTE-IDENTICAL). On EVERY `brutex sweep-all` launch, `cli.cmd_sweep_all` calls `reconcile_catalog_from_lake` per swept `(symbol, interval)` BEFORE the first mask evaluates; that reconcile re-reads each partition's `timestamp` column (`pl.read_parquet(path, columns=["timestamp"])`) AND `sha256`s the FULL file bytes (`hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes())`) even when the lake is byte-unchanged since the last launch — one of the redundant full passes in the pre-sweep prelude. **FIX (the value-safe half of the launch-latency work — the freshness/Pass-C cache is DROPPED from this PR):** (1) three ADDITIVE catalog columns `file_mtime_ns` / `file_size` / `file_ino` (`brutex/data/catalog.py`, added via three separate `ALTER TABLE partitions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ... BIGINT` in `Catalog.open`, kept OUT of the frozen 11-field `CatalogEntry` model AND the shared 11-column `upsert`/`get`/`list_partitions` SELECTs) persist a partition file's `os.stat` freshness token; a legacy pre-migration row reads a `None` token (NULL is NEVER a match — no COALESCE-to-0). (2) two NEW dedicated methods `Catalog.get_partition_stat_tokens` (bulk-load a series' `(year,month) → (mtime_ns,size,ino)` map in ONE indexed query) + `Catalog.set_partition_stat` (a separate `UPDATE`, a DuckDB fault → wrapped `CatalogError`). (3) `reconcile_catalog_from_lake` gains a NEW `stat_cache: bool = False` param: when `True`, each file is `os.stat`-ed first and, on an EXACT `(st_mtime_ns, st_size, st_ino)` token match against its stored row, the `sha256` + timestamp read + upsert (and the L1 invariant classification) are ALL skipped (`ReconcileResult.stat_cache_hits`); a changed / new / legacy-NULL-token file recomputes as today and best-effort backfills its token (a token-write failure logs `catalog.reconcile.stat_write_failed` + continues — NEVER fails the launch, the file stays a MISS next launch); a partition that vanishes between the glob and the `os.stat` (TOCTOU) is counted-skipped (`catalog.reconcile.stat_skip`), never a crash. (4) `stat_cache=True` is set at EXACTLY ONE call site — the `cmd_sweep_all` launcher, which DISCARDS the reconcile result + heals nothing there; every OTHER caller keeps the default `stat_cache=False`, so the cascade-wire L1 auto-heal consumer (`cascade_wire.py` → `heal_after_reconcile`, which reads `ReconcileResult.findings`) and the `lake audit-unique` census (which uses `scan_lake_invariants`, structurally independent of reconcile) STILL detect a byte-unchanged-but-poisoned partition on every launch (an unconditional skip would have silently suppressed heal/census detection of foreign-month / legacy-drift / dup-timestamp rows that `get_bars` WILL load into slices — a real correctness regression, guarded against here). **`st_ino` is mandatory:** every lake writer publishes via `os.replace` (a fresh inode), so an inode change defeats a same-size in-place rewrite AND a coarse-mtime external-SSD collision (the HFS+/exFAT stale-fresh class) — the same freshness envelope `lake_revision._stat_token` already trusts. **CORRECTNESS (Golden Rule #4):** the sweep's `data_snapshot_hash` (`stage3_wire.data_snapshot_hash`, `bxsnap2`) hashes the in-RAM `slices` from the ReplayFeed bar preload, NOT the catalog `raw_hash` (verified: `cmd_sweep_all` never calls `Catalog.data_snapshot_hash`; `raw_hash` feeds only `data verify` / lake-heal). The stat-cache skip only avoids RE-COMPUTING the reconcile for unchanged files; `get_bars` re-reads the ACTUAL file content, so it never changes which bars load or their values → run identity is byte-identical. REAL-RUN PROOF (fixture NIFTY lake, real `ParquetWriter` + `ReplayFeed` + `data_snapshot_hash`): OFF (stat_cache=False, cold) → digest `3bce5e3b55056073414e48a273262f38a21d305ce8b28b4f9681c9ae2110df9d`, reconciled 2 / hits 0; ON cold → SAME digest, reconciled 2 / hits 0; ON warm (same catalog re-run) → SAME digest, reconciled 0 / hits 2 — byte-identical across all three, warm launch does ZERO parquet reads + ZERO `sha256` (read-count spy). **HONEST ENVELOPE (Golden Rule #10):** this removes the redundant full-bytes-`sha256` reconcile pass (Pass A) on WARM byte-unchanged launches — a ~2-3× cut of the RECONCILE prelude (the per-partition ts-column read + full-bytes sha256 both drop to a single `os.stat`), but it does NOT make the launch near-instant: the bar preload + per-bar Decimal materialization (Pass B) remains uncached every launch and dominates the pre-sweep prelude; the Pass-C derived-TF freshness cache and the Pass-B near-instant lever are SEPARATE future work, deliberately NOT in this PR. The COLD first launch (and the first launch after any lake change or a post-upgrade catalog whose rows carry NULL tokens) stays O(P) over P partitions — byte-identical to today; only the SECOND-and-later warm launch is stat-only. **GATES:** `brutex/data/catalog.py` + `brutex/data/catalog_reconcile.py` BOTH 100.00% line + branch (171/54 + 99/28); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict brutex` clean (the lone `cma` import-not-found is a pre-existing baseline in the UNtouched `stage3_refine.py`, an env stub artifact); `pyright` 0 errors on the touched files. NEW tests: `tests/unit/test_catalog_statcache.py` (migration + the two methods incl. the closed-catalog guard + a DuckDB-fault stub-conn wrap — 9), `tests/unit/test_catalog_reconcile_statcache.py` (snapshot-hash equality OFF/cold/warm + warm zero-read spy + invalidation + NULL back-compat + TOCTOU + best-effort backfill + shared-caller non-regression incl. the `lake audit-unique` census exit-code — 10), `tests/bench/test_catalog_reconcile_statcache_o1.py` (warm per-partition flat vs partition count + warm cost invariant to per-file bar count / bytes — 2). **Files:** `brutex/data/catalog.py`, `brutex/data/catalog_reconcile.py`, `brutex/cli.py` (ONE launcher call-site, `stat_cache=True`), `tests/unit/test_catalog_statcache.py`, `tests/unit/test_catalog_reconcile_statcache.py`, `tests/bench/test_catalog_reconcile_statcache_o1.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-RECONCILE-STATCACHE-001. 1675. **DEC-CONV-COMMIT-SMOKE-DELEGATE-001 — the smoke test `tests/smoke/test_pre_push.py::TestConventionalCommit` no longer carries a hand-copied conventional-commit subject regex; it now DELEGATES to the ONE authoritative validator `scripts/ci/check-conventional-commits.sh --msg-file` (Golden Rule #11 COMMON), killing the drift** (2026-07-09 on `claude/conv-commit-smoke-delegate`; test(smoke) only — no `brutex/` source touched; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; NUMBERING: #1675 — coordinator-assigned; #1674 went to DEC-COVERAGE-MISSING-SESSIONS-001 / PR #1369 — the DEC-ID is the stable handle). ROOT CAUSE: there were exactly TWO copies of the conventional-commit subject regex — the AUTHORITATIVE comma-ACCEPTING shell checker (`scripts/ci/check-conventional-commits.sh:59`, PR #1085, backed by its `tests/redteam/test_redteam_conv.py` scope-comma + compound-prefix pins) and a DRIFTED comma-REJECTING inline copy in the smoke test (`CONVENTIONAL_COMMIT_REGEX = re.compile(r"…(\([a-z0-9_/-]+\))?…")`, single scope segment only). On a comma-scope squash — `fix(dashboard,test): make launch-button disk gate hermetic in tests — inject disk_usage probe (#1380)` — the HEAD subject PASSED the shell checker but FAILED the drifted inline regex, so the push-to-main smoke run went RED while every commit-gate + redteam pin stayed green. FIX: DELETE the inline `CONVENTIONAL_COMMIT_REGEX` (and the now-unused `import re`); add `_CONV_CHECKER = REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "ci" / "check-conventional-commits.sh"` + a `_subject_is_conventional(subject)` helper that writes the subject as the first line of a temp file and runs the checker in `--msg-file` mode (exit 0 => valid or `Merge*`, nonzero => invalid — the single source of truth, no second regex); `test_head_commit_subject_matches` skips when the checker is absent and otherwise asserts via the helper (the git-failure / empty-subject / `Merge ` skips preserved). PLUS a NEW HEAD-independent parametrized `test_msg_file_delegation_policy` giving the delegation its own teeth through `--msg-file` (accepts `fix(dashboard,test): …` + `feat(a,b,c): …` + bang + `a/b-c_d` charset; rejects empty scope `fix()`, trailing/leading empty segments, `ci+chore:` compound type, `nope:` bad type, no-colon, uppercase scope — mirroring the redteam policy). Tests-only; touched exactly two files (`tests/smoke/test_pre_push.py` + this ledger); the shell checker itself is byte-untouched.**

1695. **DEC-BXSNAP2-PARITY-GOLDEN-001 — an OBSERVATIONAL parity-golden tripwire that FREEZES the current Python `arrow_table_to_bars` → `data_snapshot_hash` (`bxsnap2`) run-identity digest, so a FUTURE Rust/Arrow port of the per-bar bar-materialization can diff against it mechanically** (2026-07-08 on `claude/bxsnap2-parity-golden`; `test(golden)` — test/fixture-only, ZERO `brutex/` + ZERO `rust/**` source touched, changes NO production behavior). CONTEXT: the sweep's run identity folds `data_snapshot_hash` (preimage `bxsnap2`, `brutex/engine/stage3_wire.py::data_snapshot_hash`) into the `blake3(… ‖ data_snapshot_hash ‖ …)` run id (Golden Rule #4). That hash streams each materialized `CandleBar`'s seven fields, and the price fields render as `Decimal(str(float)).__str__()` — CPython `str(float)` is shortest-round-trip (an integer price → `"20000.0"` NOT `"20000.00"`; a half value → `"20000.5"` NOT `"20000.50"`), and `Decimal` then re-renders a large magnitude with an UPPERCASE exponent (`1e+16` → `"1E+16"`) and EXPANDS a small one (`1e-05` → `"0.00001"`). A future Rust port that formats `f64` naively would silently diverge the run identity and break the twin-run proof; this harness FREEZES the current Python path as the oracle so any future divergence fails loudly. WHAT SHIPS (all under `tests/`): NEW `tests/golden/_bxsnap2_parity/` helper package (builds pyarrow tables in the canonical 7-column schema `Catalog.get_bars` returns, then runs them through the REAL `arrow_table_to_bars` → `CandleBar` list → `data_snapshot_hash`); NEW `tests/golden/generate_bxsnap2_parity_golden.py` deterministic regenerator; NEW frozen `tests/golden/fixtures/bxsnap2_parity_golden.json` (committed digest bytes for four edge cases — integer prices, 2dp/half-paisa tick-grid closes, the DEC-SWEEP-DATA-EDGE-GUARDS-001 #1616 bad-tick-screen KEPT-SET with a ÷10 scaled spike SKIPPED + a reopen-gap first bar KEPT, and a Diwali Muhurat evening-session KEPT-SET); NEW `tests/golden/test_bxsnap2_parity_golden.py` asserting the current path reproduces every frozen digest EXACTLY + the price-positivity REFUSAL contract (a non-positive bar RAISES at the read boundary, never enters a digest) + a focused `str(float)` → `str(Decimal(str(float)))` formatting-contract pin at the `1e16`/`1e17` sci-notation thresholds and `.0`/negative/zero (boundaries a realistic OHLC bar cannot reach, documenting the exact CPython contract the Rust port must reproduce). HONEST (Golden Rule #10): OBSERVATIONAL only — it changes NO production behavior and adds NO production surface; the frozen digests are source-committed bytes, NOT a live Rust-run comparison (the Rust port lands later and diffs against these); regenerate the fixture ONLY on a DELIBERATE Python-path change, and only with a new DEC-ID + a note that every dedup/cache run identity goes cold (the v1→v2 `bxsnap2` precedent). GATES: the NEW helper module 100% line + branch (47 statements, 0 missing); ruff `check` + `format --check` clean on all three touched test files; `pyright brutex tests` clean; `mypy --strict brutex` is unaffected (CI runs mypy on `brutex` only, not `tests`). ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope / vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar change. 1680. **DEC-SWEEP-APRIORI-TUPLE-001 — the Apriori anti-monotone level-wise PRUNED sweep candidate generator (default-OFF `BRUTEX_SWEEP_APRIORI=1`)** (2026-07-10 on `claude/sweep-apriori-prune`, PR #1393; feat(engine/sweep_apriori), DRAFT). WHAT IT SHIPS: behind the default-OFF tri-state env flag `BRUTEX_SWEEP_APRIORI=1`, a classic Apriori join + subset-prune candidate generator (NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_apriori.py`) replaces the unpruned per-cell k-tuple enumeration (`combo_mask.iter_masks_k_of_bits`) with a level-wise frequent-itemset walk (F₁ frequent singletons by hits ≥ `min_hits`; level-j candidates by joining F_{j−1} pairs sharing the first j−2 items, subset-pruning all (j−1)-subsets, conflict-pruning at j=2, then hit-filtering), dropping raw enumeration ~25× so k≤6 NIFTY fits the envelope (`n_enumerated` ~25× drop). PARITY (the merge-acceptance gate): a pruned cell sweep is BIT-IDENTICAL to the unpruned path — leaderboards + survivor sets + byte-identical results artifacts (`store_content_hash` + `cell.parquet`) + circuit-breaker counters — because DSR/overfit trial-count N = `len(kept)` (the Stage-1B survivor pool) is prune-invariant and hits(M) is anti-monotone under AND-extension so survival (hits ≥ `min_hits`) is downward-closed → the pruned candidate set is provably exact; verified with the overfit gate ACTIVE (dsr_min ∈ {0.0, 0.5, 0.95}), across multi-k, PYTHONHASHSEED-invariant (load-bearing — trial-stats Sharpe uses `math.fsum` over enumeration order), emission-order = enumeration-order (an in-order lexicographic-on-bit-position subsequence of `iter_masks_k_of_bits`). CIRCUIT BREAKER (deterministic, pure-integer): The Apriori circuit-breaker check |C_j|·n_bars > MAX_MASK_BARS (strict >, env BRUTEX_SWEEP_APRIORI_MAX_MASK_BARS default 1_159_200_000_000, MODELED/UNVERIFIED-on-M4 per Golden Rule #10) is evaluated on the WHOLE RAW per-level candidate count at the k==1 target level, every intermediate level 2..k−1, and the final level k; for k≥2 the level-1 singleton count |C₁| = n_unique ≤ 60 is DELIBERATELY NOT budget-checked (trivially bounded, provably non-runaway). A trip raises the NEW typed `SweepAprioriBudgetError` (a `SweepComboError`) → the existing TUPLE_FAILED path (loud, counted, non-zero exit, deterministic redo); the trip decision is stride-invariant and shard-invariant on the settled raw per-level counts, with NO float/`time.time()`/rate anywhere (bit-identical Python↔Rust, Golden Rule #7); #1608's parallel-sweep stall watchdog is the SEPARATE non-identity wall-clock backstop. A `>= 64`-bit vocabulary with the flag ON raises the typed `SweepAprioriUnsupportedError` (also a `SweepComboError` → TUPLE_FAILED), never a raw `ValueError` (today's vocab is 60 bits). MAX_COMBOS (kept inside this DEC): the non-Apriori path is byte-unchanged; an Apriori-aware auto-raise of the DEFAULT `max_combos` makes the k≤6 grid reachable (the shipped default would otherwise refuse k≥4) — an explicit operator `--max-combos N` WINS (the bypass replaces ONLY the argparse DEFAULT sentinel, never an explicit value; no raise, no auto-raise, no log); an out-of-range k (`k > n_unique` or `k < 0`) is FILTERED + DEFERRED to the downstream `SweepGridConfig` clean `EXIT_USER_ERROR`, never a raw traceback. HONEST (Golden Rule #10): there is no real lake on the research box — all throughput figures (`~4.3h @8 workers`, `R_walk=1.61e8 mask·bar/s`, the breaker default ≈ 2h serial) are MODELED and live only in comments/docstrings/env-defaults, never asserted measured; pending operator bars B2 (real-lake pruned-vs-unpruned re-run) + B5 (prox=50 k-cap policy). BLAST RADIUS: NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_apriori.py` + additive `brutex/engine/sweep_run.py` (branched enumeration source + shared `_count_hits` + two typed errors) + `brutex/cli.py` (`effective_max_combos` wiring) + 4 test files (unit/golden/property/bench) + `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (per-module 100% gate) + `.github/workflows/mutation.yml` (zero-survivor pairing); the #1608 guard modules (`sweep_orchestrator.py`/`sweep_parallel.py`/`sweep_supervisor.py`/`sweep_checkpoint.py` + dedup/bloom) are 0-byte diffs vs main, only fed a higher `max_combos`. `sweep_apriori.py` + `sweep_run.py` 100% line+branch; mutmut 172/172, SURVIVED 0; two consecutive clean adversarial refuter rounds (R6 + R7). ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no vocab/scope/rate change. **Files:** brutex/engine/sweep_apriori.py, brutex/engine/sweep_run.py, brutex/cli.py, tests/unit, tests/property, tests/golden, tests/bench, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/mutation.yml, docs/MIGRATION.md. **Decision ID:** DEC-SWEEP-APRIORI-TUPLE-001.
1697. **DEC-SUPPLY-CHAIN-GOVERNANCE-001 — supply-chain + repository governance hardening, the owner-action follow-ups flagged by the merged security-audit PR #1204: (a) a root LICENSE file that finally ships the PROPRIETARY / all-rights-reserved terms the packaging metadata already declared but never carried as text (Copyright (c) 2026 SJParthi; no license granted — deliberately NOT an OSS license, which would grant rights the owner never chose); (b) a root SECURITY.md coordinated-disclosure policy — supported version = `main`, vulnerability reports routed through GitHub private Security Advisories (the repository "Report a vulnerability" flow) with NO personal email hardcoded, a best-effort acknowledgement window (no fabricated response-time SLA — Golden Rule #10), a proprietary-research scope note, and an explicit request not to open public issues for security reports; (c) EVERY GitHub Actions `uses:` reference across all 19 workflow files is SHA-PINNED to its immutable 40-hex commit digest — 193 references over 18 unique actions — each keeping a trailing `# <tag>` comment so future bumps stay legible, closing the mutable-tag supply-chain risk (a re-pointed `vN` tag or moved release branch could otherwise inject code straight into privileged CI). Each digest was resolved authoritatively via `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> <ref>`, dereferencing annotated tags to their underlying commit (`^{}`) where present; validated with `actionlint` (exit 0), a full YAML parse of every workflow, and a grep proving ZERO third-party `uses:` remain on a mutable ref. Also attempted deletion of the stray `origin/undefined` ref (a harmless duplicate of an already-merged commit).** (2026-07-10 on `claude/cool-bohr-xjyesn`; chore(security); CI-governance + repo-docs ONLY — ZERO `brutex/` code touched, ZERO engine/lake/schema/scope/vocab/rate change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY). HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): SHA-pinning FREEZES each action at a known-good commit — it stops mutable-tag drift but does NOT by itself audit the pinned code, and future security patches to those actions must now be pulled in deliberately (the trailing `# <tag>` comment is the legibility aid; a scheduled dependency-bump review remains an owner task); the LICENSE + SECURITY.md are governance text, not a code change; the four unique actions with no annotated tag (branch-head or lightweight-tag refs) are pinned to that ref's commit SHA, which is correct but tracks whatever the maintainer last pushed to that ref at resolve time. **Files:** LICENSE, SECURITY.md, .github/workflows/*.yml (19 files), docs/MIGRATION.md. **Decision ID:** DEC-SUPPLY-CHAIN-GOVERNANCE-001.

(1) **G12 false crash-loop CRITICAL** — the DURABLE consecutive-corruption counter was reset ONLY on a clean checkpoint LOAD (`record_clean`), never on successful run completion, so a single crash-recovery (this run's OWN load was the corrupt one → quarantine → fresh start → COMPLETE, which never calls `record_clean`) left the count sticky at 1 durably (`run_id` timestamp-free), and a LATER, INDEPENDENT corruption escalated `1 -> 2 == threshold` into a FALSE CRITICAL `checkpoint_crash_loop` page for two corruptions SEPARATED by a fully successful run. FIX: NEW `sweep_quarantine.reset_checkpoint_corruption(run_dir)` (unlinks the durable counter file, fail-soft) called from `_finalize` at a terminal COMPLETE/SUSPECT_COMPLETE boundary (gated on `checkpoint_store is not None`), so `consecutive` now means "corruptions with no successful run in between" — matching the crash-loop intent. The existing across-enters edge test was rewritten to a GENUINE loop (each relaunch RAISES before completing, so no reset fires) + a NEW `test_g12_two_corruptions_separated_by_success_no_alert` pins the false-alert-is-gone case. (2) **C6 heal resume-startup residual** — `cmd_sweep_heal`'s liveness guard judged only `progress_verdict(progress)`, which LAGS a RESUMING run: on a crash-resume the on-disk progress file still shows the PRIOR attempt's DEAD pid until `_reset_progress_at_launch` rewrites it (AFTER the checkpoint preload), so a concurrent `sweep-heal --execute` in the enter→preload→reset window read NOT_RUNNING and could quarantine the resuming run's stores/checkpoint (contradicting the branch's own "a LIVE run is never quarantinable"). FIX: NEW pure `sweep_liveness.exit_status_running(progress)` reads the ADDITIVE `exit_status` sub-dict `read_progress` already enriches — the `exit-status.json` (state=running + LIVE pid) is written FIRST at run-core enter under the G6 flock, before the preload, so it does NOT lag; the heal now treats the run live when the progress verdict OR the fresh exit-status says so. Improves on main (main's monotonic-vs-wall bug made EVERY live run quarantinable; round-1 fixed the steady state; round-4 closes the resume-startup window). (3) **Row 19 VERIFIED** (keep_awake): the dashboard one-click job path IS keep_awake-covered — `dashboard.sweep_runner.run_sweep_from_request → cli.cmd_sweep_all → sweep_run_core` enters `keep_awake` at run-core enter (the standalone cascade_wire/supervisor internals are not operator entry points; only `--detach` survival past process death stays CLI-only, the disclosed envelope). (4) **Row 21 HONEST STATUS** (per-run log file): the `sweep_run_core(log_file=)` plumbing ships but stays deliberately UNWIRED at `cmd_sweep_all` — a run-scoped RAW log that captures the sweep's own structlog output requires file-routed logging at PROCESS START (structlog's `cache_logger_on_first_use` prevents a mid-run reroute of already-cached sweep loggers, exactly why `cmd_dashboard` configures once at startup), a CLI-dispatch-wide change out of scope for this surgical fix and carrying real cross-CLI logging-regression risk; in the meantime the run's material events ARE a `run_id`-scoped structured log ON THE INTERNAL DISK via the Row-15-mirrored `flight-recorder.jsonl`, so R40/R37 have a forensic trail today — the standalone raw run-log wiring is a NAMED follow-up (DEC-SWEEP-RUN-LOG-FILE-001). `sweep_liveness.py` + `sweep_quarantine.py` + `sweep_run_core.py` stay 100% line+branch; ruff/ruff-format/`mypy --strict`/pyright clean on the touched files. **Files (round 4):** brutex/engine/sweep_quarantine.py, brutex/engine/sweep_run_core.py, brutex/engine/sweep_liveness.py, brutex/cli.py, tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_quarantine.py, tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_run_core.py, tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_liveness.py, tests/integration/test_sweep_progress_enrichment.py, docs/MIGRATION.md, CLAUDE.md. 1714. **DEC-SWEEP-BLOOM-AUTOGROW-HEADROOM-001 — the sweep-cache resume Bloom auto-grow gains real headroom ABOVE the persisted digest count, so a within-wall over-capacity resume genuinely self-heals instead of advancing one tuple per process restart** (2026-07-09 on `claude/dedup-c6-bloom-autogrow`; fix(engine); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope / 52→60-vocab / rate-cap / lake-schema / stored-bar / run-identity change). ORIGIN = the 2026-07-08 uniqueness/dedup product audit, finding **C6**. `brutex/engine/sweep_cache.py::_auto_grow_capacity` sized the fresh in-RAM resume Bloom to `grown = max(persisted, ceil(configured_capacity × 1.25))`. Once `persisted >= 1.25 × configured_capacity` the `max` collapsed to `persisted` (ZERO headroom): the resume rebuild re-inserts every persisted digest, filling the Bloom to EXACTLY capacity, so the FIRST new `record_digest` immediately trips the FAIL_CLOSED `BloomCapacityExceeded` — a resumed sweep then advanced by only ONE tuple per process restart until the operator manually raised `--sweep-cache-bloom-capacity`, FALSIFYING the DEC-ENGINE-MISC-PACK-001 "within-wall >capacity resume self-heals" contract. Because every data pull re-keys the whole grid (a fresh `data_snapshot_hash`), the persisted count crosses any fixed configured capacity overnight, so this wedged the operator on ordinary resumes. FIX: `grown = max(ceil(persisted × 1.25), ceil(configured_capacity × 1.25))` — the `ceil(persisted × 1.25)` arm leaves 25% headroom ABOVE *persisted* so the rebuild fills to *persisted* insertions with room to spare and new records land; the `ceil(configured_capacity × 1.25)` arm keeps the empty/small-store sizing byte-identical. The `brutex.orchestrator.bloom.MAX_BLOOM_BYTES` 16 GiB hardware-envelope wall refusal (`SweepCacheCapacityError`, CLAUDE.md §8) is preserved byte-for-byte and still fails closed on the (now larger) grown sizing — a capacity that would bust the wall still refuses, never silently overflows. IDENTITY-NEUTRAL (Golden Rule #4): the Bloom is an L1 prefilter over the LMDB exact ground truth and is NEVER part of run identity — `combo_digest` (blake3) is byte-untouched and no golden / descriptor / fixture / vocab file changed (the diff touches exactly 3 files: the source + the unit + the property test). Adds a CONSEQUENCE test `test_resumed_over_capacity_records_more_than_one_new_tuple` (seed 5, resume at `bloom_capacity=3`, record 2 NEW digests — both land, >1 tuple of progress) that FAILS before the fix (0 tuples, capacity 5 reached) and PASSES after (grown 7, headroom 2); the unit + property formula-value pins are updated to the new headroom formula (values only — the 16 GiB wall arm and the `persisted <= capacity` identity arm are unchanged). `sweep_cache.py` 100% line+branch under the strict per-module `--cov=brutex.engine` gate (2516 unit tests green); ruff / ruff-format clean, `mypy --strict` clean on the touched module, pyright at the origin/main baseline. 1716. **DEC-SWEEP-RESUME-STORE-GUARD-001 — the grid-sweep resume/cache skip tiers gain a stat-level INTACT-ARTIFACTS gate, closing the confirmed S5b silent-data-loss defect: deleting SOME tuple store Parquets (checkpoint/dedup-cache/sentinels kept) and re-running the SAME grid read `skipped_resume=N, tuples_run=0`, exited clean, and left the deleted finalists PERMANENTLY missing — the operator explicit acceptance scenario "massive pull → delete → re-run must never silently lose data"** (2026-07-09 on `claude/dedup-s5b-resume-store-guard`, base `873666f4` = the #1330 `claude/sweep-unkillable-core` tip; fix(engine); PROVISIONAL entry number = this branch's ledger-max(#1622)+1 — RENUMBER-ON-MERGE against live main + in-flight PRs, the #1546-#1550/#1617 precedent; DEC-SWEEP-RESUME-STORE-GUARD-001 is the stable key). **THE CONFIRMED DEFECT (S5b, coordinator-approved MAJOR; evidence `scratchpad/dedup-fix/S5B_VERDICT.md` + the `repro_5b.py`/`repro_5b_cacheonly.py` pair, both re-run pre/post on this tree — pre-fix STILL-LOSES via the kill-switch-OFF arm, post-fix RECOVERED):** BOTH skip tiers fired before any store touch — the sequential checkpoint tier (`sweep_supervisor.py` `index < resume_from → continue`) and cache tier (`guards.cache.seen(...)`), AND their parallel twins in `sweep_parallel._gate_or_dispatch` (REQUIRED scope extension: the production CLI DEFAULTS to the parallel driver at workers>1, proven equally store-blind) — while the store-content self-heal (`_sentinel_resume`) lives inside `run_one_tuple`, never reached. **THE FIX (both tiers, both drivers):** NEW pure `tuple_complete.missing_tuple_artifacts(store_path) -> tuple[str, ...]` — exactly THREE `is_file()` existence probes (store Parquet · completion sentinel · trial-stats sidecar), zero reads, zero hashing; `()` = INTACT (skip honoured), any missing name → fall through to `run_one_tuple`, whose existing `_sentinel_resume` self-heals with a FULL byte-identical redo. PAIRING IS FILENAME-LEVEL only (both sibling names append suffixes to the digest-carrying store filename — name-adjacency IS the pairing at stat level); the sentinel's `tuple_digest` field and `store_content_hash` are deliberately NOT read or re-hashed per skip (O(1)-stat contract). THE THIRD PROBE (sidecar) is a justified extension of the pinned store+sentinel pair: sentinel and sidecar are co-written under the SAME `trial_stats_digest is not None` condition (sweep_run.py) and the grid drivers always supply the digest, so sentinel-present ⟹ sidecar-was-written — a missing sidecar is always a DELETION (the same silent-loss class, feeding Stage-4 DSR deflation), the stat is free, and a forced redo rewrites all three (test-pinned co-write invariant). GATING: sequential checkpoint tier via an `itertools.islice` prefix pre-scan collecting `forced: set[int]` (O(resume_count) time — a disclosed lightweight second prefix enumeration — O(#forced) memory); sequential cache tier via an inline lazy stat; a forced prefix tuple BYPASSES the cache tier directly to `run_one_tuple` (artifacts known-missing; `checkpoint.record` no-ops monotonically, `cache.record` re-records idempotently); parallel resume+cache tiers compute the predicate at most ONCE per tuple and reuse it; the parallel `quarantined_prior` tier stays FIRST and UNGATED. PATH SOURCE (the reproducer-compatibility keystone): `make_store_for` refactored from a bare lambda to the frozen `TupleStoreProvider` dataclass — `__call__` byte-identical (`load_or_create_store(tuple_store_path(...))`), NEW `.store_path(tuple_)` seam; the supervisor resolves its probe as explicit kw-only `store_path_for=` if given, else duck-typed `getattr(store_for, "store_path", None)`, else honestly INERT (one `resume_store_guard_inert` INFO — bespoke-lambda library callers byte-identical pre-fix); the parallel driver computes `tuple_store_path(self._root, tuple_, self._grid)` directly. ZERO-ROW SHAPE (verified first-hand): a completed ZERO-finalist tuple persists ALL THREE artifacts (`store.flush()` runs unconditionally and renders the full schema from empty row lists → a schema-only 0-row Parquet with a real content_hash; sidecar+sentinel under the always-supplied digest), so the predicate reads it INTACT and it keeps SKIPPING on every resume — no per-resume re-run tax (own test, double-resume pinned). THE ONE LEGITIMATELY ARTIFACT-LESS "completed" SHAPE is the distinct NO-BARS tuple (checkpoint-recorded with zero artifacts, `store_for` never called): under the guard it is stat-indistinguishable from a full-trio deletion, so it falls through on EVERY resume and re-settles cheaply as no-bars — a DISCLOSED, bounded behavior change (count shifts `skipped_resume` → `tuples_skipped_no_bars`; one `bars_for` probe per resume; fail-safe direction = re-verify; own test pins both arms; kill switch restores legacy). KILL SWITCH `BRUTEX_SWEEP_RESUME_STORE_GUARD` — DEFAULT ON (a data-loss guard must never require opt-in); explicit falsy restores the byte-identical pre-fix skip loop (the honest OFF: the S5b loss mode RETURNS — an informed emergency/pathological-stat-latency escape hatch, and the bench baseline arm); junk → fail-loud ValueError naming var+value BEFORE any tuple work, resolved once per driver run parent-side via `tuple_complete.resume_store_guard_enabled` over the COMMON `sweep_lookahead.env_flag_tristate` (imported, never copied), with the CLI resolving it EAGERLY pre-sweep for a clean `EXIT_USER_ERROR` (the BRUTEX_RESULTS_DEPTH precedent). MEASURED A/B (contract point 3; best-of-5 MIN, 200 fully-completed tuples, build sandbox 2026-07-09; `tests/bench/test_resume_store_guard_bench.py`): unguarded resume 0.0033 s → guarded 0.0141 s = ratio 4.23×, per-tuple guard overhead ≈ 0.054 ms (one ~200-byte BLAKE3 path digest + ≤3 lstats + the islice prefix re-enumeration over a ~17 µs/tuple nearly-free baseline loop) — an HONEST relative ratio over a nearly-free loop, absolute ~11 ms per 200 resumed tuples; gates = fixed 10× robust on/off ceiling + tier-routed per-tuple flatness (50-vs-200) + structural spies (exactly ONE predicate evaluation per skipped tuple, ZERO with guard off, ZERO store opens on an intact resume). HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10): the gate detects MISSING artifacts ONLY — a present-but-truncated/corrupt/content-swapped Parquet or sentinel still skips at the gate and heals only when the tuple re-enters (`_sentinel_resume` re-hash) or opens on the run path (G1 quarantine); TOCTOU (an artifact deleted between stat and skip) is missed THIS run and heals on the next resume; wedged-volume stat latency adds ≤3 lstats/tuple (the kill switch is the named operator lever). (b) HONEST floor accounting — `finished_at` (feeding `computed_at` + `compute_duration`, the adaptive floor's input) is now captured AFTER sizing completes, so the floor throttles for compute PLUS sizing whenever the deep walk does run; lock-wait stays EXCLUDED (the capture precedes the insert lock — source-order-pinned). 1723. **DEC-ARCH-EVAL-TRILLION-SCALE-001 — trillion-scale architecture evaluation: MEASURED verdict KEEP DuckDB+Parquet+stats-manifest AND KEEP vanilla JS — the O(1)-at-scale guarantee is an ARCHITECTURE property (finalists-only persistence + write-time manifests + materialized rollups + the bounded wire contract), not a language/engine property; two named serving follow-ups carry it** (2026-07-11 on `claude/arch-eval-trillion-scale`; docs(research); NEW `docs/research/ARCHITECTURE_TRILLION_SCALE_EVAL.md`; research/evaluation decision, DOCS-ONLY — ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope/vocab/rate change; the ledger number is coordinator-ASSIGNED — live-main max was #1711 at assignment, gaps are legal per the validator, and NO collision was found at append time). **METHOD:** three measurement workstreams — (1) a DB-serving benchmark over lakes built with the REAL production writers (`ParquetWriter` candle lakes at 0.98M / 9.8M / 48.9M rows; real `ResultsStore.flush` stores at 10/100/1000 × 1000 finalist rows; the engine `write_top100` → display `load_top100` chain), ≥20-rep median+p99, log-log exponent fits `t = a·N^b`; (2) a headless-Chromium 141 (Playwright) frontend render benchmark whose row renderer is a line-for-line mirror of the real screener render, incl. a MEASURED React 18.3.1 comparison; (3) a read-only file:line-cited architecture audit of the serving path. An earlier DB measurement pass ran concurrently with the 50M lake build and was DISCARDED as contaminated; every number is from the clean re-run. **HEADLINE MEASUREMENTS:** (a) /db serving is per-DATASET-depth-bounded — the control experiment: a fresh 6-month symbol written into the 49M-row lake pages in **12.4 ms vs 12.8 ms in the 0.98M-row lake** (total lake size irrelevant; dataset depth grows with YEARS, ~12 month files/yr); manifest-ON exponents b≈0.33–0.47 vs OFF 0.63–0.84 (the manifest is worth 4–7× at 50M and manifest-OFF crosses 1 s at ≈260M proportional rows — the kill switch is a cliff); a single dataset needs ~1,800 month files (≈150 years of 1-minute bars) to cross 1 s at b=0.47 — structurally impossible for the partition scheme; (b) **the ONE measured sub-second breach is /results**: `load_sweep_scan` cold is strictly O(stores×rows) — 205 ms @10 stores → 23.7 s @1000 stores (b≈1.03, crosses 1 s at ≈55 stores) — and even the revision-cached WARM leaderboard rank is 904 ms PER POLL @1M finalist rows (b≈1.17); the one-click top100 is flat by construction (1.9 ms median, ≤100 entries); (c) the ClickHouse A/B is **VERIFIED** (chdb 4.2.0 installed): parquet-in-place ClickHouse is SLOWER than DuckDB on every dashboard-shaped page/count/slice (110.9 vs 83.8 ms page1 · 212.8 vs 59.5 ms count · 83.3 vs 44.9 ms slice); a real MergeTree copy buys 13× page lookups (5.9 vs 84 ms) + 4.7× full-lake aggregation (771 ms vs 3.6 s @48.9M) at the cost of a SECOND store (735 MB vs 213 MB parquet, 3.4×) + a 9.04 s/48.9M-row ingest sync + a daemon in the zero-services envelope — while the one-day whole-market movers READ off a PRE-BUILT DuckDB daily rollup is **2.7 ms** (build cost 3.70 s; ~940× vs the 2,524.8 ms raw scan — the honest framing is "pre-aggregation beats switching engines", NOT an engine-speed ratio: MergeTree's 771 ms from-scratch rollup is itself FASTER than the 3.70 s rollup BUILD); (d) frontend — UNCAPPED render is O(rows) in BOTH vanilla JS (paint ≈ N^0.94; 100k rows = 29.3 s main-thread block) AND React 18 (paint ≈ N^1.09; 50k = 14.6 s; JS cost ~1.4–1.5× vanilla) — same asymptote, constants differ; CAPPED render (the existing SHOW_ALL_CAP=1000) is flat (~190–265 ms regardless of a 100k-row payload); WINDOWED render is flat 0.7–0.9 ms sync with ZERO longtasks from 100 to 500,000 rows (5000× range); NO client compute at the repo's actual caps exceeds 15 ms (sort-5k 6.7 ms · filter 0.3 ms · cumsum 0.1 ms · 85k-cell format 15.0 ms) — a framework swap or Rust→WASM kernel has no latency lever. The audit grounds the spine: only top-K finalists per tuple are ever flushed (`sweep_run.py:1774-1817`; `results_store.py:537-543`) so the ~33B trials (Phase-10 730B) NEVER reach serving — persisted output ≈ tuples × top_k ≈ 10⁶–10⁷ rows; the 10y × full-universe LAKE is ~1.5–2B rows / ~3.6M files, never a trillion — the trillion-class number is the discarded trial stream (a COMPUTE problem for the Rust kernels + funnel, irrelevant to any serving engine). **VERDICT A: KEEP DuckDB+Parquet+stats-manifest — no ClickHouse / distributed migration** (the migration-cost dimensions all weigh against: byte-identical golden-pinned parquet rendering + re-flush idempotence, flock/`LakeWriteHalt` semantics, the hash-chained audit JSONL, `data_snapshot_hash` run identity, the single-M4-Pro zero-services envelope; MergeTree parts are not byte-deterministic). **VERDICT B: KEEP vanilla JS — the data-shipping contract (server pagination + capped/windowed render) is the lever, not the language.** The Rust-everywhere directive is explicitly RECONCILED (doc §9): DuckDB is a C++ ENGINE, not Python — the serving glue around it may convert to Rust per the directive (the duckdb Rust crate + arrow-rs serve it natively) ORTHOGONALLY to this verdict; a Rust rewrite preserving the same scan shapes preserves the same measured breaches, so the rollup follow-ups are the latency fixes regardless of serving language. **NAMED FOLLOW-UPS (not in this change):** (a) the /results persisted cross-store leaderboard rollup — top-K materialized at sweep flush time (the `top100_artifact` pattern generalized; the #1614 write-hook seam) so serving reads O(K), never O(stores); (b) generalized materialized rollups for whole-lake aggregation surfaces (movers-style; the measured ~940×); (c) file rollups for the audit's other named O(total) gaps (the `runs_revision` uncapped per-poll stat walk; the O(files) maintenance walks); (d) the viewport-bounded frontend contract on any new surface (windowed render for anything >1000 rows). **HONEST LIMITS (Golden Rule #10):** no literal 1B+/trillion-row lake was materialized (largest 48.9M rows; everything beyond is extrapolation via the fitted exponents, labelled as such); the sandbox (4-vCPU Xeon, 15 GB) is NOT the production M4 Pro — absolute ms are environment-specific, the CURVES and exponents are the evidence; the /results warm-rank 904 ms is in-sandbox @1M finalist rows (the M4 Pro is likely faster but the exponent is hardware-independent); chdb ≠ a tuned ClickHouse server deployment; the frontend was measured on a synthetic-but-shape-identical page, not the live dashboard. the `setInterval(pollRunSweep, 1200)` registration byte-unchanged — visible-tab cadence identical); (2) BOTH pollers fetch via the COMMON `bx-poll.js` `BXPoll.fetchJson('/api/v1/sweep-progress', BXPoll.DEFAULTS.FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS)` — the abort timer stays ARMED through the BODY read and a non-ok status THROWS, so EVERY failure mode (non-ok, rejection, abort, malformed body) funnels into ONE counted catch and never settles state — making the DEC-PULL-UI-STALENESS-001 posture claim TRUE (the entry's earlier draft over-claimed it with a plain unbounded `fetch()` — corrected here); defer guarantees BXPoll is defined before any INTERVAL tick or click callback fires — with ONE exception the round-2 review caught: the parse-time IMMEDIATE `pollSweepProgress()` kickoff runs DURING parsing, BEFORE the deferred bx-poll.js executes, so a bare synchronous kick TypeError'd on `window.BXPoll` on every fresh load of `/` (a second TypeError inside the catch → an unhandled promise rejection + console error, plus a spurious `__bxHbSweepErr` heartbeat blip — self-healing on the first 2 s tick, but a regression vs the interim guarded draft and exactly the class a Playwright console-error gate trips); the kickoff is now LOAD-ORDER-GUARDED — `if (window.BXPoll) pollSweepProgress(); else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', pollSweepProgress);` (defer scripts complete before DOMContentLoaded, so the deferred first paint stays prompt; `pollRunSweep` needs no guard — click/interval only, post-load) — and the interval/click calls stay unconditional; the interim inline backoff-constant fallback is DELETED (dead code that duplicated the COMMON law's constants — Golden Rule #11: `BXPoll.backoffDelayMs` is called directly, no second copy); (3) counted-failure exponential backoff in the DEC-PULL-UI-STALENESS-001 posture — quick retries then 3 s→30 s capped doubling, NEVER a give-up — implemented as skip-N-ticks (`runSweepNextTs`/`sweepProgressNextTs` gated at the top of each poller; the interval keeps ticking, no timer re-armed/cleared on failure — clearInterval remains ONLY the sweep-finished terminal arm, now reachable ONLY from a parsed-OK payload); (4) per-poller GENERATION guards (`runSweepGen`/`sweepProgressGen` — the #1558 gbPollGen / BXPoll pollSeq precedent): each entry stamps `++gen` and both the success and catch arms drop a superseded response, so a visibilitychange catch-up or a slower-than-cadence response can never repaint stale progress out of order nor mis-count a failure; (5) a NEW visibilitychange catch-up in the RUN CONTROLS IIFE, scoped `!document.hidden && sweepPoll` (only an ARMED poll fires; an idle Operator tab stays silent) and clearing the backoff gate; `pollSweepProgress`'s existing catch-up clears its gate too (its `__bxHbSweepErr` heartbeat hook now fires inside the ONE counted catch). DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: `tests/integration/test_dashboard_js_perf_frontend.py`'s `_POLLER_GUARDS` does NOT gain v29.html — that pin set is the skip-render-memo idiom for the uniform `poll()`/`setInterval(poll, 4000)` pages (its parametrized tests assert the 4 s cadence line, which v29 does not have); the v29 pins live in the poll-hygiene suite. HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10): SOURCE-STRING pins, not a browser-executed behavioural test (no JS runtime in CI; the #1557 Playwright browser-truth job does not drive these pollers) — the inline script block is `node --check` syntax-verified in-session; visible-tab happy-path cadence/data is byte-identical (first-statement early return + unchanged `setInterval` lines); TWO sanctioned visible behavior changes: a non-ok `/api/v1/sweep-progress` response no longer renders its error body as progress NOR fires the false-terminal "✅ Sweep undefined" (counted retry instead — a correctness fix), and a wedged/stalled endpoint now reads "(retrying)" under capped backoff instead of hammering at full cadence. TESTS: `tests/unit/test_dashboard_poll_hygiene.py` carries seven v29 pins (guard-before-fetch + cadence survival · the COMMON bounded-fetch law — fetchJson×2, zero bare sweep-progress fetches, zero inline backoff copy · the load-order-guarded parse-time kickoff — the guarded token present AND a bare synchronous `pollSweepProgress();` line negatively pinned so it cannot re-drift · counted-backoff state/gate/reset via `BXPoll.backoffDelayMs` · generation guards on both arms of both pollers · the armed-scoped catch-up · the pollSweepProgress backoff + heartbeat-in-catch + gate-clearing catch-up) following that file's substring-pin idiom; suite 21/21 green + the v29-adjacent suites (js-perf frontend, widget-visibility pause, sweep-run route wiring, ux-design, oneclick frontend, nav consistency) green. GATES: ruff + ruff-format clean on the touched test file; `python scripts/ci/validate_ledger_numbering.py` exit 0; conventional-commit subjects verified. **Files:** `brutex/dashboard/templates/v29.html`, `tests/unit/test_dashboard_poll_hygiene.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this entry). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-POLL-HYGIENE-002.
