1759. **DEC-DASHBOARD-READ-SCREEN-001 — the dashboard "split-brain" fix: `/movers` + `/db` bar reads routed through ONE COMMON engine-parity screen (`bad_tick` + `price_sanity`), so a corrupt bar can never render one number on `/movers` and a different one on `/db`, nor diverge from what the engine refuses** (2026-07-09 on `claude/dashboard-splitbrain-screen`; fix(dashboard)). ROOT: the engine screens stored bars at its read boundary (`feed/replay.py::arrow_table_to_bars` — positivity + OHLC-ordering + `BadTickScreen`, DEC-SWEEP-DATA-EDGE-GUARDS-001 #1616), but the two dashboard readers read the SAME stored partitions RAW — so an ×10 fat-finger spike (a self-consistent SCALED bar, positive + ordered) is DROPPED by the engine yet SERVED by the dashboard: `/movers` fabricates a Top-Value turnover + a spurious %-move (and `MoversSnapshotCache` caches it), `/db` shows the raw spike row; the same class of positivity-impossible bars (`high<low`, negative close) the engine quarantines is served raw on both. FIX (COMPOSE the EXISTING PUBLIC predicates, ZERO engine hot-path change): NEW `brutex/data/bar_screen.py` `SessionBarScreen` composes `bad_tick.BadTickScreen`/`is_bad_tick`/`bad_tick_screen_enabled` (the `BRUTEX_BAD_TICK_SCREEN` kill switch) with a NEW scalar `price_sanity.price_row_insane` (the per-row twin of the vectorized `price_violation_expr`, pinned row-wise by a scalar==vector property test) into ONE causal per-session screen; two thin wrappers drive it — polars `screen_frame` for `/movers` and `screen_rows` (bounded prior-bar `seed_bar` for cross-page bad-tick left-edge correctness, mirroring the `_intraday_prev_close_by_page_date` predecessor read) for the `/db` DuckDB page. WIRED: `/movers` M1 `_read_cut_1m_frame` (the choke point feeding turnover + display bars via `spot_session_value_paisa` + `_read_session_bars`), M2 `_read_intraday_bars` stored derived-TF branch, M3 `_read_daily_bars`, M5 `movers_futures._read_future_session`; `/db` D1 `query_candles` page read (seeded via NEW `_bad_tick_seed_bar`). DISPOSITION mirrors the engine with ONE sanctioned divergence: bad-tick → DROP + one WARN/session (the split-brain fix); INSANE (positivity/ordering) → DROP + count (`insane_dropped`) rather than the engine's whole-symbol RAISE, so `/movers` == `/db` (the anti-split-brain goal), the corrupt bar is never SERVED (the engine's "refuse to serve" holds for THAT bar), and the good remainder still renders. The ANTI-DIVERGENCE ORACLE (property test) pins `SessionBarScreen`'s KEEP-set == `arrow_table_to_bars`'s kept set over random bar streams, so the two call sites can never diverge from each other OR the engine, and both inherit any future internal first-bar-handling change automatically — DEC-BADTICK-HEAD-SEED-001 COORDINATION: the reader gates ONLY on the public objects and never forks the logic; if that fix adds a public `seed_close`/`seed_prev_close` param, the ONE `SessionBarScreen` construction site adopts it (flagged in-code). CLEAN-LAKE BYTE-IDENTITY (the ship gate): the screen only ever DROPS (never edits/reorders/re-types), so on a lake with no insane + no bad-tick bars every row classifies KEEP and both wrappers return the SAME input object — the existing `/movers` (320000/318660) + `/db` goldens pass UNMODIFIED (the ONE property test whose synthetic generator draws independent ≥4× minute jumps — a bad tick the engine ALSO screens — had its absolute-value oracle updated to mirror the screen; the TF-invariance property it tests is unchanged and stays green; no byte-equality fixture touched). Kill-switch parity: `BRUTEX_BAD_TICK_SCREEN=0` → the bad-tick arm is OFF on BOTH engine and dashboard (consistent raw view); `price_sanity` stays always-on both sides (the engine's unconditional positivity guard). HONEST: the `/db` page-local bad-tick screen's left-edge double-edge case (a spike on the page's first row whose true predecessor was itself a dropped spike) is not reproduced by a page-local screen — the whole-day `/movers` reader is always correct; the seed read (now a BOUNDED 8-bar screened WINDOW, not just the raw immediate predecessor — so a SINGLE spike / short cluster before the page no longer wrongly baselines the page's first good row) closes the common single-edge case, the deep-cluster residual is documented; the `/db` page `total` stays a dataset-wide count (over-counts by the screened rows on corrupt data only). OPTIONS-SCOPE AMENDMENT (hostile-review FIX-FIRST MAJOR-1, same branch): `SessionBarScreen`/`screen_frame`/`screen_rows` gain a `bad_tick_enabled` param splitting the screen into TWO independent-scope arms — the INSANE/positivity arm (`price_row_insane`) is UNIVERSAL (kept on spot/futures/options + all `/db` candle + `/db` option pages), but the ×4 BAD-TICK arm applies ONLY to engine-screened instruments (SPOT/INDEX + FUTURES) and is OFF for OPTIONS. Root: `_read_future_session` serves BOTH futures AND options (`movers_options.compute_options_candidates` calls it), so the initial wire gave options the SPOT-calibrated 4× threshold — but option PREMIA legitimately move ≥4×/minute on leverage (a deep-OTM ₹0.10→₹0.50 = 5×), so legit option bars would be DROPPED (a wrong options Top-Value + a stale LTP), AND `/db query_option_candles` was UNSCREENED → a brand-new `/movers`-options-vs-`/db`-options split-brain. Fix: the options `_read_future_session` call passes `bad_tick=False` and `query_option_candles` screens `bad_tick_enabled=False` (insane-only, no bad-tick seed), so `/movers`-options == `/db`-options (both insane-only, no 4× false-drops) while spot/futures keep the full engine-parity screen; the 4× threshold is justified ONLY by NSE index circuit-breaker physics and the engine never screens options (REFERENCE_ONLY), so there is no parity to break. Tests added: a legit ≥4× option-premium move is KEPT on both `/movers`-options (`_read_future_session(bad_tick=False)`) and `/db`-options (`query_option_candles`), a positivity-insane option bar IS dropped on both (the unconditional insane arm), futures still get the 4× screen, spot unchanged. MINOR-1 (baseline `resolve_prev_close`/`resolve_prev_oi`/`_prior_session_last_from_minute` reads are NOT screened → a prior-session spike survives into `prev_close`/`prev_oi`, a residual spurious %-move on the BASELINE side) is DISCLOSED in the resolver docstrings + here (the live LTP/turnover side IS screened; heal/re-pull the poisoned prior session is the real remedy) — INCLUDING the WITHIN-one-`/db`-page case: a page spanning day D's trailing spike + D+1's head both DROPS the spike row from the served page AND still USES it as D+1's %-change baseline (via the unscreened `_intraday_prev_close_by_page_date`) — the same residual, the same deferral, named explicitly. MINOR-2 (`/db` `_count_total` counts the screened-out bar) disclosed + test-pinned. MINOR-3 handled (the 8-bar seed window) + the eager per-page seed read cost disclosed. BLOCKER AMENDMENT (hostile-review round 1, found independently by two reviewers — the THIRD options-serving path): the `/db` "F&O candles" tab (`query_candles(segment="FNO", symbol=<CE/PE contract>)`, reached via the FNO cascade which offers CE/PE contracts) was screening option premia with the default-ON ×4 bad-tick arm — false-dropping a legit ≥4× premium bar while `total` still counted it, AND re-creating the split-brain vs both `/movers`-options and the `/db` expired-options tab for the identical contract. Fix is KIND-DERIVED at the call site (the recommended contract for any future options surface — decode the symbol, never remember-per-caller): `query_candles` decodes `parse_fno_symbol(symbol)` when `is_fno`; `option_type is not None` (CE/PE) → `bad_tick_enabled=False` + `seed_bar=None` (the seed read is pure waste with the cross-row arm off — one bounded DuckDB query per option page saved); FUT + unparseable F&O symbols keep the full default screen (`bad_tick_enabled=None` preserves the `BRUTEX_BAD_TICK_SCREEN` kill-switch read — never a hard `True` override; `screen_rows`' docstring now warns options callers explicitly). Tests: FNO/CE + FNO/PE keep the 5× premium (the live served-vs-dropped asymmetry shape pinned), FNO/FUT still drops the ×10 spike, the insane arm still fires on FNO/CE, and a THREE-WAY agreement test pins `query_candles(FNO/CE)` == `query_option_candles` == the movers options read over the same premium sequence. RESILIENCE (round-1 reviewer 4): `screen_rows` gains the seed-helper's `isinstance(ts, datetime)` guard — a schema-drifted page row with a None/junk `timestamp` cell (union_by_name null-fill) is served RAW (never sorted/classified/dropped, never a TypeError 500 — the DEC-DB-CORRUPT-SKIP-001 never-500 posture) while the datetime rows around it are still screened; test-pinned. NAMED FOLLOW-UP (recorded, deliberately NOT fixed here): NaN prices bypass `price_row_insane` AND poison the `BadTickScreen` baseline (`prev_close=nan` → every later comparison False → the ×4 arm silently disabled for that session's remainder) — INHERITED from the vectorized `price_violation_expr` (scalar==vector parity holds; the engine read boundary shares the same blind spot), so the fix is an ENGINE-WIDE price_sanity/bad_tick NaN screen on its own track, never a dashboard-side fork [ROUND-2 SUPERSESSION — the DASHBOARD side is now CLOSED: refuter round 2 EMPIRICALLY confirmed the engine REFUSES a NaN bar (`CandleBar` raises `decimal.InvalidOperation`, escaping even `arrow_table_to_bars`' `except ValueError`) while the screen KEPT it (`price_row_insane` was NaN-blind — every NaN comparison False), so the dashboard SERVED what the engine REFUSES, breaking the central invariant; `price_row_insane` gains a SCALAR-ONLY `math.isnan` arm (all four OHLC → insane) — a DELIBERATE, documented scalar-vs-vector asymmetry (the vectorized `price_violation_expr` — the engine prebuild path — is untouched; NaN excluded from the scalar==vector parity pin's input space with the asymmetry named; outcome-parity holds because the engine refuses NaN downstream at CandleBar anyway); a NaN bar also never advances the bad-tick baseline (`prev_close=nan` would silently disable the ×4 arm — test-pinned on both wrappers). The ENGINE-side vectorized twin + the `arrow_table_to_bars` except-clause gap (decimal.InvalidOperation escapes the quarantine wrapper) remain the NAMED ENGINE follow-up]. HONEST-COST AMENDMENT (round-1 reviewer 3, measured): the screen is NOT free on clean data — `screen_frame` materialises 5 columns + runs an O(rows) per-row Python classify pass BEFORE deciding same-object (measured linear: 375 rows 0.303 ms / 3,750 rows 2.546 ms / 37,500 rows 24.711 ms), so every "no-op / zero overhead" comment is REWORDED to "same-object on clean data; O(rows) Python screen pass per read" and NEW `tests/bench/test_bar_screen_cost.py` pins the LINEARITY honestly (a 10x frame must cost ≥2x — the inverse teeth: a future genuinely-flat rewrite fails the pin and re-earns the flat claim consciously) + the same-object identity; the polars-vectorized / Rust rewrite that would EARN a flat claim (the engine's vectorized `price_violation_expr` is the template) is a NAMED follow-up, not claimed. 1743. **DEC-TRADESIM-OPEN-SESSION-GUARD-001 — the trade-sim OPEN-position session-boundary guard: an open position never survives an IST session-date change — on the first pushed bar whose session date differs from the position's entry-session date, the walker closes it retroactively at the PRIOR session's last stored bar (the exact `finish()` idiom: `exit_price = pos.last_bar.close`, `exit_ts = pos.last_bar.timestamp`, `exit_idx = pos.last_idx`) under the NEW append-only exit reason `session_gap`; any pending next-open exit armed on the dead session is SUBSUMED (cleared), no excursion is folded from the boundary bar, the boundary bar never arms a new entry (earliest re-arm i+1, earliest new fill i+2 — the step-(C) `closed is None` law), and the Rust kernel mirrors the numerics bit-for-bit via the existing `session_idx` ordinals with ZERO new FFI inputs** (2026-07-11 on `claude/tradesim-open-session-guard`; the entry number is coordinator-ASSIGNED from the reservation map — reserved by the ledger-coordinator session 2026-07-11, the next free number above the in-flight reservation bands; live-main tail #1723 at assignment — gaps are legal, the #1711/#1692 precedent). **THE BUG (the asymmetric twin of R2-OC-2):** the pending-ENTRY session gate existed on both sides (`trade_sim.py` step (A) ⇔ `trade_sim.rs`), but an OPEN position had NO session guard — when a session's stored bars ended BEFORE any forced-exit-window bar (a session-tail data hole the #1031 machinery legitimately stores, or a stitched-series roll gap on `NSE-NIFTY-FUT`), the position silently rode the overnight gap and closed against the NEXT session's prices. EXECUTED repro (day-D 2024-01-02 tail-holed at 11:14, day-D+1 opening +₹500): V1 a TP "hit" by the gap bar fabricated +30000 paisa; V1b the next day's 15:20 forced bar fabricated +50000; V2 a pending NEXT_OPEN stop filled at the next session's open (+50000); V3 the Mode-B signal twin (+50000); MFE/MAE contamination mfe=50100 (the gap bar's range folded in). 1753. **DEC-PREMERGE-M4PRO-NONBLOCK-001 — the pre-merge gate treats the NON-required self-hosted `m4pro-absolute-throughput` bench check as NON-BLOCKING: a HARDCODED `NONBLOCKING_CHECK_NAMES` constant UNIONED with the caller's `IGNORE_CHECK_NAMES` at all three rollup scan sites, so an offline-runner pending-forever m4pro check can never refuse a merge — while a FAILED m4pro is surfaced as a WARN-only line that never affects the exit code and every REQUIRED check still blocks fully** (2026-07-12 on `claude/premerge-m4pro-nonblock`; fix(ci); CI-gate script + redteam tests + docs only — ZERO brutex/ source change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema change; entry number #1753 = renumbered #1751 → #1752 → #1753 at the 2026-07-12 coordinator de-collision — PR #1486 (earlier-opened) claimed #1751 at the first resnapshot, then #1486/#1485 also claimed #1752; the coordinator drain-order map assigns #1487 = #1753 (#1486 = #1752, #1485 = #1754 — gaps legal), verified free on the merged tree (post-merge main max #1751, PR #1488's DEC-DASHBOARD-PULL-CONTENTION-RESILIENCE-001)). **ROOT:** `scripts/ci/pre-merge-check.sh` fail-closes on ANY pending check (the pending scan, pre-change lines 262-273 — correct Z+ posture for REQUIRED checks), but `bench-m4pro.yml`'s `m4pro-absolute-throughput` job (job id at `.github/workflows/bench-m4pro.yml:123`; the job carries no `name:` field, so the check-run rollup name IS the job id) runs ONLY on the self-hosted M4-Pro runner — with that runner offline the check sits QUEUED forever on any push touching a bench trigger path, and the gate refused the merge indefinitely (coordinator-reported live instance: the auto-merge refusal on PR #1463's flip, actions run 29184955540). The script's EXISTING exact-name skip mechanism (`IGNORE_CHECK_NAMES`, DEC-MERGE-LIVE-ROLLUP-001) could not carry the fix: it is an env DEFAULT (`"${IGNORE_CHECK_NAMES:-}"`) and `auto-merge.yml` (line ~470) invokes the script with a caller-SET `IGNORE_CHECK_NAMES: "Auto-merge on green CI"` — so folding m4pro into that default would be CLOBBERED on exactly the auto-merge path that needs it. **FIX (three surgical pieces, the gate's fail-closed posture untouched for every required check):** (1) a NEW HARDCODED constant `NONBLOCKING_CHECK_NAMES="m4pro-absolute-throughput"` — deliberately NOT env-overridable (broadening the non-blocking set requires a code change + a new DEC, never a caller env tweak); (2) at ALL THREE scan sites (rollup count / failed / pending) the ignore set becomes the UNION `IGNORE_CHECK_NAMES ∪ NONBLOCKING_CHECK_NAMES` (same comma-split/strip/drop-empties parsing idiom), so the caller's value can never clobber the hardcoded set and the excluded m4pro entry also never inflates the `EXPECTED_MIN_CHECKS` count floor; (3) a WARN-ONLY report after the failed-checks scan — a NONBLOCKING check whose conclusion is in (FAILURE, CANCELLED, TIMED_OUT) prints "⚠️  Non-blocking check(s) in a failed state (never block merge — DEC-PREMERGE-M4PRO-NONBLOCK-001):" + the names, guarded `|| true` so it can NEVER affect the exit code; a pending/absent non-blocking check is silently skipped (that is what ignoring means). **EVIDENCE the exemption is safe (re-verified on this tree):** `m4pro-absolute-throughput` is NOT in ci.yml's `ci-ok` aggregate-gate `needs:` list (grep-verified zero m4pro members) AND is NOT among branch protection's required contexts — absent from the 22-member `expected_required_checks` set asserted by `.github/workflows/branch-protection-drift.yml` (the 21 directly-required CI job contexts plus the `"CI OK (aggregate gate)"` aggregate context, none of them m4pro; the round-1 hostile review corrected this clause — the original "the branch-protection required context is CI OK (aggregate gate) only" wording overstated a 1-member set where the drift workflow asserts 22); MIGRATION.md #382 (DEC-M4PRO-PR-TRIGGER-001) states verbatim "`m4pro-*` is NOT in the required `CI OK (aggregate gate)` set"; MIGRATION.md #1534 (DEC-BENCH-ABS-BASELINE-001) states "bench-m4pro stays a NON-required, non-PR check … a regression is caught post-merge on push/daily-cron as a red run + issue, NOT as a merge blocker". **HONEST envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ONLY m4pro is exempted — the hardcoded set holds exactly one name; every required check still blocks (pinned by the new redteam tests incl. the pending-`CI OK (aggregate gate)`-still-blocks and failed-required-still-blocks cases); a genuinely broken bench regression is caught POST-merge on the self-hosted runner exactly as DEC-BENCH-ABS-BASELINE-001 designed, and the FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT tolerance is THIS GATE's verdict only (round-3 claim-scoping): on the auto-merge path the workflow's EARLIER ci-check step — the `failing` awk scan at `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` lines 282-289, matching conclusions failure|cancelled|timed_out|action_required|stale and exempting ONLY "Auto-merge on green CI" — still refuses a FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT m4pro before pre-merge-check.sh ever runs (pre-existing behavior, deliberately untouched — that workflow is outside this change's file-set), so the WARN line ADDS merge-time visibility at this gate and the failed-state tolerance applies at pre-merge-check.sh only; the PENDING shape — the motivating offline-runner incident — IS non-blocking END-TO-END: a QUEUED check carries no conclusion (ci-check's jq maps it to "pending", which the failing regex never matches) and this gate's pending scan exempts it; the run-29184955540 / PR-#1463 incident citation is coordinator-reported context, not locally re-derivable (no `gh` against live CI in the build sandbox); NAMED RESIDUAL (review-round-2-verified, live runs 29172994876 + 29189211057): the sibling `bench-m4pro.yml` job `bless-baseline` ("Bless baseline candidate (bot PR from measured artifact)", `needs: m4pro-absolute-throughput`) is EQUALLY non-required yet deliberately NOT exempted — the operator authorization covers exactly `m4pro-absolute-throughput`, broadening requires a new DEC — and it cannot block in the offline-runner scenario (its needs-downstream check-run is not instantiated while m4pro sits QUEUED; ## DEC-CI-SWEEP-REHEARSAL-TIMEOUT-001 (2026-07-11)

1765. **DEC-CI-SWEEP-REHEARSAL-TIMEOUT-001 — raise the CI `timeout-minutes` BUDGET for the "Sweep full-chain rehearsal (R38)" job (15 → 30) and the "Benchmarks (O(1) NFR gates)" job (15 → 25) to absorb transient shared-runner contention; ONLY `timeout-minutes:` values change, no O(1) ratio ceiling / bench threshold / test assertion is touched** (2026-07-11 on `claude/ci-sweep-rehearsal-timeout`; ci; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake stays REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope/vocab/rate change; CI-config-only — no `brutex/` source, no test/bench assertion). **Why (contention, NOT a regression):** the R38 rehearsal's measured baseline is ~29 s for its 21 tests (ci.yml inline comment, 2026-07-07). On PR #1462 (2026-07-11) that job's 21 tests PASSED (`tuples_failed=0`) but the JOB was auto-cancelled at 17:48 when it hit the old 15-min cap. That 17:48 wall-time was dominated by the JOB's setup, NOT sweep compute: the install plus the two from-source cargo Rust wheel builds (fno-math + trading-core, each behind a 3× network-retry loop) are the network-flaky, contention-sensitive phases that stretched the job. The sweep-compute leg itself has its own hard in-test ceiling `assert rehearsal.seconds_first < 300.0` (`tests/integration/test_sweep_full_chain_rehearsal.py:255`), and the 21 tests PASSED on #1462 — so the sweep provably ran in under 5 minutes even during the contended run, and the timeout raise CANNOT mask a sweep regression: a genuine slowdown trips that 300 s assertion and fails the tests regardless of the job's `timeout-minutes`. Per Golden Rule #10 a real sweep slowdown would be fixed in the sweep, not the timeout; this raises only the BUDGET for the setup/build spike. **Also bumped (thin margin):** the `bench` (Benchmarks O(1) NFR gates) job's cap was 15 min against a banked ~10.9-min real wall-time — only ~4.1 min (~27%) headroom, thin enough that one shared-runner contention spike could auto-cancel it — raised 15 → 25 for the same budget-for-contention reason; the O(1) ratio ceilings in `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py` are UNTOUCHED, so a genuine perf regression still fails the ratio gate. **What changed:** exactly two `timeout-minutes:` values in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (R38 15→30, bench 15→25) plus honest inline-comment updates citing the PR #1462 run; `git diff --stat` shows the ONLY files changed are `.github/workflows/ci.yml` + `docs/MIGRATION.md` (this ledger entry). This CI-only PR does NOT modify `CLAUDE.md` (it legitimately skips the active-branch line; the §1==§3 branch-consistency test is already satisfied). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** touches ONLY timeout-minutes; `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py` and every bench/test assertion are byte-untouched; no engine/scope/vocab/rate change; the raise masks the setup/build wall-time spike, not a masked sweep slowdown (the 300 s in-test ceiling still fails any real regression). **Decision ID:** DEC-CI-SWEEP-REHEARSAL-TIMEOUT-001.

1777. **DEC-CROSSVERIFY-S3-WRITE-POSTURE-001 — BruteX's FIRST sanctioned AWS WRITE surface: `s3:PutObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::tv-prod-cold/crossverify/*` ONLY** (2026-07-12 on `claude/crossverify-producer`; companion to #1776). The IAM grant is operator-provisioned and PutObject-ONLY — NO Get/Head/List/Delete — so the publisher NEVER reads remote state: idempotency is journal-side (deterministic bytes over a deduped read + the pinned mapper; a key journaled published with matching staged sha256 skips; a crash between put and journal-save re-puts IDENTICAL bytes — S3 per-key PUT is atomic last-writer-wins, so every path CONVERGES; a changed lake re-renders differently and the overwrite is the CORRECT action). The SSM READ-only pledge (DEC-AWS-ONLY-CREDS-001 / DEC-TOKEN-BROKER-AWS-001) is UNCHANGED — this write scope is additive, bucket-prefix-bounded, and named in its own DEC precisely because the recorded posture was read-only. boto3 rides the NEW dedicated optional extra `crossverify = ["boto3>=1.34,<2.0"]` (the token-broker shape; extras name their posture — read-broker vs write-publisher); CI NEVER installs it — the PUT-only `S3PutClient` Protocol + `tests/fakes/fake_s3_client.py` + the lazy `# pragma: no cover` `build_real_s3_client` factory (the aws_client.py template verbatim; retryability classified by exception class-NAME string, never a botocore import) keep 100% coverage with no install and no network. AWS credentials ride boto3's default chain; region default `ap-south-1` (`BRUTEX_CROSSVERIFY_AWS_REGION`). HONEST: no real S3 put runs in CI — the live put is an operator acceptance step post-IAM-grant (runbook `docs/runbooks/crossverify-producer.md`, never claimed done); with a PutObject-only grant remote state is unverifiable from BruteX — convergence rests on deterministic bytes + last-writer-wins + the local journal. ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX. **Decision ID:** DEC-CROSSVERIFY-S3-WRITE-POSTURE-001.
1778. **DEC-CROSSVERIFY-DAY-DERIVE-001 — the day-scoped derive composition: month-bounded 19-TF materialize + windowed 1day on the heal-recall template, never stamping** (2026-07-12 on `claude/crossverify-producer`; companion to #1776). `brutex/crossverify/prebuild_leg.py` composes EXISTING primitives ONLY — per pulled/exported coordinate TWO derives: (1) `materialize_lake_timeframes(..., tfs=MATERIALIZABLE_TFS, include_daily=False, months={(day.year, day.month) UTC}, incremental=False)` — month-bounded (an NSE session never crosses a UTC month; `months=` STRUCTURALLY forces no-skip/no-stamp, and `months= + include_daily=True` RAISES — hence the two-call shape, both verified in-tree) and (2) `derive_daily_for_targets` with the ±1-day pad window + the FNO OI/positional resampler arm, the exact lake-heal recall composition. The load-bearing "a partial derive must never stamp" invariant is preserved BY CONSTRUCTION (no new stamping rule — the stamp redesign is the named follow-up DEC-PREBUILD-DAY-SCOPED-STAMP-001). Per-symbol failure isolation (counted + capped-logged, never blocks the 1-minute export — the export reads 1-minute only); `LakeWriteHalt` re-raises to the runner (suspect exit 2). HONEST cost envelope: O(touched symbols × one UTC month of 1-minute bars) × 19 resamples + O(symbols × 3-day window) for 1day — bounded analysis, NOT measured, NOT O(1), NEVER O(full history); the derive stamp stays STALE for every touched symbol so the next nightly full prebuild re-derives their history anyway — EXACTLY today's post-pull behaviour (the day's pull moves `source_1m_token` regardless): the producer adds a bounded early derive, removes nothing, adds NO new nightly cost (the double-derive disclosed, not hidden). 1752. **DEC-GROWW-ERRORCODE-ASCII-GUARD-001 — a Unicode-digit vendor error `code` no longer crashes the WHOLE pull raw: the two `int(<vendor code>)` coercions (`errors._classify_generic` + `auth._vendor_status`) gain the house `isascii() and isdigit()` guard, so a non-ASCII-digit code (`'²'`) rides the existing generic/unknown-code arm instead of escaping as a raw ValueError** (2026-07-12 on `claude/groww-errorcode-ascii-guard`; fix(adapter/groww); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope/vocab/rate-cap/lake-schema change; entry number renumbered from #1751 after PR #1488 landed #1751 (DEC-DASHBOARD-PULL-CONTENTION-RESILIENCE-001) — the merge-reconcile the original append-note anticipated; live-main max #1750 at append, #1751 at the reconcile). DEFECT (adversarial-audit AREA 8 / R1, MAJOR, reachability LOW — reproduced 3× in-sandbox): `'²'.isdigit()` is True but `int('²')` raises `ValueError`, so a malformed/hostile vendor error payload whose `code` is a No-category Unicode digit escaped `from_groww_exception` (pre-fix origin/main line numbers: errors.py:470 via the :534-535 generic arm; post-fix the guarded coercion sits at errors.py:470-480 and the generic arm at :544-545) out of `GrowwClient._call` (client.py:293-294 wraps EVERY vendor call — client.py untouched, its line numbers unchanged) into `run_ingest.py`'s non-BruteXError contract → the WHOLE pull died raw as an anonymous code bug instead of classifying/quarantining (sync AND async producer side); the `auth._vendor_status` sibling (pre-fix auth.py:121; post-fix the guard sits at :123) carried the same class (production-UNREACHABLE in the AWS-only read-only config — it sits on the token-MINT failure path; it bites non-read-only local-dev configs). REPRO (executed at origin/main 1106bca before fixing): `from_groww_exception(exc_with_code('²'))` → `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '²'`; the `_vendor_status` twin identical; Nd-category digits (`'١٢٣'`) int-coerce fine — only No-category digits raise. FIX (minimal, the exact class the repo fixed 3× before — `greeks_enrich_pass._is_canonical_digits` #1536, the lake_invariants stem guards #1594 R2): both coercions guard `code.strip().isascii() and code.strip().isdigit()` before `int()`; ASCII digit-string codes map BYTE-IDENTICALLY (parity-pinned `'429'`/`'500'`/`' 429 '` in errors; `'429'`→429 in auth). SANCTIONED NARROWING (disclosed, pinned): an Nd-category non-ASCII digit string (`'٤٢٩'`/`'٥٠٣'`) previously int-coerced (→ the rate-limit map / status 503) and now rides the generic arm / returns None — no vendor payload has ever been observed carrying non-ASCII status digits, and a real throttle beside a non-ASCII code is still caught by the rate-limit message hints (pinned). TESTS: `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py` +3 (`'²'` + `'①'` map to the terminal base `GrowwError` and never raise; the Nd narrowing + hint-sniff pin; the ASCII-parity pins) and `tests/unit/test_groww_auth.py` +1 (the `_vendor_status` superscript/Arabic-Indic/ASCII trio) — all 4 new tests verified FAILING on the reverted fix (raw ValueError) and passing post-fix; the whole groww unit family re-run green (1508 passed, 4 skipped — optional `cma`/`growwapi` extras absent in the sandbox). GATES: `brutex.adapters.groww.errors` 100.00% line+branch (78 stmts/24 branches) on its stem suite; `brutex.adapters.groww.auth` 100.00% (52/10) on its ci.yml gate file; ruff check + ruff format clean on all 4 touched files; `mypy --strict` clean on both touched modules + both test files; pyright NOT run in this sandbox (stated honestly). **Files:** `brutex/adapters/groww/errors.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/auth.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_errors.py`, `tests/unit/test_groww_auth.py`, `docs/MIGRATION.md`. **Decision ID:** DEC-GROWW-ERRORCODE-ASCII-GUARD-001.
1774. **DEC-PULL-TODAY-COMPLETENESS-GATE-001 — the pre-settle TODAY minute-completeness gate: a post-close pull whose trailing window covers TODAY's IST session WITHHOLDS today's bars from the lake and defers the window (streak-EXEMPT re-pullable `FAILED`) until the fetched day passes per-class completeness criteria — so the vendor's still-settling forming-shape rows can never be keep-first-frozen into the lake nor settle the window `SUCCESS`** (2026-07-12 on `claude/pull-today-completeness-gate`; feat(adapter/groww); ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no scope/vocab/rate/lake-schema change; pull-INTEGRITY only — fetch pacing byte-identical; entry number renumbered #1751 → #1755 → #1774 — the first hop at the 2026-07-13 merge-reconcile (main's #1488 wave took #1751 for DEC-DASHBOARD-PULL-CONTENTION-RESILIENCE-001 and #1752 for DEC-GROWW-ERRORCODE-ASCII-GUARD-001; #1755/#1756 verified free at that instant), the second per the coordinator's fresh authoritative reservation map clearing all in-flight reservations (live ceiling #1773 at assignment) — the #1664/#1692 pattern). **ROOT CAUSE (the permanence proof):** MIGRATION.md #837 (DEC-GROWW-FORMING-BAR-PARSE-001) recorded empirically that the CURRENT trading day's intraday rows come back 6-element (`open_interest` slot dropped, `volume` typically `None`) "until the vendor's EOD settlement"; the parse DESTROYS that shape (`brutex/adapters/groww/parser.py` pads `open_interest=None`, `brutex/data/candle_fields.py` maps absent volume → `0` — a 6-element forming row and a settled zero-volume row are byte-identical `CandleBar`s); the authoritative `1minute` partition is written keep-first ONLY (`brutex/data/parquet_writer.py` `_merge_write` — a same-timestamp value difference is a `BarConflict`, the STORED bar wins, and `_bar_values_equal` compares volume + open_interest), so ONE stored still-settling day is PERMANENT — every settled re-pull is discarded forever; and once the window settles `SUCCESS` the skip rule never re-fetches it at all. A `clamp_window_end`-minted covers-today window (`end == today+1`, mintable only at/after 15:30 IST) is exactly the shape that stores it. THE SETTLE-SKIP RULE ruled the demotion STREAK-EXEMPT: a same-evening until-clean loop can record the demotion 3+ times, and a streak-BUMPING demotion would settle the window `SKIPPED` at `EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD` — and because the next 01:30 nightly plans the SAME equal-end window (`prune_superseded` keeps equal-end rows), that SKIPPED would silently skip day-D's data for up to ~48 h. **WHAT SHIPPED:** (1) NEW pure clock-free classifier `brutex/data/today_completeness.py` (the `partial_window_detect`/`observe_all_filtered` template): `classify_today_completeness` (covers-today = STRICT `window_end == clamp_today + 1 day`; `is_holiday_data_available` abstain; `get_session is None` ⇒ vacuous `non_trading` pass; distinct-IST-minute-floor count; `session_last_bar_complete` VERBATIM for the close edge), `split_today_bars` (prior/today/later by `astimezone(IST).date()`), the guarded fail-open `observe_today_completeness` wiring BOTH tails call (any internal error ⇒ one `ingest.window.today_gate_error` WARN + pre-gate exposure), and the fail-loud `resolve_today_completeness_enabled` env switch `BRUTEX_TODAY_COMPLETENESS_GATE` (default ON; junk raises; the `market_hours.py` byte-shape; resolved ONCE per pull at the arm sites — never mid-run). (2) THE PER-CLASS CRITERIA TABLE: `INDEX_SPOT` = count == `session.duration_minutes` (375 regular/Budget-weekend, 60 Muhurat — never a hardcoded 375) AND the close-edge law, `count_short`/`count_excess`/`last_bar_incomplete` all demote (volume/OI carry zero signal on an index — `drop_volume` forces 0, OI always None; zero today bars FAIL via the count — indices always print); `CASH_SPOT` = the all-zero-volume shape ONLY (count/last-bar deliberately NOT demanded — the #1031 illiquid-name re-pull-storm lesson; a designed extension beyond the spec's literal "(iii) for FNO" wording — same bug class, same mechanism); `FUT` = ANY-bar OI-null (`oi_null_settling` — an all-bars rule would pass a progressively-settling mixed day and freeze its null minutes) OR all-zero-volume mandatory, count-vs-expected OBSERVE-ONLY (`ingest.window.today_count_short` INFO, `demoted=False` — a far-serial-month future is legitimately sparse); `OPTION` (CE/PE) = the OI-null shape only (zero-volume option minutes are routine); FNO zero-today-bars ABSTAINS (`no_today_bars` — a dead strike/dormant far-month prints nothing); `raw_bars == 0` is structurally the EMPTY channel (`classify_window_status` ignores `degraded` at raw 0 — the "legit vendor-empty day never false-demotes" pin, both spines) with observe-only `ingest.window.today_empty` visibility on INDEX/FUT. (3) THE WRITE LAW at both tails (`brutex/adapters/groww/ingest.py::_process_window_tail` + `brutex/adapters/groww/option_ingest.py::_process_option_window_tail`, between `drop_bars_after` and the append): PASS/inert/abstain ⇒ append the ORIGINAL bars object (byte-identical — pinned); FAIL ⇒ append only bars with IST date < `clamp_today` (the window's settled history still lands; today + any boundary `today+1` leak withheld in one stroke) + `ledger.record(degraded=True, degraded_reason=TODAY_INCOMPLETE)` with the Ruling-G(5) priority head (`TODAY_INCOMPLETE > ALL_FILTERED > INTERIOR_GAP > SUSPECTED_PARTIAL` — the streak-exempt protection must own the covers-today case); `raw_bars`/`in_pull_fetches`/retry-split invariants pass through untouched; session-exempt symbols (GIFTNIFTY) not judged; the gate lives entirely inside the ONE tail each spine has, so sync and async-pipeline modes execute the same code (parity pinned — ledger rows + lake bytes SHA-equal). (4) CLOCK COHERENCE: `clamp_today: date | None = None` appended LAST on the frozen `_RawWindow`/`_OptionRawWindow` payloads (the `empty_fetches` additive precedent), stamped by the producer from the SAME resolved instant `clamp_window_end` used — a midnight-crossing drain is judged against the date that MINTED the window's end; `None` (a legacy constructor) keeps the gate INERT (fail-open, never a fresh tail clock read); the gate takes NO position at the 15:30:00 boundary — it inherits the clamp's `>=` side by construction (`tests/unit/test_session_close_boundary_pin.py` untouched). (5) LEDGER SEMANTICS (`brutex/data/window_ledger.py`): NEW `STREAK_EXEMPT_DEGRADED_REASONS = frozenset({TODAY_INCOMPLETE})` — a streak-exempt demotion is TIME-transient evidence (expires at the session boundary by construction) treated like FAILED for streak purposes (a settle lag is no more evidence of permanent emptiness than a 429), so `record()`'s degraded arm PRESERVES the streak and the settle arm gains the twin `not in` guard (belt — with the exemption a threshold streak is unreachable; a forged-high-streak restore is regression-pinned and both membership mutants were hand-applied + verified killed); `TODAY_INCOMPLETE` joins `DEMOTED_SETTLE_REASONS` DEFENSIVELY (the `"DEGRADED"` precedent — a SKIPPED settle carrying it is structurally unreachable but must never read "vendor confirmed no trades"); the degraded tombstone + discard-on-settle apply unchanged (free protection); NO new persisted column (`LedgerRowTuple` untouched — the exemption is a pure function of the persisted `degraded_reason`); `suppress_settle` NOT overloaded. Same-evening re-pulls are budget-bounded (drain passes 2 · retry rounds 3 · `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS` 5) — each a legitimate "has the vendor settled yet?" re-check; at the next pull whose window no longer covers today the gate is inert and the settled bars land (nothing partial was ever stored — the write guard is exactly what makes the re-pull LAND; the convergence + zero-conflict lifecycle is integration-pinned against a REAL lake, and the gate-off counterfactual reproduces the keep-first freeze). (6) ARM SITES — ALL FOUR production pulls, each resolving the env ONCE with dry-run/inspect short-circuited to `False` WITHOUT touching the env: the bulk `pull_all_spot` phase (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — which `detect_completeness_gaps` NEVER reached; this gate rides its OWN spine parameter `today_completeness_gate: bool = False` threaded through `run_groww_spot_ingest(_with_retry)`/`ingest_spot` and `run_groww_option_ingest`/`ingest_option_contract`), the single-symbol `pull_candles` phase, the CLI `cmd_fetch` pass (`brutex/cli.py`, beside `market_closed`), and the F&O `_run_phase` (`brutex/dashboard/historical_pull.py`); all four wiring-spied (live ⇒ resolved flag, dry-run ⇒ False under a junk env). (7) UI: `db_view.window_status_label` reads `"today's session not yet settled by vendor (will re-pull)"` on a `FAILED` + `TODAY_INCOMPLETE` row. (8) OBSERVABILITY (module-owned, both spines share ONE emission discipline): `ingest.window.today_incomplete` WARN capped 20/pull + exactly-one `ingest.window.today_incomplete_suppressed` summary (flushed on the observation past the cap — monotone-approximate: `suppressed_count`/`total_incomplete` are FLUSH-time counts at observation #cap+1, a FLOOR never the pull's final total — a 3000-demotion FNO evening logs "suppressed 1 of 21"; the TRUE per-pull total is the window ledger's `FAILED` + `TODAY_INCOMPLETE` rows, one per demoted window; a true-total pull-END flush would need a post-drain seam at all four arm sites and is deliberately NOT built — the event is a heads-up, the ledger is the count (round-1 R3-MINOR-1; this matches the binding design's literal "flushed on the next observe past the cap" wording while diverging from the #1649a build-end-true-total convention it cites — the divergence is now DISCLOSED here + in the module docstrings rather than silently implied)), `today_count_short` INFO capped 20, `today_gate_abstain` INFO once per (pull, reason), `today_empty` WARN capped 20, `today_gate_error` WARN uncapped; no PASS event (silence = health). (9) HERMETICITY: `tests/conftest.py` gains `os.environ.setdefault(TODAY_COMPLETENESS_GATE_ENV, "0")` beside the market-hours line (the #1692 wall-clock philosophy; the gate's own tests inject `env=`/`clamp_today`/`now_ist` explicitly and stay armed on both arms). **Honest envelope (Golden Rules #1/#10):** (a) fetched-bars boundary — the gate judges what THIS fetch returned; an already-stored partial day under an already-settled pre-fix window is neither detected nor repaired (remediation = the #1775 runbook procedure; mechanised audit = named follow-up DEC-LAKE-AUDIT-SETTLING-ROWS-001); (b) the shape checks are parsed-bar INFERENCE — the literal 6-vs-7 row length is destroyed at parse; OI-null (any-bar) and all-zero-volume are heuristics whose false positives (a settled row with a genuinely null OI cell / a genuinely all-zero-volume settled CASH day) cost one bounded streak-exempt same-evening deferral each, never a loss, never a SKIP — the #1775 probe's raw-shape transcript measures whether those classes exist; AND the CASH all-zero-volume rule has the SAME false-NEGATIVE weakness the FUT criterion's ANY-bar law was chosen to avoid (round-2 review, disclosed): a PROGRESSIVELY-settling mixed CASH day — some minutes already settled `volume > 0`, some still forming `volume == 0` — PASSES the all-bars rule, the forming zero-volume minutes are appended, and keep-first freezes THEM forever (a per-MINUTE partial freeze, not a whole-day one); this residual is conditional on UNVERIFIED per-minute CASH settlement behavior (nothing in #837 establishes whether the vendor settles a cash day minute-by-minute or atomically) and is PROBE-MEASURABLE — the #1775 probe's per-CASH-symbol `raw_null_volume`/`rows_len6` fields across the five slots answer whether a mixed pre-settle CASH shape exists at all; a CASH ANY-bar zero-volume rule was deliberately NOT chosen (it would false-demote every illiquid microcap with ONE quiet minute, every evening — the #1031 re-pull-storm class); the `RawPayloadHook` is deliberately NOT plumbed to the tails (retry-ladder aggregation across two spines + the async queue for no additional decision power; the escalation path, if the probe finds a material settled-null-OI class, is an additive `parse_candle_rows` shape-counter seam — named, not claimed); (c) NO FNO/CASH density or close-edge demand — sparse/short days settle SUCCESS if the shape is settled (sparsity ≠ incompleteness, the #1031 stance); count + last-bar demotion teeth are INDEX-spot-only; the FUT count is observe-only (a hypothetical settled-shape-but-truncated same-day FUT response settles SUCCESS short — missing timestamps self-heal via keep-first UNION on any later covering pull; only same-timestamp values freeze); (d) the wrapper is fail-open — a crashed classifier logs `today_gate_error` and degrades to pre-gate exposure (a diagnostic bug must not demote-loop a production pull); (e) EMPTY-today rides the EXISTING EMPTY machinery — residual pre-existing path: 3 clean same-evening EMPTYs could settle a today window SKIPPED, healing via re-tiling/`reopen-skipped`; visibility added (`today_empty`), mechanism deliberately unchanged; (f) latency envelope — a vendor that never settles by the last same-evening round leaves the window FAILED; data lands at the next pull where the window no longer covers today (the 01:30 nightly, ≤ ~9 h) — nothing lost or frozen PROVIDED the vendor has settled by that first non-covers-today re-pull; a later-settling vendor is exactly why the nightly must be scheduled after the probe-measured settle time + margin (the #1775 runbook — which also warns an evening pull must never span IST midnight against a still-unsettled day, since the day-scoped gate goes inert once `clamp_today` rolls); (g) Muhurat: a post-close pull on a Muhurat day BEFORE the evening session demotes correctly-but-noisily — the production full-range trailing tile carries prior days' bars, so the wrapper runs and today's INDEX count reads 0/60 → `count_short` demote; a today-only tile with NO prior-day bars instead rides the raw-EMPTY channel (no demotion) — and heals next pull either way (1 day/yr; 2026-11-08 has NO `MUHURAT_SESSIONS` entry yet ⇒ reads as holiday ⇒ vacuous pass until the timing circular lands); (h) out-of-coverage (≥2027) dates abstain (logged) — dormant, not wrong; (i) the bulk-spot `detect_completeness_gaps` hole is OBSERVED not fixed — the #1031 interior-gap/truncation demotions stay dead on `pull_all_spot` (named follow-up DEC-BULK-SPOT-COMPLETENESS-FLAG-001) [CLOSED by DEC-BULK-SPOT-COMPLETENESS-FLAG-001, #1794 (renumbered #1792 → #1793 → #1794 across its merge-reconciles) — `pull_all_spot` now threads `detect_completeness_gaps=not dry_run`, the cli.py idiom]; THIS gate has its own parameter and IS wired there; (j) the vendor EOD settlement time is UNDOCUMENTED — the #1775 probe measures it, nothing claimed; a `nightly_summary` "N today-windows deferred" Telegram line is the named follow-up DEC-TODAY-GATE-NIGHTLY-SURFACE-001; (k) with the market-hours guard kill-switched OFF a 15:30-15:35 pull reaches the gate seconds after close and demotes until the vendor serves the full day — extra bounded rounds, never a wrong settle. **GATES:** `brutex/data/today_completeness.py` 100.00% line+branch STANDALONE (`tests/unit/test_today_completeness.py`, NEW ci.yml per-module gate) + WIRED into `mutation.yml`'s per-module zero-survivor mutmut loop (round-1 R2-M3 — the historical-runner empty-timeout pair, drop-pinned by the file's `TestMutationWorkflowWiring`; the weekly gate enforces zero survivors on its own schedule — the ledger/classifier membership mutants hand-applied in-session were each verified killed); the ci.yml per-module gates for `window_ledger`/`pull_controller`/`historical_pull`/`db_view` re-measured 100.00%; `ingest.py`/`option_ingest.py`/`run_ingest.py` 100.00% over their covering suites; ruff/ruff-format clean; `mypy --strict brutex` clean; pyright 0 errors; the full test matrix incl. the byte-identity pins (non-today month-file SHA-256 + record equality, complete-day SUCCESS, legit-vendor-empty, sync-vs-pipeline parity) green. **Files:** `brutex/data/today_completeness.py`, `brutex/data/window_ledger.py`, `brutex/adapters/groww/{ingest,option_ingest,run_ingest}.py`, `brutex/dashboard/{pull_controller,historical_pull,db_view}.py`, `brutex/cli.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, tests. **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-TODAY-COMPLETENESS-GATE-001. **Builds on** DEC-GROWW-FORMING-BAR-PARSE-001 (#837), DEC-INTERIOR-GAP-DETECT-001/DEC-PARTIAL-WINDOW-REPULL-001 (#1031), DEC-INGEST-BOUNDARY-INTEGRITY-001 (#1294), DEC-GROWW-MARKET-HOURS-GUARD-001 (#1692).

1784. **DEC-MERGE-QUEUE-001 — GitHub MERGE-QUEUE adoption PREP for `main`: the `merge_group` trigger wired into the ONE workflow that produces every required check (ci.yml) + the ci-ok required-context name extended to merge-group refs + queue-aware auto-merge (enqueue-first via enablePullRequestAutoMerge, the pre-queue direct squash-merge kept as fallback) — EVIDENCE ONLY, the merge-queue ruleset itself is deliberately NOT enabled** (2026-07-13 on `claude/merge-queue-workflows`; ci(workflows); workflow files + this ledger + workflow-pin tests ONLY — ZERO `brutex/` source change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; no lake/schema/scope/vocab/rate change; the required-check SET is untouched — no context added or removed). INVENTORY (the load-bearing finding, verified by a job-name census across all 21 workflow files): ALL 22 branch-protection required contexts (the expected snapshot pinned in `.github/workflows/branch-protection-drift.yml`) are produced by ONE workflow — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — 21 static job `name:`s (Lint (ruff) / Type check (mypy + pyright) / Unit tests + coverage (100% gate) / Property tests (hypothesis) / Benchmarks (O(1) NFR gates) / Golden-master tests / Security scan (bandit + pip-audit) / Docstring coverage (interrogate) / License compliance / Rust (fno-math build + clippy + test) / make run smoke (cold-start boot) / Banned pattern scan / Secret scan (gitleaks) / CodeQL (Python SAST) / Semgrep (python + owasp + security-audit) / Trivy (filesystem + config scan) / CycloneDX SBOM generation / Vulture (dead code detection) / jscpd (code duplication) / Python mutation (mutmut on critical modules) / Proof bundle (aggregate CI artifacts)) plus the DYNAMIC `ci-ok` job name, which minted "CI OK (aggregate gate)" ONLY on `pull_request` events (DEC-CI-OK-PR-ONLY-NAME-001) — so pre-change NO required check could ever report on a merge-group ref and every queued PR would hang until the queue timed it out (the classic merge-queue deadlock); NO other workflow produces a required context. CHANGES: (1) ci.yml gains `merge_group:` in its `on:` block — the ONLY workflow that needs it; deliberately NOT added anywhere else (auto-merge / bench-m4pro / branch-protection-drift / dep-audit / dep-freshness-nightly / doctor-daily / gitleaks / mutation / pre-merge-gate / redteam-nightly / release / rust-fuzz-smoke / safety / sbom / security-audit / soak-selfhosted / stress-nightly / verify-m4pro produce no required context). (2) the `ci-ok` name expression mints "CI OK (aggregate gate)" on `pull_request` OR `merge_group` — the queue evaluates required checks against ITS OWN speculative merge commit, and a merge-group check run lands on that SHA, never on a PR head SHA, so the DEC-CI-OK-PR-ONLY-NAME-001 shadowing hole stays closed (check runs are keyed by commit). (3) the `test` job's touched-module coverage gate diffs against `github.event.merge_group.base_sha` on queue refs (absent on every other event — PR + push runs byte-identical). (4) the SEVEN PR-only sub-gates (conv-commits / zplus-pr-guard / definition-of-ready / dec-id-validator / bugfix-regression-scan / bugfix-reversion-check / no-hallucination-scan) + the bench baseline-governance step SKIP on merge_group exactly as they already do on push-to-main — ci-ok treats skipped==pass, none of them is a DIRECT required context, and each already enforced the PR on its own pull_request run — deliberately unchanged. (5) auto-merge.yml goes QUEUE-AWARE: the merge step FIRST attempts `gh pr merge --auto --squash` (the GraphQL enablePullRequestAutoMerge mutation — on a merge-queue-ruled base that mutation IS GitHub's enqueue API) and FALLS BACK to the pre-queue direct squash-merge whenever enabling is not applicable (repo auto-merge disallowed + no queue — TODAY's world — or a PR already in clean status), so this lands safely BEFORE any ruleset flips; and the mergeable-check denylist tolerates `mergeable_state=blocked` IFF a `merge_queue` rule is LIVE-detected on main via the rules-for-branch endpoint (default-token-readable, no admin scope; a probe failure reads 0 rules and refuses as before — fail-closed) — without this, `blocked` (the queue-normal state of a fully-green PR, since a queue refuses direct merges) would strand EVERY PR after the flip; dirty/behind/unknown and queue-less `blocked` refuse byte-identically, and the ci-check all-green + rollup-gate laws are untouched upstream of the tolerance. (6) pre-merge-gate.yml needs NO change (its workflow_run filter ignores merge_group CI completions — an informational-only surface), and auto-merge's own workflow_run job-`if` likewise ignores merge_group CI completions (the queue completes its own merges). TESTS: `tests/redteam/test_redteam_automerge_safety.py` gains the TestMergeQueueReadiness pin class — ci.yml carries the merge_group trigger; ci-ok mints the required context on merge_group too; the enqueue attempt precedes (and gates) the direct fallback; the blocked-tolerance is conditional on the live merge_queue rule probe; the `dirty|behind|blocked|unknown)` refusal pattern stays intact — and every pre-existing automerge/fork-harden/premerge pin passes UNMODIFIED. NOT DONE (deliberately — evidence-only prep, operator flip required): the merge-queue RULESET itself is NOT created or enabled (no admin API write attempted; the exact ruleset JSON + operator click-path ship in the PR body — merge method SQUASH, max 5 entries per group build, min group size 1, ~5-minute wait, ALLGREEN required-check semantics); branch deletion after a QUEUE-completed merge relies on the repo's auto-delete-head-branches setting (the enqueue path drops `--delete-branch`, which gh refuses to combine with `--auto`); the branch-protection-drift expected snapshot + `docs/runbooks/github-branch-protection-setup.md` are NOT reshaped for a ruleset world (named follow-up for the flip PR). HONEST LIMITS + live evidence: `GET repos/SJParthi/bruteX/branches/main/protection` returned 404 to the Actions token on the 2026-07-13 drift-detector run (run 29224469670; the detector has failed daily since at least 2026-07-09, and its issue-open step ALSO fails because the `branch-protection-drift` label does not exist in the repo), so the 22-context set is enforced TODAY only by auto-merge.yml's client-side gates — the future queue ruleset MUST therefore carry its OWN required_status_checks rule naming the 22 contexts, or the queue would wait on nothing; queue FAILURE SEMANTICS are paid in wall-clock — a red/timed-out group entry is auto-ejected (the PR is dequeued and needs a fix + re-enqueue), the remaining group is REBUILT without it, and every (re)build pays a full CI lap (~2 h on this repo's slowest chain), so one poisoned group costs multiple laps; `merge_group` supports NO `paths:` filtering (irrelevant today — ci.yml is unfiltered — but any FUTURE paths-filtered required check would deadlock the queue: GitHub auto-passes path-skipped required checks on PRs, NOT in merge groups — refuse at review); the direct-fallback race handler's `not mergeable` grep predates this change and can mis-LOG a queue-refused direct merge as already-merged success (log-only — nothing merges; unreachable while the enqueue path succeeds); the blocked-tolerance probe reads the RULESETS endpoint (`rules/branches/main`), so ONLY a RULESET-configured merge queue is visible to it — a classic branch-protection-checkbox queue stays invisible and `blocked` keeps being refused (fail-closed; the shipped flip path IS the ruleset, so this is by design); gitleaks/CodeQL event-agnosticism on merge_group is asserted from their invocation shape (a plain `gitleaks detect` scan; codeql-action init/analyze on a real branch ref), not from a live queue run — the first real queue lap is the completion proof.

1785. **DEC-SWEEP-LOCK-PULL-CONCURRENCY-001 — the dashboard sweep route + the nightly sweep leg stop holding the LAKE pull flock through the sweep: CLI parity (G10 preload-only SH + G6 own the sweep-vs-pull exclusion), fixing the CONFIRMED dashboard/nightly G10 SELF-CONFLICT BLOCKER (LakeBusyError at every sweep preload since the G10 landing commit 3f32b3e) AND delivering the operator requirement that the daily pull + crossverify→S3 run CONCURRENTLY with a multi-day sweep** (2026-07-13 on `claude/sweep-lock-pull-concurrency`; fix(sweep); entry number #1785 = next free after the live-main tail #1784, clear of the in-flight reservations #1776–#1779 — gaps are legal, DEC-IDs are the stable handles per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001). **THE CONFIRMED BLOCKER (executed repro, 2026-07-13 investigation at HEAD 70d44a3):** the dashboard `POST /api/v1/sweep/run` started its sweep job via `BackgroundPullJob.start(...)` WITHOUT `cross_process_lock=False` (pre-fix app.py:7439-7445), so `start()` took `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` on `<lake_root>/.locks/pull_singleflight.lock` for the sweep's WHOLE run — and `cmd_sweep_all`'s G10 preload guard (`lake_read_guard`, `LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB` on the SAME file via `pull_singleflight_lock_path`, a NEW fd in the SAME process) was DENIED, because flock(2) locks attach to the open file description ("an attempt to lock the file using one of these file descriptors may be denied by a lock that the calling process has already placed via another file descriptor" — the repo itself pins this direction at `tests/unit/test_engine_sweep_singleflight.py` `test_g10_in_process_pull_ex_refuses_guard`, and app.py's crossverify comment already documented the mechanism). Verbatim executed evidence (Repro B — the REAL `BackgroundPullJob` composed exactly like the route): `job.start returned: True` … worker → `LakeBusyError: a pull/heal is running against this lake — wait for it to finish or stop it (pull single-flight lock held exclusively at /tmp/brutex-dashjob-repro-9m5kefh9/.locks/pull_singleflight.lock); refusing to preload sweep bars over a partition tree being rewritten` … job snapshot `state='error'` with that detail — the dashboard sweep DEAD ON ARRIVAL within seconds of the click, on every click, since G10 landed with the T1 sweep-core train commit `3f32b3e` (DEC-SWEEP-UNKILLABLE-CORE-001 #1712). The NIGHTLY failed identically: `collision_fn` entered the LAKE pull lock into the chain-lifetime `locks` ExitStack (pre-fix nightly/run.py:394-400, released only at chain exit — the #1612 acquire-and-HOLD design, written BEFORE G10 existed) and the sweep leg's real `cmd_sweep_all` self-conflicted the same way → a FAILED SWEEP link every night (chain breaker, cron-red). CI-BLIND by construction: every route test fakes `run_sweep_from_request` (`tests/unit/test_dashboard_sweep_run_route.py`) and the nightly tests inject a fake `run_sweep` seam (`tests/integration/test_nightly_chain_e2e.py`, `tests/unit/test_nightly_run.py`) — no CI path ever composed the real job flock with the real G10 guard. And even ABSENT the self-conflict, both compositions violated the OPERATOR REQUIREMENT: a job-level/chain-level whole-run EX hold locks the daily spot pull AND the crossverify producer (45-min bounded lock wait, `DEFAULT_LOCK_WAIT_S=2700.0` — `brutex/crossverify/config.py`) out for the sweep's 2-4-DAY wall time. **THE FIX (CLI parity at both sites — the bare CLI `brutex sweep-all` already had the right law):** (1) the sweep route's `start(...)` gains `cross_process_lock=False` (the crossverify precedent, app.py:5346): `cmd_sweep_all` owns the exclusion itself — the G10 lake read-guard held across the bar PRELOAD ONLY (`brutex/engine/sweep_singleflight.py` — "held across the PRELOAD ONLY … once the bars are in memory the sweep is immune to lake writes") + the G6 `sweep_run_lock` results-root single-flight; (2) the nightly's LAKE pull lock moves from the chain-lifetime `locks` stack into a NEW `lake_stack` closed in `pull_fn`'s `finally` — EXACTLY the account lock's existing post-PULL+PREBUILD release pattern (pre-fix run.py:509-513) — with a `locks.callback(lake_stack.close)` backstop so EVERY earlier failure path still releases (crash-safe; the capability-refusal arm closes it explicitly like the account stack); the stale run.py:9-19 module docstring ("no sweep-level flock exists") rewritten — G6 exists at `sweep_run_core.py` since #1712 and G10 at the cmd_sweep_all preload; (3) `BackgroundPullJob.start`'s `cross_process_lock=False` docstring widened from "the sanctioned use is a ZERO-WRITE run" to the two sanctioned classes — (a) zero-write runs (dry-run Greeks-backfill scan) and (b) runs whose CALLEE owns its own lock discipline on the SAME flock file(s) (the crossverify route + now the sweep route); ## DEC-CROSSVERIFY-OWED-SENTINEL-001 (2026-07-14)

1810. **DEC-CROSSVERIFY-OWED-SENTINEL-001 — the durable owed-day sentinel: a one-click Pull-Spot day whose box dies/sleeps/closes BEFORE the cross-verify tail ever starts is no longer SILENTLY skipped — both pull launchers write a durable "cross-verify OWED for <day>" marker at pull-tail-commit ENTRY, the runner's NEW step D3 COMPLETES a never-started owed prior day on the next run with the manual `--day` machinery verbatim, the marker clears ONLY at the day's completed material verdict, and owed days read LOUD on the /universe panel via the EMIT-ON-PRESENT `owed_days` progress field** (2026-07-14 on `claude/crossverify-owed-sentinel`; fix(crossverify); renumbered #1792 → #1810 at the 2026-07-15 club-T fold — main took #1792 for DEC-SPOTONLY-PREBUILD-EMPTY-EXCLUDE-001; DEC-IDs are the stable handles per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001; fixes the umbrella-assurance finding MAJOR-1 (CONFIRMED)). **THE DEFECT (file:line grounded):** on the one-click Pull-Spot flow (the dashboard `/pull-pipeline?scope=spot-only` launcher + its self-arming scheduler AND the CLI `brutex pull-all-spot`) the cross-verify → S3 push for "today" fires as the launcher's LAST step, downstream of the long prebuild — a box that died mid-prebuild (or mid-pull, or anywhere before the tail) skipped the day's same-day publish with ZERO loud signal: nothing in the pull chain wrote a crossverify sentinel, and BOTH catchup scans (`brutex/crossverify/journal.py` — `scan_pending_journals` + `scan_withheld_journals`, the step-D/D2 sources in `brutex/crossverify/run.py`) iterate days that HAVE a journal, so a NEVER-STARTED day (no journal) was structurally invisible to every catchup; the only loud signal was the launchd deadman — a separate operator install (`brutex crossverify install`) the one-click flow neither performs nor depends on, evaluated only on a manual `brutex crossverify status`. Bar DATA itself was never at risk (the next run's incremental pull heals it) — the gap was the day's same-day cross-verify + S3 publish and any loud "owed" signal. **THE FIX (one owed-store module, one law):** (1) NEW `brutex/crossverify/owed.py` — one atomic JSON marker per owed day at `<lake_root>/.crossverify/owed/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json` (per-day files make multi-day stacking + idempotent clears trivial; not `*.parquet` ⇒ invisible to every lake scanner). LAWS: **names-only scan** — the OWED verdict is the file's NAME, never its bytes (`list_owed_days` is one `os.scandir` of entry names; NO entry is ever opened, so a planted FIFO / device symlink can never hang the route poll, and a corrupt/tampered marker still reads OWED — owed-unknown degrades to OWED, never to a silent de-arm); **content is forensics only** — `load_owed_marker` (the run-time scan's diagnostic read) rides the shared #1614 round-7 regular-file-only fd-capped loader (`brutex.dashboard.pull_intent.read_sidecar_bytes` — `O_NONBLOCK` + `S_ISREG` on the open descriptor, the size cap on the SAME `fstat`), so even the diagnostic read never hangs/crashes on a planted inode (corrupt ⇒ `None` + ONE `crossverify.owed_marker_unreadable` WARN, the day STAYS owed); **best-effort-loud** — `mark_owed`/`clear_owed` never raise (a read-only volume / a directory planted at the marker path logs ONE `crossverify.owed_mark_failed`/`owed_clear_failed` WARN and returns False — never a failed pull, never silent); **kill-switch coherent** — the launchers mark through `mark_owed_for_pull`, which resolves the `BRUTEX_CROSSVERIFY_*` surface once and marks NOTHING under `BRUTEX_CROSSVERIFY=off` or junk env (one WARN — markers must never accumulate while the feature is deliberately off or unrunnable). (2) MARKER WRITE at pull-tail-commit ENTRY on BOTH surfaces: the dashboard spot-only `_work` body (`brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `if spot_only and not dry_run:` before `run_full_pipeline`, so the marker lands BEFORE the pull/prebuild chain; day = the route's `launch_day`) and the CLI `cmd_pull_all_spot` (`brutex/cli.py` — locks held, before the pipeline builder; day = the `--auto` gate's IST clock law, injected `now` seam wins); dry-runs, refused starts, full-scope and fno-only runs mark nothing (the tail is Spot-exclusive by the #1779 ruling). (3) NEVER-STARTED-DAY CATCHUP — run.py's NEW step D3 (`_owed_catchup_scan`, after D2, same `config.publish and not config.dry_run` gate, skipped after a nonretryable recovery abort exactly like the D2/orphan scans): `scan_owed_days` (the `scan_withheld_journals` window law — `today − catchup_days … today − 1`, `BRUTEX_CROSSVERIFY_CATCHUP_DAYS` bounded, oldest first) feeds each owed prior day to the NEW defaulted seam `CrossverifySeams.run_day`, whose production binding (`default_seams._run_day`) is the manual `--day` machinery VERBATIM — a recursive `run_crossverify` over `replace(config, day=prior, skip_pull=True, catchup_days=0)` (vendor-free: today's pull leg owns the vendor window; `catchup_days=0` is the structural recursion bound) with fresh day-bound `default_seams` carrying the SAME injections (so the prebuild/holder-note closures bind the PRIOR day, never today); the rerun acquires the lock trio in its own step F — legal because D3 runs BEFORE the outer step F (nothing held). Folding laws: the rerun's `publish_failed` count folds into the outer state (the final verdict stays loud, exit 2); a rerun `suspect` is the step-D/K whole-run halt class; a rerun `publish_failed`/`refused` ABORTS the scan (the step-D/D2 abort law — later days would fail identically, markers kept); a rerun `withheld_partial`/`blocked` CONTINUES (the day's journal now carries the honest record — D2 re-gates it next run once the lake heals); `run_day=None` (injected test seams) degrades honestly — owed days surfaced with ONE `crossverify.owed_rerun_unavailable` WARN, never silently dropped. ## DEC-CI-SECRETS-SCAN-DIFFBOUND-001 (2026-07-17)

1951. **DEC-CI-SECRETS-SCAN-DIFFBOUND-001 — bound the REQUIRED gating `secrets` (gitleaks) job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to the PR/push diff instead of gitleaks' implicit all-refs full-history walk, killing the cross-branch FALSE-POSITIVE that intermittently reds unrelated PRs' `secrets` gate** (2026-07-17 on `claude/ci-secrets-scan-diffbound`; fix(ci); entry number #1951 queue-master-allocated — gaps are legal per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001). **THE DEFECT (CONFIRMED, executed root-cause):** the `secrets` job (in the `ci-ok` needs list — a REQUIRED merge gate) checks out at `fetch-depth: 0` and runs `gitleaks detect --source . --config .gitleaks.toml --redact --verbose --exit-code 1` with NO `--log-opts`. gitleaks v8.21.2 given no `--log-opts` HARDCODES `git log -p -U0 --full-history --all` (sources/git.go:49-52), so `--all` walks EVERY fetched ref; under `fetch-depth: 0` (every `origin/*` branch fetched) it reaches UNRELATED sibling branches and flags a false positive on `.github/workflows/core-rust-parity.yml:181` (rule `generic-api-key`, commit `72b2c9b9`) — a hardware-fingerprint literal (`mac16-8-14c10p4e-48g-arm64`) that lives ONLY on the sibling branch `claude/rust-slice-t35-leaves`, NOT on main. That intermittently reds the gating `secrets` job on PRs whose OWN diff is clean. **THE FIX (scopes, does NOT weaken):** make the gitleaks step EVENT-AWARE, mirroring the sibling `.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml`'s proven `--log-opts` handling. A small inline shell computes `LOG_OPTS` from `github.event_name` (context passed via `env:`, never inline-interpolated into the script): `pull_request` → `--no-merges origin/${PR_BASE_REF:-main}..HEAD` (the PR's own commits vs its base — full PR-diff coverage PRESERVED, identical to gitleaks.yml), EXPLICITLY guarded fail-closed (the base ref is verified present with `git cat-file -e "origin/${PR_BASE_REF:-main}^{commit}"`; on absence the step emits `::error::` and `exit 1` rather than scan nothing); `push` → `--no-merges ${BEFORE_SHA}..${AFTER_SHA}` with the all-zeros/unknown-`before` first-push case guarded to fall back to a bounded `-1 HEAD` tip scan (never an empty/zero-patch range); `merge_group` → `--no-merges ${MG_BASE_SHA}..${MG_HEAD_SHA}` (the merge candidate's commits), likewise EXPLICITLY guarded fail-closed via `git cat-file -e`/parent-derivation/`exit 1`; the DEFAULT (and `workflow_dispatch`) is `-1 HEAD` — so NO gating path (PR / push / merge_group / dispatch) ever re-introduces the all-refs full-history walk, and the two PER-PR gating paths (pull_request + merge_group) are EXPLICITLY fail-closed when the diff range cannot be resolved — each guards its base ref with `git cat-file -e` and `exit 1`s on absence rather than let a git error be the only backstop — while the push path deliberately RETAINS the bounded first-push tip-scan (`-1 HEAD`, never an empty range) and is NOT an explicit `exit 1`: an explicit refusal there would reject a legitimate FIRST push to a new branch (all-zeros `before` → the fallback). Every other flag is verbatim (`--source . --config .gitleaks.toml --redact --verbose --exit-code 1`); `fetch-depth` is UNCHANGED; the `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist is untouched. **SCOPES-NOT-WEAKENS:** the PR-diff coverage a required secret-scan must have is byte-for-byte what gitleaks.yml already ships on `pull_request` (`--no-merges origin/${BASE_REF}..HEAD`); this only removes the cross-branch history the gate never intended to walk. The weekly `schedule` full-history all-branch scan (`--all --full-history`) still lives in the dedicated `gitleaks.yml` — the catch-all safety net is unaffected; only the fast PER-PR gate is scoped. CI-only — ZERO `brutex/` source change; ENGINE UNCHANGED — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY/SENSEX; F&O lake REFERENCE_ONLY; no lake/schema/scope/vocab/rate change; no new routes, no new env vars. **HARDENING ROUND (hostile-review SHIP + 2 MINORs, folded pre-merge):** (MINOR-1, FIXED) the `merge_group` path could FAIL OPEN on a REQUIRED merge gate — on a `merge_group` event HEAD is the SPECULATIVE MERGE commit, so when `MG_BASE_SHA` was empty/unfetched the old `-1 HEAD` fallback ran `git log -p -U0 -1 HEAD` over a merge commit, which emits ZERO patch lines → gitleaks scanned NOTHING and exited GREEN. The `merge_group` fallback is now NON-EMPTY-or-fail-closed: primary stays `--no-merges ${MG_BASE_SHA}..${MG_HEAD_SHA}` when the base is present+fetched; if it is missing but HEAD is a merge commit (both `HEAD^1` and `HEAD^2` resolve) it derives `--no-merges HEAD^1..HEAD^2` (the PR's incoming commits vs the queue tip, independent of the missing env var); if even that cannot resolve it FAILS CLOSED (`::error::` + `exit 1`) rather than scan a zero-patch speculative merge. The guiding rule: on the `merge_group` required-gate path gitleaks NEVER runs against an empty range and exits green. (NIT-2, FIXED) `PR_BASE_REF` is now `set -u`-safe via `origin/${PR_BASE_REF:-main}` (behavior-preserving — the `pull_request` trigger is `branches:[main]`, so the effective command stays byte-identical `--no-merges origin/main..HEAD`, and a validated positive gitleaks proof on that exact form holds). **SECOND HARDENING ROUND (explicit fail-closed on the `pull_request` path):** the `pull_request` path is now EXPLICITLY guarded fail-closed to match the `merge_group` pattern — it verifies the base ref exists with `git cat-file -e "origin/${PR_BASE_REF:-main}^{commit}"` and, on absence, emits `::error::pull_request: base ref origin/${PR_BASE_REF:-main} not found — refusing to scan (fail-closed)` and `exit 1`. This corrects the prior posture in which the `pull_request` path was NOT explicitly fail-closed: it relied on `set -euo pipefail` plus a downstream git error inside `gitleaks detect` as the only backstop against a missing/unfetched base ref — implicit, not an explicit refusal on a required security gate. With this change the two PER-PR gating paths (pull_request + merge_group) are EXPLICITLY fail-closed when the diff range cannot be resolved — each guards its base ref with `git cat-file -e` and `exit 1`s if the base is missing rather than let a git error be the only backstop. The push path deliberately RETAINS the bounded first-push tip-scan (`-1 HEAD`) and is deliberately NOT an explicit `exit 1`: an explicit refusal there would REJECT a legitimate FIRST push to a new branch (where `github.event.before`/`BEFORE_SHA` is the all-zeros SHA → the fallback), so it stays a bounded tip scan — with the disclosed MINOR-2 (a multi-commit force-push directly to `main` can under-scan the earlier commits — abnormal, an operator-only path, and those commits were already gated on their PR) standing as its documented honest-limit alongside NIT-1 (evil-merge / conflict-resolution content, pre-existing, NOT a regression). Byte-identical in the normal case: when the base ref IS present (PR base = main), the effective command is unchanged `gitleaks detect --source . --config .gitleaks.toml --log-opts="--no-merges origin/main..HEAD" --redact --verbose --exit-code 1`, so the prior positive gitleaks proof holds verbatim. **HONEST LIMITS (documented, NOT fixed):** (MINOR-2) the `push` path's first-push/force-push fallback is still `-1 HEAD` (tip commit only) — an ABNORMAL multi-commit force-push directly to `main` (post-PR-gate, an operator-only path) would under-scan the earlier pushed commits; the required PER-PR gate is unaffected. (NIT-1, PRE-EXISTING — NOT a regression) evil-merge / conflict-resolution content introduced by a merge commit itself is not scanned by `--no-merges` — the PRIOR implicit `--all` walk was equally `git log -p`-blind to merge-commit diffs, so this is no worse than before; the weekly full-history `gitleaks.yml` remains the catch-all.

## DEC-CI-PROOFBUNDLE-MKDIR-GATE-001 (2026-07-17)

1953. **DEC-CI-PROOFBUNDLE-MKDIR-GATE-001 — the `proof-bundle` CI job stops hard-failing on a concurrency-superseded (cancelled) run: it now SKIPS on cancellation via `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` and `mkdir -p proof` guards the manifest step** (2026-07-17, FOLDED into PR #1631 / `claude/ci-secrets-scan-diffbound`; fix(ci); entry number #1953 — gaps are legal per DEC-LEDGER-RENUMBER-001). **THE DEFECT:** the `proof-bundle` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, "aggregate CI artifacts") was `if: always()` and `needs` the producer jobs (test/bench/trivy/sbom). When a new push CONCURRENCY-CANCELS an in-flight run, those producers are cancelled and upload no artifacts, so the four `actions/download-artifact` steps (`continue-on-error: true`) find nothing and `proof/` is never created; the "Generate proof manifest" step's first command `cat > proof/MANIFEST.txt <<EOF` then exits 1 with `proof/MANIFEST.txt: No such file or directory` → a spurious red "Proof bundle" check + false-red webhooks across the whole superseded wave. **THE FIX (two-part, CI-hygiene only):** (1) the job's `if: always()` → `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` — it still runs on producer SUCCESS *or* FAILURE (aggregating a partial proof, the intended behavior), but SKIPS when the run was cancelled/superseded, so a cancelled run no longer runs-and-fails the check; (2) belt-and-braces, `mkdir -p proof` is prepended to the "Generate proof manifest" step's `run:` (before the `cat > proof/MANIFEST.txt`), so even a real (non-cancelled) run that downloaded zero artifacts creates the dir instead of hard-failing. The per-step `if: always()` on the download + manifest + upload sub-steps is UNCHANGED (it only governs within a running job; the job-level `!cancelled()` gate is what skips a cancelled run). **FOLD PROVENANCE:** delivered as an additive commit to the in-flight gitleaks gate-clear PR #1631 (DEC-CI-SECRETS-SCAN-DIFFBOUND-001, #1951) per the coordinator ruling, retiring the standalone #1953 PR; the SANCTIONED `secrets`/gitleaks hunk in the same `ci.yml` is BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNTOUCHED (the two diff hunks land entirely inside the separate `proof-bundle` job).
